translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.
interpretation: This verse is known as the 'Basmalah' and is considered a fundamental component of many aspects of Islamic practice. It is a prayer and a declaration of faith, reminding the believer of the compassionate and merciful nature of Allah. It is commonly recited before beginning any significant action, such as reading the Qur'an, performing prayers, or starting a new day.
orig: بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: الحمد لله رب العالمين

translation: The Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate
interpretation: This is not a complete verse, but rather the beginning of every chapter (surah) in the Qur'an, except for one. These are the names of God, and they serve as a reminder of His attributes of mercy and compassion. The recitation of these names is a form of remembrance of God and an expression of one's faith in His mercy and compassion.
orig: الرحمن الرحيم

translation: Master of the Day of Judgment.
interpretation: The phrase 'Master of the Day of Judgment' is a name for God, emphasizing His sovereignty and control over the Day of Judgment. This is the day when all of humanity will be resurrected and judged for their actions during their earthly lives. The verse serves as a reminder of God's ultimate power and authority, and the inevitability of the Day of Judgment. It encourages believers to live righteously in preparation for that day, and to place their trust in God's mercy and justice.
orig: مالك يوم الدين

translation: You alone we worship, and You alone we ask for help.
interpretation: The verse is a declaration of monotheism and a statement of faith in the oneness of God. It emphasizes the belief that God is the only one worthy of worship and that He is the only source of help and support. It is a reminder of the fundamental Islamic belief in the absolute sovereignty and power of God. The verse also highlights the importance of seeking help and guidance from God in all aspects of life.
orig: إياك نعبد وإياك نستعين

translation: Guide us to the straight path
interpretation: This verse is a supplication to God, asking for guidance to the straight path. It is a recognition of the need for divine guidance in order to navigate the complexities of life and make the right choices. It emphasizes the importance of following the path of righteousness and avoiding the path of error and deviation. It is a reminder that only through the guidance of God can one find the truth and attain success in this life and the hereafter.
orig: اهدنا الصراط المستقيم

translation: The path of those upon whom You have bestowed favor, not of those who have evoked [Your] anger or of those who are astray.
interpretation: The verse describes the path or way of life that leads to success and happiness, and distinguishes it from the path of those who have earned God's anger or are astray. The verse emphasizes the importance of following the path of righteousness and avoiding the path of sin and disbelief. It serves as a reminder that God bestows His favor on those who choose the right path and that those who choose the wrong path will face the consequences of their actions.
orig: صراط الذين أنعمت عليهم غير المغضوب عليهم ولا الضالين

translation: The (revelation) of the Book (the Quran) is from Allah, the Exalted in Power, Full of Wisdom.
interpretation: The verse asserts that the Quran is a revelation from Allah, the all-powerful and wise. It highlights the divine origin of the Quran, and emphasizes the qualities of Allah as being all-powerful and wise. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance and significance of the Quran, and the greatness of the one who revealed it.
orig: الم

translation: This is the Book in which there is no doubt, a guidance for the righteous.
interpretation: The verse affirms that the Qur'an is a guide for those who are mindful of God and strive to live righteously. The phrase 'no doubt in it' emphasizes the certainty and truth of the Qur'an's teachings. The verse serves as a reminder that the Qur'an is a source of guidance for those who seek to live a virtuous life, and a confirmation of the validity of the path of righteousness.
orig: ذلك الكتاب لا ريب فيه هدى للمتقين

translation: Those who believe in the unseen, establish prayer, and give out of what We have provided for them.
interpretation: The verse describes the characteristics of believers, who have faith in the unseen (such as the afterlife and God's power), establish prayer, and give charity from the provision that God has given them. This verse emphasizes the importance of faith, worship, and generosity, and highlights the relationship between human beings and God, where people are expected to use the resources they have been given in a responsible and generous way.
orig: الذين يؤمنون بالغيب ويقيمون الصلاة ومما رزقناهم ينفقون

translation: And those who believe in what has been revealed to you, [O Muhammad], and what was revealed before you, and they are certain of the Hereafter.
interpretation: The verse speaks about those who believe in the revelations brought by the Prophet Muhammad and those that were revealed before him, and who are certain of the Hereafter. The verse highlights the importance of believing in all of the revelations from God and having certainty in the existence of the Hereafter. This verse serves as a reminder to believers to have faith in all of the messages from God and to have a strong conviction in the afterlife.
orig: والذين يؤمنون بما أنزل إليك وما أنزل من قبلك وبالآخرة هم يوقنون

translation: Those are on (right) guidance from their Lord, and those are the successful.
interpretation: The verse distinguishes between two groups of people: those who are guided by their Lord and those who are not. The first group, those who are on the right guidance from their Lord, are described as the successful ones. This implies that following the guidance of one's Lord leads to success, both in this life and in the hereafter. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of seeking and following the guidance of the Creator in order to achieve true success and happiness.
orig: أولئك على هدى من ربهم وأولئك هم المفلحون

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve - it is the same to them whether you warn them or do not warn them - they will not believe.
interpretation: The verse highlights the closed-mindedness of the disbelievers and their rejection of the truth, no matter how much they are warned or reminded. The verse emphasizes the futility of trying to convince those who are set in their ways and unwilling to listen to reason or accept the truth. The verse serves as a reminder to the believers to focus their efforts on those who are open to guidance and to not be disheartened by the rejection of the disbelievers.
orig: إن الذين كفروا سواء عليهم أأنذرتهم أم لم تنذرهم لا يؤمنون

translation: Allah has set a seal upon their hearts and upon their hearing, and over their vision is a veil. And for them is a great punishment.
interpretation: The verse describes the state of those who have rejected the truth and closed themselves off from guidance. A seal has been set upon their hearts, ears, and eyes, preventing them from understanding and accepting the message of Islam. As a result, they are veiled from the truth and face a severe punishment. The verse serves as a warning to those who reject the message of Islam, emphasizing the consequences of denying the truth and turning away from God.
orig: ختم الله على قلوبهم وعلى سمعهم وعلى أبصارهم غشاوة ولهم عذاب عظيم

translation: And among the people are those who say, 'We believe in Allah and the Last Day,' but they are not believers.
interpretation: The verse highlights the hypocrisy of certain individuals who claim to believe in Allah and the Day of Judgment, but their actions and beliefs contradict their statements. The verse emphasizes that simply declaring one's faith is not sufficient, and that true belief must be reflected in one's words and actions. The verse serves as a warning to those who may outwardly profess their faith, but inwardly harbor doubts or engage in actions that contradict their faith. It reminds believers to consistently live out their faith in all aspects of their lives and to guard against hypocrisy.
orig: ومن الناس من يقول آمنا بالله وباليوم الآخر وما هم بمؤمنين

translation: They deceive Allah and those who believe, but they deceive not except themselves, and they perceive not.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the actions of those who try to deceive both God and the believers. However, the verse emphasizes that the only ones they truly deceive are themselves. They are unaware of the reality of their actions and the consequences of their deception. The verse serves as a warning to those who engage in deception and hypocrisy, reminding them that they cannot hide their true intentions from God and that their actions will ultimately harm themselves.
orig: يخادعون الله والذين آمنوا وما يخدعون إلا أنفسهم وما يشعرون

translation: In their hearts is a disease, so Allah increased their disease; and for them is a painful punishment because they were lying.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the punishment of those who have a disease in their hearts, meaning they are spiritually sick and have rejected the truth. As a result of their rejection, God increased their spiritual sickness, and they are threatened with a painful punishment. The verse serves as a warning to those who reject the truth and emphasizes the serious consequences of their actions. The punishment is a result of their lying and rejection of the truth.
orig: في قلوبهم مرض فزادهم الله مرضا ولهم عذاب أليم بما كانوا يكذبون

translation: But when it is said to them, 'Do not cause corruption in the land,' they say, 'We are only reformers.'
interpretation: The verse is addressing a group of people who are being told not to cause corruption in the land. However, instead of heeding this warning, they claim that they are actually reformers. The verse highlights the hypocrisy of these people, who claim to be working for the betterment of society while in reality they are causing corruption. The verse serves as a warning to those who engage in deception and hypocrisy, reminding them that their true intentions will be exposed and that they will be held accountable for their actions.
orig: وإذا قيل لهم لا تفسدوا في الأرض قالوا إنما نحن مصلحون

translation: Indeed, they are the corrupters, but they do not perceive.
interpretation: The verse describes a group of people as the 'corrupters', indicating that they are causing harm and damage. However, the verse also highlights the fact that these people are unaware of the consequences of their actions and do not realize the harm they are causing. The verse serves as a warning to those who engage in destructive and harmful behavior, reminding them that their actions have consequences and that they will be held accountable for them.
orig: ألا إنهم هم المفسدون ولكن لا يشعرون

translation: And when it is said to them, 'Believe as the people have believed,' they say, 'Shall we believe as the foolish have believed?' Indeed, they are the foolish, but they know it not.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the rejection of faith by a group of people, who, when invited to believe like the majority of people, mockingly ask if they should believe as the foolish have believed. The verse highlights the arrogance and stubbornness of these people, who, despite their ignorance, consider themselves superior to others. The verse also emphasizes the importance of humility and open-mindedness in accepting the truth and the guidance of God. Ultimately, the verse serves as a reminder that those who reject faith and guidance will be exposed for their foolishness and ignorance, while those who embrace it will be rewarded with knowledge and wisdom.
orig: وإذا قيل لهم آمنوا كما آمن الناس قالوا أنؤمن كما آمن السفهاء ألا إنهم هم السفهاء ولكن لا يعلمون

translation: And when they meet those who believe, they say, 'We believe,' but when they are alone with their devils, they say, 'Indeed, we are with you; indeed, we were only mocking.'
interpretation: The verse describes the hypocrisy of certain individuals who outwardly claim to believe in the faith, but inwardly reject it. When they are in the company of believers, they pretend to be believers themselves, but when they are alone with their devils or inner selves, they confess their disbelief and mock the believers. The verse serves as a warning against hypocrisy and highlights the importance of sincerity and authenticity in one's faith.
orig: وإذا لقوا الذين آمنوا قالوا آمنا وإذا خلوا إلى شياطينهم قالوا إنا معكم إنما نحن مستهزئون

translation: In which Allah mocks them and provides for them a livelihood while they persist in their disbelief.
interpretation: The verse refers to the situation where Allah mocks the disbelievers and provides them with a livelihood despite their rejection of faith. The verse highlights the irony of the situation where Allah, in His infinite wisdom and power, allows the disbelievers to enjoy the blessings of life while they continue to reject Him. The verse serves as a reminder of the ultimate fate of the disbelievers and the futility of their actions, and emphasizes the importance of faith and belief in Allah.
orig: الله يستهزئ بهم ويمدهم في طغيانهم يعمهون

translation: Those are the ones who bought error in place of guidance, so their trade did not profit them, nor were they guided.
interpretation: The verse describes those who have chosen to follow error and falsehood instead of guidance and truth. The verse emphasizes the negative consequences of this choice, noting that their 'trade' or actions did not bring them any benefit or profit. The verse also highlights that they have strayed from the path of guidance and are not being led in the right direction.
orig: أولئك الذين اشتروا الضلالة بالهدى فما ربحت تجارتهم وما كانوا مهتدين

translation: Like them is the one who kindles a fire, then when it illuminates what is around him, God takes away their light, leaving them in darkness where they cannot see.
interpretation: The verse uses the metaphor of someone who lights a fire, only to have it taken away by God, leaving them in darkness, to illustrate the consequences of those who commit sins and then are left in spiritual darkness, unable to find their way. The verse serves as a warning to those who engage in sinful behavior, reminding them that their actions can lead to a state of spiritual blindness, where they are unable to see the truth and find their way back to God. The verse emphasizes the importance of turning away from sin and seeking God's guidance in order to avoid ending up in a state of spiritual darkness.
orig: مثلهم كمثل الذي استوقد نارا فلما أضاءت ما حوله ذهب الله بنورهم وتركهم في ظلمات لا يبصرون

translation: Deaf, dumb, and blind - so they will not return (to the right path).
interpretation: The verse describes people who are spiritually deaf, dumb, and blind, meaning that they are unable or unwilling to understand and accept the truth. The phrase 'so they will not return' implies that they have strayed from the right path and are unlikely to find their way back. The verse may serve as a warning or a critique of those who reject or ignore the message of Islam, emphasizing the consequences of their actions and the importance of spiritual sight and hearing.
orig: صم بكم عمي فهم لا يرجعون

translation: Or like a rainstorm from the sky, wherein is darkness, thunder, and lightning. They put their fingers in their ears against the thunderclaps, in dread of death. But Allah is encompassing of the disbelievers.
interpretation: The verse uses the imagery of a violent thunderstorm to describe God's punishment of the disbelievers. The storm is characterized by darkness, thunder, and lightning, and the people are depicted as putting their fingers in their ears in fear of the thunderclaps. Despite their attempts to protect themselves, the verse emphasizes that God's punishment is inevitable and all-encompassing, as indicated by the phrase 'But Allah is encompassing of the disbelievers.' The verse serves as a reminder of the power and authority of God, and the consequences of disbelief and rejection of His signs.
orig: أو كصيب من السماء فيه ظلمات ورعد وبرق يجعلون أصابعهم في آذانهم من الصواعق حذر الموت والله محيط بالكافرين

translation: The lightning almost snatches away their sight, whenever it flashes for them, they walk therein and when darkness covers them, they stand still. And if Allah willed, He could have taken away their hearing and their sight. Indeed, Allah is over all things competent.
interpretation: The verse describes the experience of people in the darkness, when they are suddenly struck by a flash of lightning. The lightning allows them to see for a moment, but when it disappears, they are left in darkness again and are unable to move forward. The verse emphasizes the power of Allah, who can take away their senses if He wills. The verse serves as a reminder of the power and control of Allah, and the vulnerability and dependence of human beings.
orig: يكاد البرق يخطف أبصارهم كلما أضاء لهم مشوا فيه وإذا أظلم عليهم قاموا ولو شاء الله لذهب بسمعهم وأبصارهم إن الله على كل شيء قدير

translation: O mankind, worship your Lord, who created you and those before you, so that you may become righteous.
interpretation: The verse addresses all of humanity and commands them to worship their Lord, who is the creator of all beings, including those who lived before the current generation. By worshipping the one true God, people can attain righteousness and avoid the errors of the past. This verse emphasizes the importance of worship and obedience to God, and the ultimate goal of attaining righteousness, which is a fundamental principle of Islamic teachings.
orig: يا أيها الناس اعبدوا ربكم الذي خلقكم والذين من قبلكم لعلكم تتقون

translation: Who has made the earth a bed for you, and the heavens a canopy; and sent down from the heavens, rain, and brought forth therewith fruits for your sustenance; so do not set up rivals to God when you know (better).
interpretation: The verse speaks about God's blessings and provisions for humanity, such as the earth as a bed, the sky as a canopy, the rain that brings forth fruits, and the resulting sustenance for people. The verse then commands people not to associate partners with God, reminding them that they have knowledge of God's oneness and power. The verse emphasizes the importance of recognizing and being grateful for God's blessings and avoiding shirk (associating partners with God).
orig: الذي جعل لكم الأرض فراشا والسماء بناء وأنزل من السماء ماء فأخرج به من الثمرات رزقا لكم فلا تجعلوا لله أندادا وأنتم تعلمون

translation: But if you are in doubt about what We have revealed to Our servant, then produce a surah like it and call upon your witnesses other than Allah, if you are truthful.
interpretation: The verse challenges the doubters of the Qur'an to produce a surah (chapter) similar to it, if they truly believe that it is not from God. This challenge is seen as impossible to fulfill, as the Qur'an's eloquence and beauty are considered to be unmatched. The verse also invites the doubters to bring their witnesses to support their claim, other than Allah, if they are truthful in their doubt. This verse serves as a confirmation of the Qur'an's divine origin and as a means of silencing the doubters and deniers.
orig: وإن كنتم في ريب مما نزلنا على عبدنا فأتوا بسورة من مثله وادعوا شهداءكم من دون الله إن كنتم صادقين

translation: But if you do not [people, obey God and His Messenger, then fear the Fire, whose fuel is people and stones, prepared for the disbelievers.
interpretation: The verse warns of the punishment of the Fire for those who do not obey God and His Messenger. The Fire is described as being fueled by people and stones, indicating that it is a severe and unquenchable punishment. The Fire is said to be prepared for the disbelievers, emphasizing that it is a certainty for those who do not believe in God. The verse serves as a reminder to people to obey God and His Messenger in order to avoid this punishment and attain salvation.
orig: فإن لم تفعلوا ولن تفعلوا فاتقوا النار التي وقودها الناس والحجارة أعدت للكافرين

translation: And give good news to those who believe and do good deeds that they will have gardens beneath which rivers flow. Whenever they are provided with fruit from it as provision, they will say, 'This is what we were provided with before,' and it will be given to them in resemblance. And for them in it are purified spouses, and they will abide therein eternally.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the reward for those who believe in God and do good deeds. They are promised gardens beneath which rivers flow, and whenever they are provided with fruit from it, they will recognize it as the same provision they had before. This repetition of the same provision in the afterlife emphasizes the abundance and continuity of the blessings that the believers will receive. Additionally, the verse mentions that the believers will have purified spouses in the gardens, and they will live there eternally. The verse serves as a motivation for believers to continue doing good deeds, reminding them of the great reward that awaits them in the afterlife.
orig: وبشر الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات أن لهم جنات تجري من تحتها الأنهار كلما رزقوا منها من ثمرة رزقا قالوا هذا الذي رزقنا من قبل وأتوا به متشابها ولهم فيها أزواج مطهرة وهم فيها خالدون

translation: Indeed, Allah does not shy away from presenting an example - that of a mosquito or what is smaller than it. So those who believe know that it is truth from their Lord. But as for those who disbelieve, they say, 'What does Allah mean by this example?' Thus, many go astray from it and many are guided by it. But those who are transgressors only go further astray from the right path.
interpretation: The verse highlights the power and greatness of Allah by using the example of a mosquito or something even smaller. Those who have faith understand and acknowledge the truth of this example as a sign from their Lord. However, the disbelievers question and mock the example, leading many astray. At the same time, the example guides many others towards the right path. The verse emphasizes the importance of faith in understanding and accepting the signs of Allah and the consequences of disbelief and transgression.
orig: إن الله لا يستحيي أن يضرب مثلا ما بعوضة فما فوقها فأما الذين آمنوا فيعلمون أنه الحق من ربهم وأما الذين كفروا فيقولون ماذا أراد الله بهذا مثلا يضل به كثيرا ويهدي به كثيرا وما يضل به إلا الفاسقين

translation: Those who break the covenant of God after its confirmation and sever that which God has commanded to be joined and make mischief in the land, those are the losers.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the people who break the covenant of God, sever what God has commanded to be joined, and cause corruption in the land. These people are described as the losers. The verse emphasizes the importance of upholding the covenant of God and following God's commands. It also highlights the negative consequences of causing corruption and discord in the society. The verse serves as a reminder that those who engage in such actions will ultimately be the losers in this life and in the hereafter.
orig: الذين ينقضون عهد الله من بعد ميثاقه ويقطعون ما أمر الله به أن يوصل ويفسدون في الأرض أولئك هم الخاسرون

translation: How can you disbelieve in Allah while you were dead and He gave you life; then He will cause you to die and then give you life; then to Him you will be returned?
interpretation: The verse is addressing the disbelievers and questioning their disbelief in Allah, despite the clear evidence of His existence and power. The verse reminds them that they were once dead (in a state of non-existence) and Allah gave them life. This is a reference to their creation and the creation of all living beings. The verse then goes on to say that Allah will cause them to die and then give them life again, which is a reference to the Day of Resurrection. The verse emphasizes the power and control that Allah has over life and death. The verse ends by stating that all of humanity will be returned to Allah, which is a reminder of the ultimate destination of all souls and the importance of leading a righteous life in preparation for the Day of Judgment.
orig: كيف تكفرون بالله وكنتم أمواتا فأحياكم ثم يميتكم ثم يحييكم ثم إليه ترجعون

translation: He it is Who created for you all that is in the earth; then turned He to the heaven, and fashioned seven heavens; and He is aware of all things.
interpretation: The verse affirms that it is God who has created everything on earth and then turned His attention to the heavens, creating seven layers of heavens. The verse emphasizes God's power and knowledge, stating that He is aware of all things. The verse serves as a reminder of God's greatness and His role as the creator of all things, and encourages people to reflect on the wonders of His creation and the intricacies of His design.
orig: هو الذي خلق لكم ما في الأرض جميعا ثم استوى إلى السماء فسواهن سبع سماوات وهو بكل شيء عليم

translation: And when your Lord said to the angels, 'Indeed, I will make upon the earth a successive authority.' They said, 'Will You place in it one who causes corruption therein and sheds blood, while we declare Your praise and sanctify You?' He said, 'Indeed, I know that which you do not know.'
interpretation: The verse describes a conversation between God and the angels, in which God announces His intention to place a 'successive authority' on Earth. The angels express their concern that this authority will cause corruption and shed blood, while the angels praise and sanctify God. God responds by asserting that He has knowledge that the angels do not possess. The verse can be interpreted as a statement of God's sovereignty and power, and His ability to control the course of events on Earth, despite the potential for corruption and violence. It also highlights the contrast between the angels' pure and unchanging nature, and the imperfections and challenges that are inherent in human existence.
orig: وإذ قال ربك للملائكة إني جاعل في الأرض خليفة قالوا أتجعل فيها من يفسد فيها ويسفك الدماء ونحن نسبح بحمدك ونقدس لك قال إني أعلم ما لا تعلمون

translation: And He taught Adam all the names, then presented them to the angels. He said: 'Inform Me of the names of these, if you are truthful.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about God teaching Adam all the names, and then presenting them to the angels. God then challenges the angels to inform Him of the names of these, if they are truthful. The verse highlights the unique status of Adam, who was given the knowledge of all the names by God. The verse also emphasizes the importance of truthfulness, as the angels are only able to fulfill God's request if they are truthful. The verse can be interpreted as a reminder of the special relationship between God and humanity, and the responsibility of humans to seek knowledge and be truthful.
orig: وعلم آدم الأسماء كلها ثم عرضهم على الملائكة فقال أنبئوني بأسماء هؤلاء إن كنتم صادقين

translation: They said, 'Exalted are You! We have no knowledge except what You have taught us. Indeed, You are the Knowing, the Wise.'
interpretation: The verse is a statement of surrender and recognition of God's power and knowledge by the people. They acknowledge that they have no knowledge except what God has taught them and that God is the All-Knowing and Wise. This verse emphasizes the idea of God's omniscience and the limitations of human knowledge. It also highlights the importance of recognizing and submitting to God's power and wisdom.
orig: قالوا سبحانك لا علم لنا إلا ما علمتنا إنك أنت العليم الحكيم

translation: He said, 'O Adam, inform them of their names.' And when he had informed them of their names, He said, 'Did I not tell you that I know the unseen of the heavens and the earth and I know what you reveal and what you were hiding?'
interpretation: The verse recounts a conversation between God and Adam, in which God asks Adam to inform the angels of the names of all things. After Adam successfully completes this task, God asserts His omniscience and omnipresence, emphasizing that He knows both the visible and invisible aspects of the heavens and the earth. The verse underscores God's all-encompassing knowledge and power, and serves as a reminder of the limits of human knowledge and ability.
orig: قال يا آدم أنبئهم بأسمائهم فلما أنبأهم بأسمائهم قال ألم أقل لكم إني أعلم غيب السماوات والأرض وأعلم ما تبدون وما كنتم تكتمون

translation: And when We said to the angels: 'Prostrate yourselves before Adam', they prostrated themselves, except Iblis; he refused and was arrogant, and he was of the disbelievers.'
interpretation: The verse describes the event of the creation of Adam, where God commanded the angels to prostrate before him. All the angels obeyed, except for Iblis (Satan), who refused and was arrogant. This verse highlights the fundamental difference between the obedient angels and the disobedient Satan, and emphasizes the importance of obedience and humility before God. It also sets the stage for the subsequent story of the fall of Adam and Eve and the entry of sin into the world, and serves as a reminder of the consequences of disobedience and arrogance towards God.
orig: وإذ قلنا للملائكة اسجدوا لآدم فسجدوا إلا إبليس أبى واستكبر وكان من الكافرين

translation: And We said, 'O Adam, dwell you and your spouse in the Garden and eat from wherever you will, but do not approach this tree, lest you become of the wrongdoers.'
interpretation: The verse describes God's command to Adam and his spouse to live in the Garden and eat from its fruits, with the exception of one tree. The command serves as a test for Adam and his spouse, and their obedience or disobedience will determine their status. The verse highlights the importance of obedience to God's commands and the consequences of disobedience, as disobedience will result in becoming one of the wrongdoers. The verse also sets the stage for the story of the fall of Adam and Eve, which serves as a foundational story in Islamic theology and ethics.
orig: وقلنا يا آدم اسكن أنت وزوجك الجنة وكلا منها رغدا حيث شئتما ولا تقربا هذه الشجرة فتكونا من الظالمين

translation: Then Satan made them both fall from it, and he made them not realize of what they were in. And We said, 'Go down, one of you an enemy to the other. And for you on the earth is a dwelling place and enjoyment for a time.'
interpretation: The verse describes the expulsion of Adam and Eve from Paradise as a result of their disobedience to God, caused by Satan's deception. The verse highlights the loss of their previous state of bliss and their new reality of enmity and strife. The verse also emphasizes the temporary nature of their existence on earth, with a dwelling place and enjoyment being provided for a limited time. The verse carries a message of the consequences of disobedience and the transient nature of worldly pleasures, and ultimately serves as a reminder of the ultimate purpose of human existence, which is to worship and obey God.
orig: فأزلهما الشيطان عنها فأخرجهما مما كانا فيه وقلنا اهبطوا بعضكم لبعض عدو ولكم في الأرض مستقر ومتاع إلى حين

translation: And when Adam received words from his Lord, He relented towards him. Indeed, He is the Accepting of repentance, the Merciful.
interpretation: The verse speaks about Adam, the first human, and his repentance after committing a mistake. When Adam received words (or instructions) from his Lord, he felt remorse and repented, and God, being the Accepting of repentance and Merciful, forgave him. The verse highlights the importance of repentance and the boundless mercy of God towards his creation, even after they have erred.
orig: فتلقى آدم من ربه كلمات فتاب عليه إنه هو التواب الرحيم

translation: We said: 'Get down all of you from here.' Then, if comes to you Guidance from Me, whoever follows My Guidance will have no fear, nor will they grieve.
interpretation: The verse speaks about God's command to the people to descend from a place, which is believed to be heaven or a state of bliss. The verse implies that if the people receive guidance from God, those who follow it will have nothing to fear and will not be grieved. The verse highlights the importance of following God's guidance and the blessings that come with it, such as the absence of fear and grief. The verse serves as a reminder to the people to seek and follow God's guidance, and to have faith in His plan and protection.
orig: قلنا اهبطوا منها جميعا فإما يأتينكم مني هدى فمن تبع هداي فلا خوف عليهم ولا هم يحزنون

translation: But those who disbelieved and denied Our signs - they are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the fate of those who disbelieved in God and denied His signs. The verse makes it clear that these people will be the companions of the Fire, meaning that they will reside in Hell. The verse emphasizes the permanence of their punishment, as they will abide therein forever. The verse serves as a warning to those who reject God and His signs, reminding them of the severe consequences of their disbelief and denial.
orig: والذين كفروا وكذبوا بآياتنا أولئك أصحاب النار هم فيها خالدون

translation: O Children of Israel, remember My favor which I have bestowed upon you and fulfill My covenant that I will fulfill your covenant, and fear Me.
interpretation: The verse is addressed to the Children of Israel, reminding them of God's favor upon them and urging them to fulfill their covenant with God. The verse emphasizes the importance of keeping the covenant and the need to fear God. The verse serves as a reminder of the special relationship between God and the Children of Israel, and the responsibilities that come with it. The verse also highlights the importance of honoring commitments and the consequences of breaking them.
orig: يا بني إسرائيل اذكروا نعمتي التي أنعمت عليكم وأوفوا بعهدي أوف بعهدكم وإياي فارهبون

translation: And believe in what I have sent down, confirming what is with you, and be not the first to disbelieve in it, and do not sell My verses for a small price; and fear Me.
interpretation: The verse commands believers to have faith in the revelation sent down by God, which confirms and builds upon the previous revelations. The verse warns against being the first to disbelieve in it and against selling the verses (i.e. the revelation) for a small price. This can be interpreted as a warning against compromising one's faith for worldly gain or temporary pleasure. The verse also emphasizes the importance of fearing God, and it serves as a reminder that the revelation is a sacred trust that should not be treated lightly or sold for a small price.
orig: وآمنوا بما أنزلت مصدقا لما معكم ولا تكونوا أول كافر به ولا تشتروا بآياتي ثمنا قليلا وإياي فاتقون

translation: And do not mix truth with falsehood, nor conceal the truth while you know [it].
interpretation: The verse is a command from God to His believers to uphold the truth and not to mix it with falsehood. It also forbids them from concealing the truth, especially when they are aware of it. This verse emphasizes the importance of honesty, integrity, and transparency in all aspects of life. It serves as a reminder that God is aware of the actions of His believers and that they will be held accountable for their deeds. The verse encourages believers to stand up for the truth and not to succumb to the pressures of falsehood, even if it means going against popular opinion or facing adversity.
orig: ولا تلبسوا الحق بالباطل وتكتموا الحق وأنتم تعلمون

translation: And establish prayer and give zakah and bow with those who bow [in worship].
interpretation: The verse is a command from God to establish the five daily prayers (salah), to give the obligatory charity (zakah), and to bow in prayer with other believers. By performing these acts of worship, Muslims are able to strengthen their faith, purify their souls, and establish a connection with God. This verse emphasizes the importance of community and unity in Islam, as believers are encouraged to worship together and support one another in their spiritual journey. Additionally, the verse serves as a reminder of the importance of giving to those in need and helping to create a just and equitable society.
orig: وأقيموا الصلاة وآتوا الزكاة واركعوا مع الراكعين

translation: You enjoin people to be righteous, but forget your own selves, while you recite the Scripture! Will you not reflect?
interpretation: The verse addresses those who enjoin others to be righteous and virtuous, but neglect their own selves and fail to practice what they preach. The verse points out the hypocrisy of these individuals, who recite the Scripture but do not reflect on its teachings or apply them to their own lives. The verse serves as a reminder for these people to practice self-reflection and self-improvement, and to lead by example rather than hypocrisy.
orig: أتأمرون الناس بالبر وتنسون أنفسكم وأنتم تتلون الكتاب أفلا تعقلون

translation: And seek help through patience and prayer, and indeed, it is difficult except for the humbly submissive [to Allah].
interpretation: The verse encourages believers to seek help through patience and prayer during times of hardship and difficulty. The verse emphasizes that this is not an easy task, but only those who are humbly submissive to Allah's will can truly succeed in this endeavor. This verse serves as a reminder that patience and prayer are powerful tools for overcoming adversity, but they require a deep sense of humility and submission to Allah's will.
orig: واستعينوا بالصبر والصلاة وإنها لكبيرة إلا على الخاشعين

translation: Those who think that they will meet their Lord (on the Day of Judgment) and that they will return to Him.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the belief of certain individuals who think that they will meet their Lord on the Day of Judgment and that they will return to Him. This verse highlights the importance of having the right belief and understanding the reality of the Day of Judgment. It reminds us that we will all return to our Creator and be held accountable for our actions. The verse encourages us to prepare for this inevitable day by living a righteous life and striving to please Allah.
orig: الذين يظنون أنهم ملاقو ربهم وأنهم إليه راجعون

translation: O children of Israel, remember My favor which I have bestowed upon you and that I have preferred you over the worlds.
interpretation: The verse addresses the children of Israel and reminds them of God's favor and blessings upon them. It emphasizes that God has chosen and preferred them above all other nations, which highlights their special status and responsibility. The verse encourages the children of Israel to remember and be grateful for these blessings and to recognize their unique position. It also serves as a reminder for them to live up to this responsibility and to honor the trust placed in them by God.
orig: يا بني إسرائيل اذكروا نعمتي التي أنعمت عليكم وأني فضلتكم على العالمين

translation: And fear a day where no soul will suffice for another, nor will intercession be accepted from it, nor will compensation be taken from it, nor will they be helped.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the Day of Judgment, emphasizing the individual responsibility of every person and the severity of that day. On this day, no soul will be able to atone for another's sins, nor will any form of intercession be accepted. Furthermore, compensation or ransom will not be allowed, and no one will be able to help or support another. The verse highlights the importance of taking responsibility for one's own actions and seeking God's forgiveness and mercy, as there will be no second chances on the Day of Judgment.
orig: واتقوا يوما لا تجزي نفس عن نفس شيئا ولا يقبل منها شفاعة ولا يؤخذ منها عدل ولا هم ينصرون

translation: And when We delivered you from the house of Pharaoh, they were inflicting on you the worst of punishment, killing your sons and sparing your women, and therein was a great trial from your Lord.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the deliverance of the Israelites from the oppression of Pharaoh and his people. The verse highlights the severity of the punishment inflicted upon the Israelites, who were killing their sons and sparing their women, indicating the depth of their hatred and cruelty. The verse also emphasizes the trial and test that this situation presented for the Israelites, as a means of purification and strengthening of their faith. The verse serves as a reminder of God's protection and deliverance of the oppressed, and the significance of patience and steadfastness in the face of adversity.
orig: وإذ نجيناكم من آل فرعون يسومونكم سوء العذاب يذبحون أبناءكم ويستحيون نساءكم وفي ذلكم بلاء من ربكم عظيم

translation: And when We separated the sea for you and saved you and drowned the people of Pharaoh while you were looking on.
interpretation: The verse describes the parting of the Red Sea, which allowed the Israelites to escape from the army of Pharaoh. The verse highlights God's role in saving the Israelites and punishing the unjust people of Pharaoh. The phrase "while you were looking on" emphasizes the miraculous nature of the event and the direct involvement of God in the salvation of the Israelites. The verse serves as a reminder of God's power and the ultimate fate of those who persist in their oppression and disbelief.
orig: وإذ فرقنا بكم البحر فأنجيناكم وأغرقنا آل فرعون وأنتم تنظرون

translation: And when We appointed with Moses a time of forty nights, then you took the calf (for worship) after him and you were unjust.
interpretation: The verse refers to the story of the Israelites, who were led by Moses, when they were commanded to wait for Moses for forty nights. However, they grew impatient and created a golden calf to worship, which was an act of injustice and disobedience. The verse serves as a reminder of the consequences of impatience and disobedience and highlights the importance of having faith and trust in God's plan.
orig: وإذ واعدنا موسى أربعين ليلة ثم اتخذتم العجل من بعده وأنتم ظالمون

translation: Then We pardoned you after that, so perhaps you would be grateful.
interpretation: The verse is speaking to a group of people (presumably the believers) and reminding them of a past transgression for which they were forgiven. The verse emphasizes God's mercy and forgiveness, as He chose to pardon them despite their wrongdoing. The purpose of this reminder is to encourage the people to express gratitude for God's forgiveness and to lead them to a more mindful and thankful way of living. The verse can also be seen as a call for repentance, reminding the people that God is always ready to forgive and that they should not take His mercy for granted.
orig: ثم عفونا عنكم من بعد ذلك لعلكم تشكرون

translation: And when We gave Moses the Book and the Discrimination, that perhaps you would be guided.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the giving of the Book (Torah) and the Discrimination (the ability to distinguish between right and wrong) to Moses. The purpose of this was to guide the people. This verse highlights the significance of divine guidance and the importance of scripture and wisdom in leading people on the right path.
orig: وإذ آتينا موسى الكتاب والفرقان لعلكم تهتدون

translation: And when Moses said to his people: 'O my people, indeed you have wronged yourselves by taking the calf [for worship]. So turn in repentance to your Creator and kill yourselves. That is best for you with your Creator.' Then He turned to you in forgiveness. Indeed, He is the All-Forgiving, the Most Merciful.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the story of the Israelites worshipping the calf while Moses was away. Moses, upon his return, calls out his people for their wrongdoing and commands them to repent to their Creator and to kill themselves as a form of atonement. This commandment is not to be taken literally, but rather, it symbolizes their complete and utter devotion and submission to God. After their repentance, God, being the All-Forgiving and the Most Merciful, forgives them. The verse serves as a reminder of the severity of committing sins and the importance of repentance and seeking forgiveness from God.
orig: وإذ قال موسى لقومه يا قوم إنكم ظلمتم أنفسكم باتخاذكم العجل فتوبوا إلى بارئكم فاقتلوا أنفسكم ذلكم خير لكم عند بارئكم فتاب عليكم إنه هو التواب الرحيم

translation: But when you said, 'O Moses, we will not believe in you until we see Allah plainly.' So the punishment seized you while you were looking on.
interpretation: The verse describes the story of the Israelites' demand for a visible sign from God, and their rejection of Prophet Moses's message until they see God with their own eyes. The verse then describes how they were punished while they were looking on, emphasizing the sudden and unexpected nature of the punishment. The verse serves as a reminder of the dangers of demanding signs and proofs from God, and the consequences of rejecting God's messengers. It also highlights the importance of faith and trust in God, even in the absence of visible signs and proofs.
orig: وإذ قلتم يا موسى لن نؤمن لك حتى نرى الله جهرة فأخذتكم الصاعقة وأنتم تنظرون

translation: Then We raised you up after your death, that you might give thanks.
interpretation: The verse speaks about God raising the people up after their death, so that they may give thanks. This verse could be interpreted as a reference to the resurrection of the dead on the Day of Judgment. On that day, people will be raised from their graves and called to account for their actions in this world. They will be given the opportunity to express their gratitude to God for the blessings they received in their earthly lives, and to seek His forgiveness for their sins. The verse emphasizes the importance of giving thanks to God, and the great reward that awaits those who are grateful for His blessings.
orig: ثم بعثناكم من بعد موتكم لعلكم تشكرون

translation: And We shaded you with clouds and sent down on you manna and quails: 'Eat of the good things We have provided for you.' They did not wrong Us, but they wronged themselves.
interpretation: The verse speaks about God's provision for the people, shading them with clouds and providing them with manna (a type of food) and quails. The verse emphasizes the goodness of the provisions and encourages the people to eat of the good things. The verse also highlights that the people did not wrong God, but they wronged themselves, indicating that their actions have consequences and they are ultimately responsible for their own well-being.
orig: وظللنا عليكم الغمام وأنزلنا عليكم المن والسلوى كلوا من طيبات ما رزقناكم وما ظلمونا ولكن كانوا أنفسهم يظلمون

translation: And when We said, 'Enter this town and eat from it wherever you will in ease and enter the gate prostrate, and say, "Forgive us," and we will forgive you your sins. And we will increase the righteous.'
interpretation: The verse describes God's instructions to a group of people to enter a town and eat from it freely, as a sign of His generosity. They are also told to enter the town in a humble and respectful manner, by prostrating themselves and asking for forgiveness for their sins. The verse highlights the idea of divine mercy and forgiveness, as God promises to forgive the sins of those who enter the town with humility and sincerity. It also emphasizes the importance of gratitude and righteousness, as God promises to increase the rewards of those who are virtuous and do good deeds.
orig: وإذ قلنا ادخلوا هذه القرية فكلوا منها حيث شئتم رغدا وادخلوا الباب سجدا وقولوا حطة نغفر لكم خطاياكم وسنزيد المحسنين

translation: But those who wronged changed [their] words to a statement other than what they were spoken. So We sent down upon those who wronged a punishment from the sky because they were defiantly disobedient.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the punishment of those who changed their words or promises from what they had originally agreed upon, and who were unjust and disobedient towards God. The verse emphasizes the consequences of changing one's words and going against what is right and true. The punishment was sent down from the sky, indicating its certainty and severity. The verse serves as a reminder that those who act unjustly and go against their word will face God's punishment.
orig: فبدل الذين ظلموا قولا غير الذي قيل لهم فأنزلنا على الذين ظلموا رجزا من السماء بما كانوا يفسقون

translation: And when Moses asked his people for water, We said, 'Strike the rock with your staff.' Then twelve springs gushed out from it. Every group knew its drinking place. Eat and drink from the provision of Allah, and do not cause corruption in the land as corruptors.
interpretation: The verse describes an incident where Moses strikes a rock with his staff, causing twelve springs of water to gush out. This miracle provided water for the people and demonstrated Moses' prophethood. The verse emphasizes the importance of using natural resources wisely and responsibly, and not causing corruption or destruction in the land. The provision of water is seen as a blessing from God, and the people are encouraged to be grateful and not wasteful. The verse also highlights the unity of the community, as each group had its designated water source, and no one was left without access to water. The verse serves as a reminder to be mindful of the impact of our actions on the environment and to use resources responsibly.
orig: وإذ استسقى موسى لقومه فقلنا اضرب بعصاك الحجر فانفجرت منه اثنتا عشرة عينا قد علم كل أناس مشربهم كلوا واشربوا من رزق الله ولا تعثوا في الأرض مفسدين

translation: And when you said, 'O Moses, we will not endure one kind of food, so call upon your Lord to bring forth for us from what the earth grows, of its herbs, its cucumbers, its garlic, its lentils, and its onions.' He said, 'Would you exchange that which is better for that which is worse? Go down to Egypt; indeed, there you will have what you have asked for.' And humiliation and poverty were inflicted upon them, and they were struck with death because of their rebellion against the signs of Allah and their dis killing of the prophets without right. That was because they disobeyed and were transgressors.
interpretation: The verse describes the Israelites' lack of patience and gratitude for the manna and quails that God provided for them, and their demand for a variety of food from the earth. God, through Moses, warns them against exchanging the better for the worse and commands them to go back to Egypt if they insist on their demand. The verse mentions the consequences of their disobedience and rejection of God's signs and prophets, including humiliation, poverty, and death. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of gratitude, patience, and obedience to God's commands, and the dire consequences of disobedience and rejection of God's messengers.
orig: وإذ قلتم يا موسى لن نصبر على طعام واحد فادع لنا ربك يخرج لنا مما تنبت الأرض من بقلها وقثائها وفومها وعدسها وبصلها قال أتستبدلون الذي هو أدنى بالذي هو خير اهبطوا مصرا فإن لكم ما سألتم وضربت عليهم الذلة والمسكنة وباءوا بغضب من الله ذلك بأنهم كانوا يكفرون بآيات الله ويقتلون النبيين بغير الحق ذلك بما عصوا وكانوا يعتدون

translation: Indeed, those who have believed and those who have been Jews and the Sabians and the Christians - those [among them] who have believed in Allah and the Last Day and done righteousness - they will have their reward with their Lord, and no fear will there be concerning them, nor will they grieve.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the reward of those who believe in Allah and the Day of Judgment and do righteous deeds, regardless of their religion. These people include believers, Jews, Sabians, and Christians. The verse emphasizes that these individuals will receive their reward from their Lord and will not have to fear or grieve. The verse serves as a message of hope and reassurance for those who believe and do good, regardless of their religious affiliation.
orig: إن الذين آمنوا والذين هادوا والنصارى والصابئين من آمن بالله واليوم الآخر وعمل صالحا فلهم أجرهم عند ربهم ولا خوف عليهم ولا هم يحزنون

translation: And when We took your covenant and raised above you the Mount (Tur), take what We have given you with strength and remember what is in it, perhaps you will be God-fearing.
interpretation: The verse refers to the covenant that God made with the Israelites at Mount Sinai, where they agreed to follow His laws and commandments. God reminds them to uphold their end of the covenant by taking what He has given them (His guidance and laws) and using their strength to follow them. The verse also emphasizes the importance of remembering the covenant and its terms, as a reminder for them to be mindful of their actions and be God-fearing. The verse serves as a reminder for all believers to uphold their covenants and agreements, and to be mindful of God's guidance in their actions.
orig: وإذ أخذنا ميثاقكم ورفعنا فوقكم الطور خذوا ما آتيناكم بقوة واذكروا ما فيه لعلكم تتقون

translation: Then you will surely follow after them in their footsteps. Then surely you will come after them, except that Allah should grant you mercy; then you would not be equals (with them).
interpretation: The verse speaks about the consequences of following in the footsteps of those who have committed injustice and sin. The verse emphasizes that the listeners will inevitably follow the same path, unless they are granted mercy by God. The verse serves as a warning and a call to repentance, urging the listeners to turn away from the ways of the unjust and seek God's mercy and forgiveness. The last part of the verse highlights the importance of God's mercy, as without it, the listeners would be no different from those who have come before them.
orig: ثم توليتم من بعد ذلك فلولا فضل الله عليكم ورحمته لكنتم من الخاسرين

translation: And you have already known those among you who transgressed on the Sabbath, so We said to them, 'Be (like) apes, despised and hated.'
interpretation: The verse refers to a group of people from among the Israelites who transgressed by working on the Sabbath, despite God's command to rest on that day. As a punishment, God transformed them into apes, making them an example of disobedience and transgression for others. The verse emphasizes the importance of obedience and respect for God's commands, and the serious consequences of disobedience and transgression.
orig: ولقد علمتم الذين اعتدوا منكم في السبت فقلنا لهم كونوا قردة خاسئين

translation: And We made it a lesson for those who came after, and an evident warning to those who fear God.
interpretation: The verse speaks about a past event that was made into a lesson for future generations and a warning for those who are mindful of God. The event could be a punishment or a consequence of actions taken by people in the past. The verse emphasizes the importance of learning from the past and the need for those who fear God to take heed of the warning. The verse serves as a reminder that our actions have consequences and that we should strive to learn from the experiences of those who came before us in order to avoid making the same mistakes.
orig: فجعلناها نكالا لما بين يديها وما خلفها وموعظة للمتقين

translation: And when Moses said to his people: 'Verily, Allah commands you to sacrifice a cow', they said: 'Are you making a mockery of us?' He said: 'I seek refuge with Allah, lest I should be one of the ignorant.'
interpretation: The verse relays a conversation between Moses and his people, where God has commanded them to sacrifice a cow. The people react negatively, accusing Moses of taking them in jest. Moses denies this and swears by God that he is not among the ignorant. The verse highlights the importance of obedience to God's commands and the seriousness of taking God's name in vain. The people's response of disbelief and mockery demonstrates their lack of faith and understanding, and Moses' response serves as a reminder of the importance of respect and reverence for God.
orig: وإذ قال موسى لقومه إن الله يأمركم أن تذبحوا بقرة قالوا أتتخذنا هزوا قال أعوذ بالله أن أكون من الجاهلين

translation: They said, 'Call upon your Lord to make clear to us what it is.' He said, 'Indeed, He says, 'It is a cow neither trained to plow the earth nor to irrigate the field; whole, between excrement and blood.' So do as you are commanded.'
interpretation: This verse relays a conversation between the people and Moses, where the people are asking Moses to clarify what kind of cow they are required to sacrifice. God responds by describing the specifications of the cow, and Moses relays the message to the people. The verse emphasizes the need for the people to follow God's commandments exactly as they are given, without making any substitutions or alterations. The description of the cow is detailed and specific, indicating the importance of following God's instructions precisely and not attempting to substitute or alter them based on one's own judgment or understanding. This serves as a reminder that God's commands must be followed exactly, and that there is no room for interpretation or deviation from the instructions given.
orig: قالوا ادع لنا ربك يبين لنا ما هي قال إنه يقول إنها بقرة لا فارض ولا بكر عوان بين ذلك فافعلوا ما تؤمرون

translation: They said, 'Call upon your Lord to make clear to us what her color is.' He said, 'Indeed, He says, 'She is a cow, yellowish-brown, delighting the beholders.'
interpretation: The verse describes a conversation between Moses and the Israelites, where they are trying to understand God's commandment to sacrifice a cow. The Israelites ask Moses to specify the color of the cow, and God responds by describing it as a yellowish-brown color that delights the beholders. The verse highlights the Israelites' lack of understanding and their need for clear guidance from God. It also emphasizes the importance of following God's commands, even if they may seem unusual or difficult to understand.
orig: قالوا ادع لنا ربك يبين لنا ما لونها قال إنه يقول إنها بقرة صفراء فاقع لونها تسر الناظرين

translation: They said, 'Call upon your Lord to show us which one of them is the correct one. Indeed, to us the cows appear similar, and indeed, we, if Allah wills, are guided.'
interpretation: The verse describes a situation where the people are confused and uncertain about which one of two cows is the correct one. They ask the speaker to ask their Lord for clarification, indicating their belief in the power and knowledge of the speaker's Lord. The people's inability to distinguish between the two cows highlights their need for divine guidance, and their statement 'if Allah wills, we are guided' shows their understanding that guidance ultimately comes from God. The verse highlights the human need for divine guidance and the limitations of human perception and understanding.
orig: قالوا ادع لنا ربك يبين لنا ما هي إن البقر تشابه علينا وإنا إن شاء الله لمهتدون

translation: It is said: 'Indeed, it is a cow neither old nor young, but between the two; so do what you are commanded.' They said: 'Now you have come with the truth, so have her slaughter!' And they almost did not do it.
interpretation: The verse describes a conversation between a group of people and an individual who is giving them instructions about a cow that they are to sacrifice. The cow is described as being of a specific age, neither old nor young, but between the two. The people initially doubted the truth of the instruction, but when they were convinced of its authenticity, they agreed to carry it out. However, the verse ends by saying that they 'almost did not do it', indicating their reluctance or hesitation. The verse can be interpreted as a test of the people's faith and obedience, and a reminder of the importance of following God's commands without hesitation or delay.
orig: قال إنه يقول إنها بقرة لا ذلول تثير الأرض ولا تسقي الحرث مسلمة لا شية فيها قالوا الآن جئت بالحق فذبحوها وما كادوا يفعلون

translation: But when you killed a soul, then (you became) disputers among yourselves, and God was resolving whatever you were concealing.
interpretation: The verse addresses a situation where a soul has been killed, and it highlights the disagreements and disputes that arise among people as a result. Despite these disagreements, the verse emphasizes that God has the ultimate power to reveal and resolve the hidden truths. The verse may serve as a reminder of the consequences of taking a life and the disruptive impact it has on communities. It also underscores the idea that God has knowledge of all that is hidden and will ultimately bring it to light.
orig: وإذ قتلتم نفسا فادارأتم فيها والله مخرج ما كنتم تكتمون

translation: And We said, 'Strike him with part of it.' Thus Allah brings the dead to life, and He shows you His signs, that perhaps you may understand.
interpretation: The verse speaks about a command from God to strike someone with a part of something, which results in the revival of the dead. This event serves as a demonstration of God's power and serves as a sign for those who witness it. The purpose of this sign is to encourage reflection and understanding. The verse highlights the theme of resurrection and the power of God over life and death, urging people to think deeply about the meaning and significance of the event.
orig: فقلنا اضربوه ببعضها كذلك يحيي الله الموتى ويريكم آياته لعلكم تعقلون

translation: Then your hearts became hard after that, so they are like rocks, or even harder. For there are rocks from which rivers burst forth, and there are some of them that split open and water comes out, and there are some of them that fall down out of fear of Allah. And Allah is not unaware of what you do.
interpretation: The verse describes the hardening of the hearts of the people after receiving divine guidance. The verse uses the metaphor of rocks to emphasize the stubbornness and unyielding nature of the people's hearts. The verse also highlights the contrast between the hardness of the people's hearts and the responsiveness of the earth, which yields water and sustenance. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of being receptive to divine guidance, and the consequences of hardening one's heart to it. The verse also emphasizes that Allah is aware of all actions, and that nothing escapes His knowledge.
orig: ثم قست قلوبكم من بعد ذلك فهي كالحجارة أو أشد قسوة وإن من الحجارة لما يتفجر منه الأنهار وإن منها لما يشقق فيخرج منه الماء وإن منها لما يهبط من خشية الله وما الله بغافل عما تعملون

translation: And do you (polytheists) expect that they will believe in you, while a group of them used to hear the words of Allah, then they used to distort it knowingly after they had understood it.
interpretation: The verse addresses the polytheists and questions their expectation that others will believe in them. It highlights the hypocrisy of those who had heard the words of Allah (the Quran), understood their meaning, but still chose to distort and twist them knowingly. The verse serves as a reminder of the deceit and betrayal of those who claim to believe but act otherwise, and emphasizes the importance of remaining true to one's faith and beliefs.
orig: أفتطمعون أن يؤمنوا لكم وقد كان فريق منهم يسمعون كلام الله ثم يحرفونه من بعد ما عقلوه وهم يعلمون

translation: And when they meet those who believe, they say, 'We believe,' but when they are alone with one another, they say, 'Do you tell them of what God has revealed to you, so they can argue about it before your Lord?' Have you no sense?
interpretation: The verse speaks about the hypocrisy of certain individuals who claim to believe in the faith, but in reality, they have doubts and do not truly believe. These individuals pretend to believe when they are in the company of other believers, but when they are alone, they mock and question the revelations that have been shared with the believers. The verse serves as a warning to the hypocrites, urging them to reflect on their actions and to consider the consequences of their disbelief. It also serves as a reminder to the believers to be aware of the presence of hypocrites in their midst, and to not be swayed by their false displays of faith.
orig: وإذا لقوا الذين آمنوا قالوا آمنا وإذا خلا بعضهم إلى بعض قالوا أتحدثونهم بما فتح الله عليكم ليحاجوكم به عند ربكم أفلا تعقلون

translation: They do not know that God knows what they conceal and what they declare.
interpretation: The verse highlights the all-knowing nature of God. It emphasizes that God is aware of all human actions, both the ones that are hidden and the ones that are public. The verse serves as a reminder that nothing can be concealed from God and that people should be mindful of their actions, as they will ultimately be held accountable for them.
orig: أولا يعلمون أن الله يعلم ما يسرون وما يعلنون

translation: And among them are some who have no knowledge of the Scripture except wishful thinking, and they but guess.
interpretation: The verse highlights the ignorance of some individuals regarding the Scripture, and their understanding of it is based on mere wishful thinking rather than actual knowledge. Despite their lack of understanding, they still have the audacity to form opinions and make assumptions, which are also prone to error. This verse serves as a reminder that true understanding and wisdom can only be attained through knowledge and learning, and that hasty judgments and uninformed opinions can often lead to misguided conclusions.
orig: ومنهم أميون لا يعلمون الكتاب إلا أماني وإن هم إلا يظنون

translation: Woe to those who write the Book with their own hands, then say, 'This is from Allah,' that they may sell it for a small price. So woe to them for what their hands have written and woe to them for what they earn.
interpretation: The verse warns of the severe punishment for those who falsely attribute to Allah a scripture that they have written themselves, in order to sell it for a small gain. The verse emphasizes the severe consequences of their actions, both for what they have written and for the sinful gains they have earned. The verse serves as a warning to those who would manipulate and distort religious teachings for their own selfish ends, reminding them of the certainty of divine retribution for their deceitful actions.
orig: فويل للذين يكتبون الكتاب بأيديهم ثم يقولون هذا من عند الله ليشتروا به ثمنا قليلا فويل لهم مما كتبت أيديهم وويل لهم مما يكسبون

translation: And they say, 'Never will fire touch us, except for a few numbered days.' Say, 'Have you taken a covenant with Allah? Then Allah will not break His covenant. Or do you say about Allah that which you do not know?'
interpretation: The verse addresses the disbelievers who deny the punishment of Hellfire and claim that it will only touch them for a limited number of days. The speaker (believed to be the Prophet Muhammad) challenges their false sense of security by reminding them of their covenant with Allah, which He will not break. The verse questions their claim and challenges their knowledge of Allah, suggesting that they are speaking about Allah without knowledge or understanding of His power and justice. The verse serves as a warning to those who deny the reality of Hellfire and the consequences of their actions, urging them to reflect on their beliefs and seek the truth.
orig: وقالوا لن تمسنا النار إلا أياما معدودة قل أتخذتم عند الله عهدا فلن يخلف الله عهده أم تقولون على الله ما لا تعلمون

translation: Indeed, whoever earns evil and is encompassed by their sins - those are the companions of the Fire; they will remain in it.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the fate of those who commit sins and are consumed by their wrongdoings. The verse warns that these individuals will become companions of the Fire and will remain in it eternally. This serves as a reminder that sins have consequences and that those who continue to commit them will face severe punishment in the afterlife. It is a call for people to reflect on their actions and strive for righteousness in order to avoid such a fate.
orig: بلى من كسب سيئة وأحاطت به خطيئته فأولئك أصحاب النار هم فيها خالدون

translation: And those who believe and do good deeds, they are the inhabitants of Paradise, they will abide therein [forever].
interpretation: The verse describes the fate of those who have faith in God and do good deeds. They are promised a place in Paradise, where they will live eternally. The verse emphasizes the reward of good deeds and the ultimate destination of those who lead a righteous life, providing hope and motivation for believers to strive for righteousness and faithfulness.
orig: والذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات أولئك أصحاب الجنة هم فيها خالدون

translation: And when We took a covenant from the Children of Israel, (commanding) 'Worship none but Allah; and be good to parents, and to relatives, and to orphans, and to the needy, and speak kindly to people; and perform prayer and give alms;' then you turned away, except a few of you, and you are averse.
interpretation: The verse speaks about a covenant that was taken from the Children of Israel, in which they were commanded to worship only Allah, be good to their parents, relatives, orphans, and the needy, speak kindly to people, perform prayer and give alms. However, most of them turned away from the covenant and were averse. The verse highlights the importance of fulfilling covenants and the consequences of breaking them. It also emphasizes the importance of treating others with kindness and compassion, and the significance of performing religious duties and obligations.
orig: وإذ أخذنا ميثاق بني إسرائيل لا تعبدون إلا الله وبالوالدين إحسانا وذي القربى واليتامى والمساكين وقولوا للناس حسنا وأقيموا الصلاة وآتوا الزكاة ثم توليتم إلا قليلا منكم وأنتم معرضون

translation: And when We took your covenant, [saying], 'Do not shed your blood or evict one another from your homes,' then you acknowledged [this] while you were witness.
interpretation: The verse refers to a covenant or agreement that was made between God and a group of people. The terms of the covenant were that they should not shed each other's blood or evict each other from their homes. By acknowledging and accepting these terms, the people were effectively promising to uphold them and behave in a just and peaceful manner. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of abiding by one's promises and treating others with fairness and respect. It also highlights the serious consequences of breaking a covenant or agreement.
orig: وإذ أخذنا ميثاقكم لا تسفكون دماءكم ولا تخرجون أنفسكم من دياركم ثم أقررتم وأنتم تشهدون

translation: Then you are the ones who kill one another and expel a group of your people from their homes, oppressing them in sin and wrongdoing, and if they come to you as captives, you ransom them, although their expulsion was unlawful for you. Do you believe in part of the Book and disbelieve in part? Then what is the recompense of those who do that among you except disgrace in the worldly life; and on the Day of Resurrection they will be sent back to the most severe punishment. And Allah is not unaware of what you do.
interpretation: The verse addresses a group of people who are committing acts of violence and oppression against each other, including killing, expelling people from their homes, and taking captives. The verse criticizes their actions and their selective adherence to the teachings of the Book (referring to the Qur'an), as they engage in wrongdoing while claiming to believe in the scripture. The verse warns of the consequences of their actions, which include disgrace in this life and severe punishment in the hereafter. The verse emphasizes that Allah is aware of all their deeds and will hold them accountable for their actions.
orig: ثم أنتم هؤلاء تقتلون أنفسكم وتخرجون فريقا منكم من ديارهم تظاهرون عليهم بالإثم والعدوان وإن يأتوكم أسارى تفادوهم وهو محرم عليكم إخراجهم أفتؤمنون ببعض الكتاب وتكفرون ببعض فما جزاء من يفعل ذلك منكم إلا خزي في الحياة الدنيا ويوم القيامة يردون إلى أشد العذاب وما الله بغافل عما تعملون

translation: Those are they who have purchased the life of this world at the price of the Hereafter. Their punishment shall not be lightened, nor shall they be helped.
interpretation: The verse speaks about people who have prioritized the pleasures and desires of this world over the Hereafter. These people have effectively 'purchased' the temporary pleasures of this world at the expense of their Hereafter. The verse warns that the punishment for these people will be severe, and they will not receive any help or relief. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of prioritizing the Hereafter over the worldly life and the dangers of becoming overly attached to worldly pleasures.
orig: أولئك الذين اشتروا الحياة الدنيا بالآخرة فلا يخفف عنهم العذاب ولا هم ينصرون

translation: And We had already given Moses the Scripture and made contact with him after him with messengers. And We gave Jesus, the son of Mary, clear proofs and supported him with the Pure Spirit. But is it not that whenever a messenger came to you, [O Children of Israel], with what your souls did not desire, you became arrogant, and some you denied and some you killed?
interpretation: The verse speaks about the history of sending prophets to the Children of Israel and their rejection of them. The verse highlights the pattern of the people's response to the prophets, who brought them messages that did not align with their desires. The people responded with arrogance, denial, and even violence towards the messengers. The verse serves as a reminder of the consequences of rejecting the message of God and the prophets, and the importance of humility and openness to the guidance of God.
orig: ولقد آتينا موسى الكتاب وقفينا من بعده بالرسل وآتينا عيسى ابن مريم البينات وأيدناه بروح القدس أفكلما جاءكم رسول بما لا تهوى أنفسكم استكبرتم ففريقا كذبتم وفريقا تقتلون

translation: And they said, 'Our hearts are wrapped up.' But Allah has cursed them for their disbelief, so little is their faith.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the disbelievers who claim that their hearts are 'wrapped up' or 'veiled' from understanding the truth. However, the verse emphasizes that their disbelief has earned them a curse from Allah, and their faith is minimal. The verse serves as a reminder that disbelief and rejection of truth will not be accepted by God, and those who persist in this path will face severe consequences.
orig: وقالوا قلوبنا غلف بل لعنهم الله بكفرهم فقليلا ما يؤمنون

translation: And when there came to them a Book from God verifying that which they already possess, and aforetime they used to pray for victory over those who disbelieved, but when there came to them that which they knew (to be the truth) they disbelieved therein, therefore Allah's curse is on the disbelievers.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the response of a group of people to a revelation from God, which confirmed their previous scripture. Despite their previous prayers for victory over the disbelievers, when the truth was presented to them, they rejected it. As a result, the verse states that God's curse is upon the disbelievers. The verse highlights the importance of accepting and recognizing the truth when it is presented, regardless of previous beliefs or prejudices. The verse serves as a warning to those who reject the truth and the consequences of their actions.
orig: ولما جاءهم كتاب من عند الله مصدق لما معهم وكانوا من قبل يستفتحون على الذين كفروا فلما جاءهم ما عرفوا كفروا به فلعنة الله على الكافرين

translation: Woe to those who give short measure - those who, when they have to receive their due from people, demand that it be given in full. But when they have to give measure or weight to others, they defraud them! Do such people think that they will escape God's judgment? Those who believe and do good deeds will be admitted to Gardens graced with flowing streams, where, with their Lord's permission, they will stay forever. God's punishment is severe.
interpretation: The verse warns those who are unjust and practice dishonest trading by taking full measure when receiving from others, but giving less than what is due when they are the ones giving measure or weight. The verse questions whether these people think they will escape God's judgment. The verse then contrasts the fate of the unjust with that of the believers who do good deeds, who will be admitted to paradise. The verse emphasizes the severe punishment that awaits the unbelievers, serving as a warning to those who engage in unjust practices and a reminder of the importance of fairness and honesty in all dealings.
orig: بئسما اشتروا به أنفسهم أن يكفروا بما أنزل الله بغيا أن ينزل الله من فضله على من يشاء من عباده فباءوا بغضب على غضب وللكافرين عذاب مهين

translation: And when it is said to them, 'Believe in what Allah has revealed', they say, 'We believe in what has been revealed to us,' and they disbelieve in what is beyond that, and it is the truth confirming what is with them.
interpretation: The verse addresses those who claim to believe in the revelations of God, but in fact, they only believe in what has been revealed to them and reject anything that comes after. The verse emphasizes that the truth (what is beyond what they believe in) confirms what they already have. The verse serves as a critique of those who claim to be believers, yet cherry-pick which revelations they choose to follow, and reject the ones that challenge their beliefs or way of life. The verse also implies that true believers should not only accept the parts of revelations that align with their beliefs but should also accept and follow all the revelations from God, including the ones that challenge their beliefs or way of life.
orig: وإذا قيل لهم آمنوا بما أنزل الله قالوا نؤمن بما أنزل علينا ويكفرون بما وراءه وهو الحق مصدقا لما معهم قل فلم تقتلون أنبياء الله من قبل إن كنتم مؤمنين

translation: And indeed, Moses came to you with clear proofs, then you took the calf [for worship] after him while you were unjust.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the Israelites' rejection of Moses's message and their worship of the golden calf after he had provided them with clear evidence of God's oneness. The verse highlights the unjust and ungrateful nature of the Israelites, who turned away from the truth and chose to worship a false deity. This verse serves as a reminder of the importance of staying steadfast on the path of righteousness and not being swayed by falsehood and ignorance.
orig: ولقد جاءكم موسى بالبينات ثم اتخذتم العجل من بعده وأنتم ظالمون

translation: And when We took your covenant and raised above you the Mount (saying): 'Take what We have given you with strength and hear.' They said: 'We hear and we disobey.' And they drank in their hearts with rebellion through their disbelief. Say: 'Bad is that which you command me to do if you are believers.'
interpretation: The verse describes a moment when God took a covenant from a group of people and gave them a command to follow.
