Despite their promise to obey, the people disobeyed and drank in their hearts with rebellion through their disbelief. The verse emphasizes the contradiction between the people's words and their actions, as they claim to be believers but act in disbelief. The verse serves as a reminder that true faith is reflected in one's actions, not just words. The command for the listener to say 'Bad is that which you command me to do if you are believers' highlights the inconsistency between the people's claim of faith and their disobedience.
orig: وإذ أخذنا ميثاقكم ورفعنا فوقكم الطور خذوا ما آتيناكم بقوة واسمعوا قالوا سمعنا وعصينا وأشربوا في قلوبهم العجل بكفرهم قل بئسما يأمركم به إيمانكم إن كنتم مؤمنين

translation: Say, 'If the abode of the Hereafter with God is yours exclusively apart from the people, then you should long for death if you are truthful.'
interpretation: The verse is a challenge to those who claim that they have a special relationship with God and that the afterlife is reserved for them. The challenge is for them to hasten their death, if they truly believe what they claim. The verse is a reminder that death is inevitable and that no one can escape it. It also serves as a warning to those who are arrogant and think that they are better than others, reminding them that they will be held accountable for their actions and that their claims will be tested in the afterlife.
orig: قل إن كانت لكم الدار الآخرة عند الله خالصة من دون الناس فتمنوا الموت إن كنتم صادقين

translation: And they will never desire to leave what they have ascribed to Him, and Allah is Knowing of the unjust.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the unbelievers who will not give up their false beliefs and will not desire to leave what they have ascribed to God. The verse emphasizes the stubbornness of the unbelievers and their refusal to accept the truth. Despite the fact that God is all-knowing and aware of their injustice, they persist in their falsehood. The verse serves as a reminder that God knows the actions of all people, and that those who persist in their injustice and falsehood will not be able to escape the consequences of their actions.
orig: ولن يتمنوه أبدا بما قدمت أيديهم والله عليم بالظالمين

translation: And you will find them (the disbelievers) the most eager of people for life, and (yet) among them are those who embrace disbelief. For such, (it would be as if) every soul rejoices in (the prospect of) attaining a life of a thousand years. Yet, such would not escape the punishment (of Allah) even if they were to live for a number of centuries. And Allah is all-seeing of what they do.
interpretation: The verse highlights the eagerness of the disbelievers for worldly life and their rejection of the truth. Despite their desire for long life, they will not be able to escape the punishment of Allah. The verse serves as a reminder that the pleasures of this world are temporary and that the consequences of disbelief and sin are severe. It emphasizes that Allah is all-knowing and sees all that people do, indicating that no one can escape His judgment.
orig: ولتجدنهم أحرص الناس على حياة ومن الذين أشركوا يود أحدهم لو يعمر ألف سنة وما هو بمزحزحه من العذاب أن يعمر والله بصير بما يعملون

translation: Say, 'Who is an enemy to Gabriel?' For he it is who hath revealed him (the Qur'an) to thy heart by Allah's leave, confirming that which was before him, and a guidance and glad tidings to the believers
interpretation: The verse speaks about the revelation of the Qur'an through the angel Gabriel to the Prophet Muhammad. The verse asks a rhetorical question, 'Who is an enemy to Gabriel?' to emphasize the importance and the truth of the revelation. The verse affirms that the Qur'an has been revealed to the heart of the Prophet Muhammad by the will of Allah through Gabriel. The verse also explains that the Qur'an confirms and builds upon previous revelations, and that it serves as a guidance and glad tidings for the believers. The verse emphasizes the significance of the revelation and the role of Gabriel in the process, and it serves as a reminder of the divine origin of the Qur'an.
orig: قل من كان عدوا لجبريل فإنه نزله على قلبك بإذن الله مصدقا لما بين يديه وهدى وبشرى للمؤمنين

translation: Whoever is an enemy to Allah, His angels, His messengers, Jibril (Gabriel), and Mikael (Michael) - then indeed, Allah is an enemy to the disbelievers.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of having a positive relationship with God, His angels, and His messengers, including Jibril (Gabriel) and Mikael (Michael). To be an enemy to any of them is to be an enemy to God Himself, which is a dangerous position to be in. The verse serves as a warning to those who may be hostile towards God or His messengers, and it reminds them of the serious consequences of their actions. Ultimately, the verse encourages believers to maintain a strong and positive relationship with God and His messengers, and to avoid any actions or attitudes that may be perceived as hostile or disrespectful towards them.
orig: من كان عدوا لله وملائكته ورسله وجبريل وميكال فإن الله عدو للكافرين

translation: And We have certainly sent down to you clear signs and a message, and none deny them except the unrighteous.
interpretation: The verse asserts that God has sent clear signs and a message (referring to the Qur'an) to the Prophet Muhammad. However, these signs and message are denied by the unrighteous or immoral people. The verse emphasizes the clarity and explicitness of the signs and message, and the responsibility of the unrighteous for their denial and rejection of it. The verse may serve as a warning to those who deny the message of Islam, reminding them of the consequences of their denial and the importance of accepting and following the guidance of God.
orig: ولقد أنزلنا إليك آيات بينات وما يكفر بها إلا الفاسقون

translation: And when We made a covenant with them, a group of them cast it aside; but the greater part of them were unbelievers.
interpretation: The verse speaks about a group of people who broke their covenant with God, despite having promised to uphold it. The verse highlights that the majority of these people were unbelievers, indicating that their lack of faith was the root cause of their disregard for their covenant. This verse serves as a reminder that breaking a promise or covenant with God has serious consequences, and that unbelief and disobedience go hand in hand.
orig: أوكلما عاهدوا عهدا نبذه فريق منهم بل أكثرهم لا يؤمنون

translation: And when there came to them a Messenger from God verifying that which they already possess [the Scriptures], a party of those who were given the Scripture threw the Book of God behind their backs as if they did not know [it].
interpretation: The verse describes the response of some of the People of the Scripture (Jews and Christians) when a Messenger from God (Prophet Muhammad) came to them with a message that confirmed the truth of their own Scriptures. Instead of accepting the message and following the truth, a group of them rejected it and treated the Book of God (the Qur'an) with disrespect and disregard, casting it behind their backs. The verse highlights their rejection and denial of the truth, despite having it in their possession. The verse serves as a reminder of the consequences of rejecting God's message and the importance of recognizing and accepting the truth when it is presented.
orig: ولما جاءهم رسول من عند الله مصدق لما معهم نبذ فريق من الذين أوتوا الكتاب كتاب الله وراء ظهورهم كأنهم لا يعلمون

translation: And follow that which the devils relate against the kingdom of Solomon. As for Solomon, he was not unbelieving, but the devils were unbelievers. They teach the people sorcery, and that which was revealed to the two angels in Babylon, Harut and Marut. But they do not teach anyone unless they say: 'We are only a temptation, do not be unbelievers.' From these two (angels) people learn that by which they cause a separation between a man and his wife; but they injure no one thereby, except with the permission of God; and they learn that by which they cause the death of a soul which God would have kept alive; and they learn that by which they cause disease in a body which God would have kept sound; and they learn what harm they may cause, and what benefit they may bring. But they know surely that he who buys it will have no share in the hereafter; and surely evil is the price for which they sell their souls, had they but known.
interpretation: The verse warns against following the teachings of the devils, who spread falsehood and deceit about the kingdom of Solomon. While Solomon himself was not unbelieving, the devils who spread these lies were. The verse specifically mentions that the devils teach people sorcery and other harmful practices, such as causing separation between a man and his wife, causing harm to others, and even causing death. These actions are only permitted with the permission of God, and those who engage in them will not have a share in the hereafter. The verse emphasizes the great harm and evil of these practices, and the ultimate destruction that awaits those who engage in them. The verse serves as a warning to those who may be tempted by the lies and deceit of the devils, reminding them of the grave consequences of their actions.
orig: واتبعوا ما تتلو الشياطين على ملك سليمان وما كفر سليمان ولكن الشياطين كفروا يعلمون الناس السحر وما أنزل على الملكين ببابل هاروت وماروت وما يعلمان من أحد حتى يقولا إنما نحن فتنة فلا تكفر فيتعلمون منهما ما يفرقون به بين المرء وزوجه وما هم بضارين به من أحد إلا بإذن الله ويتعلمون ما يضرهم ولا ينفعهم ولقد علموا لمن اشتراه ما له في الآخرة من خلاق ولبئس ما شروا به أنفسهم لو كانوا يعلمون

translation: And if they had believed and guarded themselves against evil, a reward from Allah would have been better; surely (if) they had known.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the rewards that would have been given to the people if they had believed in God and protected themselves from evil deeds. The verse highlights the fact that the reward from God would have been far better than anything they could have achieved in this world. The phrase 'if they had known' emphasizes the importance of knowledge and understanding of God's message. The verse serves as an invitation for people to embrace faith and righteousness, and to strive for God's pleasure and rewards in the hereafter.
orig: ولو أنهم آمنوا واتقوا لمثوبة من عند الله خير لو كانوا يعلمون

translation: O you who have believed, do not say, 'Listen to us,' but say, 'Look at us,' and be hearing, and fear for the disbelievers is a painful punishment.
interpretation: The verse addresses the believers and instructs them on how to interact with others. Instead of saying 'listen to us', they are told to say 'look at us' and to be attentive. The verse warns of a painful punishment for the disbelievers, emphasizing the importance of faith and righteousness. The verse encourages the believers to be mindful of their actions and to be a good example for others, rather than just expecting others to listen to them. This verse serves as a reminder of the significance of actions and the consequences of disbelief.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تقولوا راعنا وقولوا انظرنا واسمعوا وللكافرين عذاب أليم

translation: Those who disbelieve from among the People of the Scripture and the idolators would not like that any good should be sent down to you from your Lord. But Allah chooses for His mercy whom He wills, and Allah is the possessor of great bounty.
interpretation: The verse highlights the opposition of the disbelievers, both from the People of the Scripture (Jews and Christians) and the idolators, towards the revelation of good (guidance) upon the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) from his Lord. Despite their opposition, the verse emphasizes that Allah chooses whom He wills for His mercy and that He is the possessor of great bounty. This verse serves as a reminder that while some may reject the message, Allah's mercy and bounty are not limited and are bestowed upon whom He wills.
orig: ما يود الذين كفروا من أهل الكتاب ولا المشركين أن ينزل عليكم من خير من ربكم والله يختص برحمته من يشاء والله ذو الفضل العظيم

translation: None of Our verses do We abrogate or cause to be forgotten, but We bring [one] better than it or similar to it. Do you not know that Allah is over all things competent?
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the perfection and completeness of the Quran, stating that none of its verses are abrogated or forgotten. Instead, a better or similar verse is brought in its place. This highlights the divine origin of the Quran and its preservation by God. The verse also serves as a reminder of God's power and control over all things, emphasizing His ability to bring about what He wills.
orig: ما ننسخ من آية أو ننسها نأت بخير منها أو مثلها ألم تعلم أن الله على كل شيء قدير

translation: Do you not know that to God belongs the kingdom of the heavens and the earth and that you have no protector apart from God and no helper?
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the power and sovereignty of God over all things, reminding the reader that God has control over both the heavens and the earth. The verse also points out that humans have no protector or helper apart from God, highlighting the idea that all power and strength come from God alone. This verse can serve as a reminder of the importance of relying on and seeking help from God in all matters, and of the limitations of human power and protection.
orig: ألم تعلم أن الله له ملك السماوات والأرض وما لكم من دون الله من ولي ولا نصير

translation: Or do you (people) desire that your Messenger should go back (from preaching the truth) as Musa (Moses) was sent back before, and whoever seeks a religion other than Islam, it will never be accepted of him, and in the Hereafter, he will be among the losers.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of following the message brought by the Prophet Muhammad and the importance of accepting Islam as the only true religion. The verse draws a comparison between the Prophet Muhammad and Musa (Moses), suggesting that those who reject the message of the Prophet Muhammad, just like those who rejected Musa, will not be accepted and will be among the losers in the Hereafter. The verse serves as a reminder that Islam is the only true religion and that those who seek any other religion will not be accepted. It serves as a warning to those who reject the message of Islam and a call for them to reflect and reconsider their beliefs.
orig: أم تريدون أن تسألوا رسولكم كما سئل موسى من قبل ومن يتبدل الكفر بالإيمان فقد ضل سواء السبيل

translation: And had it been that
interpretation: No interpretation
orig: ود كثير من أهل الكتاب لو يردونكم من بعد إيمانكم كفارا حسدا من عند أنفسهم من بعد ما تبين لهم الحق فاعفوا واصفحوا حتى يأتي الله بأمره إن الله على كل شيء قدير

translation: And establish prayer and give zakah and whatever of good (deeds) you send forth for yourselves before you, you will find it with Allah. Indeed, Allah is seeing of what you do.
interpretation: The verse is emphasizing the importance of performing good deeds and the establishment of prayer and zakah (charity) in Islam. The verse encourages believers to do good deeds and send them forth for themselves, indicating that these deeds will be a form of investment for them in the afterlife. The verse also reminds believers that Allah sees and is aware of all that they do, emphasizing the importance of sincerity and accountability in their actions. The verse serves as a motivation for believers to strive for good deeds and to establish a strong relationship with Allah through prayer and charity.
orig: وأقيموا الصلاة وآتوا الزكاة وما تقدموا لأنفسكم من خير تجدوه عند الله إن الله بما تعملون بصير

translation: And they say, 'No one will enter Paradise unless they are a Jew or a Christian.' Say, 'Produce your proof, if you are being truthful.'
interpretation: The verse addresses those who claim that only Jews or Christians will enter Paradise. The speaker (who is believed to be the Prophet Muhammad) challenges them to produce their proof or evidence for this claim, if they are being truthful. This verse emphasizes the importance of having valid evidence and proof for religious beliefs and claims, and it rejects any form of discrimination or exclusion based on religion or belief. The verse encourages critical thinking, questioning and the pursuit of knowledge, rather than blindly following traditions or prejudices.
orig: وقالوا لن يدخل الجنة إلا من كان هودا أو نصارى تلك أمانيهم قل هاتوا برهانكم إن كنتم صادقين

translation: Yes, whoever submits his face to God and is righteous, indeed his reward is with his Lord, and there is no fear for them, nor will they grieve.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the reward of those who submit themselves to God and lead a righteous life. The verse highlights the certainty of the reward for such individuals, which is with their Lord. Furthermore, such individuals have no fear or grief as they are protected from the harm and negativity of this world. This verse serves as a source of comfort and motivation for those who strive to lead a righteous life and submit themselves to God.
orig: بلى من أسلم وجهه لله وهو محسن فله أجره عند ربه ولا خوف عليهم ولا هم يحزنون

translation: And the Jews say that the Christians follow nothing (of guidance), and the Christians say that the Jews follow nothing (of guidance), while they both recite the Scripture. Thus, say (O Muhammad, to both of them): 'Then, if you both are guided, (then) follow what has been revealed to you (from Allah).' And indeed, this (Qur'an) explains to them the matters in which they differ. So, is it (the Qur'an) that they should believe in it or not? Indeed, whoever is hostile to Allah and His Messenger, then surely, Allah is severe in retribution.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the disagreement and conflict between the Jews and Christians, both of whom claim to follow the Scripture. The verse highlights their hypocrisy in claiming to follow the Scripture, while at the same time rejecting each other's beliefs and practices. The verse encourages the Prophet Muhammad to remind both parties to follow the guidance that has been revealed to them, and not to be influenced by the falsehood and misguidance of others. The verse emphasizes the importance of adhering to the guidance of Allah, and warns of the severe consequences for those who are hostile towards Allah and His Messenger. The verse also highlights the role of the Qur'an in explaining and resolving the differences between the Jews and Christians, and invites them to believe in its guidance and teachings.
orig: وقالت اليهود ليست النصارى على شيء وقالت النصارى ليست اليهود على شيء وهم يتلون الكتاب كذلك قال الذين لا يعلمون مثل قولهم فالله يحكم بينهم يوم القيامة فيما كانوا فيه يختلفون

translation: And who is more unjust than those who prevent the servants of Allah from entering His mosques and strive toward their destruction? As for those, they will not cease to be surrounded by failure in this world, and upon them is a great punishment in the Hereafter.
interpretation: The verse highlights the severe consequences for those who prevent others from entering and worshiping in the mosques of Allah and who instead strive to destroy them. The verse emphasizes the extreme injustice of such actions and the negative consequences that result. The verse indicates that such people will face failure and humiliation in this world and a severe punishment in the afterlife. The verse serves as a reminder to respect and protect the places of worship and the right to worship for all people.
orig: ومن أظلم ممن منع مساجد الله أن يذكر فيها اسمه وسعى في خرابها أولئك ما كان لهم أن يدخلوها إلا خائفين لهم في الدنيا خزي ولهم في الآخرة عذاب عظيم

translation: To God belong the east and the west, so wherever you turn, there is the face of God. Indeed, God is all-encompassing, knowing.
interpretation: The verse affirms the omnipresence and boundlessness of God, emphasizing that God is present in every direction and in every place. The verse encourages the believer to turn towards God, regardless of their orientation, as God is all-encompassing and all-knowing. The verse may also serve as a reminder of the unity and interconnectedness of the universe, as all things are ultimately part of God's creation. The verse may also be interpreted as a call for humility and submission, as the believer recognizes their place within the vastness of God's creation and the limitations of their own knowledge and understanding.
orig: ولله المشرق والمغرب فأينما تولوا فثم وجه الله إن الله واسع عليم

translation: And they said, 'Allah has taken a son.' Exalted is He! Rather, to Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth. All are devoutly obedient to Him.
interpretation: The verse is a rejection of the claim made by some people that Allah (God) has taken a son. The verse emphasizes that such a claim is false and blasphemous, and it affirms the absolute oneness and uniqueness of Allah. The verse also highlights the sovereignty and power of Allah, stating that everything in the heavens and the earth belongs to Him and is obedient to Him. The verse serves as a reminder of the greatness of Allah and the importance of affirming His oneness and rejecting any form of polytheism or associating partners with Him.
orig: وقالوا اتخذ الله ولدا سبحانه بل له ما في السماوات والأرض كل له قانتون

translation: Creator of the heavens and the earth. And when He decrees a matter, He only says to it, 'Be,' and it is.
interpretation: The verse highlights the power and might of God as the Creator of the heavens and the earth. The verse emphasizes that when God decrees a matter, it is done immediately and without question. The Arabic word 'kun' in the verse means 'be', and it is used to show the absolute power and authority of God. The verse serves as a reminder of the greatness of God and His ability to create and control all things, and it instills a sense of awe and reverence for the Divine.
orig: بديع السماوات والأرض وإذا قضى أمرا فإنما يقول له كن فيكون

translation: And those who have no knowledge say, 'Why does not God speak to us, or a sign come to us?' So said those before them, their hearts are alike. We have indeed made clear the signs to a people who are certain.
interpretation: The verse addresses the people who lack knowledge and question why God does not speak to them or send them a sign. This is similar to the disbelievers who came before them, whose hearts were also closed to the truth. The verse emphasizes that God's signs and messages have been made clear to those who are certain and believe. The verse serves as a reminder to those who question and doubt, encouraging them to open their hearts to the truth and have faith.
orig: وقال الذين لا يعلمون لولا يكلمنا الله أو تأتينا آية كذلك قال الذين من قبلهم مثل قولهم تشابهت قلوبهم قد بينا الآيات لقوم يوقنون

translation: Indeed, We have sent you, [O Muhammad], with the truth as a bringer of good tidings and a warner. And you will not be asked about the companions of the Blaze.
interpretation: The verse confirms that Muhammad is a prophet who has been sent with the truth, bringing good news and warning of the consequences of rejecting the message. The last part of the verse, 'And you will not be asked about the companions of the Blaze', suggests that the responsibility of the prophet is to deliver the message, and the outcome of people's choices is not his concern. This verse emphasizes the importance of the role of the prophet and the freedom of choice given to people, and the consequences of their actions.
orig: إنا أرسلناك بالحق بشيرا ونذيرا ولا تسأل عن أصحاب الجحيم

translation: And never will the Jews nor the Christians be satisfied with you until you follow their religion. Say: 'Indeed, the guidance of Allah is the (only) guidance.' If you were to follow their desires after what has come to you of knowledge, there would be no protector for you from Allah and no helper.
interpretation: The verse highlights the tension between Muslims and followers of other religions, specifically Jews and Christians. It emphasizes that the only true guidance comes from God and that Muslims should not be swayed by the desires of others, even if they are people of knowledge. The verse warns that if Muslims were to follow the desires of Jews and Christians, they would have no protector or helper from God. The verse serves as a reminder to Muslims to remain steadfast in their faith and not to be influenced by the beliefs and practices of others, even if they are people of authority or knowledge.
orig: ولن ترضى عنك اليهود ولا النصارى حتى تتبع ملتهم قل إن هدى الله هو الهدى ولئن اتبعت أهواءهم بعد الذي جاءك من العلم ما لك من الله من ولي ولا نصير

translation: Those to whom We have given the Scripture recite it as it should be recited. They are the ones who believe in it. And whoever disbelieves in it - it is they who are the losers.
interpretation: The verse distinguishes between those who are given the scripture (presumably referring to the followers of previous religions who were given divine revelations, such as Jews and Christians) and those who truly believe and follow its teachings. The verse emphasizes the importance of reciting and following the scripture as it was intended, and those who do so are described as believers. On the other hand, those who reject or disbelieve in the scripture are considered the losers. The verse serves as a reminder of the significance of adhering to and respecting the teachings of the scripture, and the consequences of disbelief and rejection.
orig: الذين آتيناهم الكتاب يتلونه حق تلاوته أولئك يؤمنون به ومن يكفر به فأولئك هم الخاسرون

translation: O children of Israel, remember My favor which I have bestowed upon you and that I have preferred you over the worlds.
interpretation: The verse addresses the children of Israel and reminds them of the favor and blessings that God has given them. It emphasizes that they have been chosen and given preferential treatment over all other nations. The verse serves as a call for the children of Israel to be grateful for the blessings they have received and to remember their special status in the eyes of God. It is also a reminder for them to live up to the expectations that come with being chosen and preferred, and to be a positive example for other nations.
orig: يا بني إسرائيل اذكروا نعمتي التي أنعمت عليكم وأني فضلتكم على العالمين

translation: And fear a Day when no soul will suffice for another soul at all, nor will intercession be accepted from it, nor will compensation be taken from it, nor will they be helped.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the Day of Judgment and the ultimate accountability of each individual. The verse emphasizes that no soul will be able to help another soul on that day, and that there will be no intercession accepted, no compensation will be sufficient, and no one will be able to help or save anyone else. The verse serves as a reminder of the severity of the Day of Judgment and the importance of taking personal responsibility for one's actions, as each person will be held accountable for their own deeds and no one else's.
orig: واتقوا يوما لا تجزي نفس عن نفس شيئا ولا يقبل منها عدل ولا تنفعها شفاعة ولا هم ينصرون

translation: And when his Lord tested Abraham with words, and he fulfilled them, He said, 'Indeed, I will make you a leader for the people.' Abraham said, 'And of my descendants?' My covenant does not include the wrongdoers.'
interpretation: The verse describes a test that God presented to the prophet Abraham, which he passed. As a reward for his faith and obedience, God promised to make Abraham a leader for the people. However, Abraham asked if his descendants would also be included in this covenant. God replied that those who are unjust and commit wrongdoing will not be a part of this covenant. The verse highlights the importance of righteousness and obedience to God, and the promise of leadership and blessings for those who follow God's path.
orig: وإذ ابتلى إبراهيم ربه بكلمات فأتمهن قال إني جاعلك للناس إماما قال ومن ذريتي قال لا ينال عهدي الظالمين

translation: And when We made the House a place of return for the people and a sanctuary, and (take) from Abraham and Ishmael the station of Ibrahim as a place of prayer, and We charged Abraham and Ishmael, (saying), 'Purify My House for those who perform Tawaf and those who make the retreat and those who bow and prostrate.
interpretation: This verse speaks about the importance of the Kaaba (the 'House') in Mecca as a place of return and sanctuary for the people. It highlights the significance of the station of Abraham, which was designated as a place of prayer. The verse also emphasizes the importance of maintaining the purity of the Kaaba for the various acts of worship, including Tawaf (circumambulation), retreat, bowing, and prostration. By charging Abraham and Ishmael with this responsibility, the verse underscores the importance of their legacy and the continuation of these practices. Overall, the verse serves as a reminder of the significance of the Kaaba as a place of worship and the importance of preserving its sanctity for future generations.
orig: وإذ جعلنا البيت مثابة للناس وأمنا واتخذوا من مقام إبراهيم مصلى وعهدنا إلى إبراهيم وإسماعيل أن طهرا بيتي للطائفين والعاكفين والركع السجود

translation: And when Abraham said, 'My Lord, make this city (Mecca) a place of security and provide its people with fruits, such of them as believe in God and the Last Day.' And God said, 'And whoever disbelieves, I will grant him enjoyment for a little while, then I will force him to the punishment of the Fire, and what an evil destination.'
interpretation: The verse highlights Abraham's prayer for Mecca to be a secure and prosperous city, with God's provision of fruits for its people. However, the verse also emphasizes that those who disbelieve in God and the Day of Judgment will be granted temporary enjoyment, but will ultimately be forced to face the punishment of the Fire. The verse serves as a reminder that disbelief and rejection of God's signs will not go unpunished, and that the consequences of such actions are severe and everlasting.
orig: وإذ قال إبراهيم رب اجعل هذا بلدا آمنا وارزق أهله من الثمرات من آمن منهم بالله واليوم الآخر قال ومن كفر فأمتعه قليلا ثم أضطره إلى عذاب النار وبئس المصير

translation: And when Abraham and Ishmael were raising the foundations of the House, [saying], 'Our Lord, accept [this] from us. Indeed You are the Hearing, the Knowing.'
interpretation: The verse describes the story of Abraham and Ishmael building the Kaaba in Mecca. The two prophets are praying to God and asking him to accept their efforts in building the House. The verse emphasizes the greatness of God by describing him as the 'Hearing, the Knowing', highlighting his ability to hear their prayers and his knowledge of their intentions. The verse can be seen as a model of submission and devotion to God, as well as a reminder of the importance of building a relationship with him through prayer and worship.
orig: وإذ يرفع إبراهيم القواعد من البيت وإسماعيل ربنا تقبل منا إنك أنت السميع العليم

translation: Our Lord, and make us submissive to You and from our descendants a nation submissive to You, and show us our rites and accept our repentance. Indeed, You are the Accepting of repentance, the Merciful.
interpretation: The verse is a supplication to God, asking Him to make the speaker and their descendants submissive to Him, and to show them the correct way to worship Him. The speaker also asks for their repentance to be accepted, acknowledging that God is the One who accepts repentance and is merciful. The verse highlights the importance of submission to God, the need to follow the correct religious practices, and the significance of repentance in Islam.
orig: ربنا واجعلنا مسلمين لك ومن ذريتنا أمة مسلمة لك وأرنا مناسكنا وتب علينا إنك أنت التواب الرحيم

translation: Our Lord, send among them a messenger from themselves who will recite to them Your verses and teach them the Book and wisdom and purify them. Indeed, You are the Exalted in Might, the Wise.
interpretation: The verse is a supplication to God to send a messenger from among the people who will recite God's verses, teach them the Book (the Qur'an) and wisdom, and purify them. The verse highlights the importance of having a messenger who can guide the people and help them understand and follow God's teachings. The verse emphasizes the role of the messenger in purifying the people and the need for God's guidance in achieving this goal. The verse also acknowledges God's power and wisdom, and seeks His help in sending a messenger to the people.
orig: ربنا وابعث فيهم رسولا منهم يتلو عليهم آياتك ويعلمهم الكتاب والحكمة ويزكيهم إنك أنت العزيز الحكيم

translation: But whoever desires a religion other than Islam, it will never be accepted from him, and in the hereafter he will be among the losers.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of Islam as the one true religion and the only acceptable path to God. Those who choose a different religion or path will not have their beliefs accepted by God. Moreover, they will be considered as losers in the afterlife. The verse encourages the acceptance and submission to Islam, and it serves as a warning to those who choose to follow a different path.
orig: ومن يرغب عن ملة إبراهيم إلا من سفه نفسه ولقد اصطفيناه في الدنيا وإنه في الآخرة لمن الصالحين

translation: When his Lord said to him, 'Submit,' he said, 'I have submitted myself to the Lord of the worlds.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the story of the prophet Ibrahim (peace be upon him) and his unwavering faith in God. When God commanded him to submit, he responded by saying 'I have submitted myself to the Lord of the worlds', indicating his complete devotion and obedience to God. The verse serves as a model for Muslims to follow, emphasizing the importance of submission and obedience to God, and the importance of responding to God's commands with faith and trust.
orig: إذ قال له ربه أسلم قال أسلمت لرب العالمين

translation: And Abraham enjoined his sons and Jacob, saying, 'My sons, indeed God has chosen for you the religion, so do not die except while you are Muslims.'
interpretation: The verse relays the message of Abraham to his sons and Jacob, emphasizing the importance of adhering to the religion chosen by God. The message serves as a reminder to remain steadfast in faith and not to die except as a Muslim, meaning in a state of submission and obedience to God's will. The verse highlights the significance of passing down religious teachings from one generation to another, and the importance of preserving and upholding these teachings in one's own life.
orig: ووصى بها إبراهيم بنيه ويعقوب يا بني إن الله اصطفى لكم الدين فلا تموتن إلا وأنتم مسلمون

translation: Or were you witnesses when death approached Jacob, when he said to his sons, 'What will you worship after me?' They said, 'We will worship your God and the God of your fathers, Abraham, Ishmael, and Isaac - one God; and to Him we have submitted ourselves.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the death of Jacob and his request to his sons about who they will worship after him. The verse emphasizes the unity of God and the submission of Jacob's sons to Him. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of monotheism and the unity of God in Islam. It also highlights the continuity of the Islamic faith, as Jacob's sons affirm their belief in the same God worshipped by their ancestors, Abraham, Ishmael, and Isaac. The verse can also be seen as a message of unity and continuity within the Islamic community, as Muslims are reminded that they are part of a larger community of believers that extends back to the time of the Prophet Abraham.
orig: أم كنتم شهداء إذ حضر يعقوب الموت إذ قال لبنيه ما تعبدون من بعدي قالوا نعبد إلهك وإله آبائك إبراهيم وإسماعيل وإسحاق إلها واحدا ونحن له مسلمون

translation: That is a nation that has passed away; it will have what it earned, and you will have what you earned. And you will not be asked about what they used to do.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the separation of different nations and the consequences of their actions. Each nation will receive the consequences of their own actions and will not be held accountable for the actions of others. This serves as a reminder to focus on one's own actions and not to be concerned with the actions of others. It also emphasizes the concept of individual accountability and the importance of taking responsibility for one's own actions.
orig: تلك أمة قد خلت لها ما كسبت ولكم ما كسبتم ولا تسألون عما كانوا يعملون

translation: And they said, 'Be Jews or Christians, then you will be guided.' Say, 'Rather, the religion of Abraham, inclining toward truth, and he was not of the polytheists.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about a group of people who are urging the believers to adopt either Judaism or Christianity, claiming that it will guide them. However, the believers are instructed to respond by asserting their faith in the religion of Abraham, which is characterized by its inclination toward truth. The verse emphasizes the importance of following the monotheistic faith of Abraham and rejecting the worship of multiple gods. It serves as a reminder that the true path is not limited to any particular religion, but rather, it is based on the fundamental principle of monotheism and the rejection of idolatry.
orig: وقالوا كونوا هودا أو نصارى تهتدوا قل بل ملة إبراهيم حنيفا وما كان من المشركين

translation: Say, 'We have believed in Allah and what has been revealed to us and what was revealed to Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, and the Tribes, and what was given to Moses, Jesus, and the prophets from their Lord. We make no distinction between any of them, and we are Muslims [submitting] to Him.'
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the unity and continuity of the Islamic faith with previous monotheistic religions. It affirms the belief in God and the revelations given to the prophets, starting from Abraham and including Moses and Jesus. The verse emphasizes the equal importance of all revelations and the unity of the message of monotheism. The verse also emphasizes the submission of the believers to God and the importance of not discriminating between any of the prophets or their revelations. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of unity and inclusiveness in the Islamic faith and the importance of recognizing the shared monotheistic heritage with other religions.
orig: قولوا آمنا بالله وما أنزل إلينا وما أنزل إلى إبراهيم وإسماعيل وإسحاق ويعقوب والأسباط وما أوتي موسى وعيسى وما أوتي النبيون من ربهم لا نفرق بين أحد منهم ونحن له مسلمون

translation: But if they believe in what you believe in, they have indeed guided; but if they turn away, they are only in dissension, and Allah will suffice you against them. And He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the guidance of people who believe in the same things that the speaker believes in. However, if they reject the message, they are only causing discord and division. The verse reminds the speaker that Allah will be sufficient in dealing with those who reject the message. The verse emphasizes the importance of faith and the consequences of rejecting it, and the ultimate power and knowledge of Allah.
orig: فإن آمنوا بمثل ما آمنتم به فقد اهتدوا وإن تولوا فإنما هم في شقاق فسيكفيكهم الله وهو السميع العليم

translation: The color (of God) - and who is better than God in color? And to Him do we prostrate ourselves.
interpretation: The verse is emphasizing the perfection and uniqueness of God's 'color' or essence. The author is stating that nothing can compare to God's greatness and beauty, and in response to this, the author and other believers prostrate themselves in worship to God.
orig: صبغة الله ومن أحسن من الله صبغة ونحن له عابدون

translation: Say, 'Do you dispute with us about Allah while He is our Lord and your Lord? And we are to be resurrected to Him alone, and to Him is our return?'
interpretation: The verse is a statement made by the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) addressing the disbelievers who were disputing and debating about Allah and His religion. The verse emphasizes the unity of God and the fact that both the believers and the disbelievers will be resurrected and return to Him. The verse is a call for the disbelievers to recognize the truth of Islam and to stop their disputes and arguments. It also serves as a reminder of the ultimate accountability to Allah on the Day of Judgment, emphasizing the importance of faith and submission to Allah.
orig: قل أتحاجوننا في الله وهو ربنا وربكم ولنا أعمالنا ولكم أعمالكم ونحن له مخلصون

translation: Or say you that Abraham and Ishmael and Isaac and Jacob and the twelve patriarchs were Jews or Christians? Say, 'Do you know better or does Allah?' And who is more unjust than he who conceals a testimony he has from Allah? And Allah is not unaware of what you do.
interpretation: The verse questions the claim that the prophets Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, and the twelve patriarchs were Jews or Christians. The verse instructs the listener to consider whether they know better than God about the religious affiliation of these prophets. The verse emphasizes the unrighteousness of concealing a testimony from God and reminds the listener that God is aware of all actions. The verse serves as a reminder that religious labels and affiliations do not determine a person's relationship with God and that concealing the truth is a grave sin.
orig: أم تقولون إن إبراهيم وإسماعيل وإسحاق ويعقوب والأسباط كانوا هودا أو نصارى قل أأنتم أعلم أم الله ومن أظلم ممن كتم شهادة عنده من الله وما الله بغافل عما تعملون

translation: That is a nation that has passed away for what it had earned. And you will surely find something similar to it. And what you are promised will certainly come to pass. And you will not be asked about what they used to do.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the consequences of actions, emphasizing that every person or nation will bear the consequences of their own deeds. The phrase 'you will surely find something similar to it' serves as a warning that the same fate will befall those who follow in the footsteps of the transgressors. The verse reminds the readers that they will not be questioned about the sins of others, but will be held accountable for their own actions. Ultimately, the verse emphasizes the importance of individual responsibility and accountability, and the inevitability of divine justice.
orig: تلك أمة قد خلت لها ما كسبت ولكم ما كسبتم ولا تسألون عما كانوا يعملون

translation: The foolish among the people will say, 'What has turned them away from the path they used to follow?' Say, 'To God belongs the east and the west. He guides whom He wills to a straight path.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the foolish people who question the change in the path or beliefs of others. The verse instructs the Prophet Muhammad to respond to them by asserting the power and knowledge of God, who guides whom He wills to the right path. The verse emphasizes the ultimate control and wisdom of God, and the limited understanding of humans. It also highlights the futility of questioning God's actions and the importance of following the path guided by God.
orig: سيقول السفهاء من الناس ما ولاهم عن قبلتهم التي كانوا عليها قل لله المشرق والمغرب يهدي من يشاء إلى صراط مستقيم

translation: And thus have We made you a just community that you may be witnesses over the people and the Messenger may be a witness over you. And We did not make the qiblah which you used to face except that We might make evident who follows the Messenger from who turns back on his heels. And indeed, it is difficult except for those whom Allah has guided. And never would Allah have caused you to lose your faith. Indeed Allah is, to the people, Kind and Merciful.
interpretation: The verse highlights the importance of the Muslim community as witnesses and followers of the Messenger, and the role of the Messenger as a witness over the community. The verse also explains the reason for changing the direction of prayer (qiblah) from Jerusalem to Mecca, which was to distinguish between those who truly follow the Messenger and those who turn back on their heels (i.e. those who reject the Messenger). The verse emphasizes the guidance of Allah, which is crucial for staying on the right path, and the kindness and mercy of Allah towards the people.
orig: وكذلك جعلناكم أمة وسطا لتكونوا شهداء على الناس ويكون الرسول عليكم شهيدا وما جعلنا القبلة التي كنت عليها إلا لنعلم من يتبع الرسول ممن ينقلب على عقبيه وإن كانت لكبيرة إلا على الذين هدى الله وما كان الله ليضيع إيمانكم إن الله بالناس لرءوف رحيم

translation: We see your turning your face about in the heaven; now We will surely turn you to a qiblah which will please you, turn then your face in the direction of the sacred mosque; and wherever you are, turn your faces towards it. And surely those who have been given the Book know that it is the truth from their Lord. And Allah is not unaware of what they do.
interpretation: The verse speaks about God's command to the Prophet Muhammad to change the direction of prayer (qiblah) from Jerusalem to Mecca. The verse emphasizes the divine guidance and the willingness of God to please the Prophet. The verse also addresses the people who have been given the Book (Jews and Christians) and reminds them that the new qiblah is the truth from their Lord. The verse implies that the previous qiblah was not the true one and that the change of qiblah is a confirmation of the truth of Islam. The verse also emphasizes God's knowledge of what people do, reminding them of the importance of their actions and their accountability before God.
orig: قد نرى تقلب وجهك في السماء فلنولينك قبلة ترضاها فول وجهك شطر المسجد الحرام وحيث ما كنتم فولوا وجوهكم شطره وإن الذين أوتوا الكتاب ليعلمون أنه الحق من ربهم وما الله بغافل عما يعملون

translation: And if you should follow the majority of those who were given the Scripture, they would mislead you from the way of Allah. You would then be among the losers.
interpretation: The verse warns against following the majority of those who were given the Scripture (Jews and Christians) as they would mislead one from the way of Allah and result in loss. The verse emphasizes the importance of staying on the path of righteousness, even if it goes against the majority, and the dangers of blindly following the guidance of others without proper understanding and discernment.
orig: ولئن أتيت الذين أوتوا الكتاب بكل آية ما تبعوا قبلتك وما أنت بتابع قبلتهم وما بعضهم بتابع قبلة بعض ولئن اتبعت أهواءهم من بعد ما جاءك من العلم إنك إذا لمن الظالمين

translation: Those to whom We have given the Scripture recognize it as they recognize their children. And indeed, a group of them conceal the truth while they know [it].
interpretation: The verse speaks about the people who have received the Scripture (the Torah and the Gospel) and have the ability to recognize its truth. This recognition is compared to the way they recognize their own children. However, a group of them conceal the truth despite knowing it. This act of concealing the truth is a form of injustice and a rejection of God's guidance. The verse serves as a reminder to those who have received the Scripture to be truthful and just in their interpretation and implementation of it, and not to conceal or distort the truth for personal gain or other reasons.
orig: الذين آتيناهم الكتاب يعرفونه كما يعرفون أبناءهم وإن فريقا منهم ليكتمون الحق وهم يعلمون

translation: The truth is from your Lord, so do not be among the doubters.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of accepting the truth from one's Lord and having unwavering faith. The command 'do not be among the doubters' implies that having doubts is a choice, and one must strive to strengthen their faith and avoid falling into doubt and uncertainty. This verse encourages believers to have firm conviction in their faith and to always seek the truth from their Lord, and to avoid being among those who harbor doubts and uncertainty.
orig: الحق من ربك فلا تكونن من الممترين

translation: To Him is the orientation of everything in the heavens and the earth; so follow the way of righteousness, wherever you may be. You will surely return to Him in the end. Indeed, He is all-embracing, all-knowing.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes that everything in the heavens and the earth belongs to God, and therefore, the right way of living is to follow the path of righteousness, regardless of where one may be. The verse also reminds the reader that everyone will ultimately return to God, and that God has power over all things and has complete knowledge of all things.
orig: ولكل وجهة هو موليها فاستبقوا الخيرات أين ما تكونوا يأت بكم الله جميعا إن الله على كل شيء قدير

translation: From whatever [place] you come out, turn your face toward the sacred mosque. And indeed, this is the truth from your Lord. And Allah is not unaware of what you do.
interpretation: The verse instructs the reader to turn their face towards the sacred mosque (Kaaba) regardless of the direction they are coming from. This is a command for all Muslims to face the Kaaba during their prayers. The verse emphasizes the importance of this practice by stating that it is the truth from the Lord. The verse also reminds the reader that Allah is all-knowing and aware of all actions, emphasizing the importance of obedience and reverence towards Allah.
orig: ومن حيث خرجت فول وجهك شطر المسجد الحرام وإنه للحق من ربك وما الله بغافل عما تعملون

translation: From wherever you emerge, turn your face toward the Holy Mosque. And wherever you may be, turn your faces toward it so that people will not have an argument against you, except for those among them who commit wrong; so do not fear them, but fear Me. And so that I may complete My blessings upon you and so that you may be guided.
interpretation: This verse outlines the proper etiquette for Muslims when determining the direction of prayer (qibla). Muslims are instructed to face the Holy Mosque (in Mecca) during prayer, regardless of their location. This is to ensure unity and avoid disputes among the believers. The verse emphasizes the importance of focusing on one's relationship with God, rather than being concerned with the opinions of others. By following this command, Muslims can fully receive God's blessings and guidance. The verse can be seen as a reminder of the importance of unity, focus, and trust in God during worship.
orig: ومن حيث خرجت فول وجهك شطر المسجد الحرام وحيث ما كنتم فولوا وجوهكم شطره لئلا يكون للناس عليكم حجة إلا الذين ظلموا منهم فلا تخشوهم واخشوني ولأتم نعمتي عليكم ولعلكم تهتدون

translation: As we have sent among you a messenger from yourselves, reciting to you our verses and purifying you and teaching you the book and wisdom and teaching you that which you did not know.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the sending of a messenger from among the people themselves, who recites the verses of God, purifies the people, teaches them the book (the Qur'an), and gives them wisdom and knowledge. The verse emphasizes the role of the messenger in guiding the people and providing them with the necessary tools to live a righteous life. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of following the teachings of the messenger and seeking knowledge and wisdom.
orig: كما أرسلنا فيكم رسولا منكم يتلو عليكم آياتنا ويزكيكم ويعلمكم الكتاب والحكمة ويعلمكم ما لم تكونوا تعلمون

translation: So remember Me, I will remember you. Be grateful to Me, and do not reject Me.
interpretation: The verse is a direct address from God, reminding people to remember and acknowledge Him in their daily lives. In return, God promises to remember and recognize the actions of His people. The verse also encourages people to express gratitude and thankfulness towards God for His blessings and to avoid disbelief and rejection of Him. The verse emphasizes the importance of the relationship between humans and God, and the mutual recognition and gratitude that should exist between them.
orig: فاذكروني أذكركم واشكروا لي ولا تكفرون

translation: O you who have believed, seek help through patience and prayer. Indeed, Allah is with the patient.
interpretation: The verse is a command to the believers to seek help through patience and prayer in times of difficulty. It emphasizes the importance of patience and prayer in overcoming hardships and trials. The verse also reassures the believers that Allah is with those who are patient, indicating that they are not alone in their struggles. Overall, the verse encourages believers to rely on their faith and relationship with Allah during difficult times, and to seek His help through patience and prayer.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا استعينوا بالصبر والصلاة إن الله مع الصابرين

translation: And do not say about those who are killed in the way of Allah, 'They are dead.' Rather, they are alive, but you do not perceive.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the idea that those who are killed while fighting for the sake of Allah (in a just cause) are not dead, but alive. The verse encourages believers not to mourn for them as if they have lost them forever, but rather to understand that they are alive in a different form. The verse implies that the believers will be rewarded for their sacrifice in the afterlife. It also encourages the believers to have faith and trust in Allah's plan and not to lose hope. The verse serves as a reminder that death is not the end, but a transition to another form of existence.
orig: ولا تقولوا لمن يقتل في سبيل الله أموات بل أحياء ولكن لا تشعرون

translation: And We will surely test you with something of fear and hunger and a loss of wealth and lives and fruits, but give good tidings to the patient.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the various trials and tribulations that God will test humanity with, including fear, hunger, loss of wealth and lives, and scarcity of resources. Despite these hardships, the verse encourages patience and reminds the believers of the rewards for those who remain steadfast in their faith during difficult times. The verse emphasizes the inevitability of trials in life and encourages believers to remain patient and steadfast in their faith, knowing that God will ultimately reward their perseverance.
orig: ولنبلونكم بشيء من الخوف والجوع ونقص من الأموال والأنفس والثمرات وبشر الصابرين

translation: When a disaster strikes them, they say, 'Indeed we belong to Allah, and indeed to Him we will return.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the believers' response to a calamity or disaster. Upon facing such a situation, the believers immediately recognize and submit to the divine decree, saying 'Indeed we belong to Allah, and indeed to Him we will return.' This statement reflects their faith in Allah's wisdom and justice, and their acceptance of His will, even when it brings hardship and suffering. The verse serves as a reminder of the believers' ultimate reliance on and trust in Allah, and their understanding that all that befalls them is part of a greater divine plan.
orig: الذين إذا أصابتهم مصيبة قالوا إنا لله وإنا إليه راجعون

translation: Those are upon whom are blessings from their Lord and mercy. And those are the guided ones.
interpretation: The verse speaks about a group of people who have received blessings and mercy from their Lord. These people are also described as being guided. The verse suggests that the blessings, mercy, and guidance come from a higher power, or God, and that those who receive these gifts are on the right path. The verse can be seen as a message of hope and reassurance for those who are seeking guidance and striving to live a righteous life, promising them that they will be blessed and guided by God.
orig: أولئك عليهم صلوات من ربهم ورحمة وأولئك هم المهتدون

translation: Indeed, al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah are among the symbols of Allah. So whoever makes Hajj to the House or performs 'Umrah—there is no blame upon him for walking between them. And whoever volunteers good—then indeed, Allah is appreciative and knowing.
interpretation: This verse speaks about the significance of al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah, two hills in Mecca that are considered sacred in Islam. The verse states that there is no blame on those who make a pilgrimage to the Kaaba or perform 'Umrah (a lesser pilgrimage) if they walk between these two hills. The verse also encourages good deeds and notes that Allah is appreciative and knowing, implying that such deeds do not go unnoticed and will be rewarded.
orig: إن الصفا والمروة من شعائر الله فمن حج البيت أو اعتمر فلا جناح عليه أن يطوف بهما ومن تطوع خيرا فإن الله شاكر عليم

translation: Indeed, those who conceal what We have sent down of clear proofs and guidance, after We have made it clear for the people in the Book - those, Allah curses them and curses them the cursers.
interpretation: The verse condemns those who conceal the clear signs and guidance that has been sent down from God, after it has been made clear in the scripture. These people are condemned by both God and those who curse. The verse emphasizes the importance of sharing and spreading the message of God, rather than concealing it. The verse serves as a warning to those who choose to hide or distort the truth, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's judgement.
orig: إن الذين يكتمون ما أنزلنا من البينات والهدى من بعد ما بيناه للناس في الكتاب أولئك يلعنهم الله ويلعنهم اللاعنون

translation: Except for those who repent, correct themselves, and make things clear. So for those, I will turn to them. And I am the One who is most forgiving, most merciful.
interpretation: The verse offers a way out of the punishment for those who are willing to change their ways. It sets out three conditions for forgiveness: repentance, correcting one's actions, and making things clear. This can be interpreted as a call for sincere repentance and a change of heart, as well as a commitment to make amends for past wrongs. The verse emphasizes the mercy and forgiveness of God, and His readiness to accept those who truly turn to Him. It serves as a message of hope and a call for reform for those who may have strayed from the right path.
orig: إلا الذين تابوا وأصلحوا وبينوا فأولئك أتوب عليهم وأنا التواب الرحيم

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieved and died while they were disbelievers - upon them is the curse of Allah and the angels and all of the people.
interpretation: The verse pronounces a curse upon those who have rejected faith and died while persisting in their disbelief. The curse is not only from Allah, but also from the angels and all of humanity, emphasizing the severity and finality of their fate. This verse serves as a warning to those who deny the truth, reminding them of the eternal consequences of their rejection of faith and the certainty of divine retribution for their unbelief.
orig: إن الذين كفروا وماتوا وهم كفار أولئك عليهم لعنة الله والملائكة والناس أجمعين

translation: In it they will abide eternally; the punishment will not be lightened for them, nor will they be reprieved.
interpretation: The verse describes the fate of certain people who will reside in a place of punishment eternally, with no relief or reprieve. The punishment they receive will not be eased, and they will not be given a break from it. This verse emphasizes the severity of the punishment and the permanence of their fate, serving as a warning to those who might find themselves in similar circumstances.
orig: خالدين فيها لا يخفف عنهم العذاب ولا هم ينظرون

translation: And your God is one God: there is no deity except Him, the Compassionate, the Merciful.
interpretation: The verse affirms the oneness of God and denies the existence of any other deity. It emphasizes the uniqueness and exclusivity of God by stating that there is no deity except Him. The verse also describes God with two of His most important attributes: the Compassionate and the Merciful, highlighting His benevolence and kindness towards His creation. This verse serves as a fundamental principle in Islamic belief, emphasizing the importance of monotheism and the belief in the compassionate and merciful nature of God.
orig: وإلهكم إله واحد لا إله إلا هو الرحمن الرحيم

translation: Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth and the alternation of the night and the day are signs for those of understanding. Who remember Allah while standing or sitting or [lying] on their sides and contemplate the creation of the heavens and the earth, [saying], 'Our Lord, You did not create this aimlessly; exalted are You [above such a thing]; then protect us from the punishment of the Fire.'
interpretation: This verse highlights various signs in the universe, including the creation of the heavens and the earth, the alternation of night and day, and the movement of celestial bodies. These signs are meant for those who reflect and use their intellect. The verse encourages believers to remember Allah in all situations, whether standing, sitting, or lying down. It also encourages contemplation and reflection on the creation of the universe, leading to a deeper appreciation and gratitude for the divine presence. The verse concludes with a prayer for protection from the punishment of the Fire, emphasizing the importance of faith and righteousness in the face of divine judgment.
orig: إن في خلق السماوات والأرض واختلاف الليل والنهار والفلك التي تجري في البحر بما ينفع الناس وما أنزل الله من السماء من ماء فأحيا به الأرض بعد موتها وبث فيها من كل دابة وتصريف الرياح والسحاب المسخر بين السماء والأرض لآيات لقوم يعقلون

translation: And among mankind is he who takes besides Allah, other gods which he loves as he loves Allah. But those who believe, love Allah more (than anything else). And if only the unjust could see, when they see the punishment, that the power entirely belongs to Allah, and that Allah is severe in punishment.
interpretation: The verse highlights the distinction between those who worship Allah and those who worship other gods. Those who truly believe in Allah love Him more than anything else, while those who commit injustice and associate others with Allah in worship, love these other beings as much as they love Allah. However, the verse warns that when the unjust see the punishment of Allah, they will realize that the power belongs to Him alone and that His punishment is severe. This serves as a reminder to those who may be straying from the path of Allah, to turn back to Him and to worship Him alone, before it is too late.
orig: ومن الناس من يتخذ من دون الله أندادا يحبونهم كحب الله والذين آمنوا أشد حبا لله ولو يرى الذين ظلموا إذ يرون العذاب أن القوة لله جميعا وأن الله شديد العذاب

translation: When those who followed [others in disbelief] were separated from those who followed [the truth], they saw the punishment, and their ties were cut off.
interpretation: The verse describes the moment when the believers and the disbelievers are separated on the Day of Judgment. Those who followed the truth are saved, while those who followed the disbelievers are punished. The verse emphasizes the finality of this separation, as the ties between the two groups are cut off, indicating that there is no possibility of reconciliation or return. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of following the truth and the consequences of following falsehood.
orig: إذ تبرأ الذين اتبعوا من الذين اتبعوا ورأوا العذاب وتقطعت بهم الأسباب

translation: And those who have taken others as protectors besides Him [Allah] say, 'If we had had anything to do with the guidance, we would not have been among the wrongdoers.' Likewise, Allah leaves astray whom He wills and guides whom He wills. And no one will be wronged even equal to a thread [the width of a hair].
interpretation: The verse highlights the hypocrisy of those who claim to follow a path of guidance, yet still take protectors besides Allah. They claim that if they had any role in guiding others, they would not have been among the wrongdoers. However, the verse emphasizes that Allah is the one who guides and misguides as He wills, and no one can escape His decree. The verse serves as a reminder that no one will be wronged even to the extent of a thread, and that Allah's justice is absolute.
orig: وقال الذين اتبعوا لو أن لنا كرة فنتبرأ منهم كما تبرءوا منا كذلك يريهم الله أعمالهم حسرات عليهم وما هم بخارجين من النار

translation: O mankind, eat from whatever is on earth lawful and good and do not follow the footsteps of Satan. Indeed, he is to you a clear enemy.
interpretation: The verse addresses all of humanity, instructing them to eat only what is permissible and pure from the earth. It warns against following the ways of Satan, who is described as a clear enemy. The verse emphasizes the importance of making righteous choices in one's actions and avoiding that which is forbidden, as following Satan's path leads to harm and destruction. The verse serves as a reminder to seek guidance and stay on the path of righteousness, and to be aware of and avoid the traps and schemes of Satan.
orig: يا أيها الناس كلوا مما في الأرض حلالا طيبا ولا تتبعوا خطوات الشيطان إنه لكم عدو مبين

translation: He only commands you to do evil and wrong and to attribute to Allah what you do not know.
interpretation: The verse highlights the prohibition of disobedience and sin, and the warning against attributing false things to God. The verse emphasizes the importance of avoiding evil and wrongdoing, and not making false claims about God. The verse serves as a reminder that God only commands good and righteousness, and that any act of evil or falsehood is a violation of God's commands. The verse encourages believers to strive for righteousness, and to avoid falling into the trap of disobedience and sin.
orig: إنما يأمركم بالسوء والفحشاء وأن تقولوا على الله ما لا تعلمون

translation: And when it is said to them, 'Follow what Allah has revealed,' they say, 'Rather, we will follow what we found our fathers doing.' Even if their forefathers had no understanding or guidance.
interpretation: The verse highlights the stubbornness and resistance of certain people to follow the guidance of Allah. When they are asked to follow the teachings of Islam, they refuse and insist on following the traditions and practices of their ancestors. The verse criticizes this behavior and emphasizes that blindly following the ways of the forefathers, especially when they lack understanding or guidance, is not a valid justification for not accepting the truth. The verse serves as a reminder to be open-minded and receptive to new ideas and guidance, rather than being bound by tradition and dogma.
orig: وإذا قيل لهم اتبعوا ما أنزل الله قالوا بل نتبع ما ألفينا عليه آباءنا أولو كان آباؤهم لا يعقلون شيئا ولا يهتدون

translation: And the example of those who disbelieve is like the example of the one who calls out to that which does not hear except callings of a screamer and a madman. (They are) deaf, dumb and blind. So they do not use their reason.
interpretation: The verse uses a metaphor to describe the state of the disbelievers. They are likened to a person who is shouting and calling out to something that cannot hear or respond, similar to the screams of a madman. This is a depiction of their futile efforts in their disbelief. The verse further emphasizes that the disbelievers are deaf, dumb, and blind, meaning that they are unable to comprehend the truth and guidance that is presented to them. They lack the ability to use their reason and understanding, thus they remain in their state of disbelief and ignorance.
orig: ومثل الذين كفروا كمثل الذي ينعق بما لا يسمع إلا دعاء ونداء صم بكم عمي فهم لا يعقلون

translation: O believers, eat from the good things We have provided for you, and give thanks to God if it is Him you worship.
interpretation: The verse addresses the believers and encourages them to eat from the good things that God has provided for them, while also reminding them to be thankful to God for their sustenance. The verse emphasizes the importance of gratitude and acknowledges God as the ultimate provider and the one who is worthy of worship. The verse encourages a mindful and thankful approach to the blessings of life, and it serves as a reminder of the relationship between the believers and God, urging them to be conscious of their actions and to remember God in all aspects of their lives.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا كلوا من طيبات ما رزقناكم واشكروا لله إن كنتم إياه تعبدون

translation: Forbidden to you is that which dies of itself, and blood, and flesh of swine, and that on which any other name than that of Allah has been invoked, and the strangled (animal) and that beaten to death, and that killed by a fall and that killed by being smitten with the horn, and that which wild beasts have eaten, except what you slaughter, and what is sacrificed on stones set up (for idols) and that you divide by the arrows; that is a transgression. This day have those who disbelieve despaired of your religion, so fear them not, and fear Me. This day have I perfected for you your religion and completed My favor on you and chosen for you Islam as a religion; but whoever is compelled by hunger, not inclining willfully to sin, then surely Allah is Forgiving, Merciful.
interpretation: This verse from Surah Al-Maidah outlines the food that is forbidden for Muslims to consume, including animals that have died of natural causes, blood, pork, and animals that have been slaughtered in the name of any other deity but Allah. The verse also forbids the consumption of animals that have been strangled, beaten to death, killed by a fall, or gored to death by a horn. However, if an animal is slaughtered according to Islamic law, it is permissible to eat, even if it has been divided by the use of arrows. The verse emphasizes that these laws are not meant to be transgressed, and those who disbelieve in the religion should not be feared. Instead, Muslims should fear Allah and strive to uphold their faith. The verse concludes by stating that Allah is forgiving and merciful towards those who are compelled by hunger to eat forbidden food, as long as they do not willfully sin.
orig: إنما حرم عليكم الميتة والدم ولحم الخنزير وما أهل به لغير الله فمن اضطر غير باغ ولا عاد فلا إثم عليه إن الله غفور رحيم

translation: Indeed, those who conceal what Allah has sent down of the Book and sell it for a small price, they consume in their bellies not but the fire. And Allah will not speak to them on the Day of Resurrection, nor will He purify them. And they will have a painful punishment.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the people who conceal the revelations of Allah and sell them for a small price. The verse highlights the punishment that awaits them, which is that they will consume nothing but fire in their bellies. Furthermore, Allah will not speak to them on the Day of Judgment nor will He purify them. They will also face a painful punishment. The verse strongly condemns the act of concealing the revelations of Allah and selling them for personal gain, and warns of the severe consequences of such actions.
orig: إن الذين يكتمون ما أنزل الله من الكتاب ويشترون به ثمنا قليلا أولئك ما يأكلون في بطونهم إلا النار ولا يكلمهم الله يوم القيامة ولا يزكيهم ولهم عذاب أليم

translation: Those are they who have purchased error at the price of guidance, and their trade has brought them no gain, nor have they been guided.
interpretation: The verse speaks about people who have chosen to reject guidance and instead follow error and misguidance. The verse emphasizes the foolishness of this choice, as it has brought them no benefit or enlightenment, but rather has led them further astray. The verse serves as a warning to those who may be tempted to follow the wrong path, reminding them of the ultimate futility and harm of such a choice.
orig: أولئك الذين اشتروا الضلالة بالهدى والعذاب بالمغفرة فما أصبرهم على النار

translation: That is because Allah has revealed the Book in truth. And indeed, those who disagree - their disagreement is far removed.
interpretation: The verse asserts the truth of the Book (the Qur'an) that has been revealed by Allah. The verse also highlights the division and disagreement among those who oppose the message of the Qur'an. The disagreement of these people is described as being far removed, indicating that it is baseless and without merit. The verse emphasizes the importance of adhering to the truth of the Qur'an and the futility of opposing it.
orig: ذلك بأن الله نزل الكتاب بالحق وإن الذين اختلفوا في الكتاب لفي شقاق بعيد

translation: Righteousness is not that you turn your faces to the east or the west, but righteousness is [in] one who believes in Allah, the Last Day, the angels, the Book, and the prophets and gives wealth, in spite of love for it, to relatives, orphans, the poor, and the traveler, and whoever is sincere in purifying himself, and those who establish prayer and give zakah and those who fulfill their promise when they promise and those who are patient in poverty and hardship and during battle. Those are the ones who have been true, and it is those who are the righteous.
interpretation: The verse defines what it means to be righteous and just in the eyes of God. It emphasizes that righteousness is not just about performing certain actions, such as facing a particular direction during prayer, but rather it is about one's belief in God, the Last Day, angels, scripture, and prophets. The verse also highlights the importance of generosity, purification, prayer, and fulfilling one's promises. It also mentions the importance of patience and perseverance during hardship and poverty. The verse serves as a reminder that true righteousness is not just about outward actions, but also about one's inner beliefs and character. It is a call for the believers to be true and righteous in all aspects of their lives.
orig: ليس البر أن تولوا وجوهكم قبل المشرق والمغرب ولكن البر من آمن بالله واليوم الآخر والملائكة والكتاب والنبيين وآتى المال على حبه ذوي القربى واليتامى والمساكين وابن السبيل والسائلين وفي الرقاب وأقام الصلاة وآتى الزكاة والموفون بعهدهم إذا عاهدوا والصابرين في البأساء والضراء وحين البأس أولئك الذين صدقوا وأولئك هم المتقون

translation: O you who have believed, prescribed for you is legal retribution for those murdered - the free for the free, the slave for the slave, and the female for the female. But whoever forgives and reaches a reconciliation among themselves - then indeed, that is a closure to them from your Lord, a mercy. And whoever transgresses thereafter - then indeed, for him is a severe punishment.
interpretation: This verse sets forth the principle of 'qisas' or retaliation in cases of murder, with the punishment being equivalent to the crime. However, it also allows for forgiveness and reconciliation, which is seen as a 'mercy' from God. Those who choose to forgive and reconcile will have their sins forgiven, while those who transgress or commit further wrongs after this will face severe punishment. The verse emphasizes the importance of justice, but also encourages forgiveness and reconciliation as a means of achieving mercy and closure.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا كتب عليكم القصاص في القتلى الحر بالحر والعبد بالعبد والأنثى بالأنثى فمن عفي له من أخيه شيء فاتباع بالمعروف وأداء إليه بإحسان ذلك تخفيف من ربكم ورحمة فمن اعتدى بعد ذلك فله عذاب أليم

translation: And there is life for you in retaliation, O you who have understanding, that you may become righteous.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the concept of 'qisas' or retaliation in Islamic law and its benefits. The verse suggests that there is a deeper purpose and wisdom behind the concept of retaliation, which is to promote justice, fairness, and righteousness. The verse addresses those who are wise and understanding, urging them to reflect and consider the greater good of implementing retaliation as a means of achieving justice and deterring wrongdoing. The verse encourages the pursuit of righteousness and reminds believers of the importance of upholding justice and fairness in their lives.
orig: ولكم في القصاص حياة يا أولي الألباب لعلكم تتقون

translation: It is written for you, when death approaches one of you, that you make a bequest to parents and next of kin in kindness, a duty for the righteous.
interpretation: The verse outlines the responsibility of Muslims towards their parents and relatives when they are near death. It emphasizes the importance of leaving a bequest for one's parents and next of kin, as a form of kindness and a duty for those who are righteous. This verse encourages Muslims to remember and provide for their loved ones even in their final moments, as a way of fulfilling their religious and moral obligations.
orig: كتب عليكم إذا حضر أحدكم الموت إن ترك خيرا الوصية للوالدين والأقربين بالمعروف حقا على المتقين

translation: But whoever replaces it after hearing it, then indeed, the sin is only upon those who replace it. Indeed, Allah is Hearing and Knowing.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the consequences of changing or altering the words of Allah after hearing them. The verse makes it clear that the sin lies solely with those who commit this act of alteration. The verse emphasizes that Allah is all-hearing and all-knowing, implying that He is aware of the actions of those who choose to alter His words and will hold them accountable for their actions.
orig: فمن بدله بعدما سمعه فإنما إثمه على الذين يبدلونه إن الله سميع عليم

translation: And whoever fears from his brother mistrust or wrongs, then he makes reconciliation between them, then there is no sin on him. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the importance of reconciliation and forgiveness between people. If someone fears that their brother (in a general sense, meaning another person) may have mistrust or wrong them, and they take the initiative to reconcile and make things right between them, then they will not be held accountable for the wrongs that may have been done. This verse emphasizes the importance of resolving conflicts and promoting peace and harmony among people. It also highlights the compassionate nature of Allah, who is Forgiving and Merciful towards those who strive for reconciliation and forgiveness.
orig: فمن خاف من موص جنفا أو إثما فأصلح بينهم فلا إثم عليه إن الله غفور رحيم

translation: O you who have believed, decreed upon you is fasting as it was decreed upon those before you that you may become righteous.
interpretation: The verse commands the believers to fast, as it was a commandment for those who came before them, in order that they may attain piety and righteousness. The verse emphasizes the importance of fasting and its role in cultivating a sense of fear and consciousness of God. By following the example of those who came before them, the believers are encouraged to fulfill this religious obligation and strive for spiritual growth and development.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا كتب عليكم الصيام كما كتب على الذين من قبلكم لعلكم تتقون

translation: Prescribed for you when illness strikes you, or a journey is too long, are: breaking the fast and feeding a poor person. But for those who can fast only with extreme difficulty, there is a compensation: feeding a poor person. It is better for you if you only knew.
interpretation: The verse outlines the rules for fasting during times of illness or long journeys. If one is unable to fast due to illness or travel, they are required to feed a poor person instead. However, those who are able to fast but find it extremely difficult can choose to feed a poor person instead.
