The verse emphasizes the importance of helping those in need, either by fasting or by providing sustenance to the less fortunate. The verse encourages compassion and generosity towards others, and highlights the rewards of such actions.
orig: أياما معدودات فمن كان منكم مريضا أو على سفر فعدة من أيام أخر وعلى الذين يطيقونه فدية طعام مسكين فمن تطوع خيرا فهو خير له وأن تصوموا خير لكم إن كنتم تعلمون

translation: Ramadan is the month in which the Qur'an was sent down as a guidance for the people, and as clear signs of guidance and the criterion [between right and wrong]. So whoever among you witnesses the month, let him fast it. And whoever is ill or on a journey - then an equal number of other days. Allah intends for you ease and does not intend for you hardship and [so that] you may complete the number and exalt Allah for that [to] which He has guided you; and perhaps you will be grateful.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the significance of the month of Ramadan, in which the Qur'an was revealed as a guidance for humanity. The verse encourages Muslims to fast during this month, and it provides exceptions for those who are ill or traveling. The verse emphasizes that God wants ease for the believers and does not want to make things difficult for them. The verse encourages Muslims to complete the fast and to be grateful for the guidance that God has given them. This verse serves as a reminder of the importance of the month of Ramadan and the significance of the Qur'an, and it encourages Muslims to follow the guidance of the Qur'an and to be grateful for it.
orig: شهر رمضان الذي أنزل فيه القرآن هدى للناس وبينات من الهدى والفرقان فمن شهد منكم الشهر فليصمه ومن كان مريضا أو على سفر فعدة من أيام أخر يريد الله بكم اليسر ولا يريد بكم العسر ولتكملوا العدة ولتكبروا الله على ما هداكم ولعلكم تشكرون

translation: And when My servants ask you concerning Me, then indeed I am near; I respond to the invocation of the supplicant when he calls upon Me. So let them respond to Me and believe in Me, so that they may be guided.
interpretation: The verse speaks about God's closeness to His servants and His readiness to respond to their invocations. The verse encourages the believers to call upon God and have faith in Him, as this will guide them. The verse emphasizes the importance of responding to God, which is a sign of faith and devotion. The verse also highlights the idea that God is always near and ready to listen to the prayers of His servants, and that by calling upon Him, they can find guidance and be answered.
orig: وإذا سألك عبادي عني فإني قريب أجيب دعوة الداع إذا دعان فليستجيبوا لي وليؤمنوا بي لعلهم يرشدون

translation: It has been made permissible for you on the night of fasting to go to your wives [for sexual relations]. They are a garment for you and you are a garment for them. Allah is Knowing that you were deceiving yourselves, so He has turned to you and forgiven you. So now, have relations with them and seek what Allah has decreed for you. And eat and drink until the white thread of dawn becomes distinct to you from the black thread [of night]. Then complete the fast until the sunset. And do not have relations with them as long as you are staying in the mosques for the worship of Allah, but when you return to your homes, then have relations with them - the limits of Allah are made clear - so do not approach them to have relations with them while you are in the state of ihram for Hajj or Umrah. Thus does Allah make clear His verses for the people that they may become righteous.
interpretation: The verse outlines the rules and guidelines for sexual relations during the month of Ramadan, the ninth month of the Islamic calendar. It highlights the permissibility of intimacy between spouses during the night of fasting, emphasizing that they are a source of comfort and protection for each other. The verse also acknowledges the human tendency to deceive oneself and encourages forgiveness and repentance. It sets the boundaries for sexual activity, specifying that it is prohibited during the daytime fast and during the state of ihram for Hajj or Umrah. The verse serves as a reminder to Muslims of the importance of maintaining a balance between their religious obligations and their marital responsibilities, and of the need to follow the guidance and rules set by Allah in order to attain righteousness and live a fulfilling life.
orig: أحل لكم ليلة الصيام الرفث إلى نسائكم هن لباس لكم وأنتم لباس لهن علم الله أنكم كنتم تختانون أنفسكم فتاب عليكم وعفا عنكم فالآن باشروهن وابتغوا ما كتب الله لكم وكلوا واشربوا حتى يتبين لكم الخيط الأبيض من الخيط الأسود من الفجر ثم أتموا الصيام إلى الليل ولا تباشروهن وأنتم عاكفون في المساجد تلك حدود الله فلا تقربوها كذلك يبين الله آياته للناس لعلهم يتقون

translation: And do not consume one another's wealth unjustly among yourselves, and offer it as a gift to the rulers so that you may consume a part of people's wealth sinfully while you know.
interpretation: The verse highlights the prohibition of consuming each other's wealth unjustly and giving it as a bribe to the rulers in order to gain an unfair advantage. The verse emphasizes the sinful nature of this act and the fact that it is done knowingly. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of justice and fairness in economic transactions and the consequences of engaging in unjust practices.
orig: ولا تأكلوا أموالكم بينكم بالباطل وتدلوا بها إلى الحكام لتأكلوا فريقا من أموال الناس بالإثم وأنتم تعلمون

translation: They ask you concerning the sacred months, say: they are the fixed seasons of God, in which the unbelievers are invited to the unarmed pilgrimage; this that they may witness the benefits provided for them, and mention the name of God, according to the practices of their fathers;- unbelievers were preventing others from the pilgrimage path; and if any unbeliever prevents anyone from performing the pilgrimage in it, or any wrong is done to him, we will make him suffer a painful punishment.
interpretation: The verse explains the significance of the sacred months in Islam and the importance of the pilgrimage. It emphasizes that the sacred months are fixed by God and are a time for unbelievers to witness the benefits provided for them and to mention the name of God. The verse also highlights the unjust actions of the unbelievers in the past, such as preventing others from the pilgrimage path. The verse serves as a reminder of the consequences of such actions and the punishment that will be inflicted on those who prevent others from fulfilling their religious obligations.
orig: يسألونك عن الأهلة قل هي مواقيت للناس والحج وليس البر بأن تأتوا البيوت من ظهورها ولكن البر من اتقى وأتوا البيوت من أبوابها واتقوا الله لعلكم تفلحون

translation: Fight in the way of God those who fight you but do not transgress. Indeed, God does not love transgressors.
interpretation: The verse establishes the principle of just war in Islam, where fighting is permitted only in self-defense and against those who are fighting Muslims. The verse prohibits transgression or aggression towards the enemy, emphasizing that God does not approve of such actions. The verse serves as a reminder that Muslims must maintain their moral and ethical standards even in the midst of war, and that the ultimate goal of fighting is to uphold justice and righteousness.
orig: وقاتلوا في سبيل الله الذين يقاتلونكم ولا تعتدوا إن الله لا يحب المعتدين

translation: And kill them wherever you overtake them and expel them from wherever they have expelled you, and fitnah is worse than killing. And do not fight them near the Sacred Mosque until they fight you there. But if they fight you, then kill them. Such is the recompense of the disbelievers.
interpretation: The verse gives permission for Muslims to defend themselves and fight their oppressors. It emphasizes the importance of fighting oppression and standing up for justice. At the same time, it sets boundaries for fighting, forbidding fighting near the Sacred Mosque and only allowing it in self-defense. The verse serves as a guide for Muslims in dealing with oppression and persecution, encouraging them to stand up for their rights while adhering to the principles of justice and morality.
orig: واقتلوهم حيث ثقفتموهم وأخرجوهم من حيث أخرجوكم والفتنة أشد من القتل ولا تقاتلوهم عند المسجد الحرام حتى يقاتلوكم فيه فإن قاتلوكم فاقتلوهم كذلك جزاء الكافرين

translation: But if they stop, then indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the mercy and forgiveness of God towards those who commit wrongdoings, but then repent and turn away from their sins. The verse emphasizes the compassionate nature of God and His readiness to forgive those who truly regret their actions and seek His forgiveness. The verse serves as a reminder that it is never too late to seek God's forgiveness and that He is always ready to grant it to those who truly repent.
orig: فإن انتهوا فإن الله غفور رحيم

translation: Fight them until there is no fitnah, and religion is all for Allah. But if they cease, then there is no aggression except against the oppressors.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the commandment to fight against those who cause corruption and disorder (fitnah) until religion is solely for Allah. However, if the enemies cease and stop causing fitnah, then there should be no further aggression except against the oppressors. The verse highlights the importance of establishing peace and justice, and the necessity of fighting against those who obstruct this goal. At the same time, it emphasizes the prohibition of aggression and oppression, and the importance of distinguishing between the oppressors and those who have ceased to cause corruption and disorder.
orig: وقاتلوهم حتى لا تكون فتنة ويكون الدين لله فإن انتهوا فلا عدوان إلا على الظالمين

translation: The sacred month is for the sacred month, and for the sacramental offerings there is a sacrament; so whosoever has been compelled in ignorance therein, and afterward repents, Allah is Forgiving, Merciful. And whoso transgresses the limits of Allah after this, he indeed wrongs his own soul; and against these violators is a grievous chastisement.
interpretation: The verse explains the rules of engagement during sacred months and sacramental offerings. It states that any transgression during these times will be met with a similar response. However, if a person commits a violation out of ignorance and repents, God is forgiving and merciful. The verse warns against violating the limits set by God, emphasizing that those who do so will harm themselves and face severe punishment. The verse promotes the importance of adhering to the rules set by God and seeking forgiveness and repentance when mistakes are made.
orig: الشهر الحرام بالشهر الحرام والحرمات قصاص فمن اعتدى عليكم فاعتدوا عليه بمثل ما اعتدى عليكم واتقوا الله واعلموا أن الله مع المتقين

translation: And spend in the way of Allah and do not throw yourselves into destruction with your own hands, and do good; indeed, Allah loves those who do good.
interpretation: The verse encourages Muslims to spend in the way of Allah and to avoid actions that would lead to self-destruction. It emphasizes the importance of doing good and highlights the fact that Allah loves those who do good. The verse encourages Muslims to strive for righteousness and to avoid actions that would lead to harm and destruction. It serves as a reminder that Allah loves those who are mindful of their actions and strive to do good.
orig: وأنفقوا في سبيل الله ولا تلقوا بأيديكم إلى التهلكة وأحسنوا إن الله يحب المحسنين

translation: And complete the Hajj and 'Umrah for Allah. But if you are prevented, then [offer] what can be easily obtained with ease of sacrificial animals. And do not shave your heads until the sacrificial animal reaches its place of slaughter. And whoever among you is ill or has an ailment of the head [making shaving necessary must offer] a ransom of fasting or charity or sacrifice. And when you are secure, then whoever performs 'Umrah [during the Hajj months] followed by Hajj [should] offer what can be easily obtained with ease of sacrificial animals. And whoever cannot find [such an animal] - then a fast of three days during Hajj and seven when you have returned [home] - those are ten complete [days]. And it is for whoever volunteers exceeding that [by vowing] - so fulfill the vow of a pilgrim. And know that Allah is Exalted in Might and Knowing.
interpretation: The verse provides instructions for Muslims on how to complete the pilgrimage to Mecca, known as Hajj and 'Umrah. It emphasizes the importance of fulfilling the obligations of the pilgrimage and the need to make sacrifices as a form of worship. The verse also provides exceptions for those who are unable to fulfill certain aspects of the pilgrimage due to illness or financial hardship. The verse reminds Muslims to be mindful of their responsibilities towards Allah and to be aware of the consequences of their actions. It also encourages Muslims to fulfill any vows they have made to Allah and to strive for excellence in their worship. The verse also emphasizes the power and knowledge of Allah, reminding Muslims of the importance of obedience and reverence towards Allah.
orig: وأتموا الحج والعمرة لله فإن أحصرتم فما استيسر من الهدي ولا تحلقوا رءوسكم حتى يبلغ الهدي محله فمن كان منكم مريضا أو به أذى من رأسه ففدية من صيام أو صدقة أو نسك فإذا أمنتم فمن تمتع بالعمرة إلى الحج فما استيسر من الهدي فمن لم يجد فصيام ثلاثة أيام في الحج وسبعة إذا رجعتم تلك عشرة كاملة ذلك لمن لم يكن أهله حاضري المسجد الحرام واتقوا الله واعلموا أن الله شديد العقاب

translation: Hajj is (only) for the people who are able to undertake the journey to the House (of Allah in Mecca). And whoever denies the right to Hajj, then he is disbeliever. And there is no sin on you if you seek the bounty of your Lord (during Hajj). But when you are over the sacrificial animals, then remember the name of Allah according to your sacrifice. And eat therefrom and feed the beggar who does not ask, and the poor who ask not. Thus have We made them for you a symbolic example. So there is no sin on you if you seek the bounty of your Lord. And when you return from the state of Ihram, remember Allah as you remember your fathers or with a more remembered remembrance. But of mankind is he who says: 'Our Lord! Give us (Your bounties) in this world!' And he will have no share in the Hereafter. And of mankind is he who says: 'Our Lord! Give us good in this world and good in the Hereafter, and protect us from the torment of the Fire!' And these will have a share of what they have earned. And Allah is swift in account. And remember Allah during the appointed Days. But whoever hastens to leave in two days, there is no sin on him and whoever stays on, there is no sin on him, for him who fears Allah and keeps his duty. And fear Allah and know that you will be gathered unto Him. And of mankind is he who buys the amusement of this world at the price of his Hereafter. And of mankind is he who is intelligent. So, (O Muhammad) ask Allah for forgiveness for them (your followers) or do not ask forgiveness for them. If you ask forgiveness for them seventy times, Allah will not forgive them. Because they disbelieved in Allah and His Messenger. And Allah guides not the people who are Fasiqun (rebellious, disobedient to Allah). They (the believers) are those on whom are the blessings from Allah, the All-Merciful, and the All-Compassionate. They (the believers) are those on whom are the blessings from Allah and His Mercy (i.e. who are the pious and righteous persons). They will enter Gardens under which rivers flow, to dwell therein forever (i.e. in Paradise). Such is the reward of those who purify themselves.
interpretation: The verse outlines the rules and etiquettes of the Hajj pilgrimage and emphasizes the importance of remembering and worshipping Allah during this time. The verse warns against immoral behavior such as fornication, trading, and arguing during Hajj. It encourages the pilgrims to be kind and generous to the needy. The verse also highlights the importance of seeking Allah's bounty and forgiveness during Hajj. The verse ends with a reminder of the ultimate goal of Hajj, which is to purify oneself and seek Allah's pleasure. Those who truly purify themselves and follow Allah's commandments will be rewarded with blessings, mercy, and a place in Paradise.
orig: الحج أشهر معلومات فمن فرض فيهن الحج فلا رفث ولا فسوق ولا جدال في الحج وما تفعلوا من خير يعلمه الله وتزودوا فإن خير الزاد التقوى واتقون يا أولي الألباب

translation: You are not at fault if you seek bounty from your Lord. But when you pour forth from 'Arafat, remember Allah at the Sacred Monument and remember Him as He has guided you, and previously you were certainly among the astray.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the actions of the pilgrims during the Hajj pilgrimage. It reminds them that it is not wrong to seek blessings from God, but they must also remember and worship Him at the appropriate times and places. The verse mentions the 'Arafat, a plain near Mecca, where the pilgrims gather to perform a ritual. At this time, they are reminded to remember God and give thanks for His guidance. The verse also acknowledges that the pilgrims were once lost and astray, but have now been guided to the right path.
orig: ليس عليكم جناح أن تبتغوا فضلا من ربكم فإذا أفضتم من عرفات فاذكروا الله عند المشعر الحرام واذكروه كما هداكم وإن كنتم من قبله لمن الضالين

translation: And withdraw from them while they are engaged in their talks and seek forgiveness from God. Indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: The verse advises the believers to withdraw from those who are engaged in disbelief and sinful talk, and instead, seek forgiveness from God. This advice emphasizes the importance of avoiding unnecessary engagement with those who are not receptive to the message of Islam. By seeking forgiveness from God, the believers are reminded of their own shortcomings and are encouraged to focus on their own spiritual growth and development. The verse highlights God's infinite mercy and forgiveness, emphasizing that He is always ready to accept those who repent and seek His forgiveness.
orig: ثم أفيضوا من حيث أفاض الناس واستغفروا الله إن الله غفور رحيم

translation: So when you have completed your rites, remember Allah like your remembrance of your fathers or with a more intense remembrance. And among the people is he who says, 'Our Lord, give us in this world,' and he will have in the Hereafter no share.
interpretation: The verse reminds the believers to remember Allah after completing their religious rites, with a remembrance that is as deep or even deeper than their remembrance of their fathers. This demonstrates the importance of maintaining a strong connection with Allah at all times. The verse also highlights the contrast between those who focus on this worldly life and those who focus on the hereafter. It mentions that some people only ask for worldly gains and will not have any share in the hereafter. This serves as a warning against being overly focused on worldly gains, and neglecting one's duties towards Allah.
orig: فإذا قضيتم مناسككم فاذكروا الله كذكركم آباءكم أو أشد ذكرا فمن الناس من يقول ربنا آتنا في الدنيا وما له في الآخرة من خلاق

translation: And among them is he who says, 'Our Lord, give us good in this world and good in the hereafter, and protect us from the punishment of the Fire.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the prayer of some believers who ask God to grant them good in both this world and the hereafter, and to protect them from the punishment of the Fire (Hell). These believers recognize the importance of both the temporal and the eternal aspects of their existence, and they seek God's mercy and protection in both realms. The verse highlights the importance of seeking God's blessings and protection, and the importance of recognizing the transient nature of this world and the eternal nature of the hereafter.
orig: ومنهم من يقول ربنا آتنا في الدنيا حسنة وفي الآخرة حسنة وقنا عذاب النار

translation: Those are the ones who will have a share of what they have earned, and God is swift in reckoning.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the just deserts of those who have earned a specific fate through their actions. The verse emphasizes that God is swift in reckoning, indicating that the consequences of people's actions will be meted out swiftly and without delay. The verse serves as a reminder that people will ultimately be held accountable for their actions and that they should not take God's patience for granted.
orig: أولئك لهم نصيب مما كسبوا والله سريع الحساب

translation: And remember Allah in specific numbered days. Then whoever hastens [his departure] in two days, there is no sin upon him; and whoever delays, there is no sin upon him, for him who fears Allah and fears the explicit reminder. And fear Allah and know that you will be gathered to Him.
interpretation: This verse reminds believers to remember and worship Allah during specific numbered days, which may refer to religious holidays or pilgrimages. The verse also emphasizes that there is no sin for those who choose to either hasten or delay their departure during these days. However, the verse warns those who fear Allah to be mindful of the explicit reminder and to approach these days with reverence and respect. The verse concludes by reminding believers of the ultimate gathering and judgement before Allah, emphasizing the importance of their actions and their accountability before God.
orig: واذكروا الله في أيام معدودات فمن تعجل في يومين فلا إثم عليه ومن تأخر فلا إثم عليه لمن اتقى واتقوا الله واعلموا أنكم إليه تحشرون

translation: And among the people are those who, if you entrust them with a Qintar, they will return it to you. And among the people are those who, if you entrust them with a single Dinari, they will not return it to you, unless you keep standing over them. That is because they say, 'There is no blame on us if we lost it, or if we were to blame, then it is only a small amount.' But the blame is only on those who do not believe in Allah and the Last Day. And they are ever disobedient.
interpretation: The verse highlights the contrasting behaviors of different types of people when it comes to trust and accountability. On one hand, there are those who can be trusted with a large sum of money (a Qintar) and will return it in full. On the other hand, there are those who cannot be trusted even with a small amount (a Dinari) and will not return it unless closely monitored. The verse explains that this behavior is a result of their disbelief in Allah and the Day of Judgment. The verse serves as a reminder that accountability is a reflection of one's belief and faith, and that those who are not mindful of their responsibilities will be held accountable for their actions.
orig: ومن الناس من يعجبك قوله في الحياة الدنيا ويشهد الله على ما في قلبه وهو ألد الخصام

translation: But when he turns away (from you, O Muhammad), his effort in the land is to make mischief therein and to destroy the crops and the cattle. And Allah does not like mischief.
interpretation: The verse describes the actions of a person who, after turning away from the teachings of Islam, is intent on causing corruption and destruction in the land. This is manifested through the deliberate damage of crops and livestock, which are symbols of prosperity and sustenance. The verse emphasizes that such behavior is displeasing to God. The verse may serve as a reminder of the importance of promoting peace, harmony, and stability, and the negative consequences of actions that undermine these values.
orig: وإذا تولى سعى في الأرض ليفسد فيها ويهلك الحرث والنسل والله لا يحب الفساد

translation: But when it was said to him, 'Fear Allah,' pride took him to sin, so Hell is sufficient for him, and it is an evil bed.
interpretation: The verse speaks about an individual who, when warned to fear God, responded with pride and continued to sin. The verse highlights the destructive nature of pride and its consequences, which in this case is eternal damnation in Hell. The verse serves as a warning to those who let pride and arrogance get in the way of their faith and obedience to God. It emphasizes the importance of humility and submission to God's will, and the severe consequences of disobedience.
orig: وإذا قيل له اتق الله أخذته العزة بالإثم فحسبه جهنم ولبئس المهاد

translation: And among the people is he who sells himself, seeking the pleasure of Allah, and Allah is affectionate towards the servants.
interpretation: The verse highlights the act of a person who willingly sacrifices their own interests and desires for the sake of pleasing God. Such a person is willing to 'sell' themselves, or give up their own desires, for the greater good and in the service of God. The verse emphasizes that God is 'affectionate' towards such servants, indicating that those who make such sacrifices will be rewarded and cared for by God. The verse serves as an inspiration for believers to strive for selflessness and devotion in their service to God, and to trust in God's love and care for them.
orig: ومن الناس من يشري نفسه ابتغاء مرضات الله والله رءوف بالعباد

translation: O you who have believed, enter into Islam completely [and] perfectly and do not follow the footsteps of Satan. Indeed, he is to you a clear enemy.
interpretation: The verse calls upon the believers to fully commit to Islam and not to follow the ways of Satan, who is their clear enemy. The verse emphasizes the importance of complete devotion to the faith and warns against any form of compromise or following the ways of evil. The verse encourages the believers to strive for perfection in their faith and to be vigilant against the deception and cunning of Satan.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا ادخلوا في السلم كافة ولا تتبعوا خطوات الشيطان إنه لكم عدو مبين

translation: But if you fall back after clear signs have come to you, then know that Allah is Exalted in Power, Wise.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the consequences of turning away from the signs of God, even after they have been made clear. The verse warns that if people fall back into disbelief or wrongdoing, they should know that God is all-powerful and wise. This statement emphasizes the futility of trying to defy or escape from God's will, as well as the ultimate wisdom of His judgments. The verse may serve as a reminder of the importance of staying steadfast on the path of righteousness and heeding the signs of God, lest one incurs the wrath of the Almighty.
orig: فإن زللتم من بعد ما جاءتكم البينات فاعلموا أن الله عزيز حكيم

translation: Do they then wait only for Allah to come to them in the shadows of the clouds, and the angels (also)? But the matter has been decreed (so)! And to Allah are (all) affairs returned.
interpretation: The verse speaks about people who are waiting for a sign from God, expecting Him to come to them in the shadows of the clouds, accompanied by angels. However, the verse emphasizes that the matter has already been decreed and that all affairs are returned to God. The verse suggests that people should not wait for a dramatic sign from God, but rather recognize and submit to His power and authority in all matters. The verse may also serve as a reminder that God's power is not limited to grand gestures, but is present and active in all things, even in the seemingly mundane occurrences of everyday life.
orig: هل ينظرون إلا أن يأتيهم الله في ظلل من الغمام والملائكة وقضي الأمر وإلى الله ترجع الأمور

translation: Ask the Children of Israel how many clear signs We have given them. And whoever replaces the favor of Allah after it has come to him - then indeed, Allah is severe in penalty.
interpretation: The verse addresses the Children of Israel and reminds them of the many clear signs and blessings that God has given them. It warns those who replace the favor of Allah with ingratitude and sin, emphasizing that God's punishment is severe for those who reject His blessings and commit injustice. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of gratitude and obedience to God, and the consequences of turning away from His guidance.
orig: سل بني إسرائيل كم آتيناهم من آية بينة ومن يبدل نعمة الله من بعد ما جاءته فإن الله شديد العقاب

translation: Beautified for those who disbelieve is the life of this world, and they ridicule those who believe and those who are mindful of God. But those who are mindful of God will be above them on the Day of Resurrection. And God gives provision to whom He wills without measure.
interpretation: The verse contrasts the temporary enjoyment of this world for those who disbelieve with the eternal reward for those who believe and are mindful of God. The disbelievers ridicule and look down upon the believers, but the believers will be rewarded and elevated on the Day of Resurrection. The verse emphasizes that God provides for whom He wills, without measure or limit, and that ultimate provision and success lies with Him, not with the temporary pleasures of this world.
orig: زين للذين كفروا الحياة الدنيا ويسخرون من الذين آمنوا والذين اتقوا فوقهم يوم القيامة والله يرزق من يشاء بغير حساب

translation: Mankind were one community, then Allah sent the prophets, the bearers of good news and warners, and He sent down with them the Book with the truth, that He might judge between the people in that in which they differed. And none differed except after the clear proofs had come to them, through caprice among themselves. And Allah guided whom He willed, but had those who were given the Scripture known the grace that had been given them, they would not have rejected it for a considerable gain. And We have caused enmity and hatred to exist between them till the Day of Resurrection. And Allah will inform you of that on which you differ.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the role of prophets in guiding mankind and the importance of the scripture in resolving disputes and conflicts. The verse highlights the negative consequences of rejecting the grace of God and the scripture, leading to enmity and hatred among people. The verse emphasizes that guidance comes from God and He guides whom He wills. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of following the guidance of the prophets and the scripture to avoid conflicts and disputes.
orig: كان الناس أمة واحدة فبعث الله النبيين مبشرين ومنذرين وأنزل معهم الكتاب بالحق ليحكم بين الناس فيما اختلفوا فيه وما اختلف فيه إلا الذين أوتوه من بعد ما جاءتهم البينات بغيا بينهم فهدى الله الذين آمنوا لما اختلفوا فيه من الحق بإذنه والله يهدي من يشاء إلى صراط مستقيم

translation: Or do you think that you will enter the Garden while yet the state of those who have passed away before you has not come upon you; distress and affliction have visited them, and they were shaken, till the Messenger and those who believe with him said: 'When will the help of Allah come?' Surely, the help of Allah is near.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the idea that people might have that they will enter paradise without having to go through the same trials and tribulations that previous generations have gone through. The verse emphasizes that distress, affliction, and shaking have visited those who came before, and that the Messenger and the believers with him have asked when the help of God will come. The verse serves as a reminder that the help of God is near, but that it might not come without going through hardship and difficulties.
orig: أم حسبتم أن تدخلوا الجنة ولما يأتكم مثل الذين خلوا من قبلكم مستهم البأساء والضراء وزلزلوا حتى يقول الرسول والذين آمنوا معه متى نصر الله ألا إن نصر الله قريب

translation: They ask you (O Muhammad) what they should spend in (the way of) Allah. Say: 'Whatever wealth you spend, it is for your parents and relatives and orphans and the poor and the wayfarer, and whatever good you do, Allah is aware of it.'
interpretation: The verse addresses the question of what one should spend in the way of Allah. The answer given is that wealth should be spent on parents, relatives, orphans, the poor, and travelers. These categories represent those who are in need and are deserving of assistance. Additionally, the verse emphasizes that all good deeds are known to Allah, indicating that they will not go unnoticed or unrewarded.
orig: يسألونك ماذا ينفقون قل ما أنفقتم من خير فللوالدين والأقربين واليتامى والمساكين وابن السبيل وما تفعلوا من خير فإن الله به عليم

translation: Fighting has been made obligatory upon you, though it is disliked by you. And perhaps you dislike a thing while it is good for you, and perhaps you love a thing while it is bad for you. And Allah knows and you do not know.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the commandment of fighting or jihad, which is obligatory upon the believers, even if they find it unpleasant or distasteful. The verse highlights the limited knowledge and understanding of humans, as contrasted with the all-encompassing knowledge of Allah. The verse suggests that sometimes people dislike what is actually good for them and like what is bad for them, indicating that people's judgments and preferences are not always reliable or correct. The verse serves as a reminder that people should submit to Allah's commands, even if they do not fully understand or agree with them, and trust that Allah knows what is best for them.
orig: كتب عليكم القتال وهو كره لكم وعسى أن تكرهوا شيئا وهو خير لكم وعسى أن تحبوا شيئا وهو شر لكم والله يعلم وأنتم لا تعلمون

translation: They ask you concerning the sacred month - fighting therein. Say, 'Fighting therein is a great [sin], but a greater [sin] in the sight of Allah is to prevent access to the path of Allah, to disbelieve in Him, to disbelieve in the sacred mosque, and to expel its people from it.' And equality in religion is greater than killing. And they will continue to fight you until they turn you back from your religion if they are able. And whoever of you reverts from his religion [to disbelief] and dies while he is a disbeliever - for those, their deeds have become worthless in this world and the Hereafter, and those are the companions of the Fire, they will abide therein eternally.
interpretation: The verse addresses the question of fighting during the sacred month and states that while fighting during this time is a serious sin, there are even greater sins in the sight of God. These include preventing access to the path of God, disbelief in Him, disbelief in the sacred mosque, and expelling its people. The verse emphasizes the importance of maintaining religious equality and the gravity of turning away from one's religion. The verse warns that the disbelievers will continue to fight until they turn believers away from their religion. The verse highlights the severe consequences for those who turn away from their religion and die as disbelievers, stating that their deeds will be worthless in this world and the hereafter, and they will be companions of the Fire, residing therein eternally.
orig: يسألونك عن الشهر الحرام قتال فيه قل قتال فيه كبير وصد عن سبيل الله وكفر به والمسجد الحرام وإخراج أهله منه أكبر عند الله والفتنة أكبر من القتل ولا يزالون يقاتلونكم حتى يردوكم عن دينكم إن استطاعوا ومن يرتدد منكم عن دينه فيمت وهو كافر فأولئك حبطت أعمالهم في الدنيا والآخرة وأولئك أصحاب النار هم فيها خالدون

translation: Indeed, those who have believed and those who have emigrated and fought in the cause of Allah - those expect the mercy of Allah. And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: The verse highlights the qualities and actions that are pleasing to God, and the reward that awaits those who possess them. The three groups of people mentioned - those who believe, those who emigrate for the sake of their faith, and those who strive in the way of God - are all promised the mercy of God. This promise serves as a source of hope and motivation for believers to strive for righteousness and to persevere in the face of adversity. At the same time, the verse reminds us of God's forgiving and merciful nature, emphasizing that His mercy is available to all those who seek it, regardless of their past mistakes or shortcomings.
orig: إن الذين آمنوا والذين هاجروا وجاهدوا في سبيل الله أولئك يرجون رحمت الله والله غفور رحيم

translation: They ask you about wine and gambling, say: 'In them is a great sin, and some benefits for people, but their sin is greater than their benefit.' And they ask you what they should spend, say: 'The excess.' In this way, God makes clear to you the verses, so that you may reflect.
interpretation: The verse addresses the question of whether it is permissible to consume alcohol and gamble. The verse advises that while there may be some benefits to these activities, the sin associated with them outweighs these benefits. The verse also answers the question about how much one should spend, advising that it should be within one's means. The verse emphasizes the importance of reflection and understanding of God's signs, and encourages believers to think deeply about the consequences of their actions.
orig: يسألونك عن الخمر والميسر قل فيهما إثم كبير ومنافع للناس وإثمهما أكبر من نفعهما ويسألونك ماذا ينفقون قل العفو كذلك يبين الله لكم الآيات لعلكم تتفكرون

translation: And they ask you concerning orphans. Say: 'The best thing to do is to improve their situation. And if you adopt them, then they are your brothers. And Allah knows the mischief-makers from the reformers. And if Allah had willed, He would certainly have given you more than that. Indeed, Allah is All-Mighty, All-Wise.'
interpretation: The verse addresses a question about orphans and advises to take care of them and improve their situation. If adoption is considered, then the adopted orphans should be treated like brothers. The verse emphasizes that God knows who are the mischief-makers and who are the reformers. The verse highlights that if God willed, He could have given more than that, indicating that taking care of orphans is a great deed, but God is capable of giving even more. The verse conveys the message that taking care of orphans is a responsibility and an act of kindness, and those who do so will be rewarded by God.
orig: في الدنيا والآخرة ويسألونك عن اليتامى قل إصلاح لهم خير وإن تخالطوهم فإخوانكم والله يعلم المفسد من المصلح ولو شاء الله لأعنتكم إن الله عزيز حكيم

translation: And do not marry polytheistic women until they believe. And indeed, a slave woman who believes is better than a polytheist, even if she pleases you. And do not marry polytheistic men until they believe. And indeed, a slave man who believes is better than a polytheist, even if he pleases you. Those invite to the Fire, and Allah invites to Paradise and forgiveness, by His permission. And He makes clear His verses to the people that perhaps they may remember.
interpretation: The verse prohibits Muslims from marrying polytheists and emphasizes the importance of marrying individuals who share the same faith and beliefs. The verse highlights the superiority of a believer, whether a slave or a free person, over a polytheist, regardless of how appealing or attractive the latter may seem. The verse also serves as a reminder that those who invite others to polytheism and disbelief are ultimately leading people towards the Fire, while Allah guides towards Paradise and forgiveness. The verse encourages people to reflect on the signs and messages of Allah, in the hope that they may remember and heed the warnings.
orig: ولا تنكحوا المشركات حتى يؤمن ولأمة مؤمنة خير من مشركة ولو أعجبتكم ولا تنكحوا المشركين حتى يؤمنوا ولعبد مؤمن خير من مشرك ولو أعجبكم أولئك يدعون إلى النار والله يدعو إلى الجنة والمغفرة بإذنه ويبين آياته للناس لعلهم يتذكرون

translation: And they ask you concerning menstruation. Say: It is an Adha (a harmful thing for a husband to have a sexual intercourse with his wife while she is having her menses), therefore, keep away from women during menses and do not approach them until they are pure. And when they have purified themselves, then come to them from where Allah has ordained for you (i.e. from the rear side of the woman or from where the missionary position is allowed). Verily, Allah loves those who turn unto Him in repentance and loves those who purify themselves.
interpretation: The verse provides guidance on the matter of menstruation and sexual relations. It explains that menstruation is impure and that it is harmful for a husband to have sexual intercourse with his wife during this time. The verse advises men to avoid contact with their wives during menstruation and to wait until they have purified themselves before resuming sexual relations. The verse emphasizes the importance of purity and repentance, stating that Allah loves those who turn to Him in repentance and those who purify themselves. This verse serves as a reminder of the importance of maintaining physical and spiritual purity in all aspects of life, including intimate relationships.
orig: ويسألونك عن المحيض قل هو أذى فاعتزلوا النساء في المحيض ولا تقربوهن حتى يطهرن فإذا تطهرن فأتوهن من حيث أمركم الله إن الله يحب التوابين ويحب المتطهرين

translation: Your wives are a field for you, so go to your field as you wish and send (something) good for yourselves and be aware of Allah and know that you will meet Him and give good tidings to the believers.
interpretation: The verse uses the metaphor of a field to describe women and encourages men to approach them in a respectful and ethical manner. The verse emphasizes the importance of treating one's spouse with kindness and consideration, and the need to seek personal fulfillment in a way that is consistent with Islamic values and principles. The verse also reminds believers of the inevitability of death and the importance of living a righteous life in preparation for the afterlife. The verse serves as a reminder to strive for self-improvement and to be mindful of one's actions and their consequences.
orig: نساؤكم حرث لكم فأتوا حرثكم أنى شئتم وقدموا لأنفسكم واتقوا الله واعلموا أنكم ملاقوه وبشر المؤمنين

translation: And do not make [Allah] a means ofattaining your oaths by swearing by Him while you hide something within yourselves, for then He would make you aware of it. Indeed, Allah is, of all things, Knowing.
interpretation: The verse warns against using God's name in vain or making false oaths by Him while hiding something within oneself. The verse emphasizes that God is all-knowing and will make one aware of their deceit. The verse serves as a reminder to be truthful and sincere in one's actions and words, and to avoid using God's name for personal gain or manipulation.
orig: ولا تجعلوا الله عرضة لأيمانكم أن تبروا وتتقوا وتصلحوا بين الناس والله سميع عليم

translation: Allah will not punish you for oaths which you utter unintentionally, but He will punish you for the oaths which you swear in earnest. The expiation for breaking an oath is to feed ten poor persons, on a scale of the average of that with which you feed your own families, or to clothe them, or to set free a slave; and if any one cannot find this, then he should fast for three days. This is the expiation for breaking oaths when you have sworn; but keep your oaths. Thus Allah makes clear to you His signs, so that you may be grateful.
interpretation: The verse explains the rules regarding oaths in Islam and the consequences of breaking them. It emphasizes that God does not hold people accountable for unintentional oaths, but rather for those that are made deliberately. The verse goes on to describe the expiation for breaking an oath, which is to feed or clothe ten poor people, set free a slave, or fast for three days. This serves as a reminder to Muslims to take their oaths seriously and to avoid breaking them. It also highlights the importance of gratitude towards God, and the significance of His signs in guiding people towards righteousness.
orig: لا يؤاخذكم الله باللغو في أيمانكم ولكن يؤاخذكم بما كسبت قلوبكم والله غفور حليم

translation: For those who swear off their wives, a waiting period of four months, but if they return, then indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: The verse outlines the waiting period for a man who wants to divorce his wife. If a man swears off his wife, he must wait for four months before the divorce is final. This waiting period allows both parties to reflect on their decision and possibly reconcile. If they reconcile during this time, then God is Forgiving and Merciful, indicating that God will forgive them for the difficulties they caused each other during this time of separation. The verse emphasizes the importance of giving both parties time to reflect and reconcile before making a final decision on the divorce.
orig: للذين يؤلون من نسائهم تربص أربعة أشهر فإن فاءوا فإن الله غفور رحيم

translation: And when they decide on a divorce, then indeed Allah is Hearing and Knowing.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the decision of divorce made by a couple. The verse emphasizes that even though the couple has made the decision to separate, Allah is aware and all-hearing of their actions. The verse serves as a reminder that even in personal and private matters, God is always present and knows what is happening. It is a call for people to be mindful of their actions and decisions, as they will be held accountable for them in the sight of God.
orig: وإن عزموا الطلاق فإن الله سميع عليم

translation: And those who are pregnant among your wives, wait in patience for three months; and if they give birth to a child, then keep your duty to Allah and give (the child) a reasonable (free) gift. And if there is any dispute between them concerning it, then the dispute shall be referred to the court of law; and they (the court) shall judge between you with fair judgment. And whoever does not obey Allah and His Messenger, then surely Allah is severe in punishment.
interpretation: This verse outlines the responsibilities of both parents in the case of a pregnancy. Pregnant wives are instructed to wait patiently for three months before taking any action. If the child is a boy, the father is required to provide a reasonable gift to the mother. If there is a dispute regarding the gift, it should be taken to court and resolved through fair judgment. The verse emphasizes the importance of obedience to Allah and His messenger, and warns of severe punishment for those who do not comply. The verse also highlights the importance of fairness and justice, and the role of the court of law in resolving disputes.
orig: والمطلقات يتربصن بأنفسهن ثلاثة قروء ولا يحل لهن أن يكتمن ما خلق الله في أرحامهن إن كن يؤمن بالله واليوم الآخر وبعولتهن أحق بردهن في ذلك إن أرادوا إصلاحا ولهن مثل الذي عليهن بالمعروف وللرجال عليهن درجة والله عزيز حكيم

translation: Divorce is twice, then keep [them] in an acceptable manner or release them with kindness, and it is not lawful for you to take anything of what you have given them unless both fear that they will not be able to maintain the limits of Allah. But if you fear that they will not be able to maintain the limits of Allah, then there is no blame upon them for what she gives in settlement. These are the limits of Allah, so do not transgress them. And whoever transgresses the limits of Allah - it is those who are the wrongdoers.
interpretation: The verse outlines the rules for divorce in Islam. It states that a man can divorce his wife twice, after which he must either keep her in a good and fair manner or release her with kindness. He is not allowed to take back any of the dowry or gifts he has given her, except if both parties fear that they will not be able to abide by the limits set by God. In this case, the wife can give back a settlement, but it is not obligatory. The verse emphasizes the importance of adhering to the limits set by God and warns against transgressing them, as those who do so are considered wrongdoers.
orig: الطلاق مرتان فإمساك بمعروف أو تسريح بإحسان ولا يحل لكم أن تأخذوا مما آتيتموهن شيئا إلا أن يخافا ألا يقيما حدود الله فإن خفتم ألا يقيما حدود الله فلا جناح عليهما فيما افتدت به تلك حدود الله فلا تعتدوها ومن يتعد حدود الله فأولئك هم الظالمون

translation: And if he has divorced her [irrevocably], then she is not lawful to him afterward until she marries a husband other than him. And if he divorces her [i.e., the second husband], then it is no sin upon them both if they reunite, provided they think that they can observe the limits set by Allah. These are the limits set by Allah, which He makes clear to a people who know.
interpretation: The verse outlines the rules of divorce and remarriage in Islam. If a man divorces his wife irrevocably, she becomes unlawful for him to remarry until she marries another man. If her second husband divorces her, then the first husband can remarry her, provided that both parties believe they can abide by the limits set by Allah. These limits refer to the rules and regulations governing marriage and divorce in Islam. The verse emphasizes the importance of adhering to these limits and makes clear that they have been revealed by Allah to guide the actions of those who have knowledge and understanding of them.
orig: فإن طلقها فلا تحل له من بعد حتى تنكح زوجا غيره فإن طلقها فلا جناح عليهما أن يتراجعا إن ظنا أن يقيما حدود الله وتلك حدود الله يبينها لقوم يعلمون

translation: And when you have divorced women and they have fulfilled their term, then retain them in kindness or release them in kindness. And do not retain them by force, to transgress [against them]. And whoever does that has certainly wronged himself. And do not take the signs of Allah in jest. And remember the favor of Allah upon you and His covenant with which He bound you when you said, 'We hear and we obey'; and fear Allah. Indeed, Allah is Knowing of that within the breasts.
interpretation: This verse outlines the rules for divorce in Islam, emphasizing the importance of treating one's former spouse with kindness and respect. The verse forbids men from retaining their former wives by force or transgressing against them, and it warns against taking the signs of Allah (i.e., the verses of the Qur'an) in jest. The verse also reminds believers of the favor of Allah upon them and the covenant they made with Him, urging them to fear Allah and be mindful of His knowledge. The verse promotes fairness, compassion, and mindfulness in the context of divorce, and it encourages believers to uphold their covenant with Allah and strive to live in accordance with His will.
orig: وإذا طلقتم النساء فبلغن أجلهن فأمسكوهن بمعروف أو سرحوهن بمعروف ولا تمسكوهن ضرارا لتعتدوا ومن يفعل ذلك فقد ظلم نفسه ولا تتخذوا آيات الله هزوا واذكروا نعمت الله عليكم وما أنزل عليكم من الكتاب والحكمة يعظكم به واتقوا الله واعلموا أن الله بكل شيء عليم

translation: And when you have divorced women and they have fulfilled their term, then hold not to them in (to) harm so that they may marry other of whom they will if they are pleased with you (by) a fair agreement. This (is) admonished with it (in) whom of you believes in God and the Last Day. That (is) purer for you and cleaner. And God knows and you know not.
interpretation: The verse provides guidance on the treatment of women after a divorce. Once the waiting period (‘ajal) has been completed, men are instructed not to harm their former wives and to allow them to marry other men if they wish. This is presented as a fair and just solution for all parties involved. The verse emphasizes the importance of believing in God and the Day of Judgment in guiding one’s actions and decisions. By following these teachings, individuals can purify themselves and gain a better understanding of God’s will. The verse serves as a reminder that while humans may not always understand the reasoning behind certain events, God is all-knowing and wise in His judgments.
orig: وإذا طلقتم النساء فبلغن أجلهن فلا تعضلوهن أن ينكحن أزواجهن إذا تراضوا بينهم بالمعروف ذلك يوعظ به من كان منكم يؤمن بالله واليوم الآخر ذلكم أزكى لكم وأطهر والله يعلم وأنتم لا تعلمون

translation: And the mothers may nurse their children for two whole years, for those who wish to complete the nursing. And upon the father is the provision and the clothing of the mother according to the accepted norms. No soul is burdened beyond its capacity. No mother should be harmed through her child, nor should the child be harmed by his mother. And upon the heir is the like of that. And if they both desire weaning through mutual consent and consultation, then there is no blame upon them. And if you wish for your children to be nursed by foster mothers, then there is no blame upon you as long as you pay what is due in a fair manner. And fear Allah and know that Allah sees what you do.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the rights and responsibilities of mothers and fathers in relation to the care and provision for their children, particularly during the period of breastfeeding. The verse emphasizes the importance of mutual consent and consultation between the parents in matters related to the care of their children. The verse also highlights the principle of justice and fairness in the payment of wages for foster mothers. The verse encourages parents to fulfill their responsibilities towards their children and to be mindful of the limits set by Allah. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of taking care of the young and vulnerable in society, and the consequences of neglecting these responsibilities.
orig: والوالدات يرضعن أولادهن حولين كاملين لمن أراد أن يتم الرضاعة وعلى المولود له رزقهن وكسوتهن بالمعروف لا تكلف نفس إلا وسعها لا تضار والدة بولدها ولا مولود له بولده وعلى الوارث مثل ذلك فإن أرادا فصالا عن تراض منهما وتشاور فلا جناح عليهما وإن أردتم أن تسترضعوا أولادكم فلا جناح عليكم إذا سلمتم ما آتيتم بالمعروف واتقوا الله واعلموا أن الله بما تعملون بصير

translation: And for those of you who die and leave behind wives, they (the wives) should wait by themselves for four months and ten days. Then when their waiting period is fulfilled, there is no blame on you for what they do for themselves in a decent way. And Allah is aware of what you do.
interpretation: The verse outlines the waiting period for widows before they can remarry. It emphasizes the importance of respecting the widow's autonomy and decision-making during this time. The verse also highlights the accountability of individuals before God for their actions. It reminds the community of their responsibility towards the widows, while also respecting their privacy and personal choices during their time of mourning.
orig: والذين يتوفون منكم ويذرون أزواجا يتربصن بأنفسهن أربعة أشهر وعشرا فإذا بلغن أجلهن فلا جناح عليكم فيما فعلن في أنفسهن بالمعروف والله بما تعملون خبير

translation: And there is no blame upon you concerning that which you propose, outwardly, of the speech (i.e., the proposal of marriage) to women, or conceal within yourselves. Allah knows that you will remember them (i.e., the women) and Allah knows that which is in yourselves. And notifying them of your intention is better, so that you do not commit sin unknowingly. And do not make the binding covenant of marriage until the written-out period of waiting has passed. And know that Allah knows what is within yourselves, so beware of Him and know that Allah is Forgiving and Forbearing.
interpretation: The verse provides guidance on the etiquette of proposing marriage to women. It emphasizes that there is no blame on the person who proposes, either in openly expressing their intention or in keeping it private. However, notifying the woman of the intention is encouraged, so as to avoid any unintentional sin. The verse also advises against making a binding covenant of marriage until the waiting period has passed, indicating the importance of taking the time to reflect and consider the decision. The verse reminds the reader that Allah is aware of their inner thoughts and intentions, and encourages them to be mindful of their actions and seek forgiveness from Allah, who is Forgiving and Forbearing.
orig: ولا جناح عليكم فيما عرضتم به من خطبة النساء أو أكننتم في أنفسكم علم الله أنكم ستذكرونهن ولكن لا تواعدوهن سرا إلا أن تقولوا قولا معروفا ولا تعزموا عقدة النكاح حتى يبلغ الكتاب أجله واعلموا أن الله يعلم ما في أنفسكم فاحذروه واعلموا أن الله غفور حليم

translation: There is no blame upon you if you divorce women before you have touched them or appointed for them a dowry; and provide for them (i.e., the women) the settlement (in accordance with what is) reasonable - the doer of good has a better reward with Allah.
interpretation: This verse provides guidance on the rules of divorce in Islam. It states that if a man divorces a woman before consummating the marriage or setting a dowry, he is not blameworthy. However, he is still responsible for providing a fair settlement for the woman. The verse emphasizes the importance of treating women fairly and justly, even in the event of divorce. The verse also suggests that those who act with kindness and generosity towards their spouses will be rewarded by Allah.
orig: لا جناح عليكم إن طلقتم النساء ما لم تمسوهن أو تفرضوا لهن فريضة ومتعوهن على الموسع قدره وعلى المقتر قدره متاعا بالمعروف حقا على المحسنين

translation: And if you have intimacy with them before they reach their term, then indeed, for them is half of what was decreed for him, unless they both forgo it. And if they both forgo it, then that is nearest to righteousness. And do not forget the favor of Allah upon you and that Allah, of what you do, is Seeing.
interpretation: This verse addresses the issue of intimacy with divorced women before the end of their waiting period. If such intimacy occurs, then the woman is entitled to half of the mahr (dowry) that was agreed upon, unless both parties choose to forgo it. If both parties choose to forgo it, then it is considered more righteous. The verse reminds the people not to forget the favor of Allah upon them and that Allah sees all that they do.
orig: وإن طلقتموهن من قبل أن تمسوهن وقد فرضتم لهن فريضة فنصف ما فرضتم إلا أن يعفون أو يعفو الذي بيده عقدة النكاح وأن تعفوا أقرب للتقوى ولا تنسوا الفضل بينكم إن الله بما تعملون بصير

translation: Establish prayer at the two ends of the day and in the first hours of the night. Surely, good deeds drive away bad deeds. That is a reminder for the mindful.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of establishing prayer at specific times during the day, including the two ends of the day (dawn and late afternoon) and the first hours of the night. The verse also highlights the benefits of performing good deeds, which can help to drive away bad deeds. The verse serves as a reminder for the mindful, encouraging them to establish a consistent prayer routine and to engage in good deeds as a way of staying on the right path.
orig: حافظوا على الصلوات والصلاة الوسطى وقوموا لله قانتين

translation: But if you fear, [O Muhammad], they will not obey you, then, if you become confident in their obedience, [O believers], offer prayer; indeed, remembrance of Allah is greater; and Allah knows that which you do.
interpretation: The verse addresses the Prophet Muhammad and the believers, giving them guidance on how to handle a situation where they fear that the disbelievers will not obey them. The verse advises them to offer prayer and remember Allah, as His remembrance is greater than their fear. The verse emphasizes the importance of remembering and worshiping Allah, regardless of the circumstances and challenges faced. It also highlights that Allah is aware of their actions and deeds, reinforcing the idea that He is all-knowing and all-seeing.
orig: فإن خفتم فرجالا أو ركبانا فإذا أمنتم فاذكروا الله كما علمكم ما لم تكونوا تعلمون

translation: And those of you who die and leave behind wives should bequeath unto their wives a year's maintenance without causing them to depart from their homes. But if they leave of their own accord, then there is no blame on you for what they do with themselves within the allowed period. And Allah is Exalted in Power, Wise.
interpretation: This verse outlines the responsibilities of a husband towards his wife after his death. If a man dies and leaves behind a wife, he is required to bequeath a year's maintenance for her. However, the wife has the option to leave the home if she so chooses, and the husband's family will not be held responsible for her actions during this time. The verse emphasizes the importance of providing for one's family and treating them with kindness and respect, even after death. It also highlights the power and wisdom of Allah, who has established these guidelines for the betterment of society.
orig: والذين يتوفون منكم ويذرون أزواجا وصية لأزواجهم متاعا إلى الحول غير إخراج فإن خرجن فلا جناح عليكم في ما فعلن في أنفسهن من معروف والله عزيز حكيم

translation: And unmarried women shall wait by themselves, as is seemly, without displaying their beauty, except that which is apparent thereof, and let them draw their veils over their bosoms, and not display their beauty save to their husbands, or their fathers, or their husbands' fathers, or their sons, or their husbands' sons, or their brothers, or their brothers' sons, or their sisters' sons, or their women, or those whom their right hands possess, or male servants free of physical needs, or small children who have no sense of the shame of sex; and let them not strike their feet so as to make known what they hide of their adornments. And turn unto Allah together, O believers, in order that you may succeed.
interpretation: The verse outlines the rules of modesty and behavior for unmarried women, instructing them to wait in seclusion and to cover themselves, except for what is necessary. The verse emphasizes the importance of modesty and discretion, and lists the exceptions to the rule, such as family members and servants. The verse serves as a reminder for believers to adhere to the teachings of Islam and to conduct themselves in a modest and respectful manner. The ultimate goal is to succeed and find favor with Allah.
orig: وللمطلقات متاع بالمعروف حقا على المتقين

translation: Thus does Allah make clear to you His signs that you may understand.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the role of divine guidance in helping people understand the signs of God. By making His signs clear, God enables people to reflect, understand and ultimately make the right choices. The verse can be seen as a call for reflection and contemplation of God's signs in the world, and a reminder that understanding comes from God's guidance.
orig: كذلك يبين الله لكم آياته لعلكم تعقلون

translation: Have you not seen those who went forth from their homes, though they were thousands, for fear of death? Then Allah said unto them: Die; then He gave them life. Lo! Allah is a Lord of Kindness to mankind, but most of mankind give not thanks.
interpretation: The verse describes the experience of a group of people who fled from their homes in fear of death, only to be commanded by God to die. However, God then gave them life again, emphasizing His power and mercy. The verse highlights the unpredictability of life and death, and the ultimate control that God has over both. The verse also serves as a reminder of the importance of gratitude and thankfulness towards God, as most people do not give thanks for the blessings they receive.
orig: ألم تر إلى الذين خرجوا من ديارهم وهم ألوف حذر الموت فقال لهم الله موتوا ثم أحياهم إن الله لذو فضل على الناس ولكن أكثر الناس لا يشكرون

translation: And fight in the way of God and know that God is Hearing, Knowing.
interpretation: The verse is a command for Muslims to fight in the way of God and a reminder of God's omniscience and omnipresence. The verse encourages Muslims to engage in jihad, or struggle, in the path of God, which can be interpreted as both armed struggle against oppression and the inner struggle to be a good Muslim. The verse emphasizes the importance of knowing that God is all-hearing and all-knowing, which serves as a reminder that Muslims are always accountable for their actions and that God is aware of their intentions and efforts. The verse encourages Muslims to strive for righteousness and justice, knowing that God is with them and aware of their struggles.
orig: وقاتلوا في سبيل الله واعلموا أن الله سميع عليم

translation: Who is it that will lend Allah a goodly loan so that He may multiply it for him many times over? And it is Allah who withholds and gives abundance, and to Him you will be returned.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the concept of making a 'loan' to God, which is understood as doing good deeds and helping others. In return, God will reward the person with a great increase in good. The verse emphasizes God's power over wealth and resources, and His ability to give or withhold as He sees fit. The verse also reminds the reader that all things will ultimately be returned to God, implying that one should be mindful of their actions and strive to do good in order to receive a great reward in the afterlife.
orig: من ذا الذي يقرض الله قرضا حسنا فيضاعفه له أضعافا كثيرة والله يقبض ويبسط وإليه ترجعون

translation: Have you not seen those who were unjust among the Children of Israel after the time of Moses, when they said to their prophet, 'Send us a king, that we may fight in the way of Allah'? He said, 'Would you not then fight if fighting was prescribed for you?' They said, 'Why should we not fight in the way of Allah when we have been driven out from our homes and our children?' But when fighting was prescribed for them, they turned away, except for a few of them. And Allah is aware of the wrongdoers.
interpretation: The verse describes the unjust behavior of some members of the Children of Israel who, after the time of Moses, asked their prophet to appoint a king to lead them in fighting for the cause of God. When the prophet asked them if they would fight if it was prescribed for them, they initially agreed, citing their displacement from their homes and the persecution of their children. However, when fighting was indeed prescribed for them, most of them backed out, except for a few. The verse highlights the hypocrisy and insincerity of those who claimed to be willing to fight for God's cause but ultimately refused to do so when the time came. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of sincerity and steadfastness in one's faith and actions, and the consequences of hypocrisy and insincerity.
orig: ألم تر إلى الملإ من بني إسرائيل من بعد موسى إذ قالوا لنبي لهم ابعث لنا ملكا نقاتل في سبيل الله قال هل عسيتم إن كتب عليكم القتال ألا تقاتلوا قالوا وما لنا ألا نقاتل في سبيل الله وقد أخرجنا من ديارنا وأبنائنا فلما كتب عليهم القتال تولوا إلا قليلا منهم والله عليم بالظالمين

translation: And their prophet said to them: 'God has appointed Talut (Saul) as your king.' They said: 'How can he have kingship over us, when we are more deserving of it than him, and he has not been given enough wealth?' He said: 'God has chosen him over you, and has increased him in knowledge and stature. And God grants kingship to whom He wills, and God is all-embracing, all-knowing.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the appointment of Talut (Saul) as king by God, and the people's reaction to it. The verse emphasizes that God chooses and appoints leaders, regardless of their wealth or social status, and the people should accept and respect the decision of God. The verse highlights the importance of knowledge and wisdom, which Talut was granted by God, and the people were lacking. The verse also implies that the people's focus on wealth and lineage as qualifications for leadership is misguided, and that God looks at the inner qualities of a person. The verse serves as a reminder that God is all-knowing and all-embracing, and that He has the power to grant kingship to whomever He wills.
orig: وقال لهم نبيهم إن الله قد بعث لكم طالوت ملكا قالوا أنى يكون له الملك علينا ونحن أحق بالملك منه ولم يؤت سعة من المال قال إن الله اصطفاه عليكم وزاده بسطة في العلم والجسم والله يؤتي ملكه من يشاء والله واسع عليم

translation: And their prophet said to them: 'Indeed, the sign of his kingdom is that the chest will come to you, in it is tranquility from your Lord and a relic of what was left by Moses and Aaron. The angels will carry it. Indeed, in that is a sign for you, if you are believers.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about a sign from God that will confirm the legitimacy of a prophet's claim to leadership. The sign is the arrival of a chest, which contains tranquility from God and a relic of what was left by Moses and Aaron. The chest will be carried by angels. The verse emphasizes that this is a clear sign for the people, if they are believers. The verse may be referring to a specific historical event, but it can also be seen as a metaphor for the guidance and reassurance that God provides to those who believe in Him and follow His prophets.
orig: وقال لهم نبيهم إن آية ملكه أن يأتيكم التابوت فيه سكينة من ربكم وبقية مما ترك آل موسى وآل هارون تحمله الملائكة إن في ذلك لآية لكم إن كنتم مؤمنين

translation: When Talut set out with the armies, he said, 'Indeed, Allah will test you with a river. So whoever drinks from it is not of me, and whoever does not taste it is indeed of me, except one who takes [a handful] with his hand.' But they drank from it, except a few of them. Then when he and those who believed with him crossed it, they said, 'There is no power for us today against Jalut and his soldiers.' But those who were certain that they would meet Allah said, 'How many a small company has overcome a large company by permission of Allah.' And Allah is with the patient.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the story of Prophet Talut (Saul) and his army, and their encounter with the river. Those who drank from the river were considered disobedient, except for those who took a handful with their hands. This test separated the obedient from the disobedient. Despite passing this test, the army still feared Jalut and his soldiers, but the believers among them remained steadfast and certain that they would meet Allah. The verse teaches the importance of obedience and trust in God, even in the face of fear and adversity. It emphasizes that victory comes from God and that the believers must remain patient and steadfast.
orig: فلما فصل طالوت بالجنود قال إن الله مبتليكم بنهر فمن شرب منه فليس مني ومن لم يطعمه فإنه مني إلا من اغترف غرفة بيده فشربوا منه إلا قليلا منهم فلما جاوزه هو والذين آمنوا معه قالوا لا طاقة لنا اليوم بجالوت وجنوده قال الذين يظنون أنهم ملاقو الله كم من فئة قليلة غلبت فئة كثيرة بإذن الله والله مع الصابرين

translation: And when they advanced towards Jalut and his forces, they said: 'Our Lord, pour down patience on us, and make our feet firm, and help us against the disbelieving people.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the prayer of the believers when they were facing the army of Jalut (Goliath). They asked for patience, firmness of their feet, and help from their Lord against the disbelievers. The verse emphasizes the reliance of the believers on their Lord in times of hardship and danger. It also shows the strength of their faith and their trust in God's help and support. The verse serves as a reminder that in times of trials and tribulations, believers should seek help from their Lord and have patience and steadfastness. It also highlights the importance of standing up against disbelief and wrongdoing.
orig: ولما برزوا لجالوت وجنوده قالوا ربنا أفرغ علينا صبرا وثبت أقدامنا وانصرنا على القوم الكافرين

translation: And We defeated them by permission of Allah and David killed Goliath, and Allah gave him the kingdom and wisdom and taught him of that which He willed. And if Allah had not repelled some people by others, the earth would have been corrupted, but Allah is full of bounty to the worlds.
interpretation: The verse describes a victory achieved through divine intervention, where the unbelievers were defeated by the will of Allah and David (a prophet in Islamic tradition) killed Goliath. The victory is attributed to Allah's permission, highlighting the belief in divine power and sovereignty. The victory leads to David's ascent to the throne and the granting of wisdom, indicating the connection between righteous leadership and divine favor. The verse also emphasizes the importance of balance in the world, as without Allah's intervention, the earth would have been corrupted. The verse serves as a reminder of the role of divine intervention in human affairs and the importance of maintaining balance and order in the world.
orig: فهزموهم بإذن الله وقتل داوود جالوت وآتاه الله الملك والحكمة وعلمه مما يشاء ولولا دفع الله الناس بعضهم ببعض لفسدت الأرض ولكن الله ذو فضل على العالمين

translation: Those are the verses of Allah that We recite to you in truth. And indeed, you are one of the messengers.
interpretation: The verse confirms that the verses being recited are indeed the words of Allah and that they are being recited truthfully. Additionally, the verse reveals the identity of the recipient of the revelation, stating that the Prophet Muhammad is one of the messengers of Allah. This serves as a reminder of the divine origin of the Quran and the role of the Prophet Muhammad in delivering Allah's message to humanity.
orig: تلك آيات الله نتلوها عليك بالحق وإنك لمن المرسلين

translation: Those are the messengers, some of whom We have favored over others. To some of them God spoke directly, and some of them He raised in rank. And We gave Jesus, son of Mary, clear signs and supported him with the Holy Spirit. If God had willed, those who followed after them would not have fought among each other, but God does as He wills.,
interpretation: The verse highlights the special status of some of the messengers of God, some of whom were favored over others. It mentions that God spoke directly to some of them and raised others in rank. Jesus, son of Mary, is singled out for mention as having been given clear signs and being supported by the Holy Spirit. The verse suggests that if God had willed, the people who came after the messengers would not have fought and disagreed amongst each other. However, the verse emphasizes that God has the power to do as He wills.
orig: تلك الرسل فضلنا بعضهم على بعض منهم من كلم الله ورفع بعضهم درجات وآتينا عيسى ابن مريم البينات وأيدناه بروح القدس ولو شاء الله ما اقتتل الذين من بعدهم من بعد ما جاءتهم البينات ولكن اختلفوا فمنهم من آمن ومنهم من كفر ولو شاء الله ما اقتتلوا ولكن الله يفعل ما يريد

translation: O you who have believed, spend from that which We have provided for you before there comes a Day in which there will be no trade, nor friendship, nor intercession, and the disbelievers - they are the wrongdoers.
interpretation: The verse addresses the believers and commands them to spend from the provisions that God has given them before the arrival of a Day when there will be no commerce, no close relationships, and no intercession. This Day refers to the Day of Judgment, when people will be held accountable for their actions. The verse warns that on this Day, the disbelievers will be the wrongdoers, emphasizing the consequences of disbelief and the importance of faith and good deeds.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا أنفقوا مما رزقناكم من قبل أن يأتي يوم لا بيع فيه ولا خلة ولا شفاعة والكافرون هم الظالمون

translation: Allah, there is no god but He, the Living, the Self-Subsisting. Slumber seizes Him not, nor sleep. To Him belongs what is in the heavens and what is in the earth. Who is he that can intercede with Him but by His permission? He knows what is before them and what is behind them, while they encompass nothing of His knowledge but what He will. His throne includes the heavens and the earth, and the preserving of them oppresses Him not; and He is the Exalted, the Great.
interpretation: This verse is a declaration of the oneness of God, emphasizing His unique and eternal nature. The verse highlights several attributes of God, including His self-sufficiency, His knowledge of all things, and His power over all things. The verse emphasizes that God is free from all limitations, such as sleep and slumber, and that He has complete control over all of creation. The verse also emphasizes that God is the only one who can be interceded with, and that His knowledge is complete and encompasses all things, both past and present. The verse serves as a reminder of God's greatness and His ultimate power and authority over all of creation.
orig: الله لا إله إلا هو الحي القيوم لا تأخذه سنة ولا نوم له ما في السماوات وما في الأرض من ذا الذي يشفع عنده إلا بإذنه يعلم ما بين أيديهم وما خلفهم ولا يحيطون بشيء من علمه إلا بما شاء وسع كرسيه السماوات والأرض ولا يئوده حفظهما وهو العلي العظيم

translation: Let there be no compulsion in religion. Truth has become clear from error. So whoever disbelieves in the false gods and believes in God has certainly grasped the most trustworthy handhold that will never break. And God is Hearing, Knowing.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of freedom of religion and the clarity of truth from falsehood. It states that there should be no compulsion in religion, and that the truth has become clear from error. Those who reject false gods and believe in God have grasped the most trustworthy handhold that will never break. This handhold represents the guidance and protection of God, which is unbreakable and secure. The verse also highlights God's attributes of being Hearing and Knowing, indicating that He is aware of the actions and intentions of His servants, and that He is always listening to their prayers and supplications.
orig: لا إكراه في الدين قد تبين الرشد من الغي فمن يكفر بالطاغوت ويؤمن بالله فقد استمسك بالعروة الوثقى لا انفصام لها والله سميع عليم

translation: Allah is the ally of those who believe. He brings them out from darkness into the light. And those who disbelieve - their allies are the Taghut. They bring them out from the light into darkness. Those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide eternally therein.
interpretation: The verse contrasts the fate of believers and disbelievers. Believers are under the protection of Allah, who guides them from darkness to light. On the other hand, disbelievers are associated with the Taghut (false deities), who lead them from light to darkness. This contrast highlights the guidance and protection provided to believers, while emphasizing the misguidance and destruction faced by disbelievers. The verse serves as a reminder that choosing the right path leads to guidance and salvation, while straying from it leads to misguidance and eternal damnation.
orig: الله ولي الذين آمنوا يخرجهم من الظلمات إلى النور والذين كفروا أولياؤهم الطاغوت يخرجونهم من النور إلى الظلمات أولئك أصحاب النار هم فيها خالدون

translation: Have you not considered the one who disputed with Abraham about his Lord [saying], 'It has led me astray.' So Abraham said, 'My Lord is the one who gives life and causes death.' [The disbeliever] said, 'I take refuge in a powerful protector.' [Abraham] said, 'Indeed, Allah is the one who takes you to the morning and the one who brings you to the evening.' [The disbeliever] was arrogant, so Allah sent astray the one who was unjust. Indeed, Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people.
interpretation: The verse recounts a conversation between the Prophet Abraham and an unbeliever who claimed that his idol led him astray. Abraham rejected the idol as a false god and affirmed that Allah is the one who gives life and causes death. The unbeliever took refuge in a powerful protector, but Abraham pointed out that Allah controls the daily cycle of the sun, rising and setting. Despite this evidence, the unbeliever remained arrogant and unyielding, and so Allah allowed him to remain astray. The verse serves as a reminder that Allah is the only true God, and that those who reject Him and cling to false idols will not be guided.
