orig: ألم تر إلى الذي حاج إبراهيم في ربه أن آتاه الله الملك إذ قال إبراهيم ربي الذي يحيي ويميت قال أنا أحيي وأميت قال إبراهيم فإن الله يأتي بالشمس من المشرق فأت بها من المغرب فبهت الذي كفر والله لا يهدي القوم الظالمين

translation: Or like one who passed by a township, (while) it was in a state of ruin, he said, 'How will Allah bring this to life after its death?' So Allah caused him to die for a hundred years; then He revived him. He said, 'How long have you remained (dead)?' The (man) said, 'I have remained a day or part of a day.' He said, 'Rather, you have remained one hundred years. Look at your food and your drink; it has not changed with time. And look at your donkey; and thus We make you a sign for the people. And look at the bones - how We raise them and then We cover them with flesh.' And when it became clear to him, he said, 'I know that Allah is over all things competent.'
interpretation: The verse describes the story of a man who passed by a ruined town and questioned how it could be brought back to life by God. As a response, God caused the man to die for a hundred years and then resurrected him. The verse emphasizes the power and ability of God to bring the dead back to life and to do anything He wills. The man was surprised to find that his food, drink, and donkey had not changed, despite the long period of time that had passed. The verse also highlights the ability of God to reconstruct and rebuild the bones and cover them with flesh. The man, upon realizing the power and ability of God, acknowledged and submitted to His greatness and competence over all things.
orig: أو كالذي مر على قرية وهي خاوية على عروشها قال أنى يحيي هذه الله بعد موتها فأماته الله مائة عام ثم بعثه قال كم لبثت قال لبثت يوما أو بعض يوم قال بل لبثت مائة عام فانظر إلى طعامك وشرابك لم يتسنه وانظر إلى حمارك ولنجعلك آية للناس وانظر إلى العظام كيف ننشزها ثم نكسوها لحما فلما تبين له قال أعلم أن الله على كل شيء قدير

translation: And [mention, O Muhammad], when Abraham said, 'My Lord, show me how You give life to the dead.' [Allah] said, 'Have you not believed?' [Abraham] said, 'Yes, but [I ask] only that my heart may be satisfied.' [Allah] said, 'Take four birds and commit them to yourself. Then [after slaughtering them] put on each hill a portion of them; then call them - they will come [flying] to you in haste. And know that indeed Allah is Exalted in Might and Wise.'
interpretation: The verse relates a conversation between God and the prophet Abraham, in which Abraham asks to be shown how God gives life to the dead. In response, God asks Abraham if he does not already believe, to which Abraham replies that he does believe but seeks further assurance. God then instructs Abraham to take four birds, cut them into pieces, and place a portion of each bird on different hills. Abraham is then told to call the birds, and they will come to him, demonstrating God's power to bring the dead back to life. The verse emphasizes the greatness and wisdom of God, who has the power to give life and take it away. The story also serves to strengthen Abraham's faith and serves as a reminder of God's omnipotence for the believers.
orig: وإذ قال إبراهيم رب أرني كيف تحيي الموتى قال أولم تؤمن قال بلى ولكن ليطمئن قلبي قال فخذ أربعة من الطير فصرهن إليك ثم اجعل على كل جبل منهن جزءا ثم ادعهن يأتينك سعيا واعلم أن الله عزيز حكيم

translation: Like those who spend their wealth in the way of Allah is like a seed [which grows] seven spikes, in every spike is a hundred grains, and Allah multiplies for whom He wills, and Allah is All-Encompassing, Knowing.
interpretation: The verse uses the metaphor of a seed growing into multiple stalks of grain to illustrate the rewards of spending wealth in the way of Allah. The verse suggests that the rewards for such actions are multiplied, and that Allah grants abundance to whomever He wills. The verse emphasizes the boundless generosity of Allah and His knowledge of all things, and serves as an encouragement for Muslims to give charitably and support the cause of Allah.
orig: مثل الذين ينفقون أموالهم في سبيل الله كمثل حبة أنبتت سبع سنابل في كل سنبلة مائة حبة والله يضاعف لمن يشاء والله واسع عليم

translation: Those who spend their wealth in the way of Allah and then do not follow up what they have spent with reminders [i.e. insult or injury] will have their reward with their Lord, and there will be no fear for them, nor will they grieve.
interpretation: The verse highlights the reward for those who spend their wealth for the sake of Allah, without expecting any compensation or recognition in return. These individuals do not engage in any negative behavior or reminders, such as insults or injuries, towards those they have helped. The verse emphasizes the generosity and selflessness of these individuals, and the great reward they will receive from their Lord. The verse also highlights the peace of mind and absence of fear or grief that these individuals will experience, as they are content with their actions and confident in the reward from their Lord.
orig: الذين ينفقون أموالهم في سبيل الله ثم لا يتبعون ما أنفقوا منا ولا أذى لهم أجرهم عند ربهم ولا خوف عليهم ولا هم يحزنون

translation: A good word is better than a charitable deed followed by injury. Indeed, Allah is Self-Sufficient and Forgiving.
interpretation: The verse highlights the importance of choosing one's words wisely and the negative consequences of following a good deed with harm. The verse suggests that a good word, or a kind statement, is of greater value than a charitable act that is followed by harm or injury. The verse emphasizes the power of words and the importance of using them in a positive and uplifting manner. The verse concludes by reminding the reader of Allah's attributes of Self-Sufficiency and Forgiveness, indicating that while Allah does not need our good deeds, He is always ready to forgive our mistakes and transgressions.
orig: قول معروف ومغفرة خير من صدقة يتبعها أذى والله غني حليم

translation: O you who have believed, do not invalidate your charities with reminders or injury, like one who spends his wealth [only] to be seen by the people and does not believe in Allah and the Last Day. His example is like that of a smooth stone upon which is dust; then a torrent strikes it and it becomes level, and [the torrent] carries away something of that with which it was adorned. And Allah does not guide the disbelieving people.
interpretation: The verse warns against invalidating charitable acts through reminders or harm, comparing it to someone who spends only to be seen by people and does not truly believe in God or the Day of Judgment. This person's example is likened to a smooth stone with dust that is struck by a torrent and becomes level, carrying away what it was adorned with. The verse emphasizes the importance of sincerity in acts of charity, and the negative consequences of insincerity and hypocrisy. It serves as a reminder that God does not guide those who reject faith and engage in insincere deeds.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تبطلوا صدقاتكم بالمن والأذى كالذي ينفق ماله رئاء الناس ولا يؤمن بالله واليوم الآخر فمثله كمثل صفوان عليه تراب فأصابه وابل فتركه صلدا لا يقدرون على شيء مما كسبوا والله لا يهدي القوم الكافرين

translation: And the example of those who spend their wealth seeking God's pleasure and to strengthen their souls is like a garden on a hill, which is hit by a rainstorm, then it brings forth its fruits in double. And even if it is not hit by a rainstorm, then dew is enough for it. And God is all-seeing of what you do.
interpretation: The verse uses the metaphor of a garden on a hill to illustrate the rewards of those who spend their wealth for the sake of God and to strengthen their souls. The garden, like the righteous individuals, benefits from the rainstorm, which represents the blessings and rewards from God. The garden produces fruits in double, indicating the abundance of rewards for the righteous. The verse also emphasizes that even if the garden does not receive the rainstorm, it still receives the dew, which is sufficient for it. This implies that the righteous will still receive rewards, even if they do not receive worldly blessings. The verse concludes by affirming that God is all-seeing of the actions of people, emphasizing the importance of sincerity and pure intentions in acts of worship.
orig: ومثل الذين ينفقون أموالهم ابتغاء مرضات الله وتثبيتا من أنفسهم كمثل جنة بربوة أصابها وابل فآتت أكلها ضعفين فإن لم يصبها وابل فطل والله بما تعملون بصير

translation: Shall I inform you of what is better for you in the way of reward and a better end? [It is] gardens from beneath which rivers flow, wherein you have fruits of every kind and protection from your Lord and forgiveness. [Is that] better or the garden of the disbelievers like a rainwater-driven [storm] garden which is enclosed, so when the heat strikes it, it becomes barren, and its wealth is destroyed. [It is] such that it will be a painful torment. So, [O Muhammad], the disbelievers advise one another to hasten toward disbelief, and when they witness the punishment, they say, 'Is there any way to return [to the world]?'
interpretation: The verse contrasts the blessings and rewards of paradise with the punishment of the disbelievers. The first part of the verse describes the blessings of paradise, such as gardens with flowing rivers, fruits of all kinds, protection from the Lord, and forgiveness. The second part of the verse describes the punishment of the disbelievers as a barren and destroyed garden. The verse emphasizes the contrast between the two outcomes and serves as a warning to those who do not believe and commit sins. The verse encourages the believers to seek the blessings of paradise and avoid the punishment of the disbelievers.
orig: أيود أحدكم أن تكون له جنة من نخيل وأعناب تجري من تحتها الأنهار له فيها من كل الثمرات وأصابه الكبر وله ذرية ضعفاء فأصابها إعصار فيه نار فاحترقت كذلك يبين الله لكم الآيات لعلكم تتفكرون

translation: O you who have believed, spend from the good things which you have earned and from that which We have brought forth for you from the earth, and do not aim toward the bad [of it] to spend from it, while you would not take it except while you are unaware of it. And know that Allah is Free of need and Praiseworthy.
interpretation: This verse addresses the believers and encourages them to spend from their wealth that which is good and earned through lawful means. It also reminds them to avoid spending from unlawful sources. The verse emphasizes the importance of being mindful of one's actions and avoiding ignorance. The verse concludes by reminding the believers that Allah is self-sufficient and praiseworthy, and does not need their wealth. The verse encourages the believers to be generous, mindful of their actions and to remember that all their wealth ultimately belongs to Allah.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا أنفقوا من طيبات ما كسبتم ومما أخرجنا لكم من الأرض ولا تيمموا الخبيث منه تنفقون ولستم بآخذيه إلا أن تغمضوا فيه واعلموا أن الله غني حميد

translation: Shaitan (Satan) promises you poverty and commands you to commit Fahsha (evil deeds, i.e. to fornicate, to steal, to rob, to tell lies, to disobey, etc.), but Allah promises you Forgiveness from Himself and Bounty, and Allah is All-Sufficient for His creatures' needs, All-Knower.
interpretation: The verse contrasts the promises of Satan with the promises of God. Satan tempts people by promising them wealth and encouraging them to commit sins, while God promises forgiveness and bounty. The verse emphasizes that God is all-sufficient for the needs of His creatures and all-knowing. The verse serves as a reminder that people should not be deceived by the temporary pleasures and material gains promised by Satan, and instead seek the forgiveness and blessings of God.
orig: الشيطان يعدكم الفقر ويأمركم بالفحشاء والله يعدكم مغفرة منه وفضلا والله واسع عليم

translation: He grants wisdom to whom He wills, and whoever is granted wisdom has been given much good. And none remember except those of understanding.
interpretation: The verse highlights the importance of wisdom and emphasizes that it is a gift from God that He bestows upon whom He wills. The verse suggests that those who are granted wisdom are truly fortunate and have received a great gift. Furthermore, the verse indicates that only those who possess understanding can truly appreciate and remember this wisdom. The verse serves as a reminder that wisdom is a precious gift that should be cherished and used wisely.
orig: يؤتي الحكمة من يشاء ومن يؤت الحكمة فقد أوتي خيرا كثيرا وما يذكر إلا أولو الألباب

translation: And neither your expenditure nor your vow is concealed from Allah. And indeed, for the unjust there is no helper.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the all-knowing nature of Allah, stating that He is aware of all expenditures and vows made by individuals. The verse also highlights the consequences of injustice, stating that there is no helper for the unjust. This verse serves as a reminder that all actions and intentions are known to Allah, and that those who commit unjust acts will not have any support or aid in the end.
orig: وما أنفقتم من نفقة أو نذرتم من نذر فإن الله يعلمه وما للظالمين من أنصار

translation: If you disclose your charitable gifts, it is well, but if you hide them and give them to the poor, it will be better for you, and He will remove from you some of your evil deeds. And Allah, of what you do, is All-Aware.
interpretation: The verse highlights the merits of charitable giving and encourages believers to give in secrecy. Disclosing one's charitable deeds may earn praise and recognition from others, but giving in secret, without seeking recognition, is considered superior. The verse promises that such hidden acts of kindness will result in the removal of some of one's sins. The verse emphasizes that God is aware of all that we do, and that our actions have consequences. The verse encourages believers to strive for inner goodness and to seek God's pleasure above all else.
orig: إن تبدوا الصدقات فنعما هي وإن تخفوها وتؤتوها الفقراء فهو خير لكم ويكفر عنكم من سيئاتكم والله بما تعملون خبير

translation: You are not responsible for their guidance, but Allah guides whom He wills. And whatever good you spend, it is for yourselves, and you do not spend except seeking the countenance of Allah. And whatever good you spend, it will be returned to you, and you will not be wronged.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes that ultimate guidance comes from Allah, and individuals cannot force others to follow the right path. The verse encourages spending in charity for the sake of seeking Allah's pleasure and not for recognition or personal gain. The verse further states that any good deed will not be wasted and will be rewarded by Allah. The verse encourages generosity and reminds believers that their good deeds will not go unnoticed or unrewarded, and they will not be wronged in the process.
orig: ليس عليك هداهم ولكن الله يهدي من يشاء وما تنفقوا من خير فلأنفسكم وما تنفقون إلا ابتغاء وجه الله وما تنفقوا من خير يوف إليكم وأنتم لا تظلمون

translation: For the poor among the Muhajireen who were expelled from their homes and their properties, seeking bounty from Allah and [His] approval and supporting Allah and His Messenger, those are the truthful. And [for] those who were established in the land and [subsequently] were driven out from it, only because they said, 'Our Lord is Allah,' and there was not upon them from sin - the recompense of the wrongdoers among them is nothing except that they be destroyed. And for the poor among the Muhajireen who were expelled from their homes and their properties, who seek bounty from Allah and [His] approval and support Allah and His Messenger, those are the truthful. They will be given their reward twice over, because they are patient, and they repel evil with good and spend [in the way of Allah] from what We have provided them.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the poor Muhajireen (refugees) who were expelled from their homes and properties for seeking bounty from Allah and His approval and supporting Allah and His Messenger. The verse distinguishes between the Muhajireen and the wrongdoers among them, emphasizing that the recompense of the wrongdoers is destruction. The verse highlights the patience and good deeds of the Muhajireen, who repel evil with good and spend in the way of Allah. The verse promises the Muhajireen a reward twice over for their patience and good deeds. The verse serves as a reminder of the consequences of wrongdoing and the rewards of patience, perseverance, and good deeds.
orig: للفقراء الذين أحصروا في سبيل الله لا يستطيعون ضربا في الأرض يحسبهم الجاهل أغنياء من التعفف تعرفهم بسيماهم لا يسألون الناس إلحافا وما تنفقوا من خير فإن الله به عليم

translation: Those who spend their wealth in the way of Allah by night and day, secretly and publicly, shall have their reward with their Lord, and there shall be no fear for them, nor shall they grieve.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the reward of those who spend their wealth in the way of God, both in private and in public. The verse emphasizes the generosity and selflessness of these individuals, who give to others regardless of the time of day and without seeking recognition. The verse suggests that these individuals will be rewarded by God, and they will not have to fear or grieve. The verse serves as an encouragement for Muslims to be generous and to give to others, and it emphasizes the spiritual rewards of such actions.
orig: الذين ينفقون أموالهم بالليل والنهار سرا وعلانية فلهم أجرهم عند ربهم ولا خوف عليهم ولا هم يحزنون

translation: Those who eat interest will not stand (on the Day of Resurrection) except as one stands who is beaten by Satan's touch. That is because they say, 'Trade is like interest.' But Allah has permitted trade and has forbidden interest. So whoever has received an admonition from his Lord and desists may have what is past, and his affair rests with Allah. And whoever returns to (dealing in interest or usury) - those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide eternally therein.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the severe consequences of dealing with interest or usury. Those who engage in such practices are compared to a person who is beaten by Satan, emphasizing the negative impact of such actions on the individual's spiritual well-being. The verse highlights the distinction between trade and interest, making it clear that while trade is permissible, interest is forbidden. However, the verse also offers a way out for those who have fallen into this sin, as long as they repent and desist from their actions. Those who persist in this sin are warned of the grave consequences, as they will be companions of the Fire and will abide therein eternally. The verse serves as a warning to those who engage in interest or usury, urging them to repent and turn away from these practices before it is too late.
orig: الذين يأكلون الربا لا يقومون إلا كما يقوم الذي يتخبطه الشيطان من المس ذلك بأنهم قالوا إنما البيع مثل الربا وأحل الله البيع وحرم الربا فمن جاءه موعظة من ربه فانتهى فله ما سلف وأمره إلى الله ومن عاد فأولئك أصحاب النار هم فيها خالدون

translation: Allah destroys interest and grows alms, and Allah does not love any ungrateful sinner.
interpretation: The verse highlights the contrasting outcomes of engaging in unjust practices, such as usury (represented by 'interest'), and righteous deeds, such as charity (represented by 'alms'). The verse states that Allah will destroy the former and grow the latter, emphasizing the negative consequences of engaging in unjust practices. Furthermore, the verse states that Allah does not love those who are ungrateful (represented by 'ungrateful sinner') and reinforces the importance of gratitude and piety in Islamic teachings.
orig: يمحق الله الربا ويربي الصدقات والله لا يحب كل كفار أثيم

translation: Indeed, those who have believed and done righteous deeds and established prayer and given zakah, for them is a reward with their Lord, and there will be no fear concerning them, nor will they grieve.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the reward for those who believe in God, do good deeds, establish prayer and give zakah (charity). These individuals have secured a reward from their Lord and they will not have to fear or grieve. The verse emphasizes the importance of faith, good deeds and the establishment of prayer and zakah as the means to salvation. It serves as an encouragement for believers to strive for righteousness and to fulfill their religious duties, as they will be rewarded for their efforts in the hereafter.
orig: إن الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات وأقاموا الصلاة وآتوا الزكاة لهم أجرهم عند ربهم ولا خوف عليهم ولا هم يحزنون

translation: O you who have believed, fear Allah and give up what remains [due to you] of interest, if you should be believers.
interpretation: The verse is a command from God to the believers to fear Him and to give up any remaining interest or usury that they may be holding. The verse emphasizes the importance of avoiding interest as a fundamental aspect of faith, and it serves as a reminder to the believers to purify themselves from any unethical financial practices. It also implies that a true believer cannot have a balance of usury or interest, and that the act of giving up such earnings is a necessary step in the path towards complete faith and submission to God.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا اتقوا الله وذروا ما بقي من الربا إن كنتم مؤمنين

translation: But if you do not (heed, i.e. obey), then be informed of a war from Allah and His Messenger. And if you repent, then your capital (i.e. property, wealth, etc.) will be yours, and you shall not do injustice nor be done injustice.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the consequences of disobedience towards God and His messenger. If the people do not heed the warnings and continue to disobey, they will face a war from God and His messenger. However, if they repent, then their wealth and property will be returned to them and they will not be treated unjustly. The verse emphasizes the importance of obedience and repentance, and the consequences of disobedience and injustice. It also highlights the mercy of God, who gives the people a chance to repent and make amends before it is too late.
orig: فإن لم تفعلوا فأذنوا بحرب من الله ورسوله وإن تبتم فلكم رءوس أموالكم لا تظلمون ولا تظلمون

translation: And if one is in hardship, let him consider ease [as something to be aspired for], and let him be mindful of [the reality that] being honest and truthful is better for him if he knows.
interpretation: This verse speaks about how one should respond to hardship or difficulty. It advises that in such situations, one should strive for ease and consider the benefits of being honest and truthful. The verse suggests that these qualities are not only morally good but also beneficial for the individual. This interpretation highlights the importance of maintaining a positive attitude and being truthful even in difficult circumstances. It encourages individuals to look for solutions and to strive for honesty and integrity in their actions.
orig: وإن كان ذو عسرة فنظرة إلى ميسرة وأن تصدقوا خير لكم إن كنتم تعلمون

translation: And fear a Day when you will be returned to Allah, then every soul will be compensated for what it earned, and they will not be wronged.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the Day of Judgment when all souls will return to Allah and be held accountable for their actions. The verse emphasizes that every soul will receive its just deserts, and no one will be wronged. This means that those who have done good will receive their reward, and those who have done evil will receive their punishment. The verse serves as a reminder to people to fear this Day and to do good deeds so that they may be successful on the Day of Judgment.
orig: واتقوا يوما ترجعون فيه إلى الله ثم توفى كل نفس ما كسبت وهم لا يظلمون

translation: O you who have believed, when you contract a debt for a specified term, write it down. And let a scribe write [it] between you in justice. Let no scribe refuse to write as Allah has taught him. So let him write and let the one who incurs the obligation dictate. And let him fear Allah, his Lord, and not leave anything out of it. But if the one who incurs the obligation is of limited understanding or weak or unable to dictate himself, then let his guardian dictate in justice. And call to witness two witnesses from among your men. And if there are not two men [available], then a man and two women from those whom you accept as witnesses - so that if one of them [i.e., the women] errs, then the other can remind her. And let not the witnesses refuse when they are called upon. And do not be [too] weary to write it, whether it is small or large, for its [i.e., the contract's] term. That is more just in the sight of Allah and more reliable as evidence and more likely that you will not be in need of it. And if it is a transaction between you [hand-to-hand], then there is no blame upon you if you do not write it. But have witnesses when you trade. And let no scribe or witness be harmed. And if you do [it], then indeed, it is grave oppression. And fear Allah. And Allah teaches you, and Allah is Knowing of all things.
interpretation: The verse outlines the rules of financial transactions and contracts in Islam. It stresses the importance of fairness and justice, and the need for clear documentation of financial agreements. The verse requires that any debt or financial agreement must be recorded in writing, in the presence of a fair and just scribe, and that both parties should be given the opportunity to review and approve the document. The verse also stipulates that witnesses should be present during the transaction. If one of the witnesses is a woman, there should be another woman present as a backup, in case the first woman makes an error in her testimony. The verse emphasizes the importance of honesty and transparency in financial dealings, and warns against fraud and deception. It also highlights the significance of upholding contracts and fulfilling financial obligations. The verse serves as a guide for Muslims in their financial transactions, emphasizing the values of fairness, justice, and integrity.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا إذا تداينتم بدين إلى أجل مسمى فاكتبوه وليكتب بينكم كاتب بالعدل ولا يأب كاتب أن يكتب كما علمه الله فليكتب وليملل الذي عليه الحق وليتق الله ربه ولا يبخس منه شيئا فإن كان الذي عليه الحق سفيها أو ضعيفا أو لا يستطيع أن يمل هو فليملل وليه بالعدل واستشهدوا شهيدين من رجالكم فإن لم يكونا رجلين فرجل وامرأتان ممن ترضون من الشهداء أن تضل إحداهما فتذكر إحداهما الأخرى ولا يأب الشهداء إذا ما دعوا ولا تسأموا أن تكتبوه صغيرا أو كبيرا إلى أجله ذلكم أقسط عند الله وأقوم للشهادة وأدنى ألا ترتابوا إلا أن تكون تجارة حاضرة تديرونها بينكم فليس عليكم جناح ألا تكتبوها وأشهدوا إذا تبايعتم ولا يضار كاتب ولا شهيد وإن تفعلوا فإنه فسوق بكم واتقوا الله ويعلمكم الله والله بكل شيء عليم

translation: And if you are on a journey and cannot find a writer, then let (one) of you entrust (his affairs) to (another) and if you trust one another then let the one who is trusted deliver (his trust) and let him fear Allah, his Lord. And do not conceal testimony, and whoever conceals it - then indeed, his heart is sinful, and Allah is Knowing of what you do.
interpretation: The verse provides guidance for travelers who cannot find a writer to document their affairs. It advises them to trust one another and fulfill their responsibilities. Concealing testimony is forbidden and considered a sinful act. The verse emphasizes the importance of honesty and trustworthiness in all actions and transactions, and the need to be mindful of God's knowledge and accountability.
orig: وإن كنتم على سفر ولم تجدوا كاتبا فرهان مقبوضة فإن أمن بعضكم بعضا فليؤد الذي اؤتمن أمانته وليتق الله ربه ولا تكتموا الشهادة ومن يكتمها فإنه آثم قلبه والله بما تعملون عليم

translation: To God belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth, and whether you reveal what is in yourselves or conceal it, God will call you to account for it. Then He will forgive whom He wills and punish whom He wills, and God is over all things competent.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes God's omniscience and sovereignty over all things, reminding people that they will be held accountable for their actions, both those that are visible and those that are hidden. The verse also highlights God's mercy and justice, as He will forgive those whom He wills and punish those whom He wills. This serves as a reminder for people to be mindful of their actions and to seek God's forgiveness.
orig: لله ما في السماوات وما في الأرض وإن تبدوا ما في أنفسكم أو تخفوه يحاسبكم به الله فيغفر لمن يشاء ويعذب من يشاء والله على كل شيء قدير

translation: The Messenger has believed in what was revealed to him from his Lord, and [so have] the believers. All of them have believed in Allah and His angels and His books and His messengers, [saying], 'We make no distinction between any of His messengers.' And they say, 'We hear and we obey. [We seek] Your forgiveness, our Lord, and to You is the [final] destination.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of faith in Allah, His angels, His books, and His messengers. It highlights the unity of the believers, who do not distinguish between any of Allah's messengers. The verse also emphasizes the importance of obedience and seeking forgiveness from Allah. The verse serves as a reminder of the ultimate destination of all human beings, which is with Allah. The verse encourages believers to follow the example of the messenger and to have a strong and unwavering faith in Allah and His messengers.
orig: آمن الرسول بما أنزل إليه من ربه والمؤمنون كل آمن بالله وملائكته وكتبه ورسله لا نفرق بين أحد من رسله وقالوا سمعنا وأطعنا غفرانك ربنا وإليك المصير

translation: Allah does not burden a soul beyond that it can bear: for it is only that which it has earned, and against it is that which it has deserved. Our Lord! Condemn us not if we forget, or fall into error; our Lord! Lay not on us a burden as Thou didst lay on those before us; Our Lord! Impose not on us that which we have not the strength to bear; pardon us, grant us Thy forgiveness, and have mercy on us. Thou art our Protector, so give us victory over the unbelieving people.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the principle of justice and fairness in Islam. It emphasizes that Allah does not burden a soul beyond its capacity and that each person is responsible for their own actions. The verse also highlights the concept of forgiveness and mercy, and the importance of seeking Allah's protection and guidance. The verse is a reminder that Allah is just and fair, and that He will not hold people accountable for more than they can bear. It also encourages people to seek Allah's forgiveness and mercy, and to seek His help in dealing with the burden of their sins. The verse also serves as a call to believers to seek victory over the unbelievers, emphasizing the importance of standing up for one's beliefs and fighting against oppression and injustice.
orig: لا يكلف الله نفسا إلا وسعها لها ما كسبت وعليها ما اكتسبت ربنا لا تؤاخذنا إن نسينا أو أخطأنا ربنا ولا تحمل علينا إصرا كما حملته على الذين من قبلنا ربنا ولا تحملنا ما لا طاقة لنا به واعف عنا واغفر لنا وارحمنا أنت مولانا فانصرنا على القوم الكافرين

translation: The (revelation) of this Book (the Quran) is from Allah, the Almighty, the Wise.
interpretation: The verse asserts that the Quran is a revelation from Allah, the Almighty and Wise. This statement emphasizes the divine origin and authority of the Quran, and the importance of recognizing and submitting to its guidance. The attributes of Allah, Almighty and Wise, further highlight the power and wisdom behind the revelation, and underscore the importance of accepting and following its teachings.
orig: الم

translation: Allah, there is no god but He, the Living, the Sustainer.
interpretation: The verse is a declaration of the oneness of God, asserting that Allah is the only god worthy of worship. The attributes of 'the Living' and 'the Sustainer' highlight God's power and control over all things, emphasizing His ability to give and sustain life. The verse serves as a reminder of the greatness and uniqueness of God, and invites the reader to reflect on the power and mercy of the one true God.
orig: الله لا إله إلا هو الحي القيوم

translation: The Qur'an has been revealed to you with the truth, confirming what was revealed before it, and He revealed the Torah and the Gospel.
interpretation: The verse affirms that the Qur'an is a revealed scripture from God, brought down with truth and as a confirmation of the previous scriptures, namely the Torah and the Gospel. This verse emphasizes the continuity of the divine message and the harmony between the different revelations. It also serves as a validation of the earlier prophets and their messages, and highlights the unity of the divine message across different religious traditions.
orig: نزل عليك الكتاب بالحق مصدقا لما بين يديه وأنزل التوراة والإنجيل

translation: Before, guidance from Us came to the people, and We sent down the Distinguisher (Qur'an). Indeed, those who disbelieve in the verses of Allah have a severe punishment, and Allah is exalted in might, the Avenger.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the guidance that was given to the people in the past and the sending down of the Qur'an, which distinguishes truth from falsehood. The verse warns of severe punishment for those who disbelieve in the signs of God. The verse highlights the power and might of God, emphasizing that He will exact retribution.
orig: من قبل هدى للناس وأنزل الفرقان إن الذين كفروا بآيات الله لهم عذاب شديد والله عزيز ذو انتقام

translation: Indeed, Allah is not unaware of any atom's weight in the earth and in the sky.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the all-encompassing knowledge and awareness of God. It states that God is aware of every single atom's weight, both on earth and in the sky. This implies that nothing is hidden from God, and that He has complete knowledge of all that exists, both in the physical and spiritual realms. The verse serves as a reminder of God's greatness and omniscience, encouraging believers to be mindful of their actions and to seek His guidance and mercy.
orig: إن الله لا يخفى عليه شيء في الأرض ولا في السماء

translation: He it is Who shapes you in the wombs as He pleases. There is no deity but He, the Exalted in Might, the Wise.
interpretation: The verse affirms the power and control of God over all of creation, emphasizing His role in shaping and creating human beings in the wombs. The verse emphasizes the complete power and control of God over all things and the complete dependence of all things on Him. The verse also emphasizes the oneness of God, affirming that there is no deity but Him. The attributes of God as 'Exalted in Might' and 'Wise' serve to highlight His power and knowledge, emphasizing His ability to do as He pleases and His wisdom in all that He does.
orig: هو الذي يصوركم في الأرحام كيف يشاء لا إله إلا هو العزيز الحكيم

translation: He it is Who has sent down upon you the Book; in it are verses clear that are the Essence of the Book, and others ambiguous. As for those in whose hearts is swerving, they follow that of it which is ambiguous, seeking to mislead and seeking to interpret it; and none knows its interpretation except Allah and those firmly rooted in knowledge; they say, 'We believe in it; all is from our Lord;' and none do mind except men of understanding.
interpretation: The verse highlights the dual nature of the Quran, containing both clear and unambiguous verses as well as those that are open to interpretation. It warns against those who follow their own interpretations to mislead others and create mischief. It emphasizes that the true interpretation of the Quran is known only to Allah and those deeply rooted in knowledge. The verse encourages believers to have faith in the Quran and acknowledge that all knowledge comes from their Lord, and it distinguishes between those who truly understand from those who merely claim to.
orig: هو الذي أنزل عليك الكتاب منه آيات محكمات هن أم الكتاب وأخر متشابهات فأما الذين في قلوبهم زيغ فيتبعون ما تشابه منه ابتغاء الفتنة وابتغاء تأويله وما يعلم تأويله إلا الله والراسخون في العلم يقولون آمنا به كل من عند ربنا وما يذكر إلا أولو الألباب

translation: Our Lord, let not our hearts deviate after You have guided us and grant us mercy from Yourself. Indeed, You are the Bestower.
interpretation: The verse is a supplication to God, asking Him to keep the hearts of the believers firm on the path of guidance, and not allow them to deviate from it. The verse also highlights the importance of God's mercy and the fact that it is only from Him that it can be obtained. The verse emphasizes the greatness and generosity of God by referring to Him as the 'Bestower', indicating that He is the one who bestows His blessings and mercy upon His servants.
orig: ربنا لا تزغ قلوبنا بعد إذ هديتنا وهب لنا من لدنك رحمة إنك أنت الوهاب

translation: Our Lord, surely You will gather the people for a Day about which there is no doubt. Indeed, Allah will not break the appointment.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the Day of Judgment, which is certain to occur and is a matter of no doubt. The verse emphasizes that Allah will not break His promise or appointment for the Day of Judgment. The verse serves as a reminder of the inevitability of the Day of Judgment and the importance of being prepared for it. It also highlights the trustworthiness of Allah and His promises.
orig: ربنا إنك جامع الناس ليوم لا ريب فيه إن الله لا يخلف الميعاد

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve, their wealth and their children will not avail them against Allah at all, and those are the companions of the Fire.
interpretation: The verse highlights the ultimate powerlessness of wealth and children in protecting disbelievers from the punishment of Allah. Despite their earthly possessions and offspring, they will not be able to escape the consequences of their disbelief. The verse serves as a reminder that true security and protection come from Allah alone and that material wealth and family ties cannot provide a shield against divine retribution. The verse ends with a stark warning that those who reject faith will be companions of the Fire, emphasizing the grave consequences of disbelief.
orig: إن الذين كفروا لن تغني عنهم أموالهم ولا أولادهم من الله شيئا وأولئك هم وقود النار

translation: Thus did Pharaoh and those before him deny the signs of their Lord, so Allah seized them for their sins. And Allah is strong in retribution.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the denial of Pharaoh and those before him of the signs of their Lord, and as a result, they were punished by God for their sins. The verse emphasizes the power and strength of God's retribution and serves as a reminder of the consequences of denying God's signs and committing sins.
orig: كدأب آل فرعون والذين من قبلهم كذبوا بآياتنا فأخذهم الله بذنوبهم والله شديد العقاب

translation: Say to the disbelievers: 'You will be defeated and gathered together to Hell; what an evil resting place!'
interpretation: The verse is a message from the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to the disbelievers, warning them of their impending defeat and the consequences of their rejection of Islam. The phrase 'you will be defeated' suggests a decisive and irreversible loss, while 'gathered together to Hell' implies that they will be sent to eternal punishment and suffering. The phrase 'what an evil resting place' emphasizes the horror and dread of Hell, and serves as a reminder of the stark contrast between the fate of the believers and the disbelievers in the afterlife.
orig: قل للذين كفروا ستغلبون وتحشرون إلى جهنم وبئس المهاد

translation: There has already been for you an example in the two factions that met [in combat]: one was fighting in the cause of Allah, and the other of which were disbelievers. They met by chance, and We put them to trial by means of one another. And the disbelievers were defeated.
interpretation: The verse presents a lesson from a historical event where two groups met in combat, one fighting for the cause of God and the other consisting of disbelievers. The two groups encountered each other unexpectedly, and God put them to the test through each other. The disbelievers were defeated in this encounter. The verse highlights the importance of fighting for the cause of God and the consequences of disbelief. It serves as a reminder that God tests people through various means and that the outcome of these tests can have significant consequences. The verse encourages believers to reflect on the events of the past and to learn from them in order to make informed decisions in their own lives.
orig: قد كان لكم آية في فئتين التقتا فئة تقاتل في سبيل الله وأخرى كافرة يرونهم مثليهم رأي العين والله يؤيد بنصره من يشاء إن في ذلك لعبرة لأولي الأبصار

translation: Beautified for people is the love of that which they desire - of women and sons, heaped-up sums of gold and silver, fine branded horses, and cattle and tilled land. That is the enjoyment of worldly life, but Allah with Him is the best of provision.
interpretation: The verse describes the things that people commonly desire and find pleasure in, such as wealth, children, and material possessions. These things are described as 'beautified' or 'adorned' for people, indicating that they are attractive and appealing to them. However, the verse reminds us that these are only temporary pleasures of this worldly life. The true and everlasting provision comes from God. The verse serves as a reminder to prioritize the pursuit of God's pleasure and provision over worldly desires and possessions.
orig: زين للناس حب الشهوات من النساء والبنين والقناطير المقنطرة من الذهب والفضة والخيل المسومة والأنعام والحرث ذلك متاع الحياة الدنيا والله عنده حسن المآب

translation: Say, 'I will inform you of a better (reward) than that: for those who are pious, for those who fear their Lord and keep their duty to their Lord, (there will be) Gardens, beneath which rivers flow, to abide in them, and pure companions, and contentment from Allah. And Allah is Seeing (all) your deeds.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the reward for those who are pious and fear their Lord. It contrasts the transient nature of worldly pleasures with the eternal bliss of the hereafter. The verse describes the reward for the righteous as gardens beneath which rivers flow, a place where they will abide forever, accompanied by pure companions and contentment from Allah. The verse emphasizes that Allah is aware of all the deeds of His servants, and it serves as a motivation for the believers to strive for piety and righteousness in order to attain the ultimate reward in the hereafter.
orig: قل أؤنبئكم بخير من ذلكم للذين اتقوا عند ربهم جنات تجري من تحتها الأنهار خالدين فيها وأزواج مطهرة ورضوان من الله والله بصير بالعباد

translation: Those who say, 'Our Lord, we have believed, so forgive us our sins and protect us from the punishment of the Fire.'
interpretation: The verse speaks of the prayer and supplication of the believers, who seek forgiveness for their sins and protection from the punishment of the Fire. The verse emphasizes the faith of the believers, who acknowledge their sins and turn to God for mercy and forgiveness. The verse also highlights the importance of seeking protection from the punishment of the Fire, which is a reference to Hell. The verse serves as a reminder to the believers of the importance of seeking forgiveness and striving to lead righteous lives, as well as the reality of the consequences of their actions and the ultimate destination of the sinners.
orig: الذين يقولون ربنا إننا آمنا فاغفر لنا ذنوبنا وقنا عذاب النار

translation: The patient, and the true (in word and deed), and the observers of the Prayer, and the givers of poor-rate, and the performers of the pilgrimage and the performers of the irham (for Hajj and 'umrah), and those who pay the welfare tax - they are assuredly guided.
interpretation: The verse describes the qualities of righteous individuals who are guided on the right path. These qualities include patience, truthfulness, observing the prayer, giving charity, performing the pilgrimage and 'umrah, and paying the welfare tax. These actions reflect a strong commitment to one's faith and a dedication to helping others. By emphasizing these qualities, the verse serves as a reminder of the importance of leading a righteous life and the rewards that come with it.
orig: الصابرين والصادقين والقانتين والمنفقين والمستغفرين بالأسحار

translation: Surely, Allah bears witness that there is no god but He - and (so do) the angels and those possessed of knowledge, upholding justice; there is no god but He, the Almighty, the Wise.
interpretation: The verse affirms the oneness of God, asserting that there is no god but He. This declaration is supported by the testimony of the angels and those endowed with knowledge. The verse emphasizes the absolute justice of God, describing Him as the Almighty and the Wise. The verse serves to remind believers of the fundamental principle of monotheism and the importance of upholding justice and wisdom in all their actions.
orig: شهد الله أنه لا إله إلا هو والملائكة وأولو العلم قائما بالقسط لا إله إلا هو العزيز الحكيم

translation: Indeed, the religion with Allah is Islam. And those to whom the Scripture was given did not differ except after knowledge had come to them, out of jealousy between them. And whoever disbelieves in the verses of Allah, then indeed, Allah is swift in account.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes that the true religion in the sight of God is Islam. It also mentions that those who were given previous scriptures (such as the Jews and Christians) only differed and disagreed after knowledge (of Islam) had come to them. This disagreement and division was due to jealousy and rivalry among them. The verse also warns those who disbelieve in the signs or verses of God, stating that God is swift in reckoning and accounting for their deeds, and will hold them accountable for their actions.
orig: إن الدين عند الله الإسلام وما اختلف الذين أوتوا الكتاب إلا من بعد ما جاءهم العلم بغيا بينهم ومن يكفر بآيات الله فإن الله سريع الحساب

translation: But if they dispute with you, say, 'I have submitted myself to Allah, and so too have those who follow me.' And say to those who have been given the Book and the Unlettered, 'Have you too submitted yourselves?' So if they submit, then indeed they are rightly guided; but if they turn away, then it is only upon you to convey the message. And Allah is Seeing of the servants.
interpretation: The verse addresses the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, and instructs him on how to respond if people dispute with him about his message. The verse emphasizes the submission to Allah and the unity of those who follow the Prophet. It also invites the People of the Book (Jews and Christians) and the Unlettered (pagans) to submit themselves to Allah. The verse highlights the importance of conveying the message of Islam and leaving the outcome to Allah, who is aware of the actions of His servants.
orig: فإن حاجوك فقل أسلمت وجهي لله ومن اتبعن وقل للذين أوتوا الكتاب والأميين أأسلمتم فإن أسلموا فقد اهتدوا وإن تولوا فإنما عليك البلاغ والله بصير بالعباد

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve in the signs of Allah and kill the prophets without right and kill those who command justice from the people, give them good tidings of a painful punishment.
interpretation: The verse warns of a painful punishment for those who disbelieve in the signs of God, kill the prophets unjustly, and kill those who command justice among the people. The verse emphasizes the severity of their actions and the consequences that will follow. It serves as a reminder to those who reject the truth and commit injustices, that they will be held accountable for their actions and will face a severe punishment from God.
orig: إن الذين يكفرون بآيات الله ويقتلون النبيين بغير حق ويقتلون الذين يأمرون بالقسط من الناس فبشرهم بعذاب أليم

translation: Those are the ones whose deeds have become worthless in this world and the hereafter, and they will have no helpers.
interpretation: The verse describes the fate of those whose deeds have been rendered worthless, both in this life and in the hereafter. The verse emphasizes the finality of their situation and the lack of any support or help for them. This verse serves as a warning to those who engage in wrongdoing and sinful behavior, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the fact that they cannot rely on anyone to save them from the consequences of their actions. The verse also emphasizes the importance of leading a righteous life and doing good deeds, as these are the only things that will be of value in the hereafter.
orig: أولئك الذين حبطت أعمالهم في الدنيا والآخرة وما لهم من ناصرين

translation: Have you not seen those who were given a portion of the Scripture, who call out to the Book of Allah and then turn away after guidance has come to them, not holding it in true esteem?
interpretation: The verse addresses the believers and asks them if they have seen those who were given a portion of the Scripture (Jews and Christians) and yet call out to the Book of Allah (the Quran), seeking its guidance. However, after receiving guidance, they turn away from it and do not hold it in true esteem. This verse criticizes those who seek guidance from the Quran but do not follow it or give it the respect it deserves. It serves as a reminder to the believers to hold fast to the guidance of the Quran and not be like those who reject it after receiving it.
orig: ألم تر إلى الذين أوتوا نصيبا من الكتاب يدعون إلى كتاب الله ليحكم بينهم ثم يتولى فريق منهم وهم معرضون

translation: That is because they said, 'You will not touch us except for a few days.' And they were unmindful in their heedlessness of what they were inventing.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the disbelievers who denied the resurrection and the punishment of the hereafter, and they thought that they would not be punished in this world. They claimed that they would not be touched by the fire except for a few days. The verse emphasizes their heedlessness and ignorance as they were unmindful of the consequences of their false beliefs and inventions. The verse serves as a reminder that God's punishment will reach those who deny His signs and persist in their disbelief, and it is a warning against underestimating the consequences of one's words and actions.
orig: ذلك بأنهم قالوا لن تمسنا النار إلا أياما معدودات وغرهم في دينهم ما كانوا يفترون

translation: And how will it be when We gather them for a Day about which there is no doubt and every soul will be recompensed for what it earned, and they will not be wronged.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the Day of Judgment, which is certain and cannot be doubted. On this day, every person will receive the recompense for what they have earned, and they will not be wronged or treated unjustly. This verse emphasizes the fairness and justice of God's judgment, and serves as a reminder that every person is responsible for their own actions and will be held accountable for them. The verse encourages people to reflect on their lives and to prepare for the inevitable Day of Judgment by doing good deeds and avoiding sin.
orig: فكيف إذا جمعناهم ليوم لا ريب فيه ووفيت كل نفس ما كسبت وهم لا يظلمون

translation: Say: 'O Allah, Owner of Sovereignty, You give sovereignty to whom You will and You take sovereignty away from whom You will. You honor whom You will and You humble whom You will. In Your hand is all good. Indeed, You are over all things competent.'
interpretation: The verse is a supplication to Allah, the Owner of Sovereignty, acknowledging His power and control over all things. It recognizes that Allah has the power to give and take away sovereignty, to honor and humble whomever He wills. The verse also highlights the fact that all good is in Allah's hand and that He is competent over all things. This verse can serve as a reminder of Allah's power and greatness, and as a source of comfort and reliance for believers, who recognize that all things are ultimately in Allah's hands.
orig: قل اللهم مالك الملك تؤتي الملك من تشاء وتنزع الملك ممن تشاء وتعز من تشاء وتذل من تشاء بيدك الخير إنك على كل شيء قدير

translation: He brings the night as a cover over the day, and He brings the day as a cover over the night, and He has subjected the sun and the moon (to His Law), each running its course for a term appointed; and Allah is aware of all that you do.
interpretation: The verse describes the natural phenomena of the day turning into night and vice versa, and the order and predictability of the sun and the moon in their orbits. This is seen as a sign of God's power and control over the universe. The verse also emphasizes God's knowledge of all human actions, implying that every action is accounted for and will be judged.
orig: تولج الليل في النهار وتولج النهار في الليل وتخرج الحي من الميت وتخرج الميت من الحي وترزق من تشاء بغير حساب

translation: Let not the believers take the disbelievers as allies instead of the believers. And whoever does that, then he has no relation with Allah, except that you fear from them. And Allah warns you of Himself, and to Allah is the [final] destination.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of believers maintaining a strong bond with each other and not forming alliances with disbelievers. The verse warns that anyone who does this will have no relation with Allah, except out of necessity. The verse serves as a reminder to believers to be cautious of disbelievers and to remain steadfast in their faith. The verse also highlights the ultimate authority of Allah and that all matters return to Him.
orig: لا يتخذ المؤمنون الكافرين أولياء من دون المؤمنين ومن يفعل ذلك فليس من الله في شيء إلا أن تتقوا منهم تقاة ويحذركم الله نفسه وإلى الله المصير

translation: Say, 'If you conceal what is in your hearts or reveal it, Allah knows it. And He knows what is in the heavens and what is in the earth. And Allah is over all things competent.'
interpretation: The verse is a statement from the Prophet Muhammad, addressing the hypocrites who hide their disbelief and pretend to be believers. It emphasizes that Allah is all-knowing and aware of the secrets and intentions of people, whether they are hidden or revealed. The verse reminds the hypocrites that they cannot deceive Allah and encourages them to be truthful and sincere in their faith. It also serves as a reminder for all believers that Allah is all-powerful and capable of handling all matters, emphasizing the importance of trust and reliance on Him.
orig: قل إن تخفوا ما في صدوركم أو تبدوه يعلمه الله ويعلم ما في السماوات وما في الأرض والله على كل شيء قدير

translation: On the Day when every soul will find present what it has done of good and what it has done of evil, (it will wish) that between it and its evil there were a great distance.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the Day of Judgment when every person will be held accountable for their actions, both good and bad. The verse emphasizes the reality of this Day and the fact that every person will be recompensed for their deeds. The verse also highlights the regret that people will feel when they see the consequences of their sins and wish that there was a great distance between them and their evil actions. The verse serves as a reminder to people to do good and avoid evil, as they will have to face the consequences of their actions on the Day of Judgment.
orig: يوم تجد كل نفس ما عملت من خير محضرا وما عملت من سوء تود لو أن بينها وبينه أمدا بعيدا ويحذركم الله نفسه والله رءوف بالعباد

translation: Say, [O Muhammad], 'If you should love Allah, then follow me, [so] Allah will love you and forgive you your sins.' And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: The verse is a message from Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to the people, inviting them to follow him and the path of Islam. The verse promises that if the people truly love God, they should follow the Prophet, and as a result, God will love them and forgive their sins. The verse emphasizes the importance of following the teachings of Islam and the guidance of the Prophet as a means of earning God's love and forgiveness. The verse also highlights God's attribute of being Forgiving and Merciful, indicating that God is willing to forgive those who sincerely repent and turn to Him.
orig: قل إن كنتم تحبون الله فاتبعوني يحببكم الله ويغفر لكم ذنوبكم والله غفور رحيم

translation: Say, 'Obey Allah and the Messenger.' But if they turn away - then indeed, Allah does not love the disbelievers.
interpretation: The verse is a command from Allah to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to tell the people to obey Allah and the Prophet. If they refuse, then Allah does not love the disbelievers, meaning those who reject faith and refuse to obey Allah and His Messenger. This verse emphasizes the importance of obedience to Allah and His Messenger and the consequences of disbelief and disobedience. It serves as a reminder that Allah does not love those who reject His message and guidance.
orig: قل أطيعوا الله والرسول فإن تولوا فإن الله لا يحب الكافرين

translation: Indeed, Allah has preferred Adam and Noah and the family of Abraham and the family of 'Imran above the worlds.
interpretation: The verse highlights the special status of certain prophets and their families, who have been chosen by God above all other creation. This selection is not based on any merit on their part, but is a manifestation of God's grace and favor. The verse serves as a reminder of the unique position of these prophets and their families in the divine plan and emphasizes their importance in the religious and spiritual history of humanity.
orig: إن الله اصطفى آدم ونوحا وآل إبراهيم وآل عمران على العالمين

translation: Relations of some of them to others, and Allah is Hearing and Knowing.
interpretation: The verse describes the complex relationships that exist between people, emphasizing the intricate connections that exist between different individuals. The verse also highlights Allah's omniscience and omnipresence, reminding the reader that Allah is aware of all that happens and that nothing is hidden from Him. The verse may serve as a reminder to be mindful of one's actions and to strive for positive relationships with others, knowing that Allah is aware of all that we do and say.
orig: ذرية بعضها من بعض والله سميع عليم

translation: When the wife of 'Imran said, 'My Lord, I have vowed to You what is in my womb, dedicated (for Your service), so accept this from me. Indeed, You are the Hearing, the Knowing.'
interpretation: The verse is a statement of the wife of 'Imran, who has dedicated her unborn child to the service of God. She makes this vow to God, expressing her devotion and commitment to Him. She seeks God's acceptance of her vow, acknowledging His ability to hear and know all things. The verse highlights the importance of making and fulfilling vows to God, and the significance of dedicating one's life to His service.
orig: إذ قالت امرأت عمران رب إني نذرت لك ما في بطني محررا فتقبل مني إنك أنت السميع العليم

translation: So when she (Mary) bore him (Jesus), she said, 'My Lord, I have delivered a female.' And Allah was most knowing of what she delivered, and the male is not like the female. And I have named her Mary, and I seek refuge for her and her descendants in You from Satan, the expelled.'
interpretation: The verse describes Mary's reaction to the birth of Jesus, expressing her surprise and concern about delivering a female child. However, she accepts and submits to God's will, acknowledging His knowledge and power over all things. Mary also seeks refuge for herself and her descendants from Satan, highlighting her piety and devotion to God. The verse emphasizes the importance of trusting and relying on God, even in the face of unexpected circumstances and challenges.
orig: فلما وضعتها قالت رب إني وضعتها أنثى والله أعلم بما وضعت وليس الذكر كالأنثى وإني سميتها مريم وإني أعيذها بك وذريتها من الشيطان الرجيم

translation: So accept this from me. Indeed, Allah is Exalted in Might and Wise. And establish prayer for My remembrance. Indeed, the station of My Lord is exalted and supreme. Allah has given me of the kingship and taught me the book. And You, O My Lord, are the granter of good. So accept my supplication. Indeed, You are the Hearing, the Knowing.
interpretation: This verse is a prayer of Prophet Zakariyya (peace be upon him) to God, expressing his gratitude and humility. He acknowledges God's power and wisdom and commits to establishing prayer for God's remembrance. He also recognizes the greatness of God and his role in granting him kingship and knowledge. The verse emphasizes the importance of prayer and the recognition of God's power and wisdom. It also highlights the Prophet Zakariyya's devotion and humility towards God.
orig: فتقبلها ربها بقبول حسن وأنبتها نباتا حسنا وكفلها زكريا كلما دخل عليها زكريا المحراب وجد عندها رزقا قال يا مريم أنى لك هذا قالت هو من عند الله إن الله يرزق من يشاء بغير حساب

translation: Zechariah called upon his Lord, saying, 'My Lord, grant me from Yourself a good offspring. Indeed, You are always hearing the prayer.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the prayer of the prophet Zechariah to God for a righteous offspring. The verse emphasizes the faith of Zechariah in God's power and his belief that God is always listening to his prayers. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of prayer and the power of God's blessings in fulfilling the desires of His believers.
orig: هنالك دعا زكريا ربه قال رب هب لي من لدنك ذرية طيبة إنك سميع الدعاء

translation: The angels called him while he was standing in prayer in the sanctuary, 'Indeed, Allah gives you good tidings of Yahya, confirming a word from Allah and name of the righteous, and a prophet from among the righteous.'
interpretation: The verse announces the birth of John the Baptist (Yahya) to his father, Zechariah, while he was standing in prayer in the sanctuary. The angels conveyed the good news that John would be a righteous prophet, and that he would confirm the word of God, emphasizing his important role in the continuation of God's message. This verse highlights the significance of John's birth and his role as a prophet, and serves as a reminder of the importance of prayer and the presence of the divine in everyday life.
orig: فنادته الملائكة وهو قائم يصلي في المحراب أن الله يبشرك بيحيى مصدقا بكلمة من الله وسيدا وحصورا ونبيا من الصالحين

translation: He said, 'My Lord, how can I have a boy when age has overtaken me and my wife is barren?' He said, 'Even so, Allah does what He will.'
interpretation: The verse relays a conversation between an unnamed individual and God, where the individual expresses disbelief at the possibility of having a child in his old age and with a barren wife. God responds by asserting His power and authority, stating that He can do as He pleases. The verse emphasizes God's omnipotence and the limits of human understanding and control. It serves as a reminder of the power and wisdom of God, and the limitations of human knowledge and perception.
orig: قال رب أنى يكون لي غلام وقد بلغني الكبر وامرأتي عاقر قال كذلك الله يفعل ما يشاء

translation: He said, 'My Lord, give me a sign.' He said, 'Your sign is that you will not speak to the people for three days except by signs, and remember your Lord much and glorify Him night and day.'
interpretation: The verse describes a conversation between a prophet and God, where the prophet asks for a sign from God. God responds by giving him a sign, which is that he will not be able to speak to the people for three days, except by signs. The verse emphasizes the importance of remembering and glorifying God, both during the night and the day. The verse can be interpreted as a reminder of the power and authority of God, and the importance of relying on God's guidance and support, even in the face of challenges or difficulties. The verse may also be seen as a test of the prophet's patience and perseverance, as he is required to communicate through signs rather than speech for a period of time.
orig: قال رب اجعل لي آية قال آيتك ألا تكلم الناس ثلاثة أيام إلا رمزا واذكر ربك كثيرا وسبح بالعشي والإبكار

translation: And when the angels said: 'O Mary! Verily, Allah has chosen you, and made you pure, and has preferred you above the women of the worlds.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the special status of Mary, the mother of Jesus, as chosen and favored by God above all women. The verse emphasizes her purity and high standing, highlighting her unique position in the eyes of God. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of Mary in Islamic tradition, as a symbol of faith, devotion, and obedience to God's will.
orig: وإذ قالت الملائكة يا مريم إن الله اصطفاك وطهرك واصطفاك على نساء العالمين

translation: O Mary, be devoutly obedient to your Lord, prostrate yourself and bow with those who bow [in prayer].
interpretation: The verse addresses Mary, the mother of Jesus, and commands her to be devoutly obedient to her Lord, to prostrate herself in prayer, and to bow in worship with those who bow. This verse emphasizes the importance of submission and obedience to God, and the act of prayer and worship as a means of drawing closer to God. It also highlights the unity of the believers in their worship and devotion to God, and the importance of joining together in prayer and worship as a community of believers.
orig: يا مريم اقنتي لربك واسجدي واركعي مع الراكعين

translation: That is part of the news of the unseen which We reveal to you (O Muhammad). And you were not with them when they cast their pens to decide which of them should be responsible for Maryam, nor were you with them when they disputed.
interpretation: The verse highlights the unique role of the Prophet Muhammad as a recipient of divine revelation, emphasizing that he was not present when the people of the past made certain decisions or engaged in disputes. The verse refers specifically to the decision of who would be responsible for the care of Maryam (Mary) and a dispute that the people had, neither of which Muhammad was a part of. The verse serves as a reminder of the limitations of human knowledge and the special status of the Prophet as a conduit for divine guidance.
orig: ذلك من أنباء الغيب نوحيه إليك وما كنت لديهم إذ يلقون أقلامهم أيهم يكفل مريم وما كنت لديهم إذ يختصمون

translation: When the angels said: 'O Mary, indeed God gives you good news of a word from Him, his name is the Messiah, Jesus, the son of Mary, distinguished in this world and the hereafter, and one of those brought near.'
interpretation: The verse announces the good news of the birth of Jesus, the Messiah, to Mary. The verse emphasizes the special status of Jesus in both this world and the next, and describes him as one of those who are brought near to God. The announcement of Jesus' birth serves as a reminder of God's power and mercy, as well as a sign of his plan for humanity's salvation. The verse also highlights Mary's role as a vessel for the divine and her special status as the mother of Jesus.
orig: إذ قالت الملائكة يا مريم إن الله يبشرك بكلمة منه اسمه المسيح عيسى ابن مريم وجيها في الدنيا والآخرة ومن المقربين

translation: and speaks (the human being) to him in the cradle and in maturity and among the righteous.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the miraculous ability of humans to communicate and learn from a very young age. By speaking to the human in the cradle, the verse highlights the God-given potential for language and communication that is present from birth. By mentioning communication 'in maturity', the verse emphasizes the ongoing ability of humans to communicate and learn throughout their lives. The final phrase, 'among the righteous', suggests that communication and learning are particularly important for those who strive to live righteous lives and seek guidance from God.
orig: ويكلم الناس في المهد وكهلا ومن الصالحين

translation: She said, 'My Lord, how can I have a child, when no man has ever touched me?' He said, 'In the same way that God creates whatever He wills. When He decides on a thing, He says to it, "Be!" and it is.'
interpretation: The verse relays a conversation between an unnamed woman and God, where the woman expresses her disbelief at the possibility of having a child without having been touched by a man. God responds by explaining that He has the power to create whatever He wills, and that when He decrees something, it comes into existence. The verse emphasizes God's power and control over all things, and the limitations of human understanding and perception in the face of divine power.
orig: قالت رب أنى يكون لي ولد ولم يمسسني بشر قال كذلك الله يخلق ما يشاء إذا قضى أمرا فإنما يقول له كن فيكون

translation: And We verily gave Moses the Scripture and caused a communication with him, then We gave Jesus, son of Mary, clear arguments and strengthened him with the Holy Spirit.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the revelation of scripture to both Moses and Jesus. The verse emphasizes that both Moses and Jesus received divine guidance and support. The verse can be interpreted as a recognition of the validity of both Judaism and Christianity as religions that were revealed by God. The verse can also be seen as a message of unity and inclusivity, emphasizing the commonalities between different religions and their shared origin from the same God.
orig: ويعلمه الكتاب والحكمة والتوراة والإنجيل

translation: And (I have come to you, O Children of Israel,) as a messenger from your Lord, to confirm for you many of the scriptures already revealed, and to come with a clear sign from your Lord: I create for you out of clay the likeness of a bird; then I breathe into it and it becomes a bird, by the leave of God. And I heal the blind and the leper, and bring the dead to life, by the leave of God. And I inform you of what you eat and what you store in your houses. Surely, therein is a sign for you, if you believe.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the coming of a messenger from God to the Children of Israel, who confirms the scriptures that have been revealed before and brings a clear sign from God. The sign that is mentioned is the ability of the messenger to create a bird out of clay, breathe life into it, heal the blind and the leper, and bring the dead back to life. The verse emphasizes that these miracles are done by the leave of God, highlighting the power and authority of God. The verse also mentions that the messenger has knowledge of what the people eat and what they store in their houses, indicating the messenger's knowledge and awareness of the people's actions. The verse ends by stating that there is a sign in all of this for the people, if they choose to believe.
orig: ورسولا إلى بني إسرائيل أني قد جئتكم بآية من ربكم أني أخلق لكم من الطين كهيئة الطير فأنفخ فيه فيكون طيرا بإذن الله وأبرئ الأكمه والأبرص وأحيي الموتى بإذن الله وأنبئكم بما تأكلون وما تدخرون في بيوتكم إن في ذلك لآية لكم إن كنتم مؤمنين

translation: And [We sent him, Moses,] with the truth confirmed, to Pharaoh, saying, 'Release My servants.' Indeed, he was of those who were haughty. And We had certainly given him, of old, nine signs. But every time he came to them with something new, they laughed at it. And behind them was the punishment of a terrible day. Thus do We recompense the unjust people. And Moses said, 'O Pharaoh, indeed I am a messenger from the Lord of the worlds, [who is] worthy of being believed. And I am sent to you only as a clear warner.' But when he brought them the truth from Us, they said, 'Slay the sons of those who have believed with him and keep alive their women.' But the plans of the unbelievers are not except in error.
interpretation: The verse speaks about Moses' mission from God to Pharaoh, to free the Israelites from his oppression. The verse highlights the resistance and arrogance of Pharaoh, who refuses to acknowledge the truth and even plots to kill the sons of the believers. The verse emphasizes the futility of the unbelievers' plans, which will ultimately lead to their downfall and punishment. The verse serves as a reminder of the consequences of rejecting God's messengers and the importance of heeding their warnings.
orig: ومصدقا لما بين يدي من التوراة ولأحل لكم بعض الذي حرم عليكم وجئتكم بآية من ربكم فاتقوا الله وأطيعون

translation: Indeed, Allah is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him. This is a straight path.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the oneness of God, stating that Allah is the Lord of both the speaker and the listener. The verse commands the listener to worship Allah, and implies that this worship is the only way to the straight path. The verse is a reminder of the importance of monotheism and the importance of worshiping Allah alone. It also highlights the concept of tawhid (oneness of God) and the importance of following the straight path, which is the path of Islam.
orig: إن الله ربي وربكم فاعبدوه هذا صراط مستقيم

translation: But when Jesus felt [their] disbelief, he said, 'Who are my supporters for [the cause of] Allah?' The disciples said, 'We are the supporters of Allah. We have believed in Allah and testify that we are Muslims [submitting to Him].'
interpretation: The verse speaks about a moment when Jesus (peace be upon him) asked his disciples who among them would support him in the cause of God. In response, the disciples expressed their unwavering faith in God and declared themselves as supporters of God, submitting to His will. The verse highlights the importance of faith and submission to God, as well as the significance of standing up for the cause of God. It also emphasizes the importance of community and unity among believers in their support for each other and for the cause of God.
orig: فلما أحس عيسى منهم الكفر قال من أنصاري إلى الله قال الحواريون نحن أنصار الله آمنا بالله واشهد بأنا مسلمون

translation: Our Lord, we have believed in what You have sent down and have followed the Messenger, so write us down with those who bear witness.
interpretation: The verse is a supplication of the believers to God, expressing their faith in the revelation that has been sent down and their obedience to the Messenger. They ask God to record them among the righteous and the witnesses. The verse highlights the importance of faith and obedience in Islam, and the desire of the believers to be recognized and rewarded for their good deeds in the hereafter.
orig: ربنا آمنا بما أنزلت واتبعنا الرسول فاكتبنا مع الشاهدين

translation: They planned and Allah planned, but Allah is the best of planners.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the contrast between the plans of humans and the plans of God. The verse emphasizes the ultimate power and wisdom of God, who is described as the 'best of planners'. The verse suggests that while humans may plan and plot, their plans are ultimately subject to the will of God. The verse serves as a reminder that God is all-knowing and all-powerful, and that His plans are always superior to those of humans. It encourages believers to trust in God's wisdom and to have patience and faith, even in the face of uncertainty and difficulty.
orig: ومكروا ومكر الله والله خير الماكرين

translation: When Allah said, 'O Jesus, indeed I will take you and raise you to Myself and purify you from those who disbelieve and make those who follow you superior to those who disbelieve until the Day of Resurrection. Then to Me you will return, and I will judge between you concerning that in which you used to differ.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the ascension of Jesus to heaven by God. Jesus is purified from the disbelievers and his followers are made superior to them until the Day of Judgment. On that day, Jesus will return to God and God will judge between them regarding their differences. The verse emphasizes the power and authority of God, as well as the ultimate judgment that will take place on the Day of Resurrection. It also highlights the distinction between believers and disbelievers and the consequences of their beliefs.
orig: إذ قال الله يا عيسى إني متوفيك ورافعك إلي ومطهرك من الذين كفروا وجاعل الذين اتبعوك فوق الذين كفروا إلى يوم القيامة ثم إلي مرجعكم فأحكم بينكم فيما كنتم فيه تختلفون

translation: But as for those who disbelieved, We will punish them with a severe punishment in this world and the hereafter, and they will have no helpers.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the punishment of those who disbelieve. The verse emphasizes the severity of the punishment that the disbelievers will face in both this world and the hereafter. The verse also highlights that the disbelievers will not have any helpers or protectors. The verse serves as a warning to those who reject faith and a reminder of the consequences of disbelief.
orig: فأما الذين كفروا فأعذبهم عذابا شديدا في الدنيا والآخرة وما لهم من ناصرين

translation: But as for those who believe and do good deeds, surely We shall remunerate them their rewards in full, and Allah loves not the unjust.
interpretation: The verse contrasts the fate of those who believe and do good deeds with those who are unjust. The believers and doers of good deeds will receive their full rewards from Allah, while Allah does not love those who are unjust. The verse emphasizes the importance of faith and good deeds, and the promise of rewards for those who follow this path. At the same time, it warns against injustice and the consequences of being unjust.
orig: وأما الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات فيوفيهم أجورهم والله لا يحب الظالمين

translation: That is what We recite to you of the verses and the wise reminder.
interpretation: The verse is emphasizing the importance of the message being conveyed, which is part of the revelation from God. The message is conveyed through verses (ayat), which are signs of God's existence and power, and a reminder (dhikr) that serves as a guide for those seeking wisdom and truth. The verse encourages the reader to reflect on the message and to understand its significance, as it contains valuable lessons and teachings for those who seek guidance and enlightenment.
orig: ذلك نتلوه عليك من الآيات والذكر الحكيم

translation: Indeed, the example of Jesus to Allah is like that of Adam; He created him from dust then said to him, 'Be,' and he was.
interpretation: The verse draws a comparison between Jesus and Adam, stating that Jesus's example before God is like that of Adam. Both Jesus and Adam were created by God, with Adam being created from dust and Jesus being created without a father. This emphasizes the power and ability of God to create whatever He wills, without being limited by the laws of nature. The verse also highlights the similarities between Jesus and Adam, both of whom are prophets and servants of God. This serves as a reminder that all of humanity is equal in the eyes of God and that all people are created by God and are subject to His will and power.
orig: إن مثل عيسى عند الله كمثل آدم خلقه من تراب ثم قال له كن فيكون

translation: The truth is from your Lord, so be not of those who doubt.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of believing in and following the truth, which comes from one's Lord. The verse advises the listener not to be among those who have doubts or are skeptical about the truth. The verse encourages the listener to have faith and trust in the truth, and not to be swayed by doubts or uncertainties. The verse may be seen as a call to have certainty in one's beliefs and to have conviction in the truth of one's faith.
orig: الحق من ربك فلا تكن من الممترين
