orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تكونوا كالذين كفروا وقالوا لإخوانهم إذا ضربوا في الأرض أو كانوا غزى لو كانوا عندنا ما ماتوا وما قتلوا ليجعل الله ذلك حسرة في قلوبهم والله يحيي ويميت والله بما تعملون بصير

translation: But if you are killed or die in the way of Allah, then forgiveness from Allah and mercy are better than what they accumulate.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the rewards for those who are killed or die while striving in the way of Allah. It emphasizes that the forgiveness and mercy from Allah are greater than any material possessions or worldly gains that the people could accumulate. The verse serves as a source of motivation and encouragement for those who are engaged in the struggle for their faith and as a reminder of the great rewards that await them in the hereafter. It also highlights the significance of sacrifice and martyrdom in Islam and the ultimate victory of good over evil.
orig: ولئن قتلتم في سبيل الله أو متم لمغفرة من الله ورحمة خير مما يجمعون

translation: But if you are slain, or die, surely to Allah you will be gathered.
interpretation: The verse reminds believers of the certainty of death and the inevitability of meeting their Lord, regardless of whether they are killed or die naturally. It emphasizes the ultimate unity of all souls in the afterlife, and the importance of striving for righteousness and preparing for the Day of Judgment, rather than being overly attached to the temporary pleasures and fears of this world.
orig: ولئن متم أو قتلتم لإلى الله تحشرون

translation: By the mercy of Allah, you were lenient with them; and if you had been harsh and hardhearted, they would have scattered from around you. So pardon them and ask forgiveness for them and consult them in the matter. And when you have decided, then rely upon Allah. Indeed, Allah loves those who rely [upon Him].
interpretation: The verse highlights the importance of showing mercy and leniency towards others, and the positive outcomes that can result from doing so. The verse explains that if the prophet (peace be upon him) had been harsh and unforgiving, the people would have scattered and left him. However, by being merciful and lenient, they were able to stay together and work towards a common goal. The verse encourages the prophet (peace be upon him) to consult with the people and seek their input, and to rely on Allah for guidance and support. The verse emphasizes that relying on Allah is highly valued and loved by Him.
orig: فبما رحمة من الله لنت لهم ولو كنت فظا غليظ القلب لانفضوا من حولك فاعف عنهم واستغفر لهم وشاورهم في الأمر فإذا عزمت فتوكل على الله إن الله يحب المتوكلين

translation: If Allah helps you, then there is no victor over you; but if He abandons you, then who is there that can help you after Him? And upon Allah let the believers rely.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of relying on Allah and trusting in His help and support. It suggests that if Allah is on the side of the believers, then they will be victorious, and no one will be able to defeat them. However, if Allah abandons them, then no one else will be able to help them. Therefore, the verse encourages the believers to place their trust and reliance solely on Allah, and not to look to anyone else for help. This is because Allah is the only one who has the power to truly help and support them.
orig: إن ينصركم الله فلا غالب لكم وإن يخذلكم فمن ذا الذي ينصركم من بعده وعلى الله فليتوكل المؤمنون

translation: And it is not for a prophet to defraud, and whoever defrauds will come with what he defrauded on the Day of Resurrection. Then every soul will be compensated for what it earned, and they will not be wronged.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of honesty and fairness, particularly for prophets. It warns that those who commit fraud will be held accountable and will have to pay back what they took unjustly on the Day of Judgment. The verse reassures that every soul will receive what it deserves for its actions and that no one will be wronged.
orig: وما كان لنبي أن يغل ومن يغلل يأت بما غل يوم القيامة ثم توفى كل نفس ما كسبت وهم لا يظلمون

translation: Then which is better: the one who follows the pleasure of Allah or one upon whom is the wrath of Allah, and whom is a descending doom (of Hell), and it is an evil destination.
interpretation: The verse presents a rhetorical question that highlights the contrast between two types of people: those who follow the pleasure of Allah and those who incur His wrath. The verse emphasizes the dire consequences of earning Allah's wrath, which includes descending doom and an evil destination, and contrasts it with the blessings of following Allah's pleasure. The verse encourages the reader to reflect on their own actions and choose the path that leads to Allah's pleasure, rather than His wrath.
orig: أفمن اتبع رضوان الله كمن باء بسخط من الله ومأواه جهنم وبئس المصير

translation: They are different levels with Allah, and Allah is Seeing of what they do.
interpretation: The verse highlights the concept of different levels or degrees of reward and status that people will have with Allah on the Day of Judgment. The verse emphasizes Allah's all-encompassing knowledge and awareness of the actions of human beings, reminding them that they will be held accountable for their deeds. The verse serves as a motivation for believers to strive for higher levels of righteousness and piety, and as a warning for those who are heedless of their accountability before Allah.
orig: هم درجات عند الله والله بصير بما يعملون

translation: Certainly, Allah conferred a great favor on the believers when He sent among them a Messenger from among themselves, reciting to them His verses, and purifying them, and teaching them the Book and wisdom, although they were before in clear error.
interpretation: The verse highlights the blessings that Allah bestowed upon the believers by sending a Messenger from among themselves. This Messenger, Muhammad (peace be upon him), recited the verses of the Qur'an to them, purified their souls, and taught them the Book (Qur'an) and wisdom. The verse emphasizes the significance of this event, as the believers were previously in clear error. This verse serves as a reminder of the importance of following the guidance of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and the blessings that come with it.
orig: لقد من الله على المؤمنين إذ بعث فيهم رسولا من أنفسهم يتلو عليهم آياته ويزكيهم ويعلمهم الكتاب والحكمة وإن كانوا من قبل لفي ضلال مبين

translation: Or have you not seen when a calamity strikes you, similar to it you say, 'How is this?' Say, 'It is from yourselves. Indeed, Allah is over all things competent.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the experience of calamity and the human tendency to question and express surprise when faced with adversity. The verse advises the reader to respond to calamity with the understanding that it is a consequence of their own actions. The verse emphasizes God's power and control over all things, reminding the reader of the ultimate reality of Divine justice.
orig: أولما أصابتكم مصيبة قد أصبتم مثليها قلتم أنى هذا قل هو من عند أنفسكم إن الله على كل شيء قدير

translation: And you (Muhammad) will not be responsible for their guidance, but Allah guides whom He wills. And whatever of good reaches you, it is from Allah, and whatever of evil befalls you, it is from yourself. And We have sent you (O Muhammad) as a messenger to mankind, and Allah is sufficient as a witness.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the limitations of the prophet Muhammad's role as a guide for his people. It emphasizes that the ultimate responsibility for guidance lies with God and that He guides whom He wills. The verse also highlights the role of Muhammad as a messenger sent by God to mankind. Furthermore, it explains that any good that reaches the believers is from God, while any evil that befalls them is from themselves, meaning their own actions. This verse serves as a reminder that the ultimate power and control belongs to God, and that the prophet's role is limited to delivering the message.
orig: وما أصابكم يوم التقى الجمعان فبإذن الله وليعلم المؤمنين

translation: And let those who oppose the Messenger's commandment beware, lest a trial befall them or a painful punishment. And indeed, they oppose not but those who believe among
interpretation: No interpretation
orig: وليعلم الذين نافقوا وقيل لهم تعالوا قاتلوا في سبيل الله أو ادفعوا قالوا لو نعلم قتالا لاتبعناكم هم للكفر يومئذ أقرب منهم للإيمان يقولون بأفواههم ما ليس في قلوبهم والله أعلم بما يكتمون

translation: Those who say to their brothers, 'If you had stayed with us, you would surely have been spared.' So now, why don't you stay and strive along with us so that you may protect yourselves from death, if you are truthful.
interpretation: The verse addresses people who make false promises to their brothers, claiming that if they had stayed with them, they would have been protected from harm. The verse challenges these individuals to prove their sincerity by joining the struggle and fighting alongside their brothers instead of merely making empty promises. The verse highlights the importance of taking action and striving for one's own protection, rather than relying on false promises and inaction.
orig: الذين قالوا لإخوانهم وقعدوا لو أطاعونا ما قتلوا قل فادرءوا عن أنفسكم الموت إن كنتم صادقين

translation: And reckon not those who are killed in the way of Allah as dead; nay, they are alive, with their Lord, well provided for.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes that those who are killed while fighting for the cause of God are not dead, but alive and well provided for by their Lord. The verse challenges the common notion of death and encourages believers to view martyrdom as a form of life. It serves as a source of comfort and motivation for those who are fighting for their faith and a reminder of the ultimate reward that awaits them in the afterlife. The verse also highlights the significance of martyrdom in Islamic teachings and the high status of martyrs in the eyes of God.
orig: ولا تحسبن الذين قتلوا في سبيل الله أمواتا بل أحياء عند ربهم يرزقون

translation: They are joyful because of what Allah has bestowed upon them from His bounty, and they rejoice for those who have not yet joined them [the deceased], that there will be no fear concerning them, nor will they grieve.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the joy and gratitude of a group of people for the blessings they have received from Allah. They are not only content with their own blessings, but they also feel happiness for those who have not yet joined them (the deceased), meaning they hope for their salvation. The verse emphasizes the absence of fear and grief for these people, indicating a state of tranquility and peace of mind. The verse can be interpreted as a reminder to be grateful for what we have, and to have good wishes for others, even after our death, as it leads to a state of serenity and contentment.
orig: فرحين بما آتاهم الله من فضله ويستبشرون بالذين لم يلحقوا بهم من خلفهم ألا خوف عليهم ولا هم يحزنون

translation: They rejoice in a grace from Allah and His favor; that Allah does not waste the reward of the believers.
interpretation: The verse highlights the blessings and favor that believers receive from Allah, and the fact that Allah does not let the reward of believers go to waste. This verse emphasizes the importance of faith and good deeds, and the blessings that come with it. The verse serves as a reminder that Allah rewards those who believe in Him and do good deeds, and that these rewards will not be lost or wasted. It also serves as a motivation for believers to continue doing good deeds and have faith in Allah, knowing that their efforts will be rewarded.
orig: يستبشرون بنعمة من الله وفضل وأن الله لا يضيع أجر المؤمنين

translation: Those who responded to God and the Messenger after being afflicted with a disaster - for those of them who do good and fear - a great reward.
interpretation: The verse speaks about those who faced a disaster but still responded to God and the Messenger, and for those among them who do good and are mindful of God, a great reward is promised. The verse emphasizes the resilience and perseverance of the believers in the face of adversity, and the reward that awaits them for their steadfastness. The verse serves as an encouragement for the believers to remain steadfast in their faith, and to continue doing good, despite the challenges they may face.
orig: الذين استجابوا لله والرسول من بعد ما أصابهم القرح للذين أحسنوا منهم واتقوا أجر عظيم

translation: Those to whom the people said, 'Indeed, the people have gathered against you, so fear them.' But it increased them only in faith, and they said, 'Sufficient for us is Allah, and [He] is the best disposer of affairs.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about a group of people who were faced with a situation where the people had gathered against them, causing fear and anxiety. However, instead of succumbing to fear, they increased in faith and placed their trust in Allah, recognizing that He is the best disposer of affairs. The verse highlights the importance of having faith in Allah and relying on Him during difficult times, and it serves as a reminder that Allah is always there to support and protect His believers.
orig: الذين قال لهم الناس إن الناس قد جمعوا لكم فاخشوهم فزادهم إيمانا وقالوا حسبنا الله ونعم الوكيل

translation: Then turn in repentance to your Lord and submit to Him before the punishment comes upon you, for then you cannot be helped. And follow the best of what has been revealed to you from your Lord before the punishment comes upon you suddenly while you are unaware.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the importance of turning to God in repentance and submitting to Him before the punishment comes. It emphasizes the urgency of seeking God's forgiveness and following His guidance before it is too late. The verse warns that once the punishment comes, it will be too late for repentance and there will be no help. The verse encourages believers to follow the best of what has been revealed to them from God, indicating the importance of adhering to the teachings of Islam and living a righteous life.
orig: فانقلبوا بنعمة من الله وفضل لم يمسسهم سوء واتبعوا رضوان الله والله ذو فضل عظيم

translation: That is but Satan who instills it (evil) into those who believe not, so fear them not, but fear Me, if you are indeed believers.
interpretation: The verse addresses the believers and advises them not to fear the disbelievers, but rather to fear God. The verse explains that the source of the fear and anxiety that the disbelievers instill in the hearts of the believers is actually Satan. The verse encourages the believers to have faith and trust in God and not to let the fear of the disbelievers deter them from their path. The verse also serves as a reminder of the importance of faith and trust in God, and the insignificance of the disbelievers in comparison to God.
orig: إنما ذلكم الشيطان يخوف أولياءه فلا تخافوهم وخافون إن كنتم مؤمنين

translation: And let not those who hasten to disbelief grieve you (O Muhammad). Indeed, they will not harm Allah at all. Allah intends that He should not give them a portion in the Hereafter, and for them is a great punishment.
interpretation: The verse speaks about those who hasten to disbelief and not to be grieved by it. The verse reassures the Prophet Muhammad that the disbelievers will not harm Allah in any way. The verse explains that Allah has a plan for them, which is not to give them a portion in the Hereafter. The verse also warns that they will face a great punishment as a consequence of their disbelief.
orig: ولا يحزنك الذين يسارعون في الكفر إنهم لن يضروا الله شيئا يريد الله ألا يجعل لهم حظا في الآخرة ولهم عذاب عظيم

translation: Indeed, those who have purchased disbelief with faith - they will not harm Allah at all, and for them is a painful punishment.
interpretation: The verse highlights the consequences of exchanging faith for disbelief, which is a grave sin and will incur a severe punishment. The verse stresses that such actions will not harm Allah in any way, emphasizing the power and supremacy of Allah over His creation. The verse serves as a warning to those who might be tempted to abandon their faith or to engage in actions that are contrary to it, reminding them of the severe consequences of such actions and the ultimate power of Allah.
orig: إن الذين اشتروا الكفر بالإيمان لن يضروا الله شيئا ولهم عذاب أليم

translation: And let not the unbelievers think that Our granting them respite is good for theirselves; We grant them respite only that they may increase in sin, and for them is a shameful punishment.
interpretation: The verse warns unbelievers not to mistake God's patience and respite for favor or benefit towards them. The respite is granted only to increase their sins and further condemn themselves. The verse emphasizes that the ultimate fate of the unbelievers will be a shameful punishment, and it serves as a reminder of the consequences of their disbelief and rejection of God's message.
orig: ولا يحسبن الذين كفروا أنما نملي لهم خير لأنفسهم إنما نملي لهم ليزدادوا إثما ولهم عذاب مهين

translation: God would not leave the believers in the state you are in, until He distinguishes the bad from the good. Nor will God inform you of the unseen. But God chooses from among His messengers whom He wills. So believe in God and His messengers. If you believe and are conscious of God, then for you there is a great reward.
interpretation: The verse speaks about God's plan for the believers, emphasizing that God will not leave them in their current state without distinguishing between the good and the bad among them. The verse also highlights that God has the power to know the unseen, but He chooses not to reveal it to His messengers. Instead, God selects certain messengers to convey His message. The verse encourages the believers to have faith in God and His messengers, and if they do so while being mindful of God, they will be rewarded greatly.
orig: ما كان الله ليذر المؤمنين على ما أنتم عليه حتى يميز الخبيث من الطيب وما كان الله ليطلعكم على الغيب ولكن الله يجتبي من رسله من يشاء فآمنوا بالله ورسله وإن تؤمنوا وتتقوا فلكم أجر عظيم

translation: And let not those who are stingy with what Allah has given them of His bounty think that it is good for them. Rather, it is bad for them. They will have a tightening of their accounts around their necks on the Day of Resurrection. And to Allah belongs the inheritance of the heavens and the earth. And Allah is acquainted with what you do.
interpretation: The verse warns those who are stingy with their wealth and resources, reminding them that their miserliness will not benefit them in the long run. Instead, their stinginess will result in a 'tightening of their accounts' around their necks on the Day of Judgment. The verse emphasizes that all wealth and resources come from Allah, and He is aware of all that people do. The inheritance of the heavens and the earth belongs to Allah, reminding people that their wealth is temporary and insignificant compared to the eternal blessings of the afterlife. Ultimately, the verse serves as a warning to those who prioritize their wealth and possessions over their faith and generosity towards others.
orig: ولا يحسبن الذين يبخلون بما آتاهم الله من فضله هو خيرا لهم بل هو شر لهم سيطوقون ما بخلوا به يوم القيامة ولله ميراث السماوات والأرض والله بما تعملون خبير

translation: Indeed, Allah has heard the words of those who said, 'Allah is poor, and we are rich.' We will record what they said and kill the prophets unjustly, and We will say, 'Taste the punishment of the Fire.'
interpretation: The verse describes the blasphemous words of those who deny God's power and sovereignty, claiming that they are self-sufficient and do not need God. The verse emphasizes that God is aware of their words and actions, and that they will be held accountable for their unjust killings of the prophets. The ultimate punishment for their arrogance and disbelief is the taste of the Fire, which symbolizes the painful consequences of their rejection of God's guidance and mercy.
orig: لقد سمع الله قول الذين قالوا إن الله فقير ونحن أغنياء سنكتب ما قالوا وقتلهم الأنبياء بغير حق ونقول ذوقوا عذاب الحريق

translation: That is because of what your hands have sent forth, and because Allah is not unjust to the servants.
interpretation: The verse explains that people's actions have consequences, and that what they have done in the past will affect their present and future. The verse emphasizes that Allah is just and fair, and that He does not wrong His servants. This means that any punishment or hardship that people face is a result of their own actions, not because of any injustice on the part of Allah. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of taking responsibility for one's actions and seeking forgiveness and redemption.
orig: ذلك بما قدمت أيديكم وأن الله ليس بظلام للعبيد

translation: Those who say, 'Allah has promised us not to believe in any messenger until he brings us an offering which the fire consumes.' Say: 'Messengers have come to you before me with clear signs and what you say, so why did you kill them, if you are truthful?'
interpretation: The verse addresses those who deny the messengers of God and demand that they bring a miraculous sign as proof of their prophethood. The verse specifically mentions the demand for an offering to be consumed by fire. The verse then challenges these people by reminding them of previous messengers who brought clear signs and yet were still rejected and killed. The verse serves as a rebuke to those who deny the messengers and demand signs, and as a reminder that past messengers were also rejected and killed despite bringing clear evidence. The verse also highlights the unjust and hypocritical nature of those who demand signs while at the same time rejecting and killing the messengers who bring them.
orig: الذين قالوا إن الله عهد إلينا ألا نؤمن لرسول حتى يأتينا بقربان تأكله النار قل قد جاءكم رسل من قبلي بالبينات وبالذي قلتم فلم قتلتموهم إن كنتم صادقين

translation: But if they deny you, then indeed, before you, have denied [messengers] messengers many peoples who were bringers of clear proofs, scriptures, and enlightening writings.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the rejection of prophets and their messages by disbelievers. It reminds the audience that many messengers before the prophet Muhammad (PBUH) had faced the same denial and rejection from their people. The verse highlights the fact that these messengers brought clear proofs, scriptures, and enlightening writings, but their people still rejected them. This verse serves as a reminder that rejection of prophets and their messages is not a new phenomenon, and that it has happened many times before. It also emphasizes the importance of recognizing and accepting the truth when it is presented, and the consequences of rejecting it.
orig: فإن كذبوك فقد كذب رسل من قبلك جاءوا بالبينات والزبر والكتاب المنير

translation: Every soul will taste death. And only on the Day of Resurrection will you be repaid in full for what you have done. So, he who is drawn away from the Fire and admitted to the Garden has attained his goal. And what is the life of this world but the enjoyment of delusion.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the inevitability of death and the Day of Judgment, where people will be recompensed for their deeds. The verse highlights the ultimate goal of avoiding the Fire and entering Paradise, indicating that this is the ultimate success. The verse also suggests that the pleasures of this world are fleeting and illusory, and should not be the focus of one's life.
orig: كل نفس ذائقة الموت وإنما توفون أجوركم يوم القيامة فمن زحزح عن النار وأدخل الجنة فقد فاز وما الحياة الدنيا إلا متاع الغرور

translation: And that He may test you in that which you have given of your property and your selves, and that you may strive in (the way of) the All-merciful; and that you may testify against yourselves. And that you may become pious.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the purpose of trials and tests that people face in their lives, particularly in relation to their wealth and their selves. The verse emphasizes the importance of striving in the way of God, and the role of these tests in helping people become more pious and mindful of their actions. The verse also suggests that these tests serve as a means of self-reflection and an opportunity for individuals to assess their own beliefs and behavior. The verse encourages people to be patient and steadfast in the face of these trials, and to use them as a means of spiritual growth and development.
orig: لتبلون في أموالكم وأنفسكم ولتسمعن من الذين أوتوا الكتاب من قبلكم ومن الذين أشركوا أذى كثيرا وإن تصبروا وتتقوا فإن ذلك من عزم الأمور

translation: And when God took a covenant from those who were given the Scripture, to make it clear to mankind and not to hide it, but they cast it behind their backs and sold it for a small price. Woe to those who sell it for a small price.
interpretation: This verse speaks about the covenant that God made with the people who were given the Scripture (the Torah and the Gospel) to make it clear to mankind and not to hide it. However, they went against this covenant and hid the truth, selling it for a small price. The verse strongly condemns this act of betrayal and warns those who sell the truth for their own benefit and gain. It serves as a reminder of the importance of upholding one's covenant and the severe consequences of betraying it.
orig: وإذ أخذ الله ميثاق الذين أوتوا الكتاب لتبيننه للناس ولا تكتمونه فنبذوه وراء ظهورهم واشتروا به ثمنا قليلا فبئس ما يشترون

translation: Do not think of those who rejoice in what they have done and love to be praised for what they have not done, (that) they will escape punishment. Indeed, they will have a painful punishment.
interpretation: The verse warns against arrogance and self-delusion, particularly among those who take pleasure in their own deeds and seek recognition for accomplishments they did not achieve. The verse emphasizes that such people will not escape punishment, and that they will face a painful retribution for their actions. The verse serves as a reminder that true success and recognition come from God, and that false pride and arrogance are false sources of satisfaction that will ultimately lead to downfall.
orig: لا تحسبن الذين يفرحون بما أتوا ويحبون أن يحمدوا بما لم يفعلوا فلا تحسبنهم بمفازة من العذاب ولهم عذاب أليم

translation: And to Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth, and Allah is over all things competent.
interpretation: The verse affirms the sovereignty of Allah over all of creation, emphasizing that both the heavens and the earth belong to Him. The phrase 'and Allah is over all things competent' highlights the power and ability of Allah, and emphasizes that He has complete control and authority over all things. This verse serves as a reminder of the greatness and majesty of Allah, and encourages believers to have faith and trust in His power and ability.
orig: ولله ملك السماوات والأرض والله على كل شيء قدير

translation: Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth and the alternation of the night and the day are signs for those of understanding.
interpretation: The verse highlights the wonders of creation, including the heavens, the earth, and the cycles of night and day, as evidence of God's existence and power. The verse suggests that these signs are intended for those who are endowed with understanding or wisdom. The verse encourages reflection and contemplation of the natural world as a means of gaining knowledge and insight into the divine. At the same time, the verse implies a distinction between those who are receptive to these signs and those who are not, highlighting the importance of open-mindedness and intellectual curiosity in understanding the world and its creator.
orig: إن في خلق السماوات والأرض واختلاف الليل والنهار لآيات لأولي الألباب

translation: Those who remember Allah while standing, sitting, and lying on their sides, and contemplate the creation of the heavens and the earth: 'Our Lord, You did not create this in vain. Exalted are You! Save us from the punishment of the Fire.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the practice of remembering and contemplating Allah (God) in all positions and at all times. The people described in this verse are constantly aware of Allah and His creation, and they express their gratitude and reverence for Him. They recognize that the creation of the heavens and the earth is not without purpose, and they seek protection from the punishment of the Fire. The verse encourages Muslims to cultivate a constant awareness of Allah and to express their gratitude and reverence for Him through remembrance and contemplation.
orig: الذين يذكرون الله قياما وقعودا وعلى جنوبهم ويتفكرون في خلق السماوات والأرض ربنا ما خلقت هذا باطلا سبحانك فقنا عذاب النار

translation: Our Lord, indeed You are bringing whoever you want into the Fire. Indeed, there is no helper for the unjust.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the power of God to bring anyone He wants into the Fire (of Hell) and the lack of help for the unjust. The verse emphasizes the absolute power of God over all of His creation and the inevitable fate of the unjust. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of leading a righteous life and the consequences of unjust actions.
orig: ربنا إنك من تدخل النار فقد أخزيته وما للظالمين من أنصار

translation: Our Lord, indeed we have heard a caller calling to faith, [saying], 'Believe in your Lord.' So we have believed. So forgive us our sins and forgive us our transgressions and make us die among the righteous.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the acceptance of faith by a group of people who heard a caller urging them to believe in their Lord. They responded positively and believed in their Lord. They then ask their Lord for forgiveness of their sins and transgressions and request to die among the righteous. The verse emphasizes the importance of responding to the call of faith and the significance of seeking forgiveness and aspiring to live a righteous life.
orig: ربنا إننا سمعنا مناديا ينادي للإيمان أن آمنوا بربكم فآمنا ربنا فاغفر لنا ذنوبنا وكفر عنا سيئاتنا وتوفنا مع الأبرار

translation: Our Lord, and give us what You have promised us through Your messengers, and do not disgrace us on the Day of Resurrection. Indeed, You do not break [Your] promise.
interpretation: The verse is a supplication to God, asking Him to fulfill His promises made through His messengers. It expresses the believers' fear of being disgraced on the Day of Judgment, and their trust in God's promise that He will not break His word. The verse conveys the believers' hope and faith in God's mercy and justice, and their reliance on His promises as a source of comfort and reassurance in the face of the uncertainty of the hereafter.
orig: ربنا وآتنا ما وعدتنا على رسلك ولا تخزنا يوم القيامة إنك لا تخلف الميعاد

translation: And their Lord answered them, 'I will not let the deed of any worker among you, whether male or female, be lost. And those who emigrated and were driven out from their homes, and suffered harm in My cause, and fought and were slain, I will surely absolve them of their sins and admit them into gardens through which rivers flow, as a reward from Allah. And Allah has the best reward.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the promise of God to those who have emigrated, been driven out of their homes, and suffered harm in the way of God. These individuals have fought and even been killed, and God promises to absolve them of their sins and admit them into gardens through which rivers flow. The verse emphasizes the importance of actions, stating that God will not let the deeds of any worker, whether male or female, go to waste. The verse serves as a reminder of the rewards that await those who are steadfast in their faith and are willing to make sacrifices for the sake of God.
orig: فاستجاب لهم ربهم أني لا أضيع عمل عامل منكم من ذكر أو أنثى بعضكم من بعض فالذين هاجروا وأخرجوا من ديارهم وأوذوا في سبيلي وقاتلوا وقتلوا لأكفرن عنهم سيئاتهم ولأدخلنهم جنات تجري من تحتها الأنهار ثوابا من عند الله والله عنده حسن الثواب

translation: Let not the turning of the disbelievers in the cities deceive you.
interpretation: The verse warns against being deceived by the apparent stability or prosperity of the disbelievers in their cities. The verse suggests that the disbelievers may appear to be secure and successful, but their ultimate fate is one of destruction and punishment. The verse serves as a reminder to remain steadfast in faith and to not be swayed by the temporary success of those who reject God's message.
orig: لا يغرنك تقلب الذين كفروا في البلاد

translation: A little provision, then to Us will be their return, then surely Hell will be their resting place, an evil bed (indeed)!
interpretation: The verse speaks about the fate of those who indulge in the pleasures of this world and ignore their ultimate destination, which is Hell. The verse suggests that they will be given only a 'little provision' in this world, and then they will be returned to Us (God), and their final destination will be Hell. The phrase 'an evil bed (indeed)' emphasizes the wretchedness and misery of their fate. The verse serves as a warning to those who are preoccupied with the materialistic pleasures of this world and neglect their religious duties and the hereafter.
orig: متاع قليل ثم مأواهم جهنم وبئس المهاد

translation: But as for those who fear their Lord, they will have gardens beneath which rivers flow, to dwell therein forever, as a gift from God. And with God is the best (reward) for the righteous.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the reward for those who fear their Lord, emphasizing the beautiful and everlasting gardens that await them. These gardens, filled with flowing rivers, serve as a symbol of God's grace and generosity towards the righteous. The verse also highlights the ultimate and perfect reward that God has in store for the righteous, reminding the believers that nothing is comparable to the blessings of God. The verse serves as a source of motivation and encouragement for the believers to continue their path of righteousness and piety, reminding them of the ultimate reward that awaits them in the hereafter.
orig: لكن الذين اتقوا ربهم لهم جنات تجري من تحتها الأنهار خالدين فيها نزلا من عند الله وما عند الله خير للأبرار

translation: And indeed, among the People of the Book there are some who believe in Allah and what has been revealed to you and what has been revealed to them, [being] humbly submissive to Allah. They do not exchange the verses of Allah for a small price. Those will have their reward with their Lord. Indeed, Allah is swift in account.
interpretation: The verse highlights the existence of people among the People of the Book (Jews and Christians) who believe in Allah, the revelations given to the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH), and their own scriptures. These people are humble and submissive to Allah, and they do not sell the verses of Allah for a small price, meaning they do not compromise their faith for worldly gains. The verse promises a reward for these people from their Lord. It also emphasizes that Allah is swift in settling accounts and reckoning deeds, a reminder that all actions will be judged and rewarded or punished accordingly.
orig: وإن من أهل الكتاب لمن يؤمن بالله وما أنزل إليكم وما أنزل إليهم خاشعين لله لا يشترون بآيات الله ثمنا قليلا أولئك لهم أجرهم عند ربهم إن الله سريع الحساب

translation: O believers, be patient and endure. Establish unity and fear God, that you may prosper.
interpretation: The verse is a call to believers to be patient and endure in the face of hardships. It emphasizes the importance of unity and obedience to God's commands. By being patient and obedient, believers can achieve success and prosperity. The verse serves as a reminder that God's favor and blessings are attained through patience, endurance, and obedience to His commands.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا اصبروا وصابروا ورابطوا واتقوا الله لعلكم تفلحون

translation: O mankind, fear your Lord, who created you from one soul and created from it its mate and dispersed from both of them many men and women. And fear Allah, through whom you ask one another, and the wombs. Indeed, Allah is ever over you, an Observer.
interpretation: The verse begins with a command to all of humanity to fear their Lord, who created them from a single soul and from that soul created its mate, and from both of them created many men and women. The verse emphasizes the importance of fearing Allah and being mindful of His presence at all times, as He is the one who is asked for help and support. The verse also mentions the importance of respecting and being mindful of the ties of kinship and the wombs, as these are signs of Allah's power and mercy. The verse serves as a reminder of the unity of humanity and the importance of maintaining strong family ties and being mindful of Allah's presence and power.
orig: يا أيها الناس اتقوا ربكم الذي خلقكم من نفس واحدة وخلق منها زوجها وبث منهما رجالا كثيرا ونساء واتقوا الله الذي تساءلون به والأرحام إن الله كان عليكم رقيبا

translation: And give orphans their properties, and do not substitute the bad for the good; and do not consume their properties along with your own. That surely is a great sin.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of taking care of orphans and protecting their property. It forbids the substitution of bad or inferior goods in place of the good or superior goods that belong to the orphans. Additionally, it warns against consuming the orphans' properties along with one's own, stating that such actions are a great sin. The verse serves as a reminder to those who are responsible for the care of orphans to act with fairness, integrity, and honesty towards them, and to ensure that their properties are protected and preserved.
orig: وآتوا اليتامى أموالهم ولا تتبدلوا الخبيث بالطيب ولا تأكلوا أموالهم إلى أموالكم إنه كان حوبا كبيرا

translation: And if you fear that you will not be just in treating orphans, then marry those women that seem good to you: two, three, or four of them. But if you fear that you will not be equitable (in treating them), then marry only one, or a slave girl that your right hand possesses. That makes it more likely that you will not be partial.
interpretation: The verse provides guidance on marriage and the treatment of orphans. It acknowledges the concern that some men may have about being fair to orphans under their care, and offers a solution: marry other women if that concern is present. The verse allows men to marry up to four women, but warns against being partial or unfair. If there is a fear of being partial, then the man should marry only one woman or a slave girl. The verse emphasizes the importance of fairness and justice in all marital relationships, and encourages men to consider the well-being of orphans in their care.
orig: وإن خفتم ألا تقسطوا في اليتامى فانكحوا ما طاب لكم من النساء مثنى وثلاث ورباع فإن خفتم ألا تعدلوا فواحدة أو ما ملكت أيمانكم ذلك أدنى ألا تعولوا

translation: And give to the women their dowries willingly, but if they remit any part of it willingly, then it is acceptable for you, and it is no sin for you. And give her wealth willingly, not by coercion. Indeed, if you coerce your women, then indeed you are sinful.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the rights of women in regards to their dowries. It emphasizes the importance of giving the dowry willingly and without coercion. If the women choose to remit any part of it, then it is acceptable. However, if the husband coerces his wife into remitting any part of her dowry, then he is considered sinful. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of respecting the rights of women in financial matters and treating them with fairness and justice.
orig: وآتوا النساء صدقاتهن نحلة فإن طبن لكم عن شيء منه نفسا فكلوه هنيئا مريئا

translation: And do not give to the foolish your property that Allah has made for you a means of support, but feed and clothe them from it and speak to them a word of honest advice.
interpretation: The verse advises against giving one's wealth to the foolish, and instead encourages the provision of food, clothing, and kind words. The verse emphasizes the importance of using one's wealth wisely and responsibly, and the obligation to assist those in need. The verse also highlights the significance of giving advice and guidance, but in a respectful and considerate manner.
orig: ولا تؤتوا السفهاء أموالكم التي جعل الله لكم قياما وارزقوهم فيها واكسوهم وقولوا لهم قولا معروفا

translation: And test the orphans until they reach marriageable age. Then if you perceive in them sound judgement, return to them their property. And do not consume it extravagantly and quickly, before they grow up. And whoever is rich, let him abstain; and whoever is poor, let him eat reasonably. And when you return their property to them, then call upon witnesses. And sufficient is Allah as Accountant.
interpretation: This verse speaks about the responsibility of guardians towards orphans, emphasizing the importance of testing their maturity and judgement before returning their property to them. The verse warns against wasting the orphan's wealth and encourages those who are rich to be generous and those who are poor to be reasonable in their consumption. The verse also highlights the importance of accountability, urging guardians to call upon witnesses when returning the orphan's property. Overall, the verse promotes justice, fairness, and responsibility towards the vulnerable members of society.
orig: وابتلوا اليتامى حتى إذا بلغوا النكاح فإن آنستم منهم رشدا فادفعوا إليهم أموالهم ولا تأكلوها إسرافا وبدارا أن يكبروا ومن كان غنيا فليستعفف ومن كان فقيرا فليأكل بالمعروف فإذا دفعتم إليهم أموالهم فأشهدوا عليهم وكفى بالله حسيبا

translation: To the men is a share of what the parents and close relatives leave, and to the women is a share of what the parents and close relatives leave, be it small or large - a determined share.
interpretation: The verse outlines the inheritance rights of men and women. It states that both men and women have a right to inherit from their parents and close relatives, and that the share of inheritance is not dependent on the quantity of the inheritance but rather is a fixed share. This verse emphasizes the importance of fairness and equality in the distribution of inheritance and the recognition of the rights of both men and women in this matter.
orig: للرجال نصيب مما ترك الوالدان والأقربون وللنساء نصيب مما ترك الوالدان والأقربون مما قل منه أو كثر نصيبا مفروضا

translation: And when the distribution (of inheritance) is made to those who are the relatives, and the orphans, and the poor, be careful of (your duty to) them, and speak to them a word of kindness and justice.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the distribution of inheritance and the importance of treating relatives, orphans, and the poor with kindness and fairness. The verse emphasizes the responsibility of the person making the distribution to be mindful of their duty towards these vulnerable groups and to speak to them in a kind and just manner. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of treating all people with fairness and compassion, regardless of their social status or circumstances.
orig: وإذا حضر القسمة أولو القربى واليتامى والمساكين فارزقوهم منه وقولوا لهم قولا معروفا

translation: And let those fear who, if they left behind them descendants, would be afraid for them. So let them fear Allah and speak words of appropriate reconciliation.
interpretation: This verse speaks to those who, should they have descendants, would be concerned for their well-being and safety. The verse instructs these individuals to fear and revere Allah, and to speak words that promote reconciliation and unity. The verse highlights the importance of considering the impact of one's actions on future generations, and the responsibility to create a harmonious and peaceful community through righteous behavior and respectful communication.
orig: وليخش الذين لو تركوا من خلفهم ذرية ضعافا خافوا عليهم فليتقوا الله وليقولوا قولا سديدا

translation: Indeed, those who devour the property of orphans unjustly are only consuming into their bellies fire; they will be flamed in a Blaze.
interpretation: The verse strongly condemns the act of consuming the property of orphans unjustly, and warns of severe consequences for those who engage in such behavior. The verse uses vivid and powerful imagery to describe the punishment for this sin, likening it to consuming fire that will ultimately lead to being flamed in a Blaze. The verse serves as a reminder to uphold justice and protect the rights of the vulnerable, such as orphans, and to avoid actions that harm others for personal gain.
orig: إن الذين يأكلون أموال اليتامى ظلما إنما يأكلون في بطونهم نارا وسيصلون سعيرا

translation: God enjoins you concerning your children: for the male, what is equal to the share of two females. But if there are only females, for them is two-thirds of what he leaves. And if there is one, for her is half. And for his parents, to each one of them is a sixth of what he leaves if he has a child. But if he has no child and his parents inherit from him, then for his mother is one-third. And if he has brothers and sisters, then for his mother is a sixth, after any bequest he may have made or debt. As for your parents and your children, you know not which of them is nearest to you in benefit. This is an obligation from God. Indeed, God is knowing and wise.
interpretation: The verse outlines the rules of inheritance for male and female children, as well as parents. It emphasizes the importance of fairness and justice in the distribution of inheritance, and the need to provide for both male and female children. The verse also acknowledges the role of parents in the upbringing of their children, and the right of mothers to a share of their child's inheritance. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of family and the responsibilities that come with it, and the obligation to follow God's commands. The verse also highlights God's knowledge and wisdom in setting these rules, and the importance of recognizing and accepting them.
orig: يوصيكم الله في أولادكم للذكر مثل حظ الأنثيين فإن كن نساء فوق اثنتين فلهن ثلثا ما ترك وإن كانت واحدة فلها النصف ولأبويه لكل واحد منهما السدس مما ترك إن كان له ولد فإن لم يكن له ولد وورثه أبواه فلأمه الثلث فإن كان له إخوة فلأمه السدس من بعد وصية يوصي بها أو دين آباؤكم وأبناؤكم لا تدرون أيهم أقرب لكم نفعا فريضة من الله إن الله كان عليما حكيما

translation: And for you is half of what your wives leave if they have no child. But if they have a child, then for you is a fourth of what they leave, after any bequest they may have made or debt. And for them is a fourth of what you leave if you have no child. But if you have a child, then for them is a third of what you leave, after any bequest you may have made or debt, except for a son; in that case, his share is a half of what you leave. And for his mothers is a sixth, if he has a brother or sister. But if they are more than that, then they share in a third, after any bequest you may have made or debt, in accordance with a decree from Allah. And Allah is all-knowing and forbearing.
interpretation: The verse outlines the rules of inheritance for different scenarios, with a focus on fairness and justice. The verse begins by stating that if a woman dies and leaves no children, her husband is entitled to half of her estate. However, if she has a child, the husband's share decreases to a fourth of the estate. Similarly, if a man dies and leaves no children, his wife is entitled to a fourth of his estate, but if he has a child, her share decreases to a third. The verse also stipulates that if a man dies and leaves a mother, she is entitled to a sixth of his estate, but if he has siblings, they share a third of his estate, after any debts or bequests have been made. The verse emphasizes the importance of fairness and justice in inheritance matters, and underscores the idea that these rules have been decreed by Allah, who is all-knowing and forbearing.
orig: ولكم نصف ما ترك أزواجكم إن لم يكن لهن ولد فإن كان لهن ولد فلكم الربع مما تركن من بعد وصية يوصين بها أو دين ولهن الربع مما تركتم إن لم يكن لكم ولد فإن كان لكم ولد فلهن الثمن مما تركتم من بعد وصية توصون بها أو دين وإن كان رجل يورث كلالة أو امرأة وله أخ أو أخت فلكل واحد منهما السدس فإن كانوا أكثر من ذلك فهم شركاء في الثلث من بعد وصية يوصى بها أو دين غير مضار وصية من الله والله عليم حليم

translation: That is the limit of Allah which He gives example to whom He wills among His servants. And whoever fears Allah and keeps his duty to Him, He will remit his sins from him and will enlarge his reward.
interpretation: The verse explains that the limits or boundaries set by Allah are given as examples to certain servants of Allah. The verse emphasizes the importance of fearing Allah and fulfilling one's duties towards Him. Those who do so will have their sins forgiven and their rewards increased. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of obedience and devotion to Allah and the great reward that awaits those who follow His path.
orig: تلك حدود الله ومن يطع الله ورسوله يدخله جنات تجري من تحتها الأنهار خالدين فيها وذلك الفوز العظيم

translation: And whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger and transgresses His boundaries - He will admit him into a fire, wherein he will abide eternally, and he will have a humiliating punishment.
interpretation: The verse warns of the consequence of disobeying Allah, His Messenger, and transgressing His boundaries. The punishment for such actions is being admitted into a fire where one will abide eternally and face a humiliating punishment. This verse serves as a reminder of the importance of obedience to Allah and His Messenger, and the severe consequences of disobedience.
orig: ومن يعص الله ورسوله ويتعد حدوده يدخله نارا خالدا فيها وله عذاب مهين

translation: And for those of you who commit lewdness, take four of you as witnesses against them. And if they testify, then confine the guilty women to the houses until death takes them or Allah ordains for them a way.
interpretation: This verse outlines the punishment for lewd or immoral behavior among women in a community. If such behavior is witnessed by four individuals, those witnesses are required to testify against the guilty parties. If the guilt is established through this testimony, the women are to be confined to their homes until either they pass away or God provides a way for them. This punishment serves as a deterrent for such behavior and emphasizes the importance of community accountability for maintaining moral standards.
orig: واللاتي يأتين الفاحشة من نسائكم فاستشهدوا عليهن أربعة منكم فإن شهدوا فأمسكوهن في البيوت حتى يتوفاهن الموت أو يجعل الله لهن سبيلا

translation: And if two men among you commit a lewd act, punish them both. But if they repent and rectify themselves, then leave them alone. Indeed, Allah is ever Returning (to mercy), All-Compassionate.
interpretation: The verse outlines the punishment for a specific sin (a lewd act) committed by two men from the Muslim community. The punishment is to be carried out by the community, emphasizing the importance of collective responsibility and justice. However, if the sinners repent and rectify themselves, the community is instructed to leave them alone, indicating the value of forgiveness and second chances in Islamic teachings. The verse ends by highlighting God's attribute of forgiveness and compassion, reminding the community of God's boundless mercy towards His creations.
orig: واللذان يأتيانها منكم فآذوهما فإن تابا وأصلحا فأعرضوا عنهما إن الله كان توابا رحيما

translation: Verily, the repentance is only for Allah for those who do evil in ignorance and then repent soon afterwards – indeed, it is they for whom Allah will turn in forgiveness, and Allah is ever Knowing and Wise.
interpretation: The verse explains the conditions under which repentance (tawbah) is accepted by Allah. It is for those who commit sins out of ignorance and then repent soon afterwards. The verse emphasizes the importance of seeking forgiveness and turning back to Allah as soon as possible after committing a sin. The verse also highlights Allah's attribute of being all-knowing (alim) and all-wise (hakeem), indicating that Allah's forgiveness is not arbitrary but is based on His wisdom and knowledge of the individual's circumstances and sincerity of repentance.
orig: إنما التوبة على الله للذين يعملون السوء بجهالة ثم يتوبون من قريب فأولئك يتوب الله عليهم وكان الله عليما حكيما

translation: And repentance is not for those who do evil deeds, until when death comes to one of them, he says, 'Indeed, I have repented now,' or those who die while they are disbelievers. Those - We have prepared for them a painful punishment.
interpretation: The verse highlights that true repentance is not a characteristic of those who commit evil deeds. Repentance is only accepted from those who sincerely regret their actions and turn towards righteousness. The verse emphasizes that death is a certainty, and it is then that the reality of one's actions becomes clear. Those who die as disbelievers or those who do not repent until the very end, will face a painful punishment. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of sincere repentance and the urgency to turn towards righteousness before it is too late.
orig: وليست التوبة للذين يعملون السيئات حتى إذا حضر أحدهم الموت قال إني تبت الآن ولا الذين يموتون وهم كفار أولئك أعتدنا لهم عذابا أليما

translation: O you who have believed, it is not lawful for you to inherit women by compulsion. And do not make difficulties for them in order to take [back] part of what you gave them unless they commit a clear immorality. And live with them in kindness. For if you dislike them - perhaps you dislike a thing and Allah makes therein much good.
interpretation: The verse outlines the rights and responsibilities of men towards their wives. It forbids men from inheriting women against their will or causing them difficulties in order to take back part of the dowry. Instead, men are instructed to treat their wives kindly and live with them in a good and fair manner. The verse acknowledges that there may be situations where a man may dislike his wife, but it reminds him that God may have placed much good in the situation. The verse emphasizes the importance of treating one's spouse with kindness, fairness, and respect, and avoiding actions that may harm or distress them.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا يحل لكم أن ترثوا النساء كرها ولا تعضلوهن لتذهبوا ببعض ما آتيتموهن إلا أن يأتين بفاحشة مبينة وعاشروهن بالمعروف فإن كرهتموهن فعسى أن تكرهوا شيئا ويجعل الله فيه خيرا كثيرا

translation: And if you wish to replace one wife with another and you have given one of them a qintar, do not take anything from it. Would you take it in disdain and a manifest sin?
interpretation: The verse speaks about the prohibition of taking back a gift or compensation given to a wife in the event of divorcing her and replacing her with another. The verse emphasizes the importance of treating all wives fairly and justly, and not taking advantage of them. The verse also highlights the negative consequences of taking back a gift in disdain and as a manifest sin. The verse serves as a reminder to be fair and just in all dealings and to avoid taking advantage of others in any situation.
orig: وإن أردتم استبدال زوج مكان زوج وآتيتم إحداهن قنطارا فلا تأخذوا منه شيئا أتأخذونه بهتانا وإثما مبينا

translation: And how can you take it when some of you have already gone ahead, making a covenant so stern?
interpretation: The verse is addressing a group of people who have taken an oath or covenant, but then some of them have gone back on their word and violated the agreement. The verse is questioning how they can expect to be successful or prosper when they have already broken a solemn promise. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of keeping one's word and upholding agreements, and the consequences of not doing so. It suggests that those who violate their covenants will face negative consequences, while those who honor their commitments will be rewarded.
orig: وكيف تأخذونه وقد أفضى بعضكم إلى بعض وأخذن منكم ميثاقا غليظا

translation: And do not marry those women whom your fathers married, except what has already occurred. Indeed, it was abomination and hateful, and an evil way.
interpretation: The verse prohibits marrying women who were previously married by one's father, except for cases where it has already occurred. The verse considers such marriages to be abomination, hateful, and a bad practice. The verse aims to prevent the continuation of such practices and to promote moral values and ethical behavior in society.
orig: ولا تنكحوا ما نكح آباؤكم من النساء إلا ما قد سلف إنه كان فاحشة ومقتا وساء سبيلا

translation: Forbidden to you are your mothers, and your daughters, and your sisters, and your paternal aunts, and your maternal aunts, and the daughters of your brother, and the daughters of your sister, and your mothers who have given suck to you, and your foster-sisters, and the mothers of your wives, and your step-daughters who are in your guardianship, (born) of your wives to whom you have gone in, but if you have not gone in to them, there is no blame on you (in marrying their daughters), and the wives of your sons who are of your own loins, and that you should have two sisters together, except what has already past; surely Allah is Forgiving, Merciful.
interpretation: The verse outlines the degrees of female relatives that are forbidden for marriage, including mothers, daughters, sisters, aunts, and step-daughters. The verse emphasizes the importance of maintaining familial relationships and avoiding any form of incest. The exception is made for foster-sisters and the daughters of wives from previous relationships, as long as there has been no sexual contact. The verse also highlights Allah's forgiveness and mercy towards those who make mistakes and repent.
orig: حرمت عليكم أمهاتكم وبناتكم وأخواتكم وعماتكم وخالاتكم وبنات الأخ وبنات الأخت وأمهاتكم اللاتي أرضعنكم وأخواتكم من الرضاعة وأمهات نسائكم وربائبكم اللاتي في حجوركم من نسائكم اللاتي دخلتم بهن فإن لم تكونوا دخلتم بهن فلا جناح عليكم وحلائل أبنائكم الذين من أصلابكم وأن تجمعوا بين الأختين إلا ما قد سلف إن الله كان غفورا رحيما

translation: And married women except those whom your right hands possess are forbidden to you; but those of whom you seek content (by reciting religious verses) are lawful for you, provided that you seek them with means of wealth and not through fornication. So when you have enjoyed them by reciting religious verses, then give them their prescribed time (due to them according to Islamic law), but there is no blame on you concerning that which you mutually agree after the prescribed time. Surely, Allah is All-Knowing, Wise.
interpretation: This verse outlines the rules of permissible and forbidden relationships for Muslim men. It forbids men from having sexual relationships with married women, except those who are their slaves or captives. However, men are allowed to have relationships with women through the practice of mut'ah, or temporary marriage, where a man gives a woman a dower and they agree on a specific time period for the relationship. After this time period, the man is required to pay the woman a prescribed amount of money. The verse emphasizes the importance of not engaging in sexual relationships outside of these bounds, and reminds Muslims that Allah is all-knowing and wise, and that following these rules is a way to seek His pleasure and avoid His wrath.
orig: والمحصنات من النساء إلا ما ملكت أيمانكم كتاب الله عليكم وأحل لكم ما وراء ذلكم أن تبتغوا بأموالكم محصنين غير مسافحين فما استمتعتم به منهن فآتوهن أجورهن فريضة ولا جناح عليكم فيما تراضيتم به من بعد الفريضة إن الله كان عليما حكيما

translation: And whoever among you cannot afford to marry free, believing women, then (let him marry) from the believing maids whom your right hands possess. And Allah knows best your faith: so (marry) the one who is righteous among them, and the one who is pious among your maids. And give them their wages, the agreed-on wages, and do not force them to prostitution, so that you may take (back) part of what you have given them, unless they commit a clear immorality. Then, if they commit immorality, they shall receive from you half of the punishment that is prescribed for free women. This is for him among you who fears immorality. But if you are patient, it is better for you. And Allah is Forgiving, Merciful.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the permissibility of marriage to slaves or maidservants, known as 'maidens whom your right hands possess', for those who cannot afford to marry free, believing women. The verse emphasizes the importance of treating these women fairly and with respect, giving them their wages and not forcing them into prostitution. If a maiden commits immorality, she will receive half of the punishment prescribed for free women. The verse encourages patience and self-restraint, reminding that God is Forgiving and Merciful.
orig: ومن لم يستطع منكم طولا أن ينكح المحصنات المؤمنات فمن ما ملكت أيمانكم من فتياتكم المؤمنات والله أعلم بإيمانكم بعضكم من بعض فانكحوهن بإذن أهلهن وآتوهن أجورهن بالمعروف محصنات غير مسافحات ولا متخذات أخدان فإذا أحصن فإن أتين بفاحشة فعليهن نصف ما على المحصنات من العذاب ذلك لمن خشي العنت منكم وأن تصبروا خير لكم والله غفور رحيم

translation: God wants to make clear to you and guide you to the ways of those before you, and to forgive you. And God is all-knowing, wise.
interpretation: The verse speaks about God's intention to guide and clarify the path for the believers by showing them the examples of those who came before them. The verse also highlights God's willingness to forgive and His all-encompassing knowledge and wisdom. The verse serves as a reminder of God's mercy and guidance, encouraging the believers to reflect on the lessons from the past and to seek forgiveness for their sins.
orig: يريد الله ليبين لكم ويهديكم سنن الذين من قبلكم ويتوب عليكم والله عليم حكيم

translation: And Allah wants to turn to you (in forgiveness), and wants you to turn to Him, and wants you to strive hard in His cause. And He wants to forgive you. And Allah is the All-Knower, All-Wise.
interpretation: The verse highlights Allah's desire for forgiveness and guidance for the believers. It emphasizes the importance of turning to Allah and striving hard in His cause. The verse encourages believers to seek Allah's forgiveness and to work towards His cause. The verse serves as a reminder that Allah is all-knowing and all-wise and that His commands and desires are for the ultimate benefit of the believers.
orig: والله يريد أن يتوب عليكم ويريد الذين يتبعون الشهوات أن تميلوا ميلا عظيما

translation: Allah intends to lighten your burden, for man was created weak.
interpretation: The verse highlights God's compassion and mercy towards human beings. It emphasizes that God wants to alleviate the burden of His believers, as He recognizes the inherent weakness of human beings. This verse serves as a reminder of God's compassion and willingness to help His believers in their time of need.
orig: يريد الله أن يخفف عنكم وخلق الإنسان ضعيفا

translation: O you who have believed, do not consume one another's wealth unjustly but only [in lawful] business by mutual consent. And do not kill yourselves [or one another]. Indeed, Allah is to you ever Merciful.
interpretation: The verse addresses the believers and commands them not to consume each other's wealth unjustly, but only in legitimate business transactions based on mutual consent. It also forbids them from killing one another. The verse emphasizes the importance of fairness and justice in economic transactions and the sanctity of human life. The verse serves as a reminder to the believers to uphold these values and to avoid harming one another. It highlights the mercy of God towards the believers, encouraging them to show mercy and compassion towards one another.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تأكلوا أموالكم بينكم بالباطل إلا أن تكون تجارة عن تراض منكم ولا تقتلوا أنفسكم إن الله كان بكم رحيما

translation: And whoever does that, being unjust and wronging [others], then We will drive him into a Fire. And that, for Allah, is [always] easy.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the punishment for those who commit unjust and wrongful acts. It warns that those who engage in such behavior will be driven into a Fire, indicating the severe consequences of their actions. The verse emphasizes that this punishment is not difficult for Allah to implement, highlighting the power and authority of God. The verse serves as a reminder that no one can escape the consequences of their actions and that God's punishment for unjust behavior is both just and inevitable.
orig: ومن يفعل ذلك عدوانا وظلما فسوف نصليه نارا وكان ذلك على الله يسيرا

translation: If you avoid the major sins which you are forbidden from, We will remit your (minor) sins, and admit you to a noble entrance (Paradise).
interpretation: The verse offers a conditional promise of forgiveness and admission to Paradise for those who abstain from committing major sins. By avoiding the major sins, one's minor sins will be forgiven, and they will be granted entry into Paradise through a noble and honorable gate. This verse highlights the importance of avoiding sin and emphasizes the significance of good deeds in achieving forgiveness and attaining a high status in the afterlife.
orig: إن تجتنبوا كبائر ما تنهون عنه نكفر عنكم سيئاتكم وندخلكم مدخلا كريما

translation: And do not covet that by which Allah has made some of you exceed others. For men is a share of what they have earned, and for women is a share of what they have earned. And ask Allah of His bounty. Indeed Allah is ever, of all things, Knowing.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of being content with one's own circumstances and not being envious of what others have been given by Allah. It teaches that both men and women have a share of what they have earned and that they should ask Allah for His bounty. The verse serves as a reminder that Allah is aware of all things and that everything happens according to His knowledge and wisdom.
orig: ولا تتمنوا ما فضل الله به بعضكم على بعض للرجال نصيب مما اكتسبوا وللنساء نصيب مما اكتسبن واسألوا الله من فضله إن الله كان بكل شيء عليما

translation: And for every one We have appointed a nasl (a helpers) from among the Shaitans (devils) to be a qarin (intimate companion) to him.
interpretation: The verse highlights the reality that every human being has a devilish companion who constantly tries to lead them astray from the right path. This companion, who is appointed by God, is always present and eager to misguide people into committing sins and wrongdoings. This verse serves as a reminder for people to be vigilant and to constantly seek God's guidance and protection from the whispers and temptations of the devil.
orig: ولكل جعلنا موالي مما ترك الوالدان والأقربون والذين عقدت أيمانكم فآتوهم نصيبهم إن الله كان على كل شيء شهيدا

translation: Men are the protectors and maintainers of women, as Allah has given the one more (strength) than the other, and they support them from their means. Therefore the righteous women are devoutly obedient, (and) guard in (the husband's) absence what Allah would have them guard. As to those women on whose part you see ill-conduct, admonish them (first), (next), refuse to share their beds, (and last) beat them (lightly); but if they return to obedience, seek not against them means (of annoyance). Surely, Allah is ever Most High, Most Great.
interpretation: The verse outlines the roles and responsibilities of men and women in a marriage. Men are considered to be the protectors and maintainers of women, and are expected to support them financially. In return, righteous women are expected to be obedient and guard what is entrusted to them in their husbands' absence. If a woman is disobedient, the verse outlines a series of steps that can be taken to correct her behavior, including admonishment, refusal of sexual relations, and light physical punishment. However, if she repents, her husband should not seek further means of annoyance. The verse emphasizes the importance of obedience and respect in a marriage, and the role of men as providers and protectors.
orig: الرجال قوامون على النساء بما فضل الله بعضهم على بعض وبما أنفقوا من أموالهم فالصالحات قانتات حافظات للغيب بما حفظ الله واللاتي تخافون نشوزهن فعظوهن واهجروهن في المضاجع واضربوهن فإن أطعنكم فلا تبغوا عليهن سبيلا إن الله كان عليا كبيرا

translation: But if you fear a breach between them, then send a committee from among them, and a committee from among them. If they both desire reconciliation, Allah will make it between them. Indeed, Allah is ever Knowing and Acquainted.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the steps to be taken if there is a fear of a breach or split between two groups or parties. The suggested solution is to send a committee or group of representatives from each side to mediate and find a resolution. If both parties are willing to reconcile and work towards peace, then God will make a way for them. The verse emphasizes the importance of reconciliation and the role of the community in resolving conflicts. It highlights God's knowledge and awareness of the situation, indicating that He is the ultimate source of guidance and resolution.
orig: وإن خفتم شقاق بينهما فابعثوا حكما من أهله وحكما من أهلها إن يريدا إصلاحا يوفق الله بينهما إن الله كان عليما خبيرا

translation: And worship Allah and associate nothing with Him, and to parents do good, and to relatives, orphans, the needy, the near neighbor, the neighbor farther away, the companion at your side, the traveler, and what your right hands possess. Indeed, Allah does not like those who are self-deluding and boastful.
interpretation: The verse outlines the various groups of people that Muslims should treat with kindness, respect, and generosity, including parents, relatives, the needy, neighbors, travelers, and slaves. The verse emphasizes the importance of avoiding shirk (associating partners with Allah) and encourages Muslims to show compassion and generosity towards all people, regardless of their status or relationship to the believer. The verse also warns against self-delusion and boastfulness, which are seen as unacceptable traits in the eyes of Allah. Overall, the verse highlights the importance of treating others with kindness, fairness, and respect, and avoiding arrogance, self-delusion, and other negative traits.
orig: واعبدوا الله ولا تشركوا به شيئا وبالوالدين إحسانا وبذي القربى واليتامى والمساكين والجار ذي القربى والجار الجنب والصاحب بالجنب وابن السبيل وما ملكت أيمانكم إن الله لا يحب من كان مختالا فخورا

translation: Those who are stingy and enjoin stinginess on people and hide what Allah has given them of His bounty, and we have prepared for the disbelievers a humiliating punishment.
interpretation: The verse speaks about those who are stingy and encourage others to be stingy as well, while hiding the blessings that Allah has given them. The verse highlights the hypocrisy of these people and their lack of gratitude for the blessings they have received. The verse also mentions that a humiliating punishment has been prepared for the disbelievers. This verse serves as a reminder of the importance of being generous and grateful for the blessings that we have received, and the consequences of being stingy and ungrateful. It also serves as a warning to the disbelievers of the punishment that awaits them.
orig: الذين يبخلون ويأمرون الناس بالبخل ويكتمون ما آتاهم الله من فضله وأعتدنا للكافرين عذابا مهينا

translation: And those who spend their wealth to be seen by people, and do not believe in God nor in the Last Day - and whoever has Satan as a companion, then indeed, he is a companion of blaze.
interpretation: The verse speaks about those who spend their wealth only to be seen by people and not out of faith in God or the Day of Judgment. The verse highlights the superficiality and insincerity of their actions. The verse warns that those who associate with Satan will suffer dire consequences, as they are companions of the blaze (Hellfire). The verse serves as a reminder that acts of worship and charity should be done solely for the pleasure of God, not for the praise or recognition of people.
orig: والذين ينفقون أموالهم رئاء الناس ولا يؤمنون بالله ولا باليوم الآخر ومن يكن الشيطان له قرينا فساء قرينا

translation: And what is (the matter) with them, that they believe not in Allah and the Last Day, and they spend not (in charity) out of what Allah hath given them?
interpretation: The verse questions the disbelievers for not believing in Allah and the Day of Judgment, and for not spending in charity from the provision that Allah has given them. The verse highlights the importance of faith and good deeds, and the failure of the disbelievers to recognize and act on these fundamental aspects of the Islamic teachings.
orig: وماذا عليهم لو آمنوا بالله واليوم الآخر وأنفقوا مما رزقهم الله وكان الله بهم عليما

translation: Indeed, Allah does not wrong even the weight of an atom, and if it is a good deed, He multiplies it and gives from His self a great reward.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes Allah's justice and fairness, stating that Allah does not wrong even the weight of an atom. This implies that Allah is aware of and will reward every good deed, no matter how small. The verse goes on to say that if it is a good deed, Allah multiplies it and gives a great reward from Himself. This highlights the abundance of Allah's mercy and generosity towards those who do good. The verse serves as a motivation for believers to perform good deeds, assuring them that their efforts will not be in vain and that they will be rewarded abundantly by Allah.
orig: إن الله لا يظلم مثقال ذرة وإن تك حسنة يضاعفها ويؤت من لدنه أجرا عظيما

translation: But how (will it be) when We bring from every people a witness, and We bring you (O Muhammad) against these as a witness?
interpretation: The verse speaks about the Day of Judgment and the role of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) as a witness against his people. The verse emphasizes that on the Day of Judgment, God will bring a witness from every nation to testify against them. At the same time, the Prophet Muhammad will be brought as a witness against his own people. The verse serves as a reminder of the gravity of the Day of Judgment and the importance of belief and righteous actions. It also highlights the role of the Prophet Muhammad as a guide and a warner for his people, and the significance of following his teachings and guidance.
orig: فكيف إذا جئنا من كل أمة بشهيد وجئنا بك على هؤلاء شهيدا

translation: That day, those who disbelieved and disobeyed the messenger will wish that the earth would swallow them up, and they will not hide from God any of their words.
interpretation: The verse describes the fate of those who disbelieved and disobeyed the messenger on the Day of Judgment. They will regret their actions and wish that the earth would swallow them up, but it will be too late. They will not be able to hide any of their words from God, who knows everything. The verse serves as a warning to those who reject the message of the prophet and encourages them to repent and follow the right path before it is too late.
orig: يومئذ يود الذين كفروا وعصوا الرسول لو تسوى بهم الأرض ولا يكتمون الله حديثا

translation: O you who have believed, do not approach prayer while you are intoxicated until you know what you are saying, nor while in a state of janabah, except those passing through [a place of prayer], until you have washed [your whole body]. And if you are ill or on a journey or one of you comes from the place of relieving himself or you have contacted women and do not find water, then seek clean earth and wipe over your faces and hands with some of it. Indeed, Allah is ever Pardoning and Forgiving.
interpretation: The verse provides guidelines for Muslims regarding their prayer and cleanliness. It forbids approaching prayer while intoxicated or in a state of janabah (impurity after sexual intercourse) unless one is passing through a place of prayer. It emphasizes the importance of being in a state of cleanliness and clarity of mind during prayer. For those who cannot find water for ablution, the verse provides an alternative by wiping over the face and hands with clean earth. The verse highlights God's forgiveness and pardon for those who strive to follow these guidelines, even in difficult circumstances.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تقربوا الصلاة وأنتم سكارى حتى تعلموا ما تقولون ولا جنبا إلا عابري سبيل حتى تغتسلوا وإن كنتم مرضى أو على سفر أو جاء أحد منكم من الغائط أو لامستم النساء فلم تجدوا ماء فتيمموا صعيدا طيبا فامسحوا بوجوهكم وأيديكم إن الله كان عفوا غفورا

translation: Have you not seen those who were given a portion of the Scripture, buying error and desiring that you too might go astray?
interpretation: The verse addresses the Prophet Muhammad and questions him if he has seen those who have received a portion of the Scripture (the Jewish and Christian people) and yet they buy into error and misguidance. They not only follow falsehood but also wish for others, including the Prophet Muhammad and his followers, to go astray as well. The verse criticizes these people for their rejection of the truth and their active efforts to mislead others, revealing their hypocrisy and lack of faith.
orig: ألم تر إلى الذين أوتوا نصيبا من الكتاب يشترون الضلالة ويريدون أن تضلوا السبيل

translation: But Allah is sufficient as a Knower of your enemies, and Allah is sufficient as a Supporter, and Allah is sufficient as a Helper.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the all-knowing and all-powerful nature of Allah, who is sufficient as a protector and helper for the believers. The verse is a reminder that Allah is aware of the enemies of the believers and will provide them with the necessary support and aid. It is a source of comfort and assurance for the believers, reminding them that they do not need to rely on anyone but Allah, who is sufficient as their protector and helper.
orig: والله أعلم بأعدائكم وكفى بالله وليا وكفى بالله نصيرا

translation: Of those who have been given the Scripture, there are some who would drag you back to unbelief after you have believed, out of envy on their own account, even after the truth has become clear to them. So forgive and forbear till Allah may give His command. Surely Allah has power over all things.
interpretation: The verse speaks about a group of people who have received the Scripture (Jews and Christians) but they try to mislead the believers away from their faith due to their own envy. Despite the truth being clear to them, they still persist in their attempts to misguide the believers. The verse advises the believers to forgive and forbear, and to leave the matter to God, who has the power to deal with them as He wills. This verse highlights the importance of maintaining one's faith in the face of adversity and the importance of patience and forgiveness in dealing with those who seek to harm us.
orig: من الذين هادوا يحرفون الكلم عن مواضعه ويقولون سمعنا وعصينا واسمع غير مسمع وراعنا ليا بألسنتهم وطعنا في الدين ولو أنهم قالوا سمعنا وأطعنا واسمع وانظرنا لكان خيرا لهم وأقوم ولكن لعنهم الله بكفرهم فلا يؤمنون إلا قليلا
