orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا آمنوا بالله ورسوله والكتاب الذي نزل على رسوله والكتاب الذي أنزل من قبل ومن يكفر بالله وملائكته وكتبه ورسله واليوم الآخر فقد ضل ضلالا بعيدا

translation: Indeed, those who have believed then disbelieved, then believed, then disbelieved, then increased in disbelief - upon them shall be Allah's wrath, and for them is a severe punishment.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the grave consequences for those who repeatedly believe and disbelieve in God. The repetition of their disbelief indicates a deep-seated rejection of faith, and as a result, they are subjected to God's wrath and a severe punishment. The verse serves as a warning to those who waver in their faith and emphasizes the importance of maintaining a steadfast belief in God.
orig: إن الذين آمنوا ثم كفروا ثم آمنوا ثم كفروا ثم ازدادوا كفرا لم يكن الله ليغفر لهم ولا ليهديهم سبيلا

translation: Warn the hypocrites that they will have a painful punishment.
interpretation: The verse addresses the hypocrites, who outwardly profess their faith but inwardly harbor disbelief. They are warned of a painful punishment that awaits them. The verse emphasizes the certainty of the punishment and serves as a warning to those who claim to be believers but do not act accordingly. It reminds them of the importance of sincerity and authenticity in their faith.
orig: بشر المنافقين بأن لهم عذابا أليما

translation: Those who take the disbelievers as allies instead of the believers, they seek might through them. Indeed, might belongs to Allah entirely.
interpretation: The verse warns against forming alliances with disbelievers instead of believers, and seeking their help and support in order to gain power and prestige. The verse emphasizes that true might and power belong solely to God, and that those who seek it through unlawful means will ultimately fail. The verse serves as a reminder to Muslims to remain loyal to their faith and community, and not to seek help or support from those who do not believe in Islam. It also serves as a warning to those who oppose Islam, that their power and might is temporary and will not protect them from God's ultimate power and judgment.
orig: الذين يتخذون الكافرين أولياء من دون المؤمنين أيبتغون عندهم العزة فإن العزة لله جميعا

translation: It has already been revealed to you in the Book that when you hear the verses of Allah being disbelieved and ridiculed, then do not sit with them until they engage in a conversation other than that. Indeed, you will be similar to them. Indeed, Allah will gather the hypocrites and the disbelievers all together in Hell.
interpretation: The verse advises believers on how to respond when they encounter disbelievers who reject and mock the verses of Allah. The verse commands the believers not to sit with them and engage in conversation that is not related to the disbelief and mockery, as this may lead to the believers becoming like them. The verse emphasizes the severe consequences of disbelief and ridicule, as both hypocrites and disbelievers will be gathered together in Hell. The verse serves as a warning to the believers to be cautious of the company they keep and to stand firm in their belief in the face of disbelief and mockery.
orig: وقد نزل عليكم في الكتاب أن إذا سمعتم آيات الله يكفر بها ويستهزأ بها فلا تقعدوا معهم حتى يخوضوا في حديث غيره إنكم إذا مثلهم إن الله جامع المنافقين والكافرين في جهنم جميعا

translation: Those who wait on you (O Muhammad) will surely, if you gain a victory from Allah, say: 'Were we not with you?' And if the disbelievers have a success, they say (to them): 'Did we not gain the mastery over you, and did we not protect you from the believers?' Allah will judge between you on the Day of Resurrection. And Allah will not give the disbelievers over the believers a way (to overcome them).'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the behavior of two groups of people: those who wait and observe the outcome of events, and the disbelievers who claim superiority over the believers. The verse highlights the hypocrisy of the first group, who will try to claim credit for any victory, even though they did not participate in it. The verse also criticizes the disbelievers for their boasts and their attempts to dominate the believers. The verse emphasizes that Allah will be the ultimate judge on the Day of Resurrection and will not allow the disbelievers to prevail over the believers. The verse serves as a reminder to the believers to remain steadfast in their faith and to not be swayed by the false claims of their enemies.
orig: الذين يتربصون بكم فإن كان لكم فتح من الله قالوا ألم نكن معكم وإن كان للكافرين نصيب قالوا ألم نستحوذ عليكم ونمنعكم من المؤمنين فالله يحكم بينكم يوم القيامة ولن يجعل الله للكافرين على المؤمنين سبيلا

translation: Indeed, the hypocrites [think to] deceive Allah, but He is deceiving them. And when they stand for prayer, they stand lazily, showing [themselves off], to the people, and they do not remember Allah except a little.
interpretation: The verse highlights the hypocrisy of certain individuals who pretend to be religious and pious, but in reality, they are far from it. They try to deceive Allah, but Allah is aware of their deceit and is deceiving them, meaning that they are only harming themselves. When they stand for prayer, they do so in a lazy and insincere manner, and their primary concern is to be seen by the people, rather than to genuinely worship Allah. They remember Allah only a little, indicating their lack of sincerity and true devotion.
orig: إن المنافقين يخادعون الله وهو خادعهم وإذا قاموا إلى الصلاة قاموا كسالى يراءون الناس ولا يذكرون الله إلا قليلا

translation: Skipping to and fro between them, (the disbelievers are) unaware of their death, even if eerstwhile you (Muhammad) converse with one of them, he is absorbed in this worldly life (and) unaware of his death. And indeed, if (due to) Allah's bounty, he gives (someone) a taste of (the blessings of) His provision, he becomes stingy, and turns away (from the remembrance of Allah). Indeed, man is ungrateful.
interpretation: The verse describes the heedlessness of the disbelievers towards the reality of death and the fleeting nature of worldly pleasures. They are depicted as moving aimlessly between different things, unaware that their death is near, even when they are in the presence of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). The verse highlights the ingratitude of humans, who, when blessed with Allah's provisions, become stingy and forgetful of their Creator. The verse serves as a reminder to be mindful of the transient nature of worldly blessings, to avoid being ungrateful and stingy, and to remember Allah in all circumstances.
orig: مذبذبين بين ذلك لا إلى هؤلاء ولا إلى هؤلاء ومن يضلل الله فلن تجد له سبيلا

translation: O you who believe! do not take the unbelievers for friends instead of the believers; do you desire that you should give to Allah a manifest proof against yourselves?
interpretation: The verse warns believers against taking unbelievers as friends or allies over believers. It questions the intention of those who would do so, asking if they want to provide clear evidence against themselves and go against God's will. The verse emphasizes the importance of maintaining strong ties with the believers and being loyal to the community of believers, rather than siding with those who reject or oppose the faith.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تتخذوا الكافرين أولياء من دون المؤمنين أتريدون أن تجعلوا لله عليكم سلطانا مبينا

translation: Indeed, the hypocrites will be in the lowest depths of the Fire, and you will not find for them a helper.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the fate of the hypocrites, who outwardly profess faith but inwardly harbor disbelief. They will be in the lowest depths of the Fire, which indicates the severity of their punishment. The verse emphasizes that they will have no helper or protector to save them from their fate. The verse serves as a warning to those who claim to be believers but do not act according to their faith, reminding them that hypocrisy is a grave sin that will not go unpunished.
orig: إن المنافقين في الدرك الأسفل من النار ولن تجد لهم نصيرا

translation: Except for those who repent, correct themselves, hold fast to God, and dedicate their religion to God: such will be with the believers. And God will grant the believers a great reward.
interpretation: The verse offers a way for people to avoid the punishment mentioned earlier in the Qur'an. It outlines the steps that people should take in order to be saved from the punishment and to be with the believers. These steps include repentance, correction of actions, holding fast to God, and dedicating one's religion solely to God. The verse promises a great reward for those who follow this path and become believers. This verse serves as a message of hope and a call for repentance and submission to God.
orig: إلا الذين تابوا وأصلحوا واعتصموا بالله وأخلصوا دينهم لله فأولئك مع المؤمنين وسوف يؤت الله المؤمنين أجرا عظيما

translation: What will Allah do with the punishment for you if you believe and express gratitude? And Allah is Ever Appreciative, All-Knowing.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the relationship between divine punishment, gratitude, and faith. It suggests that if people believe in Allah and express gratitude, they will be protected from the punishment. The verse emphasizes that Allah is Appreciative and All-Knowing, indicating that He is aware of the intentions and actions of His servants. The verse encourages people to cultivate a sense of gratitude and faith in Allah, and to trust in His mercy and justice.
orig: ما يفعل الله بعذابكم إن شكرتم وآمنتم وكان الله شاكرا عليما

translation: Allah does not like the public mention of evil except by one who has been wronged. And Allah is Hearing and Knowing.
interpretation: The verse highlights that Allah does not approve of the public mention of evil or wrongdoing, except for the person who has been wronged. This emphasizes the importance of avoiding the spreading of negative speech and gossip. However, it also acknowledges that there may be situations where speaking out about wrongdoing is necessary, especially if one has been personally wronged. The verse ends by emphasizing that Allah is all-hearing and all-knowing, reminding us that He is aware of all that is said and done.
orig: لا يحب الله الجهر بالسوء من القول إلا من ظلم وكان الله سميعا عليما

translation: If you disclose good, or conceal it, or pardon an evil, then surely Allah is Pardoning, Powerful.
interpretation: The verse highlights the different ways in which people can respond to a situation where they may choose to disclose or conceal a good deed, or forgive an evil committed by someone else. Regardless of the choice made, the verse emphasizes that God is always forgiving and powerful, indicating that God's mercy and forgiveness are always available to those who seek it. The verse encourages people to strive for good deeds and to forgive, knowing that God's power and mercy are greater than any human shortcomings or mistakes.
orig: إن تبدوا خيرا أو تخفوه أو تعفوا عن سوء فإن الله كان عفوا قديرا

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve in Allah and His messengers and desire to discriminate between Allah and His messengers and say, 'We believe in some and disbelieve in some' and desire to take a way in between -
interpretation: The verse highlights the rejection of disbelievers towards Allah and His messengers, and their desire to discriminate between them. It emphasizes their false claim of believing in some messengers while rejecting others, and their attempt to create a path that is separate from the belief in all of Allah's messengers. This verse serves as a warning to those who try to distort the unity of the message brought by the prophets, and affirms that such behavior is a rejection of the fundamental principles of faith.
orig: إن الذين يكفرون بالله ورسله ويريدون أن يفرقوا بين الله ورسله ويقولون نؤمن ببعض ونكفر ببعض ويريدون أن يتخذوا بين ذلك سبيلا

translation: Those are indeed the disbelievers, the definitive ones, and We have prepared for the disbelievers a humiliating punishment.
interpretation: The verse categorically states that certain people are disbelievers and emphasizes the certainty of their fate. The punishment prepared for them is described as humiliating, which indicates that it will not only be severe but also a source of shame and disgrace. The verse serves as a warning to those who reject faith and emphasizes the serious consequences of disbelief.
orig: أولئك هم الكافرون حقا وأعتدنا للكافرين عذابا مهينا

translation: And those who believe in Allah and His messengers and do not differentiate between any of them - those will be given their rewards, and Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the reward for those who believe in Allah and His messengers and do not differentiate or discriminate between any of them. These individuals will receive their rewards from Allah, who is Forgiving and Merciful. The verse emphasizes the importance of believing in all of Allah's messengers, without discrimination or bias towards any one of them, and the reward that awaits those who do so.
orig: والذين آمنوا بالله ورسله ولم يفرقوا بين أحد منهم أولئك سوف يؤتيهم أجورهم وكان الله غفورا رحيما

translation: The people of the scripture ask you to bring down a book from the sky to them. They asked Moses for greater things than that, and they said, 'Show us Allah openly.' So the punishment overtook them for their wrongdoing. Then they took the calf [for worship] after clear proofs had come to them. So We forgave them for that, and We gave Moses clear authority.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the people of the scripture asking the Prophet Muhammad to bring down a book from the sky. This request is similar to the one made by the followers of Moses, who asked for greater signs and proofs. However, when they saw the punishment that came upon them because of their wrongdoing, they took the calf for worship. Despite this, God forgave them and gave Moses clear authority. The verse emphasizes the importance of accepting and following the signs and proofs that God sends, and the consequences of rejecting them or demanding more proofs as a form of disbelief.
orig: يسألك أهل الكتاب أن تنزل عليهم كتابا من السماء فقد سألوا موسى أكبر من ذلك فقالوا أرنا الله جهرة فأخذتهم الصاعقة بظلمهم ثم اتخذوا العجل من بعد ما جاءتهم البينات فعفونا عن ذلك وآتينا موسى سلطانا مبينا

translation: And We made above them a mountain (of Our promise) and We said to them: 'Enter the gate prostrating (to your Lord),' and We said to them: 'Do not transgress the Sabbath,' and We took from them a solemn covenant.
interpretation: This verse speaks about God's commandments to a group of people, emphasizing the importance of obedience and respect for divine laws. The verse mentions that God made a mountain above them as a symbol of His promise and power. God commanded them to enter the gate while prostrating, showing their submission and devotion to their Lord. They were also forbidden to transgress the Sabbath, indicating the significance of honoring the sacred days of rest. Furthermore, God took a solemn covenant from them, highlighting the importance of their commitment and accountability. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of obedience and respect for divine laws, and the consequences of disobedience and transgression.
orig: ورفعنا فوقهم الطور بميثاقهم وقلنا لهم ادخلوا الباب سجدا وقلنا لهم لا تعدوا في السبت وأخذنا منهم ميثاقا غليظا

translation: For breaking their covenant, and rejecting the signs of Allah, and killing the prophets unjustly, and saying: Our hearts are wrapped (against every reminder); nay, but Allah set a seal on them because of their disbelief, so they believe not but a little.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the punishment of those who broke their covenant with God, rejected His signs, unjustly killed the prophets, and claimed that their hearts were sealed against any reminder of the truth. The verse emphasizes the hardness of their hearts and their rejection of God's guidance. The verse serves as a reminder of the consequences of breaking one's covenant with God, rejecting His signs, and harming His messengers. The verse also highlights the severity of their disbelief and the fact that they only believe in a small amount, indicating their rejection of the truth and their stubbornness in their disbelief.
orig: فبما نقضهم ميثاقهم وكفرهم بآيات الله وقتلهم الأنبياء بغير حق وقولهم قلوبنا غلف بل طبع الله عليها بكفرهم فلا يؤمنون إلا قليلا

translation: And for their disbelief and speaking against Mary with a great slander.
interpretation: The verse refers to the punishment of a group of people for their disbelief in God and their slander against Mary, the mother of Jesus. The verse emphasizes the gravity of their actions by describing their slander as 'great'. The verse serves as a reminder of the severe consequences of disbelief and speaking falsely against innocent people, particularly those who are revered in Islam.
orig: وبكفرهم وقولهم على مريم بهتانا عظيما

translation: And they say, 'We have killed the Messiah, Jesus, son of Mary, the messenger of Allah.' And they did not kill him, nor did they crucify him; but it was made to appear so to them. And indeed, those who differ in this matter - there is no knowledge of it for them, except conjecture. And they did not kill him with certainty.
interpretation: The verse addresses the denial of Jesus' crucifixion and subsequent death, and the belief that he was killed and crucified. The verse categorically denies these claims, stating that Jesus was not killed or crucified, but that it was made to appear so. The verse highlights the uncertainty and conjecture surrounding this matter, emphasizing that those who differ in opinion have no knowledge of it. The verse serves to correct the false belief in Jesus' death and to assert the truth of his survival and ultimate ascension to God.
orig: وقولهم إنا قتلنا المسيح عيسى ابن مريم رسول الله وما قتلوه وما صلبوه ولكن شبه لهم وإن الذين اختلفوا فيه لفي شك منه ما لهم به من علم إلا اتباع الظن وما قتلوه يقينا

translation: But indeed, Allah has elevated him to Himself. And indeed, Allah is Exalted in Might and Wise.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the exaltation of a specific individual by God. While the exact identity of this person is not mentioned in the verse, the context suggests that it refers to a prophet or a righteous servant of God who has been taken up to heaven. The verse emphasizes the greatness and power of God, who is described as 'Exalted in Might' and 'Wise'. The verse may serve as a source of hope and comfort for believers, reminding them that God has the power to exalt and reward those who are close to Him.
orig: بل رفعه الله إليه وكان الله عزيزا حكيما

translation: And indeed, among the People of the Book (Jews and Christians) are those who believe in him (Muhammad SAW) before his death and on the Day of Resurrection will be witnesses over them.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the presence of believers among the People of the Book (Jews and Christians) who will believe in Prophet Muhammad (SAW) before his death and will serve as witnesses for them on the Day of Resurrection. This verse highlights the significance of faith and belief in the true prophets of God, and the ultimate accountability of all people on the Day of Judgment. It also emphasizes the continuity of the message of monotheism and the unity of God in the Abrahamic traditions.
orig: وإن من أهل الكتاب إلا ليؤمنن به قبل موته ويوم القيامة يكون عليهم شهيدا

translation: Because of the wrongdoing of those who were given the Scripture, We have prevented them from certain good things, except as a punishment for them: they have persisted in disobedience, and have repeatedly transgressed.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the punishment of those who were given the Scripture (Jews and Christians) due to their wrongdoing and transgression. The verse mentions that some good things were made unlawful for them as a punishment for their disobedience, and they continued to persist in their ways. The verse serves as a reminder of the consequences of disobedience and transgression, and that those who persist in their sinful ways will face punishment.
orig: فبظلم من الذين هادوا حرمنا عليهم طيبات أحلت لهم وبصدهم عن سبيل الله كثيرا

translation: And their Lord took them in task for what they used to do, and was severe in retribution. And they had taken to them the wealth of people in vanity, and that which they used to build, We have made it as rubble of scattered ruins. And of them there are some who hears the command of his Lord and they, before the punishment comes to them, respond. So We will put on their faces ease, until the time when they meet their appointed term. And others there are who are unjustly rebellious. And the fire will be their shelter. If they ask for water, they will be given water like molten brass that will scald their faces. How evil is the drink and how evil is the resting place.
interpretation: The verse describes the punishment of a group of people who were unjust and took the wealth of others in vanity. Their Lord punished them severely for their actions. The verse highlights the consequences of unjust actions and the certainty of God's punishment. The verse also mentions that some of them will respond and turn back to God before the punishment comes and they will be given ease. However, others will be unjustly rebellious and the fire will be their shelter. The verse serves as a warning to those who are unjust and reminds them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: وأخذهم الربا وقد نهوا عنه وأكلهم أموال الناس بالباطل وأعتدنا للكافرين منهم عذابا أليما

translation: But as for those who are deeply rooted in knowledge and the believers, they believe in what has been revealed to you, [O Muhammad], and what was revealed before you. And they are certain of the hereafter. These are the guided ones. Those - We will grant them a noble provision.
interpretation: The verse distinguishes between two groups of people: those who are deeply rooted in knowledge and the believers. Both groups share a common belief in the revelations that were given to the Prophet Muhammad and those that were revealed before him. They are also certain of the hereafter. These individuals are described as the guided ones. The verse concludes by stating that those who possess these qualities will be granted a noble provision. The verse emphasizes the importance of knowledge, faith, and certainty in the hereafter. It also highlights the reward that awaits those who possess these qualities, indicating that their actions and beliefs align with God's will.
orig: لكن الراسخون في العلم منهم والمؤمنون يؤمنون بما أنزل إليك وما أنزل من قبلك والمقيمين الصلاة والمؤتون الزكاة والمؤمنون بالله واليوم الآخر أولئك سنؤتيهم أجرا عظيما

translation: We have revealed to you, as We revealed to Noah and the prophets after him, and We revealed to Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, and the tribes, and to Jesus, Job, Jonah, Aaron, and Solomon, and We gave David a book of Psalms.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the revelation of divine guidance and wisdom to various prophets throughout history, including Noah, Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, Jesus, Job, Jonah, Aaron, Solomon, and David. The verse emphasizes the continuity and consistency of the divine message, which has been revealed to different prophets at different times and places. The verse also highlights the significance of the revelation to the prophet Muhammad, who is included in the same category as the previous prophets. The verse serves as a reminder of the divine guidance that has been given to humanity, and the importance of following the teachings of the prophets, who all received revelations from the same source.
orig: إنا أوحينا إليك كما أوحينا إلى نوح والنبيين من بعده وأوحينا إلى إبراهيم وإسماعيل وإسحاق ويعقوب والأسباط وعيسى وأيوب ويونس وهارون وسليمان وآتينا داوود زبورا

translation: And We have already sent messengers before you, O Muhammad, [some] of whom We have narrated to you their stories, and some of whom We have not narrated to you. And Allah spoke to Moses directly.
interpretation: The verse highlights the continuity of prophethood and the fact that Prophet Muhammad is not the first messenger sent by God. The verse mentions that some of the stories of the previous messengers have been shared, while others have not. This may serve as a reminder that there is much more to learn about the history of prophethood. The verse also emphasizes the unique relationship between God and Moses, as God spoke to Moses directly, highlighting the significance of Moses's prophethood in the Abrahamic tradition.
orig: ورسلا قد قصصناهم عليك من قبل ورسلا لم نقصصهم عليك وكلم الله موسى تكليما

translation: Messengers as bringers of good news and warners so that mankind will have no argument against Allah after the messengers. And Allah is Exalted in Power, Wise.
interpretation: The verse highlights the role of messengers (prophets) as bringers of good news and warners, reminding people of the consequences of their actions. The verse emphasizes that after the messengers have conveyed the message of Allah, people will have no excuse for not following the path of righteousness. The verse also emphasizes the greatness and wisdom of Allah, who has the power to hold people accountable for their actions and who has sent messengers to guide humanity.
orig: رسلا مبشرين ومنذرين لئلا يكون للناس على الله حجة بعد الرسل وكان الله عزيزا حكيما

translation: But Allah bears witness to that which He has revealed to you, [O Muhammad], that He has sent it down with His knowledge, and the angels bear witness, and Allah is sufficient as a witness.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the divine origin of the revelation that was given to the Prophet Muhammad. Both God and the angels bear witness to the truth of the revelation, and God's knowledge is the source of the revelation. The verse serves to affirm the authenticity and truth of the Qur'an and emphasizes the power and authority of God as the source of all knowledge and truth.
orig: لكن الله يشهد بما أنزل إليك أنزله بعلمه والملائكة يشهدون وكفى بالله شهيدا

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieved and averted from the way of Allah have surely gone astray far away.
interpretation: The verse asserts that those who reject faith and obstruct others from the path of God have strayed far from the right path. The verse emphasizes the severity of their error, indicating that they are not just slightly off course but have wandered far away from the truth. The verse serves as a warning to those who reject faith and obstruct others from the way of God, highlighting the consequences of their actions and the danger of their rejection of the truth.
orig: إن الذين كفروا وصدوا عن سبيل الله قد ضلوا ضلالا بعيدا

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve and wrong themselves will not have forgiveness from Allah, nor will He guide them to a way.
interpretation: The verse states that those who disbelieve in Allah and commit wrong actions against themselves or others will not receive forgiveness from Allah. Additionally, Allah will not guide them to the right path. This verse emphasizes the serious consequences of disbelief and wrongdoing, and the importance of seeking Allah's forgiveness and guidance.
orig: إن الذين كفروا وظلموا لم يكن الله ليغفر لهم ولا ليهديهم طريقا

translation: Except the path of Hell, they will be in it, abiding therein forever. And that was easy for Allah.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the fate of those who do not follow the right path, they will end up in Hell and will remain there forever. The verse emphasizes the ease with which Allah can punish those who disobey Him. It serves as a reminder of the severity of the consequences of sin and the importance of following the right path.
orig: إلا طريق جهنم خالدين فيها أبدا وكان ذلك على الله يسيرا

translation: O mankind, indeed the Messenger has come to you with the truth from your Lord, so believe, it is better for you. But if you disbelieve - then indeed, to Allah belongs that which is in the heavens and the earth. And Allah is ever Knowing and Wise.
interpretation: The verse addresses all of humanity, reminding them that the Messenger has come to them with the truth from their Lord. The verse urges people to believe, emphasizing that it is in their best interest to do so. However, if they choose to disbelieve, the verse reminds them that everything in the heavens and the earth belongs to God, and that God is all-knowing and all-wise. The verse serves as a reminder that people have the free will to choose whether or not to believe, but that there will be consequences for their choices.
orig: يا أيها الناس قد جاءكم الرسول بالحق من ربكم فآمنوا خيرا لكم وإن تكفروا فإن لله ما في السماوات والأرض وكان الله عليما حكيما

translation: O People of the Scripture, do not exceed limits in your religion and do not say about Allah except the truth. Indeed, the Messiah, Jesus, the son of Mary, is a messenger of Allah and His word, which He directed to Mary, and a soul [created at a command] from Him. So believe in Allah and His messengers, and do not say, 'Three'; desist - it is better for you. Indeed, Allah is only one God. Exalted is He above having a son. To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. And sufficient is Allah as Disposer of affairs.
interpretation: The verse addresses the People of the Scripture (Jews and Christians) and warns them against exaggeration and falsehood in their religion. It emphasizes the oneness of God and the prophethood of Jesus, the son of Mary, and encourages belief in Allah and His messengers. The verse also forbids the use of the word 'Three' when referring to God, and urges the People of the Scripture to desist from such a statement. The verse stresses the sovereignty of Allah over all that exists in the heavens and the earth, and affirms His ability to manage all affairs.
orig: يا أهل الكتاب لا تغلوا في دينكم ولا تقولوا على الله إلا الحق إنما المسيح عيسى ابن مريم رسول الله وكلمته ألقاها إلى مريم وروح منه فآمنوا بالله ورسله ولا تقولوا ثلاثة انتهوا خيرا لكم إنما الله إله واحد سبحانه أن يكون له ولد له ما في السماوات وما في الأرض وكفى بالله وكيلا

translation: The Messiah will never be too proud to be a servant of Allah, nor will the angels near [to Him]. And those who are too proud - Allah will gather them all together unto Him.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of humility and submission to God. It states that even the Messiah and the angels do not consider themselves too great to serve God. The verse then warns those who are arrogant and refuse to submit to God, stating that they will be gathered together by God on the Day of Judgment. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of humility and obedience to God, and the consequences of arrogance and disobedience.
orig: لن يستنكف المسيح أن يكون عبدا لله ولا الملائكة المقربون ومن يستنكف عن عبادته ويستكبر فسيحشرهم إليه جميعا

translation: But as for those who believe and do good deeds, their reward is with their Lord, and no fear shall there be concerning them, nor shall they grieve. And as for those who are ungrateful and arrogant, so will I feed them a punishment severe, for they were evildoers.
interpretation: The verse contrasts the fates of two groups of people: those who believe in God and do good deeds, and those who are ungrateful and arrogant. For the believers, their reward is with their Lord, and they have no reason to fear or grieve. For the ungrateful and arrogant, they will receive a severe punishment from God, as they have done evil. The verse emphasizes the importance of faith and good deeds, and the consequences of arrogance and ungratefulness. It serves as a reminder that God will reward the righteous and punish the wrongdoers.
orig: فأما الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات فيوفيهم أجورهم ويزيدهم من فضله وأما الذين استنكفوا واستكبروا فيعذبهم عذابا أليما ولا يجدون لهم من دون الله وليا ولا نصيرا

translation: O mankind, indeed there has come to you a clear proof from your Lord, and We have sent down to you a clear light.
interpretation: The verse addresses all of humanity, reminding them that they have received clear evidence and proof from their Lord. This proof is likely a reference to the revelation of the Qur'an, which serves as a guide and a source of truth for believers. The verse also mentions the descent of a 'clear light', which may refer to the guidance and enlightenment that the Qur'an brings to those who follow its teachings. The verse emphasizes the importance of recognizing and accepting this proof and light, as it comes from the Lord and serves as a source of truth and guidance for believers.
orig: يا أيها الناس قد جاءكم برهان من ربكم وأنزلنا إليكم نورا مبينا

translation: But as for those who believe in God and hold fast to Him, He will admit them to His mercy and grace and guide them to Him on a straight path.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the fate of those who believe in God and hold fast to Him. They will be admitted to God's mercy and grace, and He will guide them to Him on a straight path. The verse emphasizes the importance of faith and holding fast to God, and the rewards that come with it. It serves as a source of comfort and hope for the believers, reminding them that God's mercy and guidance are available to those who believe in Him and hold fast to Him.
orig: فأما الذين آمنوا بالله واعتصموا به فسيدخلهم في رحمة منه وفضل ويهديهم إليه صراطا مستقيما

translation: They ask you [O Muhammad] concerning the inheritance of a deceased person without a child. Say, 'God instructs you concerning it: for a man who has no child, but has a sister, she receives half of what he leaves, and he inherits from her if she has no child. But if there are two sisters, they receive two-thirds of what he leaves. If there are brothers and sisters, the male receives the share of two females. God makes this clear to you, so that you may not go astray. And God is Knowing of all things.'
interpretation: The verse outlines the rules of inheritance for a deceased person who does not have any children. The verse emphasizes the importance of following God's instructions regarding inheritance and warns against deviating from them. The verse also highlights the fairness of the distribution of inheritance among the relatives of the deceased. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of understanding and following God's commands in all matters, including the distribution of inheritance, and the consequences of deviating from them. The verse also emphasizes God's knowledge of all things, indicating that He is aware of the actions of His servants and will hold them accountable for their deeds.
orig: يستفتونك قل الله يفتيكم في الكلالة إن امرؤ هلك ليس له ولد وله أخت فلها نصف ما ترك وهو يرثها إن لم يكن لها ولد فإن كانتا اثنتين فلهما الثلثان مما ترك وإن كانوا إخوة رجالا ونساء فللذكر مثل حظ الأنثيين يبين الله لكم أن تضلوا والله بكل شيء عليم

translation: O you who have believed, fulfill (your) covenants. Permitted to you is (the use of) grazing livestock, (such as) camels and cattle, as long as you are established upon the earth. And (it is) your religion, (so) do not be equated with the idolaters. Indeed, Allah orders what He wills.
interpretation: The verse addresses the believers and commands them to fulfill their covenants and agreements. It then grants them permission to benefit from the grazing livestock, such as camels and cattle, as long as they are settled and established in the land. The verse also emphasizes the distinction between the believers and the idolaters, warning against being equated with them. The verse concludes by affirming that Allah has the power and authority to decree and command as He wills.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا أوفوا بالعقود أحلت لكم بهيمة الأنعام إلا ما يتلى عليكم غير محلي الصيد وأنتم حرم إن الله يحكم ما يريد

translation:
O you who have believed, do not profane the symbols of Allah and the sacred month or the offerings and the sacrificial animals and the garlands, that you may know what is unlawful and lawful. And fear Allah. Indeed, Allah is severe in penalty. 

Permitted to you on the day of al-Fitr is the eating of food and drink until the white thread of dawn becomes distinct to you from the black thread. Then complete the fast until the sun sets. And do not have relations with your wives while you are in retreat in the mosques. Those are great sins. 

It is not lawful for you to inherit women by compulsion. And do not put constraint on them in order to take [back] part of what you gave them unless they commit a clear immorality. And live with them in kindness. For if you dislike them - perhaps you dislike a thing and Allah makes therein much good. 

But if you want to replace one wife with another and you have given one of them a great deal, do not take [back] from it anything. Would you take it by slander and manifest sin? 

And how could you take it while you have gone in unto each other and they have taken from you a solemn covenant?
interpretation: The verse begins by reminding the believers not to profane the symbols of God and to respect the sacred month, offerings, and sacrificial animals. It emphasizes the importance of knowing what is lawful and unlawful and the need to fear God, as He is severe in punishment. The verse then goes on to give specific instructions about the day of al-Fitr, including the permissibility of eating and drinking until dawn and the prohibition of relations with wives while in retreat in the mosques. It also forbids inheriting women by compulsion and puts emphasis on treating them kindly. The verse encourages living with one's wife in kindness, even if one dislikes them, as God may bring about much good from it. It also forbids taking back any part of the dowry unless the wife commits a clear immorality. The verse ends by emphasizing the importance of treating one's wife with respect and kindness, and fulfilling one's covenants.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تحلوا شعائر الله ولا الشهر الحرام ولا الهدي ولا القلائد ولا آمين البيت الحرام يبتغون فضلا من ربهم ورضوانا وإذا حللتم فاصطادوا ولا يجرمنكم شنآن قوم أن صدوكم عن المسجد الحرام أن تعتدوا وتعاونوا على البر والتقوى ولا تعاونوا على الإثم والعدوان واتقوا الله إن الله شديد العقاب

translation: Prohibited to you are dead animals, blood, the flesh of swine, and that which has been dedicated to other than Allah, and [those animals] killed by strangling or by a violent blow or by a head-long fall or by the goring of horns, and those from which a wild animal has eaten, except what you [are able to] slaughter [before its death], and what is crushed by hooves and that which is slaughtered on altars [to other than Allah]. And [also prohibited is] that you seek decision through divination or by [observing] the casting of arrows. That is grave disobedience. This day those who disbelieve have despaired of [defeating] your religion; so fear them not, but fear Me. This day I have perfected for you your religion and completed My favor upon you and have approved for you Islam as a religion. But as for he who is forced [by necessity], neither desiring [it] nor transgressing [its limit], then indeed, your Lord is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: The verse outlines various prohibitions for Muslims, including the consumption of dead animals, blood, pork, and animals dedicated to other than Allah. It also forbids the practice of divination and the seeking of decisions through such means. The verse emphasizes the importance of following these prohibitions and the consequences of disobedience. The verse also highlights the completion and perfection of Islam as a religion and the mercy and forgiveness of Allah for those who are forced by necessity to commit sins. The verse serves as a reminder to Muslims to adhere to their religion and not to fear those who disbelieve, but rather to fear Allah. It also emphasizes the importance of obedience and the consequences of disobedience.
orig: حرمت عليكم الميتة والدم ولحم الخنزير وما أهل لغير الله به والمنخنقة والموقوذة والمتردية والنطيحة وما أكل السبع إلا ما ذكيتم وما ذبح على النصب وأن تستقسموا بالأزلام ذلكم فسق اليوم يئس الذين كفروا من دينكم فلا تخشوهم واخشون اليوم أكملت لكم دينكم وأتممت عليكم نعمتي ورضيت لكم الإسلام دينا فمن اضطر في مخمصة غير متجانف لإثم فإن الله غفور رحيم

translation: They ask you what is lawful for them. Say: 'Lawful for you are all good things, as well as what you have taught your hunting animals, teaching them of that which God has taught you.' So eat from what they catch for you, and mention the name of God upon it, and fear God. Indeed, God is swift in account.
interpretation: The verse addresses a question about what is permissible for people to consume, and it answers that all good and pure things are lawful for them. Additionally, the verse also permits the consumption of animals hunted by trained hunting animals, such as dogs or falcons, as long as the person has taught the animal how to hunt, and the animal has hunted the animal in accordance with the teachings of God. The verse emphasizes the importance of mentioning the name of God before consuming the hunted animal, and it reminds people to be mindful of God and fear Him. The verse also warns that God is swift in reckoning and accounting for people's actions, emphasizing the importance of obedience and reverence towards God.
orig: يسألونك ماذا أحل لهم قل أحل لكم الطيبات وما علمتم من الجوارح مكلبين تعلمونهن مما علمكم الله فكلوا مما أمسكن عليكم واذكروا اسم الله عليه واتقوا الله إن الله سريع الحساب

translation: This day are (made) lawful for you good things, and the food of those who have been given the Book is lawful for you, and your food is lawful for them; and the chaste from among the believing women and the chaste from among those who have been given the Book before you, when you give them their dowries, in a lawful manner, the chaste, not the fornicators, nor the taking of paramours; and whoever disbelieves in the faith, then his work is of no account, and he in the hereafter will be one of the losers.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the permissibility of certain things, including good food and marriage with chaste women from among the believers and those from among the people of the book. The verse emphasizes the importance of following the law in matters of marriage and the prohibition of fornication and taking paramours. The verse also warns those who disbelieve in the faith that their deeds will be in vain and they will be losers in the hereafter.
orig: اليوم أحل لكم الطيبات وطعام الذين أوتوا الكتاب حل لكم وطعامكم حل لهم والمحصنات من المؤمنات والمحصنات من الذين أوتوا الكتاب من قبلكم إذا آتيتموهن أجورهن محصنين غير مسافحين ولا متخذي أخدان ومن يكفر بالإيمان فقد حبط عمله وهو في الآخرة من الخاسرين

translation: O you who have believed, when you rise to perform prayer, wash your faces and your forearms to the elbows and wipe over your heads and your feet to the ankles. And if you are in a state of janabah, then purify yourselves. But if you are sick or on a journey or one of you comes from the place of relieving himself or you have contacted women and do not find water, then seek clean earth and wipe over your faces and hands with it. Allah does not intend to make difficulty for you, but He intends to purify you and complete His favor upon you that you may be grateful.
interpretation: This verse outlines the steps for performing ablution (wudu) before prayer, emphasizing the importance of cleanliness and purification. The verse also provides alternatives for those who are unable to find water, such as wiping over clean earth. The verse highlights the compassion and mercy of Allah, as He does not intend to make things difficult for His believers but rather to purify and bless them. The verse serves as a reminder for Muslims to maintain their cleanliness and purity, and to be grateful for Allah's blessings.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا إذا قمتم إلى الصلاة فاغسلوا وجوهكم وأيديكم إلى المرافق وامسحوا برءوسكم وأرجلكم إلى الكعبين وإن كنتم جنبا فاطهروا وإن كنتم مرضى أو على سفر أو جاء أحد منكم من الغائط أو لامستم النساء فلم تجدوا ماء فتيمموا صعيدا طيبا فامسحوا بوجوهكم وأيديكم منه ما يريد الله ليجعل عليكم من حرج ولكن يريد ليطهركم وليتم نعمته عليكم لعلكم تشكرون

translation: And remember the favor of Allah upon you and His covenant with which He has bound you when you said, 'We hear and we obey'; and fear Allah. Indeed, Allah is Knowing of that within the breasts.
interpretation: The verse reminds the believers of the favor and blessings that God has bestowed upon them and the covenant that He has made with them. The covenant refers to the agreement that the believers made with God when they said 'We hear and we obey', indicating their willingness to follow and obey God's commands. The verse urges the believers to fear God and be mindful of His knowledge and awareness of their thoughts and intentions. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of upholding one's covenant with God and the significance of obedience and submission to His will.
orig: واذكروا نعمة الله عليكم وميثاقه الذي واثقكم به إذ قلتم سمعنا وأطعنا واتقوا الله إن الله عليم بذات الصدور

translation: O you who have believed, be witnesses for Allah in justice, and do not let the hatred of a people prevent you from being just. Be just; that is nearer to righteousness. And fear Allah; indeed, Allah is Acquainted with what you do.
interpretation: The verse is a command to the believers to be witnesses for Allah and to uphold justice, regardless of any personal biases or prejudices they may have. It emphasizes the importance of being fair and impartial, and not allowing the hatred of a particular group of people to influence one's judgment. By being just, one is closer to righteousness, and it is a reminder to fear Allah and be aware of His knowledge of all actions. This verse serves as a moral guideline for the believers, encouraging them to be fair and just, and to act with integrity and righteousness.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا كونوا قوامين لله شهداء بالقسط ولا يجرمنكم شنآن قوم على ألا تعدلوا اعدلوا هو أقرب للتقوى واتقوا الله إن الله خبير بما تعملون

translation: Allah has promised those who believe and do righteous deeds, for them forgiveness and a great reward.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the promise of Allah to those who have faith and do good deeds. The promise is of forgiveness and a great reward. The verse highlights the importance of both belief and actions, emphasizing that it is not enough to simply have faith, but it must be accompanied by good deeds. The promise of forgiveness and great reward serves as motivation for believers to strive for righteousness and to lead a life in accordance with the teachings of Islam.
orig: وعد الله الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات لهم مغفرة وأجر عظيم

translation: But those who disbelieved and denied Our signs - those are the companions of the Fire.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the fate of those who disbelieve in God and deny His signs or revelations. The verse states that they will be companions of the Fire, which is a reference to Hell. The verse emphasizes the importance of believing in God and accepting His signs, and the serious consequences of denying or rejecting them. The verse serves as a warning to those who do not believe, urging them to reconsider their position before it is too late.
orig: والذين كفروا وكذبوا بآياتنا أولئك أصحاب الجحيم

translation: O believers, remember the blessings of God upon you, when they (disbelievers) extended their hands towards you, but God withheld their hands from you. Fear God, and on God let the believers rely.
interpretation: The verse reminds the believers to be grateful for God's blessings and protection. It recalls a time when the disbelievers had hostile intentions towards the believers and extended their hands against them, but God intervened and protected the believers. The verse encourages the believers to fear God and put their trust in Him. The verse may serve as a source of comfort and reassurance for the believers, reminding them of God's power and protection in the face of adversity.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا اذكروا نعمت الله عليكم إذ هم قوم أن يبسطوا إليكم أيديهم فكف أيديهم عنكم واتقوا الله وعلى الله فليتوكل المؤمنون

translation: And indeed, Allah had taken a covenant from the children of Israel, and appointed twelve leaders from among them. And Allah said, 'Indeed, I am with you, if you establish prayer and give zakah and believe in My messengers and support them and lend Allah a good loan, I will surely remove from you your misdeeds and admit you to gardens beneath which rivers flow. But whoever of you disbelieves after that has certainly gone astray.',
interpretation: The verse highlights a covenant made between God and the children of Israel, where God appointed twelve leaders from among them. God promises to be with them and grant them forgiveness and entry into gardens beneath which rivers flow if they establish prayer, give zakah (charity), believe in God's messengers, and support them. However, those who disbelieve after making this covenant will have strayed from the right path. The verse emphasizes the importance of upholding one's covenant with God and the rewards for obedience, as well as the consequences of disbelief and disobedience.
orig: ولقد أخذ الله ميثاق بني إسرائيل وبعثنا منهم اثني عشر نقيبا وقال الله إني معكم لئن أقمتم الصلاة وآتيتم الزكاة وآمنتم برسلي وعزرتموهم وأقرضتم الله قرضا حسنا لأكفرن عنكم سيئاتكم ولأدخلنكم جنات تجري من تحتها الأنهار فمن كفر بعد ذلك منكم فقد ضل سواء السبيل

translation: For their breaking their covenant, and their disbelieving in the signs of Allah, and their slaying the prophets without right, and their saying: Our hearts are wrapped; nay, Allah has set a seal upon them because of their disbelief, so they believe not, except a few;-
interpretation: The verse speaks about the punishment of those who broke their covenant with God, disbelieved in His signs, killed the prophets unjustly, and claimed that their hearts are sealed and they cannot believe. The verse highlights the hardness of their hearts and their rejection of faith. The verse emphasizes that only a few among them believe. The verse serves as a reminder of the consequences of breaking the covenant with God, disbelieving in His signs, and committing unjust acts. It also highlights the mercy of God, who forgives and overlooks the sins of those who repent and turn to Him.
orig: فبما نقضهم ميثاقهم لعناهم وجعلنا قلوبهم قاسية يحرفون الكلم عن مواضعه ونسوا حظا مما ذكروا به ولا تزال تطلع على خائنة منهم إلا قليلا منهم فاعف عنهم واصفح إن الله يحب المحسنين

translation: And of those who say, 'We are Christians,' We have taken their covenant, but they have forgotten a part of that whereof they were reminded. So We have stirred up enmity and hatred among them till the Day of Resurrection; and Allah will inform them of what they did.
interpretation: This verse speaks about those who identify as Christians but have forgotten or disregarded a part of their covenant with God. As a result, God has caused enmity and hatred to exist among them until the Day of Judgment. The verse highlights the consequences of forgetting or ignoring one's covenant with God and the discord that can result from it. Ultimately, God will inform them of their actions on the Day of Judgment, implying that there will be accountability for their actions.
orig: ومن الذين قالوا إنا نصارى أخذنا ميثاقهم فنسوا حظا مما ذكروا به فأغرينا بينهم العداوة والبغضاء إلى يوم القيامة وسوف ينبئهم الله بما كانوا يصنعون

translation: O People of the Scripture, our messenger has come to you making clear to you much of what you used to hide of the book and forgiving much. There has come to you from God a light and a clear book.
interpretation: The verse addresses the People of the Scripture (Jews and Christians) and announces the arrival of God's messenger who clarifies for them many aspects of the scripture that they had previously concealed. The messenger also forgives many of their sins. The verse highlights the significance of the messenger's arrival by describing the revelation as a light and a clear book from God. This verse emphasizes the importance of understanding and following the teachings of the scripture and the guidance brought by the messenger, and it serves as a reminder of the mercy and forgiveness of God towards those who seek His guidance.
orig: يا أهل الكتاب قد جاءكم رسولنا يبين لكم كثيرا مما كنتم تخفون من الكتاب ويعفو عن كثير قد جاءكم من الله نور وكتاب مبين

translation: Guides God with it whom He wills of those who follow His contentment to the ways of peace, and brings them out of the darknesses into the light by His permission, and guides them to a straight path.
interpretation: The verse speaks about God's guidance being granted to those who follow His pleasure and are led to the paths of peace. This guidance brings them out of darkness and into light through His permission, and leads them to a straight path. The verse highlights the importance of following God's will and contentment, and the blessings that come with it, such as guidance, peace, and being led to a straight path. The verse serves as a reminder that God is the one who guides and leads, and that by following His will, one can attain the blessings of guidance and a righteous path.
orig: يهدي به الله من اتبع رضوانه سبل السلام ويخرجهم من الظلمات إلى النور بإذنه ويهديهم إلى صراط مستقيم

translation: Indeed, they have disbelieved who have said, 'Surely, Allah is the Messiah, son of Mary.' So say, 'Who then can do anything against Allah, if He had willed to destroy the Messiah, son of Mary, and those who are on the earth together? And Allah is the One Who is the Lord of the heavens and the earth and all that is between them. So He creates what He pleases, and Allah is over all things competent.'
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the power and sovereignty of Allah, and the blasphemy of those who claim that the Messiah, son of Mary, is a god. The verse rejects this belief and affirms that Allah is the only one worthy of worship and has power over all things. The verse serves as a reminder that Allah has the power to do as He pleases, and no one can prevent Him from carrying out His will. The verse also highlights that Allah is the Lord of the heavens and the earth and all that is between them, and that He creates what He pleases, and that He has power over all things.
orig: لقد كفر الذين قالوا إن الله هو المسيح ابن مريم قل فمن يملك من الله شيئا إن أراد أن يهلك المسيح ابن مريم وأمه ومن في الأرض جميعا ولله ملك السماوات والأرض وما بينهما يخلق ما يشاء والله على كل شيء قدير

translation: And the Jews and the Christians say, 'We are the children of God and His beloved.' Say, 'Then why does He punish you for your sins? You are merely human, of those He has created. He forgives whom He wills, and He punishes whom He wills. And God's is the dominion of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them, and to Him is the final destination.'
interpretation: The verse addresses the Jews and Christians who claim to be the children of God and His beloved. The verse challenges this claim by asking why they are punished for their sins if they are truly God's children. The verse emphasizes that humans are merely a creation of God, and He has the power to forgive or punish whomever He wills. The verse also reaffirms God's sovereignty over the heavens and the earth and the ultimate destination of all creation is to Him. The interpretation of this verse highlights the importance of recognizing one's place as a creation of God, and the need to seek His forgiveness and mercy, rather than making false claims of special status or relationship with Him.
orig: وقالت اليهود والنصارى نحن أبناء الله وأحباؤه قل فلم يعذبكم بذنوبكم بل أنتم بشر ممن خلق يغفر لمن يشاء ويعذب من يشاء ولله ملك السماوات والأرض وما بينهما وإليه المصير

translation: O People of the Scripture, indeed has come to you Our Messenger making clear to you much of what you used to conceal of the Scripture and passing over much. Indeed, there has come to you a light from Allah and a clear Book. By it, Allah guides those who pursue His pleasure to the ways of peace and brings them out from darkness into light, by His will, and guides them to a straight path.
interpretation: This verse is a message to the People of the Scripture (Jews and Christians) from the Muslim believers, reminding them that the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) has been sent as a messenger to clarify and confirm the truth of their scriptures, which had been distorted and concealed over time. The verse emphasizes the importance of the Quran, which is described as a clear and detailed revelation from Allah, that guides people to the right path and leads them out of darkness and into light. The verse also highlights the power and ability of Allah to accomplish all things, and the guidance he provides to those who seek His pleasure.
orig: يا أهل الكتاب قد جاءكم رسولنا يبين لكم على فترة من الرسل أن تقولوا ما جاءنا من بشير ولا نذير فقد جاءكم بشير ونذير والله على كل شيء قدير

translation: And when Moses said to his people: 'O my people! Remember the favor of Allah upon you when He appointed among you prophets, and made you kings, and gave you that which He has not given to any other among the nations.'
interpretation: In this verse, Moses reminds his people of the blessings and favors that Allah has bestowed upon them. These blessings include the appointment of prophets and the granting of kingship among them, as well as the provision of resources and provisions that were not given to any other nation. The verse serves as a call to gratitude and remembrance of Allah's blessings, emphasizing the unique position and privilege that the people of Moses have been given. The verse also highlights the importance of recognizing and appreciating the blessings that one has been given, as a way of expressing gratitude and devotion to Allah.
orig: وإذ قال موسى لقومه يا قوم اذكروا نعمة الله عليكم إذ جعل فيكم أنبياء وجعلكم ملوكا وآتاكم ما لم يؤت أحدا من العالمين

translation: O my people, enter the Holy Land which Allah has assigned to you and do not turn back [from it] and thus become losers.
interpretation: The verse is addressed to the Israelites, calling them to enter and inhabit the Holy Land that God has promised them. The verse warns them not to turn away from this land and to persist in their journey, for if they do, they will become losers. The verse emphasizes the importance of fulfilling God's commands and the consequences of disobedience. It serves as a reminder of the blessings and rewards that come from following God's path and the negative outcomes that result from straying from it.
orig: يا قوم ادخلوا الأرض المقدسة التي كتب الله لكم ولا ترتدوا على أدباركم فتنقلبوا خاسرين

translation: They said, 'O Moses, indeed there are within it a people of great strength, and indeed, we will not enter it until they exit it. But if they exit, then indeed, we will enter.'
interpretation: The verse recounts the words of the Israelites to Moses, expressing their fear and unwillingness to enter the Holy Land because of the presence of powerful inhabitants. They insist that they will not enter until the inhabitants leave, and even then, only if they are certain of their departure. The Israelites' lack of faith is highlighted, as they prioritize their own safety and comfort over trust in God's promise and protection.
orig: قالوا يا موسى إن فيها قوما جبارين وإنا لن ندخلها حتى يخرجوا منها فإن يخرجوا منها فإنا داخلون

translation: Two men who feared that Allah would punish them said, 'Enter the door of the fortress; when you have entered it, you will surely overcome. And upon Allah, rely, if you are believers.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about two individuals who fear Allah's punishment and take action by seeking refuge in a fortress. They encourage each other and express confidence in their ability to overcome their challenges, but ultimately place their trust in Allah. The verse highlights the importance of seeking protection and help from Allah, and emphasizes the significance of faith and reliance on Him in times of difficulty and uncertainty.
orig: قال رجلان من الذين يخافون أنعم الله عليهما ادخلوا عليهم الباب فإذا دخلتموه فإنكم غالبون وعلى الله فتوكلوا إن كنتم مؤمنين

translation: They said, 'O Moses, we will never enter it as long as they are in it. So go, you and your Lord, and fight! We are here, remaining.'
interpretation: The verse describes the response of the Israelites to Moses' call to enter the Holy Land. They refuse to enter the land while their enemies are present, and instead tell Moses to go and fight along with his Lord. The Israelites' lack of faith and willingness to remain in their current state is highlighted in their statement. The verse serves as a reminder of the consequences of a lack of faith and the importance of trusting in God's plan.
orig: قالوا يا موسى إنا لن ندخلها أبدا ما داموا فيها فاذهب أنت وربك فقاتلا إنا هاهنا قاعدون

translation: He said, 'My Lord, I have control over myself and my brother; so part us from the wrongdoing people.'
interpretation: The verse is a conversation between a prophet and God, in which the prophet asks God to save him and his brother from the unjust people around them. The verse highlights the prophet's desire to be separated from the wrongdoers and his recognition of his inability to control or change their actions. The verse emphasizes the importance of surrounding oneself with righteous individuals and avoiding the company of those who engage in unjust and sinful behavior.
orig: قال رب إني لا أملك إلا نفسي وأخي فافرق بيننا وبين القوم الفاسقين

translation: He said, 'It is forbidden for them for forty years. They will wander on the earth. So do not grieve over the corrupt people.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about a group of people who have been forbidden from a certain thing for forty years. They will wander on the earth, and the speaker advises not to grieve over the corrupt people. The verse suggests a sense of justice, where the people are being punished for their wrongdoings. The verse also emphasizes the importance of patience and detachment from the corrupt people, as grieving over them will not change their fate. The verse serves as a reminder that those who commit sins and corruption will face the consequences of their actions.
orig: قال فإنها محرمة عليهم أربعين سنة يتيهون في الأرض فلا تأس على القوم الفاسقين

translation: And relate to them the story of the two sons of Adam in truth, when they both offered an offering, and it was accepted from one of them, but not accepted from the other. The one whose offering was not accepted said, 'I will surely kill you.' The other said, 'Indeed, Allah only accepts from the righteous [who fear Him].'
interpretation: The verse relates the story of the two sons of Adam who offered a sacrifice, but Allah only accepted the sacrifice of one of them. This caused jealousy and anger in the other son, leading him to threaten to kill his brother. The response of the brother whose sacrifice was accepted is a lesson in patience and faith, as he attributes the acceptance of his sacrifice to Allah's favor upon the righteous. This story serves as a reminder of the importance of righteousness and submission to Allah's will, as well as the dangers of jealousy and anger. It teaches that Allah does not accept offerings or deeds from those who are not righteous and that the acceptance of deeds is dependent on one's piety and submission to Allah.
orig: واتل عليهم نبأ ابني آدم بالحق إذ قربا قربانا فتقبل من أحدهما ولم يتقبل من الآخر قال لأقتلنك قال إنما يتقبل الله من المتقين

translation: If you stretch your hand against me to kill me, I will not stretch my hand against you to kill you. Indeed, I fear Allah, the Lord of the worlds.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the importance of avoiding violence and retaliation, even in the face of harm. The speaker refuses to retaliate against the threat of being killed, and instead chooses to fear and respect God, the Lord of the worlds. The verse emphasizes the importance of upholding moral values and maintaining peace, even when faced with adversity and danger.
orig: لئن بسطت إلي يدك لتقتلني ما أنا بباسط يدي إليك لأقتلك إني أخاف الله رب العالمين

translation: Indeed, I wish to guide you to my religion and your religion, then you will be of the patchwork of the Fire, and that is the reward of the unjust.
interpretation: The verse speaks about a person who wants to lead someone else astray, inviting them to follow a path of unbelief and wrongdoing. The verse makes it clear that this path will only lead to the Fire of Hell, and that this is the just reward for those who reject the truth and commit injustices. The verse serves as a warning against following false teachings and against leading others astray.
orig: إني أريد أن تبوء بإثمي وإثمك فتكون من أصحاب النار وذلك جزاء الظالمين

translation: He killed his brother and so he ended up losing himself as well.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the consequences of committing a grave sin, specifically the act of killing one's own brother. The verse emphasizes that the act of killing one's brother not only leads to the loss of the brother's life, but also results in the loss of the killer's own self. This can be interpreted as a loss of honor, dignity, and moral values, as well as a loss of a place in the hereafter. The verse serves as a reminder that every action has consequences, and that committing grave sins can lead to severe and irreversible losses.
orig: فطوعت له نفسه قتل أخيه فقتله فأصبح من الخاسرين

translation: And Allah sent a raven (to teach him) that it might show him how to hide the nakedness of his brother. He said: 'Oh, I wish I could be like this raven and hide the nakedness of my brother!' Then he became regretful.
interpretation: The verse describes the story of a man who was tasked by God to learn how to cover the nakedness of his brother, using a raven as an example. The man expressed his regret for not being able to do what the raven did, indicating that he wished he had covered his brother's nakedness. This story serves as a lesson about the importance of modesty and the consequences of neglecting it. It highlights the role of animals as examples for human beings and the importance of learning from them. The verse also emphasizes the regret and repentance of the man, encouraging the reader to reflect on their actions and seek forgiveness for any wrongdoings.
orig: فبعث الله غرابا يبحث في الأرض ليريه كيف يواري سوءة أخيه قال يا ويلتا أعجزت أن أكون مثل هذا الغراب فأواري سوءة أخي فأصبح من النادمين

translation: For that reason, We decreed upon the Children of Israel that whoever kills a soul unless for a soul or for corruption [done] in the land - it is as if he had slain mankind entirely. And whoever saves one - it is as if he had saved mankind entirely. And Our messengers had certainly come to them with clear proofs. Then indeed many of them, after that, were upon the earth unjust.
interpretation: The verse outlines the principles of justice and retribution, stating that the taking of a single innocent life is as grave a sin as killing all of humanity, while saving a life is equivalent to saving all of humanity. The verse emphasizes the importance of maintaining justice and the sanctity of life. It also highlights the role of God's messengers in delivering clear proofs and messages to the people, yet despite this, many of them continued to act unjustly on earth. The verse serves as a reminder of the significance of every life and the importance of upholding justice, as well as a warning to those who persist in unjust actions despite receiving clear guidance.
orig: من أجل ذلك كتبنا على بني إسرائيل أنه من قتل نفسا بغير نفس أو فساد في الأرض فكأنما قتل الناس جميعا ومن أحياها فكأنما أحيا الناس جميعا ولقد جاءتهم رسلنا بالبينات ثم إن كثيرا منهم بعد ذلك في الأرض لمسرفون

translation: The recompense of those who wage war against Allah and His Messenger and strive to create mischief in the land is only that they be killed or crucified or their hands and their feet be cut off on opposite sides or they be exiled from the land. That is their disgrace in this world, and for them is a great torment in the Hereafter.
interpretation: The verse outlines the punishment for those who fight against Allah and His Messenger and cause corruption in the land. The punishment includes being killed, crucified, having their hands and feet cut off on opposite sides, or being exiled from the land. These are the consequences for their actions in this world, and they will also face a severe punishment in the afterlife. The verse serves as a warning to those who engage in such behavior and a reminder of the severe consequences they will face for their actions.
orig: إنما جزاء الذين يحاربون الله ورسوله ويسعون في الأرض فسادا أن يقتلوا أو يصلبوا أو تقطع أيديهم وأرجلهم من خلاف أو ينفوا من الأرض ذلك لهم خزي في الدنيا ولهم في الآخرة عذاب عظيم

translation: except those who repent before you have power over them; know that Allah is Forgiving, Merciful.
interpretation: The verse speaks about those who have repented before they were overcome by punishment or retribution. The verse emphasizes the mercy and forgiveness of God towards those who have repented before it was too late. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of repentance and the boundless mercy of God towards those who seek His forgiveness.
orig: إلا الذين تابوا من قبل أن تقدروا عليهم فاعلموا أن الله غفور رحيم

translation: O believers, fear Allah and seek the means of approach to Him and strive in His cause, that you may prosper.
interpretation: The verse is a call to believers to fear and worship God, seek His closeness, and strive in His cause. The verse encourages believers to make an effort and strive in the way of God, with the promise that they may prosper and be successful. The verse emphasizes the importance of seeking closeness to God through righteous actions, and the significance of striving in His cause. The verse serves as a reminder for believers to focus on their relationship with God, and to work towards achieving success in both this world and the hereafter.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا اتقوا الله وابتغوا إليه الوسيلة وجاهدوا في سبيله لعلكم تفلحون

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve - if they had all that is in the earth and the like of it with it, they would offer it as ransom to be saved from the punishment on the Day of Resurrection. But it will not be accepted from them, and for them is a painful punishment.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the fate of those who disbelieve in God and the Day of Judgment. The verse highlights the futility of wealth and material possessions in the face of divine punishment. Even if the disbelievers were to offer all the wealth on earth as a ransom, it would not be accepted from them. The verse emphasizes the severity of the punishment that awaits them on the Day of Resurrection, which will be painful and unavoidable. The verse serves as a warning to those who deny the truth and rely on their worldly possessions, reminding them that they cannot escape the consequences of their disbelief.
orig: إن الذين كفروا لو أن لهم ما في الأرض جميعا ومثله معه ليفتدوا به من عذاب يوم القيامة ما تقبل منهم ولهم عذاب أليم

translation: They desire to get out of the Fire, but never will they get out of it, and for them is an enduring punishment.
interpretation: The verse describes the desire of certain people to escape from the Fire of Hell, but they will ultimately fail in their attempt. The verse emphasizes the permanence of their punishment, which is described as 'enduring', indicating that they will remain in Hell for eternity. The verse serves as a warning to those who persist in their sins, reminding them that there is no escape from the consequences of their actions and that their punishment will be everlasting.
orig: يريدون أن يخرجوا من النار وما هم بخارجين منها ولهم عذاب مقيم

translation: And (as for) the man who steals and the woman who steals, cut off their hands as a recompense for what they have earned, an exemplary punishment from Allah. And Allah is Mighty, Wise.
interpretation: The verse outlines the punishment for theft, which is the amputation of the hand of both the man and the woman who steal. This is described as a recompense for what they have earned, and an exemplary punishment from Allah. The verse emphasizes the severity of the crime of theft and the importance of deterring it through strict punishment. The verse also highlights the power and wisdom of Allah, who has prescribed this punishment as a means of maintaining justice and order in society.
orig: والسارق والسارقة فاقطعوا أيديهما جزاء بما كسبا نكالا من الله والله عزيز حكيم

translation: But if someone repents after committing wrongdoing and mends their ways, surely, God will turn to them in forgiveness. Indeed, God is All-Forgiving, All-Compassionate.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the opportunity for repentance and forgiveness from God for those who have committed wrongdoing. The verse emphasizes the importance of turning away from sin and making amends, as this will lead to God's forgiveness. The verse also highlights God's attributes of being All-Forgiving and All-Compassionate, indicating that God's mercy is always available for those who seek it. The verse serves as a message of hope, encouraging people to seek forgiveness and strive towards righteousness.
orig: فمن تاب من بعد ظلمه وأصلح فإن الله يتوب عليه إن الله غفور رحيم

translation: Do you not know that to God belongs the kingdom of the heavens and the earth? He punishes whom He wills and forgives whom He wills. And God is over all things competent.
interpretation: The verse affirms the power and sovereignty of God over all things, emphasizing His ability to punish or forgive whomever He wills. The verse reminds the reader of the ultimate power and control of God, and the importance of recognizing and submitting to this power. The verse serves as a reminder of the consequences of actions, and the importance of seeking forgiveness and repentance. The verse also emphasizes the limitless power of God, who has the ability to do all things.
orig: ألم تعلم أن الله له ملك السماوات والأرض يعذب من يشاء ويغفر لمن يشاء والله على كل شيء قدير

translation: O Messenger, let it not grieve you that those who rush into disbelief (hasten to commit disbelief) from among those who say, 'We believe' with their mouths but have no faith in their hearts. And of the Jews are those who listen to falsehood, listening to others who have not come to you (O Muhammad). They distort the words beyond their (actual) places, saying, 'If you are given this, take it; but if you are not given it, beware!' And whoever Allah wants to put to trial - you will not be able to do him any good, nor can you prevent him from (committing) any harm. Those are the ones Allah has not intended to purify their hearts. For them there is disgrace in this world, and for them is a great punishment in the Hereafter.
interpretation: This verse is addressed to the Prophet Muhammad, advising him not to be saddened by those who claim to believe but do not truly have faith in their hearts. It also mentions a group of Jews who listen to falsehood and distort the words of the Prophet. The verse emphasizes that Allah is the one in control of all matters and that the Prophet cannot guide those whom Allah does not intend to guide. The verse serves as a reminder that those who are not truly believers will face disgrace in this world and a severe punishment in the afterlife.
orig: يا أيها الرسول لا يحزنك الذين يسارعون في الكفر من الذين قالوا آمنا بأفواههم ولم تؤمن قلوبهم ومن الذين هادوا سماعون للكذب سماعون لقوم آخرين لم يأتوك يحرفون الكلم من بعد مواضعه يقولون إن أوتيتم هذا فخذوه وإن لم تؤتوه فاحذروا ومن يرد الله فتنته فلن تملك له من الله شيئا أولئك الذين لم يرد الله أن يطهر قلوبهم لهم في الدنيا خزي ولهم في الآخرة عذاب عظيم

translation: Indeed, We have heard the speech of the foremost [of them], submitting in [to] falsehood, allotting falsehood. And if they come to you, [O Muhammad], judge between them or turn away from them. And if you turn away from them - indeed, they are not believers. And if you judge, judge between them with justice. Indeed, Allah loves those who act justly.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the duty of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) when dealing with people who come to him with falsehood and lies. The verse offers two options: either to judge between them or to turn away from them. If the Prophet (peace be upon him) turns away from them, it means that they are not believers. However, if he chooses to judge, he must do so with justice, as Allah loves those who act justly. The verse emphasizes the importance of justice and fairness, and it highlights the responsibility of the Prophet (peace be upon him) to uphold these values. The verse also reminds the believers of the negative consequences of lying and falsehood, and it encourages them to seek truth and justice in all their actions.
orig: سماعون للكذب أكالون للسحت فإن جاءوك فاحكم بينهم أو أعرض عنهم وإن تعرض عنهم فلن يضروك شيئا وإن حكمت فاحكم بينهم بالقسط إن الله يحب المقسطين

translation: And how do they judge you while they have the Torah, in which is the judgment of Allah; then they turn away after that and they are not believers.
interpretation: The verse criticizes those who claim to follow the Torah but do not apply its teachings and judgments in their dealings with others. Instead, they judge according to their own desires and whims, despite having the guidance of the Torah. The verse highlights the hypocrisy of these individuals, who claim to be believers but do not truly believe or follow the teachings of their own scripture. The verse serves as a reminder that true faith requires not only belief, but also action and adherence to the commands of God.
orig: وكيف يحكمونك وعندهم التوراة فيها حكم الله ثم يتولون من بعد ذلك وما أولئك بالمؤمنين

translation: Indeed, We sent down the Torah, in which was guidance and light. The prophets who submitted [to Allah] judged by it for the Jews, as did the rabbis and scholars by that they were entrusted with of Allah's book and were witnesses over it. So do not fear the people but fear Me, and do not sell My verses for a small price. And those who do not judge by what Allah has revealed - then it is those who are the disbelievers.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the significance of the Torah and its role in providing guidance and light to the people. It highlights the responsibility of the prophets, rabbis, and scholars to judge by the Torah and uphold its teachings. The verse warns against fearing people over God and selling the verses of God for a small price, which can be interpreted as a warning against compromising religious principles for worldly gain. The verse also emphasizes the importance of judging by what God has revealed and the consequences of not doing so, which is depicted as a characteristic of the disbelievers.
orig: إنا أنزلنا التوراة فيها هدى ونور يحكم بها النبيون الذين أسلموا للذين هادوا والربانيون والأحبار بما استحفظوا من كتاب الله وكانوا عليه شهداء فلا تخشوا الناس واخشون ولا تشتروا بآياتي ثمنا قليلا ومن لم يحكم بما أنزل الله فأولئك هم الكافرون
