translation: And We have already written in the Book, 'My punishment will touch him who disbelieves and is unjust among you.' Indeed, it will touch him who denies and turns away - so there is no refuge for him: [It will touch him] in the very place where he disputed Our verses.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the punishment that will befall those who disbelieve and act unjustly. It emphasizes that the punishment is certain and will be meted out without exception. The verse refers to a 'Book' in which God's decree has been written, indicating that the fate of the unbelievers is predetermined and unchangeable. The punishment will be directed specifically at those who deny God's signs and turn away from the truth. The verse serves as a warning to those who reject God's message and act unjustly, reminding them of the inevitable consequences of their actions.
orig: وكتبنا عليهم فيها أن النفس بالنفس والعين بالعين والأنف بالأنف والأذن بالأذن والسن بالسن والجروح قصاص فمن تصدق به فهو كفارة له ومن لم يحكم بما أنزل الله فأولئك هم الظالمون

translation: And We made him (i.e. Jesus) a sign for the Children of Israel, a mercy from Us, and a messenger to him our gospel, in which was guidance and light, and a confirmation of the Torah that was before it, a guidance and a warning for those who are pious.
interpretation: The verse speaks about Jesus as a sign, a mercy, and a messenger from God for the Children of Israel. The verse highlights that Jesus brought the Gospel, which contained guidance and light, and served as a confirmation of the Torah. The Gospel was also a guidance and a warning for those who were pious. The verse emphasizes the role of Jesus as a messenger, bringing divine revelation to the people, and the importance of the Gospel as a source of guidance and light. The verse also suggests that the message of Jesus was in line with the previous revelation, the Torah, and served to confirm and build upon it. Overall, the verse highlights the continuity of the divine message and the role of Jesus in bringing guidance and mercy to the people.
orig: وقفينا على آثارهم بعيسى ابن مريم مصدقا لما بين يديه من التوراة وآتيناه الإنجيل فيه هدى ونور ومصدقا لما بين يديه من التوراة وهدى وموعظة للمتقين

translation: And let the people of the Gospel judge by what Allah has revealed in it. And whoever does not judge by what Allah has revealed - then upon them is punishment.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the importance of following the teachings of God as revealed in the Gospel for the people of the Gospel. It emphasizes that those who do not judge by what God has revealed are wrongdoers and will be punished. The verse highlights the significance of adhering to divine guidance and the consequences of ignoring it.
orig: وليحكم أهل الإنجيل بما أنزل الله فيه ومن لم يحكم بما أنزل الله فأولئك هم الفاسقون

translation: And We have sent down to you the Book in truth, confirming what was before it of the Scripture and as a guardian over it. So judge between them by what Allah has revealed and do not follow their inclinations away from what has come to you of the truth. For each of you, We have made a law and a clear way. And if Allah had willed, He would have made you one nation, but that He might test you in what He has given you; so compete in good. To Allah is your return all together, and He will inform you concerning that over which you used to differ.
interpretation: The verse confirms the truth of the Qur'an as a revelation from God, and its role as a guardian of previous scriptures. It emphasizes the importance of following God's guidance in making judgments, and not being swayed by personal desires or the opinions of others. The verse highlights the diversity of laws and paths for different people, and the idea that God could have made everyone the same, but chose not to in order to test humanity. The verse encourages competition in good deeds and reminds that all will return to God, who will inform them of the truth of their differences.
orig: وأنزلنا إليك الكتاب بالحق مصدقا لما بين يديه من الكتاب ومهيمنا عليه فاحكم بينهم بما أنزل الله ولا تتبع أهواءهم عما جاءك من الحق لكل جعلنا منكم شرعة ومنهاجا ولو شاء الله لجعلكم أمة واحدة ولكن ليبلوكم في ما آتاكم فاستبقوا الخيرات إلى الله مرجعكم جميعا فينبئكم بما كنتم فيه تختلفون

translation: And judge between them by what Allah has revealed and do not follow their inclinations and beware of them lest they tempt you away from some of what Allah has revealed to you. And if they turn away - then know that Allah only intends to afflict them with some of their sins. And indeed, many among the people are defiantly disobedient.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the responsibility of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) in judging between people, and the importance of following the revelation from Allah in doing so. It warns against being influenced by the desires of others and the importance of being wary of them, as they may lead astray from the teachings of Islam. The verse also explains that if people turn away from the teachings of Islam, it is a result of Allah's will to afflict them with some of their sins. It also highlights that many people are disobedient and defiant towards Allah's commands.
orig: وأن احكم بينهم بما أنزل الله ولا تتبع أهواءهم واحذرهم أن يفتنوك عن بعض ما أنزل الله إليك فإن تولوا فاعلم أنما يريد الله أن يصيبهم ببعض ذنوبهم وإن كثيرا من الناس لفاسقون

translation: Do they then seek the judgement of (the days of) ignorance? And who is better than Allah to judge for a people who have certainty (in their belief).
interpretation: The verse is addressing those who seek judgment according to the ways of ignorance (Jahiliyah), which refers to the period of time before Islam was revealed, when people were ignorant of the true teachings of God and followed their own desires and traditions. The verse asks if there is anyone better than Allah to judge for a people who have certainty in their belief. The verse emphasizes that Allah's judgment is the best and most just for those who have true faith. The verse serves as a reminder to those who may be swayed by the ways of ignorance and to remind them of the importance of seeking judgment from Allah and following His guidance.
orig: أفحكم الجاهلية يبغون ومن أحسن من الله حكما لقوم يوقنون

translation: O you who have believed, do not take the Jews and the Christians as allies. They are [in fact] allies of one to another. And whoever among you takes them as allies will surely be of them. Indeed, Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people.
interpretation: The verse warns believers against taking Jews and Christians as allies or friends, emphasizing that they are allies to each other and that anyone who takes them as allies will become one of them. The verse highlights the importance of maintaining a clear distinction between the Muslim community and other religious groups and warns against forming close ties with them. The verse also emphasizes that Allah does not guide those who commit wrongdoing or injustice, indicating that forming alliances with Jews and Christians is a form of wrongdoing and injustice.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تتخذوا اليهود والنصارى أولياء بعضهم أولياء بعض ومن يتولهم منكم فإنه منهم إن الله لا يهدي القوم الظالمين

translation: And you will see those in whose hearts is a disease hastening to it, saying, 'We are afraid a misfortune may befall us.' But perhaps Allah will bring about a victory or a decision from Him, and they will become, over what they were concealing, regretful.
interpretation: The verse describes those who are driven by fear and anxiety, rushing to engage in a matter that they believe may harm them. They express their fear of a calamity befalling them, but at the same time, they hope for a victory or a decision from God that would save them. However, their actions and motivations are driven by their own selfish desires and fears, rather than by faith and trust in God. As a result, they end up regretting their actions and the consequences that follow. The verse serves as a warning against following one's desires and fears, and emphasizes the importance of placing one's trust in God and seeking His guidance in all matters.
orig: فترى الذين في قلوبهم مرض يسارعون فيهم يقولون نخشى أن تصيبنا دائرة فعسى الله أن يأتي بالفتح أو أمر من عنده فيصبحوا على ما أسروا في أنفسهم نادمين

translation: And those who believe say, 'Are these the ones who swore by Allah their strongest oaths that indeed they were with you?' Their deeds have become worthless, and they have become losers.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the hypocrisy of certain individuals who had previously sworn their strongest oaths of allegiance to the believers, but have now turned away from them. The verse emphasizes the emptiness and worthlessness of their actions, indicating that their previous oaths and promises have amounted to nothing. The verse serves as a warning to those who are insincere in their faith and actions, reminding them that their insincerity will not go unnoticed and that their deeds will ultimately be shown to be worthless.
orig: ويقول الذين آمنوا أهؤلاء الذين أقسموا بالله جهد أيمانهم إنهم لمعكم حبطت أعمالهم فأصبحوا خاسرين

translation: O you who have believed, if one of you should leave his religion - Allah will bring forth in place of them a people He loves and who love Him, who are humble toward the believers and hard against the disbelievers, striving in the cause of Allah and not fearing the blame of a critic. That is the favor of Allah; He bestows it upon whom He wills. And Allah is all-encompassing and knowing.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the consequences of leaving one's religion. It reassures the believers that if someone were to leave their religion, God will replace them with a better community who are loved by God and who love Him in return. This new community will be humble towards the believers and firm against the disbelievers, striving in the cause of God without fear of criticism. The verse emphasizes that this is a favor from God, and He bestows it upon whom He wills. The verse serves as a reminder of God's power and knowledge, and that He will always provide for his believers.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا من يرتد منكم عن دينه فسوف يأتي الله بقوم يحبهم ويحبونه أذلة على المؤمنين أعزة على الكافرين يجاهدون في سبيل الله ولا يخافون لومة لائم ذلك فضل الله يؤتيه من يشاء والله واسع عليم

translation: Indeed, only Allah and His Messenger are obligated to you, and those who believe. Those who establish prayer and give zakah while they are bowing.
interpretation: The verse highlights the ultimate authority and responsibility of Allah, His Messenger, and those who believe in establishing prayer and giving zakah. The phrase 'while they are bowing' emphasizes the importance of being in a state of worship and devotion while fulfilling one's religious obligations. This verse serves as a reminder of the importance of maintaining a strong spiritual connection with Allah and upholding one's religious duties, even in the midst of daily life.
orig: إنما وليكم الله ورسوله والذين آمنوا الذين يقيمون الصلاة ويؤتون الزكاة وهم راكعون

translation: And if you obey Allah and His Messenger and believe - then for the believers is a great reward.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the reward for those who believe in Allah and His Messenger and follow their teachings. The verse emphasizes the importance of obedience to Allah and His Messenger and the reward that awaits those who believe. The phrase 'the believers is a great reward' indicates that the reward is not only for the believers in this life but also in the hereafter. The verse serves as a motivation for the believers and a reminder of the ultimate goal of their faith.
orig: ومن يتول الله ورسوله والذين آمنوا فإن حزب الله هم الغالبون

translation: O you who have believed, do not take the Jews and the Christians as allies. They are [in fact] allies of one another. And whoever is an ally to them among you - then indeed, he is [one] of them. Indeed, Allah does not guide the unjust people.
interpretation: The verse warns Muslims not to take Jews and Christians as allies, as they are allies of each other and anyone who aligns with them is considered one of them. The verse emphasizes the importance of being mindful of one's associations and the impact they can have on one's faith and actions. The verse serves as a reminder to remain loyal to the Muslim community and to avoid being influenced by those who oppose Islam. It also highlights the consequences of being unjust and going against the guidance of Allah.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تتخذوا الذين اتخذوا دينكم هزوا ولعبا من الذين أوتوا الكتاب من قبلكم والكفار أولياء واتقوا الله إن كنتم مؤمنين

translation: And when you call to prayer, they take it as a jest and a play. That is because they are a people who do not reason.
interpretation: The verse describes the attitude of certain people towards the call to prayer. Instead of taking it seriously and responding to it with reverence, they treat it as a joke or a form of entertainment. The verse suggests that this behavior is a result of their lack of understanding or reason. The verse serves as a critique of those who do not take their religious obligations seriously and fail to engage in thoughtful reflection about their actions.
orig: وإذا ناديتم إلى الصلاة اتخذوها هزوا ولعبا ذلك بأنهم قوم لا يعقلون

translation: Say, 'O People of the Scripture (Jews and Christians)! Do you take vengeance on us only because we believe in Allah and in what has been revealed to us and what was revealed before, and because most of you are Fasiqun (rebellious, disobedient to Allah)?
interpretation: The verse is a message from the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) to the People of the Scripture (Jews and Christians), questioning their motives for taking vengeance on the Muslims. The verse highlights the reasons for the Muslims' belief and the sources of their faith, including what was revealed to them and what was revealed before. The verse also points out the disobedience and rebellion of most of the People of the Scripture, implying that their actions are not based on true religious beliefs but rather on personal grudges and enmity.
orig: قل يا أهل الكتاب هل تنقمون منا إلا أن آمنا بالله وما أنزل إلينا وما أنزل من قبل وأن أكثركم فاسقون

translation: Say: 'Do I inform you of something worse than that punishment from Allah? Those whom Allah has cursed and with whom He became angry and of whom He made of monkeys and swine and worshipers of idols - such are in a worse position and further astray from the sound way.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the fate of those who have earned the wrath of God. These are people who have been cursed by God, who are angry with them, and who have transformed them into monkeys and pigs. Additionally, they have become worshipers of idols. The verse makes it clear that these people are in a much worse state than those who are facing punishment. Furthermore, they are far astray from the right path. The verse serves as a warning to those who turn away from the worship of the one true God and engage in idolatry and other sins.
orig: قل هل أنبئكم بشر من ذلك مثوبة عند الله من لعنه الله وغضب عليه وجعل منهم القردة والخنازير وعبد الطاغوت أولئك شر مكانا وأضل عن سواء السبيل

translation: And when they come to you, they say, 'We believe!' But indeed, they have disbelieved with their mouths, and they have disbelieved with their hearts, and they are truly disbelievers. And when they meet you, they say, 'We believe!' But when they are alone, they go about in the land spreading corruption. But Allah does not love the corruptors.
interpretation: The verse describes the hypocrisy of certain individuals who claim to believe in Islam but in reality, they are disbelievers. They outwardly express their faith, but inwardly, they reject it. They are described as corruptors who engage in sinful and destructive behavior. The verse highlights the deceptive nature of these individuals and emphasizes that God sees their true intentions and actions. The verse serves as a warning to those who claim to believe but do not act accordingly and a reminder of the importance of sincerity and consistency in faith.
orig: وإذا جاءوكم قالوا آمنا وقد دخلوا بالكفر وهم قد خرجوا به والله أعلم بما كانوا يكتمون

translation: And you see many of them hastening to sin and enmity and consuming unlawful things; indeed, how evil is what they used to do.
interpretation: The verse describes the actions of certain individuals who are eager to commit sins, create discord and consume unlawful things. The verse ends with a strong condemnation of their actions, emphasizing how evil their deeds are. This verse serves as a warning to those who engage in such behavior and a reminder of the negative consequences of their actions.
orig: وترى كثيرا منهم يسارعون في الإثم والعدوان وأكلهم السحت لبئس ما كانوا يعملون

translation: Had not the scholars and religious leaders forbidden them from uttering sin and consuming ill-gotten gains, they would have been committing terrible deeds.
interpretation: The verse highlights the role of scholars and religious leaders in guiding their communities and preventing them from committing sins. It emphasizes the potential consequences of not having such guidance, as people would be free to commit terrible deeds without any restraint. This verse serves as a reminder to those in positions of religious leadership of the importance of their role in guiding their communities and preventing them from straying from the right path.
orig: لولا ينهاهم الربانيون والأحبار عن قولهم الإثم وأكلهم السحت لبئس ما كانوا يصنعون

translation: And the Jews say, 'God's hand is tied up.' Be their hands tied up, and be they cursed for what they say! Rather, both His hands are spread open. He gives and spends however He wills. And what you have been given is but a fleeting pleasure. Indeed, God is ever a Lord of retribution, severe. And they have taken their scholars and monks as lords besides God, and [also] the Messiah, the son of Mary. And they were not commanded except to worship one God. Exalted is He above whatever they associate with Him. They want to extinguish the light of God with their mouths, but God refuses except to perfect His light, although the disbelievers dislike it. It is He who has sent His Messenger with the guidance and the religion of truth to manifest it over all religion, although they who associate others with God dislike it. You are surely going to hear much that is disliked from those who were given the Scripture before you, and from the associators. But if you are patient and reverent, then indeed, that is of the greatest constancy.
interpretation: The verse criticizes the Jews for their disbelief and their claim that God's hand is tied up, indicating that they believe God is unable to help them. The verse emphasizes that God's hands are open and that He gives and spends however He wills. The verse also criticizes the Jews for taking their scholars and monks as lords besides God and for wanting to extinguish the light of God with their mouths. The verse emphasizes that God's light will be perfected and that the disbelievers will not be able to stop it. The verse also mentions that the Prophet Muhammad was sent with the guidance and the religion of truth to manifest it over all religion. The verse serves as a reminder to the believers to be patient and reverent in the face of the disbelief and disliked words of those before them. The verse also emphasizes that the believers should not be swayed by the disbelief of others and should remain steadfast in their faith.
orig: وقالت اليهود يد الله مغلولة غلت أيديهم ولعنوا بما قالوا بل يداه مبسوطتان ينفق كيف يشاء وليزيدن كثيرا منهم ما أنزل إليك من ربك طغيانا وكفرا وألقينا بينهم العداوة والبغضاء إلى يوم القيامة كلما أوقدوا نارا للحرب أطفأها الله ويسعون في الأرض فسادا والله لا يحب المفسدين

translation: And if only the People of the Scripture had believed and been righteous, We would have forgiven them their sins and admitted them to Gardens of Bliss.
interpretation: The verse offers a hypothetical scenario where if the People of the Scripture (Jews and Christians) had believed and acted righteously, God would have forgiven their sins and granted them access to the Gardens of Bliss. The verse highlights the significance of faith and righteousness in earning God's forgiveness and blessings. This message serves as a reminder for all believers, regardless of their religious background, to strive for righteousness and strengthen their faith in God.
orig: ولو أن أهل الكتاب آمنوا واتقوا لكفرنا عنهم سيئاتهم ولأدخلناهم جنات النعيم

translation: And if only they had upheld the Torah and the Gospel and that which was revealed to them from their Lord, they would have consumed [provision] from above them and from beneath their feet. There would have come from them a community in compliance, and [even] more than that. But they turned away, so We took from them [the punishment] for their sins. And they came upon a people who were unjust. So they struck them with the permission of Allah, and David killed Goliath. And Allah gives victory to whom He wills. And Our command is not delayed.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the consequences of not following the teachings of the Torah, the Gospel, and the revelations from their Lord. If they had upheld these teachings, they would have been provided for and a righteous community would have emerged. However, they turned away from these teachings and were punished for their sins. The verse highlights that God's punishment is a result of their own actions and that God gives victory to whom He wills. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of following God's teachings and the consequences of turning away from them.
orig: ولو أنهم أقاموا التوراة والإنجيل وما أنزل إليهم من ربهم لأكلوا من فوقهم ومن تحت أرجلهم منهم أمة مقتصدة وكثير منهم ساء ما يعملون

translation: O Messenger, proclaim what has been revealed to you from your Lord, and if you do not, then you have not conveyed His message, and Allah will protect you from the people. Indeed, Allah does not guide the disbelieving people.
interpretation: The verse addresses the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and commands him to deliver the message that has been revealed to him by his Lord. The verse emphasizes the importance of this task and warns that if the Prophet fails to fulfill it, he will not have conveyed the message. The verse also mentions that Allah will protect the Prophet from the harm of the people. The verse ends with a statement that Allah does not guide the disbelieving people, emphasizing the importance of faith and obedience to Allah's message.
orig: يا أيها الرسول بلغ ما أنزل إليك من ربك وإن لم تفعل فما بلغت رسالته والله يعصمك من الناس إن الله لا يهدي القوم الكافرين

translation: Say, 'O People of the Scripture (Jews and Christians)! You have nothing until you uphold the Tawrah (Torah), the Injeel (Gospel), and that which has been revealed to you from your Lord [Allah].' And whatever has been revealed to you [O Muhammad] from your Lord will surely increase many of them in transgression and disbelief. So do not grieve over the disbelieving people.'
interpretation: The verse is directed towards the People of the Scripture, i.e. the Jews and Christians. It commands them to uphold the Tawrah (Torah) and the Injeel (Gospel), in addition to the revelation sent to the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH). The verse highlights the importance of adhering to the teachings of all revealed scriptures, and not just selectively following certain parts. The verse also warns that some people will increase in transgression and disbelief upon hearing the new revelation. The verse advises the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) not to grieve over the disbelievers, as it is not his responsibility to change their hearts and minds.
orig: قل يا أهل الكتاب لستم على شيء حتى تقيموا التوراة والإنجيل وما أنزل إليكم من ربكم وليزيدن كثيرا منهم ما أنزل إليك من ربك طغيانا وكفرا فلا تأس على القوم الكافرين

translation: Indeed, those who believed and those who were Jews or Christians or Sabeans [before Prophet Muhammad] - those [among them] who believed in Allah and the Last Day and did righteousness - will have their reward with their Lord, and no fear will there be concerning them, nor will they grieve.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the reward of those who believe in God and the Day of Judgment, and do good deeds, regardless of their religion. These people will have no fear or sadness, and their reward will come from God. The verse emphasizes the importance of faith and good deeds, and the ultimate reward that awaits those who follow this path, regardless of their religious background.
orig: إن الذين آمنوا والذين هادوا والصابئون والنصارى من آمن بالله واليوم الآخر وعمل صالحا فلا خوف عليهم ولا هم يحزنون

translation: We took a covenant from the Children of Israel and sent to them messengers. Whenever a messenger came to them with what they did not desire, some of them denied and some of them killed.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the covenant that God made with the Children of Israel and the messengers that were sent to them. However, when a messenger came with a message that the people did not like, some of them denied the message and some of them even killed the messenger. The verse highlights the rejection and hostility that the messengers faced from the people, despite the covenant that was made. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of accepting and following the message of God's messengers, even if it goes against one's desires or expectations.
orig: لقد أخذنا ميثاق بني إسرائيل وأرسلنا إليهم رسلا كلما جاءهم رسول بما لا تهوى أنفسهم فريقا كذبوا وفريقا يقتلون

translation: And they thought there would be no Fitnah (trial or punishment), so they became blind and deaf; then Allah turned to them with forgiveness, then (again) many of them became blind and deaf; and Allah is Seeing what they do.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the people who underestimated the possibility of a trial or punishment from God and became heedless and unaware. Despite God's forgiveness, many of them continued to ignore His signs and repeated their previous actions. The verse highlights the importance of being mindful of God's signs and avoiding heedlessness. It also emphasizes that God is all-seeing and aware of every action that people do.
orig: وحسبوا ألا تكون فتنة فعموا وصموا ثم تاب الله عليهم ثم عموا وصموا كثير منهم والله بصير بما يعملون

translation: Indeed, they have disbelieved who say, 'Allah is the Messiah, the son of Mary.' While the Messiah has said, 'O Children of Israel, worship Allah, my Lord and your Lord.' Indeed, whoever associates partners with Allah - Allah has forbidden him Paradise, and his refuge is the Fire. And there are no helpers for the wrongdoers.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of monotheism and the rejection of any form of polytheism or association of partners with Allah. The verse first mentions those who have disbelieved by saying that Allah is the Messiah, the son of Mary, which is a denial of the fundamental Islamic belief in the oneness of God. The verse then contrasts this statement with the words of the Messiah himself, who calls on the Children of Israel to worship Allah, the Lord of both the Messiah and the Children of Israel. The verse ends by emphasizing the severe consequences of associating partners with Allah, which includes being forbidden from Paradise and having the Fire as one's refuge. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of maintaining the oneness of God and the grave consequences of any form of polytheism or association of partners with Allah.
orig: لقد كفر الذين قالوا إن الله هو المسيح ابن مريم وقال المسيح يا بني إسرائيل اعبدوا الله ربي وربكم إنه من يشرك بالله فقد حرم الله عليه الجنة ومأواه النار وما للظالمين من أنصار

translation: Indeed, those who say, 'Allah is the third of three' have disbelieved. And there is no god except one God. And if they do not desist from what they are saying, there will afflict those who disbelieved among them a painful punishment.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the oneness of God and rejects the belief that there can be a 'third' god in addition to God. The verse warns those who hold this belief of a painful punishment if they do not desist from their false belief. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of monotheism in Islam and the consequences of shirk (associating partners with God). It also highlights the importance of seeking knowledge and understanding of the fundamental beliefs of Islam in order to avoid deviation and error.
orig: لقد كفر الذين قالوا إن الله ثالث ثلاثة وما من إله إلا إله واحد وإن لم ينتهوا عما يقولون ليمسن الذين كفروا منهم عذاب أليم

translation: Why do they not turn to Allah and seek His forgiveness? And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: The verse is a rhetorical question, urging the listeners or readers to reflect on why they do not turn to Allah and seek His forgiveness. The verse emphasizes the importance of seeking Allah's forgiveness and His willingness to forgive. The verse serves as a reminder that Allah is Merciful and Forgiving, encouraging the believers to seek His forgiveness and repent from their sins.
orig: أفلا يتوبون إلى الله ويستغفرونه والله غفور رحيم

translation: The Messiah, son of Mary, was only a messenger; messengers have passed away before him. His mother was a truthful woman. They both used to eat food. Look how We make clear to them signs, then look how they are deluded.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the humanity of Jesus, son of Mary, by stating that he and his mother were like any other human beings, eating food and requiring sustenance. The verse also confirms that Jesus was a messenger, just like other messengers who came before him. The verse challenges the disbelievers to reflect on the signs that have been made clear to them, yet they still choose to reject the truth and be led astray. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of recognizing and accepting the truth, and not being deceived by falsehood.
orig: ما المسيح ابن مريم إلا رسول قد خلت من قبله الرسل وأمه صديقة كانا يأكلان الطعام انظر كيف نبين لهم الآيات ثم انظر أنى يؤفكون

translation: Say, 'Do you worship that which does not possess for you neither harm nor benefit - but Allah, He is the Hearing, the Knowing?'
interpretation: The verse addresses the worship of false gods or idols that have no power to bring benefit or harm, and contrasts it with the worship of Allah, who is the All-Hearing and All-Knowing. The verse challenges the people to reflect on the futility of worshipping false gods and encourages them to turn towards the one true God, Allah. The verse serves as a reminder to the believers to be mindful of their worship and to direct it solely towards Allah, who has power and control over all things.
orig: قل أتعبدون من دون الله ما لا يملك لكم ضرا ولا نفعا والله هو السميع العليم

translation: Say, 'O People of the Scripture (Jews and Christians)! Do not exceed the limits in your religion and do not say about Allah except the truth. The Messiah, Jesus, the son of Mary, was only a Messenger of Allah and His Word which He bestowed upon Mary and a soul from Him. So believe in Allah and His Messengers. And do not say, 'Three (Trinity)'; desist - it is better for you. Indeed, Allah is only one God. Exalted is He above having a son. To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. And sufficient is Allah as Disposer of affairs.',
interpretation: The verse addresses the People of the Scripture, Jews and Christians, and advises them not to exaggerate in their religion and to speak only the truth about God. It emphasizes the oneness of God and denies the Christian belief in the Trinity. It confirms that Jesus was a Messenger of God and a created being, not a deity or a part of a trinity. The verse calls upon the People of the Scripture to believe in God and His Messengers and not to associate partners with God. It reminds them that God is the only deity worthy of worship and that He has power over all things in the heavens and the earth.
orig: قل يا أهل الكتاب لا تغلوا في دينكم غير الحق ولا تتبعوا أهواء قوم قد ضلوا من قبل وأضلوا كثيرا وضلوا عن سواء السبيل

translation: Cursed were those who disbelieved among the Children of Israel by the tongue of David and of Jesus, the son of Mary. That was because they disobeyed and were transgressors.
interpretation: The verse curses those who disbelieved among the Children of Israel, and it attributes the curse to the tongues of David and Jesus, son of Mary. The curse is a result of their disobedience and transgression. The verse emphasizes the consequences of disbelief and disobedience, and it highlights the role of prophets as bearers of divine messages and judgments.
orig: لعن الذين كفروا من بني إسرائيل على لسان داوود وعيسى ابن مريم ذلك بما عصوا وكانوا يعتدون

translation: They were not forbidden from committing an abominable deed, so how evil was what they used to do.
interpretation: The verse highlights the wickedness of a group of people who were not restrained from committing a grave sin. The verse emphasizes the heinous nature of their actions by describing it as 'an abominable deed'. The verse serves as a reminder that sinning has severe consequences and that the severity of the punishment is proportional to the gravity of the sin. The verse also highlights the importance of restraining oneself from commining sins and emphasizes the need for self-control and discipline.
orig: كانوا لا يتناهون عن منكر فعلوه لبئس ما كانوا يفعلون

translation: Indeed, you see many of them embracing those who disbelieve. How wretched is that which they have put forth for themselves that Allah's wrath is upon them, and in the punishment, they will abide forever.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the actions of some people who associate with and support those who disbelieve in Allah, despite the harm it brings upon them. The verse highlights the negative consequences of this action, as Allah's wrath is upon them and they will remain in punishment forever. The verse serves as a warning to those who are considering following a similar path, emphasizing the severe consequences of their actions and the importance of staying on the right path.
orig: ترى كثيرا منهم يتولون الذين كفروا لبئس ما قدمت لهم أنفسهم أن سخط الله عليهم وفي العذاب هم خالدون

translation: And if they had believed in Allah and the Prophet and that which has been revealed to him, they would not have taken them as allies, but many of them are defiantly disobedient.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the disbelievers who did not believe in Allah, the Prophet Muhammad, and the revelations that were sent down to him. If they had truly believed, they would not have taken the disbelievers as their allies. However, many of them were defiantly disobedient and refused to accept the truth. This verse highlights the importance of having faith in Allah and the Prophet, and the consequences of not doing so, such as being misguided and taking the wrong people as allies.
orig: ولو كانوا يؤمنون بالله والنبي وما أنزل إليه ما اتخذوهم أولياء ولكن كثيرا منهم فاسقون

translation: You will surely find the most intense of people in enmity toward those who have believed [to be] the Jews and those who associate others with Allah; and you will find the nearest of them in affection to those who have believed those who say, 'We are Christians.' That is because among them are priests and monks, and because they are not arrogant.
interpretation: The verse highlights the animosity of the Jews and polytheists towards the believers. At the same time, it points out that the Christians are the closest in affection to the believers. This is because among the Christians there are righteous people such as priests and monks who are humble and not arrogant. This verse emphasizes the importance of humility and righteousness, and it serves as a reminder to be mindful of one's behavior and attitude towards others. It also encourages unity and understanding among different religious groups.
orig: لتجدن أشد الناس عداوة للذين آمنوا اليهود والذين أشركوا ولتجدن أقربهم مودة للذين آمنوا الذين قالوا إنا نصارى ذلك بأن منهم قسيسين ورهبانا وأنهم لا يستكبرون

translation: And when they hear what has been revealed to the Messenger, you see their eyes overflowing with tears because of the truth they have recognized. They say, 'Our Lord, we have believed, so register us among the witnesses.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the emotional response of people when they hear the truth (the message of Islam) revealed to the Prophet Muhammad. They are deeply moved by the truth and their eyes overflow with tears. They express their belief in the message and request to be registered among the witnesses. The verse emphasizes the emotional impact of the message of Islam and the strong conviction and commitment of those who believe in it. It also highlights the importance of bearing witness to the truth and the desire of believers to be associated with it.
orig: وإذا سمعوا ما أنزل إلى الرسول ترى أعينهم تفيض من الدمع مما عرفوا من الحق يقولون ربنا آمنا فاكتبنا مع الشاهدين

translation: And why should we not believe in Allah and what has come to us, and we aspire that our Lord will admit us along with the righteous people.
interpretation: The verse expresses the speaker's belief in Allah and their desire to be admitted into paradise alongside the righteous people. The speaker questions why they should not hold this belief and aspiration, implying that it is the correct and natural course of action. This verse highlights the importance of faith in Allah and the pursuit of righteousness as a means of achieving salvation and eternal happiness in the afterlife.
orig: وما لنا لا نؤمن بالله وما جاءنا من الحق ونطمع أن يدخلنا ربنا مع القوم الصالحين

translation: But God rewarded them for what they said with gardens beneath which rivers flow, where they will abide eternally. And that is the reward of the doers of good.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the reward of those who utter good words and do good deeds. They are promised gardens beneath which rivers flow, where they will abide eternally. This is the reward of the doers of good. The verse emphasizes the importance of good speech and actions, and the great reward that awaits those who strive to do good in this life. It serves as a source of motivation and hope for believers, reminding them of the blessings and rewards that come from leading a righteous life.
orig: فأثابهم الله بما قالوا جنات تجري من تحتها الأنهار خالدين فيها وذلك جزاء المحسنين

translation: But those who disbelieved and denied Our signs - those are the companions of the Fire.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the fate of those who disbelieved in God and denied His signs or revelations. The verse clearly states that these people will be the companions of the Fire, which is a metaphor for Hell. The verse emphasizes the importance of believing in God and accepting His signs as a way of avoiding the punishment of Hell. The verse serves as a warning to those who reject God's message, reminding them of the severe consequences of their disbelief and denial.
orig: والذين كفروا وكذبوا بآياتنا أولئك أصحاب الجحيم

translation: O you who have believed, do not prohibit the good things which Allah has made lawful for you and do not transgress. Indeed, Allah does not like transgressors.
interpretation: The verse addresses the believers and commands them not to prohibit or forbid the good things that God has made lawful for them. This includes not only material goods, but also intangible things such as freedom, rights, and opportunities. The verse also commands the believers not to transgress or exceed the limits set by God. The verse emphasizes the importance of adhering to God's laws and commands, and the consequences of disobedience. The verse serves as a reminder to the believers to respect and appreciate the blessings and provisions that God has given them, and to avoid overstepping their bounds or imposing unnecessary restrictions on themselves or others.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تحرموا طيبات ما أحل الله لكم ولا تعتدوا إن الله لا يحب المعتدين

translation: And eat of what Allah has provided for you [which is] lawful and good, and fear Allah, in whom you are believers.
interpretation: The verse encourages Muslims to eat from the sustenance that Allah has provided for them, but to only consume what is halal (lawful) and tayyib (good). This includes not only food and drink, but also all aspects of life. The verse also reminds Muslims to fear Allah and be mindful of Him, as they are believers in Him. This verse serves as a reminder to Muslims to live a life that is pleasing to Allah and to be conscious of the source of their blessings.
orig: وكلوا مما رزقكم الله حلالا طيبا واتقوا الله الذي أنتم به مؤمنون

translation: Allah will not take you to task for your inadvertent oaths, but He will take you to task for your deliberate oaths; for its expiation (a deliberate oath) feed ten poor persons, on a scale of the average of that wherewith you feed your own families, or clothe them, or manumit a slave. If that is beyond your means, fast for three days. That is the expiation for the oaths ye have sworn. But keep your oaths. Thus doth Allah make clear to you His signs, that haply ye may be thankful.
interpretation: This verse explains the rules for dealing with oaths in Islam. It makes a distinction between unintentional oaths and deliberate oaths, stating that God will not hold people accountable for unintentional oaths. However, for deliberate oaths, the verse outlines the process of expiation. This can be done through feeding ten poor people, clothing them, or freeing a slave. If these actions are not feasible, then fasting for three days is an alternative. The verse emphasizes the importance of keeping one's oaths and expresses the hope that people will be grateful for God's guidance. The verse serves as a reminder of the seriousness of oaths and the need for sincerity and truthfulness in one's words and actions.
orig: لا يؤاخذكم الله باللغو في أيمانكم ولكن يؤاخذكم بما عقدتم الأيمان فكفارته إطعام عشرة مساكين من أوسط ما تطعمون أهليكم أو كسوتهم أو تحرير رقبة فمن لم يجد فصيام ثلاثة أيام ذلك كفارة أيمانكم إذا حلفتم واحفظوا أيمانكم كذلك يبين الله لكم آياته لعلكم تشكرون

translation: O you who have believed, indeed, intoxicants, gambling, [sacrificing on] stone alters, and divining arrows are but defilement from the work of Satan, so avoid it that you may be successful.
interpretation: The verse commands the believers to avoid intoxicants, gambling, sacrificing on stone alters, and divining arrows as they are impure and harmful practices that come from the work of Satan. By avoiding these acts, the believers can attain success in this life and the hereafter. The verse emphasizes the importance of staying away from sin and following the path of righteousness and piety.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا إنما الخمر والميسر والأنصاب والأزلام رجس من عمل الشيطان فاجتنبوه لعلكم تفلحون

translation: Satan only wants to cause enmity and hatred among you by wine and gambling, and to prevent you from the remembrance of Allah and from prayer. Will you, then, desist?
interpretation: The verse warns against the negative consequences of wine and gambling, which can cause enmity and hatred among people and distract them from the remembrance of God and prayer. Satan is the instigator of these vices, and the verse urges the believers to resist his temptations. The question at the end of the verse, 'Will you, then, desist?' emphasizes the importance of avoiding these vices and focusing on spiritual practices. The verse serves as a reminder that engaging in harmful behaviors can have serious consequences, and that it is essential to prioritize one's relationship with God and community.
orig: إنما يريد الشيطان أن يوقع بينكم العداوة والبغضاء في الخمر والميسر ويصدكم عن ذكر الله وعن الصلاة فهل أنتم منتهون

translation: And obey Allah and obey the Messenger and beware. And if you turn away - then know that upon Our Messenger is only the clear conveyance.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of obedience to Allah and His Messenger, and warns against disobedience. The verse also highlights the responsibility of the Messenger to convey the message clearly. If the people choose to turn away from the message, it is not the responsibility of the Messenger. The verse serves as a reminder to the believers of their duty to obey and follow the teachings of Islam, and the consequences of rejecting the message.
orig: وأطيعوا الله وأطيعوا الرسول واحذروا فإن توليتم فاعلموا أنما على رسولنا البلاغ المبين

translation: For those who have believed and done righteous deeds, there is no blame for what they ate [in the past] so long as they fear [God] and believe and do righteous deeds and then fear [God] and believe and then fear [God] and do good. And God loves the doers of good.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the absence of blame for past actions of those who have believed in God, performed righteous deeds, and continue to fear God and do good. The verse emphasizes the importance of a continuous cycle of faith, righteous deeds, and fear of God. It indicates that as long as a person maintains this cycle, they will not be held accountable for their past actions. The verse encourages believers to strive for continuous improvement and to always strive to do good. The verse also highlights God's love for those who do good, emphasizing the importance of performing good deeds not for the sake of avoiding blame, but for the sake of pleasing God and earning His love.
orig: ليس على الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات جناح فيما طعموا إذا ما اتقوا وآمنوا وعملوا الصالحات ثم اتقوا وآمنوا ثم اتقوا وأحسنوا والله يحب المحسنين

translation: O believers, Allah will surely test you with something related to the game that your hands and spears can attain, that Allah may know who fears Him unseen. So whoever transgresses after that, then for him is a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse speaks about a test from God that involves hunting or obtaining something through effort. The purpose of this test is for God to know who among the believers truly fears Him in private. Those who continue to transgress or disobey after this test will receive a painful punishment. The verse emphasizes the importance of obedience and reverence towards God, even when one is not being observed. It serves as a reminder to believers to uphold their faith and moral values at all times.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا ليبلونكم الله بشيء من الصيد تناله أيديكم ورماحكم ليعلم الله من يخافه بالغيب فمن اعتدى بعد ذلك فله عذاب أليم

translation: O you who have believed, do not kill game while you are in the state of pilgrimage. And whoever of you kills it intentionally - the penalty is equivalent to what he has unjustly killed of livestock, as judged by two just men among you as an offering to reach the Kaaba, or an expiation: the feeding of needy people or the equivalent of that in fasting, so that he may taste the consequence of his deed. Allah has pardoned what is past, but whoever returns [to violation], Allah will take retribution from him. And Allah is Exalted in Might and Owner of Retribution.
interpretation: The verse sets rules for Muslims during the state of pilgrimage, forbidding them from killing game. If someone intentionally kills game, the penalty is equivalent to what he has unjustly killed of livestock. The verse provides options for expiation, such as offering the livestock to reach the Kaaba, feeding the needy, or fasting. The verse emphasizes the importance of repentance and the consequences of actions, stating that Allah has pardoned past sins, but will take retribution on those who return to violation. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of following the rules set by Allah, and the consequences of not doing so.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تقتلوا الصيد وأنتم حرم ومن قتله منكم متعمدا فجزاء مثل ما قتل من النعم يحكم به ذوا عدل منكم هديا بالغ الكعبة أو كفارة طعام مساكين أو عدل ذلك صياما ليذوق وبال أمره عفا الله عما سلف ومن عاد فينتقم الله منه والله عزيز ذو انتقام

translation: Made lawful to you is the game of the sea and its food as sustenance for you and for the travelers, and prohibited to you is the game of the land as long as you are in the state of pilgrimage. And fear Allah, to whom you will be gathered.
interpretation: The verse outlines the permissibility of hunting and consuming sea creatures during one's travels, while also forbidding the hunting of land animals during the state of pilgrimage. The verse emphasizes the importance of respecting and following these laws, and fearing God, as all people will ultimately be gathered before Him. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of following God's laws, and the consequences of disobedience.
orig: أحل لكم صيد البحر وطعامه متاعا لكم وللسيارة وحرم عليكم صيد البر ما دمتم حرما واتقوا الله الذي إليه تحشرون

translation: Make God's Kaaba, the Sacred House, a stabilizer for the people, and (make) the sacred month, and the animals for sacrifice and the garlands (a stabilizer). That is so that you may know that God knows what is in the heavens and what is in the earth, and that God is all-knowing of all things.
interpretation: The verse describes the role of the Kaaba, the sacred month, the animals for sacrifice, and the garlands as stabilizers for the people. These symbols of Islam serve as a reminder of the presence and knowledge of God. By establishing these symbols, people are reminded of the all-encompassing knowledge of God, who knows everything in the heavens and the earth. The verse emphasizes the importance of these symbols in reminding people of their faith and their relationship with God.
orig: جعل الله الكعبة البيت الحرام قياما للناس والشهر الحرام والهدي والقلائد ذلك لتعلموا أن الله يعلم ما في السماوات وما في الأرض وأن الله بكل شيء عليم

translation: Know that indeed Allah is severe in penalty and indeed Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the severity of Allah's punishment for those who commit wrongdoing, while also highlighting Allah's forgiveness and mercy for those who repent and seek forgiveness. It serves as a reminder that Allah's attributes of punishment and mercy coexist, and that individuals should be mindful of their actions and seek Allah's forgiveness to avoid the severe penalty.
orig: اعلموا أن الله شديد العقاب وأن الله غفور رحيم

translation: The messenger is not but a clear warner. And Allah knows what you disclose and what you conceal.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the role of the messenger (Prophet Muhammad) as a clear warner, whose duty is only to convey the message from Allah. The second part of the verse highlights Allah's all-knowing nature, emphasizing that He knows both what people disclose and what they conceal. This verse can be interpreted as a reminder that the responsibility of the messenger is to convey the message, while the responsibility of the people is to heed the message and be aware that nothing can be hidden from Allah.
orig: ما على الرسول إلا البلاغ والله يعلم ما تبدون وما تكتمون

translation: Say, 'The evil and the good are not equal, even if the abundance of the evil pleases you.' So fear Allah, O possessors of intellect, that you may succeed.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of distinguishing between good and evil, and not allowing oneself to be deceived by the abundance of evil. The verse commands the reader to fear Allah and to use their intellect to discern the difference between the two. The verse implies that those who possess intellect will recognize the importance of this distinction and will strive to succeed by following the path of good. The verse serves as a warning against allowing oneself to be swayed by the abundance of evil and a reminder to use one's intellect and fear of Allah to guide one's actions.
orig: قل لا يستوي الخبيث والطيب ولو أعجبك كثرة الخبيث فاتقوا الله يا أولي الألباب لعلكم تفلحون

translation: O you who have believed, do not ask about matters which, if they are shown to you, will distress you. And if you ask about them while the Qur'an is being revealed, they will be shown to you. Allah has pardoned them, and Allah is Forgiving and Forbearing.
interpretation: The verse advises believers not to inquire about certain matters that, if revealed, would cause them distress or anxiety. If they do ask about these matters while the Qur'an is being revealed, they will be shown the answers. However, Allah has already forgiven these matters, demonstrating His mercy and patience towards His believers. The verse encourages believers to have patience and trust in Allah, and not to seek out information that may cause them harm or distress.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تسألوا عن أشياء إن تبد لكم تسؤكم وإن تسألوا عنها حين ينزل القرآن تبد لكم عفا الله عنها والله غفور حليم

translation: And they had asked her before, she and her people, then they became disbelievers after that.
interpretation: The verse speaks about a group of people who asked a woman (presumably a prophet or a messenger) a question, but then rejected her message and became disbelievers. The verse highlights the rejection of truth and the stubbornness of people in their disbelief, despite having the opportunity to learn and understand. The verse serves as a reminder that even after being exposed to the truth, some people may still choose to reject it and face the consequences of their actions.
orig: قد سألها قوم من قبلكم ثم أصبحوا بها كافرين

translation: And
interpretation: No interpretation
orig: ما جعل الله من بحيرة ولا سائبة ولا وصيلة ولا حام ولكن الذين كفروا يفترون على الله الكذب وأكثرهم لا يعقلون

translation: And when it is said to them, 'Come to what Allah has revealed and to the Messenger,' they say, 'Sufficient for us is what we found our forefathers doing.' Even if their forefathers had no knowledge and guidance?
interpretation: The verse addresses the people who reject the message of Islam and refuse to follow the guidance brought by the Prophet Muhammad. Instead, they insist on following the traditions and beliefs of their ancestors. The verse questions the validity of their actions, implying that blindly following the ways of the past without seeking knowledge and guidance is a flawed approach. The verse serves as a reminder that true guidance comes from Allah and His messenger, and it is important to follow their teachings rather than clinging to outdated customs and traditions.
orig: وإذا قيل لهم تعالوا إلى ما أنزل الله وإلى الرسول قالوا حسبنا ما وجدنا عليه آباءنا أولو كان آباؤهم لا يعلمون شيئا ولا يهتدون

translation: O you who have believed, upon you is yourselves. If you follow the right guidance, it will benefit you. And if you turn away, then only upon yourselves is [the consequence of] your misdeed. And you are not at all a guider for Him.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the individual responsibility of believers for their own actions. It states that if they follow the right guidance, they will benefit from it, but if they turn away from it, they will bear the consequences of their misdeeds. The verse also makes it clear that the believers are not responsible for guiding God, as He is not in need of guidance from His creation.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا عليكم أنفسكم لا يضركم من ضل إذا اهتديتم إلى الله مرجعكم جميعا فينبئكم بما كنتم تعملون

translation: O you who have believed, when death approaches one of you, two just ones from among you shall strive (as witnesses). And if there are not two men (available), then a man and two women from those other than you (as witnesses); so if you distort (the testimony), then indeed We have prepared for the deceivers a painful punishment.
interpretation: The verse outlines the rules for witnessing the last will and testament of a dying person. It emphasizes the importance of having two just male witnesses, and if not possible, then one man and two women from outside the family. The verse warns against distorting the testimony and reminds the witnesses of the severe consequences of their actions. The verse also highlights the importance of justice and fairness in the Islamic community.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا شهادة بينكم إذا حضر أحدكم الموت حين الوصية اثنان ذوا عدل منكم أو آخران من غيركم إن أنتم ضربتم في الأرض فأصابتكم مصيبة الموت تحبسونهما من بعد الصلاة فيقسمان بالله إن ارتبتم لا نشتري به ثمنا ولو كان ذا قربى ولا نكتم شهادة الله إنا إذا لمن الآثمين

translation: But if you come upon them, engaging in sinful acts, then turn away from them until they enter into some other affair. And if Satan should cause you to forget, then do not remain after the reminder with the wrongdoing people. Indeed, for the wrongdoers is a painful punishment.
interpretation: The verse provides guidance on how to deal with people who are committing sins. If one comes across such people, they are instructed to turn away from them and leave them alone. The verse emphasizes the importance of avoiding sin and not being a part of it. If one forgets and stays with the wrongdoers, they are reminded to leave once they remember. The verse serves as a warning to those who engage in sinful acts, reminding them of the severe punishment that awaits them. It also encourages believers to be mindful of their actions and to avoid being associated with wrongdoing.
orig: فإن عثر على أنهما استحقا إثما فآخران يقومان مقامهما من الذين استحق عليهم الأوليان فيقسمان بالله لشهادتنا أحق من شهادتهما وما اعتدينا إنا إذا لمن الظالمين

translation: That is easier for them that they should bear witness to the truth on their own behalf, or else they should fear that another charge like that of falsehood may be brought against them. And urge not such upon them that can afford no help; but if they deny you, surely Allah loves not the ungrateful.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the importance of bearing witness to the truth, and the consequences of not doing so. People are encouraged to be truthful and to be mindful of the potential consequences of their actions. The verse highlights the importance of being honest and sincere, and the dangers of being ungrateful and denying the truth. The verse encourages people to be mindful of their responsibilities and to be aware of the consequences of their actions. It also emphasizes the importance of not urging people to do things that they are unable to do, and the importance of being understanding and compassionate towards those who are in need of help.
orig: ذلك أدنى أن يأتوا بالشهادة على وجهها أو يخافوا أن ترد أيمان بعد أيمانهم واتقوا الله واسمعوا والله لا يهدي القوم الفاسقين

translation: The day when God will gather the messengers and say, 'What was your response?' They will say, 'We have no knowledge. Indeed, You are the Knower of the unseen.'
interpretation: The verse describes the Day of Judgment when God will gather all the messengers and ask them about their mission and the response of their people to their message. The messengers will confess their ignorance of the outcome of their mission and acknowledge God's knowledge of the unseen. This verse highlights the ultimate accountability of all messengers and the submission of even the most exalted beings to God's knowledge and power.
orig: يوم يجمع الله الرسل فيقول ماذا أجبتم قالوا لا علم لنا إنك أنت علام الغيوب

translation: When Allah said, 'O Jesus, son of Mary, remember My favor upon you and upon your mother when I supported you with the Holy Spirit, you spoke to the people in the cradle and in maturity; and [remember] when I taught you writing, wisdom, and the Torah and the Gospel; and when you designed from clay [what was] like a bird with My permission, then you breathed into it, and it became a bird with My permission; and you healed the blind and the leper with My permission; and when you brought forth the dead with My permission; and when I restrained the Children of Israel from you when you came to them with the clear proofs, and those who disbelieved among them said, 'This is nothing but obvious magic.'
interpretation: The verse is a direct address from Allah to Jesus, recounting the many blessings and miracles that Allah bestowed upon him. The verse emphasizes that all of Jesus's abilities and miracles were granted to him by Allah, including his ability to speak as a baby, his knowledge of the scriptures, and his power to heal and bring back the dead. The verse also mentions the disbelief and rejection that Jesus faced from some of the Children of Israel, despite the clear signs and evidence he presented to them. The verse serves to remind the reader of the power and mercy of Allah, who bestows blessings and miracles upon whom He wills, and who has the power to give life and take it away.
orig: إذ قال الله يا عيسى ابن مريم اذكر نعمتي عليك وعلى والدتك إذ أيدتك بروح القدس تكلم الناس في المهد وكهلا وإذ علمتك الكتاب والحكمة والتوراة والإنجيل وإذ تخلق من الطين كهيئة الطير بإذني فتنفخ فيها فتكون طيرا بإذني وتبرئ الأكمه والأبرص بإذني وإذ تخرج الموتى بإذني وإذ كففت بني إسرائيل عنك إذ جئتهم بالبينات فقال الذين كفروا منهم إن هذا إلا سحر مبين

translation: And when I inspired the disciples, (saying), 'Believe in Me and in My messenger,' they said, 'We believe. And bear witness that we are Muslims.'
interpretation: The verse describes the moment when Jesus (peace be upon him) called upon his disciples to believe in him and his messengership. The disciples responded positively, declaring their faith in both Jesus and his message. They also declared their submission to God by stating that they were Muslims. This verse emphasizes the importance of believing in the prophets and their messages, and the importance of submitting oneself to God's will.
orig: وإذ أوحيت إلى الحواريين أن آمنوا بي وبرسولي قالوا آمنا واشهد بأننا مسلمون

translation: When the disciples said: 'O Jesus, son of Mary, can your Lord send down to us a table from heaven?' Jesus replied: 'Fear God, if you are indeed believers.'
interpretation: The verse recounts a conversation between Jesus and his disciples, in which the disciples request that Jesus' Lord send down a table from heaven. Jesus responds by urging them to fear God and have faith, implying that such a miracle would only be possible if they truly believe. The verse highlights the importance of faith and the need for believers to have trust and patience in God's plan, rather than seeking out signs and wonders as proof of His existence or power.
orig: إذ قال الحواريون يا عيسى ابن مريم هل يستطيع ربك أن ينزل علينا مائدة من السماء قال اتقوا الله إن كنتم مؤمنين

translation: They said, 'We want to eat from it and to calm our hearts, and we know that you have told us the truth, and we will be among its witnesses.'
interpretation: The verse describes a group of people who are speaking to a prophet or a messenger of God. They express their desire to partake of a certain thing (it is not specified what) and explain that their intention is not only to eat from it, but also to find comfort and peace in it. They acknowledge that the prophet has been truthful in his teachings and announce their intention to be witnesses to the event or situation. The verse highlights the importance of belief and trust in the words of the prophet, and the significance of being a witness to God's signs and miracles.
orig: قالوا نريد أن نأكل منها وتطمئن قلوبنا ونعلم أن قد صدقتنا ونكون عليها من الشاهدين

translation: Said Jesus the son of Mary: 'O God, our Lord, send down to us a table from heaven to be for us a festival for the first of us and the last of us and a sign from You, and provide for us, and You are the best of providers.'
interpretation: In this verse, Jesus is praying to God and asking him to send down a table from heaven that will serve as a feast for his community, both past and present. He is asking for this not only as a means of sustenance, but also as a sign from God, a manifestation of His power and benevolence. Jesus is expressing his trust and dependence on God, and his certainty that God is the best of providers. The verse can be understood as a metaphorical representation of God's grace and blessings, and as a reminder of the importance of faith and trust in God.
orig: قال عيسى ابن مريم اللهم ربنا أنزل علينا مائدة من السماء تكون لنا عيدا لأولنا وآخرنا وآية منك وارزقنا وأنت خير الرازقين

translation: Allah says, 'I have already sent it to you in detail, so if any among you disbelieves, then indeed, I will punish him with a punishment that will be more severe than that of most of the worlds.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the revelation of divine guidance in detail, and warns those who reject it of the severe punishment that will follow. The punishment is described as being more severe than that of most of the worlds, emphasizing the gravity of the offense of disbelief. The verse serves as a warning to those who deny or ignore the divine message, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: قال الله إني منزلها عليكم فمن يكفر بعد منكم فإني أعذبه عذابا لا أعذبه أحدا من العالمين

translation: And when Allah said, 'O Jesus, son of Mary, did you say to the people, 'Take me and my mother as deities besides Allah?'' He said, 'Exalted are You! It was not for me to say that to which I have no right. If I had said it, You would have known it. You know what is within myself, and I do not know what is within Yourself. Indeed, You are the Knower of the unseen.
interpretation: The verse is a conversation between God and Jesus, where God asks Jesus if he told people to take him and his mother as deities besides God. Jesus denies this and affirms his belief in the oneness of God. The verse emphasizes Jesus's submission and obedience to God and his recognition of God's knowledge and power. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of monotheism and the rejection of any form of polytheism or idolatry.
orig: وإذ قال الله يا عيسى ابن مريم أأنت قلت للناس اتخذوني وأمي إلهين من دون الله قال سبحانك ما يكون لي أن أقول ما ليس لي بحق إن كنت قلته فقد علمته تعلم ما في نفسي ولا أعلم ما في نفسك إنك أنت علام الغيوب

translation: I did not say to them anything except what I was commanded: 'Worship Allah, my Lord and your Lord.' And I was a witness over them as long as I was among them, but when You took me up, You were the Observer over them, and You are, over every thing, Witness.
interpretation: The verse is a statement by a prophet or a messenger, who is speaking about his role and responsibilities towards his people. He emphasizes that he only conveyed the message of worshipping one God, Allah, and was a witness to their actions while he was among them. However, after his departure, he acknowledges that it is God who is the ultimate observer and witness over them. The verse highlights the role of a prophet as a messenger and a witness, and the ultimate power and knowledge of God as the all-seeing and all-knowing.
orig: ما قلت لهم إلا ما أمرتني به أن اعبدوا الله ربي وربكم وكنت عليهم شهيدا ما دمت فيهم فلما توفيتني كنت أنت الرقيب عليهم وأنت على كل شيء شهيد

translation: If you punish them, they are Your servants, and if You forgive them, indeed You are the Exalted in Might, the Wise.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the relationship between God and humanity, highlighting the power and wisdom of God. The verse states that even if God were to punish His servants, they are still His creation, and if He forgives them, it further demonstrates His greatness and wisdom. The verse reminds the reader of the ultimate power and control that God has over all of creation, and the importance of seeking His forgiveness and mercy.
orig: إن تعذبهم فإنهم عبادك وإن تغفر لهم فإنك أنت العزيز الحكيم

translation: Allah has said, 'This is the day on which the truthful will benefit from their truthfulness.' For them are gardens beneath which rivers flow, forever in them, Allah will be pleased with them, and they will be pleased with Him. That is the great triumph.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the ultimate reward for the truthful on the Day of Judgment. It emphasizes the eternal bliss and happiness that await them in the form of gardens with flowing rivers. The verse highlights the mutual satisfaction between Allah and the truthful, indicating a perfect and harmonious relationship. The verse serves as a source of motivation for believers to strive for truthfulness and honesty, promising them the greatest triumph and success in the hereafter.
orig: قال الله هذا يوم ينفع الصادقين صدقهم لهم جنات تجري من تحتها الأنهار خالدين فيها أبدا رضي الله عنهم ورضوا عنه ذلك الفوز العظيم

translation: To Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them, and He is over all things competent.
interpretation: The verse affirms the sovereignty and power of Allah over all of creation, including the heavens, the earth, and everything in between. The verse emphasizes that Allah is competent over all things, indicating His complete control and authority over the universe. This verse serves as a reminder of the greatness and majesty of Allah, and the smallness and dependence of human beings in comparison. It also encourages believers to have trust and reliance on Allah, knowing that He has the power and ability to handle all affairs.
orig: لله ملك السماوات والأرض وما فيهن وهو على كل شيء قدير

translation: ‘Praise be to God, who created the heavens and the earth, and made the darkness and the light. Then those who disbelieve in their Lord, they are the ones who will continue to judge unjustly.’
interpretation: The verse begins by praising God for His creation of the heavens and the earth, and for the contrasting elements of darkness and light. The verse then contrasts those who disbelieve in God with those who recognize and worship Him. The disbelievers are characterized as those who will continue to judge unjustly. The verse emphasizes the fundamental difference between those who acknowledge and worship God, and those who deny and disbelieve in Him, and the consequences of that denial in terms of their actions and judgment.
orig: الحمد لله الذي خلق السماوات والأرض وجعل الظلمات والنور ثم الذين كفروا بربهم يعدلون

translation: He it is who created you from clay, then decreed a term, and a term known (to Him), thereafter you are merely a disputer.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the power of God as the creator of human beings, made from clay and given a specific term of life. The verse highlights the limited knowledge and understanding of human beings, as they can only estimate the length of their lives, while God has full knowledge of it. The verse serves as a reminder of the human's limited control over their lives and the futility of their disputes in the face of God's power and knowledge.
orig: هو الذي خلقكم من طين ثم قضى أجلا وأجل مسمى عنده ثم أنتم تمترون

translation: And He is Allah, in the heavens and in the earth, and He knows your secret and what you reveal, and He knows what you earn.
interpretation: The verse affirms the all-encompassing knowledge and awareness of Allah, who is present in both the heavens and the earth. The verse emphasizes that Allah knows everything about human beings, including their secrets and what they reveal, as well as what they earn. This knowledge is all-encompassing and extends to all aspects of human existence. The verse serves as a reminder of the all-knowing and all-seeing nature of Allah, and the importance of leading a righteous life in accordance with His teachings, as every action and intention is known to Him.
orig: وهو الله في السماوات وفي الأرض يعلم سركم وجهركم ويعلم ما تكسبون

translation: And never came to them a sign from the signs of their Lord except they were averse to it.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the people's rejection and denial of the signs sent by their Lord. Every time a sign was sent, the people rejected it and turned away from it. The verse emphasizes the people's closed-mindedness and unwillingness to accept the truth, even when it was presented to them in the form of clear signs from their Lord. The verse serves as a reminder of the consequences of denying the truth and the importance of being open to the signs and messages sent by God.
orig: وما تأتيهم من آية من آيات ربهم إلا كانوا عنها معرضين

translation: They have indeed disbelieved in the Reminder (the Quran) when it came to them, so soon will they know. As for the news of what they used to mock, it will come to them.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the disbelievers who rejected the truth (the Quran) when it was presented to them. The verse warns them that they will soon come to know the reality, and the consequences of their disbelief. The verse also mentions that they will receive news of what they used to mock and ridicule, indicating that their mockery will turn against them and they will face the consequences of their actions.
orig: فقد كذبوا بالحق لما جاءهم فسوف يأتيهم أنباء ما كانوا به يستهزئون

translation: Have they not seen how many a generation before them We have destroyed, whom We had established in the earth more firmly than We have established you, and We sent the heavens upon them with abundant rain, and made rivers to flow beneath them; and We destroyed them because of their sins, and established after them another generation?
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of previous generations who were given more favorable conditions than the current generation, yet they were destroyed due to their sins. The verse highlights the power of God in establishing and destroying civilizations, and the consequences of human disobedience. It serves as a warning to the current generation, urging them to reflect on the fate of their predecessors and to avoid making the same mistakes.
orig: ألم يروا كم أهلكنا من قبلهم من قرن مكناهم في الأرض ما لم نمكن لكم وأرسلنا السماء عليهم مدرارا وجعلنا الأنهار تجري من تحتهم فأهلكناهم بذنوبهم وأنشأنا من بعدهم قرنا آخرين

translation: And if We had sent down upon you a written (scripture) on parchment, and they had touched it with their hands, the disbelievers would have said, 'This is nothing but obvious magic.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the reaction of the disbelievers when they are faced with clear signs and evidence from God. The verse mentions that even if God had sent down a scripture on parchment, and the disbelievers had touched it with their own hands, they would have still rejected it and called it 'obvious magic'. This shows the stubbornness and closed-mindedness of the disbelievers, who refuse to accept the truth even when it is presented to them in a clear and tangible form. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of having faith and being open to the signs of God, rather than being swayed by doubt and disbelief.
orig: ولو نزلنا عليك كتابا في قرطاس فلمسوه بأيديهم لقال الذين كفروا إن هذا إلا سحر مبين

translation: And they say, 'Why has not a treasure been sent down to him, or why has not an angel come with him?' But if We had sent down a treasure or an angel, the matter would have been settled; then they would not have been given any respite.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the disbelievers questioning why a treasure or an angel has not been sent down to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). The verse emphasizes that if such a thing had happened, the matter would have been settled and the disbelievers would not have been given any respite. The verse serves as a reminder that the truth of the Prophet Muhammad's message is not dependent on material proofs or supernatural signs, but rather on the guidance of God and the believers' faith and understanding. It also highlights the disbelievers' lack of understanding and their rejection of the message despite the evidence and signs that have been presented to them.
orig: وقالوا لولا أنزل عليه ملك ولو أنزلنا ملكا لقضي الأمر ثم لا ينظرون

translation: And if We had made him a king, We would have made him a man of lowly birth, and We would have kept him constantly under Our surveillance.
interpretation: The verse suggests that even if God had given someone a position of power and authority, such as a king, He would have still maintained control and kept a close eye on them. The phrase 'man of lowly birth' could mean that God would have chosen someone who was humble and unassuming for the position, or it could be a reminder that no matter how powerful a person becomes, they are still subject to God's will. The verse serves as a reminder that even those in positions of power are not beyond God's reach and are ultimately accountable to Him.
orig: ولو جعلناه ملكا لجعلناه رجلا وللبسنا عليهم ما يلبسون

translation: And they have mocked Our messengers before; then, the punishment seized them suddenly, as they were doing wrongdeeds.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the mockery and disbelief of previous nations towards God's messengers. It highlights that these disbelievers not only rejected the messengers, but they also mocked them. The verse then describes that the punishment from God came upon them suddenly and took them by surprise while they were in the midst of committing sins and wrongdoings. This verse serves as a reminder of the consequences of mocking and disbelieving in God's messengers and the certainty of God's punishment towards those who commit wrongdoings.
orig: ولقد استهزئ برسل من قبلك فحاق بالذين سخروا منهم ما كانوا به يستهزئون

translation: Say, 'Travel through the land and observe how was the end of the deniers.'
interpretation: The verse is a command from God to the Prophet Muhammad to tell the disbelievers to travel through the land and observe the fate of past nations who rejected God's messengers. By doing so, the disbelievers will understand the consequences of denying the truth and the ultimate end of those who reject God's message. This verse serves as a warning to the disbelievers and a reminder to the believers of the importance of faith and obedience to God's commands.
orig: قل سيروا في الأرض ثم انظروا كيف كان عاقبة المكذبين

translation: Say, 'Who provides for you from the heaven and the earth? Say, 'It is Allah; indeed, He has heard and knows [all things]. If you invoke [only] aside from Him, then indeed, you are [truly] unjust people.' But whether you hide what is in your breasts or reveal it, indeed, Allah knows it. Then He will pardon whom He wills and punish whom He wills, and Allah is over all things competent.' Say, 'To whom belongs the earth and whoever is in it, if you should know?' They will say, 'To Allah.' Say, 'Then how are you deluded?' Rather, We have brought them the truth, and indeed, they are liars. Say, 'What thing is greatest in testimony?' Say, 'Allah is Witness between me and you. And this Qur'an has been revealed to me that I may warn you with it and whomever it reaches. Do you bear witness that there are other gods with Him?' Say, 'I do not bear witness.' And say, 'Indeed, He is only one God, and indeed, I am free of what you associate [with Him].' Those to whom We have given the Book recognize it as they recognize their sons. But indeed, a party of them conceal the truth while they know [it].
interpretation: This passage is a series of commands to the Prophet Muhammad to say certain things to the disbelievers. The overall message is that Allah is the only God and the provider of all things, and that the disbelievers are unjust and deluded for associating other gods with Him. The passage emphasizes Allah's knowledge and power, and His ability to pardon or punish as He wills.
