The Prophet is told to ask the disbelievers about the true ownership of the earth and its inhabitants, and to declare that he does not bear witness to the existence of other gods. The passage ends by stating that those who have been given the Book (i.e. the Jews and Christians) recognize the truth, but some of them conceal it. The passage serves as a reminder of the truth of monotheism and the falsehood of polytheism, and a call to bear witness to the oneness of Allah.
orig: قل لمن ما في السماوات والأرض قل لله كتب على نفسه الرحمة ليجمعنكم إلى يوم القيامة لا ريب فيه الذين خسروا أنفسهم فهم لا يؤمنون

translation: To Him belongs what is in the heavens and what is on the earth, and He is the Hearing, the Knowing.
interpretation: The verse affirms that everything in the heavens and on earth belongs to God, emphasizing His power and sovereignty over all of creation. The phrase 'He is the Hearing, the Knowing' highlights God's complete knowledge and awareness of all things, and His ability to hear and respond to His creatures' prayers and needs. This verse can serve as a reminder of God's greatness and omnipotence, and inspire awe and reverence for Him.
orig: وله ما سكن في الليل والنهار وهو السميع العليم

translation: Say, 'Is it other than Allah that you order me to worship, while He is the Creator of the heavens and the earth and He feeds and is not fed?' Say, 'Indeed, I have been commanded to be the first [among you] who submits [to Allah as a Muslim] and be not of the polytheists.'
interpretation: The verse is a command to Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to declare his faith and submission to Allah alone, and to not associate any partners with Him. The verse emphasizes Allah's power and control over all of creation, and His ability to provide for His creation without needing anything in return. The verse also highlights the importance of submitting to Allah and being a part of the Muslim community, and the importance of not being among the polytheists. The verse serves as a reminder and a call to faith and submission to Allah for the Prophet and his followers.
orig: قل أغير الله أتخذ وليا فاطر السماوات والأرض وهو يطعم ولا يطعم قل إني أمرت أن أكون أول من أسلم ولا تكونن من المشركين

translation: Say, 'I only fear the punishment of a tremendous Day, if I disobey my Lord.'
interpretation: The verse is a statement made by a prophet or a messenger, urging people to heed his warning and follow the right path. The speaker expresses their fear of the punishment on the 'tremendous Day' (referring to the Day of Judgment) if they disobey their Lord. This verse emphasizes the importance of obedience to God and the gravity of the consequences of disobedience. It serves as a reminder that there will be a reckoning for all our actions, and that we should fear the punishment of the Day of Judgment and strive to obey God in order to avoid it.
orig: قل إني أخاف إن عصيت ربي عذاب يوم عظيم

translation: Whoever turns away from it that day - He will have deserved wrath upon himself, and that will be an obvious failure.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the consequences for those who turn away from the truth or the right path on a particular day. The verse warns that such people will face wrath and that this will be a clear and obvious failure. The verse emphasizes the importance of following the right path and not turning away from it, and it highlights the serious consequences for those who do not heed this warning.
orig: من يصرف عنه يومئذ فقد رحمه وذلك الفوز المبين

translation: And if God touches you with harm, there is no remover of it except Him; and if He touches you with good, He is over all things competent.
interpretation: The verse highlights the complete power and control that God has over all things, both positive and negative. The phrase 'if God touches you with harm' refers to any adversity or hardship that a person may experience, and emphasizes that only God has the power to remove or alleviate it. Similarly, the phrase 'if He touches you with good' refers to any blessings or positive experiences, and reaffirms that God is the source of all goodness and has the power to grant or withhold it. The verse encourages believers to recognize and submit to God's power and control over all aspects of their lives.
orig: وإن يمسسك الله بضر فلا كاشف له إلا هو وإن يمسسك بخير فهو على كل شيء قدير

translation: And He is Exalted above His servants, and He is the Knower, the Exalted in Might, the Wise.
interpretation: The verse affirms the greatness and power of God, who is described as being exalted and superior to His servants. The verse emphasizes God's all-encompassing knowledge and His absolute power, as He is described as the Knower, the Exalted in Might, and the Wise. The verse serves as a reminder of God's majesty and omnipotence, and encourages believers to recognize and submit to His greatness.
orig: وهو القاهر فوق عباده وهو الحكيم الخبير

translation: Say, 'What is greater as a witness?' Say, 'God is a sufficient witness between me and you. He knows what is in the heavens and the earth.' And those who believe in false deities along with God, say, 'If God had willed, we would not have worshipped them.' So, say to them, 'Is there for God any partners who have created the heavens and the earth? Or have they established any foundation?' Say to them, 'Who are the ones that control the treasures of mercy, if it is Him you call on?' Say to them, 'Is it other than God that you order me to worship?' And, 'It is already determined that apart from God, I will not worship any other deity.' I am commanded to be the first of those who submit, saying, 'I fear the punishment of a painful Day.'
interpretation: The verse is a conversation between the Prophet Muhammad and the disbelievers. The Prophet asks the disbelievers to bring a witness greater than God, emphasizing God's knowledge of all things. The disbelievers are reminded that they should not worship false deities, and the Prophet asserts his submission to God alone. The verse emphasizes the oneness of God and the importance of worshipping only Him. The Prophet also highlights the consequences of disbelief, warning of the punishment of a painful Day. The verse serves as a reminder of the power and greatness of God, and the importance of submitting to Him alone.
orig: قل أي شيء أكبر شهادة قل الله شهيد بيني وبينكم وأوحي إلي هذا القرآن لأنذركم به ومن بلغ أئنكم لتشهدون أن مع الله آلهة أخرى قل لا أشهد قل إنما هو إله واحد وإنني بريء مما تشركون

translation: Those to whom We have given the Scripture recognize it as they recognize their own sons. But indeed, a party of them conceal the truth while they are aware of it.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the recognition of the truth (the message of Islam) by those who have been given the scripture (Jews and Christians). They are able to recognize the truth just as they recognize their own children. However, despite this recognition, some of them conceal the truth and refuse to accept it, even though they are aware of its truth. This is a criticism of those who choose to reject the truth and deny it, even though they know it to be true.
orig: الذين آتيناهم الكتاب يعرفونه كما يعرفون أبناءهم الذين خسروا أنفسهم فهم لا يؤمنون

translation: And who is more unjust than he who invents a lie about Allah or denies His signs? Surely, the unjust will not prosper.
interpretation: The verse highlights the grave consequences of lying about Allah or denying His signs. Those who commit such acts are described as being extremely unjust and are warned that they will not prosper. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of upholding the truth and acknowledging the signs of Allah, and the severe consequences for those who do not.
orig: ومن أظلم ممن افترى على الله كذبا أو كذب بآياته إنه لا يفلح الظالمون

translation: And the Day when We will gather them all together, then We will say to those who associated others with Us, 'Where are your partners, those whom you claimed?'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the Day of Judgment, when all people will be gathered together before God. On that day, God will address those who associated others with Him in worship and ask them about their 'partners' or deities whom they claimed to be equal to God. This verse emphasizes the futility of idolatry and the falsehood of associating partners with God. It serves as a reminder to those who worship anything other than God, urging them to reflect on the emptiness of their claims and the certainty of God's judgment.
orig: ويوم نحشرهم جميعا ثم نقول للذين أشركوا أين شركاؤكم الذين كنتم تزعمون

translation: But they were not long in coming to a blameworthy end: they said, 'Our Lord, had we but a while longer, we would have been among the right-guided.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about a group of people who did not heed the warnings and continued to commit wrongdoings. They only turned to God and expressed their regret when they faced the consequences of their actions. The verse highlights the futility of their regret as it was too late for them to change their ways. The verse serves as a reminder that it is important to act righteously and avoid falling into wrongdoings, rather than waiting until it is too late and facing the consequences of one's actions.
orig: ثم لم تكن فتنتهم إلا أن قالوا والله ربنا ما كنا مشركين

translation: Consider how they lied to themselves, and how they strayed from the truth that they used to deny.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the self-deception and delusion of those who deny the truth. They lied to themselves and strayed from the right path. The verse highlights the consequences of their denial and rejection of the truth, and serves as a reminder that their falsehood will not benefit them in the end.
orig: انظر كيف كذبوا على أنفسهم وضل عنهم ما كانوا يفترون

translation: And among them are those who listen to you, but We have set veils on their hearts, such that they do not understand it, and deafness in their ears. And even if they see every sign, they will not believe in it until when they come to you arguing, those who disbelieve say, 'This is nothing but the myths of the ancients.'
interpretation: The verse describes a group of people who hear the message of the prophet but are unable to understand or accept it due to the veils that God has placed on their hearts. They are also described as being deaf, emphasizing their inability to comprehend the message. Despite seeing clear signs and evidence, they still refuse to believe. Instead, they dismiss the message as mere myths and stories of the past. The verse highlights the hard-heartedness and stubbornness of those who reject the message of the prophet, and the futility of trying to convince them with logic or reason.
orig: ومنهم من يستمع إليك وجعلنا على قلوبهم أكنة أن يفقهوه وفي آذانهم وقرا وإن يروا كل آية لا يؤمنوا بها حتى إذا جاءوك يجادلونك يقول الذين كفروا إن هذا إلا أساطير الأولين

translation: And they forbid it while they themselves are guilty of it, and they do it (i.e., commit sins); but they are not aware of it. And if they were to know of it, they would not have done it. But their awareness and understanding comes only when it is too late, and they are already punished for it.
interpretation: The verse speaks about people who forbid others from committing sins, but they themselves commit those sins. They are not aware of their own sins, and if they had knowledge of them, they would not commit them. However, their awareness and understanding comes only when it is too late, and they are already punished for their sins. The verse highlights the hypocrisy of people who judge others for their sins, while they themselves commit the same sins. It also emphasizes the importance of self-awareness and self-reflection, and the dangers of hypocrisy and double standards.
orig: وهم ينهون عنه وينأون عنه وإن يهلكون إلا أنفسهم وما يشعرون

translation: And if you could but see when they stand before the Fire, they will say, 'Oh, if only we could return, we would not deny the signs of our Lord and we would be among the believers.'
interpretation: The verse describes the regret of the disbelievers when they stand before the Fire (Hell) and realize the reality of their situation. They express their desire to return to the worldly life, promising that they would not deny the signs of their Lord and would be among the believers. This verse emphasizes the importance of faith and obedience to God, highlighting the consequences of disbelief and denial of God's signs. The verse also serves as a reminder that it is never too late to turn back to God and change one's ways.
orig: ولو ترى إذ وقفوا على النار فقالوا يا ليتنا نرد ولا نكذب بآيات ربنا ونكون من المؤمنين

translation: It was already revealed to them what they were concealing, but never would they revert [to righteousness]. And if they were to see a sign, they would not believe in it. And if it was not for the favor of Allah upon you and His mercy, you would have followed the devil, except for a few.
interpretation: The verse speaks about people who concealed the truth and rejected it, even when it was revealed to them. Despite knowing the truth, they refused to change their ways and would not believe even if they saw a sign. The verse highlights the hard-heartedness of these people and their rejection of the truth. The verse also mentions the importance of God's mercy in guiding people towards the right path, as without it, one would be led astray. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of accepting the truth, even when it goes against one's desires or beliefs.
orig: بل بدا لهم ما كانوا يخفون من قبل ولو ردوا لعادوا لما نهوا عنه وإنهم لكاذبون

translation: And they say, 'It is only our worldly life, and we are not being resurrected.'
interpretation: The verse presents the disbelievers' denial of the afterlife and their belief that this world is their only life. They argue that they will not be resurrected after their death. This interpretation highlights the contrast between the believers and the disbelievers, emphasizing the importance of faith in the afterlife and the consequences of denying it.
orig: وقالوا إن هي إلا حياتنا الدنيا وما نحن بمبعوثين

translation: And if you could but see when they stand before their Lord, He will say, 'Is this not the truth?' They will say, 'Yes, indeed.' He will say, 'Then taste the punishment for your disbelief.'
interpretation: The verse describes the Day of Judgment when the disbelievers will stand before God and acknowledge the truth. However, it will be too late for them to repent or make amends, as they will immediately receive punishment for their disbelief. The verse serves as a warning to those who deny the truth and a reminder of the consequences of disbelief.
orig: ولو ترى إذ وقفوا على ربهم قال أليس هذا بالحق قالوا بلى وربنا قال فذوقوا العذاب بما كنتم تكفرون

translation: Indeed, those who have denied the meeting with Allah have lost. So when the Hour comes upon them unexpectedly, they will say, 'Oh, [how great is] our regret over what we neglected.', while they bear their burdens on their backs. Indeed, what they bear is difficult.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the fate of those who deny the meeting with Allah and do not believe in the Day of Judgment. The verse highlights the sudden and unexpected arrival of the Hour (the Day of Judgment), which will cause great regret for those who did not prepare for it. They will bear the burden of their sins and actions on their backs, which will be a heavy load. The verse serves as a warning to those who deny the meeting with Allah and a reminder to prepare for the Day of Judgment.
orig: قد خسر الذين كذبوا بلقاء الله حتى إذا جاءتهم الساعة بغتة قالوا يا حسرتنا على ما فرطنا فيها وهم يحملون أوزارهم على ظهورهم ألا ساء ما يزرون

translation: And this worldly life is nothing but a play and amusement. And indeed, the home of the Hereafter - that is the true life, if only they knew.
interpretation: The verse highlights the fleeting and insignificant nature of worldly life, describing it as a mere play and amusement. In contrast, the verse emphasizes the importance of the hereafter, describing it as the true and everlasting life. The verse serves as a reminder for people to focus on their hereafter, and to strive for righteousness and piety in order to attain a better life in the hereafter. The verse suggests that people should reflect and ponder upon the reality of life and the purpose of their existence, and not be deceived by the temporary pleasures of this world.
orig: وما الحياة الدنيا إلا لعب ولهو وللدار الآخرة خير للذين يتقون أفلا تعقلون

translation: Indeed, We know that it grieves you that they say, 'But indeed, they (i.e., the disbelievers) do not deny you,' but rather, the unjust reject the verses of Allah.
interpretation: The verse acknowledges the pain that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) feels when he is falsely accused of being denied by the disbelievers. However, the verse clarifies that the disbelievers do not deny the Prophet, but rather, they reject the signs of God. The verse emphasizes the rejection of the unjust and the importance of recognizing and accepting the signs of God, which is a fundamental aspect of faith.
orig: قد نعلم إنه ليحزنك الذي يقولون فإنهم لا يكذبونك ولكن الظالمين بآيات الله يجحدون

translation: And indeed, before you, messengers have been denied, but they bore with patience the denial, and they were harmed until Our help came to them. And there is no changing the words of Allah. And you have certainly come to them with clear proofs.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the patience and perseverance of the messengers of God in the face of denial and harm from the people. It highlights that the messengers did not change the message of God, despite facing opposition and suffering. The verse also emphasizes that the coming of the prophet (presumably referring to the Prophet Muhammad) with clear signs and proofs is in accordance with the will of God and that the words of God cannot be changed. The verse serves as a reminder of the steadfastness of the messengers and the certainty of God's plan, encouraging the believers to remain firm in their faith and trust in God's guidance and protection.
orig: ولقد كذبت رسل من قبلك فصبروا على ما كذبوا وأوذوا حتى أتاهم نصرنا ولا مبدل لكلمات الله ولقد جاءك من نبإ المرسلين

translation: And if their turning away is difficult for you, then if you are able, seek a tunnel into the earth or a stairway into the sky, and bring them a sign. And if Allah had willed, He would have gathered them upon guidance. So do not be among the ignorant.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the difficulty of dealing with people who turn away from the message of the prophet. It advises the prophet, if faced with this difficulty, to seek a miraculous sign from Allah to show to the disbelievers, but also acknowledges that this is ultimately up to Allah's will. The verse also emphasizes that if Allah wanted, He could have guided them, but He did not. The verse serves as a reminder to the prophet that he is not responsible for the disbelief of the people, and that he should not be like the ignorant, who do not understand the nature of Allah's will and power.
orig: وإن كان كبر عليك إعراضهم فإن استطعت أن تبتغي نفقا في الأرض أو سلما في السماء فتأتيهم بآية ولو شاء الله لجمعهم على الهدى فلا تكونن من الجاهلين

translation: It is only those who respond to their Lord who will attain success. And as for the dead, Allah will resurrect them; then to Him they will be returned.
interpretation: The verse highlights the importance of responding to Allah's call and being obedient to Him in order to achieve success. The second part of the verse reminds us of the inevitability of death and the resurrection of the dead by Allah. Ultimately, all of humanity will return to Allah and be held accountable for their actions in this life.
orig: إنما يستجيب الذين يسمعون والموتى يبعثهم الله ثم إليه يرجعون

translation: And they say, 'Why has no sign been sent down to him from his Lord?' Say, 'Indeed, God is able to send down a sign, but most of them do not know.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the disbelievers challenging the Prophet Muhammad to produce a sign from God as proof of his prophethood. The response from the Prophet, as instructed by God, is that God has the ability to send down a sign, but most people do not know this. The verse emphasizes God's power and knowledge, and the limitations of human understanding. It also highlights the disbelievers' lack of faith and their rejection of the truth despite the evidence presented to them.
orig: وقالوا لولا نزل عليه آية من ربه قل إن الله قادر على أن ينزل آية ولكن أكثرهم لا يعلمون

translation: And there is no creature on earth or bird that flies with its wings spread out, but they are communities like you. We have not neglected anything in the Book. Then unto their Lord they will be gathered.
interpretation: The verse highlights the oneness of all of God's creation, emphasizing that all creatures, whether on land or in the air, are part of communities similar to humans. The verse also emphasizes the completeness and comprehensiveness of God's knowledge, stating that nothing has been neglected in the Book. The final part of the verse serves as a reminder of the ultimate destiny of all creatures, which is to be gathered before their Lord on the Day of Judgment.
orig: وما من دابة في الأرض ولا طائر يطير بجناحيه إلا أمم أمثالكم ما فرطنا في الكتاب من شيء ثم إلى ربهم يحشرون

translation: And those who have disbelieved in Our verses, upon them is a blindness and deafness will come upon them in your presence, and Allah is capable of doing that; And those who are guided, He increases them in guidance and gives them their righteousness.
interpretation: The verse highlights the consequences of disbelieving in the signs of God. Those who reject the truth are afflicted with blindness and deafness, preventing them from understanding and accepting the guidance offered to them. This punishment is not limited to the hereafter, but can also occur in this world, as indicated by the phrase 'in your presence'. In contrast, those who are guided by God are given even more guidance and are granted righteousness. The verse emphasizes the power of God to guide or misguide individuals, and the importance of accepting the truth in order to receive God's guidance and blessings.
orig: والذين كذبوا بآياتنا صم وبكم في الظلمات من يشإ الله يضلله ومن يشأ يجعله على صراط مستقيم

translation: Say, 'What if God's punishment came to you or the Hour (of Judgment) came upon you? Do you then call upon any other than God, if you are truthful?'
interpretation: The verse challenges the disbelievers to reflect on the consequences of their actions and their ultimate destiny on the Day of Judgment. The verse asks, 'What if God's punishment came to you or the Hour (of Judgment) came upon you?' This question serves as a warning and a reminder of the impending Day of Judgment and the reality of divine retribution. The verse then asks, 'Do you then call upon any other than God, if you are truthful?' This question highlights the futility of worshiping and seeking help from other than God, and emphasizes the importance of turning to God in repentance and seeking His forgiveness. The verse serves as a call to the disbelievers to recognize and submit to the truth, and to turn away from falsehood and idolatry.
orig: قل أرأيتكم إن أتاكم عذاب الله أو أتتكم الساعة أغير الله تدعون إن كنتم صادقين

translation: But rather, it is you who call upon Him, so He removes whatever affliction you are suffering from, as for
interpretation: No interpretation
orig: بل إياه تدعون فيكشف ما تدعون إليه إن شاء وتنسون ما تشركون

translation: And indeed, We have sent messengers before you to other towns, then We seized them with poverty and hardship that perhaps they would humble themselves [to Allah].
interpretation: The verse speaks about the sending of messengers to various towns before the time of the Prophet Muhammad. Despite the messengers' efforts, the people of those towns were afflicted with poverty and hardship as a form of divine punishment. The purpose of this punishment was to encourage the people to humble themselves before God and seek His mercy. The verse highlights the importance of humility and submission to God's will, even in the face of adversity and hardship.
orig: ولقد أرسلنا إلى أمم من قبلك فأخذناهم بالبأساء والضراء لعلهم يتضرعون

translation: But if We had sent down on them a storm of affliction, they would surely have humbled themselves to their Lord,
interpretation: No interpretation
orig: فلولا إذ جاءهم بأسنا تضرعوا ولكن قست قلوبهم وزين لهم الشيطان ما كانوا يعملون

translation: But when they forgot what they had been reminded of, We opened for them the doors of every (good) thing until, when they rejoiced in what they were given, We seized them suddenly, and behold, they were in despair.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the consequences of forgetting the signs and reminders of God. When people forget the guidance they have received, they are given more opportunities to do good, but when they become heedless and complacent, God seizes them unexpectedly, leading to their despair. The verse serves as a warning to those who have been given guidance, reminding them to be mindful of their actions and to be grateful for the blessings they have received, lest they fall into heedlessness and suffer the consequences.
orig: فلما نسوا ما ذكروا به فتحنا عليهم أبواب كل شيء حتى إذا فرحوا بما أوتوا أخذناهم بغتة فإذا هم مبلسون

translation: He severed the hands of the men of the town in retaliation for their injustice. And praise be to Allah, the Lord of the worlds.
interpretation: The verse describes the punishment of a town's people for their injustice, and the severing of their hands as a form of retribution. The verse also highlights the power and justice of God, as it ends with praise and gratitude to Allah, the Lord of the worlds. The verse serves as a reminder of the consequences of injustice and the ultimate authority of God over all of His creation.
orig: فقطع دابر القوم الذين ظلموا والحمد لله رب العالمين

translation: Say, 'Have you considered if Allah should take away your hearing and your sight and set a seal upon your hearts, who is there - other than Allah - who could bring them back to you?' See how We make clear the signs, yet still they turn away.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the power and ability of God to take away the senses and faculties of human beings, and how only God can restore them. The verse emphasizes the importance of recognizing and acknowledging the signs of God and the consequences of denying or ignoring them. The verse serves as a warning to those who reject or deny the signs of God, emphasizing the futility of their actions and the ultimate power of God to judge and punish them. The verse also highlights the clarity of the signs of God and the responsibility of human beings to understand and interpret them correctly.
orig: قل أرأيتم إن أخذ الله سمعكم وأبصاركم وختم على قلوبكم من إله غير الله يأتيكم به انظر كيف نصرف الآيات ثم هم يصدفون

translation: Say, 'Have you considered: if Allah's punishment came to you suddenly or openly, will anyone other than the wrongdoing people be destroyed?'
interpretation: The verse is a rhetorical question posed by the speaker, asking the audience to consider the consequences of Allah's punishment. The punishment is described as coming suddenly or openly, emphasizing its inevitability and the lack of control that people have over it. The verse suggests that only the wrongdoing people will be destroyed, implying that those who are not unjust will be spared. The verse serves as a warning to those who engage in unjust actions, reminding them of the impending punishment and the importance of repentance.
orig: قل أرأيتكم إن أتاكم عذاب الله بغتة أو جهرة هل يهلك إلا القوم الظالمون

translation: And We did not send the messengers except as bearers of good news and warners. So whoever believes and does righteousness, there is no fear for them, nor will they grieve.
interpretation: The verse affirms that prophets were sent only to bring good news and to warn people. Those who believe and do good deeds will not have to fear or grieve, indicating a promise of safety and happiness for the righteous. The verse emphasizes the role of the messengers as guides and protectors of the believers, and encourages people to have faith and follow the right path to attain salvation and peace of mind.
orig: وما نرسل المرسلين إلا مبشرين ومنذرين فمن آمن وأصلح فلا خوف عليهم ولا هم يحزنون

translation: And for those who have disbelieved in Our verses, punishment will touch them for their transgressions.
interpretation: The verse warns of the punishment that will be faced by those who reject the signs (verses) of God. The punishment will come as a consequence of their transgressions, emphasizing the connection between their disbelief and the negative consequences they will experience. The verse serves as a reminder that actions have consequences, and that rejection of God's signs and engaging in transgressions will not go unpunished.
orig: والذين كذبوا بآياتنا يمسهم العذاب بما كانوا يفسقون

translation: Say, 'I do not say to you that I possess the treasures of God, nor do I know the unseen, nor do I say to you that I am an angel. I only follow what is revealed to me.' Say, 'Then are the blind and the seeing equal? Will you not then reflect?'
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the limitations of human knowledge and abilities, and the importance of following divine guidance. The speaker asserts that they do not possess God's treasures or know the unseen, and that they are not an angel. They only follow what is revealed to them. The verse then asks a series of rhetorical questions, comparing the blind and the seeing, to highlight the absurdity of treating unequal things as equal. The verse encourages reflection and discernment, inviting the listeners to consider the significance of these questions and the implications of their actions.
orig: قل لا أقول لكم عندي خزائن الله ولا أعلم الغيب ولا أقول لكم إني ملك إن أتبع إلا ما يوحى إلي قل هل يستوي الأعمى والبصير أفلا تتفكرون

translation: And warn those who fear that they will be gathered to their Lord, that they will have no protector or intercessor besides Him, so that they may be mindful.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the importance of warning those who fear the Day of Judgment and the accountability they will face before their Lord. It emphasizes that on that Day, they will not have any protector or intercessor besides God, and that this realization should encourage them to be mindful and righteous in their actions. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of accountability and the significance of leading a righteous life in preparation for the Day of Judgment.
orig: وأنذر به الذين يخافون أن يحشروا إلى ربهم ليس لهم من دونه ولي ولا شفيع لعلهم يتقون

translation: And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord in the morning and the evening, seeking His countenance. For you are not responsible for their reckoning; and neither are they responsible for your reckoning. So drive them not away, and you will thus be among the unjust.
interpretation: The verse advises against driving away or mistreating those who worship and seek the countenance of their Lord at different times of the day. The verse emphasizes that the responsibility for one's own reckoning lies solely with the individual and that no one can bear the burden of another's sins. Therefore, the verse advises against mistreating or driving away those who engage in worship and devotion, and instead encourages coexistence and tolerance. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of respecting and upholding the rights of others, regardless of their religious beliefs or practices.
orig: ولا تطرد الذين يدعون ربهم بالغداة والعشي يريدون وجهه ما عليك من حسابهم من شيء وما من حسابك عليهم من شيء فتطردهم فتكون من الظالمين

translation: And We thus test some of them against others, that they might say: 'Are these the ones upon whom Allah has conferred favor from among us?' Is not Allah most knowing of the grateful?
interpretation: The verse speaks about a test that God imposes on some people, comparing them to others, so that they might recognize God's favor upon them. The verse raises a rhetorical question, asking whether those who are being tested are the ones who have received God's blessings. The verse emphasizes God's knowledge and awareness of those who are grateful for His blessings. The verse suggests that the test is a means of distinguishing between those who are grateful and those who are not, and highlights the importance of recognizing and expressing gratitude for God's blessings.
orig: وكذلك فتنا بعضهم ببعض ليقولوا أهؤلاء من الله عليهم من بيننا أليس الله بأعلم بالشاكرين

translation: And when those who believe in Our verses come to you, say, 'Peace be upon you.' Your Lord has written mercy upon Himself. So whoever of you commits a sin out of ignorance and then repents after that and corrects himself - indeed, He is Forgiving and Merciful.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the appropriate greeting and behavior towards those who believe in the signs (verses) of God. The verse instructs the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) to greet them with 'Peace be upon you' when they come to him. The verse emphasizes the inherent mercy of God, who has written it upon Himself, and encourages the believers to repent and correct themselves if they commit a sin out of ignorance. The verse reassures the believers of God's forgiveness and mercy towards those who sincerely repent and strive to improve themselves.
orig: وإذا جاءك الذين يؤمنون بآياتنا فقل سلام عليكم كتب ربكم على نفسه الرحمة أنه من عمل منكم سوءا بجهالة ثم تاب من بعده وأصلح فأنه غفور رحيم

translation: And thus do We diversify the verses so that they may say, 'You have studied (it thoroughly).'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the diversity of verses in the Qryan and the reason behind it, which is to challenge the disbelievers who deny the truth of the Quran and claim that it is a work of human creation. The verse emphasizes the importance of understanding the meaning and message behind the verses and the significance of recognizing the truth of the Quran. The verse serves as a reminder to the believers to be firm in their faith and not be swayed by the doubts and denials of the disbelievers.
orig: وكذلك نفصل الآيات ولتستبين سبيل المجرمين

translation: Say, 'Indeed, I have been commanded to worship Allah, not associating anything with Him.' Say, 'Indeed, I am upon clear evidence from my Lord, and you have not been given of it. If you were upon the way, you would have followed me. But there is not from you any gratitude.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the command from Allah to the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) to worship only Him and not to associate anything with Him. The verse emphasizes the importance of worshipping Allah alone and not following the desires of others. The verse also highlights the fact that the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) has clear evidence from his Lord, while the disbelievers do not have any of it. The verse serves as a reminder to the disbelievers that if they were on the right path, they would have followed the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) and expressed gratitude, but they are not, and they do not.
orig: قل إني نهيت أن أعبد الذين تدعون من دون الله قل لا أتبع أهواءكم قد ضللت إذا وما أنا من المهتدين

translation: Say, 'I am indeed a plain warner. No blame attaches to me: my duty is only to convey (the message) clearly.' No belief do I know of you, (readers), save that haply men of sense may warn. It is Allah Who will call you to account for what you used to do.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the role of the Prophet Muhammad as a warner who is delivering the message of Allah. The verse emphasizes that the Prophet is not responsible for the people's actions, and his duty is only to convey the message clearly. The verse suggests that the Prophet has no knowledge of the people's beliefs and that he is only trying to warn those who may be receptive to the message. The verse also highlights that the ultimate judgement belongs to Allah and that He will hold people accountable for their actions.
orig: قل إني على بينة من ربي وكذبتم به ما عندي ما تستعجلون به إن الحكم إلا لله يقص الحق وهو خير الفاصلين

translation: Say, 'If I had that which you are impatient for me to hasten, between me and you would be the matter resolved, and Allah is most knowing of the wrongdoers.'
interpretation: The verse is a response from the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to those who were urging him to hasten the revelation of God's punishment upon their enemies. The Prophet reminds them that if he had the power to immediately resolve the matter, he would do so. However, the Prophet emphasizes that the decision and timing of the punishment belongs solely to God, who has knowledge of the wrongdoers and their actions. The verse teaches patience and trust in God's plan and justice, and a reminder that only God has the power to bring about true resolution and justice.
orig: قل لو أن عندي ما تستعجلون به لقضي الأمر بيني وبينكم والله أعلم بالظالمين

translation: And with Him are the keys of the unseen; none knows them except Him. And He knows what is on the land and in the sea. Not a leaf falls but that He knows it, and there is not a grain in the darkness of the earth, nor anything fresh or dry, that is not recorded in a clear book.
interpretation: The verse highlights God's omniscience and control over the universe. The 'keys of the unseen' refer to God's knowledge of all that is hidden and unknown to humans. The verse emphasizes that God has knowledge of everything, from the smallest details such as a falling leaf or a grain of sand, to the larger events that occur on land and at sea. The verse also states that all of this information is recorded in a 'clear book', indicating that nothing is forgotten or goes unnoticed by God. The verse serves as a reminder of God's power and knowledge, and encourages believers to trust in and submit to God's will.
orig: وعنده مفاتح الغيب لا يعلمها إلا هو ويعلم ما في البر والبحر وما تسقط من ورقة إلا يعلمها ولا حبة في ظلمات الأرض ولا رطب ولا يابس إلا في كتاب مبين

translation: And it is He who takes your souls by night, and knows what you have done by day, then raises you up in it (night) so that a specified term may be fulfilled. Then to Him will be your return, then He will inform you of what you used to do.
interpretation: The verse speaks about God's power over life and death, and His knowledge of all human actions. The verse emphasizes that God takes people's souls at night and knows what they have done during the day. The verse also highlights that God raises people up during the night for a specified term, and after that, they will return to Him and He will inform them of their actions. The verse serves as a reminder of God's omniscience and omnipotence and the inevitability of the Day of Judgment, where people will be held accountable for their actions.
orig: وهو الذي يتوفاكم بالليل ويعلم ما جرحتم بالنهار ثم يبعثكم فيه ليقضى أجل مسمى ثم إليه مرجعكم ثم ينبئكم بما كنتم تعملون

translation: And He is the Exalted in Might, above His slaves, and He sends guardians over you, until when death comes to one of you, Our messengers take him, and they do not neglect [their duty].
interpretation: The verse affirms the greatness and power of God, who is above His creation and has control over all aspects of life and death. The verse states that God sends guardians or protectors over the believers, and when the time of death comes for one of them, God's messengers take their souls, fulfilling their duty without negligence. The verse emphasizes the power of God over life and death, and the certainty of the soul's departure from the body at the appointed time, reminding the believers of the transience of life and the importance of preparing for the afterlife.
orig: وهو القاهر فوق عباده ويرسل عليكم حفظة حتى إذا جاء أحدكم الموت توفته رسلنا وهم لا يفرطون

translation: Then to Allah belongs [all] sovereignty of the heavens and the earth. And to Allah, [due] return [of all matters]. So to Him is the [final] destination.
interpretation: The verse affirms the sovereignty of Allah over the heavens and the earth, and emphasizes that all matters will ultimately return to Him. It serves as a reminder that Allah is the final destination and ultimate judge of all things, and that all power and authority belong to Him alone.
orig: ثم ردوا إلى الله مولاهم الحق ألا له الحكم وهو أسرع الحاسبين

translation: Say, 'Who will save you from the darkness of land and sea? You call upon Him in secret and in the open, hoping that if He saves us from this, we will be among the thankful.'
interpretation: The verse is a challenge to the disbelievers who are facing difficulties and hardships in their lives. It asks them who can save them from the perils of the land and sea, emphasizing that they call upon God in secret and in the open, hoping for His help and salvation. The verse highlights the human need for God's protection and mercy, and the fact that people turn to God in times of distress. At the same time, it reminds the believers to be thankful and grateful to God for His blessings and protection, and to remember that He is the only source of help and support in times of need.
orig: قل من ينجيكم من ظلمات البر والبحر تدعونه تضرعا وخفية لئن أنجانا من هذه لنكونن من الشاكرين

translation: Say, 'Allah will surely deliver you from it (the plague) and from every adversity, and still you associate others with Him.'
interpretation: The verse is a message from the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to the people, reassuring them that Allah has the power to save them from the plague and all other forms of hardship. Despite this, the people persist in associating partners with Allah, a grave sin in Islamic teachings. The verse serves as a reminder of Allah's power and mercy, and a call for the people to turn to Him alone, abandoning the worship of any other deities.
orig: قل الله ينجيكم منها ومن كل كرب ثم أنتم تشركون

translation: Say, 'He is capable of sending upon you punishment from above you or from beneath your feet or of dividing you into factions and making you taste one another's violence.' Look how We vary the signs! Perhaps they will understand.
interpretation: The verse speaks about God's power and ability to punish those who disbelieve and commit injustice. The verse mentions three different ways in which God's punishment can manifest: from above, from beneath, or by dividing people into factions and causing them to fight each other. The verse emphasizes God's control over all things and the inevitability of His punishment for those who do not heed His warnings. The verse serves as a reminder to the disbelievers and a call for them to reflect on the signs of God's power and wisdom. The phrase "Look how We vary the signs" highlights the different ways in which God's signs and messages are presented, indicating that the disbelievers should take heed and understand the meaning behind these signs.
orig: قل هو القادر على أن يبعث عليكم عذابا من فوقكم أو من تحت أرجلكم أو يلبسكم شيعا ويذيق بعضكم بأس بعض انظر كيف نصرف الآيات لعلهم يفقهون

translation: And they denied you [Muhammad] and the truth after it had come to them, and they are unaware of it. Say, 'I am not a guardian over you.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the rejection of the truth (Islam) by the disbelievers despite its arrival in their community. The verse emphasizes the ignorance of the disbelievers, who deny the truth and are unaware of its significance. The Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) is instructed to declare that he is not responsible for them as they have chosen to reject the truth. The verse highlights the importance of personal responsibility and accountability, and the consequences of denying the truth despite its clear presentation.
orig: وكذب به قومك وهو الحق قل لست عليكم بوكيل

translation: For every statement, there is an end, and you will surely come to know.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the inevitability of an end for every statement or matter. It reminds the reader that nothing in this world is permanent, and that all things will eventually come to an end. The second part of the verse, 'and you will surely come to know', reinforces the idea of the certainty of the end and the ultimate truth. The verse can be interpreted as a reminder to be mindful of one's words and actions, as they will have consequences that will be known in the end.
orig: لكل نبإ مستقر وسوف تعلمون

translation: And when you see those who engage in debate about Our verses, then turn away from them until they engage in a different conversation. And if Satan should cause you to forget, then do not remain after the reminder with the wrongdoing people.
interpretation: The verse advises the believers to avoid engaging in debates with those who reject or question the signs (verses) of God. Instead, the believers are instructed to turn away from such people and wait until they start talking about something else. However, if the believer forgets and continues to stay with the wrongdoing people, the verse warns that Satan may take advantage of this lapse in judgement. Therefore, the believers must be mindful of Satan's schemes and not stay with the wrongdoing people after being reminded of the importance of avoiding such debates.
orig: وإذا رأيت الذين يخوضون في آياتنا فأعرض عنهم حتى يخوضوا في حديث غيره وإما ينسينك الشيطان فلا تقعد بعد الذكرى مع القوم الظالمين

translation: And upon the believers there is no blame for their forgiveness of others and for their peace offerings, so that Allah may accept their forgiveness and their peace offerings, and Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the believers and emphasizes that they are not blamed for forgiving others and making peace offerings. The verse highlights the positive outcome of these actions, as it leads to God accepting their forgiveness and peace offerings. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of forgiveness and making peace, and the positive impact it can have on one's relationship with God. It also emphasizes God's forgiving and merciful nature.
orig: وما على الذين يتقون من حسابهم من شيء ولكن ذكرى لعلهم يتقون

translation: And leave alone those who have taken their religion as amusement and diversion, and whom the life of this world has deluded. But remind with it (the Qur'an) lest a soul be encumbered by what it has earned. It has no helper or intercessor besides Allah. And if it offers every compensation, it will not be taken from it. Those are the ones who are given drink from a drink of pure confusion, and they will be severely punished because of what they used to deny.
interpretation: The verse speaks about those who have made a mockery of their religion and are distracted by the worldly life. The verse warns of the danger of becoming too attached to the material world and neglecting one's religious duties. It reminds that ultimately, each person will be held accountable for their actions and no one can intercede on their behalf except for Allah. Those who persist in their disbelief and denial will be punished severely. The verse serves as a reminder to the believers to strive for balance in their lives and not to neglect their religious obligations in pursuit of worldly pleasures.
orig: وذر الذين اتخذوا دينهم لعبا ولهوا وغرتهم الحياة الدنيا وذكر به أن تبسل نفس بما كسبت ليس لها من دون الله ولي ولا شفيع وإن تعدل كل عدل لا يؤخذ منها أولئك الذين أبسلوا بما كسبوا لهم شراب من حميم وعذاب أليم بما كانوا يكفرون

translation: Say, 'Invoke those you assume [to be] beyond Allah, which neither benefits you nor harms you, for to Allah is the final destination.' And thus is made pleasing to the disbelievers their fabrication, and they are averse from the way of truth. And thus was made pleasing to the Pharaoh and those before him their fabrication, and they were guided to destruction. And who is more unjust than one who invents about Allah a lie or denies His verses? Indeed, the wrongdoers will not succeed.'
interpretation: The verse warns against the futility of worshipping false deities and emphasizes the ultimate power and authority of Allah. It highlights the foolishness of the disbelievers who cling to their false idols and reject the truth. The verse also draws a parallel between the Pharaoh and his people, who were destroyed for their disbelief, and the disbelievers of the present day. The verse serves as a warning to those who deny the truth and a reminder of the consequences of their actions. The verse emphasizes that the only path to success and salvation is through submission to Allah and following His guidance.
orig: قل أندعو من دون الله ما لا ينفعنا ولا يضرنا ونرد على أعقابنا بعد إذ هدانا الله كالذي استهوته الشياطين في الأرض حيران له أصحاب يدعونه إلى الهدى ائتنا قل إن هدى الله هو الهدى وأمرنا لنسلم لرب العالمين

translation: And establish prayer and fear Him, and it is He to whom you will be gathered.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of establishing prayer and having a fear of God, reminding the reader that they will ultimately be held accountable for their actions on the Day of Judgment. The phrase 'it is He to whom you will be gathered' serves as a reminder of the unity and power of God, and the certainty of the Day of Judgment. The verse encourages the reader to lead a righteous life and to prepare for the Day of Judgment through their actions and devotion in this life.
orig: وأن أقيموا الصلاة واتقوه وهو الذي إليه تحشرون

translation: And He it is who created the heavens and the earth in truth, and on the day He says: Be, it is. His word is the truth, and His is the Kingdom on the day the trumpet is blown, the day the secret of the heavens and the earth is manifest, and He is the Wise, the Knowing.
interpretation: The verse affirms the power and sovereignty of God as the creator of the heavens and the earth. It highlights the absolute authority of God, as His words bring about existence. The verse describes the day of judgment, when the trumpet will be blown and the secret of the heavens and the earth will be revealed. This is a reminder of the ultimate power and knowledge of God, who is described as wise and all-knowing.
orig: وهو الذي خلق السماوات والأرض بالحق ويوم يقول كن فيكون قوله الحق وله الملك يوم ينفخ في الصور عالم الغيب والشهادة وهو الحكيم الخبير

translation: And [mention, O Muhammad], when Abraham said to his father Azar, 'Do you take idols as deities? Indeed, I see you and your people in clear error.'
interpretation: The verse recounts a conversation between Abraham and his father Azar, where Abraham expresses his shock and disbelief at his father's worship of idols. Abraham's statement serves as a reminder of the falsehood of idol worship and the clarity of guidance that Abraham had received from God. The verse challenges the reader to reflect on their own beliefs and actions, and to consider whether they are following the truth or falsehood.
orig: وإذ قال إبراهيم لأبيه آزر أتتخذ أصناما آلهة إني أراك وقومك في ضلال مبين

translation: And thus did We show Abraham the kingdom of the heavens and the earth that he would be among the certain [in faith].
interpretation: The verse speaks about a moment of revelation and certainty for the prophet Abraham, when he was shown the kingdom of the heavens and the earth. This vision served to strengthen his faith and conviction, and he became one of the certain in faith. The verse highlights the importance of divine guidance and revelation in the spiritual journey of the prophets, and the transformative power of such experiences in shaping their beliefs and actions.
orig: وكذلك نري إبراهيم ملكوت السماوات والأرض وليكون من الموقنين

translation: When the night covered him, he saw a star. He said, 'This is my Lord.' But when it disappeared, he said, 'I do not like those that disappear.'
interpretation: The verse describes a person who, when it became dark, saw a star and mistakenly thought it was his Lord. However, when the star disappeared, he realized his mistake and expressed his dislike for things that are not constant and reliable. The verse can be interpreted as a reminder of the impermanence of creation and the importance of recognizing and worshipping the only true God, who is eternal and unchanging. It may also be seen as a warning against the dangers of idolatry and the fleeting nature of false deities.
orig: فلما جن عليه الليل رأى كوكبا قال هذا ربي فلما أفل قال لا أحب الآفلين

translation: When he saw the moon rising up, he said: 'This is my Lord!' But when it went down, he said: 'If my Lord does not guide me, I will surely be of the people who are astray.'
interpretation: The verse describes a person who, upon seeing the moon rise, mistakes it for his Lord, but then realizes his mistake when the moon sets. He then prays to his Lord for guidance, acknowledging that without it, he will be among the lost. The verse highlights the importance of seeking guidance from God and recognizing the limits of one's own understanding. It also emphasizes the importance of humility and the recognition of one's own limitations, as well as the need for continual guidance and support from a higher power.
orig: فلما رأى القمر بازغا قال هذا ربي فلما أفل قال لئن لم يهدني ربي لأكونن من القوم الضالين

translation: When the sun was covered, he said, 'This is my Lord, this is greater.' But when it (the sun) moved away, he said, 'O my people, I am indeed free from what you associate (with Him).'
interpretation: The verse speaks about a person who, upon seeing the sun being covered, mistakenly takes it as a sign of the power of a deity other than God. However, when the sun reappears, the person immediately realizes his mistake and declares his freedom from the false deities that his people worship. The verse highlights the importance of recognizing the true power of God and the dangers of associating partners with Him. It serves as a reminder to be mindful of one's beliefs and not to be swayed by false signs or superstitions.
orig: فلما رأى الشمس بازغة قال هذا ربي هذا أكبر فلما أفلت قال يا قوم إني بريء مما تشركون

translation: Indeed, I have turned my face toward He who created the heavens and the earth, as a hanif, and I am not of those who associate others with Allah.
interpretation: The verse is a statement of faith and devotion to the one true God, who created the heavens and the earth. The speaker declares that they have turned their face towards God, indicating a complete and total devotion to Him. The term 'hanif' refers to someone who is not a Jew or a Christian, but who follows the natural and pure religion of submission to God. The speaker also explicitly denounces shirk, or the association of partners with God, emphasizing the monotheistic nature of their faith. The verse expresses a strong and unwavering commitment to the worship of the one true God.
orig: إني وجهت وجهي للذي فطر السماوات والأرض حنيفا وما أنا من المشركين

translation: And his people argued with him. He said: 'Do you argue with me regarding God? He has guided me, and I fear not what you associate with Him. Except what my Lord wills. My Lord encompasses all things in knowledge. Will you not then remember?'
interpretation: The verse describes a conversation between a prophet and his people, who are arguing with him about God. The prophet declares his faith in God and his lack of fear of the idols that his people worship. He asserts that he follows the guidance of God and that God's knowledge encompasses all things. He urges his people to remember and reflect on this truth. The verse highlights the prophet's unwavering faith and his commitment to spreading God's message, despite the opposition he faces from his people. It also serves as a reminder to the readers of the importance of having a strong faith in God, and the importance of seeking guidance from Him.
orig: وحاجه قومه قال أتحاجوني في الله وقد هدان ولا أخاف ما تشركون به إلا أن يشاء ربي شيئا وسع ربي كل شيء علما أفلا تتذكرون

translation: And how can you fear what I have associated, while you fear not that you have associated with Allah that for which He has not sent down authority? So which of the two parties has a greater right to security - if you should know.
interpretation: The verse addresses the hypocrisy of those who fear the consequences of their actions in this world, but do not fear the association of partners with Allah, which is a much greater sin. The verse questions which of the two groups, those who fear the consequences of their actions or those who associate partners with Allah, have a greater right to security. The verse serves as a reminder that the fear of Allah and avoiding sin should be the utmost priority for believers. The verse emphasizes the importance of having a proper understanding of what is truly important and worthy of fear, and what is not.
orig: وكيف أخاف ما أشركتم ولا تخافون أنكم أشركتم بالله ما لم ينزل به عليكم سلطانا فأي الفريقين أحق بالأمن إن كنتم تعلمون

translation: Those who believe and do not mix their faith with injustice, they are the ones who will have security and they are the guided ones.
interpretation: The verse distinguishes between those who truly believe and practice their faith with justice, and those who mix their faith with injustice. The verse promises security and guidance for the former group, indicating that they are on the right path and will be rewarded for their righteousness. The verse serves as a reminder that faith and justice go hand in hand, and that true believers are those who uphold justice and avoid injustice in all their actions.
orig: الذين آمنوا ولم يلبسوا إيمانهم بظلم أولئك لهم الأمن وهم مهتدون

translation: And that is our argument which we gave to Abraham against his people. We raise in degrees whom We will. Indeed, your Lord is wise, knowledgeable.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the argument or proof that God gave to Abraham to use against his disbelieving people. The verse emphasizes God's power and knowledge in choosing and raising in degrees whom He will. The verse serves as a reminder of God's wisdom and knowledge in dealing with humanity and His ability to raise or lower individuals or groups according to His will.
orig: وتلك حجتنا آتيناها إبراهيم على قومه نرفع درجات من نشاء إن ربك حكيم عليم

translation: And We gave him Isaac and Jacob, and both of them We guided. And We made Noah a predecessor among the guided. And from his descendants, David, Solomon, Job, Joseph, Moses, and Aaron. And thus We reward the doers of good.
interpretation: The verse highlights a series of prophets and righteous individuals who were guided by God, starting with Abraham and his sons Isaac and Jacob. The verse then mentions Noah, David, Solomon, Job, Joseph, Moses, and Aaron as examples of those who were guided. The verse emphasizes the reward that God gives to those who do good and follow His guidance. The verse can be seen as a reminder that God guides and rewards those who strive to live a righteous life, just as He guided and rewarded the prophets and righteous individuals mentioned in the verse.
orig: ووهبنا له إسحاق ويعقوب كلا هدينا ونوحا هدينا من قبل ومن ذريته داوود وسليمان وأيوب ويوسف وموسى وهارون وكذلك نجزي المحسنين

translation: And Zachariah and John and Jesus and Elias, each one of them was of the righteous.
interpretation: The verse mentions four prophets, Zachariah, John, Jesus, and Elias, and describes them as being righteous. The verse emphasizes the righteousness of these prophets, highlighting their virtuous character and actions. The verse serves as a reminder that righteousness is a key characteristic of prophets and a goal that all believers should strive for. It also reinforces the idea that prophets are chosen by God due to their virtuous character and actions.
orig: وزكريا ويحيى وعيسى وإلياس كل من الصالحين

translation: And mention Ishmael and Al-Yasa' and Yunus, and Lot, all of them among the best.
interpretation: The verse is a command to the Prophet Muhammad to remember and mention the stories of certain prophets who were among the best and most righteous of people. These prophets include Ishmael, Al-Yasa' (also known as Elisha), Yunus (also known as Jonah), and Lot. By mentioning their stories and examples, the verse encourages believers to follow in their footsteps and strive for righteousness and goodness in their own lives.
orig: وإسماعيل واليسع ويونس ولوطا وكلا فضلنا على العالمين

translation: And of their fathers and their descendants and their brothers and We chose them and We guided them to a straight path.
interpretation: The verse highlights the relationship between the chosen people of God and their ancestors, descendants, and siblings, indicating the importance of family and lineage in the Islamic faith. The verse also emphasizes the guidance and selection of these people by God, who led them to a straight path. The verse can be interpreted as a reminder that the blessings of God are not limited to an individual, but extend to their families and future generations. Additionally, the verse implies that being chosen and guided by God is a great honor, and those who are chosen have a responsibility to uphold the teachings of Islam and lead a righteous life.
orig: ومن آبائهم وذرياتهم وإخوانهم واجتبيناهم وهديناهم إلى صراط مستقيم

translation: That is the guidance of Allah. He guides with it whom He wills of His servants. But if they had associated others with Him, surely, much of what they did would have been in vain.
interpretation: The verse explains that the guidance of Allah is a gift given to whom He wills of His servants. The verse highlights the importance of following Allah's guidance and warns of the consequences of associating others with Him. The verse suggests that if people were to associate others with Allah, much of their good deeds would be rendered useless. The verse serves as a reminder of the significance of monotheism and the importance of following Allah's guidance.
orig: ذلك هدى الله يهدي به من يشاء من عباده ولو أشركوا لحبط عنهم ما كانوا يعملون

translation: Those are they to whom We gave the Scripture and authority and prophethood; but if they disbelieve in it, then indeed We have entrusted it to a people who are not disbelievers in it.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the people who were given the scripture, authority, and prophethood, but if they disbelieve in it, then God has entrusted it to a people who will not disbelieve in it. The verse emphasizes the importance of belief and faith, and the consequences of disbelief. It highlights that God will always protect and preserve His message, even if it means transferring it to a new group of people who will uphold it. The verse serves as a reminder that God's plan is always in motion, and that He will always ensure that His message is preserved and protected.
orig: أولئك الذين آتيناهم الكتاب والحكم والنبوة فإن يكفر بها هؤلاء فقد وكلنا بها قوما ليسوا بها بكافرين

translation: Those are the ones whom Allah has guided, so take their guidance as an example. Say, 'I do not ask you for any compensation for it. It is only a reminder for the worlds.'
interpretation: The verse highlights the importance of following the guidance of those who have been guided by Allah. The speaker declares that they do not seek any reward for conveying this message and that it is only a reminder for all of humanity. The verse emphasizes the significance of guidance and the importance of heeding the examples set by those who have been guided by Allah. It also stresses the selflessness of the speaker, who does not seek any personal gain from conveying this message.
orig: أولئك الذين هدى الله فبهداهم اقتده قل لا أسألكم عليه أجرا إن هو إلا ذكرى للعالمين

translation: And they did not estimate Allah with true estimation when they said, 'Allah has not sent down anything upon a human.' Say, 'Who then sent down the scripture that Moses came with, a light and a guidance for the people?' You make it into separate pages, revealing them and concealing much. And you have been taught that which you knew not, neither you nor your fathers. Say, 'Allah,' then leave them in their trifling. They will know.
interpretation: The verse criticizes the people for underestimating Allah's power and capability. They deny that Allah has sent down anything to humans, which is a clear rejection of the revelations brought by prophets, including the scripture that Moses came with. The verse points out their hypocrisy in making the scripture into separate pages, revealing and concealing much, while they have been taught that which they knew not, neither they nor their fathers. The verse commands the believers to say 'Allah' and then leave the disbelievers in their trifling, indicating that the believers should not engage in fruitless debates and arguments with the disbelievers. The disbelievers will eventually come to know the truth, implying that they will realize their mistake and regret their disbelief in the hereafter.
orig: وما قدروا الله حق قدره إذ قالوا ما أنزل الله على بشر من شيء قل من أنزل الكتاب الذي جاء به موسى نورا وهدى للناس تجعلونه قراطيس تبدونها وتخفون كثيرا وعلمتم ما لم تعلموا أنتم ولا آباؤكم قل الله ثم ذرهم في خوضهم يلعبون

translation: And this is a Book which We have sent down, blessed and confirming what was before it, that thou mayest warn the Mother City and those around it; and those who believe in the hereafter believe in it, and they are constant in guarding their prayers.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the Qur'an being a blessed book, sent down to confirm the previous revelations. The verse highlights the Qur'an's role in warning the people of the Mother City (Mecca) and its surroundings, as well as those who believe in the hereafter. These believers are described as being consistent in their prayers. The verse emphasizes the continuity and confirmation of the Qur'an with previous revelations, and its role in reminding people of the importance of faith and prayer.
orig: وهذا كتاب أنزلناه مبارك مصدق الذي بين يديه ولتنذر أم القرى ومن حولها والذين يؤمنون بالآخرة يؤمنون به وهم على صلاتهم يحافظون

translation: And who is more unjust than one who invents a lie about Allah or says, 'It has been revealed to me,' while nothing has been revealed to him, and one who says, 'I will reveal [something] like what Allah has revealed'? And if you could but see when the wrongdoers are in the overwhelming pangs of death and the angels are stretching forth their hands, [saying], 'Deliver your souls! Today you will be awarded the punishment of [extreme] humiliation for what you used to say about Allah other than the truth and you were, toward His verses, being arrogant.'
interpretation: The verse highlights the severe consequences of lying about Allah, falsely claiming to have received revelation, and arrogantly rejecting Allah's verses. The verse describes the punishment that awaits the wrongdoers on the Day of Judgment, when they are in the throes of death and the angels come to take their souls. The verse emphasizes the extreme humiliation and disgrace that the wrongdoers will face as a result of their actions and their rejection of the truth. The verse serves as a warning against arrogance and falsely attributing words to Allah, and it reminds people of the reality of death and the consequences of their actions.
orig: ومن أظلم ممن افترى على الله كذبا أو قال أوحي إلي ولم يوح إليه شيء ومن قال سأنزل مثل ما أنزل الله ولو ترى إذ الظالمون في غمرات الموت والملائكة باسطو أيديهم أخرجوا أنفسكم اليوم تجزون عذاب الهون بما كنتم تقولون على الله غير الحق وكنتم عن آياته تستكبرون

translation: And you have come to Us alone as We created you the first time, and you have left behind what We had provided for you, and We do not see with you your 'intercessors' whom you claimed were helping you. Indeed, it has become clear between you and them that they are not your helpers.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the Day of Judgment and the moment when people will stand before God and realize that they are alone, without any of their worldly possessions or intercessors. The verse emphasizes the powerlessness of the things and people that people relied on in their earthly lives, and how they will not be able to help them on the Day of Judgment. The verse serves as a reminder to focus on the relationship with God, rather than relying on worldly possessions or intermediaries, as they will not be able to help in the end.
orig: ولقد جئتمونا فرادى كما خلقناكم أول مرة وتركتم ما خولناكم وراء ظهوركم وما نرى معكم شفعاءكم الذين زعمتم أنهم فيكم شركاء لقد تقطع بينكم وضل عنكم ما كنتم تزعمون

translation: Indeed, it is Allah who causes the grain and the date seed to sprout. He brings the living out of the dead and the dead out of the living. That is Allah, so how are you deluded?
interpretation: The verse highlights the power and control of Allah over all aspects of life and death. It emphasizes that it is Allah who causes the growth of plants from seeds, and it is also Allah who has the power to bring the dead back to life. The verse serves as a reminder to the readers that Allah is the one who has control over everything and that they should not be deluded or distracted from this reality. The verse may also be interpreted as a warning against the rejection of Allah's power and authority, and a call to recognize and submit to it.
orig: إن الله فالق الحب والنوى يخرج الحي من الميت ومخرج الميت من الحي ذلكم الله فأنى تؤفكون

translation: By the dawn and (by) the ten nights, and (by) the even and the odd, and (by) the night when it departs, There are signs for the wise.
interpretation: The verse speaks about various signs in the universe that serve as a reminder of God's power and wisdom. The signs mentioned include the dawn, ten nights (which could refer to the last ten days of Ramadan), the even and odd numbers, and the night when it departs (which could refer to the end of the night). These signs are meant for the wise, indicating that only those who reflect and ponder upon these signs will be able to understand their true meaning and significance.
orig: فالق الإصباح وجعل الليل سكنا والشمس والقمر حسبانا ذلك تقدير العزيز العليم

translation: And He it is who has made for you the stars that you may guidance thereby in the darkness of land and sea. We have detailed the signs for a people who have knowledge.
interpretation: The verse highlights the role of stars as guidance for people in the darkness of land and sea. The verse emphasizes God's provision of signs (ayat) for people, including the stars, to help them navigate and find their way. The verse also highlights the importance of knowledge and understanding of these signs. The verse implies that those who have knowledge can better understand and make use of the signs that God has provided. The verse can be seen as a reminder to seek guidance and knowledge in order to navigate the challenges and uncertainties of life.
orig: وهو الذي جعل لكم النجوم لتهتدوا بها في ظلمات البر والبحر قد فصلنا الآيات لقوم يعلمون

translation: And He it is who created you from a single soul, and then (He created) its mate of like nature, and He has provided for you of cattle eight kinds. You are clothed from (their) wool, and you ride on them, and you eat of what they (the cattle) eat; and you have in them a means of satisfaction; and by (the grace of) Allah you are carried (moving) (along the land), and surely Allah is ever All-Kind to people, All-Aware.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the creation of humanity by God, who created us from a single soul and then created its mate. The verse emphasizes the interconnectedness of human beings and their dependence on the natural world for sustenance and survival. The eight kinds of cattle mentioned in the verse serve as a source of clothing, transportation, food, and other benefits for people. The verse also highlights God's kindness and awareness towards humanity. The verse serves as a reminder of our dependence on God and the natural world, and the importance of treating both with respect and gratitude.
orig: وهو الذي أنشأكم من نفس واحدة فمستقر ومستودع قد فصلنا الآيات لقوم يفقهون

translation: And it is He who sends down water from the sky, and from it We bring forth every kind of plant, and from it We bring forth the verdure from which We create grain piled up in layers, and from the palm trees - of its sheaths come forth clusters of dates, and gardens of grapes and olives and pomegranates, similar and unlike; look at its fruit when it bears fruit and at its ripening; there are indeed signs in that for a people who believe.
interpretation: The verse highlights the power and mercy of God, who sends down water from the sky, which leads to the growth of various kinds of plants and fruits. The verse describes the different stages of growth, from the emergence of the plants to the formation of grains and clusters of dates, and the ripening of fruits. The description of the diversity of fruits - 'similar and unlike' - emphasizes the richness and abundance of God's creation. The verse concludes with a call to reflect on the signs of God's power and mercy in the natural world, and a reminder for people to believe.
orig: وهو الذي أنزل من السماء ماء فأخرجنا به نبات كل شيء فأخرجنا منه خضرا نخرج منه حبا متراكبا ومن النخل من طلعها قنوان دانية وجنات من أعناب والزيتون والرمان مشتبها وغير متشابه انظروا إلى ثمره إذا أثمر وينعه إن في ذلكم لآيات لقوم يؤمنون

translation: And they have set up equals to Allah, the jinn and the mankind, and they have made of the slaves of Allah, sons and daughters without knowledge; high is Allah above what they set up.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the grave sin of associating partners with Allah, which includes the worship of the jinn and mankind. The verse emphasizes the ignorance of those who commit this sin, as they make slaves of Allah into their sons and daughters without any knowledge. The verse ends by emphasizing the greatness of Allah, who is far above what they attribute to Him.
orig: وجعلوا لله شركاء الجن وخلقهم وخرقوا له بنين وبنات بغير علم سبحانه وتعالى عما يصفون

translation: He is the Originator of the heavens and the earth. How can He have a child when He has no companion? He created all things, and He is, over all things, Knowing.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes God's unique and independent nature as the creator of the heavens and the earth. It asserts that God does not have a child, as He has no companion, and affirms His role as the creator of all things. The verse emphasizes God's all-encompassing knowledge and power over all things. The verse can be seen as a response to those who believe in the idea of God having a child or companion, and serves to assert God's absolute oneness and uniqueness.
orig: بديع السماوات والأرض أنى يكون له ولد ولم تكن له صاحبة وخلق كل شيء وهو بكل شيء عليم

translation: That is Allah, your Lord; there is no god but He, the Creator of all things, so worship Him. And He is Disposer of all things.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the oneness and supremacy of Allah as the only god and the creator of everything. It commands people to worship Allah alone, and reaffirms His control over all things. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of worshiping and submitting to Allah, and the ultimate power and authority that He holds over all of creation.
orig: ذلكم الله ربكم لا إله إلا هو خالق كل شيء فاعبدوه وهو على كل شيء وكيل

translation: Man cannot see Him, but He sees man. He is the Subtle, the Acquainted.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the unseen nature of God and His ability to see all things. The verse emphasizes the limitations of human perception and understanding in comparison to God's infinite knowledge and power. The phrase 'He is the Subtle, the Acquainted' highlights God's intimate knowledge of all things and His ability to perceive even the smallest details, despite His hiddenness from human sight. The verse serves as a reminder of the transcendence of God and the limitations of human understanding, inviting reflection on the nature of divine reality and the human condition.
orig: لا تدركه الأبصار وهو يدرك الأبصار وهو اللطيف الخبير

translation: There has come to you from your Lord enlightenment (verses/signs/lessons). So whoever sees (understands/takes lesson), it is for his own soul, and whoever is blind (willfully ignorant), it is against him, and I am not a guardian over you.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the signs or lessons (referred to as 'verses' in this translation) sent by the Lord to humanity. Those who understand and take heed of these lessons will benefit themselves, while those who remain willfully ignorant or blind to these lessons will bear the consequences upon themselves. The verse emphasizes the individual's responsibility for their own understanding and actions, and the lack of responsibility the speaker has over them.
orig: قد جاءكم بصائر من ربكم فمن أبصر فلنفسه ومن عمي فعليها وما أنا عليكم بحفيظ

translation: And thus do We make the verses clear and plain, so that they may say: 'You have studied (it well),' and that We may make it clear for a people who know.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the revelation of the verses (signs) of God, which are made clear and plain for people to understand. The verse suggests that some people may accuse the prophet of having studied and memorized the verses, rather than receiving them through revelation. However, the main purpose of the revelation is to make the verses clear and understandable for those who are willing to learn and seek knowledge.
orig: وكذلك نصرف الآيات وليقولوا درست ولنبينه لقوم يعلمون

translation: Follow what has been revealed to you from your Lord, there is no deity but Him, and turn away from the polytheists.
interpretation: The verse commands the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) to follow the revelation from his Lord, which is the Qur'an, and to not associate any partners with Him. The verse also instructs the Prophet to turn away from the polytheists, who reject the oneness of God and associate partners with Him. The verse emphasizes the importance of following the guidance of God and staying away from those who reject it. It serves as a reminder that the only true deity is God, and that associating partners with Him is a grave sin.
orig: اتبع ما أوحي إليك من ربك لا إله إلا هو وأعرض عن المشركين

translation: And if Allah had willed, they would not have associated (anything with Him). And We have not made you a guardian over them, nor are you responsible for them.
interpretation: The verse highlights the power and will of Allah, stating that if Allah had willed, the people would not have committed shirk (associating partners with Allah). The verse emphasizes that it is not the responsibility of the Prophet (peace be upon him) to force people to believe or to be their guardian, as they have free will. The verse serves as a reminder that the ultimate power and control belong to Allah, and that the responsibility of the Prophet is only to convey the message of Islam.
orig: ولو شاء الله ما أشركوا وما جعلناك عليهم حفيظا وما أنت عليهم بوكيل

translation: And do not insult those who invoke other than Allah, for then they would insult Allah in ignorance out of transgression. Like that, We make pleasing to every people their deeds. Then to their Lord is their return, and He will inform them about what they used to do.
interpretation: The verse advises against insulting those who worship deities other than Allah, as such behavior would lead to insulting Allah Himself.
