The verse highlights the negative consequences of acting out of ignorance and transgression, and emphasizes that every people will be pleased with the outcome of their actions. Ultimately, all will return to their Lord, who will inform them of the true nature of their deeds. The verse serves as a reminder to respect the beliefs of others, even if they differ from one's own, and to be aware of the consequences of one's actions.
orig: ولا تسبوا الذين يدعون من دون الله فيسبوا الله عدوا بغير علم كذلك زينا لكل أمة عملهم ثم إلى ربهم مرجعهم فينبئهم بما كانوا يعملون

translation: And they swear by God with the most earnest of oaths that if a sign came to them, they would surely believe in it. Say: 'The signs are only with Allah; and most surely, when it came to them, they would not believe.'
interpretation: The verse addresses the disbelievers who claim that they will believe if they are given a sign from God. However, the verse states that the signs are only with God and that when they are presented with them, the disbelievers will not believe. The verse highlights the stubbornness and denial of the disbelievers, who refuse to accept the truth even when faced with clear evidence. It also emphasizes that faith and belief are not a result of external signs, but rather a matter of acceptance and submission to God.
orig: وأقسموا بالله جهد أيمانهم لئن جاءتهم آية ليؤمنن بها قل إنما الآيات عند الله وما يشعركم أنها إذا جاءت لا يؤمنون

translation: And We shall turn their hearts and their eyes away (from the truth) as they did not believe in it the first time, and We shall leave them in their transgression, blindly wandering on.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the fate of those who reject the truth and do not believe, even after being given guidance. Their hearts and eyes will be turned away from the truth, meaning they will be unable to comprehend or accept it. Furthermore, they will be left in their transgression, and will continue to wander blindly, unable to find the right path. The verse serves as a warning to those who reject the truth and continue to transgress, emphasizing the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's judgment.
orig: ونقلب أفئدتهم وأبصارهم كما لم يؤمنوا به أول مرة ونذرهم في طغيانهم يعمهون

translation: And if We had sent down the angels to them, and the dead had spoken to them, and We had gathered together all things before their eyes, they would not have believed, unless Allah had willed it; but most of them are ignorant.
interpretation: The verse highlights the stubbornness and closed-mindedness of those who refuse to believe in God. Even if angels were sent down to them, if the dead were to speak to them, or if all things were gathered together before their eyes, they still would not believe, unless God willed it. The verse emphasizes that belief cannot be forced or compelled, and that most people lack the understanding and wisdom to comprehend the truth. The verse serves as a reminder that belief is a gift from God, and that only those who are chosen by Him can truly understand and accept the truth.
orig: ولو أننا نزلنا إليهم الملائكة وكلمهم الموتى وحشرنا عليهم كل شيء قبلا ما كانوا ليؤمنوا إلا أن يشاء الله ولكن أكثرهم يجهلون

translation: And thus have We made for every prophet an enemy, Shayatin (devils) among mankind and jinn, inspiring one another with adorned speech as a delusion. But if your Lord had willed, they would not have done it, so leave them and that which they invent.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the existence of enemies for every prophet, who are devils from both mankind and jinn. These devils inspire each other with delusional and deceptive speech, which they use to mislead people. However, the verse clarifies that if God had willed, these enemies would not have been able to do what they do. Therefore, the prophets are instructed to leave them alone and not engage with their falsehoods.
orig: وكذلك جعلنا لكل نبي عدوا شياطين الإنس والجن يوحي بعضهم إلى بعض زخرف القول غرورا ولو شاء ربك ما فعلوه فذرهم وما يفترون

translation: And let not the hearts of those who disbelieve in the Hereafter incline, from that which they have been reminded, and amuse themselves with it. And prohibit them, and stay away from them. And if you invite them to guidance, they will not follow you. It is the same for them whether you invite them or you are silent.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the attitude of those who do not believe in the afterlife. Despite being reminded of the truth, they do not believe and instead indulge in worldly pleasures. The verse advises the believers to stay away from such people and not to be affected by their disbelief. The verse also mentions that even if the believers invite them to guidance, they will not follow. The verse emphasizes the futility of trying to convince those who are set in their disbelief and the importance of focusing on one's own faith and actions.
orig: ولتصغى إليه أفئدة الذين لا يؤمنون بالآخرة وليرضوه وليقترفوا ما هم مقترفون

translation: And is it not God alone whose help you seek while it is He who has revealed to you the Book in detail, and those to whom We have given the Book know that it is sent down from your Lord with truth, so be not of those who doubt.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of seeking help and guidance from God alone, as He is the one who has revealed the scripture in detail. The verse also reminds the believers of the truth of the revelation and the certainty of its divine origin, as those to whom the earlier scriptures were revealed are aware of it. The verse warns against doubting the revelation and encourages the believers to have complete faith in it, and not to associate any partners with God in their worship and seeking help.
orig: أفغير الله أبتغي حكما وهو الذي أنزل إليكم الكتاب مفصلا والذين آتيناهم الكتاب يعلمون أنه منزل من ربك بالحق فلا تكونن من الممترين

translation: And the word of your Lord has been fulfilled in truth and in justice. None can change His words, and He is the Hearing, the Knowing.
interpretation: The verse affirms the certainty and reliability of God's word, emphasizing that it is true and just. The verse also emphasizes that God's word cannot be changed or altered, and that He is all-knowing and all-hearing. The verse serves as a reminder of the power and authority of God, and the certainty of His decrees. The verse may also serve as a source of comfort and reassurance for believers, reminding them that God's word is unchangeable and that He is aware of all that happens in the world.
orig: وتمت كلمت ربك صدقا وعدلا لا مبدل لكلماته وهو السميع العليم

translation: And if you obey most of those on the earth, they will mislead you from the way of Allah. Indeed, they follow not except assumption, and indeed, they are not but falsifying.
interpretation: The verse warns against following the majority of people on earth, as they may lead one astray from the path of Allah. The verse explains that these people only follow conjecture and are not guided by truth or certainty. Furthermore, they are described as falsifiers, emphasizing their lack of credibility and reliability.
orig: وإن تطع أكثر من في الأرض يضلوك عن سبيل الله إن يتبعون إلا الظن وإن هم إلا يخرصون

translation: Indeed, your Lord is most knowing of those who stray from His way, and He is most knowing of those who are guided.
interpretation: The verse affirms that Allah is all-knowing and all-aware of the actions of His creations. He knows who has strayed from His path and who has not. The verse emphasizes Allah's attribute of being all-knowing and highlights the fact that He is the one who guides and leads astray. It serves as a reminder that Allah is aware of our actions and that we will be held accountable for our deeds. It also emphasizes the importance of seeking guidance from Allah and following His path.
orig: إن ربك هو أعلم من يضل عن سبيله وهو أعلم بالمهتدين

translation: And eat and drink of that which Allah has provided and profusely bestowed on you. And give thanks for the bounty of Allah, if it is Him that you serve.
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to enjoy the blessings and provisions given by Allah, while also being mindful and grateful for them. The command to 'eat and drink' is a reminder of the abundance of resources that Allah has provided for humanity's sustenance. At the same time, believers are reminded to express their gratitude for these blessings, and to serve Allah in response to His generosity. The verse emphasizes the importance of recognizing and acknowledging the source of all good things, and encourages a grateful and mindful approach to the consumption of resources.
orig: فكلوا مما ذكر اسم الله عليه إن كنتم بآياته مؤمنين

translation: And why should you not eat of that over which the name of Allah has been mentioned, while He has already explained to you that which is unlawful for you, except under compulsion of necessity? And indeed, many people are led astray by their own desires, without knowledge. Indeed, your Lord is most knowing of the transgressors.
interpretation: The verse addresses the importance of eating only that which is permissible in Islam and avoiding what is forbidden. It emphasizes that God has already explained what is unlawful, except in cases of extreme necessity. The verse also highlights the dangers of being led astray by one's own desires and ignorance. Ultimately, the verse serves as a reminder that God is all-knowing and aware of those who transgress and disobey His commands.
orig: وما لكم ألا تأكلوا مما ذكر اسم الله عليه وقد فصل لكم ما حرم عليكم إلا ما اضطررتم إليه وإن كثيرا ليضلون بأهوائهم بغير علم إن ربك هو أعلم بالمعتدين

translation: And leave alone the outer [appearance] of sin and its inner [consequences]. Indeed, those who earn sin will suffer for what they have done.
interpretation: The verse advises the believers to avoid not only committing sin but also from being associated with it, whether it is by appearance or by inner motivation. The verse warns that those who commit sins will inevitably face the consequences of their actions. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of staying away from sin and maintaining a pure heart and intention.
orig: وذروا ظاهر الإثم وباطنه إن الذين يكسبون الإثم سيجزون بما كانوا يقترفون

translation: And do not eat of that on which the name of Allah has not been mentioned, for indeed, it is grave disobedience. And indeed do the devils inspire their allies [among men] to dispute with you. And if you obey them, indeed you would be associators [of partners with Him].
interpretation: The verse forbids eating of food that does not have the name of God mentioned over it, emphasizing the importance of acknowledging God's blessings. The verse warns against the consequences of disobedience and associating partners with God. The verse also highlights the deceitful tactics of the devils, who inspire their human allies to create disputes and lead people astray. By following the devils, one would be associating partners with God, a grave sin in Islamic teachings.
orig: ولا تأكلوا مما لم يذكر اسم الله عليه وإنه لفسق وإن الشياطين ليوحون إلى أوليائهم ليجادلوكم وإن أطعتموهم إنكم لمشركون

translation: Or [consider such an example] of one who was dead to whom We gave life and made for him light by which he walks among the people, like one who is in darkness, unaware of them. Thus, for the disbelievers, their deeds are like a mirage in a lowland which a thirsty person supposes to be water - until, when he comes to it, he finds it to be nothing, but he finds Allah before him, and Allah will reward him for what he used to do.
interpretation: The verse describes the contrast between the fate of the believers and the disbelievers. The believers are described as those who have been given life and light, allowing them to walk among the people and be aware of their surroundings. On the other hand, the disbelievers are described as those who are in darkness, unaware of their surroundings and their ultimate fate. The deeds of the disbelievers are compared to a mirage in a lowland, giving a false sense of hope and satisfaction, until it is too late and they are faced with the reality of their situation. The verse emphasizes the importance of belief and the consequences of disbelief, reminding the reader that God sees and rewards all actions.
orig: أومن كان ميتا فأحييناه وجعلنا له نورا يمشي به في الناس كمن مثله في الظلمات ليس بخارج منها كذلك زين للكافرين ما كانوا يعملون

translation: And thus do We make in every city the greatest criminals thereof to be its leaders, so they plot therein. But they plot only against themselves, and they are not aware.
interpretation: The verse describes how God allows the worst criminals in each town to become its leaders, causing them to plot and scheme. However, the verse emphasizes that their scheming is directed only towards themselves, and they are not aware of the consequences of their actions. This verse may serve as a critique of those who are in power and commit unjust acts, highlighting the negative impact of their actions on themselves and society as a whole.
orig: وكذلك جعلنا في كل قرية أكابر مجرميها ليمكروا فيها وما يمكرون إلا بأنفسهم وما يشعرون

translation: And when there comes to them a sign, they say, 'Never will we believe until we are given like that which was given to the messengers of Allah.' Allah is most knowing of where He places His message. Humiliation will come to the unjust people by a punishment coming in accordance with what they used to conspire.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the disbelievers' response to divine signs and their refusal to believe until they receive the same treatment as the messengers of Allah. The verse emphasizes that Allah is all-knowing and places His message where He wills. The verse warns of the humiliation that unjust people will face through a punishment that fits their conspiracies and schemes, indicating that they will not escape the consequences of their disbelief and rejection of divine signs.
orig: وإذا جاءتهم آية قالوا لن نؤمن حتى نؤتى مثل ما أوتي رسل الله الله أعلم حيث يجعل رسالته سيصيب الذين أجرموا صغار عند الله وعذاب شديد بما كانوا يمكرون

translation: For he whom Allah wills to guide, He expands his breast to Islam; and he whom He wills to lead astray, He makes his breast narrow and constricted, as if he is climbing up to the sky. Thus does Allah place defilement upon those who do not believe.
interpretation: The verse explains the relationship between human will and divine guidance. It highlights the fact that God has the power to guide or misguide whomever He wills. For those whom God guides, their hearts are open and receptive to the message of Islam. However, those who are led astray have constricted and narrow hearts, making it difficult for them to accept the truth. The verse emphasizes the importance of God's guidance and the consequences of being led astray. It serves as a reminder that God places defilement upon those who do not believe, indicating their separation from God and the negative consequences of their disbelief.
orig: فمن يرد الله أن يهديه يشرح صدره للإسلام ومن يرد أن يضله يجعل صدره ضيقا حرجا كأنما يصعد في السماء كذلك يجعل الله الرجس على الذين لا يؤمنون

translation: And this is the straight path of your Lord, we have detailed the verses for a people who remember.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the 'straight path' that has been ordained by the Lord. It highlights that the verses (of the Qur'an) have been revealed to provide guidance to the people. The verse emphasizes the importance of remembering and reflecting upon the verses, which is a prerequisite for staying on the straight path. The verse serves as a reminder for the believers to continuously engage with the teachings of the Qqur'an and strive to follow the path of righteousness and guidance.
orig: وهذا صراط ربك مستقيما قد فصلنا الآيات لقوم يذكرون

translation: For them will be the home of peace with their Lord, and He will be their protecting friend because of what they used to do.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the reward for the righteous servants of God. They will have a home of peace with their Lord, and He will be their protector and friend because of their good deeds. The verse emphasizes the importance of good actions and their impact on shaping a person's destiny. The home of peace and the protection of God are promised to those who strive for righteousness and act in accordance with God's will, indicating that their efforts will not be in vain and they will be rewarded for their good deeds.
orig: لهم دار السلام عند ربهم وهو وليهم بما كانوا يعملون

translation: And the Day when He will gather them all together, (it will be) as if they had not remained (in the world) but an hour of the day, and they will recognize each other. The criminals will say to the keepers of Hell, 'Pray to your Lord to lighten for us a day of the punishment.' They will say, 'Did there not come to you your messengers with clear proofs?' They will say, 'Yes.' They will reply, 'Then pray!' But the prayer of the disbelievers is not but in error.'
interpretation: The verse describes the Day of Judgment when all people will be gathered together and it will seem as if they had only stayed in the world for an hour. The criminals will plead with the keepers of Hell to ask God to lighten their punishment, but the keepers will remind them that messengers had come to them with clear proofs and warnings. The criminals will admit that they had indeed received the messages, but it will be too late for them. The verse emphasizes the importance of heeding the warnings of God's messengers and the consequences of ignoring them. The verse also highlights the futility of the prayers of the disbelievers, who will only be in error.
orig: ويوم يحشرهم جميعا يا معشر الجن قد استكثرتم من الإنس وقال أولياؤهم من الإنس ربنا استمتع بعضنا ببعض وبلغنا أجلنا الذي أجلت لنا قال النار مثواكم خالدين فيها إلا ما شاء الله إن ربك حكيم عليم

translation: And thus do We seize some of the wrongdoers: they were merely enjoying themselves.
interpretation: The verse describes the fate of some of the wrongdoers who were seized by God's punishment. They were preoccupied with their own pleasures and did not pay attention to the consequences of their actions. The verse serves as a reminder that those who engage in wrongdoing and ignore the signs of God's punishment will ultimately face the consequences of their actions.
orig: وكذلك نولي بعض الظالمين بعضا بما كانوا يكسبون

translation: O company of jinn and men, did not messengers come to you from among you, reciting My signs to you and warning you of the meeting of this day of yours? They will say, 'We bear witness against ourselves'; and the life of the world has deluded them, and they have borne witness against themselves that they were disbelievers.'
interpretation: The verse addresses both jinn and humans, reminding them that they have received messengers from among themselves who recited the signs of God and warned them of the Day of Judgment. However, despite these warnings, the people were deluded by the worldly life and failed to heed the message. As a result, they will bear witness against themselves on the Day of Judgment, acknowledging that they were disbelievers.
orig: يا معشر الجن والإنس ألم يأتكم رسل منكم يقصون عليكم آياتي وينذرونكم لقاء يومكم هذا قالوا شهدنا على أنفسنا وغرتهم الحياة الدنيا وشهدوا على أنفسهم أنهم كانوا كافرين

translation: That is because your Lord would not destroy the towns unjustly while their people were heedless.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the justice of God, stating that He does not destroy communities without a reason or while their people are unaware. This verse may be seen as a reassurance to those who are facing difficulties and challenges in their lives, reminding them that God is just and does not punish without reason. It also highlights the importance of being aware and mindful of one's actions, as ignorance or heedlessness is not a valid excuse for wrongdoing.
orig: ذلك أن لم يكن ربك مهلك القرى بظلم وأهلها غافلون

translation: And for every man We have fastened his fate to his neck, and We will produce for him on the Day of Resurrection a record which he will find wide open
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the concept of individual accountability for one's actions in this life. The phrase 'We have fastened his fate to his neck' suggests that each person carries the consequences of their actions with them, and these consequences will be revealed on the Day of Judgment. The 'record' that will be produced on that day represents the complete and accurate account of each person's deeds, which they will not be able to deny or dispute. The verse encourages people to reflect on their actions and to prepare for the Day of Judgment by living a righteous and just life.
orig: ولكل درجات مما عملوا وما ربك بغافل عما يعملون

translation: But your Lord is the Generous One, the Owner of Mercy. If He wills, He can take you away and bring about whom He wills after you, just as He brought you into existence from the children of other people.
interpretation: The verse highlights the power and mercy of God, emphasizing that He is the ultimate authority and can do as He pleases. The verse reminds the reader that God created them from the lineage of other people and can replace them with others if He so chooses. The verse serves as a reminder of the fleeting nature of human existence and the need to be mindful of God's commands and live a righteous life.
orig: وربك الغني ذو الرحمة إن يشأ يذهبكم ويستخلف من بعدكم ما يشاء كما أنشأكم من ذرية قوم آخرين

translation: Indeed, what you are promised is not far away; and indeed, [none] of you can escape.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the inevitability of the punishment or event that has been promised to the disbelievers. It emphasizes that the promised day is not far away, and that no one can escape or avoid it. The verse serves as a warning to those who deny or ignore the signs of the approaching day, reminding them of the reality of the promise and the futility of their efforts to evade it.
orig: إن ما توعدون لآت وما أنتم بمعجزين

translation: Say, 'O my people, work according to your position; indeed, I am working. And you will come to know who will have a position of humiliation and to whom will be a painful punishment.'
interpretation: The verse is a message from the prophet to his people, urging them to do their duty and to work hard. The prophet himself is also working and striving to deliver the message of God. The verse implies that there will be a day of reckoning, when the righteous and the wicked will be distinguished. Those who are unjust and oppressive will suffer a painful punishment, while those who are righteous and just will be honored and respected. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of leading a righteous life and doing good deeds, as well as the consequences of wrongdoing and injustice.
orig: قل يا قوم اعملوا على مكانتكم إني عامل فسوف تعلمون من تكون له عاقبة الدار إنه لا يفلح الظالمون

translation: And they assign to Allah from that which He has produced of crops and livestock a share, and they say, 'This is for Allah' - according to their claim - and for our 'partners.' But what is for their 'partners' does not reach Allah, while what is for Allah reaches their 'partners.' Unjust is what they rule.
interpretation: The verse criticizes the practice of assigning a share of crops and livestock to Allah, while also setting aside a share for other deities or partners. The verse makes clear that the share that is set aside for the 'partners' does not reach Allah, while what is for Allah reaches the 'partners.' The verse emphasizes the injustice of this practice, as it highlights the absurdity of the idea that something could be taken away from what is due to Allah. The verse serves as a reminder of the oneness of Allah and the futility of associating partners with Him.
orig: وجعلوا لله مما ذرأ من الحرث والأنعام نصيبا فقالوا هذا لله بزعمهم وهذا لشركائنا فما كان لشركائهم فلا يصل إلى الله وما كان لله فهو يصل إلى شركائهم ساء ما يحكمون

translation: And similarly, We adorned for many of the polytheists their lives, so they would rejoice. They only take their religion as a pastime and adornment. But if God willed, they would not have done so. So leave them and their false inventions.
interpretation: The verse describes how God allowed many polytheists to live comfortable and enjoyable lives, so that they would be content and not seek the truth. However, their religion was only a form of entertainment and adornment for them, rather than a true devotion to God. The verse emphasizes that even if they had not chosen to live this way, it was ultimately God's will. The verse advises to leave them alone and not to engage with their false beliefs and practices.
orig: وكذلك زين لكثير من المشركين قتل أولادهم شركاؤهم ليردوهم وليلبسوا عليهم دينهم ولو شاء الله ما فعلوه فذرهم وما يفترون

translation: And they say, 'These are cattle and so is the offspring of cattle that are barren; they do not produce except by our claim.' And cattle for which the backs of their slaughter are prohibited, and cattle that are not mentioned with the name of Allah. They have made a lie upon Him. Indeed, He will repay them for what they used to fabricate.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the disbelievers who deny the divine signs and blessings, specifically in relation to the cattle. They claim that the barren cattle do not produce offspring, and that certain types of cattle are forbidden, and that the name of Allah is not mentioned upon them, which is a lie. The verse serves as a reminder that Allah is aware of their false claims and will hold them accountable for their actions, and that they will be punished for their lies and rejection of the truth.
orig: وقالوا هذه أنعام وحرث حجر لا يطعمها إلا من نشاء بزعمهم وأنعام حرمت ظهورها وأنعام لا يذكرون اسم الله عليها افتراء عليه سيجزيهم بما كانوا يفترون

translation: And they say, 'What is in the wombs of these animals is pure for us and forbidden for our wives.' But if it is stillborn, then they are partners in it. May He punish them! How perverse they are! Indeed, He is Watchful over them.
interpretation: The verse criticizes the hypocrisy and double standards of certain people, who declare that the meat of certain animals is pure and permissible for them to consume, while declaring it forbidden for their wives. However, they do not apply the same standard to stillborn animals, considering them pure and permissible for all. The verse condemns this behavior as perverse and unjust, and warns of God's punishment for those who act in such a manner. The verse emphasizes God's knowledge and awareness of their actions, and serves as a reminder of the importance of consistency and fairness in one's beliefs and actions.
orig: وقالوا ما في بطون هذه الأنعام خالصة لذكورنا ومحرم على أزواجنا وإن يكن ميتة فهم فيه شركاء سيجزيهم وصفهم إنه حكيم عليم

translation: Those who kill their children foolishly without knowledge, and forbid what Allah has provided for them, inventing a lie about Allah - they are indeed the lost.
interpretation: The verse is a condemnation of those who commit infanticide and those who prohibit what God has provided for them. These people are described as being misguided and lost. The verse emphasizes the gravity of their actions, which are not only foolish and lacking in knowledge, but also a fabrication of lies about God. The verse serves as a warning against such behavior and highlights the severe consequences of going against God's will.
orig: قد خسر الذين قتلوا أولادهم سفها بغير علم وحرموا ما رزقهم الله افتراء على الله قد ضلوا وما كانوا مهتدين

translation: And it is He who produces gardens, [both] trellised and untrellised, and date palms, and crops of different shapes and tastes, and olives and pomegranates, similar and dissimilar. Eat of its fruit when it yields and give its due [zakah] on the day of its harvest. And do not waste; indeed, He does not like wasters.
interpretation: The verse highlights God's role as the creator of various types of sustenance, including gardens, date palms, crops, olives, and pomegranates. The diversity in the shape, taste, and type of these provisions emphasizes God's power and generosity. The verse commands people to enjoy the fruits of their harvest while also giving its due zakah (charity) on the day of its harvest. The verse also warns against wasting and emphasizes that God does not approve of wasters. The verse encourages people to be mindful of their consumption and to share their resources with others, promoting a sense of community and gratitude for God's blessings.
orig: وهو الذي أنشأ جنات معروشات وغير معروشات والنخل والزرع مختلفا أكله والزيتون والرمان متشابها وغير متشابه كلوا من ثمره إذا أثمر وآتوا حقه يوم حصاده ولا تسرفوا إنه لا يحب المسرفين

translation: And of the cattle are some for burden and some for slaughter. Eat of what Allah has provided for you and do not follow the footsteps of Satan. Indeed, he is to you a clear enemy.
interpretation: The verse highlights the different uses of cattle, some for transportation and some for food. It reminds people to be grateful for the provisions from God and not to follow the ways of Satan who is their clear enemy. The verse encourages people to be mindful of their actions, to be grateful for what they have, and to avoid following the destructive paths that lead away from God.
orig: ومن الأنعام حمولة وفرشا كلوا مما رزقكم الله ولا تتبعوا خطوات الشيطان إنه لكم عدو مبين

translation: Then eight pairs: two of sheep, two of goats. Say, 'Are the two males among them unlawful or the two females? Or is it that you declare unlawful the males and females that are paired? Or are you knowledgeable of something while I do not know?', (Qur'an 6:143-144).
interpretation: The verse is a rhetorical question from God to the disbelievers who were criticizing the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) for consuming certain types of food. The verse highlights the absurdity of their criticism by using a hypothetical example of eight pairs of animals, two of which are sheep and two of which are goats. The verse challenges the disbelievers to explain why they consider some of these animals unlawful while others are not. The verse emphasizes the lack of knowledge and understanding of the disbelievers, and the irrationality of their criticisms. The verse also serves as a reminder that God is the ultimate source of all knowledge and that He has the power to make certain things lawful or unlawful.
orig: ثمانية أزواج من الضأن اثنين ومن المعز اثنين قل آلذكرين حرم أم الأنثيين أما اشتملت عليه أرحام الأنثيين نبئوني بعلم إن كنتم صادقين

translation: And of the camels, two and of the cows, two, say, 'Is it the two males or the two females?' Then say, 'Forbidden to you is their flesh and their blood and their wool and their hair.' Do you seek to enact judgement among them? Or is it that you are a people transgressing? But as for those of you who withdraw from them in reverence, then they are not blameworthy. Indeed, God is ever forgiving and merciful to the people. And for every nation there is a lesson in that which they earned. So when there came to them Our clear verses, they said, 'This is obvious magic!' And they denied them. So We took revenge from them. So observe how was the end of the deniers.
interpretation: The verse outlines the laws of eating certain animals and emphasizes the importance of following God's commands. It highlights the concept of 'taharat' or purity and the prohibition of consuming impure substances such as meat, blood, wool, and hair of certain animals. The verse also refers to the concept of 'taghut' or transgression and the consequences of going against God's will. The verse serves as a reminder that every nation has faced consequences for their actions and serves as a lesson for others. The verse concludes by describing the fate of those who denied God's signs and messages, emphasizing the importance of recognizing and accepting God's truth.
orig: ومن الإبل اثنين ومن البقر اثنين قل آلذكرين حرم أم الأنثيين أما اشتملت عليه أرحام الأنثيين أم كنتم شهداء إذ وصاكم الله بهذا فمن أظلم ممن افترى على الله كذبا ليضل الناس بغير علم إن الله لا يهدي القوم الظالمين

translation: Say, 'I do not find in that which has been revealed to me anything forbidden for one who eats it, unless it is a dead animal or blood poured forth or flesh of swine, for indeed, it is impure, or it is a sinful innovation of which has been dedicated to other than Allah.' But whoever is forced [by necessity], neither desiring [it] nor transgressing [its limit], then indeed, your Lord is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the dietary laws in Islam and permits the consumption of all food except for four categories: dead animals, blood, swine flesh, and food that has been dedicated to other than Allah. However, the verse also provides an exception for those who are forced to eat these forbidden foods due to necessity and not out of desire or transgression. The verse emphasizes the mercy and forgiveness of Allah towards those who find themselves in such situations. It serves as a reminder that Allah is the Most Forgiving and Merciful, and that He understands the struggles of His servants.
orig: قل لا أجد في ما أوحي إلي محرما على طاعم يطعمه إلا أن يكون ميتة أو دما مسفوحا أو لحم خنزير فإنه رجس أو فسقا أهل لغير الله به فمن اضطر غير باغ ولا عاد فإن ربك غفور رحيم

translation: And for those who are guided, We have made unlawful every animal with undivided hooves, and from the cattle and sheep We have made unlawful their fat, except what is carried on their backs or in their intestines or what is mixed with their bones. We have made it unlawful for them, striving for a sin. And indeed, We will punish them for it.
interpretation: The verse outlines the dietary restrictions for those who are guided (i.e. believers), making unlawful certain types of animals and their fat. The verse emphasizes that these restrictions are not arbitrary, but rather a form of punishment for striving for sin. The verse serves as a reminder for believers to be mindful of their actions and to avoid sin, as even the food they consume has consequences. The verse also highlights the mercy of God, as the restrictions only apply to certain parts of the animals and not to all of them. The verse ultimately serves as a guide for believers, providing them with clear instructions and boundaries for their actions.
orig: وعلى الذين هادوا حرمنا كل ذي ظفر ومن البقر والغنم حرمنا عليهم شحومهما إلا ما حملت ظهورهما أو الحوايا أو ما اختلط بعظم ذلك جزيناهم ببغيهم وإنا لصادقون

translation: But if they deny you, say, 'Your Lord is the Lord of Mercy, possessing vast forgiveness, who will not punish them while they are unjust to themselves.',
interpretation: The verse addresses the Prophet Muhammad, PBUH, and gives him a response to give if the disbelievers deny his message. The response emphasizes the merciful and forgiving nature of God, who is willing to forgive even the most unjust of people. However, the verse also makes it clear that God will not forgive those who continue to wrong themselves, indicating that repentance and a change of heart are necessary for forgiveness. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of seeking God's forgiveness and turning away from sin and injustice.
orig: فإن كذبوك فقل ربكم ذو رحمة واسعة ولا يرد بأسه عن القوم المجرمين

translation: Those who associate others with Allah will say, 'If Allah had willed, we would not have associated [anything] and neither would our fathers, nor would we have forbidden anything.' Thus did those before them deny until they tasted Our punishment. Say, 'Do you have any knowledge that you can produce for us? You are only following assumption, and you are only guessing.'
interpretation: The verse addresses those who associate partners with Allah, rejecting their claim that they were compelled to do so by their ancestors or tradition. The verse reminds them that previous nations also denied the truth until they experienced divine punishment. The verse challenges the disbelievers to produce any knowledge or evidence to support their beliefs and exposes their reliance on conjecture and speculation. The verse serves as a warning to those who reject the truth and follow falsehood, emphasizing the futility of their beliefs and the consequences of their actions.
orig: سيقول الذين أشركوا لو شاء الله ما أشركنا ولا آباؤنا ولا حرمنا من شيء كذلك كذب الذين من قبلهم حتى ذاقوا بأسنا قل هل عندكم من علم فتخرجوه لنا إن تتبعون إلا الظن وإن أنتم إلا تخرصون

translation: Say, 'The argument is only with Allah. If He had willed, He would have guided you all together.'
interpretation: The verse is a statement made by the prophet Muhammad, directed towards the disbelievers who rejected his message. The verse emphasizes that the ultimate argument and judgement belongs to God alone, and that if God had willed, He could have guided all of humanity to the right path. The verse serves as a reminder that the responsibility for guidance lies with God, and that the rejection of the message by the disbelievers is not due to any shortcomings on the part of the prophet, but rather a result of their own free will and rejection of God's guidance.
orig: قل فلله الحجة البالغة فلو شاء لهداكم أجمعين

translation: Say, 'Are those who know that what has been revealed to me is the truth from your Lord the same as those who are unaware?' So, do not associate yourself with them, and do not argue with the disbelievers. Surely, those who disbelieve in the Hereafter are engaged in opposing their Lord. Indeed, they have incurred a great wrath.'
interpretation: The verse draws a contrast between those who recognize the truth of the revelation brought by the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and those who are unaware or reject it. The Prophet is instructed not to associate himself with those who deny the truth or argue with them. Instead, he should leave them to their disbelief. The verse emphasizes that those who reject the revelation and deny the Hereafter are in opposition to their Lord and have incurred His wrath. The verse serves as a reminder to the Prophet (peace be upon him) and his followers to remain steadfast in their belief and avoid engaging in fruitless arguments with the disbelievers.
orig: قل هلم شهداءكم الذين يشهدون أن الله حرم هذا فإن شهدوا فلا تشهد معهم ولا تتبع أهواء الذين كذبوا بآياتنا والذين لا يؤمنون بالآخرة وهم بربهم يعدلون

translation: Say, 'Come, I will recite what your Lord has prohibited to you. [He commands] that you not associate anything with Him, and to be good to your parents. Do not kill your children out of poverty; We provide for you and them. And do not approach immoralities - what is apparent of them and what is concealed. And do not kill the soul which Allah has made sacred except in the cause of justice. This has He instructed you that perhaps you will use reason.'
interpretation: The verse lays out various prohibitions and commands from God, emphasizing the importance of monotheism and the sanctity of human life. The verse commands believers not to associate anything with God, to be kind to their parents, and to avoid immoral acts. It also forbids the killing of children out of poverty, emphasizing that God provides for all. The verse commands believers not to take a life unless it is in the cause of justice, and to avoid both the outward and hidden aspects of immorality. The verse serves as a reminder of God's commands and the importance of using reason and reflection when considering one's actions. It encourages believers to reflect on the value of human life and the importance of upholding justice and righteousness.
orig: قل تعالوا أتل ما حرم ربكم عليكم ألا تشركوا به شيئا وبالوالدين إحسانا ولا تقتلوا أولادكم من إملاق نحن نرزقكم وإياهم ولا تقربوا الفواحش ما ظهر منها وما بطن ولا تقتلوا النفس التي حرم الله إلا بالحق ذلكم وصاكم به لعلكم تعقلون

translation: And come not near to the orphan's property except in the way of improvement until he attains his maturity. And give full measure and weight in justice. We burden not any soul but that within its capacity. And when you speak, be just even if it concerns a near relative. And fulfill the covenant. Indeed, the covenant will be questioned about. And give full measure when you measure, and weigh with a balance that is straight. That is better and fairer in the end.
interpretation: The verse outlines the ethical treatment of orphans and their property, emphasizing the importance of fairness and justice. It forbids coming near the orphan's property except in a way that improves it until they reach maturity. The verse also encourages honesty and fairness in all dealings, whether with a close relative or not. The verse stresses the importance of upholding covenants and being truthful in speech. It reminds us that we will be held accountable for our actions and encourages us to be honest and fair in all our dealings, as it leads to a better outcome in the end.
orig: ولا تقربوا مال اليتيم إلا بالتي هي أحسن حتى يبلغ أشده وأوفوا الكيل والميزان بالقسط لا نكلف نفسا إلا وسعها وإذا قلتم فاعدلوا ولو كان ذا قربى وبعهد الله أوفوا ذلكم وصاكم به لعلكم تذكرون

translation: And this is My straight path, so follow it and do not follow other paths that will separate you from My path. This is what I command you with, so that you may be mindful.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the importance of following the straight path of God, which is the only path that leads to righteousness and salvation. The verse warns against following other paths, which will only lead to deviation and separation from God's path. The verse emphasizes the importance of obedience and compliance with God's commandments, and the ultimate goal of achieving mindfulness and consciousness of God.
orig: وأن هذا صراطي مستقيما فاتبعوه ولا تتبعوا السبل فتفرق بكم عن سبيله ذلكم وصاكم به لعلكم تتقون

translation: Then We gave Moses the Scripture, complete (in all things), and detailed, a guidance and a mercy, that they might believe in the meeting with their Lord.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the giving of the Scripture (Torah) to Moses, which was complete, detailed, and a guidance and mercy for the people. The purpose of the Scripture was to help the people believe in the meeting with their Lord. This verse emphasizes the importance of the Scripture and its role in providing guidance, mercy, and helping people have faith in the meeting with their Lord.
orig: ثم آتينا موسى الكتاب تماما على الذي أحسن وتفصيلا لكل شيء وهدى ورحمة لعلهم بلقاء ربهم يؤمنون

translation: And this is a Book which We have sent down, blessed; so follow it and be righteous, that you may receive mercy.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the Qur'an as a blessed book that has been sent down from God. The verse commands the believers to follow the teachings of the Qur'an and to be righteous. By doing so, the believers will be eligible to receive mercy from God. The verse emphasizes the importance of following the guidance of the Qur'an and the significance of righteousness in the path of receiving God's mercy.
orig: وهذا كتاب أنزلناه مبارك فاتبعوه واتقوا لعلكم ترحمون

translation: Say, '(As for) the Book, We have sent it down only upon a part of them (the Jews and the Christians) in the past. And even if you (O Muhammad) were to follow their (Jews and Christians) desires after the knowledge that has come to you (about the Oneness of Allah, the Laws of Islamic Monotheism, and this Quran), then indeed you will be among the Zalimun (wrong-doers, polytheists, etc.).'
interpretation: The verse addresses the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) and instructs him to remind the people that the scripture (the Torah and the Gospel) was only sent down to certain groups of people (the Jews and the Christians) before. The verse warns that if the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) was to follow the desires of these people, despite knowing the truth of Islamic monotheism and the Quran, then he would be among the unjust. This verse serves as a reminder to the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) and the believers to adhere to the teachings of Islam and not be swayed by the desires of those who oppose the message of Islam.
orig: أن تقولوا إنما أنزل الكتاب على طائفتين من قبلنا وإن كنا عن دراستهم لغافلين

translation: Or do you say, 'If only the Qur'an had been revealed to us, we would have been more guided than them.' Now the sign has come to you from your Lord, and a guidance and a mercy. So who is more unjust than those who reject the signs of Allah and turn away from them? We will repay those who turn away from Our signs with a painful punishment for their turning away.
interpretation: The verse addresses the disbelievers who deny the truth of the Qur'an and claim that they would have been more guided if it had been revealed to them. The verse then affirms that the sign (referring to the Qur'an) has indeed come to them from their Lord, and it serves as a guidance and a mercy. The verse emphasizes the unjustness of those who reject the signs of Allah and turn away from them. The verse concludes by stating that those who turn away from the signs of Allah will be punished for their actions with a painful punishment.
orig: أو تقولوا لو أنا أنزل علينا الكتاب لكنا أهدى منهم فقد جاءكم بينة من ربكم وهدى ورحمة فمن أظلم ممن كذب بآيات الله وصدف عنها سنجزي الذين يصدفون عن آياتنا سوء العذاب بما كانوا يصدفون

translation: Do they then wait only for the angels to come to them, or your Lord (Himself), or certain of the signs of your Lord? On the day when certain of the signs of your Lord come, no good will it do to a soul to believe then, if it believed not before, nor earned good (by deeds of righteousness) through its faith.
interpretation: The verse speaks about people who are waiting for a sign from God, either in the form of angels or a specific manifestation of God's power. The verse emphasizes that it will be too late for repentance and good deeds on the day when such signs appear. The verse serves as a warning that faith must be practiced and proven through good deeds, and that it will be of no use to believe only when the signs of God's power are already manifested.
orig: هل ينظرون إلا أن تأتيهم الملائكة أو يأتي ربك أو يأتي بعض آيات ربك يوم يأتي بعض آيات ربك لا ينفع نفسا إيمانها لم تكن آمنت من قبل أو كسبت في إيمانها خيرا قل انتظروا إنا منتظرون

translation: Indeed, those who have divided their religion and become sects, you are not with them in anything. Their affair is only to Allah; then He will inform them about what they used to do.
interpretation: The verse speaks about those who have divided their religion and become sects, and emphasizes that they are not associated with the speaker in any way. The verse states that their fate and judgment is solely in the hands of Allah, and that He will inform them about the consequences of their actions. The verse serves as a warning to those who create divisions within the religion, reminding them that they will ultimately be held accountable for their actions and that their fate is in the hands of God.
orig: إن الذين فرقوا دينهم وكانوا شيعا لست منهم في شيء إنما أمرهم إلى الله ثم ينبئهم بما كانوا يفعلون

translation: Whoever comes with a good deed will have ten times the like of it, and whoever comes with an evil deed will not be recompensed except with the like of it, and they will not be wronged.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the rewards and punishments for good and evil deeds, respectively. It emphasizes the generosity of God in rewarding good deeds, as one good deed will be multiplied by ten. On the other hand, the verse highlights the fairness of God in punishing evil deeds, as the punishment will be equivalent to the evil deed. The verse serves as a motivation for believers to do good deeds and avoid evil deeds, and it reassures them that they will be treated justly by God.
orig: من جاء بالحسنة فله عشر أمثالها ومن جاء بالسيئة فلا يجزى إلا مثلها وهم لا يظلمون

translation: Say, 'Indeed, my Lord has guided me to a straight path - a correct religion, the creed of Abraham, inclining toward truth. And he was not of those who associate others with Allah.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the guidance that the speaker has received from their Lord to a straight path, which is the correct religion and the creed of Abraham. The verse emphasizes the importance of following the path of truth and not associating any partners with God. The speaker distances themselves from those who associate others with God, highlighting the importance of monotheism in Islam. The verse serves as a reminder to Muslims to stay on the straight path and to follow the example of Abraham in their faith and actions.
orig: قل إنني هداني ربي إلى صراط مستقيم دينا قيما ملة إبراهيم حنيفا وما كان من المشركين

translation: Say, 'Indeed, my prayer, my rites of sacrifice, my living and my dying are all for Allah, the Lord of the worlds.'
interpretation: The verse is a statement of faith and devotion by the speaker, declaring that all aspects of their life, including their worship, sacrifices, and even their death, are dedicated to Allah, the Lord of the worlds. This declaration reflects a deep sense of submission and surrender to Allah, recognizing that all of life is a trust from Him and that all actions should be performed in accordance with His will. The verse emphasizes the importance of maintaining a strong connection with Allah, and striving to live a life that is pleasing to Him, in every moment and in every aspect of one's existence.
orig: قل إن صلاتي ونسكي ومحياي ومماتي لله رب العالمين

translation: There is no companion except Him, and thus I have been commanded, and I am the first of the Muslims.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the oneness of God, stating that there is no companion or partner to Him. The speaker, who is believed to be the Prophet Muhammad, states that he has been commanded to worship and submit to God alone. The speaker also identifies himself as the first of the Muslims, signifying his role as the leader of the Muslim community. The verse can be interpreted as a declaration of faith and a call to monotheism, highlighting the importance of submitting to and worshipping one God in Islam.
orig: لا شريك له وبذلك أمرت وأنا أول المسلمين

translation: Say, 'Shall I seek a lord other than God, while He is the Lord of all things?’ No soul burdened bears the burden of another. To your Lord is your return, and He will inform you of what you used to differ in.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the unity and oneness of God as the Lord of all things, and rejects the idea of seeking any other lord or deity. It also stresses the individual responsibility of every person for their own actions and burdens, and the fact that no one can bear the burden of another. The verse ends by reminding us that we will all return to our Lord, who will inform us of the truth of the matters we used to differ in, indicating the ultimate justice and truth of God's judgment.
orig: قل أغير الله أبغي ربا وهو رب كل شيء ولا تكسب كل نفس إلا عليها ولا تزر وازرة وزر أخرى ثم إلى ربكم مرجعكم فينبئكم بما كنتم فيه تختلفون

translation: And it is He who made you successors on the earth and raised some of you above others in degrees [of rank] that He may test you through what He has given you. Indeed, your Lord is swift in penalty, but indeed, He is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: The verse speaks about God's role in making humans successors on earth and creating a hierarchical system among them to test them. The verse emphasizes God's swiftness in punishment and His mercy and forgiveness. The verse reminds humans that they are being tested through the blessings they have received and that they will be held accountable for their actions. It also highlights the importance of recognizing God's power and mercy, and the need to use the blessings and opportunities given to us in a responsible and just manner.
orig: وهو الذي جعلكم خلائف الأرض ورفع بعضكم فوق بعض درجات ليبلوكم في ما آتاكم إن ربك سريع العقاب وإنه لغفور رحيم

translation: N
interpretation: N
orig: المص

translation: A book has been revealed to you (O Muhammad), so let there not be in your heart any discomfort concerning it, so that you may warn with it, and as a reminder to the believers.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the revelation of the Qur'an to the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) and encourages him not to feel distressed or overwhelmed by it. Instead, he is instructed to use the Qur'an as a means of warning and reminding people of the consequences of their actions and the importance of faith and obedience to God. The verse emphasizes the role of the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) as a warner and a reminder to the believers, and encourages him to fulfill this role with confidence and determination.
orig: كتاب أنزل إليك فلا يكن في صدرك حرج منه لتنذر به وذكرى للمؤمنين

translation: Follow what has been sent down to you from your Lord and do not follow other than Him any protectors. Little is it that you remember.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of following the guidance sent down by one's Lord, and discourages the following of any other protectors or leaders. The verse suggests that the believers should be mindful of their actions and not be easily swayed by the influence of others. The phrase 'little is it that you remember' implies that the believers have a tendency to forget and to stray from the path of righteousness. The verse serves as a reminder to the believers to stay steadfast on the path of God and not to be influenced by the opinions or actions of others.
orig: اتبعوا ما أنزل إليكم من ربكم ولا تتبعوا من دونه أولياء قليلا ما تذكرون

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: وكم من قرية أهلكناها فجاءها بأسنا بياتا أو هم قائلون

translation: And never did their prayer benefit them once the punishment came to them, except [when they said], 'Indeed, we were wrongdoers.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the futility of prayer and repentance once the punishment of God has been decreed. The people, when faced with the punishment, admitted their wrongdoing, but it was too late. The verse emphasizes the importance of seeking forgiveness and turning to God before the onset of punishment. It serves as a reminder that it is never too early to repent, but once the punishment has come, it is too late.
orig: فما كان دعواهم إذ جاءهم بأسنا إلا أن قالوا إنا كنا ظالمين

translation: We shall certainly question those to whom the Message was sent, and We shall certainly question the Messengers.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the questioning of both the people who received the message of God and the messengers who were sent to convey it. This questioning will take place in the afterlife, where every person will be held accountable for their actions and beliefs. The verse emphasizes the importance of the message and the responsibility of those who received it, as well as the messengers who delivered it. It serves as a reminder that all will be judged fairly and justly in the afterlife, and that everyone will be held accountable for their actions and decisions.
orig: فلنسألن الذين أرسل إليهم ولنسألن المرسلين

translation: So We shall make them taste a punishment short of the chastisement of the Hereafter; this (punishment) is because of what their hands have sent before them, and We are never unjust to them.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the punishment that will be inflicted upon people in this life as a consequence of their actions, before they receive their final judgement in the afterlife. The punishment is described as a taste of what is to come, a prelude to the ultimate chastisement of the hereafter. The punishment is a result of the actions that they have committed in the past, and it serves as a reminder that God is not unjust and that the consequences of their actions will be meted out in due time.
orig: فلنقصن عليهم بعلم وما كنا غائبين

translation: And the balance that day will be true. So, as for those whose scales are heavy, they are the successful ones.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the Day of Judgment and the use of a balance to weigh the good and bad deeds of people. The verse emphasizes the fairness and accuracy of the balance, as it is described as 'true' on that day. The verse highlights the importance of good deeds, as those whose scales are heavy with good deeds will be considered successful on the Day of Judgment. The verse serves as a motivation for people to strive for good deeds and virtuous actions, reminding them that their deeds will be weighed and evaluated on the Day of Judgment.
orig: والوزن يومئذ الحق فمن ثقلت موازينه فأولئك هم المفلحون

translation: And those who are afraid that they will be questioned about their deeds, it is they who have lost their souls, because of their disregard for Our verses.
interpretation: The verse speaks about those who fear the questioning of their deeds, and it is they who have lost their souls. This fear is a result of their disregard for the signs and messages of God. The verse highlights the importance of paying attention to and reflecting on the signs of God, and the consequences of ignoring or disregarding them. The verse serves as a warning to those who are negligent of God's signs, reminding them of the importance of paying heed to them and the danger of ignoring them.
orig: ومن خفت موازينه فأولئك الذين خسروا أنفسهم بما كانوا بآياتنا يظلمون

translation: And We have made the earth for you as a spread out, and have placed therein for you means of livelihood, little of you will be grateful.
interpretation: The verse highlights the bounties and provisions that God has bestowed upon humanity by creating the earth and providing for their sustenance. The use of the word 'spread out' suggests that the earth has been made vast and spacious for the benefit of its inhabitants. Despite these blessings, the verse notes that only a few will express gratitude for these gifts. This verse serves as a reminder to be thankful for the many blessings in our lives and to recognize that they come from God.
orig: ولقد مكناكم في الأرض وجعلنا لكم فيها معايش قليلا ما تشكرون

translation: And We have certainly created you, [O Mankind], then formed you and then We said to the angels, 'Prostrate to Adam'; so they prostrated, except for Iblees. He was not of those who prostrated.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the creation of human beings and the command given by God to the angels to prostrate before Adam. All the angels obeyed God's command, except for Iblees (Satan) who refused to prostrate. The verse highlights the significance of obedience to God's command and the consequences of disobedience, as shown by the actions of Iblees. The verse also emphasizes the special status of human beings, as they are the only creation worthy of such reverence and respect from the angels. Overall, the verse serves as a reminder of the importance of obedience and humility towards God, and the dangers of arrogance and disobedience.
orig: ولقد خلقناكم ثم صورناكم ثم قلنا للملائكة اسجدوا لآدم فسجدوا إلا إبليس لم يكن من الساجدين

translation: He said, 'What prevents me from prostrating myself to you when you have commanded me?'
interpretation: The verse is a continuation of the story of the angels' refusal to prostrate themselves before Adam, as commanded by God. Here, Iblis (Satan) is speaking and questioning why he cannot prostrate himself before Adam. He argues that he is better than Adam because he was created from fire, while Adam was created from clay. The verse highlights the arrogance and pride of Iblis, which ultimately leads to his downfall and condemnation. The verse also emphasizes the importance of obedience to God's commands, even when they may seem difficult or unjust. Disobedience and pride can lead to severe consequences, as seen in the case of Iblis.
orig: قال ما منعك ألا تسجد إذ أمرتك قال أنا خير منه خلقتني من نار وخلقته من طين

translation: He said, 'Get down from it, all of you. Indeed, you are unappreciative.' So out you went, all of you. Indeed, you are but transgressors.
interpretation: The verse recounts the story of the expulsion of Adam and Eve from Paradise. After they had disobeyed God by eating from the forbidden tree, God commanded them to leave and descend to Earth. The verse emphasizes the fall of humanity from a state of grace and blessings to a state of sin and transgression. The verse serves as a reminder of the consequences of disobedience and the importance of gratitude and humility.
orig: قال فاهبط منها فما يكون لك أن تتكبر فيها فاخرج إنك من الصاغرين

translation: He said, 'Bring me to the Day of Resurrection.'
interpretation: The verse is a quote from someone who is asking to be shown the Day of Resurrection. This day is also known as the Day of Judgment, when all of humanity will be resurrected and judged by God for their deeds in this life. The person in this verse is expressing a desire to witness this momentous event, either out of curiosity, piety, or fear. However, the verse does not specify whether this request is granted or not, leaving it up to the reader's interpretation.
orig: قال أنظرني إلى يوم يبعثون

translation: He said, 'Indeed, you are of those who look.',
interpretation: The verse is a statement made by an unspecified person, referring to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) as someone who observes and reflects on the signs of God. The word 'look' here means more than just seeing with the eyes, but rather observing and contemplating the universe and the signs of God within it. This verse can be interpreted as a recognition of the Prophet's role as a messenger and a guide, who reflects on the signs of God and shares his reflections with others in order to convey the message of Islam.
orig: قال إنك من المنظرين

translation: He said, 'So by what [means] have you diverted me from the right path, I will now sit in ambush for them on Your straight path.'
interpretation: The verse describes the words of someone who has been misguided and has deviated from the right path. The person is blaming someone else (perhaps an angel or a prophet) for diverting them from the right path. They then express their intention to lay in wait for the followers of the right path, indicating their desire to harm or mislead them. The verse can be interpreted as a warning about the dangers of being misguided and the importance of staying on the right path, as well as the consequences of attempting to harm those who are on the right path.
orig: قال فبما أغويتني لأقعدن لهم صراطك المستقيم

translation: Then We shall certainly seize you from
interpretation: No interpretation
orig: ثم لآتينهم من بين أيديهم ومن خلفهم وعن أيمانهم وعن شمائلهم ولا تجد أكثرهم شاكرين

translation: He will bring out from every sect a witness against them, and I will bring against you from them a witness, and I have prepared for the disbelievers a humiliating punishment.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the Day of Judgment and the reckoning of people for their deeds. It mentions that a witness will be brought against each sect or group of people, and a witness will also be brought against the disbelievers. The verse emphasizes the inevitability of the punishment for the disbelievers, which will be humiliating. The verse serves as a warning to those who reject faith and encourages them to reflect on the consequences of their disbelief.
orig: قال اخرج منها مذءوما مدحورا لمن تبعك منهم لأملأن جهنم منكم أجمعين

translation: O Adam, dwell you and your wife in the garden, and eat of the plenty therein where you will, but approach not this tree, lest you be of the unjust.
interpretation: The verse addresses Adam and his wife, inviting them to live and enjoy the bounties of the garden, but with a clear prohibition to approach a specific tree. The verse warns them of the consequences of disobedience, emphasizing the importance of adhering to God's commands. The verse serves as a reminder of the significance of obedience and the dangers of disobedience, setting the stage for the story of Adam and Eve's fall from grace.
orig: ويا آدم اسكن أنت وزوجك الجنة فكلا من حيث شئتما ولا تقربا هذه الشجرة فتكونا من الظالمين

translation: But Satan whispered to them both, to reveal to them that which was concealed from them of their private parts. He said, 'Your Lord has only forbidden you from this tree lest you become angels or become of the immortal.',
interpretation: The verse describes Satan's temptation of Adam and Eve, leading them to eat from the forbidden tree. The verse highlights Satan's cunning and deceit, as he whispers to them and reveals their private parts, causing them to feel shame and insecurity. Satan's words suggest that by eating from the tree, they will become like angels or gain eternal life, but this is a lie. The verse serves as a reminder of the dangers of following one's desires and the deception of Satan, who seeks to lead people astray from the path of God.
orig: فوسوس لهما الشيطان ليبدي لهما ما ووري عنهما من سوآتهما وقال ما نهاكما ربكما عن هذه الشجرة إلا أن تكونا ملكين أو تكونا من الخالدين

translation: And I am to you a faithful adviser.
interpretation: The verse is spoken by the prophet Joseph (Yusuf) to his parents, after he has been reunited with them in Egypt. Joseph is assuring his parents that he will be a good and trustworthy adviser to them. This verse emphasizes the importance of giving good advice and being a reliable support system for one's family and loved ones. It also highlights Joseph's character as a just and righteous person, who is worthy of trust and respect.
orig: وقاسمهما إني لكما لمن الناصحين

translation: And We had made them sure of Our promise, but they forgot it. And when they tasted the tree, their private parts became apparent to them, and they began to sew on themselves leaves from the garden. And their Lord called out to them, 'Did I not forbid you from that tree and tell you that Satan is an enemy to you?'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the story of Adam and Eve, when they were made to dwell in the garden and were forbidden from eating from a certain tree. Despite the promise made to them, they forgot and disobeyed, leading to their downfall. The verse highlights the consequences of their disobedience, including the loss of their innocence and the realization of their vulnerability. The verse serves as a reminder of the consequences of forgetting God's promise and disobeying His commands, and the importance of being mindful of Satan's schemes and deceptions.
orig: فدلاهما بغرور فلما ذاقا الشجرة بدت لهما سوآتهما وطفقا يخصفان عليهما من ورق الجنة وناداهما ربهما ألم أنهكما عن تلكما الشجرة وأقل لكما إن الشيطان لكما عدو مبين

translation: They said, 'Our Lord, we have wronged ourselves, and if You do not forgive us and have mercy on us, we will surely be among the losers.'
interpretation: The verse shows the remorse and regret of a group of people who recognize that they have wronged themselves and committed sins. They turn to God, seeking His forgiveness and mercy. They acknowledge their loss and the negative consequences of their actions, recognizing that without God's forgiveness and compassion, they will be among the losers. The verse emphasizes the importance of seeking God's forgiveness and mercy, and the need for repentance and a change of heart in order to avoid the negative consequences of one's actions.
orig: قالا ربنا ظلمنا أنفسنا وإن لم تغفر لنا وترحمنا لنكونن من الخاسرين

translation: He said, 'Descend from it, some of you to others, as enemies. And for you on the earth is a dwelling place and enjoyment for a time.'
interpretation: The verse is a statement made by an unnamed speaker, most likely God, instructing a group of people to descend from a place and become enemies to one another. The verse suggests that there will be a period of time where the people will have a place to live and enjoyment, but it does not specify how long this period will last. The verse may be interpreted as a warning or a punishment, indicating that the people's actions have led to this outcome. The verse also highlights the power of the speaker, who has the ability to control the fate of the people and determine their living conditions.
orig: قال اهبطوا بعضكم لبعض عدو ولكم في الأرض مستقر ومتاع إلى حين

translation: In it you live, and in it you die, and from it you will be taken out (on the Day of Resurrection).
interpretation: The verse reminds people of the fleeting nature of life and the inevitability of death. It emphasizes that people's existence is transient and limited to this world, and that they will ultimately be taken out of it on the Day of Resurrection. The verse encourages people to reflect on the purpose of their lives and to prepare for the hereafter, as this world is only a temporary abode.
orig: قال فيها تحيون وفيها تموتون ومنها تخرجون

translation: O children of Adam, We have sent down upon you clothing to cover your private parts and as adornment, and the clothing of righteousness, that is better. That is from the signs of Allah, so perhaps they will remember.
interpretation: The verse addresses the children of Adam, reminding them of the purpose of clothing, which is to cover their private parts and serve as adornment. However, the verse goes beyond the physical aspect of clothing and introduces the concept of 'the clothing of righteousness', which is described as being better than the physical clothing. This 'clothing of righteousness' is a metaphor for good character and virtuous deeds, which are highly valued in Islam. The verse emphasizes the importance of righteousness and urges people to strive for it. The verse concludes by stating that these signs are from Allah, and the hope is that people will remember and reflect on them.
orig: يا بني آدم قد أنزلنا عليكم لباسا يواري سوآتكم وريشا ولباس التقوى ذلك خير ذلك من آيات الله لعلهم يذكرون

translation: O children of Adam, let not Satan tempt you as he removed your parents from Paradise stripping them of their clothing to show them their private parts. Indeed, he sees you, he and his tribe, from where you do not see them. Indeed, We have made the devils allies for those who do not believe.
interpretation: The verse warns the children of Adam, meaning all of humanity, against the temptations of Satan. It reminds them of how Satan caused their ancestors, Adam and Eve, to be expelled from Paradise by leading them into sin. The verse highlights the danger of Satan and his followers, who are able to deceive and mislead humans in ways that are not always apparent. The verse also emphasizes that those who do not believe in God are particularly vulnerable to the influence of Satan and his followers. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of staying vigilant and resisting temptation in order to avoid the same fate as the first humans.
orig: يا بني آدم لا يفتننكم الشيطان كما أخرج أبويكم من الجنة ينزع عنهما لباسهما ليريهما سوآتهما إنه يراكم هو وقبيله من حيث لا ترونهم إنا جعلنا الشياطين أولياء للذين لا يؤمنون

translation: And when they commit an indecency, they say: 'We found our fathers doing this,' and 'Allah has commanded us thus.' Say: 'Nay, Allah never commands what is indecent. Are you saying concerning Allah what you know not?'
interpretation: The verse addresses the people who commit sins and then try to justify their actions by claiming that their ancestors did the same and that it is what God has commanded them. The verse rejects this justification and makes it clear that God never commands what is indecent or impure. The verse challenges the people to consider whether they truly know what they are saying about God and encourages them to reflect on the immorality of their actions and the importance of obeying God's commands.
orig: وإذا فعلوا فاحشة قالوا وجدنا عليها آباءنا والله أمرنا بها قل إن الله لا يأمر بالفحشاء أتقولون على الله ما لا تعلمون

translation: Say, 'My Lord has commanded justice. So, maintain your positions in prayer, and call upon Him, making religion pure for Him as you have been created upon it.'
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of justice and commands the believers to uphold it. It also encourages them to establish their prayer and call upon God with a sincere and pure intention. The verse reminds the believers of their original state of purity and instructs them to maintain it by practicing their religion as they were created upon it. This verse serves as a reminder to the believers to maintain their faith, be just, and worship God with a pure heart.
orig: قل أمر ربي بالقسط وأقيموا وجوهكم عند كل مسجد وادعوه مخلصين له الدين كما بدأكم تعودون

translation: A group [of people] whom We have guided, and a group [of people] upon whom is misguidance [i.e., astray], indeed, they have taken the devils as allies instead of Allah and they think that they are guided.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the division of people into two groups, those who are guided and those who are astray. The latter group has taken the devils as allies instead of Allah and they mistakenly believe that they are on the right path. This verse highlights the importance of following the guidance of Allah and warns against the dangers of being misguided by the deception of the devils.
orig: فريقا هدى وفريقا حق عليهم الضلالة إنهم اتخذوا الشياطين أولياء من دون الله ويحسبون أنهم مهتدون

translation: O children of Adam, take your adornment at every mosque, and eat and drink, but be not extravagant. Indeed, He likes not those who commit extravagance.
interpretation: The verse addresses the children of Adam, reminding them to maintain their appearance and attend the mosques. It encourages them to eat and drink, but with moderation and restraint. The verse warns against extravagance and waste, emphasizing that God does not approve of such behavior. The verse encourages Muslims to maintain a balance in all aspects of their lives, including their diet and appearance, and to avoid excess and extravagance.
orig: يا بني آدم خذوا زينتكم عند كل مسجد وكلوا واشربوا ولا تسرفوا إنه لا يحب المسرفين

translation: Say, 'Who has forbidden the adornment of God which He has produced for His servants, and the goodly provisions?' Say, 'They are for the believers in the present life, purely, on the Day of Resurrection.' Thus do We distinguish the signs for a people who know.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the blessings of God and the prohibition of forbidding these blessings. The verse emphasizes that the adornments and provisions are from God and are meant for His servants to enjoy. The verse also highlights the distinction between believers and non-believers, stating that the blessings are pure for the believers in this life and on the Day of Resurrection. The verse serves as a reminder that God's signs and blessings are clear and distinguishable for those who possess knowledge and understanding.
orig: قل من حرم زينة الله التي أخرج لعباده والطيبات من الرزق قل هي للذين آمنوا في الحياة الدنيا خالصة يوم القيامة كذلك نفصل الآيات لقوم يعلمون

translation: Say, 'My Lord has only forbidden immoralities, whether committed openly or secretly, sins and wrongdoing without right, and that you associate with Allah that for which He has not sent down any authority, and that you say about Allah that which you do not know.'
interpretation: The verse outlines the prohibitions set forth by the speaker's Lord. These include immoralities committed both openly and secretly, sins, and wrongdoing without justification. Additionally, the verse forbids associating anything with Allah for which He has not sent down any authority, and making false claims about Allah without knowledge. The verse highlights the importance of following the guidelines set forth by Allah and avoiding actions and speech that go against His teachings.
orig: قل إنما حرم ربي الفواحش ما ظهر منها وما بطن والإثم والبغي بغير الحق وأن تشركوا بالله ما لم ينزل به سلطانا وأن تقولوا على الله ما لا تعلمون

translation: And for every people is a term, so when their time has come, they cannot delay it nor can they advance it an hour.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the predetermined fate of every community and the inevitability of the hour of their destruction. Once the appointed time arrives, it cannot be delayed or postponed, no matter what efforts the people make. Similarly, they cannot bring forward their time of reckoning. The verse serves as a reminder of the power of God over all things and the futility of human efforts to escape the consequences of their actions.
orig: ولكل أمة أجل فإذا جاء أجلهم لا يستأخرون ساعة ولا يستقدمون

translation: O children of Adam, when messengers come to you from among you, reciting My verses to you, then whoever becomes pious and corrects himself - there will be no fear concerning them, nor will they grieve.
interpretation: The verse addresses all of humanity, reminding them of the role of the prophets in conveying God's message. The verse emphasizes the importance of heeding the message of the prophets and acting upon it by becoming pious and correcting one's behavior. Those who do so will have nothing to fear and will not be subject to grief, indicating the peace and tranquility that comes with living a righteous life in accordance with God's will.
orig: يا بني آدم إما يأتينكم رسل منكم يقصون عليكم آياتي فمن اتقى وأصلح فلا خوف عليهم ولا هم يحزنون

translation: And those who have disbelieved in Our verses and become arrogant from them - those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein eternally.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the fate of those who disbelieve in the signs or verses of God and are arrogant towards them. The consequence of their actions is that they will become companions of the Fire and will abide therein eternally. The verse emphasizes the severity of the punishment for those who reject God's messages and the importance of humility and acceptance of God's guidance.
orig: والذين كذبوا بآياتنا واستكبروا عنها أولئك أصحاب النار هم فيها خالدون

translation: And who is more unjust than those who invent a lie about Allah or deny His signs? Those will receive their due share in this worldly life, then to Us is their return; then We will make them taste the severe punishment on the Day of Resurrection.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the unjust actions of those who lie about God or deny His signs. These people will receive their due share in this life, but ultimately they will be returned to God and will face severe punishment on the Day of Resurrection. The verse serves as a warning against lying about God and denying His signs, emphasizing the certainty of punishment for those who commit these acts of unbelief.
orig: فمن أظلم ممن افترى على الله كذبا أو كذب بآياته أولئك ينالهم نصيبهم من الكتاب حتى إذا جاءتهم رسلنا يتوفونهم قالوا أين ما كنتم تدعون من دون الله قالوا ضلوا عنا وشهدوا على أنفسهم أنهم كانوا كافرين

translation: He said, 'Enter the Fire among nations that have passed away before you, both jinn and men.'
