Every time a nation enters, it curses its sister until, when they have all joined together there, the last of them will say about the first of them, 'Our Lord, these have led us astray, so give them a double punishment in the Fire.' He will say, 'For each one there is double, but you do not know.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the punishment of sinners who are compared to previous nations of jinn and humans who have entered the Fire. The verse emphasizes the severity of their punishment, as they will receive 'a double punishment in the Fire'. The verse also highlights the regret of the last group of sinners who will blame the first group for leading them astray. The verse serves as a warning to those who persist in their sins and lead others astray, reminding them of the severe consequences of their actions and the unavoidability of God's punishment.
orig: قال ادخلوا في أمم قد خلت من قبلكم من الجن والإنس في النار كلما دخلت أمة لعنت أختها حتى إذا اداركوا فيها جميعا قالت أخراهم لأولاهم ربنا هؤلاء أضلونا فآتهم عذابا ضعفا من النار قال لكل ضعف ولكن لا تعلمون

translation: And the first of them said to the last of them: 'You shall not overcome us.' But they surely saw the punishment, and it was said: 'Taste the punishment of eternity for what you used to do.'
interpretation: The verse describes a conversation between two groups of people, where the first group arrogantly claims that the second group will not be able to overcome them. However, the verse reveals that both groups ultimately faced God's punishment. The punishment was a consequence of their past actions and serves as a reminder of the consequences of arrogance and injustice. The punishment is described as eternal, emphasizing the severity of their actions and the eternal consequences of their choices.
orig: وقالت أولاهم لأخراهم فما كان لكم علينا من فضل فذوقوا العذاب بما كنتم تكسبون

translation: Indeed, those who have denied Our signs and become arrogant toward them - the gates of heaven will not be opened for them, nor will they enter Paradise until the camel passes through the eye of the needle. And thus do We recompense the criminals.
interpretation: The verse warns of the consequences of denying the signs of God and becoming arrogant towards them. The verse uses the metaphor of a camel passing through the eye of a needle to emphasize the impossibility of those who have denied God's signs and become arrogant towards them from entering Paradise. The verse serves as a reminder of the severe consequences of arrogance and disbelief. Those who persist in these attitudes will not be granted entry into heaven and will instead face punishment for their actions.
orig: إن الذين كذبوا بآياتنا واستكبروا عنها لا تفتح لهم أبواب السماء ولا يدخلون الجنة حتى يلج الجمل في سم الخياط وكذلك نجزي المجرمين

translation: For them there will be a bed of Hell (Fire), and over them coverings (of Hell-Fire). And thus do We recompense the wrong-doers.
interpretation: The verse describes the punishment for the wrong-doers, who will have a bed of Hell and coverings of Hell-Fire above them. This punishment is a recompense for their wrong-doing, emphasizing the just nature of God's punishment. The verse serves as a warning to those who commit sins and wrong-doings, reminding them of the severe consequences of their actions and the fairness of God's judgment.
orig: لهم من جهنم مهاد ومن فوقهم غواش وكذلك نجزي الظالمين

translation: And those who believe and do good deeds, We charge no soul beyond its capacity. Those are the ones who will be in Paradise, abiding therein as eternal residents.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the people who believe in God and do good deeds. It emphasizes that God does not burden any soul beyond its capacity. The ones who do believe and do good deeds will be in Paradise, living there eternally. This verse serves as a message of hope and reassurance for those who strive to live a righteous life, and a reminder that God does not demand from us more than we are capable of. It also highlights the ultimate reward for those who lead a life of faith and righteousness.
orig: والذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات لا نكلف نفسا إلا وسعها أولئك أصحاب الجنة هم فيها خالدون

translation: And We removed whatever of hardness was in their breasts, so the rivers flowed from beneath them. And they said, 'Praise be to Allah, who has guided us to this.' And we would not have been guided if Allah had not guided us. Indeed, the messengers of our Lord came with the truth.' And they will be invited to eternal abode.
interpretation: The verse describes the transformation of a group of people who had hardness in their hearts, preventing them from seeing the truth. However, through divine intervention, the hardness was removed and they were able to see and understand the truth. They express their gratitude to God for guiding them and acknowledge that they would not have been guided without His help. The verse emphasizes the role of the messengers in conveying the truth and the ultimate destination of these people being the eternal abode. The verse highlights the importance of divine guidance and the role of messengers in leading people to the truth.
orig: ونزعنا ما في صدورهم من غل تجري من تحتهم الأنهار وقالوا الحمد لله الذي هدانا لهذا وما كنا لنهتدي لولا أن هدانا الله لقد جاءت رسل ربنا بالحق ونودوا أن تلكم الجنة أورثتموها بما كنتم تعملون

translation: And the inhabitants of Paradise will call out to the inhabitants of the Fire, 'Indeed, we have found what our Lord promised us to be true. Have you found what your Lord promised you to be true?' They will say, 'Yes.' So a crier will call between them, 'The curse of Allah is upon the wrongdoers.'
interpretation: The verse describes a scene in the afterlife where the people of Paradise will call out to the people of the Fire, expressing that they have found the promises of their Lord to be true. The people of the Fire will confirm that they too have found the promises of their Lord to be true, indicating that they are aware of the reality of their situation and the consequences of their actions. Then, a crier will proclaim the curse of Allah upon the wrongdoers. The verse emphasizes the reality of the afterlife, the fulfillment of divine promises, and the distinction between the righteous and the wrongdoers. It serves as a reminder of the importance of leading a righteous life and the consequences of wrongdoing.
orig: ونادى أصحاب الجنة أصحاب النار أن قد وجدنا ما وعدنا ربنا حقا فهل وجدتم ما وعد ربكم حقا قالوا نعم فأذن مؤذن بينهم أن لعنة الله على الظالمين

translation: Those who reject the path of God and seek to twist it, while they deny the Hereafter.
interpretation: The verse describes those who oppose the path of God, meaning they reject or resist God's guidance and teachings. They also seek to twist or distort the path, indicating their attempts to mislead others and spread falsehood. Despite their denial of the Hereafter, the verse serves as a reminder that their actions will not go unnoticed and they will be held accountable for their actions on the Day of Judgment.
orig: الذين يصدون عن سبيل الله ويبغونها عوجا وهم بالآخرة كافرون

translation: And between them is a barrier, and on al-A'raf are men who recognize all by their mark. And they call out to the inhabitants of Paradise, 'Peace be upon you.' They have not [yet] entered it, but they hope.
interpretation: The verse describes a scene in the afterlife where there is a barrier separating two groups of people. On the side called al-A'raf are men who can recognize others by their marks or signs. These people call out to the inhabitants of Paradise, greeting them with peace. However, they have not yet entered Paradise themselves, but they hope to do so. This verse may be interpreted as a description of the different fates of people in the afterlife, with some residing in Paradise and others in a different, separate place. The verse also highlights the concept of recognition in the afterlife, where individuals are known by their actions or beliefs. Additionally, the verse emphasizes the hope of those on al-A'raf, indicating the possibility of redemption or improvement even in the afterlife.
orig: وبينهما حجاب وعلى الأعراف رجال يعرفون كلا بسيماهم ونادوا أصحاب الجنة أن سلام عليكم لم يدخلوها وهم يطمعون

translation: And when their eyes were turned away, they said, 'Our Lord, make us not a trial for the unrighteous people.'
interpretation: The verse describes a moment when the eyes of certain people were turned away, possibly in death or in a transition to another state. At that moment, they pleaded with God not to make them a trial or a test for the unrighteous people. The verse suggests that these individuals were aware of the corrupting influence they might have on others and sought to avoid it, even after death. It also serves as a reminder to be mindful of the impact of one's actions on others and to strive for righteousness in all aspects of life.
orig: وإذا صرفت أبصارهم تلقاء أصحاب النار قالوا ربنا لا تجعلنا مع القوم الظالمين

translation: And the inhabitants of the enclosures called out to men whom they recognized by their marks, saying: 'Surely, you will not leave us to abandon you, nor will you be faithful to us.',
interpretation: The verse describes the inhabitants of the enclosures (a group of people who were protected or isolated) calling out to some men they recognized by their marks or signs. These men were probably allies or friends of the inhabitants. The inhabitants pleaded with the men not to abandon them and to remain faithful to their alliance. The verse may be interpreted as a critique of those who break their promises and abandon their allies in times of need. It may also serve as a reminder of the importance of loyalty and trustworthiness in relationships.
orig: ونادى أصحاب الأعراف رجالا يعرفونهم بسيماهم قالوا ما أغنى عنكم جمعكم وما كنتم تستكبرون

translation: Those who you swore that God would not show mercy to, enter Paradise. There is no fear concerning them, nor will they grieve.
interpretation: The verse speaks about a group of people who were considered by others as not worthy of God's mercy. However, the verse reveals that these people will enter Paradise, and they will not have to fear or grieve. The verse emphasizes the power of God's mercy and His ability to forgive and grant salvation to anyone He chooses. The verse serves as a reminder that no one is beyond the reach of God's mercy and that He has the final say in the fate of all His creations.
orig: أهؤلاء الذين أقسمتم لا ينالهم الله برحمة ادخلوا الجنة لا خوف عليكم ولا أنتم تحزنون

translation: And the inhabitants of the Fire called out to the inhabitants of the Garden, 'Pour upon us some water or some of what Allah has provided you.' They said, 'Indeed, Allah has forbidden them both upon the disbelievers.'
interpretation: The verse describes a scene in which the people of Hell call out to the people of Paradise, asking them to share some water or provisions with them. However, the people of Paradise refuse, explaining that God has forbidden them from sharing with the disbelievers. The verse emphasizes the reality of the division between the believers and the disbelievers, and the consequences of disbelief. It serves as a reminder of the importance of faith and obedience to God, and the rewards and blessings that come with it, as well as the consequences of disbelief and rejection of God's message.
orig: ونادى أصحاب النار أصحاب الجنة أن أفيضوا علينا من الماء أو مما رزقكم الله قالوا إن الله حرمهما على الكافرين

translation: Those who take their religion as amusement and play, and whose life of this world is the only concern, will be dismissed from God on the Day of Resurrection. They will not be allowed to answer any questions nor will they be given respite.
interpretation: The verse warns those who treat their religion as a form of entertainment or a trivial matter, and who are preoccupied with the pleasures of this world. Such people will be rejected by God on the Day of Judgment and will not be given the opportunity to explain themselves or to defend their actions. They will not be granted any respite, and the consequences of their actions will be immediate and eternal. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of taking one's religion seriously and of preparing for the afterlife.
orig: الذين اتخذوا دينهم لهوا ولعبا وغرتهم الحياة الدنيا فاليوم ننساهم كما نسوا لقاء يومهم هذا وما كانوا بآياتنا يجحدون

translation: And We have already sent down to them a Book (the Qur'an) which We have detailed with knowledge, a guidance and a mercy for a people who believe.
interpretation: The verse refers to the sending down of the Qur'an, which is a source of guidance and mercy for the believers. The verse highlights that the Qur'an is not just a collection of stories or rules, but a detailed and comprehensive book sent down with knowledge. The verse serves as a reminder to the believers of the importance of the Qur'an in their lives, and the guidance and mercy it provides for those who believe and follow its teachings.
orig: ولقد جئناهم بكتاب فصلناه على علم هدى ورحمة لقوم يؤمنون

translation: Do they then wait for anything other than the Hour [i.e., the Day of Resurrection] to come to them suddenly? On the Day it comes to them, some will be brought forward [for punishment], and others will be sent back [to life for more chances], and they will be asked about what they used to do.
interpretation: The verse warns people about the imminent arrival of the Day of Judgment, which will come unexpectedly. It describes the two possible outcomes for people on that Day: some will be punished for their deeds, while others will be given more opportunities to do good. The verse emphasizes the importance of accountability for one's actions, as people will be questioned about what they used to do. It serves as a reminder to prepare for the inevitable Day of Judgment and to strive for righteousness in order to avoid punishment.
orig: هل ينظرون إلا تأويله يوم يأتي تأويله يقول الذين نسوه من قبل قد جاءت رسل ربنا بالحق فهل لنا من شفعاء فيشفعوا لنا أو نرد فنعمل غير الذي كنا نعمل قد خسروا أنفسهم وضل عنهم ما كانوا يفترون

translation: Indeed, your Lord is Allah, who created the heavens and the earth in six days, then He established Himself above the Throne. He covers the night with the day, seeking it rapidly, and (by) the sun, and the moon, and the stars subjected by His command. Indeed, His is the creation and the command. Blessed is Allah, Lord of the worlds.
interpretation: The verse affirms the oneness of God as the creator of the heavens and the earth in six days. The verse emphasizes God's power and control over all of creation, including the natural phenomena of the day and night, the sun, the moon, and the stars. The verse highlights the greatness and majesty of God by describing Him as the one who established Himself above the Throne and subjected all of creation by His command. The verse serves as a reminder of God's power and control over all aspects of life and the importance of recognizing and submitting to His will.
orig: إن ربكم الله الذي خلق السماوات والأرض في ستة أيام ثم استوى على العرش يغشي الليل النهار يطلبه حثيثا والشمس والقمر والنجوم مسخرات بأمره ألا له الخلق والأمر تبارك الله رب العالمين

translation: Invite to your Lord with wisdom and good admonition, and argue with them in a way that is best. Indeed, your Lord is most knowing of who has strayed from His way, and He is most knowing of who is guided.
interpretation: This verse encourages the Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) and his followers to invite people to Islam with wisdom and good admonition, and to engage in respectful and thoughtful dialogue with those who reject their message. The verse emphasizes the importance of understanding and compassion in spreading the message of Islam, and the ultimate knowledge and wisdom of God in guiding people towards the right path. The verse also highlights the importance of patience and persistence in conveying the message, and the role of God in determining the outcome of these efforts.
orig: ادعوا ربكم تضرعا وخفية إنه لا يحب المعتدين

translation: And do not commit corruption in the land after its reformation, and call upon Him in fear and hope. Indeed, the mercy of Allah is near to the doers of good.
interpretation: This verse is urging people to avoid causing corruption and mischief in the land, after it has been reformed or improved. Instead, they should call upon God in a state of fear and hope, recognizing their dependence on Him and their need for His guidance and protection. The verse ends on a positive note, emphasizing that the mercy of God is close to those who strive to do good and to live righteously.
orig: ولا تفسدوا في الأرض بعد إصلاحها وادعوه خوفا وطمعا إن رحمت الله قريب من المحسنين

translation: And it is He who sends the winds as heralds of His mercy, until, when they bear a heavy-laden cloud, We drive it to a dead land and then send down water with it, and We bring forth thereby every kind of fruit. Likewise, We will bring forth the dead; perhaps you will be reminded.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the power and mercy of God, who sends the winds that carry the clouds and bring forth rain, leading to the growth of various fruits. The verse highlights the idea of resurrection and the revival of the dead, drawing a parallel between the growth of plants and the resurrection of the dead. The verse serves as a reminder to people about the signs of God's existence and power, encouraging them to remember and reflect on these signs, and to turn to God in repentance and gratitude.
orig: وهو الذي يرسل الرياح بشرا بين يدي رحمته حتى إذا أقلت سحابا ثقالا سقناه لبلد ميت فأنزلنا به الماء فأخرجنا به من كل الثمرات كذلك نخرج الموتى لعلكم تذكرون

translation: But the good land, its vegetation emerges by the permission of its Lord, and that which is bad, nothing emerges except scarce, thus do We explain the signs for a people who give thanks.
interpretation: The verse contrasts the fertility of good land with that of bad land, emphasizing that the growth of vegetation on good land occurs by the will of its Lord, while on bad land, vegetation is scarce. The verse highlights the idea that God's signs are explained for those who are grateful. The verse may serve as a reminder that God's blessings are not equally distributed and that those who are grateful for what they have will be rewarded.
orig: والبلد الطيب يخرج نباته بإذن ربه والذي خبث لا يخرج إلا نكدا كذلك نصرف الآيات لقوم يشكرون

translation: Indeed, We sent Noah to his people, [saying], 'O my people, worship Allah. You have no deity other than Him. Indeed, I fear for you the punishment of a tremendous Day.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about Prophet Noah's (pbuh) mission to his people, calling them to worship only one God and warning them of the punishment of a tremendous Day. The verse emphasizes the importance of monotheism and the danger of associating partners with God. The verse also highlights the role of prophets as warner and guide, reminding people of the consequences of their actions and the importance of repentance and submission to God.
orig: لقد أرسلنا نوحا إلى قومه فقال يا قوم اعبدوا الله ما لكم من إله غيره إني أخاف عليكم عذاب يوم عظيم

translation: Said the elders of his people, 'Indeed, we see you in clear error.'
interpretation: The verse describes the disbelief and rejection of the Prophet Noah's message by his people. The elders of his community accused him of being in clear error and rejected his call to worship one God. This verse highlights the opposition and rejection faced by Prophets and messengers of God, and serves as a reminder of the importance of staying steadfast in the face of adversity and continuing to spread the message of truth.
orig: قال الملأ من قومه إنا لنراك في ضلال مبين

translation: He said, 'O my people, I am not guilty of misconduct, but I am a messenger from the Lord of the Worlds.'
interpretation: The verse is a statement made by a prophet who is denying any wrongdoing on his part and declaring that he is a messenger from the Lord of the Worlds. This declaration is a common theme in the Qur'an, where prophets assert their innocence and proclaim their mission to guide people to the right path. The verse emphasizes the prophet's commitment to his mission and his determination to fulfill it despite the opposition and rejection he may face from his people. The verse also highlights the importance of prophethood and the role of prophets as intermediaries between God and humanity, tasked with delivering God's message to people and guiding them towards righteousness.
orig: قال يا قوم ليس بي ضلالة ولكني رسول من رب العالمين

translation: I bring you the messages of my Lord and I advise you and I know from God what you do not know.
interpretation: The speaker in this verse asserts their role as a messenger or prophet, bringing the messages of their Lord to the audience. They also offer their advice and guidance, emphasizing their superior knowledge and understanding, which comes from God. The verse highlights the importance of listening to and following the guidance of the prophet, as they have access to divine knowledge and wisdom that is not available to others.
orig: أبلغكم رسالات ربي وأنصح لكم وأعلم من الله ما لا تعلمون

translation: And marvel you at the reminder that has come to you from your Lord, through a man from among you, to warn you, so that you may fear Him, and perhaps you will show mercy.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the astonishment of the people at the message of warning and guidance that they have received from their Lord through one of their own. The verse emphasizes the importance of the message, which is to fear God and show mercy. The verse serves as a reminder that the guidance comes from the Lord and is delivered through a human being. It calls on the people to pay attention to the message, to take it seriously, and to act upon it by fearing God and showing mercy to others.
orig: أوعجبتم أن جاءكم ذكر من ربكم على رجل منكم لينذركم ولتتقوا ولعلكم ترحمون

translation: But they denied him, so We saved him and those with him in the ship, and We drowned those who denied Our signs. Indeed, they were a blind people.
interpretation: The verse speaks about a group of people who denied the truth and rejected the messenger, and as a result, they were punished by being drowned. Meanwhile, the messenger and his followers were saved and protected. The verse emphasizes the consequences of denying the signs of God and the certainty of God's punishment for those who reject the truth. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of recognizing and accepting the truth, and the consequences of denying it.
orig: فكذبوه فأنجيناه والذين معه في الفلك وأغرقنا الذين كذبوا بآياتنا إنهم كانوا قوما عمين

translation: And to 'Ad [We sent] their brother Hud. He said, 'O my people, worship Allah; you have no deity other than Him. Then will you not fear Him?'
interpretation: The verse introduces the Prophet Hud, who was sent to the people of 'Ad as a warner. Hud calls his people to worship only Allah and to abandon the worship of any other deities. The verse emphasizes the importance of monotheism and the need to fear and worship only one God. The verse also highlights the role of prophets as warners and guides, reminding people of their responsibility to acknowledge and submit to the one true God.
orig: وإلى عاد أخاهم هودا قال يا قوم اعبدوا الله ما لكم من إله غيره أفلا تتقون

translation: The leaders of his people who disbelieved said, 'Indeed, we see you in clear error, and indeed, we think you are of the liars.'
interpretation: The verse describes the disbelievers among the people of a prophet rejecting his message and accusing him of lying. The use of the word 'clear error' highlights the certainty and confidence with which the disbelievers rejected the prophet's message. The verse serves as a reminder that those who reject the message of God and His messengers will face severe consequences for their disbelief and rejection.
orig: قال الملأ الذين كفروا من قومه إنا لنراك في سفاهة وإنا لنظنك من الكاذبين

translation: He said, 'O my people, I am not a foolish person, but I am a messenger from the Lord of the Worlds.'
interpretation: The verse relays a message from a prophet who is denying the accusations of being foolish or unintelligent. Instead, the prophet asserts that they are a messenger sent from the Lord of the Worlds. This statement emphasizes the prophet's divine mission and their role as a mediator between the divine and human realms. The verse highlights the importance of prophethood and the significance of the message being delivered. The prophet's words serve as a reminder to the community of the importance of heeding the message and recognizing the divine origin of the prophet's authority.
orig: قال يا قوم ليس بي سفاهة ولكني رسول من رب العالمين

translation: I bring you the messages of my Lord and I am to you a sincere adviser.
interpretation: The verse is a statement made by a prophet or a messenger of God, who is bringing the messages of his Lord to the people. The prophet or messenger sees himself as a sincere and trustworthy advisor to the people, and he conveys the messages of God to them with the intention of guiding and advising them towards the right path. The verse emphasizes the importance of the role of the prophet or messenger as a conveyor of God's messages and as a guide for the people, and it highlights the sincerity and trustworthiness of the prophet or messenger in fulfilling this role.
orig: أبلغكم رسالات ربي وأنا لكم ناصح أمين

translation: And marvel you at the reminder that has come to you from your Lord through a man from among you, to warn you? Remember when He made you successors after the people of Noah, and increased you in stature greatly? So remember the blessings of Allah that you may prosper.
interpretation: The verse speaks about a reminder or warning that has come to the people from their Lord through a man from among them. The verse reminds the people of their history and heritage, specifically when they were made successors after the people of Noah and were given great stature. The verse calls on the people to remember the blessings of God and to reflect on them, with the hope that they may prosper. The verse emphasizes the importance of remembering and being grateful for the blessings of God, and the potential consequences of forgetting or ignoring them.
orig: أوعجبتم أن جاءكم ذكر من ربكم على رجل منكم لينذركم واذكروا إذ جعلكم خلفاء من بعد قوم نوح وزادكم في الخلق بسطة فاذكروا آلاء الله لعلكم تفلحون

translation: They said, 'You have come to us to tell us that we should worship only Allah and give up what our forefathers used to worship.' Bring us what you promise us, if you are among the truthful.'
interpretation: The verse recounts the words of the disbelievers who rejected the message of the prophet to worship only one God and abandon the idolatrous practices of their ancestors. They challenged the prophet to prove his truthfulness by fulfilling his promise. The verse highlights the resistance and disbelief of the people towards the new teachings and their demand for a tangible proof, showing the difficulty of propagating a new belief system and the common human tendency to cling to tradition and familiarity.
orig: قالوا أجئتنا لنعبد الله وحده ونذر ما كان يعبد آباؤنا فأتنا بما تعدنا إن كنت من الصادقين

translation: He said, 'Upon you have come from your Lord punishment and wrath, do you argue with me concerning the names which you and your forefathers have named? Allah has not sent down any authority for them. So wait, I too am with you among those who wait.'
interpretation: The verse relays a conversation where the addressee is informed of the punishment and wrath of their Lord. The addressee is questioned for arguing about the names they and their ancestors have given, implying that these names lack any authority from Allah. The verse urges the addressee to wait, suggesting that the matter is not yet resolved and that the speaker will also wait with them among those who are patient. The verse can be interpreted as a warning against arrogance and a reminder of the power and authority of Allah.
orig: قال قد وقع عليكم من ربكم رجس وغضب أتجادلونني في أسماء سميتموها أنتم وآباؤكم ما نزل الله بها من سلطان فانتظروا إني معكم من المنتظرين

translation: But We saved him and his companions by mercy from Us, and We cut the last remnant of those who denied Our signs and were not believers.
interpretation: The verse speaks about God's mercy towards a group of people, including a specific individual, and their deliverance from a group of disbelievers. The verse highlights God's compassion towards the believers and His punishment towards those who reject His signs and are not believers. The phrase 'We cut the last remnant' implies the complete destruction of the disbelievers, leaving no trace behind. The verse serves as a reminder of the ultimate triumph of truth and justice over falsehood and oppression.
orig: فأنجيناه والذين معه برحمة منا وقطعنا دابر الذين كذبوا بآياتنا وما كانوا مؤمنين

translation: And to Thamud (We sent) their brother Salih. He said, 'O my people, worship Allah; you have no deity other than Him. Indeed, a sign for you has come: this she-camel of Allah - a sign for you. So leave her to eat in the land of Allah and do not touch her with harm, lest you be seized by a painful punishment.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the Prophet Salih being sent to the people of Thamud as a warner, urging them to worship only one God. He presents a sign to them in the form of a she-camel, which they are instructed to leave alone and not harm. The verse emphasizes the importance of respecting and preserving the signs of God, as well as the consequences of not heeding the warnings and disobeying God's commands. It serves as a reminder of the power and authority of God, and the importance of following His instructions.
orig: وإلى ثمود أخاهم صالحا قال يا قوم اعبدوا الله ما لكم من إله غيره قد جاءتكم بينة من ربكم هذه ناقة الله لكم آية فذروها تأكل في أرض الله ولا تمسوها بسوء فيأخذكم عذاب أليم

translation: And remember when you were made successors after the people of 'Ād, and you settled in the land, building upon its plains and carving homes from the mountains. So remember the graces of Allah and do not be wicked corruptors in the land.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the early history of humanity, reminding the listeners of their origins and their responsibilities. The verse states that the listeners are successors of a previous civilization, the people of 'Ād, who have been destroyed for their sins. The verse then describes how the listeners settled in the land, building homes and establishing a new society. However, the verse warns them not to forget the graces of God and not to become corruptors in the land. The verse emphasizes the importance of remembering God and living a righteous life, as a reminder of the consequences of forgetting God and becoming wicked. The verse serves as a call to mindfulness and gratitude, urging the listeners to live a responsible and moral life.
orig: واذكروا إذ جعلكم خلفاء من بعد عاد وبوأكم في الأرض تتخذون من سهولها قصورا وتنحتون الجبال بيوتا فاذكروا آلاء الله ولا تعثوا في الأرض مفسدين

translation: The elite of his people, who were arrogant, said to those of his people who were oppressed, 'Do you know that a righteous messenger has been sent to you from your Lord?' They said, 'Indeed, we are believers in what has been sent down to us.'
interpretation: The verse describes a confrontation between two groups of people in a community, where one group (the elite) is arrogant and oppressive, and the other group (the oppressed) is weak and marginalized. The elite group is expressing their disbelief and skepticism about the arrival of a righteous messenger from the Lord, sent to guide and support the oppressed group. The oppressed group, however, declares their faith and belief in the message that has been revealed to them. The verse highlights the conflict and tension between the two groups, and the significance of the message that has been sent to the oppressed group, who are receptive to it and willing to embrace it.
orig: قال الملأ الذين استكبروا من قومه للذين استضعفوا لمن آمن منهم أتعلمون أن صالحا مرسل من ربه قالوا إنا بما أرسل به مؤمنون

translation: Those who have been arrogant said, 'Indeed, we disbelieve in what you have been reminded of.'
interpretation: The verse highlights the rejection and disbelief of those who are arrogant in the face of the truth. The phrase 'what you have been reminded of' refers to the message or reminder that has been given to the believers. The verse emphasizes the contrast between the believers and the arrogant, and suggests that the arrogant reject the truth because of their own arrogance and pride. The verse serves as a warning to those who are arrogant and prideful, reminding them that their rejection of the truth will not change its validity or power.
orig: قال الذين استكبروا إنا بالذي آمنتم به كافرون

translation: So they hamstrung the she-camel and rebelled against the command of their Lord, and said, 'O Salih, bring us what you promise us, if you are indeed one of the messengers.'
interpretation: The verse describes the actions of the people of the prophet Salih, who disobeyed God's command and hamstrung the she-camel that was sent as a sign from God. The people's rejection of Salih's message and their demand for a sign is a clear example of their disbelief and rejection of God's message. The verse serves as a reminder of the consequences of disbelief and the importance of accepting and following the message of God's messengers.
orig: فعقروا الناقة وعتوا عن أمر ربهم وقالوا يا صالح ائتنا بما تعدنا إن كنت من المرسلين

translation: And the striking seizure took them in the morning, and they were found lifeless in their homes.
interpretation: The verse describes a sudden and unexpected event, referred to as a 'striking seizure', that overtook the people while they were in their homes. The result of this event was that they were found dead in their homes. The verse emphasizes the suddenness and unexpectedness of the event, as well as its severity, as the people had no time to prepare or escape. The verse may be interpreted as a warning of the consequences of disbelief and wrongdoing, and the suddenness with which death can come, leaving no time for repentance.
orig: فأخذتهم الرجفة فأصبحوا في دارهم جاثمين

translation: And he (Noah) turned away from them and said, 'O my people, indeed I have conveyed to you the message of my Lord and advised you, but you do not like those who advise.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the Prophet Noah's (pbuh) frustration and disappointment towards his people for not heeding his warnings and advice. Despite his best efforts to convey the message of his Lord, the people rejected his message and did not appreciate his efforts to guide them. The verse highlights the common struggle of the prophets in delivering the message of God and the rejection they faced from their people. It also emphasizes the importance of being open-minded and receptive to advice and guidance, and the consequences of rejecting it.
orig: فتولى عنهم وقال يا قوم لقد أبلغتكم رسالة ربي ونصحت لكم ولكن لا تحبون الناصحين

translation: And Lot, when he said to his people, 'Do you approach unnatural desire? Do not approach it. Indeed, you are a people behaving ignorantly.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the Prophet Lot's warning to his people against committing lewd and immoral acts. The verse highlights the Prophet's efforts to guide his people away from ignorance and deviance, and his call for them to abandon their sinful ways. The verse serves as a reminder to the importance of upholding moral values and avoiding actions that go against the teachings of Islam. It also emphasizes the role of prophets as guides and warners, and the responsibility of the community to heed their advice.
orig: ولوطا إذ قال لقومه أتأتون الفاحشة ما سبقكم بها من أحد من العالمين

translation: Indeed, you come to the men with lust instead of the women. Rather, you are a people behaving ignorantly.
interpretation: The verse addresses a group of people who have an inappropriate desire for other men, rather than women. The verse strongly condemns this behavior, describing it as ignorance and going against the natural order of things. This verse can be interpreted as a condemnation of homosexuality and a reminder that such actions are unacceptable in the eyes of God.
orig: إنكم لتأتون الرجال شهوة من دون النساء بل أنتم قوم مسرفون

translation: And the only answer of his people was that they said: 'Expel them from your town! They are a people who purify themselves.'
interpretation: The verse describes the response of the people to a certain individual (who is not mentioned in the verse). Instead of listening to the individual or considering his message, the people's response is to expel him and his followers from their town. The verse highlights the close-mindedness and rejection of the people, who are unwilling to engage with those who are different from them. The phrase 'they are a people who purify themselves' suggests that the people being expelled have a strong sense of morality and cleanliness, and that the people expelling them are the ones who are truly unjust and impure.
orig: وما كان جواب قومه إلا أن قالوا أخرجوهم من قريتكم إنهم أناس يتطهرون

translation: But We saved him and his family, except his wife; she was of those who remained behind.
interpretation: The verse speaks about a person who was saved along with his family, with the exception of his wife who was left behind. The phrase 'remained behind' implies that she was not among those who were chosen for salvation. The verse highlights the distinction between those who are saved and those who are not, emphasizing the importance of being among the chosen ones. It serves as a reminder that one's fate is not in their own hands, but rather in the hands of the divine power, and that being among the righteous and obedient is crucial for salvation.
orig: فأنجيناه وأهله إلا امرأته كانت من الغابرين

translation: And We sent down upon them a rain, then see how was the end of the wicked.
interpretation: The verse describes a punishment sent down from God upon a group of people in the form of a heavy rain. The phrase 'then see how was the end of the wicked' encourages the reader to reflect on the consequences of the actions of these people. The verse serves as a warning to those who persist in their wrongdoing, and emphasizes the reality of God's punishment and the ultimate fate of the unrighteous.
orig: وأمطرنا عليهم مطرا فانظر كيف كان عاقبة المجرمين

translation: And to the city of his people, Shu'ayb said, 'O my people, worship Allah; you have no deity other than Him. Indeed, a clear proof from your Lord has come to you; so give full measure and weight and do not deprive people of their due and do not commit abuse on the earth, spreading corruption.' This is better for you, if you are believers.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the Prophet Shu'ayb (peace be upon him) calling his people to worship only one God, Allah, and to give up their false deities. The verse highlights the importance of fairness and justice in all actions, including giving full measure and weight, not cheating people, and not causing corruption in the land. The verse emphasizes that these actions are in the best interest of the people, if they are believers. The verse serves as a reminder to be fair and just in all dealings and to avoid corruption and harm to others, as these actions are pleasing to God and beneficial for society.
orig: وإلى مدين أخاهم شعيبا قال يا قوم اعبدوا الله ما لكم من إله غيره قد جاءتكم بينة من ربكم فأوفوا الكيل والميزان ولا تبخسوا الناس أشياءهم ولا تفسدوا في الأرض بعد إصلاحها ذلكم خير لكم إن كنتم مؤمنين

translation: And do not stay (i.e., loiter) in every road threatening and averting from the way of Allah those who believe in Him and seeking to make it crooked. And remember when you were few and He increased you. And see how was the end of the corrupters.
interpretation: The verse warns against obstructing or hindering those who believe in Allah and seek to follow His way, and against attempting to distort or corrupt the path of righteousness. The verse reminds the believers of their humble beginnings, when they were few in number, and how Allah increased their numbers and gave them strength. The verse concludes by urging the believers to reflect on the fate of those who spread corruption and mischief, serving as a warning against following in their footsteps.
orig: ولا تقعدوا بكل صراط توعدون وتصدون عن سبيل الله من آمن به وتبغونها عوجا واذكروا إذ كنتم قليلا فكثركم وانظروا كيف كان عاقبة المفسدين

translation: And if a party of you believe in that with which I have been sent and a party do not believe, then be patient until Allah judges between us, and He is the best of judges.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the division among people regarding the message brought by the Prophet Muhammad. Some people believe in it, while others do not. The verse advises the believers to be patient and wait for God's judgment, as He is the best of all judges. This verse highlights the importance of patience and trust in God's justice, and it encourages the believers to remain steadfast in their faith and not to be swayed by the disbelief of others.
orig: وإن كان طائفة منكم آمنوا بالذي أرسلت به وطائفة لم يؤمنوا فاصبروا حتى يحكم الله بيننا وهو خير الحاكمين

translation: Said the elite among his people to Joseph: 'Expel your companion and his followers from our city, or else you yourselves will be expelled from our religion.' Said Joseph: 'Even if we were unwilling,'
interpretation: The verse describes a confrontation between Joseph and the elite members of his community, who demand that he and his followers leave their city. Joseph's response shows his unwillingness to comply and highlights the coercive nature of the elite's demand. The verse emphasizes the exclusivity of the elite's religion and their desire to maintain their power and control. The verse can be interpreted as a warning against the dangers of religious extremism and intolerance, and the importance of respecting the rights and beliefs of others.
orig: قال الملأ الذين استكبروا من قومه لنخرجنك يا شعيب والذين آمنوا معك من قريتنا أو لتعودن في ملتنا قال أولو كنا كارهين

translation: We have indeed fabricated against Allah a grave falsehood, if we ever return to your religion after Allah has saved us from it. And it is not for us to return to it except that Allah, our Lord, should will. Our Lord's knowledge encompasses all things. Upon Allah we have relied. Our Lord, decide between us and our people in truth, and You are the best of those who decide.
interpretation: The verse is a statement of remorse and submission from a group of people who had previously rejected the truth. They acknowledge that they had lied about Allah and admit their wrongdoing. They express their inability to return to their previous ways without Allah's will. They place their trust in Allah and seek His guidance in resolving their disputes with their people. The verse emphasizes the power and knowledge of Allah, and the reliance of the believers on Him. It serves as a reminder of the importance of seeking truth and justice, and the ultimate control of Allah over all things.
orig: قد افترينا على الله كذبا إن عدنا في ملتكم بعد إذ نجانا الله منها وما يكون لنا أن نعود فيها إلا أن يشاء الله ربنا وسع ربنا كل شيء علما على الله توكلنا ربنا افتح بيننا وبين قومنا بالحق وأنت خير الفاتحين

translation: And the leaders of his people, who disbelieved, said, 'If you follow Shu'ayb, indeed, you will be losers.'
interpretation: The verse describes the disbelievers among the people of the Prophet Shu'ayb rejecting his message and warning the believers that they will be losers if they follow him. The verse highlights the opposition and rejection faced by the prophets and their followers, as well as the false sense of security and arrogance of the disbelievers who refuse to accept the truth. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of staying steadfast on the path of righteousness and not being swayed by the negative influence of those who reject the message of God.
orig: وقال الملأ الذين كفروا من قومه لئن اتبعتم شعيبا إنكم إذا لخاسرون

translation: And the striking seizure took them in the morning, and they were found lifeless in their homes.
interpretation: The verse describes a sudden and unexpected event, referred to as 'the striking seizure', that overtook a group of people in the morning. As a result of this event, they were found dead in their homes. The verse highlights the suddenness and unexpectedness of this event, leaving no time for the people to escape or prepare. It serves as a reminder of the fragility of life and the importance of being prepared for the unexpected, including the possibility of divine judgment.
orig: فأخذتهم الرجفة فأصبحوا في دارهم جاثمين

translation: Those who denied Shu'ayb (as a prophet) were as if they had never dwelt therein (in the town). Those who denied Shu'ayb (as a prophet) were certainly the losers.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the people who denied the prophet Shu'ayb and as a result, they were destroyed and it was as if they had never lived in that town. The verse emphasizes the negative consequences of denying a prophet and the severe punishment that comes with it. The phrase 'Those who denied Shu'ayb (as a prophet) were certainly the losers' serves as a warning to those who reject the message of the prophets and emphasizes the negative outcome of such denial.
orig: الذين كذبوا شعيبا كأن لم يغنوا فيها الذين كذبوا شعيبا كانوا هم الخاسرين

translation: And he took a distance from them and said, 'O my people, indeed I have conveyed to you the messages of my Lord and advised you, so how is it that I should feel regret for a disbelieving people?'
interpretation: The verse speaks about a prophet who has fulfilled his duty of conveying the message of God to his people and advising them. Despite his efforts, the people have not accepted the message and have remained disbelievers. The prophet expresses his detachment from their disbelief, stating that he has no reason to feel regret or sorrow for a people that has rejected the truth. The verse highlights the responsibility of the prophet to convey the message and the futility of trying to change the hearts of those who refuse to believe.
orig: فتولى عنهم وقال يا قوم لقد أبلغتكم رسالات ربي ونصحت لكم فكيف آسى على قوم كافرين

translation: And We did not send any prophet to a town except that We seized its people by misfortune and hardship, perhaps they would humble themselves.
interpretation: The verse describes the experience of the people of every town to which a prophet was sent. They were afflicted with misfortune and hardship, in order to bring them to their knees and humble themselves. This verse highlights the severity of the consequences of rejecting the message of the prophets and continuing in disbelief. It also emphasizes the importance of humility and submission to God's will.
orig: وما أرسلنا في قرية من نبي إلا أخذنا أهلها بالبأساء والضراء لعلهم يضرعون

translation: Then We substituted badness for goodness until they were utterly destitute and said, 'Evil has afflicted our forefathers,' so We seized them suddenly while they were unaware.
interpretation: The verse describes a situation where God replaced goodness with badness, leading to the downfall of a people. Despite their awareness of the suffering of their ancestors, they failed to recognize the significance of their own actions. As a result, God seized them suddenly and unexpectedly, emphasizing the importance of recognizing and learning from past mistakes, and the consequences of neglecting this responsibility.
orig: ثم بدلنا مكان السيئة الحسنة حتى عفوا وقالوا قد مس آباءنا الضراء والسراء فأخذناهم بغتة وهم لا يشعرون

translation: And if the people of the towns had believed and been righteous, We would have opened upon them blessings from the heaven and the earth; but they denied, so We took them for what they were earning.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the missed opportunity for the people of the towns to receive blessings from God due to their disbelief and lack of righteousness. The verse highlights the conditional nature of God's blessings, which were dependent on the people's belief and righteousness. The people's denial of God's signs resulted in them receiving the consequences of their actions. The verse serves as a reminder that God's blessings are conditional on people's faith and actions, and that disbelief and sin can result in the loss of these blessings.
orig: ولو أن أهل القرى آمنوا واتقوا لفتحنا عليهم بركات من السماء والأرض ولكن كذبوا فأخذناهم بما كانوا يكسبون

translation: Do the people of the towns then feel secure from Our punishment coming to them in the middle of the day or the middle of the night?
interpretation: The verse questions the sense of security felt by the people of the towns, challenging their assumption that they are safe from God's punishment. The phrase 'in the middle of the day or the middle of the night' emphasizes the suddenness and unexpectedness of the punishment, which can strike at any time. The verse serves as a reminder that no one is immune from God's judgment and that people should always be mindful of their actions and their relationship with God.
orig: أفأمن أهل القرى أن يأتيهم بأسنا بياتا وهم نائمون

translation: Or have the people of the towns believed that Our punishment will not come to them at night while they are asleep?
interpretation: The verse questions the belief of the people of the towns who think that they are safe from God's punishment at night while they are asleep. The verse emphasizes the power and control of God, who can strike at any time, whether during the day or at night, and no one can escape or prevent it. The verse serves as a reminder to the people to be mindful of their actions and to always be prepared for the arrival of God's punishment, as it can come unexpectedly and swiftly.
orig: أوأمن أهل القرى أن يأتيهم بأسنا ضحى وهم يلعبون

translation: Then do they feel secure from the plan of Allah? No one feels secure from the plan of Allah except the losing people.
interpretation: The verse highlights the futility of feeling secure from Allah's plan, emphasizing that no one can truly be safe from it. The verse serves as a reminder that those who do not fear and respect Allah's power and plan are the ones who are truly losing. The verse encourages believers to be mindful of Allah's plan and to avoid being among the losing people by following Allah's commands and seeking His mercy and forgiveness.
orig: أفأمنوا مكر الله فلا يأمن مكر الله إلا القوم الخاسرون

translation: Has not there guided those who inherited the earth after its (previous) people, that if We willed, We could punish them for their sins and seal up their hearts so they would not hear?
interpretation: The verse speaks about the guidance that was given to those who inherited the earth after its previous inhabitants. It highlights the power of God to punish people for their sins and to seal up their hearts so that they become unable to hear or heed the guidance. The verse serves as a warning to those who are heedless of their actions and their consequences, emphasizing the power of God and the importance of paying attention to the guidance that has been given to them.
orig: أولم يهد للذين يرثون الأرض من بعد أهلها أن لو نشاء أصبناهم بذنوبهم ونطبع على قلوبهم فهم لا يسمعون

translation: Those towns!—We relate to you some of their stories—surely messengers came to them with clear signs, but they would not believe in what they had previously denied.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the story of towns that rejected the messengers and the signs that were sent to them. Despite the clear evidence, the people of these towns refused to believe. The verse highlights the hard-heartedness of the unbelievers and their rejection of the truth, even when it is presented to them in a clear manner. The verse serves as a reminder that God will ultimately seal the hearts of those who persist in denying the truth, and that their disbelief will not benefit them in the end.
orig: تلك القرى نقص عليك من أنبائها ولقد جاءتهم رسلهم بالبينات فما كانوا ليؤمنوا بما كذبوا من قبل كذلك يطبع الله على قلوب الكافرين

translation: And We did not find most of them committed to their covenant, but indeed, We found most of them to be transgressors.
interpretation: The verse highlights the lack of commitment among people to uphold their covenants and obligations. It emphasizes that most people do not fulfill their promises, and instead, they are found to be transgressors or wrongdoers. This verse serves as a reminder to people to honor their commitments and to avoid transgression, as failure to do so has consequences. It also implies that those who fail to keep their promises and commit to their obligations will face the consequences of their actions.
orig: وما وجدنا لأكثرهم من عهد وإن وجدنا أكثرهم لفاسقين

translation: Then We sent after them Moses with Our signs to Pharaoh and his council, but they wronged themselves therewith. So see how was the end of the corrupters.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the sending of Moses to Pharaoh and his council with the signs of God, as a continuation of the previous verse in Surah Al-Momtahanah. Despite the signs, the people of Pharaoh wronged themselves and persisted in their corruption. The verse ends by urging the reader to reflect on the consequences of the actions of the corruptors, inviting them to consider the fate of those who reject the message of God and persist in their wrongdoing.
orig: ثم بعثنا من بعدهم موسى بآياتنا إلى فرعون وملئه فظلموا بها فانظر كيف كان عاقبة المفسدين

translation: And Moses said, 'O Pharaoh, indeed I am a messenger from the Lord of the worlds.'
interpretation: The verse relays a message from Moses to Pharaoh, in which Moses identifies himself as a messenger from the Lord of the Universes. This statement asserts Moses's authority and mission from God, and sets the stage for the ongoing conflict between Moses and Pharaoh in the Qur'an. The verse emphasizes the idea that Moses's message and authority come directly from the one and only God, and that Pharaoh should therefore listen and submit to his commands.
orig: وقال موسى يا فرعون إني رسول من رب العالمين

translation: I truly say about Allah that I do not say except the truth. Indeed, I have brought you a clear sign from your Lord, so I have sent with me the children of Israel.
interpretation: The speaker in this verse asserts their honesty and truthfulness in their message from God. They bring a clear sign from the Lord as proof of their claim. Additionally, the speaker reveals that they are accompanied by the children of Israel, which may signify the importance and legitimacy of their message.
orig: حقيق على أن لا أقول على الله إلا الحق قد جئتكم ببينة من ربكم فأرسل معي بني إسرائيل

translation: He said, 'If you have come with a sign, then bring it, if you are one of the truthful.'
interpretation: The verse is a challenge from a disbeliever to the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) to bring a sign or proof of his prophethood. The disbeliever doubts the authenticity of the Prophet's message and asks for a miraculous sign as a form of proof. The verse highlights the skepticism and rejection of the Prophet's message by some of the disbelievers, and the Prophet's response to their demands with patience and perseverance.
orig: قال إن كنت جئت بآية فأت بها إن كنت من الصادقين

translation: And [Moses] cast down his staff, and behold, it was a serpent manifest.
interpretation: The verse describes the moment when Moses, at God's command, throws down his staff, which then transforms into a serpent. This transformation serves as a miraculous sign from God, confirming Moses' prophethood and his authority. This event is a significant moment in the story of Moses, as it marks the beginning of his mission as a prophet and his role in leading the Israelites out of Egypt.
orig: فألقى عصاه فإذا هي ثعبان مبين

translation: And (when) his hand is lifted up, behold, it is white (with fear) for the onlookers.
interpretation: The verse describes the physical manifestation of fear in a person when they are faced with a terrifying situation. When the person lifts up their hand, it is described as being white with fear, indicating the extreme level of terror and dread they are experiencing. The verse may be interpreted as a warning to those who are heedless of the consequences of their actions, and a reminder that fear and punishment can come suddenly and unexpectedly.
orig: ونزع يده فإذا هي بيضاء للناظرين

translation: The nobles of Pharaoh's people said: 'He is certainly a knowledgeable sorcerer!'
interpretation: The verse describes the reaction of Pharaoh's nobles when they witnessed the miracles performed by Moses. Instead of recognizing the truth and submitting to God, they dismissed the miracles as the work of a knowledgeable sorcerer. This interpretation highlights the stubbornness and denial of Pharaoh and his people, who refused to believe in Moses and the message he brought from God. The verse serves as a reminder of the dangers of arrogance, pride, and the rejection of God's signs.
orig: قال الملأ من قوم فرعون إن هذا لساحر عليم

translation: He intends to drive you out of your land, then what is your opinion?
interpretation: The verse is a rhetorical question addressed to the disbelievers who were opposing the Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) and planning to drive him and his followers out of their land. The verse challenges them to consider the consequences of their actions and to reflect on the fact that they will ultimately be powerless against God's will. The verse serves as a reminder that no one can escape God's plan and that those who oppose God and His messenger will face severe consequences.
orig: يريد أن يخرجكم من أرضكم فماذا تأمرون

translation: They said, 'Swear fealty to him and to his brother' and 'Send forth emissaries to the cities'
interpretation: The verse speaks about a command given to people to pledge allegiance to a certain individual and his brother, and to send emissaries to various cities. The verse emphasizes the importance of unity and cooperation in spreading the message of the individual being referred to. The verse may be referring to a specific historical event or it may be a general command for all believers. The verse highlights the significance of sending messengers to different cities as a means of propagating the message and gaining support for the cause. The verse may also be interpreted as a call for the establishment of a just and righteous society through the unification of people and the spread of the message.
orig: قالوا أرجه وأخاه وأرسل في المدائن حاشرين

translation: They will come to you with every sorcerer [who is] skilled.
interpretation: The verse speaks about people bringing sorcerers who are skilled in their craft. The verse may be referring to the disbelievers who brought sorcerers to challenge the prophet Muhammad (PBUH) and his followers. The verse serves as a warning to the prophet (PBUH) and his followers that they will face challenges and opposition in their mission to spread the message of Islam. It also emphasizes the deception and falsehood of sorcery, which is contrasted with the truth of Islam.
orig: يأتوك بكل ساحر عليم

translation: Then the sorcerers came to Pharaoh and said, 'Indeed, for us is a reward if we are the predominant.'
interpretation: The verse describes the moment when the sorcerers came to Pharaoh and claimed that they would be rewarded if they were to prevail in their magic contest against Moses. The verse highlights the arrogance and pride of the sorcerers, who were more concerned about their own victory and reward than the truth and the well-being of the people. The verse serves as a reminder of the dangers of arrogance and selfishness, and the importance of humility and submission to God's will.
orig: وجاء السحرة فرعون قالوا إن لنا لأجرا إن كنا نحن الغالبين

translation: He said, 'Yes, you are indeed of the nearest (to me).'
interpretation: The verse is a conversation between a prophet and God, where God confirms that the prophet is among those who are closest to Him. The verse emphasizes the special relationship between the prophet and God, highlighting the prophet's righteousness and devotion. The verse serves as a reminder of the rewards for those who are close to God, through their obedience and submission to His will.
orig: قال نعم وإنكم لمن المقربين

translation: They said, 'O Moses, either you throw [the staff] or we will be the ones to throw [it].'
interpretation: The verse shows a moment of confrontation between Moses and his opponents, who challenge him to throw his staff. The verse highlights the tension and the power struggle between Moses and his opponents, who refuse to believe in him and his message. The verse also emphasizes the opposing sides' determination and readiness for a confrontation, as they insist on either throwing the staff themselves or seeing Moses do it. The verse serves as a prelude to the miraculous events that follow, in which Moses' staff turns into a serpent, demonstrating his divine power and authority.
orig: قالوا يا موسى إما أن تلقي وإما أن نكون نحن الملقين

translation: And [Pharaoh] said, 'Cast him into the chest' - and when they had cast him, they cast him into the sea, and the sea engulfed him. And as he was going along, a bird picked him up and brought him to the shore, and a certain woman of Pharaoh's family nursed him.'
interpretation: This verse is a continuation of the story of Moses, who was cast into the sea as a baby by Pharaoh's order. However, the sea miraculously engulfed him and protected him. Then, a bird picked him up and brought him to the shore, where a woman from Pharaoh's family found him and took him in. This verse highlights the theme of divine intervention and protection of the prophets, even in the face of seemingly insurmountable odds. It also emphasizes the role of human kindness and compassion in the preservation of life.
orig: قال ألقوا فلما ألقوا سحروا أعين الناس واسترهبوهم وجاءوا بسحر عظيم

translation: And We inspired Moses, saying: 'Cast your staff.' And behold! It swallowed what they were falsely contriving.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the story of Moses and his staff, which was used as a miracle from God to demonstrate his power and truth. When Moses was commanded by God to cast his staff, it turned into a snake and swallowed the 'tricks' or 'illusions' of the sorcerers who opposed Moses. The verse emphasizes the power of God and the weakness of those who rely on falsehood and deception. It serves as a reminder that the truth will always prevail over falsehood and that those who persist in their disbelief and opposition to God's messengers will ultimately be defeated.
orig: وأوحينا إلى موسى أن ألق عصاك فإذا هي تلقف ما يأفكون

translation: So the truth has come to pass and what they were doing has vanished.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the fulfillment of truth and the disappearance of falsehood. It emphasizes the transient nature of falsehood and the enduring quality of truth. The verse suggests that the previous actions or beliefs of people, which were based on falsehood, have been proven wrong and have disappeared in the face of truth. The verse serves as a reminder that truth will always prevail over falsehood and encourages people to seek and follow the truth.
orig: فوقع الحق وبطل ما كانوا يعملون

translation: They prevailed therein, and the (unbelieving) people of the city were indeed wrongdoers.
interpretation: The verse speaks about a group of people who were able to gain power and control over another group, referred to as 'the people of the city'. However, the verse makes it clear that the people who gained power were not on the side of righteousness, but rather, they were the wrongdoers. The verse can be seen as a warning against the pursuit of power and control through unjust means, emphasizing that such actions will not go unpunished.
orig: فغلبوا هنالك وانقلبوا صاغرين

translation: And the sorcerers were cast down prostrate.
interpretation: The verse describes the fate of the sorcerers who opposed the Prophet Muhammad and his message. When they were defeated in their attempt to disprove the Prophet, they were left humiliated and powerless, symbolized by being cast down prostrate. This verse serves as a reminder that those who oppose the truth and insist on their falsehood will ultimately be defeated and humiliated, and it is a call for the believers to remain steadfast and firm in their faith.
orig: وألقي السحرة ساجدين

translation: They said, 'We have believed in the Lord of the worlds.'
interpretation: The verse is a statement of faith and belief in Allah, the Lord of the worlds. It emphasizes the universality of Allah's power and control over all of creation. The statement of faith is a declaration of belief in Allah and His oneness, and a rejection of all false gods and idols. This verse can serve as a reminder of the importance of faith and belief in Allah, and the need to submit to His will and guidance in all aspects of life.
orig: قالوا آمنا برب العالمين

translation: Lord of Moses and Aaron
interpretation: The phrase 'Lord of Moses and Aaron' is a form of address or invocation, used to refer to God in the Qur'an. It emphasizes the special relationship between God and the two prophets, Moses and Aaron, and underscores their status as chosen messengers of God. The phrase can also be understood more broadly as an affirmation of God's sovereignty and power over all of creation, including the prophets and other human beings.
orig: رب موسى وهارون

translation: Pharaoh said, 'Have you believed in Him before I gave you permission? This is indeed a plot you have plotted in the city to expel its people. But soon you will come to know.'
interpretation: Pharaoh, the ruler of Egypt, is expressing his disbelief and anger towards the people who have believed in God without his permission. He accuses them of plotting against the city and its people, and he warns them of the consequences of their actions. The verse highlights Pharaoh's tyranny and oppression, as well as his belief in his own power and authority. It also shows the courage and determination of those who have chosen to believe in God despite the risks and dangers they face.
orig: قال فرعون آمنتم به قبل أن آذن لكم إن هذا لمكر مكرتموه في المدينة لتخرجوا منها أهلها فسوف تعلمون

translation: I will cut off your hands and your feet alternately, and I will crucify you all.
interpretation: The verse describes a severe punishment that will be inflicted upon a group of people. The punishment includes cutting off their hands and feet alternately and then crucifying them all. This verse is often understood as a metaphor for the severe consequences of committing serious sins or crimes. It serves as a warning to those who engage in unlawful activities, emphasizing the certainty of punishment for their actions.
orig: لأقطعن أيديكم وأرجلكم من خلاف ثم لأصلبنكم أجمعين

translation: They said, 'Indeed, we are to our Lord returning.'
interpretation: The verse is a statement made by the people in response to a situation of hardship or calamity. They express their belief that they will return to their Lord, acknowledging God's power and control over their lives. The verse can be seen as an expression of faith and submission to God's will, as well as a reminder of the ultimate destiny of all human beings, which is to return to their Creator. The verse also emphasizes the importance of maintaining a strong and unwavering faith in God, even in the face of adversity and challenges.
orig: قالوا إنا إلى ربنا منقلبون

translation: And We punish none but those who deserve it, and when Our command is issued, We cannot delay it, if We so desired.
interpretation: The verse explains that punishment is only given to those who deserve it, and that once God's command for punishment is issued, it cannot be delayed. This emphasizes the power and authority of God and the inevitability of His commands. The verse also highlights the importance of faith in God's signs and the importance of patience in the face of adversity. The verse serves as a reminder that God's justice will ultimately be served, and that those who are patient and believe in God's signs will be rewarded.
orig: وما تنقم منا إلا أن آمنا بآيات ربنا لما جاءتنا ربنا أفرغ علينا صبرا وتوفنا مسلمين

translation: And the leaders of Pharaoh's people said: 'Will you leave Moses and his people to cause corruption in the land and to abandon you and your gods?' He said: 'We will kill their sons and let their women live, and we have the upper hand over them.'
interpretation: The verse describes the leaders of Pharaoh's people expressing their concern about Moses and his people, accusing them of causing corruption in the land and abandoning Pharaoh and his gods. Pharaoh responds by threatening to kill the sons of Moses's people and keep their women alive, asserting his dominance over them. The verse highlights the oppressive and unjust nature of Pharaoh and his people, and sets the stage for the conflict between them and Moses and his followers.
orig: وقال الملأ من قوم فرعون أتذر موسى وقومه ليفسدوا في الأرض ويذرك وآلهتك قال سنقتل أبناءهم ونستحيي نساءهم وإنا فوقهم قاهرون

translation: Moses said to his people, 'Seek help through God and be patient. Indeed, the earth belongs to God; He gives it as inheritance to whom He wills of His servants. And indeed, the (good) end is for the righteous.'
interpretation: In this verse, Moses advises his people to seek help from God and be patient in the face of adversity. He reminds them that the earth ultimately belongs to God and that He will give it as an inheritance to whom He wills from His servants. The verse concludes by emphasizing that the ultimate outcome is favorable for the righteous, implying that those who are patient and trust in God's plan will be rewarded in the end.
orig: قال موسى لقومه استعينوا بالله واصبروا إن الأرض لله يورثها من يشاء من عباده والعاقبة للمتقين

translation: They say: 'Has there not been a while since punishment came to us before you came to us?' He said: 'Perhaps your Lord will destroy your enemy and make you successors on the earth, so He may see how you behave.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the people's response to a prophet who has come to warn them of God's punishment. The people question why the punishment has not come yet, and the prophet responds by saying that God may destroy their enemies and make the believers successors on the earth, so He can observe their actions and see how they behave. The verse highlights the idea that God is all-knowing and all-seeing, and that He will test and observe His servants. It also emphasizes the importance of righteous behavior and the consequences of ignoring the warnings of God's messengers.
orig: قالوا أوذينا من قبل أن تأتينا ومن بعد ما جئتنا قال عسى ربكم أن يهلك عدوكم ويستخلفكم في الأرض فينظر كيف تعملون

translation: And We took the family of Pharaoh (with years of drought) and lessened the produce of the land for them, so that they might take heed.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the punishment of the family of Pharaoh through years of drought and a decrease in the produce of the land, as a means for them to reflect and learn a lesson. The verse highlights the patience and determination of God in guiding people towards the right path, and the consequences of ignoring the signs and continuing to commit injustice. The verse also serves as a reminder for the importance of taking heed of the signs and lessons presented in life, and the need to reflect and change one's ways before it is too late.
orig: ولقد أخذنا آل فرعون بالسنين ونقص من الثمرات لعلهم يذكرون

translation: And when good comes to them, they say, 'This is ours.' But if a trial befalls them, they immediately turn their backs in distress. And (because of this), they have no faith.
interpretation: The verse describes the behavior of people who are ungrateful and unfaithful. When they receive blessings and good things in life, they quickly claim ownership and take credit for it. However, when they face difficulties and trials, they immediately lose hope and become desperate. They reject faith and are unable to see the wisdom behind their struggles. The verse serves as a reminder to be grateful for the blessings we receive and to remain steadfast and patient during hardships, trusting in God's divine plan.
orig: فإذا جاءتهم الحسنة قالوا لنا هذه وإن تصبهم سيئة يطيروا بموسى ومن معه ألا إنما طائرهم عند الله ولكن أكثرهم لا يعلمون

translation: And they say, 'Whatever sign you bring us to cast a spell upon us with it, we will not believe in you.'
interpretation: The verse describes the disbelievers' rejection of the prophet's message and their refusal to believe, no matter what signs or evidence are presented to them. The phrase 'to cast a spell upon us' implies that the disbelievers view the prophet's message as a form of magic or deception. The verse highlights the closed-mindedness and stubbornness of those who reject the truth, and the challenge they pose to the prophet's mission. It also serves as a reminder that faith cannot be forced and requires open-mindedness and receptivity to the divine message.
orig: وقالوا مهما تأتنا به من آية لتسحرنا بها فما نحن لك بمؤمنين

translation: And We sent upon them the flood and the locusts, the lice, and the frogs, and the blood, distinct signs, but they were haughty and were a people sinful.
interpretation: The verse describes the punishment of a people who were unjust and haughty. They were sent various signs and afflictions, including floods, locusts, lice, frogs, and blood, as a form of divine retribution. Despite these clear and distinct signs, they remained arrogant and continued to commit sins. The verse serves as a reminder of the consequences of arrogance and sin, and the certainty of divine retribution for those who do not heed the signs and warnings of their wrongdoing.
orig: فأرسلنا عليهم الطوفان والجراد والقمل والضفادع والدم آيات مفصلات فاستكبروا وكانوا قوما مجرمين

translation: And when the punishment descended upon them, they said, 'O Moses, invoke your Lord for us according to what He has promised you. If You remove the punishment from us, we will surely believe in you, and we will send with you the Children of Israel.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the people of Moses (peace be upon him) who, when faced with a punishment, hastily turned to Moses for help and made a promise to believe in him and aid him if he could remove the punishment. This verse highlights the tendency of people to turn to God and His messengers in times of hardship and distress, even if they have previously been disbelievers or disobedient. It also serves as a reminder of the importance of having a strong and unwavering faith in God, and not just seeking His help in times of need. The verse emphasizes the need for consistent and steadfast belief and obedience, rather than making hasty promises in times of desperation.
orig: ولما وقع عليهم الرجز قالوا يا موسى ادع لنا ربك بما عهد عندك لئن كشفت عنا الرجز لنؤمنن لك ولنرسلن معك بني إسرائيل

translation: And when We removed from them the punishment for a while, they were sure to commit transgressions.
interpretation: The verse describes the situation after God had removed a punishment from a group of people. Despite having been given a reprieve, the people continued to commit transgressions and violations. The verse highlights the persistent disobedience of the people and their lack of gratitude for being given a second chance. It serves as a reminder that God's punishment is not arbitrary, but rather a response to the actions of human beings, and that continued disobedience will ultimately lead to negative consequences.
orig: فلما كشفنا عنهم الرجز إلى أجل هم بالغوه إذا هم ينكثون

translation: So We took revenge on them, and We drowned them in the sea because they disbelieved in Our signs and were heedless of them.
interpretation: The verse describes the punishment of a people who disbelieved in the signs of God and were heedless of them. As a consequence, they were punished by being drowned in the sea. This verse serves as a reminder of the importance of believing in and paying heed to the signs of God, and the severe consequences of disbelief and heedlessness.
orig: فانتقمنا منهم فأغرقناهم في اليم بأنهم كذبوا بآياتنا وكانوا عنها غافلين

translation: And We inherited the towns which the people who were oppressed had inhabited in the eastern and western regions of the earth, whom We had blessed. And your Lord's good word was fulfilled for the Children of Israel, because of their patience. And We destroyed whatever Pharaoh and his people were making and whatever they were building.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the blessings of God on the Children of Israel and the destruction of Pharaoh and his people. It highlights the fulfillment of God's promise to the Children of Israel and their patience in the face of oppression. The verse also emphasizes the destruction of the works and constructions of Pharaoh and his people, indicating the futility of their efforts and the ultimate power of God. The verse serves as a reminder of the blessings and protection that God provides to those who are oppressed and the consequences of oppression and arrogance.
orig: وأورثنا القوم الذين كانوا يستضعفون مشارق الأرض ومغاربها التي باركنا فيها وتمت كلمت ربك الحسنى على بني إسرائيل بما صبروا ودمرنا ما كان يصنع فرعون وقومه وما كانوا يعرشون

translation: And We passed by the Children of Israel in the sea, and they came to a people who were worshipping idols. They said, 'O Moses, make for us a god as they have gods.' He said, 'Indeed, you are a people behaving ignorantly.'
interpretation: The verse describes the Israelites' encounter with a group of idol-worshippers during their journey out of Egypt. The idol-worshippers' behavior is described as ignorant, and the Israelites are warned against following their ways. The verse highlights the distinction between the worship of the one true God and the false worship of idols. It also emphasizes the importance of maintaining a strong faith and avoiding the influence of those who do not share that faith.
orig: وجاوزنا ببني إسرائيل البحر فأتوا على قوم يعكفون على أصنام لهم قالوا يا موسى اجعل لنا إلها كما لهم آلهة قال إنكم قوم تجهلون

translation: Indeed, they were neglectful of what they were doing, and what they were doing was in vain.
interpretation: The verse highlights the futility and meaninglessness of the actions of certain people who were neglectful and careless in their deeds. The verse suggests that these people were not fully aware or mindful of the significance of their actions, and therefore, their efforts were in vain. The verse serves as a reminder to be mindful of one's actions and to strive for purpose and meaning in life.
orig: إن هؤلاء متبر ما هم فيه وباطل ما كانوا يعملون

translation: He said, 'Do you want a lord other than Allah, while He is the one who has favored you over the worlds?'
interpretation: The verse is a statement made by an unnamed person, who is expressing shock and disbelief at the idea of choosing a lord other than Allah. The person emphasizes that Allah has already favored the audience over all other creations, implying that they should be grateful and loyal to Him.
