The verse can be interpreted as a reminder of the importance of gratitude and loyalty towards Allah, and a warning against the dangers of shirk (associating partners with Allah). It emphasizes the unique and exalted status of Allah, and the unworthiness of any other deity to be worshipped.
orig: قال أغير الله أبغيكم إلها وهو فضلكم على العالمين

translation: And when We delivered you from the house of Pharaoh, they were inflicting evil on you, killing your sons and sparing your women, and in that was a great trial from your Lord.
interpretation: The verse recounts the story of Moses and the Israelites being delivered from the oppression of Pharaoh and his people. The verse highlights the cruelty of Pharaoh's regime, who not only inflicted harm on the Israelites but also killed their sons and allowed their women to live. This was a part of a great trial from the Lord, testing the faith and resilience of the Israelites. The verse serves as a reminder of the blessings of freedom and the hardships faced by the Israelites, emphasizing the importance of gratitude and perseverance in the face of adversity.
orig: وإذ أنجيناكم من آل فرعون يسومونكم سوء العذاب يقتلون أبناءكم ويستحيون نساءكم وفي ذلكم بلاء من ربكم عظيم

translation: And We appointed with Moses a time of thirty nights, and completed them with (an additional) ten, so the term of his Lord was completed in forty nights. And Moses said to his brother Aaron: 'Take my place among my people, act righteously and do not follow the way of the corruptors.'
interpretation: This verse speaks about the appointment of Moses with a specific period of time, during which he was to receive divine revelation. The period was initially set for thirty nights, but was then extended by an additional ten nights, making a total of forty nights. During this time, Moses was to be absent from his people, and so he appointed his brother Aaron as his successor, instructing him to act righteously and not to follow the way of the corruptors. The verse emphasizes the importance of leadership and the responsibility that comes with it, as well as the need for righteousness and integrity in the face of corruption and wrongdoing.
orig: وواعدنا موسى ثلاثين ليلة وأتممناها بعشر فتم ميقات ربه أربعين ليلة وقال موسى لأخيه هارون اخلفني في قومي وأصلح ولا تتبع سبيل المفسدين

translation: And when Moses came to Our appointed time and his Lord spoke to him, he said, 'My Lord, show me that I may look at You.' (Allah) said, 'You will not see Me, but look at the mountain; if it should remain in its place, then you will see Me.' So when his Lord manifested Himself to the mountain, He made it crumble, and Moses fell down unconscious. And when he awoke, he said, 'Exalted are You! I have repented to You, and I am the first of the believers.'
interpretation: The verse describes the encounter between Moses and God, where Moses requests to see God. However, God declines the request and tells Moses to look at the mountain, promising that if the mountain remains in its place, Moses will see Him. When God manifests Himself to the mountain, it crumbles, and Moses faints from the overwhelming experience. Upon regaining consciousness, Moses praises God and expresses his repentance, acknowledging his faith and becoming the first of the believers. The verse emphasizes the greatness and majesty of God, and the limitations of human perception in comprehending His divine nature. It also highlights the importance of humility and submission before God, as demonstrated by Moses' repentance and recognition of his faith.
orig: ولما جاء موسى لميقاتنا وكلمه ربه قال رب أرني أنظر إليك قال لن تراني ولكن انظر إلى الجبل فإن استقر مكانه فسوف تراني فلما تجلى ربه للجبل جعله دكا وخر موسى صعقا فلما أفاق قال سبحانك تبت إليك وأنا أول المؤمنين

translation: He said, 'O Moses, I have chosen you above the people with My messages and My words, so take what I have given you and be of the thankful.'
interpretation: The verse is a communication from God to Moses, in which God informs Moses that He has chosen him above the people through His messages and words. God commands Moses to take what has been given to him (the revelation) and to be thankful for this great honor. The verse highlights the special status of Moses and the responsibility that comes with it, and emphasizes the importance of gratitude and appreciation for the blessings and responsibilities bestowed upon one.
orig: قال يا موسى إني اصطفيتك على الناس برسالاتي وبكلامي فخذ ما آتيتك وكن من الشاكرين

translation: And We had written for him on the tablets concerning every thing an admonition and a detailed explanation of all things; then take it (with strength) and charge your people to take the better (thereof); I will show you the home of the sinners.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the revelation of divine knowledge and guidance to a prophet, through the writing of admonitions and detailed explanations on tablets. The prophet is instructed to take the guidance with strength and to urge his people to choose the best from it. The verse then mentions that the prophet will be shown the destination of the sinners, indicating the consequences of ignoring the guidance and choosing a path of sin and transgression. The verse highlights the importance of adhering to divine guidance and the consequences of deviating from it.
orig: وكتبنا له في الألواح من كل شيء موعظة وتفصيلا لكل شيء فخذها بقوة وأمر قومك يأخذوا بأحسنها سأريكم دار الفاسقين

translation: I will divert from My signs those who are arrogant on the earth without right, even if they see every sign, they do not believe in it. And if they see the way of right guidance, they do not take it as a way, but if they see the way of error, they take it as a way. That is because they have denied My signs and have been heedless of them.
interpretation: The verse speaks about God's decision to turn away from those who are arrogant and unjust on earth, despite the evidence of God's signs being presented to them. The verse highlights the fact that even when the signs are shown to them, they refuse to believe. Furthermore, when the right path is presented to them, they do not choose it. Instead, they prefer the path of error and wrongdoing. This is because they have rejected God's signs and have been heedless of them. The verse serves as a warning to those who are arrogant and unjust, emphasizing the consequences of their actions and the importance of recognizing and following God's signs.
orig: سأصرف عن آياتي الذين يتكبرون في الأرض بغير الحق وإن يروا كل آية لا يؤمنوا بها وإن يروا سبيل الرشد لا يتخذوه سبيلا وإن يروا سبيل الغي يتخذوه سبيلا ذلك بأنهم كذبوا بآياتنا وكانوا عنها غافلين

translation: And those who have disbelieved in Our verses and the meeting of the Hereafter, their deeds have become worthless. Do they think that they can outstrip Us?
interpretation: The verse highlights the consequences of disbelief in the signs of God and the Day of Judgment. Those who reject God's messages and deny the existence of the afterlife will find that their deeds are in vain. The second part of the verse challenges the disbelievers, questioning whether they think they can escape God's judgment and outrun the consequences of their actions. The verse serves as a warning to those who reject the truth and emphasizes the futility of their efforts in avoiding the inevitable reckoning.
orig: والذين كذبوا بآياتنا ولقاء الآخرة حبطت أعمالهم هل يجزون إلا ما كانوا يعملون

translation: And the people of Moses, after him, took to themselves [for worship] the calf - a mere body; was it not that a calf consumes grass, so they did not reason? And he (Moses) left it (the calf) broken-hearted, but they were wrongdoers.
interpretation: The verse describes the actions of the people of Moses after he had left them, when they made a calf out of their jewelry and began to worship it. The verse criticizes their lack of reason and understanding, as they failed to realize that a calf is only an animal that eats grass and cannot guide or speak to them. The verse highlights the foolishness of their actions and their rejection of the guidance of Moses. The verse also mentions that Moses was deeply saddened by their behavior. Overall, the verse serves as a reminder of the importance of using reason and following the guidance of the prophets, rather than following one's own desires and whims.
orig: واتخذ قوم موسى من بعده من حليهم عجلا جسدا له خوار ألم يروا أنه لا يكلمهم ولا يهديهم سبيلا اتخذوه وكانوا ظالمين

translation: And when it fell in their hands, they realized that they had made a mistake. They said, 'If only our Lord had not shown us mercy and forgiven us, we would have been among the losers.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about a group of people who have experienced a calamity or a hardship (represented by 'it' in the verse), which they recognize as a consequence of their own mistakes (represented by 'they had made a mistake'). The people express their gratitude for God's mercy and forgiveness, recognizing that without it, they would have been among the 'losers' or the unsuccessful ones. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of recognizing one's mistakes, seeking forgiveness, and being grateful for God's mercy and compassion.
orig: ولما سقط في أيديهم ورأوا أنهم قد ضلوا قالوا لئن لم يرحمنا ربنا ويغفر لنا لنكونن من الخاسرين

translation: And when Moses returned to his people in anger and sadness, he said: 'How evil you have treated me since I left you! Were you hastening the command of your Lord?' And when he threw down the tablets and took hold of his brother by the head, dragging him towards him, he said: 'Son of my mother! Indeed, the people have made me very angry and nearly killed me. So do not align me with the wrongdoing people.'
interpretation: The verse describes the return of Moses to his people after receiving the tablets from God. However, instead of being welcomed with joy and respect, Moses is met with anger and rejection. In response, Moses expresses his disappointment and sadness, and throws down the tablets in frustration. The verse emphasizes the tension and conflict between Moses and his people, highlighting the difficulties and challenges that Moses faces in his mission. At the same time, the verse also highlights the humanity of Moses and his vulnerability, as he expresses his fear and anger towards his people. Ultimately, the verse serves as a reminder of the importance of faith and obedience to God, and the challenges and struggles that come with leading a righteous life.
orig: ولما رجع موسى إلى قومه غضبان أسفا قال بئسما خلفتموني من بعدي أعجلتم أمر ربكم وألقى الألواح وأخذ برأس أخيه يجره إليه قال ابن أم إن القوم استضعفوني وكادوا يقتلونني فلا تشمت بي الأعداء ولا تجعلني مع القوم الظالمين

translation: He said, 'My Lord, forgive me and my brother and admit us into Your mercy, and You are the Most Merciful of the merciful.'
interpretation: The verse is a prayer of a person asking for forgiveness for themselves and their brother and seeking admission into God's mercy. The verse highlights the individual's recognition of their own faults and the need for God's mercy and forgiveness. It also shows the person's concern for their sibling and their desire for both of them to be granted God's mercy. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of seeking forgiveness, showing compassion towards others, and striving for God's mercy.
orig: قال رب اغفر لي ولأخي وأدخلنا في رحمتك وأنت أرحم الراحمين

translation: Indeed, those who take the disbelievers as allies instead of the believers, and then seek to hide it, will not find from Allah a way out. And for them is a painful punishment.
interpretation: The verse warns against taking disbelievers as allies instead of believers, and then trying to conceal it. Such people will not find a way out from God's punishment. The verse emphasizes the seriousness of this action and the severe consequences that come with it. It serves as a reminder to remain loyal to one's faith and community and not to compromise it for worldly gains or relationships.
orig: إن الذين اتخذوا العجل سينالهم غضب من ربهم وذلة في الحياة الدنيا وكذلك نجزي المفترين

translation: And those who have done evil, then repented and believed, surely your Lord, after that, is Forgiving, Merciful.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the opportunity for forgiveness and mercy from God for those who have committed sins, then repented and believed. The verse emphasizes the boundless mercy and forgiveness of God, who, even after a person has done wrong, is willing to forgive and show compassion. The verse serves as a message of hope for those who have strayed from the right path, reminding them that it is never too late to turn back to God and seek His forgiveness.
orig: والذين عملوا السيئات ثم تابوا من بعدها وآمنوا إن ربك من بعدها لغفور رحيم

translation: And when the anger abated from Moses, he took up the tablets; in them was guidance and mercy for those who fear their Lord.
interpretation: The verse speaks about Moses receiving the tablets (presumably the Ten Commandments) after his anger had subsided. These tablets contained guidance and mercy for those who are mindful and fearful of their Lord. The verse highlights the importance of self-control and patience, as well as the blessings that come from following God's guidance and being merciful towards others.
orig: ولما سكت عن موسى الغضب أخذ الألواح وفي نسختها هدى ورحمة للذين هم لربهم يرهبون

translation: And Moses chose for Us seventy men from his people, and when the quake seized them, he said, 'My Lord, if You had willed, You could have destroyed them before and me [as well]. Would You destroy us for what the foolish among us have done? This is not but a trial by which You cause whom You will to stray, and You guide whom You will. You are our Protector, so forgive us and have mercy upon us; and You are the best of forgivers.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about Moses choosing seventy men from his people to meet with God. However, when a quake struck them, Moses prayed to God, expressing that if God had willed, He could have destroyed them before. Moses questioned whether they should be destroyed for the actions of the foolish among them. The verse highlights that God causes some to stray and guides others, emphasizing God's power and control over all things. Moses then asked for forgiveness and mercy for himself and his people, acknowledging God's attributes of being the best of forgivers.
orig: واختار موسى قومه سبعين رجلا لميقاتنا فلما أخذتهم الرجفة قال رب لو شئت أهلكتهم من قبل وإياي أتهلكنا بما فعل السفهاء منا إن هي إلا فتنتك تضل بها من تشاء وتهدي من تشاء أنت ولينا فاغفر لنا وارحمنا وأنت خير الغافرين

translation: And write for us a good deed in this world and in the hereafter, indeed, we have turned unto You. He said: My punishment, I afflict therewith whom I will, and My mercy embraces all things, so I shall write it down for those who are pious and give the alms and those who believe in Our signs.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the reward for good deeds, both in this world and in the hereafter. The speaker, who is believed to be the prophet Moses, is asking God to record a good deed for them in both worlds. God responds by stating that His punishment will be inflicted on whom He wills, and His mercy embraces all things. However, God promises to write down the good deed for those who are pious, give alms, and believe in God's signs. The verse highlights the importance of good deeds and faith, and the promise of reward for those who are righteous and obedient to God.
orig: واكتب لنا في هذه الدنيا حسنة وفي الآخرة إنا هدنا إليك قال عذابي أصيب به من أشاء ورحمتي وسعت كل شيء فسأكتبها للذين يتقون ويؤتون الزكاة والذين هم بآياتنا يؤمنون

translation: Those who follow the Messenger, the unlettered prophet, whom they find written down with them in the Torah and the Gospel, he enjoins upon them what is right and forbids them what is wrong, and makes lawful for them the good things and prohibits for them the evil things, and relieves them of their burden and the shackles that were upon them. So those who believe in him and support him and help him and follow the light that has been sent down with him - it is those who will be successful.
interpretation: The verse speaks about those who follow the unlettered prophet, who is mentioned in the Torah and the Gospel. The prophet enjoins what is right, forbids what is wrong, and makes lawful the good things and prohibits the evil things. The verse emphasizes the relief and freedom that the prophet brings to the people, by relieving them of their burden and the shackles that were upon them. The verse encourages people to believe in the prophet, support him, help him, and follow the light that has been sent down with him. The verse promises success and blessings for those who do so.
orig: الذين يتبعون الرسول النبي الأمي الذي يجدونه مكتوبا عندهم في التوراة والإنجيل يأمرهم بالمعروف وينهاهم عن المنكر ويحل لهم الطيبات ويحرم عليهم الخبائث ويضع عنهم إصرهم والأغلال التي كانت عليهم فالذين آمنوا به وعزروه ونصروه واتبعوا النور الذي أنزل معه أولئك هم المفلحون

translation: Say, 'O mankind, indeed I am the Messenger of Allah to you all, [from Him] to whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. There is no deity except Him; He gives life and causes death.' So believe in Allah and His Messenger, the Prophet who can neither read nor write [i.e., Muhammad] who believes in Allah and His words - and follow him that you may be guided.
interpretation: The verse is a message from the Prophet Muhammad, who is introducing himself as the Messenger of God to all of humanity. He emphasizes that God is the only deity and that He has power over all things. The Prophet calls on people to believe in God and His words, and to follow the Prophet himself, who is described as an unlettered prophet who believes in God. The verse is an invitation to guidance and the right path, and it emphasizes the importance of following the Prophet in order to achieve guidance.
orig: قل يا أيها الناس إني رسول الله إليكم جميعا الذي له ملك السماوات والأرض لا إله إلا هو يحيي ويميت فآمنوا بالله ورسوله النبي الأمي الذي يؤمن بالله وكلماته واتبعوه لعلكم تهتدون

translation: And among the people of Moses was a group that guided by the truth, and by it they acted justly.
interpretation: The verse highlights the presence of a righteous group among the followers of Moses who were guided by the truth and acted justly. This group played a crucial role in upholding justice and truth among the people of Moses, and their presence served as a positive influence and example for others. The verse emphasizes the importance of having a strong and just leadership, and the positive impact it can have on a community.
orig: ومن قوم موسى أمة يهدون بالحق وبه يعدلون

translation: And We cut them up into twelve tribes, nations. And We inspired to Moses, when his people asked him for water, 'Strike with your staff the stone.' And from it gushed forth twelve springs. Every people knew its drinking place. And We caused the clouds to overshadow them with shade. And We sent down to them manna and quails, 'Eat of the good things We have provided for you.' But they were not wronging Us but rather themselves. But they were ungrateful.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the Israelites, who were divided into twelve tribes and were provided with water, shade, manna, and quails by God. The verse emphasizes God's generosity and provision for the Israelites, despite their wrongdoing and ingratitude. The verse serves as a reminder of God's power and ability to provide for and protect His people, as well as a warning to those who do not show gratitude for the blessings they have received.
orig: وقطعناهم اثنتي عشرة أسباطا أمما وأوحينا إلى موسى إذ استسقاه قومه أن اضرب بعصاك الحجر فانبجست منه اثنتا عشرة عينا قد علم كل أناس مشربهم وظللنا عليهم الغمام وأنزلنا عليهم المن والسلوى كلوا من طيبات ما رزقناكم وما ظلمونا ولكن كانوا أنفسهم يظلمون

translation: And when it was said to them, 'Dwell in this town and eat from it wherever you will, and say, 'Relieve us [of our burden],' and enter the gate prostrate, We will forgive you your sins and will increase [reward] for the righteous.',
interpretation: The verse describes an invitation to the people to live in a town, eat from its resources, and follow certain instructions such as saying 'Relieve us [of our burden]' and entering the gate while prostrating. In return, God promises to forgive their sins and increase the reward for the righteous. The verse highlights the blessings and rewards that come from following God's commands and demonstrates God's mercy and forgiveness towards those who repent and seek forgiveness.
orig: وإذ قيل لهم اسكنوا هذه القرية وكلوا منها حيث شئتم وقولوا حطة وادخلوا الباب سجدا نغفر لكم خطيئاتكم سنزيد المحسنين

translation: But those who were unjust changed [their] words to a statement other than that which they were told. So We sent upon them a curse from the sky because of what they were earning.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the punishment of those who changed God's message and acted unjustly. The verse highlights the consequences of altering God's message and emphasizes that God will not let such actions go unpunished. The 'curse from the sky' symbolizes God's wrath and represents a severe form of punishment. The verse serves as a warning to those who distort God's message or act unjustly, reminding them of the severe consequences of their actions.
orig: فبدل الذين ظلموا منهم قولا غير الذي قيل لهم فأرسلنا عليهم رجزا من السماء بما كانوا يظلمون

translation: And ask them about the town that was by the sea, when they transgressed on the Sabbath, when their fish came to them openly on their Sabbath day, and on the day they did not keep Sabbath, they did not come to them. In this way, We tested them because of their disobedience.
interpretation: The verse speaks about a town located near the sea, whose people transgressed on the Sabbath day. The verse mentions that their fish, which they relied on for sustenance, would come to them openly on the Sabbath, but not on the days they did not keep the Sabbath. This was a test from God, a way of punishing them for their disobedience. The verse serves as a reminder of the consequences of disobedience and transgression, and the importance of upholding religious laws and commandments.
orig: واسألهم عن القرية التي كانت حاضرة البحر إذ يعدون في السبت إذ تأتيهم حيتانهم يوم سبتهم شرعا ويوم لا يسبتون لا تأتيهم كذلك نبلوهم بما كانوا يفسقون

translation: And when a community of them said, 'Why does God not punish us or chastise us for our sins?' They said, 'Seek forgiveness from your Lord and repent to Him. Perhaps you will be guided.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about a group of people questioning why they have not yet been punished for their sins. The response from others in the community is for them to seek forgiveness from God and repent. The verse highlights the importance of seeking forgiveness and turning back to God, as a means of avoiding punishment and receiving guidance. It also implies that punishment may still be forthcoming, and that repentance should not be delayed.
orig: وإذ قالت أمة منهم لم تعظون قوما الله مهلكهم أو معذبهم عذابا شديدا قالوا معذرة إلى ربكم ولعلهم يتقون

translation: But when they forgot what they had been reminded of, We saved those who had forbidden evil and seized those who were unjust with a severe punishment because of their sins.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the consequences of forgetting the teachings of God and engaging in unjust and evil actions. Those who were saved were those who had forbidden evil and remained righteous, while those who were unjust and sinned received severe punishment. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of remembering and following God's teachings, and the consequences of forgetting and engaging in unjust actions.
orig: فلما نسوا ما ذكروا به أنجينا الذين ينهون عن السوء وأخذنا الذين ظلموا بعذاب بئيس بما كانوا يفسقون

translation: But when they were insolent about that which they had been forbidden, We said to them, 'Be apes, despised.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the punishment of a group of people who disobeyed God's commands and were insolent towards His prohibitions. As a result, they were transformed into apes, becoming a symbol of disgrace and rejection. The verse serves as a warning to those who disregard God's commands and engage in sinful behavior, emphasizing the severe consequences of such actions and the ultimate authority of God in meting out justice.
orig: فلما عتوا عن ما نهوا عنه قلنا لهم كونوا قردة خاسئين

translation: And when your Lord inspired the angels, 'I am with you, so strengthen those who have believed. I will cast terror into the hearts of those who disbelieved, so strike upon the necks and strike from them every fingertip.' That is because they opposed Allah and His Messenger. And whoever opposes Allah and His Messenger - indeed, Allah is severe in penalty.
interpretation: The verse describes a scene of divine intervention in a battle between believers and disbelievers. The Lord inspires the angels to support the believers and strike fear into the hearts of the disbelievers. The violent imagery of striking the necks and fingertips emphasizes the severity of the punishment for those who oppose Allah and His messenger. The verse serves as a reminder of the power and authority of Allah and the consequences of opposing Him and His messenger.
orig: وإذ تأذن ربك ليبعثن عليهم إلى يوم القيامة من يسومهم سوء العذاب إن ربك لسريع العقاب وإنه لغفور رحيم

translation: And We cut them off in the midst of their life, while some of them were righteous, and some were otherwise, and We left upon them a sign: perhaps they might return.
interpretation: The verse speaks about God's punishment of a group of people, some of whom were righteous while others were not. Despite the presence of righteous individuals, the entire community was subjected to God's punishment. After the punishment, a sign was left behind, possibly as a reminder or a lesson for those who survived. The verse highlights the power and authority of God, who can punish or show mercy to whomever He wills. It also serves as a warning to communities and individuals to turn away from sin and strive for righteousness.
orig: وقطعناهم في الأرض أمما منهم الصالحون ومنهم دون ذلك وبلوناهم بالحسنات والسيئات لعلهم يرجعون

translation: Then there succeeded them an generation who inherited the Book, they choose to take the goods of this lower world, and say, 'It will be forgiven us'; and if an opportunity of the like of that which they were given comes to them, they take it; was not the covenant of the Book taken from them that they should not say concerning Allah anything but the truth, and they study what is in it; and the abode of the hereafter is better for those who keep their duty; do you not then understand?
interpretation: The verse criticizes a generation that inherited the Book (referring to the Torah) but prioritized worldly gains over the teachings of the scripture. Despite committing sins and taking advantage of opportunities similar to those they were previously given, they assumed that they would be forgiven. The verse reminds them of their covenant to speak the truth about God and study the scripture. It emphasizes that the hereafter is superior for those who uphold their duties, urging them to reflect and understand the significance of their actions and the consequences of neglecting their responsibilities.
orig: فخلف من بعدهم خلف ورثوا الكتاب يأخذون عرض هذا الأدنى ويقولون سيغفر لنا وإن يأتهم عرض مثله يأخذوه ألم يؤخذ عليهم ميثاق الكتاب أن لا يقولوا على الله إلا الحق ودرسوا ما فيه والدار الآخرة خير للذين يتقون أفلا تعقلون

translation: And those who hold fast to the Book and establish prayer – indeed, We do not waste the reward of those who do good.
interpretation: The verse speaks about those who hold fast to the Book (referring to the Qur'an) and establish prayer. The verse emphasizes that the reward for these individuals who do good will not be wasted. The verse serves as a reminder and an assurance for those who follow the teachings of the Qur'an and establish prayer, that their efforts and good deeds will not be in vain. It also serves as an invitation for those who have not yet embraced these practices, to do so and reap the rewards.
orig: والذين يمسكون بالكتاب وأقاموا الصلاة إنا لا نضيع أجر المصلحين

translation: And when We appointed for them a time, and We gave a fair warning to them, then We came to them with destruction. While We had shown them the way to a clear salvation, yet they preferred blindness to insight, so the punishment overtook them. And We destroyed them equally, and We reduced them to ruins, and thus do We recompense the unjust.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of a people who were given a fair warning and a chance to repent, but they chose to ignore it and continued in their unjust ways. The verse highlights the power and authority of God, who can destroy and reduce to ruins those who defy Him. The verse serves as a reminder that God's punishment is a consequence of people's actions and that He has the power to recompense the unjust. The verse emphasizes the importance of heeding God's warnings, seeking guidance, and choosing the path of righteousness and justice.
orig: وإذ نتقنا الجبل فوقهم كأنه ظلة وظنوا أنه واقع بهم خذوا ما آتيناكم بقوة واذكروا ما فيه لعلكم تتقون

translation: And when your Lord took from the children of Adam, from their loins, their descendants and made them bear witness of themselves, [saying] 'Am I not your Lord?' They said, 'Yes, we have borne witness.' [This] lest you should say on the day of resurrection, 'Indeed, we were of this unaware.'
interpretation: The verse describes a covenant made by God with the descendants of Adam, in which they bear witness that God is their Lord. This covenant serves as a reminder for people on the Day of Judgment, so that they cannot claim ignorance of God's Lordship. The verse emphasizes the importance of recognizing and acknowledging God's oneness and sovereignty, and the significance of this recognition in the hereafter. It also highlights the role of this covenant as a means of accountability for people, as they will be reminded of their prior knowledge and affirmation of God's Lordship on the Day of Judgment.
orig: وإذ أخذ ربك من بني آدم من ظهورهم ذريتهم وأشهدهم على أنفسهم ألست بربكم قالوا بلى شهدنا أن تقولوا يوم القيامة إنا كنا عن هذا غافلين

translation: Or do you say, 'We found our forefathers upon a religion, and we are only following in their footsteps?'
interpretation: The verse addresses those who blindly follow the religion of their ancestors without considering its truth or falsehood. The verse questions the validity of this approach, implying that it is not a sufficient justification for continuing to practice a certain religion. The verse encourages critical thinking and questioning, and emphasizes the importance of personal responsibility and accountability in matters of faith. It suggests that individuals should not simply follow the traditions of their forefathers, but rather, they should strive to understand the truth and act accordingly.
orig: أو تقولوا إنما أشرك آباؤنا من قبل وكنا ذرية من بعدهم أفتهلكنا بما فعل المبطلون

translation: And thus do We make the verses clear, and perhaps they will return.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the way in which God reveals His signs and verses (ayat), making them clear for people to understand. The verse suggests that the purpose of these revelations is to guide people back to the right path. The phrase 'and perhaps they will return' implies that even though the revelations are clear, there is still a possibility that people will not heed the message and will not change their ways. The verse conveys a sense of hope and patience, indicating that God will continue to send down His revelations, giving people the opportunity to reflect and repent.
orig: وكذلك نفصل الآيات ولعلهم يرجعون

translation: And relate to them the news of him to whom We gave Our signs, but he abandoned them, so Satan followed him, and he became of the deviators.
interpretation: The verse speaks about someone who was given divine signs or revelations, but chose to abandon them. As a result, Satan took advantage of the situation and led him astray. The verse serves as a warning about the dangers of rejecting or ignoring divine guidance, and the consequences of following one's desires and the whispers of Satan. The verse emphasizes the importance of adhering to divine guidance and remaining steadfast on the path of righteousness.
orig: واتل عليهم نبأ الذي آتيناه آياتنا فانسلخ منها فأتبعه الشيطان فكان من الغاوين

translation: And if We had willed, We could have raised him thereby, but he clung to the earth and followed his own desire. So his example is like the example of a dog: if you drive it away, it laps up or if you leave it, it [still] laps up. Such is the example of the people who denied Our signs; so relate the stories that perhaps they will give thought.
interpretation: The verse uses the metaphor of a dog to describe a person who rejects God's signs and follows their own desires. The dog is driven away but continues to lap up water, just as the person who rejects God's signs remains stubborn in their disbelief. The verse serves as a warning to those who deny God's signs, emphasizing the futility of their actions and the consequences of their disbelief. The verse encourages the telling of stories and parables to make the message clear and to encourage reflection and contemplation.
orig: ولو شئنا لرفعناه بها ولكنه أخلد إلى الأرض واتبع هواه فمثله كمثل الكلب إن تحمل عليه يلهث أو تتركه يلهث ذلك مثل القوم الذين كذبوا بآياتنا فاقصص القصص لعلهم يتفكرون

translation: The example of the people is like that of the crops which We send down upon them: they then forget and take pleasure.
interpretation: The verse uses the example of crops to illustrate the behavior of people who reject God's signs. Just as crops are sent down for the benefit of people, but the people forget their source of sustenance and indulge in hedonistic pleasures, the people similarly forget and ignore God's signs. The verse serves as a reminder that people should not be ungrateful for the blessings they receive, and should not forget their Creator.
orig: ساء مثلا القوم الذين كذبوا بآياتنا وأنفسهم كانوا يظلمون

translation: Whoever Allah guides - he is the one who is guided; and whoever He misguides - it is those who are the losers.
interpretation: The verse explains the ultimate power of Allah's guidance, and the consequences of being misguided. Those who are guided by Allah are on the right path, while those who are misguided are the ones who will suffer the consequences. The verse emphasizes the importance of seeking Allah's guidance and following His path, as it leads to success and salvation. On the other hand, those who stray from Allah's path and are misguided will ultimately be the losers in this life and the hereafter.
orig: من يهد الله فهو المهتدي ومن يضلل فأولئك هم الخاسرون

translation: And We have certainly created for Hell many of the jinn and mankind. They have hearts with which they do not understand, they have eyes with which they do not see, and they have ears with which they do not hear. Those are like cattle; rather, they are more astray. Those - they are the heedless.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the creation of many jinn and mankind for Hell. These individuals have physical senses such as hearts, eyes, and ears, but they do not use them to understand or perceive the truth. They are likened to cattle, who do not have the capacity for understanding or guidance. However, the people described in this verse are even more astray than animals. The verse serves as a warning to those who are heedless and unaware, emphasizing the consequences of their lack of understanding and perception of the truth.
orig: ولقد ذرأنا لجهنم كثيرا من الجن والإنس لهم قلوب لا يفقهون بها ولهم أعين لا يبصرون بها ولهم آذان لا يسمعون بها أولئك كالأنعام بل هم أضل أولئك هم الغافلون

translation: And to God belong the best names, so invoke Him by them and leave those who blaspheme in His names. They will be recompensed for what they used to do.
interpretation: The verse affirms that the most beautiful and perfect names belong to God, and encourages the believers to invoke Him by these names. The verse also warns against those who blaspheme or misuse God's names, and emphasizes that they will be held accountable for their actions. The verse highlights the importance of using and invoking God's names in a manner that is respectful and mindful of their true meaning and significance.
orig: ولله الأسماء الحسنى فادعوه بها وذروا الذين يلحدون في أسمائه سيجزون ما كانوا يعملون

translation: And We have created for Us a nation who will act justly and guided by the truth.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the creation of a nation that will uphold justice and be guided by the truth. This nation will be created for the benefit of God and will fulfill its purpose by acting in accordance with these principles. The verse highlights the importance of justice and truth as fundamental values that guide the actions and decisions of this nation. It also emphasizes the role of God in creating such a nation, indicating that it is a divine plan and that the nation has a special purpose in the grand scheme of things.
orig: وممن خلقنا أمة يهدون بالحق وبه يعدلون

translation: And those who have disbelieved in Our verses, We will surely lead them [to punishment] from where they do not perceive.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the fate of those who disbelieve in the signs or verses of God. The verse warns that these people will be led to punishment from a direction they do not expect or perceive, indicating the unexpected and inescapable nature of divine retribution. The verse serves as a warning to those who reject God's revelations and emphasizes the certainty of divine judgment for those who deny the truth.
orig: والذين كذبوا بآياتنا سنستدرجهم من حيث لا يعلمون

translation: And I will grant them respite; indeed, My plan is firm.
interpretation: The verse speaks about God's intention to grant respite to certain people, despite their wrongdoing. However, the verse also emphasizes that this respite is not a sign of weakness or forgiveness, but rather part of God's firm plan. The verse suggests that God's plan is unchangeable and that the people who are granted respite will ultimately face the consequences of their actions.
orig: وأملي لهم إن كيدي متين

translation: Have they not considered what was done to their predecessors, how many the generations We destroyed before them? They were greater in power than they are. They have no protector from Us.
interpretation: The verse reminds people to reflect on the fate of their predecessors, who were destroyed by God for their sins and transgressions. The verse emphasizes that these earlier civilizations were more powerful and prosperous than the current one, yet they were not spared from God's punishment. The phrase 'They have no protector from Us' underscores the absolute power and authority of God, who cannot be thwarted or resisted by any created being. The verse serves as a warning to those who are complacent in their sins, urging them to take heed of the lessons of history and to turn towards God in repentance before it is too late.
orig: أولم يتفكروا ما بصاحبهم من جنة إن هو إلا نذير مبين

translation: Have they not looked at the kingdom of the heavens and the earth and all that Allah has created, and that it may be that the end of their term has drawn near? So, in what statement (or conversation) after this will they believe?
interpretation: The verse challenges people to reflect on the wonders of the universe and the signs of Allah's creation. It emphasizes the nearness of the end of their term, and questions the people's ability to believe in any statement or conversation after this. The verse encourages people to ponder and reflect on the signs of Allah, and to recognize the impending end of their lives. It serves as a reminder to people to turn to Allah, and to have faith in His signs and messages before it is too late.
orig: أولم ينظروا في ملكوت السماوات والأرض وما خلق الله من شيء وأن عسى أن يكون قد اقترب أجلهم فبأي حديث بعده يؤمنون

translation: Whoever Allah leaves astray, there is no guide for him. And He leaves them in their transgression, blinding them.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the fate of those who are led astray by Allah, meaning that they have strayed from the right path and committed sins. The verse emphasizes that once Allah has left someone to stray, there is no guide who can help them. Furthermore, Allah leaves them in their transgression, allowing them to continue in their sinful ways. The verse ends by saying that Allah causes them to be veiled or blinded, meaning that they are unable to see the truth or understand the consequences of their actions. The verse serves as a reminder of the severity of straying from the right path and the danger of continuing in sinful ways, as Allah will not guide those who have been left to stray and will allow them to continue in their transgression.
orig: من يضلل الله فلا هادي له ويذرهم في طغيانهم يعمهون

translation: They ask you about the Hour (Day of Judgment): when will it come to pass? Say: Knowledge of it rests only with my Lord. He alone will reveal its time; it weighs heavily on the heavens and the earth. It will not come upon you except suddenly. They ask you as if you were eager for it. Say: Knowledge of it is with God alone. But most people do not know.
interpretation: The verse addresses the question about the Day of Judgment and its timing. The verse emphasizes that only God has the knowledge of when it will take place and that it will come suddenly, without warning. The verse also highlights the irony that people ask as if the one being asked is eager for the Day of Judgment. The verse serves as a reminder that knowledge of the Day of Judgment is solely in the hands of God and that most people lack this knowledge.
orig: يسألونك عن الساعة أيان مرساها قل إنما علمها عند ربي لا يجليها لوقتها إلا هو ثقلت في السماوات والأرض لا تأتيكم إلا بغتة يسألونك كأنك حفي عنها قل إنما علمها عند الله ولكن أكثر الناس لا يعلمون

translation: Say, 'I have no control over any harm or benefit coming to myself except as God wills. If I had knowledge of the unseen, I would have acquired much good, and no evil would have touched me. I am but a warner and bringer of good news to a people who believe.'
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the idea that humans are not in control of their lives and that everything happens according to God's will. The speaker acknowledges that they do not have knowledge of the unseen and therefore cannot avoid harm or ensure good. The speaker is portrayed as a warner and a bringer of good news, emphasizing the importance of faith and belief. The verse serves as a reminder that humans should trust in God's plan and submit to His will.
orig: قل لا أملك لنفسي نفعا ولا ضرا إلا ما شاء الله ولو كنت أعلم الغيب لاستكثرت من الخير وما مسني السوء إن أنا إلا نذير وبشير لقوم يؤمنون

translation: It is He who created you from a single soul and created from it its mate that he might dwell in security with her. And when he covered her, she carried a light burden and passed by, but when it became heavy, they both invoked Allah, their Lord, 'If You should give us a righteous child, we will surely be among the grateful.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the creation of human beings and their natural inclination towards companionship. It highlights the role of God in creating a companion for each person, so that they can live in security and peace. The verse then goes on to describe the experience of pregnancy and childbirth, emphasizing the shared responsibility of both parents in the upbringing of the child. The verse concludes with the parents' prayer for a righteous child, and their commitment to be among the grateful if their prayer is answered. The verse can be interpreted as a celebration of the beauty and significance of human relationships, as well as a reminder of the importance of gratitude and righteousness in the face of God's blessings.
orig: هو الذي خلقكم من نفس واحدة وجعل منها زوجها ليسكن إليها فلما تغشاها حملت حملا خفيفا فمرت به فلما أثقلت دعوا الله ربهما لئن آتيتنا صالحا لنكونن من الشاكرين

translation: But when he (Zachariah) came to him (his Lord) with a goodly word, he confirmed him (Zachariah) with His good pleasure. Verily, Allah is of what they do a knower.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the story of Zachariah and his prayer to God for a son. In this part of the story, Zachariah comes to God with a goodly word, which refers to his prayer. God responds by confirming Zachariah's prayer and granting him a son, John. The verse emphasizes God's knowledge of all that people do, indicating that God knows the intentions and actions of Zachariah and responds accordingly. The verse serves to remind people that God is aware of their prayers and actions, and that He responds to those who come to Him with good intentions and deeds.
orig: فلما آتاهما صالحا جعلا له شركاء فيما آتاهما فتعالى الله عما يشركون

translation: Or like one who chooses a god other than Allah, who can neither benefit him nor harm him - (it is) the duty of such a one to account.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the foolishness of choosing a god other than Allah, who has no power to benefit or harm anyone. The verse emphasizes the responsibility and accountability of those who make such a choice, indicating that they will be held accountable for their actions. The verse serves as a reminder to those who may be tempted to worship false gods or idols, reminding them of the futility of such actions and the certainty of being held accountable for their choices.
orig: أيشركون ما لا يخلق شيئا وهم يخلقون

translation: And they cannot aid them, nor can they aid themselves.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the powerlessness of certain individuals or groups in the face of adversity or punishment from God. The phrase 'they cannot aid them' likely refers to other people or external forces that the individuals had previously relied on for support, but who are now unable or unwilling to help. The phrase 'nor can they aid themselves' emphasizes the complete helplessness of these individuals, as they are unable to save themselves from their situation. The verse serves as a reminder of the limits of human power and control, and the ultimate dependence of all beings on God's mercy and protection.
orig: ولا يستطيعون لهم نصرا ولا أنفسهم ينصرون

translation: And if you invite them to guidance, they will not follow you. It is the same for you whether you invite them or remain silent.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the rejection of guidance by certain people. No matter how much one tries to guide them towards the right path, they will not follow. The verse emphasizes that the responsibility of guiding others lies with the individual, but the outcome is not in their hands. Whether the individual chovers to invite them to guidance or remains silent, the outcome remains the same. This verse highlights the importance of patience and perseverance in the face of rejection and the ultimate wisdom and justice of God's plan.
orig: وإن تدعوهم إلى الهدى لا يتبعوكم سواء عليكم أدعوتموهم أم أنتم صامتون

translation: Indeed, those you invite besides Allah are servants like you. So invite them, and let them respond to you, if you are truthful.
interpretation: The verse addresses the people who worship and invoke beings other than Allah, stating that these beings are merely 'servants' like them. The verse challenges the people to call upon these beings and see if they will respond, implying that they will not. The verse emphasizes the futility of worshipping and invoking other than Allah, and serves as a reminder that only Allah has the power to respond and grant the needs of His servants.
orig: إن الذين تدعون من دون الله عباد أمثالكم فادعوهم فليستجيبوا لكم إن كنتم صادقين

translation: Will they not then go about contemplating, or have they ears to hear, or eyes to see? And why not then invoke, along with Him, their 'associates' [other deities]? So let them devise a plan, then not see [or feel at all]!
interpretation: The verse challenges the disbelievers to contemplate and consider the signs of God around them, and questions their senses, asking if they are unable to hear, see or feel. The verse then invites them to invoke their 'associates' or other deities, if they are so inclined, and to come up with a plan. However, the verse implies that they will not be able to see or feel the results of their plan, indicating the futility of their actions and their inability to comprehend the truth. The verse serves as a call to the disbelievers to reflect on their beliefs and actions, and to turn to God for guidance and understanding.
orig: ألهم أرجل يمشون بها أم لهم أيد يبطشون بها أم لهم أعين يبصرون بها أم لهم آذان يسمعون بها قل ادعوا شركاءكم ثم كيدون فلا تنظرون

translation: Indeed, my protector is Allah, who has sent down the Book; and He is the protector of the righteous.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the speaker's faith in Allah as their protector and the source of guidance. The phrase 'who has sent down the Book' refers to the Quran, and the 'righteous' refers to those who follow its teachings. The verse highlights the importance of relying on Allah and seeking His protection, particularly for those who strive to live righteously and follow the guidance of the Quran.
orig: إن وليي الله الذي نزل الكتاب وهو يتولى الصالحين

translation: And those whom you call upon instead of Him cannot help you, nor can they help themselves.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the powerlessness of false gods or deities that people may worship instead of Allah. These entities cannot provide any assistance or support, neither to the people who worship them nor to those who call upon them for help. This highlights the futility of idolatry and the importance of putting one's faith solely in Allah, who has the power to help and support His believers.
orig: والذين تدعون من دونه لا يستطيعون نصركم ولا أنفسهم ينصرون

translation: And if you invite them to guidance, they do not hear; and if you look at them, they do not see.
interpretation: The verse describes the rejection and ignorance of people who are not open to guidance. The phrase 'if you invite them to guidance' suggests an effort to help or direct them towards the right path, but they refuse to listen or heed the warning. The second part of the verse, 'if you look at them, they do not see', further emphasizes their lack of understanding or comprehension. The verse highlights the challenge of trying to reach those who are not receptive to guidance, and serves as a reminder that ultimately, it is up to each individual to choose whether or not to accept the truth.
orig: وإن تدعوهم إلى الهدى لا يسمعوا وتراهم ينظرون إليك وهم لا يبصرون

translation: Show forgiveness, enjoin what is good, and turn away from the ignorant.
interpretation: The verse instructs believers on how to interact with those who are ignorant or acting ignorantly. It advises them to show forgiveness and to enjoin what is good, which means to encourage and promote good actions and behavior. At the same time, they should turn away from the ignorant, which means to avoid engaging with them in a negative way or responding to their ignorance with more ignorance. By following these instructions, believers can create a positive and constructive environment around them and avoid unnecessary conflicts and confrontations.
orig: خذ العفو وأمر بالعرف وأعرض عن الجاهلين

translation: And if a suggestion from Satan assails your mind, then seek refuge in Allah; indeed, He is the Hearing, the Knowing.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the importance of seeking protection from Satan and his whispers. When a person is tempted or influenced by Satan, they should immediately seek refuge in Allah, who is the All-Hearing and All-Knowing. By seeking refuge in Allah, a person can protect themselves from the negative influence of Satan and find strength and guidance in their faith. The verse serves as a reminder that Satan is always present and looking for ways to lead people astray, and that seeking protection from Allah is the best way to stay on the right path.
orig: وإما ينزغنك من الشيطان نزغ فاستعذ بالله إنه سميع عليم

translation: As for those who fear Allah, when a suggestion from Satan assails them, they remember and then they become seeable.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the behavior of the righteous people when they are tempted by Satan. When they are struck by a suggestion from Satan, they remember and become aware, implying that they remember and turn to Allah, seeking His protection and guidance. This verse highlights the importance of being vigilant against Satan's whispers and turning to Allah in times of temptation. It also emphasizes the role of remembrance of Allah as a means of protection against evil.
orig: إن الذين اتقوا إذا مسهم طائف من الشيطان تذكروا فإذا هم مبصرون

translation: And their brothers were more powerful than them in power, so they expelled them, and they were not due to return.
interpretation: The verse describes a situation where a group of people (referred to as 'them') were expelled from their homes by their more powerful brothers. The word 'expelled' implies a forcible removal and a sense of injustice. The phrase 'not due to return' emphasizes the finality of their expulsion, and the severity of the separation between the two groups.
orig: وإخوانهم يمدونهم في الغي ثم لا يقصرون

translation: And when the verse is not conveyed to them, they say: 'Why have you not brought it?' Say: 'I only follow what is revealed to me from my Lord. Indeed, this is enlightenment from your Lord, and a guidance and mercy for a people who believe.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the response of the disbelievers when they are not presented with a sign or proof. They question why the sign has not been brought, and the response is that the speaker only follows what is revealed to them from their Lord. The verse emphasizes the importance of guidance and mercy for those who believe, and the revelation from the Lord as the source of enlightenment and guidance. The verse highlights the distinction between those who believe and those who do not, and the importance of faith in receiving guidance and mercy.
orig: وإذا لم تأتهم بآية قالوا لولا اجتبيتها قل إنما أتبع ما يوحى إلي من ربي هذا بصائر من ربكم وهدى ورحمة لقوم يؤمنون

translation: And when the Qur'an is recited, then listen to it and pay attention that you may be shown mercy.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of listening to and paying attention when the Qur'an is being recited. By doing so, the listener may be shown mercy. This verse serves as a reminder to Muslims of the importance of being attentive and respectful during the recitation of the Qur'an, and also highlights the potential rewards of doing so.
orig: وإذا قرئ القرآن فاستمعوا له وأنصتوا لعلكم ترحمون

translation: And remember your Lord within yourself, in humility and in fear, without being loud in speech, in the morning and the evening; and be not of those who are neglectful.
interpretation: The verse encourages the believer to remember and worship their Lord in a state of humility and fear, both in the morning and in the evening. The believer is instructed to do this quietly and without being ostentatious. The verse serves as a reminder to the believer to be mindful of God and to maintain a consistent practice of worship, both at the start and end of the day. The verse also warns against being neglectful or heedless in one's worship and relationship with God.
orig: واذكر ربك في نفسك تضرعا وخيفة ودون الجهر من القول بالغدو والآصال ولا تكن من الغافلين

translation: Indeed, those who are with your Lord do not disdain His worship. They glorify Him and prostrate to Him.
interpretation: The verse describes the attitude of those who are in the presence of God. They do not disdain or look down upon worshiping God, but rather, they glorify Him and prostrate to Him. This verse emphasizes the importance of humility and submission to God. It serves as a reminder that true believers recognize the greatness of God and their own limitations, and they respond with reverence and devotion. This verse also highlights the importance of prostration, which is a physical act of submission that is highly valued in Islamic worship.
orig: إن الذين عند ربك لا يستكبرون عن عبادته ويسبحونه وله يسجدون

translation: They ask you concerning the spoils of war. Say, 'The spoils of war belong to Allah and the Messenger.' So fear Allah and adjust your differences, and obey Allah and His Messenger, if you are believers.
interpretation: This verse speaks about the distribution of spoils of war and emphasizes that they belong to God and His Messenger. The verse commands the believers to fear God, settle their disputes, and obey God and His Messenger. The verse highlights the importance of obedience and submission to God and His Messenger, and the necessity of resolving conflicts and disagreements among the believers. The verse serves as a reminder that the spoils of war are a blessing from God, and that they should be distributed in accordance with His commands and the guidance of His Messenger.
orig: يسألونك عن الأنفال قل الأنفال لله والرسول فاتقوا الله وأصلحوا ذات بينكم وأطيعوا الله ورسوله إن كنتم مؤمنين

translation: The believers are only those who, when Allah is mentioned, their hearts become fearful, and when His verses are recited to them, it increases them in faith and upon their Lord they rely.
interpretation: The verse describes the characteristics of true believers, who, when they hear the name of Allah, feel a sense of fear and reverence. When they hear or read the verses of the QQur'an, their faith increases and they place their trust in their Lord. This verse highlights the importance of having a deep and meaningful relationship with Allah, one that is characterized by a constant striving to increase in faith and a reliance on Allah in all aspects of life.
orig: إنما المؤمنون الذين إذا ذكر الله وجلت قلوبهم وإذا تليت عليهم آياته زادتهم إيمانا وعلى ربهم يتوكلون

translation: Those who establish the prayer and from what We have provided for them, they spend.
interpretation: The verse highlights the importance of establishing the prayer and giving charity. Those who fulfill these obligations are described as being among those who are grateful for God's blessings and use them in a way that pleases Him. The verse serves as a reminder to believers to be mindful of their duties towards God and to use their wealth and resources in a way that benefits themselves and others. It emphasizes the connection between faith and actions and the importance of putting faith into practice.
orig: الذين يقيمون الصلاة ومما رزقناهم ينفقون

translation: Those are they who believe truly, for them are grades of dignity with their Lord, and forgiveness, and a generous provision.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the rewards for those who truly believe. These believers will receive 'grades of dignity' from their Lord, which implies a high status and respect in the hereafter. They will also be granted forgiveness for their sins, as well as a generous provision, indicating a life of abundance and prosperity. The verse serves as a source of motivation and encouragement for believers to strive for righteousness and strengthen their faith, as it highlights the blessings and rewards that await them in the afterlife.
orig: أولئك هم المؤمنون حقا لهم درجات عند ربهم ومغفرة ورزق كريم

translation: How [was it] that your Lord sent you forth from your home in the early morning, indeed, a party of the believers were averse.
interpretation: The verse describes the departure of the Prophet Muhammad from his home in Mecca in the early morning, accompanied by a group of believers, while others among the believers were reluctant or unwilling to leave. The verse highlights the difficulties and challenges faced by the early Muslims, and the sacrifices they had to make in order to fulfill their religious obligations. It also emphasizes the leadership and determination of the Prophet Muhammad, who was willing to face opposition and adversity in order to fulfill his mission. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of perseverance and commitment in the face of hardship and opposition, and the rewards that come from staying true to one's beliefs and values.
orig: كما أخرجك ربك من بيتك بالحق وإن فريقا من المؤمنين لكارهون

translation: They argue with you concerning the truth even after it has become clear, as if they were being driven to death while they are looking on.
interpretation: The verse describes people who argue and dispute about the truth even after it has been made clear to them. The verse compares their behavior to that of people who are being driven towards death, yet they continue to observe and do nothing about it. The verse highlights the stubbornness and rejection of these people, who refuse to accept the truth despite its clarity. It serves as a warning to those who deny the truth and emphasizes the consequences of their denial and rejection.
orig: يجادلونك في الحق بعدما تبين كأنما يساقون إلى الموت وهم ينظرون

translation: And when Allah promises you one of the two parties that it will be yours and you wish that the other party would be yours, and Allah intends to establish the truth by His words and to eliminate the disbelievers.
interpretation: The verse speaks about a situation where God promises one of two parties to the believers, and they wish for the other party as well. However, God's intention is to establish the truth through His words and to cut off the disbelievers. The verse highlights the limitations of human desires and the ultimate wisdom of God's plan. It serves as a reminder to the believers to trust in God's wisdom and to have patience in the face of uncertainty, knowing that God's ultimate goal is to establish the truth and to eliminate falsehood.
orig: وإذ يعدكم الله إحدى الطائفتين أنها لكم وتودون أن غير ذات الشوكة تكون لكم ويريد الله أن يحق الحق بكلماته ويقطع دابر الكافرين

translation: So that the truth may be established, and the falsehood vanquished, even if the evildoers dislike it.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the establishment of truth and the vanquishing of falsehood, even if the evildoers dislike it. This verse emphasizes the importance of justice and truth, and the unwavering commitment of God to establish them, regardless of the opposition of those who commit wrongdoing. The verse serves as a reminder that the ultimate triumph of truth and justice is inevitable, and that those who commit wrongdoing will not be able to prevent it.
orig: ليحق الحق ويبطل الباطل ولو كره المجرمون

translation: When you implore your Lord for help, He will answer you, 'I am reinforcing you with a thousand angels, following one after another.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the promise of God to provide help and support to those who call upon Him in times of need. The verse emphasizes the magnitude of the help that will be provided, with a thousand angels being sent to assist. The phrase 'following one after another' highlights the continuous and unending nature of the support that will be given. The verse serves as a reminder of the power and mercy of God, and encourages believers to seek His help and guidance in times of difficulty.
orig: إذ تستغيثون ربكم فاستجاب لكم أني ممدكم بألف من الملائكة مردفين

translation: And He (God) has only made it (Islam) as a religion for you (mankind) by putting ease in it, and thus that your hearts may be at rest with it, and so that the people may be guided; and (know that) there is no guidance except from God; and (also know that) God is All-Knowing, All-Wise.
interpretation: The verse highlights that Islam is a religion that is easy to follow and that it brings peace and tranquility to the hearts of those who adopt it. The verse emphasizes that guidance can only come from God, and that God is All-Knowing and All-Wise. The verse can be interpreted as a reminder that people should not make religion difficult or burdensome, and that the ultimate goal of religion is to bring peace and guidance to the hearts of believers. It also highlights the importance of seeking guidance from God and recognizing that God is the source of all knowledge and wisdom.
orig: وما جعله الله إلا بشرى ولتطمئن به قلوبكم وما النصر إلا من عند الله إن الله عزيز حكيم

translation: When the clouds gather over you, providing you with shade, and when water descends from the sky upon you, giving you drink and vegetation, and when He sets in order for you the winds, and the clouds are held in suspense between heaven and earth - indeed, these are signs for a people who understand.
interpretation: The verse describes the various blessings and signs of God that people often take for granted. These blessings include the clouds that provide shade, the rain that gives life to the earth and sustenance to people, the winds that bring freshness and renewal, and the delicate balance of the natural world. These blessings are described as signs for those who are able to understand and appreciate them. The verse encourages people to reflect on the wonders of nature and to recognize the hand of God in all things, as a means of deepening their faith and gratitude.
orig: إذ يغشيكم النعاس أمنة منه وينزل عليكم من السماء ماء ليطهركم به ويذهب عنكم رجز الشيطان وليربط على قلوبكم ويثبت به الأقدام

translation: When your Lord revealed to the angels: 'I am with you, so make those who believe stand firm. I will cast terror into the hearts of those who disbelieved. So strike upon the necks and strike from them every fingertip.'
interpretation: The verse describes a scene of divine intervention, where God reveals to the angels that He is with them and commands them to instill fear in the hearts of the disbelievers. The angels are instructed to strike the disbelievers at the necks and to cut off their fingers, indicating a violent and decisive punishment. The verse emphasizes the power and authority of God, who stands with the believers and against the disbelievers. It serves as a reminder of the consequences of disbelief and the ultimate triumph of God's will.
orig: إذ يوحي ربك إلى الملائكة أني معكم فثبتوا الذين آمنوا سألقي في قلوب الذين كفروا الرعب فاضربوا فوق الأعناق واضربوا منهم كل بنان

translation: That is because they opposed Allah and His Messenger. And whoever opposes Allah and His Messenger - then indeed, Allah is severe in penalty.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of following and believing in Allah and His Messenger, and the severe consequences for those who oppose them. The verse serves as a warning to those who reject or challenge the teachings of Islam and the authority of the Prophet Muhammad. The phrase 'Allah is severe in penalty' implies that the punishment for those who oppose Allah and His Messenger is severe and unavoidable. This verse encourages believers to remain steadfast in their faith and obedience, and to avoid opposing Allah and His Messenger in order to avoid the severe consequences.
orig: ذلك بأنهم شاقوا الله ورسوله ومن يشاقق الله ورسوله فإن الله شديد العقاب

translation: That is [the reality of] My punishment among the communities of Jinn and mankind that have preceded you. So taste [the punishment]. Indeed, the disbelievers will have a punishment.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the reality of God's punishment that has been meted out to communities of Jinn and mankind that have existed before the current one. The phrase 'So taste [the punishment]' emphasizes the inevitability of the punishment for the disbelievers. The verse serves as a warning to the disbelievers, reminding them of the consequences of their disbelief and the certainty of God's punishment. The punishment for the disbelievers is a severe and ongoing one, as indicated by the phrase 'Indeed, the disbelievers will have a punishment'.
orig: ذلكم فذوقوه وأن للكافرين عذاب النار

translation: O you who have believed, when you encounter those who disbelieve advancing [for battle], do not turn your backs [in retreat]
interpretation: The verse is a command to the believers to stand firm and not retreat when they encounter non-believers who are advancing in battle. This verse emphasizes the importance of bravery and steadfastness in the face of adversity and the need for the believers to stand together as a unified front. It serves as a reminder that retreating or turning away from the fight can lead to defeat and loss of faith. The verse encourages the believers to be resolute in their beliefs and actions, and to always strive to uphold justice and righteousness.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا إذا لقيتم الذين كفروا زحفا فلا تولوهم الأدبار

translation: And who is more unjust than he who is reminded of the verses of his Lord, then turns away from them? Indeed, it is those who will lose themselves who refuse to engage with the signs of their Lord. And We will bring them, on the Day of Resurrection, to account in a way they will not be able to resist. Indeed, it is they who have lost themselves, and they are not the ones guided.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the fate of those who are reminded of the verses of their Lord, but then turn away from them. These people are described as being unjust and those who will ultimately lose themselves. The verse emphasizes the importance of engaging with the signs of God and warns of the consequences of ignoring them. The verse serves as a reminder that on the Day of Resurrection, those who turned away from the verses of God will be held accountable in a way they cannot resist. The verse serves as a warning to those who ignore the signs of God and a reminder of the importance of engaging with them.
orig: ومن يولهم يومئذ دبره إلا متحرفا لقتال أو متحيزا إلى فئة فقد باء بغضب من الله ومأواه جهنم وبئس المصير

translation: You did not kill them, but it was Allah who killed them; and you threw not, [O Muhammad], when you threw, but it was Allah who threw; and that He might test the believers by a beautiful trial from Him. Indeed, Allah is Hearing and Knowing.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes that it is ultimately God who has control over life and death, and that it is He who determines the outcome of events. The verse clarifies that the actions of the Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) are guided by God, and that it is God who is the true agent behind the events. The verse also highlights the wisdom of God's actions, as the events are described as a "beautiful trial" (حسنا) for the believers. The verse serves as a reminder of God's omnipotence and omniscience, and that all events, including the outcome of battles and conflicts, are determined by God's will.
orig: فلم تقتلوهم ولكن الله قتلهم وما رميت إذ رميت ولكن الله رمى وليبلي المؤمنين منه بلاء حسنا إن الله سميع عليم

translation: That is because Allah leaves astray the disbelievers
interpretation: The verse explains that the reason for a certain situation or outcome is because Allah allows the disbelievers to go astray. This implies that Allah guides those who are worthy of guidance and allows those who are not to go astray. It serves as a reminder that Allah is the ultimate controller of all actions and events, and that His will is always done.
orig: ذلكم وأن الله موهن كيد الكافرين

translation: If you (plural) help (in the cause of) Him, He will help you (plural) when you helped (Him). And if you turn away, He has no need of you. Indeed, Allah is independent of all creation. And if you help (in the cause of) Allah, He will help you and plant firmly your feet. But as for the disbelievers, they will be gathered into Hell.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the relationship between God and the believers, emphasizing that God will help those who help Him in His cause. The verse also highlights God's independence from His creation, reminding the believers that God does not need them, but they need Him. Furthermore, the verse promises that if the believers help God, He will help them and give them strength. However, those who do not believe will be punished and gathered into Hell. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of faith and action, and the consequences of disbelief and inaction.
orig: إن تستفتحوا فقد جاءكم الفتح وإن تنتهوا فهو خير لكم وإن تعودوا نعد ولن تغني عنكم فئتكم شيئا ولو كثرت وأن الله مع المؤمنين

translation: O you who have believed, obey Allah and His Messenger and do not turn away from him while you are hearing.
interpretation: The verse is a command to the believers to obey God and His Messenger, and not to turn away from him while they are hearing. The verse emphasizes the importance of obedience and attentiveness to the message of the Messenger, and the seriousness of turning away from it. The verse can be interpreted as a warning against distraction and heedlessness, and a call to pay attention and be mindful of the message of the Messenger. It also emphasizes the importance of obedience and submission to God and His Messenger as a fundamental aspect of faith.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا أطيعوا الله ورسوله ولا تولوا عنه وأنتم تسمعون

translation: And be not like those who say, 'We have heard,' while they hear not.
interpretation: The verse is a warning against hypocrisy and insincerity. It speaks about people who claim to have heard and understood, but in reality, they do not listen or make an effort to comprehend. This behavior is often seen in those who make a show of their faith, but do not truly believe or practice it. The verse serves as a reminder to truly listen, understand, and act upon the teachings of Islam, rather than simply paying lip service to it.
orig: ولا تكونوا كالذين قالوا سمعنا وهم لا يسمعون

translation: Indeed, the worst of living creatures in the sight of Allah are those who are deaf and dumb, who do not use their reason.
interpretation: The verse describes the worst type of creatures, from the perspective of God, as those who are deaf and dumb and do not use their reason. This description can be interpreted as a condemnation of those who are stubborn, close-minded, and refuse to use their intellect and understanding. These individuals are spiritually and morally bankrupt, and their inability to reason and understand prevents them from recognizing the truth and following the path of righteousness. This verse serves as a warning and a call for individuals to reflect on their actions, use their reason, and strive for spiritual growth and enlightenment.
orig: إن شر الدواب عند الله الصم البكم الذين لا يعقلون

translation: And if Allah had known any good in them, He would have made them hear. And if He had made them hear, they would have turned away, while they are disobedient.
interpretation: The verse speaks about Allah's knowledge of the true nature of people and His decision not to guide those who are undeserving of His guidance. The verse suggests that if Allah had found any goodness in them, He would have guided them. However, even if He had made them hear His message, they would have turned away from it. The verse highlights the fact that those who are disobedient and reject Allah's guidance will not be guided, no matter what means are used to guide them.
orig: ولو علم الله فيهم خيرا لأسمعهم ولو أسمعهم لتولوا وهم معرضون

translation: O you who have believed, respond to Allah and to the Messenger when he calls you to that which gives you life. And know that Allah intervenes between a man and his heart and that to Him you will be gathered.
interpretation: The verse commands the believers to respond to Allah and His Messenger when they are called upon to follow the path that leads to life. It emphasizes the importance of obedience and submission to the divine will. The verse also highlights the power and knowledge of Allah, who is able to intervene between a person and their own heart, and who will gather all of humanity on the Day of Judgment.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا استجيبوا لله وللرسول إذا دعاكم لما يحييكم واعلموا أن الله يحول بين المرء وقلبه وأنه إليه تحشرون

translation: And fear a trial which will not strike exclusively the wrongdoers among you and know that Allah is severe in punishment.
interpretation: The verse warns the listeners to be aware of a coming trial or test, which will not only affect the unjust among them, but may also affect the righteous. The verse emphasizes the severity of Allah's punishment and encourages the listeners to be mindful of their actions and to avoid wrongdoing. The verse serves as a reminder that no one is immune from the consequences of their actions and that Allah's punishment is severe.
orig: واتقوا فتنة لا تصيبن الذين ظلموا منكم خاصة واعلموا أن الله شديد العقاب

translation: And remember when you were few and helpless in the land, fearing that people might kidnap you, and He sheltered you, supported you with His victory, and provided you with good things, so that you might be grateful.
interpretation: The verse recounts a time when the early Muslims were a small and vulnerable community, fearing for their safety. Despite their weakness, God protected and supported them, providing them with resources and victory. The verse emphasizes the blessings and protection that God has bestowed upon the believers, and serves as a reminder to express gratitude for these blessings. It also highlights the theme of divine support and protection for the faithful, even in the face of adversity.
orig: واذكروا إذ أنتم قليل مستضعفون في الأرض تخافون أن يتخطفكم الناس فآواكم وأيدكم بنصره ورزقكم من الطيبات لعلكم تشكرون

translation: O you who have believed, do not betray Allah and the Messenger or knowingly betray your trusts.
interpretation: The verse addresses the believers and commands them not to betray Allah, the Messenger, or their trusts. The verse emphasizes the importance of honesty, integrity, and reliability in dealing with others and with the responsibilities that have been entrusted to them. The verse serves as a reminder that betraying trusts and commitments is a serious offense that goes against the teachings of Islam and the values of a believer.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تخونوا الله والرسول وتخونوا أماناتكم وأنتم تعلمون

translation: And know that your wealth and your children are a trial, and that surely with Allah is a great reward.
interpretation: The verse highlights the fact that wealth and children, which are often considered blessings, can also be a source of trial and temptation for humans. It reminds people that these worldly possessions are temporary and should not be the focus of one's life. Instead, the verse encourages believers to strive for the ultimate reward from Allah, which is much greater and everlasting. The verse serves as a reminder to maintain a balance between enjoying the blessings of this world and preparing for the hereafter.
orig: واعلموا أنما أموالكم وأولادكم فتنة وأن الله عنده أجر عظيم

translation: O you who have believed, if you fear Allah, He will make for you a distinction and will forgive for you your sins and will forgive for you your sins, and Allah is the possessor of great bounty.
interpretation: The verse addresses the believers and advises them to fear Allah, reminding them that if they do so, Allah will make a way out for them and will forgive their sins.
