The verse emphasizes the greatness of Allah's mercy and forgiveness, and encourages the believers to seek Allah's forgiveness and mercy through their obedience and fear of Him. The verse serves as a reminder that Allah is the most merciful and generous, and that He will always provide for and help those who turn to Him in repentance and fear.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا إن تتقوا الله يجعل لكم فرقانا ويكفر عنكم سيئاتكم ويغفر لكم والله ذو الفضل العظيم

translation: And when those who disbelieved plotted against you to either confine you or kill you or expel you. And they were plotting and Allah was plotting, but Allah is the best of plotters.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the plotting of the disbelievers against the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and their intentions to either confine, kill or expel him. However, the verse highlights that Allah is the best of plotters, indicating that the outcome of their plotting will not be in their favor. The verse serves as a reminder that those who plot against the believers and the messenger of Allah will face the consequences of their actions and that Allah's plan will always prevail.
orig: وإذ يمكر بك الذين كفروا ليثبتوك أو يقتلوك أو يخرجوك ويمكرون ويمكر الله والله خير الماكرين

translation: And when Our verses are recited to them, they say: 'We have heard this. If we willed, we could say something similar. This is nothing but tales of the ancients.'
interpretation: The verse describes the response of some people when they hear the verses (ayat) of the Qur'an being recited to them. Instead of accepting the message and reflecting on its meaning, they dismiss it by saying that they have heard it before and that they could come up with something similar if they wanted to. The verse suggests that these people view the Qur'an as just a collection of old stories or myths, rather than a revelation from God. The verse serves as a reminder that the Qur'an is not just a recitation, but a message that requires reflection and contemplation.
orig: وإذا تتلى عليهم آياتنا قالوا قد سمعنا لو نشاء لقلنا مثل هذا إن هذا إلا أساطير الأولين

translation: And when they said, 'O Allah, if this is the truth from You, then rain down upon us stones from the sky or bring upon us a painful punishment.'
interpretation: The verse describes the people's response to a message brought to them by a prophet. They demanded a sign from Allah, either in the form of stones raining down from the sky or a painful punishment. This verse highlights the people's disbelief and their rejection of the message brought to them. They asked for a dramatic and miraculous sign, rather than accepting the message through faith and reason. This verse serves as a reminder of the consequences of disbelief and the importance of accepting the truth with an open mind and heart.
orig: وإذ قالوا اللهم إن كان هذا هو الحق من عندك فأمطر علينا حجارة من السماء أو ائتنا بعذاب أليم

translation: And never will Allah punish them while you are among them, and Allah will not punish them while they seek forgiveness.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the protection of the believers from God's punishment while they are among them, and the mercy of God towards those who seek forgiveness. The verse emphasizes the mercy and compassion of God towards his believers, and the importance of seeking forgiveness. The verse serves as a source of comfort and reassurance to the believers, reminding them of the mercy and protection of God, and encouraging them to continuously seek forgiveness for their sins and mistakes.
orig: وما كان الله ليعذبهم وأنت فيهم وما كان الله معذبهم وهم يستغفرون

translation: But what is [the matter] with them that they are, from the Reminder, turning away? And when they are reminded, they do not remember. And when they see a sign, they ridicule it. And they say, 'This is not but obvious magic. And when we are dutiful, it is not that we will be punished.', So they are unaware.
interpretation: The verse criticizes the people for turning away from the Reminder (the Qur'an) and not remembering it when they are reminded. It also mentions their disbelief and mockery of the signs of God. The verse emphasizes the people's lack of understanding and awareness of the consequences of their actions, specifically their belief that they will not be punished for their disbelief and disobedience. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of paying attention to the signs of God, and the consequences of ignoring them.
orig: وما لهم ألا يعذبهم الله وهم يصدون عن المسجد الحرام وما كانوا أولياءه إن أولياؤه إلا المتقون ولكن أكثرهم لا يعلمون

translation: And their prayer at the House was nothing but whistling and clapping. So taste the punishment because of what you used to deny.
interpretation: The verse describes the disbelievers' actions during their pilgrimage to the Kaaba, the House of God, where their prayers were nothing but meaningless sounds, such as whistling and clapping. The verse then announces the punishment that they will receive as a result of their disbelief and denial of God's signs. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of sincerity and reverence in prayer and the consequences of disbelief and hypocrisy.
orig: وما كان صلاتهم عند البيت إلا مكاء وتصدية فذوقوا العذاب بما كنتم تكفرون

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve spend their wealth to prevent (people) from the path of Allah. So they will spend it; then it will be for them a regret, and then they will be overcome. And indeed, those who disbelieve - to Hell they will be gathered.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the actions of those who disbelieve in God and how they spend their wealth in order to prevent people from following the path of God. However, their efforts will ultimately be in vain, as they will come to regret their actions and be overcome. The verse ends by stating that those who disbelieve will be gathered in Hell, emphasizing the consequences of their disbelief and actions.
orig: إن الذين كفروا ينفقون أموالهم ليصدوا عن سبيل الله فسينفقونها ثم تكون عليهم حسرة ثم يغلبون والذين كفروا إلى جهنم يحشرون

translation: Allah will distinguish the wicked from the good and will place the wicked, one on top of another, and then heap them all together in Hell. They will be the ones who have lost.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the Day of Judgment, when Allah will distinguish between the righteous and the wicked. The wicked will be placed one on top of another and then thrown into Hell. This image emphasizes the severity of the punishment that awaits the wicked and the complete destruction of those who have chosen a life of sin and injustice. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living a life of immorality and oppression, urging them to repent and change their ways before it is too late.
orig: ليميز الله الخبيث من الطيب ويجعل الخبيث بعضه على بعض فيركمه جميعا فيجعله في جهنم أولئك هم الخاسرون

translation: Say to the disbelievers: 'If they cease (from disbelief), their past will be forgiven. But if they return (to disbelief), then the example of the previous nations has already passed.'
interpretation: The verse addresses the disbelievers and offers them a chance for forgiveness if they stop their disbelief. However, if they persist in their disbelief, then they will face the consequences, just like the previous nations that have already passed. The verse emphasizes the importance of repentance and the consequences of not taking the opportunity for forgiveness.
orig: قل للذين كفروا إن ينتهوا يغفر لهم ما قد سلف وإن يعودوا فقد مضت سنت الأولين

translation: Fight them until there is no fitnah, and [until] the religion, all of it, is for Allah. And if they cease - then indeed, Allah is Seeing of what they do.
interpretation: The verse speaks about fighting against the unbelievers until there is no more fitnah (temptation or trial) and the religion is solely for Allah. This means that the fighting will continue until the unbelievers are either defeated or submit to Islamic rule. The verse emphasizes the importance of fighting against those who stand in the way of the spread of Islam. However, if the unbelievers cease their opposition, then Allah is all-knowing and sees all that they do, implying that they will be held accountable for their actions. The verse can be interpreted as a call to spread Islam and establish its dominance, with the use of force if necessary.
orig: وقاتلوهم حتى لا تكون فتنة ويكون الدين كله لله فإن انتهوا فإن الله بما يعملون بصير

translation: But if they turn away, then know that Allah is your protector. Excellent is the protector, and Excellent is the helper.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the role of Allah as a protector and helper for those who believe. The verse states that if the people reject the message, then they should know that Allah is their protector and helper. This statement emphasizes the idea that even if the people reject the message, Allah is still there to support and protect the believers. The verse also highlights the excellent qualities of Allah as a protector and helper, emphasizing the idea that Allah is the best and most reliable protector and helper that one can have. The verse serves as a source of comfort and reassurance for the believers, reminding them that Allah is always there for them, no matter what.
orig: وإن تولوا فاعلموا أن الله مولاكم نعم المولى ونعم النصير

translation: And know that whatever of a thing you gain, a fifth of it is for Allah and for the Messenger and for the near of kin and the orphans and the needy and the wayfarer, if you believe in Allah and the Last Day. And Allah is over all things competent.
interpretation: The verse outlines the distribution of war booty and emphasizes the importance of giving a portion of it to the needy and the vulnerable members of society. The verse begins by stating that whatever one gains, a fifth of it belongs to Allah, the Messenger, the relatives, the orphans, the needy, and the traveler. The verse then reiterates the importance of believing in Allah and the Day of Judgment. The verse concludes by emphasizing Allah's power and control over all things, reminding the believers of the ultimate authority and justice of Allah.
orig: واعلموا أنما غنمتم من شيء فأن لله خمسه وللرسول ولذي القربى واليتامى والمساكين وابن السبيل إن كنتم آمنتم بالله وما أنزلنا على عبدنا يوم الفرقان يوم التقى الجمعان والله على كل شيء قدير

translation: When you were on the nearer bank and they were on the yonder bank, and the caravan was lower than you. If you had made an appointment, you would have certainly failed in the appointment. But (it was ordained) that Allah might accomplish a matter already ordained (in His Knowledge); so that He might cause to perish those who perished by a clear proof and establish those who lived by a clear proof. Surely Allah is All-hearing, All-knowing.
interpretation: The verse describes a situation where two groups are separated by some distance, and one group is lower in position than the other. If the two groups had made an appointment to meet, they would have failed to keep it. But, the verse explains that God had a pre-ordained plan that had to be fulfilled. This plan involved the destruction of some people by a clear proof (of God's power), and the survival of others by a clear proof (of God's mercy). The verse emphasizes that God is all-hearing and all-knowing, implying that everything that happens is part of God's plan and that God has complete knowledge of all things.
orig: إذ أنتم بالعدوة الدنيا وهم بالعدوة القصوى والركب أسفل منكم ولو تواعدتم لاختلفتم في الميعاد ولكن ليقضي الله أمرا كان مفعولا ليهلك من هلك عن بينة ويحيى من حي عن بينة وإن الله لسميع عليم

translation: When God shows them to you in your dreams as few; if He showed them to you as many, you would have faltered and quarreled, and there is no doubt in that. But God has spared you, for He knows the secrets of the hearts.
interpretation: The verse speaks about a situation where God shows the disbelievers to the believers in their dreams as a small group, but if they were to see them in reality as a large group, they would have faltered and quarreled. The verse highlights the mercy and knowledge of God, who spares the believers from the fear and confusion that would result from seeing the disbelievers in large numbers. The verse emphasizes the importance of trust in God's knowledge and wisdom, and the importance of relying on Him in all situations, even when faced with overwhelming odds.
orig: إذ يريكهم الله في منامك قليلا ولو أراكهم كثيرا لفشلتم ولتنازعتم في الأمر ولكن الله سلم إنه عليم بذات الصدور

translation: And when you meet them, they seem to be few and you seem to be few, but Allah is the one to decide between you, and to Allah will be the return.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the uncertainty and unpredictability of battles or conflicts. When two sides meet, each side may perceive the other as small in number, but it is ultimately up to God to decide the outcome. The verse reminds the believers that despite their efforts, the outcome of battles or conflicts is ultimately in God's hands. The verse also emphasizes the importance of trusting in God's will and returning to Him as the ultimate judge and decision-maker.
orig: وإذ يريكموهم إذ التقيتم في أعينكم قليلا ويقللكم في أعينهم ليقضي الله أمرا كان مفعولا وإلى الله ترجع الأمور

translation: O believers, when you encounter a faction, then stand firm and remember Allah much that you may prosper.
interpretation: This verse is a command to the believers to be steadfast and maintain their ground when they encounter an opposing faction. It also advises them to remember and worship God excessively, emphasizing the importance of faith and devotion during times of conflict. The verse aims to instill a sense of confidence and resilience in the believers, encouraging them to rely on their faith and the power of God to overcome any challenges they face.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا إذا لقيتم فئة فاثبتوا واذكروا الله كثيرا لعلكم تفلحون

translation: And obey Allah and His Messenger and do not dispute and you will succeed. And be patient, indeed Allah is with the patient.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of obedience to Allah and His Messenger and the dangers of disputes and disagreements among people. By following these commands, the verse promises success. The verse also encourages patience, highlighting that Allah is with those who are patient. The verse can be seen as a call for unity and obedience among the Muslim community and a reminder of the rewards of patience and perseverance.
orig: وأطيعوا الله ورسوله ولا تنازعوا فتفشلوا وتذهب ريحكم واصبروا إن الله مع الصابرين

translation: And be not like those who came out of their homes boastfully and to be seen of men, and hinder (men) from the way of Allah. And Allah is encompassing what they do.
interpretation: The verse warns against behaving like the people who leave their homes ostentatiously and to be seen by others, while preventing others from following the path of God. The verse emphasizes that God is all-knowing and encompassing of all that they do, and will hold them accountable for their actions. The verse serves as a reminder to act with sincerity and humility, and not for the sake of gaining recognition or praise from others. It also highlights the importance of not hindering others from practicing their faith and following the path of God.
orig: ولا تكونوا كالذين خرجوا من ديارهم بطرا ورئاء الناس ويصدون عن سبيل الله والله بما يعملون محيط

translation: And when the devil adorned for them their deeds and said, 'No one can overcome you today, and indeed, I am your protector.' But when the two hosts saw each other, he turned on his heels and said, 'Indeed, I am free of you. Indeed, I see what you do not see. Indeed, I fear Allah, and Allah is severe in punishment.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the moment when the devil deceives people into thinking that they are invincible and that he is their protector. However, when the two armies face each other, the devil immediately abandons them, showing his true nature as a deceiver. The verse highlights the fleeting nature of worldly alliances and the ultimate power of God, who is the only one who can truly protect and help. The verse serves as a reminder that the devil is always looking for ways to deceive people and lead them astray, and that true protection and guidance can only come from God. The verse also emphasizes the importance of fearing God and being aware of one's actions, as God is severe in punishment.
orig: وإذ زين لهم الشيطان أعمالهم وقال لا غالب لكم اليوم من الناس وإني جار لكم فلما تراءت الفئتان نكص على عقبيه وقال إني بريء منكم إني أرى ما لا ترون إني أخاف الله والله شديد العقاب

translation: When the hypocrites and those in whose hearts is a disease say, 'These people are deceived by their religion.' But whoever puts their trust in Allah - indeed, Allah is Exalted in Might and Wise.
interpretation: The verse highlights the attitude of hypocrites and those who harbor ill-feelings towards those who truly believe. They accuse the believers of being misguided in their faith. However, the verse emphasizes the power and wisdom of Allah, and encourages trust in Him. The verse serves as a reminder that true believers should not be swayed by the criticisms and accusations of those who do not truly believe and instead place their trust in Allah, who is all-powerful and wise.
orig: إذ يقول المنافقون والذين في قلوبهم مرض غر هؤلاء دينهم ومن يتوكل على الله فإن الله عزيز حكيم

translation: And if you could see when the disbelievers are made to stand before the angels, they are striking their faces and their backs, and tasting the punishment of the Blaze.
interpretation: The verse describes the fate of the disbelievers on the Day of Judgment. They will be made to stand before the angels, who will mete out punishment by striking their faces and their backs. The disbelievers will also taste the punishment of the Blaze, indicating the severity and intensity of the punishment they will receive. The verse serves as a warning to those who reject faith and reminds them of the consequences of their disbelief.
orig: ولو ترى إذ يتوفى الذين كفروا الملائكة يضربون وجوههم وأدبارهم وذوقوا عذاب الحريق

translation: That is because of what your hands have sent forth, and because Allah is not unjust to the servants.
interpretation: The verse explains that people's actions have consequences and that what they do will ultimately come back to them. This is followed by the reassurance that God is not unjust and that He will treat His servants fairly. The verse highlights the importance of taking responsibility for one's actions, and the justice of God in dealing with people based on their deeds.
orig: ذلك بما قدمت أيديكم وأن الله ليس بظلام للعبيد

translation: Thus it was, but We made them leaders inviting to the Fire; and on the Day of Judgment, wrath and torment will touch them first.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the leaders of Pharaoh and those before them who rejected the signs of God. These leaders are described as inviting others to the Fire, meaning they are leading people towards punishment. The verse warns that on the Day of Judgment, wrath and torment will first touch them. This interpretation highlights the consequences of leading others astray and the severe punishment that awaits those who reject God's signs and guidance.
orig: كدأب آل فرعون والذين من قبلهم كفروا بآيات الله فأخذهم الله بذنوبهم إن الله قوي شديد العقاب

translation: That is because God does not change the grace that He has bestowed upon a people until they change what is in themselves. And God is All-Hearing, All-Knowing.
interpretation: The verse explains that God does not alter the blessings and favors that He has given to a people until they change their own actions and behavior. This implies that people have the power and the ability to change their circumstances through their own actions. The verse also emphasizes that God is All-Hearing and All-Knowing, meaning that He is aware of all that we do and say, and that He will ultimately hold us accountable for our actions.
orig: ذلك بأن الله لم يك مغيرا نعمة أنعمها على قوم حتى يغيروا ما بأنفسهم وأن الله سميع عليم

translation: Thus did Pharaoh and those before him deny the signs of their Lord. So We punished them for their sins, and We drowned the people of Pharaoh. And they were all wrongdoers.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the denial of Pharaoh and those before him of the signs of their Lord, and the punishment they received for their sins. The verse emphasizes the consequences of denying the signs of God and the punishment that follows. The drowning of the people of Pharaoh serves as an example of the ultimate fate of those who reject the signs of God. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of recognizing and accepting the signs of God, and the consequences of denying them.
orig: كدأب آل فرعون والذين من قبلهم كذبوا بآيات ربهم فأهلكناهم بذنوبهم وأغرقنا آل فرعون وكل كانوا ظالمين

translation: Indeed, the worst of creatures in the sight of Allah are those who disbelieve - they will not believe.
interpretation: The verse highlights the gravity of disbelief in the sight of God, stating that those who reject faith are the 'worst of creatures'. The repetition of the word 'believe' emphasizes the firm rejection of faith by these individuals. This verse serves as a reminder of the serious consequences of disbelief and the importance of faith in God.
orig: إن شر الدواب عند الله الذين كفروا فهم لا يؤمنون

translation: Those who have broken their covenant with Me, though indeed, they had understood its terms.
interpretation: The verse speaks about individuals who have willfully and knowingly broken their covenant or agreement with God. These individuals had a clear understanding of the terms and conditions of the covenant, yet they still chose to disregard it. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of upholding one's commitments and honoring one's word, and highlights the consequences of betraying the trust of God.
orig: الذين عاهدت منهم ثم ينقضون عهدهم في كل مرة وهم لا يتقون

translation: But if you meet them in battle, then beware of them, perhaps you may fear them, and this may remind them.
interpretation: The verse gives guidance to Muslims when they encounter enemies in battle. It advises them to be cautious and careful, as the enemy can be dangerous. The verse suggests that this fear may lead the enemies to remember and reflect on their actions, potentially leading to a change of heart. This interpretation highlights the importance of maintaining a strong and vigilant stance in the face of adversity, while also leaving room for the possibility of repentance and change in the hearts of the enemies.
orig: فإما تثقفنهم في الحرب فشرد بهم من خلفهم لعلهم يذكرون

translation: But if you fear betrayal from a people, then throw their treaty to them openly. Indeed, Allah does not like the deceitful.
interpretation: The verse provides guidance on how to handle a situation where one fears betrayal from a people with whom a treaty has been made. The instruction is to 'throw their treaty to them openly', which can be interpreted as a call to end the agreement and make it clear that the relationship has ended. The verse emphasizes the importance of honesty and integrity in all interactions and warns against deceit. The verse serves as a reminder that God does not approve of those who are deceitful and untrustworthy.
orig: وإما تخافن من قوم خيانة فانبذ إليهم على سواء إن الله لا يحب الخائنين

translation: And let not the unbelievers think they can outstrip (Us): surely they cannot escape.
interpretation: The verse warns the unbelievers not to think that they can escape or avoid the consequences of their disbelief and rejection of God's message. The verse emphasizes that they cannot outrun or outwit God, and that their attempts to do so are futile. The verse serves as a reminder that God's power and knowledge are all-encompassing, and that those who reject His message will ultimately face His judgment.
orig: ولا يحسبن الذين كفروا سبقوا إنهم لا يعجزون

translation: And prepare against them whatever you are able of power and of steeds of war by which you may terrify the enemy of Allah and your enemy and others besides them whom you do not know [but] Allah knows. And whatever you spend in the cause of Allah, He will compensate it for you, and you will not be wronged.
interpretation: The verse encourages believers to prepare themselves militarily against the enemies of Allah and their own enemies, as well as others who are unknown to them but known to Allah. This preparation is to be done through the use of power and war horses, in order to instill fear in the hearts of the enemies. The verse also promises that any expenses incurred in the cause of Allah will be reimbursed and that believers will not be wronged. The verse emphasizes the importance of taking action and being prepared in the face of adversity and danger, and the promise of divine reward and justice for those who do so.
orig: وأعدوا لهم ما استطعتم من قوة ومن رباط الخيل ترهبون به عدو الله وعدوكم وآخرين من دونهم لا تعلمونهم الله يعلمهم وما تنفقوا من شيء في سبيل الله يوف إليكم وأنتم لا تظلمون

translation: And if they incline to peace, then incline to it [also] and rely upon Allah. Indeed, it is He who is the Hearing, the Knowing.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the importance of responding to calls for peace and reconciliation. If the other party is willing to make peace, then the believer should also be willing to do the same. The verse emphasizes the importance of relying on God in all matters, as He is the All-Hearing and All-Knowing. This verse can serve as a reminder to be open to peace and to trust in God's guidance and wisdom in all situations.
orig: وإن جنحوا للسلم فاجنح لها وتوكل على الله إنه هو السميع العليم

translation: But if they intend to deceive you, then indeed Allah is sufficient for you. It is He who supported you with His help and with the believers.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the protection and support that believers receive from God when facing deceit and treachery from others. The verse emphasizes that God's help and support is sufficient for the believers, and that they should not fear or be intimidated by the deceit of others. The verse serves as a reminder that God is always on the side of the believers and that they can always rely on His help and support. The verse also highlights the importance of unity and solidarity among the believers, who stand together in the face of adversity and deception.
orig: وإن يريدوا أن يخدعوك فإن حسبك الله هو الذي أيدك بنصره وبالمؤمنين

translation: And if you had spent all that is in the earth, you could not have united their hearts, but Allah has united them. Indeed, He is Exalted in Might and Wise.
interpretation: The verse highlights the power of God in bringing people together and uniting their hearts. The verse emphasizes that no amount of wealth or resources could have achieved this unity, if it was not for God's will. The verse serves as a reminder of God's power and wisdom, and the limitations of human abilities. It also emphasizes the importance of seeking God's help and guidance in bringing about unity and harmony among people.
orig: وألف بين قلوبهم لو أنفقت ما في الأرض جميعا ما ألفت بين قلوبهم ولكن الله ألف بينهم إنه عزيز حكيم

translation: O Prophet, sufficient for you is God and those who follow you among the believers.
interpretation: The verse is a source of comfort and reassurance for the Prophet Muhammad, indicating that God and his followers are sufficient for him. The verse emphasizes the importance of having a strong faith and a supportive community, and it implies that the Prophet should not be concerned about those who reject his message. The verse can also be seen as a reminder for Muslims to support and follow the example of the Prophet, and to have faith in God during times of hardship and adversity.
orig: يا أيها النبي حسبك الله ومن اتبعك من المؤمنين

translation: O Prophet, urge the believers to fight. If there are among you twenty [who are] steadfast, they will overcome two hundred. And if there are among you one hundred [who are] steadfast, they will overcome a thousand of those who have disbelieved because they are a people who do not understand.
interpretation: The verse is a command from God to the Prophet Muhammad to urge the believers to fight. The verse emphasizes the importance of steadfastness and perseverance, stating that even a small group of believers can defeat a larger group of disbelievers if they are steadfast. The verse also highlights the lack of understanding and wisdom among the disbelievers. The verse serves as a reminder to the believers of their strength and ability to overcome their enemies if they remain steadfast and united.
orig: يا أيها النبي حرض المؤمنين على القتال إن يكن منكم عشرون صابرون يغلبوا مائتين وإن يكن منكم مائة يغلبوا ألفا من الذين كفروا بأنهم قوم لا يفقهون

translation: Now Allah has lightened your burden, for He knows that you are weak. So if there are among you one hundred steadfast ones, they will overcome two hundred. And if there are among you one thousand, they will overcome two thousand by Allah's leave. And Allah is with the steadfast.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the mercy of God and His understanding of the weakness of His believers. It explains that even if the believers are outnumbered, they can still overcome their enemies if they are steadfast and patient. The verse emphasizes the importance of patience and perseverance in the face of adversity and the promise of God's help and support for those who remain steadfast. The verse serves as a source of encouragement and motivation for the believers, emphasizing that through their patience and perseverance, they can overcome any obstacle and achieve victory.
orig: الآن خفف الله عنكم وعلم أن فيكم ضعفا فإن يكن منكم مائة صابرة يغلبوا مائتين وإن يكن منكم ألف يغلبوا ألفين بإذن الله والله مع الصابرين

translation: It is not (possible) for any prophet to deceive (or be unfaithful to his trust) so as to bring about evil in the land, because if he does this, he will be dealing falsely with respect to the revelations of Allah. And We (Allah) would surely seal up the heart of the one (prophet) who does this, so he would not be able to guide (people) aright. But this (story) is a reminder, and verily, for every evildoer, there is a punishment (in this life and in the Hereafter),
interpretation: The verse highlights the importance of trust and honesty for prophets, stating that it is not possible for a prophet to deceive or act unfaithfully. If a prophet were to do so, they would be acting falsely towards the revelations of Allah and would have their heart sealed, preventing them from guiding people. The verse serves as a reminder that there are consequences for wrongdoing and that every evildoer will face punishment, both in this life and in the Hereafter.
orig: ما كان لنبي أن يكون له أسرى حتى يثخن في الأرض تريدون عرض الدنيا والله يريد الآخرة والله عزيز حكيم

translation: Had it not been for the Book from Allah, they would have judged you in the matter of the dispute. Then indeed, there would have been about you a great punishment.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the importance of the guidance provided by the word of God in resolving disputes and preventing harm. Without the guidance of the Book (presumably referring to the Qur'an), people would have judged each other unfairly and harshly, leading to a great punishment. The verse highlights the importance of adhering to the teachings of the Qur'an and using it as a guide in all aspects of life, in order to avoid the consequences of straying from the right path.
orig: لولا كتاب من الله سبق لمسكم فيما أخذتم عذاب عظيم

translation: And eat of that which is lawful and good on the earth, and do not follow the footsteps of Satan. Indeed, he is to you a clear enemy. And eat of that which Allah has provided for you and be grateful to Allah, if it is [indeed] Him that you worship.
interpretation: The verse encourages believers to eat from the good and lawful provisions on earth, while warning them against following the ways of Satan, who is their clear enemy. The verse also reminds them to be thankful for the sustenance that God has provided for them, if they truly worship Him. The verse emphasizes the importance of obedience to God's commands, gratitude, and avoiding the temptations of Satan. It serves as a reminder to live a righteous life and to be mindful of one's actions and motivations.
orig: فكلوا مما غنمتم حلالا طيبا واتقوا الله إن الله غفور رحيم

translation: O Prophet, say to those who are in your hands [captives of war] from the disbelievers: If Allah knows within yourselves any good, He will give you [something] better than what has been taken from you and will forgive you, and Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse addresses the Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) and instructs him to convey a message to the captives of war who are in the Muslims' possession. The message is that if the captives possess any good within themselves, meaning if they have faith or good deeds, then God will give them something better than their freedom and possessions that were taken from them. Additionally, God will forgive them. This verse highlights the infinite mercy and generosity of God, and encourages the believers to be kind and merciful to the captives, even in times of war. It also encourages the captives to have hope in God's mercy and forgiveness.
orig: يا أيها النبي قل لمن في أيديكم من الأسرى إن يعلم الله في قلوبكم خيرا يؤتكم خيرا مما أخذ منكم ويغفر لكم والله غفور رحيم

translation: And if they intend to deceive you, then indeed they have already deceived themselves, and Allah is sufficient for you; and He is the best of helpers.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the situation where people may have the intention to deceive or betray someone. However, the verse reassures that if that is the case, then they have already wronged and deceived themselves first. The verse emphasizes that God is sufficient as a protector and helper, and that He is the best and wisest of helpers. The verse serves as a reminder that those who intend to harm or deceive others will ultimately harm and deceive themselves, and that God will always be there to protect and help those who remain faithful and true.
orig: وإن يريدوا خيانتك فقد خانوا الله من قبل فأمكن منهم والله عليم حكيم

translation: Indeed, those who have believed and emigrated and fought with their wealth and lives in the cause of Allah and those who gave shelter and aided - they are allies of one another. But those who believed and did not emigrate - for you there is no responsibility until they emigrate. And if they seek help of you for the religion, then upon you is assistance, except against a people between you and whom is a treaty. And Allah is Seeing of what you do.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the relationship between believers who have emigrated and fought for the cause of Allah, those who gave them shelter and support, and those who believed but did not emigrate. The verse highlights the bond of brotherhood and mutual support among the believers who have emigrated and those who gave them shelter and aid. However, the verse also makes it clear that those who believed but did not emigrate do not have the same level of responsibility towards the believers as those who have emigrated. The verse also emphasizes the importance of helping and supporting the believers in their struggle for the religion, except when there is a treaty with the people who are fighting against them. The verse reminds the believers of the importance of their actions, as Allah is watching over them.
orig: إن الذين آمنوا وهاجروا وجاهدوا بأموالهم وأنفسهم في سبيل الله والذين آووا ونصروا أولئك بعضهم أولياء بعض والذين آمنوا ولم يهاجروا ما لكم من ولايتهم من شيء حتى يهاجروا وإن استنصروكم في الدين فعليكم النصر إلا على قوم بينكم وبينهم ميثاق والله بما تعملون بصير

translation: And those who disbelieve are allies of one another, except against you, (O Muhammad), and except those among them who are allies againts you out of fear because their people would otherwise put them to punishment. And Allah warns you of Himself, and to Allah is the final destination.
interpretation: The verse highlights the alliances among the disbelievers and emphasizes their opposition towards the believers. However, there are some who secretly support the believers due to fear of retribution from their own people. The verse serves as a warning from Allah, reminding that He is aware of all actions and that everyone will return to Him. The verse may also suggest that such alliances and conflicts are a trial and source of corruption in the world, and that true security and safety can only be found in Allah.
orig: والذين كفروا بعضهم أولياء بعض إلا تفعلوه تكن فتنة في الأرض وفساد كبير

translation: And those who believe and emigrate and strive in the cause of Allah and those who give shelter and help, they are the true believers, for them is forgiveness and a generous provision.
interpretation: The verse highlights the qualities of true believers in Islam, who not only believe in Allah but also take action by emigrating, striving, providing shelter and helping in the cause of Allah. These actions demonstrate their commitment and dedication to their faith. As a reward for their faith and actions, they are promised forgiveness and a generous provision in this world and the hereafter. The verse encourages Muslims to not only have faith but also to actively work towards promoting and establishing it, and assures them of Allah's mercy and generosity.
orig: والذين آمنوا وهاجروا وجاهدوا في سبيل الله والذين آووا ونصروا أولئك هم المؤمنون حقا لهم مغفرة ورزق كريم

translation: And those who believed and emigrated and fought with you, they are your kinfolk. And Allah is well-aware of the relations between (all of) you. Surely, Allah is All-Knowing.
interpretation: The verse highlights the bond between the believers who emigrated and fought alongside the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). These believers are considered as kinfolk and their relationship is recognized by Allah. The verse emphasizes the importance of unity and brotherhood among the believers. It also indicates that Allah is well-aware of the relationships between all believers, and He is the All-Knowing, who sees and knows all.
orig: والذين آمنوا من بعد وهاجروا وجاهدوا معكم فأولئك منكم وأولو الأرحام بعضهم أولى ببعض في كتاب الله إن الله بكل شيء عليم

translation: Freedom from God and His Messenger to those of you who have entered into a covenant with the polytheists.
interpretation: The verse grants freedom from God and His Messenger to those who had entered into a covenant with the polytheists. This verse was revealed in the context of the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah, where the Muslims were given permission to abandon their pledge of allegiance to the polytheists and break free from their obligations towards them. The verse emphasizes the importance of upholding one's faith and loyalty to God and His Messenger above all other commitments, and the freedom that comes with this unwavering commitment.
orig: براءة من الله ورسوله إلى الذين عاهدتم من المشركين

translation: They will have the power of the earth for four months, and know that Allah will not fail in His promise but will disgrace the unbelievers.
interpretation: The verse speaks about a period of time, during which the unbelievers will have control and power over the earth for four months. However, the verse also reminds them that this power is temporary and that they should not be deluded by it. The verse emphasizes that Allah's promise will be fulfilled and that the unbelievers will ultimately be disgraced and defeated. The verse serves as a reminder to the believers to remain steadfast and patient in the face of adversity and to trust in Allah's ultimate victory over the unbelievers.
orig: فسيحوا في الأرض أربعة أشهر واعلموا أنكم غير معجزي الله وأن الله مخزي الكافرين

translation: And an announcement from Allah and His Messenger to the people on the Day of the Great Pilgrimage that Allah is disassociated from the polytheists, and [so is] His Messenger. So if you repent, it is better for you; but if you turn away - then know that you are not associators of Allah's power. And give good tidings to the disbelievers of a painful punishment.
interpretation: The verse announces Allah's and His Messenger's disassociation from the polytheists on the Day of the Great Pilgrimage. The verse gives the people a choice between repentance and continuation of their disbelief. If they choose to repent, it will be better for them. However, if they persist in their disbelief, they will be informed that they cannot associate themselves with Allah's power. The verse ends with a warning of a painful punishment for the disbelievers, emphasizing the consequences of their rejection of faith.
orig: وأذان من الله ورسوله إلى الناس يوم الحج الأكبر أن الله بريء من المشركين ورسوله فإن تبتم فهو خير لكم وإن توليتم فاعلموا أنكم غير معجزي الله وبشر الذين كفروا بعذاب أليم

translation: Except those of the polytheists with whom you have a treaty, and who have not broken their treaty with you nor have supported anyone against you. So fulfill their treaty to them to the end of their term. Indeed, Allah loves those who fear Him.
interpretation: This verse outlines the proper treatment of polytheists with whom a treaty has been made. As long as these polytheists uphold their end of the treaty, not harming or supporting enemies against the believers, the believers are to uphold their end of the treaty as well. This verse emphasizes the importance of honoring one's commitments and demonstrating respect and fairness towards others, even those of different religious beliefs. The verse also highlights the value of piety and fear of God in the eyes of the believers.
orig: إلا الذين عاهدتم من المشركين ثم لم ينقصوكم شيئا ولم يظاهروا عليكم أحدا فأتموا إليهم عهدهم إلى مدتهم إن الله يحب المتقين

translation: But when the forbidden months have passed, then kill the polytheists wherever you find them and capture them and besiege them and sit in wait for them at every lookout post. But if they repent, establish prayer, and give zakah, let them go on their way. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: The verse outlines the treatment of polytheists after the end of the forbidden months. It instructs Muslims to fight against them wherever they are found, capture them, and besiege them. However, if the polytheists repent, establish prayer, and give zakah (charity), then Muslims are to leave them alone. The verse emphasizes the importance of submission to God and the establishment of prayer and charity as a means of avoiding conflict and obtaining forgiveness from God.
orig: فإذا انسلخ الأشهر الحرم فاقتلوا المشركين حيث وجدتموهم وخذوهم واحصروهم واقعدوا لهم كل مرصد فإن تابوا وأقاموا الصلاة وآتوا الزكاة فخلوا سبيلهم إن الله غفور رحيم

translation: And if one of the polytheists seeks your protection, grant him protection so that he may hear the words of Allah. Then deliver him to his place of safety - that is because they are a people who do not know.
interpretation: The verse outlines the proper treatment of a polytheist who seeks protection from a Muslim. The Muslim is instructed to grant the polytheist protection and allow him to hear the words of Allah, which is likely a reference to the Quran. After this, the polytheist is to be returned to a place of safety. The verse explains that this is necessary because the polytheists are a people who lack knowledge or understanding. This verse can be seen as an example of the Quran's emphasis on compassion and protection towards all people, even those who hold different beliefs.
orig: وإن أحد من المشركين استجارك فأجره حتى يسمع كلام الله ثم أبلغه مأمنه ذلك بأنهم قوم لا يعلمون

translation: How can there be a covenant for the polytheists with Allah and His Messenger, except those who have earned your grudge - so as long as they are upright toward you, be upright toward them. Indeed, Allah loves the righteous -
interpretation: The verse speaks about the impossibility of a covenant between the polytheists and Allah and His Messenger, with the exception of those who have earned the believers' grudge. The verse emphasizes the importance of fairness and uprightness towards these exceptions as long as they remain upright towards the believers. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of maintaining just and fair relationships with others, even if they have different beliefs, and the value of righteousness in the eyes of Allah.
orig: كيف يكون للمشركين عهد عند الله وعند رسوله إلا الذين عاهدتم عند المسجد الحرام فما استقاموا لكم فاستقيموا لهم إن الله يحب المتقين

translation: And if they had shown you (O Muhammad) the outward respect which they outwardly pretend, but Allah does not guide the people who are transgressors unjust.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the hypocrisy of certain people who outwardly show respect to the Prophet Muhammad, but inwardly they do not believe and are unjust. The verse emphasizes that God does not guide such people who are transgressors and unjust. The verse serves as a reminder that outward actions alone are not enough and that inner belief and righteousness are also necessary. It also serves as a warning to those who pretend to be righteous but are not, that God sees their true intentions and will not be deceived by their false displays of respect.
orig: كيف وإن يظهروا عليكم لا يرقبوا فيكم إلا ولا ذمة يرضونكم بأفواههم وتأبى قلوبهم وأكثرهم فاسقون

translation: And buy with the signs of Allah a slight price and turn away from His way; surely they are evil-doers.
interpretation: The verse is a condemnation of those who reject the signs of Allah (i.e. His revelations) and turn away from His way, in exchange for a small and temporary gain. The verse emphasizes the wickedness of their actions, as they prioritize worldly gains over the path of Allah. The verse serves as a reminder that true success and happiness can only be achieved by following the path of Allah, and that those who reject His signs and prioritize worldly gains will ultimately be unsuccessful.
orig: اشتروا بآيات الله ثمنا قليلا فصدوا عن سبيله إنهم ساء ما كانوا يعملون

translation: They do not observe taqwa in relation to a believer except with suspicion, and these are the transgressors.
interpretation: The verse addresses those who harbor suspicion and mistrust towards believers, and are constantly on the lookout for any wrongdoing on their part. The verse labels such individuals as transgressors, highlighting the negative consequences of their actions. This verse emphasizes the importance of trust and goodwill towards fellow believers and warns against baseless suspicion and mistrust, which can lead to transgression and harm.
orig: لا يرقبون في مؤمن إلا ولا ذمة وأولئك هم المعتدون

translation: But if they repent and establish prayer and give zakah, then they are your brothers in religion. And We detail the signs for a people who know.
interpretation: The verse provides a way for the disbelievers to be reconciled with the believers. If they repent from their disbelief, establish prayer, and give zakah (charity), then they will become brothers in religion with the believers. This verse emphasizes the importance of repentance, prayer, and charity in the path towards becoming part of the Muslim community. The verse also highlights that the signs (ayat) are detailed for a people who have knowledge, indicating that the message is intended for those who are willing and able to understand and reflect upon the meaning of the revelation.
orig: فإن تابوا وأقاموا الصلاة وآتوا الزكاة فإخوانكم في الدين ونفصل الآيات لقوم يعلمون

translation: And if they break their oaths after their covenant and mock your religion, then fight the leaders of disbelief - indeed, they have no regard for their oaths - perhaps they will desist.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the actions that should be taken against those who break their oaths and mock the religion of the believers. The verse commands the believers to fight against the leaders of disbelief, who have no regard for their oaths. The purpose of this fighting is to make the disbelievers stop their actions and to uphold the honor of the religion. The verse emphasizes the seriousness of breaking oaths and mocking the religion, and the importance of taking action against those who engage in such behavior.
orig: وإن نكثوا أيمانهم من بعد عهدهم وطعنوا في دينكم فقاتلوا أئمة الكفر إنهم لا أيمان لهم لعلهم ينتهون

translation: Why would you not fight in the cause of God and the oppressed among the men, women, and children who say, 'Our Lord, take us out of this town, whose inhabitants are unjust, and appoint for us from Yourself a protector and appoint for us from Yourself a helper?'
interpretation: The verse is a call to fight in the cause of God and to defend the oppressed, who are being wronged by their unjust neighbors. The verse mentions the vulnerable members of society - men, women, and children - who are suffering at the hands of their oppressors. They call out to God for help and deliverance from their difficult situation. The verse emphasizes the importance of standing up for justice and fighting against oppression. It also highlights the significance of fighting for the sake of God, rather than out of fear of the oppressors. Ultimately, the verse reminds the believers of their duty to help the oppressed and work towards creating a just and equitable society.
orig: ألا تقاتلون قوما نكثوا أيمانهم وهموا بإخراج الرسول وهم بدءوكم أول مرة أتخشونهم فالله أحق أن تخشوه إن كنتم مؤمنين

translation: Fight them, and Allah will punish them by your hands and will disgrace them and give you victory over them and heal the hearts of a believing people.
interpretation: The verse is a command to fight against the unbelievers, and it describes the outcome of the battle as a punishment from Allah, a disgrace for the unbelievers, and a victory for the believers. The verse also highlights the healing effect of the victory on the hearts of the believers, suggesting that their faith is strengthened and their morale is boosted as a result of the victory. The verse can be interpreted as a call to stand up for one's beliefs and to fight against those who seek to undermine or destroy them, with the assurance that Allah will be on the side of the believers and will give them the upper hand.
orig: قاتلوهم يعذبهم الله بأيديكم ويخزهم وينصركم عليهم ويشف صدور قوم مؤمنين

translation: But may Allah turn away their defiance, for indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful. And Allah is Expert in punishment.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the power of God's forgiveness and mercy, and his ability to turn away the defiance of those who disbelieve. The verse emphasizes that despite the defiance of some people, God is Forgiving and Merciful, and has the power to forgive and show mercy to whomever He wills. The verse also reminds us that God is All-Knowing and Wise, and his punishment is just and appropriate for those who deserve it.
orig: ويذهب غيظ قلوبهم ويتوب الله على من يشاء والله عليم حكيم

translation: Then do you think that you will be left alone while Allah has not yet known those among you who have striven and remained patient and not taken others as allies besides Allah and His Messenger and the believers? And Allah is aware of what you do.
interpretation: The verse addresses the believers and questions their assumption that they will be left alone without being tested or scrutinized by God. The verse emphasizes that God is aware of the actions of the believers and their level of commitment and patience in the face of adversity. The verse serves as a reminder that God knows who among the believers are true and sincere, and who have not taken allies besides God and His Messenger. The verse encourages the believers to remain steadfast in their faith and actions, as God is watching and aware of their efforts.
orig: أم حسبتم أن تتركوا ولما يعلم الله الذين جاهدوا منكم ولم يتخذوا من دون الله ولا رسوله ولا المؤمنين وليجة والله خبير بما تعملون

translation: It is not for the polytheists to maintain the mosques of Allah while they witness against themselves with disbelief. Their deeds have become worthless, and they will abide in the Fire.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of faith and belief in the oneness of God in order to maintain and uphold the mosques of Allah. Those who commit disbelief and polytheism, and actively bear witness against themselves by their actions, will have their deeds rendered worthless and they will abide eternally in the Fire. The verse serves as a warning to those who engage in shirk (polytheism) and disbelief, highlighting the severe consequences of such actions and the futility of their deeds in the eyes of Allah.
orig: ما كان للمشركين أن يعمروا مساجد الله شاهدين على أنفسهم بالكفر أولئك حبطت أعمالهم وفي النار هم خالدون

translation: Whoever builds a mosque for God, seeking the pleasure of God, observing proper worship and giving the appropriate zakat, then it becomes a bond upon them so long as they establish the practice of prayer and give the zakat, and fear none but God. It is possible that they will be among those guided.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the rewards of building a mosque for the sake of God. It highlights the importance of faith, prayer, and charity in the act of building a mosque. The verse emphasizes that the act of building a mosque is not a one-time act, but a continuous commitment to establish prayer and give zakat. The verse also suggests that those who build a mosque with the right intention and fulfill their religious obligations may be among the guided ones. It serves as an encouragement for Muslims to build mosques as a means of seeking God's pleasure and as a way of fulfilling their religious duties.
orig: إنما يعمر مساجد الله من آمن بالله واليوم الآخر وأقام الصلاة وآتى الزكاة ولم يخش إلا الله فعسى أولئك أن يكونوا من المهتدين

translation: Have you made the providing of water to the pilgrim and the maintenance of the Sacred Mosque equal to (the deeds of) one who believes in Allah and the Last Day and strives hard in the way of Allah? They are not equal in the sight of Allah. And Allah guides not the people who are unjust.
interpretation: The verse highlights the unequal value that God places on different actions and deeds. Specifically, it contrasts the act of providing water to pilgrims and maintaining the Sacred Mosque with the actions of a true believer, who believes in God and the Last Day and strives hard in the way of God. The verse emphasizes that these actions are not equal in the sight of God, and that God does not guide those who are unjust and do not recognize the true value of actions and deeds.
orig: أجعلتم سقاية الحاج وعمارة المسجد الحرام كمن آمن بالله واليوم الآخر وجاهد في سبيل الله لا يستوون عند الله والله لا يهدي القوم الظالمين

translation: Those who have believed and emigrated and fought in the cause of Allah with their wealth and their lives are greater in degree with Allah, and it is those who are the triumphant.
interpretation: The verse speaks about those who have believed in Allah, emigrated for His cause, and fought in His way, exerting their wealth and their lives. These individuals are given a higher status by Allah and are considered triumphant. The verse emphasizes the significance of making sacrifices for the sake of Allah and the great reward that awaits those who do so, highlighting the importance of perseverance and dedication in the face of adversity and challenges.
orig: الذين آمنوا وهاجروا وجاهدوا في سبيل الله بأموالهم وأنفسهم أعظم درجة عند الله وأولئك هم الفائزون

translation: Their Lord will give them good news: 'I will let you enter My Garden. I will be generous to you and let you enter My blissful domain.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about God giving good news to a group of people, promising them entry into His Garden (Paradise) and His generosity. The verse emphasizes the blissful and joyful nature of the Garden, where they will reside eternally. The verse serves as a reward for those who have lived righteously and piously, and a source of motivation for believers to strive for God's pleasure and Paradise.
orig: يبشرهم ربهم برحمة منه ورضوان وجنات لهم فيها نعيم مقيم

translation: They will abide therein forever. Indeed, for Allah is a great reward.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the reward for those who have done good deeds and have earned a place in heaven. The verse emphasizes the eternal nature of this reward, as they will 'abide therein forever'. The verse also highlights the greatness of the reward that comes from Allah, reminding the believers of the ultimate goal of their actions and the immense blessings that await them in the afterlife.
orig: خالدين فيها أبدا إن الله عنده أجر عظيم

translation: O you who have believed, do not take your fathers or your brothers as allies if they have preferred disbelief over belief. And whoever of you takes them as allies - those are the wrongdoers.
interpretation: The verse warns believers not to take their disbelieving parents or siblings as allies or protectors, even if they are close relatives. Those who choose to align themselves with unbelievers over believers are considered wrongdoers. The verse emphasizes the importance of maintaining one's faith and not compromising it for the sake of familial relationships. It serves as a reminder that ultimate loyalty should be to God and the believers, and that choosing the side of disbelief is a grave error.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تتخذوا آباءكم وإخوانكم أولياء إن استحبوا الكفر على الإيمان ومن يتولهم منكم فأولئك هم الظالمون

translation: Say, 'If your parents, your spouses, your children, your brothers, your kin, the wealth you have amassed, the commerce you fear may decline, and the homes you find pleasing are more beloved to you than Allah and His Messenger and striving in His cause, then wait until Allah comes with His command.' And indeed, Allah does not guide the transgressing people.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the importance of prioritizing one's love and obedience to Allah and His Messenger over the love of worldly possessions and relationships. The verse lists various worldly attachments, such as family, wealth, and homes, and warns that if these are more beloved to a person than Allah and His Messenger, then they should wait for Allah's command, which implies that they will face the consequences of their misplaced priorities. The verse emphasizes that Allah does not guide those who transgress and prioritize worldly pleasures over their religious obligations.
orig: قل إن كان آباؤكم وأبناؤكم وإخوانكم وأزواجكم وعشيرتكم وأموال اقترفتموها وتجارة تخشون كسادها ومساكن ترضونها أحب إليكم من الله ورسوله وجهاد في سبيله فتربصوا حتى يأتي الله بأمره والله لا يهدي القوم الفاسقين

translation: Certainly, Allah has supported you in many towns and on the day of Hunayn, when you rejoiced in your great number, but it availed you naught, and the earth became narrow for you despite its spaciousness, then you turned back in retreat.
interpretation: The verse describes a specific event in Islamic history, the Battle of Hunayn, where Muslims were victorious with God's help despite being outnumbered. The verse highlights the insignificance of numbers and worldly power in the face of God's support. Despite the Muslims' initial confidence in their large numbers, they were unable to achieve victory on their own and the earth seemed to constrict around them. The verse serves as a reminder that true strength comes from God and that even in the face of seemingly insurmountable odds, one should rely on God's help and support.
orig: لقد نصركم الله في مواطن كثيرة ويوم حنين إذ أعجبتكم كثرتكم فلم تغن عنكم شيئا وضاقت عليكم الأرض بما رحبت ثم وليتم مدبرين

translation: Then Allah sent down tranquility upon His Messenger and upon the believers and sent down soldiers you did not see and punished those who disbelieved. And that is the reward of the disbelievers.
interpretation: The verse describes how Allah sent down tranquility upon the Prophet Muhammad and the believers during a time of conflict, and how Allah also sent down unseen soldiers to aid them in their struggle. At the same time, Allah punished those who disbelieved and rejected the message of Islam. The verse makes it clear that this was a just consequence for the disbelievers, and that this punishment is the reward for those who reject faith and refuse to submit to Allah.
orig: ثم أنزل الله سكينته على رسوله وعلى المؤمنين وأنزل جنودا لم تروها وعذب الذين كفروا وذلك جزاء الكافرين

translation: Then Allah turns in mercy to whom He wills; and Allah is the Forgiving, the Merciful.
interpretation: The verse highlights Allah's attribute of being Merciful and Forgiving. It emphasizes that Allah, in His infinite mercy, may turn to anyone He wills and forgive them, despite their past actions. This verse serves as a reminder that no one is beyond the reach of Allah's mercy and forgiveness, and that it is never too late to turn back to Him and seek His forgiveness. It also serves as a source of hope and comfort for those who have made mistakes, encouraging them to never lose hope in Allah's mercy and to always strive to better themselves.
orig: ثم يتوب الله من بعد ذلك على من يشاء والله غفور رحيم

translation: O you who have believed, the polytheists are indeed unclean, so let them not approach Al-Masjid Al-Haram after this year. And if you fear poverty, Allah will enrich you from His bounty if He wills. Indeed, Allah is Knowing and Wise.
interpretation: The verse is addressing the believers, reminding them that the polytheists are unclean and should not be allowed to approach the sacred mosque after a certain year. The verse acknowledges the fear of poverty that the believers might have if they were to exclude the polytheists, but reassures them that God can enrich them if He wills. The verse emphasizes God's knowledge and wisdom, suggesting that the command to exclude the polytheists is a wise and just decision.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا إنما المشركون نجس فلا يقربوا المسجد الحرام بعد عامهم هذا وإن خفتم عيلة فسوف يغنيكم الله من فضله إن شاء إن الله عليم حكيم

translation: Fight those who do not believe in Allah or in the Last Day and who do not consider unlawful what Allah and His Messenger have made unlawful and who do not adopt the religion of truth from those who were given the Scripture - [fight] until they give the jizyah willingly while they are humbled.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the command to fight against those who do not believe in Allah, the Last Day, and the laws set by Allah and His Messenger. This includes those who do not follow the 'religion of truth' from among the people of the Scripture. The fighting is to continue until they willingly pay the jizyah, a tax levied on non-Muslims living under Islamic rule, while they are in a state of humiliation. This verse is often cited as a justification for violence against non-Muslims, but it is important to note that the Qur'an also emphasizes the importance of peaceful coexistence and religious freedom. The verse should be understood in its historical context and in light of the overall message of the Qur'an.
orig: قاتلوا الذين لا يؤمنون بالله ولا باليوم الآخر ولا يحرمون ما حرم الله ورسوله ولا يدينون دين الحق من الذين أوتوا الكتاب حتى يعطوا الجزية عن يد وهم صاغرون

translation: And the Jews say: 'Ezra is the son of God', and the Christians say: 'The Messiah is the son of God'. That is the saying from their mouths, imitating the saying of those who disbelieved before. May Allah destroy them! How are they deluded?
interpretation: The verse criticizes the Jews and Christians for their belief in the divinity of Ezra and Jesus respectively, which is considered a form of shirk (polytheism) in Islam. The verse equates their beliefs to those of the disbelievers who were destroyed by Allah in the past. The verse serves as a warning to those who associate partners with Allah and a reminder of the consequences of shirk. The verse emphasizes the importance of maintaining the unity and oneness of Allah, and the danger of deviating from the true teachings of Islam.
orig: وقالت اليهود عزير ابن الله وقالت النصارى المسيح ابن الله ذلك قولهم بأفواههم يضاهئون قول الذين كفروا من قبل قاتلهم الله أنى يؤفكون

translation: They have taken their rabbis and monks as lords besides Allah, and also the Messiah, the son of Mary. And they were not commanded except to worship one God; there is no deity except Him. Exalted is He above whatever they associate with Him.
interpretation: The verse criticizes the actions of those who take their religious leaders and the Messiah (Jesus) as intermediaries between themselves and God, and worship them instead of worshipping God alone. This is a grave sin and a violation of the fundamental principle of monotheism in Islam. The verse commands the believers to worship only one God and not to associate any partners with Him. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of maintaining the unity and purity of the worship of God in Islam.
orig: اتخذوا أحبارهم ورهبانهم أربابا من دون الله والمسيح ابن مريم وما أمروا إلا ليعبدوا إلها واحدا لا إله إلا هو سبحانه عما يشركون

translation: They want to extinguish the light of Allah with their mouths, but Allah will perfect His light, although the disbelievers dislike it.
interpretation: The verse highlights the struggle between the believers and the disbelievers, where the latter seeks to suppress the truth and extinguish the light of Allah. However, the verse emphasizes that Allah's light will always prevail and be perfected, despite the disbelievers' efforts to extinguish it. This verse serves as a reminder that the truth cannot be suppressed and that those who reject it will ultimately be unsuccessful in their attempts.
orig: يريدون أن يطفئوا نور الله بأفواههم ويأبى الله إلا أن يتم نوره ولو كره الكافرون

translation: He it is Who sent His Messenger with guidance and the religion of truth, that He may make it prevail over all religions, however much the idolaters may be averse.
interpretation: The verse asserts that it is God who sent His messenger with guidance and the true religion, with the purpose of making it prevail over all other religions. Despite the opposition from the idolaters, the true religion will still be made victorious. This verse emphasizes the ultimate victory of the truth and the importance of following the guidance of God and His messenger, regardless of any opposition or resistance.
orig: هو الذي أرسل رسوله بالهدى ودين الحق ليظهره على الدين كله ولو كره المشركون

translation: O you who have believed, indeed many of the rabbis and the monks consume the wealth of the people unjustly and avert [people] from the way of Allah. And those who hoard gold and silver and do not spend it in the way of Allah - give them news of a painful punishment.
interpretation: The verse criticizes certain religious leaders, including rabbis and monks, who unjustly consume the wealth of the people and mislead them from the path of Allah. The verse also condemns those who hoard wealth and do not spend it for the sake of Allah. These people are warned of a severe punishment. The verse may be interpreted as a reminder of the importance of using one's wealth and resources for the betterment of society and for the sake of Allah, rather than hoarding it for personal gain. The verse may also be seen as a warning against those who misuse their religious authority for personal gain and mislead people from the true path of Allah.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا إن كثيرا من الأحبار والرهبان ليأكلون أموال الناس بالباطل ويصدون عن سبيل الله والذين يكنزون الذهب والفضة ولا ينفقونها في سبيل الله فبشرهم بعذاب أليم

translation: On the Day when it (Hell) will cover them (the unbelievers) from above with its (Hell's) covering, and from beneath their feet with its (Hell's) covering, He (Allah) will burn them in a Blazing Fire. This is the very thing about which you used to dispute!
interpretation: The verse describes the fate of the unbelievers on the Day of Judgment when Hell will envelop them from above and below. They will be burned in a blazing fire as a consequence of their disbelief and disputes about it in their worldly life. The verse emphasizes the reality of Hell and the consequences of disbelief, serving as a warning for those who deny or question the truth of Islam.
orig: يوم يحمى عليها في نار جهنم فتكوى بها جباههم وجنوبهم وظهورهم هذا ما كنزتم لأنفسكم فذوقوا ما كنتم تكنزون

translation: Indeed, the number of months with Allah is twelve [lunar] months in the book of Allah [Qur'an] since the day He created the heavens and the earth; of these, four are sacred. That is the correct religion, so do not wrong yourselves during them. And fight against the polytheists altogether just as they fight against you altogether. And know that Allah is with those who fear Him [pious].
interpretation: The verse outlines the number of months in a year, which is twelve lunar months, and emphasizes the sanctity of four of these months. It commands Muslims not to wrong themselves during these sacred months and to fight against the polytheists who oppress them. The verse also reminds Muslims that Allah is with those who fear Him and follow the right path.
orig: إن عدة الشهور عند الله اثنا عشر شهرا في كتاب الله يوم خلق السماوات والأرض منها أربعة حرم ذلك الدين القيم فلا تظلموا فيهن أنفسكم وقاتلوا المشركين كافة كما يقاتلونكم كافة واعلموا أن الله مع المتقين

translation: Indeed, forgetfulness is increased in kufr (disbelief), it causes astray those who disbelieve. They make it halal in some years and haram in some years, to make up for what God has forbidden. They thus permit what God has forbidden. They violate God's prohibitions, making their deeds seem good to them. And God guides not the disbelieving people.
interpretation: The verse highlights the negative consequences of kufr (disbelief) and forgetfulness, which cause people to stray from the right path. The verse speaks about the actions of those who disbelieve, specifically in relation to the prohibitions of God. They make certain actions permissible in some years and impermissible in others, depending on their own desires and interests. In doing so, they permit what God has forbidden and violate His prohibitions. This allows them to justify their wrong actions and makes their deeds appear good in their own eyes. However, the verse emphasizes that God does not guide such disbelieving people, implying that they are on a path to destruction and are in need of guidance and repentance.
orig: إنما النسيء زيادة في الكفر يضل به الذين كفروا يحلونه عاما ويحرمونه عاما ليواطئوا عدة ما حرم الله فيحلوا ما حرم الله زين لهم سوء أعمالهم والله لا يهدي القوم الكافرين

translation: O you who have believed, what is [the matter] with you when you are told to go out in the cause of Allah and you adhere heavily to the earth? Are you satisfied with the life of this world rather than the Hereafter? But what is the enjoyment of worldly life compared to the Hereafter except a [very] little.
interpretation: The verse addresses the believers and reproaches them for their reluctance to respond to the call to fight in the way of Allah. It questions their priorities and asks whether they value the temporary pleasures of this world over the eternal rewards of the Hereafter. The verse serves as a reminder of the fleeting nature of worldly life and the great significance of the Hereafter. It encourages the believers to be mindful of their actions and to strive for the ultimate goal of pleasing Allah and achieving success in the Hereafter.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا ما لكم إذا قيل لكم انفروا في سبيل الله اثاقلتم إلى الأرض أرضيتم بالحياة الدنيا من الآخرة فما متاع الحياة الدنيا في الآخرة إلا قليل

translation: But if you do not go forth, He will punish you with a painful punishment and will replace you with another people, and you will not harm Him at all, and Allah is over all things competent.
interpretation: The verse warns of the consequences of not following God's command, stating that those who do not comply will be punished with a painful punishment. The verse also emphasizes that God's power is absolute and that He is capable of replacing those who disobey Him with a new people. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of obedience and submission to God's will, and the consequences of disobedience.
orig: إلا تنفروا يعذبكم عذابا أليما ويستبدل قوما غيركم ولا تضروه شيئا والله على كل شيء قدير

translation: If you do not aid him, Allah has already aided him when those who disbelieved had driven him out, the second of two, when they were in the cave, when he said to his companion, 'Do not grieve, indeed Allah is with us.' So Allah sent down upon him serenity and supported him with soldiers you did not see and made the word of those who disbelieved the lowest and the word of Allah, that is the highest; and Allah is Exalted in Might and Wise.
interpretation: The verse relates the story of the Prophet Muhammad and his companion Abu Bakr when they were hiding in a cave during their migration from Mecca to Medina. Despite being pursued by the disbelievers, the verse reassures the believers that Allah is with them and will protect them. The verse highlights the power of Allah and the significance of faith in facing adversity. The words of the disbelievers are made inferior, while the words of Allah are made supreme, emphasizing the ultimate triumph of truth and justice. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of faith and trust in Allah during difficult times and the certainty of His support and protection for the believers.
orig: إلا تنصروه فقد نصره الله إذ أخرجه الذين كفروا ثاني اثنين إذ هما في الغار إذ يقول لصاحبه لا تحزن إن الله معنا فأنزل الله سكينته عليه وأيده بجنود لم تروها وجعل كلمة الذين كفروا السفلى وكلمة الله هي العليا والله عزيز حكيم

translation: March forth, whether light or heavy, and strive with your wealth and your lives in the way of Allah. That is better for you, if you only knew.
interpretation: The verse is a call to action for Muslims to strive and fight in the way of God, using both their wealth and their lives. The phrase "march forth, whether light or heavy" can be interpreted as a call for all Muslims, regardless of their circumstances or abilities, to contribute to the cause. The verse emphasizes the importance of this struggle, stating that it is "better for you" if one understands the significance of this action. The verse can be seen as a call for Muslims to actively participate in the spread of Islam and the establishment of a just society, even if it requires sacrifice and struggle.
orig: انفروا خفافا وثقالا وجاهدوا بأموالكم وأنفسكم في سبيل الله ذلكم خير لكم إن كنتم تعلمون

translation: Had it been near, when they were wronging themselves, they would have certainly fled forth. But their appointed time came upon them while they were unaware.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the people who were guilty of wrongdoing and sin. Had the punishment been near, they would have tried to escape, but their appointed time came upon them unexpectedly, and they were caught off guard. The verse highlights the human tendency to underestimate the consequences of their actions and the suddenness of divine retribution. It emphasizes the importance of being mindful of one's actions and constantly seeking forgiveness and repentance.
orig: لو كان عرضا قريبا وسفرا قاصدا لاتبعوك ولكن بعدت عليهم الشقة وسيحلفون بالله لو استطعنا لخرجنا معكم يهلكون أنفسهم والله يعلم إنهم لكاذبون

translation: Allah blots out (forgives) whom He wills, and increases the wrong-doers in punishment.
interpretation: The verse explains that Allah has the power to forgive those whom He wills and to increase the punishment of those who do wrong. This verse emphasizes Allah's mercy and justice. It reminds the believers that Allah is the ultimate judge and that they should strive to be among those who are forgiven, not among those who are increased in punishment. It also serves as a warning to those who commit wrong-doing that they will not escape the consequences of their actions and that their punishment will be increased if they persist in their ways.
orig: عفا الله عنك لم أذنت لهم حتى يتبين لك الذين صدقوا وتعلم الكاذبين

translation: Let not those who believe in God and the Last Day ask your permission to miss the fight with their goods and their selves; God knows those who do right.
interpretation: The verse encourages believers in God and the Last Day to participate in jihad (struggle) with their wealth and their selves. It reminds them that God knows those who do right and will reward them accordingly. The verse emphasizes the importance of participating in the struggle for one's faith and one's community, and encourages believers to contribute their resources and their efforts towards this cause.
orig: لا يستأذنك الذين يؤمنون بالله واليوم الآخر أن يجاهدوا بأموالهم وأنفسهم والله عليم بالمتقين

translation: Only those who do not believe in God and the Last Day ask your leave, so they are in doubt, so they fluctuate in their doubt.
interpretation: The verse describes the behavior of those who do not believe in God and the Day of Judgment. They are uncertain and hesitant, constantly wavering in their disbelief. These individuals are the ones who ask the Prophet for permission to leave his presence, revealing their lack of commitment and faith. The verse highlights the indecisiveness and inner turmoil that characterizes those who reject the message of Islam.
orig: إنما يستأذنك الذين لا يؤمنون بالله واليوم الآخر وارتابت قلوبهم فهم في ريبهم يترددون

translation: And if they had intended to leave, they would have prepared for it [their departure], but Allah disliked their departure, so He kept them stupefied. And it was said, 'Remain where you are with those who remain.'
interpretation: The verse describes the punishment of a group of people who had planned to leave or escape, but were unable to do so because of God's will. The verse highlights the power of God and His ability to control the actions of His creations. The people's intention to leave was known to God, and He prevented them from doing so. The verse also emphasizes the importance of obedience and submission to God's will, as the people were commanded to 'remain where you are with those who remain.' The verse serves as a reminder that God is all-knowing and all-powerful and that those who defy His will face consequences.
orig: ولو أرادوا الخروج لأعدوا له عدة ولكن كره الله انبعاثهم فثبطهم وقيل اقعدوا مع القاعدين

translation: If they had gone among you, they would only have added to your confusion, and they would have sought to mislead you from the path of God. There are some among you who would listen to them, but God is aware of the unjust.
interpretation: The verse warns against the dangers of outsiders who, if allowed to mix with the community, would only bring confusion and lead people astray from the path of God. The verse recognizes that some people within the community may be susceptible to the false teachings of these outsiders, but also emphasizes that God is aware of the unjust and will ultimately hold them accountable for their actions.
orig: لو خرجوا فيكم ما زادوكم إلا خبالا ولأوضعوا خلالكم يبغونكم الفتنة وفيكم سماعون لهم والله عليم بالظالمين

translation: Indeed, they had sought discord before and turned others away from the way of Allah. Until there came the truth, and the command of Allah became clear, while they were against it.
