translation: For those who believe and do good deeds, their Lord guides them by their faith. Beneath them flow rivers in the gardens of delight.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the reward of those who have faith in God and do good deeds. It highlights that God guides these individuals through their faith, and they are granted access to the gardens of paradise, where rivers flow beneath them. The verse serves as a promise of the blessings and rewards that await the righteous and the believers in the afterlife, emphasizing the importance of faith and righteousness in one's journey towards God.
orig: إن الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات يهديهم ربهم بإيمانهم تجري من تحتهم الأنهار في جنات النعيم

translation: Their invitation therein will be, 'Exalted are You, O Allah,' and their greeting therein will be, 'Peace.' And the conclusion of their prayer will be, 'Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds.'
interpretation: The verse describes the invocation and greetings of the righteous people in heaven. They will glorify and praise God, exalting His greatness and majesty. They will greet each other with peace, reflecting the harmony and serenity of the place. The conclusion of their prayer will be a doxology of praise and gratitude, acknowledging God's sovereignty over all creation. The verse conveys the spirit of reverence, unity, and thankfulness that characterizes the people of heaven, and serves as a model for the believers on earth to emulate.
orig: دعواهم فيها سبحانك اللهم وتحيتهم فيها سلام وآخر دعواهم أن الحمد لله رب العالمين

translation: And if Allah had hastened for the people their punishment, (it would have been) in the instant they sought to reform. But We leave those who do not expect to meet Us in their transgression, blindly wandering.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the punishment of people and the idea that if God were to hasten their punishment, it would come immediately upon their seeking to change their ways. However, God's patience allows for the continuation of those who persist in their transgression and do not expect to meet God. This verse highlights God's mercy and patience, as well as the consequences of not seeking forgiveness and continuing in sin.
orig: ولو يعجل الله للناس الشر استعجالهم بالخير لقضي إليهم أجلهم فنذر الذين لا يرجون لقاءنا في طغيانهم يعمهون

translation: And when harm touches man, he calls upon Us, either standing or sitting or lying down, but when We remove his harm from him, he passes on as if he had never called upon Us to the harm that touched him. Thus do We make attractive to the transgressors what they used to do.
interpretation: The verse describes the behavior of people when they face hardship or harm. When they are in distress, they turn to God for help, regardless of whether they are standing, sitting, or lying down. However, as soon as their difficulty is removed, they forget about their previous suffering and the help they received from God. They move on as if they had never called upon God in the first place. The verse highlights the human tendency to take blessings for granted and to forget about God when things are going well. The verse serves as a reminder that God is the one who removes harm and grants relief, and that people should not forget this fact when they are no longer in need. The verse also emphasizes the attractiveness of sin and transgression, which can lead people astray and make them forgetful of God's blessings.
orig: وإذا مس الإنسان الضر دعانا لجنبه أو قاعدا أو قائما فلما كشفنا عنه ضره مر كأن لم يدعنا إلى ضر مسه كذلك زين للمسرفين ما كانوا يعملون

translation: And We have already destroyed towns around you while they were unjust, and their messengers came to them with clear evidences, but they were not believing. Thus do We recompense the criminal peoples.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of communities that were unjust and did not believe in the messengers who brought them clear evidence and proofs. The verse emphasizes that this was not a singular occurrence, but rather a pattern of behavior where communities were destroyed for their wrongdoing. The verse serves as a reminder that the same fate awaits those who persist in their injustice and disbelief. It highlights the importance of accepting and following the guidance brought by the messengers of God.
orig: ولقد أهلكنا القرون من قبلكم لما ظلموا وجاءتهم رسلهم بالبينات وما كانوا ليؤمنوا كذلك نجزي القوم المجرمين

translation: Then We made you successors in the earth after them so that We may see how you will act.
interpretation: The verse speaks about God's decision to make humans successors on earth after previous generations. The purpose of this is to observe and test human's actions. This verse highlights the concept of humans being responsible for their actions and the idea that they are being constantly evaluated by God. It also emphasizes the significance of the role of humans as successors on earth and the importance of using this role for the betterment of the world and not for causing destruction and chaos.
orig: ثم جعلناكم خلائف في الأرض من بعدهم لننظر كيف تعملون

translation: And when Our verses are recited to them clearly, those who disbelieve say, 'Bring us a Qur'an other than this, or change it.' Say, [O Muhammad], 'It is not for me to change it on my own accord. I only follow what is revealed to me. Indeed, I fear, if I were to disobey my Lord, the punishment of a tremendous day.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the response of the disbelievers when they hear the verses of the Qur'an being recited to them. They ask for a different Qur'an or for the current one to be changed. The Prophet Muhammad responds by stating that he does not have the authority to change the Qur'an and that he only follows what is revealed to him. He also expresses his fear of disobeying his Lord and the consequences of receiving punishment on a tremendous day (Day of Judgment). The verse highlights the rejection and denial of the disbelievers towards the Qur'an and the truth it brings. It also emphasizes the importance of following and submitting to the revelation from God, and the consequences of disobedience.
orig: وإذا تتلى عليهم آياتنا بينات قال الذين لا يرجون لقاءنا ائت بقرآن غير هذا أو بدله قل ما يكون لي أن أبدله من تلقاء نفسي إن أتبع إلا ما يوحى إلي إني أخاف إن عصيت ربي عذاب يوم عظيم

translation: Say, 'If it had been the will of Allah, I would not have recited it to you, nor would He have made it known to you, for I had remained among you a lifetime before it. Will you not then understand?'
interpretation: The verse is a response from the Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) to the disbelievers who questioned the authenticity of the Quran and his prophethood. The verse emphasizes that the revelation of the Quran and its message is not dependent on the Prophet's will, but rather it is a divine revelation from Allah. The verse also highlights the fact that the Prophet had been living among the disbelievers for a long time before the revelation, yet they did not believe. The verse serves as a call for reflection and understanding, urging the disbelievers to ponder upon the truth of the revelation and the signs of Allah around them.
orig: قل لو شاء الله ما تلوته عليكم ولا أدراكم به فقد لبثت فيكم عمرا من قبله أفلا تعقلون

translation: And who is more unjust than he who invents a lie about Allah or denies His signs? Indeed, the criminals will not succeed.
interpretation: The verse highlights the severity of inventing a lie about Allah or denying His signs, emphasizing that such actions are a form of injustice. The verse warns that those who commit these acts will not prosper or succeed. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of upholding the truth and acknowledging the signs of Allah, and the severe consequences of distorting or denying them.
orig: فمن أظلم ممن افترى على الله كذبا أو كذب بآياته إنه لا يفلح المجرمون

translation: And they worship besides Allah that which does not benefit them nor harm them and say, 'These are our intercessors with Allah.' Say, 'Do you inform Allah of something He does not know in the heavens or on the earth?' Exalted is He and high above what they associate with Him.
interpretation: The verse speaks about people who worship false deities, believing that these deities can benefit or harm them. They also believe that these deities can intercede with God on their behalf. The verse rejects these notions and asserts that these deities have no power or influence, and that they cannot benefit or harm anyone. The verse also emphasizes the all-knowing nature of God, stating that He has knowledge of everything in the heavens and on the earth. The verse serves as a reminder that God is exalted and high above what the people associate with Him, and that He does not need intercessors to speak on their behalf.
orig: ويعبدون من دون الله ما لا يضرهم ولا ينفعهم ويقولون هؤلاء شفعاؤنا عند الله قل أتنبئون الله بما لا يعلم في السماوات ولا في الأرض سبحانه وتعالى عما يشركون

translation: And mankind were but one community, then they differed. And had it not been for a word that had already gone forth from your Lord, it would have been judged between them in respect to that in which they differ.
interpretation: The verse highlights the inherent unity of mankind and the subsequent differences that arose among them. The verse suggests that if it were not for a decree from God, these differences would have been resolved by divine judgement. The verse implies that these differences are not insignificant, but rather, they are a matter of importance and would have been addressed by God. The verse also suggests that the diversity of opinions and beliefs among people is not something new, but has always existed. It serves as a reminder of the need for understanding, compassion, and tolerance in the face of differences, and the ultimate justice of God.
orig: وما كان الناس إلا أمة واحدة فاختلفوا ولولا كلمة سبقت من ربك لقضي بينهم فيما فيه يختلفون

translation: And they say, 'Why has not an Ayah been sent down to him from his Lord?' Say, 'Indeed, the unseen (Ghayb) is only for Allah. So wait; indeed, I am with you among those who wait.'
interpretation: The verse is a response to those who question why a sign or miracle has not been sent down to the Prophet Muhammad from his Lord. The verse explains that the unseen (Ghayb) is only known to Allah, and therefore, it is not up to humans to dictate when or how a sign should be sent. The Prophet is instructed to respond by telling them to be patient and wait, as he too is among those who are waiting for Allah's decree. The verse emphasizes the importance of patience and trust in Allah's plan, and the limitations of human knowledge and understanding.
orig: ويقولون لولا أنزل عليه آية من ربه فقل إنما الغيب لله فانتظروا إني معكم من المنتظرين

translation: And when We bestow mercy upon the people after distress has touched them, at once they devise plans against Our signs. Say, 'God is swifter in planning.' Indeed, Our messengers write down what you plan.',
interpretation: The verse highlights the ingratitude and disbelief of people who, after experiencing God's mercy and relief from hardship, immediately start to plot against His signs and revelations. The verse advises the believers to respond to such behavior by reminding themselves that God's planning is swifter and more comprehensive than that of humans. Furthermore, it emphasizes that the angels record all of the disbelievers' plots, which will ultimately be used as evidence against them on the Day of Judgment.
orig: وإذا أذقنا الناس رحمة من بعد ضراء مستهم إذا لهم مكر في آياتنا قل الله أسرع مكرا إن رسلنا يكتبون ما تمكرون

translation: It is He who makes you travel by land and sea, until when you are embarked on the ships, and they sail with them with a favorable wind, and they rejoice in it, then comes a storm wind and the wave comes at them from every side, and they assume that they are encompassed by it, they call upon Allah, making their religion sincerely His, 'If You rescue us from this, we will surely be among the grateful.'
interpretation: The verse describes the experience of sailors at sea during a sudden and violent storm. The sailors are initially joyful as they sail on a calm and favorable wind, but their situation quickly changes as a storm wind approaches and waves surround them from every side. In this moment of desperation, the sailors call upon God, sincerely dedicating their religion to Him. The verse emphasizes the power and unpredictability of the natural world and the human experience of vulnerability and dependence on God. It reminds believers of the importance of maintaining a sincere and devoted faith, even in times of prosperity and ease, in preparation for the potential challenges and trials that may come in the future.
orig: هو الذي يسيركم في البر والبحر حتى إذا كنتم في الفلك وجرين بهم بريح طيبة وفرحوا بها جاءتها ريح عاصف وجاءهم الموج من كل مكان وظنوا أنهم أحيط بهم دعوا الله مخلصين له الدين لئن أنجيتنا من هذه لنكونن من الشاكرين

translation: But when We let them taste mercy after adversity had touched them, behold! They began to plot against Our signs! Say, 'Enjoy yourselves, for surely, you are going to know!'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the people who, after experiencing God's mercy, started to plot against His signs (i.e. His revelations). The verse advises the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to respond to these people by saying 'Enjoy yourselves, for surely, you are going to know!'. This statement serves as a warning to those who reject God's signs and a reminder that they will be held accountable for their actions. The verse emphasizes that the enjoyment of this world is temporary and that ultimately, all of humanity will return to God and be judged based on their deeds.
orig: فلما أنجاهم إذا هم يبغون في الأرض بغير الحق يا أيها الناس إنما بغيكم على أنفسكم متاع الحياة الدنيا ثم إلينا مرجعكم فننبئكم بما كنتم تعملون

translation: The likeness of the worldly life is as water which We send down from the sky, then the plants of the earth mingle with it, from which men and cattle eat until when the earth is clad in its adornments and is beautified and its people think that they have power over it, Our command comes to it by night or by day and We make it as a harvest, as if it had not flourished yesterday. Thus do We explain the signs in detail for a people who reflect.
interpretation: The verse uses the metaphor of water and plants to illustrate the transient and ephemeral nature of worldly life. Just as water nourishes the earth and supports the growth of plants, the world provides the means for human sustenance and development. However, when people become arrogant and think they have control over their lives and resources, God's command comes suddenly and unexpectedly, either by night or by day, and everything is destroyed. The verse emphasizes the fragility of human existence and the need for humility and reflection. It serves as a reminder that all power and control belong to God, and that human beings should not take their prosperity for granted. The verse encourages people to reflect upon the signs of God in the world around them and to recognize the ultimate purpose of their existence.
orig: إنما مثل الحياة الدنيا كماء أنزلناه من السماء فاختلط به نبات الأرض مما يأكل الناس والأنعام حتى إذا أخذت الأرض زخرفها وازينت وظن أهلها أنهم قادرون عليها أتاها أمرنا ليلا أو نهارا فجعلناها حصيدا كأن لم تغن بالأمس كذلك نفصل الآيات لقوم يتفكرون

translation: And Allah invites to the home of peace and guides whom He wills to a straight path.
interpretation: The verse highlights Allah's invitation to His home of peace, which is a metaphor for paradise. The verse emphasizes that Allah guides whomever He wills to the straight path, which refers to the right and virtuous way of life. The verse conveys a message of hope and mercy, reminding believers that Allah guides and helps those who seek His guidance and strive to live a righteous life.
orig: والله يدعو إلى دار السلام ويهدي من يشاء إلى صراط مستقيم

translation: For those who have done good is the best (reward) and even more (than that), neither darkness nor shame shall cover their faces, they are companions of the garden, they will abide therein (forever).
interpretation: The verse speaks about the reward for those who have done good deeds. It states that the best reward awaits them, and they will receive even more than what they expect. The verse emphasizes that these people will not experience any darkness or shame, indicating that they will be free from any negative feelings or regrets. The verse also mentions that they will be companions of the garden, which is a reference to heaven, and they will live there forever. The verse serves as a motivation for people to do good deeds and emphasizes the great rewards that await them in the afterlife.
orig: للذين أحسنوا الحسنى وزيادة ولا يرهق وجوههم قتر ولا ذلة أولئك أصحاب الجنة هم فيها خالدون

translation: And those who earn evil deeds, their recompense is equivalent to their deeds, and they will be encompassed by disgrace. There is not for them from God any protector. It is as if the darkness of the night covered their faces, and they will be among the companions of the Fire, therein they will abide eternally.
interpretation: The verse describes the fate of those who commit sins and evil deeds. Their punishment will be equal to their sins, and they will be surrounded by disgrace. The verse emphasizes that there will be no protection for them from God. The imagery of darkness covering their faces highlights the severity of their situation and the loss of guidance. The verse concludes by stating that these people will be among the companions of the Fire, indicating their eternal damnation in hell.
orig: والذين كسبوا السيئات جزاء سيئة بمثلها وترهقهم ذلة ما لهم من الله من عاصم كأنما أغشيت وجوههم قطعا من الليل مظلما أولئك أصحاب النار هم فيها خالدون

translation: And the Day We gather them all together, then We say to those who associated others with Us, 'Where are those you used to associate with?'
interpretation: The verse describes the Day of Judgment when all people will be gathered together before God. God addresses those who associated partners with Him, asking them where their false gods are, implying that they will be of no help to them on that Day. The verse emphasizes the ultimate powerlessness and insignificance of false gods, and the certainty of facing God alone on the Day of Judgment. It serves as a reminder of the futility of associating partners with God, and the importance of worshipping and serving Him alone.
orig: ويوم نحشرهم جميعا ثم نقول للذين أشركوا مكانكم أنتم وشركاؤكم فزيلنا بينهم وقال شركاؤهم ما كنتم إيانا تعبدون

translation: For Allah is sufficient as a witness between me and you. Indeed, if we were to neglect our worship of Him, we would surely be unaware (of its significance).
interpretation: The verse highlights the sufficiency of Allah as a witness between the speaker and the person being addressed. It implies that there is no need for any other intermediary or proof in their relationship with Allah. The second part of the verse serves as a reminder that neglecting the worship of Allah would be a sign of ignorance and unawareness of its significance. This verse emphasizes the importance of maintaining a strong connection with Allah and prioritizing His worship above all else.
orig: فكفى بالله شهيدا بيننا وبينكم إن كنا عن عبادتكم لغافلين

translation: For every soul, there is (a duty) upon it to repay what it has earned, and they will be brought back to God, their true Master, and what they used to falsely attribute to God will leave them.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the principle of accountability and justice in the afterlife. Each soul will be recompensed for its actions, and people will be held accountable for their deeds and will be brought back to God, who is the ultimate owner and master of all souls. The verse also highlights the falsity of the beliefs and attributions that people make to God, which will be proven wrong and will not be able to help them in the afterlife.
orig: هنالك تبلو كل نفس ما أسلفت وردوا إلى الله مولاهم الحق وضل عنهم ما كانوا يفترون

translation: Say, 'Who provides for you from the sky and the earth? Or who controls hearing and sight? And who brings out the living from the dead and brings out the dead from the living? And who manages the affair?' They will say, 'God.' Say, 'Then will you not fear Him?'
interpretation: The verse is a rhetorical question posed by the speaker, highlighting the power and control that God has over all aspects of life and the universe. The questions are meant to make the listener reflect on the numerous blessings they receive from God, such as the provision of food and sustenance, the ability to hear and see, and the power to give life and death. The verse emphasizes God's complete control and management of all affairs. The final question, 'Then will you not fear Him?' serves as a call to action, urging the listener to recognize God's power and authority and to show reverence and fear towards Him.
orig: قل من يرزقكم من السماء والأرض أمن يملك السمع والأبصار ومن يخرج الحي من الميت ويخرج الميت من الحي ومن يدبر الأمر فسيقولون الله فقل أفلا تتقون

translation: That is Allah, your Lord; there is no deity except Him, so where are you being led astray?
interpretation: The verse asserts that Allah is the only God and the only Lord, and it questions the believers about their deviation from the right path. The verse emphasizes the importance of following the right path and the dangers of straying from it. It reminds the believers of the consequences of following false deities and the importance of staying true to the one and only God. The verse serves as a warning and a reminder for the believers to stay on the right path and to avoid being led astray.
orig: فذلكم الله ربكم الحق فماذا بعد الحق إلا الضلال فأنى تصرفون

translation: Thus, the word of your Lord is fulfilled against those who transgress: that they will not believe.
interpretation: The verse asserts that the divine decree has been fulfilled against the transgressors, in that they will not believe. The word 'transgressors' implies that these individuals have exceeded the bounds of what is morally acceptable, and their disbelief is a consequence of their actions. The verse emphasizes the power and authority of the divine word and the inevitability of its fulfillment, despite the transgressors' disbelief.
orig: كذلك حقت كلمت ربك على الذين فسقوا أنهم لا يؤمنون

translation: Say, 'Who among your associates can begin the creation, then repeat it?' Say, 'It is Allah who begins the creation, then repeats it. So how are you deluded?'
interpretation: The verse is a challenge to the polytheists who associate partners with Allah, asking them who among their 'associates' has the power to create and then recreate. The verse affirms that it is only Allah who has the power to begin the creation and then repeat it, a clear reference to the Day of Judgment. The verse serves to remind the polytheists of the power and greatness of Allah and the futility of their worship of false gods. It challenges them to consider the evidence and not be deluded by their false beliefs.
orig: قل هل من شركائكم من يبدأ الخلق ثم يعيده قل الله يبدأ الخلق ثم يعيده فأنى تؤفكون

translation: Say, 'Is there any of your partner-gods who guides to the truth?' Say, 'God guides to the truth.' Is He then who guides to the truth more worthy to be followed, or he who himself does not find the way unless he is guided? Then, what is the matter with you, how do you judge?
interpretation: This verse is a challenge from the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to the polytheists to reflect on the true nature of guidance. It asks if any of their partner-gods can guide to the truth, and then affirms that it is only God who guides to the truth. The verse highlights the importance of following the one who guides to the truth, and questions the judgment of those who follow false gods. The verse emphasizes the uniqueness of God's guidance and the futility of following anyone else. It serves as a call to the polytheists to recognize the truth and to submit to the one true God.
orig: قل هل من شركائكم من يهدي إلى الحق قل الله يهدي للحق أفمن يهدي إلى الحق أحق أن يتبع أمن لا يهدي إلا أن يهدى فما لكم كيف تحكمون

translation: And most of them follow nothing but conjecture. Indeed, conjecture can not replace the truth in any way. Indeed, God is Knowing of what they do.
interpretation: The verse highlights the dangers of following conjecture and speculation, rather than relying on the truth. The verse suggests that many people are guided by their own assumptions and opinions, rather than seeking the truth. The verse emphasizes that conjecture is insufficient and cannot replace the truth. The verse also reminds that God is all-knowing and aware of all the actions of people, and that they will be held accountable for their actions.
orig: وما يتبع أكثرهم إلا ظنا إن الظن لا يغني من الحق شيئا إن الله عليم بما يفعلون

translation: And this Qur'an is not something that has been invented by ourselves, but it is a confirmation of what was before it, and a detailed explanation of the Scripture, there is no doubt in it, from the Lord of the worlds.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the divine origin of the Qur'an and rejects the notion that it was invented by humans. The verse explains that the Qur'an confirms the previous scriptures and provides a detailed explanation of them. The verse also highlights the certainty and truth of the Qur'an, leaving no room for doubt. The verse serves as a reminder of the divine nature of the Qur'an and its role in confirming and explaining the previous scriptures, and the importance of recognizing its truth and divinity.
orig: وما كان هذا القرآن أن يفترى من دون الله ولكن تصديق الذي بين يديه وتفصيل الكتاب لا ريب فيه من رب العالمين

translation: Or do they say, 'He has made it up'? Say, 'Then bring ten chapters like it, invented, and call upon whomever you can besides Allah, if you are truthful.'
interpretation: The verse challenges those who accuse the Prophet Muhammad of making up the Qur'an to produce ten chapters like it, implying that the Qur'an's eloquence and beauty are unique and cannot be replicated. The verse also tells the Prophet Muhammad to invite those who deny the revelation to call upon any other deity for help if they are truthful in their claim that the Qur'an is not from God. The verse emphasizes the divine origin of the Qur'an and the impossibility of creating anything similar to it, highlighting the power and greatness of God.
orig: أم يقولون افتراه قل فأتوا بسورة مثله وادعوا من استطعتم من دون الله إن كنتم صادقين

translation: But they indeed lied about that of which they had no knowledge, and they lied about My revelation as well. And I have not been unaware of what they used to do. And how (terrible) was My denial (punishment) of the previous towns!
interpretation: The verse speaks about the people who lied about God's revelation and committed injustice. It highlights that God is aware of their actions and reminds them of the consequences of their denial of His revelation. The verse concludes by emphasizing the severe punishment that was given to the previous towns that denied God's message, serving as a warning for the current disbelievers.
orig: بل كذبوا بما لم يحيطوا بعلمه ولما يأتهم تأويله كذلك كذب الذين من قبلهم فانظر كيف كان عاقبة الظالمين

translation: And among them are those who believe in it, and among them are those who do not believe in it, and your Lord is most knowing of the corrupters.
interpretation: The verse highlights the division among people in their belief and rejection of the message of God. It acknowledges that there will be those who believe and those who do not. However, the verse emphasizes that God knows best those who cause corruption and mischief. The verse may serve as a reminder of the ultimate judgement of God and the importance of holding firm to faith despite the presence of unbelievers.
orig: ومنهم من يؤمن به ومنهم من لا يؤمن به وربك أعلم بالمفسدين

translation: But if they call you a liar, say: 'My deeds are my own, and your deeds are your own. You are innocent of what I do, and I am innocent of what you do.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about how to respond when others call the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) a liar. The verse instructs him to say that he is responsible for his own actions, and they are responsible for their own actions. This statement emphasizes the individual's accountability for their actions and the importance of not being influenced by the actions of others. The verse also highlights the importance of not taking responsibility for the actions of others, as each person will be held accountable for their own deeds on the Day of Judgment.
orig: وإن كذبوك فقل لي عملي ولكم عملكم أنتم بريئون مما أعمل وأنا بريء مما تعملون

translation: And among them are those who listen to you, can you then make the deaf hear, even though they do not understand?
interpretation: The verse is addressing the Prophet Muhammad, and it speaks about the people who refuse to listen to his message, despite being given the opportunity to hear it. The verse highlights the frustration of the Prophet, who is trying to convey the message of Islam to a people who are unwilling to listen or understand. The verse emphasizes the futility of trying to communicate with those who are closed-minded and resistant to change. The verse serves as a reminder that true understanding and acceptance of the message can only come from within, and that external efforts to persuade or convince may be in vain.
orig: ومنهم من يستمعون إليك أفأنت تسمع الصم ولو كانوا لا يعقلون

translation: And among them is he who looks at you (O Muhammad); then will you guide him while he is blind! And indeed, We will let the disbelievers taste a severe punishment.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the disbelievers who reject the guidance of the Prophet Muhammad. Despite the Prophet's efforts to guide them, they remain blind to the truth. The verse highlights the futility of trying to guide someone who is not willing to see the truth. The verse also emphasizes the punishment that awaits the disbelievers, indicating that they will not escape the consequences of their rejection of the truth.
orig: ومنهم من ينظر إليك أفأنت تهدي العمي ولو كانوا لا يبصرون

translation: Indeed, Allah does not wrong the people in anything, but it is the people who wrong themselves.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes that God is just and does not wrong or oppress people. Rather, any harm or injustice that people face is a result of their own actions and decisions. This verse serves as a reminder that individuals are responsible for their own actions and that they should strive for justice and fairness in their lives. It also highlights the importance of taking responsibility for one's actions and avoiding blame and excuses.
orig: إن الله لا يظلم الناس شيئا ولكن الناس أنفسهم يظلمون

translation: And the Day We shall gather them together will be as if they had tarried but an hour of the day, they will recognize one another. Those who denied the meeting with God will have lost, and they were not guided.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the Day of Judgment, when all people will be gathered together before God. The verse emphasizes the shortness and swiftness of this event, comparing it to a brief moment in the day. The people will recognize each other, emphasizing the reality and tangibility of the event. The verse highlights the fate of those who denied the meeting with God, stating that they will have lost and that they were not guided. The verse serves as a reminder of the imminence of the Day of Judgment and the importance of believing in and preparing for it, as well as a warning to those who deny or ignore it.
orig: ويوم يحشرهم كأن لم يلبثوا إلا ساعة من النهار يتعارفون بينهم قد خسر الذين كذبوا بلقاء الله وما كانوا مهتدين

translation: And We may show you some of what We have promised them, or We may take you in death; then to Us is their return, and then Allah is, over what you do, a Witness.
interpretation: The verse speaks about God's power and control over all things, including the life and death of people. The verse mentions two possibilities: either God will show the Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) some of the punishment that will befall the disbelievers, or God will take the Prophet in death. Regardless of which of these two possibilities occurs, the verse emphasizes that all people will ultimately return to God and that God is a Witness over all that people do. The verse serves as a reminder of the power and authority of God, and the certainty of the Day of Judgment.
orig: وإما نرينك بعض الذي نعدهم أو نتوفينك فإلينا مرجعهم ثم الله شهيد على ما يفعلون

translation: And for every community, there is a messenger, so when their messenger comes, judgment is made between them in truth, and they are not wronged.
interpretation: The verse highlights the importance of prophets in guiding communities towards justice. It states that for every community, a messenger will be sent to make judgments between them in truth, ensuring that they are not wronged. This verse emphasizes the role of prophets in establishing justice and preventing oppression. It also serves as a reminder that every community will be held accountable for their actions and that the prophets will play a crucial role in ensuring that justice is served.
orig: ولكل أمة رسول فإذا جاء رسولهم قضي بينهم بالقسط وهم لا يظلمون

translation: And they say, 'When will this promise be (fulfilled), if you are truthful?'
interpretation: The verse is spoken from the perspective of the disbelievers who are questioning the promise of God and the believers who are reminding them of it. The disbelievers are expressing their disbelief and skepticism, and are challenging the believers to prove their claim by asking 'when will this promise be (fulfilled)'. The verse highlights the attitude of the disbelievers towards the divine promise, and it serves as a reminder for the believers to remain steadfast and patient in the face of adversity and skepticism.
orig: ويقولون متى هذا الوعد إن كنتم صادقين

translation: Say, 'I have no power over benefit or harm myself except as Allah wills. For every nation is an appointed time. When their time has come, they will not remain behind an hour, nor will they precede [it].'
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the powerlessness of the Prophet Muhammad and all human beings in the face of God's will. The verse reminds the Prophet and the believers that their fate is in the hands of God and that they cannot control the outcome of their actions. The verse also introduces the concept of a fixed time for every nation, meaning that every community will face a reckoning and no one can escape it. The verse encourages patience and submission to God's will, reminding the believers that they must fulfill their duties and wait for God's judgment.
orig: قل لا أملك لنفسي ضرا ولا نفعا إلا ما شاء الله لكل أمة أجل إذا جاء أجلهم فلا يستأخرون ساعة ولا يستقدمون

translation: Say, 'Have you considered: if His punishment came to you by night or by day, what part of it would the sinners hasten?'
interpretation: The verse addresses the Prophet Muhammad and commands him to ask the disbelievers a rhetorical question about God's punishment. The verse describes different times of the day, night and day, when the punishment may come. The question emphasizes the futility of trying to escape or hasten the punishment, as it is inevitable for the sinners. The verse serves as a warning to those who deny the truth and persist in their sins, urging them to reflect on the consequences of their actions and the imminence of God's punishment.
orig: قل أرأيتم إن أتاكم عذابه بياتا أو نهارا ماذا يستعجل منه المجرمون

translation: A sin, when it occurs, has no one believed in it at the time it happened, yet you are laughing thereat.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the disbelief and denial of people when faced with a sin or wrongdoing. The verse highlights the fact that when a sin occurs, people often do not believe in its consequences and may even laugh or make light of it. However, the verse serves as a reminder that the consequences of sin and wrongdoing are real and can have serious consequences. The verse encourages believers to take sin and wrongdoing seriously and to strive for righteousness and justice in all their actions and dealings.
orig: أثم إذا ما وقع آمنتم به آلآن وقد كنتم به تستعجلون

translation: Then it will be said to those who did wrong: 'Taste the eternal punishment! Are you being recompensed except for what you used to earn?'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the judgment day and the punishment of those who have done wrong. It emphasizes the idea that people will be recompensed for their actions and will not receive anything except what they have earned. The phrase 'taste the eternal punishment' highlights the severity and unending nature of the punishment that the wrongdoers will face. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of good deeds and the inevitability of being held accountable for one's actions.
orig: ثم قيل للذين ظلموا ذوقوا عذاب الخلد هل تجزون إلا بما كنتم تكسبون

translation: And they urge you to hasten the punishment! But, no! Your Lord is full of forgiveness for mankind despite their wrongdoing, and He is the One who creates the greatest circumstances.
interpretation: The verse addresses those who urge the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to hasten the punishment of God. The verse reassures the Prophet that God is full of forgiveness for mankind, despite their wrongdoings. The verse emphasizes that God is the One who has control over all circumstances, including the punishment, and that it will come at the right time. The verse serves as a reminder that God's mercy and forgiveness are greater than His punishment and that people should turn to Him in repentance rather than rushing His judgment.
orig: ويستنبئونك أحق هو قل إي وربي إنه لحق وما أنتم بمعجزين

translation: And if every soul that has wronged possessed all that is on the earth, it would offer it in ransom. And they would declare themselves free of ungratefulness when they see the punishment. Then they will be avenged on that Day with a penalty of humiliation.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the regret and remorse of those who have done wrong and committed injustices, when they are faced with the punishment on the Day of Judgment. The verse emphasizes that even if every soul that has wronged possessed all that is on the earth, it would not be enough to ransom themselves. The verse highlights the magnitude of the punishment and the insignificance of worldly possessions in the face of it. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of leading a righteous life and avoiding injustices, as there will be no escape from the consequences of one's actions on the Day of Judgment.
orig: ولو أن لكل نفس ظلمت ما في الأرض لافتدت به وأسروا الندامة لما رأوا العذاب وقضي بينهم بالقسط وهم لا يظلمون

translation: No! Indeed, for Allah is what is in the heavens and what is on the earth. No! Indeed, the promise of Allah is truth, but most of them do not know.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the power and sovereignty of Allah, stating that everything in the heavens and the earth belongs to Him. The verse then affirms the truth of Allah's promise, indicating that it will certainly be fulfilled. However, the verse also highlights the lack of understanding and knowledge among most people, as they do not fully comprehend the reality of Allah's promise and its implications. The verse serves as a reminder to people of the greatness of Allah and the importance of recognizing and submitting to His power and authority.
orig: ألا إن لله ما في السماوات والأرض ألا إن وعد الله حق ولكن أكثرهم لا يعلمون

translation: He gives life and causes death, and to Him you will be returned.
interpretation: The verse affirms the power and control of God over all aspects of life and death. The phrase 'He gives life and causes death' highlights the ultimate authority of God over all living beings. The phrase 'to Him you will be returned' emphasizes the belief in the afterlife and the ultimate accountability of all human beings before God. The verse serves as a reminder of the transience of life and the importance of leading a righteous life in preparation for the afterlife.
orig: هو يحيي ويميت وإليه ترجعون

translation: O mankind, indeed there has come to you a notification from your Lord and a healing for what is in the chests and a guidance and mercy for the believers.
interpretation: The verse addresses all of humanity, reminding them that they have received a message from their Lord. This message serves as a reminder and a source of healing for the troubles and worries that people carry in their hearts. The verse also provides guidance, leading people towards the right path and showing them the way to live a good and fulfilling life. Lastly, the verse offers mercy, specifically for those who believe in the message and follow its teachings. Overall, the verse highlights the importance of the message, its healing and guiding power, and its potential to bring mercy and compassion to those who believe.
orig: يا أيها الناس قد جاءتكم موعظة من ربكم وشفاء لما في الصدور وهدى ورحمة للمؤمنين

translation: Say, 'In the bounty of God and His mercy - in that let them rejoice': that is better than what they amass.
interpretation: The verse addresses the Prophet Muhammad and commands him to proclaim that true joy and happiness come from the bounty and mercy of God. This is presented as a superior alternative to the material possessions and wealth that people accumulate in their pursuit of happiness. The verse suggests that true joy and contentment can only be found through God's grace and mercy, and that worldly possessions are fleeting and ultimately insufficient for achieving lasting happiness.
orig: قل بفضل الله وبرحمته فبذلك فليفرحوا هو خير مما يجمعون

translation: Say, 'Have you seen what Allah has sent down to you for sustenance, but you have made some of it unlawful and some of it lawful?' Say, 'Has Allah permitted you [to do this], or are you inventing [something] about Allah?'
interpretation: The verse addresses the people who have made some of the sustenance provided by Allah unlawful and some lawful, without any permission from Allah. The verse commands the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to ask them if they have received permission from Allah to do so. Alternatively, the verse questions whether they are inventing things about Allah, implying that they are attributing something to Allah that is not true. The verse emphasizes the importance of following the guidance of Allah and not distorting it for personal gain or preference. It serves as a reminder that Allah is the provider of all sustenance and that it is not for humans to decide what is lawful and unlawful without His permission.
orig: قل أرأيتم ما أنزل الله لكم من رزق فجعلتم منه حراما وحلالا قل آلله أذن لكم أم على الله تفترون

translation: And those who falsely attribute lies to God will on the Day of Resurrection be disappointed. Indeed, God is full of bounty to the people, but most of them are not grateful.
interpretation: The verse highlights the fate of those who falsely attribute lies to God on the Day of Resurrection. The verse emphasizes that God is generous and kind to people, but most of them do not appreciate His blessings. The verse serves as a warning to those who spread falsehoods and lies about God, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's judgment.
orig: وما ظن الذين يفترون على الله الكذب يوم القيامة إن الله لذو فضل على الناس ولكن أكثرهم لا يشكرون

translation: And you are not, in [matters of] the affair, by any means, hiding, and you are not reciting from the Qur'an, and you are not doing any deed, except that We are witnesses over you when you are engaged therein. And not absent from your Lord is any matter, [weighted] as small as a mustard seed, or [greater] than that, but [all] is in a clear record.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes God's omniscience and omnipresence, stating that God is aware of all human actions and thoughts. The verse mentions that God is a witness to every matter, including what people hide, what they recite from the Qur'an, and what they do. The verse also states that nothing, not even a mustard seed, is hidden from God. The verse serves as a reminder that God is aware of every action and thought, and that all will be recorded and accounted for in the afterlife.
orig: وما تكون في شأن وما تتلو منه من قرآن ولا تعملون من عمل إلا كنا عليكم شهودا إذ تفيضون فيه وما يعزب عن ربك من مثقال ذرة في الأرض ولا في السماء ولا أصغر من ذلك ولا أكبر إلا في كتاب مبين

translation: Indeed, the allies of Allah will not fear nor will they grieve.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the ultimate protection and peace of mind that the allies or friends of God will experience. They will not have to fear anything and they will not be subject to grief or sorrow. This verse serves as a source of comfort and hope for those who are striving to be close to God, reminding them of the ultimate reward that awaits them. It also serves as a reminder for those who are not on the path of righteousness, urging them to reflect on their actions and to work towards earning God's favor and protection.
orig: ألا إن أولياء الله لا خوف عليهم ولا هم يحزنون

translation: Those who have believed and have been righteous.
interpretation: The verse describes a group of people who have both faith and righteousness. The phrase 'have believed' (آمنوا) implies a deep and committed belief in God and the teachings of Islam. The phrase 'have been righteous' (كانوا يتقون) refers to their actions and behavior, indicating that they are mindful of God's commands and strive to live in accordance with His will. Together, these qualities of faith and righteousness are highly valued in Islam and are seen as essential for a fulfilling and successful life, both in this world and in the hereafter.
orig: الذين آمنوا وكانوا يتقون

translation: They have the good news in this worldly life and in the hereafter. There is no changing the words of Allah. That is the great victory.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the good news that believers receive in this worldly life and in the hereafter. The verse emphasizes the unchangeable and eternal nature of Allah's words, indicating that the believers can have full trust and reliance on His promises. The verse also highlights the greatness of the victory that the believers will achieve. The verse serves as a source of hope and reassurance for the believers, reminding them of the blessings and rewards that await them in both this world and the hereafter.
orig: لهم البشرى في الحياة الدنيا وفي الآخرة لا تبديل لكلمات الله ذلك هو الفوز العظيم

translation: And let not their speech grieve you. Indeed, power belongs to Allah entirely. He is the Hearing, the Knowing.
interpretation: The verse addresses the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) and advises him not to be saddened or distressed by the words or criticisms of the disbelievers. It affirms that all power and authority belong to Allah alone, and that He is the All-Hearing and All-Knowing. This means that Allah is aware of the situation and has the power to handle it, so there is no need for the Prophet to feel distressed or worried. The verse serves as a reminder to the believers to place their trust and reliance in Allah and not to be affected by the words or actions of the disbelievers.
orig: ولا يحزنك قولهم إن العزة لله جميعا هو السميع العليم

translation: No! Indeed, for Allah is what is in the heavens and what is on the earth, and to Him will be returned the invocation of those who invoke besides Him, as those (others) do not intercede except on His behalf. Indeed, they are, to Him, unaware.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the oneness and uniqueness of God, stating that everything in the heavens and the earth belongs to Him. The verse criticizes those who worship other beings besides God, stating that their worship is based on mere conjecture and that these beings do not have the power to intercede on their behalf. The verse concludes by stating that these beings are unaware of the true nature of God and are therefore unable to truly represent or help those who worship them.
orig: ألا إن لله من في السماوات ومن في الأرض وما يتبع الذين يدعون من دون الله شركاء إن يتبعون إلا الظن وإن هم إلا يخرصون

translation: He it is who made for you the night that you may rest therein, and the day giving light; most surely there are signs in this for a people who hear.
interpretation: The verse highlights the wisdom and mercy of God in creating the cycle of day and night. The night is a time for rest and rejuvenation, while the day is a time for activity and productivity. The verse emphasizes that there are signs and lessons in this natural phenomenon for those who are willing to reflect and understand. It serves as a reminder that the creation of the universe and its order and rhythm are clear evidence of God's existence and power. The verse also encourages people to be among those who are open to learning and understanding the signs of God in their surroundings.
orig: هو الذي جعل لكم الليل لتسكنوا فيه والنهار مبصرا إن في ذلك لآيات لقوم يسمعون

translation: They say, 'Has God taken a son, glory be to Him! He is the Self-Sufficient! His is all that is in the heavens and all that is in the earth.' You have no authority for this. Will you say, concerning God, what you do not know?
interpretation: The verse addresses the disbelievers who claim that God has taken a son, a notion that is rejected and considered blasphemous in Islam. The verse emphasizes God's self-sufficiency and His ownership of all that is in the heavens and the earth. The verse questions the authority of those who make such claims, and it rebukes them for speaking about God without knowledge. The verse serves as a reminder that it is not permissible to attribute to God anything that is not supported by revelation, and it highlights the importance of avoiding speculation about God's nature and attributes.
orig: قالوا اتخذ الله ولدا سبحانه هو الغني له ما في السماوات وما في الأرض إن عندكم من سلطان بهذا أتقولون على الله ما لا تعلمون

translation: Say, 'Indeed, those who invent falsehoods about Allah will not succeed.'
interpretation: The verse is a command to the Prophet Muhammad to declare that those who fabricate lies about Allah will not prosper or be successful in the hereafter. The verse emphasizes the severe consequences of lying about Allah and warns against it. It also serves as a reminder that truth and honesty are highly valued in Islam and that falsehood and deception will ultimately lead to failure and ruin.
orig: قل إن الذين يفترون على الله الكذب لا يفلحون

translation: Temporary provision in this world, then to Us is their return, then We shall make them taste the severe punishment for what they used to disbelieve.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the fleeting nature of worldly possessions and the ultimate return of all beings to God. It emphasizes that God will make those who disbelieve taste severe punishment for their disbelief. The verse serves as a reminder that worldly pleasures are temporary and that ultimate justice will be served in the afterlife.
orig: متاع في الدنيا ثم إلينا مرجعهم ثم نذيقهم العذاب الشديد بما كانوا يكفرون

translation: Relate to them the story of Noah, when he said to his people: 'O my people, if my stay and my reminding you of the signs of God have become too much for you, then on God I rely. So gather your plan and your partners, and then let your plan not be against you as a source of regret. Then give your response to me and do not give me respite.'
interpretation: The verse relates the story of Noah and his people, and highlights Noah's frustration and disappointment with their lack of response to his message. Noah reminds his people of the signs of God and expresses his reliance on God. He encourages his people to gather their plan and partners, indicating that they should come together and make a decision. However, he warns them not to let their decision be a source of regret, emphasizing the importance of making the right choice. Noah then asks his people to give him a response and not to delay, indicating the urgency of the situation and the need for a decision to be made.
orig: واتل عليهم نبأ نوح إذ قال لقومه يا قوم إن كان كبر عليكم مقامي وتذكيري بآيات الله فعلى الله توكلت فأجمعوا أمركم وشركاءكم ثم لا يكن أمركم عليكم غمة ثم اقضوا إلي ولا تنظرون

translation: But if you turn away (from Islam), then know that I have not asked you for any wage. My wage is only from Allah, and I have been commanded to be among the Muslims.
interpretation: The verse is spoken from the perspective of the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH), and it addresses those who have not yet accepted Islam. The Prophet clarifies that he does not seek any material reward for his efforts in spreading the message of Islam. Rather, his reward comes solely from Allah. The verse also highlights that the Prophet has been commanded to be among the Muslims, signifying his unwavering commitment and belief in Islam. Thus, the verse emphasizes the selflessness of the Prophet and his dedication to the faith, and it serves as a reminder that true believers should not seek worldly gains but rather focus on their devotion and obedience to Allah.
orig: فإن توليتم فما سألتكم من أجر إن أجري إلا على الله وأمرت أن أكون من المسلمين

translation: But they denied him, so We saved him and those who were with him in the ship, and We made them successors, and We drowned those who denied Our signs. Then see how was the end of the warners.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the story of a prophet who was denied by his people. As a result, God saved him and his followers, while those who denied God's signs were drowned. The verse emphasizes the consequences of denying God's signs and the importance of believing in and following the prophets. The verse also highlights the role of the prophets as warners and the ultimate fate of those who reject their message. It serves as a reminder for people to reflect on the consequences of their actions and the importance of heeding the warnings of the prophets.
orig: فكذبوه فنجيناه ومن معه في الفلك وجعلناهم خلائف وأغرقنا الذين كذبوا بآياتنا فانظر كيف كان عاقبة المنذرين

translation: Then We sent after them Messengers to their people, so they came to them with clear proofs, but they were not believing in what they had rejected before. Thus do We inflict punishment upon the transgressors.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the sending of Messengers to the people after previous Messengers had failed to convince them. These new Messengers brought clear proofs and evidence, but the people still refused to believe. The verse highlights the pattern of disbelief and rejection of truth by the people, and emphasizes the punishment that follows such behavior. The verse is a reminder that those who persist in their transgression and rejection of truth will face consequences for their actions.
orig: ثم بعثنا من بعده رسلا إلى قومهم فجاءوهم بالبينات فما كانوا ليؤمنوا بما كذبوا به من قبل كذلك نطبع على قلوب المعتدين

translation: Then We sent after them Moses and Aaron to Pharaoh and his chiefs with Our signs, but they were arrogant, and they were a sinful people.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the sending of Moses and Aaron to Pharaoh and his chiefs as messengers from God. The message they brought was supported by signs from God, yet the Pharaoh and his chiefs were arrogant and rejected the message. The verse describes them as a sinful people, emphasizing their rejection of God's message and their arrogance in the face of God's signs. The verse serves as a reminder of the consequences of arrogance and rejection of God's message, and the importance of humility and submission to God's will.
orig: ثم بعثنا من بعدهم موسى وهارون إلى فرعون وملئه بآياتنا فاستكبروا وكانوا قوما مجرمين

translation: But when the truth came to them from Us, they said, 'This is clear magic'.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the people's rejection of the truth, which came to them from God. Instead of accepting it and submitting to it, they labeled it as 'clear magic'. This verse highlights the human tendency to reject and deny the truth when it goes against their preconceived notions and desires. It serves as a reminder that the truth is not always what people want to hear, and that it takes courage and humility to accept it and submit to it.
orig: فلما جاءهم الحق من عندنا قالوا إن هذا لسحر مبين

translation: Moses said, 'Do you say to the truth when it has come to you, "This is clearly magic", and you deny and turn away [from it]?'
interpretation: The verse recounts Moses' response to the people who rejected the truth (represented by Moses) and instead called it magic. Moses expresses his disbelief at their denial of the truth, despite it being clear and evident. The verse highlights the importance of recognizing and accepting the truth, even when it goes against one's preconceived notions or expectations. It also serves as a critique of those who reject the truth and instead cling to falsehoods, whether out of stubbornness, fear, or self-interest.
orig: قال موسى أتقولون للحق لما جاءكم أسحر هذا ولا يفلح الساحرون

translation: They say, 'You have only come to us that you may turn us away from our gods, and that your God and ours may become one; and that you may bring about the earth to become level under you, and then you may become ascendant tyrants.'
interpretation: The verse describes the accusations of the disbelievers against the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) and his companions. They accuse the Prophet of coming to them to change their religion and make their God the same as the Prophet's God. They also accuse the Prophet of wanting to take control of the land and becoming tyrants. The verse highlights the resistance and rejection of the disbelievers towards the message of Islam and their refusal to accept the truth.
orig: قالوا أجئتنا لتلفتنا عما وجدنا عليه آباءنا وتكون لكما الكبرياء في الأرض وما نحن لكما بمؤمنين

translation: And Pharaoh said, 'Bring to me every knowledgeable sorcerer.'
interpretation: The verse recounts Pharaoh's command to gather all the skilled sorcerers in response to Moses's miracles. Pharaoh, who is depicted as a tyrant and disbeliever in the Qur'an, refuses to acknowledge the truth of Moses's message and instead seeks to discredit him by challenging him to a contest of sorcery. The verse highlights Pharaoh's rejection of the truth and his reliance on falsehood and deception as a means of maintaining his power and authority.
orig: وقال فرعون ائتوني بكل ساحر عليم

translation: When the magicians came, Moses said to them: 'Cast what you are going to cast.'
interpretation: The verse recounts the story of the magicians who came to challenge Moses and his God. Moses, in response to their challenge, tells them to proceed with their magic. The verse emphasizes Moses' confidence in the power of his God and his willingness to confront the magicians. This story serves as a reminder of the power of faith and the importance of standing up for one's beliefs, even in the face of adversity and opposition.
orig: فلما جاء السحرة قال لهم موسى ألقوا ما أنتم ملقون

translation: But when they threw, Moses said, 'What you have brought is magic; surely Allah will make it null. Surely Allah does not make the work of the corruptors succeed.'
interpretation: The verse recounts the story of Moses and the magicians who challenged him to a contest of magic. When the magicians threw their ropes and staffs, Moses responded by declaring that what they had brought was merely magic and that it would be made null by God. Moses asserts that God will not allow the deceitful schemes of the corrupt magicians to succeed. The verse conveys the power and authority of God, who can nullify the works of those who act in corruption and deceit. It also highlights the faith and certainty of Moses in God's ability to distinguish truth from falsehood.
orig: فلما ألقوا قال موسى ما جئتم به السحر إن الله سيبطله إن الله لا يصلح عمل المفسدين

translation: And to Allah belongs the true right, but most of the criminals dislike it.
interpretation: The verse affirms that the truth and what is rightfully due belongs to Allah, meaning that all judgments and decisions rest with Him. The second part of the verse highlights the fact that most criminals or wrongdoers dislike this truth, as it implies that they will be held accountable for their actions and will have to face the consequences. The verse serves as a reminder that Allah's justice will ultimately prevail, despite the resistance of those who seek to avoid it.
orig: ويحق الله الحق بكلماته ولو كره المجرمون

translation: And none believed in Moses, except a few of his people, out of fear from Pharaoh and his establishment, that they would persecute them. Indeed, Pharaoh was exalted in the land, and indeed, he was of the transgressors.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the lack of belief in Moses by most of his people, except for a few who feared persecution by Pharaoh and his establishment. The verse highlights the power and tyranny of Pharaoh, who was exalted in the land and transgressed against his people. The verse implies that the few believers in Moses were oppressed and had to keep their faith hidden due to the risk of persecution. The verse serves as a reminder of the challenges faced by those who stand up for the truth against powerful and oppressive forces, and the importance of staying steadfast in one's faith despite the difficulties.
orig: فما آمن لموسى إلا ذرية من قومه على خوف من فرعون وملئهم أن يفتنهم وإن فرعون لعال في الأرض وإنه لمن المسرفين

translation: And Moses said, 'O my people, if you have believed in God, then put your trust in Him, if you are indeed Muslims.'
interpretation: In this verse, Moses is addressing the Israelites and urging them to have faith in God and put their trust in Him if they truly believe. The verse highlights the importance of faith and trust in God, and it serves as a reminder that true believers should rely on God and have complete trust in His plan and His abilities. The verse also implies that faith and trust go hand in hand, and that belief in God should be reflected in one's actions and decisions. Additionally, the verse may be seen as a call for the Israelites to demonstrate their faith and commitment to God by following Moses's leadership and guidance.
orig: وقال موسى يا قوم إن كنتم آمنتم بالله فعليه توكلوا إن كنتم مسلمين

translation: And they said, 'On Allah we have relied. Our Lord, make us not a trial for the unjust people.'
interpretation: The verse shows the people placing their trust and reliance in Allah, asking Him not to make them a trial or a source of temptation for the unjust people. The verse highlights the importance of seeking protection from God against falling into trials and tribulations, and the need for believers to remain steadfast and firm in their faith, even in the face of adversity and oppression from unjust people.
orig: فقالوا على الله توكلنا ربنا لا تجعلنا فتنة للقوم الظالمين

translation: And We rescued you with mercy from the disbelieving people.
interpretation: The verse refers to an instance of divine intervention where God rescued the person or group being addressed from a community of disbelievers through His mercy. The verse highlights the power of God's mercy and its role in delivering the believers from harm. It also emphasizes the negative consequences of disbelief and the importance of seeking refuge in God's mercy. The verse may serve as a reminder of God's protection and care for the believers, as well as a warning to those who reject faith and the consequences they may face.
orig: ونجنا برحمتك من القوم الكافرين

translation: And We inspired to Moses and his brother, 'Settle for your people in Egypt and make your houses places of worship and establish prayer and give good tidings to the believers.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about God's instruction to Moses and his brother to establish a community of believers in Egypt. They are told to make their houses into places of worship and to establish prayer. The verse also instructs them to give good tidings to the believers, indicating that the community of believers will face challenges and hardships, but will ultimately be successful. The verse emphasizes the importance of establishing a strong and devoted community of believers, and the role of the house of worship in fostering that community.
orig: وأوحينا إلى موسى وأخيه أن تبوآ لقومكما بمصر بيوتا واجعلوا بيوتكم قبلة وأقيموا الصلاة وبشر المؤمنين

translation: And Moses said, 'Our Lord, you have given Pharaoh and his nobles splendor and wealth in the worldly life, our Lord, so that they may lead people astray from Your path. Our Lord, make their wealth an enclosure for them and tighten their hearts so that they do not believe until they see the painful punishment.'
interpretation: The verse is a supplication by Moses to God, expressing his concern about Pharaoh and his nobles who have been given wealth and power by God, but are using it to lead people astray from the path of God. Moses prays for two things: first, that God would make their wealth a barrier for them, preventing them from using it to harm others; and second, that God would tighten their hearts, making it difficult for them to believe until they experience the painful punishment. The verse highlights the power of wealth and its potential for corruption, as well as the importance of prayer and reliance on God.
orig: وقال موسى ربنا إنك آتيت فرعون وملأه زينة وأموالا في الحياة الدنيا ربنا ليضلوا عن سبيلك ربنا اطمس على أموالهم واشدد على قلوبهم فلا يؤمنوا حتى يروا العذاب الأليم

translation: He said, 'I have responded to your call, so fear me and do not follow the way of those who do not know.'
interpretation: The verse recounts a statement made by a prophet or a messenger, who has responded to the call of his people. He commands them to fear him, meaning to believe in him and follow his teachings. He also warns them not to follow the way of those who 'do not know', meaning those who are ignorant of the truth and the right path. The verse emphasizes the importance of following the guidance of the prophet and avoiding the ways of the ignorant. It serves as a reminder that true guidance and knowledge come from the prophet, and that following any other path will lead to ignorance and error.
orig: قال قد أجيبت دعوتكما فاستقيما ولا تتبعان سبيل الذين لا يعلمون

translation: And We parted the sea for the Children of Israel, and Pharaoh and his troops pursued them in tyranny and enmity until, when the drowning overtook him, he said, 'I believe that there is no deity except the One in whom the Children of Israel believe, and I am of the Muslims.',
interpretation: The verse relates the story of the parting of the sea for the Children of Israel and the subsequent pursuit by Pharaoh and his army. The verse highlights Pharaoh's tyranny and enmity towards the Children of Israel. The dramatic moment of the verse is when Pharaoh, as he is drowning, declares his belief in the God of the Children of Israel and proclaims himself as one of the Muslims. However, this declaration comes too late, as it does not erase his past actions and the harm he inflicted upon the Children of Israel. The verse serves as a reminder of the fleeting nature of this worldly life and the importance of sincerity and consistency in faith and actions.
orig: وجاوزنا ببني إسرائيل البحر فأتبعهم فرعون وجنوده بغيا وعدوا حتى إذا أدركه الغرق قال آمنت أنه لا إله إلا الذي آمنت به بنو إسرائيل وأنا من المسلمين

translation: Indeed, you have disobeyed before and were of the corrupters.
interpretation: The verse is a condemnation of past disobedience and corruption. The subject of the verse has previously disobeyed and engaged in corrupt activities. The verse serves as a reminder of past wrongdoings and a warning that such actions have consequences.
orig: آلآن وقد عصيت قبل وكنت من المفسدين

translation: Today We shall save you in body that you may be a sign to those who come after you. Indeed, many among mankind are heedless of Our signs.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the salvation of an individual or a group of people for the purpose of being a sign or a lesson for those who come after them. The verse highlights the importance of the saved person(s) as a reminder of God's power and intervention. The verse also points out the heedlessness of many people towards the signs of God, which can be interpreted as a warning to those who ignore the lessons of history and the signs of God in their lives.
orig: فاليوم ننجيك ببدنك لتكون لمن خلفك آية وإن كثيرا من الناس عن آياتنا لغافلون

translation: And We had already sent Moses with Our signs to Pharaoh and his leaders, but they rejected them. So We took revenge on them, and We drowned them all. Then We said to the Children of Israel after that, 'Dwell securely in the land (of Egypt)'. And when the promise of the Hereafter came to be fulfilled, We gathered you together in a Day of Assembly (i.e. the Day of Resurrection). But how was the reminder (given to you)?
interpretation: The verse speaks about the story of Moses and the Children of Israel. It highlights how Moses was sent with signs to Pharaoh and his leaders, but they rejected them, leading to God's punishment of drowning them. The verse then mentions how the Children of Israel were allowed to dwell securely in the land of Egypt. However, the verse also emphasizes the importance of the Day of Resurrection, when the promise of the Hereafter will be fulfilled and all people will be gathered together. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of heeding the signs and messages sent by God, and the consequences of rejecting them.
orig: ولقد بوأنا بني إسرائيل مبوأ صدق ورزقناهم من الطيبات فما اختلفوا حتى جاءهم العلم إن ربك يقضي بينهم يوم القيامة فيما كانوا فيه يختلفون

translation: So if you are in doubt about what We have revealed to you, then ask those who have been reading the Scripture before you. Indeed, the truth has come to you from your Lord, so do not be among the doubters.
interpretation: The verse addresses the Prophet Muhammad, may peace be upon him, and advises him to consult the people of the book (Jews and Christians) if he has any doubts about the revelation he has received. The verse affirms that the truth has been revealed to him by his Lord and encourages him not to have doubts. The verse serves to emphasize the authenticity and reliability of the revelation and encourages the Prophet to seek knowledge and understanding from those who have previous knowledge of the scripture.
orig: فإن كنت في شك مما أنزلنا إليك فاسأل الذين يقرءون الكتاب من قبلك لقد جاءك الحق من ربك فلا تكونن من الممترين

translation: And be not of those who deny Allah's signs, so you become of the losers.
interpretation: The verse warns against denying the signs of God and exhorts the reader to avoid falling into the category of those who reject the truth. By doing so, one will avoid the fate of being among the losers. The verse emphasizes the importance of recognizing and accepting the signs of God, which can be interpreted as the messages and teachings in the Qur'an. By accepting and following these signs, one can find guidance and avoid the negative consequences of denial and rejection.
orig: ولا تكونن من الذين كذبوا بآيات الله فتكون من الخاسرين

translation: Indeed, those who have been unfaithful to the covenant of your Lord will not believe -
interpretation: The verse highlights the rejection of faith by those who have broken their covenant with God. The word 'unfaithful' implies a breach of trust and a failure to fulfill one's obligations towards God. The verse suggests that such individuals, despite being aware of God's message, will not believe or accept it. This verse may serve as a reminder of the importance of upholding one's covenant with God, and the consequences of breaking that trust.
orig: إن الذين حقت عليهم كلمت ربك لا يؤمنون

translation: And if only a single sign had come to them, they would surely have seen the painful punishment.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the disbelievers who rejected the signs and messages of God. The verse emphasizes the severity of the punishment that they would have faced if only one sign had come to them. The phrase 'painful punishment' implies that the punishment would have been severe and unbearable. The verse serves as a reminder to those who deny the signs of God and warns them of the consequences of their disbelief and rejection.
orig: ولو جاءتهم كل آية حتى يروا العذاب الأليم

translation: Had not the town believed and practiced righteousness, We would surely have granted them blessings from the heaven and the earth. But they denied (the Messenger), so We took them (in punishment) while they were unaware.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the missed opportunity of a town to receive blessings from God due to their disbelief and lack of righteousness. The verse highlights that if the town had believed and practiced righteousness, they would have been granted blessings from the heavens and the earth. However, they denied the truth and as a result, God took them in punishment while they were unaware and unprepared. This verse serves as a reminder of the importance of faith and righteous actions, and the consequences of disbelief and sin.
orig: فلولا كانت قرية آمنت فنفعها إيمانها إلا قوم يونس لما آمنوا كشفنا عنهم عذاب الخزي في الحياة الدنيا ومتعناهم إلى حين

translation: And if your Lord had willed, whoever is in the earth would have believed all of them altogether. So, will you (O Muhammad) force the people until they become believers?
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the power of God's will and the limits of human ability to influence others in matters of faith. It highlights the fact that even if God had willed it, not everyone on earth would have become believers. The verse also makes it clear that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) cannot force people to believe. Instead, the responsibility of the Prophet is to convey the message of Islam, and it is up to each individual to choose whether or not to accept it. This verse reminds us of the importance of free will and the limits of human power, and it emphasizes the role of God as the ultimate controller of all things.
orig: ولو شاء ربك لآمن من في الأرض كلهم جميعا أفأنت تكره الناس حتى يكونوا مؤمنين

translation: And it is not for a soul to believe except by permission of Allah, and He will place defilement upon those who do not use reason.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the role of God's will in the act of faith, stating that no soul can believe without God's permission. At the same time, the verse criticizes those who do not use reason, suggesting that they are prone to error and subject to divine punishment. The verse serves as a reminder that faith is a gift from God, and that it is important to use reason and critical thinking in order to avoid falling into error and ignorance.
orig: وما كان لنفس أن تؤمن إلا بإذن الله ويجعل الرجس على الذين لا يعقلون

translation: Say, 'Consider what is in the heavens and the earth and whatever signs and warnings could benefit a people who believe.'
interpretation: The verse addresses the Prophet Muhammad and instructs him to tell the disbelievers to consider the signs of God in the heavens and the earth, which serve as a reminder of God's power and greatness. The verse also mentions the 'signs and warnings' that could benefit a people who believe, indicating that these signs and warnings are intended to guide people towards the right path and help them avoid the consequences of disbelief. The verse emphasizes the importance of reflection and contemplation, urging people to reflect on the wonders of God's creation and use that reflection as a means of gaining guidance and understanding.
orig: قل انظروا ماذا في السماوات والأرض وما تغني الآيات والنذر عن قوم لا يؤمنون

translation: Do they then wait except for the like of the days of those who passed away before them? Say, 'Then wait, I too am with you among those who are waiting.'
interpretation: The verse is a response to those who are waiting for some calamity or punishment to befall the believers. The verse compares their situation to the people of the past who were destroyed for their disbelief and disobedience. The phrase 'then wait' is repeated to emphasize the futility of their waiting and the inevitability of the consequences of their actions. The speaker, most likely the Prophet Muhammad, declares that he is also waiting, but with the patience and certainty of faith. The verse serves as a reminder that the believers should remain steadfast and patient in the face of adversity and persecution, knowing that God is with them and that justice will ultimately prevail.
orig: فهل ينتظرون إلا مثل أيام الذين خلوا من قبلهم قل فانتظروا إني معكم من المنتظرين

translation: Then We save Our messengers and those who believe. Indeed, it is Our duty to save the believers.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the promise of God to save His messengers and those who believe in them. The verse emphasizes the responsibility of God to protect and save the believers from harm and danger. This verse serves as a source of comfort and reassurance for the believers, reminding them that God is always with them and will protect and save them. It also highlights the importance of faith and belief in God and His messengers, as those who have faith will be saved by God.
orig: ثم ننجي رسلنا والذين آمنوا كذلك حقا علينا ننج المؤمنين

translation: Say, 'O mankind, indeed if you are in doubt about my religion, then I do not worship those you worship other than Allah, but I worship Allah, who will take your souls. And I am ordered to be of the believers.'
interpretation: The verse is a message from the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) to the people, inviting them to reflect on his religion and the fact that he only worships Allah, the one who will take their souls at death. He distinguishes himself from those who worship other deities and clarifies that he has been commanded to be among the believers. This statement emphasizes the Prophet's commitment to monotheism and his role as a leader and example for the believers, encouraging them to reflect on the true nature of worship and the importance of following the right path.
orig: قل يا أيها الناس إن كنتم في شك من ديني فلا أعبد الذين تعبدون من دون الله ولكن أعبد الله الذي يتوفاكم وأمرت أن أكون من المؤمنين

translation: And surely I have turned my face toward Him who created the heavens and the earth, as a Hanif, and I am not of the polytheists.
interpretation: The verse speaks of the speaker's devotion and commitment to the worship of the one true God, who created the heavens and the earth. The speaker declares that they have turned their face towards God, indicating a complete and total dedication to the worship of God. The term 'Hanif' refers to a person who is upright and pure in their faith, and who rejects idolatry and polytheism. The speaker emphasizes their rejection of polytheism, further highlighting their commitment to monotheism. The verse can be seen as a declaration of faith and a rejection of any other deities or false gods.
orig: وأن أقم وجهك للدين حنيفا ولا تكونن من المشركين

translation: And do not leave (the worship of) Allah except for that which does not benefit or harm you. If you do, then indeed you will be of the wrongdoers.
