interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of maintaining a strong relationship with Allah and not allowing anything to come between that relationship. The verse warns against leaving the worship of Allah for anything that does not bring benefit or harm, meaning that one should not let other things distract them from their religious obligations. The verse also implies that engaging in such behavior will lead to wrongdoing. The verse serves as a reminder to prioritize one's relationship with Allah above all else and to avoid engaging in behavior that may lead one astray.
orig: ولا تدع من دون الله ما لا ينفعك ولا يضرك فإن فعلت فإنك إذا من الظالمين

translation: And if Allah touches you with harm, there is no remover of it except Him; and if He intends for you good, then there is no repeller of His favor. He causes it to reach whom He wills of His servants. And He is the Forgiving, the Merciful.
interpretation: The verse highlights the power and control that only Allah has over all things. It emphasizes that if Allah brings harm upon a person, there is no one who can remove it except Him. Conversely, if Allah intends good for a person, no one can prevent it from reaching them. The verse further emphasizes Allah's mercy and forgiveness, as He bestows His favor upon whom He wills from His servants. The verse serves as a reminder of Allah's omnipotence and the importance of seeking His favor and forgiveness.
orig: وإن يمسسك الله بضر فلا كاشف له إلا هو وإن يردك بخير فلا راد لفضله يصيب به من يشاء من عباده وهو الغفور الرحيم

translation: Say, 'O mankind, indeed the truth has come to you from your Lord. So whoever wills - let him believe; and whoever wills - let him disbelieve.' Indeed, I am not a manager over you.
interpretation: The verse speaks to all of humanity, emphasizing that the truth has come to them from their Lord. The verse then gives a choice to the people, to either believe or disbelieve. The verse highlights the individual's responsibility for their own actions and the consequences of those actions. The verse also clarifies that the speaker does not hold any authority over the people, and cannot force them to choose one way or the other. The verse encourages personal responsibility, accountability, and the freedom to choose one's own path.
orig: قل يا أيها الناس قد جاءكم الحق من ربكم فمن اهتدى فإنما يهتدي لنفسه ومن ضل فإنما يضل عليها وما أنا عليكم بوكيل

translation: And follow what has been revealed to you from your Lord, and do not be of those who associate others with Him. And be of those who are patient, and do not be of those who despair.
interpretation: The verse commands the believers to follow the guidance that has been revealed to them from their Lord, meaning the Qur'an and the teachings of the Prophet Muhammad. The verse warns against associating partners with God (a sin known as shirk), and encourages patience and steadfastness in the face of adversity. The verse emphasizes the importance of perseverance and trust in God's justice and wisdom, and discourages despair and hopelessness.
orig: واتبع ما يوحى إليك واصبر حتى يحكم الله وهو خير الحاكمين

translation: The Romans have been defeated in the nearest land, and after their defeat they will be victorious.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the defeat and subsequent victory of the Romans. It emphasizes the unexpected nature of the Roman defeat and the certainty of their victory. The verse serves as a reminder that even in the face of defeat and hardship, one should not lose hope and should continue to strive. It also highlights the divine wisdom and knowledge behind the events of the world, as the verse states that the events were decreed by a 'wise and knowledgeable' God.
orig: الر كتاب أحكمت آياته ثم فصلت من لدن حكيم خبير

translation: Prostrate yourselves not to the sun nor to the moon, but prostrate yourselves to Allah who created them, if it is Him ye wish to serve.
interpretation: The verse commands the worship of only one God, Allah, and forbids the worship of the sun and moon. The verse emphasizes the importance of worshipping the creator, Allah, rather than the created. By prostrating oneself to Allah, one is expressing their devotion, submission, and obedience to Allah. The verse serves as a reminder of the monotheistic principle of Islam, and the importance of directing all worship and devotion to Allah alone.
orig: ألا تعبدوا إلا الله إنني لكم منه نذير وبشير

translation: Seek forgiveness from your Lord and then repent to Him. He will provide you with a good provision until a specified time and will give each doer of favor his favor. But if you turn away, I fear for you the punishment of a great day.
interpretation: The verse encourages the believers to seek forgiveness from their Lord and repent to Him. It promises that those who do so will be granted a good provision until a specified time and each person will receive their due reward for their good deeds. However, the verse also warns that if they turn away from this path, the consequence will be a severe punishment on a great day.
orig: وأن استغفروا ربكم ثم توبوا إليه يمتعكم متاعا حسنا إلى أجل مسمى ويؤت كل ذي فضل فضله وإن تولوا فإني أخاف عليكم عذاب يوم كبير

translation: To God you will all return, and He has power over all things.
interpretation: The verse reminds the reader of the ultimate return to God, emphasizing His power and control over all things. This verse can be seen as a source of comfort and strength, reminding people that God is in control, even in difficult or uncertain times. It can also serve as a reminder of the transient nature of life and the importance of living a righteous and just life in preparation for the ultimate return to God.
orig: إلى الله مرجعكم وهو على كل شيء قدير

translation: No! Indeed, they (the disbelievers) are closing their breasts so that they may deny (the truth) through pride. No! When the truth has come to them, they will surely hate it. No! But when they see Our punishment, they will know who it is that is furthest from help.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the disbelievers who deny the truth and close their hearts to it due to their pride. They reject the truth even when it becomes clear to them. However, when they are faced with God's punishment, they will realize their mistake and understand that they are the ones who are most in need of help. The verse emphasizes the consequences of pride and arrogance and the importance of accepting the truth. It serves as a warning to those who deny the truth and a reminder to be humble and open-minded.
orig: ألا إنهم يثنون صدورهم ليستخفوا منه ألا حين يستغشون ثيابهم يعلم ما يسرون وما يعلنون إنه عليم بذات الصدور

translation: And there is no creature on earth but that upon Allah is its provision, and He knows its dwelling place and its depository. All is in a clear register.
interpretation: The verse affirms that all provision for creatures on earth comes from God, and that He has knowledge of their dwelling places and their needs. The verse emphasizes God's control and sustenance of all living beings, and the idea that everything is recorded and accounted for. This can be interpreted as a reminder of God's power and knowledge, and a call for gratitude and trust in His provision and care.
orig: وما من دابة في الأرض إلا على الله رزقها ويعلم مستقرها ومستودعها كل في كتاب مبين

translation: And He it is Who created the heavens and the earth in six days, and His Throne was upon the water, that He might try you which of you is best in deed. But if you say: Surely you are going to be raised after death, (the unbelievers) will certainly say: This is nothing but a manifest (false)hood.
interpretation: The verse speaks about God's creation of the heavens and the earth in six days, and the purpose behind it, which is to test humanity by seeing who among them performs the best deeds. The verse also highlights the disbelievers' denial of the resurrection, and their dismissal of it as a falsehood. The verse serves as a reminder of the purpose of life, which is to worship and serve God, and the reality of the resurrection, which will come to pass regardless of the denial of the disbelievers.
orig: وهو الذي خلق السماوات والأرض في ستة أيام وكان عرشه على الماء ليبلوكم أيكم أحسن عملا ولئن قلت إنكم مبعوثون من بعد الموت ليقولن الذين كفروا إن هذا إلا سحر مبين

translation: But if We postpone the punishment for them until a determined number of years, they will surely say, 'What is holding it back?' On the day when it reaches them, it will not be turned aside from them, and they will be overwhelmed by what they used to ridicule.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the delay of God's punishment and the reaction of the people when it finally comes. The verse explains that even if the punishment is postponed for a determined number of years, the people will still question why it has not come yet. However, when the punishment finally reaches them, it will not be turned aside, and they will be overwhelmed by what they used to ridicule. The verse serves as a reminder that God's punishment is certain and that those who mock or belittle it will not escape its consequences.
orig: ولئن أخرنا عنهم العذاب إلى أمة معدودة ليقولن ما يحبسه ألا يوم يأتيهم ليس مصروفا عنهم وحاق بهم ما كانوا به يستهزئون

translation: And if We give man a taste of mercy from Us, and then We withdraw it from him, indeed, he is despairing, ungrateful.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the human's tendency to be ungrateful and despairing when faced with the withdrawal of God's mercy. The verse emphasizes that even after experiencing God's mercy, people may still take it for granted and fail to show gratitude. When the mercy is taken away, they are left in a state of despair and ungratefulness. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of being mindful of God's blessings and expressing gratitude for them, as well as a warning of the consequences of ingratitude and taking God's mercy for granted.
orig: ولئن أذقنا الإنسان منا رحمة ثم نزعناها منه إنه ليئوس كفور

translation: And if We let him taste mercy after distress has touched him, he will surely say: 'The evil has gone away from me.' Indeed, he becomes overjoyed and boastful.
interpretation: The verse speaks about a person who experiences hardship and then receives God's mercy. Despite experiencing God's mercy, the person quickly forgets about the hardship and becomes arrogant, thinking that the hardship will not return. The verse serves as a warning against becoming complacent and forgetting about God's power and the possibility of hardship returning. It emphasizes the importance of being grateful for God's blessings and remaining humble.
orig: ولئن أذقناه نعماء بعد ضراء مسته ليقولن ذهب السيئات عني إنه لفرح فخور

translation: Except for those who are patient and do good deeds, those - they will have forgiveness and a great reward.
interpretation: The verse distinguishes between two groups of people: those who are patient and do good deeds, and those who do not. The verse promises forgiveness and a great reward for the patient and righteous, indicating that their actions are pleasing to God. The verse serves as an encouragement for individuals to be patient and to do good deeds, emphasizing the benefits of such actions in the afterlife. At the same time, the verse implies that those who do not possess patience and do not engage in good deeds will not receive the same rewards in the afterlife.
orig: إلا الذين صبروا وعملوا الصالحات أولئك لهم مغفرة وأجر كبير

translation: Perhaps you (Muhammad) are feeling overwhelmed by what they say, and feeling sad that they say: 'If only a treasure had been sent down to him, or if only an angel had come with him!' You are only a warner, and God is responsible for all things.
interpretation: The verse speaks to the Prophet Muhammad and acknowledges his feelings of frustration and sadness in response to the disbelievers who reject his message. The disbelievers demand signs and miracles, such as the sending down of a treasure or the arrival of an angel, in order to believe. However, the verse reminds the Prophet that his role is simply to warn and convey the message, while it is up to God to take care of all things. The verse encourages the Prophet to be patient and persistent in his mission, despite the challenges and opposition he faces.
orig: فلعلك تارك بعض ما يوحى إليك وضائق به صدرك أن يقولوا لولا أنزل عليه كنز أو جاء معه ملك إنما أنت نذير والله على كل شيء وكيل

translation: Or do they say, 'He has fabricated it'? Say, 'Then bring ten fabricated chapters like it, and call upon whomever you can besides Allah, if you are truthful.'
interpretation: The verse challenges the disbelievers who accuse the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) of fabricating the Qur'an. The challenge is for them to produce ten chapters like it, with the same eloquence, beauty, and wisdom. Furthermore, they are asked to seek the help of anyone besides Allah, if they truly believe that someone else could have inspired the Qur'an. The verse highlights the inability of humans to produce anything comparable to the Qur'an, and the uniqueness of its divine origin. It serves as a powerful argument against those who deny the authenticity of the Qur'an, and a reminder of the power and greatness of Allah.
orig: أم يقولون افتراه قل فأتوا بعشر سور مثله مفتريات وادعوا من استطعتم من دون الله إن كنتم صادقين

translation: But if they do not respond to you, then know that it has been revealed only by the knowledge of Allah and that there is no deity except Him. So, will you not be reminded?
interpretation: The verse addresses a situation where the people being addressed do not respond or heed the message being conveyed. The verse emphasizes that the message being conveyed is from Allah's knowledge and that there is no other deity but Him. This serves to assert the authority and truth of the message being conveyed. The verse ends with a question, "So, will you not be reminded?", which serves as a call to reflection and a reminder of the importance of the message.
orig: فإلم يستجيبوا لكم فاعلموا أنما أنزل بعلم الله وأن لا إله إلا هو فهل أنتم مسلمون

translation: Whoever desires the life of this world and its adornment - We fully repay them for their deeds therein, whereas they, therein, are not diminished.
interpretation: The verse speaks about those who prioritize the enjoyment and material wealth of this world, and strive for it. The verse states that they will receive the full recompense for their deeds in this world, and they will not be deprived of it. This implies that they will receive the consequences of their actions, both good and bad, in this world. At the same time, the verse suggests that those who are focused on the temporary pleasures of this world may neglect their spiritual well-being and the hereafter. The verse serves as a reminder that the actions in this world have consequences and that it is important to strive for balance and righteousness in one's life.
orig: من كان يريد الحياة الدنيا وزينتها نوف إليهم أعمالهم فيها وهم فيها لا يبخسون

translation: Those are the ones who will have nothing but fire for company in the hereafter. Their deeds will have been fruitless, and all that they used to do will have been in vain.
interpretation: The verse describes the fate of certain individuals in the hereafter, where they will be accompanied only by fire. Their past deeds and efforts will have been in vain, and they will not receive any rewards for them. The verse serves as a warning to those who do not believe in the afterlife or do not take it seriously, reminding them that their actions in this world will have consequences in the next.
orig: أولئك الذين ليس لهم في الآخرة إلا النار وحبط ما صنعوا فيها وباطل ما كانوا يعملون

translation: Is he then who is on clear evidence from his Lord, and he recites it (the Qur'an) a witness (to it) morning and evening, (while) he is engaged (in the prayer)? Nay, but most of them believe not. So We let upon the unjust, leaders who do not believe. So every time they commit an evil deed, they say: 'We found our fathers doing this,' and 'Indeed, We are guided by it.' So just as We have destroyed the former generations, (so) will We destroy them. Such is a promise (made) by Us (for) it is true. So do not be in doubt about it, but establish the prayer and pay the zakat and obey the Messenger, so that you may receive mercy.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the importance of following the guidance and teachings of the Qur'an, and the consequences of not doing so. The verse contrasts those who follow the clear evidence from their Lord, reciting the Qur'an and being a witness to it, with those who do not believe. The verse emphasizes that most people do not believe and follow the unjust leaders. The verse warns of the destruction of those who commit evil deeds and use the excuse of following their ancestors. The verse encourages the believers to establish the prayer, pay the zakat (charity) and obey the Messenger in order to receive mercy from God. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of faith, obedience and the consequences of disbelief and disobedience.
orig: أفمن كان على بينة من ربه ويتلوه شاهد منه ومن قبله كتاب موسى إماما ورحمة أولئك يؤمنون به ومن يكفر به من الأحزاب فالنار موعده فلا تك في مرية منه إنه الحق من ربك ولكن أكثر الناس لا يؤمنون

translation: And who is more unjust than he who invents a lie about Allah or denies His signs? Surely the guilty are not successful. (5) They will be turned back to their Lord, and their witnesses will say, 'These are they who lied against their Lord.' Surely the curse of Allah is on the unjust.
interpretation: The verse highlights the severe consequences of lying about Allah or denying His signs. Such people are described as 'more unjust' and are not successful in the Hereafter. The verse describes the scene on the Day of Judgment when the guilty will be brought before their Lord and their witnesses (their own limbs and organs) will testify against them. The verse emphasizes the truthfulness of the Day of Judgment and the accountability of every person for their actions. It serves as a warning to those who deny the signs of Allah or invent lies about Him, reminding them of the severe consequences of their actions.
orig: ومن أظلم ممن افترى على الله كذبا أولئك يعرضون على ربهم ويقول الأشهاد هؤلاء الذين كذبوا على ربهم ألا لعنة الله على الظالمين

translation: Those who oppose the path of God and desire crookedness while they are disbelievers in the hereafter.
interpretation: The verse describes people who actively oppose the path of God and seek to misguide others through their crookedness. The verse characterizes them as disbelievers in the hereafter, indicating that their lack of faith in the consequences of their actions in the afterlife is what motivates their unrighteous behavior. The verse serves as a warning to those who stray from the path of God and seek to lead others astray, reminding them of the consequences of their disbelief and unrighteous actions.
orig: الذين يصدون عن سبيل الله ويبغونها عوجا وهم بالآخرة هم كافرون

translation: Those are they who are not empowered in the earth, nor do they have, besides Allah, any guardian. So the punishment is multiplied for them, and they are not able to hear, and they are not able to see.
interpretation: The verse speaks about a group of people who are unjust and lack power and protection on earth, and have no guardian besides God. The verse highlights the severe punishment that is multiplied for them, emphasizing the consequences of their actions. The verse also mentions their inability to hear or see, which can be interpreted as their lack of understanding and awareness of the truth. The verse serves as a warning to those who follow the wrong path, reminding them of the severe consequences of their actions and their need for guidance and protection from Allah.
orig: أولئك لم يكونوا معجزين في الأرض وما كان لهم من دون الله من أولياء يضاعف لهم العذاب ما كانوا يستطيعون السمع وما كانوا يبصرون

translation: Those are the ones who lost themselves and strayed from what they were inventing.
interpretation: The verse speaks about those individuals who have lost their way and strayed from the truth. They have strayed from the path of righteousness and have instead followed their own desires and false inventions. The verse emphasizes the ultimate loss and self-destruction of those who reject the truth and choose to follow their own path, rather than the path of God.
orig: أولئك الذين خسروا أنفسهم وضل عنهم ما كانوا يفترون

translation: Indeed, they, in the Hereafter, are the losers.
interpretation: The verse asserts that those who are being referred to will be the ultimate losers in the Hereafter. The verse emphasizes the significance of the Hereafter and the consequences of one's actions in this world. It serves as a reminder that the temporary pleasures and successes of this world are insignificant compared to the eternal consequences of one's actions. The verse encourages people to focus on the Hereafter and strive to lead a righteous life in order to attain success and salvation in the next life.
orig: لا جرم أنهم في الآخرة هم الأخسرون

translation: Indeed, those who have believed and done righteous deeds and humbled themselves to their Lord - those are the companions of Paradise; they will abide therein eternally.
interpretation: The verse describes the qualities of those who will enter Paradise: belief, righteous deeds, and humility towards God. Those who possess these qualities are described as the "companions of Paradise" and will live there eternally. The verse serves as a source of hope and motivation for believers, encouraging them to strive for righteousness and humility in their actions and faith.
orig: إن الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات وأخبتوا إلى ربهم أولئك أصحاب الجنة هم فيها خالدون

translation: Like the two parties, the blind and the deaf, and the seeing and the hearing. Are they equal in comparison? Then will you not reflect?
interpretation: The verse uses the metaphor of two groups, one composed of the blind and deaf, and the other of the seeing and hearing, to emphasize the vast difference between them. The first group is depicted as being unaware and unresponsive to the world around them, while the second group is able to perceive and understand. The verse challenges the reader to consider whether these two groups can be considered equal, and then urges them to reflect on the implications of this metaphor. The verse may be interpreted as a call to consciousness and awareness, encouraging the reader to strive for understanding and enlightenment, and to reject ignorance and complacency.
orig: مثل الفريقين كالأعمى والأصم والبصير والسميع هل يستويان مثلا أفلا تذكرون

translation: And We certainly sent Noah to his people, [saying], 'Indeed, I am to you a clear warner.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the sending of the prophet Noah to his people as a clear and evident warner. The verse emphasizes the role of Noah as a prophet and a warner, who was sent by God to guide and warn his people. The verse serves as a reminder of the role of prophets as messengers of God, who bring guidance and warn people of the consequences of their actions. It also emphasizes the importance of heeding the warnings of prophets and following their guidance.
orig: ولقد أرسلنا نوحا إلى قومه إني لكم نذير مبين

translation: So worship only Me [Allah]; I am to you from the warners. Indeed, I fear for you the punishment of a terrible day.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of worshipping only one God, Allah, and the role of the speaker (who is understood to be the prophet Muhammad) as a warner. The verse also highlights the fear of the speaker for the people he is addressing, as they face the threat of a terrible punishment on the Day of Judgment. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of worship and obedience to Allah, and the urgency of repentance and seeking forgiveness before it is too late.
orig: أن لا تعبدوا إلا الله إني أخاف عليكم عذاب يوم أليم

translation: And the nobles of his people, who disbelieved, said: 'You are not but a man like us, and indeed, we think you are among the liars.'
interpretation: The verse describes the disbelievers among the people of the Prophet Noah, who rejected his message and accused him of being a liar. The verse highlights their arrogance and lack of understanding, as they failed to recognize the truth of Noah's message and instead saw him as no different from themselves. The verse serves as a reminder of the dangers of arrogance and the importance of being open to the truth, even if it comes from an unexpected source.
orig: فقال الملأ الذين كفروا من قومه ما نراك إلا بشرا مثلنا وما نراك اتبعك إلا الذين هم أراذلنا بادي الرأي وما نرى لكم علينا من فضل بل نظنكم كاذبين

translation: He said, 'O my people, do you not see that if I were to follow a way that is dear to me, and there came to me a mercy from my Lord, that you would then associate me with God?'
interpretation: The verse relays a message from a prophet who is rebuking his people for their lack of faith and their desire to associate him with God. The prophet reminds his people that even if he were to receive mercy from God and follow a path that is pleasing to him, they would still accuse him of being a partner to God. The verse highlights the stubbornness and lack of understanding of the people, and the prophet's frustration with their refusal to accept the truth. It serves as a reminder of the importance of staying true to one's beliefs, even in the face of opposition and persecution.
orig: قال يا قوم أرأيتم إن كنت على بينة من ربي وآتاني رحمة من عنده فعميت عليكم أنلزمكموها وأنتم لها كارهون

translation: And oh, my people, I do not ask you for it any wage; my wage is only from God. I am not one to drive away those who have believed; they are rather those who will meet their Lord. But I see that you are a people who do not know.
interpretation: The speaker in this verse is addressing their people and making it clear that they do not seek any compensation for their actions. They are content with their reward coming only from God. The speaker also clarifies that they are not someone who drives away believers, but rather those believers will meet their Lord. The verse concludes with the speaker expressing their observation of the people they are addressing as those who lack knowledge or understanding.
orig: ويا قوم لا أسألكم عليه مالا إن أجري إلا على الله وما أنا بطارد الذين آمنوا إنهم ملاقو ربهم ولكني أراكم قوما تجهلون

translation: And O my people! Who will help me against Allah, if I drive them away? Then will you not be reminded?
interpretation: The verse is a rhetorical question posed by a speaker, likely a prophet or a messenger of God, who is facing opposition from his people. The speaker is expressing his powerlessness against the will of Allah and asking his people if they can protect him from the consequences of his actions. The question is intended to make the people reflect on the futility of opposing God's will and the consequences of their actions. The verse emphasizes the importance of remembering and acknowledging Allah's power and control over all things, and the importance of submitting to His will.
orig: ويا قوم من ينصرني من الله إن طردتهم أفلا تذكرون

translation: And I do not say to you that with me are the treasures of God, nor do I know the unseen, nor do I say that I am an angel. I do not say to those whom you regard with disdain that God will not grant them any good. God knows best what is in their souls. Indeed, I am not but a warner.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the limitations of the speaker's knowledge and abilities. The speaker denies having access to the treasures of God or knowledge of the unseen. The speaker also denies being an angel or having the power to determine the fate of others. The speaker acknowledges that only God knows what is in the hearts of people. The speaker's role is simply to warn people of the consequences of their actions, but ultimately, it is up to God to grant or withhold good from people.
orig: ولا أقول لكم عندي خزائن الله ولا أعلم الغيب ولا أقول إني ملك ولا أقول للذين تزدري أعينكم لن يؤتيهم الله خيرا الله أعلم بما في أنفسهم إني إذا لمن الظالمين

translation: They said, 'O Noah, you have disputed with us and have prolonged the dispute with us, so bring us what you threaten us with, if you are of the truthful.'
interpretation: The verse shows the disbelievers challenging Noah's message and his warnings of punishment from God. They mock and dismiss his call, demanding him to bring forth the punishment he has been threatening them with. The verse highlights the stubbornness and rejection of the disbelievers, who refuse to believe in Noah's message despite his persistent efforts to guide them. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of patience and perseverance in the face of rejection and opposition, and the ultimate triumph of truth over falsehood.
orig: قالوا يا نوح قد جادلتنا فأكثرت جدالنا فأتنا بما تعدنا إن كنت من الصادقين

translation: It (the Qur'an) is revealed to you (Muhammad) by Allah, the Entirely Knowing, the Wise. Indeed, We are sending it down in Arabic, and surely you will comprehend. And indeed, before it, was the Book of Moses, an example and a mercy. And this is a Book confirming (the truth of) it in the Arabic language, to warn the unjust and as good news for the doers of good. Indeed, those who have been given the Book know that it is revealed from your Lord in truth. So do not be of the skeptical. And indeed, Allah is the Hearing, the Knowing. So when the Qur'an is recited, then listen to it and be silent that you may receive mercy.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the revelation of the Qur'an through Prophet Muhammad. It emphasizes that the Qur'an is revealed in Arabic, the language of the people, so that they can understand and comprehend it. The verse highlights the continuity between the Qur'an and the previous scriptures, particularly the Torah of Moses, and its role in confirming the truth of the earlier revelations. The verse is a warning to the unjust, and good news for those who do good. It emphasizes the importance of listening to the recitation of the Qur'an with attentiveness and reverence, in order to receive mercy from Allah.
orig: قال إنما يأتيكم به الله إن شاء وما أنتم بمعجزين

translation: And my advice will not benefit you, if I desire to advise you, if Allah intends to lead you astray. Indeed, He is your Lord, and to Him you will be returned.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the ultimate power and control of Allah over all things, including the guidance and misguidance of people. The verse states that even if someone (such as a prophet or a well-intentioned person) tries to advise or guide someone else, it will be of no avail if Allah has decreed that the person should be led astray. This highlights the idea that human efforts and intentions, no matter how good, are ultimately subject to the will of Allah. The verse also reminds the reader of the ultimate accountability of all people to Allah, as they will all return to Him in the end.
orig: ولا ينفعكم نصحي إن أردت أن أنصح لكم إن كان الله يريد أن يغويكم هو ربكم وإليه ترجعون

translation: Or do they say, 'He has invented it'? Say, 'If I have invented it, then I am responsible for my sin, and I am innocent of what you commit.'
interpretation: The verse is a response to those who accuse the Prophet Muhammad of fabricating the Qur'an. The Prophet asserts that if he had indeed invented the Qur'an, then he alone would bear the responsibility for his sin. However, he maintains his innocence regarding the sins and transgressions of others. The verse emphasizes the Prophet's integrity and truthfulness in delivering the message of the Qur'an and rejects any accusations of fabrication or deceit.
orig: أم يقولون افتراه قل إن افتريته فعلي إجرامي وأنا بريء مما تجرمون

translation: And We revealed to Noah, 'No one from your people will believe except those who have already believed, so do not be distressed by what they do.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about a revelation from God to the prophet Noah, advising him not to be distressed by the fact that most of his people will not believe in him. The verse emphasizes that only those who have already believed will believe, indicating that the hearts of the people are already set in their ways and are not open to faith. The verse serves as a source of comfort and strength for the prophet Noah, reminding him that his efforts to spread the message of God are not in vain and that he should not be discouraged by the resistance he faces.
orig: وأوحي إلى نوح أنه لن يؤمن من قومك إلا من قد آمن فلا تبتئس بما كانوا يفعلون

translation: And construct the ship under Our eyes and by Our inspiration, and address not Me concerning those who have done wrong; indeed, they are to be drowned.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the construction of a ship by Prophet Noah, under the guidance and inspiration of God. The verse also emphasizes that God is aware of the actions of those who have done wrong, and that they are to be punished. The verse serves as a reminder that God is the ultimate authority and that He has the power to punish those who commit injustice. The verse also emphasizes the importance of following God's guidance and inspiration in all actions.
orig: واصنع الفلك بأعيننا ووحينا ولا تخاطبني في الذين ظلموا إنهم مغرقون

translation: And He has created the heavens and the earth in truth. And whenever He says, 'Be,' then it is. And His word is the truth. And He has created you from clay, then He has decreed a term - a known term. And indeed, you are knowing. And He is the One who created death and life to test you [as to] which of you is best in deed. And He is the Exalted in Might, the Forgiving. And indeed, those who dispute concerning the signs of Allah without authority having been given to them - there is a painful punishment for them. And Allah is exalted in might, the Owner of Retribution.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the power and authority of God, who has created the heavens and the earth and has control over all things. The verse states that when God commands something to be, it is, and His word is the truth. The verse also reminds humans of their own mortality and the purpose of their existence, which is to be tested through life and death in order to determine who is best in deed. The verse warns those who argue or dispute about the signs of God without authority, stating that they will face a painful punishment. The verse reaffirms the power and majesty of God, who is exalted in might and the owner of retribution.
orig: ويصنع الفلك وكلما مر عليه ملأ من قومه سخروا منه قال إن تسخروا منا فإنا نسخر منكم كما تسخرون

translation: And you will surely know who is the one whose punishment is delayed, and that upon him is a punishment enduring.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the ultimate fate of those who are being punished for their sins. It emphasizes that the punishment is inevitable and unavoidable, and that the delay in its arrival does not mean that it will not come. The verse serves as a reminder that God's punishment is certain, and that those who continue to commit sins and injustices will ultimately face the consequences of their actions. The phrase 'punishment enduring' implies that the punishment will be ongoing and unrelenting, and that it will not be a temporary or fleeting experience.
orig: فسوف تعلمون من يأتيه عذاب يخزيه ويحل عليه عذاب مقيم

translation: Until, when Our command came, and the cup (of punishment) came forth (before them), We said: 'Carry in it two of every kind, a pair, and (take along) your family - except those against whom the word has already gone forth, and whoever believes and whatever believes along with him.',
interpretation: This verse describes the punishment that will come upon people who have rejected God's message. When God's command is issued, a 'cup' or punishment will be brought forth. The people are told to take a pair of every kind of animal and their families, except for those who have already been condemned. Only those who believe will be saved. This verse serves as a warning to those who reject God's message and a promise of salvation for those who believe.
orig: حتى إذا جاء أمرنا وفار التنور قلنا احمل فيها من كل زوجين اثنين وأهلك إلا من سبق عليه القول ومن آمن وما آمن معه إلا قليل

translation: And said, 'Ride in it, by the name of Allah, its course and its reverting; surely my Lord is Forgiving, Merciful.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about a command to ride on a means of transportation, possibly a camel or a ship, and to trust in God's guidance and protection during the journey. The person giving the command expresses their faith in God's forgiveness and mercy, and the safety and success of the journey is attributed to God's attributes. The verse encourages trust and reliance on God, and it serves as a reminder of God's forgiveness and mercy towards those who seek His help and guidance.
orig: وقال اركبوا فيها بسم الله مجراها ومرساها إن ربي لغفور رحيم

translation: But it (the flood) carried them (the disbelievers) in its waves like the overturning of mountains, and Noah called out to his son, who was apart (from Noah), 'O my son, embark with us and do not be with the disbelievers.'
interpretation: The verse describes the destructive power of the flood that was sent as punishment upon the disbelievers. It emphasizes the overwhelming force of the flood, which was so powerful that it carried the disbelievers in its waves like the overturning of mountains. The verse then mentions Noah calling out to his son, who was not with him, urging him to join him and not to be with the disbelievers. This serves as a reminder of the importance of staying away from those who reject the truth and the consequences of following them. It also highlights Noah's concern for his son's well-being and his desire for him to be saved from the punishment of the flood.
orig: وهي تجري بهم في موج كالجبال ونادى نوح ابنه وكان في معزل يا بني اركب معنا ولا تكن مع الكافرين

translation: He said, 'I shall betake myself to a mountain, it will protect me from the water.' He said, 'There is no protector today from the command of Allah but He who has mercy.' And the wave between them (mountain and the man) was like the veil of darkness.
interpretation: The verse describes a man's attempt to escape the impending punishment of a flood by seeking refuge on a mountain. However, the verse emphasizes the absolute power of God's command, stating that there is no protection from it except for those who are shown mercy. The verse also highlights the overwhelming nature of the flood, describing the wave as being like a veil of darkness. The verse serves as a reminder of the futility of human efforts to escape God's will and the power of His punishment.
orig: قال سآوي إلى جبل يعصمني من الماء قال لا عاصم اليوم من أمر الله إلا من رحم وحال بينهما الموج فكان من المغرقين

translation: And it was said, 'O earth, swallow your water, and O sky, withhold (your rain).' And the water was diminished, and the matter was accomplished, and the ship was set upon the (ark), and it was said, 'Away with the wrongdoing people.'
interpretation: The verse describes a divine command to the earth and the sky to stop the flood that was destroying the unjust people. The water receded, the divine plan was fulfilled, and the ark carrying Noah and his followers was set on dry ground. The verse concludes with a statement of condemnation for the unjust people who were destroyed by the flood. The verse emphasizes the power of God over nature and the consequences of sin and injustice. It serves as a reminder that God has the ability to control natural elements and will ultimately punish those who reject His message and commit injustices.
orig: وقيل يا أرض ابلعي ماءك ويا سماء أقلعي وغيض الماء وقضي الأمر واستوت على الجودي وقيل بعدا للقوم الظالمين

translation: And Noah called out to his Lord and said, 'My Lord, indeed my son is of my family, and indeed your promise is true; yet you are the most just of judges.'
interpretation: The verse describes Noah's plea to God to save his son from the impending flood. Noah acknowledges the truth of God's promise to destroy the unbelievers and recognizes God's justice. However, he also appeals to God's mercy and asks for his son to be saved, highlighting the complexities of faith and the human desire to protect one's loved ones, even in the face of divine justice.
orig: ونادى نوح ربه فقال رب إن ابني من أهلي وإن وعدك الحق وأنت أحكم الحاكمين

translation: He said, 'O Noah, indeed he is not of your family, for he is not one who has been righteous. So do not ask me about what you do not know. Indeed, I am to you of a warner.'
interpretation: The verse relays a conversation between an unnamed speaker and the prophet Noah. The speaker informs Noah that a certain individual is not part of his family, as he has not lived a righteous life. The speaker then advises Noah not to inquire about matters that are beyond his knowledge. The verse concludes with the speaker stating that they are a warner to Noah. The verse emphasizes the importance of leading a righteous life and the limits of human knowledge. It also highlights the role of prophets as warners and the importance of heeding their warnings.
orig: قال يا نوح إنه ليس من أهلك إنه عمل غير صالح فلا تسألن ما ليس لك به علم إني أعظك أن تكون من الجاهلين

translation: He said, 'My Lord, I seek refuge in You from asking for that of which I have no knowledge. And if You do not forgive me and have mercy on me, I will be among the losers.'
interpretation: The verse is a prayer of a humble servant seeking protection from asking for something that is beyond their knowledge. The servant recognizes the limits of their understanding and the potential harm that can come from asking for something they do not fully comprehend. The servant also acknowledges their need for forgiveness and mercy from God, recognizing that without it, they would be among the losers. The verse highlights the importance of humility, awareness of one's limitations, and dependence on God's mercy and forgiveness.
orig: قال رب إني أعوذ بك أن أسألك ما ليس لي به علم وإلا تغفر لي وترحمني أكن من الخاسرين

translation: It was said, 'O Noah, descend in peace from Us and with blessings upon you and upon the communities (that are) with you and the communities that We will grant respite.' Then We will let them taste from Us a painful punishment.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the command given to the prophet Noah to descend from the ark with his followers and the communities that will be granted respite by God. Despite this respite, God warns that these communities will still face a painful punishment in the future. The verse emphasizes the power and authority of God in granting respite and meting out punishment, reminding people of the importance of obedience and submission to God's will.
orig: قيل يا نوح اهبط بسلام منا وبركات عليك وعلى أمم ممن معك وأمم سنمتعهم ثم يمسهم منا عذاب أليم

translation: That is from the news of the unseen which We reveal to you (O Muhammad). And you were not aware of it nor your people before this. So be patient. Indeed, the (righteous) end is for the fearful.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the revelation of knowledge from the unseen to the Prophet Muhammad, which he and his people were not previously aware of. The verse emphasizes the divine origin of this knowledge and the importance of patience in receiving it. The verse also highlights the ultimate reward for those who are mindful of God (the 'righteous end') and encourages the Prophet to remain steadfast in the face of adversity and opposition.
orig: تلك من أنباء الغيب نوحيها إليك ما كنت تعلمها أنت ولا قومك من قبل هذا فاصبر إن العاقبة للمتقين

translation: And to 'Ad [We sent] their brother Hud. He said, 'O my people, worship Allah; you have no deity other than Him. Indeed, you are only inventing (lies).'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the Prophet Hud being sent to the people of 'Ad as a warner. Hud calls his people to worship only Allah, as they have no other god but Him. The verse emphasizes that the people are inventing falsehoods and denies the existence of any deity other than Allah. The verse serves to remind the people of the importance of worshiping the one true God and the consequences of inventing falsehoods and associating partners with Allah.
orig: وإلى عاد أخاهم هودا قال يا قوم اعبدوا الله ما لكم من إله غيره إن أنتم إلا مفترون

translation: O my people, I do not ask you for this reward; I only seek what is rightfully mine. My reward is only with my Lord. Will you not use your reason?
interpretation: The verse is a statement by a prophet, likely Prophet Muhammad, addressing his people. He is making it clear that he does not seek any material reward or compensation from his people for his teachings and guidance. Instead, he is only seeking what is rightfully his, which is his reward from God. He is urging his people to use their reason and think about his message, instead of ignoring or rejecting it. The verse emphasizes the importance of seeking the truth and following it, even if it goes against the desires and interests of others.
orig: يا قوم لا أسألكم عليه أجرا إن أجري إلا على الذي فطرني أفلا تعقلون

translation: And O my people, ask forgiveness of your Lord, then turn to Him in repentance; He will send the heavens upon you in showers of abundance, and will add strength to your strength; and do not turn away, guilty.
interpretation: The verse addresses the people of the Prophet and urges them to seek forgiveness from their Lord and repent to Him. The verse promises that if they do so, their Lord will send down abundant rains from the heavens and increase their strength. However, the verse also warns them not to turn away from repentance and commit sins again. The verse emphasizes the importance of seeking forgiveness, repentance, and obedience to God, and the blessings and strength that come from it.
orig: ويا قوم استغفروا ربكم ثم توبوا إليه يرسل السماء عليكم مدرارا ويزدكم قوة إلى قوتكم ولا تتولوا مجرمين

translation: They said, 'O Hood, you have not brought us clear proof, and we will not forsake our gods on your word alone, and we are not believers in you.'
interpretation: The verse describes the disbelievers' rejection of the prophet Hood's message and their refusal to abandon their false gods. The verse emphasizes the importance of clear proof and evidence in convincing people of the truth, and highlights the closed-mindedness and stubbornness of those who refuse to believe. The verse serves as a reminder of the challenges faced by prophets in delivering God's message, and the difficulty in changing the deeply ingrained beliefs and practices of people.
orig: قالوا يا هود ما جئتنا ببينة وما نحن بتاركي آلهتنا عن قولك وما نحن لك بمؤمنين

translation: If we assign to them any deity other than Allah, indeed, we would have associated with Him that of which we have no knowledge. And indeed, we are, of that, wrongdoers.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the seriousness of associating partners with Allah (God), emphasizing that such an act would be an unfounded and ignorant action. The verse emphasizes the gravity of shirk (associating partners with God) and the fact that those who commit it are wrongdoers. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of maintaining the oneness and uniqueness of Allah in worship and belief.
orig: إن نقول إلا اعتراك بعض آلهتنا بسوء قال إني أشهد الله واشهدوا أني بريء مما تشركون

translation: They planned against me, but God planned against them, so God is the best of planners.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the power of God's plan and how it always prevails over the plans of humans. The verse emphasizes that even when people plot and plan against others, God has a plan that is superior and cannot be thwarted. The verse serves as a reminder that God is in control of all things and that those who trust in Him and follow His plan will ultimately be successful, while those who oppose Him and His will face defeat.
orig: من دونه فكيدوني جميعا ثم لا تنظرون

translation: Indeed, I have relied upon Allah, my Lord and your Lord. There is no creature but that He takes its forelock. Indeed, my Lord is on a straight path.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the complete trust and reliance that the speaker has on Allah, their Lord and the Lord of the listeners. The verse then highlights the power and control that Allah has over all of His creation, taking their forelocks as a metaphor for His complete control. The verse ends by reaffirming the certainty of the path that the Lord is on, a path that is straight and true.
orig: إني توكلت على الله ربي وربكم ما من دابة إلا هو آخذ بناصيتها إن ربي على صراط مستقيم

translation: But if they turn away, then I have conveyed to them what I was sent with. And my Lord will replace them with another people, and He is capable of every thing.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the role of the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) in conveying the message of Islam to the people, and the consequences of their rejection of the message. If the people choose to turn away from the message, the Prophet has fulfilled his duty of conveying it, and it is not his responsibility if they choose to reject it. The verse also emphasizes the power and control of God over all things, and his ability to replace the disbelieving people with another nation who will accept the message. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of the role of the Prophet and the ultimate control and power of God over all things.
orig: فإن تولوا فقد أبلغتكم ما أرسلت به إليكم ويستخلف ربي قوما غيركم ولا تضرونه شيئا إن ربي على كل شيء حفيظ

translation: And when Our command came, We saved Hud and those who believed with him, by mercy from Us, and We saved them from a harsh punishment.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the story of the prophet Hud and his followers who were saved by God's mercy from a severe punishment. The verse highlights God's compassion and mercy towards those who believe and follow His messengers. It also emphasizes the protection and salvation that God provides to His believers in times of hardship and adversity, and the ultimate triumph of good over evil.
orig: ولما جاء أمرنا نجينا هودا والذين آمنوا معه برحمة منا ونجيناهم من عذاب غليظ

translation: And such were the 'Ad people, they rejected the signs of their Lord and disobeyed His messengers and followed the command of every obstinate tyrant.
interpretation: The verse describes the people of 'Ad, who are one of the ancient communities that were destroyed in Islamic tradition. The verse highlights their rejection of God's signs and their disobedience towards God's messengers, which indicates their defiance and ingratitude towards their Lord. Moreover, the verse mentions that they followed the command of every obstinate tyrant, which implies their inclination towards evil and oppression. The verse serves as a warning to those who reject God's signs and follow the command of the wicked, reminding them of the fate of the people of 'Ad and the consequences of their actions.
orig: وتلك عاد جحدوا بآيات ربهم وعصوا رسله واتبعوا أمر كل جبار عنيد

translation: And they followed what the devils taught in the matter of Solomon's kingdom. And Solomon did not disbelieve, but the devils disbelieved, teaching the people sorcery and that which was revealed to the two angels in Babel, Harut and Marut. But they do not teach anyone without saying, 'We are only a trial, so do not disbelieve.' And they learn from them that by which they cause separation between a man and his wife. But they do not harm anyone with it except by permission of Allah. And they learn what harms them and does not benefit them. And they know that whoever purchases it will have no share in the Hereafter. And wretched is that for which they sold themselves, if they only knew.
interpretation: The verse warns against following the teachings of the devils, specifically in the context of sorcery and magic. The verse mentions that the devils taught people sorcery, which they claimed was only a test and not to be taken as true. However, those who learn and practice sorcery are causing harm and separation between people, and they do so with the permission of God. The verse emphasizes that the practice of sorcery has no benefit and will lead to a loss in the afterlife. The verse serves as a warning against the dangers of following false teachings and the importance of staying true to the teachings of God.
orig: وأتبعوا في هذه الدنيا لعنة ويوم القيامة ألا إن عادا كفروا ربهم ألا بعدا لعاد قوم هود

translation: And to Thamud (We sent) their brother Salih. He said, 'O my people, worship Allah! You have no deity other than Him. He has produced you from the earth and settled you in it, so request forgiveness of Him. Then repent to Him. Indeed, my Lord is near and responsive.',
interpretation: The verse speaks about the Prophet Salih, who was sent to the people of Thamud as a warner. He called them to worship only one God, Allah, and to seek His forgiveness and repentance. The verse emphasizes the power and mercy of Allah, who created the people and provided for them, and the importance of turning to Him in repentance. The verse serves as a reminder to the importance of worshiping Allah alone and seeking His forgiveness, and the nearness and responsiveness of Allah to those who call upon Him.
orig: وإلى ثمود أخاهم صالحا قال يا قوم اعبدوا الله ما لكم من إله غيره هو أنشأكم من الأرض واستعمركم فيها فاستغفروه ثم توبوا إليه إن ربي قريب مجيب

translation: They said, 'O Salih, you were among us as a source of hope before this. Do you forbid us to worship what our forefathers worshipped? And indeed, we are in grave doubt about what you invite us to.'
interpretation: The verse describes the people of the town of Thamud expressing their disbelief and rejection of Salih's message to worship one God. They question his authority by reminding him of their previous good relationship and ask why he is now forbidding them from worshipping what their forefathers worshipped. They also express their skepticism about the new faith that Salih is inviting them to. The verse highlights the people's rejection of the message and their attachment to their traditional beliefs and practices, despite the truth and evidence presented to them.
orig: قالوا يا صالح قد كنت فينا مرجوا قبل هذا أتنهانا أن نعبد ما يعبد آباؤنا وإننا لفي شك مما تدعونا إليه مريب

translation: He said, 'O my people, do you not consider: if I were upon clear evidence from my Lord and He had given me mercy from Himself, who then can help me against God, if I disobey Him?' Then you increase me not except in loss.
interpretation: The verse relays a statement made by a prophet addressing his people. The prophet poses a rhetorical question to his people, asking them to consider the situation where he has clear evidence from his Lord and has received mercy from Him. The prophet then asks who can help him against God if he disobeys Him, emphasizing the power and authority of God. The verse concludes by stating that the people can only increase the prophet in loss if he disobeys God, indicating that disobedience and defiance of God will only lead to harm and destruction.
orig: قال يا قوم أرأيتم إن كنت على بينة من ربي وآتاني منه رحمة فمن ينصرني من الله إن عصيته فما تزيدونني غير تخسير

translation: And, O my people, this she-camel of Allah is a sign for you, so leave her to pasture in the land of Allah, and touch her not with harm, lest there seize you a near punishment.
interpretation: The verse speaks about a she-camel that has been sent as a sign from God to a specific group of people. The people are instructed to leave the she-camel alone and allow it to graze freely in the land of God. They are also warned not to harm or mistreat the she-camel in any way. The verse emphasizes the consequences of disobedience, stating that a 'near punishment' will befall those who do not heed the warning. The verse serves as a test of the people's faith and obedience to God, and serves as a reminder of the power and authority of God.
orig: ويا قوم هذه ناقة الله لكم آية فذروها تأكل في أرض الله ولا تمسوها بسوء فيأخذكم عذاب قريب

translation: And We will seal up their mouths, and their hands will speak to Us, and their legs will testify to what they have earned. [It will be said], 'Now taste the punishment of being burnt in the Fire because of what you used to deny.'
interpretation: The verse describes the Day of Judgment and the punishment of the disbelievers. The verse speaks of the sealing of the mouths of the disbelievers, and their hands and legs will testify to their sins. The verse emphasizes the certainty of the punishment and the fact that the disbelievers will not be able to deny their sins on that day. The verse serves as a warning to those who deny the truth and a reminder of the consequences of their actions.
orig: فعقروها فقال تمتعوا في داركم ثلاثة أيام ذلك وعد غير مكذوب

translation: But when Our command came, We saved Salih and those who believed with him, by mercy from Us, and from the disgrace of that day. Indeed, your Lord, He is the Exalted in Might, the Merciful.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the story of the prophet Salih and his followers who were saved from destruction by the mercy of God. The verse highlights the power of God's command and the salvation of those who believed in Salih. The verse emphasizes the contrast between the believers who were saved and the disbelievers who faced the disgrace of that day. The verse ends by reminding the reader of the attributes of God, the Exalted in Might and the Merciful, emphasizing the power and compassion of God.
orig: فلما جاء أمرنا نجينا صالحا والذين آمنوا معه برحمة منا ومن خزي يومئذ إن ربك هو القوي العزيز

translation: And took those who were unjust by surprise, so they were found in their homes at dawn, prostrate.
interpretation: The verse describes the sudden and unexpected punishment of those who were unjust. They were taken by surprise in their homes at dawn, in a state of prostration. This may indicate that they were caught off guard and were not expecting the punishment. The verse emphasizes the swiftness and severity of God's punishment for those who commit injustice, and serves as a warning for people to refrain from committing unjust acts.
orig: وأخذ الذين ظلموا الصيحة فأصبحوا في ديارهم جاثمين

translation: It is as if they had never dwelt there. Though Thamud denied their Lord. Unquestionably,
interpretation: No interpretation
orig: كأن لم يغنوا فيها ألا إن ثمود كفروا ربهم ألا بعدا لثمود

translation: And our messengers came to Abraham with good news; they said, 'Peace.' He said, 'Peace.' But soon after, a man came rushing to him.
interpretation: The verse describes a visit from God's messengers to Abraham, bringing him good news and greeting him with peace. Abraham responds with the same greeting, highlighting the peaceful and respectful atmosphere of the encounter. However, the verse quickly shifts tone with the sudden arrival of a man in a hurry. The abrupt appearance of this man creates a sense of urgency and foreshadows the revelation of important news or events. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of being receptive to God's messengers and their messages, as well as the need to act quickly when faced with important decisions or situations.
orig: ولقد جاءت رسلنا إبراهيم بالبشرى قالوا سلاما قال سلام فما لبث أن جاء بعجل حنيذ

translation: But when their hands reached not to it, they said: 'We despair not of Allah's leaving us to reach it, nor of our being driven unto it.' (So they were impatient), but when they saw Our punishment, lo! they said: 'We believe in Allah only, and we deny that whereunto we used to ascribe (partnership).'
interpretation: The verse describes the disbelievers' reaction when they were unable to reach the Ark of Noah, despite their efforts. They expressed their confidence in their ability to reach it and their belief that they would not be prevented from doing so. However, when they faced God's punishment, they immediately changed their tone and claimed to believe in God, denying their previous actions and beliefs. The verse highlights the insincerity of their faith and their lack of true belief until they faced the consequences of their actions. It serves as a reminder of the importance of true and sincere faith, and the fleeting nature of worldly desires and confidence.
orig: فلما رأى أيديهم لا تصل إليه نكرهم وأوجس منهم خيفة قالوا لا تخف إنا أرسلنا إلى قوم لوط

translation: And his wife was standing (nearby), so she laughed. Then We gave her the good news of Isaac, and after Isaac, Jacob.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the announcement of the birth of Isaac and Jacob to Abraham and his wife. The verse highlights the joy and happiness of the occasion through the wife's laughter. The announcement of the birth of Isaac is followed by the news of another son, Jacob, indicating the continuation of the prophetic lineage. The verse emphasizes the blessings and mercies of God towards Abraham and his family, and serves as a reminder of the significance of family and lineage in the Islamic tradition.
orig: وامرأته قائمة فضحكت فبشرناها بإسحاق ومن وراء إسحاق يعقوب

translation: She said, 'Woe is me! Shall I bear a child, now that I am an old woman, and this my husband, an old man? This is indeed an amazing thing!'
interpretation: The verse is a statement of disbelief and shock from an old woman who has been told that she will give birth to a child, despite her old age. She expresses her surprise and skepticism at the news, given her and her husband's advanced age. The verse highlights the miraculous nature of the upcoming birth, which serves as a sign of God's power and intervention in human affairs.
orig: قالت يا ويلتى أألد وأنا عجوز وهذا بعلي شيخا إن هذا لشيء عجيب

translation: They said, 'Are you amazed at the command of Allah? And the mercy of Allah and His blessings upon you, O people of the house. Indeed, He is Praiseworthy and Glorious.'
interpretation: The verse is a response from the people to someone, likely the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH), expressing their amazement at the command of Allah and His mercy and blessings upon the Prophet and his family. The people recognize and acknowledge Allah's praiseworthiness and glory, and they express their gratitude for His blessings. The verse highlights the importance of recognizing and expressing gratitude for Allah's blessings and mercy, and it emphasizes the significance of the Prophet's role and the blessings and mercy that Allah has bestowed upon him and his family.
orig: قالوا أتعجبين من أمر الله رحمت الله وبركاته عليكم أهل البيت إنه حميد مجيد

translation: And when Abraham's fear left and the glad tidings came to him, he began to argue with Us concerning the people of Lot.
interpretation: The verse describes the moment when Abraham's fear or anxiety subsided and he received the good news (most likely the news of the birth of his son Isaac). However, instead of being fully grateful and content, Abraham began to argue or dispute with God regarding the fate of the people of Lot. This verse highlights the human tendency to question and challenge divine decisions, even in moments of joy and gratitude. It also serves as a reminder of the importance of trust and submission to God's will, even when it goes against our own expectations and desires.
orig: فلما ذهب عن إبراهيم الروع وجاءته البشرى يجادلنا في قوم لوط

translation: Indeed, Abraham was forbearing, grieving and [constantly] returning [to Allah].
interpretation: The verse describes the character of the prophet Abraham (peace be upon him). He is described as forbearing, which means patient and able to endure difficulties. He is also described as grieving, which could refer to his concern for the state of his people and their rejection of his message. The phrase 'and [constantly] returning [to Allah]' suggests that Abraham was always repentant and seeking forgiveness from Allah. This verse serves as an example of the virtues of patience, concern for others, and constant repentance that Muslims should strive for.
orig: إن إبراهيم لحليم أواه منيب

translation: But when Abraham said, 'My Lord, show me how You give life to the dead.' [Allah] said, 'Have you not believed?' Abraham said, 'Yes, but [I ask] only that my heart may be satisfied.' [Allah] said, 'Take four birds and commit them to yourself. Then [after slaughtering them] put on each hill a portion of them; then call them - they will come [flying] to you in haste. And know that Allah is Exalted in Might and Wise.'
interpretation: In this verse, God is responding to the request of the prophet Abraham, who asked to be shown how God gives life to the dead. God tells Abraham that he should not need such proof of his belief, but then grants his request as a test of his faith. Abraham is instructed to cut up four birds and place a portion of each on separate hills. He is then told to call the birds, and they will come to him. This act is meant to demonstrate the power of God over all things, and to strengthen Abraham's faith. The verse serves as a reminder of the greatness of God and the power of faith.
orig: يا إبراهيم أعرض عن هذا إنه قد جاء أمر ربك وإنهم آتيهم عذاب غير مردود

translation: And when Our messengers came to Lot, they were troubled by them and he was distressed for them, and he said, 'This is a distressful day.'
interpretation: The verse describes the arrival of God's messengers to the prophet Lot and the negative reaction of the people of the town towards them. Lot is worried and distressed for the safety of the messengers and himself. The phrase 'This is a distressful day' emphasizes the severity of the situation and foreshadows the impending destruction of the town as a consequence of the people's rejection of the messengers and their wicked ways.
orig: ولما جاءت رسلنا لوطا سيء بهم وضاق بهم ذرعا وقال هذا يوم عصيب

translation: And his people came running to him, and before they had done so, they were doing evil deeds. He said, 'O my people, these are my daughters, they are purer for you. So fear Allah and do not disgrace me with respect to my guests. Is there not among you a righteous man?'
interpretation: The verse describes a prophet's encounter with his people, who were engaging in evil deeds. The prophet offers his daughters as an alternative for his guests, urging his people to fear God and not commit any disgraceful acts. The verse emphasizes the importance of hospitality and righteousness, as well as the need to respect and protect the dignity of guests. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of moral values and the consequences of neglecting them.
orig: وجاءه قومه يهرعون إليه ومن قبل كانوا يعملون السيئات قال يا قوم هؤلاء بناتي هن أطهر لكم فاتقوا الله ولا تخزون في ضيفي أليس منكم رجل رشيد

translation: They said, 'Indeed, we know that you have no claim concerning our daughters. Indeed, you are one of those who are unrestrained.'
interpretation: The verse describes a conversation between the people and a prophet, where the people accuse the prophet of having no right to their daughters, and claim that the prophet is unrestrained or promiscuous. The verse highlights the rejection and disbelief of the people towards the prophet, and their refusal to accept his message. The verse serves as a reminder that prophets and messengers of God often face opposition and rejection from their people, and that their role is to convey the message of God, regardless of the response from the people.
orig: قالوا لقد علمت ما لنا في بناتك من حق وإنك لتعلم ما نريد

translation: He said, 'If only I had with me strength or I could take refuge in a strong support.'
interpretation: The verse is a quote from someone in a state of despair and helplessness. The speaker wishes they had the power or the protection of a strong support to help them in their current situation. The verse conveys a sense of vulnerability and the desire for protection and strength in the face of adversity. The speaker's words may be a plea for help or a statement of their own limitations and weaknesses.
orig: قال لو أن لي بكم قوة أو آوي إلى ركن شديد

translation: They said, 'O Lot, indeed we are messengers of your Lord. They will not reach you. So bring your family while a part of the night is still night, and let not any of you look back, except your wife. Indeed, she will be struck by that which strikes them. Indeed, their appointment is in the morning. Is not the morning near?'
interpretation: The verse relays a message from Lot's people, who claim to be messengers of Lot's Lord, telling him that they will not harm him. They instruct him to gather his family and leave the city during the night, except for his wife. However, the verse also reveals that his wife will meet the same fate as the people of the city. The verse emphasizes the imminence of the punishment, as the time of their appointment with destruction is in the morning. The verse serves as a reminder of the power of God's wrath and the futility of resisting it.
orig: قالوا يا لوط إنا رسل ربك لن يصلوا إليك فأسر بأهلك بقطع من الليل ولا يلتفت منكم أحد إلا امرأتك إنه مصيبها ما أصابهم إن موعدهم الصبح أليس الصبح بقريب

translation: But when Our command came, We saved by [raising] high certain of them and seized others in a seized [state]. And it was not the blow that overwhelmed them in the morning.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the implementation of God's command, resulting in the salvation of some people and the destruction of others. The phrase 'seized in a seized [state]' suggests that the people who were destroyed were caught off guard, and the suddenness of the destruction is emphasized by the statement that it did not happen at dawn. The verse serves as a reminder that God's command can come at any time, and those who are unprepared or engaged in unjust actions may face severe consequences.
orig: فلما جاء أمرنا جعلنا عاليها سافلها وأمطرنا عليها حجارة من سجيل منضود

translation: Forgiven by your Lord and not of the wrongdoers.
interpretation: The verse speaks about someone who has been forgiven by their Lord and is therefore not among the wrongdoers. This implies that the person has been given a second chance and has been absolved of their past sins. The verse may serve as a reminder of the mercy and compassion of God, and the potential for redemption and forgiveness for those who seek it. It can also be seen as a warning to those who continue to commit wrongdoing, highlighting the distinction between those who have sought forgiveness and those who persist in their wrongdoing.
orig: مسومة عند ربك وما هي من الظالمين ببعيد

translation: And to (the people of) a town, (We sent) their brother Shu'ayb. He said, 'O my people, worship Allah; you have no deity other than Him. And do not reduce the measure and the weight. Indeed, I see you in prosperity, and indeed, I fear for you the punishment of a day encompassing.',
interpretation: The verse speaks about the Prophet Shu'ayb (peace be upon him) who was sent to his people as a warner. He called upon them to worship only one God, Allah, and not to engage in unjust practices such as reducing the measure and the weight in their transactions. Prophet Shu'ayb reminded his people of the blessings they enjoyed and expressed his concern for their well-being by warning them of an impending punishment. The punishment is described as being 'encompassing', indicating that it will affect all of them and leave no one unscathed. The verse serves as a reminder to be truthful in all our dealings, to be fair and just, and to avoid unjust practices.
orig: وإلى مدين أخاهم شعيبا قال يا قوم اعبدوا الله ما لكم من إله غيره ولا تنقصوا المكيال والميزان إني أراكم بخير وإني أخاف عليكم عذاب يوم محيط

translation: O my people, give full measure and weight in justice, and do not diminish the people their possessions, and do not cause corruption in the land.
interpretation: The verse addresses the listeners, reminding them of the importance of justice and fairness in their dealings with others. It specifically mentions the need to give full measure and weight, which suggests that people should be honest and accurate in their business transactions. The verse also warns against taking advantage of others by withholding or diminishing their possessions. Additionally, it instructs the listeners not to cause corruption in the land, which implies a broader responsibility to maintain order and stability in society. Overall, the verse emphasizes the importance of ethical behavior and social responsibility in the community.
orig: ويا قوم أوفوا المكيال والميزان بالقسط ولا تبخسوا الناس أشياءهم ولا تعثوا في الأرض مفسدين

translation: And
interpretation: No interpretation
orig: بقيت الله خير لكم إن كنتم مؤمنين وما أنا عليكم بحفيظ

translation: They said, 'O Shu'ayb, does your prayer command you that we should leave what our forefathers worshipped or that we should not do with our wealth as we please? Indeed, you are the forbearing, the right-guiding.'
interpretation: The verse shows the people of Shu'ayb (peace be upon him) expressing their disbelief and disapproval of his message. They question his command to abandon the worship of their ancestors and to stop doing as they please with their wealth. They describe Shu'ayb as being forbearing and right-guiding, but their words are laced with sarcasm and disrespect. The verse highlights the common human tendency to resist change and cling to tradition, even when it goes against reason and righteousness. It also underscores the importance of standing firm in the face of adversity and continuing to convey the message of truth, as Shu'ayb did.
orig: قالوا يا شعيب أصلاتك تأمرك أن نترك ما يعبد آباؤنا أو أن نفعل في أموالنا ما نشاء إنك لأنت الحليم الرشيد

translation: He said, 'O my people, do you see that if I have a clear sign from my Lord and He has provided me with a good provision from Him, and I do not desire to contradict you in what I forbid you from, I only desire reform as much as I can, and my success is not but through Allah. Upon Him I have relied, and to Him I return.',
interpretation: The verse is a statement made by a prophet or a righteous person, who has received a clear sign from their Lord and has been provided with a good provision. They declare that they do not wish to contradict the people in what they have been forbidden from, and they only desire to reform and guide them as much as they can. They acknowledge that their success and ability to reform comes only from Allah, and they rely and submit themselves to Him. The verse emphasizes the importance of relying on and trusting in Allah, and the responsibility of the prophet or righteous person to guide and reform the people in the best way they can.
orig: قال يا قوم أرأيتم إن كنت على بينة من ربي ورزقني منه رزقا حسنا وما أريد أن أخالفكم إلى ما أنهاكم عنه إن أريد إلا الإصلاح ما استطعت وما توفيقي إلا بالله عليه توكلت وإليه أنيب

translation: And, O my people, no wrongdoer will afflict you concerning the fracture that it may strike you like what struck the people of Noah or the people of Hud or the people of Salih, and the people of Lot are not far off from you.
interpretation: The verse warns the people of a potential punishment similar to what was faced by the people of Noah, Hud, Salih, and Lot. The phrase 'no wrongdoer will afflict you' emphasizes that the punishment is not being brought upon them by any human enemy, but rather by God as a consequence of their actions. The reference to the previous nations serves as a reminder of the power and severity of God's punishment. The verse also emphasizes the proximity of the people of Lot, indicating that they too faced a similar fate. Overall, the verse serves as a warning to the people to turn away from their wrongdoing and repent before it's too late.
orig: ويا قوم لا يجرمنكم شقاقي أن يصيبكم مثل ما أصاب قوم نوح أو قوم هود أو قوم صالح وما قوم لوط منكم ببعيد

translation: And seek forgiveness from your Lord, then turn to Him in repentance. Indeed, my Lord is Merciful and Love.
interpretation: The verse encourages the believers to seek forgiveness from their Lord and to repent to Him. It emphasizes the mercy and love of God towards His believers, encouraging them to return to Him. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of seeking forgiveness and repentance, and the boundless mercy of God towards those who seek it.
orig: واستغفروا ربكم ثم توبوا إليه إن ربي رحيم ودود

translation: They said, 'O Shu'ayb, we do not understand much of what you say, and indeed, we see you as weak among us. And were it not for your family, we would have stoned you. And you are not strong upon us.'
interpretation: The verse describes the response of the people of Shu'ayb (a prophet in Islamic tradition) to his preaching. They express their inability to understand his message and view him as weak and powerless. They even threaten to stone him if it were not for his family's protection. The verse highlights the resistance and rejection faced by prophets in their mission to guide their people towards the right path. It also emphasizes the importance of upholding the truth and standing firm against adversity, even if it means facing opposition and rejection from those around us.
orig: قالوا يا شعيب ما نفقه كثيرا مما تقول وإنا لنراك فينا ضعيفا ولولا رهطك لرجمناك وما أنت علينا بعزيز

translation: He said, 'O my people, I have sought to protect you from your Lord, and I fear His retribution upon you, but you have taken Him as an enemy after He had been your protector.' Indeed, my Lord is surrounding all that you do.
interpretation: The verse speaks about a prophet warning his people of the impending punishment from God. The prophet has tried to protect his people from God's wrath, but they have turned against him and made God their enemy. The verse emphasizes the all-encompassing knowledge and power of God, who is aware of all that the people do. The verse serves as a reminder of the consequences of turning away from God and rejecting the guidance of the prophets.
orig: قال يا قوم أرهطي أعز عليكم من الله واتخذتموه وراءكم ظهريا إن ربي بما تعملون محيط

translation: And, O my people, work according to your position. Indeed, I am working. You will come to know who will receive a humiliating punishment and who is a liar. And wait, indeed I am with you among the watchers.
interpretation: The verse is a message from a prophet or a messenger to his people, urging them to work and fulfill their responsibilities. The speaker emphasizes that he is also working and making efforts for their guidance. The verse warns of a humiliating punishment that will be faced by those who are not following the right path. It also highlights that the speaker will be a witness to the outcome and that he is watching over his people. The verse encourages the people to be patient and wait, as the speaker is with them, observing the events and the actions of people.
orig: ويا قوم اعملوا على مكانتكم إني عامل سوف تعلمون من يأتيه عذاب يخزيه ومن هو كاذب وارتقبوا إني معكم رقيب

translation: And when Our command came, We saved Shuaib and those who believed with him by mercy from Us, and the wrongdoers - the Cry seized them, so they were found lifeless in their homes.
interpretation: The verse describes the story of Prophet Shuaib and his followers who were saved by God's mercy, while the wrongdoers were punished and found dead in their homes. The verse emphasizes the power of God's command and the consequences of disbelief and wrongdoing.
