It serves as a reminder that those who reject God's message and persist in their unrighteousness will ultimately face His punishment, while those who believe and follow the right path will be saved by His mercy.
orig: ولما جاء أمرنا نجينا شعيبا والذين آمنوا معه برحمة منا وأخذت الذين ظلموا الصيحة فأصبحوا في ديارهم جاثمين

translation: It is as if they had not stayed (in their homes) except a single hour, they touched (their doom) similar to the touch of Thamud.
interpretation: The verse uses a metaphor to describe the sudden and swift destruction of a people who were unjust and disbelieving, comparing it to the quick passing of an hour. The phrase 'they touched (their doom) similar to the touch of Thamud' refers to the destruction of the people of Thamud, who were destroyed by a powerful wind sent by God. The verse serves as a warning to those who do not heed the signs of God, emphasizing the swift and severe consequences of disbelief and sin.
orig: كأن لم يغنوا فيها ألا بعدا لمدين كما بعدت ثمود

translation: And We certainly sent Moses with Our signs and a clear authority.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the mission of Moses, who was sent by God with clear signs and a clear authority to guide and lead the people. The verse emphasizes the divine nature of Moses' mission and his role as a prophet, who was chosen by God to convey His message to the people. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of prophets and their role in guiding humanity towards the right path.
orig: ولقد أرسلنا موسى بآياتنا وسلطان مبين

translation: To Pharaoh and his chiefs: 'Indeed, you have been disobedient and rebellious.'
interpretation: The verse is a message from God to Pharaoh and his followers, rebuking them for their disobedience and rebellion. The verse emphasizes the power dynamic between God and Pharaoh, with God addressing Pharaoh in a commanding tone. The use of the word 'disobedient' implies that Pharaoh and his followers have gone against God's will, and the word 'rebellious' suggests that they have actively resisted and defied God's authority. The verse serves as a reminder of the consequences of disobedience and rebellion against God, and the ultimate power and authority of God over all of His creation.
orig: إلى فرعون وملئه فاتبعوا أمر فرعون وما أمر فرعون برشيد

translation: His people rejected him, so he called upon his Lord, saying, 'I am overpowered, so help!' And We responded to him and saved him from the proximity of their harm. And thus do We save the believers.
interpretation: The verse speaks about a person whose people rejected him and his message. He turned to God for help, and God responded by saving him from his people's harm. The verse serves as a reminder of God's power and willingness to help those who are oppressed and in need. It also highlights the importance of turning to God in times of difficulty and the reward for those who have faith in Him.
orig: يقدم قومه يوم القيامة فأوردهم النار وبئس الورد المورود

translation: And they followed [so closely] what the devils had recited during the reign of Solomon. It is not blameless, a misleading falsehood. For them is a painful punishment on the Day of Resurrection.
interpretation: The verse speaks about people who followed the falsehoods and misguidance that the devils had recited during the time of Solomon. The verse makes it clear that this is not a blameless act, but rather a misleading falsehood. The verse warns that these people will face a painful punishment on the Day of Resurrection. The verse serves as a reminder of the dangers of following falsehoods and the importance of staying on the path of truth and guidance.
orig: وأتبعوا في هذه لعنة ويوم القيامة بئس الرفد المرفود

translation: That is from the news of the towns, We relate to you some of them, of which standing crops were cut down.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of certain towns and the cutting down of their crops. The verse is emphasizing the destruction of these towns and the loss of their crops. The verse can be interpreted as a warning of the consequences of disbelief and rejection of God's message. The cutting down of the crops can symbolize the destruction of the people's livelihood and resources, further emphasizing the severity of the punishment.
orig: ذلك من أنباء القرى نقصه عليك منها قائم وحصيد

translation: And We never wronged them, but they wronged themselves; so their gods, besides Allah, of no benefit to them, when the command of your Lord came, and they increased not except in ruin.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the fact that the people who were punished were not wronged by God, but rather, they wronged themselves through their own actions. The verse emphasizes that their false gods, which they worshipped besides God, were of no benefit to them when the command of God came. The verse highlights the futility of worshipping false gods and the consequences of rejecting the truth. The verse serves as a reminder that no one can save us from God's punishment except God Himself and that those who turn away from the truth will ultimately face ruin and destruction.
orig: وما ظلمناهم ولكن ظلموا أنفسهم فما أغنت عنهم آلهتهم التي يدعون من دون الله من شيء لما جاء أمر ربك وما زادوهم غير تتبيب

translation: And thus does your Lord take the towns while they are unjust. Indeed, His take is painful and severe.
interpretation: The verse describes the taking of towns by the Lord when they are unjust and committing wrongdoing. The verse emphasizes the severity and intensity of the Lord's take, indicating that it is a harsh and severe punishment. The verse serves as a warning to those who are committing injustice and wrongdoing, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: وكذلك أخذ ربك إذا أخذ القرى وهي ظالمة إن أخذه أليم شديد

translation: Indeed, in that is a sign for one who fears the punishment of the Hereafter. That is a day when mankind will be gathered together and that is a day of witnessing.
interpretation: The verse speaks about a sign or lesson for those who fear the punishment of the Hereafter. The verse describes the Day of Judgment as a day when all of humanity will be gathered together and it will be a day of witnessing. The verse emphasizes the importance of being mindful of the consequences of one's actions and the significance of the Day of Judgment. It serves as a reminder to be aware of the fleeting nature of this worldly life and to prepare for the eternal life in the Hereafter.
orig: إن في ذلك لآية لمن خاف عذاب الآخرة ذلك يوم مجموع له الناس وذلك يوم مشهود

translation: And We do not delay it except for a specified term
interpretation: The verse speaks about the timing of a certain event or events, emphasizing that their occurrence is not delayed without a specific purpose or reason. The verse suggests that everything happens according to a predetermined plan and schedule, and that the delay in the occurrence of certain events is not due to forgetfulness or negligence on the part of the one who has control over them. Instead, the delay serves a specific purpose, and the event will occur when the time is right, neither sooner nor later.
orig: وما نؤخره إلا لأجل معدود

translation: The Day when neither wealth nor children will avail, except for him who comes to Allah with a sound heart.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the Day of Judgment, when neither wealth nor children will be of any benefit to a person, except for those who come to God with a pure and sound heart. The verse emphasizes the importance of having a pure and sound heart, which is the only thing that will benefit a person on the Day of Judgment. It serves as a reminder that material possessions and worldly achievements will not be of any help on that Day, and that the ultimate goal of a person should be to have a sound heart and to come to God with it.
orig: يوم يأت لا تكلم نفس إلا بإذنه فمنهم شقي وسعيد

translation: But as for those who are ungrateful, for them is the Fire, in it they will have a bed and pitchforks.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the punishment of those who are ungrateful to God. They will be placed in the Fire, where they will have a bed and pitchforks. The bed and pitchforks symbolize the painful and harsh nature of their punishment. The verse serves as a warning to those who are ungrateful and unappreciative of God's blessings, reminding them of the severe consequences of their actions.
orig: فأما الذين شقوا ففي النار لهم فيها زفير وشهيق

translation: Abide therein forever, - He upon Whom is the dominion of the heavens and the earth; He is the Wise, the Omniscient.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the eternal nature of God's dominion over the heavens and the earth. It emphasizes God's power and knowledge, describing Him as the 'Wise' and the 'Omniscient'. The verse suggests that the people should reflect on this eternal dominion and submit to God's will, recognizing that He has the power to do as He pleases and that His decisions are always wise and just.
orig: خالدين فيها ما دامت السماوات والأرض إلا ما شاء ربك إن ربك فعال لما يريد

translation: But as for those who are blessed, they will be in Paradise, abiding therein as long as the heavens and the earth endure, except what your Lord wills. A gift without end.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the ultimate reward for those who are blessed, which is eternal life in Paradise. The verse emphasizes the permanence of this reward, comparing it to the enduring nature of the heavens and the earth. However, even this permanence is subject to the will of God, who has the power to give and take away as He pleases. The verse serves as a source of comfort and hope for believers, reminding them of the ultimate goal of their faith and the eternal bliss that awaits them in the afterlife.
orig: وأما الذين سعدوا ففي الجنة خالدين فيها ما دامت السماوات والأرض إلا ما شاء ربك عطاء غير مجذوذ

translation: So be not in doubt about what these (people) worship. They worship only as their fathers worshipped before (them). But indeed, We will give them their due reward in full, without any reduction.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the futility of doubting the false gods that others worship, as they are merely following the traditions of their ancestors. The verse emphasizes that these gods cannot benefit or harm anyone, and that their followers will receive their full punishment without any reduction. The verse serves as a reminder that worship should be directed towards the one true God, and that following false deities will only lead to negative consequences.
orig: فلا تك في مرية مما يعبد هؤلاء ما يعبدون إلا كما يعبد آباؤهم من قبل وإنا لموفوهم نصيبهم غير منقوص

translation: And We already gave Moses the Scripture, but there came to him disagreements concerning it. And if it were not for a word that had preceded from your Lord, it would have been judged between them. And indeed, they are in disquieting doubt concerning it.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the disagreements that arose among the people regarding the scripture that was given to Moses. Despite the scripture being a source of guidance, there was still conflict and uncertainty surrounding it. The verse highlights the importance of the word that had preceded from God, which prevented a judgement from being made between them. The verse emphasizes the presence of doubt and uncertainty that the people had regarding the scripture, and serves as a reminder of the importance of seeking guidance and understanding from God in order to resolve conflicts and doubts.
orig: ولقد آتينا موسى الكتاب فاختلف فيه ولولا كلمة سبقت من ربك لقضي بينهم وإنهم لفي شك منه مريب

translation: And indeed, for whatever you (people) may be doing, your Lord is surely going to give you the reward for it in full; indeed, He is all-aware of what you do.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the certainty of God's reward for people's actions, be it good or bad. The verse reminds people that God is all-aware of their actions and that they will be held accountable for them in the afterlife. The verse encourages people to do good and shun evil, as they will ultimately receive the consequences of their actions.
orig: وإن كلا لما ليوفينهم ربك أعمالهم إنه بما يعملون خبير

translation: So establish prayer as you have been commanded and those who have turned back with you [to worship Him] and do not disobey. Indeed, He sees whatever you do.
interpretation: The verse commands believers to establish prayer as they have been commanded and to not disobey God, emphasizing the importance of obedience and worship. The verse also mentions those who have turned back to worship God, indicating the importance of repentance and returning to the right path. The verse reminds believers that God sees all that they do, emphasizing the importance of accountability and the awareness of God's presence in all actions.
orig: فاستقم كما أمرت ومن تاب معك ولا تطغوا إنه بما تعملون بصير

translation: And do not leave your homes in ruins, so that the Fire may seize you, and you will not have any protectors besides Allah, then you will not be helped.
interpretation: The verse warns against neglecting or abandoning one's responsibilities and duties, as this could lead to dire consequences such as being consumed by fire and having no protectors besides God. The verse emphasizes the importance of seeking help and support from God, as there will be no other helpers in times of need. The verse serves as a reminder to be vigilant and mindful of one's actions, and to seek guidance and strength from God in all aspects of life.
orig: ولا تركنوا إلى الذين ظلموا فتمسكم النار وما لكم من دون الله من أولياء ثم لا تنصرون

translation: And establish prayer at the two ends of the day and in some hours of the night. Indeed, good deeds do away with misdeeds. That is a reminder for those who remember.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of establishing prayer at specific times of the day and night. By doing so, one's good deeds can help to erase their bad deeds. This verse serves as a reminder for those who are mindful and conscious of God, encouraging them to establish a consistent prayer routine and engage in good deeds in order to purify their souls and actions.
orig: وأقم الصلاة طرفي النهار وزلفا من الليل إن الحسنات يذهبن السيئات ذلك ذكرى للذاكرين

translation: And be patient, for surely Allah does not let the reward of the doers of good go to waste.
interpretation: The verse encourages patience and reminds the believers that Allah will not let the good deeds of the patient and righteous ones go unrewarded. The verse serves as a source of motivation and hope for those who are facing difficulties and hardships, reminding them that their patience and perseverance will be rewarded by Allah. It also emphasizes the importance of doing good deeds, as they will not be forgotten or wasted by Allah.
orig: واصبر فإن الله لا يضيع أجر المحسنين

translation: And if not that there were from the generations before you those who warned against corruption in the land except a few of them whom We saved, and those who did wrong pursued what they were indulging in, and they were unjust.
interpretation: The verse highlights the importance of warning against corruption and injustice in society, and the consequences of ignoring these warnings. The verse mentions that in previous generations, only a few people were saved from the destruction of their communities because they heeded the warnings and refrained from corruption. However, the majority of people continued in their unjust ways and faced the consequences of their actions. This verse serves as a reminder that the warnings of the past should not be ignored, and that the pursuit of injustice and corruption will ultimately lead to destruction.
orig: فلولا كان من القرون من قبلكم أولو بقية ينهون عن الفساد في الأرض إلا قليلا ممن أنجينا منهم واتبع الذين ظلموا ما أترفوا فيه وكانوا مجرمين

translation: And your Lord is not one who destroys the towns unjustly while their people are righteous.
interpretation: The verse affirms that it is not in the nature of God to destroy communities unjustly, especially if their inhabitants are righteous and just. This verse can be seen as a message of reassurance to the righteous people who may be living among the unjust. It also serves as a reminder for the unjust that their actions will not go unnoticed and that they will ultimately be held accountable for their deeds. Additionally, the verse highlights the importance of justice and righteousness, and the consequences of neglecting these values.
orig: وما كان ربك ليهلك القرى بظلم وأهلها مصلحون

translation: And if your Lord had willed, He would have made mankind one community; but they continue to differ.
interpretation: The verse highlights the fact that God has the power to make all of humanity a single community, but has chosen not to do so. Instead, people continue to differ and have different beliefs and opinions. This verse can be interpreted as a reminder of the diversity of the human experience, and the importance of respecting and understanding different perspectives. It also highlights the idea that differences and diversity are part of God's plan for humanity.
orig: ولو شاء ربك لجعل الناس أمة واحدة ولا يزالون مختلفين

translation: But except whom your Lord has mercy, and for that He created them. And your Lord's word is fulfilled: 'I will surely fill Hell with jinn and humans all together.',
interpretation: The verse speaks about the power and authority of God's word and the inevitability of His judgment. It highlights that God will fill Hell with both jinn and humans, except for those who receive His mercy. The verse emphasizes that God's word is fulfilled and that the creation of humans and jinn is for a purpose, which is to populate Hell with the unrighteous, and only those who receive God's mercy will be saved from this fate.
orig: إلا من رحم ربك ولذلك خلقهم وتمت كلمة ربك لأملأن جهنم من الجنة والناس أجمعين

translation: And We cause not you to bear, except as a mercy from Us, the reminder of the messengers, and you were not with them when they determined the matter, and a revelation was revealed to you, while you were not with them when they determined the matter, but they are a people disputing about it.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the role of the Prophet Muhammad as a messenger of God, and emphasizes that the responsibility of conveying the message is a mercy from God. The verse also highlights that the Prophet Muhammad was not present when the previous messengers determined their respective matters, and that the revelation was given to him while he was not with them. The verse implies that there were disagreements and disputes among the people regarding the message, and it serves as a reminder for the believers to be mindful of the message and to seek understanding and guidance from God.
orig: وكلا نقص عليك من أنباء الرسل ما نثبت به فؤادك وجاءك في هذه الحق وموعظة وذكرى للمؤمنين

translation: And say to those who do not believe: 'Work in your place, indeed, we are working.'
interpretation: The verse is a command for the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) to address the disbelievers and tell them to continue with their disbelief and rejection of Islam, as they will ultimately be responsible for their own actions and consequences. At the same time, the verse emphasizes that the believers, represented by the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) and his followers, will continue to strive and work for the cause of Islam. The verse highlights the division between the believers and the disbelievers, and the unchanging nature of their respective paths. It also serves as a reminder of the importance of perseverance and steadfastness in the face of adversity and opposition.
orig: وقل للذين لا يؤمنون اعملوا على مكانتكم إنا عاملون

translation: And wait, indeed we too are waiting.
interpretation: The verse is a response from the people or entities being addressed, who are told to wait, and they in turn state that they too are waiting. The context of the verse and who is being addressed is not provided, but it implies a sense of anticipation or patience from both parties. The interpretation of this verse can vary greatly depending on the context in which it is used, but in general, it can be seen as a reminder that one is not alone in their waiting and that others are also experiencing a similar situation.
orig: وانتظروا إنا منتظرون

translation: And to God belongs the unseen of the heavens and the earth, and to Him will be returned the matter, all of it, so worship Him and rely upon Him. And your Lord is not unaware of what you do.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes God's omniscience and control over all things, both the seen and the unseen. It reminds people to worship and rely on God, as He is aware of all that they do. The verse serves as a reminder of God's power and knowledge, and encourages people to turn to Him in all aspects of their lives, entrusting their affairs to Him. The verse also serves as a warning against heedlessness and a call to mindfulness and obedience towards God.
orig: ولله غيب السماوات والأرض وإليه يرجع الأمر كله فاعبده وتوكل عليه وما ربك بغافل عما تعملون

translation: So here are the verses of the clear Book.
interpretation: The verse is a confirmation that what has been revealed is indeed the truth and guidance from the clear and unambiguous Book (the Qur'an). It is a reminder to the believers that these verses are a source of wisdom and guidance, and it is their responsibility to reflect upon them, understand their meanings, and implement them in their lives.
orig: الر تلك آيات الكتاب المبين

translation: Indeed, We have sent it down as an Arabic Qur'an that you might understand.
interpretation: The verse states that the Qur'an has been sent down in the Arabic language so that people may understand its message. The verse highlights the importance of understanding the words of the Qur'an and their meanings. It suggests that the Arabic language was chosen for its clarity and eloquence, making it easier for people to comprehend the divine message. The verse also implies that the Qur'an is not just a collection of words, but a source of guidance and wisdom that requires understanding and contemplation.
orig: إنا أنزلناه قرآنا عربيا لعلكم تعقلون

translation: We relate to you the best of stories in what We have revealed to you in this Qur'an, though before it you were of those unaware.
interpretation: The verse highlights the significance and value of the stories contained within the Qur'an, describing them as the 'best of stories'. It emphasizes that these stories were revealed by God and are being shared through the Prophet Muhammad. The verse also acknowledges that the listener (the Prophet Muhammad) was previously unaware of these stories, indicating that the Qur'an is a source of new knowledge and understanding. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of the Qur'an as a source of guidance and wisdom, and encourages the reader to reflect on the stories and lessons contained within it.
orig: نحن نقص عليك أحسن القصص بما أوحينا إليك هذا القرآن وإن كنت من قبله لمن الغافلين

translation: When Joseph said to his father, 'O my father! Indeed, I have seen eleven stars and the sun and the moon; I saw them prostrating themselves to me.',
interpretation: The verse relates a dream that Joseph had, where he saw the sun, the moon, and eleven stars prostrating themselves to him. This dream is a symbol of Joseph's future greatness and power, and it serves as a sign of his special status. The dream also highlights the theme of prophecy and divine selection, as Joseph's dream is a foreshadowing of his role as a prophet and leader. The verse emphasizes the significance of dreams and visions as a means of communication from the divine realm, and it underscores the importance of recognizing and interpreting these signs in order to understand and fulfill one's destiny.
orig: إذ قال يوسف لأبيه يا أبت إني رأيت أحد عشر كوكبا والشمس والقمر رأيتهم لي ساجدين

translation: He said, 'O my son, relate not your vision to your brothers, lest they conspire against you. Indeed, the devil to man is a clear enemy.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about a warning from a father to his son not to share his vision with his brothers. The father fears that his sons may plot against him if they become jealous or envious of the vision. The verse emphasizes the enmity of Satan towards humans, and how Satan can instigate harm and discord among people. The verse serves as a reminder to be cautious of the intentions of others, and to seek protection from Satan's schemes and whispers.
orig: قال يا بني لا تقصص رؤياك على إخوتك فيكيدوا لك كيدا إن الشيطان للإنسان عدو مبين

translation: And thus will your Lord choose you and teach you the interpretation of events and complete His favor upon you and upon the family of Jacob, as He completed it before upon your ancestors, Abraham and Isaac. Indeed, your Lord is Knowing and Wise.
interpretation: The verse speaks about God's plan for the prophet Muhammad and his family, the family of Jacob. The verse emphasizes God's choice of the prophet Muhammad, His guidance of him, and the completion of His favor upon him and his family. The verse also highlights God's knowledge and wisdom in His actions. The verse serves as a reminder of God's guidance and support for the prophet Muhammad and his family, and of God's ultimate control and wisdom in all matters.
orig: وكذلك يجتبيك ربك ويعلمك من تأويل الأحاديث ويتم نعمته عليك وعلى آل يعقوب كما أتمها على أبويك من قبل إبراهيم وإسحاق إن ربك عليم حكيم

translation: Surely, in Joseph and his brothers, there are signs (ayat) for the inquirers (saalekeen).
interpretation: The verse speaks about the story of Joseph and his brothers as a source of wisdom and guidance for those who seek to learn from it. The word 'ayat' (signs) refers to the lessons and teachings that can be derived from the story, while 'saalekeen' (inquirers) refers to those who seek knowledge and understanding. The verse suggests that the story of Joseph and his brothers contains valuable lessons that can benefit those who are willing to reflect on it and learn from it.
orig: لقد كان في يوسف وإخوته آيات للسائلين

translation: When they said, 'Surely Joseph and his brother are dearer to our father than we, while we are a strong group. Indeed, our father is in clear error.',
interpretation: The verse describes the resentment and jealousy of Joseph's brothers towards him and his brother, as they feel neglected and overshadowed by their father's love and affection for them. The verse highlights the brothers' perception of their father's favoritism towards Joseph and his brother, and their belief that their father is in clear error. The verse sets the stage for the story of Joseph, and serves to illustrate the dynamics of sibling rivalry and the consequences of envy and hatred.
orig: إذ قالوا ليوسف وأخوه أحب إلى أبينا منا ونحن عصبة إن أبانا لفي ضلال مبين

translation: Kill Joseph or throw him into the ground; and the face of your father will be clear to you, and you will be after that a righteous people.
interpretation: The verse speaks about a plot by Joseph's brothers to get rid of him. They are given two options: either to kill him or to throw him into the ground and leave him to die. The verse highlights the brothers' desire to please their father and to be seen as righteous people after the act. The verse serves as a reminder of the consequences of giving in to one's desires and the potential harm it can cause to others. It also emphasizes the importance of justice and fairness towards others, even if it goes against one's own interests.
orig: اقتلوا يوسف أو اطرحوه أرضا يخل لكم وجه أبيكم وتكونوا من بعده قوما صالحين

translation: A speaker from among them said, 'Do not kill Joseph, but throw him into the bottom of the well. Some caravan will pick him up if you are to do (anything).'
interpretation: The verse relates the story of Joseph and his brothers, and specifically one brother's suggestion to not kill Joseph but instead throw him into a well. The verse highlights the treacherous and deceitful nature of the brothers, as well as their willingness to harm Joseph despite their familial bond. The verse also emphasizes the power dynamic between the brothers, as the speaker's suggestion implies that the brothers have the ability to carry out harm against Joseph with impunity. The verse serves as a narrative device, providing context and background for later events in the story of Joseph.
orig: قال قائل منهم لا تقتلوا يوسف وألقوه في غيابت الجب يلتقطه بعض السيارة إن كنتم فاعلين

translation: They said, 'O our father, why do you not trust us concerning Joseph, when we are indeed his well-wishers?'
interpretation: The verse shows the brothers of Yusuf (Joseph) expressing their frustration towards their father, who does not trust them regarding Yusuf. They claim that they are well-wishers for Yusuf and question why their father does not trust them. The verse highlights the complex family dynamics and the tensions that arise from the brothers' jealousy towards Yusuf. It also emphasizes the importance of trust and communication within a family, and the consequences of favoritism and jealousy.
orig: قالوا يا أبانا ما لك لا تأمنا على يوسف وإنا له لناصحون

translation: And send him with us tomorrow, that he may enjoy himself and play, and indeed, we will be his guardians.
interpretation: The verse speaks about a person who is being sent with a group of people the next day. The verse highlights the intention of the people to ensure the person's enjoyment and leisure. The people also take responsibility for the person's safety and well-being, as they claim to be his guardians. However, the verse does not provide any further context or information about the identity of the person or the reason for his journey. The verse may be interpreted as a message of trust and responsibility, emphasizing the importance of taking care of those who are under one's protection.
orig: أرسله معنا غدا يرتع ويلعب وإنا له لحافظون

translation: He said, 'I am only grieved that you are taking him away. I fear that the wolf may eat him while you are not paying attention.',
interpretation: The verse relays the concerns of a shepherd who is entrusting his responsibility of taking care of a child to others. He expresses his grief and fear over the possibility of harm coming to the child while in their care. The verse can be interpreted as a reminder of the importance of taking care of those who are entrusted to us, and the responsibility we have to ensure their safety and well-being.
orig: قال إني ليحزنني أن تذهبوا به وأخاف أن يأكله الذئب وأنتم عنه غافلون

translation: They said, 'If the wolf eats it while we are a group, then indeed, we are losers.'
interpretation: The verse is part of a story about a shepherd who accused a boy of stealing a sheep. The boy made a bet with the shepherd that if a wolf were to eat the sheep while they were watching, then the shepherd would be the loser. The verse is the response of the shepherd and his companions, admitting that they would indeed be the losers in such a scenario. The verse highlights the importance of making fair and just accusations, as well as the need to consider the consequences of one's words and actions.
orig: قالوا لئن أكله الذئب ونحن عصبة إنا إذا لخاسرون

translation: But when they went away with it and conspired to put him in the bottom of the well and We revealed to him: 'Indeed, you will inform them of their affair at this time, while they do not perceive.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about a group of people who conspired against a person and planned to throw him into a well. However, God had a plan for this individual and revealed to him that he would inform the people of their actions at a later time. The verse emphasizes the power of God's plan and the ultimate victory of justice. It serves as a reminder that those who commit unjust actions will be held accountable, even if it seems like they have gotten away with it in the present. The verse also highlights the importance of trust in God's plan and the belief that justice will be served, even if it may not be immediately apparent.
orig: فلما ذهبوا به وأجمعوا أن يجعلوه في غيابت الجب وأوحينا إليه لتنبئنهم بأمرهم هذا وهم لا يشعرون

translation: And they came to their father at night, weeping.
interpretation: The verse describes the children of the prophet Yusuf (Joseph) coming to their father at night, weeping. This event takes place towards the end of the story of Yusuf in the Qur'an, after Yusuf has forgiven his brothers for their past actions and has been reunited with his family. The verse highlights the emotional moment of reconciliation and forgiveness between Yusuf and his brothers, and the relief and joy that their father experiences upon seeing his family reunited.
orig: وجاءوا أباهم عشاء يبكون

translation: They said, 'O our father! We went to race, and left Joseph with our possessions, and the wolf ate him, but you will never believe us, even if we speak the truth.'
interpretation: The verse relays the story of Joseph and his brothers, and highlights the brothers' lie about what happened to Joseph. The brothers claim that a wolf ate Joseph, but their father does not believe them. The verse emphasizes the brothers' deception and their attempt to cover up their actions. The verse also highlights the father's disbelief and mistrust towards his sons, suggesting a strained relationship between them. The verse serves as a lesson about the consequences of lying and the importance of honesty and trust in relationships.
orig: قالوا يا أبانا إنا ذهبنا نستبق وتركنا يوسف عند متاعنا فأكله الذئب وما أنت بمؤمن لنا ولو كنا صادقين

translation: And they came with a false claim against him, saying, 'Indeed, we have found him unjust.' But rather, they are unjust. And he was not of those who transgressed, and he said, 'If you are telling the truth, then ask those who have been with me.' So they conspired against him, and thus, with Allah is the end of all matters.
interpretation: The verse speaks about a person who was falsely accused of wrongdoing by his enemies. Despite their false claims, the verse emphasizes that the accusers are the ones who are truly unjust. The verse highlights the unjust actions of the accusers and their lack of evidence against the accused. The accused, on the other hand, is described as someone who does not transgress and who remains patient in the face of false accusations. The verse serves as a reminder that Allah is the ultimate judge and that the outcome of all matters ultimately rests with Him.
orig: وجاءوا على قميصه بدم كذب قال بل سولت لكم أنفسكم أمرا فصبر جميل والله المستعان على ما تصفون

translation: And the caravan came, so they sent their wares forward, and made ready their load, and he [the servant they suspected of stealing] passed by, but they recognized him not. And they went on, while he was sitting in their midst, then he came after them, and he was their watcher by night.
interpretation: This verse describes a caravan that has arrived and the people are preparing to move on by loading their goods onto the camels. A servant who was previously suspected of stealing is among them, but he goes unnoticed. He ends up following them and serving as their night watchman. The verse highlights the imperfection of human perception and judgment, as well as the servant's persistence and willingness to serve despite his previous accusation.
orig: وجاءت سيارة فأرسلوا واردهم فأدلى دلوه قال يا بشرى هذا غلام وأسروه بضاعة والله عليم بما يعملون

translation: And they were given a small price for it, and they will know today which of you is untrue to his promise.
interpretation: The verse speaks about people who were given a small price for their actions, and it highlights that they will soon find out who among them has been unfaithful to their promises. The verse emphasizes the idea that the consequences of one's actions will eventually be revealed, and that people will be held accountable for their deeds. The verse serves as a reminder that true faith and commitment are not measured by material wealth or possessions, but rather by one's actions and intentions.
orig: وشروه بثمن بخس دراهم معدودة وكانوا فيه من الزاهدين

translation: And the one who bought him (Joseph) from Egypt said to his wife, 'Treat him generously, perhaps he will benefit us or we may adopt him as a son.' And in this way We established Joseph in the land, and We taught him the interpretation of events. And God has power over all things, but most people do not know.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the generosity and kindness shown by the man who bought Joseph from Egypt towards him. The verse highlights the wisdom of the man's decision, as he hoped that Joseph would bring some benefit to him and his family, or even become their adopted son. The verse also emphasizes the role of God in establishing Joseph in the land and teaching him the interpretation of events, indicating that God's plan and will are at work behind the scenes. The verse concludes by acknowledging God's power and control over all things, while also recognizing that most people are unaware of this truth.
orig: وقال الذي اشتراه من مصر لامرأته أكرمي مثواه عسى أن ينفعنا أو نتخذه ولدا وكذلك مكنا ليوسف في الأرض ولنعلمه من تأويل الأحاديث والله غالب على أمره ولكن أكثر الناس لا يعلمون

translation: And when its (the human's) term came, We took him in punishment, with fullest punishment, and We have knowledge of what they ascribe (to Us).
interpretation: The verse speaks about the punishment that humans receive when their time comes. The punishment is described as being 'with fullest punishment', indicating that it is severe and just. The verse also emphasizes that God has knowledge of what people ascribe to Him, highlighting the idea that God is all-knowing and all-seeing. The verse serves as a reminder that humans will be held accountable for their actions and that they will receive the punishment that they deserve.
orig: ولما بلغ أشده آتيناه حكما وعلما وكذلك نجزي المحسنين

translation: And (as for) the one who was in (his) house, (engaged) in sexual relations with his wife - she (too) slipped (into) the blame. And they (both) took to their heels from him. And they (too) closed the doors. And they (too) said, 'Be quiet!' He said, 'My Lord! Surely I have wronged myself! So (as for) me, He is the Most Forgiving, the Most Merciful.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about a man who was caught in the act of sexual relations with his wife by someone. Both of them panicked and tried to cover up their act by closing the doors and asking the person to be quiet. However, the man immediately recognized his mistake and turned to God for forgiveness, acknowledging that he had wronged himself. The verse highlights the importance of recognizing one's mistakes and seeking forgiveness from God. It also emphasizes the contrast between the couple's initial reaction of panic and denial and the man's ultimate recognition of his wrongdoing and his turning to God for forgiveness.
orig: وراودته التي هو في بيتها عن نفسه وغلقت الأبواب وقالت هيت لك قال معاذ الله إنه ربي أحسن مثواي إنه لا يفلح الظالمون

translation: And I have certainly pondered over it and myself, but Satan made its beautiful seeming appealing to me. So he deceived me. And indeed, I fear Allah, Lord of the worlds.
interpretation: The verse speaks about a person who is struggling with their own desires and the temptation of Satan. Despite their efforts to resist, they were deceived by the allure of sin. However, the person ultimately recognizes their mistake and expresses their fear of God, the Lord of the worlds. The verse serves as a reminder of the constant struggle between good and evil and the importance of seeking God's guidance and protection against temptation.
orig: ولقد همت به وهم بها لولا أن رأى برهان ربه كذلك لنصرف عنه السوء والفحشاء إنه من عبادنا المخلصين

translation: And keep yourself patient [by being] with those who call upon their Lord in the morning and the evening, seeking His countenance. And let not your eyes pass from them, desiring adornments of the worldly life, and do not obey one whose heart We have made heedless of Our remembrance and who follows his desire. And they [the believers] say, 'We have believed in Allah and in what was revealed to us and what was revealed to Abraham and Ishmael and Isaac and Jacob and the Descendants and what was given to Moses and Jesus and what was given to the prophets from their Lord. We make no distinction between any of them, and we are Muslims [in submission] to Him.' And if they believe in what you have been given, then they are truly believers. And if they deny you, then say, 'I have believed in what Allah has sent down of the Book and I have been commanded to do justice between you. Allah is our Lord and your Lord. For us are our deeds, and for you are your deeds. There is no need for us to associate with you in anything. There is no need for them to associate with us. And to Allah is the [final] destination.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the importance of being patient and steadfast in the company of those who worship and call upon God in the morning and evening. The verse warns against being distracted by the adornments of the worldly life and following the desires of those who are heedless of God's remembrance. The verse emphasizes the importance of believing in all of God's revelations, including those given to the prophets, and not making any distinction between them. The verse also highlights the importance of doing justice and not associating with those who deny God's message. The verse ultimately affirms that each person is responsible for their own actions and will have their own destiny with God.
orig: واستبقا الباب وقدت قميصه من دبر وألفيا سيدها لدى الباب قالت ما جزاء من أراد بأهلك سوءا إلا أن يسجن أو عذاب أليم

translation: She said, 'It has troubled me concerning my soul, and I have consulted one of its (i.e., my husband's) relatives, and indeed, he confirmed my fear. If it were not that his garment had been torn from before, I would have considered him among the liars.'
interpretation: The verse relays the words of a woman who has been unfaithful to her husband and is now expressing her fear and guilt to someone in her husband's family. She consults with a relative, who confirms her fear, and she admits that she would have considered him a liar if it were not for the torn garment, which serves as evidence of her infidelity. The verse highlights the woman's inner turmoil and her attempts to come to terms with her actions, as well as the role of evidence in uncovering the truth.
orig: قال هي راودتني عن نفسي وشهد شاهد من أهلها إن كان قميصه قد من قبل فصدقت وهو من الكاذبين

translation: And if his shirt is torn from the back, then she has lied, and he is of the truthful.
interpretation: The verse is part of a story about two people who make accusations against each other. The verse establishes a way to determine the truthfulness of their claims. If the shirt of the person being accused is torn from the back, it indicates that he was lying down and therefore could not have committed the act of which he is accused. The verse thus serves as a means of establishing justice and determining the truth in a situation where it might otherwise be difficult to do so.
orig: وإن كان قميصه قد من دبر فكذبت وهو من الصادقين

translation: Then when he saw his shirt torn at the back, he said: 'This is of your women's guile; indeed, your guile is great.'
interpretation: The verse describes a man's reaction to seeing his shirt torn at the back. He immediately attributes this to the guile or cunning of women, and asserts that their cunning is indeed great. The verse highlights the man's negative perception of women and his quickness to blame them for his misfortune. The verse can be interpreted as a criticism of such attitudes, which reinforce harmful gender stereotypes and perpetuate discrimination against women.
orig: فلما رأى قميصه قد من دبر قال إنه من كيدكن إن كيدكن عظيم

translation: So Joseph kept within himself his desire and restrained himself. He said, 'My Lord, prison is more to my liking than that to which they invite me. And if You do not avert from me their plan, I might incline toward them and [thus] be of the ignorant.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about Joseph's response when he was faced with the temptation of the wife of the Egyptian official. Joseph chose to resist the temptation and prayed to God for help. He expressed his preference for prison over giving in to the temptation. The verse highlights the importance of resisting temptation and seeking God's guidance in difficult situations. It also emphasizes the potential consequences of giving in to temptation and the importance of seeking God's protection from falling into sin.
orig: يوسف أعرض عن هذا واستغفري لذنبك إنك كنت من الخاطئين

translation: And the women in the city said, 'The noblewoman's daughter is seeking to seduce her (from herself), indeed she has been infatuated with love. We surely see her in clear error.'
interpretation: The verse describes the accusations made by the women of a city against the daughter of a noblewoman, accusing her of seeking to seduce herself and being infatuated with love. The women express their certainty in seeing her in clear error. The verse may be interpreted as a warning against slander and false accusations, emphasizing the importance of truth and justice. It may also serve as a reminder of the consequences of giving in to temptation and the destructive power of gossip and rumors.
orig: وقال نسوة في المدينة امرأت العزيز تراود فتاها عن نفسه قد شغفها حبا إنا لنراها في ضلال مبين

translation: And when heard of their scheming, he sent to them and prepared for them a banquet, and gave to each one of them a knife, and said, 'Come out to me.' So when they saw him, they admired him and cut their hands, and said, 'Allah is most great! This is not a human being; this is nothing but a noble angel!'
interpretation: The verse describes a scene where a man has invited a group of women to a banquet and has given each of them a knife. When the women see the man, they are struck by his appearance and cut their hands in astonishment, exclaiming that he is not a human being but a noble angel. The verse emphasizes the extraordinary nature of the man, whose appearance and demeanor are so striking that the women are moved to make such an exclamation. The verse can be interpreted as a metaphor for the power of righteousness and virtue, which can inspire awe and reverence in those who witness it. The verse may also be seen as a warning against judging others based on appearances, as the women in the verse initially mistake the man for an angel before realizing their error.
orig: فلما سمعت بمكرهن أرسلت إليهن وأعتدت لهن متكأ وآتت كل واحدة منهن سكينا وقالت اخرج عليهن فلما رأينه أكبرنه وقطعن أيديهن وقلن حاش لله ما هذا بشرا إن هذا إلا ملك كريم

translation: She said, 'That is what I have been threatening you with; you used to pay no attention to it, and you used to laugh at it. I leave you to your Lord; now I will go to those who invoked [Allah] with me.'
interpretation: The verse describes a conversation between a woman and a group of people who had previously dismissed her warnings about the consequences of their actions. The woman, who had been warning them, has now given up on them and is leaving them to face the consequences of their actions. The verse emphasizes the importance of heeding warnings and taking them seriously, as well as the importance of faith and seeking guidance from Allah. The woman's actions also serve as a reminder of the importance of standing up for what is right and not being swayed by the opinions of others.
orig: قالت فذلكن الذي لمتنني فيه ولقد راودته عن نفسه فاستعصم ولئن لم يفعل ما آمره ليسجنن وليكونا من الصاغرين

translation: He said, 'My Lord, the prison is dearer to me than that to which they invite me. And if You do not avert from me their plan, I will be among the ignorant.'
interpretation: The verse is a statement made by a prophet or a righteous person who is facing persecution and opposition from his people. He prefers to be in prison rather than follow the false ways of his people. He seeks God's protection from the schemes of his enemies and prays not to be among the ignorant, meaning those who are astray from the truth. The verse highlights the prophet's unwavering commitment to his faith and his rejection of the falsehood and corruption of his society.
orig: قال رب السجن أحب إلي مما يدعونني إليه وإلا تصرف عني كيدهن أصب إليهن وأكن من الجاهلين

translation: So his Lord responded to him, and He turned away from him his sin. Indeed, He is the Hearing, the Knowing.
interpretation: The verse speaks about an individual who has committed a sin, and has repented to God. The verse emphasizes God's forgiveness and mercy towards those who repent and turn back to Him. The verse also highlights God's attributes of being the "Hearing" and the "Knowing", indicating that He is aware of our actions, and is always ready to listen to our repentance. This verse serves as a reminder that no matter how great the sin, God is always ready to forgive those who truly repent and turn back to Him.
orig: فاستجاب له ربه فصرف عنه كيدهن إنه هو السميع العليم

translation: Then after they saw our signs, We punished them, so they are in complete despair.
interpretation: The verse describes the punishment of a group of people who saw signs from God but did not heed them. As a result, they were punished and are now in a state of complete despair. The verse emphasizes the importance of paying attention to the signs from God and acting upon them, as failing to do so may result in severe consequences.
orig: ثم بدا لهم من بعد ما رأوا الآيات ليسجننه حتى حين

translation: And [the king of Egypt] said, 'Bring him to me.' So when the boy was brought to him, he said, 'Indeed, I will mention you among my family.' And one of the two boys said, 'O my father, indeed I see myself pressing wine.' And the other said, 'Indeed, I see myself carrying upon my head, bread - from which I would feed the birds.' So bring us both into your deathroll; indeed, we are Muslims.'
interpretation: The verse describes a conversation between the king of Egypt and Prophet Yusuf (Joseph) after he was reunited with his brothers. Two of his brothers, who did not recognize him, describe their dreams and ask for their dreams to be interpreted. The first brother sees himself pressing wine, which is a symbol of abundance and prosperity. The second brother sees himself carrying bread, which is a symbol of sustenance and nourishment. By interpreting these dreams, Prophet Yusuf (Joseph) was able to reveal his identity and be reunited with his family. The verse emphasizes the power of dreams and their ability to reveal the truth, as well as the significance of trusting in God's plan and believing in the unseen.
orig: ودخل معه السجن فتيان قال أحدهما إني أراني أعصر خمرا وقال الآخر إني أراني أحمل فوق رأسي خبزا تأكل الطير منه نبئنا بتأويله إنا نراك من المحسنين

translation: He said, 'No food will come to you two to eat except that I will inform you of its interpretation before it comes to you while I am one of those who possess knowledge from my Lord.' Indeed, I left a community of people who do not believe in Allah and they will deny the hereafter.
interpretation: The verse speaks about a person who has been given knowledge from God and has the ability to interpret events before they occur. The person makes a statement that no food will come to them without first informing them of its interpretation. This statement emphasizes the person's ability to understand and interpret events through divine knowledge. The verse also highlights the disbelief of the person's previous community, who do not believe in God and deny the hereafter. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of faith and the consequences of disbelief.
orig: قال لا يأتيكما طعام ترزقانه إلا نبأتكما بتأويله قبل أن يأتيكما ذلكما مما علمني ربي إني تركت ملة قوم لا يؤمنون بالله وهم بالآخرة هم كافرون

translation: And I have followed the religion of my fathers, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, not being of those who associate others with Allah in worship. This has come to us from Allah, and to the people, but most of the people do not give thanks.
interpretation: The verse highlights the importance of monotheism and the rejection of idolatry, which was the religion of the speaker's ancestors. The speaker emphasizes their adherence to this tradition and their gratitude for the guidance they have received from Allah. The verse also highlights the ingratitude of most people, despite the blessings they have received from Allah. The verse encourages the reader to be grateful for the guidance they have received and to follow in the footsteps of the prophets, avoiding the sin of idolatry and being thankful for the blessings of Allah.
orig: واتبعت ملة آبائي إبراهيم وإسحاق ويعقوب ما كان لنا أن نشرك بالله من شيء ذلك من فضل الله علينا وعلى الناس ولكن أكثر الناس لا يشكرون

translation: O prisoner, is
interpretation: No interpretation
orig: يا صاحبي السجن أأرباب متفرقون خير أم الله الواحد القهار

translation: You worship besides Him only idols which you and your forefathers have invented, and for which Allah has sent down no authority. The decision is only Allah's. He has commanded that you worship none but Him. That is the right religion, but most people do not know.
interpretation: The verse criticizes the worship of idols and false gods, emphasizing that such practices have no basis in divine revelation and are merely human inventions. The verse asserts the exclusive authority of God in matters of religion, commanding the worship of none but Him. The phrase 'most people do not know' highlights the widespread ignorance and misguidance of humanity. The verse serves as a reminder of the true nature of monotheism and the importance of adhering to the teachings of God.
orig: ما تعبدون من دونه إلا أسماء سميتموها أنتم وآباؤكم ما أنزل الله بها من سلطان إن الحكم إلا لله أمر ألا تعبدوا إلا إياه ذلك الدين القيم ولكن أكثر الناس لا يعلمون

translation: O you two in the pit! Which of you will bring his lord the nearest, he who is mindful (of his duty), or he who is reckless and disdainful?
interpretation: The verse is a rhetorical question addressed to two people who are in a pit or a difficult situation. The question is asking which of the two will be closer to God, the one who is mindful of his duties and responsibilities, or the one who is reckless and disdainful. The verse highlights the importance of being mindful of one's duties towards God, and the consequences of being reckless and disdainful. The verse serves as a reminder that each person's actions have consequences and that ultimately, it is the mindful and dutiful who will be closest to God.
orig: يا صاحبي السجن أما أحدكما فيسقي ربه خمرا وأما الآخر فيصلب فتأكل الطير من رأسه قضي الأمر الذي فيه تستفتيان

translation: And [for their sin] is that upon the Day of Resurrection they will be presented as flares [for Hellfire]. So bind them firmly; indeed, they are to be questioned harshly. Then what will they know? And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon. And who is more unjust than he who invents about Allah a lie or denies His verses? Indeed, the wrongdoers will not succeed.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the fate of those who are unjust and deny the verses of Allah. They will be presented as flares for Hellfire on the Day of Resurrection and will be questioned harshly. The verse emphasizes the severity of their punishment, which is a consequence of their unjust actions. The verse also reminds of the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God, either in the morning or at noon. The verse serves as a warning to those who deny the verses of Allah and commit unjust acts, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment. The verse also highlights the gravity of inventing a lie about Allah or denying His verses, emphasizing that the wrongdoers will not succeed.
orig: وقال للذي ظن أنه ناج منهما اذكرني عند ربك فأنساه الشيطان ذكر ربه فلبث في السجن بضع سنين

translation: And the king said, 'Indeed, I have seen (in a dream) seven fat cows being eaten by seven thin cows, and seven green spikes [of grain] and others [that were] dry. But among them, I saw seven ears, full and ripe. And [then] others [were] dry. O assembly of scholars, explain to me my vision, if you are able to interpret visions.'
interpretation: The verse describes a dream that the king has had, in which he sees seven fat cows being eaten by seven thin cows, and seven green spikes of grain and others that were dry. Among them, he also saw seven ears, full and ripe. The king turns to the scholars of his court and asks them to interpret his dream. The verse emphasizes the importance of understanding and interpreting dreams, as they are often considered to be a form of divine communication. The dream in this verse is a metaphor for the state of the kingdom, and the scholars are tasked with understanding its meaning and implications for the future.
orig: وقال الملك إني أرى سبع بقرات سمان يأكلهن سبع عجاف وسبع سنبلات خضر وأخر يابسات يا أيها الملأ أفتوني في رؤياي إن كنتم للرؤيا تعبرون

translation: They said, 'We are only fabricating lies by our own accord. And we are not knowledgeable about the interpretation of dreams.'
interpretation: The verse recounts the words of some people who, after hearing the interpretation of a dream, deny its truth and claim that they were only telling lies for their own amusement. They also admit that they do not possess the knowledge to interpret dreams. The verse highlights the denial and rejection of truth by some people, despite clear evidence. It also emphasizes the importance of having knowledge and understanding before making judgments or dismissing something as false.
orig: قالوا أضغاث أحلام وما نحن بتأويل الأحلام بعالمين

translation: And the one who was saved from among them, he began to recite the signs (of God) and remember after a time, saying, 'I will inform you of its interpretation, so wait.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about a person who was saved from a group of people who were destroyed by God for their sins and injustice. After a period of time, this person begins to recite the signs of God and remembers the fate of his previous community. He then offers to interpret or explain the signs to others, asking them to wait and listen. The verse highlights the importance of remembering and reflecting on the lessons of the past, and the role of the interpreter in conveying the message of God to others. It also emphasizes the significance of patience and attentiveness in understanding the signs of God.
orig: وقال الذي نجا منهما وادكر بعد أمة أنا أنبئكم بتأويله فأرسلون

translation: Joseph, O truthful one, explain to us about seven fat cows being eaten by seven lean ones, and seven green spikes and others dry, so that I may return to the people, perhaps they will know.
interpretation: In this verse, Joseph is asked by his fellow inmates to interpret a dream. The dream consists of seven fat cows being consumed by seven lean ones, followed by the appearance of seven green spikes and seven dry ones. The verse implies that Joseph has a special ability to interpret dreams and that the inmates are seeking his guidance. The dream itself can be interpreted in various ways, but the verse does not provide the interpretation. Instead, it emphasizes the importance of understanding and interpreting signs and symbols in order to gain insight and knowledge.
orig: يوسف أيها الصديق أفتنا في سبع بقرات سمان يأكلهن سبع عجاف وسبع سنبلات خضر وأخر يابسات لعلي أرجع إلى الناس لعلهم يعلمون

translation: He said, 'Plant for seven years dabbing (your land) and leave what you harvest, except a little of it which you eat.'
interpretation: The verse relays a command from an unspecified speaker to plant and cultivate the land for a period of seven years, leaving the harvested crops to dry and rot in the fields, except for a small portion that may be consumed. The command serves as a test of faith and obedience, requiring the listener to forgo the immediate benefits of their labor for the sake of a greater, unspecified reward. The verse emphasizes the importance of patience, perseverance, and trust in the divine plan, even in the face of apparent hardship and loss.
orig: قال تزرعون سبع سنين دأبا فما حصدتم فذروه في سنبله إلا قليلا مما تأكلون

translation: Then after that,
interpretation: No interpretation
orig: ثم يأتي من بعد ذلك سبع شداد يأكلن ما قدمتم لهن إلا قليلا مما تحصنون

translation: Then will come after that a year in which people will have abundance, and they will press [olive oil and grapes].
interpretation: The verse speaks about a year that will come after a time of difficulty or hardship, during which people will have an abundance of resources and will be able to produce and enjoy the fruits of their labor. The pressing of olives and grapes is a metaphor for prosperity and abundance, as these products were valuable and important in the context of the time and place. The verse serves as a message of hope and reassurance, reminding people that after times of hardship and difficulty, there will be periods of prosperity and abundance.
orig: ثم يأتي من بعد ذلك عام فيه يغاث الناس وفيه يعصرون

translation: And the king said, 'Bring him to me.' But when the messenger came to him, he said, 'Go back to your Lord and ask Him, "Why did You make the women I have sequestered cut off their hands? For my Lord is surely full of knowledge."'
interpretation: The verse describes a conversation between a king and a messenger. The king has sequestered some women and commanded that their hands be cut off. When the messenger arrives, the king asks for the one who made this command, referring to God. The king then tells the messenger to return to God and ask why He commanded that the women's hands be cut off. The verse highlights the king's recognition of God's knowledge and power. It also emphasizes the respect and submission that the king has for God, as he acknowledges that God has a greater understanding of the situation than he does.
orig: وقال الملك ائتوني به فلما جاءه الرسول قال ارجع إلى ربك فاسأله ما بال النسوة اللاتي قطعن أيديهن إن ربي بكيدهن عليم

translation: He said, 'What is your situation that you have testified against Joseph?' They said, 'God forbid! We know nothing about his matter except good.' The woman of power said, 'Now the truth has come to light. It was I who tried to seduce him, and indeed, he is of the truthful ones.'
interpretation: The verse relays the conversation between the father of Joseph and the people who had falsely accused Joseph of a crime. The father asks them why they had testified against Joseph and they deny any wrongdoing. However, the woman who had attempted to seduce Joseph comes forward and admits her guilt. She states that Joseph is innocent and that the truth has now been revealed. The verse highlights the importance of honesty and the consequences of false accusations. It serves as a reminder that truth will always prevail over falsehood and that justice will ultimately be served.
orig: قال ما خطبكن إذ راودتن يوسف عن نفسه قلن حاش لله ما علمنا عليه من سوء قالت امرأت العزيز الآن حصحص الحق أنا راودته عن نفسه وإنه لمن الصادقين

translation: That is only so that you may know that I do not inform you of (the unseen) through my own desire, but Allah (it is who) sends down knowledge of it - and Allah is Knowing of the unseen (things).
interpretation: The verse explains that the knowledge that the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) has of the unseen is not of his own, but rather it is revealed to him by Allah. This is to make it clear that the Prophet is not making things up or speaking from his own desires, but rather he is conveying the message of Allah. The verse also emphasizes that Allah has knowledge of the unseen, indicating His omniscience and omnipotence.
orig: ذلك ليعلم أني لم أخنه بالغيب وأن الله لا يهدي كيد الخائنين

translation: And I do not absolve myself - indeed, the soul is prone to evil, except for whom my Lord has mercy - indeed, my Lord is Forgiving, Merciful.
interpretation: The verse is a statement of humility and recognition of human weakness. The speaker acknowledges that they cannot claim to be free from sin and that the soul has a natural inclination towards wrongdoing. However, the speaker also expresses faith in the mercy of their Lord, recognizing that only through His mercy can one be saved from sin. The verse emphasizes the importance of seeking God's forgiveness and mercy, and recognizing one's own limitations and need for divine guidance.
orig: وما أبرئ نفسي إن النفس لأمارة بالسوء إلا ما رحم ربي إن ربي غفور رحيم

translation: And the king said, 'Bring him to me that I may ask him. But when he came to him, he said, 'Today you are, indeed, a distinguished and trusted [one].'
interpretation: The verse describes a conversation between a king and someone who has been brought before him. The king initially intends to ask the person something, but upon meeting him, he changes his tone and compliments the person, calling him distinguished and trustworthy. The verse may be interpreted as a reminder of the importance of treating people with respect and dignity, regardless of the initial intentions or assumptions one might have towards them. It also highlights the potential for a change of heart and the ability to form a positive impression of someone upon actually meeting them.
orig: وقال الملك ائتوني به أستخلصه لنفسي فلما كلمه قال إنك اليوم لدينا مكين أمين

translation: He said, 'Set me over the treasures of the earth, I am indeed a knowledgeable guardian.'
interpretation: The verse is a statement made by someone who is asking to be put in charge of the treasures of the earth. The person making the statement portrays themselves as a knowledgeable and capable guardian, suggesting that they are the best choice for the job. The verse can be interpreted as a metaphor for power, wealth, and authority, and the person's desire to control and manage these resources. The verse can also be seen as a reminder of the dangers of power and the importance of being a responsible and wise leader, as the treasures of the earth can easily be misused or corrupted.
orig: قال اجعلني على خزائن الأرض إني حفيظ عليم

translation: And thus did We give establishment to Joseph in the land that he might settle wherever he pleased. We bestow grace on whom We will, and We do not neglect the reward of the doers of good.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the establishment of Joseph in the land, indicating his power and authority. It emphasizes that this was a result of God's grace and favor, and that it was not something that Joseph had earned or deserved. The verse also highlights that God bestows grace on whom He wills and that the doers of good will not be neglected or forgotten. The verse serves as a reminder that God's grace and reward are not based on merit but on His will and that those who do good will be rewarded.
orig: وكذلك مكنا ليوسف في الأرض يتبوأ منها حيث يشاء نصيب برحمتنا من نشاء ولا نضيع أجر المحسنين

translation: But the reward of the Hereafter is better for those who believe and fear [God].
interpretation: The verse contrasts the rewards of this world with the rewards of the Hereafter, emphasizing that the rewards of the Hereafter are superior for those who have faith in God and are mindful of His commands. The verse encourages believers to be patient and steadfast in their faith, reminding them that the temporary trials and hardships of this world are nothing compared to the eternal bliss and happiness that await them in the Hereafter. The verse also highlights the importance of having a strong faith and fear of God, which leads to righteous actions and a virtuous life.
orig: ولأجر الآخرة خير للذين آمنوا وكانوا يتقون

translation: And when Joseph's brothers came, they entered upon him, and he recognized them, but they did not recognize him.
interpretation: The verse describes the moment when Joseph's brothers came to Egypt and met Joseph, who was now a powerful figure in the Egyptian court. Joseph recognized his brothers, but they did not recognize him, emphasizing the change in their circumstances and the power dynamic between them. This event serves as a turning point in the story of Joseph and sets the stage for the events that follow, including the brothers' realization of their past actions towards Joseph and their eventual reconciliation.
orig: وجاء إخوة يوسف فدخلوا عليه فعرفهم وهم له منكرون

translation: And when We decided to destroy them, We said, 'Bring me a son from among you, and let us worship him.' Surely, I will then be adoring the one you have joined as a partner (with Allah).'
interpretation: The verse speaks about a decision made by God to destroy a people who called upon Prophet Abraham (peace be upon him) to worship a son of theirs. This was a test for the people, and the verse emphasizes the absurdity of their request and the futility of their attempt to associate partners with God. The verse serves as a reminder of the oneness of God and the importance of worshipping Him alone, without associating any partners with Him.
orig: ولما جهزهم بجهازهم قال ائتوني بأخ لكم من أبيكم ألا ترون أني أوفي الكيل وأنا خير المنزلين

translation: But if you do not bring it to me, there will be no respite for you from me, and you will not approach [me]
interpretation: The verse speaks about a situation where a particular action or demand has not been fulfilled. The consequence of not fulfilling this demand is that there will be no repentance or forgiveness granted, and the person will not be allowed to come close or have access to the one who is being addressed. This verse emphasizes the importance of fulfilling one's responsibilities and obligations, and the severe consequences of neglecting them. It serves as a warning to those who are negligent and careless in their actions, reminding them of the importance of accountability and responsibility.
orig: فإن لم تأتوني به فلا كيل لكم عندي ولا تقربون

translation: They said, 'We will surely return to our father and our family, and we will surely act (righteously).'
interpretation: The verse shows the response of a group of people who are being sent away from their father and their family. They make a promise to return and act righteously. The verse highlights the importance of family ties and the commitment to make amends and correct past mistakes. It also emphasizes the significance of one's actions and the need to strive for righteousness and goodness.
orig: قالوا سنراود عنه أباه وإنا لفاعلون

translation: And he said to his two companions, 'Make ready their baggage. Perhaps they will recognize it if they return to their people. Perhaps they will come back.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about a person instructing his two companions to prepare their baggage before they set off on a journey. The person suggests that the preparation of their baggage may help the companions recognize their belongings when they return to their people. The verse also implies that the person is hopeful that the companions may return from their journey. The verse can be interpreted as a metaphor for life's journey, emphasizing the importance of preparing for the future while being hopeful and optimistic about the outcome.
orig: وقال لفتيانه اجعلوا بضاعتهم في رحالهم لعلهم يعرفونها إذا انقلبوا إلى أهلهم لعلهم يرجعون

translation: But when they returned to their father, they said, 'O our father! We restricted ourselves from the grain, so send with us our brother [that he] may be a measure of grain for us and we will be among the upright.',
interpretation: The verse describes the story of Joseph and his brothers. In this part of the story, the brothers have returned to their father, Jacob, after their first journey to Egypt. They tell their father that they have restricted themselves from the grain and ask him to send their brother Benjamin (Joseph) with them so that he can serve as a measure of grain for them. The verse highlights the deceit of the brothers, who had previously sold Joseph into slavery, as they try to manipulate their father into allowing Benjamin to travel with them to Egypt. The verse also emphasizes the trust that the brothers claim to have, as they say that they are among the upright, even though they have committed a grave sin against their brother.
orig: فلما رجعوا إلى أبيهم قالوا يا أبانا منع منا الكيل فأرسل معنا أخانا نكتل وإنا له لحافظون

translation: He said, 'Do you believe in it when it has come to you, when you did not believe in it before, when it came to your predecessors?' But God is the best of guardians, and He is the most merciful of the merciful.
interpretation: The verse is a dialogue between an unspecified person and the believers, where the former questions the sincerity of their faith. The verse highlights the contrast between the believers' previous disbelief and their current acceptance of the truth. The verse emphasizes God's role as the best guardian and the most merciful, reminding the believers of God's attributes of protection and compassion.
orig: قال هل آمنكم عليه إلا كما أمنتكم على أخيه من قبل فالله خير حافظا وهو أرحم الراحمين

translation: And when they opened their treasures, they found that their keys had returned to them. They said, 'Oh, our father! What more should we desire? Here are our keys. Now we are believers!', Rejoicing at this, they prostrated themselves and promised to give alms.
interpretation: The verse describes the moment when a group of people open their treasures and find that their keys, which they had lost, have been returned to them. This unexpected event leads them to believe in a higher power and they declare their faith. Overwhelmed with gratitude, they prostrate themselves and pledge to give alms. The verse highlights the transformative power of gratitude and the sudden realization of the existence of a higher power that can bring about a change in people's hearts and actions.
orig: ولما فتحوا متاعهم وجدوا بضاعتهم ردت إليهم قالوا يا أبانا ما نبغي هذه بضاعتنا ردت إلينا ونمير أهلنا ونحفظ أخانا ونزداد كيل بعير ذلك كيل يسير

translation: He said, 'I will not send him with you until you give a solemn pledge to God. If you fail to keep your word, then may God's curse come upon you.' So when they had given their solemn pledge, God said, 'I am with you, as I promised you. And when We make a promise, We fulfill it.'
interpretation: This verse describes a conversation between an unnamed person and a group of people. The unnamed person demands that the group give a solemn pledge to God before he will send someone with them. If the group fails to keep their word, they will be subject to God's curse. After the group gives their pledge, God confirms that He will fulfill His promise to them. The verse emphasizes the importance of keeping one's word and the consequences of breaking a solemn pledge. It also highlights the trustworthiness of God and His commitment to fulfilling His promises.
orig: قال لن أرسله معكم حتى تؤتون موثقا من الله لتأتنني به إلا أن يحاط بكم فلما آتوه موثقهم قال الله على ما نقول وكيل

translation: He said, 'O my people, do not enter from one gate, but enter from different gates. And do not obey anyone except for those who have authority over you.' But I do not see anything that will benefit you from God. The decision is only for God. In Him, I have put my trust and to Him, I have turned penitent.'
interpretation: The verse recounts a statement made by a prophet or a righteous person, advising his people to enter a place through different gates, rather than gathering at one entrance. The advice could be interpreted as a way to avoid overcrowding and chaos, or as a symbolic act of dispersing and avoiding conformity. The second part of the verse emphasizes the importance of obedience to those in authority, but ultimately, the speaker places his trust and penitence in God alone. The verse highlights the individual's responsibility and accountability to God, and the importance of relying on God's guidance and decision, rather than relying on human authorities or conventions.
orig: وقال يا بني لا تدخلوا من باب واحد وادخلوا من أبواب متفرقة وما أغني عنكم من الله من شيء إن الحكم إلا لله عليه توكلت وعليه فليتوكل المتوكلون

translation: And when they entered from where their father commanded them, it did not avail them against God in the least, except for a cry [of mercy] from Abraham for them. And indeed, it was a decisive word. And We saved him and those with him within the limit of [Our] mercy. And We did not find for the majority of them any covenant.
interpretation: The verse speaks about a group of people who entered a place as their father had commanded them, but it did not benefit them against God's will. The verse emphasizes the powerlessness of humans in front of God's will, and the futility of their actions when they go against God's command. The verse also highlights the mercy of God, as Abraham pleaded for his people, and God saved him and those with him. However, the majority of them had no covenant with God, indicating that they were not among the believers and had not established a relationship with God. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of obeying God's command, the power of God's will, and the mercy of God towards those who believe and follow His path.
orig: ولما دخلوا من حيث أمرهم أبوهم ما كان يغني عنهم من الله من شيء إلا حاجة في نفس يعقوب قضاها وإنه لذو علم لما علمناه ولكن أكثر الناس لا يعلمون

translation: But when they entered upon Joseph, he welcomed his brother and said, 'Indeed, I am your brother, so do not be in despair over what they used to do.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the reunion of Joseph and his brother Benjamin, who were separated from each other for many years. Joseph, who was a high-ranking official in Egypt, welcomed his brother with open arms and assured him that he should not be distressed by the actions of their other brothers, who were responsible for separating them in the first place. The verse emphasizes the importance of forgiveness and the power of reconciliation, as well as the mercy and compassion that should be shown towards family members.
orig: ولما دخلوا على يوسف آوى إليه أخاه قال إني أنا أخوك فلا تبتئس بما كانوا يعملون

translation: When they had prepared their equipment, We sent against them a host that you could not see, and We cast terror into their hearts. They destroyed their houses by their own hands and the hands of the believers. So take a lesson, O people of vision.
interpretation: The verse describes a situation where a group of people had prepared their equipment and were then attacked by an unseen force sent by God. This unseen force caused fear and terror in their hearts, leading them to destroy their own homes and those of the believers. The verse serves as a lesson and a warning to the people of vision, urging them to reflect on the consequences of their actions and the power of God's retribution.
orig: فلما جهزهم بجهازهم جعل السقاية في رحل أخيه ثم أذن مؤذن أيتها العير إنكم لسارقون

translation: They said, 'And what is wrong with you? Why do you come to us in two groups?'
interpretation: The verse is a response from a group of people who are being addressed by two other groups. They are confused and ask why they are coming to them in this manner.
