The verse highlights the confusion and tension between the groups, and sets the stage for further dialogue or conflict. It may also imply a sense of division or fragmentation among the people being addressed. The verse can be interpreted as a call for understanding and unity, reminding the groups to work together and avoid unnecessary conflict.
orig: قالوا وأقبلوا عليهم ماذا تفقدون

translation: They said, 'We have lost the king's camel, and whoever brings it back will receive a load of a hundred (camels), and we are indeed truthful.',
interpretation: The verse describes a group of people who have lost the king's camel and are offering a reward to the person who brings it back. The reward is significant, one hundred camels, indicating the importance of the lost camel. The group's statement of being truthful reinforces their commitment to fulfilling their promise. This verse can be interpreted as a reminder of the importance of keeping one's word and fulfilling promises, especially when it comes to fulfilling obligations towards those in positions of authority.
orig: قالوا نفقد صواع الملك ولمن جاء به حمل بعير وأنا به زعيم

translation: They said, 'By Allah, we were indeed in manifest error when we regarded you as equals [in authority] with the Lord of the worlds.'
interpretation: The verse is a statement made by a group of people, recognizing their mistake in treating someone as equal to the Lord of the worlds. The phrase 'By Allah' is an oath, emphasizing the importance and truthfulness of their statement. The verse highlights the gravity of associating other beings or entities with the one true God and the acknowledgement of the error in doing so. It serves as a reminder of the uniqueness and oneness of God, and the importance of worshipping and submitting to Him alone.
orig: قالوا تالله لقد علمتم ما جئنا لنفسد في الأرض وما كنا سارقين

translation: They said, 'What is his punishment then, if you are truthful?'
interpretation: The verse is spoken by the disbelievers in response to the believers' message about the punishment of God for those who reject the truth. The disbelievers are questioning the validity of the punishment and challenging the believers to prove it. The verse highlights the disbelievers' rejection and denial of the truth, and their unwillingness to accept the consequences of their actions. It also serves as a reminder of the importance of faith and the belief in the unseen for the believers.
orig: قالوا فما جزاؤه إن كنتم كاذبين

translation: They say, 'His punishment is only for him who finds him in travel.' So, indeed, We will punish the unjust.
interpretation: The verse describes the disbelievers' claim that the punishment for finding someone (presumably a prophet) during travel should be borne solely by that person. However, the verse emphasizes that the punishment for the unjust will indeed be meted out. The verse serves as a reminder that the consequences of unbelief and injustice will ultimately be faced, regardless of any attempts to shift responsibility or blame onto others.
orig: قالوا جزاؤه من وجد في رحله فهو جزاؤه كذلك نجزي الظالمين

translation: But We gave preference to Joseph and his brother [in prophethood] above their people, according to Our mercy, and We made them leaders guiding by Our command. And We inspired to Moses and his brother, 'Stay in your people and reform them and bring forth My promise to them.' And We supported him with his brother and with signs from Us and a clear authority.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the special favor and preference shown by God to Joseph and his brother among their people. The verse highlights the role of these prophets as leaders and reformers of their people, and their obedience to God's command. The verse emphasizes the guidance provided by these prophets and the miracles and clear authority given to them by God. The verse serves as a reminder of the role of prophethood in guiding people towards the right path and fulfilling God's promise to them.
orig: فبدأ بأوعيتهم قبل وعاء أخيه ثم استخرجها من وعاء أخيه كذلك كدنا ليوسف ما كان ليأخذ أخاه في دين الملك إلا أن يشاء الله نرفع درجات من نشاء وفوق كل ذي علم عليم

translation: They said, 'If he (Joseph) steals, he has stolen before.' But Joseph kept it within himself and did not reveal it to them. He (Joseph) said, 'You are worse in conduct than he is, and indeed, your claim is based on nothing but mere suspicion.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the brothers of Joseph accusing him of stealing, while Joseph had actually kept their actions hidden and did not reveal them. Joseph denied their accusations and pointed out their own shortcomings, stating that their claim was based on nothing but mere suspicion. The verse highlights the importance of fairness and the dangers of making false accusations, as well as the virtue of keeping one's own sins hidden and not spreading them.
orig: قالوا إن يسرق فقد سرق أخ له من قبل فأسرها يوسف في نفسه ولم يبدها لهم قال أنتم شر مكانا والله أعلم بما تصفون

translation: They said, 'O mighty one! Indeed, he has a venerable father, so take one of us in his place. Indeed, we see you among the doers of good.'
interpretation: The verse describes a group of people addressing a mighty figure, offering to take the place of an elderly man they mention, due to the man's close relationship with the addressee. The people acknowledge the addressee's goodness and express their positive perception of him. The verse highlights the dynamics of social relationships, the importance of kinship, and the significance of the perceptions of others in such interactions.
orig: قالوا يا أيها العزيز إن له أبا شيخا كبيرا فخذ أحدنا مكانه إنا نراك من المحسنين

translation: Muaadh said: 'If we take anything except from where we have found our provision, then indeed, we would be unjust.'
interpretation: The verse is a statement by Muaadh, emphasizing the importance of taking only what is rightfully one's own and not taking anything without permission. The verse highlights the unjust nature of taking something without permission and the consequences of such actions. The verse serves as a reminder to act ethically and justly, avoiding any form of theft or taking advantage of others.
orig: قال معاذ الله أن نأخذ إلا من وجدنا متاعنا عنده إنا إذا لظالمون

translation: And when they despaired of him and had lost all hope that he would ever be returned to them, they said, 'Two of our men used to be sure securities for us regarding Joseph; his brother used to be very dutiful towards him.' Surely, Joseph's father had taken a solemn pledge from them. Indeed, you yourselves were unjust to Joseph before.' No doubt, I will never leave this land until my father permits me or Allah decides my case, and He is the best of all the judges.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the story of Joseph and his brothers, and how they despaired of ever finding him after they had sold him into slavery. The verse highlights the fact that Joseph's father had taken a solemn pledge from his brothers regarding the safety of Joseph, but they had failed to keep their promise. The verse emphasizes the importance of keeping one's word and the consequences of breaking it. The verse also highlights Joseph's unwavering commitment to doing what is right and just, and his determination to stay in Egypt until his father permits him to return or until God decides his case. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of upholding one's promises and the rewards of being patient and steadfast in the face of adversity.
orig: فلما استيأسوا منه خلصوا نجيا قال كبيرهم ألم تعلموا أن أباكم قد أخذ عليكم موثقا من الله ومن قبل ما فرطتم في يوسف فلن أبرح الأرض حتى يأذن لي أبي أو يحكم الله لي وهو خير الحاكمين

translation: Return to your father and say, 'O our father, indeed we have become aware that your son has taken property of ours, and we did not bear witness except to what we know. And we were not witnesses to the unseen.'
interpretation: The verse relays the words of the brothers of Yusuf (Joseph) as they speak to their father, Ya'qub (Jacob), after they had found their missing property in Yusuf's possession. They tell their father that they only testify to what they know and were not witnesses to the unseen. The verse emphasizes the importance of truthfulness and the limits of human knowledge. It also highlights the brothers' attempt to clear their conscience and avoid blame by being truthful about what they know and what they do not.
orig: ارجعوا إلى أبيكم فقولوا يا أبانا إن ابنك سرق وما شهدنا إلا بما علمنا وما كنا للغيب حافظين

translation: And ask the town where we were and the caravan with which we came (it will reply): 'We are indeed wicked, so forgive us, we have truly been astray.'
interpretation: In this verse, the speaker is asking the people of a town and a caravan to bear witness to the sins and transgressions of the speaker. The people of the town and the caravan are asked to testify to the speaker's wickedness and their own straying from the right path. The verse suggests that the speaker has realized the error of their ways and is seeking forgiveness. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of seeking forgiveness and acknowledging one's mistakes, as well as the role of the community in holding each other accountable for their actions.
orig: واسأل القرية التي كنا فيها والعير التي أقبلنا فيها وإنا لصادقون

translation: He (Moses) said, 'Then patience is most fitting for me. And it is Allah (Alone) Whose help can be sought against that which you describe.' So let them amuse themselves and soon will they know! Indeed, I have put my trust in Allah, my Lord and your Lord. There is no creature but He holds its forelock. Indeed, my Lord is on a Straight Path.
interpretation: In this verse, Moses responds with patience and trust in God when faced with a challenging situation. He recognizes that only God has the power to help and that seeking His help is the best course of action. He advises the people to amuse themselves, indicating that their actions will not change the outcome. Moses places his trust in God, acknowledging that God has power and control over all things. The verse emphasizes the importance of patience and trust in God during difficult times and the ultimate power and control that God has over all of His creations.
orig: قال بل سولت لكم أنفسكم أمرا فصبر جميل عسى الله أن يأتيني بهم جميعا إنه هو العليم الحكيم

translation: But he turned away from them and said, 'Oh, I am feeling sorry for Joseph!' And his eyes became white from grief, and he was filled with anguish.
interpretation: The verse describes the moment when Jacob learns of the plot by his other sons to get rid of Joseph. Despite their attempts to conceal the truth, Jacob immediately senses that something is wrong and is overwhelmed with grief and anguish. The verse highlights Jacob's deep love and concern for Joseph, and his strong emotional reaction serves to emphasize the gravity of the situation. The verse also underscores the theme of divine justice, as Joseph's brothers will eventually come to regret their actions and seek their father's forgiveness.
orig: وتولى عنهم وقال يا أسفى على يوسف وابيضت عيناه من الحزن فهو كظيم

translation: They said, 'Swear by Allah that you will not mention Yusuf (Joseph) unless you are reminded or become of the distracted.'
interpretation: The verse describes the brothers of Yusuf (Joseph) asking their father to swear that he will not mention Yusuf to them, unless he is reminded of him or becomes distracted. This is because the brothers were filled with jealousy and resentment towards Yusuf, and they wanted to forget him. The verse highlights the depth of their hatred and the lengths they were willing to go to in order to distance themselves from him. It also serves to emphasize the contrast between the righteousness of Yusuf and the wickedness of his brothers.
orig: قالوا تالله تفتأ تذكر يوسف حتى تكون حرضا أو تكون من الهالكين

translation: He said, 'I complain only of my distress and my grief to Allah, and I know from Allah that which you do not know.'
interpretation: The verse is spoken by the prophet Yunus (Jonah) in the Qur'an, after he was sent to the city of Nineveh to warn the people of God's punishment. In this verse, Yunus is expressing his frustration and distress with the people's rejection of his message. He complains only to God, as he knows that only God can truly understand his situation and provide him with the help he needs. The verse highlights the importance of relying on God and seeking His guidance and support in times of hardship and difficulty.
orig: قال إنما أشكو بثي وحزني إلى الله وأعلم من الله ما لا تعلمون

translation: O my people, go and ask forgiveness of Joseph and his brother, and do not despair of the mercy of Allah. Indeed, none despairs of the mercy of Allah except the disbelieving people.
interpretation: The verse addresses the people of the prophet Jacob, advising them to seek forgiveness from Joseph and his brother. It emphasizes the importance of not losing hope in the mercy of God and warns against despair, which is associated with disbelief. The verse encourages the people to reconcile and seek forgiveness, highlighting the boundless nature of God's mercy and the negative consequences of disbelief and despair.
orig: يا بني اذهبوا فتحسسوا من يوسف وأخيه ولا تيأسوا من روح الله إنه لا ييأس من روح الله إلا القوم الكافرون

translation: But when they entered upon him, they said, 'O Shu'ayb, indeed we were few who were unjust, so the majority among us led us astray. So now we have brought the small amount that they demanded, so give us full measure and be charitable to us. Indeed, Allah rewards the charitable.',
interpretation: The verse describes the people of Shu'ayb (a prophet in Islamic tradition) admitting their past wrongdoings and seeking forgiveness. They acknowledge their past unjust actions, attributing it to being led astray by the majority. They come to Shu'ayb with the small amount demanded of them, asking him to fulfill their request and be charitable towards them. The verse highlights the importance of forgiveness and charity, emphasizing that Allah rewards those who are charitable. It serves as a reminder of the significance of seeking forgiveness and striving towards righteousness.
orig: فلما دخلوا عليه قالوا يا أيها العزيز مسنا وأهلنا الضر وجئنا ببضاعة مزجاة فأوف لنا الكيل وتصدق علينا إن الله يجزي المتصدقين

translation: He said, 'Have you any knowledge of what you did to Joseph and his brother when you were ignorant?'
interpretation: The verse is a rebuke from someone (perhaps a prophet or a messenger) to a group of people, reminding them of their past actions towards Joseph and his brother. The people being addressed are described as 'ignorant' at the time of their actions, suggesting that they were unaware of the consequences of their behavior or the true significance of Joseph and his brother. The verse emphasizes the importance of treating others with justice and compassion, and the consequences of ignoring these moral principles.
orig: قال هل علمتم ما فعلتم بيوسف وأخيه إذ أنتم جاهلون

translation: They said, 'Are you indeed Yusuf (Joseph)?' He said, 'I am Yusuf, and this is my brother. Indeed, Allah has favored us. Indeed, whoever fears Allah and is patient, then indeed, Allah does not allow the reward of the doers of good to be lost.'
interpretation: The verse is a conversation between Yusuf (Joseph) and his brothers who did not recognize him after many years. Yusuf confirms his identity and introduces his brother. The verse highlights the role of God's favor in their lives and emphasizes the importance of fearing God, being patient, and doing good. The last sentence serves as a general principle that those who fear God and are patient in the face of adversity will not be left without their due reward. The verse encourages believers to be patient and persevere, reminding them that God will not let their good deeds go to waste.
orig: قالوا أإنك لأنت يوسف قال أنا يوسف وهذا أخي قد من الله علينا إنه من يتق ويصبر فإن الله لا يضيع أجر المحسنين

translation: They said, 'By Allah, Allah has surely distinguished you for us. Indeed, we were wrongdoers.'
interpretation: The verse describes the words of a group of people who have come to recognize the distinction or favor that God has bestowed upon an individual or group of individuals. The people acknowledge their own wrongdoing or sinfulness and recognize that the one who has received God's favor is deserving of it. The verse may be interpreted as a reminder of the importance of recognizing and acknowledging God's blessings, as well as a call to repentance for those who have strayed from the path of righteousness.
orig: قالوا تالله لقد آثرك الله علينا وإن كنا لخاطئين

translation: He (Jesus) said, 'Do not be afraid. Today, God will forgive you. He is the most merciful of the merciful.'
interpretation: In this verse, Jesus is speaking to a group of people, assuring them that they should not be afraid because God will forgive them. The verse emphasizes God's forgiveness and mercy, highlighting that He is the most merciful of all. This verse serves as a message of hope and comfort, reminding the listeners that God is always ready to forgive and show mercy to those who turn to Him, regardless of their past actions.
orig: قال لا تثريب عليكم اليوم يغفر الله لكم وهو أرحم الراحمين

translation: Take away this shirt of mine and cast it upon the face of my father; he will become seeing. And bring to me all of your people.
interpretation: In this verse, a prophet is speaking and instructing his followers to perform a specific action. He asks them to take his shirt and place it on the face of his father. This action will restore the father's sight, allowing him to see again. After this, the prophet requests that all of the people be brought to him. The verse highlights the power of the prophet and his ability to perform miracles, as well as his desire to unite and gather his community. The verse may also contain a message about the importance of family and the restoration of broken relationships.
orig: اذهبوا بقميصي هذا فألقوه على وجه أبي يأت بصيرا وأتوني بأهلكم أجمعين

translation: And when the caravan had left, their father said, 'Indeed, I find the smell of Joseph. Were it not that you considered me weak-minded.'
interpretation: The verse describes the moment when Jacob's caravan had left, and he was left alone. Jacob, the father of Joseph, noticed the smell of his son Joseph and made a comment that he is not weak-minded, implying that he is not hallucinating or imagining things. This verse highlights Jacob's deep love and longing for his son Joseph, who was lost and believed to be dead. Despite the passage of time, Jacob's faith in God and his hope of reuniting with his son remained strong. This verse serves as a reminder of the strong bond between family members and the importance of hope and faith in the face of adversity.
orig: ولما فصلت العير قال أبوهم إني لأجد ريح يوسف لولا أن تفندون

translation: They said, 'By Allah, indeed you are in clear error.',
interpretation: The verse shows the disbelievers accusing the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) of being in clear error and deviating from the right path. This accusation was a common tactic used by the disbelievers to discredit the Prophet and turn people away from his message. However, the verse serves to highlight the steadfastness and certainty of the Prophet in the face of such accusations and his unwavering belief in the truth of his message.
orig: قالوا تالله إنك لفي ضلالك القديم

translation: But when the Warner came to them, they denied him, so a seal was set upon their hearts. And they are deaf, and blind. So they will not return (to the right path).
interpretation: The verse speaks about the rejection of a Warner (prophet) by a people, which led to a seal being placed on their hearts, making them unable to understand or accept the truth. The verse emphasizes the consequences of their denial, describing them as being deaf and blind, implying that they are unable to see or hear the truth. The verse emphasizes that these people will not be able to return to the right path, indicating the finality of their rejection and the consequences that follow.
orig: فلما أن جاء البشير ألقاه على وجهه فارتد بصيرا قال ألم أقل لكم إني أعلم من الله ما لا تعلمون

translation: They said, 'O our father, ask forgiveness for our sins, indeed we have been sinners.'
interpretation: The verse shows the children of Prophet Adam (peace be upon him) seeking forgiveness for their sins from their father, Prophet Adam. They acknowledge their wrongdoing and express remorse for their actions. This verse highlights the importance of seeking forgiveness and expressing remorse for one's sins. It also emphasizes the role of family and the importance of seeking guidance and support from one's loved ones in times of hardship and error. The verse serves as a reminder of the human tendency towards sin and the need for continuous repentance and seeking of God's forgiveness.
orig: قالوا يا أبانا استغفر لنا ذنوبنا إنا كنا خاطئين

translation: He (the Prophet Muhammad) said, 'I will seek forgiveness from my Lord for you, indeed He is the Forgiving, the Merciful.'
interpretation: In this verse, the Prophet Muhammad is expressing his compassion and concern for his people by promising to seek forgiveness from God on their behalf. He emphasizes God's attributes of forgiveness and mercy, highlighting the boundless nature of God's forgiveness. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of seeking forgiveness and the infinite mercy of God towards his creations.
orig: قال سوف أستغفر لكم ربي إنه هو الغفور الرحيم

translation: But when they entered upon Joseph, his parents entered with him, and he said, 'Enter Egypt, [all of] you, if Allah wills, secure.',
interpretation: The verse recounts the story of Joseph and his parents entering Egypt. Upon meeting Joseph, he welcomed them and expressed his hope that they would enter Egypt safely and securely, if it was Allah's will. The verse highlights Joseph's respect and obedience towards Allah, as well as his compassion and kindness towards his parents. It serves as a model for believers in terms of their attitude towards their family and their faith in Allah's will.
orig: فلما دخلوا على يوسف آوى إليه أبويه وقال ادخلوا مصر إن شاء الله آمنين

translation: And He (God) raised his parents upon the throne and they both fell down in prostration to Him and said, 'O our Lord! This is the interpretation of my dream in the past which my Lord has made true, and He has indeed been kind to me, when He brought me out of the prison and brought you both from the desert after Satan had sown enmity between me and my brothers. Indeed, my Lord is Subtle in what He wills. Indeed, it is He who is the Knowing, the Wise.'
interpretation: The verse describes the fulfillment of a dream of Prophet Joseph (Yusuf) where his parents prostrate to him. This event takes place after Prophet Joseph (Yusuf) has forgiven his brothers and his parents have recognized his true identity. The verse highlights the power of God in fulfilling His promises, and the wisdom in His actions. The prostration of Prophet Joseph's (Yusuf) parents serves as a symbol of their submission to the will of God and their recognition of Prophet Joseph's (Yusuf) status as a prophet. The verse also emphasizes the role of Satan in sowing discord and enmity, but ultimately, it is God who has the power to bring about reconciliation and unity.
orig: ورفع أبويه على العرش وخروا له سجدا وقال يا أبت هذا تأويل رؤياي من قبل قد جعلها ربي حقا وقد أحسن بي إذ أخرجني من السجن وجاء بكم من البدو من بعد أن نزغ الشيطان بيني وبين إخوتي إن ربي لطيف لما يشاء إنه هو العليم الحكيم

translation: My Lord, You have given me authority and taught me interpretation of sayings. Creator of the heavens and the earth, You are my protector in this world and the hereafter. Cause me to die a Muslim and join me with the righteous.
interpretation: The verse is a prayer by the Prophet Muhammad, expressing gratitude for the blessings that God has bestowed upon him, including knowledge and authority. The Prophet acknowledges God as his protector and sustainer in both this world and the next. He prays for a peaceful death as a Muslim and to be reunited with the righteous in the afterlife. The verse highlights the importance of seeking God's guidance and protection, and expressing gratitude for His blessings, while also emphasizing the ultimate goal of a righteous life and a peaceful death.
orig: رب قد آتيتني من الملك وعلمتني من تأويل الأحاديث فاطر السماوات والأرض أنت وليي في الدنيا والآخرة توفني مسلما وألحقني بالصالحين

translation: That is from the news of the unseen which We reveal to you (O Muhammad). And you were not with them when they decided upon their affair, and they were plotting.
interpretation: The verse reveals that the information being conveyed to the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) is from the unseen, emphasizing its divine origin. The verse also highlights that the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) was not present when the disbelievers plotted against him, indicating that their decision was not based on any wrongdoing on his part. The verse serves as a reminder that the revelations received by the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) are from a higher power and that the disbelievers' rejection of his message is unjustified.
orig: ذلك من أنباء الغيب نوحيه إليك وما كنت لديهم إذ أجمعوا أمرهم وهم يمكرون

translation: And never have I been unjust to the servants (of Allah).
interpretation: The verse is spoken from the perspective of Prophet Muhammad, who is emphasizing his fairness and justice towards all people, regardless of their faith or background. The verse can be interpreted as a response to accusations of favoritism or bias towards certain individuals or groups, and serves as a reminder of the Prophet's commitment to equality and justice for all. The verse can also be seen as a reflection of the broader Islamic values of fairness, justice, and equality for all people, regardless of their religious beliefs or social status.
orig: وما أكثر الناس ولو حرصت بمؤمنين

translation: And you do not ask them for any wage; it is only a reminder for all beings.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) and his role in delivering the message of Islam. It emphasizes that the Prophet does not ask for any wage or compensation for his efforts, and that his only intention is to remind people of their purpose and responsibilities. The verse is a reminder for all beings that the message of Islam is a mercy and a guidance for those who seek it, and it is a call for all people to reflect on the meaning of life and the importance of worshipping God. The verse also highlights the selflessness and generosity of the Prophet, who dedicates his life to the service of God and humanity without expecting anything in return.
orig: وما تسألهم عليه من أجر إن هو إلا ذكر للعالمين

translation: And how many a sign is there in the heavens and the earth, which they pass by, while they are turned away from them.
interpretation: The verse highlights the many signs of God's existence and power in the heavens and the earth, which people often overlook or ignore. The phrase 'while they are turned away from them' suggests that people are preoccupied with their own concerns and are not receptive to these signs. The verse serves as a reminder to be mindful of the wonders of nature and the universe, which are constant reminders of God's greatness and power. It encourages people to reflect on these signs and to use them as a means of drawing closer to God, rather than ignoring or dismissing them.
orig: وكأين من آية في السماوات والأرض يمرون عليها وهم عنها معرضون

translation: And most of them do not believe in God except while they associate others with Him.
interpretation: The verse highlights the hypocrisy of those who claim to believe in God, but in reality, they associate others with Him, committing the sin of shirk. This verse serves as a reminder that true faith cannot coexist with shirk, and that belief in God must be pure and free from any form of association or idolatry.
orig: وما يؤمن أكثرهم بالله إلا وهم مشركون

translation: Or have they not considered that We made the night for them to rest in and the day to give them light? Indeed, in that are signs for a people who believe.
interpretation: The verse highlights the natural phenomena of day and night as evidence of God's existence and power. The night and day are presented as clear signs for those who believe, emphasizing the importance of reflection and contemplation in understanding God's creation. The verse encourages believers to recognize and appreciate the blessings they receive from God, including the ability to rest during the night and to be active during the day.
orig: أفأمنوا أن تأتيهم غاشية من عذاب الله أو تأتيهم الساعة بغتة وهم لا يشعرون

translation: Say, 'This is my way; I invite to Allah with insight, I and those who follow me. And exalted is Allah; and I am not of those who associate others with Him.'
interpretation: The verse is a message from the Prophet Muhammad, who is instructed to declare his way of inviting people to worship and follow the one true God, Allah. He makes clear that his way is based on insight and understanding, and those who follow him do so as well. The verse also emphasizes the distinction between the monotheistic believers and the polytheists, as the Prophet declares that he is not among those who associate partners with Allah.
orig: قل هذه سبيلي أدعو إلى الله على بصيرة أنا ومن اتبعني وسبحان الله وما أنا من المشركين

translation: And We sent not before you (O Muhammad) but men to whom We inspired, so ask the people of the reminder if you do not know. And (of) the town, there was not a town but We destroyed it before them, so shall they not believe? And when Abraham said, 'My Lord, show me how You give life to the dead.' (Allah) said, 'Have you not believed?' He said, 'Yes, but [I ask] that my heart may be satisfied.' (Allah) said, 'Take four birds and commit them to yourself. Then after slaughtering them, put on each hill a portion of them; then call them - they will come [flying] to you in haste. And know that Allah is Exalted in Might and Wise.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the prophets who were sent before Prophet Muhammad, and how they were inspired by God to guide their people. The verse encourages the questioning and seeking of knowledge from the people of the reminder or scholars. The verse also speaks about the destruction of towns that came before, emphasizing the disbelief of the people despite the evidence of God's power. The latter part of the verse describes a test of faith for Prophet Abraham, where he is asked to slaughter four birds and then call them, and they will come back to life. This test serves as a demonstration of God's power over life and death, and a means of satisfying the curiosity and faith of Prophet Abraham.
orig: وما أرسلنا من قبلك إلا رجالا نوحي إليهم من أهل القرى أفلم يسيروا في الأرض فينظروا كيف كان عاقبة الذين من قبلهم ولدار الآخرة خير للذين اتقوا أفلا تعقلون

translation: Until, when the messengers despaired and were certain that they had been lied to, our help came to them. And we saved whom we willed, and our punishment cannot be turned back from the criminal people.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the help that comes from God to the messengers when they are in a state of despair and feel that they have been lied to. The verse emphasizes that God saves whom He wills and that His punishment cannot be turned back from the criminal people. The verse serves as a reminder of the power and mercy of God and the importance of having faith in the face of adversity.
orig: حتى إذا استيأس الرسل وظنوا أنهم قد كذبوا جاءهم نصرنا فنجي من نشاء ولا يرد بأسنا عن القوم المجرمين

translation: Indeed, in their stories, there is a lesson for those of understanding. It (the Quran) is not a fabricated tale, but a confirmation of what was before it, and a detailed explanation of all things, and a guide and a mercy to a people who believe.
interpretation: The verse highlights the importance of learning from the stories of the past and the relevance of the Quran in providing guidance and wisdom. The verse emphasizes that the Quran is not a made-up story, but a confirmation of previous revelations and a detailed explanation of all things. The verse also mentions that the Quran serves as a guide and a mercy for those who believe, implying that those who reject the message of the Quran are denying themselves the guidance and mercy of God.
orig: لقد كان في قصصهم عبرة لأولي الألباب ما كان حديثا يفترى ولكن تصديق الذي بين يديه وتفصيل كل شيء وهدى ورحمة لقوم يؤمنون

translation: Do they not then reflect on the Qur'an? And if it were from other than Allah, they would have found in it many contradictions.
interpretation: The verse challenges people to reflect on the Qur'an and its message. It highlights the consistency and truth of the Qur'an, stating that if it were not from God, people would have found many contradictions in it. The verse emphasizes the importance of reflecting on the Qur'an and recognizing its divine origin. It serves as a reminder that the Qur'an is a source of guidance and wisdom for those who seek the truth.
orig: المر تلك آيات الكتاب والذي أنزل إليك من ربك الحق ولكن أكثر الناس لا يؤمنون

translation: It is Allah who raised the heavens without any pillars that you can see, then He established Himself on the throne. And He subjected the sun and the moon, each of them runs for an appointed term. He regulates the affair, explaining the signs that you may be certain of meeting your Lord.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the greatness and power of Allah, who has raised the heavens without any support that can be seen, and then established Himself on the throne. The verse emphasizes the subjugation of the sun and the moon, which run for a specific term, and the regulation of affairs by Allah. The verse also highlights the signs that Allah has explained for the people, so that they may be certain of meeting their Lord. The verse serves as a reminder of Allah's power and greatness, and the certainty of the Day of Judgment, urging people to reflect and take heed.
orig: الله الذي رفع السماوات بغير عمد ترونها ثم استوى على العرش وسخر الشمس والقمر كل يجري لأجل مسمى يدبر الأمر يفصل الآيات لعلكم بلقاء ربكم توقنون

translation: And it is He who spread out the earth and placed therein firmly set mountains and rivers; and of all fruits He placed therein two spouses (male and female); He causes the night to cover the day. Indeed in that are signs for a people who reflect.
interpretation: The verse highlights the power and greatness of God, who has created and designed the earth with all its features. It speaks of the mountains, rivers, and the pairing of fruits as evidence of God's design and careful planning. The verse also mentions the cycle of day and night, which serves as a reminder of the natural order of things. The verse calls on people to reflect on these signs and to consider the power and wisdom of God. It encourages people to think deeply and seriously about the world around them and to recognize the role of God in creating and maintaining it.
orig: وهو الذي مد الأرض وجعل فيها رواسي وأنهارا ومن كل الثمرات جعل فيها زوجين اثنين يغشي الليل النهار إن في ذلك لآيات لقوم يتفكرون

translation: And in the earth are tracts side by side and gardens of grapes and corn and palm trees, (growing) two and two, (alternate) between the two, watered (evenly) with one water: but We make some of them better than others to eat. Verily in this are signs for those who understand.
interpretation: The verse describes the diversity and abundance of resources that God has provided in the earth, including different types of land, crops, and fruits. The verse emphasizes the balance and harmony in the creation, as everything is watered with one water and some things are made better than others for consumption. The verse serves as a reminder of the signs of God's power and wisdom in the creation for those who reflect and understand.
orig: وفي الأرض قطع متجاورات وجنات من أعناب وزرع ونخيل صنوان وغير صنوان يسقى بماء واحد ونفضل بعضها على بعض في الأكل إن في ذلك لآيات لقوم يعقلون

translation: And if you are amazed, then amazing is their saying, 'When will we be a creation renewed?' Are we not in a creation new?' So those who disbelieved in their Lord - for them is the punishment of eternity, and they are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein eternally.
interpretation: The verse addresses those who are amazed at the idea of resurrection and the creation of a new world. It challenges them by asking whether they are not already living in a new creation. The verse then goes on to describe the fate of those who disbelieve in their Lord - they will receive the punishment of eternity and be companions of the Fire, residing therein forever. The verse serves as a reminder of the reality of resurrection and the consequences of disbelief.
orig: وإن تعجب فعجب قولهم أإذا كنا ترابا أإنا لفي خلق جديد أولئك الذين كفروا بربهم وأولئك الأغلال في أعناقهم وأولئك أصحاب النار هم فيها خالدون

translation: And they urge you to hasten the evil before the good, and indeed, preceding them were examples (of their punishment). And indeed, your Lord is full of forgiveness for the people despite their injustice, and indeed, your Lord is severe in punishment.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the people who urge for evil things to happen before good things, showing their impatience and lack of appreciation for the good. The verse reminds us that previous nations have faced punishment for their actions, serving as a warning for those who are unjust. Despite this, God is forgiving and gives people chances to repent, but also warns that the punishment for those who persist in their injustice will be severe.
orig: ويستعجلونك بالسيئة قبل الحسنة وقد خلت من قبلهم المثلات وإن ربك لذو مغفرة للناس على ظلمهم وإن ربك لشديد العقاب

translation: And those who disbelieve say, 'Why was not a sign sent down to him from his Lord?' You are only a warner, and for every people there is a guide.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the disbelievers who question why a sign has not been sent down to the prophet from his Lord. The verse responds by stating that the prophet is only a warner, and that every people has a guide. The verse emphasizes the role of the prophet as a warner, and the fact that the guidance of each people is specific to them. The verse also suggests that the disbelievers' request for a sign is a form of denial and rejection of the message being conveyed by the prophet, and that ultimately, it is up to each individual and community to accept or reject the guidance that has been provided to them.
orig: ويقول الذين كفروا لولا أنزل عليه آية من ربه إنما أنت منذر ولكل قوم هاد

translation: Allah knows what every female bears and what the wombs absorb and what they grow. And everything with Him is by measure.
interpretation: The verse highlights the all-knowing nature of Allah, emphasizing that He is aware of every detail of creation, even the most minute. The verse mentions the growth of a fetus in the womb as an example of the intricate details that are known to Allah. The phrase 'what the wombs absorb' may refer to the process of nourishment and development that occurs during pregnancy. The verse also emphasizes the precise and measured way in which Allah manages all things, indicating that nothing happens by chance or coincidence. The verse serves as a reminder of the greatness and power of Allah, and encourages believers to trust in His divine plan and wisdom.
orig: الله يعلم ما تحمل كل أنثى وما تغيض الأرحام وما تزداد وكل شيء عنده بمقدار

translation: Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, the Most Great, the High.
interpretation: The verse describes God as the one who has knowledge of both the unseen (ghayb) and the witnessed (shahada) realms. This includes all that is hidden from human perception and understanding. The verse further emphasizes God's greatness and exaltedness, using the superlative form 'the Most Great' (al-kabir) and 'the High' (al-'ali). This verse serves to remind people of God's all-encompassing knowledge and power, encouraging them to submit to and worship Him.
orig: عالم الغيب والشهادة الكبير المتعال

translation: It is the same for you whether you speak secretly or not speak, or are hidden by night or go out in the day.
interpretation: The verse highlights the all-knowing and all-seeing nature of God, emphasizing that it makes no difference whether a person speaks secretly or openly, or hides in the darkness of night or moves about in the light of day. God is aware of all actions and intentions, and nothing can be hidden from Him. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of leading a righteous life and avoiding sin, as one's actions will ultimately be judged by God.
orig: سواء منكم من أسر القول ومن جهر به ومن هو مستخف بالليل وسارب بالنهار

translation: For him are angels behind him and in front of him, who guard him by the command of God. Indeed, God does not change the condition of a people until they change what is in themselves. And when God wishes to afflict a people, there is no turning back for them, and there is not for them besides Him any protector.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the protection and care of God for the believers. It emphasizes the presence of angels that guard the believers by the command of God, both in front of them and behind them. The verse also explains that God does not change the condition of a people until they change what is in themselves, indicating that people have the power to change their destiny through their own actions. The verse concludes by mentioning that when God wishes to afflict a people, there is no turning back for them, and there is not for them besides Him any protector, emphasizing the power and authority of God and the futility of seeking protection from anyone else.
orig: له معقبات من بين يديه ومن خلفه يحفظونه من أمر الله إن الله لا يغير ما بقوم حتى يغيروا ما بأنفسهم وإذا أراد الله بقوم سوءا فلا مرد له وما لهم من دونه من وال

translation: It is He who shows you the lightning, [causing] fear and hope, and He creates the clouds.
interpretation: The verse highlights God's power and control over the natural world. The lightning is described as both inspiring fear and hope, reflecting the dual nature of human emotions in response to the unknown. The clouds are created by God as a further example of His ability to control and shape the natural world. The verse serves as a reminder of God's power and greatness, and encourages people to reflect on the wonders of the natural world and the role of the divine in shaping it.
orig: هو الذي يريكم البرق خوفا وطمعا وينشئ السحاب الثقال

translation: And the thunder glorifies Him with His praise, and the angels too, out of fear of Him; and He sends thunderbolts, so that with them He strikes whom He wills, yet they argue about Allah, while He is strong in might.
interpretation: The verse describes the natural phenomenon of thunder as a form of glorification of God, along with the angels who glorify Him out of fear. The verse emphasizes God's power and might through the sending of thunderbolts, which strike whom He wills. The verse highlights the arrogance and ignorance of those who argue about God, despite the clear signs of His power and majesty that are present in the world around them. The verse serves as a reminder of God's power and greatness, and a warning against arrogance and ignorance in the face of His signs.
orig: ويسبح الرعد بحمده والملائكة من خيفته ويرسل الصواعق فيصيب بها من يشاء وهم يجادلون في الله وهو شديد المحال

translation: To Him is the call of truth, and those they call upon besides Him respond to them not at all, except as one who stretches his hand toward water [wanting] to reach it, but it does not come to him. And the disbelievers - their deeds are like a mirage in a lowland. Which a thirsty one thinks is water, until he comes to it and finds it nothing. But he finds Allah with him, and Allah will pay him his due; and Allah is swift in account.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the futility of worshipping other than God, as those who are called upon do not respond. The metaphor of a person stretching his hand towards water, but it not coming to him, illustrates the futility of such worship. The verse also compares the actions of the disbelievers to a mirage, which appears to be water but is not, emphasizing the deceptive nature of their actions. The verse serves as a reminder of the ultimate reality, which is the oneness of God and the insignificance of all other things in comparison to Him. It also reminds that God will hold everyone accountable for their actions and will give them their due rewards or punishments.
orig: له دعوة الحق والذين يدعون من دونه لا يستجيبون لهم بشيء إلا كباسط كفيه إلى الماء ليبلغ فاه وما هو ببالغه وما دعاء الكافرين إلا في ضلال

translation: And unto God prostrate all that is in the heavens and the earth, willingly or unwillingly. Their shade is close upon them in the morning and in the afternoon.
interpretation: The verse highlights the sovereignty and power of God, as all that is in the heavens and the earth prostrate before Him, either willingly or unwillingly. The verse emphasizes the all-encompassing nature of God's control and authority, as even the shadows that provide shade to creatures in the morning and afternoon are under His command. The verse serves as a reminder of the greatness of God and the need for all of His creation to submit to His will, regardless of their desires or inclinations.
orig: ولله يسجد من في السماوات والأرض طوعا وكرها وظلالهم بالغدو والآصال

translation: Say, 'Who is the Lord of the heavens and the earth?' Say, 'Allah.' Say, 'Have you taken besides Him allies who do not possess for themselves any benefit or harm?' Say, 'Is the blind equal to the seer? Or is darkness equal to light?' Or have they attributed to Allah partners who created like His creation so that the creation seemed similar to them?' Say, 'Allah is the Creator of all things, and He is the One, the Prevailing.'
interpretation: The verse addresses the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and commands him to pose a series of questions to the disbelievers. These questions aim to challenge their belief in false deities and highlight the power and uniqueness of Allah. The verse emphasizes the vast difference between the Creator and the creation, and the inability of any created being to possess any benefit or harm for themselves, unlike Allah. The verse serves as a reminder of the power and greatness of Allah, and the futility of worshipping anything other than Him. The questions also serve to expose the irrationality of associating partners with Allah, and the impossibility of creating anything equal to His creation. The verse ultimately reaffirms the Oneness of Allah, and His complete control and power over all things.
orig: قل من رب السماوات والأرض قل الله قل أفاتخذتم من دونه أولياء لا يملكون لأنفسهم نفعا ولا ضرا قل هل يستوي الأعمى والبصير أم هل تستوي الظلمات والنور أم جعلوا لله شركاء خلقوا كخلقه فتشابه الخلق عليهم قل الله خالق كل شيء وهو الواحد القهار

translation: Descend from the sky, water, then it flows in the valleys according to its capacity. Then the flood carries along a swelling foam. And from that which they heat in the fire for the purpose of adornment or utensils, is a foam like it. Thus, Allah compares truth to falsehood. As for the foam, it disappears, but as for what benefits the people, it remains on the earth. Thus, Allah compares truth to falsehood.
interpretation: The verse uses the metaphor of foam and water to illustrate the fleeting and insignificant nature of falsehood and the enduring and beneficial nature of truth. The foam, which is temporary and worthless, is likened to falsehood, while the water, which is beneficial and nourishing, is likened to truth. The verse emphasizes the importance of recognizing and valuing truth, and the transient and insignificant nature of falsehood. The verse encourages believers to seek and uphold the truth, and to not be deceived by the superficial and temporary allure of falsehood.
orig: أنزل من السماء ماء فسالت أودية بقدرها فاحتمل السيل زبدا رابيا ومما يوقدون عليه في النار ابتغاء حلية أو متاع زبد مثله كذلك يضرب الله الحق والباطل فأما الزبد فيذهب جفاء وأما ما ينفع الناس فيمكث في الأرض كذلك يضرب الله الأمثال

translation: For those who respond to their Lord is good, and for those who do not respond, even if We had given them all that is on earth and the likes of it, they would not accept it. These have a miserable end, and their dwelling is Hell, and what a wretched destination.
interpretation: The verse contrasts the fate of those who respond to their Lord's guidance with those who do not, emphasizing the importance of responding to God's call. The verse highlights the futility of material wealth and possessions for those who are heedless of God, as even if all the wealth of the earth were given to them, they would not be content or grateful. The verse ends with a warning of the miserable end and wretched destination that awaits those who reject God's guidance, serving as a reminder of the ultimate consequences of one's actions.
orig: للذين استجابوا لربهم الحسنى والذين لم يستجيبوا له لو أن لهم ما في الأرض جميعا ومثله معه لافتدوا به أولئك لهم سوء الحساب ومأواهم جهنم وبئس المهاد

translation: Or is he who knows that what has been revealed to you from your Lord is the truth like one who is blind? Only those with understanding will remember.
interpretation: The verse contrasts those who recognize the truth of the revelation brought by the prophet with those who are blind to it. The verse suggests that those who are aware of the truth are in a better position than those who are blind to it. The verse emphasizes the importance of understanding and remembering the revelation, implying that it is a guide for those who seek the right path. The verse serves as a reminder to those who have received the message of the prophet, urging them to reflect on the truth of the revelation and to use their understanding to remember and follow it.
orig: أفمن يعلم أنما أنزل إليك من ربك الحق كمن هو أعمى إنما يتذكر أولو الألباب

translation: Those who fulfill the covenant of God and do not break the promise.
interpretation: The verse highlights the importance of fulfilling the covenant (promise or agreement) made with God and not breaking it. It serves as a reminder to be truthful and trustworthy in one's relationship with God. This quality of being truthful and keeping one's promises is highly valued in Islamic teachings and is considered as a sign of faith and righteousness. This verse can also be seen as a warning against being unfaithful and breaking promises, as it can lead to negative consequences in this world and the hereafter.
orig: الذين يوفون بعهد الله ولا ينقضون الميثاق

translation: And those who pray, performing the prayer as it is due to be performed, and they are apprehensive of the Hereafter and they come to God as Muslims.
interpretation: The verse describes the believers who perform their prayers as prescribed by God and are mindful of the Day of Judgment. They are conscious of the importance of their prayers and strive to perform them in the best manner. The verse highlights the fear of the Hereafter that these believers possess, which motivates them to lead a righteous life and worship God sincerely. The verse also emphasizes that they are Muslims, submissive to God's will and guidance.
orig: والذين يصلون ما أمر الله به أن يوصل ويخشون ربهم ويخافون سوء الحساب

translation: And as for those who persevere, seeking the countenance of their Lord, and establish prayer and spend from what We have provided them, secretly and publicly, and repel evil with good - for such there is the final attainment of the (ultimate) home -
interpretation: This verse describes the qualities of those who will attain the ultimate home or paradise. These individuals are patient and persevere in their worship of their Lord, establish prayer, give charity both publicly and privately, and respond to evil with good. By doing so, they are able to repel evil and instead promote good in the world. These actions demonstrate their commitment to their faith and their desire to please their Lord. As a result, they are promised the ultimate reward of paradise.
orig: والذين صبروا ابتغاء وجه ربهم وأقاموا الصلاة وأنفقوا مما رزقناهم سرا وعلانية ويدرءون بالحسنة السيئة أولئك لهم عقبى الدار

translation: Gardens of Eden they will enter, they and their parents, and their spouses, and their children. And the angels will enter unto them from every gate.
interpretation: The verse describes the reward for the righteous in the afterlife, where they will enter the Gardens of Eden along with their parents, spouses, and children. The inclusion of family members in this description emphasizes the importance of family and community in Islam, and the joy of being reunited with loved ones in the afterlife. The presence of angels entering from every gate highlights the grandeur and magnificence of the Gardens of Eden, and the overwhelming joy and blessings that will be experienced by the righteous.
orig: جنات عدن يدخلونها ومن صلح من آبائهم وأزواجهم وذرياتهم والملائكة يدخلون عليهم من كل باب

translation: Peace be upon you for your patience. How excellent is then the final home!
interpretation: The verse is a greeting of peace and a statement of praise for the patience of the believers. It emphasizes the excellence of the final home or abode, which is a reference to paradise. The verse serves as a source of comfort and hope for the believers, reminding them that their patience and perseverance will be rewarded with a place in paradise.
orig: سلام عليكم بما صبرتم فنعم عقبى الدار

translation: And those who break the covenant of God, after having pledged to it, and cut what God has ordered to be joined, and cause corruption in the earth - for them is the curse, and for them is the evil home.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the consequences of those who break the covenant of God, cut what God has ordered to be joined, and cause corruption in the earth. These actions are considered a severe violation of God's commands and a betrayal of the trust placed in them. The verse warns that for such individuals, there is a curse and an evil home awaiting them. The 'curse' and 'evil home' can be interpreted as a metaphor for divine punishment and a miserable existence in the hereafter. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of upholding one's covenants and following God's commands, and the severe consequences of disobedience.
orig: والذين ينقضون عهد الله من بعد ميثاقه ويقطعون ما أمر الله به أن يوصل ويفسدون في الأرض أولئك لهم اللعنة ولهم سوء الدار

translation: Allah extends provision for whom He wills and restricts, and they rejoice in the worldly life, while the worldly life is not, compared to the Hereafter, except [worthless] enjoyment.
interpretation: The verse highlights the power of Allah in providing for His creations and taking it away, and the fleeting nature of worldly pleasures. The verse serves as a reminder that the enjoyments of this world are temporary and insignificant compared to the Hereafter. The verse encourages believers to focus on the Hereafter and not be deceived by the temporary pleasures of this world. It also emphasizes the power of Allah in providing and taking away sustenance, and the importance of being grateful for what one has been given.
orig: الله يبسط الرزق لمن يشاء ويقدر وفرحوا بالحياة الدنيا وما الحياة الدنيا في الآخرة إلا متاع

translation: And those who disbelieve say, 'Why was not a sign sent down to him from his Lord?' So say, 'Indeed, God sends astray whom He wills and guides to Himself whoever turns back [to Him] -
interpretation: The verse speaks about the disbelievers' demand for a sign from God as a proof of the prophethood of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). The verse explains that the guidance from God is not something that can be demanded or forced, but it is a mercy that God bestows upon whom He wills. The verse emphasizes that God guides those who turn back to Him in repentance and submission. The verse serves as a reminder that only those who are guided by God can truly believe and follow the right path, and that the disbelievers' demand for a sign is a sign of their rejection and ingratitude towards God's signs that are already present in the world.
orig: ويقول الذين كفروا لولا أنزل عليه آية من ربه قل إن الله يضل من يشاء ويهدي إليه من أناب

translation: Those who believe and whose hearts find rest in the remembrance of God, surely, in the remembrance of God do hearts find rest.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the peace and tranquility that believers find in the remembrance of God. The verse emphasizes that true rest and contentment can be found in the remembrance of God, and that hearts will find rest only when they remember God. The verse serves as a reminder to believers to remember God often and to find solace in the remembrance of God during times of difficulty or distress.
orig: الذين آمنوا وتطمئن قلوبهم بذكر الله ألا بذكر الله تطمئن القلوب

translation: Those who believe and do righteous deeds, blessed are they and excellent is their final abode.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the reward for those who believe in God and do righteous deeds. The verse states that they are blessed and that their final abode is excellent. The verse emphasizes the positive outcome for those who lead a righteous life and encourages the reader to believe and do good deeds. The verse serves as a motivation for believers to strive for righteousness and to have faith in God's rewards.
orig: الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات طوبى لهم وحسن مآب

translation: Thus have We sent you (O Muhammad) to a community before which (other) communities have passed away, that you may recite to them what We have revealed to you, while they disbelieve in the Gracious. Say (O Muhammad): 'He is my Lord, there is no god but He; on Him do I rely, and to Him do I return (with devotion and obedience).'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the prophet Muhammad's mission to a community that had previously been inhabited by other communities that had passed away. Muhammad's role was to recite to them the revelation that he had received from God, but they disbelieved in God's mercy. The verse emphasizes the prophet's faith in God, stating that 'He is my Lord, there is no god but He; on Him do I rely, and to Him do I return (with devotion and obedience).' This statement serves as a model of faith and submission to God for the prophet and the believers. The verse also highlights the transience of human existence and the continuity of prophetic missions, reminding the believers that they are not the first to receive God's message and that they should follow the example of the prophet in their devotion and obedience to God.
orig: كذلك أرسلناك في أمة قد خلت من قبلها أمم لتتلو عليهم الذي أوحينا إليك وهم يكفرون بالرحمن قل هو ربي لا إله إلا هو عليه توكلت وإليه متاب

translation: And if We had sent down the Qur'an upon a mountain, you would have seen it humbled and rent asunder from fear of Allah. And these examples We present to the people that perhaps they may reflect. But alas, most of them are heedless. Yet, if We had willed, We could have sent a warner to every city. So, do they not see that We do not seize upon them gradually? And We come to them suddenly? But their fate is already fixed, and the preordainment of their hands. So, indeed, they will not find for themselves besides Allah a protector. But no! Rather, it is a reminder for the people, so that perhaps they will be reminded. And no one is destroy except for transgressing. So, do they not see? But indeed, they are, in most things, defiant.
interpretation: The verse describes the power and majesty of the Qur'an, using the metaphor of a mountain being destroyed if the Qur'an was revealed upon it. This is to emphasize the importance and significance of the Qur'an. The verse also highlights the fact that most people are heedless and unaware of the signs of Allah. The verse also mentions that Allah has the power to send a warner to every city, but He chooses not to. The verse also highlights the sudden and unexpected nature of Allah's punishment, emphasizing that it will come when people are not prepared. The verse serves as a reminder and a warning to those who are heedless and unaware, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of Allah's punishment. The verse also emphasizes that people's fate is already fixed, and they cannot escape from the preordainment of their hands. The verse also emphasizes that people will not find for themselves besides Allah a protector. The verse also emphasizes that no one is destroy except for transgressing and that people should reflect on this and take heed.
orig: ولو أن قرآنا سيرت به الجبال أو قطعت به الأرض أو كلم به الموتى بل لله الأمر جميعا أفلم ييأس الذين آمنوا أن لو يشاء الله لهدى الناس جميعا ولا يزال الذين كفروا تصيبهم بما صنعوا قارعة أو تحل قريبا من دارهم حتى يأتي وعد الله إن الله لا يخلف الميعاد

translation: And they have scoffed at the messengers before them; so how was My punishment and retribution?
interpretation: The verse speaks about the scoffing and mocking of the messengers of God by the disbelievers. The verse then asks a rhetorical question, 'so how was My punishment and retribution?'. This question serves as a reminder and a warning to the disbelievers of the consequences of their actions. The verse emphasizes the power and authority of God, and the certainty of His punishment for those who reject His messengers and deny His message.
orig: ولقد استهزئ برسل من قبلك فأمليت للذين كفروا ثم أخذتهم فكيف كان عقاب

translation: Is He who is over every soul responsible for what it earns, and they have made partners to God, equal to Him who has not assigned any partners to Him? Say: Name them! Or are you informing Him of what He knows not in the earth, or is it a mere conjecture? Rather, what they do is adornment for the disbelievers, and they are averse from the path. And whomever God leads astray, there is no guide for him.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the concept of individual responsibility for one's actions, and the belief in the oneness of God. It criticizes those who assign partners to God, and challenges them to provide evidence for their beliefs. The verse suggests that the belief in multiple deities is a mere conjecture, and that only God has complete knowledge. The verse also highlights the futility of trying to inform God of something He already knows, and the adornment of falsehood that the disbelievers engage in. The verse ultimately warns of the consequences of being led astray by God, and the lack of guidance for those who stray from the path of truth.
orig: أفمن هو قائم على كل نفس بما كسبت وجعلوا لله شركاء قل سموهم أم تنبئونه بما لا يعلم في الأرض أم بظاهر من القول بل زين للذين كفروا مكرهم وصدوا عن السبيل ومن يضلل الله فما له من هاد

translation: They will have a punishment in this worldly life, and the punishment of the Hereafter is more severe. And they will not find for themselves besides Allah a protector.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the punishment that will be given to certain people, both in this world and in the hereafter, with the latter being more severe. The verse also emphasizes that these people will not find any protection or help from anyone but Allah. The verse serves as a warning to those who may be committing sins or wrongdoings, reminding them that they will be held accountable for their actions and that there will be consequences both in this life and in the hereafter. Additionally, the verse highlights the ultimate power and authority of Allah, as He is the only one who can provide protection and help to His servants.
orig: لهم عذاب في الحياة الدنيا ولعذاب الآخرة أشق وما لهم من الله من واق

translation: Like the garden which is promised to the pious, rivers flow beneath it, their food is eternal and their shade, that is the reward of those who are pious, and the reward of the disbelievers is the fire.
interpretation: The verse describes the blessings of Paradise that await the pious, using the metaphor of a garden with rivers flowing beneath it. The food and shade in Paradise are eternal, signifying the never-ending blessings and joys of the Hereafter. The verse contrasts the blessings of Paradise with the punishment of the fire that awaits the disbelievers, emphasizing the importance of piety and belief in God. The verse serves as a reminder of the ultimate destination of souls and the significance of one's actions in this world.
orig: مثل الجنة التي وعد المتقون تجري من تحتها الأنهار أكلها دائم وظلها تلك عقبى الذين اتقوا وعقبى الكافرين النار

translation: And those to whom We have given the Scripture rejoice in what has been revealed to you, while among the communities are those who deny some of it. Say, 'I have only been commanded to worship Allah and not associate anything with Him. To Him I invite, and to Him is my return.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the response of different groups of people to the revelation of the Qur'an. Those who have been given previous scriptures, such as the Jews and Christians, are happy about what has been revealed to the Prophet Muhammad. However, there are also those who reject some parts of the revelation. The Prophet Muhammad is instructed to respond by saying that he has been commanded to worship only Allah and not associate any partners with Him. He invites others to follow this path and affirms that his return is to Allah.
orig: والذين آتيناهم الكتاب يفرحون بما أنزل إليك ومن الأحزاب من ينكر بعضه قل إنما أمرت أن أعبد الله ولا أشرك به إليه أدعو وإليه مآب

translation: And thus have We sent it down as an Arabic decree, and if you should follow their desires after what has come to you of knowledge, then indeed, there is for you from Allah no protector nor helper.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of adhering to the Arabic revelation (referring to the Qur'an) and not being swayed by the desires of others after gaining knowledge. The verse warns that if one were to follow their desires after gaining knowledge, they would lose the protection and help of God. This interpretation highlights the significance of remaining steadfast on the path of righteousness and not being influenced by the whims of others, even after gaining knowledge and understanding.
orig: وكذلك أنزلناه حكما عربيا ولئن اتبعت أهواءهم بعدما جاءك من العلم ما لك من الله من ولي ولا واق

translation: And We have already sent messengers before you, [O Muhammad], among the former peoples. And there never came to them a messenger but they ridiculed him. Thus do We insert disgrace into the hearts of the criminals.
interpretation: The verse highlights the consistent pattern of human behavior towards the messengers of God, who were sent to guide and warn their people. Despite the fact that these messengers brought clear signs and evidence from God, they were often ridiculed and rejected by their people. The verse emphasizes that no messenger could bring a sign without the permission of God, and that the rejection and mockery of the messengers only serves to increase the guilt and disgrace of the unbelievers. The verse serves as a reminder that the same fate that befell previous nations who rejected their messengers may also befall those who reject the message of God's final messenger, Muhammad (peace be upon him).
orig: ولقد أرسلنا رسلا من قبلك وجعلنا لهم أزواجا وذرية وما كان لرسول أن يأتي بآية إلا بإذن الله لكل أجل كتاب

translation: Allah blots out what He wills and confirms, and with Him is the Mother of the Book.
interpretation: The verse affirms that Allah has the power to erase or confirm whatever He wills and that with Him is the 'Mother of the Book', a reference to the original divine source of all knowledge and wisdom. The verse emphasizes Allah's omnipotence and sovereignty, reminding the reader of the ultimate power and authority of the divine. The verse can also be understood as a reminder that Allah has the power to forgive and erase past sins and mistakes, but also the power to confirm and uphold the consequences of one's actions. The verse encourages trust and submission to Allah's will, recognizing that all things are ultimately in His hands.
orig: يمحو الله ما يشاء ويثبت وعنده أم الكتاب

translation: And indeed, We will show you some of what We have promised them, or We will take you (O Muhammad) in death. And upon you is only the clear conveyance (of the message), and upon Us is the account.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the responsibility of the Prophet Muhammad to convey the message of Islam, and the assurance that God will hold him accountable only for delivering it, not for the outcome. The verse implies that either the Prophet will witness the consequences of the disbelievers' actions, or he will be taken in death, and God will deal with the disbelievers. The verse provides reassurance and encouragement to the Prophet and his followers, emphasizing that the outcome of their efforts is ultimately in God's hands.
orig: وإن ما نرينك بعض الذي نعدهم أو نتوفينك فإنما عليك البلاغ وعلينا الحساب

translation: Have they not seen that We come to the land, reducing it from its borders. And indeed, Allah is decisive in His punishment. And there is not for Him a competitor in respect of dispatching it. And He is swift in account.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the power and ability of God to reduce and destroy the land, emphasizing His control and dominion over all of creation. The verse also highlights the inevitability of God's punishment, stating that it is certain and without equal. The verse serves as a reminder of God's power and authority, urging people to recognize and submit to His will.
orig: أولم يروا أنا نأتي الأرض ننقصها من أطرافها والله يحكم لا معقب لحكمه وهو سريع الحساب

translation: Those before them had plotted, but all plotting is God's, He knows what every soul earns, and the disbelievers will soon know who the inheritor of the land is.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the futility of plotting and scheming against God's will. The verse emphasizes that all plotting belongs to God and that He is aware of the actions of every individual. The verse also warns the disbelievers that they will soon find out who the inheritor of the land is, indicating that they will be replaced by those who are more deserving. The verse serves as a reminder that God is all-knowing and all-powerful, and that those who oppose Him and His will will ultimately be defeated.
orig: وقد مكر الذين من قبلهم فلله المكر جميعا يعلم ما تكسب كل نفس وسيعلم الكفار لمن عقبى الدار

translation: And those who disbelieve say, 'You are not a messenger.' Say, 'Sufficient is Allah as Witness between me and you, and He with whom is knowledge of the Book.'
interpretation: The verse is a response to the disbelievers who rejected the prophethood of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). The verse commands the Prophet to declare that Allah alone is sufficient as a Witness between him and the disbelievers. The verse emphasizes the all-knowing nature of Allah, who has knowledge of the Book (the Qur'an) and is aware of the truth. The verse serves as a reminder that the truth of prophethood is not dependent on human acceptance or validation, but rather on the divine decree of Allah.
orig: ويقول الذين كفروا لست مرسلا قل كفى بالله شهيدا بيني وبينكم ومن عنده علم الكتاب

translation: Alif. Lam. Ra. [This is] a Book that We have sent down to you [Muhammad] so that you may bring forth the people from darknesses into the light by permission of their Lord to the path of the Exalted in Might, the Praiseworthy.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the Qur'an being sent down to the Prophet Muhammad as a guide for humanity. The verse highlights the role of the Qur'an in bringing people out of 'darknesses' and into 'light', indicating the enlightenment and guidance that the Qur'an provides. The 'darknesses' could refer to ignorance, disbelief, or unrighteousness, while the 'light' symbolizes knowledge, faith, and righteousness. The verse further states that the Qur'an leads people to the 'path of the Exalted in Might, the Praiseworthy', which signifies the right path that leads to God. The verse emphasizes the importance of the Qur'an as a source of guidance and enlightenment, inviting people to embrace its teachings and follow the path that it lays out.
orig: الر كتاب أنزلناه إليك لتخرج الناس من الظلمات إلى النور بإذن ربهم إلى صراط العزيز الحميد

translation: It is Allah who possesses whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, and woe to the disbelievers from a severe punishment.
interpretation: The verse affirms the power and sovereignty of Allah, who has control over all that exists in the heavens and the earth. The verse then warns of a severe punishment for the disbelievers, emphasizing the serious consequences of rejecting faith and the certainty of divine retribution. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of belief and the need to avoid disbelief and transgression.
orig: الله الذي له ما في السماوات وما في الأرض وويل للكافرين من عذاب شديد

translation: Those who prefer the life of this world over the Hereafter and hinder from the way of Allah and seek to make it deviant - those are far astray.
interpretation: The verse speaks about those who prioritize the pleasures and desires of this world over the Hereafter. These people not only neglect the path of Allah but also actively obstruct others from following it. They try to distort and corrupt the path, leading people away from it. The verse strongly condemns such behavior and considers it a form of deviation and misguidance. The verse serves as a warning to those who prioritize worldly gains and pleasures over the Hereafter, urging them to reconsider their priorities and to follow the path of Allah.
orig: الذين يستحبون الحياة الدنيا على الآخرة ويصدون عن سبيل الله ويبغونها عوجا أولئك في ضلال بعيد

translation: And We sent no messenger except in the language of his people, in order that he might make clear to them. Then God leads astray whom He wills and guides whom He wills. And He is the All-Mighty, the All-Wise.
interpretation: The verse explains that God sends messengers to every nation in the language of that nation, so that the people can understand the message. However, despite the clarity of the message, God guides whom He wills and leads astray whom He wills. This highlights the idea that human beings have free will, but ultimately, it is God who determines the outcome. The verse emphasizes God's power and wisdom, and serves as a reminder that He is the ultimate judge and controller of all things.
orig: وما أرسلنا من رسول إلا بلسان قومه ليبين لهم فيضل الله من يشاء ويهدي من يشاء وهو العزيز الحكيم

translation: And indeed We sent Moses with Our signs (ayat) that he should bring out his people from the depths of darkness into light and remind them of the days of God. Indeed in that are signs for every patient, grateful (person).
interpretation: The verse speaks about the mission of Moses, who was sent by God with signs (ayat) to lead his people out of the darkness of ignorance and sin into the light of truth and guidance. The verse also emphasizes the importance of remembering and being grateful for the blessings of God, as there are signs and lessons to be learned from the past for those who are patient and grateful. The verse serves as a reminder to the believers to be patient, grateful, and steadfast in their faith, and to remember the blessings and guidance that God has bestowed upon them.
orig: ولقد أرسلنا موسى بآياتنا أن أخرج قومك من الظلمات إلى النور وذكرهم بأيام الله إن في ذلك لآيات لكل صبار شكور

translation: And when Moses said to his people, 'Remember the favor of Allah upon you when He saved you from the people of Pharaoh, who were afflicting you with the worst of punishment, killing your sons and sparing your women. And in that is a great trial from your Lord.'
interpretation: The verse recounts the story of Moses reminding his people of the favor and mercy of Allah in saving them from the oppression of Pharaoh and his people. The verse highlights the severity of the punishment inflicted by Pharaoh, such as killing the male children and sparing the women. This serves as a reminder of the great trial and hardship that the people faced, but ultimately, it was through Allah's help and intervention that they were saved. The verse emphasizes the importance of remembering and being grateful for Allah's blessings and favors, and recognizing His power and control over all things.
orig: وإذ قال موسى لقومه اذكروا نعمة الله عليكم إذ أنجاكم من آل فرعون يسومونكم سوء العذاب ويذبحون أبناءكم ويستحيون نساءكم وفي ذلكم بلاء من ربكم عظيم

translation: And when your Lord proclaimed: 'If you are grateful, I will surely increase you [in favor]; but if you deny, indeed, My punishment is severe.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the consequences of gratitude and denial. Those who are grateful for God's blessings will be rewarded with even more, while those who deny and are ungrateful will face severe punishment. The verse emphasizes the importance of gratitude and the consequences of denial, serving as a reminder for people to be thankful for what they have been given and to avoid denial and ingratitude.
orig: وإذ تأذن ربكم لئن شكرتم لأزيدنكم ولئن كفرتم إن عذابي لشديد

translation: And Moses said, 'If you disbelieve, you and whoever is in the earth all together, then indeed, Allah is free of need and praiseworthy.',
interpretation: The verse recounts Moses' response to the disbelief of the people. Despite their rejection of faith, Moses asserts that Allah is self-sufficient and praiseworthy, implying that Allah does not need the recognition or approval of the people. The verse serves as a reminder of the ultimate power and independence of Allah, and the insignificance of those who deny His existence or refuse to submit to His will.
orig: وقال موسى إن تكفروا أنتم ومن في الأرض جميعا فإن الله لغني حميد

translation: Has there not come to you the story of those before you, the people of Noah, and 'Ad, and Thamud, and those after them? No one knows them but Allah. Their messengers came to them with clear evidences, but they put their hands in their mouths and said, 'We have disbelieved in what you have been sent with, and indeed we are, about what you invite us to, in skepticism.',
interpretation: The verse refers to the stories of previous nations, such as the people of Noah, 'Ad, and Thamud, who rejected the messengers sent to them, despite clear evidence and proofs. The verse highlights the rejection and disbelief of these people, who refused to accept the message brought by the messengers and instead mocked and ridiculed them. The verse serves as a reminder of the consequences of rejecting God's message, and emphasizes the importance of accepting and submitting to the truth, even in the face of skepticism and doubt.
orig: ألم يأتكم نبأ الذين من قبلكم قوم نوح وعاد وثمود والذين من بعدهم لا يعلمهم إلا الله جاءتهم رسلهم بالبينات فردوا أيديهم في أفواههم وقالوا إنا كفرنا بما أرسلتم به وإنا لفي شك مما تدعوننا إليه مريب

translation: Their messengers said, 'Is there doubt regarding Allah, the creator of the heavens and the earth? He calls you to forgive your sins and to delay you until an appointed term.'
