They said, 'You are but human beings like us, you wish to turn us away from what our fathers have worshipped. So bring us a clear authority.'
interpretation: The verse describes a conversation between the messengers of God and their people. The messengers invite their people to worship God and to seek His forgiveness for their sins. They also tell them that God will grant them a respite until a specified time. However, the people reject the message of the messengers and demand a clear authority or proof. They accuse the messengers of being human beings like themselves and of wanting to turn them away from the religion of their forefathers. The verse highlights the rejection and disbelief of the people towards the message of the messengers and their refusal to accept the truth.
orig: قالت رسلهم أفي الله شك فاطر السماوات والأرض يدعوكم ليغفر لكم من ذنوبكم ويؤخركم إلى أجل مسمى قالوا إن أنتم إلا بشر مثلنا تريدون أن تصدونا عما كان يعبد آباؤنا فأتونا بسلطان مبين

translation: Their messengers said to them: 'We are no more than human beings like you, but God confers favor on whom He will of His servants. It is not for us to bring you an authority except by God's leave. And upon God let the believers rely.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the messengers of God, who are reminding the people that they are also human and not superior. They emphasize that any authority or power they have is only granted by God and that it is not in their control. The verse encourages the believers to put their trust and reliance in God, as it is only through His will and permission that any good can come to them. The verse highlights the humility and dependence on God, even for those who are chosen as messengers.
orig: قالت لهم رسلهم إن نحن إلا بشر مثلكم ولكن الله يمن على من يشاء من عباده وما كان لنا أن نأتيكم بسلطان إلا بإذن الله وعلى الله فليتوكل المؤمنون

translation: And why should we not rely upon Allah while He has guided us our ways. And we will surely be patient in adversity. And upon Allah, let those who would rely, rely.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of relying on Allah and having patience in the face of adversity. The speaker questions why they should not rely on Allah, highlighting the fact that Allah has already guided them on their path. The verse also encourages the listener to have patience and to place their trust in Allah, stating that those who rely on Him will find solace and support. The verse serves as a reminder that Allah is the ultimate source of guidance and support, and that relying on Him is the key to overcoming adversity.
orig: وما لنا ألا نتوكل على الله وقد هدانا سبلنا ولنصبرن على ما آذيتمونا وعلى الله فليتوكل المتوكلون

translation: And those who disbelieved said to their messengers, 'We will surely drive you out of our land, or you will return to our religion.' So their Lord inspired to them, 'Indeed, I will destroy the wrongdoers.'
interpretation: The verse describes the defiant attitude of the disbelievers towards their messengers, who demanded that the messengers either leave their land or return to their religion. The verse then relates that God inspired the messengers, promising to destroy the wrongdoers. The verse highlights the rejection and hostility faced by the messengers in their mission to convey the message of God, and the ultimate power of God to punish those who reject His message and engage in wrongdoing.
orig: وقال الذين كفروا لرسلهم لنخرجنكم من أرضنا أو لتعودن في ملتنا فأوحى إليهم ربهم لنهلكن الظالمين

translation: And We will soon let you dwell in the land after them. That is, for one who fears My punishment and is conscious of Me.
interpretation: The verse speaks about God's promise to allow the righteous and God-conscious people to dwell in the land after the unjust and sinful people have been destroyed. The verse emphasizes the importance of fearing God's punishment and being mindful of one's actions. By being conscious of God, one can attain God's favor and live in peace and security in this world. The verse serves as a source of hope and comfort for the righteous, reminding them of God's mercy and grace towards those who fear Him and strive to live a righteous life.
orig: ولنسكننكم الأرض من بعدهم ذلك لمن خاف مقامي وخاف وعيد

translation: And ask forgiveness from your Lord and then repent to Him. Indeed, my Lord is Merciful and Loving.
interpretation: The verse encourages the reader to seek forgiveness from their Lord and to repent. It emphasizes the mercy and love of the Lord, highlighting the fact that even after committing wrongdoings, the Lord is willing to forgive and show love to the repentant. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of seeking forgiveness and turning back to God, and of the boundless mercy and love of the Lord towards His creation.
orig: واستفتحوا وخاب كل جبار عنيد

translation: Behind them is Hell, and they will be given to drink of boiling water.
interpretation: The verse describes a group of people who are destined for Hell, and emphasizes the severity of their punishment. The phrase 'behind them is Hell' suggests that there is no escape or reprieve from their fate, and the image of 'boiling water' conveys a sense of extreme pain and suffering. The verse serves as a warning to those who persist in their disbelief and wrongdoing, reminding them of the severe consequences that await them in the afterlife.
orig: من ورائه جهنم ويسقى من ماء صديد

translation: He (the unbeliever) makes a fun of it (the Qur'an) while it (the Qur'an) is being hoisted up. And it (the unbeliever) does not believe with certainty. And the death comes to him from wherever it seizes him. And indeed, from behind him is a severe punishment.
interpretation: The verse describes the attitude of the unbelievers towards the Qur'an, which they mock and do not believe in. The verse emphasizes the inevitability of death and its suddenness, as it can come to the unbeliever from any direction and at any time. Furthermore, the verse warns of a severe punishment that awaits the unbelievers after their death, which will come from behind them, indicating that it will be unavoidable and inescapable.
orig: يتجرعه ولا يكاد يسيغه ويأتيه الموت من كل مكان وما هو بميت ومن ورائه عذاب غليظ

translation: Like the companions of the garden, who denied the judgment of their Lord: until, while their companion was bringing them fruit in baskets, he said: 'Do you not give thanks?', they said: 'Glory be to you! We wait for the fate of ill-omened things.' But a shout seized them as they were looking on, and they became bodies lying prone in their place, so become of them as you see fit, the distant departure.
interpretation: The verse uses the metaphor of a group of people who, despite enjoying the blessings of a garden, deny the power and judgment of their Lord. When they are presented with fruit as a reminder of God's bounty, they respond with ingratitude and mockery. As a result, they are suddenly and swiftly punished, being turned into withered bodies in an instant. The verse serves as a warning against ingratitude and a reminder of the power and judgment of God, who can punish and destroy those who deny and mock Him.
orig: مثل الذين كفروا بربهم أعمالهم كرماد اشتدت به الريح في يوم عاصف لا يقدرون مما كسبوا على شيء ذلك هو الضلال البعيد

translation: Have you not seen that God has created the heavens and the earth in truth? If He wills, He can take you away, O mankind, and bring about a new creation.
interpretation: The verse highlights God's power and authority over the creation of the heavens and the earth, emphasizing that they were created with truth and purpose. The verse also serves as a reminder of God's ability to take away human life and replace it with a new creation, indicating the fleeting and transient nature of human existence. The verse encourages reflection and contemplation of God's power and greatness, and serves as a reminder of the need for humility and submission to God's will.
orig: ألم تر أن الله خلق السماوات والأرض بالحق إن يشأ يذهبكم ويأت بخلق جديد

translation: And that is not difficult for God.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the power and ability of God, suggesting that whatever is being referred to in the previous verse is not difficult or challenging for God to accomplish. The verse may serve as a reminder to the reader of the greatness and might of God, and of the limited nature of human abilities and understanding.
orig: وما ذلك على الله بعزيز

translation: And stand before God altogether. Then said the weak ones, 'We were indeed followers of yours; is it then that you will avail us against the punishment of God, seeing that no guardian we had?' They said, 'Had God guided us, we would have guided you; it is all the same for us whether we are impatient or endure with resignation; there is no escape for us.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about a moment of truth before God, where the weak ones among a group acknowledge their previous subservience to the more powerful ones among them. They ask if the powerful ones can protect them from God's punishment, admitting that they had no guardian to protect them. The powerful ones respond that if they had been guided by God, they would have guided the weak ones as well. They express a sense of helplessness, stating that whether they are impatient or endure with resignation, they see no way out of their situation. The verse highlights the ultimate power of God and the futility of human attempts to escape His judgment. It also suggests a critique of the powerful ones who did not guide the weak ones when they had the chance, and the consequences they all now face.
orig: وبرزوا لله جميعا فقال الضعفاء للذين استكبروا إنا كنا لكم تبعا فهل أنتم مغنون عنا من عذاب الله من شيء قالوا لو هدانا الله لهديناكم سواء علينا أجزعنا أم صبرنا ما لنا من محيص

translation: And the devil said, when the matter was decided: ‘Indeed, God has promised you the promise of truth, and I promised you and broke my promise to you. I had no authority over you, except that I invited you and you responded to me. So do not blame me, but blame yourselves. I cannot respond to your cries for help, nor can you respond to my cries for help. Indeed, I reject what you associate with me as partners before. Indeed, for the unjust is a painful punishment.’
interpretation: The verse relays a conversation between the devil and the people who followed him, after their fate was sealed. The devil admits to breaking his promise and reveals that his power over the people was limited to his ability to invite them towards sin, which they willingly accepted. The devil advises the people to hold themselves accountable for their actions, and not to blame him. The devil also states that he cannot help them or respond to their cries for help. The verse serves as a reminder of the reality of the devil's influence and the consequences of following his whispers. It highlights the importance of taking responsibility for one's actions and the severe punishment for those who commit unjust acts.
orig: وقال الشيطان لما قضي الأمر إن الله وعدكم وعد الحق ووعدتكم فأخلفتكم وما كان لي عليكم من سلطان إلا أن دعوتكم فاستجبتم لي فلا تلوموني ولوموا أنفسكم ما أنا بمصرخكم وما أنتم بمصرخي إني كفرت بما أشركتمون من قبل إن الظالمين لهم عذاب أليم

translation: And enter those who believed and did righteous deeds into Gardens beneath which rivers flow, to abide therein eternally by permission of their Lord. Their greeting therein will be 'Peace'.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the reward for those who believe in God and do good deeds. They will be granted eternal life in a paradise filled with flowing rivers, where they will be greeted with peace. The verse serves as a promise of a blissful afterlife for those who lead a righteous life in this world. It encourages people to have faith in God, do good deeds, and strive for a place in this paradise.
orig: وأدخل الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات جنات تجري من تحتها الأنهار خالدين فيها بإذن ربهم تحيتهم فيها سلام

translation: Have you not seen how Allah presents as an example a good word like a good tree, whose root is firm and whose branches are in the sky?
interpretation: The verse uses the example of a good word and a good tree to illustrate the power of positive actions and speech. The tree, with its firm roots and branches reaching towards the sky, represents stability, growth, and connection to the divine. Similarly, a good word can have a profound impact, as it is grounded in truth and has the potential to reach great heights. This verse encourages believers to choose their words wisely, understanding that their speech can have profound consequences and contribute to their spiritual growth and connection with God.
orig: ألم تر كيف ضرب الله مثلا كلمة طيبة كشجرة طيبة أصلها ثابت وفرعها في السماء

translation: And it (the earth) brings forth its plants (cattle, etc.) at every stage (of its development) by the Command of its Lord. And Allah sets forth parables (or examples) for mankind in order that they may remember (and understand the wisdom of their creation).
interpretation: The verse highlights the role of the earth in producing plants and cattle through the command of its Lord. It also emphasizes the wisdom and power of God through the use of parables or examples. These examples are set forth for mankind to understand the purpose of their creation and to remember God. The verse encourages reflection and mindfulness of God's power and wisdom in the natural world.
orig: تؤتي أكلها كل حين بإذن ربها ويضرب الله الأمثال للناس لعلهم يتذكرون

translation: And the example of an evil word is like an evil tree, uprooted from the earth, having no stability.
interpretation: The verse uses the metaphor of an 'evil word' being like an 'evil tree' to convey the idea that just as a tree that is uprooted from the earth has no stability and cannot flourish, an evil word has no foundation and cannot bear good fruit. The verse emphasizes the destructive nature of evil words and their inability to bring about any good. The metaphor serves as a warning to those who speak harmful or hurtful words, reminding them of the negative consequences of their actions and the importance of choosing their words carefully.
orig: ومثل كلمة خبيثة كشجرة خبيثة اجتثت من فوق الأرض ما لها من قرار

translation: Allah will establish those who believe, with firm word, in worldly life and in the hereafter. And Allah will misguide the wrongdoers. And Allah will do whatever He wills.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the establishment of believers in both this world and the hereafter, and the misguidance of the wrongdoers. The verse emphasizes the power and sovereignty of Allah, who can do as He wills and establishes those who believe with a firm word. The verse serves as a reminder that Allah will ultimately establish those who have faith and guide them on the right path, while those who are unjust and wrongdoers will be misguided and face the consequences of their actions.
orig: يثبت الله الذين آمنوا بالقول الثابت في الحياة الدنيا وفي الآخرة ويضل الله الظالمين ويفعل الله ما يشاء

translation: Have you not seen those who have exchanged the favor of Allah with disbelief and caused their people to descend into the dwelling place of ruin?
interpretation: The verse speaks about people who have replaced the blessings they received from God with disbelief and led their community to destruction. This verse highlights the ungratefulness of these people and the negative consequences of their actions. It serves as a warning to those who may take their blessings for granted and not appreciate the gifts they have received from God. The verse reminds us to be grateful for what we have and to use our blessings in a way that pleases God, rather than squandering them or using them for negative purposes.
orig: ألم تر إلى الذين بدلوا نعمت الله كفرا وأحلوا قومهم دار البوار

translation: Gehenna (Hell) will be brought near for (the evildoers) to embrace it: what an evil resting-place!
interpretation: The verse describes the fate of evildoers who will be made to approach Hell and embrace it as their eternal resting place. The phrase 'what an evil resting-place' emphasizes the wretchedness and horror of Hell, and serves as a warning to those who are on the path of evil, urging them to repent and turn towards good.
orig: جهنم يصلونها وبئس القرار

translation: And they have set up equals to Allah, that they may lead (men) astray from His path. Say: 'Enjoy (your brief lives)! For soon will you know (your folly)!',
interpretation: The verse speaks about the actions of those who set up equals to God, in order to lead people astray from the right path. The verse instructs the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) to tell them to enjoy their lives, but to remind them that they will soon know the consequences of their actions. The verse serves as a warning to those who associate partners with God, reminding them that their actions will not go unpunished and that they will ultimately be held accountable for their disbelief and misguidance.
orig: وجعلوا لله أندادا ليضلوا عن سبيله قل تمتعوا فإن مصيركم إلى النار

translation: Say to My servants who have believed, 'Establish prayer and give from what We have provided for them, secretly and publicly, before there comes a day when there will be no trade and no friendship.'
interpretation: The verse addresses believers and instructs them to establish prayer and give from their provisions both privately and publicly. The verse emphasizes the importance of practicing one's faith openly and sincerely, and not only in private. The verse also warns of an impending day when there will be no trade or friendship, indicating a time of great difficulty and hardship. This verse serves as a reminder for believers to prioritize their faith and good deeds, and not to be distracted by worldly pursuits and relationships. It encourages believers to prepare for the hereafter by establishing a strong relationship with God and practicing good deeds.
orig: قل لعبادي الذين آمنوا يقيموا الصلاة وينفقوا مما رزقناهم سرا وعلانية من قبل أن يأتي يوم لا بيع فيه ولا خلال

translation: It is Allah who created the heavens and the earth and sent down from the sky water with which He brought forth produce to feed you. And He subjected to you the ships to run in the sea by His command, and He subjected to you the rivers.
interpretation: The verse highlights the power and greatness of Allah as the creator of the heavens and the earth, and the provider of sustenance through the rain and the resulting vegetation. The verse also emphasizes Allah's control and power over the seas and rivers, and the ability of humans to use these resources for transportation and survival. The verse serves as a reminder of Allah's blessings and power, and the need for humans to be grateful and thankful for these blessings.
orig: الله الذي خلق السماوات والأرض وأنزل من السماء ماء فأخرج به من الثمرات رزقا لكم وسخر لكم الفلك لتجري في البحر بأمره وسخر لكم الأنهار

translation: And He has subjected to you the sun and the moon, both diligently pursuing their courses. And He has subjected to you the night and the day.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the control and power that God has over the universe and how He has subjected the sun, the moon, the night, and the day for the benefit of human beings. The verse emphasizes the regularity and predictability of the natural phenomena, which are all under God's control. The verse serves as a reminder of God's power and wisdom, and the blessings that humans receive from the natural world. It also encourages people to reflect on the signs of God in the universe and to be grateful for these blessings.
orig: وسخر لكم الشمس والقمر دائبين وسخر لكم الليل والنهار

translation: And He has given you of all that you asked for. And if you count the blessings of Allah, you will not be able to number them. Indeed, man is unjust and ungrateful.
interpretation: The verse highlights the generosity of God in providing for His people, emphasizing that God has given them all that they have asked for. The verse also points out the limitations of humans in being unable to fully appreciate or count the blessings of God. The verse concludes by noting the unjust and ungrateful nature of humans, serving as a reminder of the need for gratitude and righteousness.
orig: وآتاكم من كل ما سألتموه وإن تعدوا نعمت الله لا تحصوها إن الإنسان لظلوم كفار

translation: And (remember) when Abraham said: 'My Lord, make this city (Makkah) secure, and save me and my sons from worshipping idols.
interpretation: The verse recounts Abraham's prayer to God to protect the city of Makkah and to save him and his descendants from the worship of idols. The verse highlights Abraham's devotion to God and his rejection of idolatry. The verse also emphasizes the significance of Makkah, which would later become the holiest city in Islam, as it was chosen by God to be protected. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of monotheism and the rejection of idolatry in Islam.
orig: وإذ قال إبراهيم رب اجعل هذا البلد آمنا واجنبني وبني أن نعبد الأصنام

translation: My Lord, indeed they have led many people astray. So whoever follows me, then he is of me, and whoever disobeys me - then indeed, You are Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: The verse is a prayer from the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) addressing his Lord, expressing his concern about the people who have been misguided by others. The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) prays for those who follow him, seeking their guidance and protection. He also acknowledges God's forgiveness and mercy towards those who disobey him. The verse highlights the Prophet Muhammad's (peace be upon him) role as a leader and guide for his followers, and his trust in God's mercy and forgiveness towards all of humanity.
orig: رب إنهن أضللن كثيرا من الناس فمن تبعني فإنه مني ومن عصاني فإنك غفور رحيم

translation: Our Lord, I have settled some of my descendants in a barren valley near Your sacred House, our Lord, that they may establish prayer. So make people's hearts incline toward them and provide them with fruit. Perhaps they will be grateful.
interpretation: The verse is a supplication of the Prophet Ibrahim (peace be upon him) to Allah, in which he asks for his descendants to be established in a barren land near the Kaaba (Allah's sacred House) so that they may establish prayer. The verse highlights the importance of prayer and the desire of Prophet Ibrahim for his descendants to be guided towards righteousness. The verse also shows the Prophet's trust in Allah's provision and his hope that his descendants will be grateful for Allah's blessings. The verse can be seen as a reminder to Muslims to establish prayer and to be grateful for Allah's blessings.
orig: ربنا إني أسكنت من ذريتي بواد غير ذي زرع عند بيتك المحرم ربنا ليقيموا الصلاة فاجعل أفئدة من الناس تهوي إليهم وارزقهم من الثمرات لعلهم يشكرون

translation: Our Lord, You know whatever we conceal and whatever we reveal. And whatever is in the hearts (of men). Nothing is hidden from Allah, whether on the earth or in the heaven.
interpretation: The verse is a reminder of God's omniscience and all-encompassing knowledge. It emphasizes that God is aware of everything, both what people conceal and what they reveal, as well as what is hidden in the hearts of men. The verse indicates that nothing is hidden from God, whether on earth or in the heavens, emphasizing the all-knowing and all-seeing nature of God. The verse serves as a reminder that people should be mindful of their actions and intentions, as they are always under the watchful eye of God.
orig: ربنا إنك تعلم ما نخفي وما نعلن وما يخفى على الله من شيء في الأرض ولا في السماء

translation: All praise is to Allah, who has given me, despite my old age, Ishmael and Isaac. Indeed, my Lord is the Hearer of supplication.
interpretation: The verse is a statement of praise and gratitude from the Prophet Ibrahim (Abraham) to Allah for blessing him with two sons, Ishmael and Isaac, in his old age. The verse emphasizes the greatness of Allah and His ability to grant even the seemingly impossible. The verse also highlights the attribute of Allah as the Hearer of all supplications, a reminder that He is always listening and attentive to the needs and prayers of His servants.
orig: الحمد لله الذي وهب لي على الكبر إسماعيل وإسحاق إن ربي لسميع الدعاء

translation: My Lord, make me a maintainer of prayer, and my descendants [also]; our Lord, and accept my supplication.
interpretation: The verse is a supplication to God from a believer, asking for the ability to maintain a consistent prayer practice and for God to accept their prayers. The verse emphasizes the importance of prayer as a means of connecting with God and seeking His guidance and support. The believer is not only seeking these blessings for themselves but also for their descendants, highlighting the importance of passing down a strong faith and connection to God through the generations. The verse can serve as a reminder for Muslims to prioritize their prayer and to seek God's guidance and support in all aspects of their lives.
orig: رب اجعلني مقيم الصلاة ومن ذريتي ربنا وتقبل دعاء

translation: Our Lord, forgive me and my parents and the believers on the Day when the account will be established.
interpretation: The verse is a supplication to God for forgiveness. The speaker is asking for forgiveness for themselves, their parents, and all believers on the Day of Judgment, when all people will be held accountable for their actions. The verse highlights the importance of seeking forgiveness and expressing remorse for one's sins, as well as the importance of intercession for others. It also emphasizes the belief in the Day of Judgment, when all humans will be resurrected and judged according to their deeds, and the importance of faith and belief in God.
orig: ربنا اغفر لي ولوالدي وللمؤمنين يوم يقوم الحساب

translation: And never think that Allah is unaware of what the wrongdoers do. Rather, He only delays them until a Day on which the eyes will stare [in horror].
interpretation: The verse emphasizes that God is aware of the actions of the wrongdoers and warns them that their punishment will come on a specific Day, when the eyes of all will be filled with horror. The verse serves as a reminder that no one can escape God's judgment and that those who commit wrongdoing will ultimately be held accountable for their actions.
orig: ولا تحسبن الله غافلا عما يعمل الظالمون إنما يؤخرهم ليوم تشخص فيه الأبصار

translation: Deaf, dumb, and blind, they will not return (to the right path).
interpretation: The verse describes a group of people who are spiritually lost and disconnected from the truth. They are 'deaf' and 'dumb', meaning they are unwilling or unable to hear or speak the truth. They are also 'blind', meaning they are unable to see the truth or understand the consequences of their actions. The phrase 'they will not return (to the right path)' suggests that these people have strayed far from the path of righteousness and are unlikely to find their way back. The verse serves as a warning to those who ignore or reject the truth, emphasizing the danger of spiritual blindness and the importance of seeking guidance and enlightenment.
orig: مهطعين مقنعي رءوسهم لا يرتد إليهم طرفهم وأفئدتهم هواء

translation: And warn people of the Day when the punishment will come to them, when those who were unjust will say, 'Our Lord, delay us for a short term so that we may respond to Your call and follow the messengers.' Were you not sworn before by your Lord that you would not worship any but Him?'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the Day of Judgment and the punishment that will come to people on that day. It emphasizes the regret and remorse of those who were unjust and disbelievers, who will then wish to have a second chance to follow the messengers and worship only God. However, they will be reminded of their previous covenant with God, in which they had sworn not to worship any but Him. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in disbelief and sin, urging them to repent and follow the right path before it is too late.
orig: وأنذر الناس يوم يأتيهم العذاب فيقول الذين ظلموا ربنا أخرنا إلى أجل قريب نجب دعوتك ونتبع الرسل أولم تكونوا أقسمتم من قبل ما لكم من زوال

translation: And you dwelled in the dwellings of those who wronged themselves, and it became clear to you how We dealt with them, and We made examples for you.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the consequences of the actions of those who wronged themselves, and how the listeners (or readers) of the Qur'an are living in their dwellings. The verse emphasizes the importance of learning from the past and the consequences of wrong actions. The phrase 'it became clear to you' implies that the listeners have witnessed or experienced the consequences of the actions of the previous inhabitants of the dwellings. The verse also highlights the idea of divine justice by saying 'how We dealt with them'. The phrase 'We made examples for you' emphasizes that these stories serve as lessons and examples for the listeners to reflect on their actions and avoid following the path of those who wronged themselves.
orig: وسكنتم في مساكن الذين ظلموا أنفسهم وتبين لكم كيف فعلنا بهم وضربنا لكم الأمثال

translation: They planned their plan, but Allah planned theirs, and Allah is the best of planners. Indeed, [even] if their plan had been such that the mountains could move [i.e., be destroyed] from their places.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the power of Allah's planning and the futility of human plans. The verse emphasizes that no matter how well-laid a plan is, it cannot prevail against the will of Allah. The verse serves as a reminder that human beings should not rely solely on their own abilities and plans, but should instead seek the guidance and will of Allah. The comparison of the human plan to the power needed to move mountains highlights the vast difference in power and ability between humans and Allah, and the importance of seeking Allah's guidance and will.
orig: وقد مكروا مكرهم وعند الله مكرهم وإن كان مكرهم لتزول منه الجبال

translation: Consider not God's promise to His messengers to be delayed. Indeed, God is powerful and able to exact retribution.
interpretation: The verse warns against underestimating God's promise to His messengers, emphasizing that God's promises will be fulfilled in due time. The verse emphasizes God's power and ability to exact retribution against those who defy His messengers. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of heeding God's messengers and the consequences of ignoring their messages.
orig: فلا تحسبن الله مخلف وعده رسله إن الله عزيز ذو انتقام

translation: On the Day when the earth will be replaced by another earth, and the heavens, and they will be manifest to Allah, the One, the Prevailing.
interpretation: The verse describes the Day of Judgment, when the earth and heavens will be replaced and people will be resurrected and brought before Allah. The verse emphasizes the power and control of Allah, who is described as the One and Prevailing, indicating that all of creation is subject to His will and authority. The verse serves as a reminder of the transient nature of this world and the importance of striving for righteousness and accountability in preparation for the Day of Judgment.
orig: يوم تبدل الأرض غير الأرض والسماوات وبرزوا لله الواحد القهار

translation: And you will see the criminals that day bound together in chains.
interpretation: The verse describes the fate of criminals on the Day of Judgment. They will be seen bound together in chains, emphasizing the severity of their punishment. The image of chains suggests that they are completely powerless and unable to escape the consequences of their actions. The verse serves as a warning to those who commit crimes and act unjustly, reminding them of the severe consequences that await them in the afterlife.
orig: وترى المجرمين يومئذ مقرنين في الأصفاد

translation: Their likeness is as the likeness of a people which We sent upon a rainless day, then the blast of punishment overtook them in the forenoon.
interpretation: This verse uses a metaphor to describe a group of people who were destroyed by God's punishment. The metaphor compares them to people who were sent on a day without rain, emphasizing the absence of any warning or mercy before the punishment. The blast of punishment overtook them in the forenoon, indicating that it was sudden and unexpected. The verse serves as a reminder of the swift and severe punishment of God for those who reject His signs and continue in their disobedience.
orig: سرابيلهم من قطران وتغشى وجوههم النار

translation: Surely, Allah will reward each person according to their deeds. Indeed, Allah is swift in account.
interpretation: The verse affirms that Allah will give each person their just deserts, according to the deeds they have done. It emphasizes the swiftness of Allah's reckoning, reminding people that they will be held accountable for their actions in this world. The verse serves as a warning to those who are heedless of their responsibilities, urging them to do good deeds and avoid evil. It also brings comfort to those who have suffered injustice, assuring them that they will be rewarded for their patience and perseverance.
orig: ليجزي الله كل نفس ما كسبت إن الله سريع الحساب

translation: This is a communication to the people, and they are to be warned by it, and that they may know that He is but one God, and that men of understanding may take heed.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of understanding and recognizing the oneness of God. It serves as a warning to the people to take heed and reflect on the message being conveyed. The verse also highlights the role of communication in conveying the message and the importance of understanding and contemplation in receiving it.
orig: هذا بلاغ للناس ولينذروا به وليعلموا أنما هو إله واحد وليذكر أولو الألباب

translation: So these are the verses of the Book and a Qur'an that makes things clear.
interpretation: The verse is emphasizing the clarity and guidance provided by the Qur'an. It is described as 'Book' and 'Qur'an' which both refer to the holy scripture of Islam, which contains guidance and wisdom for those who seek it. The phrase 'makes things clear' indicates that the Qur'an provides a clear understanding of right and wrong, and of how to live a fulfilling and virtuous life. It serves as a reminder that the Qur'an is a source of wisdom and guidance for Muslims.
orig: الر تلك آيات الكتاب وقرآن مبين

translation: Perhaps those who disbelieve would like to be Muslims [i.e. submit to Islam] if they knew the consequences [of disbelief].
interpretation: The verse speaks about the possibility of the disbelievers wanting to become Muslims if they knew the consequences of their disbelief. The verse implies that the disbelievers are unaware of the true nature of their actions and the consequences that follow. It serves as a reminder that the path of disbelief leads to negative outcomes, while the path of Islam leads to success and prosperity. The verse may also be interpreted as an expression of regret from the disbelievers, reflecting their realization of the error of their ways. However, it is important to note that this interpretation is not explicitly stated in the verse, and it is ultimately left to the reader's understanding and interpretation.
orig: ربما يود الذين كفروا لو كانوا مسلمين

translation: Then let them continue in eating and enjoying themselves and let themselves be distracted by [false] hope, and soon they will know.
interpretation: The verse is a warning to those who are heedless of God's signs and continue to indulge in worldly pleasures while ignoring the consequences of their actions. The phrase 'let themselves be distracted by [false] hope' implies that they are putting their trust in something that is unreliable or false, and that they are not preparing for the future or the afterlife. The phrase 'and soon they will know' implies that they will eventually come to understand the reality of their situation, but it will be too late. The verse serves as a reminder that worldly pleasures are fleeting and that true happiness and fulfillment can only be found through obedience to God.
orig: ذرهم يأكلوا ويتمتعوا ويلههم الأمل فسوف يعلمون

translation: And We did not destroy any town except that it had a known decree.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes that the destruction of a town only occurs when it has received a clear and specific decree from God. This decree is known or 'ma'lum' in Arabic, indicating that the people of the town were aware of the consequences of their actions and the impending punishment. The verse suggests that the destruction is not arbitrary or capricious, but rather a result of a clear and just decision by God. This interpretation serves as a reminder of the importance of heeding God's warnings and avoiding the path of sin and transgression.
orig: وما أهلكنا من قرية إلا ولها كتاب معلوم

translation: No nation before them hastened its doom, nor will any nation delay it.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the inevitability of the destruction of nations that have passed away and serves as a reminder that no nation can escape its appointed time of doom. The verse conveys a sense of certainty and finality in the face of divine decree and highlights the futility of attempting to escape or delay the inevitable. It may also serve as a warning to those who are heedless of the signs of the times and the coming of the end, encouraging them to repent and turn back to God before it is too late.
orig: ما تسبق من أمة أجلها وما يستأخرون

translation: And they said, 'You to whom the Reminder has come, indeed you are mad.'
interpretation: The verse describes the disbelievers' response to the prophet Muhammad (pbuh) upon receiving the revelation of the Qur'an. The disbelievers accused the prophet of being crazy or mad, rejecting the message brought by him. This verse highlights the common reaction of people towards prophets and messengers, who were often met with disbelief, rejection, and even hostility. It serves as a reminder that those who bring the message of truth may face opposition and ridicule, but they should remain steadfast in their mission and trust in God's plan.
orig: وقالوا يا أيها الذي نزل عليه الذكر إنك لمجنون

translation: Had you (O Muhammad) brought us the angels, indeed we would have followed you then.
interpretation: The verse is a statement made by the disbelievers of Mecca, expressing their hypothetical willingness to follow the Prophet Muhammad if he had brought them angels as a proof of his prophethood. This verse highlights the superficiality of the disbelievers, as they are willing to follow only if it is convenient for them or if they see a tangible proof, and not based on the truth of the message brought by the Prophet. It also emphasizes the importance of faith and trust in the message and the messenger, rather than relying on signs and wonders as a basis for belief.
orig: لو ما تأتينا بالملائكة إن كنت من الصادقين

translation: The angels do not come down except by the truth, and they do not come down except when ordered.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the descent of angels, emphasizing that they only come down by the truth and at the command of a higher power. This could be interpreted as a reference to the belief that angels are obedient servants of God, carrying out His will and commands without question or hesitation. The verse may also serve as a reminder of the spiritual and supernatural realm that exists beyond the physical world, and that there are powerful and unseen forces at work in the universe.
orig: ما ننزل الملائكة إلا بالحق وما كانوا إذا منظرين

translation: Indeed, it is We who sent down the reminder and indeed, We will be its guardian.
interpretation: The verse affirms that it is God who has revealed the message or reminder (referring to the Qur'an) and that God will also be its protector and guardian. The verse emphasizes the divine origin of the Qur'an and the assurance that it will be preserved and protected from any corruption or alteration. This serves to assure the believers of the authenticity and reliability of the Qur'an, and that it will remain unchanged and uncorrupted for all time.
orig: إنا نحن نزلنا الذكر وإنا له لحافظون

translation: And We had certainly sent (messengers) before you among the former peoples.
interpretation: The verse refers to the fact that God had sent messengers and prophets to the previous nations and communities before the Prophet Muhammad. This verse serves to establish the continuity of the prophetic tradition and the consistency of God's message throughout history. It also emphasizes the importance of the message brought by the previous prophets and the relevance of their teachings for the Prophet Muhammad and his followers. The verse can be seen as a reminder that the message of Islam is not new but rather a continuation of the same divine guidance that was given to humanity since the beginning of time.
orig: ولقد أرسلنا من قبلك في شيع الأولين

translation: And never came there unto them a messenger but they ridiculed him.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the consistent pattern of people rejecting and ridiculing the messengers sent by God. The verse emphasizes the disbelief and rejection of the people towards the messengers, and their refusal to listen and accept the message brought by the messengers. The verse serves as a reminder that the people's rejection of the messengers and their message will not change the fact that God's message will always be delivered, regardless of the people's response.
orig: وما يأتيهم من رسول إلا كانوا به يستهزئون

translation: Thus do We let it (i.e., sin) dwell in the hearts of the transgressors.
interpretation: The verse describes how sin and wrongdoing can take root in the hearts of those who commit transgressions. It suggests that when people engage in unrighteous behavior, they become more susceptible to the influence of sin and are more likely to continue down a path of wrongdoing. This verse serves as a reminder that our actions and choices have a profound impact on our hearts and minds, and that engaging in sin can lead to a hardening of the heart and a loss of guidance.
orig: كذلك نسلكه في قلوب المجرمين

translation: They do not believe in it, though the first generations have already passed away.
interpretation: The verse refers to the disbelief of certain people in a matter of great significance, despite the fact that previous generations have already experienced the consequences of not believing. The verse may be referring to the disbelief in God, the Day of Judgment, or the teachings of the prophets. Regardless of the specific context, the verse emphasizes the importance of faith and the consequences of rejecting the truth. The reference to the passing of the first generations serves as a reminder that the truth has been revealed and experienced before, and that the disbelievers are not the first to reject it. The verse may also serve as a warning to the disbelievers, urging them to reflect on their actions before it is too late.
orig: لا يؤمنون به وقد خلت سنة الأولين

translation: And if We had opened for them a gate from the heaven, they would still have continued in their disbelief.
interpretation: The verse describes the stubbornness and unwillingness of the disbelievers to accept the truth, even in the face of clear and undeniable evidence. The image of God opening a gate from the heavens suggests a miraculous and extraordinary event that would leave no room for doubt. However, the verse suggests that even in such a situation, the disbelievers would still reject the truth and persist in their unbelief. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of faith and the dangers of closed-mindedness and stubbornness.
orig: ولو فتحنا عليهم بابا من السماء فظلوا فيه يعرجون

translation: And they said, 'Our eyes have been dulled. No, we are a people bewitched.'
interpretation: The verse describes the response of some people when they were confronted with a revelation or a sign from God. Instead of accepting the truth, they deny it and make excuses for their disbelief. They claim that their eyes are dulled and that they are under a spell, rather than admitting that they are in the wrong. This verse serves as a reminder of the human tendency to reject what goes against our beliefs and desires, and the importance of being open-minded and receptive to the truth.
orig: لقالوا إنما سكرت أبصارنا بل نحن قوم مسحورون

translation: And We have adorned the lowest heaven with lamps and made them functional for the watchers.
interpretation: The verse describes the beauty and functionality of the stars in the lowest heaven, which have been placed there for the benefit of observers. The 'lamps' (stars) serve both an aesthetic and practical purpose, providing light for those who look up at the night sky. The verse suggests that the stars are not merely decorative, but serve a greater purpose in the divine plan. The verse may also be interpreted as a reminder of the wonders of God's creation, and the intricate design and order of the universe.
orig: ولقد جعلنا في السماء بروجا وزيناها للناظرين

translation: And We have protected it from every accursed devil.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the protection of something, possibly the Qur'an or the revelation, from every devil or evil force that is accursed. The verse emphasizes the importance of the protected entity, and the great care taken by God to preserve it from any harm or corruption. The verse can be interpreted as a reminder of the divine origin of the Qur'an and its infallibility, as well as a warning against any attempts to distort or misinterpret its message.
orig: وحفظناها من كل شيطان رجيم

translation: Except for him who earns death while he is upright, for him will be a clear sign.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the fate of those who are righteous and just at the time of their death. They will be given a clear sign or indication, which could be interpreted as a sign of God's mercy and forgiveness. The verse emphasizes the importance of leading a righteous and just life and the rewards that come with it, even after death. It serves as a source of hope and comfort for those who strive to live a virtuous life and a reminder of the ultimate justice and mercy of God.
orig: إلا من استرق السمع فأتبعه شهاب مبين

translation: And We have spread out the earth, and have placed in it firm mountains, and have caused to grow in it of every beautiful kind.
interpretation: The verse highlights the magnificence of God's creation, specifically the earth and its features. The earth is described as being spread out and having firm mountains placed in it. Furthermore, God has caused every kind of beautiful thing to grow in it. The verse serves as a reminder of God's power and greatness as the creator of all things, and invites the reader to reflect on the beauty and order of the natural world.
orig: والأرض مددناها وألقينا فيها رواسي وأنبتنا فيها من كل شيء موزون

translation: And We made for you in it [the earth] livelihoods and provided for you therein means of sustenance.
interpretation: The verse highlights the blessings that God has bestowed upon humanity by providing them with a livelihood and sustenance through the earth. The verse serves as a reminder of God's generosity and the importance of being grateful for the blessings that one has. It emphasizes the interdependence of human beings on the earth and the importance of taking care of it. The verse also implies a sense of responsibility on the part of human beings to use the resources of the earth in a sustainable and responsible manner.
orig: وجعلنا لكم فيها معايش ومن لستم له برازقين

translation: No creature is there crawling on the earth, nor a bird flying on its two wings, but they are communities like you. We have neglected nothing in the Book. Then unto their Lord they will be gathered.
interpretation: The verse highlights the oneness and unity of God's creation, emphasizing that all creatures, whether they crawl on the earth or fly in the sky, are part of communities similar to humans. The verse also emphasizes that God has recorded and accounted for everything in the Book, indicating that nothing is overlooked or forgotten by God. The verse serves as a reminder of God's omniscience and omnipresence and the ultimate gathering of all creatures before their Lord on the Day of Judgment.
orig: وإن من شيء إلا عندنا خزائنه وما ننزله إلا بقدر معلوم

translation: And We send the winds as pollinators, then We send down water from the sky, and We give you to drink from it. And you are not keepers of its stores.
interpretation: The verse highlights the natural phenomena of the wind and rain, both of which are essential for the growth of plants and the provision of water. The verse emphasizes that it is God who sends down the water from the sky, and that humans are not in control of these resources. The verse serves as a reminder that humans are dependent on God's bounty and that they should be grateful for the resources they have, rather than hoarding or wasting them.
orig: وأرسلنا الرياح لواقح فأنزلنا من السماء ماء فأسقيناكموه وما أنتم له بخازنين

translation: And indeed, it is We who give life and cause death, and We are the inheritors.
interpretation: The verse affirms that it is only God who has the power to give life and cause death. The verse emphasizes God's sovereignty and control over all aspects of life and death. The phrase 'and We are the inheritors' further underscores God's ultimate power and authority, as He will remain after all creation has passed away. The verse serves as a reminder of God's greatness and power, and the need for humans to submit to and worship Him.
orig: وإنا لنحن نحيي ونميت ونحن الوارثون

translation: And We already know the first and the last among you, and We know what you do.
interpretation: The verse affirms God's omniscience and knowledge of all things, past, present, and future. It emphasizes that God knows the actions of all people, both the early believers and those who came later. The verse serves as a reminder of God's all-encompassing knowledge and the accountability of all actions, encouraging believers to live a righteous life and strive for good deeds.
orig: ولقد علمنا المستقدمين منكم ولقد علمنا المستأخرين

translation: But your Lord is surely going to gather them together; indeed, He is wise, all-knowing.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the gathering of people by the Lord on the Day of Judgment. The verse emphasizes that the gathering is certain and that the Lord is all-knowing and wise. This means that the gathering will be done in a just and fair manner, and that nothing will escape the Lord's knowledge. The verse serves as a reminder of the Day of Judgment and the ultimate accountability that people will face before the Lord.
orig: وإن ربك هو يحشرهم إنه حكيم عليم

translation: And We have certainly created man from clay, from sounding clay.
interpretation: The verse highlights the origin of human beings, who were created from clay and water. This description emphasizes the humble origins of human beings, reminding them of their lowly beginnings and their dependence on God. The verse serves as a reminder of the power and ability of God, who can create and shape human beings from seemingly insignificant materials. At the same time, the verse encourages humility and gratitude in human beings, who should remember their dependence on God and their responsibility to use their abilities and talents in the service of God and other human beings.
orig: ولقد خلقنا الإنسان من صلصال من حمإ مسنون

translation: And We created the jinn before from scorching fire.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the creation of the jinn before the creation of humans. It highlights that the jinn were created from a scorching fire, indicating their unique and separate nature from humans. This verse may serve to explain the origin of the jinn, their distinct characteristics, and their role in Islamic theology as spiritual beings that exist alongside humans in the world.
orig: والجان خلقناه من قبل من نار السموم

translation: And when your Lord said to the angels, 'Indeed, I am going to create a human from clay, argil,
interpretation: The verse describes the creation of humans by God, as commanded by God to the angels. The verse emphasizes the unique and special nature of human creation, as God forms humans from clay or argil, a substance that is moldable and changeable. This serves as a reminder of the power and wisdom of God, who has the ability to create something complex and advanced from a simple and basic material. The verse also highlights the role of the angels as observers and executors of God's commands, emphasizing the hierarchy and order in the divine realm.
orig: وإذ قال ربك للملائكة إني خالق بشرا من صلصال من حمإ مسنون

translation: And when I have proportioned him and breathed into him of My spirit, then fall down to him in prostration.
interpretation: This verse speaks of the creation of a human being by God, and how the angels are commanded to prostrate before the newly created being. The verse highlights the role of God in creating human beings and giving them life, as well as the reverence and respect that is due to God and the creation of God. The verse can also be seen as a metaphor for the submission and obedience that is required of all creation towards God, and the importance of recognizing the divine power and wisdom that is inherent in all aspects of life.
orig: فإذا سويته ونفخت فيه من روحي فقعوا له ساجدين

translation: All the angels prostrated themselves together.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the prostration of all the angels in unison. The prostration of the angels is a sign of their submission and obedience to God. The verse emphasizes the unity and harmony of the angels in their worship of God. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of submission and obedience to God, and the unity and harmony that comes from following God's will.
orig: فسجد الملائكة كلهم أجمعون

translation: except Iblis, he refused to be among the prostrate
interpretation: The verse is speaking about the moment when the angels and Satan (referred to as Iblis) were asked to prostrate before Adam. While all the angels obeyed, Iblis refused and was thereafter cursed by God. The verse emphasizes Iblis's arrogance and disobedience, highlighting the importance of submission to God's commands and the consequences of pride and rebellion.
orig: إلا إبليس أبى أن يكون مع الساجدين

translation: He said, 'O Iblis, what prevents you from prostrating yourself with the prostrators?'
interpretation: In this verse, God is addressing the devil, Iblis, who has refused to prostrate himself before Adam, the first human being. The verse highlights the disobedience of Iblis and his rejection of God's command. The question 'what prevents you?' implies that Iblis has no valid reason for his refusal, and that his actions are driven by arrogance and pride. The verse sets the stage for the story of Iblis's downfall and his transformation into the embodiment of evil, and serves as a reminder of the dangers of arrogance and disobedience towards God.
orig: قال يا إبليس ما لك ألا تكون مع الساجدين

translation: He said, 'I will never prostrate myself to a human being that Allah has created from a clot of blood.'
interpretation: The verse is a quote from the disbeliever, Abu Jahl, who refused to submit to the prophet Muhammad (pbuh) and his message. The verse emphasizes Abu Jahl's arrogance and disbelief, as he refuses to prostrate himself before anyone other than Allah. The verse serves as a reminder of the dangers of arrogance and the importance of humility, submission, and obedience to Allah and His messenger (pbuh).
orig: قال لم أكن لأسجد لبشر خلقته من صلصال من حمإ مسنون

translation: He said, 'Get out of her, for you are accused of fornication.'
interpretation: The verse is a statement made by someone, most likely a leader or authority figure, ordering a person to leave a certain place, presumably a city or community. The reason for the expulsion is that the person has been accused of fornication or illicit sexual relations. The verse highlights the social and moral consequences of sexual misconduct and the importance of upholding moral values and standards in a community.
orig: قال فاخرج منها فإنك رجيم

translation: And upon you is curse until the Day of Judgment.
interpretation: The verse is a declaration of a curse upon a specific group of people until the Day of Judgment. The curse is a severe form of punishment and indicates the severity of their actions. The verse emphasizes the permanence of the curse, which will last until the end of time, indicating the gravity of their sins and the unforgiving nature of God's punishment. The verse serves as a reminder of the eternal consequences of one's actions and the importance of living a righteous life.
orig: وإن عليك اللعنة إلى يوم الدين

translation: He said, 'My Lord, show me how You give life to the dead.'
interpretation: The verse is a conversation between the prophet Moses and God. Moses asks God to show him how He gives life to the dead. This verse emphasizes the power of God over life and death, and the inability of humans to fully comprehend the divine abilities. It also highlights the curiosity and desire of Moses to learn more about God's power, and his willingness to be shown the truth.
orig: قال رب فأنظرني إلى يوم يبعثون

translation: He said, 'So indeed, you are of those who look on.'
interpretation: The verse is a continuation of a conversation between an unidentified speaker and the prophet Moses. The speaker is expressing his disbelief or skepticism in Moses' message or abilities. The phrase 'you are of those who look on' can be interpreted as the speaker accusing Moses of being a mere observer or bystander, who talks and preaches but does not take action or make a difference. The verse can be seen as a challenge to the prophet, urging him to prove his worth and mission.
orig: قال فإنك من المنظرين

translation: Till the day of the appointed time.
interpretation: The verse refers to a specific, predestined day of judgment or reckoning, which is known only to God. The meaning of the verse is that the current state of affairs or the present condition of things will continue until the appointed day of judgment or reckoning arrives. This verse may serve as a reminder that all worldly matters are temporary and fleeting, and that ultimate justice and truth will be established on the appointed day of judgment.
orig: إلى يوم الوقت المعلوم

translation: He said, 'My Lord, because You have led me astray, I will make (mischief) beautiful to them on the earth, and I will lead them all astray,'
interpretation: The verse is a quote from the devil, who is speaking to God after being cursed and banished from heaven for refusing to prostrate to Adam. The devil complains that God led him astray, and as a result, he will lead others astray on earth by making sin and disobedience attractive to them. The verse highlights the devil's cunning and deceit, as well as his desire to corrupt and destroy humanity. It serves as a warning to be cautious of the devil's temptations and to seek protection from his schemes through faith and obedience to God.
orig: قال رب بما أغويتني لأزينن لهم في الأرض ولأغوينهم أجمعين

translation: except Your servants from among them the sincere ones
interpretation: The verse is referring to a group of people who are spared from the destruction or punishment that is being described. These people are described as 'Your servants from among them the sincere ones', indicating that they are a subset of the people being discussed, who are devoted and sincere in their faith and service to God. The verse implies that their sincerity and devotion has protected them from the fate of the rest of their community.
orig: إلا عبادك منهم المخلصين

translation: Said He, 'This is a straight path.'
interpretation: The verse is a statement from God, referring to a 'straight path'. The path represents a way of living or a moral conduct. By saying 'this is a straight path', God is indicating that there is a clear and correct way to live, and that this way is known and accessible to people. The verse may serve as a guidance for people, encouraging them to follow the right path and to stay away from deviation and error.
orig: قال هذا صراط علي مستقيم

translation: My servants, you have no authority over them, except those who follow you from the deviators.
interpretation: The verse highlights the limited control that the speaker has over their servants, emphasizing that their authority only extends to those who follow them from among the deviators. This verse can be interpreted as a reminder of the limitations of human power, and the importance of focusing on one's own actions and choices rather than attempting to control others. It may also be seen as a warning against following those who have strayed from the right path, and the importance of staying true to one's beliefs and values.
orig: إن عبادي ليس لك عليهم سلطان إلا من اتبعك من الغاوين

translation: And indeed, Hell is their promised meeting place, all together.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destiny of the unbelievers, who will be gathered in Hell. The phrase 'promised meeting place' emphasizes the certainty of this event, while 'all together' highlights the collective nature of their fate. The verse serves as a warning to those who reject the message of Islam, reminding them that they will ultimately be reunited with the unbelievers in Hell, where they will face God's punishment.
orig: وإن جهنم لموعدهم أجمعين

translation: It has seven gates, and for every gate, a portion has been assigned.
interpretation: The verse speaks about something, possibly a city or a building, that has seven gates. The verse emphasizes the division and allocation of a portion for each gate. This division may imply a specific purpose, usage, or authority for each gate. The verse can be interpreted as a symbolic representation of the order, organization, and regulation within a system or community, where each part has its own function and significance. It may also serve as a reminder of the importance of proper management and distribution of resources and responsibilities.
orig: لها سبعة أبواب لكل باب منهم جزء مقسوم

translation: Indeed, the righteous will be in gardens and rivers.
interpretation: The verse describes the reward that will be given to the righteous in the afterlife. They will reside in gardens and have access to plentiful water sources, symbolizing an abundance of blessings and joy. The verse serves as a source of hope and motivation for those who strive to live a righteous and virtuous life, promising them a beautiful and fulfilling existence in the afterlife.
orig: إن المتقين في جنات وعيون

translation: Enter it [i.e., Paradise] in peace, secure.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the blessed entrance of the righteous believers into Paradise. They are invited to enter it in a state of peace and security, free from any harm or fear. This verse highlights the tranquility and safety that the believers will experience in the Hereafter, in contrast to the turmoil and insecurity of this world. It serves as a source of hope and motivation for the believers to strive for righteousness and piety, in the hope of attaining eternal peace and security in the Hereafter.
orig: ادخلوها بسلام آمنين

translation: And We removed from their hearts the rancor of ignorance, so that they became brethren, one to another, on equal terms.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the removal of the rancor of ignorance from the hearts of people, allowing them to become brethren, one to another, on equal terms. This verse emphasizes the transformative power of knowledge and understanding, which can bring people together and create a sense of unity and equality. The verse suggests that ignorance and misunderstanding can create divisions and animosity between people, but through knowledge and understanding, these divisions can be overcome and replaced with a sense of brotherhood and equality.
orig: ونزعنا ما في صدورهم من غل إخوانا على سرر متقابلين

translation: They will not touch them in it, nor will they be touched, being purified therein.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the state of the believers in Paradise. They will be protected from any harm or punishment, and they will not cause any harm to others. The phrase 'being purified therein' suggests that they will be free from any sin or unrighteousness. The verse highlights the purity and peace that the believers will experience in Paradise, and emphasizes the contrast between the fate of the believers and the unbelievers.
orig: لا يمسهم فيها نصب وما هم منها بمخرجين

translation: Inform My servants that I am the Forgiving, the Merciful.
interpretation: The verse is a message from God, delivered through the prophet, to the servants of God. It emphasizes the merciful and forgiving nature of God, and encourages the servants to seek forgiveness and mercy. The verse can be seen as a reminder of the compassionate and benevolent character of God, and as an invitation for people to turn towards Him, seek His forgiveness and experience His mercy.
orig: نبئ عبادي أني أنا الغفور الرحيم

translation: And My punishment is the painful punishment.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the severity and intensity of God's punishment, describing it as 'the painful punishment'. This statement serves as a warning to those who disbelieve and commit sins, reminding them of the severe consequences of their actions. The verse also highlights God's power and authority, and the inevitability of His punishment for those who defy His commands.
orig: وأن عذابي هو العذاب الأليم

translation: And warn them of Abraham's guest
interpretation: The verse refers to the story of Abraham's guest, who was actually a messenger of God in the form of a man. Abraham showed great hospitality and kindness to the guest, and in return, he received important news and lessons from him. The verse can be interpreted as a command for the Prophet Muhammad to warn the disbelievers about the importance of treating guests with respect and kindness, as they may be messengers of God. It also serves as a reminder that God is aware of our actions and will hold us accountable for our treatment of others, especially those who are vulnerable or in need.
orig: ونبئهم عن ضيف إبراهيم

translation: When they came in to him, they said, 'Peace!' He said, 'Indeed, we are fearful of you.'
interpretation: The verse describes a situation where a group of people came to visit someone and greeted him with 'peace'. However, instead of responding with a similar greeting, the person replied by expressing his fear of them. The verse highlights the unease and tension that existed between the two parties. The interpretation of this verse could be that the person being visited was a prophet or a righteous person who was aware of the enmity and animosity that the people bore towards him. Despite their greeting of 'peace', he remained cautious and vigilant, knowing the true intentions of his visitors.
orig: إذ دخلوا عليه فقالوا سلاما قال إنا منكم وجلون

translation: They said, 'Do not grieve, indeed we will bring you good news of a boy, knowing.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about a group of people addressing someone who is grieving, telling them not to worry because they will bring good news. The good news is that they will bring a boy who is knowledgeable. The verse could be interpreted as a promise of the birth of a wise and intelligent son, or it could be a metaphor for something else that will bring joy and knowledge. The meaning of the verse depends on the context in which it appears in the Qur'an.
orig: قالوا لا توجل إنا نبشرك بغلام عليم

translation: He said, 'Rejoice with me, for my third wife has given birth to a son', so how do you give him the news?
interpretation: The verse relates a conversation where a man announces the birth of his son to a group of people, expressing his joy and expecting them to share in his happiness. The question that follows the announcement, 'so how do you give him the news?' suggests that the people were hesitant or unable to respond with the expected joy, possibly due to some underlying tensions or conflicts. The verse highlights the importance of sharing in each other's joys and sorrows, and the need to respond with empathy and compassion towards others.
orig: قال أبشرتموني على أن مسني الكبر فبم تبشرون

translation: They said, 'We swear by God that we will certainly defeat you, so do not be among the despairing.',
interpretation: The verse describes a situation where the disbelievers are mocking and taunting the believers, claiming that they will be victorious over them. They urge the believers not to be among the despairing, indicating that they believe the outcome of the situation is already determined and that the believers are powerless to change it. The verse serves as a reminder of the challenges and trials that the believers will face in their journey to uphold the truth, and the importance of maintaining faith and hope in the face of adversity.
orig: قالوا بشرناك بالحق فلا تكن من القانطين

translation: And who is more unjust than he who is reminded of the verses of his Lord, then turns away from them? Indeed, We will take retribution from the criminals.
interpretation: The verse highlights the unjust act of those who, despite being reminded of the verses of their Lord, choose to turn away from them. The verse emphasizes the gravity of this act and the certainty of retribution for the criminals. The verse serves as a warning to those who persist in their rejection of God's guidance and message, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the inevitability of divine retribution.
orig: قال ومن يقنط من رحمة ربه إلا الضالون

translation: He said, 'What has prevented you from prostrating yourselves before what I have created with My hands?'
interpretation: The verse is a statement made by a powerful being, most likely a god or a deity, who is questioning a group of messengers or prophets. The being asks them why they have not prostrated themselves before the creation that the being has made with their own hands. This verse suggests a power dynamic between the being and the messengers, with the being holding a position of superiority and demanding respect and submission from the messengers. The verse can be interpreted as a challenge to the messengers' faith and their belief in the supremacy of the being over their own creations.
orig: قال فما خطبكم أيها المرسلون

translation: They said, 'Indeed, we have been sent to a people of criminals.'
interpretation: The verse is a quote from a group of people who are saying that they have been sent to a people who are guilty of committing sins or crimes. The verse could be interpreted as a statement of their mission or purpose, which is to warn or guide the people who are living in sin and injustice. The verse highlights the importance of guidance and the responsibility of those who have been given the task of guiding others towards the right path. The verse could also be seen as a reminder of the consequences of living in sin and the need for repentance and change.
orig: قالوا إنا أرسلنا إلى قوم مجرمين

translation: except the people of Lot - indeed, We saved them all.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the people of Lot, who were saved from destruction while the rest of the towns were destroyed. The verse emphasizes that all the people of Lot were saved, indicating that God's mercy and salvation can extend to an entire community, even in the face of widespread sin and corruption. The verse serves as a reminder of God's mercy and compassion, and of the possibility of redemption and salvation for all, regardless of the sins of the past.
orig: إلا آل لوط إنا لمنجوهم أجمعين

translation: But not her husband - We had given him the good news of a gentle son.
interpretation: The verse speaks about a woman who has been told that she will have a child, but her husband has not received the same news. The verse emphasizes that the husband will not be part of the experience of having a child, as he has not been given the same good news. This verse may be interpreted as a way of highlighting the unique connection between a mother and her child, even before the child is born. It may also serve as a reminder that not everyone will share in the joys and experiences of others, and that each person has their own unique journey in life.
orig: إلا امرأته قدرنا إنها لمن الغابرين

translation: When the messengers came to the family of Lot.
interpretation: The verse describes the arrival of the messengers to the family of Lot. The verse is part of the story of Lot and his people, who were known for their wickedness and immoral acts. The arrival of the messengers signifies the beginning of God's plan to punish the people for their sins. The verse serves to remind the readers of the importance of heeding the warnings of the messengers and the consequences of ignoring them.
orig: فلما جاء آل لوط المرسلون

translation: He said, 'Indeed, you are a people acting corruptly.'
interpretation: The verse relays a statement made by someone (who is not explicitly identified in the verse) addressing a group of people, accusing them of acting corruptly or wickedly. The statement serves to highlight the wrongdoing of the people and sets the stage for the consequences that may follow as a result of their actions.
orig: قال إنكم قوم منكرون

translation: They said, 'No, rather we have come to you with that which they were skeptical about.'
interpretation: The verse is a continuation of a conversation between the believers and the disbelievers. The disbelievers are admitting that they have come to the believers with the very thing they were skeptical about, likely referring to a sign or proof. However, their admission comes too late, as the believers have already been vindicated. The verse serves as a reminder that those who reject the truth and mock the believers will ultimately be proven wrong, and that their disbelief will not save them from the consequences of their actions.
orig: قالوا بل جئناك بما كانوا فيه يمترون

translation: And We (God) have brought you (Muhammad) the truth, and indeed we are truthful.
interpretation: The verse is a confirmation from God that the message brought by the Prophet Muhammad is the truth. The verse emphasizes the certainty and reliability of the message, as God asserts that they are truthful. This verse serves to strengthen the faith of the believers, and to challenge the disbelievers to reflect upon the truth of the message. It also serves as a reminder that the ultimate truth and justice resides with God.
orig: وأتيناك بالحق وإنا لصادقون

translation: So seize you the people of the disbelievers with a penalty of a striking from Us in the morning. And they will not be able to repel it, and follow close upon their backs with soldiers. And they will not be helped.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the punishment of the disbelievers at the hands of God. The verse describes the sudden and overwhelming nature of the punishment, which strikes the people in the morning and leaves them unable to defend themselves. The verse also mentions the pursuit of the disbelievers by soldiers, indicating that their punishment is complete and that they will receive no help or support. The verse serves as a warning to those who reject faith and the truth, emphasizing the inevitability of their punishment and the futility of their resistance.
orig: فأسر بأهلك بقطع من الليل واتبع أدبارهم ولا يلتفت منكم أحد وامضوا حيث تؤمرون

translation: And We decreed for them the punishment of disgrace in this life; thus do We requite the wrongdoers.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the punishment that has been decreed for certain wrongdoers in this life, and it is a punishment of disgrace. This punishment is a consequence of their wrong actions and serves as a form of retribution. The verse reminds us that God does not let wrong actions go unpunished and that those who commit wrongdoers will face the consequences of their actions in this life.
orig: وقضينا إليه ذلك الأمر أن دابر هؤلاء مقطوع مصبحين

translation: And the people of the city came rejoicing.
interpretation: The verse describes the people of a city coming out in a joyful and celebratory manner. The context of the verse is important for understanding the significance of their rejoicing. In the verses preceding this one, it is mentioned that a prophet had warned the people of the city of an impending punishment from God. However, they did not heed his warning and instead continued in their ways of disbelief and sin. The verse can be interpreted as a display of their arrogance and rejection of the prophet's message. Despite the clear signs of God's power and the impending punishment, they remained stubborn and refused to repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who reject God's messengers and continue in their ways of sin, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: وجاء أهل المدينة يستبشرون

translation: He said, 'These are my guests, so do not shame me.',
interpretation: The verse is a statement made by someone who is asking others not to embarrass or shame him in front of his guests. The speaker is requesting that the people around him respect his honor and dignity by treating his guests with hospitality and kindness. The verse highlights the importance of treating guests with respect and dignity, and the negative consequences of failing to do so, such as damaging one's reputation and relationships.
orig: قال إن هؤلاء ضيفي فلا تفضحون

translation: And fear Allah and do not betray trusts.
interpretation: The verse is a command to the believers to fear Allah and to avoid betraying trusts. Betraying trusts can take many forms, such as breaking a promise, being dishonest in business dealings, or failing to fulfill one's responsibilities. By commanding the believers to fear Allah, the verse emphasizes the seriousness of betraying trusts and the consequences of such actions. The verse encourages believers to uphold their responsibilities and to be honest and trustworthy in all their dealings.
orig: واتقوا الله ولا تخزون

translation: They said, 'Have we not forbidden (the use) to ourselves from the worldly ones?'
interpretation: The verse is a statement made by a group of people, expressing their belief that they have distanced themselves from the worldly or materialistic aspects of life. However, the true meaning of their statement is questioned, as it is revealed later in the Surah that they were in fact indulging in such behaviors. The verse serves as a reminder that actions and intentions must be in alignment, and that true piety and faith cannot be achieved through mere words or claims.
orig: قالوا أولم ننهك عن العالمين

translation: They said, 'Indeed, these are our daughters,' if you are truthful.
interpretation: The verse shows a group of people denying the truth of the Prophet Muhammad's message and rejecting the idea that the people he is bringing back to life are their mothers. They instead claim that the people are their daughters, which is a clear attempt to reject the truth. The verse highlights the disbelievers' denial and rejection of the truth, and their unwillingness to accept the reality of resurrection and judgment.
orig: قال هؤلاء بناتي إن كنتم فاعلين
