It is not his responsibility to force them to accept the message or to make them believe. The verse emphasizes the importance of delivering the message clearly and without compromise, and leaving the outcome to God.
orig: فإن تولوا فإنما عليك البلاغ المبين

translation: They recognize the favor of Allah, then they deny it; and most of them are disbelievers.
interpretation: The verse highlights the ungratefulness of some people who, despite recognizing the blessings and favors they have received from Allah, deny and reject them. The verse emphasizes that the majority of these people are disbelievers, indicating their ingratitude and rejection of Allah's blessings as a sign of their disbelief. This verse serves as a reminder to be grateful for the blessings and favors we have received and not to take them for granted, as ingratitude can be a sign of disbelief and a rejection of Allah's mercy.
orig: يعرفون نعمت الله ثم ينكرونها وأكثرهم الكافرون

translation: And [on that day], We will produce from every nation a witness, and We will bring you, [O Muhammad], against these [disbelievers] as a witness. And We have sent down to you the Book as clarification for all things and as guidance and mercy and good tidings for the Muslims.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the Day of Judgment and the role of the Prophet Muhammad as a witness against the disbelievers. The verse also mentions that on that day, a witness will be produced from every nation. This emphasizes the fairness and justice of God on the Day of Judgment. The verse also highlights the importance of the Quran, which serves as a clarification for all things, a guidance, a mercy, and good tidings for the believers. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of belief in God and the accountability of one's actions on the Day of Judgment.
orig: ويوم نبعث من كل أمة شهيدا ثم لا يؤذن للذين كفروا ولا هم يستعتبون

translation: And when those who did wrong see the punishment, it will not be lightened for them, nor will they be given respite.
interpretation: The verse describes the fate of those who have done wrong and are facing punishment. The punishment will not be reduced or alleviated for them, and they will not be granted any respite or delay. The verse emphasizes the severity of the consequences for those who commit wrongdoings and act unjustly, and the lack of any opportunity for them to escape or make amends. It serves as a warning for people to avoid wrongdoing and strive for justice, as the consequences of their actions are inevitable and severe.
orig: وإذا رأى الذين ظلموا العذاب فلا يخفف عنهم ولا هم ينظرون

translation: And when those who associated others with Allah see their 'associates', they say, 'Our Lord, these are our associates whom we used to invoke instead of You.' But Allah will say, 'Indeed, you are liars.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the Day of Judgment and the fate of those who associated partners with Allah. When these people see their false gods, they will admit that they used to worship them instead of Allah. However, Allah will declare that they are liars, as their false gods will not be able to help them in any way. The verse serves as a warning to those who associate partners with Allah, emphasizing the futility of worshiping false gods and the certainty of Allah's judgment.
orig: وإذا رأى الذين أشركوا شركاءهم قالوا ربنا هؤلاء شركاؤنا الذين كنا ندعو من دونك فألقوا إليهم القول إنكم لكاذبون

translation: And cast to Allah upon that day the dispute, and depart from them; indeed, they are, in [their] dispute, unaware.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the Day of Judgment, when people will cast their disputes and differences before God. The verse highlights the fact that people will then realize the truth and the falsehood of their previous beliefs and arguments, and that they will be powerless to change the outcome. The verse also implies that people should not be too attached to their own opinions and views, and should be humble and open-minded in their search for truth.
orig: وألقوا إلى الله يومئذ السلم وضل عنهم ما كانوا يفترون

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieved and averted [people] from the path of Allah and opposed the Messenger after guidance had become clear to them - they will not harm Allah in the least, and He will make their deeds void.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the severe punishment for those who disbelieve in Allah, reject His path, and oppose the Messenger, even after guidance has been made clear to them. The verse emphasizes that the actions of such people will have no impact on Allah and that their deeds will be made void, meaning they will not be rewarded for any good deeds they may have done. This verse serves as a warning to those who reject the message of Islam and resist the guidance of the Prophet Muhammad, reminding them of the severe consequences of their actions and the futility of opposing Allah's will.
orig: الذين كفروا وصدوا عن سبيل الله زدناهم عذابا فوق العذاب بما كانوا يفسدون

translation: And on the day when We raise up a witness from every nation, then no permission will be given to intercessors, and no one will be allowed to speak, except for him whom the All-Merciful permits, and (on that day) We will raise you as a witness over these (people). And We have sent down to you the Book as a clarification of all things and as a guidance and a mercy and good news for the Muslims.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the Day of Judgment, when a witness from every nation will be raised. On that day, no intercession will be accepted, and no one will be allowed to speak, except for those who are given permission by the All-Mighty. The verse also mentions that the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) will be raised as a witness over the people. Furthermore, the verse highlights the significance of the Quran, which has been sent down as a clarification of all things, a guidance, a mercy, and good news for the believers.
orig: ويوم نبعث في كل أمة شهيدا عليهم من أنفسهم وجئنا بك شهيدا على هؤلاء ونزلنا عليك الكتاب تبيانا لكل شيء وهدى ورحمة وبشرى للمسلمين

translation: Indeed, Allah orders justice and goodness and giving to relatives and forbids immorality and badness and oppression. He admonishes you so that perhaps you will be reminded.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of living a righteous life by following the commands of Allah. It highlights the importance of justice, kindness, and maintaining ties with relatives. At the same time, it forbids immoral and wrong actions and oppression. The verse serves as a reminder to the people, urging them to remember and follow the teachings of Allah so that they can lead a successful and fulfilling life.
orig: إن الله يأمر بالعدل والإحسان وإيتاء ذي القربى وينهى عن الفحشاء والمنكر والبغي يعظكم لعلكم تذكرون

translation: And fulfill the covenant of Allah when you have agreed, and do not break the covenant after its confirmation, and indeed, Allah will account for what you do.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of fulfilling covenants and honoring agreements. It warns against breaking a covenant after it has been confirmed and reminds the listeners that God is aware of their actions. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of honesty, integrity, and trustworthiness in all aspects of life, and the consequences of violating these principles.
orig: وأوفوا بعهد الله إذا عاهدتم ولا تنقضوا الأيمان بعد توكيدها وقد جعلتم الله عليكم كفيلا إن الله يعلم ما تفعلون

translation: And be not like those who broke the promise with God after having pledged to it, and cut off their relations, making their religion a means of seeking the worldly gain. They will be overtaken by God's punishment, and God is severe in punishment.
interpretation: The verse warns against breaking promises made to God and against using religion as a means of personal gain. Those who do so will be punished by God, who is severe in punishment. The verse emphasizes the importance of keeping one's word, especially when it comes to commitments made to God, and the dangers of using religion for selfish purposes. It serves as a reminder that God sees and knows all actions, and that those who act unjustly will be held accountable for their deeds on the Day of Judgment.
orig: ولا تكونوا كالتي نقضت غزلها من بعد قوة أنكاثا تتخذون أيمانكم دخلا بينكم أن تكون أمة هي أربى من أمة إنما يبلوكم الله به وليبينن لكم يوم القيامة ما كنتم فيه تختلفون

translation: And if Allah had willed, He could have made you one nation [united in religion], but He causes to stray whom He wills and guides whom He wills. And you will surely be questioned about what you used to do.
interpretation: The verse highlights the power of Allah, who has the ability to make all of humanity follow one religion, but instead chooses to guide or misguide whoever He wills. The verse emphasizes the idea that each individual is responsible for their own actions, and will be questioned and held accountable for them in the afterlife. The verse encourages Muslims to focus on their own actions, and not to be concerned with the actions of others. It also serves as a reminder that ultimately, the fate of each person is in the hands of Allah.
orig: ولو شاء الله لجعلكم أمة واحدة ولكن يضل من يشاء ويهدي من يشاء ولتسألن عما كنتم تعملون

translation: And do not take [as friends] your fathers' enemies and your own enemies, or you will become like them. And whoever of you does that has indeed strayed from the straight path.
interpretation: The verse warns against taking enemies as friends or allies, as doing so will lead one to become like them. This is a clear prohibition and a serious warning against befriending those who are hostile to Islam and Muslims. The verse emphasizes the importance of maintaining a clear distinction between friends and enemies, and staying loyal to the Muslim community and the path of God. Those who fail to heed this warning and associate with enemies of Islam have indeed strayed from the straight path and will face severe punishment.
orig: ولا تتخذوا أيمانكم دخلا بينكم فتزل قدم بعد ثبوتها وتذوقوا السوء بما صددتم عن سبيل الله ولكم عذاب عظيم

translation: And do not sell Allah's covenant for a small price; indeed, with Allah is (the) best for you, if only you knew.
interpretation: The verse warns against undervaluing and disregarding Allah's covenant, represented here as a valuable and sacred trust. The verse advises against selling or betraying this covenant for a small or insignificant price or gain. Instead, the verse emphasizes that Allah has the best and most beneficial outcomes for His servants, if only they were aware. The verse encourages believers to uphold their covenant with Allah and to value and respect it as a sacred duty, rather than compromising it for worldly gains.
orig: ولا تشتروا بعهد الله ثمنا قليلا إنما عند الله هو خير لكم إن كنتم تعلمون

translation: Whatever you have will end, but what Allah has is lasting. And We will surely give those who were patient their reward in the best way. [Qur'an 16:96]
interpretation: The verse highlights the temporary nature of worldly possessions and the eternal nature of God's blessings. The verse reminds people that everything they have will come to an end, but what God has is everlasting. This is a reminder to be mindful of one's actions and to strive for patience and righteousness. The verse also promises that those who are patient and persevere in their faith will be rewarded in the best way. This is a message of hope and encouragement for the believers, emphasizing the importance of patience and perseverance in the face of adversity.
orig: ما عندكم ينفد وما عند الله باق ولنجزين الذين صبروا أجرهم بأحسن ما كانوا يعملون

translation: Whoever does righteousness, whether male or female, while he is a believer - We will surely cause him to live a good life, and We will surely give them their reward [in the Hereafter] according to the best of what they used to do.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the reward for those who do righteous deeds, regardless of their gender, as long as they are believers. The verse promises a good life in this world and the best reward in the hereafter for those who do good deeds. This verse encourages believers to strive for righteousness and to have faith, as they will be rewarded for their efforts in this life and the next.
orig: من عمل صالحا من ذكر أو أنثى وهو مؤمن فلنحيينه حياة طيبة ولنجزينهم أجرهم بأحسن ما كانوا يعملون

translation: So when you recite the Qur'an, seek refuge in Allah from the accursed devil.
interpretation: The verse instructs the reader of the Qur'an to seek protection from Satan before reciting the Qur'an. This highlights the importance of being in a state of purity and mindfulness when approaching the sacred text, as well as the recognition of the presence of evil forces that may try to distract or mislead the believer. By seeking refuge in Allah, the believer is reaffirming their faith and dependence on God, and is also protecting themselves from the negative influence of Satan.
orig: فإذا قرأت القرآن فاستعذ بالله من الشيطان الرجيم

translation: He has no authority over those who believe and put their trust in their Lord.
interpretation: The verse asserts that the person referred to in the previous verses (often interpreted as the devil or Satan) has no power or authority over those who have faith in God and place their trust in Him. This verse is often seen as a source of comfort and strength for believers, reminding them that they are protected from the forces of evil as long as they remain steadfast in their faith and trust in God.
orig: إنه ليس له سلطان على الذين آمنوا وعلى ربهم يتوكلون

translation: His authority is only over those who associate [others with Him] and those who submit to his rule.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the authority of someone (it is not specified who this person is), which is limited to those who associate others with God (polytheists) and those who submit to his rule. The verse suggests that the person's authority is not universal or absolute, but rather limited to certain groups of people who follow a certain belief or submit to his rule. The verse can be interpreted as a reminder that no one has absolute authority or power, and that all authority comes from God, who is the ultimate authority.
orig: إنما سلطانه على الذين يتولونه والذين هم به مشركون

translation: And when We substitute one sign for another, and Allah knows best what He reveals, they say: You are only a forger. Nay, but most of them do not know.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the signs of God and how they are replaced or changed. The verse emphasizes that only God knows the true meaning and significance of these signs. However, when the people see a new sign, they accuse the speaker of fabricating lies. The verse highlights the ignorance of the people, as they do not truly understand the meaning of the signs and are quick to judge and criticize. The verse reminds the reader to have faith in God and not to be swayed by the opinions of others.
orig: وإذا بدلنا آية مكان آية والله أعلم بما ينزل قالوا إنما أنت مفتر بل أكثرهم لا يعلمون

translation: Say, 'The Holy Spirit has brought it down by permission of your Lord from truth to make firm those who believe and as a guidance and good news for the Muslims.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the revelation of the Qur'an through the Holy Spirit, as a means of strengthening the faith of the believers, providing guidance, and bringing glad tidings to the Muslims. The verse emphasizes the divine origin of the Qur'an, as it was brought down by the Holy Spirit with the permission of God, and its role in guiding and strengthening the Muslim community.
orig: قل نزله روح القدس من ربك بالحق ليثبت الذين آمنوا وهدى وبشرى للمسلمين

translation: And indeed We know that they say, 'It is only a human being who teaches him.' The tongue to which they refer is foreign, while this (Qur'an) is a clear Arabic tongue.
interpretation: The verse addresses the claim of the disbelievers that the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) is merely a human being who was taught the Qur'an by another human. The verse rejects this claim by distinguishing between the foreign tongue that the disbelievers attribute to the origin of the Qur'an and the clear Arabic tongue in which it was revealed. The verse emphasizes the divine origin of the Qur'an and the Prophet's role as a messenger, rather than a student of a foreign language. It also highlights the eloquence and clarity of the Arabic language in which the Qur'an was revealed, which served as a sign of its divine origin and a means of conveying its message to the people.
orig: ولقد نعلم أنهم يقولون إنما يعلمه بشر لسان الذي يلحدون إليه أعجمي وهذا لسان عربي مبين

translation: Indeed, those who do not believe in the signs of Allah will not be guided, and for them is a painful punishment.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of believing in the signs of God, which refer to His messages and revelations. Those who do not believe in these signs will not be guided by God, meaning that they will not find the right path and will continue to live in misguidance. Moreover, the verse warns of a painful punishment for such people. This punishment is a consequence of their disbelief and rejection of God's signs. The verse serves as a reminder for people to reflect on the signs of God and to believe in them, as this is the path that leads to guidance and success in this life and the hereafter.
orig: إن الذين لا يؤمنون بآيات الله لا يهديهم الله ولهم عذاب أليم

translation: Only those who do not believe in the signs of God fabricate lies, and those are the liars.
interpretation: The verse identifies the people who fabricate lies as those who do not believe in the signs of God. The verse makes a clear connection between disbelief and lying, suggesting that those who reject God's signs and messages are more likely to engage in deceit and falsehood. The verse serves as a warning against lying and emphasizes the importance of faith in God and acceptance of His signs as a means of avoiding falsehood and deception.
orig: إنما يفتري الكذب الذين لا يؤمنون بآيات الله وأولئك هم الكاذبون

translation: Whoever disbelieves in Allah after his belief except one who is forced [to do so] and whose heart is still content with faith - but whoever of them willingly opens his heart to disbelief, upon them is the wrath of Allah, and for them is a great punishment.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the punishment for those who disbelieve in Allah after initially having faith, except for those who are forced to recant their faith and whose hearts remain steadfast in their belief. However, those who willingly and openly embrace disbelief face the wrath of Allah and a severe punishment. The verse serves as a warning to those who are considering abandoning their faith, emphasizing the severe consequences of such a decision and the importance of maintaining a strong and unwavering belief in Allah.
orig: من كفر بالله من بعد إيمانه إلا من أكره وقلبه مطمئن بالإيمان ولكن من شرح بالكفر صدرا فعليهم غضب من الله ولهم عذاب عظيم

translation: That is because they preferred the life of this world over the Hereafter and because God does not guide the disbelieving people.
interpretation: The verse explains the reason for the punishment of certain towns, which is their preference for the life of this world over the Hereafter. This preference indicates a lack of faith and a disregard for God's commands. The second part of the verse emphasizes that God does not guide those who reject His message and choose to live in disbelief. The verse highlights the importance of prioritizing the Hereafter and having faith in God in order to avoid punishment and attain salvation.
orig: ذلك بأنهم استحبوا الحياة الدنيا على الآخرة وأن الله لا يهدي القوم الكافرين

translation: Those are the ones upon whom Allah has placed curse of disgrace, and they will have an eternal punishment because they took the signs of Allah lightly.
interpretation: The verse speaks about a group of people who have been cursed by Allah due to their disbelief and rejection of His signs. They are described as being heedless or negligent, and as a result, they will face a severe and everlasting punishment. The verse serves as a warning to those who reject the signs and messages of Allah, emphasizing the severe consequences of their actions and the importance of paying heed to the signs of Allah.
orig: أولئك الذين طبع الله على قلوبهم وسمعهم وأبصارهم وأولئك هم الغافلون

translation: Surely, they will be the losers in the Hereafter.
interpretation: The verse asserts that those who are being referred to will be the ultimate losers in the Hereafter. The interpretation of this verse could be understood in the context of the preceding verses, which may be discussing the fate of those who deny the signs of God or those who are ungrateful for God's blessings. The verse emphasizes the significance of the Hereafter and the consequences of one's actions in this life, reminding believers to be mindful of their responsibilities towards God and to strive for success in the Hereafter.
orig: لا جرم أنهم في الآخرة هم الخاسرون

translation: But indeed, for those who have been patient after being wronged - surely, your Lord, after that, is [aware of their situation and] Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the reward for those who have been patient after facing oppression and injustice. Despite the challenges they faced, these individuals remained steadfast and endured the difficulties they encountered. The verse highlights the compassionate nature of God, who is aware of their situation and is ready to forgive and show mercy to them. The verse serves as a source of comfort and hope for those who are facing hardships and oppression, reminding them that God is aware of their situation and will reward them for their patience and perseverance.
orig: ثم إن ربك للذين هاجروا من بعد ما فتنوا ثم جاهدوا وصبروا إن ربك من بعدها لغفور رحيم

translation: A day when every soul will come disputing for itself, and every soul will be paid in full for what it has done, and they will not be wronged.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the Day of Judgment, when every soul will come to account for its actions and receive its just deserts. The verse emphasizes the fairness and accuracy of the judgement, as every soul will be paid in full for what it has done, without any injustice or wrongdoing. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of good deeds and the accountability of every individual for their actions. It also conveys the message that no one will be treated unfairly on the Day of Judgment, as every soul will receive what it deserves.
orig: يوم تأتي كل نفس تجادل عن نفسها وتوفى كل نفس ما عملت وهم لا يظلمون

translation: And Allah sets forth a parable for those who disbelieve: the town which We destroyed though it was unjust, and We set forth for it a time of famine and a warning against every ill, so that it might believe.
interpretation: The verse presents a parable for those who disbelieve, using the example of a town that was destroyed despite its initial state of peace and prosperity. The town was unjust and rejected the blessings of Allah, leading to its destruction. The verse emphasizes the warning signs and the time of famine that were given to the town, as a means for it to repent and believe. However, despite these warnings, the town continued to engage in wrongdoing, ultimately leading to its destruction. The verse serves as a reminder of the consequences of disbelief and the importance of heeding the warnings and blessings of Allah.
orig: وضرب الله مثلا قرية كانت آمنة مطمئنة يأتيها رزقها رغدا من كل مكان فكفرت بأنعم الله فأذاقها الله لباس الجوع والخوف بما كانوا يصنعون

translation: And indeed there came to them a Messenger from among them, but they denied him; so the punishment seized them while they were unjust.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the rejection of a Messenger who was sent to a group of people. Despite being one of them, they denied and rejected him, leading to their punishment. This verse highlights the consequences of rejecting the message and the messenger, and the role of injustice in bringing about divine punishment. It serves as a warning to those who reject the truth and continue to commit injustices.
orig: ولقد جاءهم رسول منهم فكذبوه فأخذهم العذاب وهم ظالمون

translation: And eat of the good and lawful things that Allah has provided for you and give thanks to Allah if it is Him that you worship.
interpretation: The verse instructs believers to eat of the good and lawful things that God has provided for them, and to give thanks to God for His blessings. The verse emphasizes the importance of gratitude and obedience to God, and the importance of consuming only what is pure and permissible. The verse also reminds believers of the ultimate purpose of their existence, which is to worship God. By following this command, believers can lead a life that is pleasing to God and in accordance with His will.
orig: فكلوا مما رزقكم الله حلالا طيبا واشكروا نعمت الله إن كنتم إياه تعبدون

translation: Forbidden to you is that which dies of itself, and blood, and flesh of swine, and that on which any other name than that of Allah has been invoked, and the strangled (animal) and that beaten to death, and that killed by a fall and that killed by being smitten with the horn, and that which wild beasts have eaten, except what you slaughter, and what is sacrificed on stones set up (for idols) and that you divide by the arrows; that is a transgression. This day have those who disbelieve despaired of your religion, so fear them not, and fear Me. This day have I perfected for you your religion and completed My favor on you and chosen for you Islam as a religion; but whoever is compelled by hunger, not inclining willfully to sin, then surely Allah is Forgiving, Merciful.
interpretation: The verse outlines various types of food that are forbidden for Muslims to consume, including carrion, blood, pork, and animals slaughtered in the name of other than Allah. The verse also forbids animals that have been strangled, beaten to death, killed by a fall, or gored by a horn, as well as animals that have been partially eaten by wild animals. However, the verse provides an exception for animals that have been slaughtered and sacrificed properly. The verse ends by emphasizing the importance of following these dietary laws, and the mercy and forgiveness of Allah towards those who may be compelled by hunger to eat forbidden food.
orig: إنما حرم عليكم الميتة والدم ولحم الخنزير وما أهل لغير الله به فمن اضطر غير باغ ولا عاد فإن الله غفور رحيم

translation: And do not say, concerning that which your tongues assert of untruth, 'This is lawful and this is unlawful,' that you may invent a lie against Allah. Indeed, those who invent a lie against Allah will not succeed.
interpretation: The verse warns against lying and twisting the truth, particularly in matters related to what is permissible and what is forbidden. It emphasizes the seriousness of speaking untruths and making false claims, especially when they are attributed to God. The verse makes it clear that those who invent lies about God will not prosper or be successful. The verse encourages honesty, integrity, and a commitment to the truth, particularly in matters of religious significance and authority.
orig: ولا تقولوا لما تصف ألسنتكم الكذب هذا حلال وهذا حرام لتفتروا على الله الكذب إن الذين يفترون على الله الكذب لا يفلحون

translation: A little amusement, and then they have a painful punishment.
interpretation: The verse describes the fate of those who indulge in temporary and fleeting pleasures, only to be met with severe punishment. The verse highlights the transient nature of worldly enjoyments, which are soon followed by divine retribution. The interpretation of this verse can be understood as a warning to those who prioritize their immediate desires and pleasures over righteousness and obedience to God. It serves as a reminder that the consequences of neglecting one's duties towards God and engaging in sinful behavior can lead to severe and unavoidable punishment.
orig: متاع قليل ولهم عذاب أليم

translation: And upon those who were guided, We have imposed restrictions on what We have recounted to you before, and wronged them not, but they wronged themselves.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the restrictions imposed on those who were guided, referring to the previous warnings and teachings that were given to them. The verse emphasizes that God did not wrong them, but they wronged themselves through their actions and choices. The verse serves as a reminder that every individual is responsible for their own actions and that there will be consequences for those who choose to go against the guidance provided to them.
orig: وعلى الذين هادوا حرمنا ما قصصنا عليك من قبل وما ظلمناهم ولكن كانوا أنفسهم يظلمون

translation: But for he who repents after his wrongdoing and reforms, indeed, your Lord thereafter is Forgiving, Merciful.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the opportunity for forgiveness and mercy from God for those who have done wrong but then repent and reform. The verse emphasizes that this forgiveness and mercy is available for those who sincerely regret their past actions and make a conscious effort to change their ways. The verse serves as a message of hope for those who have strayed from the right path, reminding them that no matter what they have done, they can always turn back to God and seek His forgiveness and mercy.
orig: ثم إن ربك للذين عملوا السوء بجهالة ثم تابوا من بعد ذلك وأصلحوا إن ربك من بعدها لغفور رحيم

translation: Indeed, Abraham was a leader who was devoutly obedient to Allah, inclining toward truth, and he was not of the polytheists.
interpretation: The verse highlights the exemplary character of the prophet Abraham, who was a devout and obedient servant of God. The verse emphasizes Abraham's commitment to the truth and his rejection of polytheism. The verse serves as a model for believers, encouraging them to follow the example of Abraham and to be steadfast in their faith and commitment to God.
orig: إن إبراهيم كان أمة قانتا لله حنيفا ولم يك من المشركين

translation: Thankful are We to Him who has guided us to this [Islamic] way, ever true.
interpretation: The verse is a statement of gratitude from the believers for being guided to the right path, which is Islam. The verse emphasizes the importance of guidance and the blessing of being on the right path. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of gratitude and appreciation for the guidance that one has received, and a recognition of the fact that it is ultimately through God's mercy that one is able to find and follow the right path.
orig: شاكرا لأنعمه اجتباه وهداه إلى صراط مستقيم

translation: And We granted them good things in this world, and indeed, in the hereafter they are among the righteous.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the blessings that God bestows upon certain people in this world and how these people will be among the righteous in the hereafter. The verse highlights the connection between the blessings received in this world and the rewards in the hereafter. It emphasizes the importance of using the blessings and opportunities given in this world in a righteous and virtuous manner, as it will lead to a positive outcome in the hereafter. The verse serves as a reminder that the ultimate goal should be to strive for righteousness and earn a place among the righteous in the hereafter.
orig: وآتيناه في الدنيا حسنة وإنه في الآخرة لمن الصالحين

translation: Then We revealed to you to follow the religion of Abraham, the monotheist; and he was not of the polytheists.
interpretation: The verse instructs the Prophet Muhammad to follow the religion of Abraham, who was a monotheist and not a polytheist. This suggests that the true religion is the one that was practiced by Abraham, which is characterized by the belief in one God. The verse emphasizes the importance of following the right path and staying away from polytheism and other false beliefs. It also highlights the continuity of the message of monotheism from Abraham to the Prophet Muhammad. The verse encourages the believers to follow the example of Abraham and to establish a strong connection with the one true God.
orig: ثم أوحينا إليك أن اتبع ملة إبراهيم حنيفا وما كان من المشركين

translation: He has only forbidden you what dies of itself, and blood, and the flesh of swine, and that which is slaughtered as a sacrifice for other than Allah; but whoever is forced [by necessity], neither desiring [it] nor transgressing [its limit], then indeed, your Lord is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse explains that the prohibition of eating certain types of food, such as animals that die of natural causes, blood, pork, and animals sacrificed to other than Allah, is intended for those who have differing opinions about these matters. The verse reminds that ultimately, it is Allah who will judge between them on the Day of Judgment regarding these disputes. The verse emphasizes the importance of adhering to these prohibitions, except in cases of necessity, and seeking forgiveness and mercy from Allah in such situations.
orig: إنما جعل السبت على الذين اختلفوا فيه وإن ربك ليحكم بينهم يوم القيامة فيما كانوا فيه يختلفون

translation: Invite to the way of your Lord with wisdom and good instruction, and argue with them in a way that is best. Indeed, your Lord is most knowing of who has strayed from His way, and He is most knowing of those who are guided.
interpretation: The verse encourages the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) to invite people to the path of God using wisdom, good admonition, and best arguments. It highlights the importance of using a gentle and respectful approach when calling people to Islam. The verse also reminds the Prophet that the ultimate outcome of people's guidance or misguidance is known only to God, who is the most knowledgeable. The verse serves as a reminder to Muslims to be patient, compassionate, and wise when calling others to Islam, and to trust in God's ultimate wisdom and justice.
orig: ادع إلى سبيل ربك بالحكمة والموعظة الحسنة وجادلهم بالتي هي أحسن إن ربك هو أعلم بمن ضل عن سبيله وهو أعلم بالمهتدين

translation: And if you punish, then punish with the like of what you were afflicted with. But if you are patient, it is better for the patient.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the principle of just retribution, stating that if one is punished, they should respond with a punishment that is equal in severity. However, the verse also encourages patience and self-restraint, suggesting that it is a better option for those who possess such qualities. This verse can be interpreted as a guidance for dealing with harm and injustice, emphasizing the importance of responding with fairness and restraint, while also acknowledging the value of patience and perseverance in the face of adversity.
orig: وإن عاقبتم فعاقبوا بمثل ما عوقبتم به ولئن صبرتم لهو خير للصابرين

translation: And be patient and your patience is only by God and do not grieve over them and do not be in distress over what they plan.
interpretation: The verse speaks about patience and trust in God during times of hardship. It reminds the believer that patience can only be achieved through God's help and that they should not be distressed by the plans of their enemies. The verse is a source of comfort and strength for the believer, encouraging them to remain steadfast in their faith and to leave the outcome of their situation in God's hands.
orig: واصبر وما صبرك إلا بالله ولا تحزن عليهم ولا تك في ضيق مما يمكرون

translation: Indeed, Allah is with those who fear Him and those who are doers of good.
interpretation: The verse highlights the special relationship between Allah and those who have taqwa (fear and consciousness of Allah) and those who do good deeds. The verse is a source of comfort and reassurance for the believers, reminding them that Allah is always with them, supporting and guiding them. The verse also serves as a motivation for the believers to strive for righteousness and to do good deeds, as they will be rewarded by Allah's presence and support. The verse also emphasizes the importance of having taqwa and doing good deeds as a means of attaining Allah's pleasure and nearness.
orig: إن الله مع الذين اتقوا والذين هم محسنون

translation: Exalted is He who took His servant by night from the Sacred Mosque to the Remote Mosque of which We have blessed the surroundings, so that We may show him of Our signs. Indeed, He is the Hearing, the Seeing.
interpretation: This verse speaks about the miraculous night journey of the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, from the Sacred Mosque in Mecca to the Remote Mosque, which is believed to be the Al-Aqsa Mosque in Jerusalem. The verse emphasizes the power and greatness of God, who is capable of taking his servant on such a journey. The verse also highlights the significance of the journey, as it was a means for the Prophet to witness some of the signs of God. The verse serves as a reminder of God's power and knowledge, and of the special status of the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him.
orig: سبحان الذي أسرى بعبده ليلا من المسجد الحرام إلى المسجد الأقصى الذي باركنا حوله لنريه من آياتنا إنه هو السميع البصير

translation: And We gave Moses the Book and made it a guidance for the Children of Israel: 'Take not other than Me as guardians.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the giving of the Book (Torah) to Moses and its function as a guidance for the Children of Israel. The verse emphasizes the unique and exclusive role of God as the guardian and protector of the Israelites. The command 'Take not other than Me as guardians' is a prohibition against associating any other deity or power with God, and a reminder of the unique and all-encompassing nature of God's protection and guidance.
orig: وآتينا موسى الكتاب وجعلناه هدى لبني إسرائيل ألا تتخذوا من دوني وكيلا

translation: Descendants of those whom We carried with Noah. Indeed, he was a grateful servant.
interpretation: The verse refers to the descendants of the people who were saved with the prophet Noah during the great flood. It highlights that Noah was a grateful servant of God. The verse is often understood as a reminder of God's mercy towards those who are grateful for His blessings and follow His commands.
orig: ذرية من حملنا مع نوح إنه كان عبدا شكورا

translation: And We decreed to the Children of Israel in the Scripture, 'You shall spread corruption in the land twice, and you shall become exceedingly haughty.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about a decree that God made against the Children of Israel in the Scripture. The decree states that the Children of Israel will commit corruption twice in the land and will become excessively arrogant. The verse serves as a reminder of the consequences of corruption and arrogance, highlighting the fact that these actions are not only harmful to others but also to the perpetrators themselves. It may also serve as a warning to those who are following a similar path, urging them to change their ways before it is too late.
orig: وقضينا إلى بني إسرائيل في الكتاب لتفسدن في الأرض مرتين ولتعلن علوا كبيرا

translation: But when the promise of the first of the two came, We sent against you Our servants, possessors of overwhelming power, and they entered the very midst of your homes; and the promise was fulfilled.
interpretation: The verse describes a situation where God's punishment was brought upon a group of people as a result of their actions. When the promised punishment arrived, God sent powerful servants to carry out the punishment. These servants were able to enter the homes of the people, signifying the complete and utter defeat of the people. The verse emphasizes the power and authority of God's servants and the inevitability of God's punishment for those who commit wrongdoing.
orig: فإذا جاء وعد أولاهما بعثنا عليكم عبادا لنا أولي بأس شديد فجاسوا خلال الديار وكان وعدا مفعولا

translation: Then We returned you to another cycle concerning them, and We supplied you with wealth and sons and made you more numerous in manpower.
interpretation: The verse speaks about a cycle of return, where the people were returned to their previous state or condition. The verse highlights the blessings that were bestowed upon them, such as wealth, children, and a larger population. The verse suggests that these blessings were given to the people as a test or a trial, and it serves as a reminder that all blessings come from God. It also emphasizes the importance of being grateful for these blessings and using them in a way that is pleasing to God.
orig: ثم رددنا لكم الكرة عليهم وأمددناكم بأموال وبنين وجعلناكم أكثر نفيرا

translation: Indeed, you will surely benefit if you are righteous, but if you are unjust, then it is against yourselves. So when the final promise comes, they will despair, and they will be brought to ruin, and they will be driven as if driven to a narrow place. And it will be said, 'Taste the punishment of eternity; this is what you used to ask for.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the consequences of people's actions in this life and the next. It emphasizes that if people are righteous, they will benefit from their actions, but if they are unjust, then the harm from their actions will be against themselves. The verse warns of the final promise, or the Day of Judgment, when people will be brought to ruin and despair. The verse describes the punishment as a narrow and confined space, emphasizing its severity and the feeling of being trapped. The verse ends with a statement that the punishment is a result of the people's own actions and what they had asked for, emphasizing the concept of accountability for one's actions.
orig: إن أحسنتم أحسنتم لأنفسكم وإن أسأتم فلها فإذا جاء وعد الآخرة ليسوءوا وجوهكم وليدخلوا المسجد كما دخلوه أول مرة وليتبروا ما علوا تتبيرا

translation: Perhaps your Lord will have mercy on you, but if you return (to sin), We will return (to punishment). And We have made Hell a prison for the disbelievers.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the possibility of God's mercy for the people, but it also warns of the consequences of returning to sin. The verse emphasizes that if the people return to their wrongdoing, God will also return to punishing them. The verse also mentions that Hell has been prepared as a prison for the disbelievers. This verse serves as a reminder of the importance of seeking God's mercy and avoiding sin, as well as the severe consequences of disbelief and continued wrongdoing.
orig: عسى ربكم أن يرحمكم وإن عدتم عدنا وجعلنا جهنم للكافرين حصيرا

translation: Indeed, this Qur'an guides to that which is most suitable and gives good news to the believers who do righteous deeds that for them will be a great reward.
interpretation: The verse highlights the guiding nature of the Qur'an towards what is best and most suitable. It also offers good news to the believers who perform righteous deeds, promising them a great reward. This interpretation emphasizes the importance of following the guidance of the Qur'an and the significance of performing good deeds, which will be rewarded by God.
orig: إن هذا القرآن يهدي للتي هي أقوم ويبشر المؤمنين الذين يعملون الصالحات أن لهم أجرا كبيرا

translation: And We have prepared for the disbelievers a painful punishment.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the punishment that has been prepared for the disbelievers. The punishment is described as painful, emphasizing the severity of the consequences for those who do not believe in the hereafter. The verse serves as a warning to those who do not believe in the afterlife, reminding them of the consequences of their disbelief.
orig: وأن الذين لا يؤمنون بالآخرة أعتدنا لهم عذابا أليما

translation: And man invokes [God] for evil as he invites [God] for good and man is ever hasty.
interpretation: The verse describes the human tendency to call upon God in times of need, whether it be for good or for evil. However, the verse highlights the fact that humans are often hasty and impulsive, even when it comes to their relationship with God. This hasty and impulsive nature can lead humans to make poor decisions and engage in harmful behavior, even while calling out to God for help or guidance. The verse serves as a reminder to be mindful and thoughtful in one's actions and words, even when invoking God, and to strive for righteousness and goodness in all aspects of life.
orig: ويدع الإنسان بالشر دعاءه بالخير وكان الإنسان عجولا

translation: And We have made the night and the day as two signs, then We erased the sign of the night and made the sign of the day visible so that you may seek bounty from your Lord and know the number of years and the calculation, and We have detailed every matter in detail.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the creation of the night and the day as signs from God. The verse highlights the importance of these signs in helping people to seek the bounty of their Lord and understand the passage of time. The phrase 'We erased the sign of the night' can be interpreted as a reference to the disappearance of the night, allowing the day to become visible. This serves as a reminder of the importance of being mindful of the passage of time and using it wisely. The verse also emphasizes the detail and precision with which God has created everything, indicating the importance of paying attention to the signs and details in the world around us as a means of gaining a deeper understanding of God's creation and seeking His bounty.
orig: وجعلنا الليل والنهار آيتين فمحونا آية الليل وجعلنا آية النهار مبصرة لتبتغوا فضلا من ربكم ولتعلموا عدد السنين والحساب وكل شيء فصلناه تفصيلا

translation: And for every human being, We have fastened to his neck a necklace which will be made clear for him on the Day of Resurrection. It will be displayed for him in a record.
interpretation: The verse speaks about a 'necklace' or 'rope' that is fastened to the neck of every human being. This 'necklace' represents the person's actions and deeds, both good and bad, that they have done in their lifetime. On the Day of Resurrection, this 'necklace' will be made clear and displayed for the person in a record. The verse emphasizes the importance of the actions and deeds that people do in their lives, as they will be held accountable for them on the Day of Resurrection. It serves as a reminder to people to do good deeds and to strive for righteousness, as they will be judged based on their actions.
orig: وكل إنسان ألزمناه طائره في عنقه ونخرج له يوم القيامة كتابا يلقاه منشورا

translation: Read your book (of deeds), sufficient is yourself this day as a reckoner.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the importance of taking account of one's own actions and deeds. It emphasizes that on the Day of Judgment, each person will be held accountable for their actions and will not be able to blame anyone else for their mistakes. The verse encourages self-reflection and self-evaluation, urging people to be mindful of their actions and to prepare for the Day of Judgment by living a righteous life. The phrase 'sufficient is yourself this day as a reckoner' indicates that each person will be their own judge on that day, and will have to bear the consequences of their actions.
orig: اقرأ كتابك كفى بنفسك اليوم عليك حسيبا

translation: Whoever is guided is only guided for [the benefit of] his soul, and whoever goes astray only goes astray to its detriment. And no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another. And We never punish until We send a messenger.
interpretation: The verse highlights the individual responsibility of human beings for their own actions. Each person is guided for their own benefit or misguided due to their own actions. No one bears the burden of another's sins. Moreover, punishment is not meted out without warning, and a messenger is always sent to convey the message and give people a chance to repent before the punishment is inflicted.
orig: من اهتدى فإنما يهتدي لنفسه ومن ضل فإنما يضل عليها ولا تزر وازرة وزر أخرى وما كنا معذبين حتى نبعث رسولا

translation: And when We decide to destroy a town, We command its affluent (people), but they defiantly disobey therein; so the Word (of punishment) is justified against it, so We destroy it utterly.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of a town that was affluent but its people were disobedient and defiant towards God's commands. The verse explains that when God decides to destroy a town, He first sends a warning to its wealthy and powerful people, but they disobey and persist in their sinful ways. As a result, God's punishment is justified and the town is destroyed completely. The verse serves as a reminder that wealth and power do not guarantee protection from God's punishment and that disobedience and defiance towards God's commands will ultimately lead to destruction.
orig: وإذا أردنا أن نهلك قرية أمرنا مترفيها ففسقوا فيها فحق عليها القول فدمرناها تدميرا

translation: And how many a generation have We destroyed after Noah, and your Lord is sufficient in taking account of the sins of His servants, knowing and seeing.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of previous generations that came after the time of the prophet Noah. The verse emphasizes the power and knowledge of God, who is sufficient in taking account of the sins of His servants and is aware of their wrongdoings. The verse serves as a reminder of the power and justice of God, and the certainty of His judgment. It also emphasizes the importance of recognizing and learning from the mistakes of the past, and the need to turn away from sin and seek forgiveness from God.
orig: وكم أهلكنا من القرون من بعد نوح وكفى بربك بذنوب عباده خبيرا بصيرا

translation: Whoever desires the immediate - We shall give him of it; We shall not withhold from him. Then as for one who is ungrateful, We shall make him experience a great punishment.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the consequences of one's desires and actions. It explains that for those who desire and seek immediate gratification, it will be given to them, but for those who are ungrateful and do not appreciate the blessings they have been given, they will face a severe punishment. This verse serves as a reminder that every action has a consequence and that those who are ungrateful and do not use their blessings in a responsible and appreciative manner will face a great punishment.
orig: من كان يريد العاجلة عجلنا له فيها ما نشاء لمن نريد ثم جعلنا له جهنم يصلاها مذموما مدحورا

translation: And whoever desires the hereafter and strives for it as he ought to strive and he is a believer - so indeed, these are the ones whose striving is appreciated (rewarded).
interpretation: The verse speaks about those who strive for the hereafter, who desire it and work towards it in the right way, and who are believers. These individuals are recognized and appreciated for their efforts. The verse encourages believers to focus on the hereafter, and to strive for it in the correct manner, implying that their efforts will not be in vain and that they will be rewarded for their actions.
orig: ومن أراد الآخرة وسعى لها سعيها وهو مؤمن فأولئك كان سعيهم مشكورا

translation: No, by no means will We assign to these - (to these) and (to those) any share (in guardianship). And indeed, the share of your Lord is better and more enduring.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes that certain groups of people (referred to as 'these' and 'those') will not be given any share in guardianship or authority. The verse then contrasts this with the blessings and generosity of the Lord, which are described as being better and more enduring than anything that these people could offer. The verse may be interpreted as a reminder that true power and authority come from God, and that worldly possessions and positions are fleeting and insignificant in comparison. It may also be seen as a warning against following the guidance of those who are not truly worthy of respect or obedience.
orig: كلا نمد هؤلاء وهؤلاء من عطاء ربك وما كان عطاء ربك محظورا

translation: Look at how We have preferred some over others, and indeed, the Hereafter is greater in ranks and greater in preference.
interpretation: The verse highlights the concept of God's preference of certain individuals or groups over others, and affirms that the Hereafter holds a greater significance and value than the worldly life. The verse suggests that the differences and inequalities that exist among people in this life are temporary and insignificant in comparison to the eternal rewards and punishments that await them in the Hereafter. It invites people to focus on striving for God's pleasure and preparing for the Hereafter, rather than being preoccupied with worldly gains and distinctions.
orig: انظر كيف فضلنا بعضهم على بعض وللآخرة أكبر درجات وأكبر تفضيلا

translation: And put not another god with Allah; or thou wilt be cast down to hell, blamed, abandoned.
interpretation: The verse warns against associating other gods with Allah, stating that the consequence of doing so is being cast down to hell, blamed, and abandoned. This verse emphasizes the importance of monotheism and the seriousness of shirk (associating partners with Allah) in Islamic teachings. It serves as a reminder to the believers to uphold the fundamental principle of tawhid (the oneness of Allah) and to stay away from any form of polytheism.
orig: لا تجعل مع الله إلها آخر فتقعد مذموما مخذولا

translation: And your Lord has decreed that you worship none but Him, and treat your parents kindly. Whether one or both of them attain old age while with you, say not to them a word of disrespect, nor shout at them, but address them in terms of honor. And, out of kindness, lower to them the wing of humility and say, 'My Lord! Bestow on them Your Mercy even as they cherished me in childhood.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of worshiping only one God and showing kindness and respect to parents. The command to worship only God is absolute and leaves no room for associating any partners with Him. The second part of the verse focuses on the treatment of parents, particularly when they reach old age. The use of terms like 'kindly', 'honor', 'humility', and 'mercy' highlights the importance of treating parents with respect, compassion, and gratitude. The verse also forbids disrespectful language or shouting at parents. By urging believers to show mercy towards their parents, the verse underscores the significance of filial piety and the importance of reciprocating the care and nurturing that parents provide to their children.
orig: وقضى ربك ألا تعبدوا إلا إياه وبالوالدين إحسانا إما يبلغن عندك الكبر أحدهما أو كلاهما فلا تقل لهما أف ولا تنهرهما وقل لهما قولا كريما

translation: And lower unto them the wing of submission through mercy, and say: My Lord, have mercy on them both, as they did care for me when I was little.
interpretation: This verse speaks about the prophet Muhammad (PBUH) showing mercy and compassion towards his parents, particularly his mother, and asking God to have mercy on them. The phrase 'lower unto them the wing of submission' is a metaphor for showing humility, care, and submission towards one's parents. The verse emphasizes the importance of respecting and caring for one's parents, and it encourages Muslims to show kindness and mercy towards their parents. The verse also teaches Muslims to pray for their parents and to ask for God's mercy and forgiveness for them, especially if they were good to them in their early years.
orig: واخفض لهما جناح الذل من الرحمة وقل رب ارحمهما كما ربياني صغيرا

translation: Your Lord is most knowing of what is in your selves. If you should be righteous, then indeed He is, to the grateful, Forgiving.
interpretation: The verse speaks about God's knowledge of the thoughts and intentions of people. It highlights that God is aware of the actions of people, and if they are righteous, then they will receive forgiveness and mercy from God. The verse serves as a reminder of God's all-encompassing knowledge and the importance of leading a righteous life, as it will result in God's forgiveness and mercy towards the grateful and righteous.
orig: ربكم أعلم بما في نفوسكم إن تكونوا صالحين فإنه كان للأوابين غفورا

translation: And give to the relative his right, and to the needy and the traveler, and do not waste wastefully.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of giving and being fair in one's dealings with others. It specifically mentions four groups of people who should be given their rights: relatives, the needy, travelers, and one's own self (by not wasting resources). By giving to these groups, one is fulfilling their obligations and helping to create a just and compassionate society. The verse serves as a reminder to be mindful of how we use our resources and to be generous to those in need.
orig: وآت ذا القربى حقه والمسكين وابن السبيل ولا تبذر تبذيرا

translation: Indeed, the planting disbelievers were brothers of the devils, and the devils are ungrateful to their Lord.
interpretation: The verse highlights the close association between the disbelievers who reject the signs of God and the devils. By describing them as 'brothers', the verse emphasizes their shared characteristics and behaviors. Both the disbelievers and the devils reject the truth and are ungrateful to their Lord. The verse serves as a warning to those who deny the signs of God and encourages them to reflect on the consequences of their actions.
orig: إن المبذرين كانوا إخوان الشياطين وكان الشيطان لربه كفورا

translation: But if you [O Muhammad] are patient and fear Allah, their plot will not harm you at all. And indeed, Allah is encompassing of what they do.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the importance of patience and fearing God in the face of adversity. It advises the Prophet Muhammad to be patient and to seek Allah's mercy when dealing with the plots of his enemies. The verse reassures the Prophet that the plot of his enemies will not harm him as long as he remains patient and fears Allah. It also emphasizes that Allah is all-knowing and all-encompassing, and is aware of everything that the enemies of the Prophet are doing.
orig: وإما تعرضن عنهم ابتغاء رحمة من ربك ترجوها فقل لهم قولا ميسورا

translation: And throw not your hand in surrender to destruction, and become altogether patient and circumspect.
interpretation: The verse advises against despair and surrender in the face of adversity. Instead, it encourages patience and cautiousness. The act of throwing one's hand in surrender is a metaphor for giving up and losing hope, which can lead to destruction. The verse encourages believers to be patient and to think carefully before acting, in order to avoid falling into a state of helplessness and despair.
orig: ولا تجعل يدك مغلولة إلى عنقك ولا تبسطها كل البسط فتقعد ملوما محسورا

translation: Indeed, your Lord extends provision for whom He wills and restricts [it]. Indeed He is, of His servants, Acquainted and Seeing.
interpretation: The verse highlights the power and control that God has over the provision and sustenance of His servants. He extends provision for whom He wills and withholds it from whom He wills. The verse emphasizes that God is aware of the circumstances of His servants and sees their actions. The verse serves as a reminder that all provision comes from God and that He has the power to give and take away as He sees fit, and thus, it encourages believers to be grateful and content with what they have been given.
orig: إن ربك يبسط الرزق لمن يشاء ويقدر إنه كان بعباده خبيرا بصيرا

translation: And do not kill your children for fear of poverty, We provide for them and for you. Indeed, their killing is a great sin.
interpretation: The verse forbids the killing of children out of fear of poverty or any other reason. It emphasizes that God will provide for both the parents and the children. The verse highlights the gravity of the sin of killing one's children, describing it as a 'great sin'. The verse encourages believers to have faith in God's provision and to avoid falling into the grave sin of taking innocent lives.
orig: ولا تقتلوا أولادكم خشية إملاق نحن نرزقهم وإياكم إن قتلهم كان خطئا كبيرا

translation: And do not approach unlawful sexual intercourse. Indeed, it is an immorality and is evil as a way.
interpretation: The verse commands believers to refrain from approaching or engaging in unlawful sexual intercourse, which is described as an immorality and an evil way. The verse emphasizes the importance of maintaining moral values and avoiding actions that are contrary to Islamic teachings. It serves as a reminder that engaging in such acts has severe consequences both in this world and in the hereafter.
orig: ولا تقربوا الزنا إنه كان فاحشة وساء سبيلا

translation: And do not kill a soul that Allah has made sacred except by right. And if anyone is killed unjustly, then We have given authority to his heir, so let him not exceed the limit in killing. Indeed, he will be supported.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the sanctity of human life and the importance of respecting it. It prohibits the killing of any soul unless it is for a just cause, and it establishes the authority of the heir of the victim to seek justice in case of an unjust killing. However, it also warns against excessive retaliation and reminds that the heir will be supported in their quest for justice. The verse promotes the values of justice, fairness, and respect for human life, highlighting the importance of upholding these values in all circumstances.
orig: ولا تقتلوا النفس التي حرم الله إلا بالحق ومن قتل مظلوما فقد جعلنا لوليه سلطانا فلا يسرف في القتل إنه كان منصورا

translation: And come not near to the orphan's property except in the way of improvement until he attains his maturity. And fulfill (every) covenant. Indeed, the covenant will be questioned about.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of treating the property of orphans fairly and with integrity. It prohibits taking advantage of the orphan's property, except in a way that is beneficial for the orphan. The verse also highlights the significance of fulfilling one's promises and covenants, as they will be questioned about it in the future. This verse serves as a reminder of the importance of justice, integrity, and responsibility towards vulnerable members of society, such as orphans, and the significance of keeping one's word.
orig: ولا تقربوا مال اليتيم إلا بالتي هي أحسن حتى يبلغ أشده وأوفوا بالعهد إن العهد كان مسئولا

translation: And fulfill the measure when you measure, and weigh with a straight balance. That is better and more righteous.
interpretation: The verse is a command from God to fulfill the measure when measuring and to weigh with a straight balance. This means that people should be honest and fair in their dealings with others, and not cheat or deceive them. By fulfilling the measure and weighing with a straight balance, people can ensure that they are being just and righteous in their actions. This verse serves as a reminder to be honest and fair in all dealings and transactions, and to strive for justice and righteousness in all aspects of life.
orig: وأوفوا الكيل إذا كلتم وزنوا بالقسطاس المستقيم ذلك خير وأحسن تأويلا

translation:
And do not walk on the earth exultantly. Indeed, you will never tear the earth apart [with its consequence], and you will never reach the mountains in height.
And be moderate in your walking, and lower your voice. Indeed, the most disagreeable of sounds is the voice of donkeys.
interpretation: The verse advises people to be humble and modest in their behavior and movements, and not to walk arrogantly or exultantly on the earth. The verse emphasizes the limits of human power and ability, stating that even if humans were to walk with all their might, they would not be able to tear the earth apart or reach the mountains in height. The verse also advises people to be moderate and gentle in their actions, and to lower their voices, as the most disagreeable of sounds is the voice of donkeys. The verse promotes a sense of humility, mindfulness, and respect for oneself and others.
orig: ولا تقف ما ليس لك به علم إن السمع والبصر والفؤاد كل أولئك كان عنه مسئولا

translation: And do not walk on the earth exultantly, indeed, you will never tear the earth and you will never reach the mountains in height.
interpretation: The verse advises against arrogance and pride, warning against walking on the earth exultantly. The verse emphasizes the limits of human abilities, stating that one cannot tear the earth or reach the mountains in height. The verse serves as a reminder of human limitations and the importance of humility. It encourages a sense of humbleness and appreciation for the creation of God, and a recognition of one's place in the world.
orig: ولا تمش في الأرض مرحا إنك لن تخرق الأرض ولن تبلغ الجبال طولا

translation: All of that was evil in the sight of your Lord, greatly detested.
interpretation: The verse expresses God's disapproval and strong dislike towards certain actions or behaviors that are referred to in the previous verses. The verse emphasizes the gravity of these actions and the severity of God's displeasure towards those who commit them. The verse serves as a warning and a reminder to the believers to avoid engaging in any behavior that is displeasing to God and to strive towards righteousness and piety.
orig: كل ذلك كان سيئه عند ربك مكروها

translation: That is some of what your Lord has revealed to you of the wisdom. And do not set up with Allah another god, lest you find yourself in Hell, blamed and forsaken.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of following the wisdom that has been revealed by one's Lord and the danger of setting up other gods besides Him. The verse warns of severe consequences for those who disobey, namely ending up in Hell, blamed and forsaken. The verse serves as a reminder to worship and submit to one God, and to avoid the worship of any other deities. This is a fundamental principle of the Islamic faith, and the verse reinforces the seriousness of this belief.
orig: ذلك مما أوحى إليك ربك من الحكمة ولا تجعل مع الله إلها آخر فتلقى في جهنم ملوما مدحورا

translation: Or is He (better than Your gods) who has created for you all that which you ask? And has made for you, from the heaven and the earth, all that you see? Or are there, among your 'partners', any who can do any of these things? Say, 'Bring forth your proof, if you are truthful.'
interpretation: The verse challenges the disbelievers to consider whether their gods can create or do any of the things that Allah has done. It highlights the power and ability of Allah by describing how He has created everything that exists and provided for all of humanity's needs. The verse ends by inviting the disbelievers to present their evidence or proof, if they truly believe in the power and ability of their gods.
orig: أفأصفاكم ربكم بالبنين واتخذ من الملائكة إناثا إنكم لتقولون قولا عظيما

translation: And We have certainly diversified in this Qur'an that they may take heed; but it increases them in nothing except disbelief.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the diversity and richness of the Qur'an, which has been revealed so that people may take heed and reflect upon its teachings. However, the verse also mentions that instead of benefiting from the guidance of the Qur'an, some people only increase in disbelief and rejection of its message. This is a reminder that the Qur'an is a source of guidance and wisdom, but its true value can only be realized by those who approach it with an open mind and a willingness to reflect and learn.
orig: ولقد صرفنا في هذا القرآن ليذكروا وما يزيدهم إلا نفورا

translation: Say, [O Muhammad], 'If there were indeed other gods besides Allah as they claim, they would have sought a way to the Lord of the Throne [Allah].'
interpretation: The verse challenges the claim of polytheists who believe in the existence of other gods besides Allah. It invites them to consider the logical consequence of their belief, i.e., if their gods were real, they would have sought a way to the Lord of the Throne, Allah, who is the ultimate authority and power. The verse emphasizes the uniqueness and supremacy of Allah, and the absurdity of associating partners with Him.
orig: قل لو كان معه آلهة كما يقولون إذا لابتغوا إلى ذي العرش سبيلا

translation: Exalted is He above what they say! He is the Most High, the Great.
interpretation: The verse is a statement of praise and exaltation of God above the falsehoods and lies spoken about Him by the disbelievers. The verse emphasizes God's greatness and His exalted position above all creation. The verse serves as a reminder of the unlimited power and majesty of God, and of the insignificance and weakness of those who oppose Him or speak ill of Him. It is a call for believers to have faith in God and to reject the falsehoods of the disbelievers.
orig: سبحانه وتعالى عما يقولون علوا كبيرا

translation: The seven heavens and the earth, and whatever is in them, exalt Him. And there is not a thing except that it exalts [God] by His praise, but you do not understand their exalting. Indeed, He is ever Forbearing and Forgiving.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the greatness and glory of God, highlighting that everything in the seven heavens and the earth, including all living creatures, constantly praise and exalt God. The verse notes that this constant exaltation and praise is beyond human comprehension. Despite the constant praise and exaltation, God remains Forbearing and Forgiving, showing His infinite mercy and compassion towards His creation.
orig: تسبح له السماوات السبع والأرض ومن فيهن وإن من شيء إلا يسبح بحمده ولكن لا تفقهون تسبيحهم إنه كان حليما غفورا

translation: But when you recite the Qur'an, We put between you and those who do not believe in the hereafter a hidden barrier.
interpretation: The verse highlights the spiritual divide that exists between the believers and the non-believers when the Qur'an is being recited. It suggests that the recitation of the Qur'an creates a barrier, a 'hidden curtain', that separates the believers from the non-believers. This barrier is a result of the non-believers' rejection of the message of the Qur'an, and their disbelief in the hereafter. The verse emphasizes the power of the Qur'an to bring clarity and understanding to those who are receptive to its message, while at the same time emphasizing the inability of the non-believers to comprehend its true meaning. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of faith and the consequences of disbelief.
orig: وإذا قرأت القرآن جعلنا بينك وبين الذين لا يؤمنون بالآخرة حجابا مستورا

translation: And We have set on their hearts veils so they do not understand it, and in their ears heaviness, and when you mention your Lord alone in the Qur'an, those who do not believe run to them in avoidance.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the hardening of the hearts and ears of those who reject the message of the Qur'an. A veil has been set on their hearts, preventing them from understanding the truth and guidance brought by the Qur'an. They also experience heaviness in their ears, further hindering them from comprehending the message. When the believers mention the Lord alone in the Qur'an, those who do not believe flee and avoid the message, showing their rejection and disbelief. The verse highlights the consequences of rejecting the truth and the difficulty of reaching those who refuse to listen and understand.
orig: وجعلنا على قلوبهم أكنة أن يفقهوه وفي آذانهم وقرا وإذا ذكرت ربك في القرآن وحده ولوا على أدبارهم نفورا

translation: We know best what they listen to, when they listen to you, and when they are alone, for when the unjust ones meet, they say, 'Indeed, you are only following a man bewitched.'
interpretation: The verse highlights God's omniscience and all-encompassing knowledge, emphasizing that He is aware of everything, including the private conversations of the unjust. The verse describes the attitude of the unjust towards those who follow the truth, accusing them of being bewitched and following a deluded man. The verse serves as a reminder that God is aware of the deceit and falsehood of those who deny the truth, and that their accusations and mockery will not diminish the truth or the power of those who follow it.
orig: نحن أعلم بما يستمعون به إذ يستمعون إليك وإذ هم نجوى إذ يقول الظالمون إن تتبعون إلا رجلا مسحورا

translation: See how they strike similitudes for you, then go away, they are unable to comprehend.
interpretation: The verse addresses the hypocrites who try to confuse and mislead the believers by presenting false arguments and similitudes. Despite their efforts, they are unable to understand the truth or lead others astray. The verse serves as a warning to the believers to be cautious of the hypocrisy and deception of such individuals, and to remain steadfast in their faith and understanding of the truth.
orig: انظر كيف ضربوا لك الأمثال فضلوا فلا يستطيعون سبيلا

translation: And they say, 'When we are bones and dust, shall we indeed be resurrected as a new creation?'
interpretation: The verse presents a rhetorical question posed by the disbelievers, expressing their disbelief and skepticism towards the concept of resurrection and the Day of Judgment. They wonder how they could be brought back to life after they have turned into bones and dust. The verse challenges the disbelievers' denial and serves as a reminder of the power and ability of God to resurrect and judge all souls, regardless of their current state or condition.
orig: وقالوا أإذا كنا عظاما ورفاتا أإنا لمبعوثون خلقا جديدا

translation: Say, 'Be stones or iron!',
interpretation: In this verse, the speaker (who is believed to be the Prophet Muhammad) challenges the disbelievers to become stones or iron, implying that they are as unyielding and unbelieving as those materials. The verse is a form of rhetorical exaggeration, used to emphasize the futility of the disbelievers' rejection of the message of Islam. The verse can be interpreted as a call to the disbelievers to reflect on their own stubbornness and consider the truth of the message, before it is too late.
orig: قل كونوا حجارة أو حديدا

translation: Or [like] creation of you. So will you not be reminded? Who originates you from the earth and then restores you to it? Then will you not be returned? And a promise [of resurrection] to bind their true reality, most surely it is near.
interpretation: The verse draws a comparison between the creation of human beings and something that is beyond their comprehension, in order to emphasize its complexity and wonder. It then asks a series of rhetorical questions to remind people of their origins and their inevitable return to the earth. The verse ends with a reminder of the promise of resurrection, which is described as being near. The verse serves as a call to contemplation and reflection, urging people to consider their origins and their fate, and to recognize the nearness of the Day of Judgment.
orig: أو خلقا مما يكبر في صدوركم فسيقولون من يعيدنا قل الذي فطركم أول مرة فسينغضون إليك رءوسهم ويقولون متى هو قل عسى أن يكون قريبا

translation: A day He will call you, and you will respond to Him with praise, and you will think that you have only tarried a little.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the Day of Judgment, when God will call upon humanity and they will respond with praise and gratitude. However, despite the fact that this day will be the end of the world, people will have the illusion that they have only been waiting for a short period of time. This verse emphasizes the suddenness and unexpectedness of the Day of Judgment, and the importance of being prepared for it at all times. It also highlights the importance of praising and thanking God, as it will be our response on that day.
orig: يوم يدعوكم فتستجيبون بحمده وتظنون إن لبثتم إلا قليلا

translation: And say to My servants that they should only speak that which is best. Indeed, Satan incites conflict and disagreement among them. Indeed, Satan is an obvious enemy to man.
interpretation: The verse commands the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to advise his followers to always speak words that are good and wholesome. This is because Satan seeks to create discord and disagreement among people. Satan is described as a clear enemy to humanity, emphasizing the danger and harm that he brings. The verse highlights the importance of choosing one's words wisely and avoiding unnecessary conflict and disagreement, as these can lead to negative consequences and harm one's relationship with God and others.
orig: وقل لعبادي يقولوا التي هي أحسن إن الشيطان ينزغ بينهم إن الشيطان كان للإنسان عدوا مبينا

translation: Your Lord is most knowing of you: if He wills, He will have mercy upon you, or if He wills, He will punish you. And We have not sent you as a warden over them.
interpretation: The verse highlights God's complete knowledge and power over all of humanity. It emphasizes that God has the choice to either show mercy or punish people, and that this decision is ultimately up to His will. The verse also makes it clear that the role of the Prophet Muhammad, upon whom be peace, is not to control or punish the people, but rather to convey God's message to them. The verse serves as a reminder of the power and wisdom of God, and the limitations of human beings.
orig: ربكم أعلم بكم إن يشأ يرحمكم أو إن يشأ يعذبكم وما أرسلناك عليهم وكيلا

translation: And your Lord knows best who is in the heavens and the earth. And indeed, We have preferred some of the prophets above others, and to Dawud We gave the Zabur.
interpretation: The verse affirms that Allah knows best who is in the heavens and the earth, emphasizing His omniscience and complete knowledge of all creation. The verse also mentions that some prophets have been preferred above others, highlighting the distinction and special status of certain prophets. Furthermore, the verse states that the Zabur (Psalms) were given to Dawud (David), indicating his prophethood and his role as a messenger of Allah.
orig: وربك أعلم بمن في السماوات والأرض ولقد فضلنا بعض النبيين على بعض وآتينا داوود زبورا

translation: Say, 'Invoke those whom you have claimed [as deities] besides Him, [O Muhammad], they have no power to remove adversity from you or even to change it.'
interpretation: The verse addresses the Prophet Muhammad and commands him to challenge the disbelievers to invoke their deities, which they claim to be equal or similar to Allah, and ask them to remove adversity or change it. The verse emphasizes the powerlessness of these deities, as they cannot bring any benefit or harm, nor can they remove harm or change it. The verse aims to show the falseness of the disbelievers' claims and the weakness of their deities, and to guide them towards the worship of the one true God, Allah, who has power and control over all things.
orig: قل ادعوا الذين زعمتم من دونه فلا يملكون كشف الضر عنكم ولا تحويلا

translation: Those are they who call out to their Lord, desiring the means [of nearness] to Him, seeking Him. 'What, is it you who will forgive sins and forgive transgressions?' They hope for His mercy and fear His punishment. Indeed, the punishment of your Lord is ever looming.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the believers who call out to their Lord, seeking His mercy and fearing His punishment. They are eager to be near to God and seek His forgiveness for their sins and transgressions.
