The verse emphasizes the power and authority of God as the one who forgives and punishes, and highlights the importance of seeking His mercy and fearing His punishment. The verse serves as a reminder to the believers of the importance of maintaining a strong and devoted relationship with God, and of the importance of seeking His forgiveness for their sins.
orig: أولئك الذين يدعون يبتغون إلى ربهم الوسيلة أيهم أقرب ويرجون رحمته ويخافون عذابه إن عذاب ربك كان محذورا

translation: And indeed, for every town, We destroy it before the Day of Resurrection or punish it with a severe punishment. Indeed, that has been written in the Book.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction or punishment of towns by God before the Day of Resurrection. The verse emphasizes the inevitability of these events, as they have already been written in the Book. This can be interpreted as a reminder of the power and knowledge of God, and the transience of human existence. It also serves as a warning for people to reflect on their actions and repent, as they will be held accountable for them in the afterlife.
orig: وإن من قرية إلا نحن مهلكوها قبل يوم القيامة أو معذبوها عذابا شديدا كان ذلك في الكتاب مسطورا

translation: And nothing prevented Us from sending signs [proofs/verses] except that the first [people] rejected them. And We gave Thamud the she-camel as a clear sign, but they wronged her, and we do not send the signs except to instill fear.
interpretation: The verse explains that the reason for the delay in sending divine signs or proofs was the rejection of earlier people. The verse then mentions the story of the Thamud tribe who were given a she-camel as a clear sign, but they treated it unjustly. The verse ends by stating that the sending of signs or verses is not merely for informational purposes, but to instill fear and make people reflect on their actions. It serves as a reminder of the consequences of rejecting divine messages and the importance of responding positively to divine guidance.
orig: وما منعنا أن نرسل بالآيات إلا أن كذب بها الأولون وآتينا ثمود الناقة مبصرة فظلموا بها وما نرسل بالآيات إلا تخويفا

translation: And when We said to you, 'Indeed, your Lord has encompassed the people.' And We made not see what We had promised them except as a trial for the people and the cursed tree in the Qur'an. And We frighten them, but it only increases them in great transgression.
interpretation: The verse speaks about a conversation between God and an unspecified person (in this context, understood to be the Prophet Muhammad) where God informs the person that He has encompassed the people (i.e., has power and control over them). The verse then mentions a vision or promise that God had previously shown to the people, which was made as a test for them. The verse also mentions a cursed tree from the Qur'an, which is understood to be a reference to the story of Adam and Eve and the forbidden tree. Despite the warnings and signs given to the people, the verse mentions that they were frightened, but it only increased their transgression and disobedience towards God. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of heeding God's signs and warnings, and the dangers of disobedience and transgression.
orig: وإذ قلنا لك إن ربك أحاط بالناس وما جعلنا الرؤيا التي أريناك إلا فتنة للناس والشجرة الملعونة في القرآن ونخوفهم فما يزيدهم إلا طغيانا كبيرا

translation: And when We said to the angels, 'Prostrate yourselves before Adam,' they prostrated themselves, except for Iblis. He said, 'Shall I prostrate myself before one You have created from clay?'
interpretation: The verse describes a conversation between God and the angels, in which God commands the angels to prostrate themselves before Adam. All of the angels comply with the command, except for Iblis (also known as Satan), who refuses to prostrate himself before a being that was created from clay. The verse highlights the arrogance and pride of Iblis, who believes himself to be superior to Adam. It also emphasizes the obedience and submission of the angels to God's will, and the consequences of disobedience and arrogance.
orig: وإذ قلنا للملائكة اسجدوا لآدم فسجدوا إلا إبليس قال أأسجد لمن خلقت طينا

translation: He said, 'Do you see this one that I have favored above you? If I were to leave him (in power) until the Day of Resurrection, he would surely corrupt your offspring, except for a few.'
interpretation: The verse is a statement made by an unspecified person, referring to a favored individual who has been given power and status. The speaker expresses concern that if this person remains in power until the Day of Judgment, they will corrupt the offspring of the people, except for a small number. The verse highlights the dangers of unchecked power and the potential for corruption, as well as the importance of accountability and limits on authority.
orig: قال أرأيتك هذا الذي كرمت علي لئن أخرتن إلى يوم القيامة لأحتنكن ذريته إلا قليلا

translation: He said, 'Go, you and whoever of them follows you, for indeed Hell will be the recompense of you all - an ample recompense.'
interpretation: The verse is a statement made by an unidentified person, most likely a prophet or a messenger, who is being rejected and persecuted by his people. He is told to leave and take with him whoever follows him. The verse emphasizes the severe consequences of rejecting the message of truth, with Hell being the punishment for those who persist in their disbelief. The phrase 'ample recompense' underscores the severity of the punishment and the gravity of the situation. The verse serves as a warning to those who reject the message of truth, urging them to reconsider their position and avoid the dire consequences of their actions.
orig: قال اذهب فمن تبعك منهم فإن جهنم جزاؤكم جزاء موفورا

translation: And amuse yourself with
interpretation: No interpretation
orig: واستفزز من استطعت منهم بصوتك وأجلب عليهم بخيلك ورجلك وشاركهم في الأموال والأولاد وعدهم وما يعدهم الشيطان إلا غرورا

translation: Indeed, My servants - you have no authority over them. And sufficient is your Lord as a guardian.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the powerlessness of humans over God's servants, and the sufficiency of God as a guardian for them. This verse can be interpreted as a reminder that humans do not have the power or authority to control or manipulate God's servants, and that God is sufficient as a guardian and protector for them. It serves as a reminder of the limits of human power and the ultimate power and control of God over all things.
orig: إن عبادي ليس لك عليهم سلطان وكفى بربك وكيلا

translation: Your Lord is the one who propels for you the ship in the sea so that you may seek of His bounty. Indeed, He has been to you Merciful.
interpretation: The verse highlights the power and mercy of God, who enables humans to travel and seek sustenance through the sea. The verse emphasizes God's role as the one who propels the ship, indicating that it is through His will and power that humans are able to travel and seek His bounty. The verse ends by reminding that God has been merciful to the people, emphasizing His compassion and kindness towards His creation.
orig: ربكم الذي يزجي لكم الفلك في البحر لتبتغوا من فضله إنه كان بكم رحيما

translation: But when the wave covers you, you believed in Him, then when He rescues you to the shore, you turn away. And man is ever ungrateful.
interpretation: The verse describes the behavior of people who only turn to God in times of distress and hardship, such as when they are caught in a storm at sea. When they are rescued, however, they quickly forget about God and return to their ingratitude. The verse emphasizes the human tendency towards ingratitude and forgetfulness, despite the blessings and mercies that God bestows upon them. The verse serves as a reminder to be constantly mindful of God and to be grateful for His blessings, even in times of ease and comfort.
orig: وإذا مسكم الضر في البحر ضل من تدعون إلا إياه فلما نجاكم إلى البر أعرضتم وكان الإنسان كفورا

translation: Or do you feel secure that He (God) will not cause the earth to swallow you, or send a sandstorm upon you? Then you will find no protector for yourselves.
interpretation: The verse warns the disbelievers of the punishment of God, which can come in the form of natural disasters, such as the earth swallowing them or a sandstorm. The verse emphasizes the vulnerability of humans in the face of God's power and their inability to protect themselves from His punishment. The verse serves as a reminder of the need for faith and submission to God, and the importance of living a righteous life.
orig: أفأمنتم أن يخسف بكم جانب البر أو يرسل عليكم حاصبا ثم لا تجدوا لكم وكيلا

translation: Or do you feel secure that He, who is over the heaven, will not cause the earth to swallow you and then suddenly it will sway? Or do you feel secure that He, who is over the heaven, will not send against you a storm of stones? Then you will know how was My warning.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the power and control that God has over the earth and the heavens. It highlights the vulnerability of human beings and their inability to protect themselves against God's punishment. The verse mentions two possible forms of punishment: the earth swallowing people and a storm of stones. These examples emphasize the suddenness and severity of God's punishment. The verse serves as a warning to those who do not believe in God or who ignore His signs, reminding them of the consequences of their disbelief and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: أم أمنتم أن يعيدكم فيه تارة أخرى فيرسل عليكم قاصفا من الريح فيغرقكم بما كفرتم ثم لا تجدوا لكم علينا به تبيعا

translation: And We have certainly honored the children of Adam and carried them on the land and the sea and provided for them from the good things and preferred them over much of what We have created, with distinction.
interpretation: The verse highlights the special status of human beings, who are the children of Adam, and the favors that God has bestowed upon them. The verse mentions that God has honored humans, carried them on land and sea, provided them with good things, and given them distinction over many of God's creations. This verse can be interpreted as a reminder of the value and dignity of human life, and of the responsibility that comes with this status. It also emphasizes the generosity and grace of God towards humans, and encourages gratitude and appreciation for these blessings.
orig: ولقد كرمنا بني آدم وحملناهم في البر والبحر ورزقناهم من الطيبات وفضلناهم على كثير ممن خلقنا تفضيلا

translation: On the Day when We will call every people with their record, whoever is given his record in his left hand, then they will read their record, and no one will injustice to them.
interpretation: The verse describes the Day of Judgment, when every person will be called to account for their actions and given their record of deeds. Those who receive their record in their left hand are those who have done more evil than good in their lives. They will read their record and will not be able to deny or dispute its contents. The verse emphasizes the fairness and justice of this process, as no one will be wronged or treated unjustly. It serves as a reminder of the importance of striving for righteousness and avoiding sin, as each person will be held accountable for their actions on the Day of Judgment.
orig: يوم ندعو كل أناس بإمامهم فمن أوتي كتابه بيمينه فأولئك يقرءون كتابهم ولا يظلمون فتيلا

translation: And whoever is blind in this [life] will be blind in the Hereafter and further astray in direction.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the fate of those who are spiritually blind and unable to see the truth in this life. These people will remain blind in the afterlife and will be even more lost and astray. The verse emphasizes the importance of seeking guidance and using one's intellect and reason to understand the truth. The verse serves as a warning to those who ignore the signs of God and fail to recognize the purpose of their existence, reminding them of the dire consequences of their actions in the afterlife.
orig: ومن كان في هذه أعمى فهو في الآخرة أعمى وأضل سبيلا

translation: But they were about to sway you away from what We have revealed to you, that you might invent against Us something other than it; and then they would surely take you as a friend. And if We had not made you firm, you would nearly have inclined to them a little.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the efforts of certain people to sway the Prophet Muhammad away from the teachings of Islam and towards inventing a different religion that would be more to their liking. The verse highlights the danger of such attempts and the importance of remaining steadfast in the face of adversity. The verse also implies that if the Prophet had not been divinely guided and supported, he might have been tempted to yield to the demands of these people. The verse serves as a reminder to the Prophet and to all believers of the importance of staying true to the teachings of Islam, even in the face of opposition and adversity.
orig: وإن كادوا ليفتنونك عن الذي أوحينا إليك لتفتري علينا غيره وإذا لاتخذوك خليلا

translation: And if We had not strengthened you, you would have slightly inclined to them.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the hypothetical situation where the speaker's faith or resolve would have been weakened, leading them to compromise or sway towards the disbelievers. However, because of God's support and strengthening of the speaker, they were able to remain firm in their convictions. The verse can be interpreted as a reminder of the importance of staying steadfast in one's beliefs and not being swayed by external pressures or influences. It also highlights the role of God's support in enabling individuals to remain strong and resolute in their faith.
orig: ولولا أن ثبتناك لقد كدت تركن إليهم شيئا قليلا

translation: If We let him taste the near approach of poverty and a hard struggle, surely after that he will be eager to us (for help), then you will not find for him any protecting supporter.
interpretation: The verse speaks about a person who is experiencing poverty and hardship. Despite this, the person does not turn to God for help, but instead continues to struggle on their own. The verse emphasizes the futility of this approach, stating that after experiencing such hardship, the person will be eager for God's help, but will not find any other source of support. The verse serves as a reminder that God is the ultimate source of help and support, and that turning to Him in times of need is the only way to overcome difficulties.
orig: إذا لأذقناك ضعف الحياة وضعف الممات ثم لا تجد لك علينا نصيرا

translation: But they were about to incite you to drive you out of the land, and when they leave you, they would not hesitate to abandon you shortly thereafter.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the intentions of some people to expel the Prophet Muhammad from his homeland. Despite their claims of friendship and support, they were planning to drive him out of the land. However, their support was insincere and short-lived, as they would quickly abandon him if given the chance. The verse serves as a reminder to the Prophet Muhammad to be wary of those who claim to be his allies, but in reality, have ulterior motives. It also highlights the transient nature of human relationships and the importance of relying on God for support and guidance.
orig: وإن كادوا ليستفزونك من الأرض ليخرجوك منها وإذا لا يلبثون خلافك إلا قليلا

translation: We did not send before you (as messengers) any but men to whom We revealed from among the people of cities.
interpretation: The verse highlights that all prophets and messengers sent by God were human beings, chosen from among the people of various towns. This emphasizes the humanity of the prophets and the relatability of their messages. It also serves to remind the people that they are capable of receiving and following the guidance sent to them, just as the people of the past had the opportunity to do so. The verse also implies that the message brought by the prophets and messengers is not something new or foreign, but rather a continuation of the same divine guidance that was revealed to previous nations.
orig: سنة من قد أرسلنا قبلك من رسلنا ولا تجد لسنتنا تحويلا

translation: Establish prayer at the decline of the sun [from its meridian] until the darkness of the night and the Qur'an of dawn. Indeed, the Qur'an of dawn is ever witnessed.
interpretation: The verse outlines the times for prayer, from the decline of the sun until the darkness of the night, and specifically mentions the recitation of the Qur'an during the early morning, referred to as the Qur'an of dawn. The verse emphasizes the significance of this time, highlighting that it is ever witnessed, implying the presence of angels or God Himself during this time. The verse encourages Muslims to establish a connection with God through prayer and recitation of the Qur'an, especially during these specific times, and to recognize the importance and blessings of these moments.
orig: أقم الصلاة لدلوك الشمس إلى غسق الليل وقرآن الفجر إن قرآن الفجر كان مشهودا

translation: And during the night, pray Tahajjud beyond what is incumbent upon you; surely it may be that your Lord will raise you to a praiseworthy station.
interpretation: The verse encourages the practice of Tahajjud, or late-night prayer, as a voluntary act of worship that goes beyond what is required. By doing so, one may be granted a 'praiseworthy station' by their Lord. The exact nature of this station is not specified in the verse, but it is often interpreted as a high level of spiritual rank or closeness to God. The verse emphasizes the potential rewards of voluntary worship and encourages believers to strive for spiritual growth and development through additional acts of devotion.
orig: ومن الليل فتهجد به نافلة لك عسى أن يبعثك ربك مقاما محمودا

translation: And say, 'My Lord, admit me an entrance of truth and exit of truth, and grant me from Yourself a sustainer (who will provide for me) a supporting one.'
interpretation: The verse is a supplication of a believer to God, asking for guidance and support. The believer asks God to admit them into heaven, which is described as an entrance and exit of truth, indicating that it is a place of ultimate truth and justice. The believer also asks for a sustainer and a supporter from God, indicating a desire for God's help and protection in this world. The verse emphasizes the importance of seeking guidance and support from God in all aspects of life, and the believer's trust and reliance on God for their needs and well-being.
orig: وقل رب أدخلني مدخل صدق وأخرجني مخرج صدق واجعل لي من لدنك سلطانا نصيرا

translation: And say, 'The Truth has come, and falsehood has vanished away. Indeed, falsehood is ever bound to vanish.'
interpretation: The verse asserts the ultimate triumph of truth over falsehood, emphasizing that falsehood is inherently weak and ephemeral. It exhorts the believers to stand firm in their faith and proclaim the truth, even in the face of adversity. The verse serves as a reminder that falsehood, no matter how powerful or pervasive it may seem, is ultimately doomed to fail and disappear. It encourages the believers to have patience and steadfastness in their faith, knowing that truth will ultimately prevail.
orig: وقل جاء الحق وزهق الباطل إن الباطل كان زهوقا

translation: And We reveal from the Qur'an that which is a healing and a mercy for the believers, and it increases the wrongdoers only in loss.
interpretation: The verse highlights the healing and mercy that the Qur'an brings to the believers, emphasizing the positive impact of the Qur'an on their lives. At the same time, the verse also addresses the wrongdoers, stating that the Qur'an only adds to their loss. This interpretation suggests that the Qur'an serves as a guide for those who seek to follow the right path, while those who persist in their wrongdoing will continue to suffer the consequences of their actions. The verse encourages believers to seek solace and guidance in the Qur'an, and to reflect on its teachings in order to lead a righteous life.
orig: وننزل من القرآن ما هو شفاء ورحمة للمؤمنين ولا يزيد الظالمين إلا خسارا

translation: But when We bestow favor upon man, he turns away and distances himself; and when adversity befalls him, he is in despair.
interpretation: The verse describes the behavior of people when they receive blessings and when they face hardships. When people are blessed with good fortune, they often become arrogant and turn away from God, forgetting the source of their blessings. However, when they encounter difficulties, they become despondent and lose hope. The verse serves as a reminder that true faith and trust in God should be consistent, regardless of the circumstances. People should be grateful for the blessings they receive and maintain their faith and patience during hardships, knowing that God is always with them.
orig: وإذا أنعمنا على الإنسان أعرض ونأى بجانبه وإذا مسه الشر كان يئوسا

translation: Say, 'Each one does according to his manner, but I am only responsible for my actions. Indeed, I am, to Him, a clear warner.'
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the individual's responsibility for their own actions, and the speaker's role as a clear warner. The verse suggests that each person has their own path or manner of living, and that the speaker (who is understood to be the Prophet Muhammad) cannot be held responsible for the actions of others. The verse encourages the listener to reflect on their own actions and to take responsibility for their own moral and ethical choices.
orig: قل كل يعمل على شاكلته فربكم أعلم بمن هو أهدى سبيلا

translation: And they ask you concerning the soul. Say, 'The soul is of the affair of my Lord. And of knowledge, you have been given but little.'
interpretation: The verse addresses a question about the soul and responds that the soul is a matter of God's domain, indicating that it is something that is ultimately known only to God. The verse also acknowledges that humans have been given limited knowledge, emphasizing the limitations of human understanding and the ultimate mystery of the soul. The verse encourages humility and reverence in the face of the unknown and the unknowable.
orig: ويسألونك عن الروح قل الروح من أمر ربي وما أوتيتم من العلم إلا قليلا

translation: And if We willed, We could take away that which We have revealed to you [O Muhammad]. Then you would not find for yourself concerning it any protector against Us.
interpretation: The verse speaks about God's power and control over the revelation that was given to the Prophet Muhammad. The verse emphasizes that if God willed, He could take away the revelation and no one could protect or help the Prophet against God's will. The verse serves as a reminder of God's omnipotence and the ultimate source of the revelation, and it also emphasizes the importance of the message and the need to follow it.
orig: ولئن شئنا لنذهبن بالذي أوحينا إليك ثم لا تجد لك به علينا وكيلا

translation: But for the grace of your Lord, you would have been among the losers.
interpretation: The verse highlights the importance of God's mercy and grace in preventing an individual from experiencing loss or misfortune. The phrase 'you would have been among the losers' implies that the person being addressed was previously on a path towards loss or destruction, but was saved by God's mercy. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of gratitude and recognition of God's blessings, as well as a warning against becoming complacent or arrogant in one's blessings, as they are ultimately a result of God's grace.
orig: إلا رحمة من ربك إن فضله كان عليك كبيرا

translation: Say, 'If mankind and the jinn were to gather in order to produce the likes of this Qur'an, they could not produce the likes of it, even if they were to assist one another.'
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the unique and inimitable nature of the Qur'an. It challenges mankind and the jinn, who are believed to possess great knowledge and power, to produce something similar to the Qur'an. The verse stresses that even with all their combined efforts and resources, they would not be able to produce something equivalent to the Qur'an. This serves as a testament to the divine origin of the Qur'an and its miraculous nature. It also serves as a reminder that the Qur'an is in a class by itself, and that it is a unique revelation from God that cannot be replicated or surpassed by any human or jinn effort.
orig: قل لئن اجتمعت الإنس والجن على أن يأتوا بمثل هذا القرآن لا يأتون بمثله ولو كان بعضهم لبعض ظهيرا

translation: And We have certainly diversified in this Qur'an for the people from every example, but most of the people are unappreciative.
interpretation: The verse highlights the diversity of examples and lessons in the Qur'an, which are meant for the guidance and enlightenment of people. However, the verse also points out that most people do not appreciate or acknowledge these lessons, and instead remain ungrateful. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of recognizing and learning from the various examples and teachings presented in the Qur'an, and of being grateful for the guidance that it provides.
orig: ولقد صرفنا للناس في هذا القرآن من كل مثل فأبى أكثر الناس إلا كفورا

translation: And they said, 'We will not believe in you until you cause a spring to gush forth for us from the earth.'
interpretation: The verse describes the disbelievers' demand for a miraculous sign from the Prophet Muhammad, specifically the ability to cause a spring to gush forth from the earth. This demand reflects their rejection of the Prophet's message and their unwillingness to believe without seeing extraordinary proof. The verse highlights the closed-mindedness and stubbornness of the disbelievers, as well as their rejection of the signs of God that are already present in the natural world. The verse serves as a reminder that true faith cannot be based on signs and wonders, but on the acceptance of the message and the submission to the will of God.
orig: وقالوا لن نؤمن لك حتى تفجر لنا من الأرض ينبوعا

translation: Or for you is a garden of palm trees and grapevines, in which rivers flow in abundance.
interpretation: The verse describes a beautiful and bountiful garden as a metaphor for the blessings and rewards that come from God. The garden is filled with palm trees and grapevines, which are both valuable and useful crops in Arabian culture. The image of rivers flowing through the garden emphasizes the abundance and richness of these blessings. The verse could be interpreted as a promise of paradise and eternal happiness for those who lead a righteous life and follow the teachings of Islam. It serves as a motivation for believers to strive for good deeds and to seek God's pleasure in this life, in order to attain His rewards in the afterlife.
orig: أو تكون لك جنة من نخيل وعنب فتفجر الأنهار خلالها تفجيرا

translation: Or the sky be split apart, so that its fragments fall down upon you, or the punishment of a mighty day be brought upon you.
interpretation: The verse describes two possible forms of punishment that may befall people who are disbelievers and reject the signs of Allah. The first possibility is that the sky may split apart and its fragments fall down upon them, indicating a catastrophic and destructive event. The second possibility is that they may face the punishment of a mighty day, which implies a day of reckoning and judgment. The verse serves as a warning to those who deny the truth and disbelieve, urging them to reflect on the consequences of their actions and the possibility of facing divine retribution.
orig: أو تسقط السماء كما زعمت علينا كسفا أو تأتي بالله والملائكة قبيلا

translation: Or do you have a sanctuary, or a stronghold, or a resort [for you and your helpers], while it is God who has given you refuge from every side? And We have sent down to you the Book as a clarification of all things and as a guidance and mercy and good tidings for the Muslims.
interpretation: The verse addresses the disbelievers who sought protection in their fortified buildings and questioned the Prophet Muhammad's (pbuh) message. The verse emphasizes that it is God who provides true refuge, and that the Qur'an has been sent down as a clarification of all things, a guidance, a mercy, and good tidings for the believers. The verse challenges the disbelievers to acknowledge the truth of the Prophet's message and to recognize God's power and protection.
orig: أو يكون لك بيت من زخرف أو ترقى في السماء ولن نؤمن لرقيك حتى تنزل علينا كتابا نقرؤه قل سبحان ربي هل كنت إلا بشرا رسولا

translation: And nothing prevented people from believing when the guidance came to them, except that they said: 'Has Allah sent a man as a messenger?'
interpretation: The verse highlights the disbelief and rejection of people towards the guidance brought by the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). Despite the guidance being presented to them, they refused to believe because of their preconceived notions and doubts about the possibility of a man being sent as a messenger from God. The verse challenges this disbelief and emphasizes the importance of accepting and following the guidance that has been sent, regardless of one's expectations or preconceptions.
orig: وما منع الناس أن يؤمنوا إذ جاءهم الهدى إلا أن قالوا أبعث الله بشرا رسولا

translation: Say, 'If there were upon the earth angels walking securely, We would have sent down upon them from the sky a sign from us - a messenger.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the power and authority of God, who has the ability to send down a messenger or a sign from the sky to any group of beings, even if they are powerful or secure. The verse emphasizes the sovereignty of God and the futility of relying on one's own strength or security. The verse may also be interpreted as a response to those who reject the message of Islam, suggesting that if they were truly worthy of divine guidance, a sign would have been sent to them. Ultimately, the verse serves as a reminder of the greatness of God and the importance of submitting to His will.
orig: قل لو كان في الأرض ملائكة يمشون مطمئنين لنزلنا عليهم من السماء ملكا رسولا

translation: Say, 'Sufficient is Allah as a witness between me and you.' Indeed, He is, of His servants, Acquainted and Seeing.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the sufficiency of God as a witness between the speaker and the listener. It highlights God's knowledge and awareness of His servants, indicating that He is aware of the truth and that His knowledge encompasses all things. The verse serves as a reminder of the all-encompassing nature of God's knowledge and His ability to bear witness to all things, and encourages the speaker and the listener to trust in God's justice and fairness.
orig: قل كفى بالله شهيدا بيني وبينكم إنه كان بعباده خبيرا بصيرا

translation: And whoever Allah guides - he is the one who is guided; and whoever He leaves astray - you will never find for them protectors among them, and We will gather them on the Day of Resurrection, [fallen] on their faces - blind, dumb and deaf. And their refuge is Hell; every time it subsides, We increase them in blazing fire.
interpretation: The verse highlights the ultimate authority of Allah in guiding or misguiding people. It emphasizes that those who are guided by Allah are truly guided, while those who are left astray by Him will not find any protectors or helpers other than Him. The verse describes the fate of the unbelievers on the Day of Resurrection, when they will be gathered with their faces fallen to the ground, blind, dumb and deaf, unable to see, speak or hear. Their final destination is Hell, where they will be subjected to unimaginable suffering and punishment. The verse serves as a warning to those who reject the guidance of Allah, reminding them of the terrible consequences of their disbelief.
orig: ومن يهد الله فهو المهتد ومن يضلل فلن تجد لهم أولياء من دونه ونحشرهم يوم القيامة على وجوههم عميا وبكما وصما مأواهم جهنم كلما خبت زدناهم سعيرا

translation: That is their reward because they disbelieved in our signs and said, 'What, when we have become bones and dust, shall we indeed be raised up in a new creation?'
interpretation: The verse explains the punishment of those who disbelieved in the signs of God and rejected the idea of resurrection. They questioned the possibility of being raised back to life after they have become bones and dust. The verse emphasizes the consequences of their disbelief and rejection of the divine message, highlighting the power and ability of God to bring back the dead to life in a new creation.
orig: ذلك جزاؤهم بأنهم كفروا بآياتنا وقالوا أإذا كنا عظاما ورفاتا أإنا لمبعوثون خلقا جديدا

translation: Have they not seen that God, who created the heavens and the earth, is able to create the likes of them, and has appointed for them a term, of which there is no doubt? But the unjust refuse [anything] except disbelief.
interpretation: The verse highlights God's power and ability to create anything, including creating beings similar to humans. The verse also mentions that God has set a term for humanity, which is certain and without doubt. However, despite this, the unjust and wrongdoers persist in disbelief and refuse to acknowledge the truth. The verse serves as a reminder of God's power and the futility of disbelief in the face of God's ultimate authority and control over all things.
orig: أولم يروا أن الله الذي خلق السماوات والأرض قادر على أن يخلق مثلهم وجعل لهم أجلا لا ريب فيه فأبى الظالمون إلا كفورا

translation: Say, 'If you had control of the treasures of my Lord's mercy, you would withhold out of fear of spending, and man is stingy.'
interpretation: The verse addresses the Prophet Muhammad and commands him to tell the disbelievers that if they had control of the treasures of God's mercy, they would still be stingy and withhold it out of fear of spending. The verse highlights the inherent stinginess of human beings and their tendency to hoard wealth, even if it is from the infinite treasures of God's mercy. The verse serves as a reminder of the transient nature of worldly possessions and the importance of being generous and charitable towards others.
orig: قل لو أنتم تملكون خزائن رحمة ربي إذا لأمسكتم خشية الإنفاق وكان الإنسان قتورا

translation: And We certainly gave Moses nine clear signs; ask the Children of Israel when he came to them, then said to him, 'Indeed, I think, O Moses, that you are fabricating [lies].'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the signs that were given to Moses and his interaction with the Pharaoh of Egypt. The verse mentions that Moses was given nine clear signs, but the Pharaoh accused him of fabricating lies. The verse emphasizes the disbelief of the Pharaoh and his people in the face of clear evidence and miracles. It serves as a reminder of the importance of having faith and accepting the truth even when it goes against our preconceived notions and beliefs.
orig: ولقد آتينا موسى تسع آيات بينات فاسأل بني إسرائيل إذ جاءهم فقال له فرعون إني لأظنك يا موسى مسحورا

translation: He said, 'Indeed, I know that none other than the Lord of the heavens and the earth has sent down these [signs], and I think you, O Pharaoh, are doomed.'
interpretation: The verse recounts the story of Moses and Pharaoh, and specifically a moment where Moses proclaims his belief in the one true God, the Lord of the heavens and the earth. Moses expresses his certainty that only the one true God could have sent down the signs and wonders that Moses has been demonstrating. Moses then states that he believes Pharaoh is doomed, implying that Pharaoh's rejection of the truth and his continued commitment to false gods will lead to his downfall. The verse highlights the theme of the ultimate power and authority of the one true God, and the consequences of rejecting that truth.
orig: قال لقد علمت ما أنزل هؤلاء إلا رب السماوات والأرض بصائر وإني لأظنك يا فرعون مثبورا

translation: But he intended to harm them through the earth, so We caused the earth to swallow him and his home.
interpretation: The verse describes a person who intended to cause harm to others through the earth, but God intervened and caused the earth to swallow him and his home. The verse emphasizes God's power and control over the earth and His ability to protect and punish as He sees fit. The verse serves as a reminder that those who seek to harm others will ultimately face the consequences of their actions, and that God is always watching and will protect His believers.
orig: فأراد أن يستفزهم من الأرض فأغرقناه ومن معه جميعا

translation: And We said after him to the children of Israel, 'Dwell in the land', then when the promise of the hereafter comes true, We will bring you as a mixed crowd.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the command of God to the children of Israel to dwell in the land. However, the verse also indicates that this dwelling is temporary, as God will bring them as a mixed crowd when the promise of the hereafter comes true. The verse emphasizes the fleeting nature of life and the ultimate destination of all human beings, which is the hereafter. The verse also implies that the people will be resurrected and gathered together, regardless of their current circumstances or status, and will be held accountable for their actions in this world.
orig: وقلنا من بعده لبني إسرائيل اسكنوا الأرض فإذا جاء وعد الآخرة جئنا بكم لفيفا

translation: And with truth have We sent down the Qur'an, and with truth has it descended. And We have not sent thee but as a bearer of good tidings and a warner.
interpretation: The verse affirms that the Qur'an has been sent down with truth and that it has descended with truth. It emphasizes the divine origin of the Qur'an and its truthfulness. The verse also explains that the Prophet Muhammad was not sent except as a bearer of good news and a warner, highlighting his role as a messenger of God's revelation and a Warner of the consequences of ignoring it.
orig: وبالحق أنزلناه وبالحق نزل وما أرسلناك إلا مبشرا ونذيرا

translation: And We have divided the Qur'an into parts, so that you may recite it to the people over a prolonged period. And We have sent it down in stages.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the division of the Qur'an into parts or chapters, allowing it to be recited over a long period. This division was done so that the revelation could be more easily understood and memorized by the Prophet Muhammad and his followers. The verse also highlights that the Qur'an was revealed in stages, over a period of time, rather than all at once. This is seen as a sign of the divine origin of the Qur'an, as it was revealed according to the needs and circumstances of the early Muslim community.
orig: وقرآنا فرقناه لتقرأه على الناس على مكث ونزلناه تنزيلا

translation: Say, 'Believe in it or do not believe in it.' Indeed, those who were given knowledge before it, when it is recited to them, they fall upon their faces in prostration.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the response of those who have been given knowledge when they hear the message of the Qur'an. When the message is recited to them, they immediately fall down in prostration, showing their humility and submission to God. The verse emphasizes the importance of knowledge and understanding, and how it leads to a strong faith and a deep connection with God. The verse also highlights the power and beauty of the QQur'an, which moves those who truly understand it to a state of worship and submission. The verse serves as a reminder for all believers to seek knowledge and understanding, and to be humble and submissive to God's message.
orig: قل آمنوا به أو لا تؤمنوا إن الذين أوتوا العلم من قبله إذا يتلى عليهم يخرون للأذقان سجدا

translation: And they say, 'Exalted is our Lord! Surely the promise of our Lord must be fulfilled.'
interpretation: The verse describes the response of the righteous people upon hearing the promise of their Lord. They exalt their Lord and express their belief that the promise of their Lord will certainly be fulfilled. The verse emphasizes the faith and certainty of the believers in the promises of God, and their reverence for the greatness and power of God.
orig: ويقولون سبحان ربنا إن كان وعد ربنا لمفعولا

translation: And they will come forth to him, (it will be) on the Day of Resurrection, crawling on their faces, blind, dumb and deaf.
interpretation: The verse describes the state of the disbelievers on the Day of Judgment. They will be crawling on their faces, indicating their humiliation and defeat. They will be blind, dumb, and deaf, symbolizing their inability to see the truth, speak the truth, and listen to the truth. The verse emphasizes the stark contrast between their current state of denial and rejection of the truth, and their ultimate fate on the Day of Judgment. It serves as a warning to those who reject the truth and a reminder of the severe consequences of their actions.
orig: ويخرون للأذقان يبكون ويزيدهم خشوعا

translation: Say, 'Invoke Allah or invoke the Most Merciful.' Whichever [name] you invoke - to Him belong the best names.' And do not recite your prayer loudly or quietly, but seek a way between that.'
interpretation: This verse encourages the believers to invoke or call upon Allah, the one and only God, by any of His beautiful names. The verse emphasizes that all of Allah's names are good and praiseworthy. The verse also advises the believers to find a balance in their prayer, neither making it too loud nor too quiet. The verse encourages the believers to seek a balance and a middle way in their worship of Allah and in their invocation of His names.
orig: قل ادعوا الله أو ادعوا الرحمن أيا ما تدعوا فله الأسماء الحسنى ولا تجهر بصلاتك ولا تخافت بها وابتغ بين ذلك سبيلا

translation: And say, 'Praise be to God, who has not taken a son and who has no partner in the Kingdom and who has no protector because of weakness.' And exalt Him with great exaltation.
interpretation: The verse is a call to praise God for His unique qualities and attributes. It emphasizes that God has no son, no partner in the Kingdom, and no protector because of weakness. These attributes distinguish God from all other deities and emphasize His absolute power and sovereignty. The verse also calls for exalting God with great exaltation, emphasizing the importance of recognizing and honoring His greatness and majesty. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of monotheism and the worship of the one true God, and encourages believers to express their gratitude and praise for God's blessings and attributes.
orig: وقل الحمد لله الذي لم يتخذ ولدا ولم يكن له شريك في الملك ولم يكن له ولي من الذل وكبره تكبيرا

translation: "All praise is for Allah who has sent down upon His servant the Book and has not placed in it any crookedness."
interpretation: The verse is praising Allah for sending down the Book (the Qur'an) and for ensuring that it is free from any errors or crookedness. This implies that the Qur'an is a perfect and complete revelation from Allah, free from any mistakes or inconsistencies. The verse serves as a reminder of the divine origin of the Qur'an and its importance as a guide for Muslims. It also emphasizes the importance of following the teachings of the Qur'an as it is a straight path that leads to the righteousness and salvation.
orig: الحمد لله الذي أنزل على عبده الكتاب ولم يجعل له عوجا

translation: As a reminder of the painful punishment from Him, and to give good news to the believers who do good that they will have a good reward.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the purpose of the Qur'an as a reminder of the painful punishment that will come from God for those who do not believe or commit injustice. At the same time, it brings good news to the believers who do good deeds, that they will receive a good reward. The verse highlights the importance of faith and good actions, and the consequences of not following God's teachings. It serves as a motivation for believers to continue doing good and a warning for those who do not, to change their ways before it's too late.
orig: قيما لينذر بأسا شديدا من لدنه ويبشر المؤمنين الذين يعملون الصالحات أن لهم أجرا حسنا

translation: But they will not stay therein (i.e. Paradise) forever.
interpretation: The verse highlights the temporary nature of even the most blissful of experiences in this world and the next. The inhabitants of Paradise will not remain therein forever, indicating that all things in this life and the next are temporary and fleeting. This verse can serve as a reminder to Muslims to be mindful of the transience of life and to focus on the eternal rewards of the hereafter.
orig: ماكثين فيه أبدا

translation: And those who say: 'Allah has taken to Himself a son',
interpretation: The verse addresses a specific group of people who make the claim that God has taken a son. This statement is a denial of the Islamic belief in the oneness and uniqueness of God (Tawhid). The verse serves as a warning to those who make this claim, reminding them of the falsity of their belief and the importance of upholding the unity of God in Islamic teachings.
orig: وينذر الذين قالوا اتخذ الله ولدا

translation: They have no knowledge of it, nor did their forefathers. It is nothing but a false claim that they utter, lying against
interpretation: No interpretation
orig: ما لهم به من علم ولا لآبائهم كبرت كلمة تخرج من أفواههم إن يقولون إلا كذبا

translation: Perhaps you (Muhammad) will kill yourself with grief, because they do not believe in this message.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the prophet Muhammad's concern and sadness over the disbelief of his people. The verse highlights the emotional toll that the prophet's mission took on him, as he feared that his people would not accept the message that had been revealed to him. The verse serves as a reminder of the challenges and difficulties that prophets face in their mission to convey God's message to humanity, and the sacrifices that they make in the process. It also emphasizes the importance of belief and faith, and the consequences of rejecting God's message.
orig: فلعلك باخع نفسك على آثارهم إن لم يؤمنوا بهذا الحديث أسفا

translation: We have made that which is on the earth an adornment for it, in order to test which of them will perform the best deed.
interpretation: The verse highlights the purpose of the creation of the earth and all the bounties within it. It explains that these are all adornments for the earth and have been created for a greater purpose, which is to test humanity. The verse emphasizes that the ultimate goal of this test is to determine who among humanity will perform the best deed. This interpretation suggests that the test of life is not only about faith, but also about actions and deeds. It encourages people to strive for excellence and righteousness in their actions, reminding them that they will be held accountable for their deeds in the afterlife.
orig: إنا جعلنا ما على الأرض زينة لها لنبلوهم أيهم أحسن عملا

translation: And indeed, We make what is on it (the earth) a bare plain, smooth.
interpretation: The verse describes the power and control of God over the earth and its transformation. The phrase 'And indeed, We make what is on it (the earth) a bare plain, smooth' implies that God has the ability to change the landscape of the earth as He pleases, making it flat and even. This verse highlights the majesty and might of God, emphasizing His role as the creator and sustainer of the universe. It also serves as a reminder of the temporary and ever-changing nature of the world, encouraging believers to focus on the eternal and unchanging nature of God.
orig: وإنا لجاعلون ما عليها صعيدا جرزا

translation: Or do you think that the people of the cave and the inscription were among Our wonderful signs?
interpretation: The verse refers to the story of the 'people of the cave' and the 'inscription' as examples of God's extraordinary signs. This reference is generally understood to be a story of a group of young Christians who sought refuge in a cave from religious persecution and fell into a deep sleep for several centuries. The 'inscription' mentioned in the verse is believed to be a reference to the inscription found near their cave that told their story. The verse emphasizes the miraculous nature of these events and encourages the reader to reflect on the power and wisdom of God. It may also serve as a reminder of the importance of faith and perseverance in the face of adversity.
orig: أم حسبت أن أصحاب الكهف والرقيم كانوا من آياتنا عجبا

translation: When the young men fled to the cave, they said, 'Our Lord, grant us mercy from Yourself and guide us in our affair correctly.'
interpretation: The verse describes the story of a group of young men who sought refuge in a cave and prayed to God for mercy and guidance. The verse emphasizes the young men's humility and submission to God, as they recognize their need for His help and guidance. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of seeking God's guidance in one's affairs and relying on His mercy and grace, rather than relying solely on one's own abilities and efforts.
orig: إذ أوى الفتية إلى الكهف فقالوا ربنا آتنا من لدنك رحمة وهيئ لنا من أمرنا رشدا

translation: And We caused them to be found in the cave, except a few, on their knees, clinging to each other. Saying: 'Lord, grant us mercy from You; surely, we have turned to You.'
interpretation: The verse describes the story of a group of people who took refuge in a cave to escape persecution. They fell into a deep sleep and remained there for many years. The verse emphasizes their state of helplessness and surrender, as they were found on their knees, clinging to each other. The verse also highlights their repentance and submission to God, as they prayed for His mercy and forgiveness. The verse serves as a reminder of the power of prayer and the importance of turning to God in times of distress and need.
orig: فضربنا على آذانهم في الكهف سنين عددا

translation: Then We sent after them, so We might know which of the two groups had greater transgression.
interpretation: The verse speaks about a situation where God sent a trial or a test after two groups of people, in order to determine which group was more unjust or transgressing. The verse suggests that both groups had engaged in some form of wrongdoing or transgression, but the extent and severity of their actions were different. By sending a trial or a test, God aimed to reveal the true nature and level of wickedness of each group. This verse can be seen as a reminder that all actions have consequences, and that God will ultimately judge and hold accountable all people for their deeds.
orig: ثم بعثناهم لنعلم أي الحزبين أحصى لما لبثوا أمدا

translation: We relate to you (O Muhammad) some of the news of Moses and Pharaoh in truth, verily, they were from our enlightened signs.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the story of Moses and Pharaoh as a truthful account. It highlights that they were among the enlightened signs from God. This verse serves as a reminder that the stories of the past are not mere tales, but lessons and guidance for the believers. It emphasizes the significance of the story of Moses and Pharaoh and encourages the believers to reflect upon it and learn from it.
orig: نحن نقص عليك نبأهم بالحق إنهم فتية آمنوا بربهم وزدناهم هدى

translation: And We bound their hearts when they stood up and said: 'Our Lord is the Lord of the heavens and the earth, we will never invoke any deity besides Him, we have indeed said, while we were unjust, that we would never associate anyone with our Lord.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about a group of people who, when standing up in prayer, declare their belief in the oneness of God and reject the worship of any other deities. They acknowledge that they had previously been unjust and had wrongly claimed that they would never associate anyone with God. The verse highlights the power of God to guide and misguide hearts, and the ability of humans to change their ways and repent for their past sins.
orig: وربطنا على قلوبهم إذ قاموا فقالوا ربنا رب السماوات والأرض لن ندعو من دونه إلها لقد قلنا إذا شططا

translation: These are My people, they have taken others as gods besides Me! What is wrong with these people? They are not but coming up with a lie against Allah.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the people who have taken other gods besides God and are therefore committing shirk (the sin of idolatry or polytheism). The verse expresses shock and disbelief at the actions of these people and questions their judgment. The verse emphasizes the seriousness of shirk and the severe consequences that come with it. The verse serves as a reminder to the importance of worshipping only one God and the dangers of associating partners with Him.
orig: هؤلاء قومنا اتخذوا من دونه آلهة لولا يأتون عليهم بسلطان بين فمن أظلم ممن افترى على الله كذبا

translation: And when you withdraw from them and what they worship other than Allah, then seek refuge in the cave. Your Lord will extend to you of His mercy and will prepare for you a way out.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the command to seek refuge in a cave when withdrawing from those who worship false gods. By doing so, God will extend His mercy to the believers and prepare a way out for them. This verse emphasizes the importance of distancing oneself from false worship and seeking God's protection. It also highlights God's mercy and compassion towards the believers, and His willingness to help and guide them through difficult times.
orig: وإذ اعتزلتموهم وما يعبدون إلا الله فأووا إلى الكهف ينشر لكم ربكم من رحمته ويهيئ لكم من أمركم مرفقا

translation: And you see the sun, when it rises, it ascends over their cave on the right, and when it sets, it sets above them on the left, while they are in it, this is from the signs of God. Whoever God guides is rightly guided, and whoever He leads astray, you will never find for him a guardian.
interpretation: The verse describes the movement of the sun, as it rises and sets, passing over a cave on the right and left of it. The verse emphasizes that this is one of the signs of God, indicating that everything in the universe is under His control and is a manifestation of His power. The verse then goes on to describe the consequences of God's guidance or misguidance, emphasizing that those who are guided by God are on the right path, while those who are led astray have no protector or guide.
orig: وترى الشمس إذا طلعت تزاور عن كهفهم ذات اليمين وإذا غربت تقرضهم ذات الشمال وهم في فجوة منه ذلك من آيات الله من يهد الله فهو المهتد ومن يضلل فلن تجد له وليا مرشدا

translation: And you think them awake, while they are asleep. And We turn them over on their right and on their left, while their dogs stretch out their forelegs in their pursuit, if you could see them, you would certainly turn back from them in aversion, and you will surely be filled with a sense of dread because of them.
interpretation: The verse describes the fate of unbelievers who are unaware of the impending doom. The verse compares them to people who are asleep and unaware of their surroundings. The phrase 'And We turn them over on their right and on their left' suggests that they are being moved or turned over, possibly in their graves, and are unable to escape their fate. The mention of their dogs and the description of their posture suggests that they are in a state of chaos and confusion. The verse warns the reader of the terrifying and fear-inspiring sight of the unbelievers in their punishment. The verse serves as a reminder of the reality of the afterlife and the consequences of disbelief.
orig: وتحسبهم أيقاظا وهم رقود ونقلبهم ذات اليمين وذات الشمال وكلبهم باسط ذراعيه بالوصيد لو اطلعت عليهم لوليت منهم فرارا ولملئت منهم رعبا

translation: And thus We made them (the people of the city) ask one another, 'How long have you stayed (here)?' They said, 'We have stayed (here) a day or part of a day.' They said, 'Your Lord is most knowing of how long you have stayed (here).' So send one of you with this your silver coin to the city, and let him look to which of them has the purest food, and let him bring you from it a provision, and let him be courteous and not make anyone aware of you.
interpretation: The verse describes a situation where the people of a city have been asked how long they have stayed there. The response indicates that it has only been a day or part of a day. The verse emphasizes that only their Lord knows the true answer. The people are then instructed to send one of their group with their silver coin to the city to find the purest food. The person should be courteous and not make their presence known. The verse suggests a sense of urgency and caution, potentially indicating that the people are in a difficult or dangerous situation. It also highlights the importance of being respectful and considerate in their interactions with others.
orig: وكذلك بعثناهم ليتساءلوا بينهم قال قائل منهم كم لبثتم قالوا لبثنا يوما أو بعض يوم قالوا ربكم أعلم بما لبثتم فابعثوا أحدكم بورقكم هذه إلى المدينة فلينظر أيها أزكى طعاما فليأتكم برزق منه وليتلطف ولا يشعرن بكم أحدا

translation: Indeed, if they expose themselves to you, they would rush to you [to fight] or engage you in secret discord. And they do not seek your decision [O Muhammad] in the matter. They are but inflaming the fire of war. Indeed, for the wrongdoers, there is not victory.
interpretation: The verse describes the hostile intentions of those who oppose the Prophet Muhammad and his followers. If given the chance, they would either attack openly or plot secretly against the Muslims. They are not interested in a fair resolution or decision from the Prophet. Instead, they are intent on causing conflict and strife. The verse highlights the aggressive and harmful nature of these opponents and emphasizes that they will ultimately not be successful in their efforts against the righteous.
orig: إنهم إن يظهروا عليكم يرجموكم أو يعيدوكم في ملتهم ولن تفلحوا إذا أبدا

translation: And thus do We make some of them (people) taste the severity of punishment, so that they might return (to obedience of God). So when they neglected what they had been reminded of, We punished them, and suddenly Allah produced for them a sample of severe punishment. So when they saw it, they said: 'We believe in Allah alone and bear witness that we indeed are Muslims (submitted to Him).' But our Word had already been passed among the former peoples (who disbelieved and were punished). So they will not believe (even) then, except a few.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the use of punishment as a means of guiding people back to the right path. It highlights the severity of the punishment and the suddenness of its arrival. Despite experiencing the punishment, some people still refuse to believe and submit to God. The verse suggests that this is a recurring pattern in human behavior, as it mentions that the same thing happened to previous nations. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of obedience and submission to God, and the consequences of denial and disbelief.
orig: وكذلك أعثرنا عليهم ليعلموا أن وعد الله حق وأن الساعة لا ريب فيها إذ يتنازعون بينهم أمرهم فقالوا ابنوا عليهم بنيانا ربهم أعلم بهم قال الذين غلبوا على أمرهم لنتخذن عليهم مسجدا

translation: They will say, 'Three [of them were lost]; the fourth, their dog.' And they will say, 'Five; the sixth, their dog.' Guessing at [the number of] the unseen, and they will not be correct. And they will say, 'Seven, and the eighth of them is their dog.' Say, 'My Lord is most knowing of their number; none knows them but a few.' So do not argue with them concerning that which you have no knowledge; and do not rely upon a hypothesis.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about people who are making guesses and assumptions about the fate of a group of people or animals, specifically three to eight people and their dog. The people are speculating about the number of survivors or victims, and they are shown to be incorrect and uncertain in their speculations. The verse emphasizes the limits of human knowledge and understanding, and it encourages the listener to refrain from arguing or speculating about matters beyond their knowledge. The verse also reminds the listener to rely on divine guidance and knowledge, as represented by the statement 'My Lord is most knowing of their number; none knows them but a few.' The verse encourages the listener to focus on what they know for certain and to avoid speculation and assumptions about the unknown.
orig: سيقولون ثلاثة رابعهم كلبهم ويقولون خمسة سادسهم كلبهم رجما بالغيب ويقولون سبعة وثامنهم كلبهم قل ربي أعلم بعدتهم ما يعلمهم إلا قليل فلا تمار فيهم إلا مراء ظاهرا ولا تستفت فيهم منهم أحدا

translation: And say not of anything, 'Indeed, I will do that tomorrow',
interpretation: The verse advises against making promises about the future that may not come to pass, or taking one's plans for granted. It reminds the reader that only Allah knows what the future holds, and that one should not be overconfident in their own abilities and plans. The verse encourages humility and mindfulness, and serves as a reminder that the best laid plans can be disrupted by unforeseen circumstances.
orig: ولا تقولن لشيء إني فاعل ذلك غدا

translation: But except whom Allah wills. And remember your Lord when you forget and say, 'Perhaps my Lord will guide me to a nearer [right] course than this.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the power of Allah's will and the importance of remembering and seeking guidance from Allah. The phrase 'But except whom Allah wills' emphasizes that only those whom Allah wills can escape from a situation or circumstance. The verse then instructs the reader to remember and seek guidance from Allah when they forget. The phrase 'Perhaps my Lord will guide me to a nearer [right] course than this' indicates the importance of seeking guidance and the belief that Allah can guide and direct the reader to a better path. The verse serves as a reminder of the power and wisdom of Allah and the importance of seeking His guidance and help in all matters.
orig: إلا أن يشاء الله واذكر ربك إذا نسيت وقل عسى أن يهدين ربي لأقرب من هذا رشدا

translation: And they stayed in their cave three hundred years, adding nine.
interpretation: The verse speaks about a group of people who stayed in a cave for a period of 300 years, with an additional nine years. The verse is a part of a story of the People of the Cave, who were believers and sought refuge in a cave to escape persecution. The verse emphasizes the long period of time that they spent in the cave, indicating their patience and steadfastness in their faith. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of remaining steadfast in one's beliefs, even in the face of adversity and persecution.
orig: ولبثوا في كهفهم ثلاث مائة سنين وازدادوا تسعا

translation: Say, 'Allah is most knowing of how long they remained. To Him belongs the unseen of the heavens and the earth. He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise. [He] knows what is before them and what will be after them, and they do not encompass a thing of His knowledge except for what He wills. His Kursi extends over the heavens and the earth, and their preservation does not tire Him, and He is the Most High, the Great.',
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's (God's) complete knowledge and power over all things, both in the heavens and on earth. The verse reminds the reader that Allah knows everything, including how long people have remained on earth, and that nothing is hidden from Him. The verse also highlights Allah's ability to know both the past and the future, and that His knowledge is all-encompassing. The verse serves as a reminder of Allah's greatness and power, and encourages the reader to have faith and trust in Him.
orig: قل الله أعلم بما لبثوا له غيب السماوات والأرض أبصر به وأسمع ما لهم من دونه من ولي ولا يشرك في حكمه أحدا

translation: And recite what has been revealed to you of the Book of your Lord, there is no changing His words, and you will not find in other than Him any refuge.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of reciting and following the word of God, as it cannot be changed or altered. It also highlights that God's words are the ultimate truth and that there is no protection or refuge from His commands. The verse serves as a reminder to the believers to adhere to the teachings of the Qur'an, and to submit to the will of God, as there is no other source of guidance or salvation.
orig: واتل ما أوحي إليك من كتاب ربك لا مبدل لكلماته ولن تجد من دونه ملتحدا

translation: And be patient with those who call upon their Lord morning and evening, seeking His countenance, and let not your eyes pass from them, desiring the adornment of the life of this world; and obey not him whose heart We have made heedless of Our remembrance, and follows his desire, and his affair has exceeded bounds.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the importance of being patient and having sabr (steadfastness) with those who worship and call upon their Lord consistently, both in the morning and in the evening. It warns against being distracted by the adornments and superficial attractions of this world, and against following those who are heedless of God's remembrance and are driven by their desires. The verse emphasizes the importance of obedience to God and following the right path, rather than being led astray by those who have exceeded bounds in their affairs.
orig: واصبر نفسك مع الذين يدعون ربهم بالغداة والعشي يريدون وجهه ولا تعد عيناك عنهم تريد زينة الحياة الدنيا ولا تطع من أغفلنا قلبه عن ذكرنا واتبع هواه وكان أمره فرطا

translation: And say, 'The truth is from your Lord.' So whoever wills, let him believe; and whoever wills, let him disbelieve. Indeed, We have prepared for the wrongdoers a fire, whose walls will surround them. If they call for help, they will be helped with water like murky oil, which burns the faces. Wretched is the drink and evil is the resting place.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the choice given to people to either believe or disbelieve in the truth from their Lord. However, the verse also highlights the consequences of disbelief, which is the punishment of a fiery hell. The verse describes the fire as having walls that surround the wrongdoers, emphasizing the idea of entrapment and no escape. The verse also describes the 'help' that the wrongdoers will receive as water like murky oil, which burns their faces and causes them suffering. The verse ends with a description of the fire as a wretched and evil resting place, reinforcing the idea of the severity of the punishment. The verse serves as a warning to those who reject the truth and a reminder of the consequences of their actions.
orig: وقل الحق من ربكم فمن شاء فليؤمن ومن شاء فليكفر إنا أعتدنا للظالمين نارا أحاط بهم سرادقها وإن يستغيثوا يغاثوا بماء كالمهل يشوي الوجوه بئس الشراب وساءت مرتفقا

translation: Indeed, those who have believed and done righteous deeds - indeed, We will not allow to be lost the reward of any who did well in deeds.
interpretation: The verse affirms that those who have faith in God and do good deeds will not have their rewards lost or wasted. The verse emphasizes the importance of righteous actions and the promise of God to preserve and protect the rewards of those who strive to do good. The verse serves as a source of hope and motivation for believers, reminding them that their efforts and good deeds will not be in vain.
orig: إن الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات إنا لا نضيع أجر من أحسن عملا

translation: Those are for them gardens of Eden, beneath which rivers flow. They will be adorned therein with bracelets of gold and will wear green garments of fine silk and brocade, reclining therein on raised couches. Excellent is the reward and plentiful is the pleasure.
interpretation: The verse describes the blessings and rewards that will be given to certain people in the afterlife. These rewards include gardens of paradise, flowing rivers, gold bracelets, fine clothing, and comfortable seating. The description of these rewards is meant to convey the greatness and magnificence of paradise and the happiness and satisfaction that the people will experience there. The verse serves as a motivation for believers to strive for righteousness and good deeds, in order to attain these rewards in the afterlife.
orig: أولئك لهم جنات عدن تجري من تحتهم الأنهار يحلون فيها من أساور من ذهب ويلبسون ثيابا خضرا من سندس وإستبرق متكئين فيها على الأرائك نعم الثواب وحسنت مرتفقا

translation: And give them an example of two men: We made one of them two gardens of grapes, and surrounded them with palm trees, and placed between them crops.
interpretation: This verse uses a metaphor to illustrate a point. It describes two men, one of whom was given two beautiful gardens filled with grapes and surrounded by palm trees, with crops planted in between. The image is one of abundance and prosperity. However, the interpretation of this verse is not explicitly stated in the text, and its meaning may depend on the context in which it is used. It could be interpreted as a reminder of the blessings that God can bestow upon people, or as a warning about the fleeting nature of worldly possessions. Ultimately, the interpretation of this verse is open to some debate and may depend on the broader theological or moral framework in which it is considered.
orig: واضرب لهم مثلا رجلين جعلنا لأحدهما جنتين من أعناب وحففناهما بنخل وجعلنا بينهما زرعا

translation: Both its fruits (
interpretation: No interpretation
orig: كلتا الجنتين آتت أكلها ولم تظلم منه شيئا وفجرنا خلالهما نهرا

translation: And he had some fruit, so he said to his companion while he was conversing with him, 'I am greater than you in wealth and more respected by people.'
interpretation: The verse describes a man who is boasting about his wealth and social status to his companion. The man's statement, 'I am greater than you in wealth and more respected by people,' reveals his arrogance and pride. The verse serves as a reminder that material possessions and social status do not guarantee moral superiority or righteousness. It also highlights the dangers of arrogance and pride, which can lead to a person's downfall.
orig: وكان له ثمر فقال لصاحبه وهو يحاوره أنا أكثر منك مالا وأعز نفرا

translation: But he entered his garden while he was unjust to himself, saying, 'I do not think that this will perish - ever.'
interpretation: The verse describes a person who enters his garden while being unjust to himself, meaning that he is not treating himself with the righteousness and virtue that is required of him. This person then makes a statement of disbelief, expressing his doubt in the perishing of his garden. The verse serves as a reminder that arrogance and a lack of faith can lead to a person's downfall, and that one's possessions and wealth are temporary and fleeting.
orig: ودخل جنته وهو ظالم لنفسه قال ما أظن أن تبيد هذه أبدا

translation: And I do not think the Hour will be established, and if I am returned to my Lord, I surely find better than it a return.
interpretation: The verse expresses a skepticism about the coming of the 'Hour' or the Day of Judgment, but it also indicates a hope for a better fate in the afterlife. The speaker believes that if they were to return to their Lord, they would find something better than the Hour. This verse can be interpreted as a reminder of the importance of faith and trust in God's plan, even when the future seems uncertain or bleak. It encourages believers to look forward to the afterlife as a place of peace and reward, rather than fearing the Day of Judgment.
orig: وما أظن الساعة قائمة ولئن رددت إلى ربي لأجدن خيرا منها منقلبا

translation: His companion said to him while he was conversing with him: 'Have you disbelieved in the One who created you from dust, then from a sperm-drop, then shaped you into a man?
interpretation: The verse describes a conversation between two people, where one of them is questioning the other's disbelief in God. The verse emphasizes the greatness of God's creation, reminding the listener of their humble beginnings as dust and a sperm-drop before being shaped into a human being. The verse serves as a reminder of God's power and greatness, and the importance of recognizing and acknowledging this power by having faith in Him.
orig: قال له صاحبه وهو يحاوره أكفرت بالذي خلقك من تراب ثم من نطفة ثم سواك رجلا

translation: But surely, I am Allah; there is no god but I; therefore serve Me (only),
interpretation: The verse is a clear declaration of the oneness of God and His sovereignty. The speaker asserts that they are Allah, the only God, and that no other god exists. The verse commands the listener to worship only this one God, and not to associate any partners with Him. This is a fundamental tenet of Islamic faith, known as Tawhid (the oneness of God). The verse emphasizes the importance of worshiping the one and only God, and the rejection of any other deities or beliefs that contradict this fundamental principle.
orig: لكنا هو الله ربي ولا أشرك بربي أحدا

translation: And if, when they entered your garden, they had said: 'What Allah wills (is done)! There is no power but with Allah!' Indeed, if you see me less than you in wealth and children,
interpretation: This verse is a continuation of a conversation between two people, one of whom has a beautiful garden. The verse emphasizes the importance of submitting to the will of God and recognizing His power and control over all things. The speaker acknowledges that, despite any perceived differences in wealth or offspring, it is ultimately God's will that prevails. The verse serves as a reminder to be humble and grateful for what one has, and to trust in God's plan, rather than becoming arrogant or boastful about one's possessions.
orig: ولولا إذ دخلت جنتك قلت ما شاء الله لا قوة إلا بالله إن ترن أنا أقل منك مالا وولدا

translation: Perhaps my Lord will give me something better than your garden, and will send upon it a torrent from the sky, so that it becomes a slippery, muddy ground.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the possibility of God granting something better than the garden being boasted about, and sending down a torrent from the sky that transforms it into a slippery, muddy ground. The verse can be interpreted as a reminder that God is all-powerful and can replace what seems valuable and good with something completely different, and that one should not place too much value and pride in material possessions. It also serves as a warning to those who boast and show off their possessions, indicating that these possessions can quickly be destroyed and taken away.
orig: فعسى ربي أن يؤتين خيرا من جنتك ويرسل عليها حسبانا من السماء فتصبح صعيدا زلقا

translation: Or its waters flow deep, then you will never be able to seek it out.
interpretation: The verse describes the fate of a town that has been destroyed and its water supply has been ruined. The phrase 'Or its waters flow deep' implies that the water has become inaccessible, perhaps due to flooding or other natural disaster. The second part of the verse, 'then you will never be able to seek it out', emphasizes the permanence of this destruction. This verse can be interpreted as a warning of the consequences of disobedience and arrogance towards God, highlighting the vulnerability of human creations in the face of God's power and wrath.
orig: أو يصبح ماؤها غورا فلن تستطيع له طلبا

translation: And let him cling to the rope of Allah and be of the sincere in religion. And let him not be of those who associate others with Allah. For then he would be of the losers.
interpretation: The verse encourages the reader to hold fast to the rope of Allah, which refers to the teachings and guidance of Islam, and to be sincere in their religious practices. It warns against associating partners with Allah, which is a grave sin and a rejection of monotheism. The verse also warns that those who commit this sin will be among the losers, meaning that they will not attain salvation or success in the hereafter.
orig: وأحيط بثمره فأصبح يقلب كفيه على ما أنفق فيها وهي خاوية على عروشها ويقول يا ليتني لم أشرك بربي أحدا

translation: And he had no group to support him against Allah nor was he one of those who could defend themselves.
interpretation: The verse speaks about an individual who had no supporters or allies to help him against God. The person was also not among those who could defend themselves, indicating their powerlessness and vulnerability in the face of God's judgment. The verse emphasizes the futility of trying to stand against God and highlights the importance of submission to His will. It serves as a reminder that no one can escape God's judgment and that resistance is futile.
orig: ولم تكن له فئة ينصرونه من دون الله وما كان منتصرا

translation: The dominion in that day will be solely for Allah (God). He will reward the (righteous) and He is the best of rewarders.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the Day of Judgment, when the dominion and power will belong solely to Allah. On this day, Allah will reward those who have done good deeds and followed the right path. The verse emphasizes that Allah is the best of all rewarders, indicating that the rewards He gives are the most just and perfect. The verse serves as a reminder that all worldly power and dominion are temporary and that ultimate power and control belong to Allah alone. It also encourages people to do good deeds and follow the right path, in order to receive the best rewards from Allah on the Day of Judgment.
orig: هنالك الولاية لله الحق هو خير ثوابا وخير عقبا

translation: And strike for them an example of the world's life: like water which We send down from the sky, then the plants of the earth mingle with it, then they become dry remnants that the winds scatter. And Allah is over all things competent.
interpretation: The verse uses the metaphor of water and plants to illustrate the fleeting and transient nature of worldly life. Just as water is sent down from the sky, nourishing the plants and causing them to grow, so too does worldly life appear to be full of blessings and prosperity. However, just as the plants eventually wither and dry up, so too does worldly life come to an end. The verse serves as a reminder that all worldly possessions and achievements are temporary and that true success lies in preparing for the afterlife. The verse emphasizes that God is all-powerful and in control of all things, and that everything in this world is temporary and fleeting compared to His power and majesty.
orig: واضرب لهم مثل الحياة الدنيا كماء أنزلناه من السماء فاختلط به نبات الأرض فأصبح هشيما تذروه الرياح وكان الله على كل شيء مقتدرا

translation: Wealth and sons are the adornment of the life of this world. And the good deed that endures (i.e. a goodly act that will remain in the Hereafter) is better with your Lord in reward and better in hope.
interpretation: The verse highlights the temporary and fleeting nature of worldly possessions, such as wealth and children, by referring to them as 'the adornment of the life of this world'. The verse then contrasts these with 'the good deed that endures', which is a goodly act that will remain in the Hereafter. The verse suggests that such deeds are of greater value and have a more lasting impact than worldly possessions. The verse encourages believers to focus on performing good deeds and seeking God's pleasure, as these will be of greater benefit to them in the Hereafter.
orig: المال والبنون زينة الحياة الدنيا والباقيات الصالحات خير عند ربك ثوابا وخير أملا
