translation: And the Day We shall cause the mountains to pass away (like clouds of dust), and you will see the earth as a levelled plain, and We shall gather them all together so that nothing will be missing of them.
interpretation: The verse describes the Day of Judgment, when the mountains will be made to pass away and the earth will be leveled. It emphasizes the completeness and totality of God's gathering of all people, stating that nothing and no one will be missing. The verse serves as a reminder of the power and authority of God, who is capable of transforming the natural world and gathering all of humanity on the Day of Judgment.
orig: ويوم نسير الجبال وترى الأرض بارزة وحشرناهم فلم نغادر منهم أحدا

translation: And show forth to your Lord truthfully the mansions; you will surely enter them, as We created you the first time, nay, you are surely going to make promises!
interpretation: The verse is a challenge to the disbelievers to present their 'mansions' or deeds before God on the Day of Judgment. The verse emphasizes that they will surely enter these mansions, just as God created them in the first place. However, the verse also highlights the irony that despite the certainty of this event, the disbelievers continue to deny and make false promises. The verse serves as a reminder that the Day of Judgment is inevitable and that all actions will be accounted for, even if the disbelievers choose to ignore this reality.
orig: وعرضوا على ربك صفا لقد جئتمونا كما خلقناكم أول مرة بل زعمتم ألن نجعل لكم موعدا

translation: And We have set forth for mankind in this Qur'an every kind of parable, that they may remember. (It is) in stories of ancient peoples. And therein is warning for them, and a teaching for those of understanding. Is it not a sign to them that the learned men of the Children of Israel knew it?
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of the Qur'an as a source of guidance and wisdom for mankind, containing various parables and stories from the past to provide lessons and warnings. The verse highlights the significance of the knowledge of the Children of Israel, who were aware of these stories and their meanings. The verse serves as a reminder for people to reflect on the signs and messages within the Qur'an and to learn from the experiences of those who came before them.
orig: ووضع الكتاب فترى المجرمين مشفقين مما فيه ويقولون يا ويلتنا مال هذا الكتاب لا يغادر صغيرة ولا كبيرة إلا أحصاها ووجدوا ما عملوا حاضرا ولا يظلم ربك أحدا

translation: And when We said to the angels, 'Prostrate before Adam,' they prostrated, except for Iblis. He was of the jinn and he broke the command of his Lord. Will you then take him and his descendants as allies instead of Me, while they are enemies to you? How wretched is the exchange for the wrongdoers!
interpretation: The verse speaks about the event of the creation of Adam and the command of God to the angels to prostrate before him. All the angels obeyed, except for Iblis, who was a jinn and refused to prostrate out of pride and arrogance. The verse emphasizes the importance of obedience to God's commands and the consequences of disobedience. The verse also warns against following the ways of Iblis and his descendants, who are described as enemies of the believers. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of choosing the right allies and the dangers of following the wrong path.
orig: وإذ قلنا للملائكة اسجدوا لآدم فسجدوا إلا إبليس كان من الجن ففسق عن أمر ربه أفتتخذونه وذريته أولياء من دوني وهم لكم عدو بئس للظالمين بدلا

translation: I swear by the creation of the heavens and the earth and by the creation of your souls, you are not My assistants in the affair of the misguided.
interpretation: The verse is a solemn oath by God, swearing by the creation of the heavens, the earth, and the souls of human beings. God emphasizes that the souls are also part of His creation, thus asserting His power and control over all of creation. The verse then refutes any suggestion that the speaker (who is believed to be the Prophet Muhammad) is an assistant or helper in the affair of the misguided. This implies that the responsibility for guiding and leading people lies solely with God, and that the Prophet is merely a messenger conveying God's message. The verse may also serve as a reminder that human beings are not capable of guiding or saving others from error, and that they should instead focus on their own relationship with God and their own salvation.
orig: ما أشهدتهم خلق السماوات والأرض ولا خلق أنفسهم وما كنت متخذ المضلين عضدا

translation: And the Day they will call upon their idols, but they will not respond to them, and We will place between them a separation.
interpretation: The verse describes the Day of Judgment when people will call upon their idols for help, but they will not receive any response. The verse emphasizes the powerlessness and falsity of idols and false gods. Furthermore, it highlights the separation that God will create between people and their false objects of worship, indicating the ultimate rejection of these false deities. The verse serves as a warning to those who worship false idols, reminding them of the futility of their worship and the need to turn to the one true God.
orig: ويوم يقول نادوا شركائي الذين زعمتم فدعوهم فلم يستجيبوا لهم وجعلنا بينهم موبقا

translation: And the criminals will see the fire and think that they are to fall into it, but they will not find a way of escape from it.
interpretation: The verse describes the fate of criminals who, upon seeing the fire of hell, will think that they are about to fall into it. However, the verse emphasizes that there will be no escape from the fire for them. The verse serves as a warning to those who commit sins and crimes, reminding them of the severe consequences of their actions and the inevitability of divine justice.
orig: ورأى المجرمون النار فظنوا أنهم مواقعوها ولم يجدوا عنها مصرفا

translation: And indeed, in this Qur'an, We have presented to the people every kind of example; and man is, most of anything, argumentative.
interpretation: The verse highlights the comprehensive nature of the Qur'an, which contains examples and lessons for all aspects of life. Despite the clarity of the Qur'an, human beings are prone to argumentation and are quick to disagree, which is a reflection of their inherent weakness and imperfection. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of humility, reflection, and submission to the divine guidance, and the need to avoid being overly critical and argumentative.
orig: ولقد صرفنا في هذا القرآن للناس من كل مثل وكان الإنسان أكثر شيء جدلا

translation: And nothing prevented people from believing when guidance came to them and from asking forgiveness of their Lord except that there came to them the custom of the former peoples or that the punishment came to them beforehand.
interpretation: The verse highlights the reasons why people fail to believe and seek forgiveness from their Lord. The two reasons are: (1) following the ways of the previous disbelieving nations and (2) being punished by God before they have a chance to repent. The verse emphasizes the importance of guidance and the need for people to seize the opportunity to believe and seek forgiveness, rather than following the ways of the disbelievers. The verse serves as a warning to those who reject the guidance and continue to commit sins, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the danger of following the ways of the previous disbelievers.
orig: وما منع الناس أن يؤمنوا إذ جاءهم الهدى ويستغفروا ربهم إلا أن تأتيهم سنة الأولين أو يأتيهم العذاب قبلا

translation: And We did not send the messengers except as bearers of good news and warners. So those who disbelieve argue with falsehood to defeat the truth and take My verses and the warning as [a mere] joke.
interpretation: The verse highlights the role of the messengers as bearers of good news and warners. It emphasizes that the disbelievers reject the message of the messengers and argue with falsehood to defeat the truth. They also take the verses of God and the warning of punishment as a joke, showing their lack of respect and disregard for the divine message. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of accepting the truth and the consequences of rejecting it.
orig: وما نرسل المرسلين إلا مبشرين ومنذرين ويجادل الذين كفروا بالباطل ليدحضوا به الحق واتخذوا آياتي وما أنذروا هزوا

translation: And who is more unjust than those who are reminded of the signs of their Lord, then turn away from them and forget what their hands have sent forth? Indeed, We have put covers over their hearts, lest they understand it, and in their ears is deafness. And even if you invite them to guidance, they will never be guided.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the unjust behavior of those who reject the signs of their Lord and turn away from them. The verse emphasizes the hard-heartedness of these people, who forget the consequences of their actions and the warnings of their Lord. The verse suggests that God has placed a veil over their hearts and ears, preventing them from understanding the truth and accepting guidance. The verse serves as a warning to those who deny the signs of God and reject the truth, emphasizing the futility of inviting them to guidance, as they are unwilling to change their ways and accept the truth.
orig: ومن أظلم ممن ذكر بآيات ربه فأعرض عنها ونسي ما قدمت يداه إنا جعلنا على قلوبهم أكنة أن يفقهوه وفي آذانهم وقرا وإن تدعهم إلى الهدى فلن يهتدوا إذا أبدا

translation: And your Lord is the Forgiving, the Merciful. If He were to seize them for what they have earned, He would surely hasten the punishment for them. But for them there is a time, they will not find a protector besides Him.
interpretation: The verse highlights God's attributes of forgiveness and mercy, contrasting them with the punishment that the people would receive if God were to seize them for their sins. The verse emphasizes the severity of the punishment and the inevitability of its arrival. However, the verse also indicates that the punishment will not come immediately, but at a predetermined time. This gives the people an opportunity to repent and seek forgiveness. The verse reminds the people that they have no protection from the punishment except through God's mercy and forgiveness.
orig: وربك الغفور ذو الرحمة لو يؤاخذهم بما كسبوا لعجل لهم العذاب بل لهم موعد لن يجدوا من دونه موئلا

translation: And such were the towns – We destroyed them when they acted unjustly, and We have appointed a time for their destruction.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes that their destruction was a result of their own actions and that their punishment was not arbitrary or without cause. The verse also highlights the inevitability of their destruction, as it was already appointed by God. The verse serves as a reminder that those who commit injustice will ultimately be held accountable for their actions and face the consequences of their actions.
orig: وتلك القرى أهلكناهم لما ظلموا وجعلنا لمهلكهم موعدا

translation: And when Moses said to his servant, 'I will not give up until I reach the junction of the two seas, or I will journey on for years.',
interpretation: The verse speaks about Moses' determination and patience in his search for knowledge and truth. Moses tells his servant that he will not rest until he reaches the junction of the two seas, or even if it takes him years. This illustrates Moses' unwavering commitment to his goal, and his willingness to persevere through challenges and difficulties. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of persistence and determination in the pursuit of one's goals, and the value of patience and hard work in the face of obstacles.
orig: وإذ قال موسى لفتاه لا أبرح حتى أبلغ مجمع البحرين أو أمضي حقبا

translation: But when the big one between them both forgot, it left it (the small one) on the land, while it took a path through the sea aggressively.
interpretation: The verse describes the story of two sea creatures, one larger than the other. When the larger creature forgot about the smaller one, it left it on the land and continued on its way through the sea with aggression. The verse can be interpreted as a metaphor for the behavior of people in power, who may forget or neglect those who are weaker or less powerful. The verse serves as a reminder to those in power to be mindful of their actions and to treat others with fairness and kindness.
orig: فلما بلغا مجمع بينهما نسيا حوتهما فاتخذ سبيله في البحر سربا

translation: But when he had passed it, he said to a boy: 'Bring us our meal. Indeed, we have encountered fatigue on this journey of ours.'
interpretation: The verse describes a scene where a traveler, after passing a town, asks his companion to bring him food as they have become tired from their journey. The verse highlights the basic human need for sustenance and rest, even in the midst of travel and exploration. The verse may also serve as a reminder of the importance of taking care of oneself and one's companions, especially in times of hardship or exhaustion.
orig: فلما جاوزا قال لفتاه آتنا غداءنا لقد لقينا من سفرنا هذا نصبا

translation: He said, 'Do you see when we were on the rock, and I forgot the fish, and none but Satan made me forget to remember it, and it took its course in the sea astonishingly.',
interpretation: The verse speaks about the story of Moses and his servant Joshua, when they were on their journey and stopped by a rock. Moses left the fish they had with them on the rock, and when they returned, they found that it had been taken by the sea. Moses realized that it was Satan who had made him forget about the fish. The verse emphasizes the power of Satan in leading people astray and the importance of being mindful and vigilant in one's actions. It also highlights the role of divine guidance in helping people to remember and recognize their mistakes.
orig: قال أرأيت إذ أوينا إلى الصخرة فإني نسيت الحوت وما أنسانيه إلا الشيطان أن أذكره واتخذ سبيله في البحر عجبا

translation: It was said, 'That is (the consequence) which we had no knowledge of - we were not acting unjustly towards them and were guided aright.'
interpretation: The verse is part of a conversation between the people of a destroyed town and God. The people are expressing their surprise and denial of any wrongdoing towards the previous inhabitants of the town. They claim that they were not unjust and were on the right path. The verse emphasizes the people's lack of knowledge and understanding of the situation, and their denial of any wrongdoing. It serves as a reminder that even those who believe they are on the right path can be mistaken, and that true guidance comes from God.
orig: قال ذلك ما كنا نبغ فارتدا على آثارهما قصصا

translation: And We found a servant of Ours among them who said: 'I will surely go to the Lord with sincerity.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about a servant of God who was found among a group of people. This servant had pledged to worship and serve God with sincerity and devotion. The verse highlights the servant's strong commitment and determination to follow the path of righteousness and to seek God's pleasure. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of sincerity and devotion in one's faith and the rewards that come with it.
orig: فوجدا عبدا من عبادنا آتيناه رحمة من عندنا وعلمناه من لدنا علما

translation: Moses said to him, 'Can I follow you so that you may teach me guidance of what you have been taught?'
interpretation: In this verse, Moses is speaking to a man who is believed to have been given knowledge and guidance from God. Moses expresses his desire to follow the man and learn from him, recognizing the value of the guidance and wisdom that the man has received. The verse highlights the importance of seeking knowledge and guidance from those who are knowledgeable and rightly guided, and the willingness of Moses to be a follower and student in order to attain that guidance.
orig: قال له موسى هل أتبعك على أن تعلمن مما علمت رشدا

translation: You said, 'Indeed, you will not be able to have patience with me.'
interpretation: The verse is a quote of someone speaking, expressing their belief that the person they are speaking to will not be able to have patience or endure their behavior. The interpretation of this verse depends on the context in which it is used, but it may be a warning or a challenge. The speaker may be expressing frustration or anger, or they may be testing the patience of the other person. Ultimately, the meaning of this verse is open to interpretation and depends on the context in which it is used.
orig: قال إنك لن تستطيع معي صبرا

translation: And how can you be patient about what you do not comprehend?
interpretation: The verse is a rhetorical question posed by the Qur'an, addressing the disbelievers who reject the message of Islam. The verse is asking how the disbelievers can remain patient and steadfast in their disbelief, when they do not fully understand or comprehend the message that they are rejecting. The verse implies that the disbelievers are being unreasonable and unjust in their rejection of the message, and that they should instead be seeking to understand and learn more about it before making a decision. The verse serves as a call to the disbelievers to open their minds and hearts to the message of Islam, and to seek guidance and understanding from God.
orig: وكيف تصبر على ما لم تحط به خبرا

translation: He said, 'You will find me, if Allah wills, patient and I will not disobey you in any matter.'
interpretation: The verse is a statement made by a person, expressing their commitment and obedience to the person being addressed. The person promises to be patient and obedient, regardless of the circumstances, as long as it is the will of God. The verse emphasizes the importance of obedience and patience, especially in the face of challenges or difficulties. It suggests that the person is willing to submit to the will of the other, even if it goes against their own desires or interests. The verse can be interpreted as a sign of respect, submission and trust in the person being addressed.
orig: قال ستجدني إن شاء الله صابرا ولا أعصي لك أمرا

translation: He said, 'So if you follow me, do not ask me about anything until I make a mention of it to you.'
interpretation: The verse is a statement made by a prophet or a messenger, instructing his followers not to ask him any questions until he himself brings up the topic of discussion. This could be interpreted as a way of maintaining focus and discipline among the followers, ensuring that they pay full attention to the message being delivered. It may also serve as a reminder that the prophet or messenger has been chosen by God to convey a specific message, and that he has the authority to determine the pace and manner of its delivery. The verse emphasizes the importance of trust and obedience in the relationship between the prophet or messenger and his followers.
orig: قال فإن اتبعتني فلا تسألني عن شيء حتى أحدث لك منه ذكرا

translation: So go on board (the ship). When they were in the ship, he (Noah) said: 'Embark in it. In the name of Allah be its moving course and its anchoring place.' Indeed, my Lord is indeed forgiving and merciful.' Then as soon as they forgot (Noah's warning) and were careless, the wave (of a storm) came to them and the ship was broken into pieces. Then they realized their mistake when there was no way of escape.
interpretation: The verse describes the story of the Prophet Noah and his people. When the people had finally boarded the ship, Noah entrusted their safety to God, hoping for His forgiveness and mercy. However, as soon as the people became careless and forgot Noah's warning, a wave from a storm hit the ship and it was destroyed. The verse emphasizes the importance of remembering and following the guidance of the prophets and the consequences of ignoring their warnings. It also highlights the power and control of God over all things and His ability to punish those who are unjust and disobedient.
orig: فانطلقا حتى إذا ركبا في السفينة خرقها قال أخرقتها لتغرق أهلها لقد جئت شيئا إمرا

translation: He said, 'Did I not tell you that you would not be able to have patience with me?'
interpretation: The verse is a statement made by someone, likely a prophet or messenger, who is facing resistance and impatience from his people. The speaker is expressing his frustration and disappointment towards the people's lack of patience and inability to endure the challenges and difficulties that have come their way. The verse highlights the theme of patience and perseverance in the face of adversity and the importance of trusting and following the guidance of the prophet or messenger.
orig: قال ألم أقل إنك لن تستطيع معي صبرا

translation: He said, 'Do not reproach me for what I have forgotten and do not make my matter difficult for me.'
interpretation: The verse is a direct speech from someone who is asking for forgiveness and understanding for something they have forgotten. They are also asking for their matter or situation not to be made difficult for them. The verse emphasizes the importance of empathy and compassion towards people who make mistakes or forget, and highlights the need for patience and understanding in dealing with others. It also highlights the human tendency to forget and the need for forgiveness and leniency in such situations.
orig: قال لا تؤاخذني بما نسيت ولا ترهقني من أمري عسرا

translation: So go forth, [O Muhammad], until you are free from protection, and say, 'Indeed, I seek refuge in the face of whom toward you has fallen the command, if you should be of the submitters.' But when he sees a deviation, he says, 'Indeed, I am of you. I will surely cooperate with you in a matter.' So Allah is most knowing of what they do.
interpretation: This verse speaks about the believers being commanded to migrate for the sake of their religion and seeking protection from those who have the power to harm them. The verse emphasizes the importance of staying true to one's faith and not compromising it for any worldly gain or protection. The verse also highlights the hypocrisy of some people who claim to be believers but quickly abandon their faith when faced with adversity. The verse serves as a reminder to remain steadfast in one's faith and not to be swayed by the pressures of the world.
orig: فانطلقا حتى إذا لقيا غلاما فقتله قال أقتلت نفسا زكية بغير نفس لقد جئت شيئا نكرا

translation: He said, 'Did I not tell you that you would not be able to have patience with me?'
interpretation: The verse is a dialogue between two people, where one person (the speaker) is expressing frustration or disappointment towards the other person, who was unable to be patient in a difficult situation. The speaker had previously warned the other person that they would not be able to endure the situation, and the other person has now proven the speaker right. The verse may be interpreted as a reminder of the importance of patience and perseverance in the face of adversity, and the consequences of giving in to frustration or anger.
orig: قال ألم أقل لك إنك لن تستطيع معي صبرا

translation: He said, 'If you ask me about anything after this, do not accompany me. I have been given permission (to leave you) from my Lord.'
interpretation: The verse is a conversation between Moses and his companion, Joshua, as they were leaving Egypt. Moses asked his companion not to ask him any questions after a certain point, as he had been granted permission by God to leave Joshua behind. The verse emphasizes the importance of obedience and respect for God's commands, as well as the need for individuals to fulfill their responsibilities and follow the guidance of their leaders.
orig: قال إن سألتك عن شيء بعدها فلا تصاحبني قد بلغت من لدني عذرا

translation: So they set out until, when they came to a people, they asked its people for food, but they refused to offer them hospitality. So they found in it a wall about to collapse, and he (one of them) repaired it. (The other) said, 'If you had wished, you could have taken for it a wage.'
interpretation: The verse describes the story of two people who were traveling and asked the people of a town for food, but they were refused hospitality. While they were there, they found a wall that was about to collapse, and one of them repaired it. The other one remarked that they could have taken payment for their work. The verse highlights the lack of hospitality and kindness shown by the people of the town, and the positive actions of the two travelers, who helped repair the wall despite the negative treatment they received. The verse may serve as a reminder of the importance of hospitality and kindness towards others, as well as the rewards of good deeds.
orig: فانطلقا حتى إذا أتيا أهل قرية استطعما أهلها فأبوا أن يضيفوهما فوجدا فيها جدارا يريد أن ينقض فأقامه قال لو شئت لاتخذت عليه أجرا

translation: He said, 'This is a parting between you and me. I will inform you of the interpretation of what you could not bear with patience.'
interpretation: The verse is a continuation of a conversation between Moses and his people. Moses has been asked by his people to bring them a sign from God, and they have become impatient while waiting for the sign. In this verse, Moses tells his people that the wait is over and that he will inform them of the interpretation of the sign. The verse emphasizes the importance of patience and trust in God's plan, and the consequences of impatience and lack of faith.
orig: قال هذا فراق بيني وبينك سأنبئك بتأويل ما لم تستطع عليه صبرا

translation: As for the ship, it belonged to the poor who plied the sea in quest of gains, and I intended to mar it, for behind them was a king who seized every ship by force.
interpretation: The verse describes a ship belonging to a group of poor people who worked at sea to earn a living. However, God had planned to destroy the ship due to a tyrant king who seized every ship that passed by, taking it by force. The verse highlights the injustice of the king and the vulnerability of the poor who are at the mercy of such rulers. It also emphasizes God's power and control over all things, including the fate of the ship and the people on board.
orig: أما السفينة فكانت لمساكين يعملون في البحر فأردت أن أعيبها وكان وراءهم ملك يأخذ كل سفينة غصبا

translation: But as for the boy, his parents were believers, and we feared that he would burden them with unbelief and disbelief.
interpretation: The verse speaks about a boy whose parents were believers. The verse explains that God was concerned that the boy might become a source of disbelief and unbelief for his parents, possibly indicating that the boy was at risk of straying from the path of faith. The verse highlights the importance of a strong religious upbringing and the impact that children can have on their parents' faith. It also serves as a reminder that God is aware of the struggles and challenges that parents face in raising their children and is concerned for their well-being.
orig: وأما الغلام فكان أبواه مؤمنين فخشينا أن يرهقهما طغيانا وكفرا

translation: And We intended that their Lord should change them for what is better; exchange for them - their Lord - a better substitution and nearer to mercy.
interpretation: The verse speaks about God's intention to replace something bad with something better for two people or groups of people. The verse emphasizes God's mercy and compassion towards his creations. The verse could be interpreted as a promise of divine intervention and help for those who are facing difficulties and hardships. It is also a reminder of God's power and ability to change and transform situations for the better, and a call for patience and trust in God's plan.
orig: فأردنا أن يبدلهما ربهما خيرا منه زكاة وأقرب رحما

translation: But as for the wall, it belonged to two orphan boys in the city, and there was beneath it a treasure for them, and their father had been righteous. So your Lord intended that they reach maturity and extract their treasure, as a mercy from your Lord. And I did not do this of my own accord. This is an explanation of what was unclear to you.
interpretation: The verse speaks about a wall that belongs to two orphan boys. The wall is hiding a treasure that was left for them by their righteous father. The verse highlights God's intention for the boys to reach maturity and be able to access their treasure as a mercy from God. The verse serves to clarify the situation of the wall and the treasure and emphasizes God's role in the events, and the prophet's lack of involvement in the matter.
orig: وأما الجدار فكان لغلامين يتيمين في المدينة وكان تحته كنز لهما وكان أبوهما صالحا فأراد ربك أن يبلغا أشدهما ويستخرجا كنزهما رحمة من ربك وما فعلته عن أمري ذلك تأويل ما لم تسطع عليه صبرا

translation: And they ask you about Dhul-Qarnain. Say, 'I will recite to you about him a reminder.'
interpretation: The verse addresses a group of people who are asking the Prophet Muhammad about a figure known as Dhul-Qarnain. The Prophet is instructed to respond by saying that he will recite to them a reminder about him. Dhul-Qarnain is a mysterious figure who is mentioned in the Qur'an as a righteous and powerful king who ruled over a vast territory. The verse implies that the story of Dhul-Qarnain holds important lessons and reminders for the listeners, and the Prophet's recitation of his story serves as a means of guidance and instruction for the people.
orig: ويسألونك عن ذي القرنين قل سأتلو عليكم منه ذكرا

translation: We had made him firm in the earth, and had given him means of access to every thing.
interpretation: The verse speaks about providing someone with the means and resources to succeed in the world. The person was given stability and support in their endeavors, and was given the ability to acquire whatever they needed. This verse can be interpreted as a metaphor for the blessings and opportunities that God gives to individuals, allowing them to build a successful and fulfilling life. The verse can also be seen as a reminder of the responsibility that comes with these blessings, and the need to use them in a responsible and just manner.
orig: إنا مكنا له في الأرض وآتيناه من كل شيء سببا

translation: Then follow (the way of) his nature as a result [of God's decree]
interpretation: The verse speaks about following the natural way of life as a result of God's decree. It emphasizes the importance of following the natural order and avoiding any deviation from it. The verse suggests that by following the natural way of life, one can achieve harmony and balance in their existence. This can be interpreted as a call to live in accordance with the laws of nature and the divine will, and to avoid any actions or behaviors that may disrupt this natural order.
orig: فأتبع سببا

translation: Until, when the sun is covered, and he finds it setting in a murky pool and finds a people by it, We said, 'O Dhul-Qarnayn, either you punish them or you take a clement course towards them.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about a figure called Dhul-Qarnayn who encounters a people near a murky pool as the sun sets. God gives Dhul-Qarnayn the choice to either punish the people or to take a kinder approach towards them. The verse highlights the power and authority of Dhul-Qarnayn, as well as the importance of making moral decisions and the consequences that result from those decisions. The verse also emphasizes the significance of the sun and its role in the daily life of people, as well as the symbolism of the sun's setting in a murky pool, which could represent the darkness and confusion of the people's actions.
orig: حتى إذا بلغ مغرب الشمس وجدها تغرب في عين حمئة ووجد عندها قوما قلنا يا ذا القرنين إما أن تعذب وإما أن تتخذ فيهم حسنا

translation: But as for him who wrongs, we shall certainly punish him. Then he will be returned to his Lord, and He will punish him with a punishment unrelenting.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the punishment that will be given to those who commit wrongdoing and injustice. The verse emphasizes that the punishment is certain and will be severe. The wrongdoer will not only be punished in this life but will also be returned to their Lord for further punishment. The phrase 'punishment unrelenting' suggests that the punishment will be ongoing and unending, indicating the seriousness of committing wrongdoing and the importance of avoiding it.
orig: قال أما من ظلم فسوف نعذبه ثم يرد إلى ربه فيعذبه عذابا نكرا

translation: But as for one who believes and does righteous deeds, for such shall be the supreme reward, and we shall speak unto them of easy reckoning
interpretation: The verse distinguishes between those who believe and do righteous deeds and those who are unjust. For those who lead a life of faith and good deeds, there is the promise of great reward. Furthermore, they will receive an easy and straightforward judgement. This verse serves as an encouragement for believers to continue on the path of righteousness and as a reminder of the blessings that come with faith and good deeds.
orig: وأما من آمن وعمل صالحا فله جزاء الحسنى وسنقول له من أمرنا يسرا

translation: Then follow (after) a consequence
interpretation: The verse speaks about a sequence of events, where one event (implied before this verse) is followed by a consequence or result. The verse emphasizes the inevitability of consequences following actions. This can be interpreted as a reminder that every action has a consequence and that people should be mindful of the results of their actions.
orig: ثم أتبع سببا

translation: Until, when the sun is obscured, it reveals over a people for whom We have not appointed a shield from it.
interpretation: The verse describes a scene where the sun is about to set and its rays reveal a group of people who have no protection from its heat or light. This image can be interpreted as a metaphor for God's punishment or judgment, which will expose and reveal the sins and wrongdoings of those who have ignored His warnings. The verse serves as a reminder of the impending day of reckoning and the importance of seeking God's protection and forgiveness.
orig: حتى إذا بلغ مطلع الشمس وجدها تطلع على قوم لم نجعل لهم من دونها سترا

translation: Thus have We seized on
interpretation: No interpretation
orig: كذلك وقد أحطنا بما لديه خبرا

translation: Then follow (after) a consequence
interpretation: The phrase 'Then follow (after) a consequence' implies a sequence of events, where one event (or action) is followed by another (or its consequence). It suggests that actions have consequences, and those consequences follow naturally from the actions taken. This phrase serves as a reminder that our actions have consequences, and that we should be mindful of the potential outcomes of our decisions and actions.
orig: ثم أتبع سببا

translation: Until, when he reached between the two mountains, he found before them a people who could hardly understand a word.
interpretation: The verse speaks about a person who travels between two mountains and encounters a group of people who have difficulty understanding speech. This verse highlights the communication barrier between the traveler and the people, emphasizing the difference in language or culture. The verse can be interpreted as a reminder of the diversity of human societies and the importance of understanding and respecting cultural differences. It can also serve as a metaphor for the challenges and opportunities that come with encountering new and unfamiliar cultures.
orig: حتى إذا بلغ بين السدين وجد من دونهما قوما لا يكادون يفقهون قولا

translation: They said, 'O Dhul-Qarnayn, indeed Gog and Magog are causing corruption in the land. So will you make between us and them a barrier?'
interpretation: The verse speaks about a conversation between the people and a figure known as Dhul-Qarnayn. The people express their concern about the corruption and destruction caused by two groups, Gog and Magog. They ask Dhul-Qarnayn if he can create a barrier between them and Gog and Magog to protect them. The verse highlights the role of leaders and powerful figures in protecting their people and the responsibility they have in addressing the challenges and threats they face.
orig: قالوا يا ذا القرنين إن يأجوج ومأجوج مفسدون في الأرض فهل نجعل لك خرجا على أن تجعل بيننا وبينهم سدا

translation: He said, 'My Lord has made it easy for me, so make me steadfast and give me strengthened help against the disbelieving people.',
interpretation: The verse is a supplication of Prophet Moses asking for God's help and strength in his struggle against the disbelievers. The verse emphasizes the importance of steadfastness and reliance on God in the face of adversity. It also highlights the challenges that prophets and believers face in their mission to spread the message of God and the importance of seeking God's help and support in overcoming these challenges.
orig: قال ما مكني فيه ربي خير فأعينوني بقوة أجعل بينكم وبينهم ردما

translation: Give me a rod of iron, until I make it straight, then when I have made it straight, then bring to me a wolf, and draw him to it. Then when I have colored it with fire, then bring to me a file, and file it a little.
interpretation: This verse is a part of a story about the prophet Moses and his interactions with the Pharaoh of Egypt. In this verse, Pharaoh is asking Moses to perform a series of tasks to prove his miraculous abilities. The tasks include making a rod straight, bringing a wolf, coloring the rod with fire, and filing it. These tasks can be interpreted as a test of Moses' prophethood and his ability to perform miracles. The Pharaoh's demand for these tasks can also be seen as a form of arrogance and a refusal to accept the truth of Moses' message. Ultimately, the story serves as a reminder of the importance of faith and the consequences of disbelief.
orig: آتوني زبر الحديد حتى إذا ساوى بين الصدفين قال انفخوا حتى إذا جعله نارا قال آتوني أفرغ عليه قطرا

translation: But they were unable to hide it (their disbelief) from Us, nor were they able to return to Us (to repent)!
interpretation: The verse speaks about the inability of the disbelievers to conceal their disbelief from God and their inability to return to God in repentance. The verse emphasizes the all-encompassing knowledge of God and His awareness of the inner thoughts and actions of His creation. The verse serves as a reminder that no one can hide their disbelief or wrongdoing from God and that it is always better to repent and seek forgiveness before it is too late.
orig: فما اسطاعوا أن يظهروه وما استطاعوا له نقبا

translation: He said, 'This is a mercy from my Lord.' But when the promise of my Lord comes to pass, He will make it (i.e. the promise) into ruin, and my Lord's promise is ever true.'
interpretation: The verse is a continuation of a conversation between a prophet and his people, where the prophet is explaining the nature of the punishment that will befall them. The prophet refers to the punishment as a mercy from his Lord, highlighting the fact that it is a form of divine justice and a means of purification for the sinners. However, the prophet also acknowledges that when the punishment comes to pass, it will bring about destruction and ruin. Despite this, the prophet affirms his belief in the truth and certainty of his Lord's promise, emphasizing the ultimate power and authority of God.
orig: قال هذا رحمة من ربي فإذا جاء وعد ربي جعله دكاء وكان وعد ربي حقا

translation: And We left some of them that day, staggering in drunkenness, while others were hidden. And We punished them with a painful punishment.
interpretation: The verse describes a scene of punishment and destruction of a group of people, some of whom were staggering in drunkenness, while others were hiding. The verse then states that they were punished with a painful punishment. The verse emphasizes the severity of the punishment and the fact that it was a consequence of their actions, specifically being in a state of drunkenness. The verse serves as a warning to those who engage in such sinful behavior and a reminder of the consequences of their actions.
orig: وتركنا بعضهم يومئذ يموج في بعض ونفخ في الصور فجمعناهم جمعا

translation: And We shall expose Hell that day to the disbelievers in full view,
interpretation: The verse describes the exposure of Hell to the disbelievers on the Day of Judgment. The visual imagery of 'exposing' Hell emphasizes the reality and tangibility of the punishment, and the fact that it will be impossible for the disbelievers to deny or ignore it. The verse serves as a warning to those who reject faith and the message of Islam, reminding them of the grave consequences of their disbelief and the imminent encounter with Hell.
orig: وعرضنا جهنم يومئذ للكافرين عرضا

translation: Those whose eyes were kept away from My remembrance and who could not hear.
interpretation: The verse describes a group of people who were deliberately avoiding the remembrance of God and were unable or unwilling to listen. The phrase 'kept away' suggests that something was actively preventing them from seeing or hearing the truth, possibly due to their own stubbornness or unwillingness to accept it. The verse may serve as a warning to those who are closed off to the word of God and highlights the importance of being open and receptive to His message.
orig: الذين كانت أعينهم في غطاء عن ذكري وكانوا لا يستطيعون سمعا

translation: Do the disbelievers then assume that they can take My servants as allies besides Me? Indeed, We have prepared for the disbelievers Hell as a close companion.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the exclusivity of the relationship between God and His servants, warning those who would take others as their protectors and allies instead of God. The verse highlights the severe consequences of this action, as God has prepared Hell for the disbelievers. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of placing one's faith and trust solely in God and of the dangers of associating partners with Him.
orig: أفحسب الذين كفروا أن يتخذوا عبادي من دوني أولياء إنا أعتدنا جهنم للكافرين نزلا

translation: Say, 'Shall We inform you of the greatest losers in their deeds?'
interpretation: The verse is a challenge from the speaker (who is believed to be the Prophet Muhammad) to the disbelievers. The speaker asks if they would like to know who are the ones who will be the 'greatest losers' in their deeds. This implies that there will be a reckoning and judgment of deeds in the afterlife, and some people will be deemed 'losers' because of the bad deeds they have done. The verse serves as a warning to the disbelievers and a call for them to reflect on their actions and repent before it is too late.
orig: قل هل ننبئكم بالأخسرين أعمالا

translation: Those whose efforts are misguided in the life of this world, while they think that they are doing good.
interpretation: The verse speaks about people who are misguided in their efforts and actions in this worldly life. Despite their belief that they are doing good, they are actually astray. This verse highlights the danger of being deceived by one's own actions and the importance of seeking guidance and truth. It serves as a reminder that good intentions alone are not enough and that actions must be guided by true knowledge and understanding. Ultimately, it is a call to reflect on the purpose of our existence and the need to strive for what truly matters in the afterlife.
orig: الذين ضل سعيهم في الحياة الدنيا وهم يحسبون أنهم يحسنون صنعا

translation: Those who disbelieve in the signs of their Lord and in their meeting with Him - their deeds have become worthless in this world and the Hereafter, and they will not be able to escape [on the Day of Resurrection].
interpretation: The verse speaks about the fate of those who disbelieve in the signs of their Lord and deny the meeting with Him. Their deeds in this world will be rendered worthless and they will not be able to escape God's judgment on the Day of Resurrection. The verse serves as a warning to those who reject God's signs and deny the Hereafter, emphasizing the futility of their actions and the inevitability of God's judgment.
orig: أولئك الذين كفروا بآيات ربهم ولقائه فحبطت أعمالهم فلا نقيم لهم يوم القيامة وزنا

translation: That is their reward - Hell - for their disbelief, and for taking My signs and My messengers as a joke.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the punishment of disbelievers who rejected God's signs and messengers and instead treated them as a source of amusement. The punishment for their actions is Hell. The verse serves as a warning to those who reject God's messages and messengers, emphasizing the seriousness of their actions and the consequences that they will face.
orig: ذلك جزاؤهم جهنم بما كفروا واتخذوا آياتي ورسلي هزوا

translation: For those who believe and do good deeds, We shall surely give them Gardens beneath which rivers flow (in Paradise).
interpretation: The verse speaks about the promise of Paradise for those who have faith and perform good deeds. The verse emphasizes the certainty of this reward, using the word 'shall' in 'We shall surely give them'. The 'Gardens beneath which rivers flow' is a metaphorical description of Paradise, emphasizing the abundance of blessings and pleasures that believers will enjoy. The verse serves as a motivation for believers to continue practicing good deeds and upholding their faith, assuring them of the ultimate reward that awaits them in the afterlife.
orig: إن الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات كانت لهم جنات الفردوس نزلا

translation: They will abide therein as long as they do not desire to leave it.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the fate of certain people who will be made to reside in a place (which is not specified in the verse) for as long as they do not express the desire to leave. The verse emphasizes the permanence of their stay, which is only broken if they express the desire to leave. The verse can be interpreted as a warning to those who are complacent and satisfied with their current situation, reminding them that their fate is ultimately in the hands of God and that their complacency may lead to a permanent state that they may not be pleased with.
orig: خالدين فيها لا يبغون عنها حولا

translation: Say, 'If the sea were ink for the words of my Lord, the sea would run out before the words of my Lord run out, even if We brought the like of it as a supplement.'
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the infinite nature of God's words and knowledge, using the metaphor of the sea as ink. The verse suggests that even if the sea was used as ink, it would run out before God's words run out, emphasizing the limitless and unending nature of God's knowledge. The verse also suggests that even if more ink was added, it would still not be enough. The verse serves as a reminder of God's greatness and the limitations of human understanding in comparison.
orig: قل لو كان البحر مدادا لكلمات ربي لنفد البحر قبل أن تنفد كلمات ربي ولو جئنا بمثله مددا

translation: Say, 'Indeed, I am only a human likeness to you. It is inspired in me that your god is one God. So whoever hopes for the meeting with his Lord - let him do righteous work and not associate anyone with the worship of his Lord.'
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the humanity and prophethood of the speaker, who is tasked with conveying the message of monotheism to the people. The verse encourages those who believe in the message to perform righteous deeds and not to associate any partners with the worship of their Lord. The verse highlights the importance of faith and good deeds in the relationship between the individual and their Lord, and the necessity of maintaining the purity of worship. The verse also emphasizes the unity of God and the importance of recognizing this unity as the foundation of faith.
orig: قل إنما أنا بشر مثلكم يوحى إلي أنما إلهكم إله واحد فمن كان يرجو لقاء ربه فليعمل عملا صالحا ولا يشرك بعبادة ربه أحدا

translation: N
interpretation: N
orig: كهيعص

translation: Mention of the mercy of your Lord to His servant Zachariah.
interpretation: The verse is a reference to the story of the prophet Zachariah and the mercy that was shown to him by God. The verse is reminding the reader of the boundless compassion and grace of God towards His servants. The verse emphasizes the importance of remembering and recognizing the mercy of God, and encourages the reader to be grateful for it. The verse serves as a reminder that God's mercy is available to all of His servants, regardless of their circumstances.
orig: ذكر رحمت ربك عبده زكريا

translation: When his Lord called him in a whisper
interpretation: The verse describes a moment of divine revelation, when the prophet Zul-Qarnain's Lord called him in a secret and private manner. This moment of revelation marks the beginning of a significant spiritual journey for Zul-Qarnain, as he receives divine guidance and wisdom. The verse highlights the intimate and personal nature of this encounter, emphasizing the special relationship between Zul-Qarnain and his Lord. The verse also serves as a reminder of the power and majesty of God, who is capable of communicating with his servants in profound and mysterious ways.
orig: إذ نادى ربه نداء خفيا

translation: He said, 'My Lord, verily my bones have grown weak, and my head is shining with gray hair, but I have never been ungrateful to You, my Lord.'
interpretation: The verse is a statement of surrender and submission to God by a servant who recognizes the signs of aging and the passage of time. The servant acknowledges the weakness of his body and the graying of his hair, and expresses gratitude for God's blessings despite these physical changes. The verse emphasizes the importance of maintaining a grateful and humble attitude towards God, even in the face of aging and the challenges of life. It also highlights the servant's recognition of God's power and sovereignty over all things, including the natural process of aging.
orig: قال رب إني وهن العظم مني واشتعل الرأس شيبا ولم أكن بدعائك رب شقيا

translation: But I fear my relatives after me, and my wife is barren. So give me from Yourself an heir.
interpretation: The verse describes the story of a man who is concerned about his legacy after his death and fears that his relatives will take control of his possessions. He also mentions that his wife is barren, which adds to his anxiety. He turns to God and asks Him to grant him a righteous heir who will carry on his legacy and maintain his name. The verse emphasizes the importance of leaving a good legacy and the role of offspring in continuing the family lineage. It also highlights the man's faith and trust in God's power and ability to grant his request.
orig: وإني خفت الموالي من ورائي وكانت امرأتي عاقرا فهب لي من لدنك وليا

translation: He will inherit me and inherit from the family of Jacob, and make him Lord in my place.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the inheritance and succession of an individual. The individual will not only inherit from the family of Jacob, but will also become a Lord or a master in the place of the speaker. This verse could be interpreted as a reference to the prophecy of the coming of Prophet Jesus, who is believed by Muslims to be a descendant of Prophet Jacob, and who will inherit the mantle of prophethood and leadership from him. The verse emphasizes the continuity of the prophetic tradition and the importance of passing down knowledge and leadership from one generation to the next.
orig: يرثني ويرث من آل يعقوب واجعله رب رضيا

translation: O Zakaria, indeed We bring you good news of a boy whose name is John. We have not given before to anyone [the like of] his name.
interpretation: The verse announces the birth of John (Yahya) to the prophet Zechariah (Zakaria). The name John is significant as it was not given to anyone before him, indicating the special status of John. The verse emphasizes the joy and blessings that come with the birth of a child, particularly when the child is destined for greatness and is sent as a prophet of God. The verse serves as a reminder of God's power and ability to bless and give good news, and the importance of recognizing and honoring the special status of prophets and their role in conveying God's message.
orig: يا زكريا إنا نبشرك بغلام اسمه يحيى لم نجعل له من قبل سميا

translation: He said, 'My Lord, how can I have a boy when my wife is barren and I have reached old age?'
interpretation: The verse is a statement made by the Prophet Zachariah, expressing his surprise and disbelief at the angel's announcement that he will be given a son. The verse highlights the advanced age of both Zachariah and his wife, who was considered barren, making the conception of a child seem impossible. This verse serves to build the narrative of the story and sets the stage for the miracle that will follow, emphasizing the power and greatness of God.
orig: قال رب أنى يكون لي غلام وكانت امرأتي عاقرا وقد بلغت من الكبر عتيا

translation: Said He, 'Even so, your Lord says, 'It is easy to Me; and I created you before, when you were nothing.'
interpretation: The verse is a statement made by God, who is referred to as 'your Lord'. God says that it is easy for Him to do something, but it is not clear from the text what that is. The second part of the verse explains that God created the listener (or readers) before, when they were nothing. This verse could be interpreted as a reminder of God's power and ability to create and control all things. It may also serve as a reminder of human vulnerability and dependence on God. The verse may be intended to inspire awe and humility in the listener or reader.
orig: قال كذلك قال ربك هو علي هين وقد خلقتك من قبل ولم تك شيئا

translation: He said, 'My Lord, grant me a sign.' He said, 'Your sign is that you will not speak to the people for three days except by signs.'
interpretation: The verse describes a conversation between an unnamed person and God, in which the person asks for a sign from God. God grants the request, but the sign is not what the person might have expected. Instead of a dramatic or miraculous event, the sign is that the person will be unable to speak to people for three days, and will be able to communicate only through gestures or writing. The verse emphasizes the importance of communication and the challenges that can arise when it is taken away. It also highlights the power of God, who can choose to grant or withhold the ability to communicate.
orig: قال رب اجعل لي آية قال آيتك ألا تكلم الناس ثلاث ليال سويا

translation: And he emerged upon his people from the sanctuary and inspired to them to glorify (God) morning and evening.
interpretation: The verse speaks about a prophet or a righteous person who emerges from a sanctuary and calls upon his people to glorify God, both in the morning and in the evening. The verse emphasizes the importance of praising and worshiping God regularly and consistently, and the role of religious leaders in reminding their communities of their spiritual obligations. The verse may also suggest that the prophet's people were neglectful of their religious duties, and that the prophet's emergence from the sanctuary serves as a wake-up call for them to return to the right path.
orig: فخرج على قومه من المحراب فأوحى إليهم أن سبحوا بكرة وعشيا

translation: O John, take hold of the Book with strength, and We gave him judgment while still a boy
interpretation: The verse refers to John the Baptist, and commands him to take hold of the Book (presumably the scriptures) with strength. This implies that John was to study, understand, and follow the teachings of the scriptures with determination and resolve. The verse also states that God gave him judgment while still a boy, indicating that John had a deep understanding of right and wrong from a young age. This serves as a reminder that age is not a barrier to gaining wisdom and knowledge, and that one should always strive to learn and understand the teachings of their faith.
orig: يا يحيى خذ الكتاب بقوة وآتيناه الحكم صبيا

translation: And a mercy from Us and a reminder for those who believe.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the blessings of mercy and a reminder from God for those who believe. The verse highlights the kindness and compassion of God towards the believers, and the provision of a reminder, which serves as a means of guidance and inspiration for them. The verse emphasizes the importance of faith and belief, and the blessings that come with it, such as God's mercy and guidance.
orig: وحنانا من لدنا وزكاة وكان تقيا

translation: And be kind to your parents. And if one or both of them reach old age with you, say not to them (so much as) 'Uff' (a word of disrespect), nor shout at them; but address them in terms of honor.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of showing respect and kindness to parents, regardless of whether they are still young or have reached old age. The verse specifically prohibits the use of harsh words or shouting at parents, and instead encourages children to speak to their parents with respect and honor. This verse serves as a reminder of the importance of filial piety and the role of parents in shaping the character and values of their children. It also highlights the dignity and respect that should be given to all individuals, especially to those who are older and have more life experience.
orig: وبرا بوالديه ولم يكن جبارا عصيا

translation: And peace be upon him the day he was born, and the day he dies, and the day he is raised to life.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the bestowal of peace upon a person on three significant occasions: the day of their birth, the day of their death, and the day of resurrection. This verse emphasizes the complete and unbroken peace that the person experiences on these important days of their existence. While the identity of the person is not specified in the verse, it is often interpreted as a reference to the Prophet Muhammad, or as a metaphor for all human beings. The verse conveys the message of peace, tranquility, and divine blessings for all humans at different stages of their lives.
orig: وسلام عليه يوم ولد ويوم يموت ويوم يبعث حيا

translation: And mention in the Book (the Qur'an) Mary, when she withdrew in seclusion from her family to the east.
interpretation: The verse speaks about Mary, the mother of Jesus, and her withdrawal to a secluded place in the east. The verse emphasizes Mary's desire for privacy and seclusion, and her dedication to worship and devotion. The verse also highlights the significance of Mary in the Islamic tradition, as she is one of the few women mentioned by name in the Qur'an. The verse can be seen as a model of piety and devotion, and a reminder of the importance of seeking solitude and spiritual reflection in one's life.
orig: واذكر في الكتاب مريم إذ انتبذت من أهلها مكانا شرقيا

translation: And We have made before them a barrier and a barrier behind them, and then We have covered them, so they do not see.
interpretation: The verse describes a situation where a barrier has been placed between the people and something that they are not meant to see, with another barrier behind them. Then, a veil has been cast over them, preventing them from seeing. The verse can be interpreted as a metaphor for the spiritual blindness of people who are unable to see the truth or understand divine messages. It suggests that these people have been separated from the truth by their own actions or choices, and as a result, they are unable to perceive it. The verse may also be interpreted as a literal description of a divine intervention, where a physical barrier and a veil have been placed to prevent people from seeing something that is being protected or hidden.
orig: فاتخذت من دونهم حجابا فأرسلنا إليها روحنا فتمثل لها بشرا سويا

translation: She said, 'I seek refuge in the All-Merciful from you, if you are indeed one who fears God.'
interpretation: The verse recounts a statement made by a woman, who seeks protection from the speaker using a supplication to the All-Merciful (Rahman), a name of God. The woman's supplication implies that she perceives a threat from the speaker and seeks divine protection from him. The woman's statement also serves to highlight the moral character of the speaker and distinguishes between those who fear God and those who do not. The verse emphasizes the importance of having a reverent and pious disposition towards God and the significance of seeking refuge in Him during times of need and danger.
orig: قالت إني أعوذ بالرحمن منك إن كنت تقيا

translation: He said, 'I am indeed a messenger of your Lord, to bestow upon you a pure boy.'
interpretation: The verse is a dialogue between two individuals, where one of them is identified as a messenger of God. The messenger brings good news of a gift from God, a pure boy. While the identity of the speaker and the recipient of the news are not specified in the verse, it emphasizes the divine origin of the gift and the role of the messenger in delivering the news. The verse may serve as a reminder of God's blessings and the role of His messengers in conveying His messages to humanity.
orig: قال إنما أنا رسول ربك لأهب لك غلاما زكيا

translation: She said, 'How can I have a boy when no man has touched me, nor have I been unchaste?'
interpretation: The verse is a quote from Maryam (Mary), the mother of Jesus, in response to the accusations of her people that she had a child without being married. Maryam asserts her innocence and denies any wrongdoing, stating that she has never been touched by a man or been unchaste. The verse emphasizes Maryam's purity and innocence, and serves as a reminder of her extraordinary experience of giving birth to Jesus through the power of God.
orig: قالت أنى يكون لي غلام ولم يمسسني بشر ولم أك بغيا

translation: It is as He said, 'My Lord will surely send upon them a punishment, for surely My warning is true.' But We delayed it only for a term appointed, (and) indeed, your Lord is commonwealth for it.
interpretation: The verse speaks about a warning from God of an impending punishment. Despite the warning, the people did not heed it and the punishment was delayed only for a fixed term. The verse emphasizes the power and authority of God, who has full control over the events and can choose to delay or hasten the punishment. The verse serves as a reminder of the power and authority of God and the importance of heeding His warnings and commands.
orig: قال كذلك قال ربك هو علي هين ولنجعله آية للناس ورحمة منا وكان أمرا مقضيا

translation: And We bore him on the (sacred) litter, and We returned him to his place of origin, (Mount) Sinai.
interpretation: The verse refers to the story of the infant Moses, who was placed in a basket and set afloat on the Nile river by his mother to save him from Pharaoh's decree to kill all male Hebrew children. The verse describes how Moses was later found and cared for by the Pharaoh's family, but eventually returned to his own people. The verse specifically mentions that Moses was carried on a litter (a type of vehicle) and returned to his original place, which is identified as Mount Sinai. This event marks the beginning of Moses' mission as a prophet and the start of a new chapter in the history of the Israelites.
orig: فحملته فانتبذت به مكانا قصيا

translation: And the palm-tree stripped bare, she said, 'Oh, I wish I had died before this and had been forgotten, completely forgotten.'
interpretation: The verse describes the regret and despair of a person who is facing a severe calamity or punishment. The stripping bare of the palm-tree is a metaphor for the complete destruction of the person's life or world. The person expresses their deep regret for not having died before the calamity struck, so that they could have been spared the pain and suffering. The phrase 'forgotten, completely forgotten' emphasizes the person's desire to erase their existence and memory from the world. The verse conveys the depth of human despair and hopelessness in the face of overwhelming tragedy and loss.
orig: فأجاءها المخاض إلى جذع النخلة قالت يا ليتني مت قبل هذا وكنت نسيا منسيا

translation: Pharaoh's wife said: 'Do not grieve! Indeed, my Lord has made for you the river beneath you as a provision.'
interpretation: The verse recounts Pharaoh's wife's words of comfort to Moses, who was placed in a basket in the river as a baby and was later found by Pharaoh's wife. Pharaoh's wife tells Moses not to grieve and assures him that God has provided for him through the river. The verse highlights Pharaoh's wife's compassion and her recognition of God's providence and care for Moses, even in the midst of difficult circumstances.
orig: فناداها من تحتها ألا تحزني قد جعل ربك تحتك سريا

translation: And shake towards you the palm-tree, it will drop on you ripe, fresh dates.
interpretation: The verse is a metaphorical description of God's blessings and provisions for His believers. The palm-tree represents a source of sustenance and the dates represent the blessings. The act of shaking the tree represents God's generosity and the ripe, fresh dates represent the blessings that are ready to be received. The verse emphasizes the ease and readiness of God's provisions for His believers, and encourages them to seek God's blessings with faith and patience.
orig: وهزي إليك بجذع النخلة تساقط عليك رطبا جنيا

translation: So eat and drink and be comforted. Surely I swear by the Lord of the worlds, I will most certainly not speak to a human being today.
interpretation: The verse speaks about a command to eat, drink, and find comfort, followed by a statement of intent by the speaker to swear by the Lord of the worlds that they will not speak to a human being that day. The verse could be interpreted as a moment of contemplation or reflection, where the speaker has decided to take a break from interacting with others and instead focus on their own thoughts and connection with the divine. The oath by the Lord of the worlds adds a sense of seriousness and solemnity to the statement, indicating that the speaker is making a significant decision or resolution.
orig: فكلي واشربي وقري عينا فإما ترين من البشر أحدا فقولي إني نذرت للرحمن صوما فلن أكلم اليوم إنسيا

translation: Then she brought him to her people, carrying him. They said, 'O Mary, indeed you have come with a thing Fariyyan.'
interpretation: The verse describes Mary bringing the baby Jesus to her people. The people are surprised and express their astonishment at the sight of a newborn baby, referring to him as 'Fariyyan', which is a word of unknown meaning. Some interpret it as something wonderful or extraordinary, highlighting the miraculous nature of Jesus' birth. The verse sets the stage for the announcement of Jesus' birth and the miracles that he will perform throughout his life.
orig: فأتت به قومها تحمله قالوا يا مريم لقد جئت شيئا فريا

translation: O sister of Aaron, your father was not a man of evil, nor was your mother unchaste.
interpretation: The verse addresses Moses' sister, Miriam, who had spoken negatively about Moses. The verse reassures her that neither her father nor her mother were immoral people, implying that Moses' character and mission should not be questioned. The verse emphasizes the importance of family and lineage, and it serves as a reminder to be mindful of our words and actions towards others, especially those who are close to us.
orig: يا أخت هارون ما كان أبوك امرأ سوء وما كانت أمك بغيا

translation: And they pointed to him. They said, 'How can we speak to one who is in the cradle, a child?'
interpretation: The verse describes the disbelievers' reaction to the miracle of Prophet Isa (Jesus) speaking from the cradle, as mentioned in the previous verses. The disbelievers were skeptical and questioned how they could communicate with a baby. This verse emphasizes the miraculous nature of the event and highlights the disbelievers' disbelief and rejection of the truth. It also serves as a reminder that God has the power to do extraordinary things, even through the most unlikely of sources, and that those who reject His signs do so at their own peril.
orig: فأشارت إليه قالوا كيف نكلم من كان في المهد صبيا

translation: He said, 'Indeed, I am a servant of Allah. He has given me the Scripture and made me a prophet.'
interpretation: The verse relays the words of the prophet Zakariya (peace be upon him) upon the announcement of the birth of his son Yahya (John the Baptist, peace be upon him). Zakariya acknowledges his servitude to Allah and attributes his appointment as a prophet and the revelation of the Scripture to Allah's will and grace. This verse highlights the importance of humility, gratitude, and reliance on Allah in the face of blessings and trials.
orig: قال إني عبد الله آتاني الكتاب وجعلني نبيا

translation: And made me blessed wherever I am and has enjoined upon me prayer and alms-giving so long as I live.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the blessings and responsibilities given to the prophet Muhammad. The verse emphasizes the perpetuity of these blessings and responsibilities, as the prophet was made blessed 'wherever I am' and was commanded to establish prayer and charity 'so long as I live'. This verse serves as a reminder of the continuous nature of the prophet's mission and the importance of fulfilling religious obligations. It also highlights the connection between blessings and responsibilities, indicating that the prophet's blessings are tied to his commitment to prayer and charity.
orig: وجعلني مباركا أين ما كنت وأوصاني بالصلاة والزكاة ما دمت حيا

translation: And be kind to my parents, and do not be ungrateful to me. Be kind to your parents and to me.
interpretation: The verse is a command from a prophet to his people to be kind to their parents and not to be ungrateful to them. The repetition of the command to be kind to parents emphasizes the importance of this act. The verse recognizes the role of parents in shaping the individual and the debt of gratitude that children owe to them. The command to avoid ingratitude towards the speaker (the prophet) indicates the importance of respecting and honoring those who have authority and knowledge. The verse encourages the cultivation of positive relationships with family members and those in positions of authority.
orig: وبرا بوالدتي ولم يجعلني جبارا شقيا

translation: And peace be upon the day I was born, and the day I die, and the day I am raised alive.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the attainment of peace on three significant days in a person's life - the day of their birth, the day of their death, and the day of their resurrection. This verse emphasizes the importance of finding peace and contentment in every stage of life, from the beginning to the end. It also highlights the belief in the afterlife and the Day of Judgment, where individuals will be resurrected and held accountable for their actions. The verse serves as a reminder to strive for inner peace and to prepare for the ultimate Day of Judgment.
orig: والسلام علي يوم ولدت ويوم أموت ويوم أبعث حيا

translation: That is Jesus, son of Mary, the word of truth about whom they are in dispute.
interpretation: The verse refers to Jesus, son of Mary, and emphasizes his true nature, which is a subject of controversy and disagreement among people. By calling Jesus 'the word of truth', the verse affirms his significance and importance in Islamic teachings. The verse suggests that despite the differing opinions and perspectives, there is a fundamental truth about Jesus that is beyond dispute and serves as a basis for understanding and reverence.
orig: ذلك عيسى ابن مريم قول الحق الذي فيه يمترون

translation: It is not for Allah to take a son; exalted is He. When He decrees an affair, He only says to it, 'Be,' and it is.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the absolute power and uniqueness of Allah, and rejects the idea of Him having a son. It states that when Allah decrees something, it is immediately brought into existence through His command. This serves as a reminder of Allah's power, sovereignty, and uniqueness, and the absolute dependence of all creation on Him.
orig: ما كان لله أن يتخذ من ولد سبحانه إذا قضى أمرا فإنما يقول له كن فيكون

translation: And indeed, Allah is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him - this is a straight path.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the unity of God and the need to worship Him alone. The phrase 'this is a straight path' indicates that following this path will lead to righteousness and success in this life and the hereafter. The verse addresses both the speaker and the listener, reinforcing the idea that all people are equal in their duty to worship God and follow His path.
orig: وإن الله ربي وربكم فاعبدوه هذا صراط مستقيم

translation: The factions among them differed, so woe to the disbelievers because of a severe punishment on a Day of Greatest Gathering.
interpretation: The verse highlights the disagreements and divisions among certain groups or factions. The verse warns of a severe punishment for the disbelievers on the Day of Judgment, which is described as the Day of Greatest Gathering. The verse emphasizes the finality and significance of this day, when all people will be gathered together before God to be judged for their actions. The verse serves as a reminder and a warning of the consequences of disbelief and discord, urging people to reflect on their beliefs and actions and to seek God's mercy and forgiveness.
orig: فاختلف الأحزاب من بينهم فويل للذين كفروا من مشهد يوم عظيم

translation: And indeed I hear the murmur of them, but soon they will know. Indeed today the unjust are in clear error.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the unjust who are in clear error and who will soon be faced with the consequences of their actions. The verse emphasizes that their fate is already sealed and that they will soon come to know the truth. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them that their actions do not go unnoticed and that they will be held accountable for them.
orig: أسمع بهم وأبصر يوم يأتوننا لكن الظالمون اليوم في ضلال مبين

translation: And warn them,
interpretation: No interpretation
orig: وأنذرهم يوم الحسرة إذ قضي الأمر وهم في غفلة وهم لا يؤمنون

translation: Indeed, we (it is) who inherit the earth and all those upon it, and to us they will be returned.
interpretation: The verse affirms that it is God who has ultimate control and ownership over the earth and all living things. The verse emphasizes the transient nature of human life and the certainty of death, reminding people that they will ultimately return to God. The verse may also serve as a reminder that God has the power to bestow or withhold blessings, and that people should be mindful of their actions and their relationship with God.
orig: إنا نحن نرث الأرض ومن عليها وإلينا يرجعون

translation: And mention in the Book (the Qur'an) Abraham: Indeed, he was a truthful prophet.
interpretation: The verse highlights the virtues of the Prophet Abraham by describing him as a 'truthful prophet'. This description emphasizes Abraham's integrity and honesty, both as a prophet and as a human being. The verse also commands the believers to 'mention' Abraham in the Book (the Qur'an), indicating the importance of preserving his legacy and remembering his role as a prophet who called people to the worship of one God. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of truthfulness and integrity in Islam, and the significance of remembering and honoring the prophets and their messages.
orig: واذكر في الكتاب إبراهيم إنه كان صديقا نبيا

translation: Behold, he said to his father: 'O my father! Why dost thou worship that which hears not, nor sees, nor can avail thee in any way?'
interpretation: The verse recounts a conversation between a prophet and his disbelieving father, where the prophet questions his father's worship of idols. The prophet highlights the futility of worshipping something that is incapable of hearing, seeing, or benefiting anyone. The verse serves to emphasize the importance of recognizing and worshipping the one true God, who is all-powerful, all-knowing, and able to hear and see all things.
orig: إذ قال لأبيه يا أبت لم تعبد ما لا يسمع ولا يبصر ولا يغني عنك شيئا

translation: O my father, indeed I have received knowledge that has not reached you, so follow me that I may guide you to a straight path.
interpretation: The verse is a message from a prophet (who is speaking to his father). The prophet has received divine knowledge that his father does not yet possess. He is inviting his father to follow him and to accept his guidance, so that he may be led to the 'straight path' (a path of righteousness and obedience to God). The verse highlights the importance of guidance and the responsibility of the prophet to pass on the divine message to others. It also emphasizes the significance of following the guidance of the prophet and the importance of the 'straight path' in Islamic teachings.
orig: يا أبت إني قد جاءني من العلم ما لم يأتك فاتبعني أهدك صراطا سويا

translation: O my father, do not worship Satan. Indeed, Satan has been, to the Most Merciful, disobedient.
interpretation: The verse is a command from a prophet to his father, urging him not to worship Satan. The verse emphasizes the wickedness of Satan and his disobedience towards God. By highlighting Satan's disobedience, the verse encourages the reader to avoid following in his footsteps and instead, to worship and obey God. The verse can be seen as a call to monotheism and a warning against the dangers of polytheism and disobedience towards God.
orig: يا أبت لا تعبد الشيطان إن الشيطان كان للرحمن عصيا

translation: O my father, I fear that a punishment from the Merciful will overtake you, so you will become (a companion) for the satan (i.e. be destroyed).
interpretation: The verse is a warning from the prophet Yusuf (Joseph) to his father, Ya'qub (Jacob), about the impending punishment from God. Yusuf fears that his father will not heed his warnings and continue to disbelieve, leading to his destruction. The verse emphasizes the urgency of repentance and the importance of believing in God's signs and messages. The verse can also be seen as a reminder of the consequences of disbelief and the importance of listening to the warnings of the prophets.
orig: يا أبت إني أخاف أن يمسك عذاب من الرحمن فتكون للشيطان وليا

translation: He said, 'Do you desire that I should leave your gods, O Abraham, if you do not stop? Then I will surely stone you, and I will surely banish you from my presence.'
interpretation: The verse recounts a conversation between the disbelievers and the prophet Ibrahim (Abraham). The disbelievers demand that Ibrahim stops criticizing their gods and ask him if he wants them to abandon their gods. If Ibrahim does not comply, they threaten to stone him and banish him from their presence. The verse highlights the opposition and hostility faced by the prophets in their mission to call people to the worship of one God. It also shows the determination and courage of Ibrahim in his stand for the truth, despite facing severe consequences.
orig: قال أراغب أنت عن آلهتي يا إبراهيم لئن لم تنته لأرجمنك واهجرني مليا

translation: He said, 'Peace be upon you.' I will ask my Lord to forgive you, for He is ever forgiving.
interpretation: The verse describes someone greeting another person with 'Peace be upon you', indicating a respectful and peaceful encounter. The speaker then offers to seek forgiveness from their Lord for the other person, emphasizing the merciful and forgiving nature of God.
