The verse highlights the importance of forgiveness and seeking mercy, both from God and from others, in promoting peace and harmony in society.
orig: قال سلام عليك سأستغفر لك ربي إنه كان بي حفيا

translation: And I will withdraw from you and from what you call upon instead of Allah and will call upon my Lord. Perhaps I will not be in extreme distress in my invocation to my Lord.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the speaker's decision to separate themselves from the disbelievers and their false objects of worship and instead call upon their Lord. The speaker is hopeful that their invocation to their Lord will not be in vain and that they will not be left in a state of extreme distress. The verse emphasizes the importance of having a strong connection with God and the importance of seeking His help and guidance in all aspects of life.
orig: وأعتزلكم وما تدعون من دون الله وأدعو ربي عسى ألا أكون بدعاء ربي شقيا

translation: But when he departed from them and that which they worshipped besides Allah, We bestowed upon him Isaac and Jacob, and each of them We made a prophet.
interpretation: The verse speaks about a person who has left behind a community that worships false gods and turned instead to the worship of Allah. As a reward for this decision, God bestows upon him two prophets, Isaac and Jacob, and makes each of them prophets as well. The verse highlights the importance of monotheism and the rewards that come from following the path of Allah, as opposed to worshipping false gods. It also emphasizes the significance of prophethood and the role that prophets play in guiding people towards the right path.
orig: فلما اعتزلهم وما يعبدون من دون الله وهبنا له إسحاق ويعقوب وكلا جعلنا نبيا

translation: And We gave them of Our mercy, and appointed for them a tongue of truth, sublime.
interpretation: The verse speaks about God's mercy and grace towards a group of people, and how He bestowed upon them a 'tongue of truth, sublime'. The phrase 'tongue of truth' implies that the people were given the ability to speak the truth, and the word 'sublime' suggests that their speech was of a high and noble nature. This verse can be interpreted as a recognition of the power of speech as a means of expressing truth and wisdom, and a reminder of the importance of using language in a responsible and uplifting way.
orig: ووهبنا لهم من رحمتنا وجعلنا لهم لسان صدق عليا

translation: And mention in the Book (the Qur'an) Moses, indeed he was chosen and he was a messenger and a prophet.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the mention of Moses in the Qur'an, highlighting his virtues and status. The verse describes Moses as being chosen, a messenger, and a prophet. These descriptions indicate Moses' special relationship with God, and his role as a leader and guide for the people. The verse serves as a reminder of the significance of Moses in Islamic teachings, and the importance of recognizing and respecting the prophets and messengers of God.
orig: واذكر في الكتاب موسى إنه كان مخلصا وكان رسولا نبيا

translation: And We called out to him from the right side of the mount, and drew him near in proximity.
interpretation: The verse speaks of a specific individual being called out to from the right side of a mountain and being drawn near in proximity. While the specific context of the verse is not explicitly stated in the given text, it is widely accepted among scholars that this refers to the story of Moses (peace be upon him) when he received the commandments from God on Mount Sinai. In this context, the verse emphasizes the special relationship between God and His messengers, and the unique experiences they undergo in receiving revelation. It also serves to highlight the significance of the commandments being revealed, as Moses is not only called out to, but also drawn near in proximity, indicating the importance of the message being delivered.
orig: وناديناه من جانب الطور الأيمن وقربناه نجيا

translation: And We gave him, from Our mercy, his brother Aaron as a prophet.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the prophet Moses and how God gave him his brother Aaron as a prophet, as an act of mercy from God. This verse highlights the importance of family and the role of Aaron in supporting and aiding Moses in his prophethood. It also emphasizes the mercy of God and how He provides for His servants in unexpected and generous ways.
orig: ووهبنا له من رحمتنا أخاه هارون نبيا

translation: And mention in the Book (the story of) Ishmael. Indeed, he was (a man of) true promise, and he was a messenger and a prophet.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the prophet Ishmael, highlighting his trustworthiness and his role as a messenger and prophet. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of fulfilling one's promises and the significance of prophethood in Islam. The mention of Ishmael in the Qur'an is also a testament to the continuity and interconnectedness of the Abrahamic traditions, emphasizing the shared values and beliefs between Islam, Judaism, and Christianity.
orig: واذكر في الكتاب إسماعيل إنه كان صادق الوعد وكان رسولا نبيا

translation: And he used to enjoin upon his people prayer and alms-giving and was most surely of those constantly bowing down in worship.
interpretation: The verse speaks about a person who was a good leader and role model for his people. He encouraged them to pray and give in charity, and he himself was deeply devoted to worship. The verse highlights the importance of leadership in promoting good deeds and setting a positive example for others to follow. The verse also emphasizes the significance of prayer and charity in one's relationship with God, and the importance of maintaining a strong spiritual connection through regular worship.
orig: وكان يأمر أهله بالصلاة والزكاة وكان عند ربه مرضيا

translation: And mention in the Book (the Qur'an) Idris (Enoch). Indeed, he was a truthful man, a prophet.
interpretation: The verse speaks about Idris (also known as Enoch in the Bible) and his status as a prophet and a truthful man. The verse commands the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to mention Idris in the Qur'an, highlighting his significance and virtues. The verse serves as a reminder of the continuity of prophethood and the truthfulness of the prophets, and encourages the believers to follow their guidance and example.
orig: واذكر في الكتاب إدريس إنه كان صديقا نبيا

translation: And We raised him to a high station.
interpretation: The verse speaks about raising someone to a high position or station. While the specific individual and context is not mentioned in the verse, it likely refers to a prophet or a righteous person who was given a position of honor and respect by God. The verse emphasizes God's power and authority in elevating individuals to positions of prominence, and may serve as a reminder that all success and status come from God.
orig: ورفعناه مكانا عليا

translation: Those are the ones upon whom Allah bestowed favor from the prophets of the descendants of Adam and from those We carried with Noah and from the descendants of Abraham and Israel and from among those We guided and chose. When the verses of the Merciful are recited to them, they fall down in prostration and weeping.
interpretation: The verse highlights the special status of certain individuals who have received Allah's favor and blessings, including prophets from the lineage of Adam, those who were saved with Noah, and those from the families of Abraham and Israel. These individuals were chosen and guided by Allah. When they hear the verses of the Quran, they respond with humility and submission, prostrating and weeping out of reverence and gratitude for the message they have received. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of humility and reverence in the presence of divine revelation and the blessings that come with it.
orig: أولئك الذين أنعم الله عليهم من النبيين من ذرية آدم وممن حملنا مع نوح ومن ذرية إبراهيم وإسرائيل وممن هدينا واجتبينا إذا تتلى عليهم آيات الرحمن خروا سجدا وبكيا

translation: And after them succeeded an generation who neglected the prayer and followed their desires, so they will encounter error.
interpretation: The verse speaks about a generation that came after another and neglected the prayer and followed their desires. The verse warns that this generation will encounter error or go astray as a result of their actions. The verse highlights the importance of prayer in maintaining a connection with God and staying on the right path. Neglecting prayer and following one's desires can lead to deviation from the right path and negative consequences. The verse serves as a reminder to prioritize the worship of God and resist the temptation of desires in order to avoid going astray.
orig: فخلف من بعدهم خلف أضاعوا الصلاة واتبعوا الشهوات فسوف يلقون غيا

translation: Except for those who repent, believe, and do righteous deeds, for they will enter Paradise, and they will not be wronged in any way.
interpretation: The verse offers a way for people to avoid the punishment mentioned earlier in the Surah, which is through repentance, belief, and righteous deeds. Those who do so will be granted entrance to Paradise and will not be wronged in any way, meaning they will receive exactly what they deserve and nothing less. This verse serves as a message of hope and mercy, highlighting the importance of turning back to God, having faith, and doing good deeds as a means of avoiding punishment and attaining salvation.
orig: إلا من تاب وآمن وعمل صالحا فأولئك يدخلون الجنة ولا يظلمون شيئا

translation: Gardens of Eden, which the Most Gracious has promised to His servants in the unseen. Indeed, His promise has come true.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the Gardens of Eden that the Most Gracious (God) has promised to His servants. The promise of God is described as being in the unseen, indicating that it is something that cannot be fully comprehended or seen by human beings. However, the verse emphasizes that God's promise has come true, implying that the believers can have full confidence in the fulfillment of God's promises. This verse serves as a source of hope and reassurance for the believers, reminding them of the beautiful rewards that await them in the afterlife as a result of their faith and obedience to God.
orig: جنات عدن التي وعد الرحمن عباده بالغيب إنه كان وعده مأتيا

translation: In it, they will not hear therein any ill speech - only peace. And their provision is supplied to them therein, morning and afternoon.
interpretation: The verse describes a peaceful and harmonious place where only words of peace are heard. The people living there have their needs supplied in the morning and in the afternoon, indicating that they have a sufficient and regular supply of sustenance. The verse may be referring to a state of paradise or a peaceful community where people live in harmony and abundance.
orig: لا يسمعون فيها لغوا إلا سلاما ولهم رزقهم فيها بكرة وعشيا

translation: That is the paradise which We shall give as inheritance to those of Our servants who are pious.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the paradise that will be given as an inheritance to the pious servants of God. The verse emphasizes the exclusivity of this paradise, which will be given only to those who have lived a righteous and god-fearing life. The verse serves as a reminder of the rewards that await those who are obedient to God and strive to lead a virtuous life.
orig: تلك الجنة التي نورث من عبادنا من كان تقيا

translation: And We do not come down except by the command of your Lord; to Him belongs what is before us and what is behind us and what is between them, and your Lord is not forgetful.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the power and knowledge of God, who controls everything in the heavens and on earth. The verse states that angels do not descend to earth except by God's command, and that God has power over all things, both past and future. The verse serves as a reminder of God's greatness and omniscience, and the idea that nothing happens without God's knowledge and permission.
orig: وما نتنزل إلا بأمر ربك له ما بين أيدينا وما خلفنا وما بين ذلك وما كان ربك نسيا

translation: Lord of the heavens and the earth, and whatever is between them, so worship Him and be constant in prayer to Him. Do you know of any name similar to His?
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the greatness and uniqueness of God as the Lord of the heavens, the earth, and all that lies between them. It commands people to worship Him and be steadfast in their devotion to Him. The verse then asks if one knows of any name similar to His, implying that there is no other god but Him. This verse serves as a reminder of the oneness of God and the importance of worshiping Him alone, while also encouraging perseverance and dedication in one's religious practices.
orig: رب السماوات والأرض وما بينهما فاعبده واصطبر لعبادته هل تعلم له سميا

translation: And man says, 'What, when I am dead, will I then be brought forth alive?'
interpretation: The verse highlights the disbelief and denial of some people regarding the resurrection and the Day of Judgment. They question and mock the idea of being brought back to life after death. The verse serves to remind us of the reality of the resurrection and the accountability of all our actions, urging us to prepare for that inevitable Day.
orig: ويقول الإنسان أإذا ما مت لسوف أخرج حيا

translation: Does not man remember that We created him before, while he was nothing?
interpretation: The verse reminds human beings of their humble origins and their dependence on the Creator. By stating that humans were created 'while he was nothing', the verse emphasizes the power and mercy of God, who brought human beings into existence from a state of non-existence. The verse encourages human beings to reflect on the nature of their existence and to be mindful of their responsibilities towards their Creator. It suggests that human beings should not be arrogant or forgetful, but should remember the blessings and mercies that God has bestowed upon them, and live their lives in accordance with His will and guidance.
orig: أولا يذكر الإنسان أنا خلقناه من قبل ولم يك شيئا

translation: So away with them, indeed We will gather them and the devils, then We will bring them around Hell, kneeling.
interpretation: The verse describes the fate of the unbelievers who will be gathered along with the devils and brought around Hell, made to kneel in submission. The use of the phrase 'So away with them' indicates a sense of finality and a decisive end to any chance of redemption for these individuals. The image of being brought around Hell, kneeling, is a powerful and terrifying one, emphasizing the gravity of their actions and the consequences that await them. The verse serves as a stark warning to those who reject faith and choose a path of disbelief, highlighting the ultimate destination of those who persist in their ways.
orig: فوربك لنحشرنهم والشياطين ثم لنحضرنهم حول جهنم جثيا

translation: Then We shall extract from every group, whoever among them was most stubborn against the Most Merciful.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the Day of Judgment, when God will extract from each group of people the one who was most stubborn and unyielding in their disbelief and rejection of God's mercy. The verse emphasizes the severity of the punishment for those who persist in their disbelief and refuse to submit to God's will, despite the countless signs and messages sent to guide them towards the right path. The verse serves as a warning to those who continue to reject God's mercy and urges them to repent and seek forgiveness before it is too late.
orig: ثم لننزعن من كل شيعة أيهم أشد على الرحمن عتيا

translation: Then We shall surely know those who were best suited for it.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the knowledge of God regarding those who are most deserving of something, in this context, it is referring to the blessings of this world. The verse emphasizes the all-knowing nature of God and His ability to judge who among His creations are truly worthy of His blessings. It serves as a reminder that God is aware of our actions and intentions and will ultimately reward those who are most deserving.
orig: ثم لنحن أعلم بالذين هم أولى بها صليا

translation: And not one of you but will pass over it: this is, with your Lord, a decree decreed.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the inevitability of death and the fact that every human being will have to face it. The phrase 'pass over it' refers to the act of crossing the bridge that leads to the afterlife. The verse emphasizes that this is a decree from God and it is inevitable and unavoidable. It serves as a reminder of the transience of life and the importance of preparing for the afterlife.
orig: وإن منكم إلا واردها كان على ربك حتما مقضيا

translation: Then We will save those who feared (God) and leave the wrongdoers in it, prone (in Hell)
interpretation: The verse speaks about the Day of Judgment and the separation of the righteous from the wicked. Those who feared God and were obedient to Him will be saved, while the wrongdoers will be left in Hell. The verse emphasizes the importance of fearing God and being mindful of one's actions in this life, as it will determine one's fate in the hereafter.
orig: ثم ننجي الذين اتقوا ونذر الظالمين فيها جثيا

translation: And when our verses are recited to them clearly, those who disbelieve say to those who believe, 'Which of the two groups is better in position and better in guidance?'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the disbelievers mocking the believers and questioning the merit of their faith. When the verses of the Quran are recited to them, they challenge the believers by asking which group has a better position and guidance. This verse highlights the arrogance and rejection of the disbelievers, who refuse to accept the truth and instead mock those who believe. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of faith and the dangers of arrogance and rejection of God's message.
orig: وإذا تتلى عليهم آياتنا بينات قال الذين كفروا للذين آمنوا أي الفريقين خير مقاما وأحسن نديا

translation: And how many a generation before them did We destroy, who had better possessions and clearer sight?
interpretation: The verse highlights the destruction of past civilizations who were more prosperous and had greater blessings than the current generation. Despite their advantages, they were destroyed due to their disbelief and ingratitude towards God. This verse serves as a reminder of the transient nature of worldly possessions and the importance of recognizing God's blessings and using them for good. Ultimately, the verse emphasizes the importance of faith and gratitude as a means of avoiding the same fate as those before them.
orig: وكم أهلكنا قبلهم من قرن هم أحسن أثاثا ورئيا

translation: Say, 'Who is it that can protect you from the Lord if He intends harm for you or intends mercy?' They will not find for themselves, besides Allah, any protector or helper.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the ultimate power and control of God, who has the ability to either show mercy or cause harm. The verse challenges people to find a protector or helper besides God, implying that no one can provide true protection or assistance. The verse serves as a reminder of the powerlessness of humans in the face of God's will and the importance of seeking God's mercy and forgiveness. It also highlights the futility of seeking protection or help from other sources, as God is the only true source of protection and help.
orig: قل من كان في الضلالة فليمدد له الرحمن مدا حتى إذا رأوا ما يوعدون إما العذاب وإما الساعة فسيعلمون من هو شر مكانا وأضعف جندا

translation: And Allah will increase those who have been guided, in guidance, and those who are righteous, in goodness, [goodness] from their Lord, [and] a righteous protector, and an excellent friend.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the rewards for those who have been guided and those who are righteous. These individuals will receive increased guidance and goodness from their Lord. Furthermore, they will have a righteous protector and an excellent friend. The verse highlights the blessings and rewards that come to those who are on the right path, emphasizing the importance of guidance and righteousness.
orig: ويزيد الله الذين اهتدوا هدى والباقيات الصالحات خير عند ربك ثوابا وخير مردا

translation: Have you seen the one who rejects Our signs and says, 'I will surely be given wealth and children [in abundance].'
interpretation: The verse speaks about those who reject the signs of God and have a sense of entitlement and arrogance, thinking that they will be given wealth and children in abundance. This verse serves as a warning to those who deny the signs of God and rely on their material possessions and worldly success, reminding them that such things are not guaranteed and that they should not be the basis for one's faith or actions.
orig: أفرأيت الذي كفر بآياتنا وقال لأوتين مالا وولدا

translation: Can I grasp the unseen, or have I been given knowledge of the unseen?
interpretation: The verse is a rhetorical question asked by the disbelievers, expressing their disbelief in the prophet Muhammad's (PBUH) message. They are essentially asking if the prophet has the ability to know the unseen or if he has been given knowledge of it. The verse implies that the disbelievers are denying the revelation and the knowledge that the prophet has been given by God. It serves as a reminder that only God has knowledge of the unseen and that the disbelievers should not deny the revelation based on their own limited understanding and knowledge.
orig: أطلع الغيب أم اتخذ عند الرحمن عهدا

translation: But We shall surely write down what he says, and We shall prolong for him the punishment.
interpretation: The verse speaks about someone who is being punished by God and is expressing their regret or trying to make excuses. However, God will not accept their excuses and will write down their words as evidence of their guilt. Moreover, God will prolong their punishment, indicating that it will be severe and unending. The verse serves as a warning to those who deny the truth and persist in their disobedience, reminding them that their words and actions are being recorded and that they will be held accountable for them in the afterlife.
orig: كلا سنكتب ما يقول ونمد له من العذاب مدا

translation: And they will inherit the load of what they used to say, and they will come to Us alone.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the accountability of people for their words and deeds, and the fact that they will face the consequences of their actions on their own. The phrase 'they will inherit the load of what they used to say' implies that people will be held responsible for their words and will not be able to escape the consequences of their speech. The phrase 'they will come to Us alone' emphasizes the individual nature of accountability and the fact that everyone will be judged according to their own deeds and will not be able to rely on the merits of others. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of responsible speech and the reality of individual accountability before God.
orig: ونرثه ما يقول ويأتينا فردا

translation: And they have taken besides Allah protectors, so they will not help them.
interpretation: The verse speaks about people who have taken protectors or allies besides Allah, thinking that these beings will help and support them. However, the verse clearly states that these protectors will not be able to help them in any way. This verse emphasizes the importance of relying solely on Allah, the one true God, and the futility of seeking help from other sources. It serves as a reminder that no one can provide help and protection like Allah, and that putting one's trust in anything other than Him is a grave mistake.
orig: واتخذوا من دون الله آلهة ليكونوا لهم عزا

translation: Rather, they will deny their worship and turn away from it.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the rejection of the truth by those who are deeply rooted in their false beliefs and practices. Despite engaging in religious rituals and worship, they will deny and reject the true path of God when it is presented to them. This verse highlights the human tendency to cling to familiar but false beliefs, even in the face of clear evidence and guidance. It serves as a reminder of the importance of being open-minded and receptive to the truth, regardless of one's prior beliefs or traditions.
orig: كلا سيكفرون بعبادتهم ويكونون عليهم ضدا

translation: Have you not seen that We sent the Shayatin (devils) upon the disbelievers to disturb them?
interpretation: The verse speaks about the sending of devils upon the disbelievers to disturb and torment them. This verse suggests that the disbelievers are being punished for their lack of faith, and that they are experiencing difficulty and turmoil as a result. The verse serves as a warning to those who reject the message of Islam, reminding them of the consequences of their disbelief and the reality of divine punishment.
orig: ألم تر أنا أرسلنا الشياطين على الكافرين تؤزهم أزا

translation: So be patient with them, for indeed, We are patient with them. And indeed, We will give them a great punishment.
interpretation: The verse speaks about God's command to be patient with the unbelievers and their rejection of the message of Islam. The verse emphasizes that God is also patient with them, but ultimately, a severe punishment will be given to them. The verse serves as a reminder for the believers to remain steadfast and patient in the face of adversity and rejection, and to trust in God's ultimate plan and justice.
orig: فلا تعجل عليهم إنما نعد لهم عدا

translation: A Day we will gather the righteous to the Merciful like a delegation.
interpretation: The verse describes the gathering of the righteous people to meet with the Merciful (God) on a specific Day. The imagery of a 'delegation' (fudan) is used to convey the significance and solemnity of this event, as if the righteous are being received as honored guests. This gathering is a promise of a positive outcome for those who have lived a righteous life, emphasizing the importance of striving for righteousness in order to be among those who are invited to this special meeting with the Merciful.
orig: يوم نحشر المتقين إلى الرحمن وفدا

translation: And We will drive the evildoers to Hell, in a thirsty state
interpretation: The verse speaks about the fate of evildoers, who will be driven to Hell in a state of thirst. The image of thirst is used to emphasize their suffering and the severity of their punishment. The verse serves as a warning to those who commit evil deeds, reminding them of the painful consequences that await them in the afterlife if they do not repent and change their ways.
orig: ونسوق المجرمين إلى جهنم وردا

translation: They cannot intercede, except for one who has taken a covenant from the Most Merciful.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the power and authority of God, by stating that no one can intercede on behalf of another, except for those who have a special covenant with the Most Merciful. This verse highlights the importance of having a close relationship with God, and the privileges that come with it, such as the ability to intercede on the Day of Judgment. The verse also serves as a reminder that ultimate power and control belong to God alone, and that no one can intercede without His permission.
orig: لا يملكون الشفاعة إلا من اتخذ عند الرحمن عهدا

translation: And they said, 'The Merciful has taken for Himself a son.'
interpretation: The verse is a rejection of the claim made by some disbelievers that the Merciful (one of the names of God) has taken a son. This claim is considered blasphemous and is rejected in the verse. The verse emphasizes the absolute oneness of God and the impossibility of Him having a son. The verse can be seen as a reminder to believers to uphold the oneness of God and not to fall into the same error as the disbelievers.
orig: وقالوا اتخذ الرحمن ولدا

translation: Indeed, you have come upon something (a great trial or punishment).
interpretation: The verse indicates that the people being addressed have encountered a significant event or trial, often understood as a punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the inevitability of the trial and the need for the people to be prepared for its consequences. The verse serves as a warning to those who may be unprepared for the trials and tribulations of life, reminding them of the need to be mindful of their actions and to seek forgiveness and repentance.
orig: لقد جئتم شيئا إدا

translation: The heavens are about to break from it, and the earth is about to split open, and the mountains are about to crumble down.
interpretation: The verse describes the imminent and catastrophic events that will occur as a result of a transgression or wrongdoing. The heavens are on the verge of breaking apart, the earth is close to splitting open, and the mountains are ready to crumble down. This imagery conveys the severity of the situation and the overwhelming power of the divine retribution. The verse serves as a warning to those who persist in their wrongful ways, emphasizing the gravity of their actions and the inevitable consequences they will face.
orig: تكاد السماوات يتفطرن منه وتنشق الأرض وتخر الجبال هدا

translation: So invite to the way of your Lord with wisdom and good instruction, and argue with them in a way that is best. Indeed, your Lord is most knowing of who has strayed from His way, and He is most knowing of who is guided.
interpretation: The verse is a command to the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) to invite people to the path of God with wisdom and good advice. It emphasizes the importance of using effective and respectful communication when engaging with those who do not believe, and encourages the use of reasoning and argumentation in a way that is most likely to be well-received. The verse also highlights God's omniscience, reminding the Prophet that God knows who has strayed from His path and who has been guided, and that the outcome is ultimately in God's hands.
orig: أن دعوا للرحمن ولدا

translation: And it is not befitting for the Most Merciful to take a son
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the transcendence and uniqueness of God as the Most Merciful. It asserts that it is not befitting for God to take a son, implying that God is above all human limitations and attributes. This verse is a rejection of any notion of God having a physical or biological offspring and reinforces the Islamic belief in the oneness of God.
orig: وما ينبغي للرحمن أن يتخذ ولدا

translation: There is not one of (the creatures) in the heavens and the earth but must come to the Most Gracious (Allah) as a slave.
interpretation: The verse affirms that all creatures in the heavens and the earth are ultimately subservient to Allah, the Most Gracious. It emphasizes the power and sovereignty of Allah, and the ultimate accountability of all creation to Him. The verse serves as a reminder of the unity and interconnectedness of all creation, and the importance of recognizing and submitting to the will of the Creator.
orig: إن كل من في السماوات والأرض إلا آتي الرحمن عبدا

translation: We have indeed recounted to you in detail before, (O Muhammad), when Musa (Moses) said to his people: 'Indeed, I have perceived a fire. I will bring you information from there, or I will bring you a burning brand that you may warm yourselves with, or (at least) that you may find a guidance.',
interpretation: The verse is a continuation of a narrative about Musa (Moses) and his people. It describes how Musa (Moses) saw a fire and told his people that he would bring them information from it or a burning brand to warm themselves or find guidance. The verse highlights Musa's (Moses) leadership and his commitment to his people. It also emphasizes the importance of seeking knowledge, guidance and light in one's life.
orig: لقد أحصاهم وعدهم عدا

translation: And every one of them will come to Us alone on the Day of Resurrection.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the individual accountability of every person on the Day of Judgment. Each person will stand before God alone, without any support or help from others. This highlights the importance of personal responsibility and accountability for one's actions and deeds. It also underscores the fairness and justice of God's judgment, as each person will be judged solely on the basis of their own actions and not on the actions of others.
orig: وكلهم آتيه يوم القيامة فردا

translation: Indeed, those who have believed and done righteous deeds - the Most Merciful will appoint for them affection.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the reward that will be given to those who have believed in God and done good deeds. The reward for these individuals is the appointment of affection from the Most Merciful. This suggests a deep and profound love and connection between God and the believers. The verse serves as a source of hope and motivation for those who strive to lead a righteous life, reminding them that their good deeds will not go unnoticed and that they will be rewarded with a special closeness to God in this life and the hereafter.
orig: إن الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات سيجعل لهم الرحمن ودا

translation: And We have only made it easy for you in language, so that you may give good news with it to the righteous and warn with it a people given to contention.
interpretation: The verse highlights the role of the speaker (in this context, the Prophet Muhammad) in conveying the message of Islam to the people. The message is made easy for the speaker to deliver, so that they may bring glad tidings to the righteous and warn those who are skeptical or in disagreement. The verse emphasizes the importance of the speaker's role in delivering the message, and the significance of the message itself in bringing hope to the righteous and warning to the disbelievers.
orig: فإنما يسرناه بلسانك لتبشر به المتقين وتنذر به قوما لدا

translation: And how many a generation before them have We destroyed. Can you find any one of them, or hear even a whisper of them?
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of previous generations who were destroyed by God for their sins. The verse emphasizes the complete annihilation of these civilizations, stating that there is no trace of them left, not even a whisper. This serves as a reminder to the listeners of the transience of this world and the consequences of ignoring God's commands. It also conveys the message that those who deny God and persist in their sinful ways will ultimately face destruction, just as previous civilizations have.
orig: وكم أهلكنا قبلهم من قرن هل تحس منهم من أحد أو تسمع لهم ركزا

translation: Then after that,
interpretation: No interpretation
orig: طه

translation: We have not sent down the Qur'an to you that you be distressed.
interpretation: The verse reassures the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) that the Qur'an was not revealed to him as a source of distress or hardship. Instead, the Qur'an was revealed as a source of guidance, mercy, and wisdom. This verse serves as a reminder that the teachings and commandments of the Qur'an should not be viewed as a burden, but rather as a means of achieving spiritual growth and fulfillment. The verse may also serve as a source of comfort and reassurance for Muslims, reminding them that the Qur'an is a source of divine guidance and support in their lives.
orig: ما أنزلنا عليك القرآن لتشقى

translation: But a reminder to whoever fears.
interpretation: The verse speaks about a reminder or admonition that is given to those who have fear or consciousness of God. It implies that the reminder is a warning to those who are aware of the consequences of their actions and are mindful of God's judgment. The verse suggests that the reminder is a means of guiding people towards righteousness and encouraging them to fear and worship God. It serves as a call to reflection and contemplation, urging people to consider the significance of their actions and the importance of their relationship with God.
orig: إلا تذكرة لمن يخشى

translation: A revelation from He who created the earth and the heavens above.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the power and authority of God as the creator of the universe. It suggests that the message being revealed (presumably, the Qur'an) comes from a divine and all-powerful being who has control over all of creation. The verse serves as a reminder of the greatness and majesty of God, and the importance of heeding the message that is being revealed.
orig: تنزيلا ممن خلق الأرض والسماوات العلى

translation: The Most Gracious (Allah) rose over (Istawa) the (Mighty) Throne (in a manner that suits His Majesty).
interpretation: This verse speaks about the majesty and power of Allah, the Most Gracious. The verse describes how Allah rose over (Istawa) the throne, indicating His supreme power and control over all of His creation. The verse emphasizes the greatness and might of Allah, and serves as a reminder of His sovereignty and authority over all things. The verse also highlights the transcendence of Allah, and the fact that He is not limited by time or space, but rather, He is the Creator and Sustainer of all that exists.
orig: الرحمن على العرش استوى

translation: To Him belongs what is in the heavens and what is on the earth and what is between them and what is beneath the ground.
interpretation: The verse affirms the power and sovereignty of God over all of creation. It emphasizes that everything in the heavens, the earth, and everything in between, as well as what is beneath the ground, belongs to Him. This includes all living and non-living things, both seen and unseen. The verse serves to remind believers of the greatness and power of God, and to inspire awe and reverence for Him. It encourages believers to recognize and submit to the will of God, and to trust in His provision and protection.
orig: له ما في السماوات وما في الأرض وما بينهما وما تحت الثرى

translation: But if you divulge (the secret), then indeed, He knows what is in the breasts (of men). And He knows what you reveal and what you conceal.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the all-knowing nature of God. It emphasizes that God is aware of everything, including what is hidden in people's hearts and what they reveal or conceal. The verse serves as a reminder that one cannot hide anything from God and should be mindful of their actions and intentions. It also highlights the importance of honesty and transparency in one's relationship with God.
orig: وإن تجهر بالقول فإنه يعلم السر وأخفى

translation: Allah, there is no god but He, to Him belong the beautiful names.
interpretation: The verse is a declaration of the oneness of God, asserting that Allah is the only god and that all other gods are false. The second part of the verse is a praise of God's beautiful names, emphasizing the perfection and majesty of God's attributes. The verse serves as a reminder of the greatness of God and the importance of recognizing and worshiping Him alone.
orig: الله لا إله إلا هو له الأسماء الحسنى

translation: And has there come to you the story of Moses?
interpretation: The verse is a rhetorical question asking if the story of Moses has reached the audience. This question implies that the story of Moses is well-known and significant. The story of Moses is mentioned multiple times in the Quran, and it is a central narrative in Islamic tradition. The verse may be interpreted as an invitation to reflect on the story of Moses and the lessons that can be learned from it.
orig: وهل أتاك حديث موسى

translation: When he saw a fire, he said to his family, 'Stay here, I have seen a fire. Perhaps I can bring you a brand from it, or I will find guidance at the fire.',
interpretation: The verse describes a person who sees a fire and is inspired to approach it, hoping to find guidance or a source of light. The person's initial reaction is to share this newfound knowledge with their family, indicating a sense of responsibility and care towards them. The verse highlights the importance of seeking guidance and light in one's journey, and the potential for unexpected sources of knowledge and understanding to emerge from one's surroundings.
orig: إذ رأى نارا فقال لأهله امكثوا إني آنست نارا لعلي آتيكم منها بقبس أو أجد على النار هدى

translation: And when Moses came to it, he was called upon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the encounter of Moses with a divine revelation. The verse emphasizes the direct and personal nature of the encounter, as Moses was 'called upon' directly. The verse serves as a reminder of the power and presence of the divine, and the possibility of direct communication between the divine and human beings.
orig: فلما أتاها نودي يا موسى

translation: I am your Lord, so take off your sandals. Indeed, you are in the sacred valley of Tuwa.
interpretation: The verse is a direct address from God to Musa (Moses) as he is commanded to remove his sandals as a sign of respect and humility before the divine presence. Musa is also informed that he is standing in the sacred valley of Tuwa, which is a significant location in the story of Musa as it is where he received his mission from God to free the Israelites from Egypt. The verse emphasizes the special relationship between Musa and God, and the significance of the encounter and the message that will follow.
orig: إني أنا ربك فاخلع نعليك إنك بالواد المقدس طوى

translation: And I have chosen you, so listen to what is revealed.
interpretation: The verse is addressing a specific person, who has been chosen for a special purpose. The person is being instructed to listen carefully to the revelation that they are about to receive. This verse emphasizes the importance of attentiveness and obedience to divine guidance, and highlights the significance of the chosen person's role in receiving and sharing this guidance with others.
orig: وأنا اخترتك فاستمع لما يوحى

translation: Indeed, I am Allah - there is no deity except Me, so worship Me and establish prayer for My remembrance.
interpretation: The verse is a powerful declaration of God's oneness and sovereignty. It commands the listener to worship only Allah and to establish prayer as a means of remembering and honoring Him. This verse emphasizes the importance of maintaining a strong and consistent relationship with God through regular worship and prayer. It also highlights the unique and exclusive nature of God, reminding the listener that there is no other deity worthy of worship or devotion.
orig: إنني أنا الله لا إله إلا أنا فاعبدني وأقم الصلاة لذكري

translation: Indeed, the Hour is coming - I almost conceal it so that every soul may be recompensed according to what it strives for.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the coming of the 'Hour' or the Day of Judgment, which is a central tenet of Islamic eschatology. The verse indicates that the coming of the Hour is inevitable, and that God has chosen to conceal its exact time so that people will not be complacent and continue to strive for what is right. The verse emphasizes the importance of individual accountability, as every soul will be recompensed according to its deeds. The verse serves as a reminder to believers to continue to strive for righteousness, and not to become complacent or neglectful of their duties towards God and society.
orig: إن الساعة آتية أكاد أخفيها لتجزى كل نفس بما تسعى

translation: So let not those who disbelieve in it (the Qur'an) deter you from conveying it. And invite (people) to your Lord. Indeed, you are on a straight path.
interpretation: The verse is addressing the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) and advising him not to be discouraged by those who disbelieve in the Qur'an from conveying and sharing its message. The verse encourages the Prophet to continue inviting people to worship and follow the path of his Lord. The verse emphasizes the importance of the Prophet's mission in spreading the message of Islam and the importance of staying steadfast on the right path despite any opposition or adversity faced.
orig: فلا يصدنك عنها من لا يؤمن بها واتبع هواه فتردى

translation: And that is not with your right hand, O Moses.
interpretation: The verse is a continuation of a conversation between God and Moses, where God is performing a miracle by parting the sea. The verse emphasizes that the miracle is not something that Moses has done with his own hand, but rather it is a divine act performed by God. The verse serves to remind the reader of the power and authority of God, and the limitations of human abilities.
orig: وما تلك بيمينك يا موسى

translation: He said, 'This is my staff. I lean on it, and I beat down leaves for my sheep with it. I have other shepherds over them.'
interpretation: The verse is a statement made by someone, most likely a shepherd or a person who tends to animals, about their staff. The staff is described as being used for multiple purposes, such as for support and for herding the animals. The person also mentions that they have other shepherds under their care. The verse gives a sense of the person's daily life and their responsibilities as a shepherd. It also highlights the importance of the staff as a tool for their work.
orig: قال هي عصاي أتوكأ عليها وأهش بها على غنمي ولي فيها مآرب أخرى

translation: Said [Pharaoh], 'Throw it [the staff] down, Moses!'
interpretation: The verse recounts Pharaoh's challenge to Moses to throw down his staff as a test of their respective powers. Pharaoh's command to 'throw it down' conveys his skepticism and disbelief in Moses' claim of being a prophet and his demand for Pharaoh to release the Israelites from slavery. The command also reflects Pharaoh's sense of superiority and his determination to maintain his power and authority over the Israelites. The verse sets the stage for the miraculous transformation of Moses' staff into a serpent, which demonstrates the power and authority of God, and ultimately leads to Pharaoh's downfall.
orig: قال ألقها يا موسى

translation: And We have certainly created you, [O Mankind], then We will surely cause you to die and then [We will] surely resurrect you.
interpretation: This verse speaks to the power and control that God has over human life. It emphasizes the three stages of human existence: creation, death, and resurrection. The verse reminds human beings that their lives are temporary and that they will ultimately be held accountable for their actions on the Day of Judgment. It serves as a reminder of the transience of life and the importance of living a righteous and devout life in preparation for the afterlife.
orig: فألقاها فإذا هي حية تسعى

translation: He said, 'Take her and fear not. We shall reinstate her to her former state.'
interpretation: The verse is a conversation between an unnamed person and an audience, where the person is instructed to take possession of something or someone (presumably a woman, as indicated by the feminine pronoun in the original Arabic text) without fear, as it will be restored to its former state. The verse emphasizes the power and control of the speaker, who is able to reinstate the woman's former state. The verse may be interpreted as a message of hope and restoration, indicating that even in difficult situations, there is the possibility of returning to a better state. The verse may also be interpreted as a reminder of the power and control that God has over all things.
orig: قال خذها ولا تخف سنعيدها سيرتها الأولى

translation: And keep your hand under your armpit, you will take it out white (i.e. unblemished) without any disease.
interpretation: This verse speaks about the importance of taking care of one's health and avoiding harm to oneself. The act of keeping one's hand under their armpit and then taking it out white and unblemished is a metaphor for maintaining good health and avoiding illness. The verse encourages believers to take steps to protect their health and avoid activities that could lead to disease or injury. It also highlights the importance of cleanliness and hygiene, as keeping one's hand under their armpit would prevent it from coming into contact with dirt and germs. Ultimately, the verse reminds believers that taking care of their health is a form of worship and a way to express gratitude for the blessings that God has bestowed upon them.
orig: واضمم يدك إلى جناحك تخرج بيضاء من غير سوء آية أخرى

translation: We will show you some of Our greatest signs.
interpretation: The verse is a promise from God to reveal some of His greatest signs or wonders to the listener or reader. This could be interpreted as a reference to the natural world and its intricate systems, or to the revelations and teachings of Islam. The verse serves as a reminder of the greatness and power of God, and the smallness and insignificance of human beings in comparison. It may also serve as an invitation to reflect on the signs of God and to seek knowledge and understanding of them.
orig: لنريك من آياتنا الكبرى

translation: Go to Pharaoh, indeed, he has transgressed.
interpretation: The verse is a command to someone (likely Moses) to go to Pharaoh and confront him. The reason for this confrontation is that Pharaoh has transgressed or exceeded the limits set by God. This transgression could refer to Pharaoh's oppression of the Israelites, his claim to divinity, or both. The verse establishes Pharaoh's tyranny and sets the stage for the larger conflict between him and Moses, which will be a central theme in the Qur'anic narrative.
orig: اذهب إلى فرعون إنه طغى

translation: Said (a soul), 'My Lord, expand for me my chest.'
interpretation: The verse is a supplication from a soul to its Lord, asking for an expansion of its chest. This expansion is often interpreted as a metaphor for the opening of the heart and the soul to guidance, knowledge, and wisdom. It is a request for the ability to understand and accept the truth, and for the strength to follow the right path. The verse highlights the importance of seeking knowledge and understanding, and the need for divine assistance in this journey towards enlightenment and wisdom.
orig: قال رب اشرح لي صدري

translation: And make my task easy for me.
interpretation: The verse is a supplication to God, asking for ease in one's affairs and responsibilities. It emphasizes the importance of seeking God's help and support in overcoming challenges and difficulties. The verse can be seen as a reminder to believers to seek God's guidance and assistance in all aspects of their lives, and to trust in His wisdom and mercy.
orig: ويسر لي أمري

translation: And undo a knot from my tongue
interpretation: The verse is a supplication or a prayer to God, asking Him to undo a knot from the speaker's tongue. The knot is a metaphor for the difficulty or impediment that the speaker experiences in speaking or expressing themselves. The verse suggests that the speaker is seeking God's help and assistance in overcoming this obstacle and communicating effectively. The verse can be interpreted as a reminder of the importance of clear and effective communication, and of the need for God's guidance and support in achieving this goal.
orig: واحلل عقدة من لساني

translation: So perhaps you will understand (me fully well).
interpretation: The phrase is spoken by a speaker, likely a prophet or a messenger, who is expressing hope that the audience will understand the message being conveyed to them. The phrase can be interpreted as a plea or a call for the audience to pay attention and make an effort to comprehend the message. It highlights the importance of effective communication and the need for the audience to be receptive to the message in order to fully understand it.
orig: يفقهوا قولي

translation: And grant me a helper from my family
interpretation: The verse is a supplication from a prophet asking for God's help and support. The prophet is asking for a helper from his family, indicating the importance of family and community in supporting and aiding each other. The verse emphasizes the need for assistance and the importance of seeking help from God in times of need.
orig: واجعل لي وزيرا من أهلي

translation: N
interpretation: N
orig: هارون أخي

translation: So, let Me alone with my grief.
interpretation: The verse is a statement made by the Prophet Moses (peace be upon him) to his people, expressing his desire for solitude to cope with the burden of his mission and the grief he experiences due to the disbelief of his people. The verse emphasizes the heavy responsibility and emotional toll that prophethood can have on a person, and highlights the importance of seeking solitude and seeking support from God during difficult times.
orig: اشدد به أزري

translation: And associate him in my affair.
interpretation: The verse speaks about associating partners with God in his affairs or actions, which is a form of shirk (associating partners with God) and is strictly prohibited in Islam. The verse emphasizes the severity of this act and the importance of worshipping and serving God alone, without any intermediaries or partners.
orig: وأشركه في أمري

translation: That We may mention Your praises much.
interpretation: The phrase 'kay nusabbiHu katheeran' in the Qur'an is a direct address to God, expressing the desire to mention and glorify Him abundantly. This phrase emphasizes the importance of praising and remembering God, and the significance of expressing gratitude for His blessings. It also highlights the human's duty to worship and honor God, and the importance of recognizing His greatness and power.
orig: كي نسبحك كثيرا

translation: And We remind you often.
interpretation: The verse is a reminder from God to the person being addressed, reminding them frequently. The purpose and content of the reminder is not specified in this particular verse, but it serves as a general reminder of God's presence and concern for the well-being of the person being addressed. It may also serve as a call to remember and follow God's teachings and commands.
orig: ونذكرك كثيرا

translation: Indeed, I was about to create you as a creature to behold.
interpretation: The verse is a statement from God, addressing the Prophet Muhammad, indicating that God was going to create him as a special creation, worthy of being looked at or admired. This verse emphasizes the special status of the Prophet Muhammad as a chosen messenger of God, and highlights his unique role in conveying God's message to humanity. The verse may also serve as a reminder of the power and wisdom of God, who has the ability to create and shape all of existence according to His will.
orig: إنك كنت بنا بصيرا

translation: He said, 'Indeed, I have come to you, O Moses,',
interpretation: The verse is a continuation of a conversation between God and Moses. It indicates that God is addressing Moses directly, emphasizing the importance of the message that is about to be conveyed. The verse sets the stage for the revelation of divine guidance and wisdom, and underscores the special relationship between God and Moses as a prophet and messenger.
orig: قال قد أوتيت سؤلك يا موسى

translation: And We have given you another turn/chance.
interpretation: The verse speaks about God's mercy and forgiveness. It suggests that God has given the person or people being addressed another chance or opportunity after a previous one. The verse can be interpreted as a reminder of God's willingness to give second chances and as an invitation to make use of this opportunity to change one's ways and turn back to God.
orig: ولقد مننا عليك مرة أخرى

translation: When We inspired to your mother what was inspired
interpretation: The verse speaks about a revelation that was given to the mother of the person being addressed (who is believed to be the Prophet Muhammad in Islamic tradition). The verse emphasizes the divine origin of the revelation, and the role of the mother in receiving and delivering it. The verse can be interpreted as a metaphorical description of the guidance and wisdom that a mother provides to her child, or as a literal reference to a specific revelation received by the mother of the Prophet Muhammad. In either case, the verse highlights the significance of the role of mothers as transmitters of knowledge, guidance, and values.
orig: إذ أوحينا إلى أمك ما يوحى

translation: So throw him into the chest, and throw the chest into the sea, and the sea will throw him up on the shore which is blessed and protected. And an enemy to Me and an enemy to him will take him, and I cast love over you from Me, and (he will be) a counselor for you to (your) eye.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the story of Moses and his sister's efforts to save him from Pharaoh's decree to kill all newborn Hebrew boys. The verse instructs the sister to throw Moses in a chest and cast it into the sea. The chest will then be thrown onto a blessed and protected shore where an enemy of Pharaoh will find him and raise him as his own. The verse emphasizes the role of God's protection and guidance in Moses' journey and his ultimate destiny. The verse also highlights the sister's trust in God's plan and her willingness to take a risk to save her brother's life.
orig: أن اقذفيه في التابوت فاقذفيه في اليم فليلقه اليم بالساحل يأخذه عدو لي وعدو له وألقيت عليك محبة مني ولتصنع على عيني

translation: When your sister goes about (in search), she says, 'Shall I direct you to someone who will take care of him?' So you both return to your mother; then she takes him back to her breast and she is not grieved, and she does not fear. And for you (O Moses), We willed to grant a (great) favor, so that you may be brought up under Our (Watchful) eye.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the early life of Moses and the role of his sister in finding a way to save him from the Pharaoh's decree to kill all male Hebrew babies. The verse highlights the protection and care that Moses received from his mother and the favor that God bestowed upon him by allowing him to grow under His watchful eye. The verse emphasizes the role of family and community in protecting and nurturing a child, and the protection and guidance that God provides for those whom He favors.
orig: إذ تمشي أختك فتقول هل أدلكم على من يكفله فرجعناك إلى أمك كي تقر عينها ولا تحزن وقتلت نفسا فنجيناك من الغم وفتناك فتونا فلبثت سنين في أهل مدين ثم جئت على قدر يا موسى

translation: And have I not taken care of myself
interpretation: The verse is a rhetorical question, spoken by someone who is reflecting on their past actions and the consequences they have brought. The speaker is acknowledging that they have not taken care of themselves or their responsibilities, and are now facing the negative results of their neglect. The verse can be interpreted as a call to self-reflection and responsibility, encouraging the reader to consider the impact of their actions on their own well-being and future.
orig: واصطنعتك لنفسي

translation: Go, you and your brother, with My signs, and do not slacken in My remembrance.
interpretation: The verse is addressed to one or two individuals, instructing them to carry the signs or messages of God and not to neglect or forget their duty of remembering and worshipping God. The verse emphasizes the importance of fulfilling the responsibility of spreading and upholding the teachings of Islam, and of maintaining a strong and consistent connection with the divine through remembrance and worship.
orig: اذهب أنت وأخوك بآياتي ولا تنيا في ذكري

translation: Go to Pharaoh, indeed, he has transgressed.
interpretation: The verse is a command to the Prophet Musa (Moses) to go to Pharaoh and confront him. The reason for this command is that Pharaoh has committed a great sin and transgressed the boundaries set by God. The verse sets the stage for the epic struggle between Musa and Pharaoh, and highlights the power dynamic between the two, with Musa being commanded by God to confront the powerful and oppressive Pharaoh. The verse also serves as a reminder of the consequences of transgressing against God's commands and oppressing others.
orig: اذهبا إلى فرعون إنه طغى

translation: So speak to him a gentle word, perhaps he may remember or fear.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the importance of using gentle and kind words when trying to convey a message or advice to someone. The verse suggests that by speaking softly and kindly, the person being addressed may be more likely to listen, understand, and reflect on the message being conveyed. The verse emphasizes the importance of using appropriate and effective communication strategies in order to achieve the desired outcome, whether it be to remind someone of something, or to instill a sense of fear or caution in them. The verse also highlights the potential for positive change and transformation that can result from gentle and considerate communication.
orig: فقولا له قولا لينا لعله يتذكر أو يخشى

translation: They said, 'Our Lord, we are afraid that a wrath may overtake us or that we may go astray.'
interpretation: The verse shows the people's fear of facing God's wrath and going astray. They are aware of their shortcomings and the possibility of being punished for them. The verse highlights the importance of being mindful of one's actions and seeking God's guidance to avoid deviating from the right path.
orig: قالا ربنا إننا نخاف أن يفرط علينا أو أن يطغى

translation: He said: 'Do not be afraid. Indeed, I am with you. I hear and I see.'
interpretation: The verse relays a message from a figure of authority or power, who speaks to reassure someone (or a group of people) who are afraid. The speaker tells them not to fear, as they are not alone – the speaker is with them. Moreover, the speaker emphasizes their presence and attentiveness by noting that they are both hearing and seeing. The verse can be interpreted as a message of comfort and support, where the speaker's presence and awareness provide a sense of safety and security. The verse can be applied in various contexts, such as a parent reassuring their child, a leader comforting their troops, or a religious figure addressing their followers.
orig: قال لا تخافا إنني معكما أسمع وأرى

translation: And when you come to them, say, 'Indeed, we are messengers of your Lord, so send with us the Children of Israel and harm them not. Indeed, we have come to you with a sign from your Lord, and peace is upon he who follows guidance.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the arrival of the messengers of God to a certain group of people, and they are instructed to deliver a message to them. The messengers are told to bring the Children of Israel with them and not to harm them. The messengers have come with a sign from their Lord, which serves as a proof of their prophethood. The verse ends with a message of peace to those who follow guidance, indicating that the messengers bring a message of peace and blessings to those who accept it and follow the right path.
orig: فأتياه فقولا إنا رسولا ربك فأرسل معنا بني إسرائيل ولا تعذبهم قد جئناك بآية من ربك والسلام على من اتبع الهدى

translation: Indeed, We have revealed to Us that the punishment is upon one who rejects and turns away.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the punishment that will befall those who reject and turn away from God's message. The use of the first person plural pronoun, "We," emphasizes the divine origin of the message. The verse serves as a warning to those who deny or ignore God's message, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: إنا قد أوحي إلينا أن العذاب على من كذب وتولى

translation: Said [one of] your Lord, O Moses.
interpretation: The verse is a continuation of a conversation between God and Moses. The speaker is identified as 'your Lord' and the addressee is Moses, who is being addressed in the plural form, possibly to include the people of Israel who are also present in the conversation. The verse emphasizes the authority of God and the reverence due to Him. The verse may also serve as a reminder of the special relationship between God and Moses, and the responsibility that comes with it.
orig: قال فمن ربكما يا موسى

translation: Said (by Himself), 'Our Lord is He who gave to each (created) thing its form and then guided (it)',
interpretation: The verse is a statement of praise and glorification of God, acknowledging His role as the creator and guide of all things. By saying 'Our Lord is He who gave to each (created) thing its form', the verse highlights God's power and ability to create and shape all things, from the smallest particles to the largest galaxies. The phrase 'then guided (it)' emphasizes God's continued involvement in the world, providing guidance and direction to all of His creation. The verse serves as a reminder of God's greatness and His role as the ultimate source of guidance and direction in life.
orig: قال ربنا الذي أعطى كل شيء خلقه ثم هدى

translation: He (Prophet Muhammad) said, 'So what about the earlier generations (who disbelieved)?'
interpretation: The verse is a continuation of the conversation between Prophet Muhammad and the disbelievers who questioned the fate of their forefathers who had passed away. The Prophet asked them about the fate of the earlier generations who had also disbelieved, implying that they too had faced the consequences of their disbelief. The verse highlights the importance of faith and righteousness and the consequences of disbelief and rejection of God's message.
orig: قال فما بال القرون الأولى

translation: Said (an angel) who had knowledge from his Lord: 'This (record of good deeds) is given to me, written down (in a book), my Lord is never unjust nor does He forget.',
interpretation: The verse speaks about an angel who has knowledge from his Lord and is given a record of good deeds. The angel states that this record is true and reliable, as it is written down in a book. The angel emphasizes the justice and infallibility of his Lord, who never does wrong and never forgets. The verse conveys the idea that every good deed is accounted for and will not be forgotten by God, and that the faithful can trust in the justice and fairness of God's judgement.
orig: قال علمها عند ربي في كتاب لا يضل ربي ولا ينسى

translation: Who made the earth a bed for you, and the sky a ceiling, and sent down water from the sky, and brought forth with it fruits as a provision for you. Therefore, do not set up rivals to God while you know (His divinity).
interpretation: The verse highlights the blessings of God, such as the earth as a bed, the sky as a ceiling, the water sent down from the sky that brings forth fruits and serves as a provision for people. The verse then commands people not to associate partners with God, emphasizing the importance of monotheism. The verse encourages people to be grateful for the blessings they received from God, and to acknowledge His oneness and greatness.
orig: الذي جعل لكم الأرض مهدا وسلك لكم فيها سبلا وأنزل من السماء ماء فأخرجنا به أزواجا من نبات شتى

translation: Eat and drink, but be not extravagant. Indeed, He does not like those who are extravagant.
interpretation: The verse reminds people to enjoy the blessings of their livestock, such as food and drink, but to avoid wasting or being extravagant. The verse emphasizes that being extravagant is not pleasing to God. The verse encourages moderation and balance in all aspects of life. It serves as a reminder that everything in this world is a blessing from God, and that we should be grateful for what we have and use it responsibly.
orig: كلوا وارعوا أنعامكم إن في ذلك لآيات لأولي النهى

translation: From it (the earth) We created you, and to it We will return you, and from it We will bring you out again.
interpretation: The verse speaks to the cyclical nature of life and death, emphasizing that all living things will return to the earth from which they came and will be brought back to life again in the future. This verse can be seen as a reminder of the power and control that God has over all of creation, as well as a reminder of the fleeting nature of life and the importance of living a righteous and virtuous life in preparation for the return to God.
orig: منها خلقناكم وفيها نعيدكم ومنها نخرجكم تارة أخرى

translation: And We have already shown him all of Our signs, but he denied them and refused.
interpretation: The verse speaks about a person who has been shown all of God's signs and evidence, but he still denied and refused to believe in them. This verse highlights the individual's rejection of the truth despite being presented with clear evidence, and emphasizes the consequences of denying God's signs. The verse serves as a reminder to be open-minded and receptive to the signs of God, and to avoid denying or ignoring them.
orig: ولقد أريناه آياتنا كلها فكذب وأبى

translation: Said
interpretation: No interpretation
orig: قال أجئتنا لتخرجنا من أرضنا بسحرك يا موسى

translation: But We will bring forth for you a magic like it, so make a date between us and you, which we will not fail to keep, nor will you, in any respect.
interpretation: The verse is a continuation of a conversation between Moses and the magicians of Pharaoh. The magicians challenge Moses to a magic contest and this verse is God's response, through Moses, accepting the challenge. The verse sets the terms of the contest, specifying a date and time for the competition and emphasizing the commitment to keep the appointment. The verse also highlights the fairness and honesty of the challenge, as both parties agree to the terms and there will be no deception or cheating. The verse ultimately serves to demonstrate the power and superiority of God's miracles over the magic of the magicians, and by extension, the false power of Pharaoh.
orig: فلنأتينك بسحر مثله فاجعل بيننا وبينك موعدا لا نخلفه نحن ولا أنت مكانا سوى

translation: He (God) said, 'The appointment for you is the Day of Adornment, and We will gather the people together.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the Day of Judgment, also known as the Day of Adornment, when all of humanity will be gathered together. This verse emphasizes the inevitability of this day and the importance of being prepared for it. It serves as a reminder that every person will be held accountable for their actions and will be judged fairly and without prejudice. It is a call for people to reflect on their lives and to strive for righteousness and justice, as these are the qualities that will be rewarded on the Day of Judgment.
orig: قال موعدكم يوم الزينة وأن يحشر الناس ضحى

translation: Then Pharaoh led his plan astray, then he gathered [his people and said],
interpretation: The verse speaks about Pharaoh's leading his people astray and gathering them to announce his plans. Pharaoh's leading his people astray refers to his deception and manipulation of his people, leading them away from the truth and towards his own selfish desires. The verse highlights Pharaoh's power and control over his people, as well as his manipulative and deceitful nature. This verse serves as a warning about the dangers of following a leader who does not have the best interests of his people at heart and instead leads them astray for his own benefit.
orig: فتولى فرعون فجمع كيده ثم أتى

translation: Moses said to them: 'Woe to you, do not tell a lie about Allah. Indeed, a penalty will touch you: those who fabricate things about Allah will fail.'
interpretation: The verse recounts Moses' warning to the Israelites not to lie about God, as doing so will result in a penalty. The verse emphasizes the seriousness of speaking falsely about God and the consequences of such actions. The verse serves as a reminder to be truthful and honest in all matters, particularly when it comes to matters of faith and religion. The verse also highlights the importance of avoiding falsehood and deception, as those who engage in such behavior are destined to fail.
orig: قال لهم موسى ويلكم لا تفتروا على الله كذبا فيسحتكم بعذاب وقد خاب من افترى

translation: They disputed among themselves in the matter and kept their talk secret.
interpretation: The verse refers to a group of people who disagreed and argued with each other about a certain matter. Instead of discussing it openly and honestly, they kept their opinions and discussions secret, suggesting that they were hiding something or were not being truthful in their dealings with each other. This verse can be seen as a warning against dishonesty, secrecy, and the dangers of hiding the truth.
orig: فتنازعوا أمرهم بينهم وأسروا النجوى

translation: They said, 'Indeed, these two are magicians who want to drive you out of your land with their magic and do away with your most cherished way.'
interpretation: The verse describes the disbelievers' accusation of Prophet Moses and his brother Aaron of being magicians who want to drive the people out of their land with their magic and destroy their way of life. The verse highlights the people's rejection and disbelief in the face of divine signs and messages, and their refusal to accept the truth even when it is presented to them in a clear and convincing manner. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of open-mindedness and humility in receiving and reflecting on divine guidance and teachings.
orig: قالوا إن هذان لساحران يريدان أن يخرجاكم من أرضكم بسحرهما ويذهبا بطريقتكم المثلى

translation: And gather your plan and then come to the summit, and today successful is the one who ascended.
interpretation: The verse speaks about a group of people who are planning something together and are then instructed to gather at a summit or high place. The verse ends by saying that the one who will be successful on this day is the one who ascended or overcame. This verse can be interpreted as a call for unity and collaboration among the believers, and it highlights the importance of striving to reach higher grounds, both physically and metaphorically. The verse can also be seen as a reference to the Day of Judgment, where the successful ones will be those who have ascended or purified themselves through their faith and good deeds.
orig: فأجمعوا كيدكم ثم ائتوا صفا وقد أفلح اليوم من استعلى

translation: They said, 'O Moses, either you throw (the staff or the stone) or we will be the first to throw (it).'
interpretation: The verse recounts an exchange between the Israelites and Moses, where the Israelites challenge Moses to throw his staff or a stone. The verse highlights the confrontational and defiant attitude of the Israelites towards Moses, who has been chosen by God as a prophet. The Israelites' challenge to Moses can be seen as a test of Moses' faith and his willingness to follow God's commands. The verse also serves as a reminder of the importance of trust and obedience to God, even in the face of adversity and opposition.
orig: قالوا يا موسى إما أن تلقي وإما أن نكون أول من ألقى

translation: It was said, 'Nay! Cast!' So when they cast, and when the mooring ropes and the stakes were torn away from them, then their hands were made to touch their idols in their worship of them.
interpretation: The verse describes a scene of people being commanded to cast their idols into the sea. When they do so, their ropes and stakes are torn away, and their hands are made to touch the idols as they try to hold on to them. This serves as a symbolic act of rejection and abandonment of their false gods. The verse emphasizes the power and control of God, who orchestrates the events to demonstrate the futility of worshipping idols and the importance of turning to the one true God.
orig: قال بل ألقوا فإذا حبالهم وعصيهم يخيل إليه من سحرهم أنها تسعى

translation: So Moses conceived a fear in himself.
interpretation: The verse describes Moses' emotional state as he receives the divine command to go to Pharaoh and demand the release of the Israelites. The phrase 'conceived a fear in himself' suggests that this fear was not a momentary or fleeting emotion, but rather a deep and abiding sense of fear and trepidation that Moses experienced as he contemplated the enormity of the task before him. This verse serves as a reminder of the human limitations and vulnerabilities, even of great prophets like Moses, and the courage and faith required to carry out God's commands, despite the fear and uncertainty that may accompany them.
orig: فأوجس في نفسه خيفة موسى

translation: We said, 'Fear not, indeed you are the uppermost.'
interpretation: The verse is a reassurance from God to the Prophet Muhammad, addressing his fear in the face of opposition and persecution. The phrase 'you are the uppermost' means that the Prophet has a higher status and position than his enemies, and that he will ultimately be victorious. The verse serves as a source of comfort and motivation for the Prophet, reminding him of his divine mission and the support he receives from God.
orig: قلنا لا تخف إنك أنت الأعلى

translation: And throw that which is in your right hand! It will swallow up that which they have crafted. What they have crafted is but the trick of a magician, and a magician will not be successful, wherever he goes.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the power of God and the weakness of those who rely on their own devices and trickery. The command to 'throw that which is in your right hand' is a metaphor for God's power and might, which will overcome and destroy the falsehoods and deceptions of those who oppose Him. The verse emphasizes that the 'trick of a magician' will ultimately be unsuccessful, no matter where they go or how cunning their deceptions may be. The verse serves as a reminder of the ultimate triumph of truth and justice over falsehood and deception, and of the futility of relying on one's own devices and trickery in the face of God's power and might.
orig: وألق ما في يمينك تلقف ما صنعوا إنما صنعوا كيد ساحر ولا يفلح الساحر حيث أتى

translation: So the sorcerers fell down in prostration. They said, 'We have believed in the Lord of Aaron and Moses.'
interpretation: The verse describes the moment when the sorcerers, who were previously trying to compete with Moses and Aaron through their magic, realize the power and truth of God. Overwhelmed by the divine signs, they fall in prostration and declare their faith in the Lord of Aaron and Moses. The verse highlights the theme of the ultimate triumph of truth and the power of faith over disbelief.
orig: فألقي السحرة سجدا قالوا آمنا برب هارون وموسى

translation: He said, 'Have you believed in him before I gave you permission? Indeed, he is your chief who has taught you magic, so I will surely cut off your hands and feet on opposite sides, and I will crucify you on the trunks of palm trees, and you will know which of us is more severe in punishment and more lasting.'
interpretation: The verse describes a conversation between an unnamed person and a group of people who have been practicing magic. The speaker accuses them of believing in someone before receiving permission, and he reveals that they have been taught magic by their 'chief'. The speaker then threatens to severely punish the group by cutting off their hands and feet, crucifying them on palm trees, and making them experience the harshest and most enduring form of punishment. The verse serves as a warning to those who practice magic and deception, emphasizing the severe consequences of such actions and the ultimate power of the speaker to inflict punishment.
orig: قال آمنتم له قبل أن آذن لكم إنه لكبيركم الذي علمكم السحر فلأقطعن أيديكم وأرجلكم من خلاف ولأصلبنكم في جذوع النخل ولتعلمن أينا أشد عذابا وأبقى

translation: They said, 'We will not believe in you or accept your guidance. We will not submit to your judgment because it is only in this world that you have any authority. You have no power to judge us in the afterlife.'
