interpretation: The verse describes the rejection of a prophet by his people, who refuse to accept his guidance and reject his authority to judge. The people deny the existence of life after death, and believe that the prophet's authority is limited to this world. The verse highlights the stubbornness and arrogance of those who reject the message of the prophet, and their refusal to submit to God's will. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of faith and submission to God's will, and the dangers of denying the truth and rejecting the guidance of the prophets.
orig: قالوا لن نؤثرك على ما جاءنا من البينات والذي فطرنا فاقض ما أنت قاض إنما تقضي هذه الحياة الدنيا

translation: Indeed, we have believed in our Lord that He may forgive us our sins and what you compelled us to [i.e., magic] from sin. And Allah is better and more enduring.
interpretation: The verse is a statement of faith by some individuals who have repented and sought forgiveness from their Lord for their sins, including their involvement in magic, which they were compelled to do. The verse emphasizes the mercy and forgiveness of Allah, who is described as better and more enduring than anything else. The verse may also serve as a reminder to those who have strayed from the right path that Allah is always ready to forgive and accept those who truly repent and seek His forgiveness.
orig: إنا آمنا بربنا ليغفر لنا خطايانا وما أكرهتنا عليه من السحر والله خير وأبقى

translation: Indeed, whoever comes to their Lord while they are a transgressor, then for them is Hell, they will neither die in it nor live.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the fate of those who meet their Lord while they have committed transgressions. The verse makes it clear that the punishment for such people is Hell, where they will neither die nor live. This implies that the punishment in Hell is eternal and that those who are sent there will suffer without end. The verse serves as a warning to those who continue to commit sins and transgressions, emphasizing the severe consequences of their actions and the importance of repentance and seeking forgiveness.
orig: إنه من يأت ربه مجرما فإن له جهنم لا يموت فيها ولا يحيى

translation: And for whoever comes to Him a believer, having done righteous deeds, for them are the highest ranks.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the reward for those who believe in God and do good deeds. These individuals will be granted the highest ranks. The verse highlights the importance of faith and good deeds, and the rewards that come with them. It serves as a source of motivation for believers to strive for righteousness and to strengthen their faith in God, as they can look forward to a high rank in the afterlife.
orig: ومن يأته مؤمنا قد عمل الصالحات فأولئك لهم الدرجات العلى

translation: Gardens of Eden, they shall enter them, thereunder rivers flow, they shall abide in them forever, that is a reward for him who has purified himself.
interpretation: The verse describes the Gardens of Eden, a place of eternal bliss and happiness, where believers will enter and live forever. The verse emphasizes the beauty and abundance of the Gardens, with rivers flowing beneath them. The verse also highlights the fact that staying in these Gardens is a reward for those who have purified themselves, that is, those who have lived a righteous and pure life. The verse serves as an incentive for believers to strive for righteousness and purity, and a promise of a reward for their efforts.
orig: جنات عدن تجري من تحتها الأنهار خالدين فيها وذلك جزاء من تزكى

translation: And We inspired Moses, 'Take My servants and strike for them a dry path in the sea, fearing neither to be overtaken [by Pharaoh] nor fearing [for yourselves].'
interpretation: The verse speaks about God inspiring Moses to lead the Israelites out of Egypt and through the sea. God commands Moses to strike the sea with his staff, causing it to split and creating a dry path for the Israelites to cross. The verse emphasizes that the Israelites should not fear being overtaken by Pharaoh's army or fear drowning in the sea. The verse serves as a reminder of God's power and ability to protect and save His people, even in seemingly impossible situations. It also highlights the trust and obedience of Moses in following God's commands, despite the challenges and dangers that lay ahead.
orig: ولقد أوحينا إلى موسى أن أسر بعبادي فاضرب لهم طريقا في البحر يبسا لا تخاف دركا ولا تخشى

translation: So Pharaoh followed them with his armies, then overtook them at the sea as it covered them.
interpretation: The verse describes the story of Pharaoh and his pursuit of the Children of Israel as they fled from Egypt. Pharaoh's armies overtook the Israelites by the sea, where they were trapped and faced certain death. However, God intervened and split the sea, allowing the Israelites to cross safely while the Pharaoh's armies were drowned. The verse emphasizes the power of God and His ability to save His people, while also highlighting the fate of those who oppress and persecute others.
orig: فأتبعهم فرعون بجنوده فغشيهم من اليم ما غشيهم

translation: And Pharaoh led his people astray and he did not guide [them]
interpretation: The verse speaks about Pharaoh leading his people astray and not guiding them. This implies that Pharaoh was not only misguided himself but also actively led his people away from the right path. The verse highlights Pharaoh's role as a corrupt and oppressive leader, who was more concerned with maintaining his own power and authority than with the well-being of his people. The verse serves as a reminder of the dangers of following corrupt leaders and the importance of seeking guidance from the right sources.
orig: وأضل فرعون قومه وما هدى

translation: O Children of Israel, We delivered you from your enemy, and We made a covenant with you on the right side of the Mount Tur, and We sent down to you manna and quails.
interpretation: The verse is addressed to the Children of Israel and speaks about God's protection and provision for them. The verse mentions that God delivered them from their enemy and made a covenant with them on the right side of the Mount Tur. Additionally, God sent down manna (a type of food) and quails for them. The verse emphasizes God's care and concern for the Israelites and His commitment to fulfilling His promises to them. The verse also serves as a reminder of God's power and ability to protect and provide for His people.
orig: يا بني إسرائيل قد أنجيناكم من عدوكم وواعدناكم جانب الطور الأيمن ونزلنا عليكم المن والسلوى

translation: Eat of the good things We have provided for you and be not ungrateful for them, but commit not an abomination on the earth as revolters.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of being grateful for the blessings that God has bestowed upon us, and of using them in a responsible and just manner. The verse warns against committing sins and transgressions, which are referred to as "abominations" and "revolting" actions. The verse reminds us that God is aware of our actions and that He is not pleased with those who commit sins. The verse encourages us to be mindful of our actions and to strive to live in accordance with God's will, in order to avoid His wrath and anger.
orig: كلوا من طيبات ما رزقناكم ولا تطغوا فيه فيحل عليكم غضبي ومن يحلل عليه غضبي فقد هوى

translation: And indeed, I am the Perpetual Forgiver of whoever repents, believes, does righteous deeds and then guides [himself] to the truth.
interpretation: The verse speaks about God's forgiveness for those who repent, believe, do righteous deeds and then follow the truth. The verse emphasizes God's willingness to forgive and His mercy towards those who make amends for their past wrongdoings, believe in Him, and strive to do good deeds. The verse serves as a message of hope for those who seek forgiveness and redemption, and encourages them to continue on the path of righteousness and guidance.
orig: وإني لغفار لمن تاب وآمن وعمل صالحا ثم اهتدى

translation: And what makes you hasten, O Moses?
interpretation: The verse is a question posed by God to Moses, urging him to be patient and not to rush in his mission. The verse emphasizes the importance of patience and trust in God's plan. The verse can be interpreted as a reminder for individuals to be mindful of their actions and to trust in the divine timing of events, rather than trying to force outcomes through their own efforts.
orig: وما أعجلك عن قومك يا موسى

translation: They said, 'Are we then to be left on our own [to perish] because of what we said, or is our return to You, [O Lord,] so that You may be pleased?'
interpretation: The verse is a dialogue between the people and God, where the people are expressing their fear and anxiety about their fate. They have realized their mistakes and are asking God if they will be left on their own because of their past actions or if they will be given a chance to return to Him so that they can please Him. The verse highlights the human tendency to seek forgiveness and redemption, even in the face of divine retribution. It also emphasizes the importance of seeking God's pleasure and approval, and the constant striving for self-improvement and moral rectitude.
orig: قال هم أولاء على أثري وعجلت إليك رب لترضى

translation: He said, 'Indeed, We will put you, [O Moses], through trials, so do not be impatient at the trial of the people, and say of them, "Surely, we are upon guidance from our Lord."'
interpretation: The verse relays a message from God to Moses, informing him that his people will be put through trials and tests. Moses is instructed not to lose patience or become frustrated with his people during these trials. Instead, he should remain steadfast and confident in the guidance they have received from God. The verse emphasizes the importance of maintaining faith and patience during difficult times, and not succumbing to frustration or despair.
orig: قال فإنا قد فتنا قومك من بعدك وأضلهم السامري

translation: Moses returned to his people, angry and grieved. He said, 'O my people, did not your Lord promise you a good promise? Was the time long for you, or did you desire that wrath from your Lord should come upon you, so you broke your promise to me?'
interpretation: The verse describes Moses' return to his people after a period of absence. He finds them in a state of disobedience and ungratefulness, despite the promises of goodness and blessings from God. Moses expresses his anger and disappointment, and questions their lack of patience and gratitude. He reminds them of God's promise and their own promise to him, and suggests that their actions may lead to God's wrath. The verse highlights the importance of patience, gratitude, and obedience, and the consequences of forgetting or breaking promises.
orig: فرجع موسى إلى قومه غضبان أسفا قال يا قوم ألم يعدكم ربكم وعدا حسنا أفطال عليكم العهد أم أردتم أن يحل عليكم غضب من ربكم فأخلفتم موعدي

translation: They said, 'We have not broken our appointment with you by our own will, but we have carried burdens from the people's ornaments, so we have thrown them away;' thus did Samiri throw.
interpretation: The verse describes the people's response to Moses when they were accused of making and worshipping the calf. They claimed that they were not responsible for breaking their appointment with Moses, but rather, they had been carrying the ornaments of the people and had thrown them away. The verse then compares their actions to that of Samiri, who had instigated the making of the calf. The verse highlights the people's attempt to shift the blame and their lack of accountability for their actions, as well as the negative consequences of their actions, as exemplified by Samiri's actions.
orig: قالوا ما أخلفنا موعدك بملكنا ولكنا حملنا أوزارا من زينة القوم فقذفناها فكذلك ألقى السامري

translation: So We brought him near as a distant object. Then, when he was near, he cried out to them, 'Do you worship that which you yourselves carve?', whereupon they denied him, so their hearts were sealed over, and they understood little.
interpretation: This verse describes the story of a man who was brought near to a group of people who worshipped idols. The man asked them if they worshipped what they themselves had carved, challenging their beliefs. However, they denied and rejected his message, and as a result, their hearts were sealed over, meaning they became stubborn and closed-minded, and they were unable to understand the truth. This verse serves as a reminder of the dangers of idol worship and the importance of being open to the truth, and it highlights the consequences of rejecting God's message.
orig: فأخرج لهم عجلا جسدا له خوار فقالوا هذا إلهكم وإله موسى فنسي

translation: Do they not see that they will not be able to ward off the decree from them, nor can they have any refuge or help?
interpretation: The verse highlights the powerlessness of humans in the face of God's decree. It emphasizes that people cannot prevent or change the fate that has been decreed for them, and that they have no control over the outcome. The verse serves as a reminder of the limits of human power and the ultimate authority of God. It encourages people to recognize and submit to God's will, and to understand that all outcomes are ultimately in His hands.
orig: أفلا يرون ألا يرجع إليهم قولا ولا يملك لهم ضرا ولا نفعا

translation: And (remember) Moses said to his people: 'O my people! Surely you have wronged yourselves by your choosing of the calf (for worship) so turn in repentance to your Creator and kill (the calf), that is better for you. Indeed, your Lord is the Most-Forgiving, the Most-Merciful.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the story of the Israelites worshipping the golden calf while Moses was receiving the commandments from God. Moses, upon his return, rebukes his people for their actions and calls them to repent and turn back to their Creator. The verse emphasizes the gravity of their sin, but also highlights the mercy and forgiveness of God, encouraging them to repent and seek forgiveness. It serves as a reminder of the importance of obedience to God's commands and the consequences of disobedience.
orig: ولقد قال لهم هارون من قبل يا قوم إنما فتنتم به وإن ربكم الرحمن فاتبعوني وأطيعوا أمري

translation: They said, 'We will not believe in you until he (Moses) comes to us.'
interpretation: The verse describes the response of some people to the message brought by a prophet or messenger. They refused to believe until Moses, a well-known and respected prophet, comes to them. This response reflects a lack of faith and trust in the prophet who is delivering the message. The verse highlights the common human tendency to seek validation from others, even when it comes to matters of faith and religion. It serves as a reminder that true belief and faith come from within and should not be contingent on external factors or validation from others.
orig: قالوا لن نبرح عليه عاكفين حتى يرجع إلينا موسى

translation: He said, 'O Aaron, what prevented you when you saw them going astray?',
interpretation: The verse is a reproach from God to Aaron, asking him why he did not intervene or prevent the Israelites from going astray when he saw them deviating from the right path. This verse emphasizes the responsibility of leaders and religious figures to guide and correct their followers when they stray from the truth. It also highlights the importance of taking action and speaking out against wrongdoing and deviation, rather than remaining silent or indifferent.
orig: قال يا هارون ما منعك إذ رأيتهم ضلوا

translation: Will you not then accept admonition, that you have transgressed my command?
interpretation: The verse is a rhetorical question addressed to the listener, urging them to heed the warning and mend their ways. The verse highlights the transgression of the listener, who has gone against the command of the speaker. The verse serves as a call to repentance, urging the listener to change their ways before it is too late.
orig: ألا تتبعن أفعصيت أمري

translation: He said, 'O son of my mother, do not cling to my beard or my hair. I fear that you will say, "You have divided the children of Israel," and you will not pay heed to my words.'
interpretation: The verse is a statement made by an unnamed person, who is addressing his mother's son. The person is cautioning the son not to touch his beard or hair, as he fears that the son will accuse him of dividing the children of Israel and not paying heed to his words. The verse highlights the speaker's concern about being misunderstood and misrepresented, and his desire to communicate effectively with the son. The verse may be interpreted as a reminder of the importance of clear communication and the need to avoid misunderstandings and misinterpretations in our interactions with others.
orig: قال يا ابن أم لا تأخذ بلحيتي ولا برأسي إني خشيت أن تقول فرقت بين بني إسرائيل ولم ترقب قولي

translation: He said, 'What has possessed you, O Samiri?'
interpretation: The verse recounts a conversation between God and the Samiri, in which God asks Samiri about the reason for his actions. The interpretation of the verse is that God is questioning Samiri about his behavior and seeking an explanation for it. This verse can be seen as a reminder of the importance of accountability and the need to be prepared to justify one's actions.
orig: قال فما خطبك يا سامري

translation: I have seen what they have not seen, so I have taken a handful (of dust) from the messenger's path and cast it (away). Thus have I relieved myself.
interpretation: The verse is a statement of the prophet Muhammad, who has been given a divine gift of seeing things that others cannot see. In response to this gift, the prophet picks up a handful of dust from the path of the messenger (which is most likely the path of the divine message) and casts it away. The act of casting away the dust can be interpreted as a symbolic act of relieving himself from the burden or responsibility of the divine message. The verse emphasizes the unique and extraordinary nature of the prophet's experience, and highlights the significance of the divine message and the responsibility that comes with it.
orig: قال بصرت بما لم يبصروا به فقبضت قبضة من أثر الرسول فنبذتها وكذلك سولت لي نفسي

translation: He said, 'Go, for you have in this life a limited time. Your appointment is fixed, you will not remain behind. Look at your god, the one you have been worshipping, we will surely burn him, then we will scatter him into the sea as dust.'
interpretation: The verse describes a conversation where the speaker is addressing someone who has been worshipping a god other than the one true God. The speaker tells the person to go away and live their life, but reminds them that their time on earth is limited and their death is inevitable. The speaker then mocks the person's god and threatens to destroy it, indicating the futility of worshipping false gods. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of worshipping the one true God, and the consequences of idolatry and false worship.
orig: قال فاذهب فإن لك في الحياة أن تقول لا مساس وإن لك موعدا لن تخلفه وانظر إلى إلهك الذي ظلت عليه عاكفا لنحرقنه ثم لننسفنه في اليم نسفا

translation: Indeed, your only God is Allah, besides whom there is no deity. He is the All-Encompassing, the All-Knowing.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the oneness of God, stating that Allah is the only deity worthy of worship. The verse further describes Allah as the 'All-Encompassing', indicating that Allah has power and control over all things, and as the 'All-Knowing', indicating that Allah has complete and perfect knowledge of all things. The verse serves as a reminder to the believers of the greatness and power of Allah, and of the importance of worshiping and serving only Him.
orig: إنما إلهكم الله الذي لا إله إلا هو وسع كل شيء علما

translation: Thus do We relate to you (Muhammad) some of the news of what has gone before; and indeed We have given you from Us a Reminder.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the revelation of some of the stories of the past to the Prophet Muhammad, and emphasizes that these stories are being revealed through divine inspiration. The phrase 'We have given you from Us a Reminder' refers to the Quran, which serves as a reminder of the stories and lessons from the past. The verse highlights the importance of the Quran as a source of guidance and wisdom for the believers, and underscores the divine origin of the revelation.
orig: كذلك نقص عليك من أنباء ما قد سبق وقد آتيناك من لدنا ذكرا

translation: But as for him who is given his record in his left hand, he will say, 'Oh, I wish I had not been given my record
interpretation: The verse speaks about the fate of those who receive their record (of deeds) in their left hand on the Day of Judgment. These individuals will regret their actions and wish they had not done what they did. The verse emphasizes the importance of good deeds and warns against the consequences of bad deeds. It reminds us that on the Day of Judgment, each person will be held accountable for their actions and will face the consequences accordingly.
orig: من أعرض عنه فإنه يحمل يوم القيامة وزرا

translation: Abiding therein, it was evil for them on the Day of Judgment, a burden.
interpretation: The verse speaks about a place or situation where people chose to stay, despite it being bad for them. On the Day of Judgment, it will be a source of burden and regret for them. The verse emphasizes the importance of making wise choices in life and the consequences of making the wrong choices. It is a reminder that the choices we make in this world will have an impact on our afterlife.
orig: خالدين فيه وساء لهم يوم القيامة حملا

translation: The Day He will inspire the Trumpet and We will gather the criminals that Day blue-eyed.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the Day of Judgment when God will sound the Trumpet and gather the sinners. The vivid imagery of the sinners being gathered with 'blue-eyed' (or 'bleary-eyed' in some translations) conveys a sense of confusion, fear, and regret. The verse emphasizes the reality of the Day of Judgment and the fate of those who have committed sins and wrongdoings. It serves as a reminder to the believers to be mindful of their actions and seek God's forgiveness, and a warning to the sinners of the impending judgment and accountability for their actions.
orig: يوم ينفخ في الصور ونحشر المجرمين يومئذ زرقا

translation: They fear for themselves; if they were to stay (away from battle) they would be punished with a painful punishment.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the fear that the hypocrites feel for themselves, as they fear the consequences of their actions. The punishment they face will be severe and painful if they do not change their ways. This verse serves as a warning to those who are hesitant or unwilling to take a stand for their beliefs and actions, reminding them of the importance of staying true to their convictions and facing the consequences with courage and determination.
orig: يتخافتون بينهم إن لبثتم إلا عشرا

translation: We know best what they say, and you (Muhammad) are not one to compel them: but remind by the Quran, him who fears My Threat.
interpretation: The verse highlights the all-knowing nature of God, who is aware of what people say and do. The verse addresses the Prophet Muhammad, reminding him that it is not his responsibility to force people to believe or follow the teachings of Islam. Instead, the Prophet is instructed to remind people of the Quran and the consequences of ignoring its teachings. The verse emphasizes the importance of da'wah (invitation) and the role of the Prophet as a reminder, rather than a compeller. The verse also highlights the significance of fearing God's punishment, encouraging people to reflect on their actions and repent.
orig: نحن أعلم بما يقولون إذ يقول أمثلهم طريقة إن لبثتم إلا يوما

translation: And they ask you about the mountains, so say: My Lord will obliterate them, obliterate them.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the mountains and how they will be obliterated or destroyed by the will of God. The repetition of the phrase 'obliterate them' emphasizes the certainty and completeness of their destruction. The verse may serve as a reminder of the power and control of God over all of creation, including the seemingly permanent and unchangeable features of the earth like mountains. It may also serve as a warning of the impermanence of the earthly life and the need to prepare for the hereafter.
orig: ويسألونك عن الجبال فقل ينسفها ربي نسفا

translation: Leaving it (the town) desolate, burst for (bursting) in it.
interpretation: The verse describes the destruction of a town that was left desolate and destroyed. The phrase 'burst for (bursting) in it' suggests a sudden and violent destruction, possibly through a natural disaster such as an earthquake or flood. The verse serves as a reminder of the power and wrath of God, and the vulnerability of human creations in the face of such events.
orig: فيذرها قاعا صفصفا

translation: You will not find in it any crookedness or curvature.
interpretation: The verse describes the straight path of God as being free from any deviation or curvature. It represents the concept of righteousness, guidance, and the right path that believers should follow. The verse can be interpreted as a reminder for Muslims to adhere to the teachings of Islam and to avoid any form of deviation from the straight path. It also highlights the importance of maintaining a righteous and just society, free from any form of crookedness or corruption.
orig: لا ترى فيها عوجا ولا أمتا

translation: That Day shall a man flee from his brother, and his mother and his father, and his wife and his children. Every man, that Day, will have enough to concern him.
interpretation: The verse describes the chaos and fear that will be present on the Day of Judgment, when people will be preoccupied with their own concerns and will not be able to help or support each other. The verse emphasizes the severity of that Day and the breakdown of family relationships, as each person will be solely focused on their own fate. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of preparing for the afterlife and seeking God's forgiveness and mercy, as it will be too late on the Day of Judgment.
orig: يومئذ يتبعون الداعي لا عوج له وخشعت الأصوات للرحمن فلا تسمع إلا همسا

translation: That day, no intercession will avail, except for (the one) to whom the Most Merciful (God) gives permission and is pleased with his word.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the Day of Judgment, when no intercession will be accepted, except for those who have received permission from the Most Merciful God and whose words are pleasing to Him. This verse emphasizes the absolute power and authority of God on the Day of Judgment and the importance of His pleasure and satisfaction. The verse serves as a reminder that ultimate salvation and acceptance on the Day of Judgment depends solely on God's mercy and grace, and that no amount of intercession or good deeds can guarantee it. It also encourages believers to strive for righteousness and seek God's pleasure in all their actions, as it is the only way to attain His mercy and forgiveness.
orig: يومئذ لا تنفع الشفاعة إلا من أذن له الرحمن ورضي له قولا

translation: He knows what is before them and what is behind them, and they cannot comprehend Him in knowledge.
interpretation: The verse affirms God's complete and perfect knowledge of all things, both what is in front of us and what is behind us. The verse emphasizes the limitations of human knowledge and comprehension, as we cannot encompass or understand God in the same way that God understands us. The verse serves as a reminder of God's omniscience and omnipotence, and encourages humility and submission to God's will and wisdom.
orig: يعلم ما بين أيديهم وما خلفهم ولا يحيطون به علما

translation: And We have already turned toward them with warnings, but My punishment is not but upon the wrongdoers.
interpretation: The verse speaks about God's warnings to the people who have committed wrongdoings and injustices. Despite these warnings, God's punishment will only be upon the wrongdoers, and not on those who have not committed any wrongs. The verse emphasizes the importance of avoiding wrongdoing and injustice, as well as the certainty of God's punishment for those who persist in committing these acts.
orig: وعنت الوجوه للحي القيوم وقد خاب من حمل ظلما

translation: And whoever does righteousness, whether male or female, while he is a believer - those will enter the Garden [of Paradise] without discomfort or despair.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the reward for those who do good deeds and believe in God. The verse emphasizes that both men and women who do good while they are believers will enter Paradise without any fear or sadness. The verse serves as a source of hope and motivation for those who strive to do good and have faith in God, assuring them of a place in Paradise. It also highlights the importance of belief and good deeds, and the promise of a positive outcome for those who follow this path.
orig: ومن يعمل من الصالحات وهو مؤمن فلا يخاف ظلما ولا هضما

translation: And thus have We sent it down as an Arabic Qur'an, and have diversified therein the warnings, in order that they may fear or it may remind them.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the Qur'an being sent down in the Arabic language and the inclusion of warnings within it. The purpose of these warnings is to either make people fear God or to remind them of the consequences of their actions. The verse highlights the importance of the Qur'an as a source of guidance and a means of instilling fear and consciousness of God in the hearts of people.
orig: وكذلك أنزلناه قرآنا عربيا وصرفنا فيه من الوعيد لعلهم يتقون أو يحدث لهم ذكرا

translation: Exalted is Allah, the King, the Truth; (there is) no deity except Him. Lord, increase me in knowledge.
interpretation: The verse begins with an exaltation of Allah as the King and the Truth, emphasizing His supremacy and power. It also reaffirms the monotheistic belief that there is no deity except Him. The verse then transitions to the speaker's prayer, asking their Lord to increase their knowledge. The verse highlights the importance of seeking knowledge, and the recognition that only Allah has the power to grant it. The verse may serve as a reminder of the importance of humility and reverence towards Allah, and the pursuit of knowledge as a means of drawing closer to Him.
orig: فتعالى الله الملك الحق ولا تعجل بالقرآن من قبل أن يقضى إليك وحيه وقل رب زدني علما

translation: And We had already given Adam beforehand knowledge; then he forgot, and We found on his part no firm resolve.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the story of Adam and his forgetfulness of the knowledge that was given to him by God. Despite this, God did not find in Adam a firm resolve or determination to uphold the knowledge and not forget it. This verse can be interpreted as a reminder of the human tendency to forget or neglect the guidance and knowledge that has been given to us, and the importance of having a firm resolve and determination to follow and uphold that guidance.
orig: ولقد عهدنا إلى آدم من قبل فنسي ولم نجد له عزما

translation: And when We said to the angels: 'Prostrate before Adam', they prostrated, except Iblis. He refused.
interpretation: The verse describes the command of God to the angels to prostrate before Adam, the first human being. All the angels obeyed, except for Iblis (also known as Satan), who refused to prostrate. The verse highlights the disobedience of Iblis, who was a jinn (a being made of smokeless fire) and was considered one of the most honored of God's creations. The verse sets the stage for the story of the fall of man and the entrance of sin and evil into the world, as well as the enmity between Iblis and humanity that continues to this day.
orig: وإذ قلنا للملائكة اسجدوا لآدم فسجدوا إلا إبليس أبى

translation: But We said, 'O Adam, indeed this is an enemy to you and to your wife. So let him not remove you both from the garden so you would be unhappy.'
interpretation: The verse describes a conversation between God and Adam, where God warns Adam about the presence of an enemy who wishes to harm him and his wife. God advises them not to follow the enemy's temptation and to remain in the garden, as leaving it would lead to unhappiness. The verse serves as a reminder that there are forces that seek to lead people astray and cause them harm, and it is important to resist such temptations and seek God's guidance and protection.
orig: فقلنا يا آدم إن هذا عدو لك ولزوجك فلا يخرجنكما من الجنة فتشقى

translation: Indeed, you will have no thirst therein nor fatigue.
interpretation: The verse describes the blessings of paradise, where the believers will not experience thirst or fatigue. The verse emphasizes the abundance and comfort of paradise, which will provide for all the needs and desires of the believers. The verse serves as a source of comfort and hope for the believers, reminding them of the rewards that await them in the afterlife and encouraging them to remain steadfast in their faith and good deeds.
orig: إن لك ألا تجوع فيها ولا تعرى

translation: And you will never feel thirsty in it, nor will you feel the heat of the sun.
interpretation: The verse describes the blessings of paradise and the comfort that the believers will experience there. Specifically, it mentions that the believers will never feel thirsty or experience the heat of the sun. This verse serves as a source of hope and motivation for the believers, reminding them of the rewards that await them in the afterlife if they remain patient and steadfast in their faith in the face of hardships and difficulties.
orig: وأنك لا تظمأ فيها ولا تضحى

translation: But Satan whispered to him, saying, 'O Adam, shall I direct you to the tree of eternity and a kingdom that will not decay?'
interpretation: The verse describes Satan's attempt to tempt Adam and Eve by offering them the forbidden tree, which promises eternal life and an unending kingdom. The verse highlights the deceptive nature of Satan and his cunning tactics to lead humans astray. The verse serves as a reminder of the dangers of following one's desires and the importance of resisting temptation, as succumbing to it can lead to negative consequences.
orig: فوسوس إليه الشيطان قال يا آدم هل أدلك على شجرة الخلد وملك لا يبلى

translation: So they both ate from it, and their private parts became apparent to them, and they began to sew on themselves leaves from the Garden, and Adam disobeyed his Lord and erred.
interpretation: The verse describes the story of Adam and Eve eating from the forbidden tree in the Garden, and the consequences that followed. After eating from the tree, their private parts became apparent to them, indicating their loss of innocence and purity. They then tried to cover themselves with leaves from the Garden. The verse also emphasizes the disobedience of Adam towards his Lord, which led to their downfall and error.
orig: فأكلا منها فبدت لهما سوآتهما وطفقا يخصفان عليهما من ورق الجنة وعصى آدم ربه فغوى

translation: Then his Lord chose him and inclined toward him and guided him.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the selection and guidance of a person by their Lord. The verse emphasizes the favor and mercy of the Lord in choosing and guiding the person, indicating that the person's success and right path are due to the Lord's guidance and support. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of seeking and following the guidance of the Lord, and the blessings that come with it.
orig: ثم اجتباه ربه فتاب عليه وهدى

translation: He said: 'Descend from it, all of you. Some of you are enemies to others.' Then, if guidance comes to you from Me, then whoever follows My guidance will neither go astray nor suffer misery.
interpretation: The verse speaks about a group of people who are descending from a place, possibly after a conflict or division among them. They are told that they are enemies to each other and that guidance will come from God. Those who follow this guidance will not go astray or suffer misery. The verse highlights the importance of guidance and the consequences of following or ignoring it. It suggests that the guidance is a way to avoid conflicts, misguidance and suffering. It also implies that the consequences of ignoring the guidance can lead to negative outcomes such as going astray or suffering.
orig: قال اهبطا منها جميعا بعضكم لبعض عدو فإما يأتينكم مني هدى فمن اتبع هداي فلا يضل ولا يشقى

translation: But whoever turns away from My remembrance, indeed, for him is a painful punishment. And We will gather him on the Day of Resurrection, blind.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the punishment for those who turn away from remembering God. The punishment is described as painful and the person who turns away will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection blind, indicating a state of ignorance and being lost. The verse emphasizes the importance of remembering God and the severe consequences of neglecting it.
orig: ومن أعرض عن ذكري فإن له معيشة ضنكا ونحشره يوم القيامة أعمى

translation: He said, 'My Lord, why have you raised me blind while I used to see?'
interpretation: The verse is a conversation between a person and God, where the person is questioning why they have been raised blind after having previously been able to see. The verse highlights the individual's confusion and frustration at the sudden change in their circumstances. The verse can be interpreted as a reminder of the fragility of human abilities and the limitations of human understanding. It may also serve as a call for patience and trust in God's plan, even when faced with seemingly inexplicable events.
orig: قال رب لم حشرتني أعمى وقد كنت بصيرا

translation: He said, 'Thus have Our signs come unto you, and you have denied them, and thus today you forget (the truth)'.
interpretation: The verse is a condemnation of the person who has repeatedly rejected the signs of God and is now in a state of forgetfulness and denial. The repetition of the word 'thus' emphasizes the continuity of the person's disbelief and their rejection of God's signs. The verse suggests that the person's denial is a result of their own actions, and that their forgetfulness is a consequence of their rejection of the truth. The verse serves as a warning to those who deny the signs of God and emphasizes the importance of recognizing and accepting the truth.
orig: قال كذلك أتتك آياتنا فنسيتها وكذلك اليوم تنسى

translation: And thus do We recompense he who is excessive, and does not believe in the signs of his Lord. And surely, the punishment of the Hereafter is more severe and more lasting.
interpretation: The verse explains that those who are excessive or transgress in their actions, and do not believe in the signs or revelations of their Lord, will be punished. The punishment in the Hereafter is described as being more severe and more lasting, emphasizing the seriousness of the consequences of disbelief and transgression. The verse serves as a warning to those who ignore or reject the signs of God, reminding them of the severe consequences of their actions in the afterlife.
orig: وكذلك نجزي من أسرف ولم يؤمن بآيات ربه ولعذاب الآخرة أشد وأبقى

translation: Have We not guided them with a clear path? Indeed, We have destroyed many towns before them who walked in their homes. There is indeed in that a lesson for those of understanding.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the guidance provided by God to past civilizations through a clear path, yet they were destroyed despite that. The verse highlights that many civilizations before them were destroyed, despite walking in their homes, indicating that they were complacent and failed to heed the signs. The verse serves as a reminder for those who are willing to understand and take heed, that destruction is the consequence of not following the clear path set by God.
orig: أفلم يهد لهم كم أهلكنا قبلهم من القرون يمشون في مساكنهم إن في ذلك لآيات لأولي النهى

translation: And but for a word that preceded from your Lord, it would have been upon them the punishment complete.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the mercy of God in delaying the punishment of a disbelieving people. The 'word' that preceded from God is likely a reference to His previous promises to send a messenger or reveal a scripture. The verse highlights the severity of the punishment that would have befallen them if not for God's mercy and patience. It serves as a reminder of God's power and justice, and the inevitability of His punishment for those who reject His signs and persist in disbelief.
orig: ولولا كلمة سبقت من ربك لكان لزاما وأجل مسمى

translation: So be patient over what they say and exalt your Lord before the rising of the sun and before its setting and during some of the night [exalt Him] and at the ends of the day, that you may be satisfied.
interpretation: The verse encourages the believers to be patient in the face of adversity and to exalt and praise God at different times of the day. By praising God at the specified times, the believers can find contentment and satisfaction. The verse also emphasizes the importance of maintaining a consistent connection with God throughout the day, whether it be during the early morning, the night, or at the end of the day. This consistent worship and remembrance of God can bring peace and fulfillment to the believer's heart, and it is a means of attaining God's pleasure and approval.
orig: فاصبر على ما يقولون وسبح بحمد ربك قبل طلوع الشمس وقبل غروبها ومن آناء الليل فسبح وأطراف النهار لعلك ترضى

translation: And let not your eye be turned by them in desire towards the kinds of the life of the world that We have given them as adornment, that We may thus try them thereby; and your Lord's provision is better and more enduring.
interpretation: The verse warns against being distracted by the worldly possessions and adornments of others, which are merely temporary and transient. These things are used by God as a test for people, to see how they respond to such temptations. The verse reassures the reader that the provision and sustenance from one's Lord is superior and more lasting than any worldly possessions. The overall message of the verse is to keep one's focus on the eternal and spiritual, rather than being consumed by the material and fleeting aspects of life.
orig: ولا تمدن عينيك إلى ما متعنا به أزواجا منهم زهرة الحياة الدنيا لنفتنهم فيه ورزق ربك خير وأبقى

translation: And command your people to prayer, and be constant therein. We ask not you for provision: We provide for you. And the (good) end is for (those) of right character.
interpretation: The verse is a command from God to the Prophet Muhammad to establish and maintain prayer within his community. The verse emphasizes the importance of prayer and the responsibility of the Prophet in leading and encouraging his people to practice it consistently. The verse also clarifies that the responsibility of providing for the community lies with God, not the Prophet. Lastly, the verse highlights the significance of righteousness and moral character in determining one's ultimate outcome.
orig: وأمر أهلك بالصلاة واصطبر عليها لا نسألك رزقا نحن نرزقك والعاقبة للتقوى

translation: And they said, 'Why has no sign been sent down to him from his Lord? Indeed, not within the former scriptures is there any mention of you.'
interpretation: The verse describes the disbelievers' demand for a sign from God as proof of the prophethood of the Prophet Muhammad. They question why no sign has been sent down to him from his Lord, implying that they do not believe in his message. The second part of the verse highlights their lack of knowledge about the Prophet Muhammad in the previous scriptures, suggesting that they are not familiar with the prophecies about him. The verse conveys the disbelievers' rejection and denial of the Prophet Muhammad's message and their refusal to accept him as a prophet without explicit proof.
orig: وقالوا لولا يأتينا بآية من ربه أولم تأتهم بينة ما في الصحف الأولى

translation: And if We had destroyed them with a punishment before this, they would surely have said: 'Our Lord! Why didst thou not send unto us a messenger? We should then have followed the messengers' guidance before we were humbled and disgraced.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the regret of people who were destroyed by God's punishment. They express their wish that they had been sent a messenger to guide them before they were humiliated and disgraced. The verse highlights the importance of guidance and the consequences of ignoring it. It teaches that people often only turn to God and his messengers when they are faced with hardship and suffering, but it is too late by then. The verse serves as a reminder to people to heed the guidance of God and his messengers while they still have the chance.
orig: ولو أنا أهلكناهم بعذاب من قبله لقالوا ربنا لولا أرسلت إلينا رسولا فنتبع آياتك من قبل أن نذل ونخزى

translation: Say, 'Wait, I too am waiting.' Then you will know who are the companions of the straight path, and who is guided.
interpretation: The verse is a command to the Prophet Muhammad to tell his people to wait, as he too is waiting, and that through this waiting, they will come to know who are the followers of the straight path (the righteous believers) and who is truly guided (by God). The verse emphasizes the importance of patience and the ultimate revelation of truth through waiting and perseverance.
orig: قل كل متربص فتربصوا فستعلمون من أصحاب الصراط السوي ومن اهتدى

translation: The reckoning (i.e. Day of Judgment) for the people has drawn near, while they are in a state of heedlessness, turning away.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the imminent arrival of the Day of Judgment, when all human beings will be held accountable for their actions. However, the verse also highlights the fact that many people are oblivious to this reality and continue to live in a state of heedlessness, turning away from the truth. The verse serves as a warning to those who are not mindful of the significance of the Day of Judgment, urging them to prepare for it by leading a righteous life and seeking God's forgiveness.
orig: اقترب للناس حسابهم وهم في غفلة معرضون

translation: And nothing comes to them of a reminder from their Lord (as a warning) but they turn away from it, while they are playing.
interpretation: The verse highlights the rejection and disregard of the people towards the reminders and warnings from their Lord. Despite the revelation of divine messages, they remain heedless and continue to engage in frivolous activities. This verse may serve as a critique of human behavior, emphasizing the importance of paying heed to divine guidance and engaging in serious reflection, rather than being consumed by worldly distractions.
orig: ما يأتيهم من ذكر من ربهم محدث إلا استمعوه وهم يلعبون

translation: No indeed! Rather, their hearts are ignorant. And they commit evil deeds, then they sell that evil for a paltry price. Woe to those who sell themselves! Do they not know that they will have to stand before their Lord, and that He will inform them of what they have done?
interpretation: The verse criticizes those who commit unjust deeds and then sell them for a small, temporary gain. The verse emphasizes the ignorance of these people, who do not understand the true consequences of their actions. The phrase 'woe to those who sell themselves' implies that these people are harming themselves and their souls by committing such deeds. The verse reminds the reader that all people will have to stand before their Lord and be held accountable for their actions, and that God knows all that they have done.
orig: لاهية قلوبهم وأسروا النجوى الذين ظلموا هل هذا إلا بشر مثلكم أفتأتون السحر وأنتم تبصرون

translation: He said, 'My Lord, knows the word in the heaven and the earth, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.'
interpretation: The verse is a statement of a believer, acknowledging the omniscience and all-hearing of God. The believer recognizes that God has knowledge of everything that is said in the heavens and on earth, and that He is all-hearing and all-knowing. This statement is an expression of the believer's faith in the power and knowledge of God, and their submission to His will.
orig: قال ربي يعلم القول في السماء والأرض وهو السميع العليم

translation: Nay, they say: 'Tales of the ancients, which he has written down, and they are dictated to him morning and evening.' Say: 'The (Qur'an) was sent down by Him who knows the secret (that is) in the heavens and the earth. Verily, He is ever Gracious, All-Knowing.'
interpretation: The verse is a response to the disbelievers who accused the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) of fabricating the Qur'an. They claimed that he was merely repeating old stories and that he had a teacher who dictated the verses to him in the morning and evening. The verse rejects these claims and affirms that the Qur'an was revealed by the All-Knowing, All-Gracious God, who has knowledge of all that is hidden in the heavens and the earth. The verse serves as a reminder that the Qur'an is a revelation from the Divine, and that it is not possible for any human being to produce anything similar to it.
orig: بل قالوا أضغاث أحلام بل افتراه بل هو شاعر فليأتنا بآية كما أرسل الأولون

translation: Have they not considered how We destroyed before them the towns of people who cried lies [to Our messages], and they will never return to them?
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of previous towns whose people rejected God's messages. The verse emphasizes the finality of the destruction, as the people will never be able to return to their former homes. This is a warning to those who reject God's message, reminding them of the consequences of their disbelief and urging them to reflect on the fate of those who came before them.
orig: ما آمنت قبلهم من قرية أهلكناها أفهم يؤمنون

translation: And We sent not before you (O Muhammad) but men to whom We inspired, so ask the people of the Reminder if you do not know.
interpretation: The verse refers to the Prophets who were sent before Prophet Muhammad, and that they were inspired by God. The verse encourages the listeners to seek knowledge from the people who have knowledge of the scriptures and the teachings of the previous Prophets. The verse highlights the importance of seeking knowledge and learning from the past, and the role of the Prophets as messengers of God who brought guidance to their people.
orig: وما أرسلنا قبلك إلا رجالا نوحي إليهم فاسألوا أهل الذكر إن كنتم لا تعلمون

translation: And We did not make them (into) bodies not eating food, nor were they to be immortal.
interpretation: The verse refers to the disbelievers who rejected the message of the prophets and denied the truth. The verse emphasizes that these disbelievers will not be given physical bodies in the afterlife, nor will they be granted eternal life. Instead, they will face the consequences of their disbelief and rejection of the truth. The verse serves as a reminder of the impermanence of this worldly life and the importance of believing in and following the truth.
orig: وما جعلناهم جسدا لا يأكلون الطعام وما كانوا خالدين

translation: Then We fulfilled our promise to them, and We saved those who were conscious of God. But We destroyed the transgressors.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the fulfillment of God's promise to punish the unjust and save the righteous. The verse highlights the importance of being conscious of God and the consequences of transgression. The righteous were saved, while the transgressors were destroyed. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of righteousness and the consequences of transgression, emphasizing that God always fulfills His promises.
orig: ثم صدقناهم الوعد فأنجيناهم ومن نشاء وأهلكنا المسرفين

translation: We have sent down to you the Book with truth, confirming what was before it, and surely, a witness over you. Therefore, will you not use your reason?
interpretation: The verse addresses the believers and reminds them that they have been sent a Book (the Qur'an) with truth, which confirms the previous revelations. The verse also emphasizes that the Qur'an serves as a witness over the believers, holding them accountable for their actions. The verse then questions the believers' use of reason, urging them to reflect and ponder upon the message of the Qur'an. The verse encourages the believers to use their intellect and understanding to recognize the truth and significance of the revelation they have received.
orig: لقد أنزلنا إليكم كتابا فيه ذكركم أفلا تعقلون

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, and after it We raised up another people.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and were replaced by new communities. This verse emphasizes the cyclical nature of divine justice, where unjust communities are destroyed and replaced by new ones, giving them a chance to learn from the mistakes of the past. It serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the inevitability of divine justice.
orig: وكم قصمنا من قرية كانت ظالمة وأنشأنا بعدها قوما آخرين

translation: And when they sensed Our punishment, behold, they were fleeing from it.
interpretation: The verse describes the reaction of people when they experienced the punishment of God. Despite being part of the community or town that was being punished, the people tried to flee or escape from the punishment when they realized what was happening. The verse highlights the severity of the punishment and the fear it instills in those who experience it. It also serves as a reminder that no one can escape or avoid the consequences of their actions, especially when it comes to the punishment of God.
orig: فلما أحسوا بأسنا إذا هم منها يركضون

translation: Do not run away from death, but return to whatever you have been given (i.e. your deeds), and make your homes a place of reflection. Perhaps you will understand.
interpretation: The verse advises against running away from death and instead encourages introspection and reflection on one's deeds. The verse urges the listener to return to their deeds and make their homes a place of contemplation and understanding. The verse suggests that through this reflection, one may gain a deeper understanding of their actions and their consequences. The verse may also serve as a reminder that death is inevitable and that it is important to prepare for it by living a righteous life.
orig: لا تركضوا وارجعوا إلى ما أترفتم فيه ومساكنكم لعلكم تسألون

translation: They said, 'Woe to us! We were indeed wrongdoers.'
interpretation: The verse shows the regret and remorse of people who recognize the error of their ways and the just consequences of their actions. It serves as a reminder that it is never too late to acknowledge one's mistakes, seek forgiveness, and strive to do better. At the same time, it highlights the importance of taking responsibility for one's actions and not waiting until it is too late to make amends.
orig: قالوا يا ويلنا إنا كنا ظالمين

translation: But their messengers came to them with clear proofs. But they said: 'Show us Allah (God) manifestly.' So they denied (the messengers) and consequently Allah (God) seized them with punishment. Indeed, He is Strong, Severe in retribution.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the disbelievers who rejected the messengers and their message, despite the clear proofs and evidence presented to them. They demanded to see Allah (God) manifestly, a demand that is not possible or reasonable, as Allah is not limited by physical form. As a result of their denial and rejection, Allah punished them. The verse emphasizes the power and severity of Allah's retribution, and serves as a warning to those who reject the message of Allah's messengers and deny the truth.
orig: فما زالت تلك دعواهم حتى جعلناهم حصيدا خامدين

translation: And We did not create the heavens and the earth and what is between them as a game.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance and seriousness of the creation of the heavens, the earth, and everything in between (which can be interpreted as all of the universe or all of existence) by stating that it was not created as a game or a meaningless pastime. This serves as a reminder that everything in existence has a purpose and meaning, and that it is all part of a larger plan and design. It also emphasizes the power and ability of the Creator, who is capable of creating such a vast and complex universe. The verse can also be seen as a warning against frivolity and taking things lightly, especially when it comes to matters related to God and religion.
orig: وما خلقنا السماء والأرض وما بينهما لاعبين

translation: And if We had willed to take a pastime, We would have taken it from Us, if We were to do so.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes God's power and sovereignty, stating that if God had wanted to create something for mere amusement, He would have done so without any need for external help. The verse serves as a reminder of God's self-sufficiency and the futility of attempting to limit or control God's actions based on human understanding or desires.
orig: لو أردنا أن نتخذ لهوا لاتخذناه من لدنا إن كنا فاعلين

translation: Nay, We hurl the truth against falsehood, so it destroys it, and lo! it (falsehood) vanishes. And woe to you for what you ascribe (to Us)!
interpretation: The verse asserts the power of truth over falsehood, stating that truth will inevitably prevail over falsehood and cause it to disappear. The verse serves as a warning to those who ascribe falsehoods to God, emphasizing the severe consequences of their actions. The verse highlights the importance of truth and the dangers of falsehood, reminding believers to uphold the truth at all times.
orig: بل نقذف بالحق على الباطل فيدمغه فإذا هو زاهق ولكم الويل مما تصفون

translation: And to Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth, and to Him belongs [all] matters. And He is over all things competent.
interpretation: The verse affirms the oneness of God, emphasizing His ownership and control over all things in the heavens and the earth. The verse also highlights God's power and ability, as He is competent over all matters. The verse serves as a reminder of the greatness and majesty of God, and the need for humans to submit to His will and worship Him alone.
orig: وله من في السماوات والأرض ومن عنده لا يستكبرون عن عبادته ولا يستحسرون

translation: They glorify [Allah] in the night and the day, and they never falter.
interpretation: The verse highlights the constant and uninterrupted glorification of Allah by certain beings, who do so both during the night and the day without ever failing or making a mistake. While the verse does not specify who these beings are, it is generally understood to refer to the angels. The verse emphasizes the perfection and consistency of the angels' worship, and serves as a reminder of the importance of maintaining one's devotion and commitment to Allah at all times.
orig: يسبحون الليل والنهار لا يفترون

translation: Or have they taken gods from the earth who can raise (the dead)?
interpretation: The verse questions the worship of false deities by asking if those who worship them believe that these deities have the power to resurrect the dead. The verse challenges the believers in these false gods and highlights the futility of their worship. The verse implies that the only true deity worthy of worship is the one who has the power to give life and take it away, a power that no false god can possess.
orig: أم اتخذوا آلهة من الأرض هم ينشرون

translation: If there had been within the towns any gods besides Allah, they both would have been ruined. So exalted is Allah, Lord of the Throne, above what they attribute.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the uniqueness and supremacy of Allah as the only deity worthy of worship. It suggests that if there were other gods in the towns, they would have caused destruction. The verse highlights the absurdity of associating partners with Allah and the blasphemy of attributing divine qualities to other than Him. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of monotheism and the ultimate power and authority of Allah as the Lord of the Throne.
orig: لو كان فيهما آلهة إلا الله لفسدتا فسبحان الله رب العرش عما يصفون

translation: He (God) cannot be questioned as to what He does, while they will be questioned.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the power and sovereignty of God, who is not accountable to anyone for His actions. In contrast, human beings are accountable for their actions and will be questioned on the Day of Judgment. The verse serves as a reminder of the fundamental difference between the Creator and the created, and the need for humans to humble themselves before God and submit to His will.
orig: لا يسأل عما يفعل وهم يسألون

translation: Or have they taken gods besides Him? Say, 'Bring your proof; this is the reminder of my Lord and a reminder before me.' Most of them do not know the truth; so they are disposed (to unbelief).'
interpretation: The verse addresses the unbelievers who worship other gods besides Allah and challenges them to present their proof or evidence for their belief. The speaker, most likely the Prophet Muhammad, asserts that the Quran is a reminder from his Lord and a confirmation of previous revelations. The verse suggests that most people do not know the truth and are therefore disposed to unbelief. The verse emphasizes the importance of providing evidence and the futility of worshiping false gods. It serves as a call to the unbelievers to reflect on the truth of Islam and to abandon their false beliefs.
orig: أم اتخذوا من دونه آلهة قل هاتوا برهانكم هذا ذكر من معي وذكر من قبلي بل أكثرهم لا يعلمون الحق فهم معرضون

translation: And We sent not before you any messenger except that We revealed to him that, 'There is no deity but Me, so worship Me.'
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the oneness of God and the importance of worshipping only Him. It states that all previous messengers, including the prophet Muhammad, received the same revelation from God, commanding them to worship only one God. The verse serves as a reminder of the fundamental principle of monotheism in Islam and the unity of all prophets in their mission to guide people towards the worship of the one true God.
orig: وما أرسلنا من قبلك من رسول إلا نوحي إليه أنه لا إله إلا أنا فاعبدون

translation: And they say: 'The Merciful has taken [for Himself] a son.' Exalted is He! Rather, they are [merely] honored servants.
interpretation: The verse addresses the disbelievers who claim that Allah (the Most Merciful) has taken a son. The verse categorically rejects this false belief and affirms that Allah is exalted and above such a thing. Instead, the verse explains that the angels, described as honored servants, are not Allah's children but rather His creation, carrying out His will and commands.
orig: وقالوا اتخذ الرحمن ولدا سبحانه بل عباد مكرمون

translation: They cannot precede Him in speech and they act by His command.
interpretation: The verse highlights the supremacy and power of God, stating that His creations cannot precede Him in speech and that they can only act according to His command. This emphasizes the subordination of all beings to God, and the belief that nothing can happen without God's will. The verse serves as a reminder of the greatness of God, and the limited power of humans, who can only act within the boundaries set by God.
orig: لا يسبقونه بالقول وهم بأمره يعملون

translation: He knows what is before them and what is behind them, and they cannot comprehend Him in knowledge. And (He) tries/tests/examines them through/by/with what is in their hands, and He has full power over them, though they perceive it not.
interpretation: The verse speaks about God's omniscience and His ability to test and try humanity through the means that are in their hands. The verse emphasizes that God knows what is before and behind humanity, indicating that He has complete knowledge of their actions and intentions. The verse also highlights that God has full power over humanity, and that they cannot comprehend Him in knowledge. The verse serves as a reminder of God's omnipotence, omniscience and His ability to test humanity through the means that are in their hands, and that they will be held accountable for their actions.
orig: يعلم ما بين أيديهم وما خلفهم ولا يشفعون إلا لمن ارتضى وهم من خشيته مشفقون

translation: And whoever of them says, 'Indeed, I am a god besides Him' - so for him is Hell. We will be to him as he was to his religion.
interpretation: The verse warns of the consequence of claiming to be a god or a deity besides Allah. The punishment for such a claim is Hell. The second part of the verse emphasizes the fitting nature of the punishment, stating that Allah will treat the person as they treated their own religion. The verse serves as a reminder of the oneness of Allah and the severe consequences of shirk (associating partners with Allah). It also highlights the principle of accountability, that a person will be recompensed for their actions in a way that is consistent with what they have done.
orig: ومن يقل منهم إني إله من دونه فذلك نجزيه جهنم كذلك نجزي الظالمين

translation: Have those who disbelieved not seen that the heavens and the earth were a closed-up form and We opened them out? And We have made from water every living thing. So they are denying what they are being reminded of.
interpretation: The verse highlights the power and greatness of God by reminding the disbelievers of the creation of the heavens and the earth. The verse emphasizes that the heavens and the earth were once closed-up and God opened them out, and made every living thing from water. The verse is a reminder to the disbelievers of the signs of God's existence and power, yet they deny and ignore these signs. The verse serves as a call to the disbelievers to reflect on the wonders of creation and to recognize and accept the power and greatness of God.
orig: أولم ير الذين كفروا أن السماوات والأرض كانتا رتقا ففتقناهما وجعلنا من الماء كل شيء حي أفلا يؤمنون

translation: And We have made in the earth firm mountains, lest it shake with them, and We have made in it broad roads that they may be guided.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the creation of firm mountains on earth to prevent it from shaking and causing destruction. Additionally, broad roads have been created to guide people. The verse highlights the mercy and consideration of God for His creations, providing them with stability and guidance. It also emphasizes the importance of guidance and the role it plays in helping people navigate their way through life.
orig: وجعلنا في الأرض رواسي أن تميد بهم وجعلنا فيها فجاجا سبلا لعلهم يهتدون

translation: And We made the sky a protected ceiling, but they are turned away from its signs.
interpretation: The verse highlights the protection and care that God has provided for humanity by making the sky a 'protected ceiling' or a source of shelter and nourishment. However, despite this provision, people are 'turned away' or distracted from recognizing and appreciating the signs of God's power and wisdom in the natural world. The verse serves as a reminder to be mindful of the blessings that we receive from God and to be grateful for them by acknowledging and reflecting on the signs of His existence and greatness around us.
orig: وجعلنا السماء سقفا محفوظا وهم عن آياتها معرضون

translation: And He it is who created the night and the day, and the sun and the moon, each in an orbit floating.
interpretation: The verse highlights the power and greatness of God as the creator of the universe. The creation of the night and day, and the movement of the sun and the moon in their orbits, serve as a reminder of the intricate design and order of the universe. The verse emphasizes that everything in the universe, including the celestial bodies, are in a constant state of motion and are obedient to God's laws. The verse serves as a reminder of God's power and control over all aspects of life and the universe, and encourages believers to reflect on the wonders of creation and to praise and worship God.
orig: وهو الذي خلق الليل والنهار والشمس والقمر كل في فلك يسبحون

translation: And We never sent a messenger before you but We revealed to him, saying, 'There is no deity but Me, so worship Me.'
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the central message of all prophets, which is the oneness of God and the importance of worshipping Him alone. The verse stresses that this message has been consistently conveyed by all prophets, including the prophet Muhammad, and that it is a fundamental principle of Islamic belief. The verse serves as a reminder of the continuity and consistency of the prophetic message, and the importance of maintaining a strong faith in the oneness of God.
orig: وما جعلنا لبشر من قبلك الخلد أفإن مت فهم الخالدون

translation: Every soul will taste death. And We test you with evil and with good by way of trial. And to Us you will be returned.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the inevitability of death and the tests that people face in life, both good and bad. These tests are a way for people to be tried and evaluated. Ultimately, all people will return to God and be held accountable for their actions in life.
orig: كل نفس ذائقة الموت ونبلوكم بالشر والخير فتنة وإلينا ترجعون

translation: And when those who disbelieved see you, they only take you as a joke. 'Is this the one who mentions your gods?' And they are disbelievers, disregarding the remembrance of the Most Merciful.
interpretation: The verse describes the attitude of the disbelievers towards the Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) and his message. They see him as a laughing stock and do not take him seriously. They mock him for mentioning their gods and reject the notion of the One God, the Most Merciful. The verse highlights the rejection of the truth by the disbelievers and their denial of the message of the Prophet Muhammad (pbuh). It serves as a reminder of the challenges faced by the Prophet (pbuh) and the importance of staying steadfast in the face of rejection and mockery.
orig: وإذا رآك الذين كفروا إن يتخذونك إلا هزوا أهذا الذي يذكر آلهتكم وهم بذكر الرحمن هم كافرون

translation: I created man in haste, and I will most certainly show you My signs; so do not rush Me.
interpretation: The verse speaks about God's creation of man and His promise to show His signs to humanity. The verse highlights God's power and sovereignty, and reminds people that they should not rush or try to hasten God's plans. The verse encourages patience and trust in God's wisdom and timing, and reminds people that God's signs and revelations will be shown to them in due time.
orig: خلق الإنسان من عجل سأريكم آياتي فلا تستعجلون

translation: And they say, 'When will this promise be (fulfilled), if you are truthful?'
interpretation: The verse is spoken by the disbelievers who are questioning the promise of God and the truth of the prophet's message. They are expressing their disbelief and challenging the prophet to prove his claim. The verse highlights the skepticism and denial of the disbelievers towards the message of the prophet and serves as a reminder of the importance of faith and belief in God's promises.
orig: ويقولون متى هذا الوعد إن كنتم صادقين

translation: If only those who disbelieved knew, when the hours are stretched out for them, the Fire will touch them on their faces, and they will not be able to turn away nor will they be given respite.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the fate of the disbelievers on the Day of Judgment. It emphasizes the inevitability of their punishment, which will be in the form of a fire that will touch their faces and cause great suffering. The verse highlights the fact that they will not be able to escape or avoid the punishment and that they will not be given any respite. The verse serves as a warning to those who reject the message of Islam and a reminder of the severe consequences of their disbelief.
orig: لو يعلم الذين كفروا حين لا يكفون عن وجوههم النار ولا عن ظهورهم ولا هم ينصرون

translation: But it seizes them suddenly, and they are overwhelmed. So they are unable to repel it, nor are they given respite.
interpretation: The verse describes the sudden and overwhelming nature of divine punishment. The use of the word 'seizes' implies that the punishment is unavoidable and catches people off guard. The phrase 'overwhelmed' suggests that the punishment is too powerful for them to resist. The inability to 'repel it' and the lack of 'respite' emphasizes the finality and severity of the punishment. The verse serves as a warning to those who ignore the signs of divine wrath and continue to commit sins, reminding them of the imminent and unavoidable consequences of their actions.
orig: بل تأتيهم بغتة فتبهتهم فلا يستطيعون ردها ولا هم ينظرون

translation: And indeed, they ridiculed the Messengers before you, but the punishment seized those who were disdainful.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the past disbelievers who ridiculed and scoffed at the Messengers sent by God. The verse highlights the consequence of their actions, as the punishment came upon those who were arrogant and disdainful. The verse serves as a reminder that mocking and rejecting the Messengers and their message will not be without consequence, and that those who follow this path will face the same fate as the past disbelievers.
orig: ولقد استهزئ برسل من قبلك فحاق بالذين سخروا منهم ما كانوا به يستهزئون

translation: Say, 'Who provides for you from the sky and the earth? Or who controls the hearing and the sight? And who brings out the living from the dead and brings out the dead from the living? And who directs the matter?' They will say, 'Allah.' Then say, 'Will you not then fear Him?'
interpretation: The verse is a challenge to the disbelievers to reflect on the signs of God's power and mercy around them, such as the provision of food and the control of the senses. The verse asks who provides for them from the sky and the earth, who controls the hearing and the sight, who brings out the living from the dead and brings out the dead from the living, and who directs the matter. The expected answer to all these questions is "Allah". After acknowledging that Allah is the one who has all these powers, the verse asks if they will not then fear Him. The verse encourages the believers to call the disbelievers to reflect on the signs of God's power and mercy, and to remind them of the importance of fearing and worshiping Allah.
orig: قل من يكلؤكم بالليل والنهار من الرحمن بل هم عن ذكر ربهم معرضون

translation: Or have they gods that can protect them from Us? They cannot help themselves, nor can they protect [others] from Us.
interpretation: The verse questions the belief of those who worship false gods and believe that these gods can protect them from the punishment of the one true God. The verse emphasizes the powerlessness of these false gods, stating that they cannot help or protect their followers. The verse serves as a reminder that only the one true God has the power to protect and help, and that those who worship false gods are ultimately powerless and without support.
orig: أم لهم آلهة تمنعهم من دوننا لا يستطيعون نصر أنفسهم ولا هم منا يصحبون

translation: But these (people) and their forefathers were enjoying themselves in their insolence and arrogance, until there came upon them Our commandment - from which they were not availing themselves. Do the disbelievers not see that We are destroying the land (by) reducing it from its borders? So will they not understand?
interpretation: The verse criticizes the people and their ancestors for their arrogance and insolence, and their failure to heed the signs of God. The verse specifically mentions the destruction of the land, which is being reduced from its borders, as a consequence of their actions. The verse serves as a warning to those who deny God and continue to engage in unjust and sinful behavior, emphasizing that they cannot escape the consequences of their actions and that God's command will ultimately come upon them.
orig: بل متعنا هؤلاء وآباءهم حتى طال عليهم العمر أفلا يرون أنا نأتي الأرض ننقصها من أطرافها أفهم الغالبون

translation: Say, 'I only warn you by revelation.' But the deaf do not hear the call when they are warned.
interpretation: The verse addresses the Prophet Muhammad, instructing him to warn the disbelievers of the impending Day of Judgment. The warning is described as being conveyed by revelation, indicating that it is a divine message from Allah. However, the verse highlights the stubbornness and heedlessness of the disbelievers, who are likened to the deaf. Despite the warning, they do not heed the call to guidance, symbolizing their rejection of the truth and their inability to comprehend the significance of the message.
orig: قل إنما أنذركم بالوحي ولا يسمع الصم الدعاء إذا ما ينذرون

translation: And if a breath of your Lord's punishment touches them, they will surely say, 'Woe to us; indeed, we were unjust.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the regret and remorse of people who have been punished by God. The phrase 'a breath of your Lord's punishment' suggests that the punishment is severe and overwhelming. The people, upon experiencing it, immediately acknowledge their wrongdoing and express their regret by saying 'woe to us; indeed, we were unjust.' This verse highlights the importance of repentance and turning back to God before it is too late. It also serves as a reminder that the consequences of sin and injustice are inevitable and can come suddenly.
orig: ولئن مستهم نفحة من عذاب ربك ليقولن يا ويلنا إنا كنا ظالمين

translation: And We will set up a just balance on the Day of Resurrection, so that no soul will be treated unjustly at all, and even if it is the weight of a grain of mustard seed, We will bring it to account; and We are sufficient as Reckoners.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the establishment of a just balance on the Day of Judgment, where no soul will be treated unjustly. The verse emphasizes the extreme precision of this balance, where even the weight of a mustard seed will not be overlooked. The verse also highlights God's role as the ultimate reckoner, indicating that every action, no matter how small, will be accounted for and judged. The verse serves as a reminder of the fairness and justice of God, and the certainty of the Day of Judgment, where every person will be held accountable for their actions.
orig: ونضع الموازين القسط ليوم القيامة فلا تظلم نفس شيئا وإن كان مثقال حبة من خردل أتينا بها وكفى بنا حاسبين

translation: And We certainly gave Moses and Aaron the criterion and a shining light and a reminder for the righteous.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the blessings and guidance that God bestowed upon Moses and Aaron. The 'criterion' refers to the ability to distinguish between right and wrong, while the 'shining light' symbolizes the guidance that they received from God. The 'reminder for the righteous' suggests that the guidance was meant to be a source of inspiration and a call to action for those who are righteous. The verse can be seen as a reminder that God provides guidance and support to those who seek to live a righteous life.
orig: ولقد آتينا موسى وهارون الفرقان وضياء وذكرا للمتقين

translation: Those who fear their Lord in secret and who are reverent of the Hour.
