The verse encourages contemplation and reflection, inviting the reader to deepen their understanding of the world around them and the role of God in it.
orig: وهو الذي يحيي ويميت وله اختلاف الليل والنهار أفلا تعقلون

translation: Nay, they say the like of what the former ones said.
interpretation: The verse refers to the disbelievers who rejected the message of the prophet and compared them to the previous nations who also rejected their prophets. The verse implies that the disbelievers are repeating the same mistakes and following the same path of their predecessors, who were destroyed as a result of their disbelief and rejection of the truth.
orig: بل قالوا مثل ما قال الأولون

translation: They will say, 'What, when we have become bones and dust, shall we then indeed be raised up (to be judged)?'
interpretation: The verse is a dialogue between the disbelievers and God on the Day of Judgment. The disbelievers question the possibility of their resurrection after they have turned into bones and dust. The verse highlights the disbelievers' disbelief and denial of the resurrection and the Day of Judgment, despite the clear signs and evidence presented to them. The verse serves as a reminder to the believers of the reality of the resurrection and the importance of preparing for it by doing good deeds and avoiding sins.
orig: قالوا أإذا متنا وكنا ترابا وعظاما أإنا لمبعوثون

translation: Indeed, we and our forefathers have been promised this - that it is but the tales of the ancients.
interpretation: The verse is a response to the disbelievers who rejected the message of the Prophet Muhammad. The verse states that both the disbelievers and their ancestors had been warned of the consequences of their disbelief. However, they dismissed the warnings as mere stories or legends, showing their disregard for the message and their stubbornness in their disbelief. The verse highlights the importance of heeding the warnings and lessons from the past, and not dismissing them as mere tales or superstitions.
orig: لقد وعدنا نحن وآباؤنا هذا من قبل إن هذا إلا أساطير الأولين

translation: Say, 'Who provides for you from the sky and the earth? Or who controls the hearing and the sight? And who brings out the living from the dead and brings out the dead from the living?'
interpretation: The verse is a challenge to the disbelievers, asking them who provides for them from the sky and the earth, who controls their senses, and who has power over life and death. The verse emphasizes the power and control of the divine being and encourages the disbelievers to reflect on this power and control, and to recognize the existence of the divine being. The verse serves as a reminder that all provisions come from the divine being, and encourages the believers to be grateful and thankful for these provisions.
orig: قل لمن الأرض ومن فيها إن كنتم تعلمون

translation: They will say to Allah, 'So were you not able to guide us?'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the Day of Judgment, when people will be held accountable for their actions and will be questioned by Allah. The people will ask Allah why He did not guide them and prevent them from committing sins. The verse emphasizes the power and knowledge of Allah, who has the ability to guide and direct His creation, but allowed these people to make their own choices. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of seeking guidance and following the right path, and the consequences of ignoring the signs and guidance from Allah.
orig: سيقولون لله قل أفلا تذكرون

translation: Say, 'Who is the Lord of the seven heavens and the Lord of the Great Throne?'
interpretation: This verse is a challenge from the Qur'an to the disbelievers, asking them to reflect on the power and authority of the one true God. The 'seven heavens' refer to the seven levels or layers of the heavens, and the 'Great Throne' refers to God's throne, symbolizing His sovereignty and control over all of creation. The verse is a call for the disbelievers to recognize and submit to the power and authority of God, and to acknowledge His role as the Lord and Creator of all things.
orig: قل من رب السماوات السبع ورب العرش العظيم

translation: They will say to God, 'So why did You not guide us?'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the regret and remorse of the people who did not follow God's guidance and are now facing the consequences of their actions. The people ask God why they were not guided, expressing their realization of the importance of God's guidance and their own failure to follow it. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of seeking and following God's guidance and the consequences of ignoring it.
orig: سيقولون لله قل أفلا تتقون

translation: Say, 'Who is it that controls the sovereignty of everything' - and He is the One who protects (all), while none can protect against Him - if you truly know?
interpretation: The verse is a challenge to the disbelievers to consider who has control over everything and who is the ultimate protector. The verse emphasizes that it is only God who has power and control over all things and that no one can protect themselves from Him. The verse is a reminder of God's power and greatness and serves as a call for the disbelievers to reflect on their beliefs and actions, encouraging them to recognize and submit to God's sovereignty.
orig: قل من بيده ملكوت كل شيء وهو يجير ولا يجار عليه إن كنتم تعلمون

translation: They will say to Allah, 'What is [your] excuse?' so say, 'By my Lord, you are ones who are constantly deviating.',
interpretation: The verse speaks about the Day of Judgment when people will be held accountable for their actions and will question God about the fairness of His judgment. In response to their questioning, God will remind them of their own deviation and transgression, indicating that they were the ones who strayed from the right path and committed injustices, and thus, they are responsible for their own fate.
orig: سيقولون لله قل فأنى تسحرون

translation: But indeed, we came to them with truth, and indeed, they are liars.
interpretation: The verse speaks about a situation where the truth (represented by 'we') was presented to a group of people, but they rejected it and continued to lie. The verse emphasizes the certainty of the truth and the falsehood of the people's claims. The verse may serve as a reminder that truth and falsehood are clear and distinct, and that ultimately, truth will prevail over falsehood.
orig: بل أتيناهم بالحق وإنهم لكاذبون

translation: Allah has not taken any son, nor is there any god along Him. (If there had been), each god would have surely taken away what he created, and some of them would have risen up over others in dominance. Exalted is Allah above what they describe!
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the oneness of God and denies the existence of any partners or children for Him. It highlights the absurdity of the claim that there could be other gods, as each god would have taken away what he created and there would have been competition and dominance among them. The verse stresses the greatness and exaltation of Allah, who is above any imperfections or attributes that people may ascribe to Him.
orig: ما اتخذ الله من ولد وما كان معه من إله إذا لذهب كل إله بما خلق ولعلا بعضهم على بعض سبحان الله عما يصفون

translation: He is the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, so He is exalted above what they associate [with Him].
interpretation: The verse affirms that Allah has knowledge of all that is unseen and all that is witnessed, and therefore, He is above and beyond any partners or equals that people may associate with Him. The verse emphasizes Allah's greatness and uniqueness and serves as a reminder that He is the only one deserving of worship and reverence.
orig: عالم الغيب والشهادة فتعالى عما يشركون

translation: Say, 'My Lord, if You should show me (the punishment) that they are promised,'
interpretation: The verse is a continuation of a conversation between the Prophet Muhammad and his Lord. The Prophet is asking his Lord to show him the punishment that the disbelievers have been promised. The verse emphasizes the Prophet's desire for guidance and his eagerness to see the consequences of disbelief. It also shows the Prophet's submission to his Lord's will and his acceptance of whatever may come his way.
orig: قل رب إما تريني ما يوعدون

translation: My Lord, do not leave me among the wrongdoing people.
interpretation: The speaker is making a fervent plea to God, asking to be saved from the company of the unjust and wrongdoing people. The verse conveys a strong sense of desperation and the desire to be separated from those who engage in unrighteous deeds. It can be seen as a prayer for guidance and protection from negative influences and a reminder of the importance of surrounding oneself with good and righteous people.
orig: رب فلا تجعلني في القوم الظالمين

translation: And We are able to replace them with better than them; indeed, We are their Patron.
interpretation: The verse speaks about God's power and ability to replace the disbelievers with a better people. The verse emphasizes that God is in control and has the power to replace those who reject His message with a better and more deserving people. The verse also implies that God is the true Patron and protector of the believers, and that they should have faith and trust in Him.
orig: وإنا على أن نريك ما نعدهم لقادرون

translation: Repel [the evil] with that which is better. We are most knowing of what they describe.
interpretation: The verse advises believers to respond to harm or evil with something better and more virtuous. This is a powerful way to neutralize the negative effects of the harm and to elevate oneself above the situation. The verse also emphasizes that God has full knowledge of the situation and the actions of the people involved. This is a reminder that God is aware of the believers' efforts to respond with patience and goodness, and that they will be rewarded for their actions.
orig: ادفع بالتي هي أحسن السيئة نحن أعلم بما يصفون

translation: And say, 'O my Lord, I seek refuge in You from the incitements of the devils.'
interpretation: The verse is a supplication to God, seeking refuge from the whispers and temptations of the devils. The verse emphasizes the importance of seeking protection from the negative influences of the devils, which can lead to misguidance and sin. The verse reminds the believers to seek God's help and guidance in order to stay on the right path and avoid falling into the traps of the devils.
orig: وقل رب أعوذ بك من همزات الشياطين

translation: And I seek refuge in You, my Lord, lest they come near.
interpretation: The verse is a supplication to God, seeking His protection and refuge from the approach of those who intend harm or evil. The speaker expresses their vulnerability and fear, and turns to God for help and safety. The verse can be seen as a reminder of the importance of seeking God's protection in times of danger or difficulty, and the power of prayer to bring comfort and peace in the face of adversity.
orig: وأعوذ بك رب أن يحضرون

translation: Until, when death comes to one of them, he says, 'My Lord, send me back,'
interpretation: The verse describes the regret of a person who has died and realizes the consequences of their actions in this world. The person asks to be sent back to life to correct their mistakes and do good deeds, but it is too late. The verse emphasizes the importance of taking advantage of the present life to prepare for the afterlife and do good deeds, as there will be no second chance after death.
orig: حتى إذا جاء أحدهم الموت قال رب ارجعون

translation: Perhaps I will do righteousness in what I have left, (it is) but a word (i.e. the saying 'subhanAllah' - Glory be to Allah), and behind them is a barrier until the Day they are resurrected.
interpretation: The verse speaks about a person expressing their hope to do righteous deeds before they die. However, they acknowledge that their statement of glorifying Allah ('subhanAllah') is just a word, and it alone is not enough. The verse highlights the reality of death and the existence of a barrier (or a screen) that separates the living from the dead until the Day of Resurrection. The verse emphasizes the importance of striving for righteousness and not relying solely on empty words or expressions, and serves as a reminder of the inevitability of death and the Day of Judgment.
orig: لعلي أعمل صالحا فيما تركت كلا إنها كلمة هو قائلها ومن ورائهم برزخ إلى يوم يبعثون

translation: But when We blow the Trumpet, there will be no family connections among them on that Day, nor will they ask about one another.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the Day of Judgment and the blowing of the Trumpet, which signals the end of the world. The verse emphasizes the destruction of all family connections and relationships, indicating that everyone will be preoccupied with their own fate. The verse also highlights that people will not be able to ask about the well-being of their loved ones, emphasizing the severity and isolation of the Day of Judgment. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of preparing for the afterlife and the transient nature of worldly relationships.
orig: فإذا نفخ في الصور فلا أنساب بينهم يومئذ ولا يتساءلون

translation: And whoever's scales are heavy [with good deeds], those are the successful.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the ultimate success and reward in the hereafter for those who have done good deeds in their lives. The 'scales' mentioned in the verse refer to the weighing of good and bad deeds on the Day of Judgment. Those whose scales are heavy with good deeds will be considered successful and will be granted entry into heaven. The verse encourages believers to strive for good deeds and righteousness in their lives, as it will ultimately lead to success and happiness in the hereafter.
orig: فمن ثقلت موازينه فأولئك هم المفلحون

translation: And whoever is afraid of the meeting with his maker, then indeed, those are the losers who have lost their souls in Hell forever.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the fate of those who fear the Day of Judgment and the meeting with their Creator. The verse makes a clear distinction between those who fear this meeting and those who do not. Those who fear it are considered the losers because they have lost their souls by their disbelief and wrongdoing. This verse serves as a warning to those who are not mindful of the Day of Judgment and the consequences of their actions. It emphasizes the importance of having a strong faith and leading a righteous life.
orig: ومن خفت موازينه فأولئك الذين خسروا أنفسهم في جهنم خالدون

translation: Their faces will be burned by fire, while they are in it, like fried locusts.
interpretation: The verse describes the fate of the unbelievers on the Day of Judgment. They will be punished by being burned in fire, and their faces will be particularly affected. The comparison of their faces to fried locusts highlights the severity of their punishment and the horror of their situation. The verse emphasizes the painful and unbearable nature of the torment of hell and serves as a warning to those who reject the message of Islam and persist in their disbelief.
orig: تلفح وجوههم النار وهم فيها كالحون

translation: Have not My signs been recited to you, yet you used to deny them?
interpretation: The verse is a reminder to the people who have been presented with the signs of God, yet they chose to deny and disbelieve in them. The phrase 'My signs' refers to the evidence and proofs of God's existence and power, which are manifested in the natural world, in prophets and their messages, and in the moral and spiritual laws that govern the universe. The verse highlights the importance of recognizing and accepting the truth, and the consequences of rejecting it. It serves as a warning to those who persist in their disbelief and denial, urging them to reflect on the signs of God and to turn to Him in repentance and submission.
orig: ألم تكن آياتي تتلى عليكم فكنتم بها تكذبون

translation: They said, 'Our Lord, the punishment we have incurred has overwhelmed us, and we have strayed in our ways.'
interpretation: The verse shows the remorse and regret of a group of people who recognize that they have been overwhelmed by the punishment they received as a result of their sins and wrongdoings. They acknowledge their mistakes and admit that they had strayed from the right path. This verse can serve as a reminder to people to reflect on their actions and behaviors, and to seek guidance and forgiveness from God before it is too late.
orig: قالوا ربنا غلبت علينا شقوتنا وكنا قوما ضالين

translation: Our Lord, take us out of it, if we return, then indeed we will be unjust.
interpretation: The verse is a plea from the people to God to take them out of a situation or place that they are in, most likely referring to a state of disbelief or sin. They acknowledge that if they are allowed to return to this state, they will inevitably become unjust and continue in their sinful ways. The verse highlights the power of God to remove individuals from harmful situations and the responsibility of the people to recognize and turn away from their own wrongdoing.
orig: ربنا أخرجنا منها فإن عدنا فإنا ظالمون

translation: He said, 'Enter it [the city] and do not speak to anyone.'
interpretation: The verse relates a command given by a figure of authority for individuals to enter a city, but with the instruction not to speak to anyone. The command to remain silent could indicate a desire for secrecy or caution. The verse can be interpreted as emphasizing the importance of obedience and discretion in certain situations. It may also suggest that the speaker has a specific purpose or plan in mind, and that speaking to others could compromise or hinder that plan.
orig: قال اخسئوا فيها ولا تكلمون

translation: Indeed, a group of My servants said, 'Our Lord, we have believed, so forgive us and have mercy on us, and You are the best of the merciful.'
interpretation: The verse highlights the prayer and plea of a group of believers who have turned to God seeking forgiveness and mercy. The verse emphasizes the humility and submissiveness of the believers, who acknowledge their sins and shortcomings and seek God's forgiveness and mercy. The verse also highlights the compassionate and merciful nature of God, who is described as the best of the merciful. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of seeking God's forgiveness and mercy and the boundless compassion and mercy that God has for His servants.
orig: إنه كان فريق من عبادي يقولون ربنا آمنا فاغفر لنا وارحمنا وأنت خير الراحمين

translation: And you took them for amusement only until you forgot My reminder and you were among them, laughing.
interpretation: The verse speaks about people who became so engrossed in their amusements and entertainment that they forgot the signs and reminders of God. The verse emphasizes the forgetfulness and heedlessness of these people, who were once part of the same community but became so absorbed in their own pleasures that they forgot the importance of remembering God. The verse serves as a warning against becoming too consumed by worldly distractions, and neglecting the remembrance of God.
orig: فاتخذتموهم سخريا حتى أنسوكم ذكري وكنتم منهم تضحكون

translation: Indeed, I will give them today the reward for their patience; indeed, they are the ones who will be successful.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the reward that will be given to a group of people for their patience. The verse emphasizes that the reward will be given 'today', indicating that the wait is over and the reward is imminent. The verse also highlights that the people who will receive the reward are 'the ones who will be successful', indicating that their patience and perseverance has led them to success. The verse serves as a reminder that patience and perseverance will be rewarded and that success will come to those who are patient and steadfast.
orig: إني جزيتهم اليوم بما صبروا أنهم هم الفائزون

translation: He said, 'How many years have you remained in the earth?'
interpretation: The verse is a conversation between God and a group of people, where God asks them how long they had been living on earth. The verse emphasizes the power and knowledge of God, who is aware of the time that has passed and the actions of his creations. The verse may serve as a reminder of the fleeting nature of life and the importance of using time wisely, living a righteous life, and preparing for the hereafter.
orig: قال كم لبثتم في الأرض عدد سنين

translation: They say, 'We have stayed only a day or part of a day.' Ask the people of remembrance.
interpretation: The verse refers to a group of people who are denying the passage of time and claiming that they have only stayed for a short period, when in reality, they have been staying for a much longer time. The instruction to 'ask the people of remembrance' suggests that there are others who have a better understanding of time and can confirm that the denying group has indeed stayed for a long period. This verse may serve as a reminder to be truthful and honest in our dealings with others and not to deny or distort the truth for our own benefit.
orig: قالوا لبثنا يوما أو بعض يوم فاسأل العادين

translation: He (God) said, 'If you had remained patient just a little longer, you would have seen (the destruction of your enemies).'
interpretation: The verse is a statement made by God, addressing a group of people who were in a state of impatience and anxiety. The verse implies that the people were awaiting a specific outcome or event, but their impatience caused them to miss out on witnessing the fulfillment of their desires. The verse serves as a reminder to be patient and trust in God's plan, as the outcome may be better than what was initially expected.
orig: قال إن لبثتم إلا قليلا لو أنكم كنتم تعلمون

translation: Do you think that We created you uselessly, and that you will not return to Us?
interpretation: The verse challenges the reader's belief in the purpose of their existence and the inevitability of their return to God. The first part of the verse questions whether humanity was created without purpose, and the second part emphasizes that all of humanity will return to God. The verse encourages the reader to reflect on the purpose of their existence and the significance of their actions, and to recognize that they will ultimately be held accountable for them. The verse also serves as a reminder of the power and wisdom of God, who created humanity for a reason and will call them to account for their lives.
orig: أفحسبتم أنما خلقناكم عبثا وأنكم إلينا لا ترجعون

translation: Exalted is Allah, the King, the Truth; there is no deity except Him, the Lord of the Noble Throne.
interpretation: The verse is a declaration of the greatness and power of Allah, the only deity worthy of worship. It emphasizes Allah's sovereignty, truth, and unique divinity. The phrase 'Lord of the Noble Throne' highlights Allah's majesty and supremacy. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of recognizing and submitting to Allah's authority, and the importance of worshiping only Him.
orig: فتعالى الله الملك الحق لا إله إلا هو رب العرش الكريم

translation: And whoever assigns partners to Allah, for him Allah has forbidden paradise. His refuge is the fire, and there will be no helpers for the unjust.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the punishment for those who associate partners with Allah. These people are forbidden from entering paradise and their fate is the fire. The verse emphasizes the severity of this sin and the dire consequences that result from it. The verse serves as a warning to those who commit shirk (associating partners with Allah) and a reminder that they will not receive any help from others in the face of God's punishment.
orig: ومن يدع مع الله إلها آخر لا برهان له به فإنما حسابه عند ربه إنه لا يفلح الكافرون

translation: And say, 'O my Lord, forgive and have mercy, for You are the best of the merciful.'
interpretation: The verse is a supplication to God, asking for forgiveness and mercy. It emphasizes God's attribute of being the most merciful, which is a reminder of His infinite compassion and forgiveness towards His creation. The verse encourages the believer to seek God's forgiveness and mercy, and to recognize that God is the ultimate source of compassion and forgiveness. It serves as a reminder to the believer to seek God's mercy and forgiveness, and to trust in His boundless compassion and kindness.
orig: وقل رب اغفر وارحم وأنت خير الراحمين

translation: We have sent it down and made it obligatory and We have detailed in it the warnings so that you may take heed.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the sending down of God's message and making it obligatory for people to follow. It also mentions the inclusion of clear warnings and signs in the message as a reminder for people to take heed and reflect upon. The verse emphasizes the importance of the message and the significance of the warnings, encouraging people to be mindful of their actions and to follow the message in order to avoid any negative consequences.
orig: سورة أنزلناها وفرضناها وأنزلنا فيها آيات بينات لعلكم تذكرون

translation: The fornicatress and the fornicator, flog each of them with a hundred stripes. And let not pity for the two of them detain you from obedience to Allah, if you believe in Allah and the Last Day. And let a party of the believers witness their punishment.
interpretation: The verse outlines the punishment for fornication (zina) in Islamic law, which is 100 lashes for both the man and the woman. The verse emphasizes the importance of upholding the law and not letting pity or compassion for the guilty parties prevent the implementation of the punishment. The verse also highlights the role of the community in witnessing the punishment, serving as a deterrent for others and reinforcing the seriousness of the offense. The verse ultimately emphasizes the importance of obedience to Allah and the belief in the Day of Judgment, where the guilty parties will be held accountable for their actions.
orig: الزانية والزاني فاجلدوا كل واحد منهما مائة جلدة ولا تأخذكم بهما رأفة في دين الله إن كنتم تؤمنون بالله واليوم الآخر وليشهد عذابهما طائفة من المؤمنين

translation: The fornicator does not marry except a fornicatress or idolatress, and the fornicatress does not marry except a fornicator or idolater, and that has been prohibited to the believers.
interpretation: The verse highlights the negative consequences of immoral behavior and emphasizes the importance of maintaining moral standards in society. It states that a fornicator can only marry a fornicatress or an idolatress, and a fornicatress can only marry a fornicator or an idolater, indicating the social isolation and marginalization that results from such actions. The verse also prohibits these marriages for believers, reinforcing the idea that such behavior is incompatible with the moral and ethical values of the Islamic faith. The verse serves as a warning against immoral behavior and emphasizes the importance of maintaining moral standards in order to uphold the cohesion and integrity of the community.
orig: الزاني لا ينكح إلا زانية أو مشركة والزانية لا ينكحها إلا زان أو مشرك وحرم ذلك على المؤمنين

translation: And those who accuse chaste women, then do not bring four witnesses, flog them with eighty lashes, and never accept their testimony ever again. And those are the transgressors.
interpretation: The verse outlines the punishment for those who make false accusations against chaste women, without providing four witnesses. The punishment for this crime is eighty lashes and their testimony will no longer be accepted. This verse emphasizes the importance of providing evidence and the severity of making false accusations. It serves as a deterrent for those who would falsely accuse others and highlights the importance of fairness and justice in society.
orig: والذين يرمون المحصنات ثم لم يأتوا بأربعة شهداء فاجلدوهم ثمانين جلدة ولا تقبلوا لهم شهادة أبدا وأولئك هم الفاسقون

translation: Except for those who repent after that and make amends, for surely Allah is All-forgiving, All-compassionate.
interpretation: The verse offers a way out for those who have committed injustices but then repent and make amends. This shows the mercy and compassion of God towards those who recognize their mistakes and strive to correct them. The verse serves as a reminder that it is never too late to turn back to God and seek forgiveness, as long as one is willing to sincerely repent and make amends for their wrongdoings.
orig: إلا الذين تابوا من بعد ذلك وأصلحوا فإن الله غفور رحيم

translation: And those who accuse their wives [of adultery] and have no witnesses except themselves - then the witness of each one of them is four testimonies, sworn by Allah, that indeed he is of the truthful.
interpretation: This verse outlines the process for dealing with accusations of adultery in the absence of witnesses, a situation that could potentially lead to false accusations. The verse requires the accuser to provide four testimonies, sworn by God, attesting to the truth of their accusation. This high standard of proof serves to protect the accused from false accusations and uphold the sanctity of marriage. The verse emphasizes the seriousness of the accusation and the need for truthfulness and integrity in the face of such a serious matter.
orig: والذين يرمون أزواجهم ولم يكن لهم شهداء إلا أنفسهم فشهادة أحدهم أربع شهادات بالله إنه لمن الصادقين

translation: And the fifth (oath is that): that the curse of Allah be upon him if he is one of the liars.
interpretation: The verse is part of a series of oaths sworn by the speaker, who calls upon various forces of nature as witnesses to the truth of his words. The fifth oath is that if the speaker is lying, then the curse of Allah will be upon him. This oath serves to emphasize the truthfulness of the speaker's words and to warn those who would falsely deny or contradict them. The verse can be seen as a reminder of the importance of honesty and the serious consequences of lying and deception.
orig: والخامسة أن لعنت الله عليه إن كان من الكاذبين

translation: And let four witnesses from among you be brought [as evidence] against them [if they accuse chaste women]. And if they do not testify, then they are indeed liars before Allah.
interpretation: This verse speaks about the requirement of having four witnesses to testify against someone who accuses a chaste woman of adultery. If the accusers are unable to produce four witnesses, then their accusation is considered a lie. This verse emphasizes the importance of evidence and the seriousness of making false accusations. It also serves as a protection for the innocent and as a deterrent against false accusations.
orig: ويدرأ عنها العذاب أن تشهد أربع شهادات بالله إنه لمن الكاذبين

translation: But
interpretation: No interpretation
orig: والخامسة أن غضب الله عليها إن كان من الصادقين

translation: And if it were not for the grace of God upon you and His mercy, and because God is All-Forgiving, All-Wise.
interpretation: The verse highlights the importance of God's grace, mercy, and forgiveness in protecting and guiding human beings. The verse emphasizes that it is only through God's mercy that people are able to avoid negative consequences and receive guidance. The phrase 'All-Forgiving, All-Wise' further emphasizes God's compassion and wisdom, suggesting that even when people make mistakes or commit wrongdoing, they can still turn to God for forgiveness and guidance. The verse serves as a reminder to be grateful for God's blessings and to seek His forgiveness and guidance in all aspects of life.
orig: ولولا فضل الله عليكم ورحمته وأن الله تواب حكيم

translation: Indeed, those who came with falsehood are a group among you. Do not consider them as an advantage to you, rather it is a disaster for you. For every man among them, there is what he has earned of sin, and as for he who has exceeded the limit against them, for him is a painful punishment.
interpretation: The verse speaks about those who bring falsehood and warns against considering them as an advantage. Instead, they are described as a disaster for the community. Each person who has participated in the falsehood will bear the burden of their own sin. Furthermore, those who have taken a leading role in spreading the falsehood will face a severe punishment. This verse serves as a warning against participating in or supporting falsehood and emphasizes individual accountability for one's actions.
orig: إن الذين جاءوا بالإفك عصبة منكم لا تحسبوه شرا لكم بل هو خير لكم لكل امرئ منهم ما اكتسب من الإثم والذي تولى كبره منهم له عذاب عظيم

translation: If the believers, men and women, had observed the Contact Prayer (Salat) when it was first prescribed for them, and had established regular prayer (Salat) and had given regular charity (Zakat), their community would have avoided decadence.
interpretation: The verse highlights the importance of three fundamental practices in Islam, namely Salat (Contact Prayer), establishing regular prayer, and giving regular charity. It emphasizes that if the believers, both men and women, had consistently practiced these obligations since they were first prescribed, their community would have been protected from moral decay and decadence. The verse serves as a reminder of the significance of these practices in preserving the moral and spiritual well-being of the Muslim community, and the consequences of neglecting them.
orig: لولا إذ سمعتموه ظن المؤمنون والمؤمنات بأنفسهم خيرا وقالوا هذا إفك مبين

translation: Had they brought four witnesses for it, then indeed, they would have been among the liars in the sight of Allah.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the requirement of evidence and witnesses in cases of accusation and the severity of the consequences for those who make false accusations without evidence. The verse implies that if the accusers had brought four witnesses for their claim, but they did not, then they would be considered liars in the sight of God. This emphasizes the importance of truthfulness and justice, and the seriousness of making false accusations. It serves as a warning to those who make false claims and do not bring sufficient evidence, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's judgment.
orig: لولا جاءوا عليه بأربعة شهداء فإذ لم يأتوا بالشهداء فأولئك عند الله هم الكاذبون

translation: And if it were not for the grace of God upon you and His mercy in the world and the hereafter, He would have made you taste a great punishment for what you have committed.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the grace and mercy of God towards people, preventing them from experiencing the full consequences of their sins. The verse emphasizes that the punishment for the wrong actions committed by people would have been severe, if not for God's mercy. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of gratitude and appreciation for God's blessings, and the need to strive for righteousness and avoid sin in order to receive His continued mercy and grace.
orig: ولولا فضل الله عليكم ورحمته في الدنيا والآخرة لمسكم في ما أفضتم فيه عذاب عظيم

translation: When it is thrown to them, they hear it, but they reject it in a proud manner. And when they are reminded of the message of their Lord, they turn away from it in aversion.
interpretation: The verse describes the behavior of those who reject the message of their Lord. When the message is presented to them, they hear it, but instead of accepting it, they reject it arrogantly. Even when they are reminded of the message, they turn away from it in aversion, showing no interest or willingness to consider it. The verse highlights the stubbornness and pride of those who reject the truth and the consequences of their actions.
orig: إذ تلقونه بألسنتكم وتقولون بأفواهكم ما ليس لكم به علم وتحسبونه هينا وهو عند الله عظيم

translation: And if you had been patient and righteous, surely, their attack would have been broken off from you. And We would have given you a powerful conquest.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the consequences of patience and righteousness in the face of adversity. It suggests that if the believers had remained patient and adhered to righteousness, their enemies would have been defeated, and they would have been granted a powerful victory. The verse encourages believers to remain steadfast in their faith and to adhere to righteousness, even in the face of adversity, as doing so will ultimately lead to success and triumph.
orig: ولولا إذ سمعتموه قلتم ما يكون لنا أن نتكلم بهذا سبحانك هذا بهتان عظيم

translation: Allah warns you (all) that you should not return to (the) like (of) it ever, if you are believers.
interpretation: The verse is a warning from Allah to the believers not to return to the state or actions of the people who were destroyed, as mentioned in the previous verses. This warning emphasizes the importance of learning from the past and avoiding the mistakes of those who were punished. By not returning to the same state, it implies the need for repentance and a change in behavior. The verse serves as a reminder to the believers to remain steadfast on the right path and not to be swayed by temptation or ignorance. It also highlights the significance of faith in shaping one's actions and avoiding the consequences of disobedience.
orig: يعظكم الله أن تعودوا لمثله أبدا إن كنتم مؤمنين

translation: And Allah will make clear to you the signs, and Allah is Knowing and Wise.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes Allah's role as the revealer of truth and understanding. The 'signs' refer to the evidence and proofs of Allah's existence and power, which will be made clear to the people. The verse reminds the believers that Allah is all-knowing and wise, and that everything happens according to His plan and purpose.
orig: ويبين الله لكم الآيات والله عليم حكيم

translation: Indeed, those who love that scandal/immorality should be spread among those who believed, for them is a painful punishment in this world and the hereafter. And Allah knows, while you do not know.
interpretation: The verse warns those who take pleasure in spreading scandal and immorality among the believers. These people will face a painful punishment both in this world and in the afterlife. The verse emphasizes the all-knowing nature of Allah, contrasting it with the limited knowledge of humans.
orig: إن الذين يحبون أن تشيع الفاحشة في الذين آمنوا لهم عذاب أليم في الدنيا والآخرة والله يعلم وأنتم لا تعلمون

translation: And if it were not for Allah's favor upon you and His mercy, and that Allah is Kind and Merciful.
interpretation: The verse highlights the importance of God's favor and mercy in the lives of people. It emphasizes that without God's kindness and mercy, people would be in a state of hardship and distress. The verse serves as a reminder to be grateful for the blessings that one has and to recognize that it is only through God's grace that these blessings have been bestowed. It also encourages people to be kind and merciful to one another, as they have received kindness and mercy from God.
orig: ولولا فضل الله عليكم ورحمته وأن الله رءوف رحيم

translation: O you who have believed, do not follow the footsteps of Satan. Indeed, he is to you a clear enemy. And he commands you to evil and immorality and that you worship others besides Allah. But as for you, you worship none but Allah. Indeed, He is the Hearing, the Knowing. Allah keeps you, from whom He wills, free of disease, and Allah is the Hearing, the Knowing. And if it were not for the favor of Allah upon you and His mercy, not one of you would have ever been pure, but Allah purifies whom He wills, and Allah is Hearing and Knowing.
interpretation: The verse warns the believers against following Satan, who is their clear enemy. Satan commands people to commit sins, immoral acts, and to worship other than God. The believers, on the other hand, are commanded to worship only God, who is all-hearing and all-knowing. The verse highlights the importance of God's grace and mercy in purifying the believers, as no one can attain purity without it. The verse serves as a reminder to the believers to stay away from Satan's temptations and to remain steadfast in their faith and worship of God.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تتبعوا خطوات الشيطان ومن يتبع خطوات الشيطان فإنه يأمر بالفحشاء والمنكر ولولا فضل الله عليكم ورحمته ما زكى منكم من أحد أبدا ولكن الله يزكي من يشاء والله سميع عليم

translation: And it is not for the possessors of grace among you to withhold the expenditure from the descendants and the poor and the emigrants in the path of Allah, and (that) you desire a (momentary) increase, and (that) you become arrogant so that you do not become equal. And give (them) and seek forgiveness from Allah. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving, Merciful.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of giving and helping those in need, including relatives, the poor, and those who have been displaced in the path of Allah. It warns against withholding this help out of arrogance or a desire for temporary gain. Instead, the verse encourages giving and seeking forgiveness from Allah. The verse highlights the compassionate and merciful nature of Allah, who forgives those who repent and turn to Him.
orig: ولا يأتل أولو الفضل منكم والسعة أن يؤتوا أولي القربى والمساكين والمهاجرين في سبيل الله وليعفوا وليصفحوا ألا تحبون أن يغفر الله لكم والله غفور رحيم

translation: Indeed, those who cast accusations of immorality at chaste, believing women are cursed in this life and the hereafter, and they will have a great punishment.
interpretation: The verse strongly condemns those who falsely accuse chaste, believing women of immorality. These accusers are cursed both in this life and in the hereafter, and they will face a severe punishment. The verse emphasizes the gravity of making false accusations and the serious consequences of such actions. It serves as a warning to those who spread rumors and engage in slander, reminding them of the importance of truth and justice.
orig: إن الذين يرمون المحصنات الغافلات المؤمنات لعنوا في الدنيا والآخرة ولهم عذاب عظيم

translation: A day on which their tongues, their hands, and their feet will bear witness against them as to what they used to do.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the Day of Judgment, when the actions of people will be judged by God. The verse emphasizes the role of the limbs (tongues, hands, and feet) as witnesses to the actions of the individuals, indicating that every action, word, and deed of a person will be accounted for on that day. The verse serves as a warning to those who commit sins and wrongdoings, urging them to repent and refrain from sinful acts as they will be held accountable for them on the Day of Judgment.
orig: يوم تشهد عليهم ألسنتهم وأيديهم وأرجلهم بما كانوا يعملون

translation: On that Day
interpretation: No interpretation
orig: يومئذ يوفيهم الله دينهم الحق ويعلمون أن الله هو الحق المبين

translation: Unrighteous women are for unrighteous men, and unrighteous men are for unrighteous women. And righteous women are for righteous men, and righteous men are for righteous women. These are free from what they say. For them is forgiveness and a generous provision.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the consequences of one's actions and how they are matched with the actions of others. It describes how unrighteous people will be with each other and how righteous people will be with each other. The verse emphasizes the importance of righteousness and its rewards, which include forgiveness and a generous provision. The verse serves as a reminder that a person's actions have consequences and that they will be matched with like-minded individuals. It encourages people to strive for righteousness and to be mindful of the company they keep.
orig: الخبيثات للخبيثين والخبيثون للخبيثات والطيبات للطيبين والطيبون للطيبات أولئك مبرءون مما يقولون لهم مغفرة ورزق كريم

translation: O you who have believed, do not enter houses other than your own houses until you ascertain welcome and greet their inhabitants. That is better for you, perhaps you will remember.
interpretation: The verse instructs Muslims to respect the privacy of others and not to enter homes without permission or prior knowledge of the inhabitants' whereabouts. The verse emphasizes the importance of greeting and seeking permission before entering someone else's home, as this is a sign of good manners and respect. The verse highlights the benefits of following this instruction, such as the possibility of being remembered and rewarded by God. Overall, the verse promotes the values of respect, courtesy, and awareness of others' feelings and rights.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تدخلوا بيوتا غير بيوتكم حتى تستأنسوا وتسلموا على أهلها ذلكم خير لكم لعلكم تذكرون

translation: And if you do not find anyone therein, then do not enter it until permission has been given to you. And if it is said to you, 'Go back,' then go back. That is purer for you. And Allah is Knowing of what you do.
interpretation: The verse outlines the etiquette of entering a house or a private property. It emphasizes the importance of seeking permission before entering and respecting the boundaries of others. If no one is present, the verse advises against entering without permission. If told to leave, one should comply immediately as it is the right thing to do. By following these guidelines, one can maintain their purity and avoid any harm or transgression. This verse is a reminder of the importance of respecting other people's privacy, seeking permission, and following the commands of Allah.
orig: فإن لم تجدوا فيها أحدا فلا تدخلوها حتى يؤذن لكم وإن قيل لكم ارجعوا فارجعوا هو أزكى لكم والله بما تعملون عليم

translation: There is no blame upon you for entering uninhabited houses where is your sustenance (stored), and Allah knows what you make public and what you conceal.
interpretation: The verse permits Muslims to enter uninhabited houses to retrieve their sustenance that is stored there. The verse emphasizes that God is all-knowing, aware of both what people do openly and what they conceal. The verse suggests that people should not be hesitant to enter such houses, as they are allowed to do so and God is aware of their actions. The verse can also be seen as a reminder for people to be mindful of their actions, as God knows everything and nothing can be hidden from Him.
orig: ليس عليكم جناح أن تدخلوا بيوتا غير مسكونة فيها متاع لكم والله يعلم ما تبدون وما تكتمون

translation: Say to the believers to lower their gaze and guard their chastity. That is purer for them. Indeed, Allah is acquainted with what they do.
interpretation: The verse instructs the believers, both men and women, to lower their gaze and guard their chastity. This commandment is considered purer and more virtuous for them. The verse emphasizes that Allah has full knowledge of their actions and deeds. The interpretation of this verse is that it encourages believers to be mindful of their behavior and to avoid any actions that may lead to immorality or sin. By lowering their gaze and guarding their chastity, believers can protect themselves from harm and maintain their purity. The verse also reminds believers that Allah is all-knowing and sees all their actions, which serves as a reminder to always act in accordance with His teachings and commands.
orig: قل للمؤمنين يغضوا من أبصارهم ويحفظوا فروجهم ذلك أزكى لهم إن الله خبير بما يصنعون

translation: And say to the believing women that they should lower their gaze and guard their modesty; that they should not display their beauty and ornaments except what (must ordinarily) appear thereof; that they should draw their veils over their bosoms and not display their beauty except to their husbands, their fathers, their husband's fathers, their sons, their husbands' sons, their brothers or their brothers' sons, or their sisters' sons, or their women, or the slaves whom their right hands possess, or male servants free of physical needs, or small children who have no sense of the shame of sex; and that they should not strike their feet in order to draw attention to their hidden ornaments. And O ye believers! turn ye all together towards Allah, that ye may attain bliss.
interpretation: This verse is addressed to the believing women and provides them with a set of guidelines on how to dress and behave in public. The verse emphasizes the importance of modesty and restraint, instructing women to lower their gaze and cover their bodies, except for what is ordinarily apparent. The verse also forbids women from displaying their beauty and ornaments in public, except to certain close relatives or slaves. Additionally, the verse instructs women not to draw attention to their hidden ornaments by striking their feet. The verse concludes by urging all believers to turn towards Allah and seek His blessings. The verse can be interpreted as a reminder of the importance of modesty and humility in Islam and the need to avoid drawing unnecessary attention to oneself in public.
orig: وقل للمؤمنات يغضضن من أبصارهن ويحفظن فروجهن ولا يبدين زينتهن إلا ما ظهر منها وليضربن بخمرهن على جيوبهن ولا يبدين زينتهن إلا لبعولتهن أو آبائهن أو آباء بعولتهن أو أبنائهن أو أبناء بعولتهن أو إخوانهن أو بني إخوانهن أو بني أخواتهن أو نسائهن أو ما ملكت أيمانهن أو التابعين غير أولي الإربة من الرجال أو الطفل الذين لم يظهروا على عورات النساء ولا يضربن بأرجلهن ليعلم ما يخفين من زينتهن وتوبوا إلى الله جميعا أيه المؤمنون لعلكم تفلحون

translation: And marry the unmarried among you and the righteous among your slaves, male or female: if they are in poverty, Allah will provide for them out of His abundance: Allah is He who has full knowledge and is acquainted with all things.
interpretation: The verse encourages marriage for the unmarried members of the community, as well as for the righteous slaves, both male and female. The verse acknowledges that poverty may be an obstacle for some, and reassures them that if they are in such a situation, God will provide for them. The verse emphasizes God's knowledge and awareness of all things, indicating that He is aware of the needs of His servants and will provide for them accordingly.
orig: وأنكحوا الأيامى منكم والصالحين من عبادكم وإمائكم إن يكونوا فقراء يغنهم الله من فضله والله واسع عليم

translation: But those who are unable to marry, let them marry from those who are permissible for them, as long as they are able to maintain financial responsibility for them. And those who are engaged in the writing of the contract, let them write it for them justly. And the one who is unable to do that, let him appoint a trustworthy person from among you. And let him bear witness along with two just men from among you, and take hold of the contract. And if it becomes too difficult for him, then let him do as he is able. And let them fulfill their covenant of chastity. And let them not take the believers as intimates of disbelievers. And whoever does that, then indeed, he has strayed from the right way. And let them not take as protectors those who have disbelieved, rather, [let them take] from those who have believed and are sincere to them. And they should establish the prayer and give zakah and obey the command of the Messenger. Indeed, those who disbelieve from among the People of the Book and the polytheists will be in the fire of hell, remaining in it forever. They are the worst of creatures.
interpretation: The verse outlines the responsibilities and regulations regarding marriage for those who are unable to marry, and those who are responsible for writing and witnessing the marriage contract. The verse emphasizes the importance of maintaining financial responsibility for one's spouse and fulfilling the covenant of chastity. The verse also warns against taking disbelievers as intimates or protectors, and encourages believers to establish the prayer, give zakah, and obey the command of the Messenger. The verse ends by stating the fate of those who disbelieve, they will be in the fire of hell, remaining in it forever. The verse serves as a guide for believers in their personal and social relationships, and reminds them of the importance of upholding their responsibilities and obligations as Muslims.
orig: وليستعفف الذين لا يجدون نكاحا حتى يغنيهم الله من فضله والذين يبتغون الكتاب مما ملكت أيمانكم فكاتبوهم إن علمتم فيهم خيرا وآتوهم من مال الله الذي آتاكم ولا تكرهوا فتياتكم على البغاء إن أردن تحصنا لتبتغوا عرض الحياة الدنيا ومن يكرههن فإن الله من بعد إكراههن غفور رحيم

translation: And We have certainly sent down to you clear signs and examples from those who have passed on before you, and exhortations for the righteous.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the revelation of clear signs and examples from previous nations to the Prophet Muhammad, as well as admonitions for the righteous. These signs and examples serve as lessons for the believers, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the importance of righteousness. The verse encourages the righteous to continue on their path and to use the lessons from the past as guidance.
orig: ولقد أنزلنا إليكم آيات مبينات ومثلا من الذين خلوا من قبلكم وموعظة للمتقين

translation: Allah is the light of the heavens and the earth. The example of His light is like a niche within which is a lamp, the lamp is within a glass, the glass is as if it were a shining star, lit from a blessed olive tree, neither of the east nor the west, its oil almost glows even if it is not touched by fire, light upon light, Allah guides to His light whom He wills, and Allah presents examples for the people and Allah is Knowing of all things.
interpretation: The verse uses the metaphor of light to describe Allah's presence and guidance. The light is described as being within a niche, a lamp and a glass, all of which serve to protect and enhance the light. The light is further described as coming from a blessed olive tree, which is neither of the east nor the west, indicating its universal nature. The light is so powerful that it almost glows without being touched by fire. The verse emphasizes the guidance that Allah provides to those whom He wills, and the use of examples to help people understand. The verse ultimately emphasizes Allah's knowledge of all things, reinforcing the idea of His omnipotence and omniscience.
orig: الله نور السماوات والأرض مثل نوره كمشكاة فيها مصباح المصباح في زجاجة الزجاجة كأنها كوكب دري يوقد من شجرة مباركة زيتونة لا شرقية ولا غربية يكاد زيتها يضيء ولو لم تمسسه نار نور على نور يهدي الله لنوره من يشاء ويضرب الله الأمثال للناس والله بكل شيء عليم

translation: In houses which Allah has allowed to be exalted and that His name be remembered in them; exalting Him in the morning and evening.
interpretation: The verse refers to houses that have been blessed by God and are used for the purpose of worship and remembrance of God. These houses are a place for the exaltation of God, both in the morning and in the evening, indicating the continuous and consistent practice of worship. The verse highlights the importance of establishing a dedicated space for worship and the regular practice of remembering and exalting God.
orig: في بيوت أذن الله أن ترفع ويذكر فيها اسمه يسبح له فيها بالغدو والآصال

translation: Men who indulge in business or commerce, (thereby) neglecting (their) remembrance of Allah and the establishment of prayer and the paying of the poor-due. They fear a day when hearts and eyes will (all) be overturned.
interpretation: The verse describes a group of men who are preoccupied with their business and commerce, and in the process, they neglect the remembrance of God, the establishment of prayer, and the payment of the poor-due (zakat). The verse warns of a day when their hearts and eyes will be overturned, indicating a state of great fear and turmoil. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of prioritizing one's relationship with God and fulfilling one's religious obligations, even in the midst of worldly pursuits.
orig: رجال لا تلهيهم تجارة ولا بيع عن ذكر الله وإقام الصلاة وإيتاء الزكاة يخافون يوما تتقلب فيه القلوب والأبصار

translation: Allah will reward them for their best deeds, and add more from His grace. And Allah provides for whom He wills without measure.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the reward that Allah gives to people for their good deeds. Not only will Allah reward them for their best deeds, but He will also give them even more through His grace. This highlights Allah's generosity and kindness towards His creation. The verse also emphasizes that Allah provides for whom He wills without measure, indicating that His provision is abundant and unlimited. The verse serves as a reminder of the blessings that Allah bestows upon His creation and the rewards that await those who do good deeds.
orig: ليجزيهم الله أحسن ما عملوا ويزيدهم من فضله والله يرزق من يشاء بغير حساب

translation: And those who disbelieved, their deeds are like a mirage in a desert. The thirsty one thinks it is water until he comes to it and finds it nothing, but he finds Allah with him, and Allah will pay him his due; and Allah is swift in account.
interpretation: The verse describes the fate of the disbelievers, likening their deeds to a mirage in a desert. The mirage gives a false hope of water to the thirsty traveler, but it disappears as he approaches it. Similarly, the deeds of the disbelievers will not benefit them in the hereafter. The verse emphasizes the futility of disbelief and warns of the consequences of rejecting the truth. The verse also highlights the justice of Allah, who will hold each person accountable for their deeds and will give them their due reward. The verse serves as a reminder of the reality of the hereafter and the importance of belief and righteous deeds.
orig: والذين كفروا أعمالهم كسراب بقيعة يحسبه الظمآن ماء حتى إذا جاءه لم يجده شيئا ووجد الله عنده فوفاه حسابه والله سريع الحساب

translation: Or like darknesses on a vast, boundless sea, overwhelmed by a wave, above which is another wave, above which are clouds, darknesses upon darknesses, when he stretches out his hand, he can hardly see it. And he for whom Allah has not appointed light - for him there is no light.
interpretation: The verse uses the metaphor of a dark and turbulent sea to convey the idea of confusion, chaos, and loss of direction. The image of one wave piling on top of another, with clouds above, gives a sense of the overwhelming power of the forces at play. The verse emphasizes the difficulty of finding one's way in such a situation, as illustrated by the person who stretches out his hand and can hardly see it. The verse then introduces the concept of light, which is associated with the guidance and favor of Allah. Those who have not been given light by Allah are left in darkness, without any guidance or hope of finding their way.
orig: أو كظلمات في بحر لجي يغشاه موج من فوقه موج من فوقه سحاب ظلمات بعضها فوق بعض إذا أخرج يده لم يكد يراها ومن لم يجعل الله له نورا فما له من نور

translation: Have you not seen that Allah praises (sabsaha) for Himself whom is in the heavens and the earth and the birds with wings outspread? Each of them has known its prayer and its praise, and Allah is Knowing of what they do.
interpretation: The verse highlights the praising and glorification of God by all of His creations, from the beings in the heavens and the earth to the birds with outspread wings. Each of these creations has its own way of worshiping and praising God, and they all do so in accordance with the knowledge that God has given them. The verse emphasizes the all-encompassing knowledge of God, who is aware of all actions of His creations. This verse can be seen as a reminder to humans to also praise and worship God, and to be mindful of the fact that God is aware of all of our actions.
orig: ألم تر أن الله يسبح له من في السماوات والأرض والطير صافات كل قد علم صلاته وتسبيحه والله عليم بما يفعلون

translation: And to God belongs the kingdom of the heavens and the earth, and to God is the final destination.
interpretation: The verse affirms the sovereignty and ownership of God over all of creation, both the heavens and the earth. It emphasizes that all things ultimately return to God, reiterating the idea of God's ultimate power and control over all that exists. This verse can serve as a reminder of the fleeting and temporary nature of worldly possessions and pursuits, and the importance of focusing on one's relationship with God and preparing for the ultimate return to Him.
orig: ولله ملك السماوات والأرض وإلى الله المصير

translation: Have you not seen that Allah sends down rain from the sky, and then the earth becomes green? Then He sends forth clouds, and We drive them to a dead land, and revive the earth with them after its death? Such is the resurrection.
interpretation: The verse describes the process of rainfall and its impact on the earth, emphasizing the power of God in bringing forth life from what appears to be dead. The verse begins by mentioning the rain that comes down from the sky, causing the earth to become green and fertile. This is followed by the mention of clouds, which are driven by God to a barren land, where they bring about life and growth. The verse then compares this process to the resurrection, emphasizing the power of God to bring forth life even after death. The verse serves as a reminder of the power and control of God over all aspects of life and the natural world, and the ultimate reality of the resurrection.
orig: ألم تر أن الله يزجي سحابا ثم يؤلف بينه ثم يجعله ركاما فترى الودق يخرج من خلاله وينزل من السماء من جبال فيها من برد فيصيب به من يشاء ويصرفه عن من يشاء يكاد سنا برقه يذهب بالأبصار

translation: Allah turns the night into the day and turns the day into the night, and there is indeed a lesson in that for those who have eyes to see.
interpretation: The verse highlights the natural phenomenon of the day turning into night and vice versa, emphasizing the power and control of Allah over the universe. The phrase 'there is indeed a lesson in that' implies that the natural world contains signs and messages for those who are willing to reflect and ponder. The verse encourages the reader to contemplate the wonders of creation and to use this contemplation as a means of gaining a deeper understanding of Allah and His ways. The verse also suggests that the cyclical nature of day and night serves as a reminder of the transient nature of life, urging the reader to make the most of their time and to use it to draw closer to Allah.
orig: يقلب الله الليل والنهار إن في ذلك لعبرة لأولي الأبصار

translation: And Allah has created every animal from water: of them there are some that creep on their bellies; some that walk on two legs; and some that walk on four. Allah creates what He wills. Indeed, Allah is over all things competent.
interpretation: The verse highlights the power and ability of Allah in creating all living beings from water. The verse mentions different ways in which animals move, emphasizing the diversity and complexity of Allah's creation. The verse also emphasizes that Allah creates whatever He wills and has the power and ability to do all things. The verse serves as a reminder of Allah's greatness and power, encouraging believers to reflect on the wonders of His creation and to have faith and trust in His will and wisdom.
orig: والله خلق كل دابة من ماء فمنهم من يمشي على بطنه ومنهم من يمشي على رجلين ومنهم من يمشي على أربع يخلق الله ما يشاء إن الله على كل شيء قدير

translation: We have indeed sent down clear signs, and Allah guides whom He wills to the Straight Path.
interpretation: The verse affirms that Allah has revealed clear signs or evidence to guide humanity. However, it is up to Allah to guide those whom He wills to the Straight Path. This path refers to the right way of living in accordance with Allah's will and commands. The verse emphasizes the importance of divine guidance and the fact that it is ultimately a matter of divine will and mercy. It also highlights the idea that not everyone will be guided, and that the responsibility for guidance lies with Allah, not with humans.
orig: لقد أنزلنا آيات مبينات والله يهدي من يشاء إلى صراط مستقيم

translation: And they say, 'We have believed in Allah and the Messenger and obeyed,' then some of them turn away after that, and those - they are not believers.
interpretation: The verse speaks about people who claim to have believed in Allah and His messenger and obeyed them, but then some of them turn away from their faith and disobey. The verse emphasizes that those who turn away from their faith after proclaiming it are not true believers. This verse serves as a reminder that faith and obedience must be consistent and steadfast, and that hypocrisy and false claims of faith will not be accepted by Allah.
orig: ويقولون آمنا بالله وبالرسول وأطعنا ثم يتولى فريق منهم من بعد ذلك وما أولئك بالمؤمنين

translation: And when they are called to Allah and His Messenger to judge between them, then a party of them turns aside.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the rejection of some people to submit to the judgement of Allah and His Messenger when they are called upon to do so. The verse highlights the division and opposition that arises when people refuse to follow the guidance of Allah and His Messenger, and instead turn away. This verse serves as a reminder that following the path of Allah and submitting to His will is the only way to achieve justice and unity.
orig: وإذا دعوا إلى الله ورسوله ليحكم بينهم إذا فريق منهم معرضون

translation: And if they had justice, they would have followed me, but glory be to Allah, Lord of the worlds.
interpretation: This verse speaks about the people who do not follow the guidance and justice, despite knowing it. The verse highlights that if they truly believed and were just, they would have followed the guidance and the speaker (who is believed to be Prophet Muhammad). However, the verse ends with a note of praise to God, acknowledging that the ultimate power and control belongs to Him, and that it is only by His will that people find the path of guidance and justice.
orig: وإن يكن لهم الحق يأتوا إليه مذعنين

translation: Is it in their hearts that Allah has sent a disease or fear have they fallen into doubt or do they fear that Allah and His Messenger will wrong them? Rather, it is they who are the wrongdoers.
interpretation: The verse is addressing people who have doubts about the message of Allah and His Messenger. The verse questions whether these people have a disease in their hearts or if they are in doubt. The verse also asks if they fear that Allah and His Messenger will wrong them. The verse answers its own questions by stating that it is actually these people who are the wrongdoers. The verse serves as a reminder to those who may have doubts or fears about the message of Allah and His Messenger. It emphasizes that those who have doubts or fears are the ones who are in the wrong, not Allah or His Messenger. The verse encourages the believers to have faith and trust in Allah and His Messenger and to not be swayed by the doubts or fears of those who are in the wrong.
orig: أفي قلوبهم مرض أم ارتابوا أم يخافون أن يحيف الله عليهم ورسوله بل أولئك هم الظالمون

translation: The believer's response when they are called to God and His Messenger to judge between them is to say, 'We hear and we obey.' And it is they who will be successful.
interpretation: The verse describes the behavior of believers when they are called upon by God and His Messenger to settle their disputes. The believers' response is to listen and obey, demonstrating their submission and obedience to God's will. This response is presented as a characteristic of those who are successful and blessed, implying that obedience and submission to God's commands leads to success and prosperity in this life and the hereafter.
orig: إنما كان قول المؤمنين إذا دعوا إلى الله ورسوله ليحكم بينهم أن يقولوا سمعنا وأطعنا وأولئك هم المفلحون

translation: And whoever obeys Allah and the Messenger - those will be with the ones upon whom Allah has bestowed favor of the prophets, the steadfast affirmers of truth, the martyrs and the righteous. And excellent are those as companions.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the rewards for those who obey Allah and His Messenger, have fear of Allah, and are mindful of Him. These individuals will be with the best of companions, including the prophets, the steadfast affirmers of truth, the martyrs, and the righteous. The verse highlights the blessings and rewards for those who follow the commands of Allah and the Messenger, and emphasizes the importance of obedience, fear, and mindfulness of Allah. The verse serves as an encouragement for believers to strive for righteousness and to seek the companionship of the righteous.
orig: ومن يطع الله ورسوله ويخش الله ويتقه فأولئك هم الفائزون

translation: And they swore by Allah their most solemn oath that if thou commandest them, they would surely go forth. Say, 'Swear not; obedience is Allah's will; verily He is aware of what you do.'
interpretation: The verse addresses people who have made a solemn oath to Allah that they will obey the Prophet's command and fight in the way of Allah. However, the verse instructs the Prophet to tell them not to swear such an oath, as obedience is already expected of them as a duty towards Allah. The verse emphasizes that Allah is aware of their actions and reminds the believers that their obedience should not be conditional on an oath, but rather a natural response to the command of Allah.
orig: وأقسموا بالله جهد أيمانهم لئن أمرتهم ليخرجن قل لا تقسموا طاعة معروفة إن الله خبير بما تعملون

translation: Say, 'Obey Allah and obey the Messenger.' But if they turn away - then upon him is only the clear delivery. And upon you is only the delivery. And if you obey him, you will be guided. And there is no blame upon the messenger except for the clear delivery.
interpretation: This verse is a command to the Prophet Muhammad to tell the people to obey Allah and obey the Messenger. If the people choose to disobey, then the only responsibility of the Prophet is to deliver the message clearly. Similarly, the listeners have the responsibility to accept and act upon the message. If they obey, they will be guided. The Prophet is not responsible for the people's actions, only for delivering the message clearly.
orig: قل أطيعوا الله وأطيعوا الرسول فإن تولوا فإنما عليه ما حمل وعليكم ما حملتم وإن تطيعوه تهتدوا وما على الرسول إلا البلاغ المبين

translation: Allah has promised those among you who believe and do good that He will surely establish them in the earth as He established those before them, and that He will strengthen their religion which He has chosen for them, and that He will change their fear into security: 'They will worship Me, not associating anything with Me.' But whoever disbelieves after that, they are the transgressors.
interpretation: The verse speaks about Allah's promise to the believers and those who do good that He will establish them in the earth and strengthen their religion. The verse emphasizes the security and stability that will be granted to them, as opposed to their current state of fear. The verse also warns those who disbelieve after this promise, stating that they are the transgressors. The verse serves as a reminder of the rewards for the believers and the consequences for the disbelievers, emphasizing the importance of faith and good deeds.
orig: وعد الله الذين آمنوا منكم وعملوا الصالحات ليستخلفنهم في الأرض كما استخلف الذين من قبلهم وليمكنن لهم دينهم الذي ارتضى لهم وليبدلنهم من بعد خوفهم أمنا يعبدونني لا يشركون بي شيئا ومن كفر بعد ذلك فأولئك هم الفاسقون

translation: And establish prayer and give zakah and obey the Messenger, that you may receive mercy.
interpretation: The verse is a command to the believers to establish prayer, give zakah (charity), and obey the Messenger (Prophet Muhammad) in order to earn mercy from God. The verse emphasizes the importance of these three actions, which are considered fundamental practices in Islam. By establishing prayer, giving zakah, and obeying the Messenger, Muslims can purify their souls, help the needy, and follow the guidance of the Prophet, which will ultimately lead them to God's mercy and blessings.
orig: وأقيموا الصلاة وآتوا الزكاة وأطيعوا الرسول لعلكم ترحمون

translation: Do not think of those who disbelieve that they are safe from the punishment. Their refuge is the Fire, and what an evil destination!
interpretation: The verse warns those who disbelieve in God and His messenger that they should not feel safe from God's punishment. The verse emphasizes that their ultimate destination is the Fire, indicating the severity of their fate. The verse serves as a reminder to the disbelievers of the consequences of their actions and the importance of turning to faith and belief in God.
orig: لا تحسبن الذين كفروا معجزين في الأرض ومأواهم النار ولبئس المصير

translation: O you who have believed, permission is not for you to take women as inheritance by parting her hand, except that you have touched her and she has become unlawful for you thereafter, nor is it for you to take (more) women (as wives) by (merely) counting their dowries. But if you want to take (more) women (as wives) by (merely) counting their dowries - then give them their dowries - there is no blame upon you for what you have agreed upon after what is prescribed. Indeed, it is more appropriate that you not take (more) women (as wives) by (merely) counting their dowries, except when you have been intimate with them. In this way you are more likely to not exceed the limit. And give to the women their dowries willingly. But if they, of their own accord, give up to you a portion thereof, then consume it with good enjoyment and without harm. And if you want to take (more) women (as wives) in place of those (whom you have divorced) - then there is no blame upon you in regard to what you have agreed upon after what is prescribed. Indeed, Allah is Knowing and Wise.
interpretation: The verse sets out the rules for marriage and inheritance in Islam. It forbids men from taking women as inheritance by parting her hand, unless they have already been intimate. It also forbids men from taking more wives by merely counting their dowries, unless they give them their full dowries. The verse emphasizes the importance of treating women fairly and with respect, and of fulfilling one's financial obligations towards them. The verse encourages men to be mindful of the limits set by God in their relationships with women, and to avoid excess and exploitation. The verse also allows for the possibility of divorce and remarriage, provided that the proper procedures are followed and the financial obligations are met. Overall, the verse promotes justice, fairness, and respect in all aspects of marriage and divorce in Islam.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا ليستأذنكم الذين ملكت أيمانكم والذين لم يبلغوا الحلم منكم ثلاث مرات من قبل صلاة الفجر وحين تضعون ثيابكم من الظهيرة ومن بعد صلاة العشاء ثلاث عورات لكم ليس عليكم ولا عليهم جناح بعدهن طوافون عليكم بعضكم على بعض كذلك يبين الله لكم الآيات والله عليم حكيم

translation: And when the children among you reach puberty, let them ask for permission, as those before them did. Thus does Allah make clear to you His verses; and Allah is Knowing, Wise.
interpretation: This verse sets the rule for children who have reached puberty to seek permission before entering the presence of others. This is a way for Allah to make His signs clear to the believers. The verse emphasizes the importance of respecting boundaries and following the examples of those who came before. By doing so, believers can better understand Allah's messages and gain a deeper understanding of His wisdom and knowledge.
orig: وإذا بلغ الأطفال منكم الحلم فليستأذنوا كما استأذن الذين من قبلهم كذلك يبين الله لكم آياته والله عليم حكيم

translation: And for women who are past childbearing age and no longer have any hope of marriage - there is no blame upon them if they remove their outer garments, provided they do not display their adornments. But it is best for them to be modest, and God is All-Hearing, All-Knowing.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the dress code for women who are past childbearing age and have no hope of getting married. These women are allowed to remove their outer garments, as long as they do not display their adornments in a way that attracts attention. However, the verse encourages them to be modest and dress in a way that is appropriate and respectful. The verse emphasizes the importance of modesty and reminds the reader that God is aware of all actions and intentions.
orig: والقواعد من النساء اللاتي لا يرجون نكاحا فليس عليهن جناح أن يضعن ثيابهن غير متبرجات بزينة وأن يستعففن خير لهن والله سميع عليم

translation: There is no blame upon the blind, nor is there blame upon the lame, nor is there blame upon the sick, nor on yourselves that you eat from your houses, or the houses of your fathers, or the houses of your mothers, or the houses of your brothers, or the houses of your sisters, or the houses of your paternal aunts, or the houses of your maternal aunts, or whatever you own of houses, or your friend's house. It is no sin for you that you eat together or separately. But when you enter houses, greet one another with a greeting from Allah, blessed and good. Thus does Allah make clear to you the verses that you may understand.
interpretation: The verse outlines the rules of hospitality and etiquette when entering homes. It emphasizes that there is no blame on certain groups of people, such as the blind, the lame, or the sick, for eating from their own homes or the homes of their relatives. The verse also states that there is no sin in eating together or separately. However, when entering a home, Muslims are instructed to greet each other with a greeting from Allah, which is blessed and good. This verse serves to remind Muslims of the importance of hospitality, kindness, and good manners towards others, particularly when entering their homes. It also highlights the mercy and compassion of Allah towards all people, regardless of their physical abilities or circumstances.
orig: ليس على الأعمى حرج ولا على الأعرج حرج ولا على المريض حرج ولا على أنفسكم أن تأكلوا من بيوتكم أو بيوت آبائكم أو بيوت أمهاتكم أو بيوت إخوانكم أو بيوت أخواتكم أو بيوت أعمامكم أو بيوت عماتكم أو بيوت أخوالكم أو بيوت خالاتكم أو ما ملكتم مفاتحه أو صديقكم ليس عليكم جناح أن تأكلوا جميعا أو أشتاتا فإذا دخلتم بيوتا فسلموا على أنفسكم تحية من عند الله مباركة طيبة كذلك يبين الله لكم الآيات لعلكم تعقلون

translation: The believers are only those who have believed in Allah and His Messenger and then doubt not but strive with their properties and their lives in the cause of Allah. It is they who are the truthful. And say, [O Muhammad], 'Acceptance of you is not but from Allah. Indeed, He is the Hearing, the Knowing. And if they turn away, then indeed - He is, of you, Exalted in Might and Wise.' Indeed, in the Messenger of Allah you have a good example to follow for whoever has hope in Allah and the Last Day and remembers Allah often.
interpretation: This verse speaks about the qualities of true believers who have faith in Allah and His Messenger and strive with their lives and properties for the cause of Allah. They are truthful and seek Allah's acceptance, knowing that it comes only from Him, as He is all-hearing and all-knowing. If people turn away from the message of the Messenger of Allah, then Allah is Exalted in Might and Wise.
