The verse also emphasizes the importance of following the example of the Messenger of Allah for those who hope in Allah and the Last Day and remember Allah often.
orig: إنما المؤمنون الذين آمنوا بالله ورسوله وإذا كانوا معه على أمر جامع لم يذهبوا حتى يستأذنوه إن الذين يستأذنونك أولئك الذين يؤمنون بالله ورسوله فإذا استأذنوك لبعض شأنهم فأذن لمن شئت منهم واستغفر لهم الله إن الله غفور رحيم

translation: Do not make the supplication of the Messenger among yourselves like a supplication of one of you to another. Indeed, Allah knows those of you who slip away, so let those who defy his command beware lest a trial strike them or a painful punishment.
interpretation: The verse warns against treating the supplication of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) casually or as equal to the supplication of any other person. It emphasizes the importance of respecting and giving special attention to the Prophet's supplication, as Allah is aware of those who neglect it. The verse also warns those who defy the commands of the Prophet to be cautious and mindful of the consequences of their actions. It implies that those who disregard the Prophet's teachings may face a trial or a severe punishment.
orig: لا تجعلوا دعاء الرسول بينكم كدعاء بعضكم بعضا قد يعلم الله الذين يتسللون منكم لواذا فليحذر الذين يخالفون عن أمره أن تصيبهم فتنة أو يصيبهم عذاب أليم

translation: No! Indeed, for Allah is what is in the heavens and what is on the earth, and indeed, to Allah will all of you be returned. On a Day [when] He will inform you about what you used to do. And Allah is, of all things, Knowing.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the power and knowledge of Allah over all things in the heavens and on earth. It reminds the reader that all of humanity will be returned to Allah on the Day of Judgment, when Allah will inform them of their actions and hold them accountable. The verse serves as a reminder of the omniscience of Allah and the inevitability of the Day of Judgment, encouraging the reader to reflect on their actions and strive for righteousness.
orig: ألا إن لله ما في السماوات والأرض قد يعلم ما أنتم عليه ويوم يرجعون إليه فينبئهم بما عملوا والله بكل شيء عليم

translation: Blessed is He who sent down the Criterion upon His servant, that he may be a warner to the worlds.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the blessing of God in sending down the 'criterion' (the Qur'an) to His servant (Prophet Muhammad) as a means of guidance for all of humanity. The verse emphasizes the role of the Prophet as a warner to the world, highlighting the importance of the message and its significance for all people. The verse serves as a reminder of the guidance and wisdom that is available to humanity, and the responsibility of the Prophet to convey this message as a warner.
orig: تبارك الذي نزل الفرقان على عبده ليكون للعالمين نذيرا

translation: He who has the kingdom of the heavens and the earth and has not taken a son and has not had a partner in the kingdom and created each thing and determined it precisely.
interpretation: The verse affirms the oneness of God, emphasizing that He has no partners or children and that He has complete control over the heavens and the earth. The verse also highlights God's power and ability to create and determine all things with precision. The verse serves as a reminder of God's greatness, power, and sovereignty, and invites the reader to reflect on the intricate order and balance of the universe, which is a manifestation of God's will and wisdom.
orig: الذي له ملك السماوات والأرض ولم يتخذ ولدا ولم يكن له شريك في الملك وخلق كل شيء فقدره تقديرا

translation: And they have taken besides Him gods who do not create anything while they are created, and they have no control over harm or benefit for themselves, and they have no control over death or life or resurrection.
interpretation: The verse criticizes the people for taking gods other than Allah, who do not possess the ability to create or control anything. These false gods are depicted as being powerless and incapable of causing harm or benefit to themselves or others. Furthermore, they have no control over death, life, or resurrection, which are all under the power of Allah alone. This verse serves as a reminder of the oneness and uniqueness of Allah, who alone possesses all power and authority.
orig: واتخذوا من دونه آلهة لا يخلقون شيئا وهم يخلقون ولا يملكون لأنفسهم ضرا ولا نفعا ولا يملكون موتا ولا حياة ولا نشورا

translation: And those who disbelieved said, 'This is nothing but a falsehood that he has invented, and he has helped him with it.' So they have committed injustice and lie.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the disbelievers' reaction to the message of the prophet. They accused the prophet of inventing falsehood and claimed that he was helped by others. The verse highlights the rejection and denial of the truth by the disbelievers, who not only rejected the message but also committed injustice and lied in the process. The verse serves as a reminder that rejection of the truth and the spreading of falsehood and injustice are not only wrong but also bring consequences.
orig: وقال الذين كفروا إن هذا إلا إفك افتراه وأعانه عليه قوم آخرون فقد جاءوا ظلما وزورا

translation: And they say, 'Tales of the ancients, which he has written down, they are read out to him at dawn and in the afternoon.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the disbelievers' accusation towards the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) of receiving stories of the past from a written source, which they claim is read out to him at dawn and in the afternoon. The verse highlights the ignorance and disbelief of the disbelievers, who refuse to accept the truth of the revelation and instead come up with false accusations. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of having faith and accepting the truth, and the consequences of rejecting it.
orig: وقالوا أساطير الأولين اكتتبها فهي تملى عليه بكرة وأصيلا

translation: Say, 'The one who knows the unseen in the heavens and the earth has sent it down. Indeed, He is Forgiving and Merciful.'
interpretation: The verse is a statement of divine authority and power. It asserts that the revelation of the Qur'an comes from a source that has knowledge of all that is hidden in the heavens and the earth. This source is described as being both Forgiving and Merciful, indicating that the revelation is a message of mercy and forgiveness for those who accept it. At the same time, the verse is also a challenge to the disbelievers, who deny the truth of the revelation, to produce any evidence that contradicts it. The verse emphasizes the divine origin of the Qur'an, and the unlimited power and knowledge of the one who sent it down.
orig: قل أنزله الذي يعلم السر في السماوات والأرض إنه كان غفورا رحيما

translation: And they say, 'What is this Messenger eating and walking in the markets? If only an angel was sent down to him, he would be with him as a warner.'
interpretation: The verse describes the disbelievers' reaction to the Prophet Muhammad's (pbuh) behavior, as they question why he eats and walks among the people. They express their desire for an angel to be sent down as a warner instead. The verse highlights the disbelievers' rejection of the Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) and their inability to recognize his prophethood. It also emphasizes the humanity of the Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) and the fact that he lived and interacted with his community, rather than being a distant and unapproachable figure. The verse serves as a reminder of the challenges faced by the Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) and the patience and perseverance he displayed in the face of adversity.
orig: وقالوا مال هذا الرسول يأكل الطعام ويمشي في الأسواق لولا أنزل إليه ملك فيكون معه نذيرا

translation: Or he is met with a provision (i.e., wealth or children) or he is given a garden from which he eats - then he is afflicted with a sickness and he becomes weak. And he says, 'If only I had taken a path with the Messenger (Prophet Muhammad).' Indeed, I would have been given provision from him.' So indeed, the unjust - they are in extreme error and astray.
interpretation: The verse describes the fate of those who reject the message of the Prophet Muhammad and instead choose to pursue worldly pleasures, such as wealth and children. These people are content and satisfied with their lives until they are faced with a calamity, such as illness or poverty. It is at this point that they regret not having followed the Prophet and wish they had taken a different path. The verse emphasizes the consequences of rejecting the message of the Prophet and the danger of becoming too focused on worldly pleasures. It serves as a reminder that true happiness and fulfillment can only be found through following the guidance of the Prophet and living a righteous life.
orig: أو يلقى إليه كنز أو تكون له جنة يأكل منها وقال الظالمون إن تتبعون إلا رجلا مسحورا

translation: See how they strike similitudes for you, then go astray, so they cannot grasp the way.
interpretation: The verse is criticizing those who try to use similitudes or examples to argue against the message of the Qur'an, but then they end up straying from the truth. Despite their attempts to understand and grasp the message, they ultimately fail and are unable to find the right path. The verse serves as a warning to those who reject the message of the Qur'an and use false arguments to support their disbelief, emphasizing the futility of their efforts and the consequences of their rejection of the truth.
orig: انظر كيف ضربوا لك الأمثال فضلوا فلا يستطيعون سبيلا

translation: Blessed is He who, if He wills, will make for you better than that, gardens beneath which rivers flow, and will make for you palaces.
interpretation: The verse speaks about God's power and generosity, emphasizing that He can provide for His believers with even more than what they currently have. The verse describes the blessings that God can give, such as gardens with rivers flowing beneath them and palaces. The verse serves as a reminder of the blessings that God can bestow upon His believers and the gratitude they should show for what they have been given.
orig: تبارك الذي إن شاء جعل لك خيرا من ذلك جنات تجري من تحتها الأنهار ويجعل لك قصورا

translation: But they denied the Hour (the Day of Judgment), and We have prepared a Blaze for him who denies the Hour.
interpretation: The verse speaks about those who deny the Day of Judgment and the consequences of their actions. The verse emphasizes that a painful punishment has been prepared for those who deny the truth. The verse serves as a warning to those who deny or ignore the signs of the Day of Judgment and reminds them of the importance of repentance and seeking forgiveness before it is too late.
orig: بل كذبوا بالساعة وأعتدنا لمن كذب بالساعة سعيرا

translation: When they saw it from a distance, they heard its loud wailing and crying.
interpretation: The verse describes the people's reaction when they saw a certain event or phenomenon from a distance. The event was so significant and terrifying that they heard its loud wailing and crying. While the verse does not provide specific details about the nature of the event, it implies that it was something ominous and threatening. The verse may be interpreted as a warning to be prepared for unexpected dangers and to be mindful of the consequences of one's actions.
orig: إذا رأتهم من مكان بعيد سمعوا لها تغيظا وزفيرا

translation: And when they boarded a [ark] from it, they were laughing at one another. But when a wave like mountains came at them, they called out to Allah, sincerely to Him in religion: 'If You should save us, we will surely be among the thankful.'
interpretation: The verse describes the story of the people who ridiculed and rejected Noah's message and boarded the ark as a form of mockery and entertainment. However, when they faced a wave that was as big as mountains, they called upon Allah with sincerity and promised to be grateful if they were saved. The verse highlights the power of Allah and the insignificance of human beings in the face of His creation. It also emphasizes the importance of sincerity and gratitude towards Allah, and the consequences of rejecting His messengers and messages.
orig: وإذا ألقوا منها مكانا ضيقا مقرنين دعوا هنالك ثبورا

translation: Do not call upon a single shout [i.e. for help] this day, but call upon many shouts [i.e. for mercy]
interpretation: The verse is a command from God to the believers, urging them to call upon Him with multiple supplications and pleas for mercy and help during a time of great distress or difficulty. The verse emphasizes the importance of persistence and insistence in du'a (supplication), and encourages believers to seek God's help and mercy through multiple expressions of devotion and worship. The verse also highlights the significance of the day, which may refer to the Day of Judgment or a day of great calamity, and underscores the need for urgent and fervent prayers in such circumstances.
orig: لا تدعوا اليوم ثبورا واحدا وادعوا ثبورا كثيرا

translation: Say, 'Is that better or the eternal garden which the righteous have been promised?' That shall be their recompense and destination.
interpretation: The verse contrasts the temporary pleasures of this world with the eternal bliss of paradise that has been promised to the righteous. The verse reminds the listener to consider their choices and the consequences that follow. The eternal garden, or paradise, is presented as the ultimate reward and destination for those who are righteous and pious. The verse encourages the listener to strive for righteousness and piety, and to seek the ultimate reward of paradise, rather than being content with the fleeting pleasures of this world.
orig: قل أذلك خير أم جنة الخلد التي وعد المتقون كانت لهم جزاء ومصيرا

translation: For them in it is what they will desire, abiding eternally. Indeed, your Lord is a promise-keeper.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the blessings and rewards that the righteous will receive in Paradise. It emphasizes the eternal nature of their stay and the fulfillment of their desires. The verse also highlights the reliability and trustworthiness of God, who is described as a 'promise-keeper', implying that those who follow His commands and live righteously can have full confidence in His promises.
orig: لهم فيها ما يشاءون خالدين كان على ربك وعدا مسئولا

translation: And the Day We gather them all together, then say to those who associated partners with Allah, 'Was it you who misled My servants, or were they the ones who went astray?'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the Day of Judgment, when all of humanity will be gathered together before God. On that day, God will address those who associated partners with Him (polytheists) and ask them if they were the ones who led God's servants astray or if it was the polytheists themselves who went astray. The verse emphasizes the ultimate accountability of the polytheists for their actions and their rejection of the truth, and highlights the futility of their attempts to mislead others from the path of God.
orig: ويوم يحشرهم وما يعبدون من دون الله فيقول أأنتم أضللتم عبادي هؤلاء أم هم ضلوا السبيل

translation: They say, 'Exalted are You! We took no friends besides You; rather, we were wronging ourselves and were not guided.',
interpretation: The verse shows the remorse and regret of a group of people who acknowledge their past mistakes and sins. They recognize the greatness of God and admit that they had taken false gods besides Him. The phrase 'We took no friends besides You' indicates their recognition of the error of their ways and their desire for forgiveness. The verse emphasizes the human tendency to stray from the right path and the importance of guidance and staying on the right path.
orig: قالوا سبحانك ما كان ينبغي لنا أن نتخذ من دونك من أولياء ولكن متعتهم وآباءهم حتى نسوا الذكر وكانوا قوما بورا

translation: They have disbelieved in what you say, so they cannot escape (from the punishment), nor can they defend themselves. And whoever among you commits evil, We will make him taste a great punishment.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the disbelief of certain people in the message brought by the prophet and their inability to escape or defend themselves against the punishment of God. The verse emphasizes the powerlessness of these people against the will of God and the consequences of their disbelief and evil actions. The verse also makes it clear that those who commit evil will be punished, with the punishment being described as 'great'. The verse serves as a warning to those who reject the message and engage in unrighteous acts, reminding them of the severe consequences of their actions and the inevitability of God's punishment.
orig: فقد كذبوكم بما تقولون فما تستطيعون صرفا ولا نصرا ومن يظلم منكم نذقه عذابا كبيرا

translation: And We sent not before you (as messengers) any but men unto whom We revealed. So ask of those who know the scripture, if you know not. They (the prophets) ate not food except for its provision (sustenance). So, indeed, they were of us, the sincere ones.
interpretation: The verse highlights that all the prophets sent by God were human beings who required sustenance to survive. This serves as a reminder that prophethood is not a superhuman quality, but rather a testament to the fact that God chooses ordinary people to convey His message. The verse also encourages seeking knowledge from those who have it, implying the importance of learning from the knowledgeable and the scriptures. The verse emphasizes the sincerity and truthfulness of the prophets, who were not exempt from the basic needs of life, but rather were chosen by God for their unwavering devotion and commitment to His message.
orig: وما أرسلنا قبلك من المرسلين إلا إنهم ليأكلون الطعام ويمشون في الأسواق وجعلنا بعضكم لبعض فتنة أتصبرون وكان ربك بصيرا

translation: And those who do not hope for Our meeting, said, 'If only the angels were sent down to us, or we could see our Lord.' Indeed, they have become arrogant with what they were given. Indeed, they are people transgressing.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the attitude of those who do not have faith in the meeting with their Lord after death. They express their disbelief by saying that they would only believe if they saw the Lord or the angels were sent down to them. This statement reflects their arrogance and rejection of the signs of God that are already present in their lives. The verse highlights their transgression and emphasizes the consequences of their arrogance and disbelief.
orig: وقال الذين لا يرجون لقاءنا لولا أنزل علينا الملائكة أو نرى ربنا لقد استكبروا في أنفسهم وعتوا عتوا كبيرا

translation: A day on which the angels will be lined up, there will be no good news for the criminals, and they will say, 'A sealed-off place!'
interpretation: The verse describes a day of reckoning when the angels will be lined up, and there will be no good news for the wrongdoers. The phrase 'a sealed-off place' implies a sense of finality and confinement, suggesting that the wrongdoers will be cut off from any possibility of redemption or escape. The verse emphasizes the gravity of the situation for the criminals, and the severity of the consequences they will face. It serves as a warning for those who commit wrongdoing, urging them to repent and seek forgiveness before it is too late.
orig: يوم يرون الملائكة لا بشرى يومئذ للمجرمين ويقولون حجرا محجورا

translation: And We have already brought about destruction for many of the former peoples, and We have varied the signs so they might remember.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of previous communities as a result of their actions. It highlights the fact that these communities had been given various signs and warnings, but they failed to take heed. The destruction of these communities serves as a reminder for those who are still alive, urging them to reflect and learn from the past. The verse emphasizes the idea that history repeats itself, and that the consequences of not learning from past mistakes can be dire.
orig: وقدمنا إلى ما عملوا من عمل فجعلناه هباء منثورا

translation: The inhabitants of Paradise that day will be in a better place and happier.
interpretation: The verse describes the state of the people who will enter Paradise on the Day of Judgment. They will be in a 'better place' and 'happier' than those who will not enter Paradise. This verse serves as a source of hope and comfort for believers, reminding them of the ultimate reward for their faith and good deeds. It also emphasizes the great contrast between the fate of the righteous and the unrighteous, and encourages believers to strive for the ultimate goal of entering Paradise.
orig: أصحاب الجنة يومئذ خير مستقرا وأحسن مقيلا

translation: And (on) the day when the sky will be rent asunder with clouds, and the angels will be sent down, descending.
interpretation: The verse describes the events of the Day of Judgment, when the sky will be torn apart by clouds and angels will descend. The imagery of the sky being rent asunder and the descent of the angels emphasizes the awe-inspiring and dramatic nature of this event. The verse serves as a reminder of the impending Day of Judgment and encourages believers to prepare for it by living righteously and following God's commands.
orig: ويوم تشقق السماء بالغمام ونزل الملائكة تنزيلا

translation: The reign on that day will be for the Merciful, and it will be a difficult day for the disbelievers.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the Day of Judgment, when God's mercy will be the only source of power and authority. The verse contrasts the experience of this day for the believers and the disbelievers. For the believers, who have accepted God's mercy and followed His teachings, this day will be a time of relief and happiness. For the disbelievers, who have rejected God's mercy and lived in disobedience, this day will be a time of hardship and difficulty. The verse emphasizes the importance of accepting God's mercy and living a righteous life, as the consequences of disbelief and disobedience will be severe on the Day of Judgment.
orig: الملك يومئذ الحق للرحمن وكان يوما على الكافرين عسيرا

translation: And (the Day) when the wrong-doer will bite at his hands, he will say, 'Oh, I wish I had taken a way with the Messenger (Muhammad).',
interpretation: The verse speaks about the regret of a wrong-doer on the Day of Judgment. The person will be biting at his hands out of regret for his actions and will express his desire to have followed the way of the Prophet Muhammad. The verse highlights the regret and remorse that will be experienced by those who did not follow the right path and did not heed the message of the Prophet. It serves as a reminder of the importance of following the right path and the consequences of deviating from it.
orig: ويوم يعض الظالم على يديه يقول يا ليتني اتخذت مع الرسول سبيلا

translation: Woe to me! Would that I had not taken so-and-so as an intimate!
interpretation: The verse is a lamentation of regret from someone who has taken a certain person as a close companion or confidant. The speaker realizes too late that this association has brought them harm or led them astray. This verse can serve as a reminder to be mindful of the company we keep and to choose our friends and associates wisely, as they can have a significant impact on our character, values, and actions.
orig: يا ويلتى ليتني لم أتخذ فلانا خليلا

translation: Indeed, he who seduced me from the remembrance after it had come to me is the devil. And indeed, the devil is a deserter of man.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the power of Satan to lead people astray from the remembrance of God, even after they have received it. The verse emphasizes the deceitful and treacherous nature of Satan, who abandons people in their time of need. The verse serves as a reminder to be vigilant and steadfast in one's faith, as Satan is always waiting for an opportunity to lead people astray. It also highlights the importance of seeking guidance and protection from God, as only He can provide true protection and support.
orig: لقد أضلني عن الذكر بعد إذ جاءني وكان الشيطان للإنسان خذولا

translation: And the Messenger said, 'O Lord, indeed my people have taken this Qur'an as something to be abandoned.'
interpretation: The verse reveals the frustration and disappointment of the Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) upon seeing the rejection and negligence of his people towards the Qur'an. The verse can be interpreted as a reflection of the struggle of the Prophet and his followers in delivering the message of Islam, and the lack of understanding and acceptance from the majority of the people. It highlights the importance of the Qur'an as a guide for mankind, and the consequences of neglecting its teachings.
orig: وقال الرسول يا رب إن قومي اتخذوا هذا القرآن مهجورا

translation: And thus have We made for every prophet an enemy from among the criminals. But sufficient is your Lord as a Guide and a Helper.
interpretation: The verse highlights the challenges faced by prophets in the form of enemies and opposition from criminals and wrongdoers. Despite these challenges, the verse reassures the prophets that their Lord will provide sufficient guidance and help. The verse can be interpreted as a reminder that those who strive for justice and righteousness may face opposition and hostility from those who are opposed to their message. However, the verse offers reassurance that God will provide the necessary guidance and support to overcome these challenges.
orig: وكذلك جعلنا لكل نبي عدوا من المجرمين وكفى بربك هاديا ونصيرا

translation: And those who disbelieved say, 'Why was the Qur'an not revealed to him all at once?' Thus, so that We may strengthen your heart with it, and We have recited it in a measured recitation.
interpretation: The verse addresses the disbelievers' criticism of the Qur'an being revealed over a period of time, rather than all at once. The verse explains that the Qur'an was revealed gradually so that the Prophet's heart could be strengthened through its gradual revelation, and so that it could be recited in a measured and eloquent manner. The verse emphasizes the wisdom behind the gradual revelation of the Qur'an, and serves as a response to the disbelievers' criticism and rejection of the message of Islam.
orig: وقال الذين كفروا لولا نزل عليه القرآن جملة واحدة كذلك لنثبت به فؤادك ورتلناه ترتيلا

translation: And they will not come to you with a parable, except that We bring you the truth and a better explanation.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the superiority of God's knowledge and understanding over that of human beings. When people present an argument or a parable to prove a point, God is able to provide a more accurate and complete explanation. This verse emphasizes the limitations of human knowledge and understanding, and highlights the all-knowing and all-powerful nature of God. It serves as a reminder that no matter how convincing a human argument may seem, God's truth and understanding is always superior.
orig: ولا يأتونك بمثل إلا جئناك بالحق وأحسن تفسيرا

translation: Those who are gathered to Hell on their faces - such is their worst place and worst journey.
interpretation: The verse describes the fate of certain people who will be gathered and sent to Hell, facing downwards. This is depicted as the worst possible destination and the worst possible journey, indicating the gravity and severity of their situation. The verse serves as a warning to those who are not on the right path, emphasizing the dire consequences of continuing down a wrong and corrupt path.
orig: الذين يحشرون على وجوههم إلى جهنم أولئك شر مكانا وأضل سبيلا

translation: And We did indeed give Moses the Book and appointed his brother Aaron with him as an assistant.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the appointment of Moses and his brother Aaron as prophets and the giving of the Book (Torah) to Moses. The verse emphasizes the partnership and support between the two brothers in carrying out their prophetic mission. The appointment of Aaron as an assistant to Moses highlights the importance of collaboration and unity in fulfilling the divine mission, and the significance of the role of the prophets in guiding and leading the community.
orig: ولقد آتينا موسى الكتاب وجعلنا معه أخاه هارون وزيرا

translation: And We said, 'Go to the people who have rejected Our signs and surely, We will destroy them, [O Prophet], as a destruction.'
interpretation: The verse describes a command from God to the Prophet to go to the people who have rejected God's signs and to inform them of their impending destruction. The destruction is described as being complete and utter, emphasizing the severity of the punishment for those who deny God's messages. The verse serves as a warning to those who reject God's signs and messengers, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: فقلنا اذهبا إلى القوم الذين كذبوا بآياتنا فدمرناهم تدميرا

translation: And the people of Noah, when they disbelieved the messengers, We drowned them and made them a sign for mankind, and We have prepared a painful punishment for the wrongdoers.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the punishment of the people of Noah who disbelieved in the messengers. The verse highlights the consequences of disbelief and rejection of God's messengers. The people of Noah were drowned and made into a sign for mankind, serving as a reminder of the consequences of disbelief. The verse also emphasizes that a painful punishment has been prepared for the wrongdoers, serving as a warning for those who reject God's message and commit wrong actions.
orig: وقوم نوح لما كذبوا الرسل أغرقناهم وجعلناهم للناس آية وأعتدنا للظالمين عذابا أليما

translation: And [We destroyed] 'Aad and Thamud and the companions of the wood and many generations between them.
interpretation: The verse refers to the destruction of four specific communities: 'Aad, Thamud, the companions of the wood (known as the people of 'Lot), and many other generations that existed between them. The verse is a reminder of the fate of these communities who were destroyed by God due to their disbelief and disobedience. The listing of these communities serves as a warning to those who follow in their footsteps, emphasizing the consequences of rejecting God's message and persisting in sin and transgression.
orig: وعادا وثمود وأصحاب الرس وقرونا بين ذلك كثيرا

translation: And for every example, have We appointed a parable in the Qur'an. But every nation received its blow (of punishment), and then We brought them lowside by side.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the use of examples and parables in the Qur'an to illustrate and explain its teachings. Every nation received its own punishment, and they were all brought low together. The verse emphasizes the importance of understanding and reflecting on the examples and lessons in the Qur'an, as well as the consequences of ignoring or rejecting its teachings. The verse serves as a reminder that all nations will be held accountable for their actions and will ultimately face the consequences of their choices.
orig: وكلا ضربنا له الأمثال وكلا تبرنا تتبيرا

translation: And they (the previous people) came upon the town which rained the evil rain. Were they not seeing it (coming)? But they were not expecting any punishment.
interpretation: The verse describes the fate of a town that was destroyed by a shower of evil rain. Despite the signs of impending doom, the people of the town did not take heed and were caught off guard by the punishment. The verse serves as a reminder that divine punishment can strike unexpectedly, even in the midst of everyday life. It encourages people to be aware of their surroundings and to take heed of the signs of approaching danger, whether natural or moral. Ultimately, the verse calls for vigilance and mindfulness, both of which are necessary for avoiding divine retribution.
orig: ولقد أتوا على القرية التي أمطرت مطر السوء أفلم يكونوا يرونها بل كانوا لا يرجون نشورا

translation: And when they see you, they treat you only as a mockery: 'Is this the one whom Allah has sent as a messenger?'
interpretation: The verse describes the disbelievers' reaction to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) when they see him. They mock and ridicule him, treating him as insignificant and unworthy of being a messenger from Allah. The verse highlights the rejection and opposition that the Prophet faced from his people, and serves as a reminder that those who reject and mock the messengers of Allah will face severe consequences in the hereafter.
orig: وإذا رأوك إن يتخذونك إلا هزوا أهذا الذي بعث الله رسولا

translation: Indeed, we were close to worshipping our idols, except that we remained patient with them. And soon they will know, when they see the punishment, who is more lost.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the speaker's past temptation to worship idols, but they remained patient and did not give in to this temptation. The verse emphasizes the power of patience and perseverance in the face of adversity. The second part of the verse serves as a warning to the disbelievers, stating that when they see the punishment (of God), they will realize who is truly astray and lost.
orig: إن كاد ليضلنا عن آلهتنا لولا أن صبرنا عليها وسوف يعلمون حين يرون العذاب من أضل سبيلا

translation: Or have you seen the one who takes his own desire as his god? Then would you be a guardian over him?
interpretation: The verse is a rhetorical question directed at the reader, asking if they have seen someone who takes their own desires and whims as their god or deity. The verse is critical of those who prioritize their own desires above all else, and who do not acknowledge or submit to a higher power. The second part of the verse asks if the reader would take on the role of a guardian or protector over such a person, implying that it would be a futile and thankless task. The verse serves as a warning against self-centeredness and a call to recognize and submit to a higher power.
orig: أرأيت من اتخذ إلهه هواه أفأنت تكون عليه وكيلا

translation: Or do you think that most of them hear or understand? They are nothing but like livestock. Rather, they are even more astray from the path.
interpretation: The verse highlights the ignorance and lack of understanding of the disbelievers, who are compared to animals. The verse emphasizes that the disbelievers do not listen or comprehend the message of Islam, and are therefore lost and astray. The verse serves as a reminder that those who reject the message of Islam are not only ignorant, but are also on a path that leads to further deviation and error.
orig: أم تحسب أن أكثرهم يسمعون أو يعقلون إن هم إلا كالأنعام بل هم أضل سبيلا

translation: Have you not seen your Lord how He extends the shadow, and if He willed, He could make it stationary? Then We made the sun its guide.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the power and control of God over the natural world. It highlights the way God extends the shadow and has the ability to make it stationary, emphasizing His control over the movement of the sun and moon. The verse then mentions the sun as a guide or a reference point, indicating the precise and orderly way in which God has created and governs the universe. The verse serves as a reminder of God's power and wisdom, and invites the reader to reflect on the wonders of creation and the signs of God's existence and oneness.
orig: ألم تر إلى ربك كيف مد الظل ولو شاء لجعله ساكنا ثم جعلنا الشمس عليه دليلا

translation: Then We seized it with a single, swift seizure.
interpretation: The verse describes the swift and decisive action of God in seizing or taking control of something (possibly a town or a people, as implied in the previous verses). The use of the word 'qabdahn' (a single, swift seizure) emphasizes the suddenness and completeness of God's action, leaving no opportunity for resistance or escape. The verse serves as a reminder of God's absolute power and control over all things, and the futility of resistance against His will.
orig: ثم قبضناه إلينا قبضا يسيرا

translation: And He it is who made for you the night a clothing and sleep a rest, and made the day a resurrection.
interpretation: The verse describes the cyclical nature of day and night, and how God has made them serve the needs of human beings. The night is described as a 'clothing' that covers and protects, and 'sleep' as a rest that rejuvenates. The day is described as a 'resurrection' that brings new life and opportunities. The verse highlights the wisdom and mercy of God in creating the natural world and providing for the needs of His creation.
orig: وهو الذي جعل لكم الليل لباسا والنوم سباتا وجعل النهار نشورا

translation: And it is He who sends the winds as heralds of His mercy, and We send down pure water from the sky.
interpretation: The verse highlights the signs of God's mercy and compassion towards His creation. The 'winds' and 'pure water' are described as messengers of God's mercy, emphasizing the abundance and generosity of His blessings. The verse serves as a reminder of God's kindness and compassion towards all of His creation, and encourages people to be grateful for the blessings they receive and to recognize the signs of God's mercy in their lives.
orig: وهو الذي أرسل الرياح بشرا بين يدي رحمته وأنزلنا من السماء ماء طهورا

translation: We will surely bring the dead to life by it and make for them, by what We have created, livestock and many people.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the power of God to bring the dead back to life and to create for them sustenance and provisions. The use of the word 'it' likely refers to a specific event or sign that is being discussed elsewhere in the Qur'an. The verse emphasizes the abundance and diversity of the provisions that God will provide, including both livestock and a large number of people. The verse may serve as a reminder of God's power and mercy, and of the blessings that He bestows upon His creation.
orig: لنحيي به بلدة ميتا ونسقيه مما خلقنا أنعاما وأناسي كثيرا

translation: And We have already sent [messengers] to nations before you, [O Muhammad], and We seized them with suffering and hardship that perhaps they would humble themselves [to Us]. Instead, despite your Lord's clear signs and warnings, most of them remained ungrateful.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the sending of messengers to previous nations as a means of reminding them of God and the signs and warnings they received. Despite these efforts, most of the people remained ungrateful and did not heed the messages. The verse highlights the pattern of human behavior in rejecting God's signs and the consequences of this rejection, which is suffering and hardship. The verse serves as a reminder to the listeners of the Prophet Muhammad to reflect on the experiences of previous nations and to not follow in their footsteps.
orig: ولقد صرفناه بينهم ليذكروا فأبى أكثر الناس إلا كفورا

translation: And if We had willed, We could have sent a warner to every town.
interpretation: The verse highlights God's power and authority by stating that if He had willed, He could have sent a warner to every town. This statement serves to emphasize the importance of the message being conveyed and the significance of the opportunity for repentance and salvation being offered. The verse also underscores the fact that the responsibility for accepting or rejecting the message lies with the people themselves, as they have been given the free will to choose between right and wrong. The verse ultimately serves as a reminder of God's mercy and justice, as He gives people the chance to change their ways before it is too late.
orig: ولو شئنا لبعثنا في كل قرية نذيرا

translation: So do not obey the disbelievers, but strive against them with a great striving.
interpretation: The verse commands Muslims not to follow the ways of the disbelievers and to instead put forth a great effort in opposing them. This effort is not limited to physical struggle, but includes all forms of resistance, such as spreading the message of Islam and striving for justice. The verse emphasizes the importance of standing up for one's beliefs and not being swayed by the actions or opinions of those who reject the truth.
orig: فلا تطع الكافرين وجاهدهم به جهادا كبيرا

translation: And it is He who has released the two seas, one fresh and sweet and one salty and bitter, and He placed a barrier between them, a partition that is forbidden.
interpretation: The verse describes God as the one who has created and separated two seas, one fresh and sweet and the other salty and bitter, and placed a barrier between them. This serves as a reminder of God's power and control over nature. The barrier or partition mentioned in the verse symbolizes the limit or boundary that God has set, which cannot be crossed. This interpretation emphasizes the idea of order and balance in the natural world and the importance of respecting the boundaries established by God.
orig: وهو الذي مرج البحرين هذا عذب فرات وهذا ملح أجاج وجعل بينهما برزخا وحجرا محجورا

translation: And it is He who created man from water and then made him blood and flesh.
interpretation: The verse highlights the power and ability of God in creating human beings. It explains that God created man from water, and then transformed that water into blood and flesh, forming a complete human being. This serves as a reminder of the greatness and majesty of God, and the wonder of His creation. It also emphasizes the dependence of human beings on God for their very existence, as they were created from something as seemingly insignificant as water.
orig: وهو الذي خلق من الماء بشرا فجعله نسبا وصهرا وكان ربك قديرا

translation: And they worship besides Allah that which does not benefit them nor harm them, and the disbeliever is ever, against his Lord, an assistant [to Satan].
interpretation: The verse highlights the futility of worshipping false deities, as they can neither bring any benefit nor cause any harm. The verse also emphasizes the misguided nature of the disbelievers, who persist in their disbelief despite the clear signs and guidance from Allah. The verse suggests that the disbelievers are in fact aiding the devil in their disobedience and rebellion against Allah, and that they are ultimately accountable for their actions on the Day of Judgment.
orig: ويعبدون من دون الله ما لا ينفعهم ولا يضرهم وكان الكافر على ربه ظهيرا

translation: And We have not sent you except as a bearer of good news and a warner.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the role of the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) as a messenger from God who brings good news and warns people. The verse emphasizes that the Prophet Muhammad's (PBUH) mission is to bring the message of Islam to people and to warn them of the consequences of rejecting the message. The verse reminds the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) that his role is to deliver the message and not to force people to accept it, and that his responsibility is to convey the message clearly and in the best way possible.
orig: وما أرسلناك إلا مبشرا ونذيرا

translation: Say, 'I do not ask you for this message any payment, except for whoever wills to take a way to his Lord.'
interpretation: The verse is addressed to the Prophet Muhammad, instructing him to declare that he does not seek any reward or payment for delivering the message of Islam. The verse emphasizes that the Prophet's motivation for spreading the message is solely to guide people to the path of their Lord. The phrase 'whoever wills to take a way to his Lord' refers to those who choose to accept the message and follow the path of Islam. The verse highlights the voluntary nature of faith and the importance of personal responsibility in one's spiritual journey.
orig: قل ما أسألكم عليه من أجر إلا من شاء أن يتخذ إلى ربه سبيلا

translation: And put your trust in the Living One who does not die, and celebrate His praise. And He is sufficient for His servants as Knower.
interpretation: The verse speaks about placing trust in the Ever-Living God who never dies and praising Him. It emphasizes that God is sufficient for His servants as a Knower, indicating that God has complete knowledge and control over all things. The verse serves as a reminder to believers to place their trust in God and to praise and thank Him for His blessings and protection. It also emphasizes the all-knowing and all-powerful nature of God, which should give comfort and assurance to believers in times of difficulty and uncertainty.
orig: وتوكل على الحي الذي لا يموت وسبح بحمده وكفى به بذنوب عباده خبيرا

translation: He who created the heavens and the earth and what is between them in six days, then He established Himself above the Throne. Then interrogate concerning Him one who is knowledgeable.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the power and might of God as the creator of the heavens, the earth, and all that exists between them. It highlights the swiftness of His creation, having completed it in just six days. The verse also describes God as establishing Himself above the Throne, indicating His sovereignty and control over all of creation. The final sentence encourages the reader to seek knowledge about God from those who are knowledgeable, implying the importance of learning and understanding the nature of God and His will.
orig: الذي خلق السماوات والأرض وما بينهما في ستة أيام ثم استوى على العرش الرحمن فاسأل به خبيرا

translation: And when it is said to them, 'Prostrate to the Most Merciful,' they say, 'And what is the Most Merciful? Should we prostrate to what you command us?' And it increases them in their transgression.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the people's rejection and disbelief in the command to prostrate to the Most Merciful (Allah). Despite being ordered to prostrate, they question who the Most Merciful is and refuse to prostrate to Him. Their response is a form of defiance and transgression, and instead of submitting to Allah's command, they increase in their rejection and disobedience. The verse highlights the arrogance and ignorance of those who reject Allah's signs and messages, and serves as a reminder of the importance of submission and obedience to Allah.
orig: وإذا قيل لهم اسجدوا للرحمن قالوا وما الرحمن أنسجد لما تأمرنا وزادهم نفورا

translation: Blessed is He who has placed in the sky constellations and placed in it a lamp and a shining moon.
interpretation: The verse praises and glorifies God for His creation of the stars and the moon in the sky. The 'constellations' and the 'lamp' (which refers to the sun) are mentioned as evidence of God's power and wisdom in creating and arranging the celestial bodies. The 'shining moon' is described as a source of light in the night sky, providing guidance and illumination for people on earth. The verse serves as a reminder of God's greatness and His role as the creator and sustainer of the universe.
orig: تبارك الذي جعل في السماء بروجا وجعل فيها سراجا وقمرا منيرا

translation: And it is He who made the night and the day as successive stages for whoever wishes to remember or desires to express gratitude.
interpretation: The verse highlights the cyclical nature of day and night, which are presented as opportunities for reflection and gratitude. The phrase 'whoever wishes to remember' implies the importance of contemplation and reflection, while 'desires to express gratitude' emphasizes the importance of being thankful for God's blessings. The verse encourages believers to use the day and night as a means of spiritual growth and development, and to appreciate the divine wisdom and mercy behind the natural order of things.
orig: وهو الذي جعل الليل والنهار خلفة لمن أراد أن يذكر أو أراد شكورا

translation: And the servants of the Most Merciful are those who walk upon the earth in humility, and when the ignorant address them, they say 'peace.'
interpretation: The verse describes the true believers as 'servants of the Most Merciful' who are characterized by their humility and peaceful demeanor. Even when they are provoked by the ignorant, they respond with peace and avoid confrontation. This verse encourages believers to embody these qualities and to respond to negativity with kindness and patience, reflecting the mercy and compassion of the Divine.
orig: وعباد الرحمن الذين يمشون على الأرض هونا وإذا خاطبهم الجاهلون قالوا سلاما

translation: And who bow and prostrate themselves in worship of their Lord,
interpretation: The verse highlights the actions of those who are devoted to their Lord through prayer and worship, specifically mentioning the physical acts of bowing (ruku) and prostration (sujood) during prayer. These actions are a demonstration of humility and submission to God, and are an important aspect of Islamic worship. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of regular prayer and devotion to God, and emphasizes the importance of physical worship in addition to spiritual devotion.
orig: والذين يبيتون لربهم سجدا وقياما

translation: And those who say, 'Our Lord, avert from us the punishment of Hell, indeed its punishment is an affliction unescapable,'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the people who are aware of the punishment of Hell and are seeking refuge from it. They recognize the severity of the punishment, describing it as an affliction that cannot be escaped. This verse emphasizes the importance of seeking protection from Hellfire, and acknowledging the gravity of the sins that could lead to it. It is a reminder for believers to constantly seek forgiveness and strive to stay away from sins.
orig: والذين يقولون ربنا اصرف عنا عذاب جهنم إن عذابها كان غراما

translation: Indeed, it was an evil abode and a place to rest.
interpretation: The verse describes a place as being evil and a bad place to stay. This description could be referring to a physical location, such as a town or a city, or it could be a metaphorical reference to a state of being or a situation. Regardless of the specific context, the verse conveys a sense of negativity and a warning about the dangers of remaining in such a place or state. It may serve as a reminder to seek out positive and beneficial environments and to avoid those that are harmful or detrimental.
orig: إنها ساءت مستقرا ومقاما

translation: And those who, when they spend, are neither profligate nor miserly, but hold a balance (just) between those (extremes).
interpretation: The verse speaks about the balance and moderation that should be practiced in spending. Those who spend should avoid being excessive or wasteful (profligate) and should also avoid being stingy or miserly. Instead, they should find a balance between these two extremes. This balance reflects a sound and virtuous character, and it is a way of showing gratitude for the blessings that one has received. The verse encourages Muslims to be mindful of their spending habits and to use their wealth in a responsible and ethical manner.
orig: والذين إذا أنفقوا لم يسرفوا ولم يقتروا وكان بين ذلك قواما

translation: And those who do not call upon another god along with Allah and do not kill the soul which Allah has forbidden, except for just cause, and do not commit fornication; and whoever does this shall meet a requital of sin.
interpretation: The verse sets forth the moral code of conduct for Muslims and emphasizes the importance of monotheism and respect for the sanctity of human life. It forbids the worship of any god other than Allah, the unlawful killing of any soul, and adultery. The verse warns that those who commit these sins will face a severe punishment for their actions. The verse also highlights the principle of justice, allowing the taking of a soul only in cases of just cause. Overall, the verse serves as a guide for Muslims in leading a righteous life and adhering to the laws of God.
orig: والذين لا يدعون مع الله إلها آخر ولا يقتلون النفس التي حرم الله إلا بالحق ولا يزنون ومن يفعل ذلك يلق أثاما

translation: His punishment is doubled on the Day of Resurrection, and he will abide therein in disgrace.
interpretation: The verse describes the punishment of a specific person on the Day of Resurrection, which is doubled and eternal. The person will remain in a state of disgrace and shame, experiencing the consequences of their actions. The verse emphasizes the severity of the punishment on the Day of Resurrection for those who have committed sins and wrongdoings, and serves as a warning for people to reflect on their actions and seek forgiveness.
orig: يضاعف له العذاب يوم القيامة ويخلد فيه مهانا

translation: Except for those who repent, believe, and do righteous work. For them, Allah will replace their evil deeds with good. And ever is Allah Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: The verse offers a way out for those who have committed wrongdoings, providing them with a path to redemption. By repenting, believing, and performing righteous deeds, they can have their sins replaced with good deeds, demonstrating Allah's infinite mercy and forgiveness. The verse encourages positive change, emphasizing that through repentance and good actions, individuals can transform their lives and earn Allah's favor.
orig: إلا من تاب وآمن وعمل عملا صالحا فأولئك يبدل الله سيئاتهم حسنات وكان الله غفورا رحيما

translation: And if someone repents and does righteous work, then indeed, God will turn to him in forgiveness. He is all-forgiving, all-merciful.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the opportunity for repentance and forgiveness for those who have committed wrongdoings. It emphasizes the importance of both repentance and righteous actions, as both are necessary for God's forgiveness. The verse also highlights God's attributes of being all-forgiving and all-merciful, showing that He is always ready to forgive those who turn to Him in repentance and strive to do good. The verse serves as a message of hope and mercy for those who have made mistakes, encouraging them to seek forgiveness and strive to do better.
orig: ومن تاب وعمل صالحا فإنه يتوب إلى الله متابا

translation: And those who do not bear false witness, and when they pass by ignorance, they pass by with dignity.
interpretation: The verse describes the behavior of individuals who do not engage in falsehood or slander, and who conduct themselves with dignity and restraint when they encounter ignorance or provocations. The verse emphasizes the importance of truthfulness and integrity in one's actions and words, and the need to maintain one's composure and honor even in the face of provocation or ignorance. The verse serves as a moral guideline for believers, encouraging them to strive for virtuous behavior and to avoid engaging in gossip, slander, or other forms of falsehood.
orig: والذين لا يشهدون الزور وإذا مروا باللغو مروا كراما

translation: And [for] those who, when reminded of the signs of their Lord, do not fall down in humble prostration [in prayer],
interpretation: This verse describes the attitude of those who, when reminded of the signs or messages of their Lord, do not respond with humility and submission. The act of prostration or bowing down in prayer is a physical expression of submission and a sign of one's recognition of God's greatness and power. The verse highlights the importance of responding to God's messages with humility and reverence, and serves as a reminder that failure to do so is a sign of a closed heart and a lack of true faith.
orig: والذين إذا ذكروا بآيات ربهم لم يخروا عليها صما وعميانا

translation: And those who say, 'Our Lord, give us from among our wives and offspring the comfort of our eyes and make us a leader for the righteous.'
interpretation: The verse is a supplication made by righteous individuals who are seeking blessings from God. They ask for their wives and offspring to be the source of their joy and comfort. Furthermore, they request to be made leaders for those who are righteous. This verse highlights the importance of family in the lives of believers and their desire to lead and guide others towards righteousness. The verse can serve as a reminder of the significance of family and the responsibility of believers to be a positive influence and guide for others.
orig: والذين يقولون ربنا هب لنا من أزواجنا وذرياتنا قرة أعين واجعلنا للمتقين إماما

translation: Those will be admitted to the chamber because of their patience, and there they will be greeted with salutations and peace.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the reward of those who are patient and persevere. They will be admitted to a chamber, which can be interpreted as a symbol of paradise or a place of peace and security. The verse emphasizes that this reward is given because of their patience and endurance. In addition, the verse mentions that they will be greeted with salutations and peace, indicating a warm and welcoming reception. The verse serves as a source of hope and motivation for those who are facing difficulties and hardships, encouraging them to be patient and endure, as they will be rewarded for their efforts.
orig: أولئك يجزون الغرفة بما صبروا ويلقون فيها تحية وسلاما

translation: And they will abide therein forever, a true abode and paradise.
interpretation: The verse describes a place where people will live in a state of perpetual goodness and stability. The words 'abide therein forever' suggest that this is a permanent and eternal state, while 'a true abode and paradise' convey the idea of a desirable and pleasant place. Overall, the verse conveys a sense of peace, happiness, and fulfillment, and may be interpreted as a promise of eternal reward for those who lead righteous lives.
orig: خالدين فيها حسنت مستقرا ومقاما

translation: Say, 'My Lord would not concern Himself with you were it not for your prayer. But you have denied (it), and will soon be in severe punishment.'
interpretation: The verse is a message from the prophet, addressed to the disbelievers, reminding them that their prayer is the only reason why God has not yet punished them for their disbelief. However, the verse also highlights that the disbelievers have denied this truth and as a result, they will soon face severe punishment. The verse emphasizes the importance of prayer and the consequences of disbelief, reminding the readers of the power of God and the importance of faith.
orig: قل ما يعبأ بكم ربي لولا دعاؤكم فقد كذبتم فسوف يكون لزاما

translation: N
interpretation: N
orig: طسم

translation: Those are the verses of the Clear Book.
interpretation: The verse is a reference to the Qur'an as the Clear Book, implying that its messages and teachings are clear and easy to understand for those who seek guidance. It serves as a reminder of the divine origin of the Qur'an and the importance of reflecting on its verses for spiritual growth and understanding.
orig: تلك آيات الكتاب المبين

translation: Perhaps you (Muhammad) are feeling sorry that they will not become believers.
interpretation: The verse addresses the Prophet Muhammad, reminding him that he cannot force others to believe and that it is not his responsibility if they choose not to accept the message of Islam. The verse may serve as a reminder to the Prophet and to all believers to be patient and steadfast in the face of rejection and to continue to convey the message of Islam with wisdom and kindness.
orig: لعلك باخع نفسك ألا يكونوا مؤمنين

translation: If We had sent down upon them a reminder from the heaven, while they were disputing, then surely, the assuring disbelievers would have said, 'This is but obvious magic!',
interpretation: The verse describes the response of the disbelievers to a sign or reminder sent down from the heavens during a time of dispute. Despite the potential significance of the sign, the disbelievers dismiss it as mere magic, demonstrating their unwillingness to accept the truth and their rejection of God's message. The verse serves as a warning to those who reject God's signs and emphasizes the consequences of disbelief.
orig: إن نشأ ننزل عليهم من السماء آية فظلت أعناقهم لها خاضعين

translation: And whenever a reminder comes to them from the Most Merciful, they turn away from it.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the people's rejection and dismissal of the signs and messages from the Most Merciful (one of the names of God in Islam, referring to His compassion and mercy). Despite receiving reminders and messages, the people turn away from them, showing their disbelief and rejection of God's mercy. The verse highlights the hard-heartedness and stubbornness of these people, and serves as a warning to those who reject God's signs and messages, emphasizing the importance of being open and receptive to God's guidance and mercy.
orig: وما يأتيهم من ذكر من الرحمن محدث إلا كانوا عنه معرضين

translation: Indeed, they have disbelieved, so news of what they used to mock will come to them.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the unbelievers who rejected the message of Islam and mocked the believers. The verse warns them that they will receive news of their own mockery and disbelief, indicating that they will face the consequences of their actions. The verse serves as a reminder that God is aware of all actions, even those that are done in mockery or disbelief, and that He will hold people accountable for their actions on the Day of Judgment.
orig: فقد كذبوا فسيأتيهم أنباء ما كانوا به يستهزئون

translation: Have they not seen how We have established upon the earth a firmly rooted stabilizer for every kind [of thing]?
interpretation: The verse highlights the power and wisdom of God in creating and maintaining the earth and all the different kinds of things that exist on it. The 'firmly rooted stabilizer' refers to the natural systems and processes that support and sustain life on earth. The verse encourages people to reflect on the signs of God's creation and to consider the intricate balance and order that exists in the natural world. It suggests that by understanding and appreciating this balance, people can gain a deeper understanding of their place in the world and their relationship with God.
orig: أولم يروا إلى الأرض كم أنبتنا فيها من كل زوج كريم

translation: Indeed in that is a sign, but most of them were not believers.
interpretation: The verse refers to a sign or evidence of God's power and justice, which should serve as a reminder and a warning to people. However, despite the clear signs and evidence, most people did not believe or have faith. The verse highlights the common human tendency to ignore or reject the truth, even when it is presented clearly. The verse may also imply a sense of disappointment or frustration on the part of the speaker, who has presented the truth to the people but has been met with disbelief and rejection.
orig: إن في ذلك لآية وما كان أكثرهم مؤمنين

translation: And indeed, your Lord is the Exalted in Might, the Merciful.
interpretation: The verse affirms the greatness and power of God, describing Him as the Exalted in Might. This emphasizes God's strength, sovereignty and authority over all of creation. At the same time, the verse also highlights God's mercy and compassion, describing Him as the Merciful. This reminds us that despite His great power, God is also loving and forgiving towards His creations. The verse serves as a reminder of God's majesty and His boundless mercy, inspiring awe and reverence in the hearts of the believers.
orig: وإن ربك لهو العزيز الرحيم

translation: And when your Lord called Moses, 'Go to the people who are unjust.'
interpretation: The verse relates the story of Moses being called by God to confront the people who were committing injustices. The verse emphasizes the responsibility of the prophets to stand up against injustice and guide people towards the right path. It also highlights the importance of addressing and correcting unjust actions, as they can lead to negative consequences. The verse can be seen as a call for individuals to take a stand against injustice and work towards creating a just society.
orig: وإذ نادى ربك موسى أن ائت القوم الظالمين

translation: The people of Pharaoh, will they not be mindful?
interpretation: The verse is a rhetorical question addressed to the people of Pharaoh, urging them to be mindful or fearful of God. It implies that despite the many signs and warnings they have received, they continue to be heedless and disobedient. The verse serves as a reminder to the importance of having consciousness and fear of God, and the consequences of ignoring His signs and commands.
orig: قوم فرعون ألا يتقون

translation: He said, 'My Lord, I fear they will deny me.'
interpretation: The verse is a quote from a prophet or messenger who is expressing his concern and fear to God about the people denying or rejecting his message. The prophet is aware of the challenges and difficulties that come with delivering the message, and is seeking God's support and guidance in fulfilling his mission. The verse highlights the importance of patience, perseverance, and reliance on God in the face of adversity, and serves as a reminder that the success of the mission ultimately lies in God's hands.
orig: قال رب إني أخاف أن يكذبون

translation: And my heart was constricted, and my tongue did not articulate, so I sent unto Haroon.
interpretation: The verse describes the speaker's difficulty in communicating their message, as their heart was constricted and their tongue was unable to articulate. In response, the speaker sent for Haroon (Aaron), who was known for his eloquence and ability to speak to people. The verse can be interpreted as a recognition of the importance of finding the right words and the right person to convey a message effectively, especially in times of difficulty or distress.
orig: ويضيق صدري ولا ينطلق لساني فأرسل إلى هارون

translation: And upon them is a sin, so I fear they will kill me.
interpretation: The verse speaks about someone who has wronged others and as a result, they fear for their life. The person is aware of their wrongdoing and the anger it has caused in others, to the point where they fear for their own safety. This verse can serve as a reminder of the consequences of our actions and the impact they can have on those around us. It also highlights the importance of seeking forgiveness and making amends for any wrongs we may have committed.
orig: ولهم علي ذنب فأخاف أن يقتلون

translation: He said, 'No, rather take my daughters. Indeed, you are among those who are guided.'
interpretation: The verse relates the story of a prophet who offers his guests, who had initially asked for his wife's hand in marriage, his daughters instead. The prophet's response highlights his wisdom and generosity, and his recognition of what is truly important. The phrase 'Indeed, you are among those who are guided' serves as a confirmation of the guests' righteousness and their acceptance of the prophet's guidance. This verse can be interpreted as a reminder of the importance of guiding others towards what is right and recognizing and appreciating those who are rightly guided.
orig: قال كلا فاذهبا بآياتنا إنا معكم مستمعون

translation: And they said to Pharaoh, 'Indeed, we are messengers of the Lord of the worlds.'
interpretation: The verse relays the message of Moses and Aaron to Pharaoh, identifying themselves as messengers of the Lord of the universes. This statement marks the beginning of a series of interactions between the two parties, where Moses and Aaron call upon Pharaoh to release the Israelites from their bondage in Egypt and allow them to worship their God. The verse highlights the courage and determination of Moses and Aaron in standing up to Pharaoh and proclaiming their faith, despite the danger and oppression they faced.
orig: فأتيا فرعون فقولا إنا رسول رب العالمين

translation: And We shall send the Children of Israel with power.
interpretation: The verse speaks about God's plan to send the Children of Israel with power. The verse suggests that the Children of Israel will be given strength and support by God, and they will be able to overcome their adversaries. The verse may refer to the Exodus of the Israelites from Egypt and their journey to the Promised Land, which was made possible through God's help and guidance. The verse may also be interpreted as a promise of God's continued support and protection of the Israelites throughout their history.
orig: أن أرسل معنا بني إسرائيل

translation: He said, 'Have We not favored you over other creation? Have you stayed among us for years of your life?'
interpretation: The verse is a rhetorical question posed by someone (the speaker is not specified in the verse) to a person they are addressing. The speaker reminds the person of the favor and blessings that have been bestowed upon them, as indicated by the phrase 'have We not favored you over other creation?'. The speaker also points out the amount of time the person has spent among them, emphasizing the duration with the phrase 'have you stayed among us for years of your life?'. The verse could be interpreted as a rebuke or a call to accountability, where the speaker is reminding the person of their privileges and the time they have been given, and perhaps suggesting that they have not lived up to those blessings.
orig: قال ألم نربك فينا وليدا ولبثت فينا من عمرك سنين

translation: And you have done your deed which you have done, and now you are of the unbelievers.
interpretation: The verse is a statement of fact, addressing an individual who has committed an unbelieving act. The phrase 'you have done your deed' implies that the individual has made a choice and taken an action that is indicative of unbelief. The statement 'now you are of the unbelievers' confirms the individual's status as an unbeliever. The verse serves as a reminder that actions have consequences and that choices have a lasting impact on one's identity and standing before God.
orig: وفعلت فعلتك التي فعلت وأنت من الكافرين

translation: He said, 'I did it while I was among the strayers.',
interpretation: The verse is a quote from a person who has acknowledged their mistake or wrongdoing. They confess to having committed an act of sin or transgression while they were among those who have lost their way, or those who are astray. This person recognizes that they were not on the right path, and that their actions were influenced by their misguidance. The verse can serve as a reminder that acknowledging and recognizing one's mistakes is an important step towards repentance and seeking forgiveness from God.
orig: قال فعلتها إذا وأنا من الضالين

translation: So I fled from you when I feared you, and my Lord granted me judgment and made me one of the messengers.
interpretation: The verse describes the story of a prophet who had to flee from his people due to fear of their reaction to his message. The prophet's fear was justified, as his people did not respond positively to his call to worship one God. After fleeing from his people, the prophet sought refuge and protection from his Lord. As a result, God granted him wisdom and made him one of the messengers, entrusting him with the responsibility of delivering God's message. This verse emphasizes the importance of standing up for what is right, even if it means facing opposition and danger. It also highlights the significance of God's protection and support for those who are dedicated to spreading His message.
orig: ففررت منكم لما خفتكم فوهب لي ربي حكما وجعلني من المرسلين

translation: And that was a favor that We bestowed upon the Children of Israel, that We appointed among them twelve leaders.
interpretation: The verse refers to a specific favor that God had granted to the Children of Israel, which was the appointment of twelve leaders among them. This favor was a sign of God's special relationship with the Children of Israel and His guidance for them. The verse highlights the importance of leadership and the role of leaders in guiding and supporting their communities. At the same time, it reminds the reader of the blessings that come from God and the importance of being grateful for them.
orig: وتلك نعمة تمنها علي أن عبدت بني إسرائيل

translation: Pharaoh said, 'And what is the Lord of the worlds?'
interpretation: Pharaoh, a powerful and arrogant ruler in ancient Egypt, questioned the existence and authority of the 'Lord of the worlds', expressing his disbelief and challenging the power of God. This verse can be interpreted as a symbol of the human tendency towards arrogance, disbelief, and rejection of God's authority. It highlights the importance of faith, humility, and submission to God's will, and serves as a reminder that God is the ultimate power and authority in the universe.
orig: قال فرعون وما رب العالمين

translation: Said He, the Lord of the heavens and the earth, and all that is between them: 'If you are truly believers!'
interpretation: The verse is a direct quote from God, who challenges the people to prove their faith by their actions. The phrase 'If you are truly believers' implies that mere verbal declaration of faith is not sufficient, and that true belief must be demonstrated through righteous deeds. The verse serves as a reminder that faith and action are intertwined and that hypocrisy and insincerity will not be accepted by God. The verse encourages the believers to examine their beliefs and actions and strive for righteousness and sincerity in their faith.
orig: قال رب السماوات والأرض وما بينهما إن كنتم موقنين

translation: He said to those around him, 'Do you not hear?'
interpretation: The verse depicts a situation where an individual is addressing a group of people, expressing his frustration and surprise that they are not listening to him. The verse could be interpreted as a call for attention and a reminder of the importance of listening and engaging in meaningful communication with those around us. It highlights the significance of paying attention to the voices and perspectives of others, and the consequences of ignoring or dismissing their concerns.
orig: قال لمن حوله ألا تستمعون

translation: Said your Lord and the Lord of your first forefathers.
interpretation: The verse speaks about God, who is the Lord of both the listener(s) and their first ancestors. The use of 'your Lord' emphasizes the personal relationship between God and the listener(s), while 'the Lord of your first forefathers' serves to establish a continuity and connection between the past and the present. This verse can be interpreted as a reminder of God's presence and involvement in the history and lives of the listener(s) and their ancestors, and of the continuity of His relationship with them.
orig: قال ربكم ورب آبائكم الأولين

translation: He said, 'Indeed, your messenger who has been sent to you is mad.'
interpretation: The verse is a quote from the disbelievers who rejected the message of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). They called the Prophet a madman, rejecting his message and denying his prophethood. The verse emphasizes the rejection and disbelief of the people in the face of the truth, highlighting their stubbornness and unwillingness to accept the message of Islam. The verse serves as a reminder of the challenges and opposition that the Prophet faced in his mission to spread the message of Islam, and the perseverance and patience that he displayed in the face of adversity.
orig: قال إن رسولكم الذي أرسل إليكم لمجنون

translation: Said He, the Lord of the east and the west: 'So will it be, if you are able to discern.'
interpretation: The verse is a statement from God, the Lord of the east and the west, in response to an unspecified group of people. The statement implies that God is aware of the limitations of human understanding and perception, and challenges the people to use their intellect and reasoning abilities to comprehend the divine message. The verse suggests that if the people are able to fully understand and discern the meaning of God's message, then the outcome will be as God has described. The verse encourages reflection and contemplation, and invites the reader to engage with the divine message in a thoughtful and deliberate way.
orig: قال رب المشرق والمغرب وما بينهما إن كنتم تعقلون

translation: He said, 'If you ascribe to me any partner, I will surely make you one of the doomed.'
interpretation: The verse is a warning from God, spoken through a prophet or messenger, to those who are considering associating partners with God. The verse emphasizes the seriousness of this act, stating that those who commit it will be among the doomed. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of monotheism, the belief in the oneness of God, and the consequences of rejecting this fundamental principle of Islam.
orig: قال لئن اتخذت إلها غيري لأجعلنك من المسجونين

translation: They said, 'If you have come to us with a sign, show it!'
interpretation: The verse is a response from the disbelievers to the prophet Muhammad, challenging him to prove his prophethood by showing them a clear sign. The verse highlights the skepticism and rejection of the disbelievers towards the prophet and their refusal to believe without seeing concrete evidence. It serves as a reminder of the challenges and opposition that the prophet faced in his mission to spread the message of Islam.
orig: قال أولو جئتك بشيء مبين

translation: He said, 'Bring it to me, if you are of the truthful.'
interpretation: The verse is a challenge issued by someone to the speaker, asking them to bring something if they are truthful. The verse can be interpreted as a test of the speaker's honesty and sincerity. The person issuing the challenge may be skeptical of the speaker's claims or statements and is asking for proof or evidence to support them. The verse highlights the importance of truthfulness and the consequences of making false claims or statements.
orig: قال فأت به إن كنت من الصادقين

translation: And he threw down his staff, and behold, it was a clear serpent.
interpretation: The verse describes the story of Moses when he was called by God to lead the Israelites out of Egypt. In this particular moment, God asks Moses to throw down his staff, and when he does, it turns into a 'clear serpent'. This event is a sign from God, demonstrating His power and authority, and confirming Moses' role as a prophet. The transformation of the staff into a serpent also symbolizes the power of God to transform and change things, as well as His ability to overcome the forces of evil and darkness. The verse serves as a reminder of God's power and sovereignty, and of the importance of following and trusting in God's messengers.
orig: فألقى عصاه فإذا هي ثعبان مبين

translation: And [when I reprimanded the angel who had been blowing the Trumpet, he] removed his hand, and behold, it was white [with rust] for the observers.
interpretation: This verse is a part of a larger narrative in which the angel who had been blowing the Trumpet is being reprimanded by God. When the angel removes his hand, it is described as being white with rust. The white color symbolizes purity and the rust symbolizes the negative effects of not fulfilling one's duties. The verse can be interpreted as a reminder of the consequences of neglecting one's responsibilities and the importance of being mindful of one's actions.
orig: ونزع يده فإذا هي بيضاء للناظرين

translation: He said, 'Indeed, this is a knowledgeable sorcerer.'
interpretation: The verse is a statement made by someone (who is not identified in the verse) about the Prophet Musa (Moses), referring to him as a 'knowledgeable sorcerer'. However, the verse is generally understood in the Qur'an as a mischaracterization of Musa's abilities. Musa was not a sorcerer, but a prophet sent by God. The verse can be interpreted as a reflection of the ignorance and disbelief of those who failed to recognize Musa's true nature and mission.
