The verse emphasizes the importance of worshiping only one God and the consequences of not doing so. It serves as a reminder to the listeners to reflect on their actions and to follow the right path.
orig: قل الحمد لله وسلام على عباده الذين اصطفى آلله خير أما يشركون

translation: Do you feel secure that He, who is over the heaven, will not cause the earth to swallow you up when it quakes? Or do you feel secure that He, who is over the heaven, will not send against you a storm of stones? Then you shall know how My warning is.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the power and control of God over the heavens and the earth, and how He can cause natural disasters and calamities to strike at any time. The verse is a reminder of the insignificance of human beings in the face of God's power and might. It warns those who deny or ignore God's existence and authority, and reminds them of the consequences of their disbelief and arrogance. The verse serves as a call to humility and submission to God, and a reminder of the Day of Judgment when all will be held accountable for their actions.
orig: أمن خلق السماوات والأرض وأنزل لكم من السماء ماء فأنبتنا به حدائق ذات بهجة ما كان لكم أن تنبتوا شجرها أإله مع الله بل هم قوم يعدلون

translation: Have they not seen that We made the earth stationary and placed within it anchors, and We made on it mountains standing firm, and We have made between the two seas a barrier? Is it not then a sign for them? But most of them do not believe.
interpretation: The verse highlights the signs of God's power and creation in the natural world. It mentions the stability of the earth, the presence of mountains, and the barrier between the seas as evidence of God's existence and power. Despite these signs, many people still do not believe. The verse serves as a reminder to those who deny God's existence or power, urging them to reflect on the wonders of the natural world and the evidence of God's hand in creation.
orig: أمن جعل الأرض قرارا وجعل خلالها أنهارا وجعل لها رواسي وجعل بين البحرين حاجزا أإله مع الله بل أكثرهم لا يعلمون

translation: One who responds to the distressed one who calls upon him, and removes evil, and makes you successors in the earth - is there a deity with Allah? Little do you remember.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the power and greatness of God, who responds to those in distress, removes evil, and gives people the opportunity to succeed and thrive on earth. The verse asks the question 'is there a deity with Allah?' implying that there is no other god but Allah, who has these qualities and abilities. The verse also highlights the forgetfulness of people, as they quickly forget the blessings and mercies they receive from God and fail to remember and acknowledge His greatness.
orig: أمن يجيب المضطر إذا دعاه ويكشف السوء ويجعلكم خلفاء الأرض أإله مع الله قليلا ما تذكرون

translation: Is He [not best] who guides you through the depths of darkness on land and sea, and who sends the winds as heralds of His mercy? Is there another god with God? High is God above what they associate with Him.
interpretation: The verse highlights the power and greatness of God by describing His ability to guide people through the darkness on land and sea, and by sending the winds as a sign of His mercy. The verse then asks a rhetorical question, 'Is there another god with God?' implying that there is no other god but God. The verse emphasizes the uniqueness and oneness of God, and rejects the idea of associating partners with Him. The verse serves as a reminder of God's power and greatness, and the importance of recognizing and worshipping Him alone.
orig: أمن يهديكم في ظلمات البر والبحر ومن يرسل الرياح بشرا بين يدي رحمته أإله مع الله تعالى الله عما يشركون

translation: Does He who begins the creation then repeats it not have power over all things? And how can you fear anything else than Allah, while He is encompassing of all things? And to Allah returns the end of all affairs. So, if you are in doubt about what We have revealed to Our servant, then produce a surah like it and call upon your witnesses other than Allah, if you are truthful.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the power and ability of God, who is capable of beginning and repeating the creation. The verse challenges the disbelievers to produce a surah (chapter) like it if they are truthful in their doubt about the revelation to the Prophet Muhammad. The verse also reminds the disbelievers that they should not fear anything other than Allah, as He encompasses all things and is the ultimate judge. The verse serves as a reminder of the power and greatness of God, and the futility of worshiping or fearing anything other than Him.
orig: أمن يبدأ الخلق ثم يعيده ومن يرزقكم من السماء والأرض أإله مع الله قل هاتوا برهانكم إن كنتم صادقين

translation: Say, 'None in the heavens and earth knows the unseen except Allah, and they do not perceive when they will be resurrected.',
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the power and knowledge of Allah, stating that no one in the heavens or the earth knows the unseen except for Him. This includes the time of resurrection, which is unknown to all beings. The verse encourages the believers to have faith in Allah's power and knowledge, and to understand that the time of resurrection is in His hands. It also serves as a reminder of the importance of living a righteous life, as the time of resurrection will come unexpectedly for all.
orig: قل لا يعلم من في السماوات والأرض الغيب إلا الله وما يشعرون أيان يبعثون

translation: But indeed, We will make them taste the nearer punishment before the greater punishment, so that they may return.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the sequence of punishments that will be faced by the disbelievers. The 'nearer punishment' refers to the trials and difficulties that they will experience in this world as a consequence of their disbelief. This punishment will serve as a warning and an opportunity for them to repent and turn back to God before the 'greater punishment' in the hereafter. The verse emphasizes the importance of taking heed of the signs and warnings in this world, and using them as a means to prepare for the ultimate judgment in the hereafter.
orig: بل ادارك علمهم في الآخرة بل هم في شك منها بل هم منها عمون

translation: And those who disbelieved said, 'Are we to be returned to dust, and our forefathers as well?'
interpretation: The verse presents a rhetorical question from the disbelievers, expressing their disbelief and denial of the resurrection and the Day of Judgment. They question the idea of being returned to dust, implying that they do not believe in the concept of life after death and the resurrection of the dead. The verse emphasizes the disbelievers' denial and rejection of the fundamental teachings of Islam, highlighting the importance of faith and belief in the unseen for the salvation of the believers on the Day of Judgment.
orig: وقال الذين كفروا أإذا كنا ترابا وآباؤنا أئنا لمخرجون

translation: We had indeed promised this to you and to our forefathers before, that this is not but tales of the former peoples.
interpretation: The verse is a reminder that the events being described have been previously promised and foretold, not only to the current generation but also to their ancestors. The verse emphasizes that these events are not mere stories or legends of the past, but a reality that has been promised. The verse may be referring to the punishment or consequences of the actions of the unjust and disbelieving people, as mentioned in the previous verse. The verse serves as a warning and a reminder for the people to take heed and reflect on the consequences of their actions.
orig: لقد وعدنا هذا نحن وآباؤنا من قبل إن هذا إلا أساطير الأولين

translation: Say, 'Travel through the land and observe how was the end of the criminals.'
interpretation: The verse is a command from God to the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) to tell the people to travel through the land and observe the fate of the criminals. The verse encourages people to reflect on the consequences of the actions of those who committed crimes and the punishment they received. It serves as a reminder that the actions of people have consequences and that those who commit crimes will ultimately be punished. The verse also encourages people to learn from the past and to avoid making the same mistakes as the criminals did. By observing the end of the criminals, people can gain a better understanding of the importance of living a righteous life and following the commands of God.
orig: قل سيروا في الأرض فانظروا كيف كان عاقبة المجرمين

translation: So be patient with what they say, and ignore them. And leave Me alone with those who deny the truth - I will soon bring them to My punishment.
interpretation: The verse speaks about how to deal with those who deny the truth and spread mischief. The verse advises the believers to be patient and not to get distressed by their words or actions. It also advises them to ignore them and leave the matter to God. The verse emphasizes that God will deal with the deniers and will bring them to His punishment. The verse serves as a reminder to the believers to trust in God's plan and not to get distracted by the mischief of the deniers.
orig: ولا تحزن عليهم ولا تكن في ضيق مما يمكرون

translation: And they say, 'When will this promise be (fulfilled), if you are truthful?'
interpretation: The verse is spoken by the disbelievers who are questioning the promise of God and the prophet. They are expressing their disbelief and challenging the prophet by asking 'when' the promise will be fulfilled, implying that they do not believe it will happen. The verse highlights the skepticism and rejection of the message by the disbelievers, and the patience and perseverance required by the prophet and the believers in the face of such opposition.
orig: ويقولون متى هذا الوعد إن كنتم صادقين

translation: Say, 'Perhaps (the reminder of) those who were before you (as transgressors) is close to you.'
interpretation: The verse is a command to the Prophet Muhammad to say or recite the statement 'Perhaps (the reminder of) those who were before you (as transgressors) is close to you.' This statement serves as a warning to the listeners or readers of the Quran to take heed of the consequences of those who came before them and committed transgressions. The verse implies that the punishment or destruction of past transgressors may be imminent or close to the current transgressors. It is a reminder of the inevitability of divine justice and the importance of heeding the warnings and lessons from history.
orig: قل عسى أن يكون ردف لكم بعض الذي تستعجلون

translation: And indeed, your Lord is Generous beyond measure, but most of the people do not give thanks.
interpretation: The verse highlights the generosity of God towards humanity, yet most people do not express gratitude for it. The verse serves as a reminder of God's boundless generosity and the ungratefulness of many people. This ingratitude is a form of injustice and a failure to recognize and appreciate the blessings they have received. The verse encourages reflection on the blessings in one's life and expressing gratitude for them, as a way of acknowledging and honoring the source of those blessings.
orig: وإن ربك لذو فضل على الناس ولكن أكثرهم لا يشكرون

translation: And indeed, your Lord is of vast knowledge. He knows what their breasts conceal and what they reveal.
interpretation: The verse highlights the all-encompassing knowledge of God, who knows not only what people openly declare but also what they conceal in their hearts. This serves as a reminder that nothing can be hidden from God, and that people will be held accountable for their thoughts and actions. It also emphasizes the importance of having a pure heart, as God is aware of the intentions and motivations behind people's actions.
orig: وإن ربك ليعلم ما تكن صدورهم وما يعلنون

translation: And not a leaf falls but that He knows it, nor is there a grain in the darkness of the earth, nor anything fresh or dry, but it is in a clear book.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the all-encompassing knowledge of God. It states that not a single leaf falls without God's knowledge and that even the smallest of details, such as a grain in the earth, is known to Him. The phrase 'a clear book' refers to the idea that everything is recorded and known to God. The verse serves as a reminder of the omniscience of God and the fact that nothing is hidden from Him. It encourages believers to live their lives with the awareness that they are being observed and recorded by God.
orig: وما من غائبة في السماء والأرض إلا في كتاب مبين

translation: Indeed, this Qur'an relates to the Children of Israel most of that over which they disagree.
interpretation: The verse highlights the Qur'an's relevance to the history and experiences of the Children of Israel, and the fact that it addresses many of the disputes and disagreements among them. The verse can be seen as an invitation for the Children of Israel to reflect on their own history and to seek guidance from the Qur'an in resolving their disputes. At the same time, the verse can also be understood as a reminder to the Muslim community of the importance of understanding and learning from the experiences of previous generations, including the Children of Israel.
orig: إن هذا القرآن يقص على بني إسرائيل أكثر الذي هم فيه يختلفون

translation: And indeed, it is a clear sign and a mercy for the believers.
interpretation: The verse speaks about a clear sign and a mercy from God, which is specifically directed towards the believers. While the specific context of the verse is not provided, it is clear that the sign and mercy are intended to benefit and help the believers. The verse serves as a reminder of God's guidance and compassion towards those who have faith in Him, and of the blessings that they can receive if they remain steadfast on the path of righteousness.
orig: وإنه لهدى ورحمة للمؤمنين

translation: Surely, your Lord will judge between them by His judgment, and He is the Exalted in Might, the Knowing.
interpretation: The verse affirms that God will judge between people with His justice, and that He is all-powerful and all-knowing. The verse emphasizes the certainty of God's judgment and the futility of trying to escape it. It serves as a reminder that God is aware of all that people do and that they will ultimately be held accountable for their actions. The verse also highlights God's attributes of being all-powerful and all-knowing, which reinforces the idea that God's judgment is just and fair, and that no one can escape it.
orig: إن ربك يقضي بينهم بحكمه وهو العزيز العليم

translation: So put your trust in Allah. Indeed, you are on explicit truth.
interpretation: The verse is a command to put one's trust in Allah, the Exalted. It emphasizes the importance of relying on Allah and having faith in His plan. The second part of the verse, 'Indeed, you are on explicit truth', is a reassurance that the one being addressed is on the right path and has the truth on their side. The verse can be seen as a source of comfort and strength for those facing difficulties, reminding them to put their trust in Allah and have faith that they are on the right path.
orig: فتوكل على الله إنك على الحق المبين

translation: Indeed, you do not recite to the dead, nor do you recite to the deaf, except that you are a Warner.
interpretation: The verse highlights the role of the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) as a Warner who delivers the message of God to the people, whether they are alive or dead, and whether they listen or not. The verse emphasizes the futility of trying to communicate with those who are not receptive to the message, as they are likened to the dead and the deaf. The verse serves as a reminder to the Prophet (PBUH) to remain steadfast in his mission, as his responsibility is to deliver the message, not to force people to accept it. The verse also serves as a call to the people to listen and heed the warning, as they will be held accountable for their actions on the Day of Judgment.
orig: إنك لا تسمع الموتى ولا تسمع الصم الدعاء إذا ولوا مدبرين

translation: And you are not a guide of the blind, away from their error, if you do not bring them the evidence, except those who believe in Our verses and submit.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the role of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) as a guide, and that his guidance is only effective for those who believe in the signs of God and submit to them. The verse suggests that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) cannot force the blind (those who reject the truth) to see the truth and follow the right path. The verse implies that the responsibility of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) is only to convey the message and present the evidence, and it is up to the people to accept or reject it. The verse also highlights the importance of faith and submission in understanding and following the message of God.
orig: وما أنت بهادي العمي عن ضلالتهم إن تسمع إلا من يؤمن بآياتنا فهم مسلمون

translation: And when the word befalls them, We shall bring forth for them a creature from the earth speaking to them, saying that the people were, with Our signs, not certain.
interpretation: The verse speaks about a sign of God's power and authority that will be shown to people at the time of judgement. When the 'word' (referring to the divine decree) befalls them, a creature will be brought forth from the earth to speak to them. This creature will testify that people were not certain or believers in the signs of God. The verse emphasizes the importance of recognizing and believing in God's signs and the consequences of disbelief. It serves as a warning to those who deny God's signs and a reminder of the Day of Judgement.
orig: وإذا وقع القول عليهم أخرجنا لهم دابة من الأرض تكلمهم أن الناس كانوا بآياتنا لا يوقنون

translation: And the Day We shall gather from every nation a party of those who rejected Our signs, then they will be set in array (for punishment).
interpretation: The verse speaks about the gathering of people from every nation who rejected the signs of God. These people will be gathered together on the Day of Judgment and will be arranged in rows, ready to receive their punishment. The verse highlights the fact that God's signs and messages have been rejected by certain people, and as a consequence, they will face the consequences of their disbelief. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of recognizing and accepting God's signs and messages, and the consequences of denying them.
orig: ويوم نحشر من كل أمة فوجا ممن يكذب بآياتنا فهم يوزعون

translation: Until, when they came, they said, 'Never did we used to reject your messages, but you have not yet brought us proof.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the disbelievers who rejected the messages brought by the prophet. The verse highlights their denial and rejection of the prophet's message despite having no knowledge or understanding of it. They claimed that they did not reject the messages, but at the same time, they demanded proof, showing their hypocrisy and lack of faith. The verse serves as a reminder that faith and belief cannot be based on doubt and denial, but rather on acceptance and submission to the message of God.
orig: حتى إذا جاءوا قال أكذبتم بآياتي ولم تحيطوا بها علما أماذا كنتم تعملون

translation: And the word (i.e. decree) fell upon them (due) to what they had been doing (i.e. oppression and injustice), so they became speechless.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the consequence of oppression and injustice, where the decree or word of God fell upon those who committed it. As a result, they became speechless, which could mean that they were unable to defend themselves or that they were struck with fear and regret. The verse serves as a warning to those who commit injustice, reminding them of the swift and severe consequences of their actions.
orig: ووقع القول عليهم بما ظلموا فهم لا ينطقون

translation: Have they not seen that We have made the night for them to rest in and the day to be vision? Indeed in that are signs for a people who believe.
interpretation: The verse highlights the natural phenomena of night and day as signs from God for those who believe. The night is described as a time for rest, while the day is a time for vision or clarity. By reflecting on these natural phenomena, believers can gain a deeper understanding of God's power and wisdom. The verse serves as a reminder for people to be grateful for God's blessings and to seek guidance from the signs around them.
orig: ألم يروا أنا جعلنا الليل ليسكنوا فيه والنهار مبصرا إن في ذلك لآيات لقوم يؤمنون

translation: And on the Day when the Trumpet will be blown, then those who are in the heavens and those who are in the earth will be terrified except whom Allah wills, and all will come to Him humbled.
interpretation: The verse describes the Day of Judgment, when the Trumpet will be blown and all of creation will be terrified, except for those whom Allah wills. The verse emphasizes the power and control of Allah, as all of creation will come to Him in a state of humility and submission. The verse serves as a reminder of the power and majesty of Allah and the inevitability of the Day of Judgment, and encourages believers to be mindful of their actions and strive for righteousness in preparation for that Day.
orig: ويوم ينفخ في الصور ففزع من في السماوات ومن في الأرض إلا من شاء الله وكل أتوه داخرين

translation: And you see the mountains, thinking them to be fixed, while they pass by like clouds. The work of God, who has made all things firm. Indeed, He is aware of what you do.
interpretation: The verse describes the mountains as seemingly permanent and unchanging, but in reality, they are in constant motion, just like clouds. This highlights the power and control of God over all of His creations. The verse emphasizes that God is aware of all that humans do, reinforcing the idea of divine accountability. It serves as a reminder of the transience of human existence and the permanence of God's knowledge and power.
orig: وترى الجبال تحسبها جامدة وهي تمر مر السحاب صنع الله الذي أتقن كل شيء إنه خبير بما تفعلون

translation: Whoever brings a good deed will have better than it, and they are secure on that day.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the reward for those who do good deeds. The reward for their good deeds will be multiplied and will be better than the deeds themselves. Furthermore, those who do good deeds will be secure on the Day of Judgment. This verse serves as a motivation for people to do good deeds, and it emphasizes the great reward that awaits those who strive to lead a righteous life.
orig: من جاء بالحسنة فله خير منها وهم من فزع يومئذ آمنون

translation: And whoever brings evil, We will make him taste a painful punishment. Then We will surely make him taste the severity of the punishment on the Day of Resurrection.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the consequences of bringing evil or committing sins. Those who do so will be punished in the afterlife with a painful punishment that will make them taste the severity of their actions. The verse serves as a warning to those who commit sins, urging them to repent and turn away from evil before it is too late.
orig: ومن جاء بالسيئة فكبت وجوههم في النار هل تجزون إلا ما كنتم تعملون

translation: I have been commanded only to serve the Lord of this city, who has made it sacred and to whom belongs all things, and I have been commanded to be one of the submitters.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the speaker's obligation to serve and submit to the Lord of the city, who is the true owner of everything. The speaker has been commanded to be one of the submitters (Muslims), which implies that the Lord of the city is the same as the God of Islam. This verse can be interpreted as a statement of faith, emphasizing the importance of submission to God and the belief in his oneness and sovereignty. It can also be seen as a declaration of the speaker's commitment to the Islamic way of life.
orig: إنما أمرت أن أعبد رب هذه البلدة الذي حرمها وله كل شيء وأمرت أن أكون من المسلمين

translation: And indeed, I swear by the Qur'an, most noble, that I am, indeed, of those who warn. So, whoever is guided, it is only due to the guidance of his Lord, and whoever strays, then say, 'Indeed, I am only one of the warner.',
interpretation: The verse begins with an oath by the Qur'an, which is described as being noble, emphasizing the importance of the message that follows. The speaker identifies themselves as a warner, someone who is conveying a message of warning. The verse then explains that those who find guidance have done so through their own effort and the guidance of their Lord, while those who stray are responsible for their own actions. The speaker reaffirms their role as a warner, emphasizing the urgency of the message and the importance of heeding the warning.
orig: وأن أتلو القرآن فمن اهتدى فإنما يهتدي لنفسه ومن ضل فقل إنما أنا من المنذرين

translation: And say, 'Praise be to God, who will show you His signs so that you will recognize them. And your Lord is not unaware of what you do.'
interpretation: The verse reminds the believers to praise God and expresses that God will show them signs that they will recognize. The verse emphasizes God's omniscience, stating that God is not unaware of what the believers do. The verse serves as a reminder that God is always present and aware of the actions of the believers, and it encourages them to be mindful of their actions and praise God for His guidance and blessings.
orig: وقل الحمد لله سيريكم آياته فتعرفونها وما ربك بغافل عما تعملون

translation: N
interpretation: N
orig: طسم

translation: Those are the verses of the clear Book.
interpretation: The verse refers to the verses of the Qur'an as the 'clear Book', emphasizing their clarity and lack of ambiguity. The verse may be emphasizing the importance of understanding and reflecting on the meanings of the verses, as they serve as a guide for those seeking the truth and the right path.
orig: تلك آيات الكتاب المبين

translation: We recite to you some of the news of Moses and Pharaoh in truth, for a people who believe.
interpretation: The verse is a promise from God that the story of Moses and Pharaoh will be told in truth, as a message for a people who believe. The verse emphasizes the importance of faith and belief in the story, as it serves as a lesson and a source of guidance for those who are receptive to it. The story of Moses and Pharaoh is a central narrative in Islamic tradition, and it serves as a powerful reminder of the power of God and the consequences of disbelief and oppression.
orig: نتلو عليك من نبإ موسى وفرعون بالحق لقوم يؤمنون

translation: Pharaoh exalted himself in the land and made its people into factions, oppressing one group of them, slaughtering their sons and sparing their women. Indeed, he was of the corrupters.
interpretation: The verse describes Pharaoh's tyranny and oppression of the people in his kingdom. He exalted himself and divided the people into factions, oppressing one group and committing heinous acts against them, such as killing their sons and sparing their women. The verse emphasizes Pharaoh's role as a corruptor, highlighting the destructive impact of his actions on society. The verse serves as a reminder of the consequences of tyranny and oppression, and the harm it can bring to a society and its people.
orig: إن فرعون علا في الأرض وجعل أهلها شيعا يستضعف طائفة منهم يذبح أبناءهم ويستحيي نساءهم إنه كان من المفسدين

translation: And We wanted to favor those who were oppressed in the land, to make them leaders and inheritors.
interpretation: The verse speaks about God's intention to favor and uplift those who have been oppressed in the land, by making them leaders and inheritors. This verse highlights God's concern for the weak and downtrodden, and His desire to give them power and authority. It also emphasizes the idea of social justice, where those who have been marginalized and exploited are given the opportunity to lead and make decisions. This verse serves as a reminder that God is just and will always support those who are oppressed.
orig: ونريد أن نمن على الذين استضعفوا في الأرض ونجعلهم أئمة ونجعلهم الوارثين

translation: And We caused them to prevail over lands, and We gave Pharaoh, Haman and their soldiers provision out of it, while they were unjust.
interpretation: The verse speaks about God's power and control over everything in the universe. It mentions that God allowed certain people to prevail and have control over lands, and provided for them and their leaders, such as Pharaoh and Haman, despite their unjust ways. This serves as a reminder that God is all-powerful and can give or take away resources and power at any time. It also highlights the consequences of unjust actions, as God may still provide for those who are unjust, but it does not mean they are safe from accountability and punishment for their actions.
orig: ونمكن لهم في الأرض ونري فرعون وهامان وجنودهما منهم ما كانوا يحذرون

translation: And We inspired to the mother of Moses, 'Nurse him; then, when you fear for him, cast him into the sea. Do not fear and do not grieve. Indeed, We will return him to you and will make him among the messengers.'
interpretation: The verse relays a message from God to the mother of Moses, instructing her to nurse him and then cast him into the sea when she fears for his safety. She is told not to fear or grieve, as God will return Moses to her and make him one of the messengers. The verse highlights the trust and faith that the mother of Moses had to have in God's plan, and the extraordinary destiny that was in store for Moses. It also emphasizes the theme of divine intervention and the protection of the prophets.
orig: وأوحينا إلى أم موسى أن أرضعيه فإذا خفت عليه فألقيه في اليم ولا تخافي ولا تحزني إنا رادوه إليك وجاعلوه من المرسلين

translation: And We took him (Pharaoh) and his troops to drown, and they were evildoers.
interpretation: The verse recounts the story of Pharaoh and his followers who were punished by God for their transgressions. The verse describes how Pharaoh and his army were destroyed, emphasizing the consequences of their wrongdoing. The verse serves as a reminder of the power of God and the ultimate fate of those who defy His commands and act unjustly.
orig: فالتقطه آل فرعون ليكون لهم عدوا وحزنا إن فرعون وهامان وجنودهما كانوا خاطئين

translation: And the wife of Pharaoh said, 'A comfort of the eye for me and for you. Kill him not; perhaps he may be of benefit to us, or we may take him as a son.' And they perceived not.
interpretation: The verse relays the words of Pharaoh's wife, who speaks in defense of the infant Moses, urging her husband not to kill him. She argues that the child could be of benefit to them or they could adopt him as their own. The verse highlights the irony of Pharaoh's household, who are oblivious to the fact that this child will grow up to challenge their power and oppression. The verse serves as a reminder of the hidden potential within individuals, and the unexpected ways in which God's plan can unfold.
orig: وقالت امرأت فرعون قرت عين لي ولك لا تقتلوه عسى أن ينفعنا أو نتخذه ولدا وهم لا يشعرون

translation: And when the heart of Moses' mother became empty [i.e., she was on the verge of revealing his identity] except that We strengthened her heart, that she might be of the believers.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the strength and faith of the mother of Moses, who was able to resist the temptation to reveal her son's identity despite the danger it posed to him. The verse highlights the role of God in supporting and strengthening her heart, allowing her to remain steadfast in her belief. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of faith and trust in God during difficult times, and the power of God to provide strength and support to those who believe in Him.
orig: وأصبح فؤاد أم موسى فارغا إن كادت لتبدي به لولا أن ربطنا على قلبها لتكون من المؤمنين

translation: She said to her brother Lut, 'O my brother, indeed I see something terrible.' So they said, 'Indeed, we are seeing you.'
interpretation: The verse describes a conversation between Lut's sister and Lut, where she expresses her fear and concern about something terrible she has seen. Lut and the others present respond by acknowledging that they see her. The verse highlights the urgency and seriousness of the situation, as Lut's sister feels compelled to speak up about what she has witnessed. The verse serves as a build-up to the larger story of Lut and the destruction of his people, emphasizing the gravity of their sins and the impending punishment from God.
orig: وقالت لأخته قصيه فبصرت به عن جنب وهم لا يشعرون

translation: And We have already prohibited for them blessings of which you did not have knowledge. Indeed, Satan promises them and excites them of what is not true. So We did not make for them an ally from it, nor a protector.
interpretation: The verse speaks about a group of people who were prohibited from receiving certain blessings, which the reader was not previously aware of. The verse explains that Satan had made false promises to these people and excited them with false hopes. Despite this, God did not provide them with support or protection, emphasizing their isolation and abandonment. The verse serves as a reminder of the deception of Satan and the consequences of following his whispers and false promises.
orig: وحرمنا عليه المراضع من قبل فقالت هل أدلكم على أهل بيت يكفلونه لكم وهم له ناصحون

translation: Then We returned him to his mother, so that she might be comforted and not grieve, and that she might know that the promise of Allah is true, but most of them do not know.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the return of a child to his mother, who had been separated from him. The mother is comforted and reassured, and she learns that the promise of God is true. However, the verse also highlights the fact that most people do not know or understand the significance of this event and the promise of God. The verse emphasizes the importance of having faith in God's promises and understanding the deeper meaning behind events in life.
orig: فرددناه إلى أمه كي تقر عينها ولا تحزن ولتعلم أن وعد الله حق ولكن أكثرهم لا يعلمون

translation: And when its (the human's) term came, We took him in a fair way, having already provided it with knowledge and power.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the end of a person's life and the moment of their death. At this moment, God takes the person's soul in a fair and just manner, after having given them knowledge and power during their lifetime. The verse emphasizes the inevitability of death and the fairness of God's actions, reminding people that they will be judged according to their deeds and given their due rewards or punishments.
orig: ولما بلغ أشده واستوى آتيناه حكما وعلما وكذلك نجزي المحسنين

translation: And he entered the city at a time when its people were heedless, and he found in it two men fighting, one from his faction and the other from his enemy, and the one from his faction cried out to him against the one from his enemy. So Moses struck him and killed him. He said, 'This is from the work of Satan. Indeed, he is an enemy, misleading and clear.'
interpretation: The verse describes the story of Moses when he came across two men fighting, one from his own faction and the other from his enemy. When the man from his faction called for his help, Moses intervened and unintentionally killed the man from the opposing faction. The verse highlights the unintentional nature of the act, as Moses was not aware of the full situation and was only trying to help. However, the verse also emphasizes the destructive consequences of violence and the dangers of intervening in conflicts without full knowledge of the situation. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of seeking understanding and wisdom before taking action, and the potential negative consequences of hasty decisions and actions.
orig: ودخل المدينة على حين غفلة من أهلها فوجد فيها رجلين يقتتلان هذا من شيعته وهذا من عدوه فاستغاثه الذي من شيعته على الذي من عدوه فوكزه موسى فقضى عليه قال هذا من عمل الشيطان إنه عدو مضل مبين

translation: He said, 'My Lord, I have wronged myself, so forgive me.' So He forgave him. Indeed, He is the Forgiving, the Merciful.
interpretation: The verse describes the conversation between a person and God, where the person admits their wrongdoing and asks for forgiveness. The verse emphasizes the mercy and forgiveness of God, as He immediately forgives the person upon their repentance. The verse serves as a reminder that God is always ready to forgive those who turn to Him in repentance, no matter how great their sins may be. It also encourages the reader to seek forgiveness and to turn to God in times of need, knowing that He is the Most Merciful and Forgiving.
orig: قال رب إني ظلمت نفسي فاغفر لي فغفر له إنه هو الغفور الرحيم

translation: He said, 'My Lord, because You have favored me, I will not be a supporter of the criminals.'
interpretation: The verse is a statement made by someone who has received favor from God and as a result, they have decided not to support or be allied with those who commit wrongdoing or crimes. This person is taking a stand against injustice and expressing their commitment to upholding what is right. The verse highlights the importance of using the blessings and favor we receive from God for good purposes, and to stand against wrongdoing, rather than enabling or supporting it.
orig: قال رب بما أنعمت علي فلن أكون ظهيرا للمجرمين

translation: So he (the fleeing slave) departed in the city, fearful and watchful, when behold, the one who had given him refuge the day before was calling out to him. Moses said to him: 'Indeed, you are a clear liar.'
interpretation: The verse describes the situation of a slave who had fled from his master and found refuge with a man in a city. However, the next day, the one who had given him refuge was calling out to him, indicating that the situation had changed and the slave was in danger again. Moses, who is narrating the story, addresses the man and accuses him of lying, likely because the man had previously promised to help and protect the slave, but was now betraying him. The verse teaches about the importance of keeping one's word and being trustworthy, and also highlights the dangers of betraying those who rely on us.
orig: فأصبح في المدينة خائفا يترقب فإذا الذي استنصره بالأمس يستصرخه قال له موسى إنك لغوي مبين

translation: But when he (Moses) desired to seize the one who was an enemy to them both, he (Moses) said, 'O Moses, do you intend to kill me as you killed someone yesterday? You only intend to be a tyrant in the land, and you do not intend to be among the doers of good.'
interpretation: The verse describes an incident where Moses desires to seize someone who is an enemy to him and his companion. The person reminds Moses of his actions from the previous day, implying that Moses had killed someone. The person accuses Moses of intending to be a tyrant and not a doer of good. The verse highlights the importance of fairness and justice, and the consequences of acting out of anger and personal vendettas. It serves as a reminder that the actions of individuals have an impact on those around them and that it is important to consider the consequences of our actions.
orig: فلما أن أراد أن يبطش بالذي هو عدو لهما قال يا موسى أتريد أن تقتلني كما قتلت نفسا بالأمس إن تريد إلا أن تكون جبارا في الأرض وما تريد أن تكون من المصلحين

translation: And there came a man from the farthest end of the city, running, and said, 'O Moses, indeed the leaders are deciding upon your killing, so depart, I am to you of those who advise.'
interpretation: The verse describes a situation where Moses is being persecuted and a man from the outskirts of the city comes running to warn him of a plot to kill him. The man advises Moses to leave the city in order to save himself. The verse highlights the importance of seeking advice and help from others, especially in times of danger and adversity. It also emphasizes the importance of being vigilant and aware of one's surroundings, as danger can come from unexpected sources. Furthermore, the verse highlights the moral responsibility of individuals to protect and warn others of danger, even if it means going against the powerful and influential leaders of the society.
orig: وجاء رجل من أقصى المدينة يسعى قال يا موسى إن الملأ يأتمرون بك ليقتلوك فاخرج إني لك من الناصحين

translation: Then he (Noah) came out of the ark, and said, 'O my Lord, my people have indeed wronged me. So, my Lord, forgive me and grant me dominion and let me die a contented death.',
interpretation: The verse recounts Noah's prayer after surviving the great flood that God had sent as a punishment for the corrupt and unjust people of his time. Noah expresses his gratitude for being saved and asks for forgiveness for any wrongs he may have committed. He also asks for two specific blessings: dominion and a contented death. The interpretation of this verse is that it highlights the importance of seeking forgiveness and expressing gratitude in the face of adversity. It also emphasizes the idea that even the most righteous individuals, like Noah, recognize their own imperfections and seek God's mercy and forgiveness.
orig: فخرج منها خائفا يترقب قال رب نجني من القوم الظالمين

translation: And when he turned his face toward the city, he said, 'Perhaps my Lord will guide me to the right way.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about a person who, while facing a difficult decision or situation, turns to God in prayer and asks for guidance. The person is unsure of the right path to take, and seeks divine assistance to make the correct choice. This verse highlights the importance of seeking God's guidance in one's life and the recognition that only through divine assistance can one find the right way. This verse serves as a reminder that in times of uncertainty and confusion, one should turn to God in prayer and seek His guidance and help.
orig: ولما توجه تلقاء مدين قال عسى ربي أن يهديني سواء السبيل

translation: And when a caravan came to a town, they found a people who were exulting (in their prosperity), and they found beside them two women who were keeping back (their flocks). They said, 'What has made you keep back (your flocks) from watering?' They said, 'We will not water (our flocks) until the shepherds have watered (their flocks). And our father is an old man.'
interpretation: The verse describes a situation where a caravan comes across a town and finds people rejoicing in their prosperity. The caravan also sees two women holding back their flocks from watering. When asked why, the women reply that they will not water their flocks until the shepherds have finished watering theirs, as their father is an old man. The verse highlights the importance of treating everyone fairly, regardless of their status or age. It teaches the value of patience and sharing resources, even in times of abundance. It also emphasizes the importance of respecting and caring for the elderly.
orig: ولما ورد ماء مدين وجد عليه أمة من الناس يسقون ووجد من دونهم امرأتين تذودان قال ما خطبكما قالتا لا نسقي حتى يصدر الرعاء وأبونا شيخ كبير

translation: He wronged them both, then he went to the shade and said, 'My Lord, I have indeed wronged myself, and I submit to You.'
interpretation: The verse describes the repentance of a person who had wronged two others. After committing the wrong, the person goes to the shade and, in a moment of reflection, realizes the gravity of their actions and the consequences of their sins. In a sincere and humble manner, the person submits to God and seeks forgiveness. The verse emphasizes the importance of recognizing and acknowledging one's wrongdoing and the power of repentance and submission to God.
orig: فسقى لهما ثم تولى إلى الظل فقال رب إني لما أنزلت إلي من خير فقير

translation: Then one of them approached him, walking shyly, and said, 'Indeed, my father invites you so that he may reward you for having watered for us.' So when he came to him and related to him the story, he said, 'Do not fear, you have been saved from the unjust people.'
interpretation: The verse describes the story of a man who had shown kindness to someone by providing them with water. In return, he is invited by the person's father to be rewarded for his good deed. The verse highlights the humility and respect shown by the person approaching the man, as she approaches him shyly. The father's gratitude and generosity towards the man are also evident in his invitation. The verse emphasizes the importance of showing kindness and gratitude towards others, as it can lead to positive outcomes and the establishment of good relationships. The verse also highlights the contrast between the unjust people and the man, who has acted with integrity and goodness.
orig: فجاءته إحداهما تمشي على استحياء قالت إن أبي يدعوك ليجزيك أجر ما سقيت لنا فلما جاءه وقص عليه القصص قال لا تخف نجوت من القوم الظالمين

translation: One of them said, 'O my father, hire him! Indeed, the most trustworthy of those who have agreed to hire is the strong, the capable.'
interpretation: The verse shows a conversation between two people, where one of them suggests hiring an individual who is both strong and capable. By emphasizing the importance of hiring someone who is trustworthy and capable, the verse highlights the significance of making good decisions and choosing reliable people. This can be interpreted as a reminder to be cautious and thoughtful when making important choices, and to seek out individuals who are competent and trustworthy in order to ensure success and avoid potential harm or loss.
orig: قالت إحداهما يا أبت استأجره إن خير من استأجرت القوي الأمين

translation: He said, 'I want to marry you to one of my two daughters on the condition that you pay me the wages of eight pilgrimages; if you complete ten, then whatever you will have over and above that, and I do not intend to make things difficult for you. You will find me, if Allah wills, one of the righteous.'
interpretation: The verse relays a man's proposition to the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) to marry one of his daughters, on the condition that he pays wages for eight or ten pilgrimages. The man emphasizes that he does not intend to make things difficult for the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) and that he considers himself to be among the righteous. The verse can be interpreted as a display of the man's generosity and respect for the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH), as well as his commitment to fulfilling his obligations and responsibilities.
orig: قال إني أريد أن أنكحك إحدى ابنتي هاتين على أن تأجرني ثماني حجج فإن أتممت عشرا فمن عندك وما أريد أن أشق عليك ستجدني إن شاء الله من الصالحين

translation: He said, 'It is between you and me. Whichever of the two terms I fulfill, there will be no injustice to me. Indeed, Allah, over what we say, is a sufficient witness.'
interpretation: The verse is a statement made by a person, who has given two options to someone else and is fulfilling one of them. The person makes it clear that they have not been unjust and that they have a witness, which is Allah, over their statement. The verse emphasizes the importance of fulfilling one's promises and the role of Allah as a witness over human actions and statements. It also highlights the idea of justice and the importance of being fair and truthful in one's dealings with others.
orig: قال ذلك بيني وبينك أيما الأجلين قضيت فلا عدوان علي والله على ما نقول وكيل

translation: And when Moses had completed the term and was traveling with his family, he saw a fire in the direction of Tur. He said to his family, 'Stay here, I have seen a fire. Perhaps I can bring you a burning brand from it or find guidance at the fire.'
interpretation: The verse describes the journey of Moses and his family after his term had ended. They come across a fire, and Moses decides to approach it to get a burning brand or to find guidance. The verse highlights Moses' leadership and his desire to provide for and protect his family. It also symbolizes the importance of seeking knowledge and guidance, even in unexpected situations. The verse can be seen as a metaphor for the spiritual journey of seeking enlightenment and guidance on one's path.
orig: فلما قضى موسى الأجل وسار بأهله آنس من جانب الطور نارا قال لأهله امكثوا إني آنست نارا لعلي آتيكم منها بخبر أو جذوة من النار لعلكم تصطلون

translation: And when it came to rest, He was called from the right side of the valley, in the blessed land, from the tree, 'O Moses, indeed I am Allah, the Lord of the worlds.'
interpretation: The verse describes the calling of Moses by God. Moses was in a blessed land near a tree when he received a message from the right side of the valley. The message was from God, who introduced Himself as the Lord of the worlds. The verse emphasizes the significance of the encounter between Moses and God, highlighting the fact that it was not a random event but a carefully planned and orchestrated moment. The verse also implies the power and authority of God, who can communicate with His servants in any way and at any time. The verse serves as a reminder of God's presence and His ability to reach out to His servants, regardless of their location or circumstances.
orig: فلما أتاها نودي من شاطئ الواد الأيمن في البقعة المباركة من الشجرة أن يا موسى إني أنا الله رب العالمين

translation: And throw down your staff, but when he saw it moving as if it were a snake, he turned back in retreat, and did not return, O Moses. And fear not, indeed you are of the secure.
interpretation: The verse speaks about God's command to Moses to throw down his staff, which then transforms into a snake. The verse highlights Moses' initial fear and retreat when he saw the transformation, but then God reassures him and tells him not to be afraid, for he is among the secure. The verse serves as a testament to God's power and ability to transform and change things, and also as a reminder of the importance of trust and faith in God, even in the face of uncertainty and fear.
orig: وأن ألق عصاك فلما رآها تهتز كأنها جان ولى مدبرا ولم يعقب يا موسى أقبل ولا تخف إنك من الآمنين

translation: Put your hand into your pocket, it will come out white [i.e., unblemished] without any harm. And draw your elbow close to you [in a gesture of protection against evil]. These are two proofs from your Lord to Pharaoh and his chiefs. Indeed, they were a people who were transgressors.
interpretation: The verse describes a miraculous sign performed by a prophet, sent by God as a messenger to the Pharaoh and his chiefs. The sign involves putting his hand into his pocket, which comes out unblemished and white, and drawing his elbow close to his side as a protective gesture. These two events are presented as proof of the prophet's truthfulness and divine mission. The verse also highlights the transgression and sinfulness of the Pharaoh and his chiefs, setting the stage for the larger narrative of the Qur'an's retelling of the story of Moses and the Israelites.
orig: اسلك يدك في جيبك تخرج بيضاء من غير سوء واضمم إليك جناحك من الرهب فذانك برهانان من ربك إلى فرعون وملئه إنهم كانوا قوما فاسقين

translation: He said, 'My Lord, I have indeed wronged myself, so I fear they will kill me.'
interpretation: The verse is a quote from a person who has wronged themselves and fears for their life. The person has done something that they regret and are afraid of the consequences. They have wronged themselves and recognize their mistake. They are afraid that their actions will lead to their death at the hands of others. The verse highlights the inner turmoil and fear that can come from a guilty conscience and the consequences of one's actions. It also shows the human desire for self-preservation and the fear of death.
orig: قال رب إني قتلت منهم نفسا فأخاف أن يقتلون

translation: And my brother Aaron is more eloquent than me, so send him with me as a helper, for I fear that they will reject me.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the prophet Moses' request to God to send his brother Aaron with him as a helper. Moses acknowledges that his brother has a more eloquent tongue than him. He fears that the people he has been sent to will reject him, and so he seeks the assistance of his brother. This verse highlights the importance of having a supportive companion in the face of adversity and the recognition of one's own strengths and weaknesses.
orig: وأخي هارون هو أفصح مني لسانا فأرسله معي ردءا يصدقني إني أخاف أن يكذبون

translation: He said, 'We will strengthen your arm through your brother, and We will give you both authority, so they will not reach you both with Our verses. You and whoever follows you will be the predominant.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about God granting power and authority to the speaker (who is believed to be the Prophet Moses) and his brother (Aaron) over the Pharaoh and his followers. The verse highlights the idea that God's help and support will be with the brothers, and they will be able to overcome the oppressive Pharaoh. The verse also emphasizes the ultimate victory of the brothers and their followers over their enemies. This verse can be seen as a source of encouragement and empowerment for those who are facing oppression and adversity, reminding them of the promise of God's support and the eventual triumph of justice.
orig: قال سنشد عضدك بأخيك ونجعل لكما سلطانا فلا يصلون إليكما بآياتنا أنتما ومن اتبعكما الغالبون

translation: But when Moses came to them with Our signs, clear, they said: 'This is nothing but a manifest sorcery, and we never heard of this among our forefathers.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the people's rejection of Moses's message and their refusal to accept his proofs and signs, which are described as clear and evident. Instead of acknowledging the truth, they dismissed his message as a false and fabricated sorcery. The verse highlights the people's closed-mindedness and their rejection of anything new or unfamiliar, even if it comes from a divine source. The verse serves as a reminder of the challenges faced by the prophets in conveying the divine message and the people's tendency to reject what they do not understand or what goes against their preconceived notions and beliefs.
orig: فلما جاءهم موسى بآياتنا بينات قالوا ما هذا إلا سحر مفترى وما سمعنا بهذا في آبائنا الأولين

translation: And Moses said, 'My Lord, I take refuge in You from the people who are oppressors and liars. And my Lord, I have done wrong to myself, so forgive me', then He forgave him. Indeed, He is the Forgiving, the Merciful. And (mention) when Moses said to his people, 'My Lord, indeed I have seen a fire. I will bring you information from it or I will bring you a burning torch that you may warm yourselves.' So when he came near it, he was called, 'O Moses, indeed I am your Lord, so remove your sandals. Indeed, you are in the sacred valley of Tuwa. And I have chosen you, so listen well to what is revealed [to you]. Indeed, I am Allah. There is no deity except Me, so worship Me and establish prayer for My remembrance.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about Moses' encounter with God and his subsequent appointment as a prophet. The verse emphasizes the power and authority of God, who calls Moses from the burning bush and commands him to remove his sandals as a sign of respect and humility. The verse also highlights the importance of prayer and worship, as God commands Moses to establish prayer for His remembrance. The verse serves as a reminder of the greatness of God and the importance of obedience and submission to His will.
orig: وقال موسى ربي أعلم بمن جاء بالهدى من عنده ومن تكون له عاقبة الدار إنه لا يفلح الظالمون

translation: Pharaoh said: 'O nobles, I do not know for you any god other than me, so kindle for me, O Haman, a fire upon the clay, and make for me a tower in order that I may look at the god of Moses, and indeed, I do think he is of the liars.'
interpretation: The verse describes Pharaoh's rejection of any god but himself and his order to Haman to build a tower so that he can see the god of Moses. Pharaoh's response shows his arrogance and disbelief in the face of Moses's message. The verse highlights the danger of arrogance and the rejection of God's message, emphasizing the consequences of rejecting the truth and following one's own desires.
orig: وقال فرعون يا أيها الملأ ما علمت لكم من إله غيري فأوقد لي يا هامان على الطين فاجعل لي صرحا لعلي أطلع إلى إله موسى وإني لأظنه من الكاذبين

translation: And he and his soldiers were arrogant upon the earth unjustly, and they thought that they would not return to Us.
interpretation: The verse describes a person and his followers who are arrogant and unjust on earth. They believe that they will not be held accountable for their actions and will not return to God. This verse serves as a reminder that all actions have consequences and that no one can escape God's judgment. It also emphasizes the dangers of arrogance and oppression, and the importance of humility and justice.
orig: واستكبر هو وجنوده في الأرض بغير الحق وظنوا أنهم إلينا لا يرجعون

translation: And We seized him and his forces, then We threw them into the sea. So observe how was the end of the wrongdoers.
interpretation: The verse describes the punishment of a tyrant and his army who were seized and thrown into the sea as a consequence of their wrongdoing. The verse concludes by encouraging the reader to reflect on the outcome of the unjust, serving as a reminder of the consequences of oppression and the ultimate fate of the wicked.
orig: فأخذناه وجنوده فنبذناهم في اليم فانظر كيف كان عاقبة الظالمين

translation: And We made them leaders inviting to the Fire; on the Day of Resurrection they will not be helped.
interpretation: The verse speaks about people who were made leaders and who led others towards hellfire. These leaders are described as being unsuccessful on the Day of Judgment, as they will not receive any help or support. The verse serves as a warning to those who lead others astray and emphasizes the seriousness of their actions, as well as the consequences they will face on the Day of Judgment.
orig: وجعلناهم أئمة يدعون إلى النار ويوم القيامة لا ينصرون

translation: And We followed them in this world with curse, and on the Day of Judgment they will be among the disdained.
interpretation: The verse speaks about a group of people who have earned God's curse in this world and will be among the disdained on the Day of Judgment. The verse emphasizes the continuity of their punishment, as they have been followed with curse in this world and will continue to be among the disdained in the afterlife. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and disobedience, reminding them of the never-ending consequences of their actions and the unavoidability of God's judgment.
orig: وأتبعناهم في هذه الدنيا لعنة ويوم القيامة هم من المقبوحين

translation: And We had already given Moses the Scripture beforehand, after We destroyed the former towns, as an enlightenment for the people and a guidance and mercy, so that they might remember.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the giving of the Scripture to Moses after the destruction of previous communities. The Scripture was given as a source of enlightenment, guidance, and mercy for the people, with the hope that they would take heed and remember. This verse can be interpreted as a reminder of the importance of scripture and its role in guiding people towards righteousness. It also highlights the consequences of ignoring the guidance and wisdom provided by scripture, as seen in the destruction of the previous communities. Ultimately, the verse encourages reflection and mindfulness of the guidance provided by scripture, in order to avoid the fate of the communities that were destroyed.
orig: ولقد آتينا موسى الكتاب من بعد ما أهلكنا القرون الأولى بصائر للناس وهدى ورحمة لعلهم يتذكرون

translation: But I was not present when they cast lots and decided the matter of Moses, nor was I one of the witnesses.
interpretation: The verse is spoken from the perspective of someone who was not present when the people of Israel cast lots and made a decision regarding Moses. The speaker did not participate in the event and was not a witness to it. The verse could be interpreted as a way for the speaker to distance themselves from the decision made about Moses and to express their lack of involvement in the matter.
orig: وما كنت بجانب الغربي إذ قضينا إلى موسى الأمر وما كنت من الشاهدين

translation: But We destroyed generations before them, and they were longer in life than them. And never have I been unjust to the people of a town, ever.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of previous generations who lived longer than the current generation. The verse emphasizes that God has not been unjust to any town, implying that the destruction of those generations was a result of their own actions. The verse serves as a reminder that all generations will be held accountable for their actions, and that God's actions are always just and fair.
orig: ولكنا أنشأنا قرونا فتطاول عليهم العمر وما كنت ثاويا في أهل مدين تتلو عليهم آياتنا ولكنا كنا مرسلين

translation: But I was not present at the mount when He was addressed; (this is) only a mercy from my Lord, so that He may warn (people) whom He wills of the coming of the Hour of Doom.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the Prophet Muhammad's experience of receiving revelation, and emphasizes that he was not physically present at Mount Sinai when God spoke to Moses. Instead, the revelation he received was a mercy from God, given so that he could warn people of the coming of the Day of Judgment. This verse highlights the importance of prophethood and the role of the prophets in conveying God's message to humanity. It also underscores the significance of the coming of the Day of Judgment, and the need for people to be aware of and prepare for it.
orig: وما كنت بجانب الطور إذ نادينا ولكن رحمة من ربك لتنذر قوما ما أتاهم من نذير من قبلك لعلهم يتذكرون

translation: And if not for the grace of God upon them, and His mercy, they would have been among the losers. But We saved them so they may be among those who are appreciative.
interpretation: The verse highlights the role of God's grace and mercy in protecting and saving people from destruction. The verse suggests that the people mentioned were on a path towards failure and loss, but God's grace and mercy intervened to save them. The verse emphasizes the importance of showing appreciation and gratitude for God's blessings. It also serves as a reminder that without God's grace and mercy, people would be among the losers, and that it is through His kindness and compassion that they have the opportunity to be among the grateful and appreciative.
orig: ولولا أن تصيبهم مصيبة بما قدمت أيديهم فيقولوا ربنا لولا أرسلت إلينا رسولا فنتبع آياتك ونكون من المؤمنين

translation: But when the truth came to them from Us, they said, 'Why is he not given like that which was given to Moses?' Did they not reject what was given to Moses before? They said, 'It is only magic, and they said, 'Indeed, we are unbelievers.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the people's rejection of the truth, represented by the arrival of the message from God. Despite the truth being presented to them, they demanded a similar sign to what was given to Moses, showing their lack of faith and their rejection of previous messages. They further rejected it by calling it magic, which indicates their disbelief and denial of the truth. The verse highlights the people's stubbornness and unwillingness to accept the truth, even when it is presented to them, and their rejection of the message is a reflection of their disbelief.
orig: فلما جاءهم الحق من عندنا قالوا لولا أوتي مثل ما أوتي موسى أولم يكفروا بما أوتي موسى من قبل قالوا سحران تظاهرا وقالوا إنا بكل كافرون

translation: Say, 'Then bring a book from God which is a better guide than both of them (the Qur'an and the scripture of the Jews and Christians) if you are truthful.'
interpretation: The verse is a challenge from the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) to the non-believers who rejected the Qur'an and followed the scripture of the Jews and Christians. The verse invites them to bring a book from God that is a better guide than the Qur'an. The verse implies that the Qur'an is the final and most complete revelation from God, and no other book can surpass it in guidance. The verse serves as a rebuke to those who reject the Qur'an and a confirmation of its divine origin and superiority.
orig: قل فأتوا بكتاب من عند الله هو أهدى منهما أتبعه إن كنتم صادقين

translation: But if they do not respond to you, then know that they only follow their desires. And who is more astray than one who follows his desire without guidance from Allah? Indeed, Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the consequences of not responding to the message of the prophet. Those who do not respond are only following their own desires and are astray. The verse emphasizes the importance of guidance from Allah and the dire consequences of following one's own desires without it. The verse serves as a reminder to the importance of listening to and following the message of the prophet and the guidance of Allah, and the danger of ignoring it.
orig: فإن لم يستجيبوا لك فاعلم أنما يتبعون أهواءهم ومن أضل ممن اتبع هواه بغير هدى من الله إن الله لا يهدي القوم الظالمين

translation: And We have already sent messages to them, perhaps they will remember.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the sending of messages or warnings to people, with the hope that they will take heed and remember or reflect on them. The verse suggests that despite these warnings, people may still choose to ignore or forget the message. The verse can be seen as a reminder of the importance of reflection and contemplation, and the need to heed the warnings and lessons presented to us.
orig: ولقد وصلنا لهم القول لعلهم يتذكرون

translation: Those whom We have given the Scripture before, they [are the ones] who believe in it.
interpretation: The verse refers to those who have received previous revelations (such as the Torah and the Gospel) and have faith in them. It highlights the belief of these individuals in the scripture that was given to them. This serves as a recognition of the validity of previous revelations and the importance of faith in them. It also emphasizes the continuity of the message of God in different religions and scriptures.
orig: الذين آتيناهم الكتاب من قبله هم به يؤمنون

translation: And when it is recited to them, they say, 'We believe in it. Indeed, it is the truth from our Lord. Indeed, we were, before it, of those who submit.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the reaction of some people when a message or a scripture is recited to them. Despite their previous disbelief or denial, they now claim to believe in the message and recognize its truth, which comes from their Lord. They also acknowledge that they were, before this revelation, among the submitters or Muslims. This verse may be seen as a confirmation of the power of the message to change hearts and minds, as well as a reminder of the importance of being consistent in faith and actions.
orig: وإذا يتلى عليهم قالوا آمنا به إنه الحق من ربنا إنا كنا من قبله مسلمين

translation: Those will be given their reward twice for their patience, and they will be rid of fear and grief.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the reward of those who are patient and do good. They will receive their reward twice, indicating a great and abundant reward. Additionally, they will be freed from fear and grief, suggesting a life free from worry and suffering. The verse serves as an encouragement for patience and good deeds, promising a positive outcome for those who choose this path.
orig: أولئك يؤتون أجرهم مرتين بما صبروا ويدرءون بالحسنة السيئة ومما رزقناهم ينفقون

translation: And when they hear ill speech, they turn away from it and say, 'For us are our deeds, and for you are your deeds. Peace will be upon you; we seek not the ignorant.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the attitude of certain people when they hear ill speech or slander. Instead of engaging with it or trying to understand it, they choose to turn away and focus on their own actions. They make it clear that they are not responsible for the actions of others and that they seek peace, not conflict. This verse can be interpreted as a reminder to focus on one's own actions and to avoid getting involved in unnecessary conflicts or disputes. It also highlights the importance of maintaining peace and avoiding ignorance in one's interactions with others.
orig: وإذا سمعوا اللغو أعرضوا عنه وقالوا لنا أعمالنا ولكم أعمالكم سلام عليكم لا نبتغي الجاهلين

translation: Indeed, you do not guide whom you love, but Allah guides whom He wills, and He is most knowing of the guided.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the ultimate power and knowledge of Allah in guiding people to the right path. While it may seem that someone is deserving of guidance, it is ultimately up to Allah to guide them. The verse serves as a reminder that human efforts to guide others, no matter how well-intentioned, are limited and that true guidance comes from Allah. It also reminds us that Allah has knowledge of those who are truly guided and that His guidance is the only one that truly matters.
orig: إنك لا تهدي من أحببت ولكن الله يهدي من يشاء وهو أعلم بالمهتدين

translation: And they said, 'If we follow your guidance, we will be uprooted from our land.' Have we not made a sacred place of security for them, where the fruits of all things are brought as provision from us? But most of them do not know.
interpretation: The verse describes the response of some people to the guidance of the speaker (who is not explicitly identified in the verse). They express their fear that following the guidance will result in their being uprooted from their land. The verse then points out that a sacred place of security has been made for them, where they receive provisions from God. Despite this, the verse notes that most of them do not have knowledge or understanding of this reality.
orig: وقالوا إن نتبع الهدى معك نتخطف من أرضنا أولم نمكن لهم حرما آمنا يجبى إليه ثمرات كل شيء رزقا من لدنا ولكن أكثرهم لا يعلمون

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so its luxuries became its ruin. So there was for them no stopping, nor were they respite except a little.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse highlights the luxuries and comforts that the people of these towns indulged in, which ultimately led to their downfall. The verse emphasizes the finality of their destruction, as the people had no chance to escape or find respite. The verse serves as a warning to those who indulge in unjust and sinful ways, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the inevitability of God's punishment.
orig: وكم أهلكنا من قرية بطرت معيشتها فتلك مساكنهم لم تسكن من بعدهم إلا قليلا وكنا نحن الوارثين

translation: And your Lord does not destroy the towns (i.e. cities) until He sends to their mother town a messenger, reciting to them Our verses. And We never destroy the towns unless the people thereof are wrongdoers.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of prophethood and the sending of messengers as a mercy from God. It explains that God does not destroy a town without first sending a messenger to recite His verses and give the people a chance to repent. The verse also reiterates that the destruction of towns is not arbitrary, but rather a consequence of the people's wrongdoing and rejection of God's message.
orig: وما كان ربك مهلك القرى حتى يبعث في أمها رسولا يتلو عليهم آياتنا وما كنا مهلكي القرى إلا وأهلها ظالمون

translation: And you do not receive any supplication but the fruit of life in the world and adornment thereof, and what is with Allah is better and more lasting. Then why are you not mindful?
interpretation: The verse highlights the fleeting and temporary nature of worldly possessions and pleasures, emphasizing that the true and lasting rewards come from God. The verse challenges the reader to consider why they are not mindful of this truth, encouraging them to reflect on their priorities and values. The verse serves as a reminder that while worldly possessions and pleasures may provide temporary satisfaction, they are ultimately insignificant compared to the blessings and rewards that come from God. The verse encourages the reader to strive for what is truly valuable and enduring, and to seek the pleasure and approval of God above all else.
orig: وما أوتيتم من شيء فمتاع الحياة الدنيا وزينتها وما عند الله خير وأبقى أفلا تعقلون

translation: Has there not been over man a period of time when he was nothing—no more than a drop of seed merging? Then We made him a small being, lodged in a secure dwelling. Then We made the sperm into a clinging clot, then of that clot We made a lump; then We made out of that lump bones, and clothed the bones with flesh; then We developed out of it another creature. So blessed be Allah, the Best of creators!
interpretation: The verse describes the process of human creation, emphasizing the power and greatness of God as the creator of all things. The verse begins by asking if people remember a time when they were nothing, and then describes the stages of human development from a sperm to a clinging clot, to a lump of flesh, to a fully formed being. The verse concludes by praising God as the Best of creators, emphasizing the miraculous nature of human creation and the need for gratitude and reverence towards God.
orig: أفمن وعدناه وعدا حسنا فهو لاقيه كمن متعناه متاع الحياة الدنيا ثم هو يوم القيامة من المحضرين

translation: And (the day) when He will call them, saying, 'Where are My associates (whom) you used to claim (existed)',
interpretation: The verse speaks of the Day of Judgment when God will call the disbelievers and ask them about their false deities and partners they used to worship and claim to exist. The verse emphasizes the truth that there are no gods but God and highlights the foolishness of those who associated partners with Him. The verse serves as a reminder that all false deities will be proven powerless and insignificant in the face of God's power and majesty on the Day of Judgment.
orig: ويوم يناديهم فيقول أين شركائي الذين كنتم تزعمون

translation: Those who are wretched said, 'Our Lord, these are the ones who misled us; so give them a double punishment in the Fire.'
interpretation: The verse describes the words of the people who have realized their mistakes and are now suffering the consequences of their actions. They recognize that they were misled and ask God to punish those who misled them. The verse emphasizes the idea of accountability for one's actions, and the consequences of leading others astray. It also highlights the severity of the punishment for those who have committed wrongdoings, as the people ask for a 'double punishment' for them. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of guidance and the dangers of misleading others, as well as the significance of taking responsibility for one's actions and facing the consequences.
orig: قال الذين حق عليهم القول ربنا هؤلاء الذين أغوينا أغويناهم كما غوينا تبرأنا إليك ما كانوا إيانا يعبدون

translation: And it was said, 'Invoke your partner-gods.' So they invoked them, but they did not respond to them, and they saw the punishment, and if they had been certain [in disbelief].
interpretation: The verse describes a situation where the disbelievers are challenged to call upon their gods for help, but their gods do not respond. This serves as a powerful demonstration of the falsehood of their beliefs. The verse then describes how the disbelievers witnessed the punishment of God, emphasizing the reality and severity of divine retribution. The final phrase, 'if they had been certain [in disbelief],' highlights the culpability of the disbelievers and their rejection of God's truth despite clear evidence.
orig: وقيل ادعوا شركاءكم فدعوهم فلم يستجيبوا لهم ورأوا العذاب لو أنهم كانوا يهتدون

translation: And (on) the day when He will call them, saying, 'What answer gave you to the messengers?'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the Day of Judgment, when God will call people to account for their actions and their response to His messengers. The verse emphasizes the gravity of the situation and the importance of responding positively to God's messengers. The verse serves as a reminder of the consequences of rejecting or ignoring God's message, and the urgency of accepting and following it. It also highlights the fact that people will be held accountable for their actions and will have to answer for their responses to God's messengers on the Day of Judgment.
orig: ويوم يناديهم فيقول ماذا أجبتم المرسلين

translation: So We sent upon them a single Blast and they became as if they were extinct dates.
interpretation: The verse describes the punishment of a disbelieving people with a single, powerful blast from God, which completely destroyed them. The comparison of the people to 'extinct dates' emphasizes the completeness and finality of their destruction. The verse serves as a reminder of the power and authority of God and the consequences of disbelief and rejection of His messengers.
orig: فعميت عليهم الأنباء يومئذ فهم لا يتساءلون

translation: But as for him who repents, believes, and does good deeds, perhaps he will be among the successful.
interpretation: The verse offers a message of hope and mercy for those who have previously engaged in wrongdoing but then repent, believe in God, and perform good deeds. By doing so, they have the possibility of being among those who are successful. The verse highlights the importance of repentance and striving for righteousness, and the potential for positive change and redemption in one's life.
orig: فأما من تاب وآمن وعمل صالحا فعسى أن يكون من المفلحين

translation: And your Lord creates what He wills and chooses; glory be to God, above what they associate!
interpretation: The verse asserts the power and will of God in creation and His sovereignty over all things. It emphasizes that God creates whatever He wants and chooses the best for His creations. The verse also denies the association of partners with God, exalting Him above the false deities that people may worship. The verse serves as a reminder of God's greatness and power, and the belief in His oneness and uniqueness, free from any partners or equals.
orig: وربك يخلق ما يشاء ويختار ما كان لهم الخيرة سبحان الله وتعالى عما يشركون

translation: And your Lord knows what their breasts conceal and what they reveal.
interpretation: The verse highlights God's all-knowing nature and emphasizes that He is aware of both what people conceal in their hearts and what they reveal through their words and actions. This serves as a reminder that nothing can be hidden from God and that people will be held accountable for their thoughts and actions on the Day of Judgment. It also encourages people to be truthful and sincere in their actions and words, as God is aware of their true intentions and motivations.
orig: وربك يعلم ما تكن صدورهم وما يعلنون

translation: And He is Allah, other than whom there is no deity, the Sovereign, the Pure, the Perfection, the Bestower of Faith, the Overseer, the Exalted in Might, the Compeller, the Supreme. Glory be to Allah above whatever they associate with Him. To Him belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. And He is over all things competent. To Him is the return.
