interpretation: The verse affirms the oneness of Allah and His absolute power and authority over all things. It attributes several beautiful names and attributes to Allah, including the Sovereign, the Pure, the Perfection, the Bestower of Faith, the Overseer, the Exalted in Might, the Compeller, and the Supreme. The verse also emphasizes Allah's greatness and superiority over all other deities. It affirms that all praise is due to Allah, both in the beginning and the end of time. The verse also asserts that all dominion belongs to Allah, both in the heavens and the earth. It emphasizes Allah's power and ability to handle all things, and that all things ultimately return to Him.
orig: وهو الله لا إله إلا هو له الحمد في الأولى والآخرة وله الحكم وإليه ترجعون

translation: Say, 'What if Allah made night for you to continue until the Day of Resurrection, then made for you a dawn revealing, from a god other than Allah, would you not then perceive?',
interpretation: The verse is a rhetorical question posed by the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) to the disbelievers. It asks them to imagine a scenario where Allah makes night last until the Day of Judgment and then creates a bright dawn, but the source of this light is a god other than Allah. The verse challenges the disbelievers to consider whether they would acknowledge and accept the new god in this situation. The verse serves to highlight the futility and absurdity of worshipping any god other than Allah, and emphasizes the unique power and authority of Allah as the only true God.
orig: قل أرأيتم إن جعل الله عليكم الليل سرمدا إلى يوم القيامة من إله غير الله يأتيكم بضياء أفلا تسمعون

translation: Say, 'What if Allah made the day continuous for you until the Day of Resurrection? What deity other than Allah could bring you light? So will you not then consider?'
interpretation: The verse is a challenge to the disbelievers who deny the Oneness of Allah and worship other deities. It asks them to consider the consequences if Allah made the day continuous, without any night, until the Day of Resurrection. The verse emphasizes the dependence of humans on Allah for light and guidance. It challenges the disbelievers to reflect on the futility of worshiping other deities that cannot benefit them in any way. The verse is a reminder of the power and mercy of Allah and the consequences of denying His Oneness.
orig: قل أرأيتم إن جعل الله عليكم النهار سرمدا إلى يوم القيامة من إله غير الله يأتيكم بليل تسكنون فيه أفلا تبصرون

translation: And out of His mercy, He has made for you the night and the day that you might rest therein and seek from His bounty, and that possibly you will be grateful.
interpretation: The verse highlights the mercy of God in creating the night and day for the benefit of human beings. It explains that the night and day provide an opportunity for rest and the pursuit of God's bounty. The verse also encourages gratitude towards God, emphasizing the importance of recognizing and appreciating His blessings. This interpretation suggests that the verse is a reminder of God's compassion and generosity, and a call for humans to be mindful of their blessings and express gratitude for them.
orig: ومن رحمته جعل لكم الليل والنهار لتسكنوا فيه ولتبتغوا من فضله ولعلكم تشكرون

translation: And (the day) when He will call them, saying, 'Where are My associates (whom) you used to claim (existed)',
interpretation: The verse speaks about the Day of Judgment when God will call the disbelievers who claimed that there were other gods besides Him. The verse emphasizes the falsehood of their claim and the ultimate truth that there is only one God. The verse serves as a reminder that all humans will be held accountable for their beliefs and actions on the Day of Judgment, and that any false gods or partners that people associate with God will not be able to help them on that Day.
orig: ويوم يناديهم فيقول أين شركائي الذين كنتم تزعمون

translation: And We took from every nation a witness, and said, 'Bring your proof.' Then they knew that the truth was with Allah, and that which they had been inventing was made lost with them.
interpretation: The verse speaks about God's justice in holding every nation accountable for their actions by taking a witness from each nation. The witness was tasked with presenting proof of their beliefs and actions. When the proof was presented, it became clear that the truth was with God and that the falsehood and deception that the people had invented was rejected and lost. The verse emphasizes the importance of having evidence and proof for one's beliefs and actions, and the consequences of following falsehood and deception. It also highlights God's ultimate justice and knowledge of the truth.
orig: ونزعنا من كل أمة شهيدا فقلنا هاتوا برهانكم فعلموا أن الحق لله وضل عنهم ما كانوا يفترون

translation: Indeed, Qarun was of the community of Moses, but he oppressed them. And We gave him treasures of which the keys would have been a burden for a company of strong men. When his people said to him, 'Do not exult. Indeed, Allah does not like the exultant.'
interpretation: The verse introduces the story of Qarun, a man who was part of the community of Moses but was characterized by his oppression of others. Despite his wealth, represented by the treasures he possessed, his arrogance and pride led him to exult and show off. However, his people warned him against this behavior, reminding him that Allah does not approve of the exultant. The verse serves as a reminder of the dangers of arrogance and pride, and the importance of humility and gratitude for one's blessings.
orig: إن قارون كان من قوم موسى فبغى عليهم وآتيناه من الكنوز ما إن مفاتحه لتنوء بالعصبة أولي القوة إذ قال له قومه لا تفرح إن الله لا يحب الفرحين

translation: And seek in what Allah has given you the home of the Hereafter, and do not forget your share of the world, and be kind as Allah has been kind to you, and do not seek corruption in the land. Indeed, Allah does not like corrupters.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the importance of balancing one's focus between the pursuit of eternal life in the hereafter and the enjoyment of the blessings of this world. It encourages believers to seek the eternal home of the hereafter through good deeds and righteous actions, while also reminding them not to neglect their share of the worldly life. The verse also emphasizes the importance of kindness and compassion, as Allah has been kind to us. At the same time, the verse warns against corruption and destruction in the land, and makes it clear that Allah does not approve of those who sow corruption. The verse serves as a reminder to live a balanced life, to be kind and compassionate, and to avoid corruption and destruction.
orig: وابتغ فيما آتاك الله الدار الآخرة ولا تنس نصيبك من الدنيا وأحسن كما أحسن الله إليك ولا تبغ الفساد في الأرض إن الله لا يحب المفسدين

translation: He said, 'I have only delivered to you that which I was sent with. Do you not know that Allah has destroyed before you of generations which were greater in power and greater in numbers? And they did not wrong except themselves.'
interpretation: The verse recounts a conversation where the speaker is explaining that they have only delivered the message they were sent with, and it is not their responsibility if the message is not heeded. The speaker then reminds the listeners that Allah has destroyed previous generations that were more powerful and numerous, but they still wronged themselves and were destroyed. The interpretation of this verse is a reminder of the power and authority of Allah, and the consequences of not heeding the message of the speaker, who is likely a prophet or messenger. The verse emphasizes the importance of taking responsibility for one's own actions and the potential consequences of not doing so.
orig: قال إنما أوتيته على علم عندي أولم يعلم أن الله قد أهلك من قبله من القرون من هو أشد منه قوة وأكثر جمعا ولا يسأل عن ذنوبهم المجرمون

translation: He came out to his people in his adornment. Those who desire the worldly life said, 'Oh, if only we had the like of what Qarun has been given. Indeed, he is of a great fortune.'
interpretation: The verse describes the people's envy and desire for wealth and status, as exemplified by Qarun. Qarun was a man who was given great wealth and status, but he became arrogant and ungrateful towards God. The people around him, instead of being content with what they have, desired the same wealth and status as Qarun. The verse serves as a reminder that the pursuit of worldly possessions and status should not be the ultimate goal in life, and that such desires can lead to arrogance and ingratitude towards God. It also highlights the dangers of envy and comparison to others, as it can lead to discontentment and a lack of appreciation for one's own blessings.
orig: فخرج على قومه في زينته قال الذين يريدون الحياة الدنيا يا ليت لنا مثل ما أوتي قارون إنه لذو حظ عظيم

translation: And those who were given knowledge said, 'Woe to you! The reward of God is better for those who believe and do good deeds. But none will receive it except the patient.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the superiority of the reward from God for those who believe and do good deeds. Those who have knowledge warn those who do not of the consequences of their actions. The verse highlights the importance of patience in receiving the reward from God. It serves as a reminder that true rewards come to those who are patient and steadfast in their faith and actions. The verse encourages the believers to have patience and perseverance, and to continue to strive for good deeds, as the ultimate reward comes from God.
orig: وقال الذين أوتوا العلم ويلكم ثواب الله خير لمن آمن وعمل صالحا ولا يلقاها إلا الصابرون

translation: And We caused the earth to swallow them and their homes, and there was for them no helper against Allah, nor were they of those who were helped.
interpretation: The verse describes the punishment of a group of people who were destroyed by causing the earth to swallow them and their homes. This event emphasizes the power and control of Allah, as no one was able to help them against His will. The verse also highlights the isolation of these people, as they were not among those who are aided or supported. This verse serves as a reminder of the ultimate power and authority of Allah and the consequences of going against His will.
orig: فخسفنا به وبداره الأرض فما كان له من فئة ينصرونه من دون الله وما كان من المنتصرين

translation: But those who were already settled in its place the day before said, 'It is but a morn of misfortune.' How will God give increase to us today, when it is He who has diminished us in the past? Thus do they not perceive?
interpretation: The verse describes the reaction of the people who were settled in a town that was destroyed by God's punishment. They express their disbelief at the sudden and unexpected nature of the destruction, and question how God could provide for them now, when it is He who had diminished their resources in the past. The verse highlights the people's lack of understanding and perception, as they fail to see the connection between their past actions and the present consequences. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of recognizing and acknowledging the signs of God, and of living a righteous and just life.
orig: وأصبح الذين تمنوا مكانه بالأمس يقولون ويكأن الله يبسط الرزق لمن يشاء من عباده ويقدر لولا أن من الله علينا لخسف بنا ويكأنه لا يفلح الكافرون

translation: That home of the Hereafter - We make it for those who do not desire exaltedness in the earth or corruption. And the outcome is for the righteous.
interpretation: The verse describes the eternal home in the hereafter that God has prepared for certain individuals. These individuals are those who do not seek corruption or exaltedness in this world. The verse highlights the idea that true success and happiness are not found in worldly gains or power, but in leading a righteous and virtuous life. The outcome, or ultimate destiny, is reserved for those who are righteous and pious, implying that their good deeds and virtuous actions will be rewarded in the afterlife.
orig: تلك الدار الآخرة نجعلها للذين لا يريدون علوا في الأرض ولا فسادا والعاقبة للمتقين

translation: Whoever comes with a good deed will have better than it, and whoever comes with an evil deed will not be recompensed except with its equivalent. But whoever comes with a good deed - their recompense is with their Lord. Upon them will be no fear, nor will they grieve.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the consequences of actions, whether good or bad. It explains that those who do good will receive a reward that is better than their deed, while those who do evil will receive a punishment equivalent to their deed. However, the verse also offers hope for those who do good, as they will receive their reward from their Lord and will not have to fear or grieve. This verse encourages people to strive for good actions and to avoid evil, as the consequences of their actions will ultimately be determined by God.
orig: من جاء بالحسنة فله خير منها ومن جاء بالسيئة فلا يجزى الذين عملوا السيئات إلا ما كانوا يعملون

translation: Indeed, it is He who has revealed to you the Qur'an. [With] a reminder for you. Your Lord is the All-Knowing, the All-Aware. [As for] who disputes with you in this matter after the knowledge has come to you, say, 'Come, let us call upon our sons and your sons, our women and your women, ourselves and yourselves, then let us earnestly pray [together] and invoke the curse of Allah upon the liars [among us].' Indeed, this is the true narration. And there is no deity except Allah. And indeed, Allah is the Exalted in Might, the Wise.
interpretation: The verse addresses the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and reminds him that it is Allah who has revealed the Quran to him. The verse emphasizes Allah's knowledge and awareness of all things. The verse then speaks to those who dispute the truth that has been revealed. It challenges them to bring forth their evidence and to earnestly pray and invoke the curse of Allah upon the liars. The verse affirms the truth of the message brought by the Prophet and the oneness of Allah. It emphasizes Allah's greatness and wisdom. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of holding firm to the truth and the consequences of rejecting it.
orig: إن الذي فرض عليك القرآن لرادك إلى معاد قل ربي أعلم من جاء بالهدى ومن هو في ضلال مبين

translation: And you did not expect that the Book would be sent down to you, except as a mercy from your Lord. So be never a supporter of the disbelievers.
interpretation: The verse highlights the merciful nature of the revelation of the Qur'an, emphasizing that it was not sent down as a punishment or a burden, but as a mercy from the Lord. This mercy is not only for the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), but also for all of humanity. The verse then instructs the Prophet not to align himself with the disbelievers, and not to support or aid them in their disbelief. This is a reminder for all believers to stand firm in their faith, and not to be swayed by the actions or beliefs of those who reject the message of Islam.
orig: وما كنت ترجو أن يلقى إليك الكتاب إلا رحمة من ربك فلا تكونن ظهيرا للكافرين

translation: And let not those who disbelieve prevent you from the remembrance of Allah. (And) invoke (Allah) in the morning and the evening. And during a part of the night, glorify Him and after prostrations. And listen the day when the Caller will call from a near place, The Day when they will hear the Blast in truth; that is the Day of coming forth.
interpretation: The verse is a command to the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) to continue to remember and worship Allah, regardless of the disbelievers' efforts to prevent him from doing so. The verse encourages the Prophet to invoke Allah in the morning and evening, and during a part of the night, as well as glorify Him and prostrate. The verse also mentions the Day of Judgment, when a caller will summon all people and they will hear the blast, indicating the end of the world. The verse emphasizes the importance of worshiping Allah and remembering Him, and the inevitability of the Day of Judgment, and encourages the believers to be steadfast in their faith and not be swayed by the disbelievers.
orig: ولا يصدنك عن آيات الله بعد إذ أنزلت إليك وادع إلى ربك ولا تكونن من المشركين

translation: And put not with Allah another ilah (god); or, (yet) you will sit down condemned and forsaken; it is Allah, (Alone,) the Lord of the Throne, (Who is) All-High, (All-Glorious). Every thing (that exists) will perish except His Face. To Him belongs the Command, and to Him will you (all) be brought back.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of worshipping only one God, Allah, and warns against associating any other gods with Him. Those who do so will be condemned and forsaken. The verse affirms that Allah is the Lord of the Throne, the All-High, and All-Glorious, and that everything in existence will perish except for His Face. This means that only Allah's existence is eternal, and all other things will come to an end. The verse also asserts that all Command and authority belongs to Allah, and all of creation will ultimately return to Him. The verse serves as a reminder of the oneness of Allah, and the ultimate accountability of all creatures to Him.
orig: ولا تدع مع الله إلها آخر لا إله إلا هو كل شيء هالك إلا وجهه له الحكم وإليه ترجعون

translation: The (revelation) of the Book (the Quran) is from Allah, the Exalted in Power, Full of Wisdom.
interpretation: The verse asserts that the Quran is a revelation from Allah, the all-powerful and wise. This declaration emphasizes the divine origin of the Quran, and the fact that it is a source of guidance and wisdom for all of humanity. The verse implies that the Quran is not a creation of human beings, but a revelation from the all-knowing and wise God. This interpretation encourages Muslims to respect and follow the teachings of the Quran, and to seek guidance from its verses in all aspects of their lives.
orig: الم

translation: And let not the people think that they will escape [from Allah's punishment] because they say, 'We believe' while they do not [truly] believe.
interpretation: The verse warns against the false belief that merely uttering the words 'We believe' will protect people from God's punishment. The verse highlights the importance of sincerity and authenticity in faith, and criticizes those who claim to believe but do not truly practice their faith. The verse serves as a reminder that outward expressions of faith are not enough, and that true belief must be reflected in actions and behavior. The verse encourages individuals to examine their beliefs and actions, and to strive for authenticity and sincerity in their faith.
orig: أحسب الناس أن يتركوا أن يقولوا آمنا وهم لا يفتنون

translation: And We indeed tested those who have gone before them. So let know
interpretation: No interpretation
orig: ولقد فتنا الذين من قبلهم فليعلمن الله الذين صدقوا وليعلمن الكاذبين

translation: Or do those who do evil deeds think that We will make them like those who believe and do righteous deeds - making their lives and their religion easier for them?
interpretation: The verse highlights the mistaken belief of those who do evil deeds, that they will be treated the same as those who believe and do good. The verse challenges this notion and emphasizes that God will not make the path easy for those who commit sins and wrongdoings. Instead, the verse serves as a reminder that God will make the path easier for those who believe and do good, in both their worldly and religious life. The verse also serves as a warning to those who are committing sins and wrongdoings, urging them to turn away from their evil ways and instead strive for righteousness and belief.
orig: أم حسب الذين يعملون السيئات أن يسبقونا ساء ما يحكمون

translation: Whoever desires the encounter with God, then indeed, the encounter with God will come. And God is all-hearing, all-knowing.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the inevitability of meeting God and the fact that it will happen when God wills it. The verse emphasizes God's omniscience and omnipresence, reminding the reader that God hears and knows all. The verse may serve as a reminder that all of our actions and intentions will be known to God and that we will ultimately be held accountable for them. It may also serve as a source of comfort and hope for those who long for the meeting with God, reminding them that it is certain and will happen in its due time.
orig: من كان يرجو لقاء الله فإن أجل الله لآت وهو السميع العليم

translation: But as for him who strives, strives only for himself, for indeed, Allah is free from need of the worlds.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of striving and working hard, but at the same time, it reminds the readers that the ultimate purpose of this striving is for one's own self and not for the sake of pleasing others. The verse also highlights the self-sufficiency of Allah, reminding the readers that Allah does not need anything from His creation, but rather, it is the creation that is in need of Allah. This verse encourages individuals to strive for their own personal growth, development and success, while keeping in mind that true fulfillment and satisfaction can only come from a relationship with Allah.
orig: ومن جاهد فإنما يجاهد لنفسه إن الله لغني عن العالمين

translation: And those who believe and do good deeds, We will surely remove from them their misdeeds, and We will surely reward them according to the best of what they used to do.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the reward for those who believe in God and do good deeds. The verse emphasizes that God will forgive their sins and reward them according to the best of what they used to do. The verse serves as a motivation for believers to continue doing good deeds and have faith in God's mercy and justice, knowing that they will be rewarded for their actions in the afterlife.
orig: والذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات لنكفرن عنهم سيئاتهم ولنجزينهم أحسن الذي كانوا يعملون

translation: And We have enjoined on man concerning his parents - his mother bears him in weakness upon weakness and his weaning is in two years - Give thanks to Me and to your parents. To Me is the final destination. But if they endeavor to make you associate with Me that of which you have no knowledge, then do not obey them. But keep company with them in this worldly life with kindness and respect. And follow the way of him who turns to Me in repentance. Then to Me will be your return, and I will inform you of what you used to do.
interpretation: This verse speaks about the relationship between human beings and their parents, emphasizing the importance of showing gratitude and respect towards them. It highlights the role of mothers in particular, who bear and nurture their children in a state of weakness. At the same time, the verse warns against following the misguided beliefs or practices of parents if they conflict with the worship of God. Ultimately, the verse reminds us that we will all return to God, who will judge us based on our actions and hold us accountable for our deeds.
orig: ووصينا الإنسان بوالديه حسنا وإن جاهداك لتشرك بي ما ليس لك به علم فلا تطعهما إلي مرجعكم فأنبئكم بما كنتم تعملون

translation: And those who believe and do good deeds, We will admit them to the ranks of the righteous.
interpretation: The verse highlights the criteria for being admitted to the company of the righteous, which are twofold: belief and good deeds. The verse suggests that those who hold faith and perform righteous actions will be granted entry into the group of the righteous. The verse serves as an encouragement for believers to uphold their faith and perform good deeds as a means of achieving a favorable outcome in the afterlife.
orig: والذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات لندخلنهم في الصالحين

translation: And among the people is he who says: 'We believe in Allah,' but when he is harmed in Allah's way, he makes partners (to Allah) of that which he has not done any good - that Allah should be equated with (His) creation. And if it befall him some good fortune from his Lord, he forgets that which he was before, and sets up equals to Allah.
interpretation: The verse describes the hypocrisy of some people who claim to believe in Allah but, when faced with harm or difficulty, they turn to other things for help and support, as if equating them with Allah. This is a form of disbelief and a rejection of the oneness of Allah. The verse also highlights the fleeting nature of their faith, as they quickly forget about Allah when they are blessed with good fortune, and start to worship and idolize the blessings instead of the One who bestowed them. The verse serves as a reminder that Allah knows best what is in the hearts of all beings, and that no one can hide their true intentions from Him.
orig: ومن الناس من يقول آمنا بالله فإذا أوذي في الله جعل فتنة الناس كعذاب الله ولئن جاء نصر من ربك ليقولن إنا كنا معكم أوليس الله بأعلم بما في صدور العالمين

translation: And let Allah know the believers and let know the hypocrites.
interpretation: This verse speaks about Allah's knowledge of the true believers and the hypocrites. The verse emphasizes that Allah has complete knowledge and understanding of the intentions and actions of all people. The believers are those who have true faith in Allah and follow His teachings, while the hypocrites are those who outwardly profess faith but inwardly harbor disbelief and doubt. The verse serves as a reminder that Allah sees all and knows all, and that He will ultimately judge each person according to their true beliefs and actions.
orig: وليعلمن الله الذين آمنوا وليعلمن المنافقين

translation: And those who disbelieved said to those who believed, 'Follow our way, and we will bear your sins.' But they will not bear any of their sins from anything. Indeed, they are liars.
interpretation: The verse highlights the false promises made by the disbelievers to the believers, inviting them to follow their way and claiming that they will bear their sins. However, the verse makes it clear that the disbelievers will not bear any of the believers' sins, emphasizing their falsehood and deceit. The verse serves as a warning to the believers to be cautious of those who make false promises and to be firm in their faith and beliefs.
orig: وقال الذين كفروا للذين آمنوا اتبعوا سبيلنا ولنحمل خطاياكم وما هم بحاملين من خطاياهم من شيء إنهم لكاذبون

translation: And let them carry their loads, and (carry) on their loads, and let them ask the bearers of the Throne (about) their (state) on the Day of Resurrection.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the heavy burden of sins and wrongdoings that people will carry with them on the Day of Judgment. The image of people carrying their loads and additional loads emphasizes the weight and gravity of their sins. The verse also mentions the bearers of the Throne, who are the angels that support God's Throne, and encourages people to ask them about their state on the Day of Resurrection. The verse conveys a sense of accountability and responsibility for one's actions and the consequences of not seeking forgiveness and repentance for sins.
orig: وليحملن أثقالهم وأثقالا مع أثقالهم وليسألن يوم القيامة عما كانوا يفترون

translation: And indeed We sent Noah to his people, and he stayed among them a thousand years less fifty, and the deluge overtook them while they were unjust.
interpretation: The verse relates the story of Prophet Noah and his people, emphasizing that he preached to them for a long period of time (a thousand years less fifty) before the flood overtook them. Despite this, they remained unjust and ignored Noah's message. The verse serves as a reminder that God gives ample time and opportunities for people to repent and change their ways, but if they persist in their wrongdoing, they will face consequences.
orig: ولقد أرسلنا نوحا إلى قومه فلبث فيهم ألف سنة إلا خمسين عاما فأخذهم الطوفان وهم ظالمون

translation: So We saved him and his companions in the ship, and We made it a sign for all peoples.
interpretation: The verse speaks about a specific event where a person and their companions were saved by God, and their ship became a sign or a lesson for all people. The verse highlights God's mercy and protection towards the believers and the use of this event as a reminder and a warning for others. It serves as a call for people to reflect on the signs and lessons in their own lives and to recognize God's power and wisdom.
orig: فأنجيناه وأصحاب السفينة وجعلناها آية للعالمين

translation: And [mention, O Muhammad], when Abraham said to his people, 'Worship Allah and fear Him. That is better for you, if you are believers.'
interpretation: The verse highlights the message of Prophet Abraham (peace be upon him) to his people, calling them to worship and fear Allah. The verse emphasizes the benefit of this action, stating that it is 'better for you, if you are believers.' This verse serves to remind us of the importance of worshipping and fearing Allah, and the positive impact it can have on our lives. It also highlights the role of prophets in guiding their people towards the right path and reminding them of their responsibilities towards Allah.
orig: وإبراهيم إذ قال لقومه اعبدوا الله واتقوه ذلكم خير لكم إن كنتم تعلمون

translation: You only worship, apart from Allah, idols, and you invent falsehood. Those whom you worship apart from Allah have no power to provide for you. So seek provision from Allah and worship Him and be grateful to Him. To Him you will be returned.
interpretation: The verse highlights the futility of worshipping false idols and making them partners with Allah. These idols, which are created by human hands, have no power to provide for the needs of the people. The verse urges people to seek provision and sustenance from Allah alone, who is the only provider. Worshipping Allah and being grateful to Him are the only ways to true success and happiness. The verse ends with a reminder that all of humanity will ultimately return to Allah and be held accountable for their actions.
orig: إنما تعبدون من دون الله أوثانا وتخلقون إفكا إن الذين تعبدون من دون الله لا يملكون لكم رزقا فابتغوا عند الله الرزق واعبدوه واشكروا له إليه ترجعون

translation: And if you deny (it, i.e. God's revelation), then already have denied (it) before you) many of the nations; and there came to them Revelators before you, and to them with clear Arguments; then, I seized the disbelievers, and how (terrible) was My Rejection!
interpretation: The verse speaks about the consequences of denying God's revelation and the punishment that will be faced by those who reject it. The verse emphasizes that the current disbelievers are not the first to deny God's message, and that many nations before them have done the same. Despite the clear arguments presented to them, they still rejected the truth. The verse serves as a reminder that God's rejection and punishment will be severe for those who persist in their disbelief and denial of His revelation.
orig: وإن تكذبوا فقد كذب أمم من قبلكم وما على الرسول إلا البلاغ المبين

translation: Have they not seen how Allah begins the creation, then repeats it? Indeed, that is easy for Allah.
interpretation: The verse highlights the power and ability of Allah to create and recreate life, emphasizing the ease with which He can do so. This serves as a reminder of Allah's omnipotence and sovereignty, and the insignificance of human beings in comparison. The verse encourages people to reflect on the signs of Allah in the world around them and to recognize His greatness and power. It also implies that just as Allah can easily create life, He can also easily bring about its end, and that people should always be mindful of this fact and strive to live in accordance with Allah's will.
orig: أولم يروا كيف يبدئ الله الخلق ثم يعيده إن ذلك على الله يسير

translation: Say, 'Travel through the land and observe how He began creation. Then Allah will produce the next creation. Indeed, Allah is over all things competent.'
interpretation: The verse encourages the listener to observe and reflect on the signs of Allah in the natural world, specifically focusing on the process of creation. By reflecting on how Allah began creation, the listener will come to understand that Allah has the power to produce a new creation. This serves as a reminder of Allah's omnipotence and ability to bring about whatever He wills. The verse may also be interpreted as a call to study and learn from the natural world, as it contains lessons and signs for those who reflect.
orig: قل سيروا في الأرض فانظروا كيف بدأ الخلق ثم الله ينشئ النشأة الآخرة إن الله على كل شيء قدير

translation: He punishes whom He wills and He forgives whom He wills. And to Him you will be returned.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the power and authority of God in meting out punishment and forgiveness. The verse reminds the reader that God is the ultimate authority and that all actions and consequences ultimately belong to Him. The last part of the verse, 'And to Him you will be returned', serves as a reminder of the Day of Judgment and the ultimate accountability of all actions to God.
orig: يعذب من يشاء ويرحم من يشاء وإليه تقلبون

translation: And you are not, within the grace of God, held as withholders, nor are you possessors of might in the land or the sky: you have none, apart from God, as a guardian or helper.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the powerlessness and dependence of humans on God, stating that people do not have control over the earth or the sky, and have no protector or helper apart from God. The phrase 'withholders' (معجزين) is interpreted to mean those who prevent or withhold blessings or good. The verse serves as a reminder of the limits of human power and control, and the ultimate dependence on God's grace and protection. The verse encourages humility and submission to God, recognizing one's own limitations and dependence on God's mercy and support.
orig: وما أنتم بمعجزين في الأرض ولا في السماء وما لكم من دون الله من ولي ولا نصير

translation: And those who disbelieved in the signs of Allah and in their meeting with Him - their punishment is that they will be desperate for My mercy, and for them is a painful punishment.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the fate of those who disbelieve in the signs of God and deny the Day of Judgment. These people will ultimately be disappointed and regretful when they realize the reality of God's mercy, but it will be too late. The verse highlights the severe consequences of disbelief and denial, emphasizing that those who choose this path will face a painful punishment.
orig: والذين كفروا بآيات الله ولقائه أولئك يئسوا من رحمتي وأولئك لهم عذاب أليم

translation: But the only answer of his people was that they said, 'Kill him or burn him.' But Allah saved him from the fire. Indeed, in that are signs for a people who believe.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the story of a prophet who was threatened by his people to be killed or burned. However, God saved him from the fire. The verse emphasizes the miraculous nature of the prophet's salvation as a sign from God. The verse serves as a reminder for the believers to reflect on the signs of God and to have faith in His protection and power.
orig: فما كان جواب قومه إلا أن قالوا اقتلوه أو حرقوه فأنجاه الله من النار إن في ذلك لآيات لقوم يؤمنون

translation: And they have said: 'You have taken (for worship) only idols instead of Allah, out of love amongst yourselves in the present life! But on the Day of Resurrection, some of you shall disown others, and some of you shall curse others, and your refuge will be the Fire, and you shall have no helpers.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about people who have taken idols as objects of worship, instead of Allah, out of love and affection for each other in this worldly life. However, on the Day of Judgment, some of them will disown and curse each other, and their final destination will be the Fire. The verse highlights the transient nature of worldly relationships and the consequences of idol worship, emphasizing that in the end, people will be left alone to face the consequences of their actions. The verse serves as a reminder to turn towards Allah and seek His guidance and protection, instead of relying on worldly relationships and false deities.
orig: وقال إنما اتخذتم من دون الله أوثانا مودة بينكم في الحياة الدنيا ثم يوم القيامة يكفر بعضكم ببعض ويلعن بعضكم بعضا ومأواكم النار وما لكم من ناصرين

translation: Lot believed in him [the messenger] and said, 'I am fleeing to my Lord. He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the belief of Lot in the messenger and his decision to flee to his Lord, who is described as the Exalted in Might and the Wise. The verse highlights the faith of Lot and his trust in God's protection and guidance. It also emphasizes the attributes of God as being all-powerful and wise, indicating that Lot's decision to flee was based on his belief in God's ability to protect him and his wisdom in guiding him to safety.
orig: فآمن له لوط وقال إني مهاجر إلى ربي إنه هو العزيز الحكيم

translation: And We gave him Isaac and Jacob and placed in his descendants prophethood and scripture, and granted him his reward in this world, and indeed he is among the righteous in the hereafter.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the blessings that God bestowed upon a particular person, including the gift of his sons Isaac and Jacob, the placement of prophethood and scripture among his descendants, and the reward that he received in this world. The verse also highlights the righteousness of this person and his status among the righteous in the hereafter. The verse can be interpreted as a recognition of the blessings and rewards that come to those who are chosen by God and who live a righteous life, and as a reminder of the ultimate reward that awaits them in the hereafter.
orig: ووهبنا له إسحاق ويعقوب وجعلنا في ذريته النبوة والكتاب وآتيناه أجره في الدنيا وإنه في الآخرة لمن الصالحين

translation: And Lot, when he said to his people: 'Indeed, you commit such immorality as no people before you have ever done.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the Prophet Lot's warning to his people about their immoral actions. The verse emphasizes the severity of their sins, stating that no people before them have ever committed such acts. This verse serves as a reminder that engaging in immoral behavior has severe consequences and that it is not a new phenomenon. It highlights the importance of avoiding sin and following the path of righteousness, as the people of Lot were destroyed as a result of their disobedience and refusal to heed the warnings of the Prophet Lot.
orig: ولوطا إذ قال لقومه إنكم لتأتون الفاحشة ما سبقكم بها من أحد من العالمين

translation: Then are you coming to the men, and taking away their property, and committing evil, and making crimes in your meetings? And how was the answer of the messengers but that they said, 'Bring to us God's punishment if you are truthful?'
interpretation: The verse describes a situation where a group of people are taking advantage of others by taking their property, committing evil deeds, and engaging in immoral activities during their meetings. The verse emphasizes the injustice and corruption of these people. The response of the messengers to their actions was to challenge them to bring God's punishment upon them if they are truthful, highlighting the certainty of God's judgment and the consequences of their actions.
orig: أئنكم لتأتون الرجال وتقطعون السبيل وتأتون في ناديكم المنكر فما كان جواب قومه إلا أن قالوا ائتنا بعذاب الله إن كنت من الصادقين

translation: Said [the] Lord, 'Aid me against the corrupting people.'
interpretation: The verse is a supplication from God for aid against those who spread corruption and disorder in the land. It highlights the struggle between good and evil, and the need for divine intervention to support the righteous and uphold justice. The verse may also serve as a call for believers to stand up against corruption and work towards creating a just and righteous society.
orig: قال رب انصرني على القوم المفسدين

translation: And when Our messengers came to Abraham with the good news, they said, 'Indeed, we will destroy the people of this town, for its people are unjust.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the announcement of the destruction of a town due to the unjust actions of its people. The messengers of God brought the news to Abraham, highlighting the certainty of the punishment that the people of the town will face due to their wrongdoings. The verse serves as a reminder of the consequences of injustice and the impartiality of God's judgment.
orig: ولما جاءت رسلنا إبراهيم بالبشرى قالوا إنا مهلكو أهل هذه القرية إن أهلها كانوا ظالمين

translation: But We saved him and his family, except for his wife; she was of those who remained behind.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the story of Lot and his people. Despite the people of Lot's disbelief and rejection of his message, God saved Lot and his family, with the exception of his wife. The phrase 'she was of those who remained behind' implies that she was among the disbelievers, and as a consequence, she was punished along with the people of Lot.
orig: قال إن فيها لوطا قالوا نحن أعلم بمن فيها لننجينه وأهله إلا امرأته كانت من الغابرين

translation: But when Our messengers came to Lot, they were troubled by them and felt oppressed, and they said, 'Do not fear and do not grieve, indeed, we will save you and your family, except for your wife - she is of those who remain behind.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the story of Prophet Lot and the people of Sodom and Gomorrah. When the angels, who were sent by God as messengers, came to Lot, the people of the town were hostile and oppressive towards them. The angels informed Lot that they will save him and his family, except for his wife, who will be left behind. This verse emphasizes the wickedness of the people of Sodom and Gomorrah and the punishment they received from God. It also highlights the role of Prophet Lot as a Prophet and a Warner, and the mercy of God in saving him and his family. Additionally, the verse can be seen as a reminder of the consequences of oppression and disbelief, and the importance of obedience and trust in God.
orig: ولما أن جاءت رسلنا لوطا سيء بهم وضاق بهم ذرعا وقالوا لا تخف ولا تحزن إنا منجوك وأهلك إلا امرأتك كانت من الغابرين

translation: We have been sending down upon the people of this town punishment from the sky because of their sins.
interpretation: The verse describes the punishment that is being inflicted upon the people of a town as a consequence of their sins. The punishment is coming from the sky, which could symbolize the power and authority of God. The use of the present tense in the Arabic text ("minanziluna") emphasizes the ongoing nature of the punishment, indicating that it is a continuous process. The verse serves as a reminder that actions have consequences, and that those who engage in sinful behavior will ultimately be held accountable for their actions.
orig: إنا منزلون على أهل هذه القرية رجزا من السماء بما كانوا يفسقون

translation: And We have certainly left a visible sign for a people who understand.
interpretation: The verse speaks about a clear sign or indication that has been left for a group of people who have the ability to understand and reflect upon it. This sign serves as a reminder and a guidance for those who are willing to acknowledge and learn from it. The verse encourages the reader to be among those who use their intellect and reason to understand the signs and messages that are presented to them, rather than ignoring or dismissing them.
orig: ولقد تركنا منها آية بينة لقوم يعقلون

translation: And to a town (was sent) their brother Shu'ayb, so he said, 'O my people, worship Allah and expect the Last Day and do not corrupt in the earth with mischief.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the Prophet Shu'ayb (peace be upon him) being sent to a town to call its people to worship Allah and to do good. The verse emphasizes the importance of expecting the Last Day and avoiding corruption and mischief in the earth. The verse serves as a reminder to the believers to follow the teachings of the Prophet Shu'ayb (peace be upon him) and to be mindful of their actions and their impact on the society. It also highlights the role of the prophets as a guide and a warner for their people.
orig: وإلى مدين أخاهم شعيبا فقال يا قوم اعبدوا الله وارجوا اليوم الآخر ولا تعثوا في الأرض مفسدين

translation: And they denied him, so the shock seized them at night, and they were found lifeless in their homes in the morning.
interpretation: The verse describes the punishment of those who rejected a prophet, resulting in a sudden and unexpected seizure at night. The use of the word 'shock' implies a sudden and violent event, emphasizing the swiftness and severity of the punishment. The phrase 'they were found lifeless in their homes in the morning' reinforces the unexpected nature of the event, as the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who reject God's messengers and reminders, emphasizing the consequences of their actions and the swiftness of God's punishment.
orig: فكذبوه فأخذتهم الرجفة فأصبحوا في دارهم جاثمين

translation: But [We destroyed] 'Aad and Thamud and indeed you have passed by their dwellings after them. And ever was the Messenger a thing accused.
interpretation: The verse mentions the destruction of the people of 'Aad and Thamud, and reminds the listeners that they have passed by the ruins of their homes. Despite the signs and evidence of the punishment that was meted out to these people, they still rejected the message of the prophets. The verse highlights the fact that prophets are often met with disbelief and rejection, and that this is not a new phenomenon. The verse serves as a reminder that the truth will ultimately prevail, and that those who reject the message will face consequences for their actions.
orig: وعادا وثمود وقد تبين لكم من مساكنهم وزين لهم الشيطان أعمالهم فصدهم عن السبيل وكانوا مستبصرين

translation: And Korah and Pharaoh and Haman, indeed Moses came to them with clear proofs, but they were arrogant in the land, and they were not [even] the first [to be so].
interpretation: The verse mentions four figures from Islamic tradition - Korah, Pharaoh, Haman, and Moses - and contrasts the arrogance of the first three with the mission of the fourth. Despite the clear evidence provided by Moses, the first three figures refused to acknowledge the truth and continued in their arrogance. The verse serves as a reminder that arrogance and rejection of God's message is not a new phenomenon, and that those who persist in these behaviors will face consequences. The verse also emphasizes the importance of humility and openness to God's message, as embodied by Moses.
orig: وقارون وفرعون وهامان ولقد جاءهم موسى بالبينات فاستكبروا في الأرض وما كانوا سابقين

translation: And We never punish until We send a messenger. So when We have decided to destroy a town, We send a command to those among them who lead a life of luxury. Then they disobey therein, so We destroy them utterly.
interpretation: The verse explains that God does not punish without first sending a messenger to warn the people. When God has decided to destroy a town, a command is sent to those who are living in luxury and comfort. However, they disobey and reject the message, leading to their destruction. The verse emphasizes the importance of heeding the warnings of the messengers and the consequences of disobedience and rejection of God's message.
orig: فكلا أخذنا بذنبه فمنهم من أرسلنا عليه حاصبا ومنهم من أخذته الصيحة ومنهم من خسفنا به الأرض ومنهم من أغرقنا وما كان الله ليظلمهم ولكن كانوا أنفسهم يظلمون

translation: Like those who take others than Allah as protectors are like the spider, who has made for itself a house, but indeed, if they only knew.
interpretation: The verse compares those who take protectors other than God to a spider, which builds its own house, but in reality, the house of a spider is weak and offers little protection. The verse suggests that those who rely on other than God for protection are building their security on a shaky foundation. The phrase 'but indeed, if they only knew' implies that if these people truly understood the futility of their actions, they would not take this path. This verse serves as a reminder that true protection and security can only come from God.
orig: مثل الذين اتخذوا من دون الله أولياء كمثل العنكبوت اتخذت بيتا وإن أوهن البيوت لبيت العنكبوت لو كانوا يعلمون

translation: Indeed, Allah knows what you invoke besides Him from things. And He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise.
interpretation: The verse affirms that Allah has knowledge of all the things that people invoke or call upon besides Him. The verse emphasizes Allah's greatness and power, referring to Him as 'the Exalted in Might', and His wisdom, referring to Him as 'the Wise'. The verse serves as a reminder that no matter what people may worship or call upon, Allah has knowledge of it and that He is the only one who truly has power and wisdom. It is a reminder of Allah's omniscience and omnipotence, and that all other deities or powers are false and ultimately powerless.
orig: إن الله يعلم ما يدعون من دونه من شيء وهو العزيز الحكيم

translation: And such examples We strike for mankind, but none comprehends them except the knowing.
interpretation: The verse suggests that God uses examples and parables to teach and guide humanity. However, the verse also emphasizes that only those who are wise and knowledgeable can truly understand and comprehend these examples. The verse may serve as a reminder that gaining knowledge and wisdom is crucial for understanding the world and God's messages. It can also be interpreted as a warning that those who lack wisdom and knowledge may not be able to comprehend the lessons and examples set before them, and may therefore miss out on an opportunity for growth and understanding.
orig: وتلك الأمثال نضربها للناس وما يعقلها إلا العالمون

translation: Allah is the one who created the heavens and the earth in truth. Indeed, in that is a sign for the believers.
interpretation: The verse affirms the power and wisdom of Allah as the creator of the heavens and the earth. The use of the word 'truth' (الحق) emphasizes the certainty and reality of Allah's creation. The verse also highlights the significance of this creation as a sign (آية) for the believers, implying that the creation of the heavens and the earth serves as a reminder of Allah's existence and power. The verse encourages believers to reflect on the wonders of creation and to seek guidance and understanding through reflection and contemplation.
orig: خلق الله السماوات والأرض بالحق إن في ذلك لآية للمؤمنين

translation: Recite what has been revealed to you of the Book and establish prayer. Indeed, prayer prohibits immorality and wrongdoing, and the remembrance of Allah is the greatest. And Allah knows what you do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of reciting and following the teachings of the Q Book (referring to the Qur'an) and establishing prayer. The verse highlights the role of prayer in preventing people from engaging in immoral and wrong actions. It also mentions the greatness of remembering and worshiping God. The verse also reminds that God has knowledge of all that people do, emphasizing the importance of accountability for one's actions.
orig: اتل ما أوحي إليك من الكتاب وأقم الصلاة إن الصلاة تنهى عن الفحشاء والمنكر ولذكر الله أكبر والله يعلم ما تصنعون

translation: And do not argue with the People of the Scripture except in a way that is best, except for those who commit injustice among them, and say, 'We believe in that which has been revealed to us and revealed to you. And our God and your God is one; and we are Muslims [in submission] to Him.'
interpretation: The verse advises Muslims to engage in respectful and constructive dialogue with followers of other religions, specifically the People of the Scripture or Jews and Christians. It emphasizes the importance of using kind and gentle words, except for those who commit injustice among them. The verse encourages Muslims to find common ground with people of other faiths and to focus on their shared belief in one God. The verse promotes unity, understanding, and peaceful coexistence among different religious communities.
orig: ولا تجادلوا أهل الكتاب إلا بالتي هي أحسن إلا الذين ظلموا منهم وقولوا آمنا بالذي أنزل إلينا وأنزل إليكم وإلهنا وإلهكم واحد ونحن له مسلمون

translation: And thus have We sent down the Book to you (O Muhammad) and those whom We have before you. So (as for) those to whom We have given the Book, they believe in it (the Quran). And as for those who disbelieve, they say, 'It is not except a lie which he (Muhammad) has forged, and those who believe in it are the unjust.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the revelation of the Quran to the Prophet Muhammad and the previous scriptures that were given to earlier prophets. The verse highlights the belief of those who have received the scriptures in the Quran, while the disbelievers reject it and consider it a falsehood. The verse emphasizes the contrast between the believers and the unbelievers, and the rejection of the Quran by the unbelievers is attributed to their disbelief and injustice. The verse reaffirms the divine origin of the Quran and the truth of its message, and it serves as a reminder that those who reject it will face consequences for their disbelief.
orig: وكذلك أنزلنا إليك الكتاب فالذين آتيناهم الكتاب يؤمنون به ومن هؤلاء من يؤمن به وما يجحد بآياتنا إلا الكافرون

translation: And never have I recited to you from a Book before this - you were not with the companions of the right -
interpretation: The verse speaks about the unique and unprecedented nature of the revelation of the Qur'an. The speaker, believed to be the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH), states that he has not recited anything from a book before this, implying the divine origin of the Qur'an. The verse also emphasizes that the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) was not present among the previous nations or communities that received revelations before, highlighting the newness and distinctiveness of the Islamic message. The verse serves as a reminder that the Qur'an is a unique and final revelation from God, and that it brings a new and comprehensive message for humanity.
orig: وما كنت تتلو من قبله من كتاب ولا تخطه بيمينك إذا لارتاب المبطلون

translation: But no, these are clear verses in the breasts of those who are given knowledge, and none reject Our verses except the wrongdoers.
interpretation: The verse highlights the clarity of the divine signs or verses (ayat) that are present in the hearts of those who have been given knowledge. At the same time, it emphasizes the rejection of these verses by the wrongdoers or unjust people. The verse suggests that true understanding and acceptance of the divine signs come with knowledge, while denial and rejection are associated with wrongdoing and injustice.
orig: بل هو آيات بينات في صدور الذين أوتوا العلم وما يجحد بآياتنا إلا الظالمون

translation: And they said, 'Why has no sign been sent down to him from his Lord?' Say, 'Indeed, the signs are only with Allah, and I am only a clear warner.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the people questioning the lack of divine signs or miracles presented by a prophet or messenger. The prophet responds by stating that the signs are solely in the hands of God and that his role is merely to convey the message clearly. The verse highlights the limitations of the prophet and the ultimate authority of God, as well as the importance of the message itself over the need for miracles or signs.
orig: وقالوا لولا أنزل عليه آيات من ربه قل إنما الآيات عند الله وإنما أنا نذير مبين

translation: Or do they not reflect upon the Qur'an? If it had been from other than Allah, they would have found within it much contradiction.
interpretation: The verse is a rhetorical question addressed to the disbelievers, urging them to reflect on the Qur'an and consider its message. The verse suggests that if the Qur'an were not from Allah, it would contain contradictions and inconsistencies. However, since it is free from such errors, it is a sign that it is a revelation from Allah. The verse emphasizes the importance of contemplating and reflecting on the Qur'an as a means of gaining guidance and understanding. It serves as a reminder that the Qur'an is a source of mercy and a reminder for those who believe.
orig: أولم يكفهم أنا أنزلنا عليك الكتاب يتلى عليهم إن في ذلك لرحمة وذكرى لقوم يؤمنون

translation: Say, 'Sufficient is Allah as a witness between me and you. Indeed, He is ever, over His servants, Acquainted, Seeing.'
interpretation: The verse is a statement made by the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) in response to the disbelievers. It emphasizes the sufficiency of Allah as a witness between the believers and the disbelievers. The verse also highlights Allah's knowledge of everything in the heavens and the earth and His acquaintance with His servants. The phrase 'bila batil' means 'without falsehood' and it implies that the disbelievers are the ones who embrace falsehood. The verse serves as a reminder of Allah's all-encompassing knowledge and His role as the ultimate judge between the believers and the disbelievers.
orig: قل كفى بالله بيني وبينكم شهيدا يعلم ما في السماوات والأرض والذين آمنوا بالباطل وكفروا بالله أولئك هم الخاسرون

translation: And they urge you to hasten the punishment, and if not for a specified term, the punishment would have come to them, and it would have been settled upon them while they were unaware.
interpretation: The verse speaks about people who are urging for God's punishment to come upon them, either out of impatience or because they do not believe it will happen. The verse emphasizes that the punishment is delayed only by God's mercy and for a specified term. If not for this, the punishment would have already come upon them and they would have been caught off guard, unaware of its arrival. The verse serves as a reminder that God's punishment is certain and will come at a time determined by Him, and that it is not for humans to rush or hasten it.
orig: ويستعجلونك بالعذاب ولولا أجل مسمى لجاءهم العذاب وليأتينهم بغتة وهم لا يشعرون

translation: They hasten you towards punishment, but indeed, Hell surrounds the disbelievers.
interpretation: The verse addresses those who hasten towards punishment, implying that they are eager for it or working towards it through their disbelief and disobedience. However, the verse reassures the believers that Hell is already surrounding the disbelievers, indicating that the disbelievers are already in a state of punishment and that they are the ones who are truly in danger. The verse serves as a warning to the disbelievers and a source of comfort for the believers, reminding them of the just consequences of disbelief and the protection that God provides for the believers.
orig: يستعجلونك بالعذاب وإن جهنم لمحيطة بالكافرين

translation: The day will come when punishment will envelop them from above and below their feet and they will be told, 'Taste the result of your actions.'
interpretation: The verse describes the day of judgment when God's punishment will befall the unbelievers. The punishment will surround them from above and below, leaving them with no escape. They will be told to 'taste' or experience the consequences of their actions, emphasizing the reality of their fate. The verse serves as a warning to those who reject God's message and continue to commit sins, reminding them of the severe consequences they will face on the day of judgment.
orig: يوم يغشاهم العذاب من فوقهم ومن تحت أرجلهم ويقول ذوقوا ما كنتم تعملون

translation: O My servants who believe, if the earth were to be owned by you entirely, then still [be aware that] to Me [belongs] your worship.
interpretation: The verse addresses the believers and reminds them that even if they were to own the entire earth, their worship and devotion should still be directed towards God. The verse emphasizes the importance of worship and devotion, regardless of one's worldly possessions or status. It serves as a reminder that all that we have is a blessing from God and ultimately, our worship and devotion belongs to Him alone.
orig: يا عبادي الذين آمنوا إن أرضي واسعة فإياي فاعبدون

translation: Every soul will taste death, and We shall then test you with the best of evils and the best of goods, and We shall unto Us.
interpretation: The verse reminds us of the inevitability of death, which will be experienced by all souls. After death, humanity will be tested with both hardships and blessings, as determined by God. Ultimately, all people will return to God and be held accountable for their actions in this life.
orig: كل نفس ذائقة الموت ثم إلينا ترجعون

translation: And those who believe and do righteous deeds, We will surely admit them to gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever. Excellent is the reward of the doers.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the reward for those who believe in God and do good deeds. These people will be admitted to gardens (paradise) where rivers flow beneath them, and they will abide therein forever. The verse emphasizes the excellent and desirable nature of the reward for those who do good deeds, and it serves as a motivation for believers to strive for righteousness and good actions in order to attain the ultimate reward of paradise.
orig: والذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات لنبوئنهم من الجنة غرفا تجري من تحتها الأنهار خالدين فيها نعم أجر العاملين

translation: Those who are patient and put their trust in their Lord.
interpretation: The verse describes the qualities of those who are considered righteous and worthy of God's favor. These individuals possess the qualities of patience and trust in their Lord. Patience in this context refers to the ability to endure hardships and difficulties with steadfastness and perseverance. Trust in their Lord signifies a deep reliance on God and a belief in His divine plan and justice. The verse highlights the importance of these qualities in the pursuit of righteousness and the attainment of God's favor.
orig: الذين صبروا وعلى ربهم يتوكلون

translation: And how many an animal carries not its own provision! Allah carries it and you. And He is All hearing, All knowing.
interpretation: The verse highlights the power and mercy of God by reminding us that even animals, which cannot provide for themselves, are cared for by God. The verse emphasizes that God is the one who provides sustenance for all creatures, including humans. This serves as a reminder that God is aware of all our needs and is capable of providing for us, even when we are unable to do so ourselves. The verse also emphasizes that God is all-hearing and all-knowing, indicating that He is aware of our every thought and action, and that nothing escapes His knowledge.
orig: وكأين من دابة لا تحمل رزقها الله يرزقها وإياكم وهو السميع العليم

translation: And if you ask them, 'Who created the heavens and the earth and subjected the sun and the moon?' they will surely say, 'It is Allah.'
interpretation: The verse highlights the oneness of God and the belief in monotheism. When asked about the creation of the heavens and the earth, and the subjugation of the sun and the moon, the people will readily admit that it is the work of Allah. This shows that even those who may not believe in God or not follow His teachings, still recognize His power and sovereignty over all of creation. The verse serves as a reminder of the greatness and power of God and the insignificance of human beings in comparison. It also highlights the importance of recognizing and acknowledging the role of God in the creation of the universe and the natural phenomena.
orig: ولئن سألتهم من خلق السماوات والأرض وسخر الشمس والقمر ليقولن الله فأنى يؤفكون

translation: Allah extends provision to whom He wills among His servants and restricts it. Indeed, Allah is, of all things, Knowing.
interpretation: The verse highlights the power and knowledge of Allah in providing for His servants. It emphasizes that Allah gives provision to whom He wills and withholds it from whom He wills, indicating that all provision ultimately comes from Allah. The verse also highlights Allah's knowledge of all things, emphasizing that nothing is hidden from Allah. The verse serves as a reminder that all blessings come from Allah and that Allah is aware of the needs of His servants.
orig: الله يبسط الرزق لمن يشاء من عباده ويقدر له إن الله بكل شيء عليم

translation: And if you ask them who sends down water from the sky, giving life to the earth after its death, they will surely say, 'God'. Say, 'Praise be to God'; but most of them do not understand.
interpretation: The verse highlights the power of God as the one who sends water from the sky, giving life to the earth after its death. The verse is addressing a hypothetical situation where the listeners are asked who is responsible for such a miracle, and the expected answer is 'God'. The verse then instructs to respond with 'Praise be to God'. However, the verse also points out that most people do not understand or appreciate the significance of this miracle, indicating their lack of understanding and gratitude towards God's blessings.
orig: ولئن سألتهم من نزل من السماء ماء فأحيا به الأرض من بعد موتها ليقولن الله قل الحمد لله بل أكثرهم لا يعقلون

translation: And this worldly life is nothing but diversion and amusement, and indeed, the home of the Hereafter - that is the true life, if only they knew.
interpretation: The verse highlights the fleeting and ephemeral nature of this worldly life, describing it as mere diversion and amusement. At the same time, it emphasizes the importance of the afterlife, describing it as the "true life". The phrase "if only they knew" expresses the regret and disappointment of those who do not recognize the true value of things and fail to understand the reality of this world and the next. The verse serves as a reminder of the transient nature of this life and the eternal nature of the afterlife, encouraging people to focus on what truly matters and to prepare for the hereafter.
orig: وما هذه الحياة الدنيا إلا لهو ولعب وإن الدار الآخرة لهي الحيوان لو كانوا يعلمون

translation: And when they board the ship, they call upon Allah sincerely to Him [in] religion, but when He delivers them to the shore, thereupon they associate others [with Him].
interpretation: The verse describes the behavior of people who, when faced with danger at sea, sincerely call upon Allah and devote themselves to Him. However, as soon as they reach safety, they revert to their previous ways of associating partners with Allah. The verse highlights the hypocrisy and ingratitude of such people and serves as a reminder of the importance of maintaining faith and sincerity in all situations, not just in times of distress.
orig: فإذا ركبوا في الفلك دعوا الله مخلصين له الدين فلما نجاهم إلى البر إذا هم يشركون

translation: That they disbelieve in that which you (Muhammad) have been given and that they may enjoy; so they will come to know.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the disbelief of people towards the message brought by the Prophet Muhammad and their desire to enjoy the life of this world. The verse suggests that they reject the revelation in order to continue in their disbelief and enjoy the pleasures of this life. However, the verse also indicates that they will eventually come to know the truth, implying that they will face the consequences of their disbelief and rejection of the message.
orig: ليكفروا بما آتيناهم وليتمتعوا فسوف يعلمون

translation: Have they not seen that We have made (some) of them unaware within walls, and We have surrounded (other) people's towns (with means) of protection. So, do they still not believe and are grateful?
interpretation: The verse speaks about the blessings and protection that God has bestowed upon certain communities by making them unaware of the dangers around them and by providing protection to others. Despite these blessings, the verse questions whether these people still refuse to believe and give thanks to God. The verse serves as a reminder of God's power and the importance of showing gratitude for His blessings, and it highlights the consequences of ingratitude by emphasizing the contrast between the protection and security enjoyed by some and the vulnerability of others.
orig: أولم يروا أنا جعلنا حرما آمنا ويتخطف الناس من حولهم أفبالباطل يؤمنون وبنعمة الله يكفرون

translation: And who is more unjust than he who invents a lie about Allah or denies the truth when it comes to him? Is there not a dwelling in Hell for disbelievers?
interpretation: The verse highlights the grave sin and injustice of lying about Allah or denying the truth when it is presented. It emphasizes the severity of this offense by questioning if there could be a more unjust act. The verse then affirms the punishment for such actions, stating that there is a dwelling in Hell for disbelievers. The verse serves as a warning to those who reject the truth or spread falsehoods about Allah, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the reality of Hell as a punishment for disbelievers.
orig: ومن أظلم ممن افترى على الله كذبا أو كذب بالحق لما جاءه أليس في جهنم مثوى للكافرين

translation: And those who strive for Us - We will surely guide them to Our paths. And indeed, Allah is with the doers of good.
interpretation: The verse speaks about those who strive for God, emphasizing that God will guide them to the right path. The verse highlights the importance of effort and striving in the way of God, and the promise of divine guidance for those who make such an effort. The verse also emphasizes that God is with those who do good, suggesting a close relationship between God and those who strive for Him. The verse serves as a source of hope and motivation for those who are working towards righteousness, reminding them that their efforts will not go unnoticed and that they will be guided and supported by God.
orig: والذين جاهدوا فينا لنهدينهم سبلنا وإن الله لمع المحسنين

translation: The (revelation) of the Book (the Quran) is from Allah, the Exalted in Power, Full of Wisdom.
interpretation: The verse asserts that the Quran is a revelation from Allah, who is described as being Exalted in Power and Full of Wisdom. This serves to establish the divine origin of the Quran, and to emphasize the majesty and wisdom of Allah. The verse can be seen as a reminder of the importance and significance of the Quran, and of the importance of recognizing and submitting to the will of Allah.
orig: الم

translation: The Romans have been defeated.
interpretation: The verse is a historical announcement of the defeat of the Romans by the Persians. Some scholars argue that this verse serves as a metaphorical reminder of the vulnerability of even the most powerful nations and individuals, emphasizing the need for constant vigilance and reliance on God. Others suggest that the verse is a call for Muslims to remain steadfast in their faith during times of hardship, as God's ultimate victory is assured. Regardless of the interpretation, the verse emphasizes the unpredictability of worldly events and the importance of trust in God's plan.
orig: غلبت الروم

translation: And at the lowest part of the land, they will be dragged; surely, they were, before that, unaware.
interpretation: The verse describes the fate of a group of people who will be dragged at the lowest part of the land, and they had been unaware of their impending punishment. The verse emphasizes the humiliating and shameful nature of their punishment, as they will be dragged through the lowest part of the land. The verse serves as a reminder that those who commit injustice and wrongdoing will ultimately be punished for their actions, and that the punishment may come in a form that is far worse than what they could have imagined.
orig: في أدنى الأرض وهم من بعد غلبهم سيغلبون

translation: The command is but a moment's matter, to God, before and after; on that day, the believers will rejoice.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the power and knowledge of God, who can accomplish His command in an instant. The verse refers to a specific moment in time, both before and after which God's command is executed. The verse then mentions that on that day, the believers will rejoice, indicating that the event is a positive one for them. The verse serves as a reminder of God's power and control over all things, and the ultimate happiness and joy that await the believers on the Day of Judgment.
orig: في بضع سنين لله الأمر من قبل ومن بعد ويومئذ يفرح المؤمنون

translation: With God's help, He gives victory to whom He wills, and He is the Exalted in Might, the Merciful.
interpretation: The verse speaks about God's power to give victory and help to whomever He wills, emphasizing His might and mercy. The verse serves as a reminder that all success and victory come from God, and it encourages believers to seek His help and support. The verse also highlights God's compassion and forgiveness, inviting people to turn to Him in repentance and trust.
orig: بنصر الله ينصر من يشاء وهو العزيز الرحيم

translation: But God has promised, and God does not break promise, but most of the people do not know.
interpretation: The verse affirms God's reliability and truthfulness in fulfilling promises. It highlights the unawareness of most people regarding this fact. The verse can be interpreted as a reminder of God's faithfulness and a call for humans to trust and have faith in God's promises. At the same time, it suggests that many people lack knowledge and understanding of God's attributes and promises, emphasizing the importance of seeking and acquiring knowledge and understanding of God's message.
orig: وعد الله لا يخلف الله وعده ولكن أكثر الناس لا يعلمون

translation: They know only the apparent aspect of the worldly life, and they are heedless of the Hereafter.
interpretation: The verse highlights the limited understanding and knowledge of certain people who are preoccupied with the superficial aspects of this worldly life. Despite their knowledge of the worldly matters, they are oblivious to the significance of the Hereafter. The verse serves as a reminder that there is more to life than just material possessions and worldly pleasures. It encourages people to focus on the eternal life and to prioritize their actions accordingly.
orig: يعلمون ظاهرا من الحياة الدنيا وهم عن الآخرة هم غافلون

translation: Have they not considered within themselves what the creation of the heavens and the earth and what is between them means? They did not create themselves. Rather, He is ever Exalted and Great. The end of all things is to an appointed time, and yet many of the people deny their meeting with their Lord.
interpretation: The verse encourages people to reflect on the creation of the heavens, the earth, and all that lies between them. It emphasizes that the creation of these things is not a result of their own doing, but rather the work of a higher power, who is exalted and great. The verse also highlights that all things have an appointed time and that many people deny or disbelieve in the meeting with their Lord. The verse serves as a reminder for people to contemplate the greatness of God's creation and the significance of the meeting with their Lord, urging them not to deny or ignore it.
orig: أولم يتفكروا في أنفسهم ما خلق الله السماوات والأرض وما بينهما إلا بالحق وأجل مسمى وإن كثيرا من الناس بلقاء ربهم لكافرون

translation: Have they not traveled through the land and seen how was the end of those before them? They were stronger than them in power, and they dug the earth and inhabited it more than they. And their messengers came to them with clear proofs. So it was not Allah who wronged them, but it was they who wronged themselves.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the consequences of the actions of previous nations and serves as a reminder for the current generation. The verse highlights the strength and power of these previous nations, who were able to conquer and inhabit the land, yet despite this, they still faced destruction due to their actions. The verse emphasizes that it was not God who wronged them, but rather, they wronged themselves through their actions. The verse encourages the current generation to reflect on the past and the consequences of actions, and to understand the importance of righteousness and obedience to God's commands.
orig: أولم يسيروا في الأرض فينظروا كيف كان عاقبة الذين من قبلهم كانوا أشد منهم قوة وأثاروا الأرض وعمروها أكثر مما عمروها وجاءتهم رسلهم بالبينات فما كان الله ليظلمهم ولكن كانوا أنفسهم يظلمون

translation: Then the end of those who did evil was the worst, because they disbelieved in the signs of Allah and made fun of them.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the severe punishment of those who commit evil deeds and reject the signs of God. They not only disbelieve in the signs but also mock and make fun of them, showing their contempt and rejection of God's guidance. The verse highlights the grave consequences of such behavior, emphasizing that the end of those who commit such acts will be the worst. The verse serves as a warning to those who reject God's signs and engage in evil deeds, urging them to reflect on their actions and seek forgiveness before it is too late.
orig: ثم كان عاقبة الذين أساءوا السوأى أن كذبوا بآيات الله وكانوا بها يستهزئون

translation: God originates creation, then He will repeat it, then unto Him you will be returned.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the power and ability of God over creation, emphasizing that God is the one who originates creation and then repeats it, indicating a cycle of life and death. The verse also reminds the reader that ultimately, all of humanity will be returned to God, implying that they will be held accountable for their actions in this life and will face judgment in the afterlife.
orig: الله يبدأ الخلق ثم يعيده ثم إليه ترجعون

translation: And on the Day of Judgment, the criminals will be in despair.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the fate of criminals on the Day of Judgment. The phrase 'the criminals will be in despair' conveys the severity of their situation, as they will be filled with regret and despair when they realize the gravity of their sins and the consequences of their actions. The verse serves as a warning to those who commit crimes and engage in unlawful activities, reminding them of the ultimate accountability for their actions and the severe punishment that awaits them on the Day of Judgment.
orig: ويوم تقوم الساعة يبلس المجرمون

translation: And they have not had among their partners any one to protect them, and they have been unfaithful to
interpretation: No interpretation
orig: ولم يكن لهم من شركائهم شفعاء وكانوا بشركائهم كافرين

translation: And on the Day when the Hour will be established, that Day they will be separated.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the Day of Judgment, when the Hour will be established and people will be separated based on their deeds. The verse emphasizes the finality of this separation, as it will take place on the Day of Judgment, when all of humanity will be held accountable for their actions. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of leading a righteous life and preparing for the Day of Judgment.
orig: ويوم تقوم الساعة يومئذ يتفرقون
