translation: But as for those who believe and do good deeds, they will be in Gardens, delighted.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the reward for those who believe in God and do good deeds. These individuals will be in gardens, a metaphor for paradise, where they will experience eternal happiness and joy. The verse serves as a source of hope and motivation for believers, emphasizing the importance of faith and good actions in achieving a positive outcome in the afterlife.
orig: فأما الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات فهم في روضة يحبرون

translation: But as for those who disbelieved and denied Our signs and the meeting of the Hereafter, they will surely be in punishment.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the fate of those who disbelieve in God and deny the signs and the Day of Judgment. The verse asserts that they will be in punishment. The verse emphasizes the reality of the punishment for those who reject the truth and do not believe in the signs and the Hereafter. It serves as a reminder and a warning for people to reflect on the consequences of disbelief and denial of the signs and the Hereafter.
orig: وأما الذين كفروا وكذبوا بآياتنا ولقاء الآخرة فأولئك في العذاب محضرون

translation: Glory to Allah when you (plural) enter, and when you (plural) retire.
interpretation: The verse is praising and glorifying God, acknowledging His presence and power at all times of the day, whether it is when people enter their homes or when they retire for the night. It serves as a reminder to believers to be mindful of God at all times and in all places, recognizing His greatness and power. The verse also highlights the importance of acknowledging God's presence in daily life and giving thanks for His blessings, both big and small.
orig: فسبحان الله حين تمسون وحين تصبحون

translation: To Him belongs all praise, in the heavens and the earth, at night and at noon.
interpretation: The verse is a declaration of God's praise, emphasizing that He is worthy of praise at all times and in all places. The mention of 'heavens and the earth' indicates that God's praise is due in all of creation, while 'night and noon' emphasizes that God is to be praised at all times, whether it be during the day or night. The verse serves as a reminder of God's greatness and the importance of praising and worshiping Him.
orig: وله الحمد في السماوات والأرض وعشيا وحين تظهرون

translation: That brings out the living from the dead and brings out the dead from the living and gives life to the earth after its death, and likewise you will be brought out.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the power of God to give life and resurrect. It mentions three examples of God's ability to bring life: bringing out the living from the dead, bringing out the dead from the living, and giving life to the earth after its death. These examples emphasize the all-encompassing power of God over life and death. The verse ends by saying 'and likewise you will be brought out', indicating that the resurrection of the dead will also happen, and that all people will be held accountable for their actions in this life. The verse serves as a reminder of the power of God and the certainty of the resurrection and judgement.
orig: يخرج الحي من الميت ويخرج الميت من الحي ويحيي الأرض بعد موتها وكذلك تخرجون

translation: And among His signs is that He created you from dust, then, when you were humans, He spread you abroad.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the creation of human beings by God, emphasizing that humans were created from dust and then were spread abroad. The verse highlights the power of God in creating human beings and His control over their existence. It also serves as a reminder of human's humble origins and their dependence on God. The verse encourages reflection on the signs of God in the creation of human beings and the natural world around them.
orig: ومن آياته أن خلقكم من تراب ثم إذا أنتم بشر تنتشرون

translation: And among His signs is that He created for you from yourselves mates that you may find tranquility in them; and He placed between you affection and mercy. Indeed in that are signs for a people who reflect.
interpretation: The verse highlights the creation of spouses for humans as one of God's signs and a means of attaining tranquility. It emphasizes the importance of affection and mercy in relationships. The verse also invites people to reflect on this aspect of God's creation and to consider the deeper meaning and significance of these relationships. The verse can be seen as a celebration of love, compassion, and the deep connections that can exist between people.
orig: ومن آياته أن خلق لكم من أنفسكم أزواجا لتسكنوا إليها وجعل بينكم مودة ورحمة إن في ذلك لآيات لقوم يتفكرون

translation: And among His signs is the creation of the heavens and the earth and the diversity of your languages and colors. Indeed, in that are signs for those of understanding.
interpretation: The verse highlights various signs of God in the world, including the creation of the heavens and the earth, as well as the diversity of languages and colors among people. The verse emphasizes that these signs are evident for those who reflect and understand, implying that one should ponder over these signs and use their intellect to comprehend the greatness and power of God. The verse encourages contemplation and reflection on the natural world as a means of understanding God's existence and wisdom.
orig: ومن آياته خلق السماوات والأرض واختلاف ألسنتكم وألوانكم إن في ذلك لآيات للعالمين

translation: And of His signs is that He shows you the night and the day and the sun and the moon are subject to Him; indeed in that are signs for a people who reason.
interpretation: The verse highlights various signs of God's power and greatness, including the alternation of day and night and the movement of celestial bodies such as the sun and the moon. These phenomena serve as evidence of God's control and authority over the universe. The verse emphasizes the importance of reflecting on and contemplating these signs, as they hold profound meaning for those who are willing to reflect and reason. The verse encourages the reader to ponder the complexity and intricacy of the natural world and to recognize the existence of a higher power beyond the physical realm.
orig: ومن آياته منامكم بالليل والنهار وابتغاؤكم من فضله إن في ذلك لآيات لقوم يسمعون

translation: And of His signs is the lightning, which strikes fear and hope, and He sends down from the sky water with which He brings the dead earth to life. Indeed in that are signs for a people who reason.
interpretation: The verse highlights several signs of God's power and greatness. The first sign is the lightning, which can inspire both fear and hope in people. The second sign is the rain that comes down from the sky, which brings life to the dead earth. The verse emphasizes the power of God to give life and to take it away. The verse is a reminder of the power of God and the importance of recognizing and reflecting on His signs. The verse is also a call to those who are able to reason and understand to reflect on these signs and to use their reason and understanding to deepen their faith and relationship with God.
orig: ومن آياته يريكم البرق خوفا وطمعا وينزل من السماء ماء فيحيي به الأرض بعد موتها إن في ذلك لآيات لقوم يعقلون

translation: And among His signs is that the heaven and the earth stand by His command; then, when He calls you, by a single call, from the earth, behold, you will come forth.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the power and control of God over the heavens and the earth, and how they are obedient to His command. The verse highlights the overwhelming and irresistible nature of God's call, which is so powerful that it can bring forth all of humanity from the earth with a single call. The verse emphasizes the greatness and majesty of God, and the insignificance and weakness of human beings in comparison. It also serves as a reminder of the Day of Judgment, when God will call forth all of humanity to stand before Him and be held accountable for their actions.
orig: ومن آياته أن تقوم السماء والأرض بأمره ثم إذا دعاكم دعوة من الأرض إذا أنتم تخرجون

translation: And to Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth. All are obedient to Him.
interpretation: The verse affirms the oneness of God and His complete sovereignty over all of creation, both in the heavens and on earth. It emphasizes that everything in the universe is obedient to God, emphasizing His power and control. The verse can be seen as a reminder of God's greatness and a call for humility and submission to His will.
orig: وله من في السماوات والأرض كل له قانتون

translation: And it is He who begins creation; then He repeats it, and that is easier for Him. And to Him belongs the highest attribute in the heavens and earth, and He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise.
interpretation: The verse highlights the power and ability of God to create and recreate, emphasizing that it is an easy task for Him. The verse also attributes the highest attribute to God, both in the heavens and on earth, establishing His supremacy and greatness. The verse further describes God as the Exalted in Might and the Wise, emphasizing His power and wisdom in all that He does. The verse serves as a reminder of the greatness and might of God, and the insignificance of human beings in comparison.
orig: وهو الذي يبدأ الخلق ثم يعيده وهو أهون عليه وله المثل الأعلى في السماوات والأرض وهو العزيز الحكيم

translation: We have put forward for you an example from yourselves. Do you have partners among those to whom your right hand possesses, so that you are equal in respect to fearing them as you fear yourselves? Thus do We make clear the signs for a people who understand.
interpretation: The verse uses a metaphor to illustrate the relationship between humans and their possessions, and how they should not associate partners with God in the blessings they receive from Him. The metaphor is of a person's right hand possessing something, which refers to the slaves or property that people owned during that time. The verse asks if these possessions are equal to the person in terms of being feared, as people fear themselves. This is used to emphasize the absurdity of associating partners with God. The verse ends by stating that these examples or signs are being presented to a people who are able to understand and reflect upon their meaning.
orig: ضرب لكم مثلا من أنفسكم هل لكم من ما ملكت أيمانكم من شركاء في ما رزقناكم فأنتم فيه سواء تخافونهم كخيفتكم أنفسكم كذلك نفصل الآيات لقوم يعقلون

translation: But they follow what the devils gave out (of the magic) in the lifetime of Solomon. Solomon did not disbelieve, but the devils disbelieved, teaching men magic and such things that came down at Babylon, to the two angels, Harut and Marut; but neither of these two (angels) taught anyone (such things) till they had said, 'We are only for trial; so do not disbelieve (in our teaching).' Thus did they learn from them the evil of witchcraft and their evil-doing, and they knew of it not.
interpretation: The verse warns against following the ways of those who do wrong and commit injustice, and instead encourages the following of truth and guidance. The verse specifically mentions the dangers of following the magic and witchcraft that was practiced during the time of Solomon, and warns against the teachings of the devils. The verse emphasizes the negative consequences of these actions and the importance of seeking guidance from God and following the right path.
orig: بل اتبع الذين ظلموا أهواءهم بغير علم فمن يهدي من أضل الله وما لهم من ناصرين

translation: So set your face toward the religion, being steadfast in the nature from Allah upon which He has created mankind; there is no changing the creation of Allah. That is the correct religion, but most of the people do not know.
interpretation: The verse calls upon the believer to adhere to the natural religion that Allah has created mankind upon, which is the correct religion. The verse emphasizes that the creation of Allah cannot be changed, meaning that the natural religion is unchangeable. However, most people do not know this and do not adhere to the correct religion. The verse serves as a reminder to the believer to stay steadfast on the correct religion and not be swayed by the ignorance of the majority.
orig: فأقم وجهك للدين حنيفا فطرت الله التي فطر الناس عليها لا تبديل لخلق الله ذلك الدين القيم ولكن أكثر الناس لا يعلمون

translation: Turn to Him in repentance, fear Him, and establish prayer. And do not be among those who associate others with Him.
interpretation: The verse is a command to the believers to turn to God in repentance, fear Him, and establish prayer. It also warns against associating others with God, which is a grave sin. The verse emphasizes the importance of having a strong and devoted relationship with God, and the need to maintain it through repentance, fear, and prayer. It serves as a reminder to the believers to be mindful of their actions and to avoid falling into the trap of associating partners with God, as it is a path that leads astray from the right path.
orig: منيبين إليه واتقوه وأقيموا الصلاة ولا تكونوا من المشركين

translation: Among those who have divided their religion and become sects, each party rejoicing in what they have.
interpretation: The verse refers to people who have allowed their religion to be divided into sects and groups, each one satisfied with what they believe and practice. The verse criticizes this division and the resulting self-righteousness, suggesting that it is not in keeping with the true spirit of religion. The verse serves as a reminder that true faith and spirituality involve unity, not division, and that true believers should not be content with their own narrow perspectives and beliefs, but should strive for a more inclusive and universal understanding of the divine will.
orig: من الذين فرقوا دينهم وكانوا شيعا كل حزب بما لديهم فرحون

translation: And when harm touches the people, they call upon their Lord in repentance; then when He gives them a taste of mercy from Him, there are some of them who associate others with their Lord.
interpretation: The verse describes the behavior of people in times of hardship and affliction. When they face harm, they turn to their Lord in repentance and seek His mercy. However, when God bestows His mercy upon them, some of them fall into the sin of associating partners with God. The verse highlights the human tendency to forget God and commit shirk (associating partners with God) when they are in a state of ease and comfort. It serves as a reminder of the importance of maintaining a strong and sincere relationship with God, and avoiding the sin of shirk at all times.
orig: وإذا مس الناس ضر دعوا ربهم منيبين إليه ثم إذا أذاقهم منه رحمة إذا فريق منهم بربهم يشركون

translation: That they disbelieve in that which you have been given and that they may indulge a little while; so you will surely know (who among them is the ultimate winner).
interpretation: The verse speaks about the disbelief of people towards the revelation brought by the prophet and their desire to enjoy worldly pleasures. The verse suggests that the disbelief and indulgence of these people is temporary, and that they will eventually come to know the truth. The verse can be interpreted as a test of faith for the believers, who are to remain steadfast in their belief despite the disbelief and opposition of others. The verse also implies that those who are patient and steadfast in their faith will ultimately be victorious.
orig: ليكفروا بما آتيناهم فتمتعوا فسوف تعلمون

translation: Or have We sent a authority upon them, so it speaks to them, as what they used to associate (with Allah)?
interpretation: The verse speaks about the possibility of God sending a powerful being or authority upon a people who associate partners with Him. The punishment in this verse is described as a being that can speak and communicate with the people, likely to convey the message of their sin and the consequences of their actions. The verse serves as a warning to those who associate partners with God and commit shirk, emphasizing the power and authority of God and the consequences of disbelief.
orig: أم أنزلنا عليهم سلطانا فهو يتكلم بما كانوا به يشركون

translation: And when We bestow mercy upon the people, they rejoice therein; but when an affliction befalls them because of what their (own) hands have previously sent forth, indeed, they are then in despair.
interpretation: The verse highlights the contrasting reactions of people when they receive blessings and when they face hardships. When people receive God's mercy, they are filled with joy. However, when they experience afflictions due to their own past actions, they become desperate. The verse reminds people that their actions have consequences, and they should not take God's blessings for granted. It also encourages them to seek God's forgiveness and repent for their sins to avoid despair and earn His mercy.
orig: وإذا أذقنا الناس رحمة فرحوا بها وإن تصبهم سيئة بما قدمت أيديهم إذا هم يقنطون

translation: Have they not seen that Allah extends provision for whom He wills and restricts? Indeed, in that are signs for a people who believe.
interpretation: The verse highlights the power and control of Allah over the provision of sustenance. It emphasizes that Allah provides for whom He wills and withholds provision from whom He wills, and this is a sign for those who believe. The verse reminds the believers to reflect on the blessings they receive and to understand that all provision comes from Allah. It also encourages them to have faith in Allah's wisdom and justice, recognizing that the distribution of resources is not arbitrary but rather a test of their faith and gratitude.
orig: أولم يروا أن الله يبسط الرزق لمن يشاء ويقدر إن في ذلك لآيات لقوم يؤمنون

translation: And give to the relative his right, and to the needy and the wayfarer, and do not spend wastefully. Indeed, those who do not give the relative his right are deniers [of the truth]. And if you turn away, then indeed, Allah is Independent of you. And Allah is the encompassing of all things.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of giving and being generous, particularly to certain groups of people: relatives, the needy, and travelers. It warns against being wasteful in spending. The verse also highlights the consequence of not giving relatives their rights, which is to deny the truth. If one turns away from fulfilling these obligations, it is important to remember that Allah is independent of human beings and is all-encompassing. The verse encourages believers to strive for the pleasure of Allah and emphasizes the importance of fulfilling one's responsibilities towards others, particularly those in need.
orig: فآت ذا القربى حقه والمسكين وابن السبيل ذلك خير للذين يريدون وجه الله وأولئك هم المفلحون

translation: And whatever you give in riba (interest) to increase in the wealth of people will not increase with Allah, but whatever you give in zakah (charity), seeking the countenance of Allah - it is those who will increase.
interpretation: The verse contrasts between two types of financial transactions: giving in riba (interest), which is considered unjust and exploitative, and giving in zakah (charity), which is considered a form of worship and a means of seeking Allah's pleasure. The verse makes it clear that while giving in riba may increase one's wealth in the worldly sense, it will not bring any increase or reward from Allah. On the other hand, giving in zakah, motivated by the desire to please Allah and seeking His countenance, will bring about an increase in blessings and rewards from Allah. The verse encourages Muslims to prioritize charity and social justice over self-interest and exploitation, and to understand that the ultimate source of increase and blessings is Allah.
orig: وما آتيتم من ربا ليربو في أموال الناس فلا يربو عند الله وما آتيتم من زكاة تريدون وجه الله فأولئك هم المضعفون

translation: It is Allah who created you, then provided for you, then will cause your death, then will bring you back to life. Is there any of your 'partners' who does anything of that? Blessed is He and exalted above what they associate with Him.
interpretation: The verse affirms the power and control of Allah over all aspects of life and death. It emphasizes that Allah is the one who created humans, provides for them, causes their death, and will bring them back to life. The verse questions the role of any 'partners' (referring to other deities) in these actions, emphasizing the oneness of Allah and his power over all things. The verse serves as a reminder of the power and greatness of Allah, and the belief in the oneness of Allah is a fundamental principle in Islam.
orig: الله الذي خلقكم ثم رزقكم ثم يميتكم ثم يحييكم هل من شركائكم من يفعل من ذلكم من شيء سبحانه وتعالى عما يشركون

translation: Corruption has appeared on land and sea because of what the hands of people have earned, so He may make them taste a part of what they have done, that perhaps they will return (to righteousness).
interpretation: The verse describes the consequences of corruption and wrongdoing, which have led to destruction and damage on land and sea. The verse emphasizes that these disasters are a result of humanity's own actions, and serves as a warning for people to reflect on the impact of their deeds. The verse ends with a note of hope, suggesting that the purpose of experiencing the consequences of their actions is to bring people back to the path of righteousness.
orig: ظهر الفساد في البر والبحر بما كسبت أيدي الناس ليذيقهم بعض الذي عملوا لعلهم يرجعون

translation: Say, 'Travel through the land and observe how was the end of those before.' Most of them were unbelievers.
interpretation: The verse encourages the believers to observe and reflect on the fate of the previous nations that inhabited the earth. By doing so, they will see that most of those nations were disbelievers, which implies that their ultimate end was not a favorable one. The verse invites the believers to learn from the lessons of history and to reflect on the consequences of disbelief. It serves as a warning to those who deny the truth and a reminder to the believers to be steadfast in their faith.
orig: قل سيروا في الأرض فانظروا كيف كان عاقبة الذين من قبل كان أكثرهم مشركين

translation: So direct your face toward the religion, inclining to truth, before there comes to you the Day from Allah of which there is no repelling. That Day, they will be dispersed [to the command] of Allah, and you will see them entering it bringing from every [kind of] profession.
interpretation: This verse speaks about the importance of directing one's face towards the true religion before the Day of Judgment arrives, a day which cannot be turned back or delayed. On that day, people will be divided according to their deeds and will enter their fate with all the different types of deeds they have done. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of following the right path and doing good deeds in preparation for the Day of Judgment.
orig: فأقم وجهك للدين القيم من قبل أن يأتي يوم لا مرد له من الله يومئذ يصدعون

translation: Whoever disbelieves, his disbelief is upon him, and whoever does righteousness, it is for their own selves.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the consequences of a person's actions, whether it be disbelief or righteousness. The verse emphasizes that the responsibility for one's disbelief lies solely with the individual and that they will bear the consequences of their actions. Similarly, those who do righteous deeds will also reap the benefits of their actions. The verse highlights the importance of individual responsibility and accountability for one's actions, and the significance of making choices that align with righteousness and belief.
orig: من كفر فعليه كفره ومن عمل صالحا فلأنفسهم يمهدون

translation: For those who believe and do righteous deeds, truly believers will have a reward beyond measure. For with God there is a magnificent reward.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the reward that will be given to those who believe in God and do good deeds. The verse emphasizes the greatness of the reward, describing it as 'beyond measure' and 'magnificent'. The verse serves as a motivation for believers to continue doing good deeds and to have faith in God, reminding them of the great reward that awaits them in the afterlife. The verse also highlights the contrast between the believers and the non-believers, stating that God does not love the non-believers.
orig: ليجزي الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات من فضله إنه لا يحب الكافرين

translation: And among His signs is that He sends the winds as heralds of good news, and that He may make you taste of His mercy, and that the ships may run at His command, and that you may seek of His bounty, and that you may be thankful.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the signs of God's power and mercy in the natural world. The winds are sent as a herald of good news, and they bring rain and sustenance, allowing ships to sail and people to benefit from God's bounty. These events are described as signs (ayat) of God's existence and power, and they serve as a reminder for people to be thankful and grateful for His blessings. The verse encourages people to seek God's mercy and bounty, and to express their gratitude through their actions and attitudes. Ultimately, the verse emphasizes the importance of recognizing and appreciating the many signs of God's power and mercy in the world around us, and of living a life that reflects our gratitude and thankfulness.
orig: ومن آياته أن يرسل الرياح مبشرات وليذيقكم من رحمته ولتجري الفلك بأمره ولتبتغوا من فضله ولعلكم تشكرون

translation: And We indeed sent before you (O Muhammad) Messengers to their own people, then they came to them with clear proofs, so We punished those who were unjust. And it was incumbent upon Us to help the believers.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the sending of Messengers by God to their respective communities, who brought clear signs and proofs of their prophethood. However, those who were unjust and committed sins were punished, and it was the duty of God to help and support the believers.
orig: ولقد أرسلنا من قبلك رسلا إلى قومهم فجاءوهم بالبينات فانتقمنا من الذين أجرموا وكان حقا علينا نصر المؤمنين

translation: It is Allah who sends the winds stirring up the clouds, then spreads them in the sky however He wills, and breaks them into fragments until you see the raindrops issuing from within them. Then when He gives it to whomever of His servants He wills, behold, they rejoice.
interpretation: The verse describes the power and control of Allah over the natural phenomena, specifically the formation of clouds and rain. It emphasizes the intricate and complex process of cloud formation and the ultimate control of Allah over it. The verse then describes the joy of the people who receive the rain, indicating the blessings and benefits that come with it. The verse serves as a reminder of the power and wisdom of Allah, and the blessings that He bestows upon His servants, and the gratitude that is required in response to these blessings.
orig: الله الذي يرسل الرياح فتثير سحابا فيبسطه في السماء كيف يشاء ويجعله كسفا فترى الودق يخرج من خلاله فإذا أصاب به من يشاء من عباده إذا هم يستبشرون

translation: And if they had been entered before by Our punishment, they would have surely known it.
interpretation: The verse highlights the inevitability of God's punishment for those who persist in their unjust ways. The phrase 'if they had been entered before by Our punishment' implies that the people had been given multiple opportunities to change their ways, but they did not. The clause 'they would have surely known it' suggests that the people would have been aware of the consequences of their actions and would have taken heed. The verse serves as a reminder that those who continue to engage in unjust behavior will ultimately face the consequences of their actions, and it will be too late for them to change their fate.
orig: وإن كانوا من قبل أن ينزل عليهم من قبله لمبلسين

translation: So see the effects of Allah's mercy, how He gives life to the earth after its death. Indeed, that (Resurrection) is the Resurrection (of the dead). And He is able to do all things.
interpretation: The verse draws a parallel between the resurrection of the dead and the revival of the earth after its death, emphasizing the power of Allah's mercy. The verse serves as a reminder of the ultimate resurrection, where all people will be brought back to life and will be held accountable for their actions. The verse also highlights the power of Allah, who has the ability to do all things and has the power to bring the dead back to life. The verse encourages the believers to reflect on the signs of Allah's power and mercy in the world around them and to have faith in the ultimate resurrection.
orig: فانظر إلى آثار رحمت الله كيف يحيي الأرض بعد موتها إن ذلك لمحيي الموتى وهو على كل شيء قدير

translation: And if We send a wind as a mercy, then they afterward turn ungrateful (disbelieving).
interpretation: The verse speaks about the people's ingratitude and disbelief despite receiving God's mercy. The verse mentions that when a wind is sent as a mercy, instead of being grateful, they become disbelievers. This verse highlights the people's rejection of God's blessings, and their ingratitude despite receiving His mercy. It serves as a reminder of the importance of being thankful for God's blessings and not taking them for granted.
orig: ولئن أرسلنا ريحا فرأوه مصفرا لظلوا من بعده يكفرون

translation: For indeed, you cannot make the dead hear, nor can you make the deaf hear the call when they turn their backs retreating.
interpretation: The verse highlights the limitations of human abilities and the futility of trying to communicate with those who are not willing to listen. The phrase 'you cannot make the dead hear' is a metaphor for those who are spiritually dead or closed-minded, emphasizing the difficulty of reaching out to them. Similarly, the phrase 'you cannot make the deaf hear the call' refers to those who turn away from the truth or refuse to listen to reason. The verse serves as a reminder that ultimately, it is up to the individual to choose whether or not to listen and respond to the message being conveyed.
orig: فإنك لا تسمع الموتى ولا تسمع الصم الدعاء إذا ولوا مدبرين

translation: And you are not, [O Muhammad], a warden over them; rather, it is a reminder for those who fear.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes that Prophet Muhammad is not responsible for guiding or protecting the unbelievers. Instead, the Qur'an serves as a reminder for those who are receptive and open to the message, specifically those who fear and have a reverence for God. This verse highlights the importance of personal responsibility in seeking guidance and the role of the Qur'an in providing that guidance for those who are willing to receive it.
orig: وما أنت بهاد العمي عن ضلالتهم إن تسمع إلا من يؤمن بآياتنا فهم مسلمون

translation: It is Allah who created you from weakness, then made after weakness strength, then made after strength weakness and white hair. He creates what He wills. And He is the Knowing, the Powerful.
interpretation: The verse highlights the power and wisdom of Allah in creating and controlling the cycle of life and death. It emphasizes that human beings are created weak and vulnerable, but through Allah's will and power, they are given strength and abilities. However, as time passes, they return to a state of weakness and aging, which is a natural part of the human condition. The verse reminds people that Allah has the power to create and control all things, and that He has knowledge of all that is hidden and unknown. The verse encourages people to reflect on the signs of Allah in the creation and to submit to His will and power.
orig: الله الذي خلقكم من ضعف ثم جعل من بعد ضعف قوة ثم جعل من بعد قوة ضعفا وشيبة يخلق ما يشاء وهو العليم القدير

translation: And on the Day of Resurrection, the criminals will be shown their deeds. They will not be wronged, not even the amount of a thread in a date stone.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the Day of Judgment when the criminals will be shown their deeds and will not be wronged, even to the extent of a mustard seed. This means that every single deed, both good and bad, will be accounted for and the consequences will be justly given. The verse emphasizes the importance of good deeds and warns against committing sins, as every action has a consequence and will be judged on the Day of Resurrection.
orig: ويوم تقوم الساعة يقسم المجرمون ما لبثوا غير ساعة كذلك كانوا يؤفكون

translation: And those who were given knowledge and faith said, 'Indeed, you have stayed in the Book of Allah until the Day of Resurrection.' This is the Day of Resurrection, but you were not aware.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the moment of resurrection and judgment, when those who possessed knowledge and faith recognize that they have been living in the world, governed by God's laws and guidance, until the Day of Resurrection. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected arrival of the Day of Resurrection, and the fact that people were not aware of its imminence. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of recognizing and acknowledging God's guidance and the fleeting nature of worldly life, and the need to be always prepared for the Day of Judgment.
orig: وقال الذين أوتوا العلم والإيمان لقد لبثتم في كتاب الله إلى يوم البعث فهذا يوم البعث ولكنكم كنتم لا تعلمون

translation: That day, no excuse of the wrongdoers will avail them, nor will they be allowed to return (to this world),
interpretation: The verse speaks about the Day of Judgment and emphasizes the finality of the punishment that the wrongdoers will receive. The verse makes it clear that there will be no opportunity for the wrongdoers to make excuses or to return to this world to make amends. The verse serves as a warning to those who are committing injustices, reminding them of the severity of the consequences of their actions and the importance of seeking forgiveness and repenting while they still have the chance.
orig: فيومئذ لا ينفع الذين ظلموا معذرتهم ولا هم يستعتبون

translation: And We have already sent forth among the former peoples, examples (of punishment), and every time there came to them a messenger, they cried: 'Fools! You are only following a man bewitched!'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the repeated pattern of human behavior in the past, where people rejected the messengers sent by God and dismissed their teachings as the ramblings of a deluded person. The verse emphasizes the foolishness of those who deny the truth and refuse to listen to the guidance sent by God. The verse serves as a reminder that the same fate that befell the previous disbelieving nations may also befall those who reject God's message in the present day.
orig: ولقد ضربنا للناس في هذا القرآن من كل مثل ولئن جئتهم بآية ليقولن الذين كفروا إن أنتم إلا مبطلون

translation: Thus does Allah seal the hearts of those who do not know.
interpretation: The verse explains that Allah (God) seals the hearts of those who lack knowledge or understanding. The sealing of the heart is a metaphor for being closed-minded, stubborn, or unwilling to accept the truth. The verse suggests that those who lack knowledge are more likely to have their hearts sealed, implying that knowledge and understanding are key to openness and receptiveness. The verse may serve as a warning to those who reject or ignore the message of Islam, suggesting that their closed-mindedness may prevent them from receiving God's guidance and mercy.
orig: كذلك يطبع الله على قلوب الذين لا يعلمون

translation: So be patient. Indeed, the promise of Allah is truth. And let not those who have no certainty cause you to despair.
interpretation: The verse encourages patience in the face of adversity, reminding the believers that God's promise is true and that they should not be discouraged by the actions of those who lack certainty or faith. The verse serves as a reminder to stay steadfast and focused on one's faith, even when faced with doubt and uncertainty from others.
orig: فاصبر إن وعد الله حق ولا يستخفنك الذين لا يوقنون

translation: The (revelation) of the Book (the Quran) from Allah, the Mighty, the Wise.
interpretation: The verse affirms that the Quran is a revelation from Allah, the Almighty and Wise. It highlights the divine nature of the Quran and the power and wisdom of Allah in revealing it. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance and significance of the Quran in the lives of Muslims, and the need to respect and understand it in order to fully appreciate its teachings and messages.
orig: الم

translation: Those are the verses of the Wise Book
interpretation: The verse is a reference to the verses of the Qur'an, which are described as being from the 'Wise Book'. This description highlights the wisdom and guidance that can be found in the Qur'an. The verse may be reminding the reader of the value and importance of the teachings of the Qur'an and encouraging them to reflect on and learn from its verses.
orig: تلك آيات الكتاب الحكيم

translation: A guidance and mercy for the doers of good.
interpretation: The verse highlights the positive outcome for those who perform good deeds, emphasizing that such actions lead to guidance and mercy from God. This verse serves as a motivation for individuals to engage in good deeds, and it provides reassurance that their actions are not in vain, but rather, they will be met with divine guidance and mercy.
orig: هدى ورحمة للمحسنين

translation: Who maintain the prayer and give the zakat and they are certain of the Hereafter.
interpretation: The verse describes the believers who establish the five daily prayers (salat) and give the obligatory charity (zakat), and they have certainty of the Hereafter. This verse emphasizes the importance of performing these two pillars of Islam, and the certainty of the Hereafter for the believers. It highlights the characteristics of the believers who have a strong faith and are mindful of their duties towards God and the Hereafter.
orig: الذين يقيمون الصلاة ويؤتون الزكاة وهم بالآخرة هم يوقنون

translation: Those are upon (right) guidance from their Lord, and those are the successful.
interpretation: The verse distinguishes between two groups of people: those who are guided by their Lord and those who are not. The guided ones are considered successful, indicating that following the guidance of one's Lord is the key to success in this life and the hereafter. This verse serves as a reminder to seek guidance from the Lord and to follow it, as it leads to success and prosperity.
orig: أولئك على هدى من ربهم وأولئك هم المفلحون

translation: And among people are those who purchase idle tales to mislead from the way of Allah without knowledge and take it in mockery. For them is a humiliating punishment.
interpretation: The verse speaks about people who buy and spread falsehoods and misinformation, leading others away from the path of God. These people do this without knowledge and for their own amusement. The verse warns that such behavior is not harmless and that these individuals will face a humiliating punishment for their actions. The verse serves as a reminder to be cautious of false information and to seek knowledge before sharing or accepting it, and it highlights the importance of staying on the path of God and avoiding actions that may lead one astray.
orig: ومن الناس من يشتري لهو الحديث ليضل عن سبيل الله بغير علم ويتخذها هزوا أولئك لهم عذاب مهين

translation: And when Our verses are recited to him, he turns away in pride as if he did not hear them, as if there was deafness in his ears. So announce to him a painful punishment.
interpretation: The verse describes a person who reacts with arrogance and pride when God's verses are recited to him. Despite hearing the verses, he pretends not to hear and acts as if he is deaf. The verse warns of the consequences of such behavior and announces a painful punishment for the individual. The verse serves as a reminder that God's verses should be received with humility and reverence, and that rejection and arrogance towards them will result in severe consequences.
orig: وإذا تتلى عليه آياتنا ولى مستكبرا كأن لم يسمعها كأن في أذنيه وقرا فبشره بعذاب أليم

translation: For those who have believed and done righteous deeds, for them are Gardens of Delight.
interpretation: The verse promises the believers and doers of righteous deeds with Gardens of Delight. The verse emphasizes the reward for those who have faith and do good deeds, and the great blessings that await them in the afterlife. The verse serves as a motivation for believers to continue practicing good deeds and to have hope in the reward from God in the afterlife.
orig: إن الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات لهم جنات النعيم

translation: Abiding therein, they will have the promise of God - He is the Exalted in Power, the Wise.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the ultimate destination of the righteous believers, who will abide in a place of bliss and happiness. The promise of God is true and certain, and it is a source of great comfort and security for the believers. The attributes of God as the Exalted in Power and the Wise indicate that the promise of God is unchangeable and that He has the power and wisdom to fulfill His promise. The verse serves as a source of hope and inspiration for the believers, reminding them of the rewards that await them in the hereafter.
orig: خالدين فيها وعد الله حقا وهو العزيز الحكيم

translation: Have not the disbelievers seen that We created the heavens and the earth with truth? Yet, they are not guided. And We have created for them the livestock, which they ride upon and from which they eat. And they have other benefits from them, and they get milk from them. And they reach, through them, their needs. And they are content with them. And they, when it is darkened for them, seek refuge in them. And from the midst of them, they produce for themselves fire, and from it they get light. And they are grateful for Our signs, but most of them are ungrateful.
interpretation: The verse highlights the blessings and benefits that God has given to the disbelievers, despite their lack of faith. The verse mentions the creation of the heavens and the earth, and the creation of livestock for the benefit of humans, including transportation, food, and other resources. The verse also mentions the ability of humans to seek refuge in the livestock during the dark and to produce fire from them for light. Despite all these blessings, the verse notes that most people are ungrateful. The verse serves as a reminder of the blessings that God has given to all people, regardless of their faith, and the importance of showing gratitude for these blessings.
orig: خلق السماوات بغير عمد ترونها وألقى في الأرض رواسي أن تميد بكم وبث فيها من كل دابة وأنزلنا من السماء ماء فأنبتنا فيها من كل زوج كريم

translation: This is the creation of Allah. So show me what those other than Him have created. Rather, the unjust are in clear error.
interpretation: The verse challenges the disbelievers to show what their deities or powers have created, implying that they have no such ability. The verse emphasizes the supremacy and uniqueness of Allah as the only creator. The second part of the verse highlights the error and misguidance of the unjust, implying that they are following falsehood and rejecting the truth.
orig: هذا خلق الله فأروني ماذا خلق الذين من دونه بل الظالمون في ضلال مبين

translation: And We had certainly given Qumam the wisdom, but he preferred blindness over guidance, so he was not grateful for Our signs. And indeed, Qumam, for whoever is ungrateful for the favor of his Lord, then indeed, Allah is self-sufficient and praiseworthy.
interpretation: The verse speaks about a person named Qumam who was given wisdom but chose to ignore it and preferred to be blind to guidance. He was ungrateful for the signs of God. The verse highlights the consequences of ingratitude and the rejection of God's signs. The verse also emphasizes that God is self-sufficient and praiseworthy, indicating that He does not need the gratitude of His creation, but it is a favor and a blessing for the one who is grateful. The verse serves as a reminder to be thankful for the blessings and guidance that we have been given and to not take them for granted.
orig: ولقد آتينا لقمان الحكمة أن اشكر لله ومن يشكر فإنما يشكر لنفسه ومن كفر فإن الله غني حميد

translation: And when Qarun's people said, 'O Qarun, indeed you have oppressed us and indeed, we have feared from God.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the people of Qarun (also known as Korah) expressing their grievances against him for his oppression and tyranny. They acknowledge the great injustice he has committed, and their fear of God's punishment. The verse serves as a reminder of the consequences of oppression and tyranny, and the ultimate power of God's justice.
orig: وإذ قال لقمان لابنه وهو يعظه يا بني لا تشرك بالله إن الشرك لظلم عظيم

translation: And We have enjoined upon man concerning his parents - his mother bears him in weakness upon weakness, and his weaning is in two years - 'Give thanks to Me and to your parents; to Me is the return.',
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of showing gratitude towards one's parents, particularly the mother who bears and nurtures the child through a long and difficult process. The verse reminds believers of their duty to be thankful to both their parents and God, and to remember that the ultimate return is to God. The verse can be seen as a reminder of the role of parents in shaping the lives of their children, and the responsibility of children to show appreciation and respect towards them.
orig: ووصينا الإنسان بوالديه حملته أمه وهنا على وهن وفصاله في عامين أن اشكر لي ولوالديك إلي المصير

translation: But if they strive to make you associate with Me that of which you have no knowledge, do not obey them. But accompany them in this world with appropriate kindness and follow the way of those who turn to Me. Then to Me is your return, and I will inform you of what you used to do.
interpretation: The verse addresses the situation where people try to make the believer associate partners with God, something which they have no knowledge of. The verse advises the believer not to obey them and to instead accompany them in this world with appropriate kindness. However, the believer should follow the way of those who turn to God and seek His guidance. Ultimately, the believer's return is to God, who will inform them of their actions and hold them accountable for their deeds.
orig: وإن جاهداك على أن تشرك بي ما ليس لك به علم فلا تطعهما وصاحبهما في الدنيا معروفا واتبع سبيل من أناب إلي ثم إلي مرجعكم فأنبئكم بما كنتم تعملون

translation: O My people! If you should be in doubt concerning my religion, I do not worship those which you worship besides Allah; but I worship Allah, who causes you to die, and I am commissioned to be of those who submit.
interpretation: The verse is a statement from a prophet (identified as 'O My people') addressing his people, asserting his belief in the oneness of God and his role as a prophet. He clarifies that he does not worship the deities that his people worship, but instead worships the one true God, who is the cause of their death. He also identifies himself as a submitter to God's will. The verse conveys the prophet's unwavering faith in the one true God and his commitment to his role as a prophet, despite the doubts and disbelief of his people.
orig: يا بني إنها إن تك مثقال حبة من خردل فتكن في صخرة أو في السماوات أو في الأرض يأت بها الله إن الله لطيف خبير

translation: O my son, establish prayer, enjoin what is right, forbid what is wrong, and be patient over what befalls you. Indeed, that is of the matters requiring determination.
interpretation: This verse is a message from a parent to their child, emphasizing the importance of establishing a strong spiritual practice through prayer, promoting good and discouraging evil, and maintaining patience in the face of adversity. The verse highlights the significance of these actions, describing them as matters that require determination and perseverance. By following this advice, the child will be on a path towards righteousness and fulfilling their responsibilities in this life.
orig: يا بني أقم الصلاة وأمر بالمعروف وانه عن المنكر واصبر على ما أصابك إن ذلك من عزم الأمور

translation: And let not your hand be chained to your neck nor let it be tied to your side, otherwise you will become blameworthy and regretful. And indeed, your Lord is Generous and Knowing.
interpretation: The verse advises against being stingy and miserly, and encourages generosity and spending in the way of God. The phrase 'let not your hand be chained to your neck' means that one should not hoard wealth and be overly possessive of it. The phrase 'let it not be tied to your side' means that one should not be overly frugal and miserly. The verse warns that such behavior will lead to blame and regret. However, the verse also reminds that God is Generous and Knowing, implying that those who are generous and spend in the way of God will be rewarded for their actions.
orig: ولا تصعر خدك للناس ولا تمش في الأرض مرحا إن الله لا يحب كل مختال فخور

translation: And let My slaves not argue about Me, for surely they are weak before Me. But not for them to send to Me a witness, and I will not be unjust to them.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the greatness and power of God, and the weakness of humans in comparison. It warns against arguing with God or disputing His will. The verse reminds believers that they cannot send a witness or intercessor to speak on their behalf, and that God will not be unjust to them. The verse encourages humility and submission to God's will, and serves as a reminder of the limits of human understanding and power.
orig: واقصد في مشيك واغضض من صوتك إن أنكر الأصوات لصوت الحمير

translation: Have you not seen that Allah has made subject to you whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth and amply bestowed upon you His favors, [both] visible and concealed? And among the people is he who disputes about Allah without knowledge and without guidance and without a clear Book.
interpretation: The verse highlights the blessings and favors that God has bestowed upon humanity, both those that are visible and those that are not. Despite these blessings, some people still dispute and argue about God without knowledge or guidance, and without a clear book or source of truth. The verse serves as a reminder of God's power and generosity, and a warning to those who reject His signs and refuse to acknowledge the truth.
orig: ألم تروا أن الله سخر لكم ما في السماوات وما في الأرض وأسبغ عليكم نعمه ظاهرة وباطنة ومن الناس من يجادل في الله بغير علم ولا هدى ولا كتاب منير

translation: And when it is said to them, 'Follow what Allah has revealed,' they say, 'Rather, we will follow what we found our fathers doing.' What, even if their fathers were wrongdoers?
interpretation: The verse highlights the stubbornness and resistance of certain people to follow the guidance of Allah. When they are instructed to follow the teachings of Allah, they refuse and insist on following the traditions and practices of their forefathers. The verse questions the validity of this attitude, implying that blind adherence to tradition is not a valid reason to disregard the guidance of Allah. The verse serves as a reminder that each individual is responsible for their own actions and that following the path of those who have done wrong in the past is not a wise or justifiable decision.
orig: وإذا قيل لهم اتبعوا ما أنزل الله قالوا بل نتبع ما وجدنا عليه آباءنا أولو كان الشيطان يدعوهم إلى عذاب السعير

translation: And whoever submits his face to God while he is a doer of good - then he has grasped the most trustworthy handhold. And to God will be the outcome of matters.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the act of submitting oneself to God and doing good deeds. The verse highlights the idea that by doing so, one has grasped the 'most trustworthy handhold', which implies a strong and secure connection with God. The verse also emphasizes that the outcome of all matters ultimately belongs to God, reminding the believer to have trust and reliance in God's divine wisdom and justice.
orig: ومن يسلم وجهه إلى الله وهو محسن فقد استمسك بالعروة الوثقى وإلى الله عاقبة الأمور

translation: And whoever denies (their accountability for) it, he will surely return to Us (for punishment); then We will inform them of what they have done. Indeed, Allah is, of that which they used to do, Knowing.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the fate of those who deny or reject the truth and their accountability for their actions. The verse emphasizes that these individuals will ultimately return to God and be informed of the consequences of their deeds. The verse also highlights God's omniscience, indicating that He is fully aware of the true nature of people's actions and intentions. The verse serves as a warning to those who deny the truth and encourages them to reflect on the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's knowledge and justice.
orig: ومن كفر فلا يحزنك كفره إلينا مرجعهم فننبئهم بما عملوا إن الله عليم بذات الصدور

translation: We let them enjoy for a little while, then We compelled them to a harsh punishment.
interpretation: The verse describes the experience of those who were allowed to enjoy worldly pleasures for a short time before being subjected to severe punishment. This punishment was not arbitrary, but rather a consequence of their actions. The verse highlights the fleeting nature of worldly enjoyment and the inevitability of divine retribution for those who engage in unjust and sinful behavior.
orig: نمتعهم قليلا ثم نضطرهم إلى عذاب غليظ

translation: And if you asked them who created the heavens and the earth, they would surely say: 'Allah'. Then leave them to their play of idolatry until a time comes when the promise of Allah is fulfilled.
interpretation: The verse highlights the inherent knowledge that even the disbelievers possess, acknowledging that it was Allah who created the heavens and the earth. However, despite this knowledge, they continue to engage in idolatry and false worship. The verse advises the believers to leave them to their own devices, and to focus on their own faith and actions, until the promise of Allah, referring to the Day of Judgment, is fulfilled. This verse serves as a reminder of the ultimate power and authority of Allah, and the futility of idol worship and false beliefs.
orig: ولئن سألتهم من خلق السماوات والأرض ليقولن الله قل الحمد لله بل أكثرهم لا يعلمون

translation: To God belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth. Indeed, God is the Free of need, the Praiseworthy.
interpretation: The verse affirms the oneness of God and His absolute sovereignty over all of creation. It emphasizes that everything in the heavens and the earth belongs to God, and that He is in need of nothing and praiseworthy in Himself. The verse serves as a reminder of God's greatness and self-sufficiency, and the complete dependence of all creation on Him.
orig: لله ما في السماوات والأرض إن الله هو الغني الحميد

translation: And if all the trees on earth were pens and the sea [were] ink, replenished thereafter by seven more seas, the words of Allah would not be exhausted. Indeed, Allah is Exalted in Might and Wise.
interpretation: The verse highlights the infinite nature of God's words and knowledge. It emphasizes that even if all the trees on earth were used as pens and the seas as ink, the words of God would not be exhausted. This serves to remind the reader of the limitless nature of God's knowledge and power. The verse also highlights God's greatness and wisdom, emphasizing that He is all-powerful and all-knowing.
orig: ولو أنما في الأرض من شجرة أقلام والبحر يمده من بعده سبعة أبحر ما نفدت كلمات الله إن الله عزيز حكيم

translation: You were not created nor were you brought forth but as a single soul, indeed, God is all-hearing, all-seeing.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the unity and commonality of all human beings, as they were all created from a single soul. This idea is meant to promote a sense of equality and unity among people. The verse also highlights God's all-encompassing knowledge and awareness of His creation, as He is described as 'all-hearing, all-seeing'. This serves as a reminder of God's omnipresence and omniscience, and the ultimate accountability of all human beings to Him.
orig: ما خلقكم ولا بعثكم إلا كنفس واحدة إن الله سميع بصير

translation: Do you not see that Allah causes the night to enter the day and causes the day to enter the night and has subjected the sun and the moon, each running [its course] for a specified term, and that Allah, with whatever you do, is Acquainted?
interpretation: The verse highlights the power and control of Allah over the natural world, specifically the day and night and the movement of the sun and moon. The verse emphasizes the order and precision of these phenomena, with each having a specified term or time limit. The verse also reminds the reader that Allah is aware of all that humans do and that nothing is hidden from Him. The verse can be seen as a reminder of human's place in the universe, and the importance of living in accordance with Allah's will and commandments.
orig: ألم تر أن الله يولج الليل في النهار ويولج النهار في الليل وسخر الشمس والقمر كل يجري إلى أجل مسمى وأن الله بما تعملون خبير

translation: That is because Allah is the Truth, and that what they invoke other than Him is falsehood, and because Allah is the Most High, the Grand.
interpretation: The verse asserts the oneness and supremacy of Allah, emphasizing that He is the only truth and that all other deities or objects of worship are false. The verse also highlights Allah's greatness and superiority, positioning Him as the highest and most supreme being. The verse can be interpreted as a reminder to believers to remain steadfast in their faith and devotion to the one true God, and to avoid being swayed by false idols or beliefs. The verse can also serve as a warning to those who worship false deities, emphasizing the futility and emptiness of their actions and the ultimate supremacy of Allah.
orig: ذلك بأن الله هو الحق وأن ما يدعون من دونه الباطل وأن الله هو العلي الكبير

translation: Do you not see that the ships sail through the sea by God's grace that you may seek of His bounty? Surely in that are signs for every grateful, patient one.
interpretation: The verse highlights the blessings of God in providing a means of transportation through the sea, allowing people to seek His bounty and provisions. The verse emphasizes the role of patience and gratitude in understanding and appreciating these signs from God. The verse serves as a reminder to be grateful for the blessings we have and to be patient in times of hardship, as these qualities allow us to recognize and appreciate the signs of God in our lives.
orig: ألم تر أن الفلك تجري في البحر بنعمت الله ليريكم من آياته إن في ذلك لآيات لكل صبار شكور

translation: And when waves envelop them like shadows, they cry out to Allah, sincere to Him in their religion. But when He delivers them to the land, some of them become judicious, and none deny Our signs except every transgressor.
interpretation: The verse describes the situation of people who are faced with a calamity, represented by the waves that envelop them. In this moment of distress, they call upon Allah, sincere in their faith. However, when they are saved and brought back to land, some of them become grateful and righteous, while others continue to deny the signs of Allah and persist in their transgression. The verse highlights the contrasting responses of people in times of hardship and serves as a reminder of the importance of being steadfast in faith and grateful for Allah's mercy.
orig: وإذا غشيهم موج كالظلل دعوا الله مخلصين له الدين فلما نجاهم إلى البر فمنهم مقتصد وما يجحد بآياتنا إلا كل ختار كفور

translation: O mankind, fear your Lord and be dutiful to Him! Surely, the promise of Allah is true. So let not this present life deceive you, nor let the (so-called) 'chief deceiver' deceive you about Allah.
interpretation: The verse addresses all of humanity, urging them to fear and be mindful of their Lord, and to be dutiful in their actions. The verse emphasizes the truth of God's promise and warns against becoming complacent or being deceived by the temporary pleasures of this world. The verse also warns against being deceived by the 'chief deceiver', understood to be Satan, who seeks to lead people astray from the truth and the path of God. The verse serves as a reminder to live a righteous life, guided by God's teachings, and to not be deceived by the transient pleasures of this world.
orig: يا أيها الناس اتقوا ربكم واخشوا يوما لا يجزي والد عن ولده ولا مولود هو جاز عن والده شيئا إن وعد الله حق فلا تغرنكم الحياة الدنيا ولا يغرنكم بالله الغرور

translation: Verily, with Allah is the knowledge of the Hour, He sends down the rain, and knows that which is in the wombs. No soul knows what it will earn tomorrow, and no soul knows in what land it will die. Verily, Allah is All-Knowing, All-Aware.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the all-encompassing knowledge of God, who has knowledge of the Hour of Judgment, the ability to send down rain, and knowledge of what is in the wombs of mothers. The verse highlights the limits of human knowledge, as no soul knows what it will earn tomorrow or where it will die. The verse serves as a reminder of the limits of human control and the ultimate knowledge and power of God.
orig: إن الله عنده علم الساعة وينزل الغيث ويعلم ما في الأرحام وما تدري نفس ماذا تكسب غدا وما تدري نفس بأي أرض تموت إن الله عليم خبير

translation: The (revelation) of the Book (the Quran) is from Allah, the Exalted in Power, Full of Wisdom.
interpretation: The verse asserts that the Quran is a revelation from Allah, the Exalted in Power and Full of Wisdom. This verse emphasizes the divine origin of the Quran and the supreme power and wisdom of Allah. It reminds the reader of the ultimate source of the guidance and teachings contained within the Quran. The verse can also be seen as a reminder of the importance of approaching and understanding the Quran with the proper respect and reverence due to its divine origin.
orig: الم

translation: The revelation of the Book is from Allah, the Exalted in Power, full of wisdom.
interpretation: The verse affirms that the Qur'an is a revelation from Allah, the Lord of the Worlds. The attributes of Allah mentioned in the verse, 'Exalted in Power' and 'full of wisdom', emphasize the importance and significance of the Qur'an. The verse is a reminder that the Qur'an is not a creation of humans, but a divine message sent for the guidance of humanity. It is a call to recognize and submit to the power and wisdom of Allah, and to accept and follow the guidance brought by the Qur'an.
orig: تنزيل الكتاب لا ريب فيه من رب العالمين

translation: Or do they say, 'He has invented it?' No, but it is the truth, confirming what was before it, [a revelation] from the Lord of the worlds. So that He may give warning to a people to whom no warner has come before, so they might be guided.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the accusation of some people that the message brought by the prophet is false and invented. However, the verse emphasizes that it is indeed the truth from the Lord of the worlds, confirming what was revealed before it. The purpose of this revelation is to warn a people who have not received any warning before, so they might have the chance to be guided.
orig: أم يقولون افتراه بل هو الحق من ربك لتنذر قوما ما أتاهم من نذير من قبلك لعلهم يهتدون

translation: It is Allah who created the heavens and the earth and what is between them in six days, then He established Himself above the Throne. There is no protector for you besides Him, and no intercessor. So will you not reflect?
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the power and greatness of God as the creator of the heavens and the earth and all that is between them. It also mentions that God established Himself above the Throne, indicating His sovereignty and control over all things. The verse also stresses that there is no protector or intercessor for humans besides God, which means that people should not rely on any other beings or powers for help and support. The verse ends with a rhetorical question, inviting people to reflect on the significance of these truths and to consider the implications for their lives.
orig: الله الذي خلق السماوات والأرض وما بينهما في ستة أيام ثم استوى على العرش ما لكم من دونه من ولي ولا شفيع أفلا تتذكرون

translation: The decision (or command) is from Allah, from the heaven to the earth; then it will ascend to Him in a day whose measure is a thousand years according to what you count.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the power and control that Allah has over all things, from the heavens to the earth. The 'decision' or 'command' refers to the divine decree and plan of Allah, which is carried out according to His will. The verse also highlights the vastness of Allah's knowledge and power, as it describes a day that is equivalent to a thousand years in human terms. This serves as a reminder of the greatness of Allah and the limited understanding of human beings, encouraging humility and submission to the divine will.
orig: يدبر الأمر من السماء إلى الأرض ثم يعرج إليه في يوم كان مقداره ألف سنة مما تعدون

translation: That is Allah, the Entire Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, the Exalted in Might, the Merciful,
interpretation: The verse affirms the all-knowing and all-powerful nature of Allah, who has knowledge of both the unseen and the witnessed. The verse emphasizes Allah's greatness and mercy, highlighting His ability to oversee and control all aspects of existence. This verse serves as a reminder of Allah's omnipotence and omniscience, and encourages believers to seek His mercy and forgiveness.
orig: ذلك عالم الغيب والشهادة العزيز الرحيم

translation: He who has perfected everything and began the creation of man from clay.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the power and ability of God, who has perfected all things and created man from clay. This verse emphasizes the greatness and might of God, who has the power to create and perfect all things. The mention of man being created from clay serves as a reminder of the humble origins of human beings and their dependence on God, who has the power to give and take life. The verse can also be seen as a reminder of the fleeting and temporary nature of human existence, and the importance of recognizing and worshipping the one true God.
orig: الذي أحسن كل شيء خلقه وبدأ خلق الإنسان من طين

translation: Then made him of the descendants of a certain repulsive water.
interpretation: The verse refers to a specific individual and speaks about the creation of his descendants from repulsive water. The verse is found in the context of a story in which God transforms a man into a donkey as a punishment for his arrogance and transgression. The repulsive water could symbolize the man's impurity and unworthiness, and the transformation of his descendants from this water highlights the consequences of his sins and the impact of his actions on his lineage. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of humility, obedience, and avoiding arrogance and transgression.
orig: ثم جعل نسله من سلالة من ماء مهين

translation: Then He proportioned him and breathed into him from His spirit, and made for you hearing, sight, and hearts. Little are you grateful.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the creation of human beings, describing how God proportioned them and breathed His spirit into them. The verse highlights the importance of the senses of hearing, sight, and the heart, which are seen as gifts from God. However, the verse ends on a negative note, emphasizing the lack of gratitude that humans typically show for these blessings. The verse serves as a reminder of the greatness of God and the importance of showing gratitude for the blessings that we have been given.
orig: ثم سواه ونفخ فيه من روحه وجعل لكم السمع والأبصار والأفئدة قليلا ما تشكرون

translation: And they said, 'If we were to follow a guidance with you, we would certainly be snatched away from our land.' Have they not seen that We made the earth stationary? But despite that, they are still in doubt about the meeting of their Lord.
interpretation: The verse describes the disbelievers' rejection of the guidance offered to them. They claim that if they were to follow the guidance, they would be removed from their land. The verse counters this claim by reminding them that the earth is stationary and that they are still in doubt about the meeting with their Lord. The interpretation of this verse is that the disbelievers are unwilling to accept guidance and are making excuses for their disbelief, despite the clear signs of God's power and existence all around them.
orig: وقالوا أإذا ضللنا في الأرض أإنا لفي خلق جديد بل هم بلقاء ربهم كافرون

translation: Say, 'The Angel of Death, who is in charge of you, will take you in accordance with a predetermined time. Then to your Lord you will be returned.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the inevitability of death and the return to God. The verse emphasizes that the Angel of Death, who is responsible for taking the souls of people, will come for each person at a predetermined time. This is a reminder of the power and control that God has over life and death. After death, people will be returned to their Lord, indicating the accountability of each person for their actions in this life and the ultimate justice of God in the hereafter.
orig: قل يتوفاكم ملك الموت الذي وكل بكم ثم إلى ربكم ترجعون

translation: And if only the transgressors could see, when they touch their heads with their hands, [saying], 'Our Lord, we have seen and we have heard, so return us [to the world], we will be righteous.' Indeed, it has been decreed for them [that they will remain] as they were, so they will not taste success.
interpretation: The verse describes the regret of sinners when they see the consequences of their actions and turn to God in repentance, asking for a second chance to do good. However, the verse states that it has been decreed for them that they will remain as they were, meaning that their repentance will not be accepted and they will not be given a second chance. The verse emphasizes the importance of making the right choices in life and the consequences of making wrong choices. It also highlights the futility of seeking forgiveness and repentance when it is too late.
orig: ولو ترى إذ المجرمون ناكسو رءوسهم عند ربهم ربنا أبصرنا وسمعنا فارجعنا نعمل صالحا إنا موقنون

translation: And if it had been Our will, We would surely have given to every soul its guidance, but the word from Me takes effect: 'I will surely fill Hell with jinn and mankind together.'
interpretation: The verse explains that God has the power to guide everyone, but He has chosen to allow people to make their own choices and decisions. The 'word from Me' refers to God's decree that many people will end up in Hell. The verse emphasizes the severity of the punishment for those who choose to disobey God and stray from the right path, and serves as a reminder of the importance of following God's guidance and living a righteous life.
orig: ولو شئنا لآتينا كل نفس هداها ولكن حق القول مني لأملأن جهنم من الجنة والناس أجمعين

translation: So taste the punishment because of what you used to forget. Indeed, We have forgotten you. And taste the punishment of permanence for what you used to do.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the punishment that the disbelievers will receive on the Day of Judgment for their past sins and their rejection of God's message. The phrase 'So taste the punishment because of what you used to forget' refers to the consequences of their actions and their failure to remember or heed the warnings of the prophets. The statement 'Indeed, We have forgotten you' emphasizes the finality of their separation from God and their fate. The phrase 'And taste the punishment of permanence for what you used to do' reiterates the enduring nature of the punishment and the gravity of their sins. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of remembering and heeding the warnings of the prophets and the consequences of ignoring them.
orig: فذوقوا بما نسيتم لقاء يومكم هذا إنا نسيناكم وذوقوا عذاب الخلد بما كنتم تعملون

translation: Only those who believe in Our verses, when they are reminded of them, fall down in prostration and exalt [Allah] with praise of their Lord, and they are not arrogant.
interpretation: The verse describes the true believers as those who, when reminded of the signs of Allah, immediately prostrate and praise their Lord, humbled and grateful. These believers do not exhibit arrogance or pride. The verse emphasizes the importance of recognizing and submitting to the signs of Allah, and the humility and gratitude that should accompany such recognition.
orig: إنما يؤمن بآياتنا الذين إذا ذكروا بها خروا سجدا وسبحوا بحمد ربهم وهم لا يستكبرون

translation: Their sides parted from their beds, they call upon their Lord in fear and hope, and they spend (in charity) out of what We have given them.
interpretation: The verse describes the behavior of believers who are awakened from their sleep, filled with fear and hope towards their Lord. They quickly get up from their beds, eager to pray and worship their Lord. They also spend their wealth in charity, out of the blessings that God has given them. The verse highlights the importance of fearing God and hoping for His mercy, as well as the importance of giving charity and being generous with one's wealth. These actions reflect the believers' gratitude towards God for His blessings and their desire to please Him.
orig: تتجافى جنوبهم عن المضاجع يدعون ربهم خوفا وطمعا ومما رزقناهم ينفقون

translation: And not a soul knows what has been hidden for them of comfort for eyes as a reward for what they used to do.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the hidden rewards that God has prepared for individuals based on their actions. The verse emphasizes the unknown nature of these rewards, stating that no one knows what they are or what they look like. The phrase 'comfort for eyes' suggests that these rewards will be a source of great joy and happiness for those who receive them. The verse serves as a reminder that our actions in this life will have consequences in the next, and encourages believers to do good deeds in the hope of receiving a positive reward in the afterlife.
orig: فلا تعلم نفس ما أخفي لهم من قرة أعين جزاء بما كانوا يعملون

translation: Is one who is a believer like one who is a sinner and wicked? They are not equal.
interpretation: The verse highlights the fundamental difference between a believer and a sinner or wicked person. It emphasizes that the two cannot be equated and that they are fundamentally different from each other. This verse could be interpreted as a reminder to the believers to strive for righteousness and to avoid falling into sin and wickedness. It could also serve as a warning to the sinners and wicked to turn away from their ways and seek forgiveness and guidance from God.
orig: أفمن كان مؤمنا كمن كان فاسقا لا يستوون

translation: As for those who believe and do good deeds, for them are the Gardens of Refuge, as a welcome for what they used to do.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the reward for those who believe in God and perform good deeds. These people will be granted gardens of refuge, which is a place of peace and security, as a reward for their actions. The verse emphasizes the importance of both faith and good deeds, and the promise of a reward for those who strive to live a righteous life.
orig: أما الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات فلهم جنات المأوى نزلا بما كانوا يعملون

translation: But as for those who are unjust, their refuge is the fire. Every time they desire to emerge from it, they are returned to it, and it is said to them, 'Taste the punishment of the fire which you used to deny.'
interpretation: The verse describes the fate of the unjust, who will find themselves in the fire as their eternal refuge. Despite their attempts to escape, they will be forced back into it every time they try to leave. The verse emphasizes the never-ending nature of their punishment, and the futility of their efforts to escape it. The phrase 'taste the punishment of the fire' serves as a reminder of the reality of the hellfire, and the consequences of their unjust actions. The verse serves as a warning to those who persist in unrighteousness, urging them to repent and turn away from their sinful ways before it is too late.
orig: وأما الذين فسقوا فمأواهم النار كلما أرادوا أن يخرجوا منها أعيدوا فيها وقيل لهم ذوقوا عذاب النار الذي كنتم به تكذبون

translation: And We will surely make them taste of the nearer punishment before the greater punishment, perhaps they will return.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the punishment that will be given to the wrongdoers, both a 'nearer punishment' and a 'greater punishment'. The 'nearer punishment' may refer to a punishment that will be experienced in this world, while the 'greater punishment' may refer to the punishment in the hereafter. The verse suggests that the punishment is a form of divine intervention aimed at guiding the wrongdoers back to the right path. The phrase 'perhaps they will return' implies that the punishment is an act of mercy and a chance for repentance and reform, rather than an act of retribution and revenge.
orig: ولنذيقنهم من العذاب الأدنى دون العذاب الأكبر لعلهم يرجعون

translation: And who is more unjust than one who is reminded of the verses of his Lord, then turns away from them? Indeed, We will punish the criminals.
interpretation: The verse highlights the unjust behavior of those who, after being reminded of the signs or verses of their Lord (referring to the Qur'an), turn away from them. The verse emphasizes the severity of this act, stating that such people are indeed unjust. The verse further warns that a punishment will be given to the wrongdoers, implying that ignoring the signs of God will not go unnoticed and will have consequences.
orig: ومن أظلم ممن ذكر بآيات ربه ثم أعرض عنها إنا من المجرمين منتقمون

translation: And We did indeed give Moses the Book and made it a guidance for the Children of Israel.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the giving of the Book (Torah) to Moses and its purpose as a guidance for the Children of Israel. The verse highlights the significance of the Torah as a divine revelation and its role in guiding the Israelites. The verse can also be seen as a reminder of the covenant between God and the Israelites, and the importance of adhering to the teachings of the Torah.
orig: ولقد آتينا موسى الكتاب فلا تكن في مرية من لقائه وجعلناه هدى لبني إسرائيل

translation: And We made from among them leaders, guiding by Our command, because of their patience and because they had certainty in Our signs.
interpretation: The verse highlights the qualities of patience and certainty in God's signs as the reasons for the selection of some individuals from the community as leaders. These leaders were chosen by God to guide others in accordance with God's command. The verse emphasizes the importance of patience and unwavering faith in God's signs as essential qualities for leadership and guidance.
