The verse suggests that those who possess these qualities will be entrusted with the responsibility of leading and guiding others, and that this role is granted by God as a result of their patience and certainty in God's signs.
orig: وجعلنا منهم أئمة يهدون بأمرنا لما صبروا وكانوا بآياتنا يوقنون

translation: Surely your Lord will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection concerning that wherein they used to differ.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the Day of Judgment, when God will settle the disputes and differences that existed among people. The verse emphasizes the ultimate justice and fairness of God, who will have the power and knowledge to make just decisions and resolve all conflicts. The verse serves as a reminder that all human beings will be held accountable for their actions and beliefs, and that God will have the final say in all matters.
orig: إن ربك هو يفصل بينهم يوم القيامة فيما كانوا فيه يختلفون

translation: Has He not guided for them, of those before them, a generation who walked securely among the homes [of those who wronged themselves], indeed in that are signs. So do they not hear?
interpretation: The verse speaks about a previous generation that was guided by God and lived securely among the homes of those who had wronged themselves. The verse highlights the fact that there are lessons and signs to be learned from the experiences of this previous generation. The verse questions why people are not listening or paying attention to these signs, emphasizing the importance of reflection and learning from the past.
orig: أولم يهد لهم كم أهلكنا من قبلهم من القرون يمشون في مساكنهم إن في ذلك لآيات أفلا يسمعون

translation: Have they not seen that We drive water to the barren land, then bring forth therewith crops whereof their cattle and they eat? Will they not then see?
interpretation: The verse highlights the power of God in providing sustenance and nourishment to both humans and animals through the process of irrigation. The rhetorical question at the end of the verse serves to emphasize the importance of recognizing and acknowledging God's power and blessings. The verse encourages people to reflect on the signs of God's existence and mercy in their daily lives and to be grateful for them.
orig: أولم يروا أنا نسوق الماء إلى الأرض الجرز فنخرج به زرعا تأكل منه أنعامهم وأنفسهم أفلا يبصرون

translation: And they say, 'When will this promise be fulfilled, if you are truthful?'
interpretation: The verse is spoken from the perspective of the disbelievers who are questioning the promise of the coming of the Day of Judgment. They are skeptical of the believers' claims and challenge them to prove the truth of their words. The verse highlights the disbelievers' lack of faith and their denial of the signs of the end times. It serves as a reminder for the believers to be patient and steadfast in their faith, and not to be swayed by the disbelievers' doubts and mockery.
orig: ويقولون متى هذا الفتح إن كنتم صادقين

translation: Say, 'On the Day of Judgment, faith of the disbelievers will not benefit them nor will they be allowed to make amends.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the unchangeable reality of the Day of Judgment, where the disbelievers' faith will not be accepted, and they will not be given the opportunity to make amends for their past actions. This verse emphasizes the importance of accepting the truth and living a righteous life, as there will be no second chances on the Day of Judgment. It serves as a warning to those who deny the truth and a reminder that the consequences of their actions will be severe and irreversible.
orig: قل يوم الفتح لا ينفع الذين كفروا إيمانهم ولا هم ينظرون

translation: So turn away from them and wait. Indeed, they are also waiting.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the command to the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) to turn away from those who reject his message and be patient. The phrase 'they are also waiting' implies that the disbelievers are waiting for the opportunity to defeat the Prophet and his followers, while the Prophet and his followers are waiting for God's help and victory. The verse emphasizes the importance of patience and perseverance in the face of adversity and the certainty of God's support for those who are steadfast in their faith.
orig: فأعرض عنهم وانتظر إنهم منتظرون

translation: O Prophet, fear Allah and do not obey the disbelievers and the hypocrites. Indeed, Allah is Knowing and Wise.
interpretation: The verse addresses the Prophet Muhammad and commands him to fear Allah and not to follow the ways of the disbelievers and the hypocrites. The verse emphasizes the importance of staying true to one's faith and not being swayed by those who do not believe or who are insincere in their beliefs. The verse reminds the Prophet that Allah is all-knowing and wise, and that He is aware of the actions and intentions of all people. This verse serves as a reminder to all believers to stay steadfast in their faith and to be wary of those who may lead them astray.
orig: يا أيها النبي اتق الله ولا تطع الكافرين والمنافقين إن الله كان عليما حكيما

translation: And follow what is revealed to you from your Lord. Indeed, Allah is, of what you do, Acquainted.
interpretation: The verse is a command for the believer to follow the guidance and teachings that have been revealed to them by their Lord. The verse emphasizes the all-knowing nature of Allah, reminding the believer that Allah is aware of all their actions, both good and bad. The verse serves as a reminder for the believer to be mindful of their actions and to strive to follow the guidance of Allah in order to attain His pleasure and mercy.
orig: واتبع ما يوحى إليك من ربك إن الله كان بما تعملون خبيرا

translation: And put your trust in Allah. Surely, Allah is sufficient as a Trustee.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of putting one's trust in Allah and having faith that He will take care of all affairs. The verse serves as a reminder that Allah is sufficient as a Trustee, indicating that one does not need to rely on anyone or anything else. The verse encourages believers to have full trust and confidence in Allah, and to seek His guidance and help in all matters.
orig: وتوكل على الله وكفى بالله وكيلا

translation: For Allah has not made for any man two hearts within him; nor has He made your wives whom you declare to be unlawful, your mothers; nor has He made your adopted sons your real sons. That is but your saying with your mouths; and Allah speaks the truth and He guides on the right path.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of truth and the consequences of false speech. It states that God has not made two hearts within a person, meaning that a person cannot have two conflicting beliefs or desires. The verse then addresses the practice of declaring certain women as unlawful, and clarifies that these women are not the mothers of the men. Similarly, the verse states that adopted sons are not the real sons of the men. The verse emphasizes that these declarations are merely words spoken by the people, and that God speaks the truth. The verse serves as a reminder to the importance of truth and the consequences of false speech, and encourages people to follow the right path as guided by God.
orig: ما جعل الله لرجل من قلبين في جوفه وما جعل أزواجكم اللائي تظاهرون منهن أمهاتكم وما جعل أدعياءكم أبناءكم ذلكم قولكم بأفواهكم والله يقول الحق وهو يهدي السبيل

translation: Invite (people) to (follow) your Lord. Indeed, you are upon a straight path. Indeed, for Us is (the responsibility of) clarifying (the truth) to them. And indeed, they will come to you (on the Day of Judgement) knowing (the truth of) their affairs. So, (O Muhammad), do not be grieved over the disbelieving people. Indeed, those who have believed and done righteous deeds - for them will be the Gardens of Paradise as a lodging. For them therein is no fatigue, nor will they be expelled. And (as for) the believers who have fear of (the punishment of) their Lord, for them is forgiveness and a great reward.
interpretation: The verse addresses the Prophet Muhammad and instructs him to invite people to the worship of their Lord and to follow the right path. It emphasizes that the responsibility of clarifying the truth lies with God and that people will come to know the truth of their actions on the Day of Judgement. The verse advises the Prophet not to be saddened by the disbelief of the people and offers hope and reassurance to those who have believed and done righteous deeds, promising them gardens of Paradise as a lodging. The verse also mentions the reward for those who fear the punishment of their Lord and do good deeds.
orig: ادعوهم لآبائهم هو أقسط عند الله فإن لم تعلموا آباءهم فإخوانكم في الدين ومواليكم وليس عليكم جناح فيما أخطأتم به ولكن ما تعمدت قلوبكم وكان الله غفورا رحيما

translation: The Prophet is closer to the believers than their own selves, and his wives are their mothers. And blood relatives are closer to one another in the decree of Allah than the believers and the emigrants, except that you do not do favor to your protectors in a way that you will be unjust to yourselves. This has been written in the decree of Allah.
interpretation: The verse highlights the special status of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) in relation to the believers, and emphasizes the importance of maintaining strong family ties and treating relatives kindly and with fairness. The verse also reminds the believers not to neglect their duties towards their protectors and to avoid being unjust to themselves. Overall, the verse promotes the values of unity, solidarity, and fairness among the believers and their families.
orig: النبي أولى بالمؤمنين من أنفسهم وأزواجه أمهاتهم وأولو الأرحام بعضهم أولى ببعض في كتاب الله من المؤمنين والمهاجرين إلا أن تفعلوا إلى أوليائكم معروفا كان ذلك في الكتاب مسطورا

translation: And when We took a covenant from the prophets, and from you, and from Noah, and Abraham, and Moses, and Jesus, the son of Mary, and We took from them a solemn covenant.
interpretation: The verse speaks about a covenant that was taken from a group of prophets, including the speaker (who is believed to be the Prophet Muhammad), Noah, Abraham, Moses, and Jesus. The covenant was a solemn one, indicating its importance and seriousness. The verse emphasizes the continuity and unity of the prophetic message and the shared responsibility of the prophets in delivering and upholding this message. The verse may also serve as a reminder to the believers of their own covenant with God and the need to fulfill their obligations and responsibilities as followers of the prophetic tradition.
orig: وإذ أخذنا من النبيين ميثاقهم ومنك ومن نوح وإبراهيم وموسى وعيسى ابن مريم وأخذنا منهم ميثاقا غليظا

translation: Those who believe and do righteous deeds ask not permission to do good deed, and they fear a day when the oppressors will be brought before the punishment. And Ibada (worship) is totally for Allah (Alone). So, invite (people) to (the way of) your Lord with wisdom and fair preaching, and argue with them in a way that is better. Truly, your Lord is Well-Aware of those who stray from His path, and He is Well-Aware of those who are guided.
interpretation: The verse highlights the contrast between the righteous believers and the disbelievers. The believers do not hesitate to do good deeds, and they fear the Day of Judgment when oppressors will be punished. They are commanded to call people to the path of their Lord with wisdom, fair preaching, and gentle argument. The verse emphasizes the importance of inviting others to the way of God, while also recognizing that God is aware of those who stray and those who are guided. The verse encourages the believers to be proactive in spreading the message of Islam and to do so in a wise, gentle, and persuasive manner.
orig: ليسأل الصادقين عن صدقهم وأعد للكافرين عذابا أليما

translation: O believers, remember the favor of God upon you when hostile forces came to you, and We sent upon them a wind and an army that you did not see. And God is, in what you do, all-seeing.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the protection and favor of God upon the believers during a time of attack by hostile forces. The verse emphasizes the unseen power and intervention of God, who sent a wind and an unseen army to defeat the enemy. The verse serves as a reminder of the constant presence and watchfulness of God, who is all-seeing and all-knowing of the actions of human beings. The verse encourages the believers to remember and be grateful for the blessings and protection of God, who is always with them and aware of their needs and struggles.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا اذكروا نعمة الله عليكم إذ جاءتكم جنود فأرسلنا عليهم ريحا وجنودا لم تروها وكان الله بما تعملون بصيرا

translation: When there came upon you from above you and from beneath you fire and smoke, and when you tasted the scorching wind, and when the earthquake seized you, what time was it then that you prayed?
interpretation: The verse describes a series of calamities that have befallen a people, including fire, smoke, scorching wind, and earthquakes. These events are described in vivid and dramatic terms, meant to inspire fear and awe. The verse then asks a rhetorical question: 'what time was it then that you prayed?'. This question serves to highlight the idea that people often turn to prayer and religion only in times of crisis and hardship, after all other options have been exhausted. The verse serves as a reminder that it is never too late to repent and turn to God, but that it is best to do so before calamity strikes.
orig: إذ جاءوكم من فوقكم ومن أسفل منكم وإذ زاغت الأبصار وبلغت القلوب الحناجر وتظنون بالله الظنونا

translation: Indeed, We will test the believers with a severe shaking.
interpretation: The verse speaks about a test that will be faced by the believers. This test will come in the form of a severe shaking or earthquake. The verse emphasizes the intensity of the test, indicating that it will be a significant challenge for the believers. The verse serves as a reminder that believers will face trials and tribulations, but these tests are ultimately a means of purification and strengthening of faith.
orig: هنالك ابتلي المؤمنون وزلزلوا زلزالا شديدا

translation: And when the hypocrites and those in whose hearts is a disease say, 'What Allah and His Messenger promised us was only delusion.'
interpretation: The verse describes the attitude of hypocrites and those who harbor doubt towards the promises of God and His Messenger. They regard the promises as false and delusional. This verse serves as a warning to the believers to be cautious of such people, who may appear to be part of the community but in reality harbor disbelief and doubt in their hearts.
orig: وإذ يقول المنافقون والذين في قلوبهم مرض ما وعدنا الله ورسوله إلا غرورا

translation: And when a group of them said, 'O people of Yathrib, you have no stand! Go back!' and a group of them asked the Prophet for permission [to stay behind], saying, 'Our homes are exposed,' and they did not mean [by 'exposed'] except for fleeing.
interpretation: The verse describes a situation where a group of people from Medina (known as Yathrib in the verse) are divided in their stance regarding a matter. One group urges the others to leave, while another group seeks permission from the Prophet to stay, citing their homes as a reason. However, the verse clarifies that their concern for their homes is not genuine, but rather an excuse to avoid the situation. The verse highlights the importance of honesty and sincerity in one's actions and intentions, and the consequences of deception and insincerity.
orig: وإذ قالت طائفة منهم يا أهل يثرب لا مقام لكم فارجعوا ويستأذن فريق منهم النبي يقولون إن بيوتنا عورة وما هي بعورة إن يريدون إلا فرارا

translation: And if We had sent down upon them a sedition from the sky, surely, they would have been disunited in it. And no time have they been given except a little.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the lack of faith and unity among people, even in the face of divine signs and interventions. The verse describes a hypothetical situation where a 'sedition' or trial is sent down from the sky, and the people would still be unable to come together and unite in response. The verse highlights the brevity of their time, emphasizing the fleeting nature of life and the importance of using it wisely. Overall, the verse serves as a reminder of the consequences of disunity and the importance of faith and unity in the face of adversity.
orig: ولو دخلت عليهم من أقطارها ثم سئلوا الفتنة لآتوها وما تلبثوا بها إلا يسيرا

translation: And they had pledged to God before, not to turn back (to disbelief) and was
interpretation: No interpretation
orig: ولقد كانوا عاهدوا الله من قبل لا يولون الأدبار وكان عهد الله مسئولا

translation: Say: 'Flight will not benefit you if you flee from death or killing, and then you will not be allowed to enjoy (your life) except for a little.'
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the futility of trying to escape death or killing, as it ultimately brings an end to all worldly pleasures and enjoyments. The verse suggests that even if one manages to escape, they will not be able to enjoy their life for long, as death is inevitable. The verse serves as a reminder of the transience of life and the importance of preparing for the afterlife. It encourages believers to focus on their actions and behavior, and to strive for righteousness and piety, rather than seeking to escape death or harm.
orig: قل لن ينفعكم الفرار إن فررتم من الموت أو القتل وإذا لا تمتعون إلا قليلا

translation: Say, 'Who is it that can protect you from Allah if He intends for you harm, or intends for you mercy?' And they will not find for themselves, besides Allah, any protector or helper.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the power and control of Allah over all things, and the futility of seeking protection from anyone other than Him. The question 'Who is it that can protect you from Allah?' is a rhetorical one, intended to make the listener reflect on their own weakness and dependence on Allah. The verse also highlights the dual nature of Allah's actions, as He has the power to bring both harm and mercy. However, regardless of His actions, the people will not find any protector or helper besides Allah. This verse can serve as a reminder of the importance of seeking Allah's mercy and protection, and the futility of relying on anyone else for help and support.
orig: قل من ذا الذي يعصمكم من الله إن أراد بكم سوءا أو أراد بكم رحمة ولا يجدون لهم من دون الله وليا ولا نصيرا

translation: Allah knows well those among you who hinder (others) and those who say, 'Come to us,' and they mean only to deceive. And they do not intend to meet you (in battle) except in a small number.
interpretation: The verse highlights the knowledge of Allah about the hypocrisy of certain individuals who invite others to come to them, but in reality, they intend to deceive them. These individuals do not have good intentions and only seek to create discord and strife. The verse emphasizes that their intentions are not sincere, and they only gather in small numbers, indicating their weakness and lack of support. The verse serves as a warning to be aware of such deceitful individuals and their nefarious intentions.
orig: قد يعلم الله المعوقين منكم والقائلين لإخوانهم هلم إلينا ولا يأتون البأس إلا قليلا

translation: Fairer in speech they are to you, when you acquire them as property, than they were to you when you met them the first time. But fairer to you they become in speech when you give them their dowries, taking them back in marriage, not to take other than them in marriage, or to bind yourselves to them irreversibly. So, what they have been promising you is more likely that they will not keep their word. Surely, when fear comes to them, you see them looking at you, their eyes rolling like one being overcome by death. Then, when fear has passed, they attack you with sharp tongues, greedy for wealth. Such have not believed. So, God has made their deeds come to naught, and for God is a swift reckoning.
interpretation: The verse describes the behavior of certain individuals who are two-faced and insincere in their dealings with others. They are polite and kind when they are trying to gain something from someone, but once they have acquired what they want, they become rude and ungrateful. The verse portrays their fear and anxiety when they are confronted with a difficult situation, and their quickness to attack and criticize when they feel safe again. The verse emphasizes the insincerity and untrustworthiness of these people and the emptiness of their promises. It serves as a warning to be cautious and not to be deceived by their smooth words and fair speeches. The verse also highlights the swift and severe punishment that God has prepared for those who are unfaithful and unjust.
orig: أشحة عليكم فإذا جاء الخوف رأيتهم ينظرون إليك تدور أعينهم كالذي يغشى عليه من الموت فإذا ذهب الخوف سلقوكم بألسنة حداد أشحة على الخير أولئك لم يؤمنوا فأحبط الله أعمالهم وكان ذلك على الله يسيرا

translation: They think the companies have not gone, and if the companies come, they would wish they were in the wilderness among the bedouins and they would ask you about news of them. If they were among you, they would not have fought except a little.
interpretation: The verse describes the disbelievers' false sense of security and their underestimation of the consequences of their actions. The verse mentions that if the 'companies' or armies of the believers come, the disbelievers would wish they were in the wilderness, far away from the battle. They would ask for news about the armies, indicating their fear and concern. The verse highlights the disbelievers' lack of commitment to their cause, as they would not have fought except for a little, even if they were among the believers. The verse serves as a reminder that those who underestimate the power of God and his believers will ultimately face the consequences of their actions.
orig: يحسبون الأحزاب لم يذهبوا وإن يأت الأحزاب يودوا لو أنهم بادون في الأعراب يسألون عن أنبائكم ولو كانوا فيكم ما قاتلوا إلا قليلا

translation: You have indeed in the Messenger of Allah an excellent example for him who hopes in Allah and the Last Day and remembers Allah much.
interpretation: The verse highlights the Messenger of Allah (Prophet Muhammad) as an excellent example for those who believe in Allah and the Day of Judgment and who remember Allah frequently. By following the Prophet's example, one can lead a life that is pleasing to Allah and secure a place in the hereafter. The verse emphasizes the importance of having hope in Allah, preparing for the hereafter, and constantly remembering Allah in one's daily life.
orig: لقد كان لكم في رسول الله أسوة حسنة لمن كان يرجو الله واليوم الآخر وذكر الله كثيرا

translation: And when the believers saw the confederates, they said, 'This is what Allah and His Messenger had promised us, and Allah and His Messenger spoke the truth.' And it only increased them in faith and submission.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the reaction of the believers when they saw the 'conferates' or enemy forces. Despite the overwhelming odds, the believers remained steadfast and firm in their faith, recognizing that the situation was a fulfillment of the promise of God and His Messenger. Rather than causing them to despair or weaken their faith, the sight of the enemy only served to increase their faith and submission to God. The verse highlights the importance of maintaining faith and trust in God, even in the face of adversity and challenges.
orig: ولما رأى المؤمنون الأحزاب قالوا هذا ما وعدنا الله ورسوله وصدق الله ورسوله وما زادهم إلا إيمانا وتسليما

translation: Among the believers are men who have been true to their covenant with Allah; of them some have completed their vow (of poverty and worship in the path of Allah), and some of them are still waiting, but they have never changed (i.e. never been unfaithful to) their determination.
interpretation: The verse highlights the qualities of some of the believers who have remained true to their covenant with Allah. These individuals have fulfilled their vow of poverty and worship, while others are still waiting to do so. The verse emphasizes their unwavering determination and commitment, as they have not changed or wavered from their promise to Allah.
orig: من المؤمنين رجال صدقوا ما عاهدوا الله عليه فمنهم من قضى نحبه ومنهم من ينتظر وما بدلوا تبديلا

translation: To those who are truthful, God will surely reward them with truth, and the hypocrites, if He wills, He will punish them, or He will turn to them in mercy. Indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the outcome of two groups of people - the truthful and the hypocrites. The truthful will be rewarded by God with truth, emphasizing the alignment of their actions with their beliefs. The hypocrites, on the other hand, face the possibility of punishment or mercy from God. The verse highlights the power and authority of God in determining the fates of individuals, and the importance of sincerity and authenticity in one's faith.
orig: ليجزي الله الصادقين بصدقهم ويعذب المنافقين إن شاء أو يتوب عليهم إن الله كان غفورا رحيما

translation: For those who disbelieve, Allah has set a seal upon their hearts, so they do not know. And in their ears is deafness, and upon them is blindness. And those who believe are against them, helping Allah; and Allah is seeing [what they do]. Indeed, Allah is sufficient for the believers in battle. And ever is Allah Exalted in Might and Wise.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the state of those who disbelieve in Allah and the contrasting state of those who believe. The verse describes how Allah has set a seal upon the hearts of the disbelievers, causing them to be ignorant and unaware. They are also described as having deafness in their ears and blindness in their eyes. On the other hand, the believers are described as being against the disbelievers, helping Allah and striving in His cause. The verse emphasizes that Allah is sufficient for the believers and that He is all-powerful and wise. The verse serves as a reminder of the stark contrast between the fate of the believers and the disbelievers, and the importance of faith and trust in Allah during times of struggle and conflict.
orig: ورد الله الذين كفروا بغيظهم لم ينالوا خيرا وكفى الله المؤمنين القتال وكان الله قويا عزيزا

translation: And those who have been made to appear before
interpretation: No interpretation
orig: وأنزل الذين ظاهروهم من أهل الكتاب من صياصيهم وقذف في قلوبهم الرعب فريقا تقتلون وتأسرون فريقا

translation: And We inherited the earth from them and their homes and their wealth, and an inheritance that they did not know. And God is capable of all things.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the power and control of God, who has inherited the earth and the possessions of previous civilizations that have been destroyed. The phrase 'an inheritance that they did not know' highlights the unexpected and sudden nature of these events, and the inability of people to foresee or prevent them. The verse emphasizes the omnipotence of God, who has the power and control over all things, and who can take or give as He pleases.
orig: وأورثكم أرضهم وديارهم وأموالهم وأرضا لم تطئوها وكان الله على كل شيء قديرا

translation: O Prophet, say to your wives: if you desire this world's life and its adornment, then come, I will provide for you and set you free in a handsome manner.
interpretation: The verse addresses the Prophet Muhammad and instructs him to convey a message to his wives. If they value the pleasures and luxuries of this world more than their current status as the wives of the Prophet, then they are free to leave and he will provide for them in a generous and dignified manner. The verse emphasizes the importance of prioritizing the hereafter over the materialistic desires of this world and highlights the Prophet's generosity and concern for the well-being of his wives, even in the face of their potential departure.
orig: يا أيها النبي قل لأزواجك إن كنتن تردن الحياة الدنيا وزينتها فتعالين أمتعكن وأسرحكن سراحا جميلا

translation: But if you are grateful, indeed Allah is Exalted in Grace to the doers of good.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the gratitude of the believers towards Allah and his messenger and the promise of great reward for those who do good. The verse encourages gratitude and good deeds, emphasizing the generosity of Allah towards those who are grateful and do good. It serves as a reminder to believers to be thankful for what they have and to strive to do good deeds, as they will be rewarded for it.
orig: وإن كنتن تردن الله ورسوله والدار الآخرة فإن الله أعد للمحسنات منكن أجرا عظيما

translation: O wives of the Prophet, whoever of you commits a clear sin, for her the punishment will be doubled, and that is easy for Allah.
interpretation: The verse addresses the wives of the Prophet Muhammad and warns them of the severe consequences of committing a clear sin. The punishment for such a sin will be doubled, indicating the gravity of the offense. The verse emphasizes the power and ability of Allah to easily mete out the punishment. The verse serves as a reminder to the wives of the Prophet, and by extension to all believers, of the importance of maintaining righteousness and avoiding sin.
orig: يا نساء النبي من يأت منكن بفاحشة مبينة يضاعف لها العذاب ضعفين وكان ذلك على الله يسيرا

translation: But as for he who is eager to meet Allah, the Lord of the worlds, and is pleased with the arrival of the Hour, and calls upon Allah frequently, [then] for him is the supreme success.
interpretation: The verse describes the characteristics of a believer who is eagerly awaiting the Day of Judgment and is constantly seeking Allah's pleasure. The believer is pleased with the arrival of the Hour, meaning they are ready and accepting of the end of this world and the beginning of the next. They frequently call upon Allah, indicating their devotion and submission to Him. The verse promises the supreme success for such a believer, emphasizing the reward that awaits them in the afterlife for their faith and actions.
orig: ومن يقنت منكن لله ورسوله وتعمل صالحا نؤتها أجرها مرتين وأعتدنا لها رزقا كريما

translation: O Prophet's wives! You are not like any other women. If you fear Allah, then be not soft in (your) speech, lest he in whose heart is a disease aspire (to adultery), but speak a word suitable.
interpretation: The verse addresses the wives of the Prophet Muhammad and emphasizes their unique status. It advises them to be mindful of their speech and behavior, as their actions can have a significant impact on others. If they fear God, they are instructed not to speak in a way that may incite desire or temptation in those with ill intentions. Instead, they are told to speak words that are appropriate and respectful. The verse serves as a reminder for all individuals, especially those in positions of influence, to be mindful of the impact of their words and actions on those around them.
orig: يا نساء النبي لستن كأحد من النساء إن اتقيتن فلا تخضعن بالقول فيطمع الذي في قلبه مرض وقلن قولا معروفا

translation: And abide in your houses and do not display yourselves like the display of the first days of ignorance; and establish prayer and give zakah and obey Allah and His Messenger. Indeed, Allah intends only to remove from you the impurity, O people of the house, and to purify you with a thorough purification.
interpretation: This verse addresses the people of the house (Ahl al-Bayt), instructing them to stay in their homes and not to display themselves like the ignorant people of the past. They are also commanded to establish prayer, give zakah (charity), and obey Allah and His Messenger. The verse highlights the importance of purification and removing impurities, both physically and spiritually. By following these instructions, the people of the house will be purified and cleansed. The verse can be interpreted as a reminder for Muslims to focus on their inner purity and devotion to Allah, rather than being preoccupied with external appearances and worldly matters.
orig: وقرن في بيوتكن ولا تبرجن تبرج الجاهلية الأولى وأقمن الصلاة وآتين الزكاة وأطعن الله ورسوله إنما يريد الله ليذهب عنكم الرجس أهل البيت ويطهركم تطهيرا

translation: And mention in your houses the verses of Allah and wisdom. Indeed, Allah is ever-Subtle, all-Aware.
interpretation: The verse is directing believers to remember and recite the verses of the Quran and wisdom in their homes. By doing this, the verse suggests that one's home becomes a place where the presence of God is invoked and the guidance of the Quran is sought. The verse also highlights the qualities of Allah as being subtle and all-aware, emphasizing the importance of recognizing and understanding the presence of God in daily life. Overall, the verse encourages the practice of incorporating the teachings of the Quran into daily life and cultivating a deeper awareness of God's presence.
orig: واذكرن ما يتلى في بيوتكن من آيات الله والحكمة إن الله كان لطيفا خبيرا

translation: For the believers, both men and women, are protectors of one another: they enjoin what is just and forbid what is evil; they perform the prayer and give the alms, and obey God and His Messenger. It is they upon whom God will have mercy: God is almighty, wise.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the role and responsibilities of the believers, both men and women. It highlights the importance of community and mutual support among the believers, who are encouraged to enjoin what is just and forbid what is evil. The verse also mentions several practices that are considered important for the believers, such as performing the prayer, giving alms, and obeying God and His Messenger. The verse emphasizes the rewards that will be given to those who fulfill these responsibilities, and the mercy of God that will be bestowed upon them. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of faith, good deeds, and obedience to God and His Messenger, and the ultimate reward that awaits the believers in the hereafter.
orig: إن المسلمين والمسلمات والمؤمنين والمؤمنات والقانتين والقانتات والصادقين والصادقات والصابرين والصابرات والخاشعين والخاشعات والمتصدقين والمتصدقات والصائمين والصائمات والحافظين فروجهم والحافظات والذاكرين الله كثيرا والذاكرات أعد الله لهم مغفرة وأجرا عظيما

translation: It is not for a believer, man or woman, when Allah and His Messenger have decided a matter, that they should [thereafter] have any choice about their affair. And whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger has certainly strayed into clear error.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of obedience and submission to the will of Allah and His messenger. It makes clear that once a decision has been made by Allah and His messenger, there is no room for disagreement or disobedience. The verse warns that those who disobey Allah and His messenger have strayed far from the right path and are in clear error. This verse serves as a reminder of the importance of obedience and submission to Allah and His messenger, and the consequences of disobedience.
orig: وما كان لمؤمن ولا مؤمنة إذا قضى الله ورسوله أمرا أن يكون لهم الخيرة من أمرهم ومن يعص الله ورسوله فقد ضل ضلالا مبينا

translation: But when you said to the one whom Allah had favored and whom you had favored, 'Retain your wife for yourself and fear Allah.' But you concealed within yourself what Allah was to disclose. And you feared the people, while Allah has greater right that you should fear Him. So when Zayd had fulfilled his desire from her, We gave her to you in marriage, so that there should be no difficulty for the believers in respect of the wives of their adopted sons when they have fulfilled their desire from them. And Allah's command must be fulfilled.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the relationship between Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) and Zayd's ex-wife Zainab. Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) advised Zayd to keep his wife and fear God, but Zayd was unable to reconcile his differences with Zainab. Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) initially hesitated to marry Zainab due to their previous familial relationship, but after Zayd divorced Zainab and there was no longer a barrier, Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) married Zainab. The verse highlights the importance of obeying God's command and prioritizing God's fear over the opinions of others. The verse also clarifies the ruling on adoption and the marriage of the adopted son's ex-wife, emphasizing that it is permissible in Islam.
orig: وإذ تقول للذي أنعم الله عليه وأنعمت عليه أمسك عليك زوجك واتق الله وتخفي في نفسك ما الله مبديه وتخشى الناس والله أحق أن تخشاه فلما قضى زيد منها وطرا زوجناكها لكي لا يكون على المؤمنين حرج في أزواج أدعيائهم إذا قضوا منهن وطرا وكان أمر الله مفعولا

translation: There is no blame upon the Prophet concerning that which Allah has commanded him. For it was the custom of Allah with those who passed on before. And the command of Allah is a decree determined.
interpretation: The verse affirms that the Prophet Muhammad is not at fault for following the commands of Allah, as it has always been the way of Allah with previous prophets. The verse emphasizes the divine nature of Allah's commands and the unchangeable nature of His decrees.
orig: ما كان على النبي من حرج فيما فرض الله له سنة الله في الذين خلوا من قبل وكان أمر الله قدرا مقدورا

translation: Those who fulfill the covenant of God and do not break the contract, and who join that which God has ordered to be joined and fear their Lord and are afraid of no one but God, and sufficient is God as a Reckoner.
interpretation: The verse describes the qualities of righteous believers who uphold their covenant with God, follow His commands, fear Him, and are not intimidated by anyone but God. These believers trust in God as their ultimate reckoner and judge. The verse highlights the importance of fulfilling one's promises, following God's orders, and having a strong and unwavering faith in Him. It also emphasizes the importance of fearing God and being mindful of one's actions, as God is the ultimate judge and reckoner of all deeds.
orig: الذين يبلغون رسالات الله ويخشونه ولا يخشون أحدا إلا الله وكفى بالله حسيبا

translation: Muhammad is not the father of any of your men, but (he is) the Messenger of Allah, and the Seal of the Prophets. And Allah has full knowledge of all things.
interpretation: The verse affirms that Prophet Muhammad is not the biological father of any man among the people, but rather the Messenger of God and the last of the prophets. This statement clarifies the relationship of the Prophet to the people and emphasizes his unique and important role as the final prophet of Islam. The verse also emphasizes God's knowledge and understanding of all things, emphasizing his omniscience and power.
orig: ما كان محمد أبا أحد من رجالكم ولكن رسول الله وخاتم النبيين وكان الله بكل شيء عليما

translation: O believers, remember Allah often.
interpretation: The verse is a command to the believers to remember and remember Allah frequently. This constant remembrance of Allah is a way for the believers to maintain their faith, stay mindful of their actions, and seek His guidance and mercy. The verse emphasizes the importance of maintaining a strong connection with Allah, and encourages the believers to engage in various forms of remembrance, such as prayer, recitation of the Quran, and meditation. By doing so, the believers can cultivate a deeper understanding of their faith, strengthen their relationship with Allah, and lead a life in accordance with His teachings.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا اذكروا الله ذكرا كثيرا

translation: And celebrate His praises in the morning and in the afternoon.
interpretation: The verse is encouraging Muslims to remember and praise God at the beginning of the day (morning) and at the end of the day (afternoon). This can be interpreted as a reminder for Muslims to be mindful of God throughout the day and to express their gratitude for His blessings and guidance. By praising God in the morning and afternoon, Muslims are reminded of their reliance on God and their duty to worship Him. This verse also emphasizes the importance of maintaining a consistent and regular practice of worship and devotion.
orig: وسبحوه بكرة وأصيلا

translation: He it is Who sends blessings on you and His angels, that He may bring you out from the depths of darkness into the light; and He is ever Merciful to the believers.
interpretation: The verse highlights the mercy and compassion of God towards the believers. It speaks of how God sends blessings upon the believers, along with His angels, with the intention of guiding them from the depths of darkness and ignorance into the light of knowledge and understanding. The verse emphasizes the boundless mercy of God towards the believers, who are constantly guided and protected by Him.
orig: هو الذي يصلي عليكم وملائكته ليخرجكم من الظلمات إلى النور وكان بالمؤمنين رحيما

translation: Greet them with a salutation of peace on the Day they meet Him. And assure them of a noble reward.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the meeting of people with God on the Day of Judgment. It instructs believers to greet them with a salutation of peace, indicating respect and reverence for the solemnity of the occasion. Additionally, the verse assures the believers of a noble reward, emphasizing the justice and mercy of God. The verse serves as a message of hope and comfort to the believers, reminding them of the rewards that await them for their faith and good deeds.
orig: تحيتهم يوم يلقونه سلام وأعد لهم أجرا كريما

translation: O Prophet, indeed We have sent you as a witness and a bringer of good tidings and a warner.
interpretation: The verse is addressing the Prophet Muhammad, reminding him of his role as a messenger of God. The verse explains that the Prophet has been sent as a 'witness' to the truth of Islam, a 'bringer of good tidings' to those who believe, and a 'warner' to those who reject the message. The verse emphasizes the importance of the Prophet's mission and the significance of his role in conveying the message of Islam to the world.
orig: يا أيها النبي إنا أرسلناك شاهدا ومبشرا ونذيرا

translation: Inviters to God, by His permission, and with visible signs and a clear script.
interpretation: The verse refers to those who invite others to the path of God, and they do so with God's permission. They are also described as having "visible signs" and a "clear script," which can be interpreted as a reference to their actions and words that serve as a clear and convincing evidence of the truth of their message. This verse highlights the importance of inviting others to the path of God and the need for those inviters to have a strong and clear message that is supported by their actions.
orig: وداعيا إلى الله بإذنه وسراجا منيرا

translation: And give good news to the believers that they have from God a great reward.
interpretation: This verse is a message of good news and hope for the believers. It promises them a great reward from God for their faith and commitment. The verse serves as a source of motivation and encouragement for the believers to continue on the path of righteousness, knowing that they will be rewarded for their efforts in this life and the next.
orig: وبشر المؤمنين بأن لهم من الله فضلا كبيرا

translation: And do not obey the disbelievers and the hypocrites, and turn away from them and trust in Allah; and sufficient is Allah as a Disposer of affairs.
interpretation: The verse advises believers not to obey the disbelievers and hypocrites, and to instead turn away from them. It emphasizes the importance of putting one's trust in Allah and recognizing that He is sufficient as a Disposer of affairs. The verse serves as a reminder to believers to be cautious of those who do not believe or are insincere in their faith and to rely on Allah in all matters.
orig: ولا تطع الكافرين والمنافقين ودع أذاهم وتوكل على الله وكفى بالله وكيلا

translation: O you who have believed, when you marry believing women and then divorce them before you have touched them, then there is no period for you to observe in their case; therefore complete the period, and pay them their dowries fairly.
interpretation: This verse addresses believers who have married believing women and then divorced them before consummating the marriage. The verse states that in this case, there is no waiting period required before the woman can marry someone else. However, the verse instructs the believers to fulfill any financial obligations they have towards the woman, such as paying her the dowry. The verse emphasizes the importance of treating all individuals, especially women, with fairness and justice in matters of marriage and divorce.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا إذا نكحتم المؤمنات ثم طلقتموهن من قبل أن تمسوهن فما لكم عليهن من عدة تعتدونها فمتعوهن وسرحوهن سراحا جميلا

translation: O Prophet, We have made lawful for you the wives to whom you have given their due dowries and those your right hand possesses from what Allah has returned to you [of captives] and the daughters of your paternal uncles and the daughters of your paternal aunts and the daughters of your maternal uncles and the daughters of your maternal aunts who emigrated with you and a believing woman if she gives herself to the Prophet [in marriage] if the Prophet wishes to marry her, [this is] only for you, excluding the believers. We are aware of what We have made obligatory upon them concerning their wives and those their right hands possess, [so do not be uneasy concerning what you have been commanded to do] and Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse speaks about the ruling on who the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) can marry. It explains that he is allowed to marry the wives he has given dowries to, the female captives that have been given to him, and the daughters of his paternal and maternal uncles and aunts. Additionally, if a believing woman offers herself to the Prophet in marriage, he is allowed to marry her. This verse emphasizes that these rulings are exclusive to the Prophet and are not applicable to other believers. The verse also reassures the Prophet that Allah is aware of the obligations placed upon the believers regarding their spouses and captives, and that He is Forgiving and Merciful.
orig: يا أيها النبي إنا أحللنا لك أزواجك اللاتي آتيت أجورهن وما ملكت يمينك مما أفاء الله عليك وبنات عمك وبنات عماتك وبنات خالك وبنات خالاتك اللاتي هاجرن معك وامرأة مؤمنة إن وهبت نفسها للنبي إن أراد النبي أن يستنكحها خالصة لك من دون المؤمنين قد علمنا ما فرضنا عليهم في أزواجهم وما ملكت أيمانهم لكيلا يكون عليك حرج وكان الله غفورا رحيما

translation: You may defer any one of them you wish, and take to yourself any one you wish, and anyone you desire of those whom you have set aside; no blame shall be upon you. That is more likely that they will not overstrain themselves, and that they will not be grieved, and that they will be content with what you have given them, all of them. And Allah is Knowing of what is in your hearts. And Allah is All-Knowing, Forbearing.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the treatment of wives in the context of polygamy, which was a common practice during the time of the Prophet Muhammad. The verse permits the husband to choose which wife to spend time with, and to set aside others temporarily. The verse emphasizes the importance of treating all wives fairly and justly, and avoiding any actions that may cause them distress or discomfort. The verse encourages the husband to be mindful of his wives' feelings and to be considerate of their needs. The verse is a reminder that Allah is all-knowing and all-aware of the husband's intentions and actions, and that he will be held accountable for his treatment of his wives.
orig: ترجي من تشاء منهن وتؤوي إليك من تشاء ومن ابتغيت ممن عزلت فلا جناح عليك ذلك أدنى أن تقر أعينهن ولا يحزن ويرضين بما آتيتهن كلهن والله يعلم ما في قلوبكم وكان الله عليما حليما

translation: It is not lawful for you (men) to take back any of your gifts (from your wives), except when both parties fear that they would be unable to keep the limits ordained by Allah. And if you fear that they would not be able to keep the limits ordained by Allah, then there is no blame on either of them if she gives something for her freedom. These are the limits ordained by Allah, so do not transgress them. And whoever transgresses the limits ordained by Allah, indeed he has wronged himself.
interpretation: The verse outlines the limits set by Allah regarding the dissolution of marriage. It emphasizes the importance of adhering to these limits and the consequences of transgressing them. The verse permits the return of gifts given to a wife only under specific circumstances where both parties fear that they cannot uphold the limits set by Allah. If this is the case, the wife can give something in exchange for her freedom. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of upholding the limits set by Allah and the seriousness of transgressing them. Those who transgress these limits wrong themselves.
orig: لا يحل لك النساء من بعد ولا أن تبدل بهن من أزواج ولو أعجبك حسنهن إلا ما ملكت يمينك وكان الله على كل شيء رقيبا

translation: O you who have believed, do not enter the Prophet's house except with his permission. Indeed, you are not to touch anything of his. Indeed, that would be greatly displeasing to the Prophet, and he would be harmed by it. Indeed, you have believed in Allah and believed in the Last Day. That has come upon you. And when you ask of them [i.e., the Prophet's wives] anything, ask it of them from behind a partition. That is purer for your hearts and their hearts. And it is not for you to harm the Messenger of Allah or to marry his wives after him ever. Indeed, that would be in the sight of Allah greatly wicked.
interpretation: The verse outlines the rules of conduct for the believers when interacting with the Prophet Muhammad's household. It emphasizes the importance of respecting the Prophet's privacy and avoiding any behavior that may cause him harm or displeasure. The verse encourages believers to ask the Prophet's wives for anything they need from behind a partition, which is described as being pure for both their hearts and the hearts of the Prophet's wives. The verse also forbids believers from marrying the Prophet's wives after his death and stresses the severity of this act in the sight of God. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of respecting the boundaries of the Prophet and his household and the consequences of violating these boundaries.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تدخلوا بيوت النبي إلا أن يؤذن لكم إلى طعام غير ناظرين إناه ولكن إذا دعيتم فادخلوا فإذا طعمتم فانتشروا ولا مستأنسين لحديث إن ذلكم كان يؤذي النبي فيستحيي منكم والله لا يستحيي من الحق وإذا سألتموهن متاعا فاسألوهن من وراء حجاب ذلكم أطهر لقلوبكم وقلوبهن وما كان لكم أن تؤذوا رسول الله ولا أن تنكحوا أزواجه من بعده أبدا إن ذلكم كان عند الله عظيما

translation: If you disclose what you are asked to conceal or rebel, indeed, Allah knows what you do.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the importance of obedience and keeping secrets. It warns against disclosing confidential information or rebelling against authority. The verse emphasizes that God is aware of all actions, both hidden and revealed. The interpretation of this verse is that individuals should be mindful of their actions and avoid disobedience and betrayal, as God has knowledge of everything they do.
orig: إن تبدوا شيئا أو تخفوه فإن الله كان بكل شيء عليما

translation: There is no blame upon them concerning their fathers, or their sons, or their brothers, or their brothers' sons, or their sisters' sons, or their women, or what their right hands possess. But fear Allah. Indeed, Allah is ever, over all things, a Witness.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the absolution of women from any blame regarding their relatives, property, or slaves. It emphasizes the importance of fearing God and being mindful of His presence in all actions. The verse serves as a reminder that God is all-seeing and all-knowing and that all actions, even those that may seem insignificant or private, will be accounted for. It also highlights the importance of treating relatives, slaves, and women with fairness and respect, and not holding any blame or grudges against them.
orig: لا جناح عليهن في آبائهن ولا أبنائهن ولا إخوانهن ولا أبناء إخوانهن ولا أبناء أخواتهن ولا نسائهن ولا ما ملكت أيمانهن واتقين الله إن الله كان على كل شيء شهيدا

translation: Indeed, Allah and His angels send blessings upon the Prophet. O you who have believed, ask blessings upon him and ask for peace upon him.
interpretation: The verse is a command to the believers to send blessings and peace upon the Prophet Muhammad. This act of sending blessings and peace upon the Prophet is highly recommended and meritorious in Islam. It is a way of expressing love, respect, and devotion towards the Prophet. By sending blessings upon the Prophet, Muslims are also seeking Allah's blessings and mercy. This verse emphasizes the importance of showing respect and reverence towards the Prophet Muhammad and the significance of seeking Allah's blessings through his intercession.
orig: إن الله وملائكته يصلون على النبي يا أيها الذين آمنوا صلوا عليه وسلموا تسليما

translation: Indeed, those who harm Allah and His Messenger - Allah has cursed them in this world and the Hereafter and prepared for them a humiliating punishment.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the severe consequences for those who harm Allah and His Messenger. The verse mentions that Allah has cursed such people in both this world and the Hereafter and has prepared a humiliating punishment for them. The verse serves as a warning to those who may harm or disrespect Allah or His Messenger, emphasizing the severe consequences of such actions and the certainty of Allah's punishment.
orig: إن الذين يؤذون الله ورسوله لعنهم الله في الدنيا والآخرة وأعد لهم عذابا مهينا

translation: And those who harm believers, men or women, without having earned it, they have certainly burdened themselves with a clear sin and a manifest transgression.
interpretation: The verse highlights the prohibition of harming believers, whether they are men or women, without justification. Those who commit such acts of harm have loaded upon themselves a clear sin and a manifest transgression. The verse emphasizes the severity of the offense and the consequences of committing it. It serves as a reminder to treat all people with respect, fairness, and justice, regardless of their gender or beliefs.
orig: والذين يؤذون المؤمنين والمؤمنات بغير ما اكتسبوا فقد احتملوا بهتانا وإثما مبينا

translation: O Prophet, tell your wives and your daughters and the women of the believers to bring down over themselves [part] of their outer garments. That is more suitable that they will be known and not be abused. And ever is Allah Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: The verse instructs the Prophet Muhammad to tell the women of his household and the female believers to wear a part of their outer garments over themselves. This is to ensure that they are recognized as modest and pious women and are not harmed or bothered. The verse emphasizes the importance of modesty and protection for women, and the role of the community in upholding these values. It also highlights the compassionate and merciful nature of God, who forgives and shows mercy to those who strive to follow His commands.
orig: يا أيها النبي قل لأزواجك وبناتك ونساء المؤمنين يدنين عليهن من جلابيبهن ذلك أدنى أن يعرفن فلا يؤذين وكان الله غفورا رحيما

translation: If the hypocrites and those in whose hearts is a disease, and the alarmists in the city do not desist, We shall certainly let you overpower them, then they will not remain your neighbors in it except for a little.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the punishment of the hypocrites, those with illness in their hearts, and the alarmists in the city who do not desist from their wrongdoings. The verse promises that they will be overpowered and will not remain as neighbors for long. The verse serves as a warning to those who engage in hypocrisy and sow discord, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: لئن لم ينته المنافقون والذين في قلوبهم مرض والمرجفون في المدينة لنغرينك بهم ثم لا يجاورونك فيها إلا قليلا

translation: Cursed, wherever they are found, they are seized and killed
interpretation: The verse speaks about the fate of those who are cursed, and are found and seized wherever they are. The punishment for these individuals is death, as they are killed after being seized. This verse may serve as a warning to those who engage in harmful or dangerous behaviors, emphasizing the severe consequences of their actions. Additionally, the verse highlights the all-encompassing power of God, who is able to find and punish those who do wrong, no matter where they are hiding.
orig: ملعونين أينما ثقفوا أخذوا وقتلوا تقتيلا

translation: The way (or custom) of Allah is that which has passed away before (in the case) of those who have passed away. And you will not find a change in the way (or custom) of Allah.
interpretation: The verse affirms that the way or custom of God in dealing with past nations and civilizations will also be applied to those who are currently alive. The verse emphasizes the unchanging nature of God's way and the inevitability of its application. The verse serves as a reminder of the consistency of God's justice and the importance of adhering to His commands and avoiding His prohibitions.
orig: سنة الله في الذين خلوا من قبل ولن تجد لسنة الله تبديلا

translation: People ask you about the Hour (of Judgment). Say: The knowledge of it is only with Allah. And what may make you perceive? Perhaps the Hour is near.
interpretation: The verse speaks about people asking the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) about the Hour (of Judgment Day). The verse emphasizes that only God has the knowledge of when the Hour will take place. The verse also suggests that the Hour might be near, encouraging people to be prepared and vigilant, and to always be mindful of their actions and their relationship with God.
orig: يسألك الناس عن الساعة قل إنما علمها عند الله وما يدريك لعل الساعة تكون قريبا

translation: Indeed, Allah has cursed the disbelievers and has prepared for them a Blaze.
interpretation: The verse states that Allah has cursed the disbelievers and has prepared a severe punishment for them in the form of a blazing fire. The curse of Allah is a serious matter and serves as a warning to those who reject faith and persist in their disbelief. The blaze or fire is a metaphor for the intense and unbearable suffering that awaits the disbelievers in the afterlife. The verse emphasizes the certainty of the punishment and the severity of the consequences of disbelief.
orig: إن الله لعن الكافرين وأعد لهم سعيرا

translation: They will abide therein forever, they will find no protector or helper for themselves there.
interpretation: The verse describes the fate of certain people who will be condemned to dwell in a place where they will not find any protection or help. This is a reference to the punishment of hell, where the disbelievers will be cast for eternity. The verse emphasizes the isolation and helplessness of these people, who will be left to suffer the consequences of their actions without any hope of escape or relief. The verse serves as a warning to those who reject the message of Islam, reminding them of the severe consequences of their rejection and the importance of seeking God's protection and guidance.
orig: خالدين فيها أبدا لا يجدون وليا ولا نصيرا

translation: The Day their faces will be turned over in the Fire, they will say, 'Oh, if only we had obeyed Allah and obeyed the Messenger.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the Day of Judgment, when the faces of the disbelievers will be turned over in the Fire. Overwhelmed by regret, they will express their remorse for not having obeyed God and His Messenger. The verse highlights the importance of obedience and submission to God and His Messenger, emphasizing the dire consequences of disobedience and rejection of God's message.
orig: يوم تقلب وجوههم في النار يقولون يا ليتنا أطعنا الله وأطعنا الرسولا

translation: And they said, 'Our Lord, we have obeyed our leaders and the elders, and they have led us astray from the way.'
interpretation: The verse describes a group of people who acknowledge their mistake and express remorse for following their leaders and elders who led them astray from the right path. The verse highlights the dangers of blindly following authority figures without questioning their actions and decisions, and the consequences of deviating from the right path. The verse serves as a reminder to be cautious and discerning in choosing one's role models and to always seek guidance from God in making decisions.
orig: وقالوا ربنا إنا أطعنا سادتنا وكبراءنا فأضلونا السبيلا

translation: Our Lord, pour out upon them a punishment double and curse them with a great curse.
interpretation: The verse is a supplication by the believers, asking God to punish the disbelievers with a double punishment and to curse them greatly. The verse highlights the intense enmity and conflict between the believers and the disbelievers, and the believers' desire for God's justice and vengeance. It also emphasizes the severity of the punishment that the disbelievers will face, as well as the magnitude of their curse. The verse serves as a reminder of the ultimate fate of those who reject God's message, and the importance of holding firm to one's faith and belief in the face of adversity.
orig: ربنا آتهم ضعفين من العذاب والعنهم لعنا كبيرا

translation: O you who have believed, be not like those who wronged Moses and then God cleared him of what they had said, and thereupon they were struck with regret.
interpretation: The verse warns the believers not to be like those who wronged Moses and then regretted it when God cleared him of the false accusations they had made. The verse emphasizes the importance of treating prophets with respect and avoiding actions that may lead to regret and punishment from God. It serves as a reminder that God is aware of all that is said and done, and will ultimately vindicate the innocent and punish the wrongdoers.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تكونوا كالذين آذوا موسى فبرأه الله مما قالوا وكان عند الله وجيها

translation: O you who have believed, fear Allah and speak words of appropriate righteousness.
interpretation: The verse is a command to the believers to fear and revere Allah, and to always speak words that are righteous and just. This verse emphasizes the importance of speech and the need for it to be truthful, kind, and just. It serves as a reminder that our words have power and can have a profound impact on others. By urging the believers to speak words of appropriate righteousness, the verse encourages them to cultivate a disposition of mindfulness and consciousness of Allah in all their actions and interactions, and to strive for righteousness and justice in all aspects of their lives.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا اتقوا الله وقولوا قولا سديدا

translation: He will set your deeds right for you and forgive you your sins. And whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger, He will admit him to gardens beneath which rivers flow, to abide in them; and that is the great success.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the mercy and forgiveness of God towards those who obey Him and His messenger. The verse emphasizes the great reward that awaits those who follow God's commandments, which is to be admitted to gardens beneath which rivers flow, indicating eternal paradise. The verse serves as an incentive for believers to obey God and His messenger, and to strive for righteousness, as it leads to the ultimate success and happiness.
orig: يصلح لكم أعمالكم ويغفر لكم ذنوبكم ومن يطع الله ورسوله فقد فاز فوزا عظيما

translation: Indeed, we offered the trust to the heavens and the earth and the mountains, but they refused to bear it, and were afraid of it; and man assumed it; indeed, he has always been, to his detriment, ignorant and unjust.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the trust (or responsibility) that was offered to the heavens, the earth, and the mountains, but they all refused to bear it. This trust was then taken up by man, who was ignorant and unjust. The verse highlights the rejection of the responsibility by the heavens, the earth, and the mountains, which emphasizes the magnitude of the trust and the unworthiness of man to bear it. The verse serves as a reminder of the trust that was given to humans and the consequences of not fulfilling it, due to their ignorance and injustice.
orig: إنا عرضنا الأمانة على السماوات والأرض والجبال فأبين أن يحملنها وأشفقن منها وحملها الإنسان إنه كان ظلوما جهولا

translation: To punish the hypocrites, men and women, and the idolaters, men and women, and to accept the repentance of the believers, men and women, and God is oft-forgiving, merciful.
interpretation: The verse describes the consequences for different groups of people: hypocrites, idolaters, and believers. The hypocrites and idolaters, both men and women, will be punished by God, while the believers, men and women, will have their repentance accepted by God. The verse emphasizes the just nature of God, who punishes the wrongdoers and forgives those who repent. It serves as a reminder of the importance of true faith and sincerity, and the consequences of hypocrisy and idolatry.
orig: ليعذب الله المنافقين والمنافقات والمشركين والمشركات ويتوب الله على المؤمنين والمؤمنات وكان الله غفورا رحيما

translation: All praise is for Allah, to Whom belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth, and to Him is the praise in the Hereafter. And He is the Wise, the Aware.
interpretation: The verse is a praise of Allah, acknowledging His ownership and control over all of the creation, both in this world and in the Hereafter. The verse emphasizes Allah's complete power and knowledge over all things, and it serves as a reminder of the ultimate reality that all praise and gratitude belong to Him. The verse encourages the believers to be mindful of Allah's presence and greatness in all aspects of their lives, and to always express their gratitude and appreciation towards Him.
orig: الحمد لله الذي له ما في السماوات وما في الأرض وله الحمد في الآخرة وهو الحكيم الخبير

translation: He knows that which goes into the earth and that which comes out of it, and that which descends from the heaven and that which ascends to it. And He is the Merciful, the Forgiving.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes God's knowledge and power over all things, both on earth and in heaven. It highlights God's omniscience, as He knows all that enters the earth and all that emerges from it, as well as all that descends from the heavens and all that ascends to it. The verse further emphasizes God's attributes of mercy and forgiveness, reminding the reader of God's compassion and willingness to forgive those who turn to Him in repentance.
orig: يعلم ما يلج في الأرض وما يخرج منها وما ينزل من السماء وما يعرج فيها وهو الرحيم الغفور

translation: And those who disbelieved say, 'The Hour will not come upon us.' Say, 'Yes, by my Lord, it will indeed come upon you. The Knower of the unseen, not even the weight of a speck of dust in the heavens or the earth escapes from Him, nor is there anything smaller or greater, but (it is) in a clear record.
interpretation: The verse addresses the disbelievers who deny the coming of the Hour (Day of Judgment). The speaker, who is believed to be the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), asserts that the Hour will certainly come, and it is a promise from his Lord. The verse emphasizes God's knowledge of the unseen and His power over all things, big or small. The reference to the weight of a speck of dust in the heavens or the earth highlights God's infinite knowledge and control over every detail of the universe. The verse also mentions a clear record, which implies that every deed, word, and thought of human beings is being recorded and will be presented on the Day of Judgment. The verse is a warning to the disbelievers and a reminder of God's power and justice.
orig: وقال الذين كفروا لا تأتينا الساعة قل بلى وربي لتأتينكم عالم الغيب لا يعزب عنه مثقال ذرة في السماوات ولا في الأرض ولا أصغر من ذلك ولا أكبر إلا في كتاب مبين

translation: For those who believe and do good deeds, their reward is forgiveness and a generous provision.
interpretation: The verse highlights the reward for those who have faith in God and do good deeds. Such individuals will receive forgiveness for their sins and a generous provision in this world and the hereafter. The verse emphasizes the importance of both faith and good deeds in earning God's pleasure and reward, and serves as a source of motivation for believers to strive for righteousness and piety in their daily lives.
orig: ليجزي الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات أولئك لهم مغفرة ورزق كريم

translation: And those who strive against Our signs, seeking to discredit them, they will bear a painful punishment.
interpretation: The verse speaks about those who reject and oppose the signs or revelations of God, trying to discredit or disprove them. The verse warns that these people will face a painful punishment for their actions. The verse emphasizes the importance of accepting and submitting to the signs of God, and the consequences of rejecting them.
orig: والذين سعوا في آياتنا معاجزين أولئك لهم عذاب من رجز أليم

translation: And those who have been given knowledge see that what has been revealed to you from your Lord is the truth, and it guides to the path of the Exalted in Might, the Praiseworthy.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the people who have knowledge and can recognize the truth of what has been revealed to the Prophet Muhammad from the Lord. This knowledge guides them to the path of the Exalted in Might, the Praiseworthy, which refers to God. The verse emphasizes the importance of knowledge and its role in guiding people to the right path, and the ultimate goal of reaching God through this path.
orig: ويرى الذين أوتوا العلم الذي أنزل إليك من ربك هو الحق ويهدي إلى صراط العزيز الحميد

translation: And those who disbelieved said: 'Shall we show you a man who will inform you (when) you are scattered in pieces (after death), that you will be (raised) in a new creation?'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the disbelievers rejecting the message of the prophet and mocking the idea of resurrection. They ask if they will be shown a man who can inform them of their fate after death, implying that they do not believe in the possibility of life after death. The verse highlights the rejection and disbelief of those who refuse to accept the message of the prophet and the concept of resurrection, and serves as a reminder of the consequences of disbelief and the reality of the afterlife.
orig: وقال الذين كفروا هل ندلكم على رجل ينبئكم إذا مزقتم كل ممزق إنكم لفي خلق جديد

translation: Then have I told a lie about Allah, or is there in Him untruth? But those who disbelieve in the Hereafter and are constant in disobedience to Allah - from them is far off (the requirement of) every good thing.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the falsehood and rejection of those who do not believe in the Hereafter and are persistent in disobedience of God. The verse emphasizes the distance and separation of these disbelievers from every good thing. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of faith in the Hereafter and the consequences of disbelief and disobedience towards God.
orig: أفترى على الله كذبا أم به جنة بل الذين لا يؤمنون بالآخرة في العذاب والضلال البعيد

translation: Have they not seen what is before them and behind them, of the sky and the earth? If We will, We can make the earth swallow them or let a piece of the sky fall upon them. Indeed, in that is a sign for every servant who turns (to God).
interpretation: The verse reminds people of the signs of God's power and control over the universe, which are evident in the natural world around them. The verse mentions the possibility of the earth swallowing people or a piece of the sky falling upon them, as a reminder of the fragility of human existence and the overwhelming power of God. The verse is a call to those who are willing to turn to God and recognize His signs, and a warning to those who ignore them.
orig: أفلم يروا إلى ما بين أيديهم وما خلفهم من السماء والأرض إن نشأ نخسف بهم الأرض أو نسقط عليهم كسفا من السماء إن في ذلك لآية لكل عبد منيب

translation: And We had certainly given to David from Us grace, O mountains, repeat with him and the birds, and We made for him iron.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the blessings that God had given to David. The verse specifically mentions the mountains and the birds, indicating that they were also part of the blessings and that they were made to glorify God along with David. The verse also mentions the giving of iron, which could be interpreted as a symbol of strength and power, and a tool for David to use in his service to God. The verse serves as a reminder of the blessings that God bestows upon His servants, and the role of these blessings in serving God and fulfilling His will.
orig: ولقد آتينا داوود منا فضلا يا جبال أوبي معه والطير وألنا له الحديد

translation: And strive as in a race in good deeds. And worship your Lord until certainty (i.e. death) comes to you.
interpretation: The verse encourages believers to strive hard and compete with each other in performing good deeds, emphasizing the importance of good actions in the life of a believer. The verse also commands believers to worship their Lord until the certainty of death comes to them, indicating that worship should continue until the very end of one's life. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of striving for righteousness and the continuity of worship in the life of a believer.
orig: أن اعمل سابغات وقدر في السرد واعملوا صالحا إني بما تعملون بصير

translation: And to Solomon (We subjected) the wind, whose morning course was a month's journey and whose afternoon course was a month's journey, and We caused a fount of molten copper to gush forth for him, and there were among the jinn some who worked before him by the leave of his Lord. And whoever of them turned aside from Our command, We let him taste of the punishment of the Blaze.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the power and blessings bestowed upon Prophet Solomon by God. It highlights the subjugation of the wind for Solomon's use, with its morning and afternoon course each being a month's journey. The verse also mentions the gushing forth of a fount of molten copper for Solomon and the help of some obedient jinns at his service. However, it also warns that anyone among the jinn who disobeys God's command will be punished. The verse serves as a reminder of God's power and control over all creation, and the consequences of disobedience towards Him.
orig: ولسليمان الريح غدوها شهر ورواحها شهر وأسلنا له عين القطر ومن الجن من يعمل بين يديه بإذن ربه ومن يزغ منهم عن أمرنا نذقه من عذاب السعير

translation: They made for Him what He wills of sanctuaries, images, and devices as mere comfort for the heart, even though He has no need of them. Rather, it is you who are in need. So, [O Muhammad], say, 'Praise be to God. He will surely show you His signs, and you will recognize them. And your Lord is not unaware of what you do.'
interpretation: The verse criticizes the people for creating images and sanctuaries for God, which are unnecessary and only serve as a comfort for their hearts. The verse emphasizes that God has no need for these creations, and it is actually the people who are in need of God's mercy and forgiveness. The verse ends with a command for the Prophet Muhammad to praise God and recognize His signs, reminding the people that God is aware of their actions and will hold them accountable for them.
orig: يعملون له ما يشاء من محاريب وتماثيل وجفان كالجواب وقدور راسيات اعملوا آل داوود شكرا وقليل من عبادي الشكور

translation: But when death comes to one of them, they say: 'Send someone else to look after us.' On the Day of Resurrection, We shall ask them: 'Was it not you who used to swear that you would never be unfaithful to us?'
interpretation: This verse describes the attitude of certain people towards death and their reluctance to accept it. When death approaches, they ask others to take their place, showing their unwillingness to face it. On the Day of Judgment, God will remind them of their previous denials and false promises, highlighting the inconsistency and insincerity of their actions. The verse serves as a reminder of the inevitability of death and the importance of being truthful and consistent in our beliefs and actions.
orig: فلما قضينا عليه الموت ما دلهم على موته إلا دابة الأرض تأكل منسأته فلما خر تبينت الجن أن لو كانوا يعلمون الغيب ما لبثوا في العذاب المهين

translation: Indeed, for a disobedient people there was a sign in their livestock: two types of cattle, one suckling and one not. Eat from the provision of your Lord, and give thanks to Him. Good land, and a forgiving Lord.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the blessings that God has given to people in the form of livestock, which serves as a sign for a disobedient people. The verse mentions two types of cattle, one that is still suckling and one that is not, emphasizing the abundance of provision from God. The people are instructed to eat from the provision of their Lord and give thanks to Him. The verse also highlights the goodness of the land and the forgiving nature of God, emphasizing the importance of gratitude and appreciation for the blessings that one has received.
orig: لقد كان لسبإ في مسكنهم آية جنتان عن يمين وشمال كلوا من رزق ربكم واشكروا له بلدة طيبة ورب غفور

translation: So turn away from them and wait. We will, soon, let them taste a painful punishment, then We will surely deliver you against them, and they will not harm you. And Allah has promised those who have believed among you and done righteous deeds that He will surely grant them succession [to authority] upon the earth just as He granted it to those before them and that He will surely establish for them [therein] their religion which He has preferred for them and that He will surely substitute for them, after their fear, security, [for] they worship Me, not associating anything with Me. But whoever disbelieves after that - then those are the defiantly disobedient.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the command for the believers to turn away from the unjust and wait for God's punishment. The verse emphasizes that the punishment will be painful and that God will ultimately grant succession and establish the religion of the believers. The verse serves as a reminder that God's promise of succession and security will only be granted to those who believe and do righteous deeds, and that those who disbelieve after that will be the defiantly disobedient.
orig: فأعرضوا فأرسلنا عليهم سيل العرم وبدلناهم بجنتيهم جنتين ذواتي أكل خمط وأثل وشيء من سدر قليل

translation: That is the recompense of them who deny (Allah's) signs, and they are rejecters of the truth.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the consequence of those who deny the signs of Allah and reject the truth. The verse establishes a clear cause-and-effect relationship between their denial and rejection, and the punishment they receive. The verse serves as a reminder that those who persist in denying the truth and rejecting Allah's signs will ultimately be held accountable for their actions and receive a fitting punishment.
