orig: ذلك جزيناهم بما كفروا وهل نجازي إلا الكفور

translation: And We have made between them and the towns which We have blessed visible towns, and We have appointed the stages between them: 'Travel in them by night and day, securely.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the arrangement of towns and the paths between them, indicating that God has made some towns visible and accessible for travel. The verse emphasizes the safety and security of travelers, encouraging them to journey through these towns during both night and day. The verse can be interpreted as a symbol of the blessings and provisions that God has provided for humanity, and the ease with which people can access these blessings if they follow the path that God has set out for them.
orig: وجعلنا بينهم وبين القرى التي باركنا فيها قرى ظاهرة وقدرنا فيها السير سيروا فيها ليالي وأياما آمنين

translation: They said, 'Our Lord, put between our journeys distance, and they wronged themselves.' So We made them stories and scattered them completely. Indeed, in that are signs for every patient, grateful one.
interpretation: The verse speaks about a group of people who wronged themselves and asked their Lord to put distance between their journeys. As a result, they were made into stories (i.e., forgotten) and scattered completely. The verse highlights the consequences of their actions and the fact that they wronged themselves. The verse also emphasizes the importance of patience and gratitude for those who seek to understand the signs of God. The verse serves as a reminder that God's decisions and actions are just and that those who are patient and grateful will be able to understand and learn from the signs of God.
orig: فقالوا ربنا باعد بين أسفارنا وظلموا أنفسهم فجعلناهم أحاديث ومزقناهم كل ممزق إن في ذلك لآيات لكل صبار شكور

translation: And indeed, Satan whispered to them, so he made their deeds seem appealing to them. But he did not mislead except a group of the disbelievers.
interpretation: The verse speaks about Satan's deception of some people, causing them to follow his ways and leading them astray. Despite his efforts, only a group of disbelievers were misled, while the believers remained steadfast in their faith. This verse serves as a reminder that Satan will always try to lead people away from the truth and that it is up to the individual to resist his temptations and remain firm in their faith. It also highlights the importance of staying vigilant against Satan's schemes and not being swayed by his deceitful ways.
orig: ولقد صدق عليهم إبليس ظنه فاتبعوه إلا فريقا من المؤمنين

translation: And he (Solomon) had no power over them (the wind and the devils) except that it was a mercy from Us. And he was truly worthy of Our praise, and was among those who submit (to Our will). And your Lord is Guardian over all things.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the power of Solomon over the wind and the devils, which was given to him as a mercy from God. The verse emphasizes that Solomon was truly worthy of God's praise and was among those who submit to God's will. The verse also reminds the reader that God is the ultimate Guardian over all things, and that Solomon's power was given to him by God and was subject to God's will.
orig: وما كان له عليهم من سلطان إلا لنعلم من يؤمن بالآخرة ممن هو منها في شك وربك على كل شيء حفيظ

translation: Say, 'Call upon those whom you claim (to be gods) besides Allah. They do not possess an atom's weight in the heavens or on the earth, nor do they have any share in either, nor is there for Him any supporter from among them.'
interpretation: The verse is a challenge from the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to the disbelievers to call upon their gods and seek their help. The verse emphasizes the powerlessness and impotence of these so-called gods, who are unable to control even an atom's weight in the heavens or on the earth. The verse also highlights the fact that these gods have no share or partnership in the creation or management of the universe, and that they cannot provide any support or assistance to their followers. The verse serves to refute the claims of the disbelievers and to establish the oneness and uniqueness of Allah, the only true God, who has power and control over all things.
orig: قل ادعوا الذين زعمتم من دون الله لا يملكون مثقال ذرة في السماوات ولا في الأرض وما لهم فيهما من شرك وما له منهم من ظهير

translation: And no intercession will benefit at all those who do wrong; theirs will be a painful punishment, except for those who repent and believe and do righteous deeds; for them, God will change their evil deeds into good ones. And ever is God Forgiving, Merciful.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the fate of those who commit wrongdoing and the futility of intercession on their behalf. It emphasizes the severe punishment that awaits them. However, the verse also provides hope for those who repent, believe, and do good deeds. For them, God will replace their evil deeds with good ones, highlighting God's forgiveness and mercy towards those who turn back to Him. The verse serves as a warning to those who persist in wrongdoing, while also offering a message of hope and redemption for those who choose to change their ways.
orig: ولا تنفع الشفاعة عنده إلا لمن أذن له حتى إذا فزع عن قلوبهم قالوا ماذا قال ربكم قالوا الحق وهو العلي الكبير

translation: Say, 'Who provides for you from the sky and the earth? Say, 'It is Allah, and either we or you are upon guidance or in clear error.'
interpretation: The verse is a challenge to consider the source of sustenance and provision in life. The question, 'Who provides for you from the sky and the earth?' is posed, and the answer is given, 'It is Allah.' The verse then presents a division between two groups: those who are upon guidance and those who are in clear error. The speaker, identified as 'we' in the verse, aligns themselves with the group of those upon guidance, and implies that the other group, 'you', are in clear error. The verse can be interpreted as a call for reflection and a reminder of the importance of recognizing and acknowledging the source of provision and guidance in life.
orig: قل من يرزقكم من السماوات والأرض قل الله وإنا أو إياكم لعلى هدى أو في ضلال مبين

translation: Say, 'Do not ask about what We have done, nor should We ask about what you do.'
interpretation: The verse is a command from God to the Prophet Muhammad to tell the people not to ask about the fate of those who have been punished by God, nor should they question God's actions. Similarly, the people should not expect the Prophet to ask about their deeds. The verse emphasizes the division between the actions of God and the actions of humans, and the importance of focusing on one's own actions and accountability before God. The verse serves as a reminder that God is the ultimate judge and that humans should not question His decisions or judgments.
orig: قل لا تسألون عما أجرمنا ولا نسأل عما تعملون

translation: Say, 'Our Lord will bring us together then He will judge between us with truth. And He is the Knowing Judge.'
interpretation: The verse is a command to the Prophet Muhammad to say that God will gather all people on the Day of Judgment and will judge between them with truth and justice. The verse emphasizes God's omniscience and His ability to discern the truth. It serves as a reminder that all people will be held accountable for their actions and that God's judgment is the ultimate and final resolution of all disputes.
orig: قل يجمع بيننا ربنا ثم يفتح بيننا بالحق وهو الفتاح العليم

translation: Say, 'Show me those you have associated with Him as partners. Indeed, He - He is Allah, the Exalted in Might, the Wise.'
interpretation: The verse is a challenge from the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to the polytheists and idol-worshippers to show and prove the existence and power of their so-called deities and partners of God. The verse emphatically affirms that there is only one God, Allah, who is the Exalted in Might and the Wise, and that no one else has any share in His divinity or power. The verse is a call to monotheism and a rejection of polytheism and idolatry. It also highlights the futility and falsehood of associating partners with Allah and the ultimate power and wisdom of Allah.
orig: قل أروني الذين ألحقتم به شركاء كلا بل هو الله العزيز الحكيم

translation: And We have not sent you, [O Muhammad], except as a mercy to the worlds. But most of the people do not know.
interpretation: The verse highlights the role of the Prophet Muhammad as a mercy to all of humanity. It emphasizes that the Prophet was not sent for a specific group of people, but for the benefit of all. However, the verse also points out that most people are unaware of this, indicating a lack of understanding or appreciation for the Prophet's mission. This verse serves as a reminder of the universal nature of the Prophet's message and the importance of recognizing and accepting it.
orig: وما أرسلناك إلا كافة للناس بشيرا ونذيرا ولكن أكثر الناس لا يعلمون

translation: And they say, 'When will this promise be (fulfilled), if you are truthful?'
interpretation: The verse is a quote from the disbelievers who are questioning the promise of God and doubting the truthfulness of the prophets. They are asking when the promise of punishment or the day of judgment will come. The verse highlights the rejection and disbelief of those who refuse to accept the message of the prophets and the warning of the consequences of their actions. It serves as a reminder of the importance of faith and the certainty of God's promise.
orig: ويقولون متى هذا الوعد إن كنتم صادقين

translation: Say to them: 'The promise of a Day which you cannot delay for a single hour nor bring forward.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about a promise from God of a Day (Judgment Day) that cannot be delayed or hastened. The verse emphasizes the inevitability of this Day and the inability of humans to change its appointed time. The verse serves as a reminder of the power of God, and the insignificance of human beings in comparison. It also stresses the importance of being prepared for this Day at all times, as it can come at any moment without warning.
orig: قل لكم ميعاد يوم لا تستأخرون عنه ساعة ولا تستقدمون

translation: And those who disbelieved say, 'We will never believe in this Qur'an and what is before it.' Even if you see the unjust (people) standing before their Lord, (they will still not believe), some of them listening (to the punishment) to others. The unjust will say to the arrogant, 'If only you had been (submissive) with us, we would indeed have been believers.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the disbelievers' rejection of the Qur'an and what was revealed before it. Despite the clear signs and evidence, they refuse to believe. The verse describes the punishment of the unjust on the Day of Judgment, where they will stand before their Lord and witness the consequences of their actions. The verse highlights the regret of the unjust, who will acknowledge the truth and wish they had followed the right path. The verse serves as a reminder of the consequences of disbelief and the importance of submission to God's guidance.
orig: وقال الذين كفروا لن نؤمن بهذا القرآن ولا بالذي بين يديه ولو ترى إذ الظالمون موقوفون عند ربهم يرجع بعضهم إلى بعض القول يقول الذين استضعفوا للذين استكبروا لولا أنتم لكنا مؤمنين

translation: Those who are proud say to those who were oppressed, 'We will drive you back!' But they had no recourse! They were the ones who were unjust.
interpretation: The verse describes a confrontation between two groups of people: those who are proud and powerful, and those who are oppressed and weak. The proud group threatens to drive the oppressed group back, but the verse makes it clear that the oppressed group has no means of defending themselves. The proud group is characterized as unjust, emphasizing the unrighteousness of their actions. The verse serves as a warning against arrogance and oppression, and highlights the importance of treating all people with justice and fairness.
orig: قال الذين استكبروا للذين استضعفوا أنحن صددناكم عن الهدى بعد إذ جاءكم بل كنتم مجرمين

translation: And those who were weak said to those who were arrogant among them, 'Truly,
interpretation: No interpretation
orig: وقال الذين استضعفوا للذين استكبروا بل مكر الليل والنهار إذ تأمروننا أن نكفر بالله ونجعل له أندادا وأسروا الندامة لما رأوا العذاب وجعلنا الأغلال في أعناق الذين كفروا هل يجزون إلا ما كانوا يعملون

translation: And We never sent a warner to a town except that the wealthy among them said, 'Indeed, we are disbelievers in what you have been sent with.'
interpretation: The verse highlights the common response of the wealthy and powerful members of a society to the message of a warner or prophet sent by God. Instead of heeding the warning and repenting, they reject the message and deny the truth of the prophet's claims. This attitude of arrogance and disbelief is often driven by a sense of entitlement and a desire to maintain their wealth and status. The verse serves as a reminder that God's message is intended for all people, regardless of their social or economic status, and that those who reject the message will face consequences for their disbelief.
orig: وما أرسلنا في قرية من نذير إلا قال مترفوها إنا بما أرسلتم به كافرون

translation: And they say, 'We have more wealth and children, and we are not going to be punished.'
interpretation: The verse describes the attitude of some people who are arrogant and boastful about their wealth and children, and who believe that they are not accountable for their actions and will not be punished for any wrongdoing. The verse challenges this false sense of security and reminds the reader that no one is exempt from God's judgment and that wealth and children are not a guarantee of protection from punishment.
orig: وقالوا نحن أكثر أموالا وأولادا وما نحن بمعذبين

translation: Say, 'Indeed, my Lord expands provision for whom He wills and restricts [it] but most of the people do not know.'
interpretation: The verse highlights the power and control of God in providing sustenance for His creations. It emphasizes that God gives provision to whom He wills and withholds it from whom He wills, and this is something that most people are not aware of. The verse can be seen as a reminder of the ultimate power and control of God, and the limitations of human control and understanding. It also encourages the acceptance of God's will and destiny, and the understanding that all provision comes from God.
orig: قل إن ربي يبسط الرزق لمن يشاء ويقدر ولكن أكثر الناس لا يعلمون

translation: And neither your wealth nor your children will bring you nearer to Us, except for him who believes and does righteousness; such are those who receive their reward with their Lord, and they will have their provision in abundance.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of faith and righteous deeds in gaining nearness to God, and downplays the significance of material wealth and lineage. The verse makes it clear that these worldly possessions will not benefit a person on the Day of Judgment, unless they are accompanied by faith and good deeds. The verse promises a great reward and provision in abundance for those who believe and do good deeds. It serves as a reminder to people not to place their trust in material wealth and to focus on cultivating faith and righteousness, which are the only things that will truly benefit them in the hereafter.
orig: وما أموالكم ولا أولادكم بالتي تقربكم عندنا زلفى إلا من آمن وعمل صالحا فأولئك لهم جزاء الضعف بما عملوا وهم في الغرفات آمنون

translation: And those who strive to frustrate Our Signs, they will surely be companions of the Fire.
interpretation: The verse warns of the consequences of rejecting or trying to frustrate the signs or messages of God. Those who engage in such behavior will be punished and will reside in the fire. The verse emphasizes the importance of accepting and understanding the signs of God, and the serious consequences of rejecting them.
orig: والذين يسعون في آياتنا معاجزين أولئك في العذاب محضرون

translation: Say, 'Indeed, my Lord extends provision for whom He wills of His servants and restricts it [for whom He wills]. And whatever you spend of anything, He replaces it. And He is the best of providers.'
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the power and control that God has over the provision of sustenance for His servants. God extends provision for whom He wills and restricts it for whom He wills. This highlights the idea that all provision comes from God and that He is the ultimate provider. The second part of the verse speaks to the concept of giving and charity, stating that whatever is spent will be replaced by God. This serves as a reminder of the blessings that come from giving and the idea that God will always provide for those who are generous. Overall, the verse emphasizes the power and control of God over all aspects of life, including the provision of sustenance and the blessings that come from giving and charity.
orig: قل إن ربي يبسط الرزق لمن يشاء من عباده ويقدر له وما أنفقتم من شيء فهو يخلفه وهو خير الرازقين

translation: And (the day) when He will gather them all together, then He will say to the angels, 'Did these (people) used to worship you?',
interpretation: The verse describes the Day of Judgment, when all people will be gathered together before God. God will ask the angels if the people used to worship them, emphasizing the powerlessness and insignificance of the false gods and idols that people worshiped in their earthly lives. The verse serves as a reminder of the futility of worshiping anything other than God and the certainty of the Day of Judgment, when all will be held accountable for their actions and beliefs.
orig: ويوم يحشرهم جميعا ثم يقول للملائكة أهؤلاء إياكم كانوا يعبدون

translation: They said, 'Exalted are You, we have no refuge from them except in You.' Rather, they were worshipping the jinn, most of them were believers in them.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the rejection of the idol worshippers when they were called to worship Allah alone. When they were asked to reject their false deities, they acknowledged Allah's greatness and power, and admitted that they had no refuge from Him. However, they were still attached to their false beliefs and practices, and the verse reveals that most of them were worshippers of the jinn. The verse highlights the misguidance of the idol worshippers and their rejection of the truth, and emphasizes the importance of worshipping Allah alone and rejecting all forms of false deities.
orig: قالوا سبحانك أنت ولينا من دونهم بل كانوا يعبدون الجن أكثرهم بهم مؤمنون

translation: Today no soul has power over another soul, nor does any soul have power over what is wrongfully earned. And We will say to those who have transgressed, 'Taste the punishment of the Fire which you used to deny.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the Day of Judgment and the powerlessness of human beings in the face of God's judgment. It emphasizes that no soul will have power over another and that no one will be able to escape the consequences of their actions. The verse specifically addresses those who have transgressed and tells them to 'taste the punishment of the Fire' that they had previously denied. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and transgression, reminding them of the certainty of God's punishment on the Day of Judgment.
orig: فاليوم لا يملك بعضكم لبعض نفعا ولا ضرا ونقول للذين ظلموا ذوقوا عذاب النار التي كنتم بها تكذبون

translation: And when Our verses are recited to them clearly, they say: 'This is only a man who wishes to divert you from what your forefathers used to worship.' And they say: 'This is nothing but a fabricated lie.' And those who disbelieve say of the truth when it comes to them: 'This is nothing but obvious magic.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the disbelievers' reaction when they hear the verses of the Qur'an being recited to them. They reject the message and accuse the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) of trying to divert them from the religion of their forefathers, and of fabricating falsehood. The verse highlights the closed-mindedness and rejection of the truth by those who refuse to accept the message of Islam. It serves as a reminder of the importance of being open-minded and receptive to the truth, and of not letting preconceived notions and biases prevent one from accepting the guidance of Allah.
orig: وإذا تتلى عليهم آياتنا بينات قالوا ما هذا إلا رجل يريد أن يصدكم عما كان يعبد آباؤكم وقالوا ما هذا إلا إفك مفترى وقال الذين كفروا للحق لما جاءهم إن هذا إلا سحر مبين

translation: And We never sent to a town before you [O Muhammad] any warner unless its wealthy ones said, 'Indeed, we found our fathers following a religion, and we will follow in their footsteps.'
interpretation: The verse highlights the resistance of people to accept new prophets and messages from God. The verse mentions that before the Prophet Muhammad, no town was sent a warner without its wealthy and influential members rejecting the message and choosing to follow the religion of their ancestors instead. This verse emphasizes the human tendency to resist change and cling to tradition, even if it means rejecting the truth and continuing in a path of error. The verse serves as a reminder that every prophet faced opposition and rejection, and it encourages the Prophet Muhammad to be patient and persistent in his mission, despite the challenges he faces.
orig: وما آتيناهم من كتب يدرسونها وما أرسلنا إليهم قبلك من نذير

translation: And those before them also disbelieved, and how terrible was My denial for the guilty ones!
interpretation: The verse refers to the disbelief of the people who lived before the time of the Prophet Muhammad. It emphasizes the severity of the punishment that was inflicted upon those who rejected the messages of the prophets. The phrase 'how terrible was My denial for the guilty ones' conveys the idea of a severe and unavoidable punishment for those who persist in their disbelief and wrongdoing. The verse serves as a warning to those who reject the message of Islam, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment for the unbelievers.
orig: وكذب الذين من قبلهم وما بلغوا معشار ما آتيناهم فكذبوا رسلي فكيف كان نكير

translation: Say, 'I only warn you of one thing: that you stand up for the sake of Allah - in pairs and individually - then reflect: there is no doubt about your companion [i.e., the Prophet Muhammad] being a warner to you from [the punishment of] a severe punishment.'
interpretation: The verse addresses the Prophet Muhammad, instructing him to warn the people of a single matter: to stand up for the sake of Allah, both collectively and individually, and then reflect on the reality of their situation. The verse emphasizes the role of the Prophet as a warner, reminding the people of the severe punishment that will inevitably come. The verse encourages the people to take heed of the warning, to reflect on their actions, and to stand up for Allah, both in their communities and as individuals. The verse serves as a call to action, urging the people to recognize the significance of the Prophet's message and to respond accordingly.
orig: قل إنما أعظكم بواحدة أن تقوموا لله مثنى وفرادى ثم تتفكروا ما بصاحبكم من جنة إن هو إلا نذير لكم بين يدي عذاب شديد

translation: Say, 'I do not ask you for any wage for it (the Quran). It is but a reminder for the worlds (mankind and jinn). No wage do I ask of you for it. It is not but a reminder for the worlds.'
interpretation: In this verse, Prophet Muhammad is being instructed to declare that he does not ask for any compensation for conveying the message of the Quran. He is merely a warner, and his only desire is to remind people of the truth. The verse emphasizes that the Prophet is not motivated by personal gain or worldly rewards, but rather by a sense of duty and responsibility towards his people. It also serves to remind the listeners of the importance of the message being conveyed, and that it is a reminder for all of humanity and the jinn.
orig: قل ما سألتكم من أجر فهو لكم إن أجري إلا على الله وهو على كل شيء شهيد

translation: Say, 'Indeed, my Lord expels the truth upon the greatest wrongdoer.'
interpretation: The verse is a statement made by the prophet Muhammad, in which he proclaims that his Lord (God) is the one who establishes the truth and exposes the wrongdoing of the greatest wrongdoer. It implies that God will ultimately make the truth known and will hold accountable those who commit the greatest of wrongs. The verse may serve as a source of comfort and reassurance for the prophet and his followers, as it asserts that God is in control and will ultimately prevail over those who oppose the truth.
orig: قل إن ربي يقذف بالحق علام الغيوب

translation: Say, 'The Truth has come, and falsehood cannot originate or repeat itself.'
interpretation: The verse is a statement made by the Prophet Muhammad, instructing him to declare that 'The Truth' (referring to Islam) has come, and that falsehood (referring to the previous religions or beliefs) cannot create anything new or bring back what it had before. This statement emphasizes the supremacy of truth over falsehood and asserts that falsehood cannot stand against the truth. It implies that the truth will always prevail and falsehood will ultimately be defeated. The verse can be interpreted as a message of reassurance to the believers, encouraging them to stay firm in their faith and not be swayed by the falsehoods of other religions or beliefs.
orig: قل جاء الحق وما يبدئ الباطل وما يعيد

translation: Say, 'If I have strayed, then I have only strayed to my own detriment. And if I am guided, it is through what my Lord reveals to me. Indeed, He is All-Hearing, Near.'
interpretation: The verse is a statement of personal responsibility and submission to God's guidance. The speaker acknowledges that if they have strayed from the right path, it is their own fault and they will bear the consequences. On the other hand, if they receive guidance, it is a gift from God, who is described as being All-Hearing and Near, emphasizing His attentiveness and accessibility to those who seek His guidance. The verse encourages the reader to take responsibility for their actions and to seek guidance from God, who is always listening and ready to help.
orig: قل إن ضللت فإنما أضل على نفسي وإن اهتديت فبما يوحي إلي ربي إنه سميع قريب

translation: And if you could but see when they are seized with terror, and there is no escape, and they are seized from a near place.
interpretation: The verse describes the fate of those who are seized with terror and have no escape from the punishment that is coming for them. They are taken from a 'near place', indicating that it is too late for them to repent or make amends for their wrongdoings. The verse serves as a warning of the impending doom for those who persist in their wrongdoings and do not heed the signs of God's punishment. It emphasizes the suddenness and inevitability of the punishment, leaving no room for escape or reprieve.
orig: ولو ترى إذ فزعوا فلا فوت وأخذوا من مكان قريب

translation: And they said, 'We believe in it.' How can they receive the reminder, (when) a group in it are unaware of Our command?
interpretation: The verse speaks about a group of people who claim to believe, but their actions do not align with their words. They are hypocrites. The verse highlights the fact that a group within this community is unaware of God's command, indicating their lack of understanding or ignorance of their faith. The verse serves as a reminder that faith requires action and understanding, not just words. It emphasizes the importance of being aware of God's command and living in accordance with it, rather than just claiming to believe.
orig: وقالوا آمنا به وأنى لهم التناوش من مكان بعيد

translation: And they disbelieved in him before and cast reproaches at him, from a distant place.
interpretation: The verse refers to the disbelievers who rejected the message of a prophet and hurled abuse at him from a distance, indicating their fear of him and their unwillingness to engage in a constructive dialogue. The verse highlights the rejection and hostility faced by prophets and messengers of God, and serves as a reminder of the challenges faced by those who strive to convey the truth to a disbelieving and hostile audience.
orig: وقد كفروا به من قبل ويقذفون بالغيب من مكان بعيد

translation: And a barrier between them and what they desire, as We have made for the people of old, surely they were in doubt concerning the meeting with their Lord.
interpretation: The verse speaks about a barrier that separates people from what they desire, similar to the barriers that were placed between previous nations and their desires. The verse implies that these barriers were a form of divine punishment, as the people of old were in doubt and uncertainty regarding the meeting with their Lord. The verse suggests that the people being referred to here are also experiencing a similar fate, and serves as a warning to those who are in doubt and uncertainty about their faith and their meeting with their Lord.
orig: وحيل بينهم وبين ما يشتهون كما فعل بأشياعهم من قبل إنهم كانوا في شك مريب

translation: All praise is for Allah, the Creator of the heavens and the earth, who made the angels messengers having two, three, or four wings. He increases in creation whatever He wills. Indeed, Allah is over all things competent.
interpretation: The verse begins with an expression of praise for God, the Creator of the heavens and the earth. It highlights God's power to create and control all things, as evidenced by the fact that He made the angels into messengers with different numbers of wings. The verse emphasizes that God has the power to increase or decrease creation as He wills, and that He is competent over all things. The verse serves as a reminder of God's power and greatness, and His control over all aspects of creation.
orig: الحمد لله فاطر السماوات والأرض جاعل الملائكة رسلا أولي أجنحة مثنى وثلاث ورباع يزيد في الخلق ما يشاء إن الله على كل شيء قدير

translation: Whatever mercy God opens up for people, no one can withhold it; and whatever He withholds, no one can release it thereafter. And He is the All-Mighty, the All-Wise.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the power and control that only God has over His mercy. No one can prevent God's mercy from reaching those who deserve it, and no one can grant mercy to those whom God has chosen not to bestow it upon. The verse also highlights God's attributes of being All-Mighty and All-Wise, reminding people of His power and knowledge, and that everything happens according to His will and wisdom.
orig: ما يفتح الله للناس من رحمة فلا ممسك لها وما يمسك فلا مرسل له من بعده وهو العزيز الحكيم

translation: O mankind, remember the favor of God upon you. Is there any creator other than God who provides for you from the heaven and the earth? There is no deity except Him. So how are you being deluded?
interpretation: The verse addresses all of humanity and reminds them of the blessings and favor that God has bestowed upon them. It emphasizes that there is no creator or provider other than God, who provides sustenance from the heavens and the earth. The verse affirms the oneness of God, and questions how people can be deluded or forgetful of this truth. The verse serves as a call to mindfulness and gratitude towards God, and a warning against the delusion of false deities or sources of sustenance.
orig: يا أيها الناس اذكروا نعمت الله عليكم هل من خالق غير الله يرزقكم من السماء والأرض لا إله إلا هو فأنى تؤفكون

translation: And if they deny you, then indeed before you, the messengers were denied, and to Allah return all matters.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the rejection and denial that the Prophet Muhammad faced from his people, and reassures him that he is not the first messenger to be denied. The second part of the verse emphasizes that all matters return to Allah, indicating that He is the ultimate judge and that justice will be served, regardless of the denial and rejection of the people. The verse serves as a source of comfort and reassurance for the Prophet Muhammad, reminding him that he is not alone in his mission and that the outcome is ultimately in the hands of Allah.
orig: وإن يكذبوك فقد كذبت رسل من قبلك وإلى الله ترجع الأمور

translation: O mankind, indeed the promise of Allah is truth, so let not the worldly life delude you and not let the deceiver (Satan) deceive you about Allah.
interpretation: The verse addresses all of humanity, reminding them of the truth of God's promise. The verse warns against becoming too attached to the worldly life, as it can lead to heedlessness and delusion. The verse also warns against being deceived by Satan, who seeks to lead people astray from the truth. The verse encourages people to stay mindful of God's promise and not be swayed by the temporary pleasures of this world or the deception of Satan.
orig: يا أيها الناس إن وعد الله حق فلا تغرنكم الحياة الدنيا ولا يغرنكم بالله الغرور

translation: Indeed, Satan is an enemy to you; so take him as an enemy. He only invites his party to be among the companions of the Blaze.
interpretation: The verse declares Satan as an enemy of humanity and instructs believers to consider him as such. Satan's sole purpose is to mislead people and invite them to join him in Hellfire. By emphasizing Satan's malevolent intentions, the verse encourages believers to seek protection from him and his temptations. This verse serves as a reminder of the spiritual battle between good and evil, and the importance of staying on the path of righteousness by avoiding Satan's deceit and trickery.
orig: إن الشيطان لكم عدو فاتخذوه عدوا إنما يدعو حزبه ليكونوا من أصحاب السعير

translation: For the disbelievers, there is a severe punishment, and for the believers who do righteous deeds, there is forgiveness and a great reward.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the two paths for humanity: one for the disbelievers who face severe punishment, and the other for the believers who do righteous deeds and earn forgiveness and a great reward. The verse emphasizes the importance of faith and good deeds, highlighting that they are the means to attain God's forgiveness and a reward in the afterlife. The verse serves as a reminder for people to reflect on their beliefs and actions and choose the path of righteousness and faith.
orig: الذين كفروا لهم عذاب شديد والذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات لهم مغفرة وأجر كبير

translation: Is he whose evil deed is made to appear attractive to him as one who is rightly guided? But Allah leaves astray whom He wills and guides whom He wills. So do not let your soul waste away in regret for them. Indeed, Allah is Knowing of what they do.
interpretation: The verse highlights the danger of being deceived by the attractiveness of one's own evil deeds, and the importance of being guided by Allah. The verse emphasizes that Allah guides whom He wills and leads astray whom He wills, and it reminds the believers not to let their souls be consumed by regret for those who have been led astray. The verse emphasizes Allah's knowledge of all that people do, and it serves as a reminder of the importance of seeking Allah's guidance and following His path.
orig: أفمن زين له سوء عمله فرآه حسنا فإن الله يضل من يشاء ويهدي من يشاء فلا تذهب نفسك عليهم حسرات إن الله عليم بما يصنعون

translation: And it is Allah who sends the winds, stirring up a cloud, then We drive it to a dead land and revive the earth with it after its death. Thus is the resurrection.
interpretation: The verse describes the natural phenomenon of the wind and clouds bringing rain to revive the earth, and uses it as a metaphor for the resurrection of the dead on the Day of Judgment. The verse emphasizes the power of Allah over all of creation, and the ability to bring life to that which was once dead. The verse serves as a reminder of the resurrection, and the ultimate judgment that will come, where all will be held accountable for their actions in this life.
orig: والله الذي أرسل الرياح فتثير سحابا فسقناه إلى بلد ميت فأحيينا به الأرض بعد موتها كذلك النشور

translation: Whoever desires power - all power belongs to God. To Him ascends the good word, and He raises the righteous deed. As for those who plot evil, they will have a severe punishment, and their plot will be void.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the ultimate power and authority of God, and encourages the believers to focus on righteous deeds and good words. It warns those who plot evil and mischief of a severe punishment. The verse suggests that the ultimate success and power belong to God, and the efforts of those who seek power and plot evil will ultimately be in vain. The verse encourages the believers to focus on the things that matter, such as righteous deeds and good words, and to trust in the power and wisdom of God.
orig: من كان يريد العزة فلله العزة جميعا إليه يصعد الكلم الطيب والعمل الصالح يرفعه والذين يمكرون السيئات لهم عذاب شديد ومكر أولئك هو يبور

translation: But it is Allah who has created you, then provided for you, then will cause you to die, and then will give you life. Are there any of your 'partners' who can do any of that? Exalted is He and high above what they associate with Him!
interpretation: The verse highlights the power and control that God has over all aspects of human life, from creation to death and back to life. It emphasizes God's role as the provider and sustainer of all life, and contrasts this with the inability of any other deity or force to have any impact on these fundamental aspects of existence. The verse serves as a reminder of God's greatness and self-sufficiency, and challenges the belief in any other deities or partners alongside God. It invites the reader to reflect on the power and wisdom of God, and to submit to His will.
orig: والله خلقكم من تراب ثم من نطفة ثم جعلكم أزواجا وما تحمل من أنثى ولا تضع إلا بعلمه وما يعمر من معمر ولا ينقص من عمره إلا في كتاب إن ذلك على الله يسير

translation: And not equal are the two seas: this fresh, sweet water, and that salty, bitter; and from each you eat fresh meat, and extract jewelry to wear; and you see the ships plowing through them so that you might seek His bounty, and perhaps you will be grateful.
interpretation: The verse highlights the contrast between two seas, one fresh and sweet, the other salty and bitter. It emphasizes the interconnectedness of all of God's creation, as humans benefit from both seas in multiple ways - for food, for jewelry, and for transportation. The verse serves as a reminder of the abundance of God's bounty and encourages gratitude for all the blessings in life. It also emphasizes the importance of seeking knowledge and understanding of the natural world as a means of appreciating God's creation.
orig: وما يستوي البحران هذا عذب فرات سائغ شرابه وهذا ملح أجاج ومن كل تأكلون لحما طريا وتستخرجون حلية تلبسونها وترى الفلك فيه مواخر لتبتغوا من فضله ولعلكم تشكرون

translation: He merges the night into the day and merges the day into the night, and He has subjected the sun and the moon - each one runs to a specified term. That is Allah, your Lord; to Him belongs sovereignty. And those whom you invoke other than Him do not possess [so much as] the membrane of a date seed.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the power and control of Allah over the natural world, specifically the day and night cycle and the movement of celestial bodies such as the sun and moon. The verse highlights the precision and order of these phenomena, as they each run to a specified term. The verse contrasts the power and sovereignty of Allah with the powerlessness of the deities and entities that people invoke besides Him, stating that they do not even possess the membrane of a date seed. The verse serves as a reminder of the greatness and power of Allah, and the insignificance of other deities and entities in comparison. It encourages the believers to put their trust and faith in the one and only God, and not to associate partners with Him.
orig: يولج الليل في النهار ويولج النهار في الليل وسخر الشمس والقمر كل يجري لأجل مسمى ذلكم الله ربكم له الملك والذين تدعون من دونه ما يملكون من قطمير

translation: Indeed, if you call them to guidance, they will not hear; indeed, if they were to hear, they would not accept. And on the Day of Resurrection, they will reject your association. And none can inform you like One who is acquainted.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the rejection and disbelief of certain people towards guidance and truth. Even if they were to hear the call to guidance, they would not accept it. The verse also highlights the ultimate rejection of these people on the Day of Resurrection, when they will reject any association or connection with the believers. The verse concludes with the reminder that only One who is acquainted, all-knowing and all-seeing, can truly inform and guide us.
orig: إن تدعوهم لا يسمعوا دعاءكم ولو سمعوا ما استجابوا لكم ويوم القيامة يكفرون بشرككم ولا ينبئك مثل خبير

translation: O mankind, you are those in need of Allah, while Allah is the Self-Sufficient, Praiseworthy.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the dependency of human beings on Allah, while Allah is independent and in need of nothing. This verse serves as a reminder of human vulnerability and the importance of recognizing and submitting to the power and greatness of Allah. It also highlights the importance of expressing gratitude and praise towards Allah, as He is the one who provides for all of our needs.
orig: يا أيها الناس أنتم الفقراء إلى الله والله هو الغني الحميد

translation: If He wills, He can take you away, [O mankind], and then produce a new creation.
interpretation: The verse speaks about God's power and control over all of creation. It emphasizes that God has the ability to take away the current creation and replace it with a new one, if He so wills. This serves as a reminder of God's greatness and power, and the limited control that humans have over their own lives. It also serves as a call for humility and submission to God's will, as well as a reminder of the fleeting and temporary nature of this world.
orig: إن يشأ يذهبكم ويأت بخلق جديد

translation: And that is not difficult for God.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the power and ability of God, stating that what is being referred to is not difficult for Him. The exact context of the verse is not provided, but it implies that God is able to do something that may seem difficult or impossible for humans. The verse serves as a reminder of God's greatness and sovereignty, and the limitations of human capabilities and understanding.
orig: وما ذلك على الله بعزيز

translation: And no bearer of burdens shall bear the burden of another, and if a heavily laden soul calls [another] to [carry] its load, nothing of it will be carried, even if he is near of kin. You warn only those who fear their Lord unseen and establish prayer. And whoever purifies himself only purifies himself for [the benefit of] his soul. And to Allah is the [final] destination.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the individual responsibility of each person for their own actions and deeds. No one can bear the burden of another's sins or wrongdoings. The verse encourages people to establish prayer and fear their Lord, reminding them that the consequences of their actions will ultimately be faced by them alone. The verse also highlights the importance of personal purification and self-improvement, stressing that it is solely for the benefit of the individual's soul. The verse concludes by reaffirming that the ultimate destination and final judgement of all people is with Allah.
orig: ولا تزر وازرة وزر أخرى وإن تدع مثقلة إلى حملها لا يحمل منه شيء ولو كان ذا قربى إنما تنذر الذين يخشون ربهم بالغيب وأقاموا الصلاة ومن تزكى فإنما يتزكى لنفسه وإلى الله المصير

translation: And the blind and the seer are not alike.
interpretation: The verse highlights the fundamental difference between the blind and the seer, implying that they cannot be treated as equals. This can be interpreted in a number of ways, such as the physical ability to see versus blindness, or the metaphorical ability to understand and perceive truth versus being spiritually or intellectually blind. Regardless of the interpretation, the verse emphasizes the importance of sight and understanding, and the significance of the differences between those who have it and those who do not.
orig: وما يستوي الأعمى والبصير

translation: But not the darkness nor the light
interpretation: The verse is a continuation of a discussion about the nature of Allah, the Islamic God. In this verse, it is emphasized that Allah is neither darkness nor light, but rather exists beyond and encompasses both. This verse can be interpreted as a reminder of the transcendence of Allah, who is beyond human understanding and comprehension. It also highlights the idea that Allah is the source of both darkness and light, and has power over both. This verse can be seen as a call for humility, reminding people of their limitations and the greatness of Allah.
orig: ولا الظلمات ولا النور

translation: Nor darkness nor abominable glare.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the nature of the Hereafter and the experience of the Day of Judgment. The phrase 'nor darkness nor abominable glare' describes the intense and uncomfortable conditions of the Day of Judgment. The darkness symbolizes the absence of light and guidance, while the 'abominable glare' refers to the intense and unbearable light that will be present. The verse emphasizes the overwhelming and terrifying nature of the Day of Judgment, serving as a warning for people to prepare for it by leading a righteous life.
orig: ولا الظل ولا الحرور

translation: And the living are not alike to the dead, indeed Allah causes whom He wills to hear, and you cannot reach (or make hear) those in the graves.
interpretation: The verse highlights the fundamental difference between the living and the dead, emphasizing that God has control over who can hear and who cannot. The verse suggests that the living have the ability to hear and respond, while the dead do not. Moreover, the verse reminds us that even though we may be alive, we cannot reach or communicate with those who are in the graves. The verse may serve as a reminder of the transience of life and the importance of using our time wisely, as well as the ultimate power and control that God holds over life and death.
orig: وما يستوي الأحياء ولا الأموات إن الله يسمع من يشاء وما أنت بمسمع من في القبور

translation: Indeed, you are only a warner.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the role of the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) as a warner, whose duty is to convey the message of Islam and warn people of the consequences of their actions. The verse reminds the Prophet that he is not responsible for the actions of the people, but rather to deliver the message. It also serves as a reminder to the believers of the importance of the role of the Prophet and the significance of the message he brought.
orig: إن أنت إلا نذير

translation: Indeed, We have sent you with the truth as a bringer of good tidings and a warner. And there is not a nation except that there has certainly come to it a warner.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the role of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) as a bringer of good news and a warner. It also makes clear that every nation in history has received a warner, meaning that no one can claim ignorance of God's message. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of following the truth and the Prophet's guidance, as well as a warning of the consequences of ignoring the message.
orig: إنا أرسلناك بالحق بشيرا ونذيرا وإن من أمة إلا خلا فيها نذير

translation: And if they deny you, then already have denied those before them. Their messengers came to them with clear proofs, and with what they used to write.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the rejection of prophets and messengers by previous nations. The verse emphasizes that if the people reject the message brought by the current prophet (who is assumed to be the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him), they are not the first to do so. Previous nations have also rejected their prophets and messengers. The verse mentions that the messengers came to these nations with clear proofs and evidence, as well as with written scriptures, yet they still rejected the message. This verse serves as a reminder that rejection of prophets and their messages is not a new phenomenon and that it has always been a characteristic of those who are stubborn and unwilling to accept the truth.
orig: وإن يكذبوك فقد كذب الذين من قبلهم جاءتهم رسلهم بالبينات وبالزبر وبالكتاب المنير

translation: Then seized those who disbelieved, how (horrible) was My rejection
interpretation: The verse speaks about the punishment of those who rejected God's message. The word 'seized' implies a sudden and powerful act of taking, emphasizing the overwhelming power of God's punishment. The phrase 'how (horrible) was My rejection' further emphasizes the severity of the punishment, indicating that it is a consequence of the rejection of God's message. The verse serves as a warning to those who reject God's message, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the power of God's punishment.
orig: ثم أخذت الذين كفروا فكيف كان نكير

translation: Have you not seen that God sends down water from the sky, and We produce therewith fruits of various colors, and among the mountains are streaks, white and red, of various colors, and (black) ravens?
interpretation: The verse highlights the wonders of God's creation, pointing to the diversity and beauty of fruits and the variations in the colors of mountains and ravens. The verse serves to remind people of the power and greatness of God, who is capable of creating such diverse and beautiful things. The verse also encourages people to reflect on the natural world around them, and to see the signs of God's existence and wisdom in all things.
orig: ألم تر أن الله أنزل من السماء ماء فأخرجنا به ثمرات مختلفا ألوانها ومن الجبال جدد بيض وحمر مختلف ألوانها وغرابيب سود

translation: And among the people and the animals and the cattle are of various colors, as also among the trees, so among the slaves of Allah, those who fear Him are of various kinds; surely Allah is the Mighty, the Forgiving.
interpretation: The verse highlights the diversity in creation, from people to animals to plants, and then draws a comparison to the diversity among the believers in their fear and reverence for God. Despite the differences in outward expressions of faith, the verse emphasizes that God is the Forgiving and the Mighty, and it serves as a reminder to all believers to fear and respect God, regardless of their individual differences.
orig: ومن الناس والدواب والأنعام مختلف ألوانه كذلك إنما يخشى الله من عباده العلماء إن الله عزيز غفور

translation: Indeed, those who recite the Book of God and establish prayer and give zakah from what We have provided them, secretly and publicly, hope for a transaction that will never perish.
interpretation: The verse highlights the importance of reciting the Qur'an, establishing prayer, and giving zakah (charity) as a means of achieving success in this life and the hereafter. These actions are described as a 'transaction' that will never perish, implying that they are a wise investment with everlasting returns. The verse encourages believers to engage in these practices consistently, both privately and publicly, as a way of expressing their faith and commitment to God. The verse serves as a reminder that true success comes from pleasing God and following His commands, rather than relying solely on worldly gains.
orig: إن الذين يتلون كتاب الله وأقاموا الصلاة وأنفقوا مما رزقناهم سرا وعلانية يرجون تجارة لن تبور

translation: that He may reward them for their deeds and increase them from His bounty. Indeed, He is Forgiving, Appreciative.
interpretation: The verse speaks about God's reward for people who have done good deeds. The verse emphasizes that God not only rewards people for their deeds, but also increases their blessings. The verse highlights God's attributes of being Forgiving and Appreciative, emphasizing that He not only rewards good deeds but also forgives and appreciates those who do them.
orig: ليوفيهم أجورهم ويزيدهم من فضله إنه غفور شكور

translation: And We have revealed to you, [O Muhammad], the Book in truth, confirming what was before it, and a protector over it. Indeed, Allah, of His servants, is Acquainted and Seeing.
interpretation: The verse affirms that the Quran is the truth, confirming and protecting the previous revelations from God. The verse emphasizes that God is well-acquainted and observant of His servants, indicating that the Quran is a guidance from a God who is aware of the needs and circumstances of His creation. The verse serves as a reminder of the divine origin of the Quran, and of the wisdom and purpose behind its revelation, which is to guide humanity towards the right path.
orig: والذي أوحينا إليك من الكتاب هو الحق مصدقا لما بين يديه إن الله بعباده لخبير بصير

translation: Then We gave the Book as inheritance to those of Our servants whom We chose. And among them is he who wrongs himself, and among them is he who is moderate, and among them is he who is foremost in good deeds by the permission of Allah. That is the great bounty.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the inheritance of the Book, which refers to the Quran, given to a select group of servants of God. Among this group, there are those who commit injustices against themselves, those who are moderate, and those who excel in good deeds. The verse highlights the diversity of the believers and their varying levels of faith and actions. At the same time, the verse emphasizes the great favor of God in giving the Quran as an inheritance, which serves as a source of guidance and wisdom for the believers. The verse encourages the believers to strive for excellence in their actions and to seek God's permission and guidance in their endeavors.
orig: ثم أورثنا الكتاب الذين اصطفينا من عبادنا فمنهم ظالم لنفسه ومنهم مقتصد ومنهم سابق بالخيرات بإذن الله ذلك هو الفضل الكبير

translation: Gardens of Eden they will enter, therein they will be adorned with bracelets of gold and pearl, and their garments therein will be silk.
interpretation: The verse describes the reward for the righteous in paradise. It speaks of gardens of Eden, a symbol of beauty, peace and happiness. Those who enter will be adorned with gold and pearl bracelets, a symbol of wealth and luxury. Their garments will be made of silk, a symbol of softness and elegance. The verse aims to describe the indescribable beauty and luxury of paradise, as a reward for those who lived a righteous life, and an incentive for those who are still striving for it.
orig: جنات عدن يدخلونها يحلون فيها من أساور من ذهب ولؤلؤا ولباسهم فيها حرير

translation: And they said, 'Praise be to God who has removed from us (our) sorrow. Indeed, our Lord is Forgiving and Appreciative.'
interpretation: The verse is a statement of gratitude and praise from a group of people who have experienced the removal of their sorrow by the mercy of God. They acknowledge God's forgiveness and appreciation, recognizing that it is only through His grace that they have been delivered from their hardship. The verse serves as a reminder of the power of God's forgiveness and the importance of expressing gratitude for His blessings, no matter the circumstances.
orig: وقالوا الحمد لله الذي أذهب عنا الحزن إن ربنا لغفور شكور

translation: Who has made the Sacred House a means of support for us, so that, [we, the believers], are not unrightful to its inhabitants nor are [we, the inhabitants], unrightful to the [pilgrims who] come to it.
interpretation: This verse refers to the Kaaba, the Sacred House in Mecca, which God has made a source of support and protection for the believers. The verse emphasizes the importance of treating the inhabitants and the visitors of the Kaaba with justice and fairness. It serves as a reminder to the believers to respect the rights of others and not to commit any injustices or transgressions against them. The verse also highlights the sanctity of the Kaaba and the importance of preserving its sacredness and dignity.
orig: الذي أحلنا دار المقامة من فضله لا يمسنا فيها نصب ولا يمسنا فيها لغوب

translation: And for those who disbelieved, for them is the fire of Hell. It will not be decreed for them that they should die, nor will its punishment be lightened for them. Thus do We reward every ungrateful one.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the punishment of Hellfire that awaits those who disbelieve in God. The verse emphasizes that the punishment of Hellfire will not be lifted from them, and they will not be granted respite from it, even at the time of their death. The verse also highlights the certainty of the punishment for those who are ungrateful and reject God's signs and messages. The verse serves as a warning to those who deny the truth and a reminder that God's punishment is just and fitting for those who reject His mercy and guidance.
orig: والذين كفروا لهم نار جهنم لا يقضى عليهم فيموتوا ولا يخفف عنهم من عذابها كذلك نجزي كل كفور

translation: And they cry in it, 'Our Lord, take us out of this! We will do righteousness - other than what we used to do.' Did We not give you long enough life that you might be reminded therein? And there came to you the warner. So taste (the consequence of your actions), and there is no helper for the unjust.
interpretation: The verse describes the regret of people who, when faced with the consequences of their actions, cry out to God for help and promise to change their ways. However, the verse reminds them that they had already been given ample time to repent and change, but they did not take advantage of it. The verse emphasizes the finality of their fate and the absence of any helper for the unjust. The verse serves as a reminder to take advantage of the opportunities for repentance and change, and not to wait until it is too late.
orig: وهم يصطرخون فيها ربنا أخرجنا نعمل صالحا غير الذي كنا نعمل أولم نعمركم ما يتذكر فيه من تذكر وجاءكم النذير فذوقوا فما للظالمين من نصير

translation: Indeed, Allah is Knowing of the unseen of the heavens and the earth. Indeed, He is Knowing of the insides of breasts.
interpretation: The verse affirms Allah's knowledge of the unseen, including the heavens and the earth. The verse emphasizes Allah's all-encompassing knowledge, extending to the insides of breasts, referring to the innermost thoughts and secrets of individuals. The verse serves as a reminder of Allah's omniscience, encouraging believers to be mindful of their thoughts and actions, knowing that Allah is aware of everything, even what is hidden within them.
orig: إن الله عالم غيب السماوات والأرض إنه عليم بذات الصدور

translation: He it is Who made you successors (khalifa) in the earth, and exalted some of you in rank above others, that He may try you by (the test of) that which He gave you. Surely your Lord is Quick in Retribution; but surely He is indeed Oft-Forgiving, Full of Love (towards the pious).
interpretation: This verse speaks about God's role in making humans successors (khalifa) on earth and giving them different ranks and responsibilities. The verse highlights the test of God's blessings, and the fact that God will quickly retaliate against those who reject His blessings and commit injustice. However, the verse also emphasizes God's forgiveness and love towards the pious. The verse suggests that humans should be mindful of their actions and use their blessings in a responsible and just manner, as they will be held accountable for their choices. The verse also reminds people that God's punishment is swift and severe, but He is also forgiving and merciful to those who repent and strive for righteousness.
orig: هو الذي جعلكم خلائف في الأرض فمن كفر فعليه كفره ولا يزيد الكافرين كفرهم عند ربهم إلا مقتا ولا يزيد الكافرين كفرهم إلا خسارا

translation: Say, 'Do you see your partner-gods whom you invoke besides Allah? Show me what they have created of the earth. Or have they a share in the heavens? Or have We given them a book so they are upon a clear proof from it? Nay, the wrongdoers promise one another only delusion.'
interpretation: The verse addresses the disbelievers who associate partners with Allah and invokes them instead of Him. The verse challenges them to show what their partner-gods have created in the earth or if they have any share in the heavens. The verse also asks if they have been given any revelation that provides clear proof. The verse concludes by stating that the wrongdoers only promise one another delusion, emphasizing the futility of their actions and their false hopes.
orig: قل أرأيتم شركاءكم الذين تدعون من دون الله أروني ماذا خلقوا من الأرض أم لهم شرك في السماوات أم آتيناهم كتابا فهم على بينت منه بل إن يعد الظالمون بعضهم بعضا إلا غرورا

translation: Indeed, Allah holds the heavens and the earth, lest they cease. And if they should cease, there is not one who can hold them back except Him. Indeed, He is Most Forbearing, Oft-Forgiving.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes Allah's power and control over the heavens and the earth, and His ability to prevent their collapse. The verse also highlights Allah's patience and forgiveness, as it states that even if the heavens and the earth were to cease, there is no one who can hold them back except Him, and yet, He is still forbearing and forgiving. The verse serves as a reminder of Allah's power and His willingness to forgive those who repent and turn back to Him.
orig: إن الله يمسك السماوات والأرض أن تزولا ولئن زالتا إن أمسكهما من أحد من بعده إنه كان حليما غفورا

translation: And they swore by God with their most solemn oath that if a warner came to them, they would be more guided than [any] of the nations. But when a warner came to them, it only increased them in arrogance.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the attitude of people who arrogantly claim that they would follow the guidance of a prophet or warner if one were to come to them. However, when a warner does come to them, instead of being guided, they become even more arrogant and reject the message. This verse serves as a critique of those who claim to be open-minded and receptive to guidance, but in reality, are not. It highlights the human tendency to reject that which challenges our beliefs and worldview and the importance of being truly open to guidance and change.
orig: وأقسموا بالله جهد أيمانهم لئن جاءهم نذير ليكونن أهدى من إحدى الأمم فلما جاءهم نذير ما زادهم إلا نفورا

translation: They waxed proud on the earth, unmindful that Our doom must needs come to them. They plotted a plot, but We plotted a plot while they perceived not. Then see how was the end of their plot! Surely We destroy the fabric they have builded and the very foundations thereof.
interpretation: The verse speaks about people who become arrogant on earth and forget that God's punishment will come to them. They plot evil, but their plot will not succeed except for its own people. The verse emphasizes that the people do not pay attention to the fate of previous nations and that God's decree cannot be changed. The verse serves as a reminder of the transience of human achievements and the ultimate power of God's punishment.
orig: استكبارا في الأرض ومكر السيئ ولا يحيق المكر السيئ إلا بأهله فهل ينظرون إلا سنت الأولين فلن تجد لسنت الله تبديلا ولن تجد لسنت الله تحويلا

translation: Have they not traveled through the land and seen how was the end of those before them, and they were stronger than them in power? And Allah is not such that He is unable to do anything in the heavens and the earth. Indeed, He is Knowing and Competent.
interpretation: The verse reminds the people to reflect on the fate of the past nations who were stronger and more powerful than them, and how they were destroyed for their wrongdoing. The verse emphasizes the all-encompassing power of God, who is capable of doing all things in the heavens and the earth. The verse serves as a warning to those who deny the signs of God and reject His message, reminding them of the inevitable consequences of their actions and the omnipotence of God.
orig: أولم يسيروا في الأرض فينظروا كيف كان عاقبة الذين من قبلهم وكانوا أشد منهم قوة وما كان الله ليعجزه من شيء في السماوات ولا في الأرض إنه كان عليما قديرا

translation: And if Allah were to seize mankind for their wrongdoing, He would not leave on it (i.e., the earth) a single living creature, but He postpones them for an appointed term. And when their term comes, then indeed, Allah has been, of His servants, Seeing.
interpretation: The verse highlights the power and authority of Allah, stating that if He were to punish people immediately for their wrongdoings, no living creature would be left on earth. However, Allah postpones their punishment to a specific term. This emphasizes Allah's patience and mercy towards his servants. The verse also reminds us that Allah sees and knows everything that his servants do, and that they will ultimately be held accountable for their actions.
orig: ولو يؤاخذ الله الناس بما كسبوا ما ترك على ظهرها من دابة ولكن يؤخرهم إلى أجل مسمى فإذا جاء أجلهم فإن الله كان بعباده بصيرا

translation: And
interpretation: No interpretation
orig: يس

translation: And the Qur'an, full of wisdom.
interpretation: The verse refers to the Qur'an as being full of wisdom. This statement highlights the divine nature of the Qur'an as a source of guidance and wisdom for all of humanity. The Qur'an is not just a book of rules and regulations, but a source of wisdom that can be applied to all aspects of life. This verse serves as a reminder of the importance of reflecting on the teachings of the Qur'an and seeking guidance from its wisdom.
orig: والقرآن الحكيم

translation: Indeed, you are of the messengers.
interpretation: The verse is a direct address to the Prophet Muhammad, confirming his role as one of the messengers of God. This verse serves as a source of strength and reassurance for the Prophet, reminding him that he is part of a long line of messengers who have been chosen by God to guide humanity. The verse also emphasizes the importance of the Prophet's mission and the significance of his role in conveying God's message to the world.
orig: إنك لمن المرسلين

translation: Upon a straight path
interpretation: The phrase 'Upon a straight path' is a reference to the right and correct way of living, in accordance with God's will and teachings. It symbolizes a life of righteousness, virtue, and obedience to God. This phrase serves as a reminder for believers to stay on the path of righteousness, and to avoid straying from it through disobedience and sin.
orig: على صراط مستقيم

translation: Descends the compassionate, the Merciful.
interpretation: The verse speaks of the descent of Allah, who is described as both al-Rahman (the Compassionate) and al-Rahim (the Merciful). This verse is often recited during the adhan (the Islamic call to prayer) and serves as a reminder of Allah's compassion and mercy towards all of humanity. It emphasizes the nearness of Allah and His constant presence in the lives of believers, offering them comfort and reassurance in times of hardship and difficulty. The verse also highlights the importance of seeking Allah's compassion and mercy, and the belief in His boundless generosity and kindness towards His creations.
orig: تنزيل العزيز الرحيم

translation: To warn a people to whom no warner has come before, so they are unaware.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the responsibility of the prophet Muhammad (PBUH) to warn the people of the consequences of their actions and guide them towards the right path. The verse highlights the fact that these people have not received a warner before, which implies that they are unaware of the punishment that awaits them if they continue to live in sin and injustice. The verse emphasizes the importance of prophethood and the role of the prophet in guiding people towards the truth and saving them from the punishment of God.
orig: لتنذر قوما ما أنذر آباؤهم فهم غافلون

translation: Indeed, the word has proven true against the majority of them, so they do not believe.
interpretation: The verse asserts that the truth of the divine message or 'word' has been demonstrated against the majority of people, yet they continue to disbelieve. The verse highlights the rejection of the truth despite clear evidence, emphasizing the importance of faith and belief in the divine message. It serves as a reminder of the significance of accepting the truth and the consequences of rejecting it.
orig: لقد حق القول على أكثرهم فهم لا يؤمنون

translation: We have put collars on their necks, reaching to their chins, so that they are held back.
interpretation: The verse describes the punishment of those who have transgressed and rebelled against God. The image of collars on their necks, reaching to their chins, conveys the idea of complete control and subjugation. The phrase 'so that they are held back' implies that they are prevented from committing any further wrongdoing. The verse serves as a reminder that God has the power to control and punish those who disobey Him, and that there are consequences for one's actions.
orig: إنا جعلنا في أعناقهم أغلالا فهي إلى الأذقان فهم مقمحون

translation: And We placed, between them, a barrier and a barrier behind them, and then We covered them so they could not see.
interpretation: The verse describes how God placed barriers between a group of people and then covered them, preventing them from seeing. The barriers could symbolize a physical or spiritual separation, and the act of covering could represent divine punishment or protection. The verse may be interpreted as a warning about the consequences of being cut off from God or as a statement of God's power to control the fate of human beings.
orig: وجعلنا من بين أيديهم سدا ومن خلفهم سدا فأغشيناهم فهم لا يبصرون

translation: And it is the same for them whether you warn them or do not warn them, they will not believe.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the stubbornness and rejection of some people in accepting the truth, despite the efforts made to warn and guide them. The verse emphasizes that whether or not the people are warned, they will not believe, indicating the futility of trying to change their minds. The verse may serve as a source of comfort and patience for those who are trying to convey the message of truth, reminding them that the outcome is not dependent on their efforts alone, but ultimately rests with the people's own choice and free will.
orig: وسواء عليهم أأنذرتهم أم لم تنذرهم لا يؤمنون

translation: You (Muhammad) are only a warner, and for every people there is a guide. Allah (God) is the One who sends astray, and He is the One who guides. And there is no change in the words of Allah. Indeed, already has come to you from your Lord a proof [i.e., the Prophet Muhammad and the Qur'an]. So, is there any who will remember?
interpretation: The verse highlights the role of the Prophet Muhammad as a warner, and that every nation has been sent a guide. It emphasizes the power of God in determining the fate of individuals, as He is the one who leads astray or guides. The verse also reaffirms the unchangeable nature of God's words, and that proof has already come to the people in the form of the Prophet Muhammad and the Qur'an. It serves as a call for reflection and remembrance of God, inviting the people to consider the significance of the message and to remember God's power and guidance.
orig: إنما تنذر من اتبع الذكر وخشي الرحمن بالغيب فبشره بمغفرة وأجر كريم

translation: Indeed, it is We who give life and cause death, and to Us is the final destination of all things. Indeed, We know that which the earth consumes of them and with Us is a book preserved.
interpretation: The verse affirms that it is God who has control over life and death and that all things ultimately return to Him. The verse emphasizes God's knowledge and power over all creation, including the earth's consumption of living things and the preservation of all things in a clear record. The verse serves as a reminder of God's omniscience and omnipotence, and the ultimate accountability of all beings to Him.
orig: إنا نحن نحيي الموتى ونكتب ما قدموا وآثارهم وكل شيء أحصيناه في إمام مبين

translation: And strike for them an example, the people of the town, when there came to them the messengers.
interpretation: The verse uses a parable to make a point, and the parable is the story of the people of a town who were visited by messengers. The verse does not provide the details of the story, but it implies that the people of the town rejected or mistreated the messengers, which led to a consequence. By using this parable, the verse emphasizes the importance of treating the messengers (or prophets) with respect and consideration, and the negative consequences of rejecting or mistreating them.
orig: واضرب لهم مثلا أصحاب القرية إذ جاءها المرسلون

translation: When We sent two to them, they denied both of them; so We reinforced them with a third, and they said, 'Indeed, we are messengers to you.',
interpretation: The verse speaks about a situation where God sent two messengers to a group of people, but they were denied and rejected. In response, God sent a third messenger to reinforce the first two. Despite the increased number of messengers, the people still refused to believe and instead claimed that the messengers were lying. The verse highlights the rejection and disbelief of the people, and the persistence of God in sending messengers to guide them. The verse may also serve as a reminder of the importance of accepting and following the guidance of the messengers, and the consequences of rejecting them.
orig: إذ أرسلنا إليهم اثنين فكذبوهما فعززنا بثالث فقالوا إنا إليكم مرسلون

translation: They say, 'You are not but human beings like us, and Allah has not revealed anything. You are only lying.'
interpretation: The verse describes the disbelievers' denial of the prophethood of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and their rejection of the revelation from Allah. The disbelievers accused the Prophet of lying and claimed that he was no different from them. The verse emphasizes the rejection of the message by the disbelievers and their denial of the truth. The verse serves as a reminder of the challenges faced by the Prophet and the importance of upholding the truth in the face of adversity.
orig: قالوا ما أنتم إلا بشر مثلنا وما أنزل الرحمن من شيء إن أنتم إلا تكذبون

translation: They said, 'Our Lord, indeed we have been wrongdoers.'
interpretation: The verse reports the words of a group of people who, in a moment of realization and acceptance of their mistakes, acknowledge their wrongdoing and express their remorse to God. They refer to themselves as 'wrongdoers', indicating their understanding of the consequences of their actions. The verse highlights the importance of taking responsibility for one's actions and seeking forgiveness, emphasizing the mercy and compassion of God towards those who truly repent.
orig: قالوا ربنا يعلم إنا إليكم لمرسلون

translation: And upon us is only the clear conveyance (of the message).
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the role of the messenger (Prophet Muhammad) in delivering the message of God clearly and without any distortion or alteration. It indicates that the responsibility of the messenger is only to convey the message and not to force people to believe or follow it. The verse also implies that the message is clear and easy to understand, and that the responsibility of accepting or rejecting it lies with the people themselves.
orig: وما علينا إلا البلاغ المبين

translation: They said, 'Indeed, we will flee from you if you do not desist. Then we will take revenge on you. And we will touch you with a painful punishment.'
interpretation: The verse describes a confrontation between the disbelievers and the prophet, where the disbelievers threaten to retaliate against the prophet and his followers if they do not stop their preaching. The verse highlights the aggression and hostility of the disbelievers towards the message of Islam and their readiness to use violence and harm against those who spread it. The verse serves as a reminder of the challenges and difficulties faced by the prophet and his companions in their mission to spread the message of Islam and the importance of patience and steadfastness in the face of adversity.
orig: قالوا إنا تطيرنا بكم لئن لم تنتهوا لنرجمنكم وليمسنكم منا عذاب أليم

translation: They said, 'Your god is only yourselves, is this not enough of a reminder? No, you are a people who exceed all limits.',
interpretation: The verse is a statement made by the disbelievers in response to the message of the prophet. They rejected the belief in the one true God and instead, they claimed that the prophet and his followers only worshiped themselves. The verse highlights the arrogance and rejection of the disbelievers, as they not only deny the message but also mock it. The phrase 'you are a people who exceed all limits' emphasizes their transgression and lack of self-control. The verse serves as a reminder of the dangers of arrogance and the importance of humility and submission to the will of God.
orig: قالوا طائركم معكم أئن ذكرتم بل أنتم قوم مسرفون

translation: And from the remote part of the city, a man running, he said, 'O my people, follow the messengers.',
interpretation: The verse describes a scene where a man is running from the outskirts of a city, calling out to the people to follow the messengers. The verse highlights the urgency and importance of the message that the man is conveying. The man's actions of running towards the city and calling out to the people suggest that he is trying to warn them of some danger or impending doom. The verse may be interpreted as a call to heed the warnings of the messengers and to follow their guidance, as the man in the verse is doing. The verse may also be seen as a reminder of the importance of spreading the message of the messengers and of the need for urgency in conveying this message to others.
orig: وجاء من أقصى المدينة رجل يسعى قال يا قوم اتبعوا المرسلين

translation: And follow those who ask not of you any reward, and they are on the right path.
interpretation: The verse advises the believers to follow those who do not seek any reward or compensation from them and who are on the right path. The verse implies that these individuals are true guides and leaders who are motivated solely by their faith and commitment to the right path. By following such individuals, the believers will be guided and protected from deviation and error. The verse encourages the believers to seek knowledge and guidance from those who are truly worthy of it and who have the best interests of the community at heart.
orig: اتبعوا من لا يسألكم أجرا وهم مهتدون

translation: But what reason could I have not to worship Him who brought me into existence and to whose return I shall be returned?
interpretation: The verse is a rhetorical question emphasizing the importance of worshiping Allah, the one who created the speaker and to whom they will return in the afterlife. The verse suggests that it is only natural and necessary for the speaker to worship Allah, and that there is no reason for them not to do so. This verse can be seen as a reminder of the relationship between the creator and the created, and the importance of fulfilling the purpose of one's existence, which is to worship Allah.
orig: وما لي لا أعبد الذي فطرني وإليه ترجعون
