translation: Shall I take as gods other than Him? If the All-Merciful wills some adversity for me, their intercession will not avail me anything, nor can they save me.
interpretation: The verse is a rhetorical question where the speaker expresses that they will not take any gods other than the All-Merciful (one of the names of God in Islam). The verse emphasizes the power and control of the All-Merciful and the futility of seeking intercession from other gods if the All-Merciful wills some adversity for the speaker. The verse reinforces the idea that there is no other god but the All-Merciful and that seeking help from any other source is pointless.
orig: أأتخذ من دونه آلهة إن يردن الرحمن بضر لا تغن عني شفاعتهم شيئا ولا ينقذون

translation: Indeed, I will surely be of the wrongdoers if I disbelieve.
interpretation: The verse is a statement of submission and acceptance of faith. The speaker acknowledges that if they were to disbelieve or deny the truth, they would be among those who are wrongdoers. The verse emphasizes the importance of faith and the consequences of disbelief, and serves as a reminder to remain steadfast in one's belief and avoid falling into disbelief and wrongdoing.
orig: إني إذا لفي ضلال مبين

translation: Indeed, I have believed in your Lord, so listen.
interpretation: The speaker in this verse has declared their faith in the Lord of the people being addressed. The speaker then urges them to listen, implying that they have an important message to share. This verse emphasizes the importance of faith and the need to be receptive to the message of the believer. It may also serve as a reminder to those who have not yet found faith to be open to the possibility and to listen to the believers around them.
orig: إني آمنت بربكم فاسمعون

translation: It was said, 'Enter Paradise.' He said, 'Oh, I wish my people could know [this].'
interpretation: The verse describes the moment when an individual is granted entry into Paradise. However, instead of rejoicing in his own salvation, the individual expresses sadness and regret that his people, who are still alive in this world, do not know or understand the great blessing that he has received. The verse highlights the importance of guiding and sharing one's blessings with others, and the deep sense of responsibility that believers have towards their communities.
orig: قيل ادخل الجنة قال يا ليت قومي يعلمون

translation: By which my Lord has forgiven me and made me of the honored
interpretation: The verse is a statement of gratitude and praise from the Prophet Muhammad, expressing his appreciation for God's forgiveness and elevation of his status. The verse emphasizes the power and mercy of God, who has the ability to forgive and bestow honor upon whom He wills. It also highlights the humility and gratitude of the Prophet Muhammad, who recognizes and acknowledges the blessings that have been bestowed upon him.
orig: بما غفر لي ربي وجعلني من المكرمين

translation: And We sent not against his people after him a host from heaven, nor was We a disposer of their affairs.
interpretation: The verse speaks about God's decision not to send a host from heaven or interfere in the affairs of a people after a certain individual (presumably a prophet or a messenger) had been sent to them. The verse emphasizes God's patience and willingness to give people the opportunity to repent and change their ways, rather than immediately punishing them. The verse also highlights the importance of the role of prophets and messengers in guiding people towards the right path and the consequences of rejecting their message.
orig: وما أنزلنا على قومه من بعده من جند من السماء وما كنا منزلين

translation: Indeed, it will be but a single shout, then when they are aware of it, they will be staring [in horror].
interpretation: The verse speaks about a sudden and catastrophic event, described as a "single shout" or "blast". The verse emphasizes the suddenness and unexpectedness of the event, as the people will be caught off guard and will only become aware of it when it is already too late. The phrase "they will be staring [in horror]" conveys the shock and fear that will be experienced by the people at the time of the event. The verse serves as a warning of the sudden and catastrophic consequences of disbelief and wrongdoing.
orig: إن كانت إلا صيحة واحدة فإذا هم خامدون

translation: But whenever a messenger came to them with what they did not desire, they would ridicule him.
interpretation: The verse describes the common reaction of people to the messengers sent by God. When the messengers brought a message that the people did not like or want to hear, they would ridicule and mock the messenger instead of listening to the message and considering its truth. This behavior is a form of denial and rejection of God's message, and it is a sign of the people's disbelief and lack of faith. The verse serves as a reminder that people should be open-minded and receptive to the message of the messengers, and not dismiss it out of hand simply because it is not what they want to hear.
orig: يا حسرة على العباد ما يأتيهم من رسول إلا كانوا به يستهزئون

translation: Have they not seen how many generations We have destroyed before them, that they will not return to them?
interpretation: The verse reminds the listeners of the fate of previous civilizations that were destroyed by God's will. The phrase 'they will not return to them' emphasizes the finality of their destruction and the impossibility of returning to the past. The verse serves as a warning to the listeners, urging them to reflect on the lessons of history and to avoid the same fate as the destroyed civilizations. It also implies that the destruction of these civilizations was a result of their actions and that the listeners should take heed and mend their ways before it is too late.
orig: ألم يروا كم أهلكنا قبلهم من القرون أنهم إليهم لا يرجعون

translation: And indeed for every matter (there is) a fixed decree.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the idea that everything in this world, including the events and outcomes of human actions, are predestined and have a fixed decree with God. This concept of predestination is an important principle in Islamic theology and provides a sense of order and certainty in the face of the apparent chaos and unpredictability of the world. The verse reminds believers that God is all-knowing and all-powerful, and that everything that happens is part of God's plan and purpose.
orig: وإن كل لما جميع لدينا محضرون

translation: And We made for them gardens of the palm-trees and grapes, and made springs gush therein for them,
interpretation: The verse describes the blessings that God bestowed upon a people, providing them with fertile land and abundant resources. The gardens of palm-trees and grapes represent the prosperity and abundance that they enjoyed. The springs that were made to gush forth for them symbolize the life-giving power of God's blessings. The verse highlights the generosity and kindness of God towards his creations, and serves as a reminder of the blessings that we often take for granted.
orig: وآية لهم الأرض الميتة أحييناها وأخرجنا منها حبا فمنه يأكلون

translation: And We made in it [i.e., the earth] gardens of palm trees and grapevines, and We caused springs to gush forth in it.
interpretation: The verse highlights the bounties and blessings that God has bestowed upon the earth, specifically the creation of gardens filled with date palms, grape vines, and flowing springs. The verse serves as a reminder of God's power and ability to create and provide for His creation. It also emphasizes the beauty and abundance of the natural world and encourages people to reflect on and appreciate the blessings that they have been given.
orig: وجعلنا فيها جنات من نخيل وأعناب وفجرنا فيها من العيون

translation: So that they may eat of its fruit and it may benefit them, what they have done with their hands. So will they not be grateful?
interpretation: The verse speaks about the blessings of the earth and the responsibility of humans to be grateful for these blessings. The verse emphasizes the importance of using the resources of the earth for the benefit of humanity and expressing gratitude for these blessings. The verse serves as a reminder to be mindful of the blessings that we have and to use them responsibly, rather than taking them for granted. It also highlights the importance of expressing gratitude for these blessings and recognizing the role of one's own efforts in obtaining them.
orig: ليأكلوا من ثمره وما عملته أيديهم أفلا يشكرون

translation: Glory be to Him who created all pairs of that which the earth grows, and of yourselves, and of that which you do not know.
interpretation: The verse is a glorification of God's power and knowledge in creating all pairs or pairs of things. This includes not only the pairs of living beings that are visible to us, such as those that grow from the earth, but also the pairs that exist within ourselves and those that we are not aware of. The verse serves as a reminder of God's greatness, His ability to create and control all things, and the limitations of human knowledge and understanding.
orig: سبحان الذي خلق الأزواج كلها مما تنبت الأرض ومن أنفسهم ومما لا يعلمون

translation: And a sign for them is the night. We withdraw from it the day, and behold, they are plunged in darkness.
interpretation: The verse uses the daily cycle of day and night as a 'sign' or reminder for people. It describes how God withdraws the day and brings on the night, plunging people into darkness. This can be interpreted as a metaphor for the human condition, where people are often in a state of ignorance and uncertainty, stumbling around in 'darkness' and unable to see the truth. The verse may also be reminding people of the power and control that God has over the natural world, and the need for humans to be mindful and respectful of this power.
orig: وآية لهم الليل نسلخ منه النهار فإذا هم مظلمون

translation: And the sun runs its course for a specified term. That is the decree of the Exalted in Might, the Knowing.
interpretation: The verse highlights the order and precision in the natural world, specifically the movement of the sun. The sun's course and the length of its journey are predetermined and follow a precise path, which is a manifestation of the power and knowledge of God. The verse serves as a reminder of the greatness of God and His control over all aspects of life, including the natural world. The verse also emphasizes the importance of understanding and recognizing the signs of God in the world, and the need to submit to His will and power.
orig: والشمس تجري لمستقر لها ذلك تقدير العزيز العليم

translation: And We have appointed the moon as a light therein, until it returns like an old palm leaf.
interpretation: The verse describes the moon as a source of light in the sky, and sets a limit to its course until it returns to its original state, likened to a withered or dried up palm leaf. This simile conveys the idea of the moon's waning and waxing, and its cyclical nature, emphasizing the order and predictability of the cosmos. The verse can also be interpreted as a reminder of the transience of earthly things, and the need to look beyond the physical world to the eternal and unchanging God.
orig: والقمر قدرناه منازل حتى عاد كالعرجون القديم

translation: The sun is not allowed to overtake the moon, nor does the night outstrip the day, but each, in its own course, is swimming.
interpretation: The verse describes the natural order of the universe, specifically the movement of the sun, moon, and the day and night. The verse emphasizes the precision and predictability of their movements, with the sun and moon following their own courses without interfering with each other. This is seen as a sign of the greatness and power of God, who has created and maintains this order. The verse also serves as a reminder that everything in the universe, including human beings, have a specific role and course to follow, and that they should not transgress or interfere with the natural order of things.
orig: لا الشمس ينبغي لها أن تدرك القمر ولا الليل سابق النهار وكل في فلك يسبحون

translation: And a sign for them is that We carried their forefathers in the laden ship.
interpretation: The verse uses the carrying of the ancestors of the people in a laden ship as a sign or evidence of God's power and control over all things. The verse may be interpreted as a reminder of God's past favors and blessings upon the people, and a call for them to be grateful and obedient. It may also serve as a reminder of the fleeting nature of worldly possessions and the importance of placing one's trust in God. Ultimately, the verse encourages the people to reflect on the signs around them and to recognize the power and wisdom of God.
orig: وآية لهم أنا حملنا ذريتهم في الفلك المشحون

translation: And We have created for them the like of it, which they ride upon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the creation of something that is comparable to the mounts or transportation that people use. The verse emphasizes the greatness of God's power and creativity in providing for His creations and providing them with the means of transportation. The verse can be interpreted as a reminder of the blessings that God has bestowed upon humanity, and a call for gratitude and appreciation for those blessings. It can also be interpreted as a metaphor for the journey of life and the various means that God has provided for people to travel through it.
orig: وخلقنا لهم من مثله ما يركبون

translation: And if We will, We will surely drown them, then there will be no shouting for them (to rescue themselves) nor will they be able to return (to the land).
interpretation: The verse speaks about God's power over people and how He can easily destroy them if He so wills. The phrase 'if We will' emphasizes God's sovereignty and control over all things. The verse describes the drowning of people as a form of punishment, and the phrase 'then there will be no shouting for them (to rescue themselves)' highlights the suddenness and completeness of the punishment. The people will be unable to save themselves or even call for help. The verse serves as a reminder of God's power and control, and the consequences of disbelief and disobedience.
orig: وإن نشأ نغرقهم فلا صريخ لهم ولا هم ينقذون

translation: but mercy from us and enjoyment for a while.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the mercy and enjoyment that comes from God. Despite the destruction and punishment that is meted out to unjust towns, God also shows mercy and allows for enjoyment for a period of time. This can be interpreted as a reminder that even in times of hardship and punishment, God's mercy is always present. The enjoyment and respite can serve as a test or a chance for people to turn back to God and repent for their sins. Ultimately, this verse highlights the balance and justice in God's actions, where punishment is meted out but is always accompanied by mercy and compassion.
orig: إلا رحمة منا ومتاعا إلى حين

translation: And when it is said to them, 'Fear what is before you and what is behind you, perhaps you will be shown mercy.'
interpretation: The verse is a warning to the people to be mindful of God's power and presence, both in the present and in the future. The phrase 'what is before you' could refer to the consequences of their actions in this life, while 'what is behind you' could refer to the Day of Judgment. The verse emphasizes the importance of seeking God's mercy through repentance and righteous deeds. The message is a call to fear God and to strive for righteousness, as a means of attaining His mercy and avoiding His punishment.
orig: وإذا قيل لهم اتقوا ما بين أيديكم وما خلفكم لعلكم ترحمون

translation: And never came to them a sign from the signs of their Lord except they turned away from it.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the people's rejection and denial of the signs of their Lord. Despite the signs and evidence presented to them, they refused to believe or acknowledge them. The verse emphasizes the people's persistent rejection and denial, as it states that they turned away from every sign that came to them. This verse serves as a reminder of the consequences of denying and rejecting the signs of God, and the importance of being open and receptive to His messages.
orig: وما تأتيهم من آية من آيات ربهم إلا كانوا عنها معرضين

translation: And when it is said to them, 'Spend from what Allah has provided for you,' those who disbelieve say to those who believe, 'Should we feed one whom, if Allah willed, He could feed?' You are only in clear error.
interpretation: This verse speaks about the response of the disbelievers when they are asked to spend from the provisions that Allah has given them. The disbelievers mock the believers and question why they should spend on others when Allah has the power to feed them Himself. The verse highlights the arrogance and lack of generosity of the disbelievers. It also serves as a reminder to the believers that the disbelievers are lost and in error. The verse emphasizes the importance of generosity and charity, and the responsibility of the believers to use the provisions given to them by Allah in a righteous and just manner.
orig: وإذا قيل لهم أنفقوا مما رزقكم الله قال الذين كفروا للذين آمنوا أنطعم من لو يشاء الله أطعمه إن أنتم إلا في ضلال مبين

translation: And they say, 'When will this promise be (fulfilled), if you are truthful?'
interpretation: The verse describes the disbelievers' questioning of the promised punishment from God. They challenge the believers by asking 'when' the promised punishment will come, if they are speaking the truth. The verse highlights the disbelievers' rejection of the truth and their refusal to believe in the signs of God, despite the clear evidence presented to them. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of faith and trust in God's promises, and the consequences of rejecting the truth.
orig: ويقولون متى هذا الوعد إن كنتم صادقين

translation: They only look forward to a single shout that will seize them while they are disputing.
interpretation: The verse describes the disbelievers' obliviousness to the impending doom, as they are too engrossed in their arguments and disputes to notice the signs of the coming punishment. The 'single shout' symbolizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the divine retribution, leaving them no time for repentance or escape. The verse serves as a warning to those who ignore the signs of the approaching end, emphasizing the importance of being vigilant and mindful of one's actions.
orig: ما ينظرون إلا صيحة واحدة تأخذهم وهم يخصمون

translation: They cannot advise each other, nor can they return to their people.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the state of people who have committed a grave sin and are beyond the point of repentance. They are so deeply entrenched in their wrongdoing that they cannot even advise each other to do good or to repent. Additionally, they are not welcomed back by their people, indicating their complete isolation and alienation from their community. This verse serves as a warning to those who persist in sin and wrongdoing, emphasizing the dire consequences of their actions and the ultimate rejection by both their peers and their community.
orig: فلا يستطيعون توصية ولا إلى أهلهم يرجعون

translation: And when We decreed death for them, We said, 'Strike their bodies with a part of the cattle.' Thus did We requite them for their transgressions.
interpretation: The verse describes the punishment of a group of people who were transgressors. When they were decreed to die, they were commanded to strike their bodies with a part of the cattle. This was a form of retribution for their sins. The verse emphasizes the power of God's decree and the consequences of disobedience and transgression.
orig: ونفخ في الصور فإذا هم من الأجداث إلى ربهم ينسلون

translation: They said, 'Oh, woe to us! Who has raised us up from our place of sleep? This is what the Most Merciful promised, and the messengers were truthful.'
interpretation: The verse describes the reaction of the people upon being resurrected on the Day of Judgment. They express their shock and disbelief at being awakened from their graves, recognizing that this is the event that the Most Merciful (one of the names of God) had promised. The people acknowledge the truth of the messengers, who had previously warned them about the Day of Judgment. The verse emphasizes the reality and significance of the Day of Judgment, and the importance of heeding the warnings of the messengers.
orig: قالوا يا ويلنا من بعثنا من مرقدنا هذا ما وعد الرحمن وصدق المرسلون

translation: Indeed, it will be but a single shout, then immediately they will all be before Us.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the Day of Judgment, describing it as a sudden and loud sound that will signal the end of the world. The verse emphasizes the swiftness and suddenness of this event, as people will immediately find themselves before God, having no time to prepare or make amends. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of being prepared for this inevitable day, and of the need to live a righteous life.
orig: إن كانت إلا صيحة واحدة فإذا هم جميع لدينا محضرون

translation: So today no soul will be wronged in the least, and you will not be treated unjustly.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the Day of Judgment, when all deeds will be accounted for and no one will be treated unjustly. It emphasizes the fairness and justice of God, who will not allow even the slightest injustice towards any soul. At the same time, the verse reminds people that they will receive the consequences of their own actions, whether good or bad, and that they will not be treated unfairly. This serves as a message of hope for those who have been wronged in their lives, and a reminder for those who have done wrong that they will be held accountable for their actions.
orig: فاليوم لا تظلم نفس شيئا ولا تجزون إلا ما كنتم تعملون

translation: Indeed, the companions of Paradise today are in [a state of] distracting enjoyment.
interpretation: The verse describes the state of those who have entered Paradise as one of distracting enjoyment and bliss. The Arabic word 'shaghal' used in the verse means 'occupation' or 'preoccupation', but in this context, it has a positive connotation, indicating a state of joy and happiness that fully engrosses the inhabitants of Paradise. The phrase 'today' emphasizes the immediacy and reality of this state of bliss for the believers who have entered Paradise. The verse serves as a source of hope and motivation for believers, reminding them of the ultimate reward for their good deeds and faith in God.
orig: إن أصحاب الجنة اليوم في شغل فاكهون

translation: Their sides depart from their beds, they call upon their Lord in fear and hope, and they spend (in charity) out of what We have given them.
interpretation: The verse describes the pious and righteous people who wake up early in the morning, in the 'shadows' or coolness of the dawn, and leave their comfortable beds to seek God's pleasure and blessings. They call upon their Lord in fear of His punishment and hope for His mercy, and they spend their wealth in charity, out of the blessings that God has given them. The verse emphasizes the importance of starting the day with acts of worship and devotion, and the reward of giving to the poor and needy. It serves as a model for the believers to follow, and a reminder of the blessings of God and the importance of gratitude and generosity.
orig: هم وأزواجهم في ظلال على الأرائك متكئون

translation: For them in it are fruits and for their sustenance whatever they ask
interpretation: The verse describes a place or situation where people have an abundance of fruits and are provided with all their needs. The phrase 'whatever they ask' emphasizes the generosity and provision of this place, highlighting its desirability and blessings. It can be interpreted as a metaphor for heaven or a state of abundance and prosperity, where all desires are fulfilled and all needs are met.
orig: لهم فيها فاكهة ولهم ما يدعون

translation: Peace, a word from a Merciful Lord.
interpretation: The verse delivers a message of peace from the 'Merciful Lord'. It serves as a reminder of the compassionate and benevolent nature of God. The verse may also be interpreted as a call for peace and serenity, encouraging individuals to seek and promote peace in their lives and in their communities.
orig: سلام قولا من رب رحيم

translation: And keep yourself apart from this day, O you criminals.
interpretation: The verse is a command to the criminals or sinners to separate themselves from the righteous. This separation is necessary to protect the righteous from the negative influence of the sinners and to prevent the sinners from further committing sins. The verse emphasizes the importance of avoiding sin and wrongdoing and encourages the sinners to reflect on their actions and repent. The verse also reminds the righteous of the importance of keeping themselves separate from sinners and of the need to protect their own faith and goodness.
orig: وامتازوا اليوم أيها المجرمون

translation: Did I not enjoin upon you, O children of Adam, that you not worship Satan - indeed, he is to you a clear enemy?
interpretation: The verse is a direct address to the children of Adam, reminding them of a previous command given to them by God. The command is to not worship Satan, who is described as a clear enemy. The verse emphasizes the importance of this command and the dangers of disobeying it. The verse can be interpreted as a warning to stay away from the temptations of Satan and to remain steadfast in the worship of God.
orig: ألم أعهد إليكم يا بني آدم أن لا تعبدوا الشيطان إنه لكم عدو مبين

translation: And worship Me this is a straight path.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of worshipping only One God and following the straight path. It suggests that worshipping God is the only way to attain righteousness and success in this life and the hereafter. The verse encourages believers to stay on the right path, which is free from any deviation and misguidance.
orig: وأن اعبدوني هذا صراط مستقيم

translation: And indeed, many a companion have We sent astray before you (O Muhammad). Then is it not that they were able to reason?
interpretation: The verse speaks about the fact that many people before the Prophet Muhammad were led astray from the right path. The verse questions whether these people were unable to use their reason and understanding. The verse is a reminder that despite being given the ability to reason and think, many people still choose to go astray. It serves as a warning to those who may be deviating from the right path and encourages them to use their reason and understanding to reflect on their actions and make amends.
orig: ولقد أضل منكم جبلا كثيرا أفلم تكونوا تعقلون

translation: This is Hell which you were promised.
interpretation: The verse is addressing the disbelievers and reminding them of the Hellfire that they were previously warned about. The verse emphasizes the reality of Hell and serves as a warning to those who deny the existence of the Hereafter and continue to commit sins. The verse also reminds the believers of the consequences of disbelief and the importance of staying steadfast on the path of righteousness.
orig: هذه جهنم التي كنتم توعدون

translation: Pray to Him today for what you have been denying.
interpretation: The verse is a command from God to the disbelievers to pray to Him, acknowledging His existence and power. The verse highlights the urgency of the situation, emphasizing that they should pray 'today', indicating that the opportunity for repentance and salvation is limited. The verse also implies that the disbelievers have been denying or rejecting the truth and the message of Islam, and that it is time for them to recognize and submit to God. The verse serves as a call for reflection and a reminder of the consequences of disbelief and denial.
orig: اصلوها اليوم بما كنتم تكفرون

translation: Today We shall seal up their mouths, and their hands will speak to Us, and their legs will bear witness to what they used to earn.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the Day of Judgment, when the actions of individuals will be accounted for. The verse describes how, on that day, the ability to speak will be taken away from people and their limbs will testify against them, revealing the truth about their deeds and actions. The verse emphasizes the inevitability of judgment and the impossibility of hiding one's actions and intentions. It serves as a reminder of the importance of leading a righteous life and of the ultimate accountability of every individual for their actions.
orig: اليوم نختم على أفواههم وتكلمنا أيديهم وتشهد أرجلهم بما كانوا يكسبون

translation: And if We willed, We could darken their eyes, and they would struggle to find the way. Then how could they see?
interpretation: The verse speaks about God's power to control the fate of human beings and the consequences of their actions. The verse suggests that if God willed, He could take away their ability to see, which would prevent them from finding their way. The phrase 'then how could they see?' emphasizes the idea that if people cannot see physically, they will be unable to perceive or understand things around them, indicating the importance of spiritual vision and understanding. The verse serves as a reminder of the limits of human power and the ultimate control of God, and the importance of seeking guidance and understanding through faith and spirituality.
orig: ولو نشاء لطمسنا على أعينهم فاستبقوا الصراط فأنى يبصرون

translation: And if We had willed, We would have certainly punished them thereupon, so they would not have been able to move forward, nor could they have returned.
interpretation: The verse speaks about God's power and authority, and the inevitability of His punishment for those who disobey Him. The verse emphasizes that if God had willed, He could have punished the disbelievers immediately, leaving them unable to flee or escape. This verse serves as a reminder of God's power and control over all things and the importance of obedience and submission to Him.
orig: ولو نشاء لمسخناهم على مكانتهم فما استطاعوا مضيا ولا يرجعون

translation: And if We let man taste mercy from Us and then withdraw it from him, surely man is ungrateful.
interpretation: The verse highlights the tendency of human beings to take God's blessings for granted and to forget to be grateful for them. The verse speaks about the experience of receiving mercy from God, and then having it taken away. This experience serves as a test for human beings, and many of them fail by not showing gratitude for the blessings they received. The verse serves as a reminder to be thankful for God's blessings and not to take them for granted.
orig: ومن نعمره ننكسه في الخلق أفلا يعقلون

translation: And We have not taught him poetry, nor is it befitting for him. It is nothing but a reminder and a clear Quran.
interpretation: The verse is refuting the claim that Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) was a poet and that the Quran was poetry. The verse asserts that Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) was not taught poetry and that it is not befitting for him. The verse emphasizes that the Quran is not poetry, but rather a reminder and a clear message from God. This verse was revealed to refute the accusations of the disbelievers who rejected the Quran by labeling it as poetry, and to affirm the divine nature of the Quran.
orig: وما علمناه الشعر وما ينبغي له إن هو إلا ذكر وقرآن مبين

translation: To warn whoever is alive and to establish the word against the disbelievers.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the purpose of the Qur'an, which is to warn those who are alive and to establish the truth of Islam against the disbelievers. The verse emphasizes the importance of the Qur'an as a means of guidance and warning for humanity, and the ultimate victory of the truth over falsehood. The verse also highlights the role of the believers in conveying the message of Islam to others, and the importance of standing firm in the face of disbelief and rejection.
orig: لينذر من كان حيا ويحق القول على الكافرين

translation: Have they not seen that We have created for them of what Our hands have made cattle, and they are their owners.
interpretation: The verse highlights the blessings that God has bestowed upon humans in the form of animals, which have been created by God's own hands. The animals are described as "cattle" which refers to any domesticated animal that is used for labor, food, or other practical purposes. The verse emphasizes that humans are the owners of these animals, which implies a responsibility to care for and protect them. This verse can be interpreted as a reminder of the relationship between humans and animals, and the importance of treating animals with kindness and compassion.
orig: أولم يروا أنا خلقنا لهم مما عملت أيدينا أنعاما فهم لها مالكون

translation: And We made them lowly therein, and they were riding on its backs, and when the matter was decided, surely, humbly, they will return to Us.
interpretation: The verse describes the fate of those who were once powerful and proud but were brought low by God's decree. They used to ride on the backs of animals, symbolizing their power and wealth, but ultimately they will return to God in a state of humility and submission. The verse reminds us that no matter how powerful or wealthy we may be, we are ultimately dependent on God's will and mercy, and that true power and dignity come from humility and submission to Him.
orig: وذللناها لهم فمنها ركوبهم ومنها يأكلون

translation: And they have therein advantages and pleasures, will they not then be grateful?
interpretation: The verse is addressing people who have been given blessings and benefits in this life. The verse asks them if they are grateful for these blessings, implying that they should be. The verse serves as a reminder to people to be thankful for what they have, and not to take it for granted. It suggests that people should recognize and appreciate the good things in their lives, and express their gratitude to God for these blessings.
orig: ولهم فيها منافع ومشارب أفلا يشكرون

translation: And they have taken besides Allah protectors [of worship], hoping that they will be helped [by them].
interpretation: The verse speaks about people who have taken protectors or deities besides Allah, hoping that they will be helped and protected by them. This is a clear act of shirk (associating partners with Allah) and a rejection of the tawhid (the oneness of Allah). The verse is a reminder that there is no deity worthy of worship except Allah and that no one can bring benefit or harm except by His will. The verse also highlights the futility of relying on false deities and the danger of associating partners with Allah, as it is a grave sin that will lead to a severe punishment.
orig: واتخذوا من دون الله آلهة لعلهم ينصرون

translation: They will not be able to aid them, and they (the disbelievers) will be to them (the believers) an army in arms.
interpretation: The verse describes the situation of the disbelievers who will not be able to help each other when they are faced with the consequences of their actions. Instead, the believers will be like a well-prepared army ready to confront them. The verse emphasizes the power and readiness of the believers, and the helplessness and vulnerability of the disbelievers, who will be unable to defend themselves.
orig: لا يستطيعون نصرهم وهم لهم جند محضرون

translation: So let not their speech grieve you. Indeed, We know what they conceal and what they declare.
interpretation: The verse addresses the Prophet Muhammad, telling him not to be saddened by the words of the disbelievers. The verse reassures the Prophet that Allah is aware of the intentions and actions of the disbelievers, both what they hide and what they make known. The verse serves as a source of comfort and strength for the Prophet, reminding him that Allah is all-knowing and that the truth will ultimately prevail.
orig: فلا يحزنك قولهم إنا نعلم ما يسرون وما يعلنون

translation: Does not man see that We have created him from a drop? Yet, behold, he is an open disputant.
interpretation: The verse highlights the contrast between the humble origins of human beings, who were created from a mere drop of fluid, and their tendency to engage in disputes and arguments. The verse suggests that humans should be humble and grateful for their creation, and should refrain from disputes and arguments. The verse may also be interpreted as a reminder that human beings are weak and vulnerable, and that they should not take their existence for granted. Ultimately, the verse invites human beings to reflect on their place in the world and to consider the purpose of their existence.
orig: أولم ير الإنسان أنا خلقناه من نطفة فإذا هو خصيم مبين

translation: And He set forth for Us a parable, and forgot His own creation. He said: Who will give life to the bones when they are decayed?
interpretation: This verse is a continuation of a conversation between God and the disbelievers, where God presents a parable to illustrate a point. The parable is about a man who forgets his own creation, and then questions who can give life to bones that have decayed. The interpretation of this verse is that God is reminding the disbelievers of their own mortality and insignificance, and that they should not be so quick to reject His message. The decayed bones serve as a metaphor for the transience of life and the inevitability of death, and the question serves to challenge the disbelievers to consider the possibility of resurrection and the power of God to give life to the dead.
orig: وضرب لنا مثلا ونسي خلقه قال من يحيي العظام وهي رميم

translation: Say, 'The one who brought her (the earth) to life the first time will bring her back to life (on the Day of Judgment), and He knows all creation.'
interpretation: The verse is a statement attributed to the Prophet Muhammad, addressed to the disbelievers who question the resurrection of the dead. The verse asserts that the same power that created the earth and brought it to life in the first place is capable of resurrecting the dead on the Day of Judgment. The verse emphasizes God's knowledge of all creation, implying that He has the power and ability to do as He wills. The verse serves as a reminder of the Day of Judgment and the ultimate power and knowledge of God, encouraging faith and submission to His will.
orig: قل يحييها الذي أنشأها أول مرة وهو بكل خلق عليم

translation: Who has made for you fire from the green tree, and behold, you kindle from it.
interpretation: The verse speaks about God's provision of fire for humans, which is made from a green tree. This fire serves as a source of warmth, light, and energy for people. The verse emphasizes the role of fire in human life and its significance in their daily activities. It also highlights the power of God, who has the ability to create such a useful and essential element from a simple green tree. The verse can be seen as a reminder of God's blessings and the importance of being grateful for them.
orig: الذي جعل لكم من الشجر الأخضر نارا فإذا أنتم منه توقدون

translation: Is not He who created the heavens and the earth able to create the like of them? Yes, and He is the Knowing Creator.
interpretation: The verse is emphasizing the power and ability of God, who created the heavens and the earth, to create anything similar or even greater than them. The verse is saying that God's ability is not limited, and He can create anything He wants, and He is the 'Knowing Creator' who has complete knowledge of all things. This verse can be seen as a reminder of God's greatness and a confirmation of His power over all of creation.
orig: أوليس الذي خلق السماوات والأرض بقادر على أن يخلق مثلهم بلى وهو الخلاق العليم

translation: His command, when He intends a thing, is only that He says to it, 'Be,' and it is.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the power and authority of God in creating and controlling the universe. The verse emphasizes that when God intends to create something, He only needs to say 'Be,' and it will come into existence. This demonstrates God's omnipotence and sovereignty over all of His creation, and it serves as a reminder of the limitations of human power and control in comparison to God's infinite abilities.
orig: إنما أمره إذا أراد شيئا أن يقول له كن فيكون

translation: Exalted is He who holds all control in His hands, and to Him you will be returned.
interpretation: The verse affirms the power and control of God over all things, and emphasizes that everything is in His hands. It also reminds us that we will all return to Him, emphasizing the ultimate accountability of every individual for their actions in this life. This verse can be seen as a reminder of the importance of living a righteous and just life, and the need to constantly strive for God's pleasure and approval.
orig: فسبحان الذي بيده ملكوت كل شيء وإليه ترجعون

translation: But as for him who is given his record in his left hand, he will say, 'Oh, I wish I had not been given my record
interpretation: The verse speaks about the Day of Judgment and the fate of those who receive their record (of deeds) in their left hand. These individuals will regret their actions and wish they had not been given their record, as it is a sign of their bad deeds and impending punishment. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of good deeds and the transience of worldly pleasures, as on the Day of Judgment, all will be held accountable for their actions.
orig: والصافات صفا

translation: So let the reminders be a reminder,
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of reminders or warnings as a means of awakening people from heedlessness and prompting them to reflect on their actions. It encourages people to take heed of the reminders and use them as an opportunity to correct their ways and turn back to the right path.
orig: فالزاجرات زجرا

translation: And the following are examples [of punishment]
interpretation: The verse provides examples or illustrations of the punishment that was mentioned earlier in the Qrayn (Chapter 13) as a consequence of disbelief and rejection of God's signs. The verse emphasizes the certainty and inevitability of God's punishment for those who persist in their disbelief and rejection of God's signs.
orig: فالتاليات ذكرا

translation: Indeed, your god is one.
interpretation: The verse affirms the oneness of God, emphasizing that the only deity worthy of worship is the one God. This statement is a fundamental principle in Islamic theology, and it distinguishes Islam from other religions that believe in multiple deities or in the divinity of human beings. The verse serves as a reminder to focus all worship, devotion, and obedience towards the one true God.
orig: إن إلهكم لواحد

translation: Lord of the heavens and the earth and what is between them, and Lord of the Easts.
interpretation: The verse affirms the oneness of God as the Lord of all creation, including the heavens, the earth, and everything that exists between them. The phrase 'Lord of the Easts' emphasizes God's control and power over all directions and all that exists in them. This verse can be seen as a reminder of God's greatness and power over all of creation, and a call to submit to His will and authority.
orig: رب السماوات والأرض وما بينهما ورب المشارق

translation: We have adorned the lowest heaven with lamps (stars) in beauty.
interpretation: The verse describes the beauty of the night sky, emphasizing the role of God in creating and adorning it with stars. The verse can be interpreted as a reminder of the majesty and power of God, who is capable of creating such a beautiful and intricate universe. Additionally, the verse can be seen as a call to appreciate and reflect on the beauty of the natural world, which serves as a sign of God's existence and greatness.
orig: إنا زينا السماء الدنيا بزينة الكواكب

translation: And kept away from every rebellious devil
interpretation: The verse speaks about God's protection of the believers from the devils. The verse emphasizes the power of God in keeping the believers safe from the harm of the devils, who are described as "rebellious". The verse serves as a reminder of God's protection and care for the believers, and of the constant presence of evil forces that seek to mislead and harm them.
orig: وحفظا من كل شيطان مارد

translation: And they do not listen to the exalted assembly (angels) and push away (reject) from every side (from all directions),
interpretation: The verse describes the actions of those who reject the message of the angels, who are described as the 'exalted assembly'. These people not only refuse to listen to the message, but they also actively push it away, rejecting it completely. The phrase 'from every side' emphasizes the complete nature of their rejection, as they reject the message from all directions and from all angles. This verse serves as a warning to those who reject the message of the angels and the truth of Islam, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the importance of listening to and accepting the truth.
orig: لا يسمعون إلى الملإ الأعلى ويقذفون من كل جانب

translation: And they will bear a burden and have a blaze (of fire).
interpretation: The verse speaks of the punishment that will befall certain people, who will bear a heavy burden and be consumed by a blaze of fire. The verse may be referring to the burden of their sins and the consequences of their actions, which will ultimately lead to their destruction. The blaze of fire represents the punishment that they will face as a result of their sins. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and reminds them of the severe consequences of their actions.
orig: دحورا ولهم عذاب واصب

translation: Except for those who are seized by seizure, then a piercing blast follows them.
interpretation: The verse speaks about a specific group of people who are not affected by the punishment that is being described. These people are those who are 'seized by seizure', which is a reference to a sudden and unexpected event, such as death. Following this event, these people are pursued by a 'piercing blast', which is a metaphor for the punishment that is faced after death. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the punishment, and serves as a reminder of the importance of being prepared for the end of one's life and the Day of Judgment.
orig: إلا من خطف الخطفة فأتبعه شهاب ثاقب

translation: And they say, 'Who is greater in creation than His creations?' Say, 'God, the One who created them, originated them from clay.'
interpretation: The verse is a response to a question or challenge posed by the disbelievers, who ask who is greater in creation than God's creations. The verse answers that it is God, the One who created and originated them from clay. The verse emphasizes God's power and creativity, and the insignificance and weakness of the creations compared to their Creator. The verse also serves as a reminder that all of creation is dependent on God and subject to His will.
orig: فاستفتهم أهم أشد خلقا أم من خلقنا إنا خلقناهم من طين لازب

translation: But they marvel and laugh
interpretation: The verse describes the disbelievers' reaction to the truth and the message brought by the believers. Instead of accepting the truth and submitting to God, they are amazed and ridicule the believers and the message. This verse highlights the arrogance and rejection of the disbelievers, and serves as a reminder of the consequences of their actions and the importance of accepting the truth and submitting to God.
orig: بل عجبت ويسخرون

translation: And when they are reminded, they do not remember.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the lack of remembrance or understanding on the part of those who are being reminded or warned. Despite being reminded or warned, they fail to take heed or learn from the reminder. The verse highlights the hard-heartedness or heedlessness of certain individuals, who are unwilling or unable to reflect on the significance of the reminder. The verse may serve as a critique of those who are indifferent to warnings or lessons, emphasizing the importance of reflection and attentiveness.
orig: وإذا ذكروا لا يذكرون

translation: And when they see a sign, they ridicule it.
interpretation: The verse refers to the disbelievers who, upon seeing a sign or a miracle from God, respond with mockery and rejection. This verse highlights the closed-mindedness and lack of faith of those who refuse to accept the truth even when it is presented to them in a clear and undeniable way. The verse serves as a reminder that God's signs and miracles should be met with reverence and acceptance, rather than scorn and ridicule.
orig: وإذا رأوا آية يستسخرون

translation: And they said, 'This is nothing but clear magic.'
interpretation: The verse is referring to the disbelievers' response towards the message of the prophet. They dismissed the message as nothing but clear magic, refusing to accept it and denying its truth. The verse highlights the closed-mindedness and rejection of those who reject the truth and refuse to believe, despite the clear signs and evidence presented to them.
orig: وقالوا إن هذا إلا سحر مبين

translation: But after we have been lifeless, indeed we were dust and bones, will we then indeed be in a creation new?
interpretation: The verse is a rhetorical question, expressing a sense of wonder and disbelief. It speaks about the process of death and decay, where the human body returns to its original state of dust and bones. The question that follows challenges the listener to consider the possibility of resurrection, suggesting that the human body, despite its seemingly final end, may be brought back to life. The verse is often interpreted as an affirmation of the Islamic belief in the Day of Judgment, where all souls will be resurrected and held accountable for their actions in the world.
orig: أإذا متنا وكنا ترابا وعظاما أإنا لمبعوثون

translation: Our first ancestors
interpretation: The phrase 'Our first ancestors' refers to the first generation of human beings, who were the children of Adam and Eve. This phrase highlights the connection between all human beings, as we all share a common origin and are part of the same family. The Qur'an often uses the term 'Our' to emphasize the shared heritage and destiny of all human beings, and to remind us of our responsibility towards each other and towards our Creator.
orig: أوآباؤنا الأولون

translation: Say, 'Yes, indeed, but you do not take admonition.'
interpretation: The verse is a response from the Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) to the disbelievers who rejected his message. The Prophet is told to say 'yes' to their rejection, indicating that the truth of his message will ultimately be proven true, regardless of their current disbelief. The phrase 'you do not take admonition' implies that the disbelievers are not heeding the warning and guidance in the message, and are therefore willfully persisting in their error.
orig: قل نعم وأنتم داخرون

translation: It is but a single (simple) admonition, and when afterwards they see the painful penalty,
interpretation: The verse refers to a warning or admonition that is being given, and describes it as a simple or single one. The verse suggests that this warning is not complicated or difficult to understand, but rather straightforward. The second part of the verse describes the 'painful penalty' that the people will see or experience after the warning. This penalty serves as a consequence for not heeding the warning, and emphasizes the seriousness of the matter. The verse highlights the importance of taking admonitions seriously and acting upon them before it is too late.
orig: فإنما هي زجرة واحدة فإذا هم ينظرون

translation: And they will say, 'Woe to us! This is the Day of Judgment.'
interpretation: The verse describes the moment of realization and regret for those who did not heed the warnings and continue to live in sin and injustice. The Day of Judgment, or 'Yawm al-Din' in Arabic, is a fundamental concept in Islamic eschatology, referring to the final day of reckoning when all human beings will be held accountable for their actions and be judged accordingly. The verse conveys the overwhelming sense of fear, guilt, and despair that will be experienced by those who face the consequences of their actions, as they come to the stark realization that it is too late for repentance and salvation.
orig: وقالوا يا ويلنا هذا يوم الدين

translation: This is the Day of Judgment which you were denying.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the Day of Judgment, which has been described in previous verses of the Qur'an. On this day, all people will be held accountable for their actions, and they will not be able to deny or reject it. The verse emphasizes the reality of the Day of Judgment, which the disbelievers had previously denied and rejected. The verse serves as a reminder of the consequences of disbelief and rejection of the truth, and the certainty of the Day of Judgment.
orig: هذا يوم الفصل الذي كنتم به تكذبون

translation: Gather together those who were unjust, as well as their spouses, and whatever they used to worship
interpretation: The verse orders the Prophet Muhammad to gather the unjust people, along with their spouses, and the things they used to worship instead of Allah. This commandment serves as a warning to the unjust and a call for them to abandon their ways and repent. By gathering them together, the Prophet can convey the message of Islam and give them a chance to embrace the true faith before it is too late. The verse also highlights the seriousness of associating other deities with Allah, which is considered a grave sin in Islam.
orig: احشروا الذين ظلموا وأزواجهم وما كانوا يعبدون

translation: And warn them of the Day of Regret, when the matter will be decided: indeed, they are negligent and they do not believe.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the duty of the Prophet (peace be upon him) to warn the disbelievers of the consequences of their actions, specifically on the Day of Judgment. The verse highlights the importance of this warning, as the people are described as being negligent and disbelieving. The 'Day of Regret' refers to the Day of Judgment, when the fate of all people will be determined and it will be too late for repentance. The verse emphasizes the urgency of the warning, as the people are not taking the matter seriously and are not prepared for the consequences of their actions.
orig: من دون الله فاهدوهم إلى صراط الجحيم

translation: And their fate is upon them, indeed they are the ones who will be questioned.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the idea that people are responsible for their own actions and will be held accountable for them. The phrase 'their fate is upon them' implies that the consequences of their actions are inevitable and unavoidable. The statement 'they are the ones who will be questioned' highlights the importance of individual responsibility and the reality of divine judgement. The verse serves as a reminder that each person will be held accountable for their actions and will face the consequences of their decisions in the afterlife.
orig: وقفوهم إنهم مسئولون

translation: What is [the matter] with you that you do not support one another?
interpretation: The verse is a rhetorical question, addressed to a group of people who are not supporting or helping one another. The verse highlights the importance of unity and cooperation among people and the negative consequences of disunity and division. The verse may be interpreted as a call to action, urging the people to come together and support one another. It may also serve as a criticism of those who are not fulfilling their obligations towards one another and are instead acting in a selfish or individualistic manner.
orig: ما لكم لا تناصرون

translation: They are, this day, submitting (to God in Islam or to the will of God)
interpretation: The verse speaks about a group of people who have accepted Islam or submitted to the will of God. The use of the present tense 'they are' indicates that this submission is happening in the present moment. The verse emphasizes the finality of their decision, as it uses the word 'this day', indicating that there is no turning back. The verse serves as a reminder that submission to God's will is the only way to true peace and contentment.
orig: بل هم اليوم مستسلمون

translation: And some of them turn to others, questioning
interpretation: The verse describes a scene where some individuals are turning to others within a group, engaging in a question-and-answer dialogue. The exact nature of the conversation is not specified, but it is clear that there is a dialogue taking place. The verse may be emphasizing the importance of communication and dialogue among people, encouraging them to engage in discussions and seek understanding from one another.
orig: وأقبل بعضهم على بعض يتساءلون

translation: They said, 'Indeed, you have come to us from the right.'
interpretation: The verse describes the words of the people as they see the arrival of the angels or the messengers from the right side. The people may have considered the right side as a sign of blessing or good omen. However, the verse does not provide further context about the situation, leaving it to the interpretation of the readers. Some may interpret it as a reference to the Day of Judgment, while others may see it as a part of a story of a specific prophet and his people. Overall, the verse emphasizes the significance of the arrival of the messengers from the right side, which could be interpreted as a sign of divine intervention or guidance.
orig: قالوا إنكم كنتم تأتوننا عن اليمين

translation: They said, 'No, but you are not believers.'
interpretation: The verse shows a group of people rejecting the faith of others, calling them 'not believers'. The verse highlights the rejection and disbelief of the people, and the division it creates between different groups. The verse may serve as a reminder of the consequences of rejecting others' beliefs and the importance of acceptance and respect towards others' faiths.
orig: قالوا بل لم تكونوا مؤمنين

translation: And We never had control over you. Rather, you were a transgressing people.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes that God never had control or power over the people, but rather it was the people themselves who were transgressors and acted unjustly. This highlights the agency of human beings in their actions and the consequences that follow. The verse serves as a reminder that individuals are responsible for their own actions and that they will be held accountable for them.
orig: وما كان لنا عليكم من سلطان بل كنتم قوما طاغين

translation: Indeed, we are among the wrongdoers, unless our Lord has mercy on us.
interpretation: The verse is a statement of humility and recognition of one's sins. The speaker acknowledges that they are among the wrongdoers, but they also express hope for God's mercy. The verse highlights the importance of seeking forgiveness and recognizing one's mistakes, as well as the ultimate power of God's mercy in determining one's fate.
orig: فحق علينا قول ربنا إنا لذائقون

translation: So we led you astray, indeed We were astray ourselves.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the consequences of leading others astray. Here, the speaker admits to having led others astray, but also acknowledges that they themselves were astray. This verse can be interpreted as a reminder that those who lead others astray will ultimately be responsible for their own actions. It also highlights the harmful effects of leading others astray and the importance of guiding people towards the right path.
orig: فأغويناكم إنا كنا غاوين

translation: For indeed, on that day they will be sharing in the punishment.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the fate of those who are unjust and disbelievers. They will be sharing in the punishment on the Day of Judgment. The verse emphasizes the unity of the punishment, indicating that all those who have committed sins and disbelieved in God will be treated equally and will receive the same punishment, regardless of their worldly status or power. The verse serves as a warning to those who continue to commit sins and disbelieve in God, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: فإنهم يومئذ في العذاب مشتركون

translation: We treat the criminals in this way.
interpretation: The verse is a statement from God that He will punish criminals for their wrongdoings. The verse emphasizes the certainty of the punishment for those who commit crimes and act unjustly. It serves as a warning to those who engage in criminal activities and a reminder that they will be held accountable for their actions.
orig: إنا كذلك نفعل بالمجرمين

translation: They were arrogant in the face of the truth when it was said to them: 'There is no deity but Allah.'
interpretation: The verse describes the attitude of certain people when they were presented with the truth of Islam, that there is no deity but Allah. Instead of accepting this truth, they responded with arrogance and rejected the message. This verse serves as a reminder that arrogance and rejection of the truth will not be accepted by God and may result in negative consequences.
orig: إنهم كانوا إذا قيل لهم لا إله إلا الله يستكبرون

translation: And they say, 'Shall we abandon our gods for a poet possessed?'
interpretation: The verse is a reference to the disbelievers' response to the Prophet Muhammad's message. They rejected his message and accused him of being a mad poet who wanted them to abandon their traditional deities. The verse highlights the resistance and denial of the disbelievers towards the truth and their unwillingness to accept the message of Islam.
orig: ويقولون أئنا لتاركو آلهتنا لشاعر مجنون

translation: But indeed, he who returns repentant [to Allah] and does righteousness - then indeed, he returns to Allah with [sincere] repentance.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the reward for those who repent and do righteous deeds. The verse emphasizes the importance of returning to Allah through repentance and righteous actions. This verse serves as a message of hope and mercy for those who have strayed from the path of righteousness, indicating that it is never too late to turn back to Allah and seek His forgiveness. The verse encourages believers to strive for righteousness and to constantly seek Allah's forgiveness and mercy.
orig: بل جاء بالحق وصدق المرسلين

translation: Indeed, you are tasters of the painful punishment.
interpretation: The verse is a statement directed towards a specific group of people, informing them that they will experience a severe and painful punishment. This punishment is a consequence of their actions and serves as a form of retribution for the wrongs they have committed. The verse emphasizes the severity and intensity of the punishment, highlighting its painful nature and the suffering that it will cause. The verse is a warning to those who engage in unjust and sinful behavior, reminding them of the inevitable consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: إنكم لذائقو العذاب الأليم

translation: And you will not be rewarded except for what you used to do.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the principle of 'just deserts', that is, people will be rewarded or punished in the afterlife based on their actions and deeds in this world. The verse serves as a reminder that the consequences of one's actions are inescapable and that each person bears the responsibility for their own actions. The verse encourages people to do good deeds and avoid evil, as they will be held accountable for their choices in the afterlife.
orig: وما تجزون إلا ما كنتم تعملون

translation: Except the servants of Allah, the purified.
interpretation: The verse distinguishes between two groups of people: those who are servants of Allah and are purified, and everyone else. The 'purified' are those who have been chosen and protected by Allah, and are free from the taint of sin and error. This verse suggests that these individuals are exempt from the fate that befalls others, which may be a reference to divine punishment for wrongdoing. The verse may serve as a reminder to strive for purity and righteousness, and to seek protection and favor from Allah.
orig: إلا عباد الله المخلصين

translation: They will have a known provision
interpretation: The verse speaks about the provision that has been determined for certain individuals. The provision is described as 'known', indicating that it is predestined and fixed. The verse may be referring to the sustenance and resources that have been allocated for people in this world, or it could be referring to the rewards that have been prepared for the righteous in the hereafter. Regardless of the interpretation, the verse highlights the idea that everything that happens in this world, including the provision that people receive, is according to God's will and decree.
orig: أولئك لهم رزق معلوم

translation: Fruits and dates as a provision.
interpretation: The phrase 'Fruits and dates as a provision' is a metaphorical expression that refers to the blessings and sustenance that God provides for humanity. The fruits and dates are symbols of the bounties of the earth and the goodness that comes from it. The provision is a reminder that God is the one who provides for His creation, and that all good things come from Him. This phrase can be interpreted as a reminder to be grateful for the blessings that we have, and to recognize that they come from God. It can also be seen as a call to use these blessings in a responsible and just way, sharing them with others and not hoarding them for ourselves.
orig: فواكه وهم مكرمون

translation: In gardens of delight
interpretation: The phrase 'In gardens of delight' is a description of paradise in Islamic belief. It is a place of eternal happiness and bliss, where believers will be rewarded for their good deeds in this world. The gardens of delight are filled with all kinds of delights and pleasures, including beautiful gardens, flowing rivers, and magnificent palaces. It is a place where all desires are fulfilled and where there is no suffering or hardship. The phrase is often used in the Qur'an to describe the reward that awaits the righteous and the believers in the afterlife.
orig: في جنات النعيم

translation: on two crossed (or confronting) lines
interpretation: The phrase 'on two crossed (or confronting) lines' is a metaphorical description of a situation of conflict or opposition between two parties or forces. It can refer to any situation where there is a clear division or disagreement, such as in a debate, a dispute, or a battle. The image of two lines crossing or confronting each other conveys the idea of a clash or collision, emphasizing the tension and hostility between the two sides. The phrase can serve as a reminder of the dangers of division and the importance of finding common ground and resolving conflicts through dialogue and understanding.
orig: على سرر متقابلين

translation: A cup or a vessel from [of] My Lord [is being] circulated among them.
interpretation: The verse describes a cup or a vessel being passed around among a group of people, and this cup is from the Lord. While the exact meaning of this verse is open to interpretation, it is often understood as a metaphor for the blessings or trials that God sends down to his creation. In this context, the verse can be interpreted as a reminder that God is constantly watching over his creation and that every moment contains a message or a sign from Him. It could also be interpreted as a warning that the blessings or trials that God sends down should not be taken for granted, but should be received with gratitude and humility.
orig: يطاف عليهم بكأس من معين

translation: White, pleasant to the drinkers.
interpretation: The verse is describing the characteristics of a drink, stating that it is white and pleasant to those who drink it. The verse may be referring to milk or another type of drink that has these qualities. The verse may be emphasizing the positive qualities of the drink, highlighting its desirability and appeal. The verse can be interpreted as a reminder to appreciate and enjoy the good things in life, while also recognizing that they come from God.
orig: بيضاء لذة للشاربين

translation: In it (the heaven) there is no darkness, and they (the angels) glorify (God) night and day, and they never get tired.
interpretation: The verse describes the heaven as a place free from any darkness and a place where the angels glorify God continuously, both day and night, without ever getting tired. This portrays heaven as a place of light, peace, and constant worship of God, without any interruption or end. It highlights the perfection and the glory of heaven, and the constant devotion of the angels, contrasting it with the imperfections and limitations of the earthly life.
orig: لا فيها غول ولا هم عنها ينزفون

translation: And by them (the unbelievers) are women limiting their gaze (to only one),
interpretation: The verse refers to women who limit their gaze, meaning they lower their gaze and avoid looking at non-mahram men. This is a characteristic of modest and righteous women. The verse is emphasizing the importance of modesty and chastity for women and is a reminder for them to uphold these virtues.
orig: وعندهم قاصرات الطرف عين

translation: Like eggs that are smashed.
interpretation: The verse uses the simile 'Like eggs that are smashed' to describe the appearance of the people when they are resurrected on the Day of Judgment. The simile conveys the fragility and vulnerability of the human body, and the dramatic transformation it undergoes at the time of resurrection. The verse emphasizes the power and might of God, who is capable of reassembling and bringing back to life the scattered parts of the human body, despite its seemingly insignificant and fragile nature.
orig: كأنهن بيض مكنون

translation: And some of them turn to others, asking questions.
interpretation: The verse describes a scene where some people are turning to others among their group to ask questions. The verse is part of a larger narrative in the Qyar'an that describes a group of people being questioned by God about their actions and beliefs. The verse highlights the importance of seeking knowledge and understanding, particularly in matters of faith and morality. It suggests that asking questions and seeking answers is a natural and necessary part of the human experience, and is encouraged in the pursuit of truth and understanding.
orig: فأقبل بعضهم على بعض يتساءلون

translation: A speaker among them said, 'Indeed, I had a close friend,'
interpretation: The verse relates a conversation among a group of people, where one of them expresses his regret and sadness over the loss of a close friend. The use of the past tense suggests that the friend has passed away or is no longer present. The verse emphasizes the sense of loss and the pain of separation, and may serve as a reminder of the fleeting nature of human relationships and the importance of cherishing them while they last.
orig: قال قائل منهم إني كان لي قرين

translation: It is only those who believe in Our signs and acknowledge them that are the truly faithful.
interpretation: The verse highlights the criteria for true faith, which is based on belief in the signs of God and acknowledging them. Those who possess true faith are those who not only believe in God, but also recognize and accept the evidence of His existence and power in the world around them. This interpretation emphasizes the importance of both belief and action in the Islamic faith.
orig: يقول أإنك لمن المصدقين

translation: If we are forgotten, are we not in truth (like) scattered dust and bones?
interpretation: The verse is a rhetorical question spoken by the people who are facing the reality of their own mortality and insignificance. They acknowledge that if they were to be forgotten, they would be no different from scattered dust and bones. The verse highlights the transience of human life and the inevitability of death. It serves as a reminder of the fleeting nature of worldly accomplishments and the ultimate insignificance of human existence in the grand scheme of things.
orig: أإذا متنا وكنا ترابا وعظاما أإنا لمدينون

translation: He said, 'Are you then watchers?'
interpretation: The verse is a continuation of a conversation between the Prophet Moses and the people of Pharaoh. In this particular verse, Pharaoh or one of his officials questions Moses and his followers, asking if they are 'watchers' or those who stay up at night to worship their Lord. The verse can be interpreted as a rhetorical question meant to mock and belittle the Israelites, implying that they are foolish and delusional for believing in a higher power. It can also be interpreted as a genuine question, reflecting the Pharaoh's confusion and misunderstanding of the Israelites' faith. In either case, the verse highlights the tension and conflict between the two groups and sets the stage for the larger narrative of the Israelites' struggle for freedom and liberation.
orig: قال هل أنتم مطلعون

translation: So let him ascend and look, then look at Hell, the punishment.
interpretation: The verse describes a command for someone to ascend and look, and then to look at Hell and the punishment. The verse may be interpreted as a warning to the person being addressed, urging them to consider the consequences of their actions and the reality of Hell. The verse emphasizes the importance of reflection and contemplation, encouraging the person to consider the reality of the afterlife and the punishment that awaits those who do not repent and turn to God. The verse serves as a reminder of the urgency of repentance and the need to seek God's forgiveness before it is too late.
orig: فاطلع فرآه في سواء الجحيم

translation: Allah says, 'Indeed, if you should be patient and fear Allah, their plot will not harm you at all.',
interpretation: The verse speaks about the protection and safety that comes from having patience and fearing God. The verse promises that if one is patient and has taqwa (fear of God), then the plots of others will not harm them. This verse is often interpreted as a reminder that those who are patient and mindful of God will be protected from the harm and difficulties that come their way, whether it be from other people or from the challenges of life. The verse encourages believers to be patient and to have taqwa, and to trust in God's protection and care.
orig: قال تالله إن كدت لتردين

translation: And if it were not for the grace of my Lord, I would surely be among those brought near (to destruction).
interpretation: The verse expresses gratitude and acknowledges the saving grace of the speaker's Lord. It implies that without the Lord's mercy, the speaker would have been among those who are destroyed. The verse can be interpreted as a reminder of the importance of gratitude and recognition of one's dependence on God's grace. It also highlights the fragility of human existence and the role of divine intervention in preserving and protecting individuals from harm.
orig: ولولا نعمة ربي لكنت من المحضرين

translation: Or are We then to leave it in its (corrupt) state?
interpretation: The verse is a rhetorical question, addressed to the believers, asking whether Allah should leave a corrupt or unjust situation unchanged. The implication is that Allah will not leave it unchanged and will take action to correct the situation. The verse can be understood as a reminder that Allah is aware of the corruption and injustice in the world and will ultimately bring about justice.
orig: أفما نحن بميتين

translation: Except our first death, and we shall not be punished.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the inevitability of death and the finality of punishment in the afterlife. The phrase 'our first death' refers to the physical death that all humans will experience. The second part of the verse emphasizes that there will be no further punishment after death, indicating that the judgment and reckoning of one's actions will occur in the afterlife. The verse can be interpreted as a reminder of the importance of leading a righteous life and preparing for the afterlife, as there will be no opportunity for repentance or making amends after death.
orig: إلا موتتنا الأولى وما نحن بمعذبين

translation: Indeed, this is the great victory.
interpretation: The verse speaks about 'the great victory' that has been achieved. The victory being referred to here is not specified, but it could refer to success in a battle, the triumph of good over evil, or the attainment of a highly sought-after goal. The use of the word 'great' emphasizes the significance and importance of the victory, highlighting its positive impact and significance. The verse serves as a reminder of the rewards that come from perseverance, hard work, and determination, and the importance of recognizing and celebrating these achievements.
orig: إن هذا لهو الفوز العظيم

translation: So let the workers work in earnest.
interpretation: The verse encourages people to work hard and put in effort towards achieving their goals. The verse can be interpreted as a call to action, urging people to strive for success and not be idle or lazy. It suggests that those who are willing to put in the work and make an effort will be rewarded for their efforts.
orig: لمثل هذا فليعمل العاملون

translation: Is this better as a reminder or the wood of the Zaqqum tree?
interpretation: The verse presents a rhetorical question, contrasting the revelation of the Qur'an (described as "this" and as a reminder) with the "wood of the Zaqqum tree." The Zaqqum tree is a symbol of punishment in the afterlife for unbelievers, as mentioned in other verses of the Qur'an. The verse challenges its audience to consider which of the two options is better: the guidance and reminder provided by the Qur'an, or the punishment represented by the Zaqqum tree. The verse serves as an invitation for the listener or reader to choose the right path and avoid the consequences of disbelief and rejection of God's message.
orig: أذلك خير نزلا أم شجرة الزقوم

translation: We made it (i.e. wealth, status, or authority) a trial for the unjust.
interpretation: The verse refers to the blessings of wealth, status, or authority that have been given to certain individuals or groups of people. These blessings are described as a "trial" or "test" (fitnah) for the unjust, meaning that they will be held accountable for how they use and abuse their privileged positions. The verse serves as a warning to those who have been given much in this world, but fail to use their blessings in a just and righteous manner. It reminds them that they will be questioned and judged based on how they have wielded their power and influence, and whether they have used it to oppress others or to uplift and support them.
orig: إنا جعلناها فتنة للظالمين

translation: Indeed, it is a tree that emerges at the base of the Hellfire.
interpretation: The verse refers to a tree that is located at the base of Hellfire. While the Qur'an does not provide further details about this tree, its proximity to the Hellfire suggests that it is a symbol of punishment and torment.
