The tree serves as a warning to those who disbelieve in God and reject His message, reminding them of the dire consequences that await them in the afterlife. The tree may also represent a barrier that prevents the disbelievers from escaping the punishment of Hellfire.
orig: إنها شجرة تخرج في أصل الجحيم

translation: It (the sun) rises as if (it is) the heads of the devils.
interpretation: The verse uses a powerful metaphor to describe the rising of the sun, comparing it to the heads of the devils. This metaphor emphasizes the intense heat and brightness of the sun, which can be overwhelming and even feel malevolent, like the devils. The verse can be interpreted as a reminder of the power and majesty of God's creation, and of the need for humans to acknowledge and submit to that power. The comparison of the sun to the heads of the devils also serves as a warning to those who are arrogant and defiant, reminding them of the consequences of their pride and disobedience towards God.
orig: طلعها كأنه رءوس الشياطين

translation: For they eat from it, then they become fully bellied.
interpretation: The verse is a description of people who consume a certain thing (which is not specified in the verse) until they are full or satiated. The verse could be a metaphorical reference to people who indulge in worldly pleasures or sins, consuming more than they need until they are 'full' or content. The verse may serve as a warning to those who are consumed by their desires and pleasures, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the importance of moderation and self-control.
orig: فإنهم لآكلون منها فمالئون منها البطون

translation: Then upon them is a similitude of boiling water, (or a rain) of tar, which they will sip.
interpretation: The verse uses a powerful and vivid metaphor to describe the punishment that awaits the unbelievers. The image of boiling water or a rain of tar that they will sip is a reference to the intense and unbearable suffering that they will experience in the afterlife. The word 'similitude' indicates that this is a comparison or a metaphor, and the phrase 'they will sip' highlights the inevitability and inescapability of this punishment. The verse serves as a warning to those who reject God's message and a reminder of the consequences of their actions.
orig: ثم إن لهم عليها لشوبا من حميم

translation: Then indeed, their return is to Hell.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destiny of certain people, whose return is to Hell. The verse emphasizes the finality of their fate and the inevitability of their punishment. The verse serves as a warning to those who persist in their sins and wrongdoings, reminding them of the severe consequences of their actions and the unavoidable reality of Hell.
orig: ثم إن مرجعهم لإلى الجحيم

translation: Indeed, they have followed their forefathers, [who were] astray.
interpretation: The verse refers to a group of people who have followed in the footsteps of their misguided ancestors. By using the word 'indeed', the verse emphasizes the certainty of their misguidance. The verse can be interpreted as a warning against blindly following the ways of previous generations without considering the truth and guidance of Islam. It reminds us to seek knowledge, reflect on our beliefs and practices, and strive for righteousness and guidance, rather than merely following tradition or the ways of our forebears.
orig: إنهم ألفوا آباءهم ضالين

translation: So they will carry on their foreheads the consequence of their deeds.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the consequences of people's actions, which will be manifested on their foreheads. The image of the consequence being carried on the forehead suggests that it will be evident and impossible to hide. The verse serves as a reminder that every action has a consequence and that people will be held accountable for their deeds, both good and bad. It emphasizes the importance of leading a righteous life and avoiding sin and wrongdoing.
orig: فهم على آثارهم يهرعون

translation: And indeed, before them, many of the first [people] were unguided.
interpretation: The verse refers to the fact that many civilizations and societies before the time of the Prophet Muhammad had gone astray and were unguided. This is used as a reminder that the people of the Prophet's time should not feel immune to the same fate. It emphasizes the importance of guidance and staying on the right path, and serves as a warning that following the wrong path can lead to a similar fate as those who came before.
orig: ولقد ضل قبلهم أكثر الأولين

translation: And We had certainly sent warners among them.
interpretation: The verse refers to the sending of messengers or warners by God to warn the people of the consequences of their actions and to guide them towards the right path. The use of the past tense 'We had certainly sent' indicates that the sending of the warners is a historical fact and that the people had no excuse for not heeding their message.
orig: ولقد أرسلنا فيهم منذرين

translation: So see how was the end of the warners.
interpretation: The verse refers to the consequences faced by those who rejected the warnings and messages of the prophets and messengers sent by God. The verse encourages the reader to reflect on the fate of the previous warners and their people, and to draw lessons from their experiences. The verse serves as a reminder that those who persist in ignoring the warnings and guidance of God will ultimately face negative consequences, while those who heed the warnings and repent will be rewarded.
orig: فانظر كيف كان عاقبة المنذرين

translation: Except the servants of Allah, the purified.
interpretation: The verse distinguishes between two groups of people: those who are servants of Allah and are purified, and everyone else. The verse implies that the servants of Allah are those who have purified themselves through their faith and actions. These individuals will be saved from the punishment that will be faced by others. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of being a true servant of Allah and striving for purification through righteous actions.
orig: إلا عباد الله المخلصين

translation: And indeed We once invited Noah, so indeed he was of the grateful.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the invitation of Prophet Noah by God. The verse highlights that Noah responded positively to the invitation, and he was among the grateful ones. This verse can be interpreted as a reminder of the importance of responding positively to God's call and being grateful for His guidance and blessings. It also serves as an example for individuals to be receptive and thankful for the guidance and opportunities presented to them.
orig: ولقد نادانا نوح فلنعم المجيبون

translation: And We saved him and his family from the great distress.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the salvation of an individual and their family from a great distress or hardship. The verse highlights the mercy and power of God in delivering His believers from adversity. The verse serves as a reminder of God's compassion and care for those who trust in Him, and of His ability to rescue them from even the most difficult of circumstances.
orig: ونجيناه وأهله من الكرب العظيم

translation: And We made their descendants the survivors.
interpretation: The verse speaks about a group of people who have been replaced by their descendants. The descendants are described as the 'survivors', indicating that they are the ones who have continued to live on and carry on the legacy of their ancestors. The verse may be referring to a specific group of people who have been replaced in this way, or it may be a more general statement about the way that generations succeed one another. The verse highlights the continuity of life and the way that the actions and legacies of previous generations can have a lasting impact on those who come after them.
orig: وجعلنا ذريته هم الباقين

translation: And We shall leave it in the later [generations] to come.
interpretation: The verse speaks about leaving something (it is unclear from the verse what that is) for the future generations. This could mean that God will allow the people to continue in their ways and face the consequences of their actions, even after the speaker (who is likely a prophet) is gone. Alternatively, it could mean that God will leave a legacy or a message for future generations to learn from. The verse emphasizes the continuity of human existence and the long-term consequences of our actions, reminding us that our choices do not only affect us, but also future generations.
orig: وتركنا عليه في الآخرين

translation: And peace be upon Noah in the worlds.
interpretation: The verse is a greeting of peace and blessings upon the prophet Noah. The phrase 'in the worlds' indicates that this greeting applies to Noah in all times and places. This verse serves as a reminder of the respect and reverence due to the prophets of God and the importance of showing kindness and compassion towards them.
orig: سلام على نوح في العالمين

translation: Indeed, we reward the doers of good in like manner.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the principle of 'just deserts' in Islam, where good deeds are rewarded with good outcomes. The phrase 'doers of good' is all-encompassing, and includes all acts of kindness, compassion, and righteousness. The verse serves as a reminder that good deeds do not go unnoticed or unrewarded, and encourages believers to strive for righteousness and goodness in all their actions.
orig: إنا كذلك نجزي المحسنين

translation: Indeed, among our worshippers, the believers
interpretation: The verse highlights a specific group of people, those who are both worshippers of God and believers. By distinguishing this group as 'among our worshippers', the verse suggests that these believers hold a special place in the eyes of God. This serves as a reminder of the importance of faith and devotion, and the rewards that come with it.
orig: إنه من عبادنا المؤمنين

translation: Then We drowned the others.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the punishment of a group of people by drowning. The phrase 'the others' implies that this is not the first group of people to be punished, but rather a second group. The use of the past tense indicates that this event has already taken place. The verse may be interpreted as a warning to those who reject God's message and persist in disbelief, as they may face a similar punishment. It also emphasizes God's power and control over all of His creations, including the ability to cause natural disasters such as floods.
orig: ثم أغرقنا الآخرين

translation: And indeed, among his followers was Abraham.
interpretation: This verse is speaking about the followers or the community of a certain person, but the specific identity of this person is not mentioned in the verse itself. The verse clarifies that among this group of followers was the prophet Abraham. The verse could be emphasizing the significance of Abraham's inclusion in this group, highlighting his status as a respected and important figure among his followers. The verse may also be reminding the reader of the continuity and connection between different prophets and their followers throughout history, and the importance of maintaining this connection and following in the footsteps of these prophets in faith and actions.
orig: وإن من شيعته لإبراهيم

translation: When his Lord revealed to his heart
interpretation: The verse speaks about a person who has received divine revelation or guidance from their Lord. The Lord revealed to the person's heart, indicating the deep and personal nature of the revelation. The verse suggests that the person has undergone a profound spiritual experience and has been chosen as a recipient of divine wisdom and knowledge. The verse may also serve as a reminder that true guidance and understanding come from within, from the depth of one's heart and soul, rather than from external sources or material possessions.
orig: إذ جاء ربه بقلب سليم

translation: When he said to his father and his people, 'What do you worship?'
interpretation: The verse recounts a conversation where the speaker, a prophet or a messenger of God, questions his father and community about their object of worship. This verse highlights the importance of monotheism and the distinction between the worship of the one true God and the worship of false idols or deities. The verse also emphasizes the role of prophets and messengers in guiding people towards the right path and calling them to abandon their false beliefs and practices.
orig: إذ قال لأبيه وقومه ماذا تعبدون

translation: Then do you take besides Him allies, such as have no power to benefit or harm themselves?
interpretation: The verse questions the belief of those who worship gods other than Allah, stating that these gods have no power to benefit or harm themselves, let alone those who worship them. The verse challenges the notion of polytheism and emphasizes the power and exclusivity of Allah as the only deity worthy of worship. The verse serves as a reminder to those who have strayed from the true path, urging them to reflect on the nature of their beliefs and the futility of worshipping false deities.
orig: أئفكا آلهة دون الله تريدون

translation: So what is your opinion about the Lord of the worlds?
interpretation: The verse is a rhetorical question, posed by the Qur'an to the reader or listener, asking for their opinion about the Lord of the worlds. This question serves to encourage reflection and contemplation about the nature of God, the Creator and Sustainer of the universe. The verse suggests that the true understanding of God's greatness and majesty is beyond human comprehension and invites the reader or listener to submit themselves to God's will in humility and devotion.
orig: فما ظنكم برب العالمين

translation: Then look at the stars, fainting.
interpretation: The verse is a command to look at the stars, but the meaning of 'fainting' is unclear and has been interpreted in different ways by scholars. Some interpret it as a metaphor for the stars' twinkling or their gradual disappearance at dawn, while others interpret it as a warning of the transience of human existence and the insignificance of human beings in the face of God's creation. Overall, the verse can be interpreted as an invitation to contemplate the beauty and mystery of the universe and to reflect on the place of human beings in the grand scheme of things.
orig: فنظر نظرة في النجوم

translation: And he said, 'Indeed, I am ill.'
interpretation: The verse relates the words of a person who, when faced with a responsibility or task, claimed to be ill. While the verse does not provide context for the illness or the task at hand, it serves as a reminder of the human tendency to avoid or shirk from duties, particularly when they become difficult or challenging. It highlights the importance of honesty and integrity, and the consequences of deception and dishonesty.
orig: فقال إني سقيم

translation: And take turns in carrying it; and in this are signs for a people who reason.
interpretation: The verse refers to a command to a group of people to take turns in carrying or attending to a certain responsibility or duty. The verse suggests that by doing so, these people can reflect on the deeper meaning and wisdom behind this task and can use it as an opportunity for contemplation and reflection. The verse implies that there are valuable lessons and insights that can be gained from fulfilling one's responsibilities and that by sharing these responsibilities with others, a community can come together and support each other in their pursuit of knowledge and understanding.
orig: فتولوا عنه مدبرين

translation: So they turned away from their gods. Then said [to them], 'Will you worship what you yourself carve?',
interpretation: The verse speaks about people who turned away from their gods and began to worship idols that they had created themselves. The verse highlights the absurdity of worshiping something that one has created, and challenges the people to consider the foolishness of their actions. The verse serves as a reminder to the importance of worshiping the one true God, and the dangers of idolatry and false worship.
orig: فراغ إلى آلهتهم فقال ألا تأكلون

translation: What is the matter with you that you do not speak?
interpretation: The verse is a question directed towards a group of people, asking them why they are not speaking. The context of the verse determines the reason for the question, and it is often used in the Quran to reproach people for their disbelief or disobedience. The verse could be interpreted as a call for the people to speak up and declare their faith or to respond to a command from God. It could also be seen as a reprimand for their silence in the face of truth or a reminder for them to seek knowledge and understanding. Overall, the verse emphasizes the importance of speech and communication in religious matters and encourages people to engage in meaningful dialogue and discourse.
orig: ما لكم لا تنطقون

translation: A respite was granted to them. Then punishment seized them while they were still unfair to themselves.
interpretation: The verse speaks about a group of people who were given respite or a chance to repent, but they continued to commit injustices and wrongdoings. As a result, punishment was meted out to them while they were still engaged in their unjust ways. The verse highlights the importance of taking advantage of the opportunities given for repentance and the severe consequences of ignoring them.
orig: فراغ عليهم ضربا باليمين

translation: So turn to Him all of you, O believers, so that you may be successful.
interpretation: The verse is a command to the believers to turn to God and seek His guidance and help. The phrase 'that you may be successful' indicates that following God's path and commandments leads to success in this life and the hereafter. The verse emphasizes the importance of unity and collective action among the believers, and the need to seek God's guidance and help in all matters.
orig: فأقبلوا إليه يزفون

translation: Said He: 'Do you worship what you yourselves carve?
interpretation: The verse is a rhetorical question posed by God, addressing those who worship idols that they themselves have created. The verse highlights the absurdity of worshipping man-made objects, emphasizing the foolishness of attributing divinity to something that is not divine. The verse serves as a call to monotheism and a reminder of the importance of worshipping the one true God, who is free from any imperfections and limitations.
orig: قال أتعبدون ما تنحتون

translation: And it is Allah who created you, then provided for you, then will cause your death, and then will give you life.
interpretation: The verse highlights the power and control of Allah over all aspects of human life. It emphasizes that Allah is the creator of human beings, and that it is He who provides for them and ultimately causes their death. However, the verse also offers a message of hope, as it states that Allah will give life again, which can be interpreted as a reference to the resurrection and the Day of Judgment. This verse encourages believers to reflect on their dependence on Allah, and to remember that He has power over all things, including life and death.
orig: والله خلقكم وما تعملون

translation: They said, 'Build for him a tower', so they threw him into the Hellfire
interpretation: The verse speaks about a group of people who, in their disbelief and rejection of God's messenger, commanded to build a tower for him and then threw him into the Hellfire. The verse is a condemnation of the actions of these disbelievers, who rejected the message of God's messenger and sought to harm him. It serves as a reminder of the severe consequences of rejecting God's message and harming His messengers.
orig: قالوا ابنوا له بنيانا فألقوه في الجحيم

translation: But they plotted a plot against him, and We made them the lowest.
interpretation: The verse speaks about a group of people who plotted against a person, but their plot was unsuccessful. As a result, God made them 'the lowest', which can be interpreted as a metaphor for being humiliated, defeated, or punished. The verse highlights the consequences of plotting against others and the ultimate power of God over human affairs.
orig: فأرادوا به كيدا فجعلناهم الأسفلين

translation: And he said, 'Indeed, I am going to my Lord. He will guide me.'
interpretation: The verse is a statement made by a believer who is facing a difficult situation and is putting their trust in God. The believer is expressing their belief that they will be guided by God and are going to their Lord for help and support. The verse emphasizes the believer's unwavering faith and trust in God's guidance and wisdom, even in the face of adversity. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of faith and trust in God during challenging times.
orig: وقال إني ذاهب إلى ربي سيهدين

translation: Lord, grant me from among the righteous.
interpretation: The speaker is making a supplication or prayer to God, asking for righteous people to be among their companions or associates. The verse emphasizes the value and importance of righteousness in Islam, and the desire of the speaker to be surrounded by individuals who possess this quality. It also highlights the individual's recognition of their own limitations and their need for guidance and support from righteous individuals in order to lead a virtuous life.
orig: رب هب لي من الصالحين

translation: And We gave him the good news of a gentle boy.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the good news that was given to a person, announcing the birth of a gentle and mild-tempered son. The verse may be referring to the prophet Ibrahim (Abraham) who was given the good news of the birth of his son, Ismail (Ishmael). The verse highlights the joy and blessings that come with the birth of a child and the hope for the future that they bring. It also emphasizes the importance of good character and virtues, such as gentleness and humility, in the upbringing of a child.
orig: فبشرناه بغلام حليم

translation: But when he reached with him [the age of] working with him, he said, 'O my son, indeed I have seen in a dream that I [must] sacrifice you. So see what you think.' He said, 'O my father, do as you are commanded. You will find me, if Allah wills, among the patient.'
interpretation: This verse describes the story of the prophet Ibrahim (Abraham) and his son, Isma'il (Ishmael), and their willingness to submit to God's command. Ibrahim tells his son about a dream he had in which God commanded him to sacrifice his son. Isma'il, in response, shows his obedience and submission to God by telling his father to fulfill God's command and he will be patient. This verse highlights the importance of submission and obedience to God's will, as well as the virtue of patience in the face of difficult trials and tribulations. It also serves as a reminder that God tests those whom He loves, and that these tests are opportunities for believers to prove their faith and gain rewards in the hereafter.
orig: فلما بلغ معه السعي قال يا بني إني أرى في المنام أني أذبحك فانظر ماذا ترى قال يا أبت افعل ما تؤمر ستجدني إن شاء الله من الصابرين

translation: And when they submitted and fell on their faces [in prayer]
interpretation: This verse speaks about the act of submission and humility before God. The people mentioned in this verse submitted to God and prostrated themselves in prayer. The verse emphasizes the importance of humility and submission in the act of prayer. It teaches that true prayer comes from a place of submission and recognition of God's greatness. This verse serves as a reminder to Muslims of the importance of humility and submission in their prayers, and the need to approach God with a humble and contrite heart.
orig: فلما أسلما وتله للجبين

translation: And We called out to him, 'O Abraham!',
interpretation: The verse speaks about God calling out to the prophet Ibrahim (Abraham). The use of the word 'We' in the verse indicates the greatness and majesty of God. The calling out to Ibrahim could be interpreted as a sign of God's guidance and direction towards the right path. This verse serves as a reminder of the special relationship between God and his prophets, and the role of prophets as recipients of divine guidance and messengers of God's message.
orig: وناديناه أن يا إبراهيم

translation: Indeed, [the revelation of] the Qur'an is a confirmation of that which was before it, and a clear exposition of the truth, a guidance and a mercy to the believers.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the Qur'an as a confirmation and explanation of previous revelations, and a guidance and mercy for the believers. It highlights the truth and clarity of the Qur'an, and its role in guiding and showing mercy to the believers. The verse implies that the Qur'an is a continuation and fulfillment of previous revelations, and that it provides guidance and mercy to those who believe and follow its teachings.
orig: قد صدقت الرؤيا إنا كذلك نجزي المحسنين

translation: Indeed, this is the manifest affliction.
interpretation: The verse speaks about a clear and evident affliction or calamity. The interpretation of this verse depends on the context in which it appears. It could be referring to a specific punishment or hardship that has befallen a certain group of people, or it could be a more general statement about the nature of afflictions in life. Regardless of the context, the verse emphasizes the clear and undeniable nature of the affliction. It suggests that the affliction is not something that can be easily ignored or dismissed, but is a clear and evident reality that demands attention and contemplation. The verse may serve as a reminder to those who are facing difficulties in life to be patient and steadfast, and to seek lessons and wisdom from their experiences.
orig: إن هذا لهو البلاء المبين

translation: And We gave them a great slaughter.
interpretation: The verse speaks about a group of people who were given a great slaughter or punishment by God. The verse emphasizes the severity of the punishment, which is described as 'great', indicating that it was severe and devastating. The verse serves as a reminder of the consequences of angering God and the severe punishment that can befall those who commit sins and transgressions.
orig: وفديناه بذبح عظيم

translation: And We left it alone in the later [periods].
interpretation: The verse refers to a place or thing that has been abandoned or left alone in later periods or times. The context of the verse will provide more information on what specifically is being referred to. However, the overall message of the verse emphasizes the idea of something being left in a state of neglect or abandonment, which can be interpreted as a consequence of human actions or lack thereof.
orig: وتركنا عليه في الآخرين

translation: Peace be upon Abraham.
interpretation: The verse is a greeting and a blessing, invoking peace and security upon the prophet Abraham. The verse can also be seen as a recognition of Abraham's virtues and his status as a prophet of God. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of showing respect and reverence to the prophets and messengers of God, and of the blessings that come from following their example and teachings.
orig: سلام على إبراهيم

translation: So We reward the doers of good.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the reward that God gives to those who do good. The verse emphasizes the certainty of the reward, which will be given to the 'doers of good', indicating that their actions are being recorded and will be recognized by God. The verse serves as a motivation for those who are doing good deeds, reminding them of the blessings that await them in the afterlife.
orig: كذلك نجزي المحسنين

translation: Indeed, among our worshippers, the believers
interpretation: The verse highlights a specific group of people who are described as 'worshippers' and 'believers' from among the servants of God. This group is being distinguished from others, potentially those who do not believe or do not worship God. The verse may be emphasizing the importance of belief and worship, or it may be setting the stage for a discussion or teaching about this specific group of people. The interpretation of this verse would depend on the context in which it appears.
orig: إنه من عبادنا المؤمنين

translation: And We gave him the good news of Isaac, a prophet from among the righteous.
interpretation: The verse announces the good news of the birth of Isaac, who would become a prophet and a righteous man. It emphasizes God's power and mercy in giving the good news to the person being addressed, who is likely to be Abraham, Isaac's father. The verse can also be seen as a promise of continuation and succession, as Isaac would carry on the legacy of his father and become a prophet. The verse serves as a reminder of God's goodness and grace towards his believers, and the blessings that come from following His will.
orig: وبشرناه بإسحاق نبيا من الصالحين

translation: And We blessed him and Isaac and from their descendants are those who are righteous and those who clearly wrong themselves.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the blessings that God bestowed upon Ibrahim (Abraham) and his son Ishaq (Isaac), and the continuation of these blessings to their descendants. However, the verse also mentions that among the descendants of Ibrahim and Ishaq are those who are righteous and those who wrong themselves. This division among the descendants of Ibrahim and Ishaq highlights the importance of individual actions and choices, even within a family or community, and the consequences of these actions. The verse serves as a reminder that blessings and guidance from God are not guaranteed for all descendants, but rather depend on individual actions and choices.
orig: وباركنا عليه وعلى إسحاق ومن ذريتهما محسن وظالم لنفسه مبين

translation: And We had already given grace to Moses and Aaron.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the grace and blessings that God had bestowed upon the prophets Moses and Aaron. The verse highlights the special status of these prophets and their unique role in the history of religion. The verse can be seen as a recognition of the important contributions of these figures in guiding people towards the right path and upholding the message of God.
orig: ولقد مننا على موسى وهارون

translation: And We saved them both, and their people, from a terrible distress.
interpretation: The verse speaks about God's mercy and salvation towards two individuals and their people, whom He saved from a great distress or calamity. The verse highlights God's compassion and His willingness to save and protect those who turn to Him in times of need. The verse serves as a reminder of God's benevolence and His capacity to deliver His servants from harm, encouraging believers to seek His help and refuge in times of difficulty.
orig: ونجيناهما وقومهما من الكرب العظيم

translation: And We aided them, so they became the ones who prevailed.
interpretation: The verse speaks about God's support and aid to a group of people, which led to their victory and dominance. The verse highlights the power of God's assistance and its ability to turn the tide of a situation in favor of those who are supported by Him. The verse serves as a reminder that ultimate success and victory come from God, and that those who rely on Him will be granted His help and support.
orig: ونصرناهم فكانوا هم الغالبين

translation: And We gave them two scriptures to follow.
interpretation: The verse refers to the giving of two scriptures or revelations to two different communities or peoples. The exact identity of these two communities and the scriptures they received is not specified in the verse, allowing for multiple interpretations. However, the verse emphasizes the importance of guidance and the responsibility of those who receive it. The scriptures serve as a source of wisdom and knowledge for the people, and it is their duty to follow and uphold the teachings and values contained within them. The verse also implies that the scriptures are not meant to be taken lightly, but rather to be studied, understood, and implemented in daily life.
orig: وآتيناهما الكتاب المستبين

translation: And We guided them both to the Straight Path.
interpretation: The verse speaks about guiding two entities (which are not specified in the verse) to the 'Straight Path'. The 'Straight Path' refers to the path of righteousness and truth, and it is a metaphor for the way of life that is pleasing to God. The verse emphasizes the guidance that was given to these entities, indicating that they were lost or astray before and were in need of divine guidance. The verse can be seen as a message of hope and mercy, highlighting God's willingness to guide those who seek His guidance and follow His path.
orig: وهديناهما الصراط المستقيم

translation: And We left them alone in the later generations.
interpretation: The verse refers to God's action of leaving certain people alone or abandoned in subsequent generations. The context of the verse provides insight into the reason for this abandonment, as it is mentioned in the previous verses that these people were given knowledge and power but they did not use it for the betterment of society. The verse emphasizes the consequences of their actions, which is being left alone or abandoned by God in the later generations. The verse can be interpreted as a warning to those who are given resources and opportunities but do not use them for the greater good, as they too may face abandonment and loneliness in the future.
orig: وتركنا عليهما في الآخرين

translation: Peace be upon Moses and Aaron
interpretation: The verse is a greeting of peace to the prophets Moses and Aaron. It is a recognition of their status as prophets and a sign of respect and reverence towards them. The verse can also be seen as a reminder of the importance of peace and the need for it in our lives. It encourages us to strive for peace in our relationships with others and with ourselves.
orig: سلام على موسى وهارون

translation: Indeed, we reward the doers of good.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the principle of reward for good deeds. It reassures the reader that good actions will not go unnoticed or unrewarded. The verse can be seen as a source of motivation for those who strive to do good, as it reinforces the belief that their efforts will be recognized and rewarded by a higher power. The verse can also serve as a reminder for those who are not mindful of their actions, encouraging them to reflect on their behavior and strive for goodness.
orig: إنا كذلك نجزي المحسنين

translation: Indeed, they are among Our believing servants.
interpretation: The verse highlights the status of certain individuals as being among the believing servants of God. This implies that they have shown faith and commitment to God and His teachings. The verse may be referring to a specific group of people who have demonstrated their belief in some way, or it may be a more general statement about all believers. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of faith and commitment to God, and the recognition and reward that comes with it.
orig: إنهما من عبادنا المؤمنين

translation: And indeed, Ilyas was among the messengers.
interpretation: The verse affirms that Ilyas (Elijah) was one of the messengers sent by God. This statement serves to emphasize the continuity and consistency of God's message and the prophetic tradition, which includes many prophets and messengers who were sent to different communities and nations throughout history. By recognizing Ilyas as one of the messengers, Muslims are reminded of the importance of upholding and following the teachings and examples of all the prophets, including Ilyas.
orig: وإن إلياس لمن المرسلين

translation: When he said to his people, 'Do not worship idols,'
interpretation: The verse relates the story of a prophet who calls upon his people to worship only one God and to abandon the worship of idols. The verse highlights the prophet's role as a warner and a guide, urging his people to turn away from their false gods and to embrace the true faith. The verse emphasizes the importance of monotheism in Islam and the rejection of idolatry, which is considered a grave sin in the religion.
orig: إذ قال لقومه ألا تتقون

translation: You call upon besides Allah upon that which neither benefits you nor harms [you] while you reject the best of creators.
interpretation: The verse criticizes the act of calling upon other deities or powers besides Allah, stating that these other beings cannot benefit or harm anyone, and therefore the act of calling upon them is futile. At the same time, the verse emphasizes the greatness of Allah as the best of creators, highlighting the foolishness of rejecting the one who has the power and control over all things.
orig: أتدعون بعلا وتذرون أحسن الخالقين

translation: Allah is your Lord and the Lord of your first forefathers.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the sovereignty and lordship of Allah, reminding the listeners of their ultimate accountability to Him. The reference to 'your first forefathers' serves to underscore that this principle applies not only to the present generation, but also to those who came before. It is a reminder that the covenant between humanity and Allah is a continuous one, and that all of mankind is subject to His will and judgment.
orig: الله ربكم ورب آبائكم الأولين

translation: And they denied him, so indeed, they are unaware [of the consequence].
interpretation: The verse speaks about the denial of a person or a group of people, likely a prophet or a messenger, and the consequences of their denial. The verse emphasizes the lack of awareness or understanding of the people who are denying, indicating that they do not fully comprehend the implications of their actions. The verse serves as a warning to those who deny the truth, reminding them that their actions do not go unnoticed and that there will be consequences for their denial.
orig: فكذبوه فإنهم لمحضرون

translation: Except the servants of Allah, the purified.
interpretation: The verse distinguishes between two groups of people: those who are servants of Allah and those who are not. The servants of Allah are described as 'purified', indicating that they are free from the taint of sin and impurity. This group of people will be saved from the punishment that is mentioned earlier in the verse. The verse emphasizes the importance of being a servant of Allah and living a pure and righteous life, as this is the only way to attain salvation and avoid the punishment of Allah.
orig: إلا عباد الله المخلصين

translation: And We left it (the town) among the later ones.
interpretation: The verse speaks about a town that has been abandoned or destroyed, and it has been left in ruins for the 'later ones' to see. The 'later ones' could refer to future generations or to those who come after the destruction. The verse highlights the consequences of the actions of the people of the town, and the impact of their destruction on those who come after them. It serves as a reminder of the importance of leaving a positive legacy and the impact of one's actions on future generations.
orig: وتركنا عليه في الآخرين

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: سلام على إل ياسين

translation: Indeed, we reward the doers of good in like manner.
interpretation: The verse affirms that good deeds will be rewarded in a like manner, emphasizing the principle of just retribution. It serves as a promise of reward for those who strive to do good and a motivation for people to lead a righteous life.
orig: إنا كذلك نجزي المحسنين

translation: Indeed, among our worshippers, the believers
interpretation: The verse is highlighting the category of people who are true believers and sincere in their worship of God. This verse may have been revealed in the context of emphasizing the distinction between those who truly believe and worship God, and those who are hypocrites or insincere in their faith. The verse can serve as a reminder for individuals to reflect on their own faith and actions, and to strive for sincerity and authenticity in their worship of God.
orig: إنه من عبادنا المؤمنين

translation: And indeed, Lot was among the messengers.
interpretation: The verse identifies Lot as one of the messengers sent by God. This signifies the importance of Lot's story in the Islamic tradition and his role as a prophet who delivered God's message to his people. The verse may also serve as a reminder that Lot's experiences and struggles, including his warnings to his people and their rejection of his message, are relevant to the broader themes of prophethood and divine justice in the Qur'an.
orig: وإن لوطا لمن المرسلين

translation: When We rescued him and his family all together
interpretation: The verse describes a specific instance of God's intervention to save an individual and their family. The rescue is depicted as a past event, and the use of the word 'all together' emphasizes the inclusivity of the salvation. The verse could be interpreted as a metaphor for God's protection and deliverance of the faithful from harm and adversity. The verse serves as a reminder of God's mercy and compassion towards those who believe in Him and seek His help.
orig: إذ نجيناه وأهله أجمعين

translation: Except an old woman among those who were left behind.
interpretation: The verse refers to an exception in a situation where something is being negated or excluded. In this case, the exception is 'an old woman among those who were left behind'. The exact context of the verse is not provided, but it is clear that the old woman is being distinguished from a larger group of people who are not mentioned. The verse may be implying that the old woman was spared or treated differently from the rest of the group, or it may simply be noting her presence in contrast to their absence. The interpretation of the verse depends on the context in which it appears.
orig: إلا عجوزا في الغابرين

translation: then we destroyed the others
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of a group of people as a result of divine intervention. The phrase 'then we destroyed' emphasizes the power and authority of the divine being in causing destruction. The destroyed group, referred to as 'the others', could imply a contrast or comparison with another group of people mentioned earlier in the text. This verse may serve as a reminder of the power and authority of the divine being and the consequences of actions that go against its will.
orig: ثم دمرنا الآخرين

translation: And indeed, you pass by them in the morning
interpretation: The verse describes the Prophet Muhammad and his companions passing by the ruins of previous civilizations in the morning, serving as a reminder of the transience and fragility of human life and the certainty of God's judgment. The passage of time and the continual movement of the believers contrasts with the stillness and ruin of the destroyed towns, emphasizing the consequences of their unrighteousness. The verse encourages the believers to reflect on the fate of these towns and to draw lessons from their example, in order to avoid a similar end.
orig: وإنكم لتمرون عليهم مصبحين

translation: But is it not the night that you despise?
interpretation: The verse is a rhetorical question addressed to the disbelievers who reject the signs of God and refuse to recognize the truth. The night here symbolizes the time of contemplation and reflection, and the verse is a call for the disbelievers to ponder upon the wonders of God's creation and to use this time for contemplation and reflection. The verse suggests that the disbelievers are missing out on a valuable opportunity for spiritual growth and development by despising the night and instead of using it for reflection, they are consumed by their disbelief and rejection of God's signs.
orig: وبالليل أفلا تعقلون

translation: And indeed, Yunus is among the messengers.
interpretation: The verse is a simple statement identifying Yunus (also known as Jonah) as one of the messengers of God. The verse does not provide any additional context or information about Yunus, but it serves as a reminder of the many prophets and messengers who were sent by God to guide humanity. The verse can be seen as an affirmation of the prophetic mission of Yunus, and a recognition of his role in conveying God's message to the people of his time. The verse may also serve as a source of inspiration and encouragement for those who follow the teachings of Yunus, reminding them of the long line of prophets and messengers who have come before them and who have paved the way for their own spiritual growth and development.
orig: وإن يونس لمن المرسلين

translation: When he was left alone with the loaded ship.
interpretation: The verse speaks about a person who was left alone on a ship that was fully loaded. The verse emphasizes the vulnerability and isolation of the person, who is now responsible for the safety and well-being of the ship and its cargo. The verse can be interpreted as a metaphor for the human condition, where individuals are often left alone to face the challenges and responsibilities of life. It can also be seen as a reminder of the importance of self-reliance, responsibility, and the need for careful and mindful actions in the face of potential dangers and difficulties.
orig: إذ أبق إلى الفلك المشحون

translation: And cooperate in righteousness and piety, and do not cooperate in sin and aggression.
interpretation: The verse encourages believers to work together in righteousness and piety, emphasizing the importance of collective action in upholding moral values. At the same time, it warns against cooperating in sin and aggression, suggesting that individuals should not support or participate in actions that are contrary to the teachings of Islam. The verse highlights the role of the community in promoting good and preventing harm, and serves as a reminder that individual actions have consequences that extend beyond the self.
orig: فساهم فكان من المدحضين

translation: Then the sperm-drop becomes a clinging clot; then (Allah) forms the clot into a chewed-like substance; then (Allah) forms the chewed-like substance into bones; then (Allah) clothes the bones with flesh; then He develops it into another creation. So blessed is Allah, the Best of Creators.
interpretation: The verse describes the process of creation of a human being, from the initial stage of a sperm-drop to a fully formed human. The verse emphasizes the complexity and intricacy of the creation process and the role of Allah in it, highlighting His power and greatness as the Best of Creators. The verse serves as a reminder of the miraculous nature of life and the need for gratitude and appreciation towards the Creator.
orig: فالتقمه الحوت وهو مليم

translation: But he was certainly of the musbers.
interpretation: The verse is referring to a specific individual who was known for performing the musbfh (prostration) as an act of worship. However, the verse is not providing any further context or information about this person's identity or the circumstances of their musbfh. The verse may be implying that the individual's musbfh was not sincere or not accepted by God, as the verse is preceded by a discussion of people whose good deeds will not be accepted in the afterlife. The exact interpretation of this verse depends on its context within the Qur'an and the hadith literature.
orig: فلولا أنه كان من المسبحين

translation: Carrying him in his mother's womb until the day he is resurrected.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the process of carrying a child in the womb until the day of resurrection. This verse is often interpreted as a metaphor for the care and protection that God provides to each individual from the moment of conception until the end of their life. The verse emphasizes the sacredness of human life and the importance of treating all human beings with dignity and respect, regardless of their age or stage of development.
orig: للبث في بطنه إلى يوم يبعثون

translation: And We have destroyed it with a single blow, while it was unaware.
interpretation: The verse describes the destruction of a town or community that was unaware and unprepared for God's punishment. The phrase 'with a single blow' conveys the suddenness and severity of the punishment, leaving no opportunity for the people to repent or escape. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of being mindful of one's actions and seeking God's forgiveness, as well as a warning of the consequences of ignorance and heedlessness towards God's commands.
orig: فنبذناه بالعراء وهو سقيم

translation: And We caused to grow upon it a tree springing out from a single bank.
interpretation: The verse describes the growth of a tree from a single bank or root. This verse is part of a larger passage that describes the blessings that God has bestowed upon the earth. The tree is a symbol of growth and abundance, and its appearance from a single bank or root emphasizes the power and wisdom of God's creation. The verse serves as a reminder of the beauty and complexity of the natural world, and encourages believers to reflect on the wonders of God's creation and to be grateful for His blessings.
orig: وأنبتنا عليه شجرة من يقطين

translation: And We sent it (the reminder) to a hundred thousand or more.
interpretation: The verse refers to the sending of a reminder or a message to a large number of people, specifically mentioned as 'a hundred thousand or more'. The exact nature of the reminder or message is not specified in the verse, but it is clear that it is being sent to a large population. The verse may be interpreted as a reminder of God's message or a call to remember and follow God's teachings. The large number of people being addressed emphasizes the importance and relevance of the message to a wide audience, and highlights the significance of the reminder in guiding people towards the right path.
orig: وأرسلناه إلى مائة ألف أو يزيدون

translation: But believe, and I will forgive you your sins and admit you to Gardens beneath which rivers flow.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the promise of forgiveness and admission to Paradise for those who believe. The verse emphasizes the power of belief and its ability to erase past sins. The promise of Paradise, with its rivers and gardens, is held out as an incentive for people to turn to faith. The verse can be seen as an invitation to embrace belief and to seek forgiveness and salvation through faith in God.
orig: فآمنوا فمتعناهم إلى حين

translation: And ask them about the daughters of Allah; and they have [for themselves] sons.
interpretation: The verse is a rhetorical question directed towards the disbelievers, challenging them to explain their belief in the daughters of Allah. The verse emphasizes the absurdity of their belief, as it is illogical and against the fundamental Islamic belief in the oneness of God. The second part of the verse, 'and they have [for themselves] sons', further highlights the absurdity of their belief, as it suggests that the disbelievers are attributing sons to Allah, while they themselves have sons. This verse serves to refute the false beliefs of the disbelievers and to reaffirm the Islamic belief in the oneness of God.
orig: فاستفتهم ألربك البنات ولهم البنون

translation: Or have We created the angels females, while they were witnesses?
interpretation: The verse is a rhetorical question that challenges the idea that angels could be female. The verse emphasizes the maleness of the angels, who are described as witnesses. This verse is part of a larger argument in the Qur'an that rejects the Christian belief in the divinity of Jesus and the Trinity. By rejecting the idea that angels could be female, the verse underscores the absolute otherness and transcendence of God and the angels, who are fundamentally different from human beings and their limited understanding of gender and sexuality.
orig: أم خلقنا الملائكة إناثا وهم شاهدون

translation: Indeed, they are, from their own fabrications, saying:
interpretation: The verse is a continuation of a conversation or a statement, and it is indicating that the people mentioned are speaking falsely and making up their own lies. The verse emphasizes the fabricated and untrue nature of their speech. The interpretation of this verse could be that it is a warning against lying and false speech, and a reminder of the consequences of such actions.
orig: ألا إنهم من إفكهم ليقولون

translation: And God has not taken a son, and indeed, they are liars.
interpretation: The verse categorically denies the claim that God has taken a son and asserts that those who make this claim are liars. This verse is part of the Qur'an's rejection of the Christian belief in the divinity of Jesus and the notion of God having a son. The verse affirms the absolute oneness and uniqueness of God, who is free from any imperfections or human attributes.
orig: ولد الله وإنهم لكاذبون

translation: He chooses the daughters over the sons.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the preference of daughters over sons. The Arabic word 'istafa' means to choose or to prefer, and in this context, it refers to the preference of daughters over sons. The verse is part of a larger passage that discusses the blessings and trials that come with having daughters. While having daughters is often considered a trial and a source of shame in some cultures, the Qur'an highlights the blessings and virtues of daughters. The verse encourages Muslims to appreciate and value their daughters and to treat them with kindness and respect.
orig: أصطفى البنات على البنين

translation: What is [the matter] with you that you judge?
interpretation: The verse is a rhetorical question posed by the Qur'an, addressing those who are judging or passing judgement without proper knowledge or authority. The verse challenges the legitimacy and fairness of their judgement, and serves as a reminder of the importance of seeking knowledge, understanding and wisdom before making a judgement. It emphasizes the importance of humility and the recognition of one's own limitations, and highlights the dangers of hasty and uninformed judgement.
orig: ما لكم كيف تحكمون

translation: So do not associate [with Him].
interpretation: The verse is a command from God to His prophet Muhammad, and by extension to all believers, to not associate anything or anyone with God in worship or veneration. This is one of the fundamental tenets of Islamic faith, known as Tawhid (the oneness of God). The verse emphasizes the importance of maintaining the purity of monotheism and the dangers of associating partners with God, which is considered a grave sin in Islam. The verse serves as a reminder to stay steadfast on the path of pure monotheism and avoid any deviations or innovations in religious practices.
orig: أفلا تذكرون

translation: Or do you have a clear authority?
interpretation: The verse is a rhetorical question that challenges the disbelievers to produce any authority or proof that supports their rejection of Islam and the message of the Prophet Muhammad. It implies that they have no valid proof or authority, and that their denial is baseless and unjustified. The verse serves as a reminder that the truth of Islam is clearly established and that those who reject it do so without any valid reason or evidence.
orig: أم لكم سلطان مبين

translation: And bring your Book (of deeds) if you are truthful.
interpretation: This verse is a challenge to the disbelievers who rejected the message of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). They demanded proof and evidence for his claims, so this verse asks them to bring their own 'book of deeds' if they are truthful in their denial of the Prophet's message. The verse implies that the disbelievers' deeds will be weighed and measured on the Day of Judgment, and they will be held accountable for their actions. The verse serves as a reminder that each person is responsible for their own actions and will be judged accordingly.
orig: فأتوا بكتابكم إن كنتم صادقين

translation: And they have put between Him and the Jannah a barrier, and indeed, they will be aware [of their error]!
interpretation: The verse speaks about the actions of those who place a barrier between themselves and Paradise, committing sins and disobedience towards God. The verse emphasizes that these people will ultimately realize their mistake, as they will be fully aware of their actions and their consequences in the afterlife. The verse serves as a warning to those who engage in sinful behavior, reminding them that their actions have consequences and that they will ultimately be held accountable for them.
orig: وجعلوا بينه وبين الجنة نسبا ولقد علمت الجنة إنهم لمحضرون

translation: Glory be to Allah, far above (all) that they associate (with Him).
interpretation: The verse is a declaration of tawheed, the Islamic concept of the oneness of God. It asserts that Allah is free from any imperfections or weaknesses, and is far above all the false deities and attributes that people may associate with Him. This verse serves as a reminder to Muslims to maintain a strong faith in the oneness of God, and to avoid the sin of shirk, or associating partners with God. It emphasizes the transcendence and perfection of Allah, and encourages believers to worship and praise Him alone.
orig: سبحان الله عما يصفون

translation: Except the servants of Allah, the purified.
interpretation: The verse distinguishes between two groups of people: those who are servants of Allah and those who are not. The servants of Allah are described as 'purified', indicating that they have been chosen and set apart for a special purpose. This group is exempted from the fate of destruction that is mentioned in the previous verse. The verse emphasizes the importance of being a servant of Allah and being purified, and it encourages believers to strive for this status in order to be saved from the punishment of Allah.
orig: إلا عباد الله المخلصين

translation: So indeed, you and what you worship
interpretation: The verse is a continuation of a discussion about the power and sovereignty of God. The phrase 'So indeed, you and what you worship' is a reminder that all of creation, including the people and the things they worship, are subject to God's control. The verse emphasizes the insignificance of the things that people may worship, whether they be idols, other people, or even themselves, in comparison to the greatness of God. The verse serves as a call to worship and submit to the one true God, and to recognize the futility of worshiping anything else.
orig: فإنكم وما تعبدون

translation: You are not over it any guardians.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the ultimate power and control of God, and the insignificance of human beings in comparison. It suggests that people are not capable of protecting or guarding anything without the will of God. The verse can be seen as a reminder that people should not rely on their own strength or power, but should instead place their trust in God and submit to His will.
orig: ما أنتم عليه بفاتنين

translation: Except those who are brought to Hell
interpretation: The verse offers an exception to those who are destined for Hell, indicating that not all people will be punished in the same way. This exception highlights the idea that God's justice is not arbitrary, but rather is based on the actions and intentions of each individual. The verse may also serve as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them that they still have the opportunity to repent and change their ways before it is too late.
orig: إلا من هو صال الجحيم

translation: And not a single one of us but has a known station (with Him).
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the idea that every individual has a predestined and predetermined role or station in the grand design of the universe. This station is known only to God, and it is not for humans to question or challenge it. The verse encourages submission and acceptance of one's role in life, recognizing that it is part of a larger divine plan. It also suggests the idea of divine justice, as each person will be held accountable for fulfilling their unique role and will be treated fairly according to their actions.
orig: وما منا إلا له مقام معلوم

translation: And indeed, it is We who give life and cause death, and We are the Inheritors.
interpretation: The verse affirms that it is God who has control over life and death, and that God will be the ultimate inheritor of all that exists. This statement emphasizes God's power and sovereignty over all of creation, and the transient nature of human existence. It serves as a reminder of the fleeting nature of life and the inevitability of death, and encourages submission to God's will.
orig: وإنا لنحن الصافون

translation: And indeed, it is We who give life and cause death, and We are the Inheritors.
interpretation: The verse affirms that it is God who has control over life and death and that God will inherit the earth and all that is on it. The verse emphasizes God's power and sovereignty over all of creation, and the transience of human life and possessions. The verse may also serve as a reminder of the inevitability of death, and the importance of living a righteous life in preparation for the afterlife.
orig: وإنا لنحن المسبحون

translation: And if they argue with you,
interpretation: The verse is addressing the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, and speaks about the people who argue with him. The verse emphasizes the inevitability of such arguments and serves as a reminder to the Prophet to remain patient and steadfast in the face of opposition and criticism. The verse can also be seen as a message to the believers, encouraging them to remain firm in their faith and not to be swayed by the arguments and criticisms of the disbelievers.
orig: وإن كانوا ليقولون

translation: Had there been among us a remembrance from the first days
interpretation: The verse speaks about the longing for a reminder or a guide from the past that could help people in their current situation. The phrase 'from the first days' implies that such a reminder or guide has been absent for a long time, and its absence has led to a state of confusion or misguidance. The verse can be interpreted as a call for a return to the teachings and guidance of the past, and a reminder of the importance of preserving and following the right path as established by the early generations.
orig: لو أن عندنا ذكرا من الأولين

translation: But truly have We guided on the way to bliss those of Our servants who strive to be sincere.
interpretation: The verse highlights those who are guided by God on the path to bliss, specifically those who strive to be sincere. The word 'sincere' in this context means being completely devoted to God, without any ulterior motives or desires. The verse emphasizes the importance of sincerity in one's relationship with God and the rewards that come with it, which is being guided on the path to bliss. The verse serves as a reminder to those who are seeking guidance and the right path, to strive for sincerity in all aspects of their lives.
orig: لكنا عباد الله المخلصين

translation: They disbelieved in it, so they will know.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the disbelievers who rejected the message of God. The verse emphasizes that they will eventually come to know the truth, but it implies that it will be too late for them. The verse serves as a warning to those who reject the message of God, reminding them that their disbelief will not protect them from the consequences of their actions and that they will ultimately be held accountable for their denial of the truth.
orig: فكفروا به فسوف يعلمون

translation: And indeed, Our words have preceded to Our servants, the messengers.
interpretation: The verse refers to the message of God being delivered to His messengers before it is delivered to the people. It highlights the role of the messengers as the mediators of God's message and emphasizes the importance of their mission. The verse suggests that the message of God is predestined and that its delivery to the messengers is a part of this predestination. It also implies the significance of the message and the responsibility of the messengers to convey it accurately and effectively.
orig: ولقد سبقت كلمتنا لعبادنا المرسلين

translation: Indeed, they will be the victorious.
interpretation: The verse speaks about a group of people who will be victorious. While the context of the verse is important for understanding the identity of this group, the verse by itself emphasizes the certainty of their victory. The use of the word 'indeed' (inahum) adds emphasis to the statement, indicating that their victory is a certainty and not in doubt. The verse may serve as a source of hope and inspiration for those who are facing difficulties and challenges, reminding them that victory will ultimately be theirs if they remain steadfast and persevere.
orig: إنهم لهم المنصورون

translation: And indeed, our troops will be the conquerors.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the certainty of victory for God's troops. The verse emphasizes the power and might of God's troops, indicating that they will be victorious in their endeavors. The verse serves as a reminder to those who have faith in God, reminding them of the support and aid they will receive from God in their struggles. It also serves as a warning to those who oppose God and his believers, reminding them of the inevitable defeat they will face.
orig: وإن جندنا لهم الغالبون

translation: And kept away from them until the appointed time.
interpretation: The verse speaks about God's decision to keep away from the people until a certain time. The verse implies that God had given the people a chance to change their ways, but they did not take the opportunity. As a result, God decided to keep away from them and let them face the consequences of their actions. The verse serves as a reminder that God's patience and mercy have limits, and that people should not take His forgiveness for granted. The appointed time referred to in the verse is likely the time of judgment, when God will mete out justice to all people according to their deeds.
orig: فتول عنهم حتى حين

translation: And so, let them see; they will soon see.
interpretation: The verse is a challenge to the disbelievers, urging them to observe and reflect upon the signs of God. The phrase 'they will soon see' implies that the consequences of their actions and disbelief will become clear and evident to them in the near future. The verse serves as a reminder that God's plan will ultimately be revealed, and that those who deny His signs and messages will eventually come to understand and recognize the truth.
orig: وأبصرهم فسوف يبصرون

translation: Or have they not considered how Our punishment came to the previous nations?
interpretation: The verse is a rhetorical question, inviting the listener or reader to reflect on the fate of previous nations who were punished by God. The verse highlights the inevitability of God's punishment for those who reject His message or commit injustices. It serves as a warning to the current generation, urging them to take heed of the lessons from history and avoid repeating the mistakes of the past.
orig: أفبعذابنا يستعجلون

translation: But when (the punishment) fell upon their fields from above and ahead of them, on the day of the threatening (doom)
interpretation: The verse describes the punishment that was brought down upon the fields of the people from above and ahead of them on the day of reckoning. The punishment was sudden and overwhelming, leaving the people with no chance to escape or avoid it. The verse serves as a warning of the impending doom for those who do not heed the signs and continue to commit injustices, emphasizing the inevitability of the punishment.
orig: فإذا نزل بساحتهم فساء صباح المنذرين

translation: And turned away from them until the appointed time.
interpretation: The verse speaks about God turning away from the people who were being addressed, indicating their rejection and abandonment by the divine. The phrase 'until the appointed time' implies that their fate had already been determined and that there was nothing they could do to change it. The verse may serve as a reminder that actions have consequences and that those who persist in their wrongdoing will ultimately be left to their own devices, without the guidance and protection of God.
orig: وتول عنهم حتى حين

translation: And truly will you see (the consequence of) it with your own eyes, and then they will be repentant.
interpretation: The verse speaks about a situation where the people will witness the consequence of their actions with their own eyes, and it will be a reality that they cannot deny. The verse implies that the people had been warned or given signs, but they did not heed them and continued in their ways. The consequence will be a moment of truth for them, and they will finally understand the gravity of their actions. The verse suggests that this realization will come too late, and the people will be filled with regret and remorse, but it will be of no use, as the damage will have already been done.
orig: وأبصر فسوف يبصرون

translation: Glory be to your Lord, the Lord of Might, above what they describe.
interpretation: The verse is a declaration of God's glory and might, and a rejection of the false descriptions of God by those who deny His power. The verse emphasizes the greatness of God and the limitations of human understanding, reminding the reader of the importance of humility and reverence in the presence of the divine. The verse encourages the believers to seek knowledge and understanding of God's true nature, and to reject the misconceptions and falsehoods spread by those who deny His power and majesty.
orig: سبحان ربك رب العزة عما يصفون

translation: And peace be upon the messengers
interpretation: The verse is a greeting and a blessing of peace upon all the prophets and messengers of God. It is a recognition of their role in delivering God's message to humanity and a statement of respect and reverence for them. The verse can also be seen as a prayer for peace and blessings for all those who follow in their footsteps and strive to deliver the message of God in their own time.
orig: وسلام على المرسلين

translation: And all praise is for Allah, the Lord of the worlds.
interpretation: The verse is a simple and powerful expression of praise and gratitude to God. It asserts the greatness and power of God as the Lord of all creation. This phrase is a common opening for many Surahs in the Qamar and serves as a reminder of the importance of recognizing and acknowledging God's role as the ultimate authority and provider.
orig: والحمد لله رب العالمين

translation: And We sent the Qur'an, the reminder.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the sending down of the Qur'an as a reminder for humanity. The Qur'an serves as a guide and a source of wisdom, reminding people of the teachings of Islam and the consequences of their actions. It is a means for people to reflect on their lives and to seek guidance and enlightenment. The Qur'an is a constant reminder of God's presence and his expectations of his creation.
orig: ص والقرآن ذي الذكر

translation: But those who disbelieve, it is the same to them whether you warn them or do not warn them, they will not believe.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the stubbornness and closed-mindedness of the disbelievers. It emphasizes that no matter how much one tries to warn or guide them, they will not believe. The verse highlights the futility of trying to change the hearts and minds of those who are set in their ways and unwilling to accept the truth. It serves as a reminder that the responsibility of guiding people lies solely with God, and that one should not be disheartened by the rejection of others.
orig: بل الذين كفروا في عزة وشقاق

translation: How many a generation before them did We destroy, who cried out in despair, [but] there was no stopper [of death] for them.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of previous generations who cried out in despair but were not spared from destruction. The verse emphasizes the inevitability of death and the destruction of those who reject God's message. The phrase 'there was no stopper [of death] for them' highlights the futility of their cries and serves as a reminder of the power of God's will.
orig: كم أهلكنا من قبلهم من قرن فنادوا ولات حين مناص

translation: And they were astonished that a warner had come to them from among them, and the disbelievers said, 'This is a sorcerer, a liar.',
interpretation: The verse describes the reaction of the people when a warner (prophet) came to them from among themselves. Instead of heeding his message, they were astonished and rejected him, calling him a sorcerer and a liar. The verse highlights the denial and rejection of the prophet by the disbelievers, and their refusal to accept the truth even when it is presented to them by one of their own. It serves as a reminder of the importance of being open-minded and receptive to the message of the prophets, and the dangers of rejecting their message out of disbelief and arrogance.
orig: وعجبوا أن جاءهم منذر منهم وقال الكافرون هذا ساحر كذاب

translation: Set up no other god besides Me: then you shall be in safety.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of monotheism and the worship of one God. It suggests that the rejection of all other gods and the worship of the one true God will lead to safety and security. The verse can be interpreted as a call to abandon idolatry and other forms of false worship and to submit oneself fully to the one true God, who is the source of all protection and salvation.
orig: أجعل الآلهة إلها واحدا إن هذا لشيء عجاب

translation: And the leaders among them said: 'Go away and stick to your gods. Indeed, this is something intended (as a plan).'
interpretation: The verse describes a situation where some leaders in a community are urging others to stay committed to their idols and gods, while a group of people are questioning or challenging this belief system. The leaders dismiss the concerns and doubts of the people, and they respond by saying that the situation is a planned and intentional act. However, the context of the verse suggests that the leaders are actually trying to suppress the truth and maintain their own power and position. The verse serves as a warning against following false leaders and emphasizes the importance of seeking the truth and following it, even if it means going against the majority.
orig: وانطلق الملأ منهم أن امشوا واصبروا على آلهتكم إن هذا لشيء يراد

translation: We have not heard of such a thing in the latter religion! This is nothing but a lie!
interpretation: The verse is a response to a claim or statement that was made, most likely by the disbelievers, regarding something they have not heard of before in their religion. The response denies and rejects the claim, stating that it is nothing but a fabrication and a lie. The verse can be understood as a reminder that any claim or statement must be supported by evidence and must not contradict the teachings of the religion.
orig: ما سمعنا بهذا في الملة الآخرة إن هذا إلا اختلاق

translation: Or have We revealed to him (Muhammad)
interpretation: No interpretation
orig: أأنزل عليه الذكر من بيننا بل هم في شك من ذكري بل لما يذوقوا عذاب

translation: Or have they (the disbelievers) the treasures of the mercy of your Lord, the Exalted, the Giver?
interpretation: The verse questions whether the disbelievers possess the treasures of mercy from the Lord, who is Exalted and Generous. This question is posed to make the disbelievers reflect on their attitude towards God's mercy and to remind them of the ultimate source of all blessings. The verse suggests that the disbelievers are unaware of the true source of their sustenance and prosperity and instead attribute it to their own abilities or false deities. The verse serves as a reminder that all blessings come from God and that those who deny His existence and His mercy will ultimately be deprived of His blessings.
orig: أم عندهم خزائن رحمة ربك العزيز الوهاب

translation: Or have they taken other than Allah as protectors while He is the Protector of them? And they have not perceived.
interpretation: The verse highlights the misguided belief of some people who take protectors other than Allah, while Allah is the ultimate Protector. This verse serves as a reminder that people should be mindful of their actions and not rely on false protectors. It emphasizes the importance of recognizing Allah's power and protection, and the consequences of ignoring it.
orig: أم لهم ملك السماوات والأرض وما بينهما فليرتقوا في الأسباب

translation: Defeated, of the parties there was none.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the ultimate defeat and destruction of all parties or groups that were engaged in conflict and opposition to God's will. The verse highlights the futility of their resistance and emphasizes the power and sovereignty of God. The verse serves as a reminder that all earthly powers and conflicts are temporary and insignificant in the face of God's will and judgment.
orig: جند ما هنالك مهزوم من الأحزاب

translation: Indeed, before them, the peoples of Noah, 'Ad, and Pharaoh of the towering pillars denied [the messengers].
interpretation: The verse mentions three examples of previous nations who rejected the messengers sent to them: the peoples of Noah, 'Ad, and Pharaoh. By mentioning these examples, the verse emphasizes the consequences of denying the messengers and the warning brought by them. The verse serves as a reminder to the listeners or readers to heed the message of the current messenger and not to follow the path of the previous disbelieving nations.
orig: كذبت قبلهم قوم نوح وعاد وفرعون ذو الأوتاد

translation: And Thamud, and the people of Lut, and the companions of the Wood, those are the parties.
interpretation: The verse mentions three groups of people who were destroyed for their sins: the people of Thamud, the people of Lut (Lot), and the companions of the Wood. These groups serve as examples of the consequences of sin and disobedience towards God. The verse emphasizes the destruction of these communities, referring to them as 'parties', which implies a group of people who were united in their disbelief and disobedience. The verse serves as a warning to those who follow in their footsteps, reminding them of the fate of those who reject God's message and persist in sin.
orig: وثمود وقوم لوط وأصحاب الأيكة أولئك الأحزاب

translation: Indeed, [even] if every mankind rebeled against the Messengers, still their account would be with Us.
