interpretation: The verse emphasizes the ultimate power and justice of God, who will hold every individual accountable for their actions, regardless of whether they choose to believe or reject the Messengers. The phrase 'if every mankind rebeled' highlights the collective nature of human disobedience, while the second part of the verse reinforces the idea that God's judgment is certain and not subject to human interference. The verse serves as a reminder of the ultimate authority of God and the importance of submitting to His will.
orig: إن كل إلا كذب الرسل فحق عقاب

translation: And these look no further than a single shout or cry.
interpretation: The verse describes a group of people who underestimate or ignore the signs and warnings of the impending punishment from God. They are so absorbed in their own worldly concerns that they pay no attention to the warning signs, and are caught off guard when the punishment comes. The phrase 'a single shout or cry' suggests that the punishment will be sudden and unexpected, leaving no time for the people to repent or make amends. The verse serves as a reminder to be vigilant and mindful of the signs of God's punishment, and to always be prepared for the end times.
orig: وما ينظر هؤلاء إلا صيحة واحدة ما لها من فواق

translation: And they said, 'Our Lord, hasten for us the punishment before the Day of Reckoning.'
interpretation: The verse describes the request of a group of people who, aware of their sins and wrongdoings, ask God to hasten their punishment before the Day of Judgment. This request reflects their recognition of the consequences of their actions and their desire to atone for their sins. The verse can be interpreted as a reminder of the importance of taking responsibility for one's actions and seeking forgiveness, rather than delaying repentance until the last moment.
orig: وقالوا ربنا عجل لنا قطنا قبل يوم الحساب

translation: Be patient with what they say and remember Our servant David, the possessor of strength. Indeed, he was repentant.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the importance of patience in the face of adversity and the example of the prophet David. The verse commands the believer to be patient and endure the harm caused by others, while simultaneously reminding them of the story of the prophet David. The verse describes David as the 'possessor of strength', highlighting his power and might. However, the verse also emphasizes that despite his strength, David was also a repentant servant of God. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of patience and humility, as well as the power of repentance and seeking forgiveness from God.
orig: اصبر على ما يقولون واذكر عبدنا داوود ذا الأيد إنه أواب

translation: We have made the mountains to glorify with him in the evening and the morning.
interpretation: The verse highlights the majesty and power of God by stating that even the mountains have been made to praise and glorify Him. The phrase 'with him' refers to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), emphasizing the unity and harmony of all creation in worshipping God. The timing of the glorification, 'in the evening and the morning', further underscores the continuous and constant nature of this act of worship. The verse serves as a reminder of the greatness of God and the role of all creation, including humans, in praising and glorifying Him.
orig: إنا سخرنا الجبال معه يسبحن بالعشي والإشراق

translation: And the stork (has its) home in (different) columns, or (in other words), a building, high and spacious.
interpretation: The verse uses the example of the stork to illustrate God's power and creativity in creating diverse habitats for different creatures. The stork builds its nest in high and spacious columns or buildings, demonstrating its ability to adapt to its surroundings. This verse serves as a reminder of God's greatness and the wonders of His creation, encouraging believers to reflect on the signs of God's existence and to marvel at the complexity and diversity of the natural world.
orig: والطير محشورة كل له أواب

translation: And We strengthened the kingdom which We had given to David, and We gave him more wisdom and a decisive speech.
interpretation: The verse highlights the power and authority given to King David by God. The phrase 'We strengthened the kingdom' suggests that God gave David the ability to maintain and expand his kingdom, while 'We gave him more wisdom' indicates that David was given a deeper understanding and knowledge. The 'decisive speech' refers to David's ability to communicate effectively and make sound decisions. The verse emphasizes the special relationship between David and God, and the blessings that were bestowed upon him as a result of his faith and obedience.
orig: وشددنا ملكه وآتيناه الحكمة وفصل الخطاب

translation: And has there come to you the story of the Disputers, when they tore down the wall.
interpretation: The verse refers to an incident known as the story of the Disputers, where a group of people destroyed a wall while in dispute. The verse serves as a reminder of the consequences of causing destruction and discord, emphasizing that even seemingly small acts of aggression can have far-reaching consequences. The story of the Disputers serves as a cautionary tale, urging people to avoid conflict and strive for peace and harmony.
orig: وهل أتاك نبأ الخصم إذ تسوروا المحراب

translation: When they entered upon David, he was frightened of them, they said, 'Fear not. Two disputants, of whom we have transgressed against one, so judge between us with truth, and do not follow our inclination by deviating, and guide us to the right path.'
interpretation: The verse describes a situation where a group of people approached the Prophet David, causing him to become frightened. The people then asked David to judge between them in a dispute, promising to abide by his fair and truthful judgement. They also asked him to not be swayed by their personal desires or biases, and to guide them to the right path. The verse highlights the importance of justice and fairness in Islamic teachings, and the role of the prophets as fair judges and guides for their communities.
orig: إذ دخلوا على داوود ففزع منهم قالوا لا تخف خصمان بغى بعضنا على بعض فاحكم بيننا بالحق ولا تشطط واهدنا إلى سواء الصراط

translation: Indeed, this is my brother; he has ninety-nine ewes and I have one ewe. And he said, 'Entrust me with your ewe,' and he overpowered me in speech.
interpretation: The verse describes a situation where one brother has significantly more wealth than the other. The wealthier brother asks the poorer brother to entrust him with his only ewe, and the poorer brother complies despite being overpowered in speech by his wealthier brother. The verse highlights the importance of justice and fairness, and the dangers of being overpowered by wealth and power. It serves as a reminder to be mindful of the rights of others, especially those who are less fortunate, and to avoid taking advantage of their vulnerability.
orig: إن هذا أخي له تسع وتسعون نعجة ولي نعجة واحدة فقال أكفلنيها وعزني في الخطاب

translation: He said, 'You have certainly wronged me by asking me to hand over my sign to you. If it were not for the fact that you are my brother, I would have taken you by the head and torn you apart.' But none has the right to do that except for those who are unjust. And indeed, David and Solomon when they gave judgement regarding the field, when the sheep of a (certain) person were destroying it, so We were witnesses to their judgement. And We gave Solomon the correct understanding, and both of them were of Our sincere servants. And David, when he was tested, became fearful of his Lord, and he fell down in prostration and turned in repentance (to God).
interpretation: The verse speaks about the story of David and his judgement regarding a field that was being destroyed by the sheep of a person. When David was tested, he became fearful of his Lord and repented. The verse highlights the importance of being just and fair, and the consequences of wrongdoing. It also emphasizes the importance of repentance and seeking forgiveness from God. The verse also serves as a reminder of the power of God and His ability to test His servants, and the importance of being mindful of one's actions and seeking His guidance.
orig: قال لقد ظلمك بسؤال نعجتك إلى نعاجه وإن كثيرا من الخلطاء ليبغي بعضهم على بعض إلا الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات وقليل ما هم وظن داوود أنما فتناه فاستغفر ربه وخر راكعا وأناب

translation: And We have already forgiven you for that, and indeed, for you is a near victory.
interpretation: The verse speaks about God's forgiveness for an unspecified past action of the person being addressed. The verse emphasizes that God has already forgiven this action and that a great reward or 'near victory' is in store for the person. The verse serves as a reminder of God's mercy and forgiveness, encouraging the person to seek God's continued favor and forgiveness.
orig: فغفرنا له ذلك وإن له عندنا لزلفى وحسن مآب

translation: O Dawud, indeed We have made you a vicegerent on the earth, so judge between the people in truth and do not follow desire, lest it leads you astray from the way of Allah. Indeed, those who go astray from the way of Allah - there is a severe punishment for them for what they had forgotten on the Day of Reckoning.
interpretation: The verse addresses Prophet Dawud (David) and informs him that he has been made a vicegerent on earth, and it is his responsibility to judge between the people with truth and justice. The verse warns him not to follow his desires, as it may lead him astray from the path of Allah. The verse also mentions the severe punishment for those who deviate from the path of Allah, emphasizing the importance of staying on the right path and adhering to justice.
orig: يا داوود إنا جعلناك خليفة في الأرض فاحكم بين الناس بالحق ولا تتبع الهوى فيضلك عن سبيل الله إن الذين يضلون عن سبيل الله لهم عذاب شديد بما نسوا يوم الحساب

translation: And We created not the heavens and the earth and what is between them in vain. That is the belief of the disbelievers. So woe to the disbelievers from the Fire!
interpretation: The verse emphasizes that the creation of the heavens, the earth, and everything in between has a purpose and is not created in vain. The verse criticizes those who disbelieve in God and His signs and warns them of the consequences of their disbelief. The verse concludes by warning the disbelievers of the Fire, indicating the severe punishment that awaits them in the afterlife. The verse serves as a reminder of the significance of faith and the importance of recognizing and submitting to the truth of God's existence and oneness.
orig: وما خلقنا السماء والأرض وما بينهما باطلا ذلك ظن الذين كفروا فويل للذين كفروا من النار

translation: Or should We treat those who believe and do good deeds like the corruptors in the land? Or should We treat the righteous like the criminals?
interpretation: The verse raises a question about the fairness of treating those who believe and do good deeds in the same way as those who corrupt and cause mischief in the land. It also questions whether it is just to treat the righteous in the same way as the criminals. The verse emphasizes the importance of good deeds and righteousness and the unfairness of treating the righteous and the wicked in the same way. The verse serves as a reminder to believers to continue to strive for righteousness and to not be discouraged by the actions of those who spread corruption and chaos in the land.
orig: أم نجعل الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات كالمفسدين في الأرض أم نجعل المتقين كالفجار

translation: We have sent down to you the Book with truth, so that you may judge between people by what Allah has shown you. And do not be an advocate for the betrayers.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the revelation of the Qur'an, which was sent down to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) as a guide for humankind. The verse emphasizes the importance of using the Qur'an as a source of judgment and wisdom, and the responsibility of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to judge between people based on its teachings. The verse also warns against taking the side of those who are unjust and unfaithful, and highlights the importance of being fair and just in all actions and decisions.
orig: كتاب أنزلناه إليك مبارك ليدبروا آياته وليتذكر أولو الألباب

translation: And We gave Dawud (David) Sulaiman (Solomon). Indeed, he was a good servant. Indeed, he was repentant.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the blessings that God bestowed upon Dawud (David) by giving him Sulaiman (Solomon). The verse highlights the virtues of Sulaiman by describing him as a good servant of God, and as someone who repents and seeks forgiveness. The verse can be seen as a recognition of the prophets' humility and devotion to God, emphasizing their status as chosen servants of the Divine. The verse may also serve as a reminder of the importance of repentance and seeking forgiveness in one's relationship with God.
orig: ووهبنا لداوود سليمان نعم العبد إنه أواب

translation: When the most fearful (event) of stern punishment is held out against a people (in the form of the vision of horseriders),
interpretation: The verse describes a terrifying event, referred to as 'the most fearful (event)' of stern punishment, which is shown to a group of people. The punishment is depicted as a vision of horseriders, which is likely a metaphor for an invading army or a divine punishment. The verse is often interpreted as a warning to those who reject God's message and commit injustices, emphasizing the consequences of their actions and the inevitability of divine retribution.
orig: إذ عرض عليه بالعشي الصافنات الجياد

translation: And he said, 'Indeed, I prefer the love of good' - [that is] the remembrance of my Lord - 'over your love until the veil is lifted.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about a person who has chosen to prioritize the love and remembrance of God over the love of other things. The phrase 'the love of good' is a metaphor for the remembrance of God, emphasizing the value and importance of having a strong connection with the divine. The phrase 'until the veil is lifted' suggests that this person is waiting for the moment when the truth is revealed and the ultimate reality is unveiled. The verse highlights the importance of maintaining a strong spiritual focus and prioritizing one's relationship with God, even in the face of worldly distractions and temptations.
orig: فقال إني أحببت حب الخير عن ذكر ربي حتى توارت بالحجاب

translation: And cast them out, all together, banished, humiliated in disgrace. Their only recompense was disgrace in this world, and in the Hereafter, an exceeding great punishment.
interpretation: The verse speaks about casting out a group of people in a state of humiliation and disgrace. The punishment is both worldly and otherworldly, with the only recompense for their sins being disgrace in this life and a severe punishment in the afterlife. The verse serves as a reminder of the consequences of sin and wrongdoing, and the ultimate justice that will be served in the afterlife.
orig: ردوها علي فطفق مسحا بالسوق والأعناق

translation: And indeed, We tested Solomon and placed a body [of a creature] upon his throne. Then he returned [to worship Us].
interpretation: The verse speaks about a test that God put Solomon through, by placing a body (of a creature) on his throne. Despite this test, Solomon remained steadfast and returned to worshiping God. The verse highlights Solomon's faith and devotion to God, and his ability to remain focused on his duties as a leader and a servant of God, even in the face of unexpected challenges and tests.
orig: ولقد فتنا سليمان وألقينا على كرسيه جسدا ثم أناب

translation: He said, 'My Lord, forgive me and grant me a kingdom such that no one after me will have power like mine. Indeed, You are the Bestower.'
interpretation: The verse is a conversation between an unnamed person and God, where the person is asking for forgiveness and the granting of a powerful kingdom that no one after him will have. The person recognizes and acknowledges that only God has the power to grant such a request, as indicated by his statement 'Indeed, You are the Bestower.' The verse highlights the individual's desire for power and control, as well as his recognition of God's ultimate power and control. The verse can be interpreted as a reminder of the fleeting nature of worldly power and the importance of seeking forgiveness and a strong relationship with God.
orig: قال رب اغفر لي وهب لي ملكا لا ينبغي لأحد من بعدي إنك أنت الوهاب

translation: And We subjected to him the wind, blowing gently by his command, wherever he directed.
interpretation: The verse speaks about God's power and control over the natural elements, as exemplified by the wind. The wind obeys God's command and blows gently wherever He directs it. The verse serves as a reminder of God's power and control over all aspects of life and nature, and of the insignificance of human beings in comparison to God's greatness.
orig: فسخرنا له الريح تجري بأمره رخاء حيث أصاب

translation: And the devils, every builder and diver.
interpretation: The verse is a part of a passage that speaks about the creation of the heavens and the earth, and the role of the devils in the building of the earth. The verse states that the devils are the builders and divers of the earth. This can be interpreted as a metaphorical way of saying that the devils are the ones who sow chaos and destruction in the world. They are the ones who build up systems and institutions based on falsehood and corruption, and then plunge them into chaos and ruin. The verse serves as a reminder of the destructive and deceitful nature of the devils and the harm they can bring to human societies, and the importance of being vigilant and not being deceived by their schemes.
orig: والشياطين كل بناء وغواص

translation: And the last of them are attached to chains.
interpretation: The verse describes the fate of certain sinners who are being punished in the hereafter. The 'last of them' refers to those who are being punished at the very end, after all other punishments have been carried out. These sinners are 'attached to chains', indicating that they are in a state of complete powerlessness and subjugation. The verse serves as a warning to those who persist in their sins, reminding them of the severe consequences that await them in the afterlife.
orig: وآخرين مقرنين في الأصفاد

translation: This is a provision from Us, so relent or bear with (it), but act not unjustly.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the provision or sustenance that God gives to people. It advises people to either be grateful for what they have received and be patient, or to bear with it if they are not satisfied. However, the verse warns against acting unjustly or ungratefully towards God. The verse encourages a positive and grateful attitude towards the blessings of God, and reminds people not to take their provisions for granted or to be unjust in their dealings with others.
orig: هذا عطاؤنا فامنن أو أمسك بغير حساب

translation: And indeed, for him (i.e. the believer) with Us is a reward unending, (a) noble provision.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the reward that awaits the believers in the afterlife. The reward is described as 'unending' and 'noble', indicating its great value and significance. The verse serves as a source of hope and motivation for believers, reminding them that their good deeds and faith will not go unrewarded in the afterlife. It also highlights the greatness and generosity of God, who promises to reward His believers with the best and most noble of provisions.
orig: وإن له عندنا لزلفى وحسن مآب

translation: And remember Our servant Job, when he called upon his Lord, 'Indeed, Satan has touched me with hardship and torture.',
interpretation: The verse speaks about the prophet Job and his patience in the face of hardship and suffering. Job, also known as Ayyub in Arabic, was a prophet who faced severe trials and tribulations, including loss of wealth, family, and health. In this verse, Job is depicted as calling upon God, acknowledging that Satan has caused him harm and distress. The verse serves as a testament to Job's unwavering faith and devotion to God, and his reliance on God in times of hardship. The verse also highlights the reality of the existence of Satan, who seeks to cause harm and discord among humans. Ultimately, the story of Job serves as a reminder to believers to be patient and steadfast in the face of adversity, and to seek refuge in God during times of hardship.
orig: واذكر عبدنا أيوب إذ نادى ربه أني مسني الشيطان بنصب وعذاب

translation: Step with your foot here, a cold drink will gush out and you will drink.
interpretation: The verse speaks about a miraculous event where a drink will come out from the ground after stepping on it with the foot. The water is described as cold, indicating its refreshing and revitalizing qualities. The action of drinking emphasizes the fulfillment of a need, suggesting that the water will be beneficial and life-giving. The verse may be interpreted as a sign of God's provision and care for his people, and a reminder of the blessings that come from the earth. It may also be seen as a symbol of spiritual nourishment and sustenance, highlighting the importance of seeking and receiving sustenance from God.
orig: اركض برجلك هذا مغتسل بارد وشراب

translation: And We bestowed upon him and his family from Us grace and a reminder for the possessors of intellect.
interpretation: The verse speaks about a person (who is not explicitly named, but could be a prophet or a righteous person) who has been given grace and a reminder from God. The 'reminder' could refer to a revelation or a message from God, while the 'possessors of intellect' are those who are able to understand and benefit from the reminder. The verse emphasizes the importance of divine guidance and the ability to understand and reflect upon it, suggesting that these are blessings that are not given to everyone. The verse encourages the reader to be grateful for these blessings and to strive to be among the 'possessors of intellect' who can truly appreciate and benefit from them.
orig: ووهبنا له أهله ومثلهم معهم رحمة منا وذكرى لأولي الألباب

translation: And take in your hand a bundle of thin grass, and strike therewith, and do not break your oath. Indeed, we found him patient. Indeed, he was one of our sincere servants.
interpretation: The verse relates a story of a prophet who was instructed by God to take a bundle of thin grass and strike with it, while also being told not to break his oath. The verse then describes the prophet as patient and sincere, highlighting his virtues and obedience. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of patience, obedience and fulfilling one's promises in the eyes of God. It also emphasizes the importance of following God's commands, even if they may seem unusual or unclear.
orig: وخذ بيدك ضغثا فاضرب به ولا تحنث إنا وجدناه صابرا نعم العبد إنه أواب

translation: And mention to Our servants Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, the possessors of strength and vision.
interpretation: The verse commands the Prophet Muhammad to remember and mention to the believers the stories of the prophets Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. These prophets are described as 'the possessors of strength and vision', highlighting their virtues and qualities. The verse emphasizes the importance of remembering and learning from the examples of the prophets, and encourages the believers to follow in their footsteps. The verse also serves as a reminder of the continuity of prophethood and the unity of the message of Islam.
orig: واذكر عبادنا إبراهيم وإسحاق ويعقوب أولي الأيدي والأبصار

translation: We have indeed made it a message for the people, although most of them do not believe.
interpretation: The verse refers to a message or warning that has been sent to the people, but most of them do not believe in it. The phrase 'We have indeed made it' implies that the message has been conveyed clearly and effectively, but the people have chosen not to believe. The verse highlights the widespread rejection of the message and the fact that only a small number of people will accept it. The verse serves as a reminder that the truth will always be evident, but it is up to the people to choose whether or not to accept it.
orig: إنا أخلصناهم بخالصة ذكرى الدار

translation: And indeed, they are among the chosen favorites
interpretation: The verse speaks of a group of people who have been selected and chosen by God for His favor and grace. These individuals have been distinguished from others and given a special status in the eyes of God. The verse can be seen as a message of hope and reassurance to those who strive to please God and follow His commands, reminding them that their efforts will not be in vain and that they are among those who are beloved by God.
orig: وإنهم عندنا لمن المصطفين الأخيار

translation: And mention Ishmael and Elisha and Dhul-Kifl, and all of them were among the chosen ones.
interpretation: The verse mentions four prophets, Ishmael, Elisha, and a man referred to as Dhul-Kifl, and affirms that they were all chosen by God. This verse serves as a reminder of the prophets who came before and their status as chosen ones, and it emphasizes the continuity of the prophetic tradition. It may also serve as a source of inspiration and a reminder of the virtuous example set by these prophets for the believers. The verse encourages the believers to remember and reflect upon the lives and teachings of these prophets and to strive to follow in their footsteps.
orig: واذكر إسماعيل واليسع وذا الكفل وكل من الأخيار

translation: This is a reminder, and indeed for the righteous is a beautiful home.
interpretation: The verse speaks about a reminder or admonition, and it reassures the righteous that they have a beautiful home awaiting them. The verse highlights the importance of being righteous and mindful of God's teachings. It also offers comfort and hope to those who strive to lead a virtuous life, promising them a reward in the afterlife. The verse can also be seen as a call for the believers to persevere in their faith and good deeds, knowing that they will be rewarded for their efforts.
orig: هذا ذكر وإن للمتقين لحسن مآب

translation: Gardens of Eden, the gates of which will be opened for them.
interpretation: The verse describes the reward for the righteous in the afterlife as Gardens of Eden, a place of eternal bliss and happiness. The gates of these gardens will be opened for them, indicating that they will have easy access to this paradise and will be welcomed with open arms. This is a promise of great comfort and joy for those who have lived a righteous life and followed the teachings of Islam.
orig: جنات عدن مفتحة لهم الأبواب

translation: Reclining therein, they call out to fruits and drink.
interpretation: The verse describes a group of people who are reclining in a place of abundance and calling out for more fruits and drinks. The verse may be interpreted as a metaphor for the excessive and indulgent behavior of those who are heedless of the blessings they have been given and take them for granted. It serves as a reminder to be grateful for what we have and not to be consumed by our desires.
orig: متكئين فيها يدعون فيها بفاكهة كثيرة وشراب

translation: And among them are those who have eyes but do not see.
interpretation: The verse refers to people who are physically able to see, but are spiritually blind and unable to comprehend or understand the truth. This could be because of their rejection or denial of the truth, or because of their stubbornness and refusal to accept it. The verse serves as a reminder that physical abilities, such as sight, are not enough for understanding and accepting the truth; rather, it requires an open heart and a willingness to accept and submit to the truth.
orig: وعندهم قاصرات الطرف أتراب

translation: This is what you were promised for the Day of Reckoning.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the promise of a Day of Reckoning, where individuals will be held accountable for their actions. The verse serves as a reminder of the reality of this Day and the consequences that await people based on their deeds. It emphasizes the inevitability of this Day, and encourages people to prepare for it by living righteously and avoiding sin.
orig: هذا ما توعدون ليوم الحساب

translation: Indeed, this is our provision, which has no end.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the provision or sustenance that comes from God, and emphasizes its enduring and unending nature. The verse can be interpreted as a reminder that all blessings and provisions come from God, and that they are not guaranteed to last forever. However, in this context, the focus is on the unending nature of the provision, indicating that it is a source of ongoing and lasting blessings. This can serve as a source of comfort and reassurance for those who trust in God and rely on His provision, reminding them that their blessings and sustenance are secure and will continue as long as they remain faithful and grateful.
orig: إن هذا لرزقنا ما له من نفاد

translation: Indeed, for the transgressors there is a painful punishment.
interpretation: The verse states that there is a painful punishment awaiting those who commit transgressions or sins. This is a general warning to all people who engage in unlawful and immoral behavior, reminding them of the consequences of their actions. The punishment for such individuals will be severe and painful, reflecting the gravity of their sins and the seriousness of their transgressions.
orig: هذا وإن للطاغين لشر مآب

translation: Gehenna (Hell) will be brought (for them) nearby: then, indeed, it will depart from them, (that) day, the driving away (there) will be at distance of five hundred years.
interpretation: The verse describes the approach of Hell towards the unbelievers on the Day of Judgment. The distance it moves away each time is equivalent to a journey of five hundred years. This emphasizes the overwhelming terror and awe-inspiring nature of the Day of Judgment. The verse serves as a warning to those who reject the message of Islam, reminding them of the severe consequences of their disbelief.
orig: جهنم يصلونها فبئس المهاد

translation: "So let them taste it - boiling and bitter."
interpretation: The verse speaks about the punishment of the wrongdoers, describing it as boiling and bitter. This vivid and powerful imagery emphasizes the severity and intensity of the punishment, and serves as a warning to those who persist in their wrongdoing. The verse suggests that the punishment is a just consequence of their actions, and that they will ultimately have to face the consequences of their choices.
orig: هذا فليذوقوه حميم وغساق

translation: And the last of their kind are pairs [male and female].
interpretation: The verse refers to the final remnants of a group or species, describing them as pairs, meaning male and female. The exact context and identity of the group or species being referred to is not specified in the verse, leaving it open to interpretation based on the surrounding text. However, the verse may be emphasizing the small number and vulnerable state of the group, as the last of their kind, and the pairing of males and females as a sign of their continuation and the potential for their survival.
orig: وآخر من شكله أزواج

translation: This is a party that has come upon you, but you are not welcome. Indeed, they are the fuel of the Fire.
interpretation: The verse is a warning about a group of people who have come upon the believers, but are not welcome. These people are described as the 'fuel of the Fire', which is a metaphor for hell. This implies that they are destined for hell and will be punished for their actions. The verse serves as a reminder to be cautious of those who are against the believers and to be aware of the consequences of associating with them.
orig: هذا فوج مقتحم معكم لا مرحبا بهم إنهم صالو النار

translation: They said, 'No, you are not welcome. Indeed, you have come to us before, and wretched is the decision.'
interpretation: The verse describes the rejection and hostility of a group of people towards a certain individual or group, who have come to them. The people not only refuse to welcome them, but they also criticize their decision to come and express their discontent. The verse may be interpreted as a warning against rejection and hostility towards others, emphasizing the importance of hospitality and openness towards others, even if they have been rejected in the past. The verse may also be interpreted as a reminder that past experiences and decisions do not necessarily determine the outcome of a situation, and that one should not be quick to judge or dismiss others based on past experiences.
orig: قالوا بل أنتم لا مرحبا بكم أنتم قدمتموه لنا فبئس القرار

translation: They will say, 'Our Lord, you have brought this upon us, so increase us in punishment!'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the regret and remorse of the people who have been punished for their sins. They acknowledge that they deserve the punishment and even ask for it to be increased, showing the depth of their remorse. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of seeking forgiveness and repentance before it is too late, and of the reality of the punishment for those who persist in their sins and reject God's mercy.
orig: قالوا ربنا من قدم لنا هذا فزده عذابا ضعفا في النار

translation: And they said, 'We will never believe until we see men like ourselves being sent down before us.'
interpretation: The verse describes the disbelievers' demand for a sign from God in the form of men being sent down before them. This demand reflects their rejection of faith and their denial of the messengers that have already been sent to them. The verse highlights the arrogance and stubbornness of the disbelievers, who refuse to believe until they see something extraordinary that aligns with their own expectations. The verse serves as a reminder that faith cannot be based on such whims and desires, but rather on the message brought by the messengers of God.
orig: وقالوا ما لنا لا نرى رجالا كنا نعدهم من الأشرار

translation: Or have We taken them as a mockery, or has the time passed them by?
interpretation: The verse is a rhetorical question, asking whether the previous nations were taken as a mockery or if time has passed them by. In other words, the verse is questioning whether the previous nations were destroyed because they were treated as a joke or if they were destroyed because they failed to heed the warnings and signs from God. The verse serves as a reminder to the listeners and readers that they too will be held accountable for their actions and that they should not ignore the signs from God.
orig: أتخذناهم سخريا أم زاغت عنهم الأبصار

translation: That is the true certainty of the disputers of the Fire.
interpretation: The verse refers to the 'disputers of the Fire' who deny or question the existence of Hellfire. The verse asserts that the Fire is a real and inevitable destination for those who deny it, and it is a certainty that cannot be disputed. The verse emphasizes the reality of the punishment for the disbelievers and the importance of accepting and acknowledging the truth.
orig: إن ذلك لحق تخاصم أهل النار

translation: Say, 'Indeed, I am only a warner. And there is no deity except Allah, the One, the Prevailing.'
interpretation: The verse is a statement made by a prophet or a messenger, emphasizing their role as a warner who has been sent to convey a message from Allah. The verse also emphasizes the oneness of Allah, stating that there is no other deity worthy of worship except for Him, and that He is the One, the Prevailer, indicating His supremacy and power over all things. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of worshiping Allah alone, and the role of the prophet or messenger as a warner, conveying Allah's message to the people.
orig: قل إنما أنا منذر وما من إله إلا الله الواحد القهار

translation: Lord of the heavens and the earth and what is between them, the Exalted in Might, the Forgiving.
interpretation: The verse is a declaration of God's power and authority over all of creation, including the heavens, the earth, and everything that exists between them. The verse emphasizes God's greatness and might through the use of the titles 'Exalted in Might' and 'Forgiving'. These titles convey the idea that God is all-powerful and able to forgive those who repent and seek His forgiveness. The verse serves as a reminder of God's greatness and His capacity for mercy, inviting the reader to reflect on their relationship with God and to seek His forgiveness.
orig: رب السماوات والأرض وما بينهما العزيز الغفار

translation: Say, (This is) a great news/narration/tiding/announcement
interpretation: The verse is a command to the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) to proclaim that he has received a great and important news/narration/tiding/announcement. This news/narration/tiding/announcement is the revelation of the Quran, which was a significant and transformative event for the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) and the early Muslims. The verse emphasizes the importance of the revelation and the need to communicate it to others. It also highlights the role of the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) as a messenger of God, tasked with delivering the divine message to humanity.
orig: قل هو نبأ عظيم

translation: But you are unto him not hidden.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes that God's knowledge is all-encompassing and nothing is hidden from Him. The word 'you' refers to all of humanity, and the verse stresses that every person is fully exposed and visible to God. This interpretation reminds people of the importance of living a righteous life, as God is aware of all actions and intentions, even those that are hidden from other people.
orig: أنتم عنه معرضون

translation: I have no knowledge of what they dispute, except what is revealed to me.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the limitations of the Prophet Muhammad's knowledge. He asserts that he does not have any knowledge of the matters being disputed among the people, except for what has been revealed to him by God. This emphasizes the idea that the Prophet Muhammad is only a mortal man and that his knowledge is limited, and that he receives his knowledge through divine revelation. The verse also highlights the importance of turning to God for guidance and knowledge, as the ultimate source of truth and wisdom.
orig: ما كان لي من علم بالملإ الأعلى إذ يختصمون

translation: Indeed, it is not for me to merely convey except that I am a clear warner.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the role of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) as a clear and unequivocal warner, whose responsibility is only to convey the message of Islam. The use of the phrase 'it is not for me' highlights the divine origin of this responsibility and the limitations of the Prophet's role. This verse serves as a reminder that the responsibility of accepting or rejecting the message lies solely with the people, and that the Prophet has fulfilled his duty by delivering the message clearly.
orig: إن يوحى إلي إلا أنما أنا نذير مبين

translation: When your Lord said to the angels, 'Indeed, I am going to create a human from clay.'
interpretation: The verse describes God's intention to create a human being from clay, as revealed to the angels. This verse highlights God's power and sovereignty over all of creation and the special status of human beings in God's plan. The creation of human beings from clay is a metaphor for the humble and earthly origins of humanity, and it emphasizes the extraordinary nature of God's creation. This verse also introduces the story of the creation of human beings, and it sets the stage for the discussion of human nature, free will, and the relationship between God and humanity.
orig: إذ قال ربك للملائكة إني خالق بشرا من طين

translation: And when I have proportioned him and breathed into him of My spirit, then fall down to him in prostration.
interpretation: This verse speaks about the creation of human beings by God. When God has completed the creation of a human and breathed His spirit into them, the angels are commanded to prostrate before the newly created human being. The verse highlights the significance of human beings as the most honored of God's creation, and emphasizes the importance of respect and humility towards all human beings, as they are the recipients of God's spirit.
orig: فإذا سويته ونفخت فيه من روحي فقعوا له ساجدين

translation: All the angels fell down in prostration.
interpretation: The verse describes the act of prostration by all the angels. While the verse is brief, it emphasizes the unified and complete nature of the angels' prostration, indicating their submission and obedience to God's command. The verse can be seen as a reminder of the importance of submission and obedience to God in Islamic teachings.
orig: فسجد الملائكة كلهم أجمعون

translation: But Satan became proud and he was one of the disbelievers.
interpretation: The verse refers to Satan's rejection of God's command to prostrate to Adam, as he saw himself superior to Adam. As a result, Satan became proud and refused to obey God, leading to his downfall and condemnation. The verse serves as a reminder of the dangers of pride and arrogance, and the consequences of disobedience to God's commands.
orig: إلا إبليس استكبر وكان من الكافرين

translation: He said, 'O Shaitan, what prevented you from prostrating to what I created with My hands? Did you become too proud, or were you already among the exalted?'
interpretation: The verse is a conversation between God and Shaitan (Satan), where God asks Shaitan why he refused to prostrate to Adam, who was created by God. God asks Shaitan if he became too proud or if he already considered himself among the exalted. The verse highlights Shaitan's arrogance and disobedience towards God and contrasts it with God's power and authority in creating and commanding all things. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of humility and obedience towards God and the consequences of pride and disobedience.
orig: قال يا إبليس ما منعك أن تسجد لما خلقت بيدي أستكبرت أم كنت من العالين

translation: He said, 'I am better than him, You created me from fire and created him from clay.'
interpretation: The verse is a quote from the devil, who is refusing to bow down to Adam, the first human being. The devil is arrogantly asserting his superiority over Adam, claiming that he was created from fire while Adam was created from clay. The devil's refusal to bow down to Adam is a rejection of God's command, and it is a result of the devil's pride and arrogance. The verse highlights the dangers of pride and arrogance, and it emphasizes the importance of obedience and submission to God's will, even when it goes against our own desires or beliefs.
orig: قال أنا خير منه خلقتني من نار وخلقته من طين

translation: He said, 'Get out of her, for you are accused.',
interpretation: The verse relates the command of someone (implied to be the Prophet Moses) to an individual to leave a certain place or person, because the individual has been accused or suspected of something (implied to be a sin or wrongdoing). The verse highlights the importance of dealing with accusations and suspicions in a fair and just manner, and taking appropriate action based on evidence and truth, rather than rumors or hearsay.
orig: قال فاخرج منها فإنك رجيم

translation: And indeed, upon you is my curse until the Day of Judgment.
interpretation: The verse is a statement of divine curse and wrath towards the person or people being addressed. The curse is not temporary but will last until the Day of Judgment, indicating the severity and permanence of the transgression. This verse may be used in a context of severe condemnation and warning, emphasizing the gravity of the actions and the unforgiving nature of the consequences.
orig: وإن عليك لعنتي إلى يوم الدين

translation: He said, 'My Lord, show me how You give life to the dead.'
interpretation: The verse is a conversation between a prophet and God. The prophet is asking God to show him how He gives life to the dead, which can be interpreted as a request for understanding and knowledge of the power and ability of God. The verse highlights the faith and trust of the prophet in God's power and his desire to learn more about it. The verse can also be seen as a reminder of the ultimate power of God over life and death.
orig: قال رب فأنظرني إلى يوم يبعثون

translation: He said, 'So indeed, you are of those who look on.'
interpretation: The verse is a continuation of a conversation between an unnamed person and the disbelievers. The person is rebuking the disbelievers for their lack of faith and warning them of the consequences of their actions. The phrase 'you are of those who look on' is a metaphorical expression that describes the disbelievers as mere observers, who do not take any action or participate in the world around them. The verse serves as a reminder that passivity and indifference are not acceptable in the face of injustice and wrongdoing, and that individuals have a responsibility to act and make a difference in the world.
orig: قال فإنك من المنظرين

translation: Till the Day of the Appointed Time.
interpretation: The verse refers to a specific, predestined day in the future, known only to God, when the ultimate reckoning will take place. It emphasizes the inevitability of this day and the futility of trying to escape it. The interpretation highlights the importance of being prepared and mindful of one's actions, as the Day of the Appointed Time will bring a final and unchangeable judgment for all of humanity.
orig: إلى يوم الوقت المعلوم

translation: He said, 'Then, by your might, I will surely mislead them all.'
interpretation: The verse is a quote from Satan, who is speaking to God after he has been told that he will not have power over God's believers. Satan, feeling angry and vengeful, arrogantly declares that he will use his powers of deception and temptation to lead all of humanity astray. The verse serves as a reminder of the existence of evil in the world, and the constant struggle between good and evil. It also highlights Satan's character as a being full of pride, anger, and deceit, who seeks to lead people away from the path of God.
orig: قال فبعزتك لأغوينهم أجمعين

translation: Except your servants among them, the sincere ones.
interpretation: The verse distinguishes between two groups of people: those who are not servants of God, and those who are sincere servants of God. The sincere servants are an exception, and are protected from the fate of the others. The verse highlights the importance of being a sincere servant of God, and implies that those who are not sincere will face negative consequences. The verse may be interpreted as a call to sincerity and devotion to God, and a warning to those who are not truly devoted.
orig: إلا عبادك منهم المخلصين

translation: He says, 'No, by your Lord, I will surely plot against them, and they will surely know.',
interpretation: The verse is a continuation of a conversation between a prophet and his people who rejected his message. The prophet, in response to their rejection, prays to God to guide them or to punish them. In this verse, the prophet is saying that he will continue to convey the message of God and that his people will eventually come to know the truth, either through guidance or through punishment.
orig: قال فالحق والحق أقول

translation: I will fill Hell with you and those who follow you, all together.
interpretation: The verse is a statement made by God, addressing an individual or a group of people who are being threatened with eternal damnation. The verse emphasizes the collective nature of the punishment, indicating that not only the transgressors but also those who follow them will be condemned to Hell. The verse serves as a warning to those who persist in their disbelief and wrongdoing, and a reminder of the consequences of leading others astray.
orig: لأملأن جهنم منك وممن تبعك منهم أجمعين

translation: Say, 'I do not ask you for any wage for it, nor am I one of the pretenders.'
interpretation: This verse is a continuation of Prophet Muhammad's (pbuh) message to the people, reminding them that he does not seek any material gain from them for delivering God's message. The phrase 'nor am I one of the pretenders' further emphasizes the Prophet's sincerity and truthfulness in his mission. The verse highlights the selflessness and purity of intent of the Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) and serves as a reminder for all those who convey God's message to remain steadfast and sincere in their mission, and to not seek personal gain or fame from their actions.
orig: قل ما أسألكم عليه من أجر وما أنا من المتكلفين

translation: Indeed, it is nothing but a reminder for the worlds.
interpretation: The verse asserts that the message being conveyed is nothing but a reminder for all of humanity. This reminder is not specific to a particular group of people, but rather it is for all people, regardless of time or place. The purpose of this reminder is to guide people towards the right path and to remind them of their ultimate purpose in life, which is to worship and serve their Creator. The verse encourages people to reflect on the message and to use it as a means of achieving spiritual growth and development.
orig: إن هو إلا ذكر للعالمين

translation: And you will surely know its story after a time.
interpretation: The verse speaks about something that is currently not known or understood, but will be made clear and known in the future. The phrase 'after a time' suggests that the understanding will come at a later point in time, and that the speaker and listeners should be patient and await the revelation of the truth.
orig: ولتعلمن نبأه بعد حين

translation: The revelation of the Book is from Allah, the Exalted in Might, the Wise.
interpretation: The verse affirms that the Qur'an is a revelation from Allah, the Almighty and All-Wise. It highlights the divine origin of the Qur'an, emphasizing that it is not a human creation, but a revelation from the Creator of the universe. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of the Qur'an and its guidance for believers, and the need to approach it with reverence and respect, recognizing its divine origin and the wisdom it contains.
orig: تنزيل الكتاب من الله العزيز الحكيم

translation: Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book with truth. So worship Allah, [being] sincere to Him in religion.
interpretation: The verse asserts that the Qur'an has been revealed with truth and commands the worship of Allah in a sincere and devoted manner. The verse emphasizes the importance of having a pure and unwavering faith in Allah, and the need to direct all acts of worship solely towards Him. The verse serves as a reminder that the Qur'an is a source of guidance and truth, and that it calls for a complete and unwavering devotion to Allah, free from any form of idolatry or association with other deities.
orig: إنا أنزلنا إليك الكتاب بالحق فاعبد الله مخلصا له الدين

translation: Indeed, the religion in the sight of Allah is Islam. And those who were given the Scripture did not differ except after knowledge had come to them - out of jealousy between themselves. And whoever disbelieves in the verses of Allah, then indeed, Allah is swift in account.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of Islam as the only true religion in the sight of God. It mentions that those who were given the Scripture, meaning the Jews and Christians, only differed and became divided after knowledge and guidance had come to them. This division was due to their jealousy and competition with each other. The verse also warns against disbelieving in the verses of Allah and reminds that God is swift in account, meaning that He will hold accountable those who reject His signs and messages.
orig: ألا لله الدين الخالص والذين اتخذوا من دونه أولياء ما نعبدهم إلا ليقربونا إلى الله زلفى إن الله يحكم بينهم في ما هم فيه يختلفون إن الله لا يهدي من هو كاذب كفار

translation: If Allah had willed to take a son, He could have chosen from what He creates whatever He willed. Exalted is He; He is Allah, the One, the Prevailer.
interpretation: The verse asserts the absolute power and independence of Allah, the One and Only God, by stating that if He had willed to take a son, He could have chosen from His creation whatever He willed. However, the verse emphasizes that Allah is free from any limitations or needs, and He does not have a son. The verse affirms the Islamic belief in the oneness and uniqueness of Allah, and rejects any notion of His having a partner or a son.
orig: لو أراد الله أن يتخذ ولدا لاصطفى مما يخلق ما يشاء سبحانه هو الله الواحد القهار

translation: He created the heavens and the earth in truth. He wraps the night over the day and wraps the day over the night. He has subjected the sun and the moon, each running for a specified term. Indeed, He is the Exalted in Might, the Forgiving.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the power and greatness of God, who created the heavens and the earth and has control over the natural phenomena such as the day and night, and the sun and the moon. The verse highlights the order and precision in the universe, with the day and night alternating in a regular pattern, and the sun and moon moving in a set course. The verse also conveys a message of hope and forgiveness, as it reminds the reader that God is not only the Exalted in Might but also the Forgiving, implying that those who repent and turn to Him will find mercy and forgiveness.
orig: خلق السماوات والأرض بالحق يكور الليل على النهار ويكور النهار على الليل وسخر الشمس والقمر كل يجري لأجل مسمى ألا هو العزيز الغفار

translation: He created you from a single soul, then made from it its mate, and sent down for you of the cattle eight pairs. He creates you in the wombs of your mothers, creation after creation, in a three-fold darkness. That is God, your Lord; to Him belongs sovereignty. There is no god but He. So how are you turned away?
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the power and greatness of God as the creator of all living beings. It highlights the process of creation, starting from a single soul, and then its mate, and then eight pairs of cattle, and finally the creation of human beings in the wombs of their mothers. The verse repeats the word 'creation' to emphasize the continuous and ongoing nature of God's creation. The verse also stresses the sovereignty of God and the unity of God, and it questions the disbelief and denial of the people despite the clear signs of God's power and greatness. The verse serves as a reminder of the power and majesty of God and the need for humans to submit to His will and recognize His oneness.
orig: خلقكم من نفس واحدة ثم جعل منها زوجها وأنزل لكم من الأنعام ثمانية أزواج يخلقكم في بطون أمهاتكم خلقا من بعد خلق في ظلمات ثلاث ذلكم الله ربكم له الملك لا إله إلا هو فأنى تصرفون

translation: If you disbelieve, then indeed, God is independent of you. And He does not approve disbelief for His servants. And if you are grateful, He approves it for you. And no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another. Then to your Lord is your return, and He will inform you about what you used to do. Indeed, He is Knowing of the insides of the breasts.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the consequences of disbelief and gratitude in God. It emphasizes that God is independent of His servants and does not approve of disbelief. However, if they are grateful, He approves of their gratitude. The verse also highlights the principle of individual responsibility, stating that no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another. Ultimately, the verse reminds us that we will return to our Lord and He will inform us about our deeds. The verse encourages gratitude and belief in God, and serves as a reminder of the individual accountability for our actions.
orig: إن تكفروا فإن الله غني عنكم ولا يرضى لعباده الكفر وإن تشكروا يرضه لكم ولا تزر وازرة وزر أخرى ثم إلى ربكم مرجعكم فينبئكم بما كنتم تعملون إنه عليم بذات الصدور

translation: And when affliction touches man, he calls upon his Lord, turning to Him repentant; then when He grants him a favor from Him, he forgets Him for whom he was supplicating before and sets up equals to Allah to mislead (others) from His way. Say, 'Enjoy your disbelief for a little; indeed, you are of the companions of the Fire.'
interpretation: The verse describes the behavior of a person who turns to God in times of hardship, but then forgets about Him when things are going well. The person calls upon God in repentance when facing adversity, but once the adversity has passed and they are again enjoying blessings, they forget about the One they were supplicating and instead set up equals to God, leading others astray from the right path. The verse advises such people to enjoy their disbelief while they can, as they will soon find themselves among the companions of the Fire, a metaphor for hell.
orig: وإذا مس الإنسان ضر دعا ربه منيبا إليه ثم إذا خوله نعمة منه نسي ما كان يدعو إليه من قبل وجعل لله أندادا ليضل عن سبيله قل تمتع بكفرك قليلا إنك من أصحاب النار

translation: Is he who is devoutly obedient during the hours of the night, prostrating and standing, fearing the Hereafter and hoping for the mercy of his Lord, [than one who does not]? Say, [O Muhammad], "Are those who know equal to those who do not know?" Only they will remember [who are] people of understanding.
interpretation: The verse contrasts the behavior of two types of people: those who are devoutly obedient and fearful of the Hereafter, and those who do not have knowledge or understanding. The verse emphasizes the importance of being mindful of one's actions, being aware of the consequences of those actions, and seeking the mercy of God. It suggests that those who have knowledge and understanding will remember and act accordingly, while those who do not will not. The verse serves as a reminder to be conscious of one's actions, to seek knowledge and understanding, and to strive for the pleasure of God.
orig: أمن هو قانت آناء الليل ساجدا وقائما يحذر الآخرة ويرجو رحمة ربه قل هل يستوي الذين يعلمون والذين لا يعلمون إنما يتذكر أولو الألباب

translation: Say, 'O believers, fear your Lord. For those who did well in this world, there is a good reward. And your Lord's earth is spacious. Indeed, the patient will be given their reward without account.'
interpretation: The verse addresses the believers, reminding them to fear their Lord and do good deeds in this world. It reassures them that those who have done well will receive a good reward from their Lord, and that the earth of God is spacious, indicating that there is enough space and resources for everyone. The verse also highlights the importance of patience, emphasizing that the patient will be given their reward without account, meaning that they will not be held accountable for their actions and will receive their reward solely based on their patience and faith.
orig: قل يا عباد الذين آمنوا اتقوا ربكم للذين أحسنوا في هذه الدنيا حسنة وأرض الله واسعة إنما يوفى الصابرون أجرهم بغير حساب

translation: Say, 'Indeed, I have been commanded to worship Allah, sincere to Him in religion.'
interpretation: The verse is a command to the Prophet Muhammad to proclaim that he has been commanded to worship only one God, Allah, and to do so with complete devotion and sincerity. This is a fundamental principle of Islam, the belief in the oneness of God and the rejection of all other deities. The verse emphasizes the importance of exclusive devotion to Allah, and the necessity of sincerity in one's faith and actions. It serves as a reminder of the importance of a strong and unwavering relationship with Allah, and the need to worship Him free from any form of association or polytheism.
orig: قل إني أمرت أن أعبد الله مخلصا له الدين

translation: And I have been commanded to be the first of those who submit [to Allah].
interpretation: The verse is speaking about the role of the Prophet Muhammad as the first person to submit to the will of Allah and follow His commands. This verse emphasizes the importance of being a leader and a role model for others, and the responsibility that comes with it. The Prophet Muhammad is seen as the embodiment of submission and obedience to Allah, and his actions and teachings serve as a guide for the Muslim community. This verse also highlights the importance of being a pioneer, leading the way for others to follow, and being a positive example of faith and devotion for others to emulate.
orig: وأمرت لأن أكون أول المسلمين

translation: Say, 'Indeed, I fear, if I disobey my Lord, the punishment of a tremendous day.'
interpretation: The verse is a statement made by a prophet or a messenger, urging people to follow the teachings of God and warning them of the consequences of disobedience. The 'tremendous day' refers to the Day of Judgment, a time of great reckoning when all deeds will be accounted for. The speaker expresses their fear of God's punishment on this day, emphasizing the importance of obedience and submission to God's will. The verse serves as a reminder of the ultimate reality of the afterlife and the need to prepare for it by living a righteous life in obedience to God.
orig: قل إني أخاف إن عصيت ربي عذاب يوم عظيم

translation: Say, 'Indeed, my prayer, my sacrifice, my living and my dying are for Allah, Lord of the worlds.'
interpretation: The verse is a statement of pure monotheism and devotion to God. It emphasizes the complete and total dedication of the speaker's life to God, including their worship, sacrifices, and daily activities. The phrase 'Lord of the worlds' highlights God's sovereignty and power over all of creation. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of making God the center of one's life and dedicating all of one's actions to Him.
orig: قل الله أعبد مخلصا له ديني

translation: Worship what you will besides Him, say: 'Indeed, those who are losers are those who lose themselves and their families on the Day of Resurrection. Indeed, that is manifest loss.'
interpretation: The verse is a response to those who worship other than God and challenges them to consider the consequences of their actions. The verse defines the true 'losers' as those who lose themselves and their families on the Day of Resurrection, emphasizing the ultimate and irreversible nature of the loss. The verse serves as a warning to those who reject the worship of God and encourages them to reflect on the consequences of their disbelief and the importance of the worship of the one true God.
orig: فاعبدوا ما شئتم من دونه قل إن الخاسرين الذين خسروا أنفسهم وأهليهم يوم القيامة ألا ذلك هو الخسران المبين

translation: For them there will be a shade from
interpretation: No interpretation
orig: لهم من فوقهم ظلل من النار ومن تحتهم ظلل ذلك يخوف الله به عباده يا عباد فاتقون

translation: And for those who avoid the taghut, who do not worship them and turn to Allah, there is good news. So give good news to the servants.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the good news for those who avoid the taghut, or false deities, and turn to Allah. The verse emphasizes the importance of avoiding worship of false gods and turning towards Allah. The good news serves as a reward for those who follow the right path and stay away from sin and idolatry. The verse can also be interpreted as a command for the believers to share the good news with others, encouraging them to follow the right path and avoid the worship of false deities.
orig: والذين اجتنبوا الطاغوت أن يعبدوها وأنابوا إلى الله لهم البشرى فبشر عباد

translation: Those who listen to the Word and follow the best of it, those are they whom Allah has guided, and those are they who possess intellect.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the people who listen to the Word (of God) and follow the best of it. These are the people whom God has guided and they are the ones who possess true understanding and intellect. The verse emphasizes the importance of listening to and following the Word of God, and the reward of guidance and wisdom that comes with it. The verse also implies that those who do not follow the best of the Word are not guided and lack understanding. It serves as a reminder to be attentive to the Word of God and strive to follow its teachings in order to attain guidance and wisdom.
orig: الذين يستمعون القول فيتبعون أحسنه أولئك الذين هداهم الله وأولئك هم أولو الألباب

translation: Is he who is upon clear proof from his Lord like him to whom the evil of his deed has been made attractive, so
interpretation: No interpretation
orig: أفمن حق عليه كلمة العذاب أفأنت تنقذ من في النار

translation: But as for those who fear their Lord, for them are rooms, one above another, built, beneath which rivers flow. This is a promise of Allah. And Allah does not break promise.
interpretation: The verse describes the reward for those who fear their Lord, which are beautiful and grand rooms, built one above another. These rooms have rivers flowing beneath them, indicating a paradise full of blessings and luxuries. This is a promise from God, who never breaks his promise, emphasizing the certainty of this reward for the righteous. The verse serves as a motivation and encouragement for the believers to strive for piety and righteousness in order to attain this reward.
orig: لكن الذين اتقوا ربهم لهم غرف من فوقها غرف مبنية تجري من تحتها الأنهار وعد الله لا يخلف الله الميعاد

translation: Have you not seen that God sends down water from the sky, and it flows into rivers, then it produces different kinds of plants of different colors, then it is destroyed and you see it yellow, then it becomes straw, indeed in that is a reminder for those of understanding.
interpretation: The verse highlights the natural process of growth and decay, beginning with the rain that nourishes the earth and leads to the growth of plants in various colors. However, the plants eventually wither and turn yellow, and finally become dry straw. This process serves as a reminder for those who reflect, indicating the transient nature of life and the importance of contemplating and learning from the natural world. It encourages the believers to reflect on the signs of God in the universe and to be grateful for His blessings.
orig: ألم تر أن الله أنزل من السماء ماء فسلكه ينابيع في الأرض ثم يخرج به زرعا مختلفا ألوانه ثم يهيج فتراه مصفرا ثم يجعله حطاما إن في ذلك لذكرى لأولي الألباب

translation: So then, whoever Allah opens his breast to Islam, he is upon a light from his Lord. So woe to those whose hearts are hardened against remembrance of Allah. Those are in clear error.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the difference between those who have accepted Islam and those who have not. Those who have accepted Islam have been granted guidance and light from God, while those who reject Islam have hardened their hearts against God's remembrance. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of being open to God's guidance and the dangers of rejecting it. The phrase 'woe to those whose hearts are hardened' indicates the severe consequences for those who reject God's guidance and are in clear error.
orig: أفمن شرح الله صدره للإسلام فهو على نور من ربه فويل للقاسية قلوبهم من ذكر الله أولئك في ضلال مبين

translation: It is Allah who has revealed the best discourse, a book consistent in its frequently repeated lessons, whereof grow the skins of those who fear their Lord, then their skins and their hearts soften to the remembrance of Allah. That is Allah's guidance, which He bestows upon whom He wills. And whom Allah leads astray, for him there is no guide.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the beauty and power of the Qur'an, which is the best discourse revealed by Allah. The Qur'an is described as consistent in its lessons, and it has the power to penetrate the hearts of those who fear Allah, causing their skins and hearts to soften and become receptive to the remembrance of Allah. This is the guidance that Allah bestows upon whom He wills, while those who are led astray by Allah will have no guide. The verse highlights the power of the Qur'an and the importance of being receptive to its messages and guidance.
orig: الله نزل أحسن الحديث كتابا متشابها مثاني تقشعر منه جلود الذين يخشون ربهم ثم تلين جلودهم وقلوبهم إلى ذكر الله ذلك هدى الله يهدي به من يشاء ومن يضلل الله فما له من هاد

translation: Then who will protect him against the evil consequences on the Day of Judgment? And (as for) the unjust, (unto them will be said): 'Taste the punishment of eternity; this day you are rewarded only for what you used to do.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the Day of Judgment and the fate of those who commit injustice. It emphasizes that no one will be able to protect the unjust from the consequences of their actions on that day. The verse warns that the unjust will receive punishment for eternity, and that they will be rewarded on that day based on their past actions. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of justice and the reality of the Day of Judgment, encouraging people to reflect on their actions and strive for righteousness.
orig: أفمن يتقي بوجهه سوء العذاب يوم القيامة وقيل للظالمين ذوقوا ما كنتم تكسبون

translation: Those who lied before them (the people of the past) - the punishment came to them from where they did not perceive.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the punishment of the people who lived in the past and denied the truth (most likely referring to the denial of Prophets and Messengers sent by God). The verse highlights the unexpected and sudden nature of the punishment that came to them from a direction they did not anticipate. This emphasizes the power and control of God, and the fact that no one can escape His punishment. The verse serves as a warning to those who deny the truth and commit sins, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the imminent punishment that awaits them.
orig: كذب الذين من قبلهم فأتاهم العذاب من حيث لا يشعرون

translation: So let Allah subject them to humiliation in this worldly life, and indeed the punishment of the Hereafter is greater if they only knew.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the humiliation that Allah has subjected certain people to in this worldly life, and it also warns of an even greater punishment in the hereafter. The verse emphasizes the importance of knowledge and understanding, as the people who are being humiliated would have avoided this fate if they had known about the consequences of their actions. The verse serves as a reminder that the consequences of one's actions extend beyond this worldly life and that the punishment of the hereafter is greater and more severe.
orig: فأذاقهم الله الخزي في الحياة الدنيا ولعذاب الآخرة أكبر لو كانوا يعلمون

translation: And indeed, in this Qur'an, We have presented to mankind every kind of example; that they may remember.
interpretation: The verse highlights the various examples and parables presented in the Qur'an for the benefit of mankind. The purpose of these examples and parables is to serve as a reminder for people, so that they may reflect upon them and apply the lessons to their own lives. The verse emphasizes the importance of reflection and contemplation, and the role of the Qur'an as a source of guidance and wisdom for those who seek it.
orig: ولقد ضربنا للناس في هذا القرآن من كل مثل لعلهم يتذكرون

translation: A Qur'an in Arabic, without any deviation, so that they may be mindful.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the importance of preserving the original Arabic language of the Qur'an. It emphasizes the need for the Qur'an to be free from any deviations or errors, so that people may understand and contemplate its meaning. The verse serves as a reminder that the Qur'an is a sacred text that should be treated with respect and reverence, and that its message is intended to guide people towards righteousness and mindfulness of God.
orig: قرآنا عربيا غير ذي عوج لعلهم يتقون

translation: Allah sets forth an example for the disbelievers: a slave owned by quarreling partners and a slave belonging entirely to one man - are these two equal in comparison? Praise be to Allah! But most of them do not know.
interpretation: The verse uses a metaphor to illustrate the difference between the situation of the disbelievers and the believers. The disbelievers are compared to a slave owned by multiple, quarreling masters, while the believers are compared to a slave who belongs to a single, just master. The verse emphasizes the chaos and lack of guidance experienced by the disbelievers, in contrast to the unity and certainty of the believers. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of faith and the consequences of disbelief, and encourages the reader to reflect on their own beliefs and actions.
orig: ضرب الله مثلا رجلا فيه شركاء متشاكسون ورجلا سلما لرجل هل يستويان مثلا الحمد لله بل أكثرهم لا يعلمون

translation: Verily, you will die and indeed, they too will die.
interpretation: The verse reminds the reader of the inevitability of death, emphasizing that both the person being addressed ('you') and others ('they') will certainly die. The verse conveys a message of humility and the transient nature of life, encouraging the reader to reflect on the importance of leading a righteous life and preparing for the afterlife.
orig: إنك ميت وإنهم ميتون

translation: Then indeed, you (all) will be on the Day of Judgment before your Lord, disputing (with one another).
interpretation: The verse speaks about the Day of Judgment, when all people will be gathered before God and disputes will arise among them. The verse emphasizes the reality of the Day of Judgment and the fact that people will be held accountable for their actions, with disputes arising as a result of the consequences of those actions. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of leading a just and righteous life, and of the need to prepare for the Day of Judgment, as there will be no room for disputes or excuses on that Day.
orig: ثم إنكم يوم القيامة عند ربكم تختصمون

translation: And who is more unjust than one who lies about Allah and denies the truth while it has come to him? Is there not in Hell a dwelling place for the disbelievers?
interpretation: The verse highlights the severity of lying about Allah and denying the truth, emphasizing the unjustness of such an act. It questions the readers about the fate of those who commit this act and answers by stating that there is indeed a dwelling place in Hell for the disbelievers. The verse serves as a warning to those who deny the truth and encourages them to reconsider their beliefs and actions, reminding them of the consequences of their denial of the truth.
orig: فمن أظلم ممن كذب على الله وكذب بالصدق إذ جاءه أليس في جهنم مثوى للكافرين

translation: And [as for] he who brings the truth and testifies to it - those are the righteous.
interpretation: The verse speaks about those who bring the truth and testify to it, and it describes them as the righteous. The verse emphasizes the importance of bringing the truth and standing up for it, and it highlights the qualities of those who do so. The verse serves as a reminder to be truthful and just, and it encourages the believers to stand up for what is right and true, even if it is against the majority or the powerful.
orig: والذي جاء بالصدق وصدق به أولئك هم المتقون

translation: For them there is whatever they desire with their Lord. That is the reward of the doers of good.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the ultimate reward for those who do good. The reward for their good deeds is the fulfillment of their desires by their Lord. This reward is described as being for 'them', indicating that it is a specific group of people who have earned it through their actions. The phrase 'doers of good' emphasizes the importance of righteousness and good deeds in earning this reward. The verse serves as a motivation for believers to strive for righteousness and good deeds, promising a great reward for those who are successful in this endeavor.
orig: لهم ما يشاءون عند ربهم ذلك جزاء المحسنين

translation: May Allah forgive them for the worst of what they did and reward them with the best of what they used to do.
interpretation: The verse is a dua (supplication) made by the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) for the disbelievers who opposed and fought against him and his followers. It shows the Prophet's (pbuh) mercy and compassion towards his enemies, even in the face of their rejection and persecution. The verse also highlights the Islamic belief in God's infinite mercy and forgiveness, as well as His ability to reward good deeds and forgive sins. The verse serves as a reminder for Muslims to be merciful and compassionate towards others, even towards those who may be hostile or unkind towards them.
orig: ليكفر الله عنهم أسوأ الذي عملوا ويجزيهم أجرهم بأحسن الذي كانوا يعملون

translation: Is not God sufficient for His servant? And yet they fear (other) than Him, those who associate others with God. And whoever God leads astray, for such there is no guide.
interpretation: The verse highlights the sufficiency of God for His servant and questions the need for fearing other than Him. The verse specifically mentions those who associate others with God, implying that they are not relying solely on God and are instead seeking help from other sources. The verse emphasizes that whoever God leads astray, there is no guide for them, indicating the severity of straying from the path of God and the difficulty of finding guidance for those who have gone astray.
orig: أليس الله بكاف عبده ويخوفونك بالذين من دونه ومن يضلل الله فما له من هاد

translation: And whoever Allah guides - never will he be led astray. So is Allah not Exalted in Might, Owner of Retribution?
interpretation: The verse highlights the power of Allah's guidance and the consequences of straying from His path. The verse emphasizes that those who are guided by Allah will never be led astray, and serves as a reminder of Allah's greatness and ability to exact retribution. The verse can be interpreted as a warning to those who reject Allah's guidance and a source of comfort for those who follow it, reminding them of Allah's protection and justice.
orig: ومن يهد الله فما له من مضل أليس الله بعزيز ذي انتقام

translation: And if you ask them who created the heavens and the earth, they will surely say, 'Allah.' Then say, 'Then why have you taken besides Him protectors?' If Allah intends for me some harm, can they remove His harm? Or if He intends for me mercy, can they withhold His mercy?' Say, 'Sufficient for me is Allah; upon Him the reliant rely.'
interpretation: The verse addresses the disbelievers who claim to believe in the creation of the heavens and the earth by Allah, yet they associate others with Him in worship. The verse challenges them by asking if their protectors can remove harm or withhold mercy from Allah. The verse emphasizes the sufficiency of Allah for the believers, reminding them that they should rely solely on Him. The verse serves as a reminder to the believers to stay steadfast on the path of monotheism and not be swayed by the false beliefs of the disbelievers.
orig: ولئن سألتهم من خلق السماوات والأرض ليقولن الله قل أفرأيتم ما تدعون من دون الله إن أرادني الله بضر هل هن كاشفات ضره أو أرادني برحمة هل هن ممسكات رحمته قل حسبي الله عليه يتوكل المتوكلون

translation: Say, 'O my people, act according to your capacity, I too am acting. You will soon know.
