interpretation: In this verse, the speaker (who is believed to be the Prophet Muhammad) is addressing his people and urging them to act according to their abilities and capacities. The speaker also mentions that they (the Prophet and his followers) are also doing their part. The verse implies that the people will soon see the outcome or consequences of their actions, and the speaker seems to be implying that they will come to know the truth or the right path. The verse emphasizes the importance of taking action and responsibility for one's own deeds and suggests that the people will eventually face the consequences of their choices.
orig: قل يا قوم اعملوا على مكانتكم إني عامل فسوف تعلمون

translation: For him who is given his record in his left hand will say, 'Oh, I wish I had not been given my record
interpretation: The verse speaks about the Day of Judgment and the fate of those who receive their record (of deeds) in their left hand, which is a sign of their bad deeds and rejection by God. The person in this situation will express regret for their actions and wish they had not received their record, as it is a sign of their impending punishment. The verse serves as a warning to those who are not mindful of their actions and the consequences of their deeds, urging them to repent and turn to God before it is too late.
orig: من يأتيه عذاب يخزيه ويحل عليه عذاب مقيم

translation: Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book (the Qur'an) in truth, as a confirmation of what came before it and as a guardian over it. So judge between them by what Allah has revealed, and do not follow their desires away from the truth that has come to you. For each We have appointed a law and a way. And if Allah had willed, He would have made you one nation, but He tests you through what He has given you. So compete in good deeds. To Allah you will all return, and He will inform you concerning that over which you used to differ.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the Qur'an being sent down to the Prophet Muhammad as a guide for humanity, to judge between people according to the revelation from Allah and not to follow their desires. It highlights the diversity of laws and ways that Allah has appointed for different people, and that if Allah had willed, He could have made everyone one nation. However, Allah tests people through what He has given them, so they should compete in good deeds. Ultimately, everyone will return to Allah and He will inform them of the truth of the matters they used to differ on.
orig: إنا أنزلنا عليك الكتاب للناس بالحق فمن اهتدى فلنفسه ومن ضل فإنما يضل عليها وما أنت عليهم بوكيل

translation: It is Allah who causes deaths among you and gives you life, and among you are those who are sent back to the most miserable state for a specified term. Indeed, in that are signs for a people who reflect.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the power of God over life and death. It emphasizes that only God has the power to take life and give life, and that some people are destined to die at a specific time. The verse also mentions the existence of people who are sent back to a state of misery for a specified term, indicating that they are given a chance to reflect and repent before their death. The verse serves as a reminder of the power and wisdom of God, and encourages people to reflect on the signs of God in their lives and to use their time wisely.
orig: الله يتوفى الأنفس حين موتها والتي لم تمت في منامها فيمسك التي قضى عليها الموت ويرسل الأخرى إلى أجل مسمى إن في ذلك لآيات لقوم يتفكرون

translation: Or have they taken besides Allah protectors? Say, 'Even if they had power over nothing and did not understand?'
interpretation: The verse questions the belief of those who take protectors or intercessors besides Allah. The speaker challenges these people to consider whether their protectors have any real power or understanding. The verse emphasizes the futility of seeking help or protection from anyone other than Allah, as only He has the power and knowledge to truly help and protect. The verse serves as a reminder of the oneness of Allah and the importance of putting one's trust and faith in Him alone.
orig: أم اتخذوا من دون الله شفعاء قل أولو كانوا لا يملكون شيئا ولا يعقلون

translation: Say, 'To Allah belongs [all] intercession. To Him belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. Then to Him you will be returned.'
interpretation: The verse affirms the power and sovereignty of Allah, stating that all intercession belongs to Him and He has complete control over the heavens and the earth. The verse emphasizes the ultimate return of all creation to Allah, reminding the reader of the transient nature of this world and the eternal nature of the hereafter. The verse encourages the reader to submit to the will of Allah and to seek His forgiveness and mercy.
orig: قل لله الشفاعة جميعا له ملك السماوات والأرض ثم إليه ترجعون

translation: But when God is mentioned alone, the hearts of those who do not believe in the hereafter are filled with disgust, and when others are mentioned besides Him, they rejoice.
interpretation: The verse contrasts the reactions of believers and non-believers when God is mentioned. When God is mentioned alone, the hearts of non-believers are filled with disgust, indicating their rejection and denial of God. On the other hand, when other things are mentioned besides God, they rejoice, showing their preference for worldly pleasures over God. The verse highlights the fundamental difference between believers and non-believers, and serves as a reminder of the importance of having faith and devotion to God.
orig: وإذا ذكر الله وحده اشمأزت قلوب الذين لا يؤمنون بالآخرة وإذا ذكر الذين من دونه إذا هم يستبشرون

translation: Say, 'O Allah, Creator of the heavens and the earth, Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, You will judge between Your servants regarding what they used to differ in.',
interpretation: The verse is a supplication to Allah, the Creator of the heavens and the earth, who has knowledge of the unseen and the witnessed. It is a call for Allah to judge between His servants regarding their differences. The verse highlights Allah's ultimate wisdom and justice, and the believer's trust in Him to resolve disputes and bring about justice.
orig: قل اللهم فاطر السماوات والأرض عالم الغيب والشهادة أنت تحكم بين عبادك في ما كانوا فيه يختلفون

translation: And if only those who have done wrong could possess all that is on earth, and as much again, to ransom themselves with it on the Day of Resurrection. That day, judgment shall be passed upon them in truth, and they will not be wronged.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the futility of wealth and power in the face of God's judgment on the Day of Resurrection. The verse suggests that even if the wrongdoers were to possess all the wealth on earth and an equal amount, it would not be enough to save them from the punishment they will face on that day. The verse emphasizes the certainty of God's judgment and the truth of the reckoning on the Day of Resurrection. The verse serves as a reminder that wealth and power are temporary and cannot protect one from the consequences of their actions, and that everyone will be held accountable for their deeds on the Day of Resurrection.
orig: ولو أن للذين ظلموا ما في الأرض جميعا ومثله معه لافتدوا به من سوء العذاب يوم القيامة وبدا لهم من الله ما لم يكونوا يحتسبون

translation: And so their evils that they earned appeared to them, and they were encompassed by what they used to mock at.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the consequences of the evil actions of people. They will face the consequences of their own actions, and what they used to mock at or belittle will be the very things that will surround them. The verse is a reminder that no one can escape the consequences of their actions and that everything that one does will have an impact, either in this life or in the hereafter.
orig: وبدا لهم سيئات ما كسبوا وحاق بهم ما كانوا به يستهزئون

translation: But when harm touches man, he cries out to Us, then when We bestow on him a favor from Us, he says, 'I have only been given it because of (my) knowledge.' Rather, it is a trial, but most of them do not know.
interpretation: The verse describes the human tendency to take God's blessings for granted and to attribute them to one's own abilities or knowledge. When faced with hardship, people are quick to turn to God for help, but when they receive blessings, they often forget about God and become arrogant. The verse reminds us that these blessings are actually a test from God, a way for us to prove our gratitude and devotion. However, most people do not recognize this and continue to live in ingratitude and ignorance.
orig: فإذا مس الإنسان ضر دعانا ثم إذا خولناه نعمة منا قال إنما أوتيته على علم بل هي فتنة ولكن أكثرهم لا يعلمون

translation: Those before them indeed said the same, but to no avail was what they were earning.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the people who lived before the time of the Prophet Muhammad and rejected his message, just like the disbelievers of his time. Despite their rejection and disbelief, they claimed that they were doing good deeds and earning rewards. However, the verse clearly states that their deeds were of no avail, meaning that they did not benefit them in the hereafter. The verse serves as a warning to those who reject the message of Islam and continue to commit sins, reminding them that their deeds will not be accepted by God if they do not believe and follow His teachings.
orig: قد قالها الذين من قبلهم فما أغنى عنهم ما كانوا يكسبون

translation: So they received the evil consequences of what they did, and the wrongdoers among these will be struck by the evil consequences of what they did; and they will not be able to frustrate [it].
interpretation: The verse speaks about the reception of the consequences of evil actions by those who commit them. It emphasizes that the wrongdoers will not be able to avoid or frustrate the consequences of their actions. The verse serves as a reminder that every action has a consequence and that wrongdoers will ultimately be held accountable for their actions.
orig: فأصابهم سيئات ما كسبوا والذين ظلموا من هؤلاء سيصيبهم سيئات ما كسبوا وما هم بمعجزين

translation: Do they not know that Allah extends provision for whom He wills and restricts? Indeed, in that are signs for a people who believe.
interpretation: The verse highlights the power and control of Allah over the provision of sustenance for His creations. It emphasizes that Allah provides for whom He wills and withholds provision from whom He wills. The verse further states that this is a sign for those who believe, indicating that recognizing and accepting this reality is a characteristic of true believers. The verse serves as a reminder that all blessings come from Allah, and that one should be grateful and thankful for what they have been given, while also recognizing that the withholding of blessings is a test of faith and patience.
orig: أولم يعلموا أن الله يبسط الرزق لمن يشاء ويقدر إن في ذلك لآيات لقوم يؤمنون

translation: Say, 'O My servants who have transgressed against themselves [by sinning], do not despair of the mercy of Allah. Indeed, Allah forgives all sins.' Indeed, it is He who is the Forgiving, the Merciful.
interpretation: The verse addresses those who have sinned and transgressed against themselves, urging them not to lose hope in the mercy of God. The verse emphasizes the all-encompassing nature of God's forgiveness, reminding the sinners that God forgives all sins. The verse concludes by describing God as the "Forgiving, the Merciful," highlighting His boundless compassion and willingness to forgive. The verse serves as a message of hope and a call for repentance, encouraging sinners to turn back to God and seek His forgiveness.
orig: قل يا عبادي الذين أسرفوا على أنفسهم لا تقنطوا من رحمة الله إن الله يغفر الذنوب جميعا إنه هو الغفور الرحيم

translation: And turn to your Lord and submit to Him before the punishment comes upon you, then you will not be helped.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the importance of turning to God and submitting to Him before the punishment comes. The verse emphasizes the urgency of repentance and seeking God's forgiveness, as once the punishment arrives, it will be too late for salvation. The verse serves as a warning to those who are heedless of their sins and actions, urging them to turn to God and seek His mercy before it's too late.
orig: وأنيبوا إلى ربكم وأسلموا له من قبل أن يأتيكم العذاب ثم لا تنصرون

translation: And follow the best of what has been sent down to you from your Lord before the punishment comes upon you suddenly while you are unaware.
interpretation: The verse urges people to follow the best teachings of their Lord before they are faced with divine punishment. The punishment is described as coming unexpectedly, emphasizing the importance of being always prepared and vigilant. This verse serves as a reminder to the importance of adhering to God's teachings and living a righteous life, as the consequences of not doing so can be severe and sudden.
orig: واتبعوا أحسن ما أنزل إليكم من ربكم من قبل أن يأتيكم العذاب بغتة وأنتم لا تشعرون

translation: Say, 'My soul is grieved for my shortcomings before God, and if I could, I would indeed be of those who repent.'
interpretation: The verse is a statement of regret and a desire for repentance from the speaker, who recognizes their past shortcomings and mistakes before God. The verse emphasizes the human tendency towards error and the importance of seeking forgiveness and making amends. It serves as a reminder of the power of repentance and the potential for personal growth and transformation.
orig: أن تقول نفس يا حسرتا على ما فرطت في جنب الله وإن كنت لمن الساخرين

translation: Or say, 'If only Allah had guided me, then I would have been among the righteous.'
interpretation: The verse is spoken from the perspective of someone who recognizes their own error and acknowledges that they have strayed from the path of righteousness. They express a longing for guidance from Allah, understanding that if they had been guided, they would have been among those who are righteous. This verse can be seen as an expression of regret and a desire for change and self-improvement, highlighting the importance of seeking guidance and staying on the path of righteousness.
orig: أو تقول لو أن الله هداني لكنت من المتقين

translation: Or [you will say] when you see the punishment, 'If only I had another chance so that I could be among the doers of good.'
interpretation: The verse describes the regret of a person who is facing punishment and realizes the mistakes they made in the past. This person wishes they had another chance to do good deeds and correct their wrongs. The verse highlights the importance of taking advantage of the present moment and utilizing it for good, as there may not be a second chance. It serves as a reminder of the fleeting nature of life and the importance of using one's time wisely for the sake of God.
orig: أو تقول حين ترى العذاب لو أن لي كرة فأكون من المحسنين

translation: Then indeed, My verses came to you, but you denied them and were arrogant, and you were of the disbelievers.
interpretation: The verse addresses a person or a group of people who were given signs or verses (of God), but they rejected them and were arrogant. The verse emphasizes the rejection and arrogance of the addressees, and their disbelief in the signs. This verse may serve as a warning to those who deny and reject the signs and messages of God, and a reminder that arrogance and rejection of truth will ultimately lead to a negative outcome.
orig: بلى قد جاءتك آياتي فكذبت بها واستكبرت وكنت من الكافرين

translation: And on the Day of Resurrection, you will see those who lied about Allah (i.e., denied Him or told lies about His Messengers) having their faces covered with dust. Is there not in Hell a dwelling place for the arrogant?
interpretation: The verse speaks about the fate of those who lied about Allah, including those who denied Him or told lies about His Messengers. On the Day of Resurrection, they will be seen with their faces covered in dust, a sign of their humiliation and disgrace. The verse then asks a rhetorical question, emphasizing the fact that there is indeed a dwelling place in Hell for the arrogant and the disbelievers. The verse serves as a reminder and a warning to those who reject the truth and persist in their arrogance and disbelief, urging them to reflect on the consequences of their actions and to seek Allah's forgiveness and guidance.
orig: ويوم القيامة ترى الذين كذبوا على الله وجوههم مسودة أليس في جهنم مثوى للمتكبرين

translation: And Allah will protect those who have piety, by His grace, from evil. And they will not be grieved.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the protection that Allah provides to those who have piety and fear Him. The verse emphasizes that this protection is a result of Allah's grace, and not due to any actions of the people themselves. The verse also highlights that those who are protected will not experience any harm or grief. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of having piety and fearing Allah, and the rewards that come with it.
orig: وينجي الله الذين اتقوا بمفازتهم لا يمسهم السوء ولا هم يحزنون

translation: Allah is the Creator of all things and He is, over all things, Disposer.
interpretation: The verse affirms the power and sovereignty of Allah as the Creator of all things. It emphasizes that Allah has complete control and authority over all things, and that He is the Disposer of all affairs. This verse serves as a reminder of the greatness of Allah and the dependence of all creation on Him, and it encourages believers to have trust and reliance on Allah in all matters.
orig: الله خالق كل شيء وهو على كل شيء وكيل

translation: To Him belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth, and those who disbelieve in the signs of Allah - those are the losers.
interpretation: The verse affirms that God has power and control over all of creation, including the heavens and the earth. Those who reject or disbelieve in the signs of God are considered the losers. The verse emphasizes the importance of recognizing and accepting the signs of God, and the consequences of rejecting them. It serves as a reminder of the ultimate power and authority of God, and the importance of acknowledging and submitting to His will.
orig: له مقاليد السماوات والأرض والذين كفروا بآيات الله أولئك هم الخاسرون

translation: Say, 'Do you command me to worship other than Allah?' O ignorant!
interpretation: The verse is a challenge from the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) to the disbelievers, asking them if they command him to worship other gods besides Allah. The verse highlights the absurdity of such a demand by addressing the disbelievers as 'ignorant'. The verse emphasizes the importance of monotheism and the worship of Allah alone, and serves as a rebuke to those who call for the worship of false gods.
orig: قل أفغير الله تأمروني أعبد أيها الجاهلون

translation: And We have already sent to you, [O Muhammad], a message just as We sent to Noah and the prophets after him. And We sent to Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, the Descendants, Jesus, Job, Jonah, Aaron, and Solomon, and to David We gave the Psalms.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the continuity of the message of God, which has been sent down through various prophets, including Noah, Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, Jesus, Job, Jonah, Aaron, Solomon, and David. The message emphasizes the importance of monotheism and the consequences of shirk (polytheism or associating partners with God). The verse serves as a reminder that the message sent to the Prophet Muhammad is not new, but a continuation of the same message that was sent down to previous prophets. It also highlights the significance of following and obeying the message of God, as failure to do so will result in the loss of one's deeds and the ultimate loss of salvation.
orig: ولقد أوحي إليك وإلى الذين من قبلك لئن أشركت ليحبطن عملك ولتكونن من الخاسرين

translation: But surely, to Allah belongs the pure religion. So, those who have faith (in Him) let them establish worship and believe in Him and serve Him and strive in His cause in order that they may be successful.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of worshipping and serving Allah, and encourages believers to strive in His cause. By doing so, they can attain success in this life and the hereafter. The verse also highlights that the pure religion belongs to Allah, emphasizing the importance of following His teachings and commands.
orig: بل الله فاعبد وكن من الشاكرين

translation: And they have not appraised Allah with true appraisal, while the earth entirely will be within His grasp on the Day of Resurrection, and the heavens will be folded in His right hand. Exalted is He and high above what they associate [with Him].
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the power and greatness of Allah, stating that the earth and heavens are within His grasp and control. The verse suggests that humans have not fully appreciated or understood the true nature and power of Allah. The phrase 'on the Day of Resurrection' serves as a reminder of the Day of Judgment, when all of humanity will be held accountable for their actions. The verse serves as a call for humility and reverence towards Allah, acknowledging His power and control over all things.
orig: وما قدروا الله حق قدره والأرض جميعا قبضته يوم القيامة والسماوات مطويات بيمينه سبحانه وتعالى عما يشركون

translation: And We (God) will blow in the Trumpet, then all who are in the heavens and all who are on the earth will be terrified except whom Allah wills, then We will blow in the Trumpet, then lo! They will stand up, looking on.
interpretation: This verse describes the Day of Judgment, when God will blow in the Trumpet and all living beings will be struck with terror. The verse emphasizes the all-encompassing power of God's judgment, as all beings, both in the heavens and on the earth, will be affected. The exception, "except whom Allah wills", highlights the absolute sovereignty of God, who has the power to exempt whomever He chooses from the impending doom. The second blowing of the Trumpet will bring the dead back to life, and all will stand up, looking on in anticipation of the final judgment.
orig: ونفخ في الصور فصعق من في السماوات ومن في الأرض إلا من شاء الله ثم نفخ فيه أخرى فإذا هم قيام ينظرون

translation: And the earth shone with the light of its Lord, and
interpretation: No interpretation
orig: وأشرقت الأرض بنور ربها ووضع الكتاب وجيء بالنبيين والشهداء وقضي بينهم بالحق وهم لا يظلمون

translation: And every soul will taste death. And We test you with evil and good as a trial. And to Us you will be returned.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the inevitability of death for all souls, and the fact that God has knowledge of all that people do. The verse also mentions the idea of testing people with both good and evil as a trial, and the eventual return of all people to God. The verse emphasizes the idea of accountability for one's actions and the ultimate justice of God's judgement. It serves as a reminder of the transience of life and the importance of leading a righteous life in preparation for the afterlife.
orig: ووفيت كل نفس ما عملت وهو أعلم بما يفعلون

translation: And those who disbelieved will be gathered unto Hell, unto which they will be driven, till, when they come unto it, its gates are opened and its keepers say unto them: Did not messengers come unto you from among you, reciting unto you the verses of your Lord, and warning you of the meeting of this day of yours? They will say: Yea, indeed. But the word of punishment hath proved true against the disbelievers.
interpretation: The verse describes the fate of the disbelievers who will be gathered and driven towards Hell. When they arrive at the gates of Hell, they will be met by its keepers who will remind them that they had received messengers from among them who recited the verses of their Lord and warned them of the Day of Judgment. Despite the warnings, the disbelievers will not be able to escape the punishment that has been decreed for them.
orig: وسيق الذين كفروا إلى جهنم زمرا حتى إذا جاءوها فتحت أبوابها وقال لهم خزنتها ألم يأتكم رسل منكم يتلون عليكم آيات ربكم وينذرونكم لقاء يومكم هذا قالوا بلى ولكن حقت كلمة العذاب على الكافرين

translation: It was said, 'Enter the gates of Hell, abiding therein forever.' How evil is the dwelling place of the arrogant!
interpretation: The verse describes the fate of the arrogant and disbelievers who are told to enter the gates of Hell and live there forever. The verse emphasizes the wretchedness of their destination and the eternal nature of their punishment. The verse serves as a warning to those who are arrogant and prideful, reminding them that their arrogance will lead them to a terrible fate and that they should instead turn to God in humility and submission.
orig: قيل ادخلوا أبواب جهنم خالدين فيها فبئس مثوى المتكبرين

translation: And those who fear their Lord will be driven to Paradise in groups, till, when they reach it, and its gates are opened and its keepers say, 'Peace be upon you! You have done well! So enter it to abide (therein).
interpretation: The verse describes the reward for those who fear their Lord and lead righteous lives. They will be driven to Paradise in groups, where they will be greeted by the keepers of Paradise with peace and blessings. The verse emphasizes the joy and happiness that await the righteous in the afterlife, and the sense of accomplishment and satisfaction they will feel as they enter Paradise. The verse serves as a source of hope and motivation for those who strive to lead a righteous life, reminding them of the ultimate reward that awaits them in the afterlife.
orig: وسيق الذين اتقوا ربهم إلى الجنة زمرا حتى إذا جاءوها وفتحت أبوابها وقال لهم خزنتها سلام عليكم طبتم فادخلوها خالدين

translation: And they will say, 'Praise be to Allah, who has fulfilled His promise to us and made us inherit the earth. We will now live wherever we please in the Garden. Indeed, the reward of the doers of good is with Allah.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the gratitude of the righteous people upon entering Paradise. They will praise Allah for fulfilling His promise and allowing them to inherit the earth, where they will be able to live wherever they please in the Garden. The verse emphasizes the great reward that the doers of good will receive from Allah, indicating that the reward for righteous actions is immense and beyond our imagination.
orig: وقالوا الحمد لله الذي صدقنا وعده وأورثنا الأرض نتبوأ من الجنة حيث نشاء فنعم أجر العاملين

translation: And you will see the angels surrounding the throne, glorifying their Lord with praise. And judgment is passed between them with truth, and it is said: 'Praise be to God, Lord of the worlds.'
interpretation: The verse describes the majestic scene of the angels surrounding the throne of God, glorifying and praising Him. The verse emphasizes the perfect justice of God, as judgment is passed between the angels with truth. The passage concludes with the declaration of praise, acknowledging God as the Lord of all the worlds. The verse conveys the glory of God and the perfect justice of His judgment, inspiring awe and reverence in the hearts of the believers.
orig: وترى الملائكة حافين من حول العرش يسبحون بحمد ربهم وقضي بينهم بالحق وقيل الحمد لله رب العالمين

translation: By the heaven and the starsetter (Or the night-comer)
interpretation: This verse is a chapter name (Surah Al-Rahman) and it is a form of oath, where the Prophet Muhammad is swearing by the heavens and the starsetter or the night-comer. The verse is meant to emphasize the importance of the message that is being conveyed in the following verses. It can be interpreted as a call for attention and a way to create a sense of awe and reverence in the hearts of the listeners or readers. This is a common literary device used in the Qur'an to emphasize the significance of the message and to make it more impactful.
orig: حم

translation: The revelation of the Book is from Allah, the Exalted in Might, the Knowing.
interpretation: The verse affirms that the Qur'an is a revelation from Allah, the all-powerful and all-knowing. It emphasizes the divine origin of the scripture and the supreme power and knowledge of its author, Allah. This verse serves to establish the authority and authenticity of the Qur'an, and to remind the believers of the greatness of the one who revealed it.
orig: تنزيل الكتاب من الله العزيز العليم

translation: Forgiving of sins, accepting of repentance, severe in punishment, long-suffering, there is no god but He - to Him is the journey's end.
interpretation: The verse describes God's attributes and characteristics, highlighting His forgiveness, acceptance of repentance, and long-suffering nature. However, it also emphasizes that God is severe in punishment, reminding believers that while God is merciful and forgiving, those who commit sins and do not repent should not take His mercy for granted. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of seeking forgiveness and repenting for one's sins, while also acknowledging the consequences of not doing so.
orig: غافر الذنب وقابل التوب شديد العقاب ذي الطول لا إله إلا هو إليه المصير

translation: Who disputes about the signs of Allah except those who disbelieve? So let not their ability to move around in the cities deceive you.
interpretation: The verse highlights the futility of denying the signs of God and engaging in arguments about it, and specifically addresses those who disbelieve. The verse warns against being deceived by the apparent freedom and mobility of the disbelievers, who are able to move around freely in the cities. The verse serves as a reminder that ultimate truth and justice belong to God, and that the disbelievers' apparent power and freedom is temporary and fleeting.
orig: ما يجادل في آيات الله إلا الذين كفروا فلا يغررك تقلبهم في البلاد

translation: Before them, the people of Noah and the factions after them denied [their messengers], and each nation intended to seize its messenger and argued falsely by attacking him. So I seized them, and how [severe] was My reproof.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the disbelief and rejection of past nations towards their messengers, including the people of Noah and the factions that came after them. The verse highlights the fact that every nation plotted to seize their messenger and argued against them using falsehood in order to undermine the truth. The verse then states that these nations were punished for their actions, and the severity of the punishment is emphasized by the phrase 'how [severe] was My reproof.' This verse serves as a warning to those who reject God's messengers and engage in falsehood, as they too will face a severe punishment for their actions.
orig: كذبت قبلهم قوم نوح والأحزاب من بعدهم وهمت كل أمة برسولهم ليأخذوه وجادلوا بالباطل ليدحضوا به الحق فأخذتهم فكيف كان عقاب

translation: And thus was the Word of your Lord fulfilled upon those who disbelieved: that they shall be the companions of the Fire.
interpretation: The verse affirms that the Word of God has been fulfilled against the disbelievers, who will be the companions of the Fire. The verse emphasizes the inevitability of the fate of the disbelievers, who have rejected God's message and will suffer the consequences of their actions. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of faith and the consequences of disbelief.
orig: وكذلك حقت كلمت ربك على الذين كفروا أنهم أصحاب النار

translation: Those who bear the Throne and those around it glorify their Lord with praise, and believe in Him and ask forgiveness for those who believe, saying: 'Our Lord, You encompass all things in mercy and knowledge, so forgive those who repent and follow Your way. Protect them from the punishment of the Hellfire.'
interpretation: The verse describes a scene in heaven where angels glorify and praise God. They also ask for forgiveness for the believers. The verse highlights the all-encompassing mercy and knowledge of God and the protection from the punishment of hellfire for those who repent and follow God's way. The verse serves as a reminder of the power and greatness of God and the importance of seeking forgiveness and following God's guidance.
orig: الذين يحملون العرش ومن حوله يسبحون بحمد ربهم ويؤمنون به ويستغفرون للذين آمنوا ربنا وسعت كل شيء رحمة وعلما فاغفر للذين تابوا واتبعوا سبيلك وقهم عذاب الجحيم

translation: Our Lord, and admit them to Gardens of Eden which you have promised them, - their parents, and their spouses, and their offspring. Indeed, you are the Exalted in Might, the Wise.
interpretation: The verse is a supplication to God to admit the righteous believers into Gardens of Eden, along with their parents, spouses, and offspring. The verse highlights the mercy and compassion of God, who promises to reunite families and grant them eternal paradise. The verse also emphasizes the power and wisdom of God, who has the ability to fulfill His promises and grant the ultimate reward to those who have faith and righteousness.
orig: ربنا وأدخلهم جنات عدن التي وعدتهم ومن صلح من آبائهم وأزواجهم وذرياتهم إنك أنت العزيز الحكيم

translation: And repel evil with that which is better. Indeed, he with whom you cooperate among them will be like yourself. And whoever inclines away from the remembrance of the Most Merciful - then We appoint for him a devil, and he is to him a companion.
interpretation: The verse advises believers to respond to evil with good. It emphasizes the importance of cooperating with righteous people and avoiding those who stray from the path of God. Those who turn away from the remembrance of God will be assigned a devil as a companion, indicating the severe consequences of forgetting or neglecting God. The verse encourages believers to strive for moral excellence and to avoid being influenced by negative forces.
orig: وقهم السيئات ومن تق السيئات يومئذ فقد رحمته وذلك هو الفوز العظيم

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve invite you to the fiercest of fire, while Allah invites you to Paradise and forgiveness, by His permission. And He makes clear His verses to the people that they may remember.
interpretation: The verse contrasts the invitations of the disbelievers and of Allah, emphasizing the stark difference between the two. The disbelievers invite people to the 'fiercest of fire', a metaphor for hell and eternal punishment, while Allah invites people to Paradise and forgiveness. The verse highlights Allah's mercy and willingness to forgive, contrasting it with the harmful intentions of the disbelievers. The verse also emphasizes the importance of remembering Allah's signs and teachings, and the role of these in guiding people towards the right path.
orig: إن الذين كفروا ينادون لمقت الله أكبر من مقتكم أنفسكم إذ تدعون إلى الإيمان فتكفرون

translation: They said, 'Our Lord, you have given us and our ancestors life twice, and then you caused us to die twice. So we confess our sins, is there any way out?'
interpretation: The verse describes the conversation between the people and God, where the people acknowledge their sins and ask if there is any way out of their situation. The people recognize that they have been given life twice before, and then caused to die twice, which can be interpreted as an allusion to the cycle of life and death or to the biblical story of Adam and Eve. The people's confession of their sins and their plea for a way out highlights their remorse and their desire for forgiveness and redemption. The verse can be seen as a reminder of the power of repentance and the possibility of forgiveness for those who seek it.
orig: قالوا ربنا أمتنا اثنتين وأحييتنا اثنتين فاعترفنا بذنوبنا فهل إلى خروج من سبيل

translation: That is because, when Allah is called upon alone, you disbelieved; but if associates are attributed to Him, you believe. So, the judgement is only Allah's, the Exalted, the Great.
interpretation: The verse highlights the hypocrisy of the people who only believe in Allah when other deities are associated with Him, but disbelieve when He is called upon alone. The verse emphasizes that the judgement belongs solely to Allah, who is the Exalted and Great. The verse serves as a reminder that true faith should be consistent and not dependent on external factors. It also emphasizes the oneness of Allah and the importance of believing in Him without associating any partners with Him.
orig: ذلكم بأنه إذا دعي الله وحده كفرتم وإن يشرك به تؤمنوا فالحكم لله العلي الكبير

translation: He it is Who shows you the lightning, striking for fear and hope, and who produces the heavy clouds:
interpretation: No interpretation
orig: هو الذي يريكم آياته وينزل لكم من السماء رزقا وما يتذكر إلا من ينيب

translation: So invoke God, making your religion His whole, even if the disbelievers detest it.
interpretation: The verse is a command to the believers to worship and devote themselves completely to God, regardless of the disbelievers' rejection or disapproval. The verse encourages the believers to remain steadfast and committed to their faith, even in the face of adversity and opposition. It reminds them that their ultimate goal is to please God and seek His approval, rather than seeking the approval of others. The verse also highlights the inherent conflict between the beliefs and values of the believers and the disbelievers, and the importance of staying true to one's convictions in the face of adversity.
orig: فادعوا الله مخلصين له الدين ولو كره الكافرون

translation: Exalted is He who raised the Throne and placed thereon the Rahmah. He who subjects the sun and the moon, each running (its course) for a specified term. He who (also) subjects the night and the day, (to successive periods). He who (also) subjects the living creatures of the earth. Indeed, He who sent down the Book with truth, then indeed, Jesus, the son of Mary, was a Messenger of Allah, confirmed by the Word of Allah, the Torah and the Gospel, before him. And a Messenger to the Children of Israel, saying, 'I have come to you with a sign from your Lord. I will create for you out of clay as the form of a bird, then I will breathe into it, and it will become a bird, by the leave of Allah. I will also heal the blind and the leper, and I will give life to the dead, by the leave of Allah. I will inform you of what you eat and what you store in your houses. Surely, therein is a sign for you, if you are believers. And (I have come) confirming that which was before me of the Torah, and to make lawful to you part of what was forbidden to you. And I have come to you with a proof from your Lord. So fear Allah and obey me. Indeed, Allah is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him. This is a straight path.' Then when Jesus felt disbelief from them, he said, 'Who are my helpers in the cause of Allah?' And the disciples said, 'We are helpers (in the cause) of Allah. We believe in Allah, and testify that we are Muslims. Our Lord, we have believed in what You have revealed and have followed the Messenger, so write us among those who bear witness.' And they (the disbelievers) planned and Allah planned, and Allah is the best of the planners. And (remember) when Allah said, 'O Jesus, indeed I will take you and raise you to Myself and cleanse you from those who disbelieve and will place those who follow you above those who disbelieve until the Day of Resurrection. Then to Me is your return, and I will judge between you concerning that in which you used to differ. And as for those who disbelieved, I will punish them with a severe punishment in this world and the Hereafter. And they will have no helpers.' So is it other than the way of Allah they desire? But who is more astray than he who follows his desire without guidance from Allah. Indeed, Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people. So (it is) for their rejection of Allah's signs and His Messenger, and they were not with the believers. Indeed, Allah will defend those who believe. And indeed, they will come to know who are the companions of the clear loss. O you who have believed, fear Allah and be with the truthful.' It is not for a prophet to take captives until he has thoroughly subdued the land. You desire the goods of this world, but Allah desires for you the Hereafter. And Allah is Exalted in Might and Wise. It is not for a prophet to have captives (and) wives until he has thoroughly subdued the land. You (O Muhammad) desire what Allah has for you, and Allah desires what is for you. And Allah is Knowing and Wise. And (remember) when Allah will say, 'O Jesus, Son of Mary, did you say to the people, 'Take me and my mother as deities besides Allah?'' He will say, 'Exalted are You! It was not for me to say that which I had no right. If I had said it, You would have known it. You know what is within myself, and I do not know what is within Yourself. Indeed, it is You who is Knower of the unseen. I said not to them except what You commanded me - 'Worship Allah, my Lord and your Lord.' And I was a witness over them as long as I was among them. But when You took me, You were the Observer over them. And You are, over all things, Witness.' If You should punish them - indeed they are Your servants. And if You should forgive them - indeed, You are the Exalted in Might, the Wise.
interpretation: No interpretation
orig: رفيع الدرجات ذو العرش يلقي الروح من أمره على من يشاء من عباده لينذر يوم التلاق

translation: A day they will be displayed (in public) on which no (privilege or) concealment will be granted to them from Allah. To Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. On that day, it (the dominion) will be subjected to Him (Allah) - to Him (Alone).
interpretation: The verse describes the Day of Judgment, a day when all people will be held accountable for their actions and no one will be able to conceal anything from God. The verse emphasizes God's absolute sovereignty over the heavens and the earth, and on that day, everything will be subjected to His control. The verse serves as a reminder of the reality of the Day of Judgment and the importance of living a righteous life in preparation for that day.
orig: يوم هم بارزون لا يخفى على الله منهم شيء لمن الملك اليوم لله الواحد القهار

translation: This day every soul will be recompensed for what it earned; no injustice this day, indeed Allah is swift in account.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the principle of justice, where every soul will receive its due rewards for its actions on the Day of Judgment. The verse reassures that no injustice will occur on this day and highlights the swiftness of God's accounting. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of good deeds and the accountability of one's actions on the Day of Judgment.
orig: اليوم تجزى كل نفس بما كسبت لا ظلم اليوم إن الله سريع الحساب

translation: And warn them of the Day of Distress, when hearts will be choking in the throats, and there will be no friend nor intercessor for the unjust, who could be listened to.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the 'Day of Distress', a day of reckoning when people will be held accountable for their actions. The verse describes the fear and anxiety that will be experienced on that day, with hearts 'choking in the throats', an expression used to convey the intense emotion and overwhelming fear that will be present. The verse also emphasizes the isolation of the unjust, who will not have any friends or intercessors to help them, as their fate will be sealed and no one will be able to change it. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, urging them to repent and change their ways before it is too late.
orig: وأنذرهم يوم الآزفة إذ القلوب لدى الحناجر كاظمين ما للظالمين من حميم ولا شفيع يطاع

translation: He knows the treachery of the eyes, and what the hearts conceal.
interpretation: The verse speaks about God's all-knowing nature, emphasizing that He has knowledge of the secrets of people's hearts and the hidden intentions behind their actions. The phrase 'treachery of the eyes' refers to the deceitful and untrustworthy nature of the eyes, as they can see and witness things that are then hidden or denied. The verse serves as a reminder of God's omniscience and encourages people to be mindful of their thoughts, intentions, and actions, as nothing can be hidden from God.
orig: يعلم خائنة الأعين وما تخفي الصدور

translation: But it is Allah who judges with truth, and those they invoke besides Him cannot judge anything. Indeed, Allah - He is the Hearing, the Seeing.
interpretation: The verse asserts the supremacy of Allah's judgment and denies the ability of false deities to judge. The verse emphasizes the power and knowledge of Allah, who is described as the "Hearing, the Seeing", indicating His all-encompassing knowledge and awareness. The verse serves as a reminder of the ultimate authority of Allah, and the futility of worshiping false deities who have no power or knowledge.
orig: والله يقضي بالحق والذين يدعون من دونه لا يقضون بشيء إن الله هو السميع البصير

translation: Have they not traveled through the land and seen what was the end of those who were before them, though they were stronger than them in power and greater in number in the earth? And Allah seized them because of their sins, and they had no protector against Allah.
interpretation: The verse highlights the importance of learning from the past and the consequences of ignoring the lessons of history. It reminds the listeners that previous civilizations, who were more powerful and numerous, were destroyed by God due to their sins and transgressions. The verse serves as a warning to the listeners to reflect on the fate of their predecessors and to avoid making the same mistakes. It emphasizes that God's punishment is inevitable for those who persist in their sins and that there is no protection from His wrath.
orig: أولم يسيروا في الأرض فينظروا كيف كان عاقبة الذين كانوا من قبلهم كانوا هم أشد منهم قوة وآثارا في الأرض فأخذهم الله بذنوبهم وما كان لهم من الله من واق

translation: That is because their messengers came to them with clear proofs, but they rejected them, so Allah seized them. Indeed, He is strong and severe in punishment.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the rejection of the messengers of Allah by the people, despite the clear evidence and proofs they brought. As a result, Allah punished them severely, emphasizing His power and strength. The verse serves as a reminder that rejection of the truth and the messengers of Allah will lead to severe consequences, and that Allah has the power to punish those who reject His message.
orig: ذلك بأنهم كانت تأتيهم رسلهم بالبينات فكفروا فأخذهم الله إنه قوي شديد العقاب

translation: And We certainly sent Moses with Our signs and a clear authority.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the sending of Moses by God with divine signs and a clear authority. The signs are miracles that Moses performed to prove his prophethood and the truth of his message. The clear authority refers to the power and sovereignty that Moses was given to carry out his mission. The verse emphasizes the divine support and backing that Moses received, which allowed him to fulfill his mission and lead the Israelites out of Egypt. The verse serves as a reminder that prophets and messengers are sent by God with clear signs and authority, and that their message should be followed and believed in.
orig: ولقد أرسلنا موسى بآياتنا وسلطان مبين

translation: To Pharaoh, Haman and Qarun (Korah), saying, 'You are but charlatans.'
interpretation: The verse refers to the opposition of Pharaoh, Haman, and Qarun towards Prophet Moses and his message. They rejected the truth and accused the Prophet of being a magician and a liar. This verse serves as a reminder that those who deny the truth and persist in their arrogance and rejection of God's message will face severe consequences.
orig: إلى فرعون وهامان وقارون فقالوا ساحر كذاب

translation: But when the truth came to them from Us, they said, 'Indeed, we are unaware of what you are inviting us to.' And their rejection only increased them in great sin, and their transgression only grew more and more.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the people's rejection of the truth when it was presented to them. Despite the truth coming from God, they denied it and claimed ignorance. This rejection only increased their sins and transgression, demonstrating the consequences of rejecting God's guidance. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of accepting and following the truth, and the negative impact of rejecting it.
orig: فلما جاءهم بالحق من عندنا قالوا اقتلوا أبناء الذين آمنوا معه واستحيوا نساءهم وما كيد الكافرين إلا في ضلال

translation: Pharaoh said, 'Leave me to kill Moses and let him appeal to his Lord. I fear that he will change your religion or that he will cause corruption in the land.'
interpretation: The verse describes Pharaoh's response to the demand of Moses to free the Israelites from slavery. Pharaoh's reaction is one of fear and rejection. He wants to kill Moses and orders him to appeal to his Lord, showing his lack of respect for Moses's faith and beliefs. Pharaoh's fear is twofold: first, that Moses will change the religion of Pharaoh's people, and second, that he will cause corruption in the land. The verse highlights the confrontation between Pharaoh's tyranny and Moses's mission to liberate the Israelites and establish the worship of one God.
orig: وقال فرعون ذروني أقتل موسى وليدع ربه إني أخاف أن يبدل دينكم أو أن يظهر في الأرض الفساد

translation: And Moses said, 'I have taken refuge in my Lord and your Lord, from every overbearing person who does not believe in the Day of Recompense.'
interpretation: In this verse, Moses is expressing his protection and reliance on a higher power, seeking refuge in both his Lord and the Lord of the people he is addressing. He is distancing himself from any individual who is arrogant and disbelieving in the Day of Judgment. The verse highlights the importance of humility and belief in the face of divine reckoning, and the need to seek protection from those who reject these fundamental principles.
orig: وقال موسى إني عذت بربي وربكم من كل متكبر لا يؤمن بيوم الحساب

translation: And a believer from the family of Pharaoh, who was concealing his faith, said, 'Will you kill a man because he says, "My Lord is Allah," while he has brought you clear proofs from your Lord? And if he should be lying, then upon him will be his lie, and if he should be truthful, then some of that which he promises you will afflict you. Indeed, Allah does not guide he who is a transgressing liar.
interpretation: The verse speaks about a believer from the family of Pharaoh who kept his faith hidden. He questioned the decision of the people of Pharaoh to kill a man just because he proclaimed his faith in Allah. The believer reminded them that the man had brought clear proofs from Allah and if he was lying, then he would bear the consequences of his lie. However, if he was truthful, then some of the punishment that was promised would befall them. The verse highlights the unjust actions of the people of Pharaoh and the courage of the believer who stood up to them. It emphasizes the importance of upholding justice and the consequences of oppressing those who believe in Allah.
orig: وقال رجل مؤمن من آل فرعون يكتم إيمانه أتقتلون رجلا أن يقول ربي الله وقد جاءكم بالبينات من ربكم وإن يك كاذبا فعليه كذبه وإن يك صادقا يصبكم بعض الذي يعدكم إن الله لا يهدي من هو مسرف كذاب

translation: O my people, today you have power, being dominant in the land. But who will help us against the punishment of God, if it comes upon us?
interpretation: The verse speaks to Pharaoh and his people, reminding them of their power and dominance in the land. However, the verse also warns them of the punishment of God and asks who will help them when it comes. The verse serves as a reminder that no matter how powerful or dominant one may be, they are still subject to the will and punishment of God. The verse encourages reflection and submission to God's will, as well as a recognition of one's own vulnerability and need for divine protection.
orig: يا قوم لكم الملك اليوم ظاهرين في الأرض فمن ينصرنا من بأس الله إن جاءنا قال فرعون ما أريكم إلا ما أرى وما أهديكم إلا سبيل الرشاد

translation: And the believer who said, 'O my people, indeed I fear for you the likes of the Day of the Confederates.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about a believer who is warning his people about the impending doom that will be similar to the Day of the Confederates (also known as the Day of the Trench), a significant event in Islamic history where a coalition of enemies attacked the Muslims in Medina. The believer's warning serves as a reminder to his people about the consequences of ignoring the message of the prophet and continuing in their disbelief. The verse highlights the importance of heeding the warnings of the believers and the significance of the Day of the Confederates as a historical event that serves as a warning for future generations.
orig: وقال الذي آمن يا قوم إني أخاف عليكم مثل يوم الأحزاب

translation: Like the behavior of the people of Noah, and 'Ad, and Thamud, and those after them. And Allah does not want injustice for the servants.
interpretation: The verse refers to the people of Noah, 'Ad, and Thamud, who were all destroyed for their disbelief and disobedience towards God. The verse emphasizes that God does not want injustice for His servants, and that the destruction of these communities was not His desire but a consequence of their own actions. The verse serves as a reminder that God is just and that those who commit injustice and do not repent will face consequences. It also highlights the importance of following the path of righteousness and obedience to God.
orig: مثل دأب قوم نوح وعاد وثمود والذين من بعدهم وما الله يريد ظلما للعباد

translation: And oh my people, I fear for you the Day of the Call
interpretation: The verse is a warning from a prophet to their people about the coming Day of Judgment, referred to here as the 'Day of the Call'. The prophet expresses their fear for their people's safety and well-being on this day, emphasizing the urgency and importance of preparation and repentance. The verse serves as a call to action for the people, urging them to heed the message of the prophet and turn away from their sins before it is too late.
orig: ويا قوم إني أخاف عليكم يوم التناد

translation: A day when the people will be like scattered moths, and no one will protect them from God. Whomever God leads astray, no one will guide him.
interpretation: The verse describes the Day of Judgment as a day when people will be scattered like moths, emphasizing the chaos and confusion of that day. The verse also highlights the absolute power and authority of God, stating that no one will be able to protect or help the people on that day. The verse warns of the consequences of being led astray by God, emphasizing the finality and permanence of that fate. The verse serves as a reminder of the power and majesty of God, as well as the importance of seeking guidance and staying on the right path.
orig: يوم تولون مدبرين ما لكم من الله من عاصم ومن يضلل الله فما له من هاد

translation: And Joseph has come to you before with clear signs, but you remained in doubt about what he brought to you, until when he died, you said: 'Surely, Allah will not send any messenger after him.' Thus, Allah causes to go astray him who is extravagant, disbelieving.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the people's disbelief and rejection of Prophet Joseph's message, despite the clear signs that he brought to them. The verse highlights the people's persistent doubt and disbelief, which continued even after his death. The verse also emphasizes the consequence of their disbelief, which is that they were led astray by Allah. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of accepting and following the message of the prophets, and the consequences of rejecting and doubting their message.
orig: ولقد جاءكم يوسف من قبل بالبينات فما زلتم في شك مما جاءكم به حتى إذا هلك قلتم لن يبعث الله من بعده رسولا كذلك يضل الله من هو مسرف مرتاب

translation: Those who dispute about the signs of Allah without authority having reached them, there is nothing in their breasts but pride, they will never have it. So seek help in patience and prayer. Indeed, Allah is with the patient.
interpretation: The verse addresses those who argue and dispute about the signs or revelations of God without proper understanding or authority. It states that such people are driven by arrogance and pride, and they will not be guided. The verse advises the believers to seek help through patience and prayer, and promises that God will be with those who are patient in the face of adversity and hardship.
orig: الذين يجادلون في آيات الله بغير سلطان أتاهم كبر مقتا عند الله وعند الذين آمنوا كذلك يطبع الله على كل قلب متكبر جبار

translation: And Pharaoh said, 'O Haman! Build for me a tower that I may attain the means of access (to the heaven),'
interpretation: The verse describes Pharaoh's command to Haman to build a tower that would enable him to reach the heavens. The verse highlights Pharaoh's arrogance and his belief in his own power and authority. The tower symbolizes Pharaoh's desire for control and his rejection of the idea of accountability to a higher power. The verse serves as a reminder of the dangers of arrogance and the importance of humility and submission to God's will.
orig: وقال فرعون يا هامان ابن لي صرحا لعلي أبلغ الأسباب

translation: And I have embellished for Pharaoh the life of this world, and he leads his people astray and does not guide them. And Pharaoh says, 'I will never let the religion of Moses prevail over my religion, for I do not believe in him. And far exalted is my Lord, the Most High!'
interpretation: The verse describes Pharaoh's rejection of Moses's message and his determination to maintain his own power and religion. Pharaoh is depicted as a leader who is more concerned with his own interests and the preservation of his rule, rather than the guidance of his people. He refuses to accept the religion of Moses and denies his message. The verse highlights Pharaoh's arrogance and pride, as well as his rejection of God's message. It serves as a reminder of the dangers of arrogance and the importance of humility and submission to God's will.
orig: أسباب السماوات فأطلع إلى إله موسى وإني لأظنه كاذبا وكذلك زين لفرعون سوء عمله وصد عن السبيل وما كيد فرعون إلا في تباب

translation: And the believer said, 'O my people, follow me, I will guide you to the right path.'
interpretation: The verse describes a believer calling upon their people to follow them and promising to guide them to the right path. The verse emphasizes the importance of guidance and leadership, as well as the responsibility that comes with it. The believer is confident in their ability to lead their people to the right path, and their words serve as a reminder that true guidance can only come from those who are themselves guided by their faith. The verse also highlights the role of the individual in guiding others towards the truth, and the importance of following those who are worthy of trust and respect.
orig: وقال الذي آمن يا قوم اتبعون أهدكم سبيل الرشاد

translation: O mankind, indeed this worldly life is but diversion and play, and indeed the home of the Hereafter - that is truly life, if only they knew.
interpretation: The verse highlights the transient and fleeting nature of this worldly life, describing it as a mere diversion and play. At the same time, it emphasizes the importance of the afterlife, describing it as the true and eternal home. The verse serves as a reminder to humanity to not become too attached to the temporary pleasures of this world and to focus on preparing for the afterlife. The phrase 'if only they knew' conveys a sense of regret and emphasizes the importance of understanding and recognizing the true value and significance of the afterlife.
orig: يا قوم إنما هذه الحياة الدنيا متاع وإن الآخرة هي دار القرار

translation: Whoever does an evil deed will not be recompensed except by the like thereof; but whoever does righteousness, whether male or female, while being a believer - those will enter Paradise having been given provision therein without account.
interpretation: The verse explains the principle of 'just deserts', that is, a person will be recompensed for their actions in this life, either through punishment or reward. The verse highlights the importance of righteous deeds, regardless of gender, and the ultimate reward for those who believe in God. The verse emphasizes the generosity of God, who will provide for the believers in Paradise without measure or account. The verse serves as a motivation for believers to strive for righteousness and good deeds, and a reminder that their efforts will be recognized and rewarded in the afterlife.
orig: من عمل سيئة فلا يجزى إلا مثلها ومن عمل صالحا من ذكر أو أنثى وهو مؤمن فأولئك يدخلون الجنة يرزقون فيها بغير حساب

translation: And O my people! Why do you invite me to fight against God and be of the seducers?
interpretation: The verse is a message from a prophet who is calling his people to the path of salvation while they invite him to fight against God and join them in their disbelief. The verse highlights the stark contrast between the prophet's invitation to salvation and the people's invitation to destruction. The prophet is urging his people to choose the right path, but instead, they are inviting him to join them in their sinful ways. The verse serves as a reminder to stay steadfast on the path of truth, even in the face of opposition and persecution.
orig: ويا قوم ما لي أدعوكم إلى النجاة وتدعونني إلى النار

translation: You invite me to disbelieve in God and to associate with Him that of which I have no knowledge, while I invite you to the Exalted in Power, the Forgiving.
interpretation: The verse describes a situation where the speaker is being invited to disbelieve in God and associate partners with Him, an act which the speaker acknowledges they do not have knowledge of. In contrast, the speaker invites the other party to worship the Exalted in Power, the Forgiving. The verse highlights the contrast between the two paths, one leading to disbelief and association with God, and the other leading to the worship of the All-Powerful, the Forgiving. It emphasizes the importance of seeking knowledge and avoiding ignorance, while also encouraging the path of worship and seeking forgiveness from the All-Merciful.
orig: تدعونني لأكفر بالله وأشرك به ما ليس لي به علم وأنا أدعوكم إلى العزيز الغفار

translation: There is no blame upon you that you invite me to Guidance, for indeed, my invitation is not to you, but to Allah, and you are not a guardian over me. And I am not a guardian over you. Indeed, I am sending to you the reminder. Indeed, those who fear Allah, when an affliction touches them, they supplicate to their Lord and are responding. But as for them from whom the punishment is justified, they respond not to the reminder. And they are the ones who deny the signs of their Lord and deny the meeting with Him. So their deeds have failed and on the Day of Resurrection We will not give weight to them.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of inviting others to the path of guidance, even if it may not be accepted. The speaker clarifies that their invitation is not for themselves, but rather for the sake of Allah. The verse also highlights the difference in the reactions of those who fear Allah and those who deny Him. Those who fear Allah respond to afflictions with supplication, while those who deny Him do not respond to reminders. The verse also mentions the consequences of denying Allah and His signs, stating that their deeds will be in vain on the Day of Resurrection.
orig: لا جرم أنما تدعونني إليه ليس له دعوة في الدنيا ولا في الآخرة وأن مردنا إلى الله وأن المسرفين هم أصحاب النار

translation: And they will remember what I (the prophet Muhammad) have said to them, and take my Lord as Witness. Indeed, I have relied upon Allah, my Lord and your Lord, upon Him is my duty.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the prophet Muhammad's message being remembered and acknowledged by the people. The verse emphasizes that the prophet Muhammad has fulfilled his duty of delivering the message and that he has put his trust in God. It also highlights that both the prophet Muhammad and the people are accountable to the same God. The verse serves as a reminder that the prophet Muhammad has fulfilled his role as a messenger and that the responsibility of accepting or rejecting the message lies with the people and their accountability is to God.
orig: فستذكرون ما أقول لكم وأفوض أمري إلى الله إن الله بصير بالعباد

translation: Above them (is) what they have earned, and upon Pharaoh's people (was) an evil punishment.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the just consequences that people face for their actions. The phrase 'above them is what they have earned' indicates that people will be held accountable for their deeds, whether good or bad. The second part of the verse, 'upon Pharaoh's people was an evil punishment', highlights the severe consequences that Pharaoh and his people faced as a result of their tyranny and rejection of God's signs. The verse serves as a reminder that those who commit evil and oppress others will ultimately be punished for their actions.
orig: فوقاه الله سيئات ما مكروا وحاق بآل فرعون سوء العذاب

translation: For them will be Fire above them, and beneath them, when they encounter it on the Day of Judgment. 'Enter the people of Pharaoh, into the severest of punishment.'
interpretation: The verse describes the fate of certain people who will be punished with fire both above and below them on the Day of Judgment. The people of Pharaoh are specifically mentioned as an example of those who will receive the harshest punishment. The verse serves as a warning to those who reject God's message and commit injustices, emphasizing the severe consequences of their actions and the inevitability of the Day of Judgment.
orig: النار يعرضون عليها غدوا وعشيا ويوم تقوم الساعة أدخلوا آل فرعون أشد العذاب

translation: And when they argue in the fire, the weak will say to those who were arrogant, 'Indeed, we were your followers, so will you then absolve us of some of the fire?'
interpretation: The verse describes a scene in which people are arguing in the fire of Hell. The weak or oppressed among them address those who were arrogant and proud in the worldly life. They acknowledge their past relationship of following the arrogant ones. The weak and oppressed then ask if the arrogant ones can now absolve them from some of the punishment of the fire. This verse highlights the ultimate powerlessness of the oppressors in the face of divine justice, and the regret of those who followed them. It serves as a reminder of the consequences of arrogance and oppression, and the importance of treating others with justice and kindness.
orig: وإذ يتحاجون في النار فيقول الضعفاء للذين استكبروا إنا كنا لكم تبعا فهل أنتم مغنون عنا نصيبا من النار

translation: Those who were arrogant said, 'We are surely in a secure position.' Indeed, Allah - He has judged between the servants.
interpretation: The verse describes the attitude of the arrogant people who felt secure in their position, thinking that they were safe from any harm. However, the verse emphasizes that Allah is the one who ultimately has control and has judged between the servants. The verse serves as a reminder that no one can escape the judgment of Allah and that arrogance and pride can lead to a downfall.
orig: قال الذين استكبروا إنا كل فيها إن الله قد حكم بين العباد

translation: And those who are in the Fire said to the keepers of Hell: 'Call upon your Lord to lighten for us a day of the punishment.'
interpretation: The verse describes the desperate plea of the people who are in Hell, asking the keepers of Hell to ask their Lord to lighten the punishment for them for just one day. This verse highlights the severity of the punishment of Hell and the intense suffering of those who are in it. It also indicates that even a brief respite from the punishment would be a great relief for them. This verse serves as a reminder of the reality of Hell and the importance of avoiding it by following God's commands and staying away from sin.
orig: وقال الذين في النار لخزنة جهنم ادعوا ربكم يخفف عنا يوما من العذاب

translation: They say, 'Have not Messengers come to you with clear signs?' They say, 'Yes.' They say, 'Then pray (for your punishment).' But the prayer of the disbelievers is nothing but astray.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the disbelievers' response to the prophets and their message. The disbelievers acknowledge that messengers have come to them with clear signs, but they still reject the message. They are told to pray for their punishment, indicating that their rejection of the truth will lead to a negative outcome. The verse highlights the futility of the disbelievers' actions, as their prayers are described as being 'nothing but astray', emphasizing that their rejection of the truth has led them down a path of misguidance.
orig: قالوا أولم تك تأتيكم رسلكم بالبينات قالوا بلى قالوا فادعوا وما دعاء الكافرين إلا في ضلال

translation: Indeed, We will support Our messengers and those who believe during the life of this world and on the Day when the witnesses will stand.
interpretation: The verse speaks about God's promise to support His messengers and those who believe in them during their lives and on the Day of Judgment. The verse emphasizes the certainty of God's help and the solidarity between the believers and the messengers. The phrase 'on the Day when the witnesses will stand' refers to the Day of Judgment, when all people will be held accountable for their actions and the truth will be made clear. The verse gives hope and reassurance to the believers, reminding them that they are not alone in their struggle and that God will be with them in this world and in the hereafter.
orig: إنا لننصر رسلنا والذين آمنوا في الحياة الدنيا ويوم يقوم الأشهاد

translation: A day on which the wrongdoers will not benefit from their excuses, and for them is the curse, and they will have the worst of abodes.
interpretation: The verse speaks about a day of judgment when the wrongdoers will not be able to escape punishment despite their excuses. The verse emphasizes the severity of the punishment, which is described as a 'curse' and the 'worst of abodes'. The verse serves as a warning to those who commit wrongdoings, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment. The verse also emphasizes that no excuse will be accepted on that day and that the wrongdoers will face the consequences of their actions.
orig: يوم لا ينفع الظالمين معذرتهم ولهم اللعنة ولهم سوء الدار

translation: And We certainly gave Moses the guidance and made the Children of Israel inherit the Book.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the giving of guidance to Moses and the inheritance of the Book (Torah) by the Children of Israel. The verse highlights the special relationship between God, Moses, and the Israelites, and the significance of the revelation of the Torah to the Israelites. The verse can also be seen as a reference to the continuity of divine guidance and revelation, with the Torah serving as a foundation for the later revelations of the Qur'an. The verse may also serve as a reminder of the importance of the scriptures and the guidance they provide for the believers.
orig: ولقد آتينا موسى الهدى وأورثنا بني إسرائيل الكتاب

translation: Guidance and a reminder for those of understanding.
interpretation: The verse is providing guidance and a reminder to those who are intellectually inclined and capable of understanding. It implies that the message of the Qur'an is not only for the simple-minded, but also for those who are thoughtful and reflective. The verse encourages the readers to ponder upon the message of the Qay'n and use their intellect and understanding to gain wisdom and enlightenment.
orig: هدى وذكرى لأولي الألباب

translation: So be patient. Indeed, the promise of Allah is truth. And seek forgiveness for your sin and praise your Lord, the Most High, in the evening and the morning.
interpretation: The verse encourages patience and faith in God's promise, emphasizing its truth. It also advises the believer to seek forgiveness for their sins and to praise and worship God in the morning and evening. This regular practice of worship and seeking forgiveness is a means of drawing closer to God, seeking His mercy and blessings, and cultivating a strong and enduring faith.
orig: فاصبر إن وعد الله حق واستغفر لذنبك وسبح بحمد ربك بالعشي والإبكار

translation: Indeed, those who argue about the signs of Allah without any authority having come to them - there is in their hearts no but a disease, so follow not the desires of those - who have denied Our signs and seek to distort them or ignore them.
interpretation: The verse warns against those who argue about the signs of God without proper authority, indicating that such arguments come from a place of illness and ignorance in their hearts. The verse advises against following the desires of those who deny God's signs and seek to distort or ignore them. Instead, the verse encourages believers to seek protection in God, who is all-hearing and all-seeing, and to remain true to the teachings of Islam.
orig: إن الذين يجادلون في آيات الله بغير سلطان أتاهم إن في صدورهم إلا كبر ما هم ببالغيه فاستعذ بالله إنه هو السميع البصير

translation: The creation of the heavens and the earth is indeed greater than the creation of mankind, yet most of mankind do not know.
interpretation: The verse highlights the greatness of the creation of the heavens and the earth compared to the creation of mankind. However, it also points out that most people are unaware of this fact. This lack of awareness or appreciation for the wonders of God's creation is a recurring theme in the Qur'an and serves as a reminder of the limitations of human knowledge and understanding. The verse encourages believers to reflect on the signs of God's power and wisdom in the natural world and to recognize the true nature of their own existence as creatures of the divine Creator.
orig: لخلق السماوات والأرض أكبر من خلق الناس ولكن أكثر الناس لا يعلمون

translation: But not equal are the blind and the seeing, nor are (the) darknesses and the light, nor the shade and the heat; and not equal are the living and the dead. Indeed, Allah causes to hear whom He wills, but you cannot make those in the graves hear.
interpretation: The verse highlights the fundamental differences between various contrasting pairs, emphasizing the unequal nature of the blind and the seeing, darkness and light, shade and heat, and the living and the dead. By drawing attention to these disparities, the verse underscores the importance of recognizing the inherent value and significance of each aspect. Furthermore, the verse asserts that Allah grants the ability to hear to those whom He wills, while the deceased cannot be made to hear. This statement serves to emphasize the power and authority of Allah, and the limitations of human abilities.
orig: وما يستوي الأعمى والبصير والذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات ولا المسيء قليلا ما تتذكرون

translation: Indeed, the Hour is coming. There is no doubt about it, but most of the people do not believe.
interpretation: The verse affirms the coming of the 'Hour', which refers to the Day of Judgment. The verse emphasizes the inevitability of this event and the lack of doubt about its occurrence. However, the verse also highlights the disbelief of most people in this reality. The verse serves as a warning to the disbelievers and a reminder to the believers of the importance of faith and preparation for the Day of Judgment.
orig: إن الساعة لآتية لا ريب فيها ولكن أكثر الناس لا يؤمنون

translation: And your Lord says, 'Call upon Me; I will respond to you.' Indeed, those who are too arrogant to worship Me will enter Hell, disgraced.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of worshiping God and the consequences of arrogance and disbelief. By encouraging the believers to call upon God, the verse highlights the accessibility and willingness of God to respond to the prayers of His servants. On the other hand, those who are too proud and arrogant to worship God will be punished and enter Hell in a state of disgrace and dishonor. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of humility and submission to God, and the dangers of arrogance and pride.
orig: وقال ربكم ادعوني أستجب لكم إن الذين يستكبرون عن عبادتي سيدخلون جهنم داخرين

translation: It is Allah who made for you the night that you may rest therein and the day giving sight. Indeed, Allah is full of grace to the people, but most of the people are not grateful.
interpretation: The verse highlights the blessings of Allah in creating the night and day, providing a time for rest and a time for sight. The verse emphasizes Allah's grace and generosity towards humanity, but laments that most people do not express gratitude for these blessings. The verse serves as a reminder to be thankful for the blessings bestowed upon us, and to recognize Allah's role in providing for our needs.
orig: الله الذي جعل لكم الليل لتسكنوا فيه والنهار مبصرا إن الله لذو فضل على الناس ولكن أكثر الناس لا يشكرون

translation: That is Allah, your Lord, Creator of all things. There is no deity except Him, so how are you deluded?
interpretation: The verse affirms the oneness of Allah as the creator of all things and emphasizes that there is no deity but Him. The verse then questions the reader about their rejection or ignorance of this truth, as they are being deluded or misled. The verse serves as a reminder of the unity and power of Allah, and the importance of recognizing and submitting to this truth.
orig: ذلكم الله ربكم خالق كل شيء لا إله إلا هو فأنى تؤفكون

translation: Thus does Allah (itself) seal the heart of those who deny His signs.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the sealing of the hearts of those who reject the signs of God. The act of sealing the heart implies that these individuals have become hardened and resistant to the truth, and are therefore unable to accept or understand the message of God. This is a consequence of their denial and rejection of the divine signs and revelations. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of being open and receptive to the messages and guidance of God.
orig: كذلك يؤفك الذين كانوا بآيات الله يجحدون

translation: It is Allah who has made for you the earth a dwelling place and the sky a ceiling and has formed you and perfected your forms and provided you with good things. That is Allah, your Lord; then blessed is Allah, Lord of the worlds.
interpretation: The verse highlights the blessings that Allah has bestowed upon humanity, including the earth as a dwelling place, the sky as a ceiling, the creation and perfecting of human forms, and the provision of good things. The verse emphasizes that Allah is the one and only Lord of all the worlds and is worthy of praise and blessings. The verse serves as a reminder of the greatness of Allah and the blessings that humans often take for granted, encouraging gratitude and reverence towards the Creator.
orig: الله الذي جعل لكم الأرض قرارا والسماء بناء وصوركم فأحسن صوركم ورزقكم من الطيبات ذلكم الله ربكم فتبارك الله رب العالمين
