translation: He is the Living (One). There is no god but He. So call upon Him, making your religion sincere to Him. Praise be to Allah, the Lord of the worlds.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the oneness of God and the importance of worshipping Him alone. It commands the believers to call upon God and make their religion pure and sincere for Him. The verse also praises God and acknowledges His lordship over all the worlds. The verse serves as a reminder to the believers to focus their worship on the one true God, and to strive for purity and sincerity in their faith and actions.
orig: هو الحي لا إله إلا هو فادعوه مخلصين له الدين الحمد لله رب العالمين

translation: Say, 'Indeed, I have been commanded to worship the Lord of the worlds (i.e., Allah) alone, having been sent clear proofs from my Lord. And I am commanded to be of those who submit (in Islam) to the Lord of all realms.'
interpretation: The verse is a command to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to worship only the Lord of the worlds (Allah) and to follow the guidance that has been revealed to him. The command to worship Allah alone is based on the clear proofs and evidence that the Prophet has received from his Lord. The verse also emphasizes the importance of submitting to Allah, the Lord of all realms, and the need to follow His commands. The verse is a reminder of the importance of faith and obedience to Allah, and the need to reject false deities and beliefs.
orig: قل إني نهيت أن أعبد الذين تدعون من دون الله لما جاءني البينات من ربي وأمرت أن أسلم لرب العالمين

translation: He it is Who created you from dust, then from a sperm-drop, then from a clot, then brings you forth as a child, then that you may reach maturity, then that you may become elders - though some of you die before - and that you may reach an appointed term, and that you may understand.
interpretation: The verse describes the stages of human creation and development, from the creation of humans from dust, to the creation of a sperm-drop, to the formation of a clot, to the birth of a child, and then reaching maturity and becoming elders. The verse emphasizes the role of God in the process of creation and development, and the fact that some people may die before reaching the appointed term. The verse encourages people to reflect on the process of their creation and the significance of their existence, and to understand the wisdom behind the events that occur in their lives.
orig: هو الذي خلقكم من تراب ثم من نطفة ثم من علقة ثم يخرجكم طفلا ثم لتبلغوا أشدكم ثم لتكونوا شيوخا ومنكم من يتوفى من قبل ولتبلغوا أجلا مسمى ولعلكم تعقلون

translation: He is the one who gives life and causes death, and when He decides on a matter, He only says to it, 'Be' and it is.
interpretation: The verse affirms the power and control of God over all things, emphasizing His ability to give life and cause death. The phrase 'when He decides on a matter' highlights the sovereignty of God and His ultimate authority over all events and decisions. The final phrase 'He only says to it, "Be" and it is' is a powerful reminder of the creative power of God, and His ability to bring about whatever He wills, without any difficulty or obstacle.
orig: هو الذي يحيي ويميت فإذا قضى أمرا فإنما يقول له كن فيكون

translation: Have you not seen those who argue about the verses of God, how they are turning away?
interpretation: The verse highlights the behavior of those who engage in futile arguments about the verses of God, and emphasizes their rejection and denial of the truth. These people are so preoccupied with their own opinions and interpretations that they turn away from the divine message. The verse serves as a reminder that such behavior is misguided and that true guidance comes from accepting and submitting to God's will.
orig: ألم تر إلى الذين يجادلون في آيات الله أنى يصرفون

translation: Those who have disbelieved in the scriptures and in what We sent down with Our messengers - they will soon come to know.
interpretation: The verse speaks about those who have disbelieved in the scriptures (such as the Torah, the Psalms, and the Gospel) and denied the revelations sent down by God through His messengers. The verse warns that these disbelievers will soon come to know the truth and the consequences of their denial. The verse serves as a reminder of the certainty of God's judgment and the ultimate triumph of truth over falsehood.
orig: الذين كذبوا بالكتاب وبما أرسلنا به رسلنا فسوف يعلمون

translation: When the shackles are around their necks and the chains, they are dragged along
interpretation: The verse describes the punishment of sinners in the afterlife, where they will be punished with shackles and chains around their necks, and will be dragged along. This image conveys the idea of complete subjugation and control by God, and the utter helplessness of the sinners. It is a powerful warning of the consequences of sin and disobedience towards God, and the ultimate power and authority of God over all of His creations.
orig: إذ الأغلال في أعناقهم والسلاسل يسحبون

translation: In boiling water, then in the Fire shall they be burned.
interpretation: The verse describes the punishment of the unbelievers who will be punished in boiling water, followed by being burned in the Fire. The verse emphasizes the severity of the punishment that awaits the unbelievers. The image of boiling water and burning in the Fire is a metaphor for the intense suffering and unbearable pain that the unbelievers will experience. The verse serves as a warning to those who reject the message of Islam, reminding them of the severe consequences of their disbelief.
orig: في الحميم ثم في النار يسجرون

translation: Then it will be said to them, 'Where are those you used to associate (with Allah)?'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the Day of Judgment and the fate of those who used to associate partners with Allah. On that day, they will be asked about their associates and where they are, implying that their associates will not be able to help or save them from the punishment of Allah. The verse emphasizes the importance of worshipping Allah alone and the consequences of associating partners with Him, which is a grave sin in Islam. It also serves as a reminder that on the Day of Judgment, everyone will be held accountable for their beliefs and actions, and no one will be able to intercede on their behalf.
orig: ثم قيل لهم أين ما كنتم تشركون

translation: They have said (of their false deities), 'There is no deity except Allah,' yet they were unjust to themselves. [They did not truly believe]. So without a doubt, Allah is most surely going to guide the disbelievers astray.
interpretation: The verse highlights the hypocrisy of those who claim to believe in Allah, but still commit injustices and wrong their own selves. The verse emphasizes that such people are not true believers, and that Allah will ultimately lead those who reject the truth and persist in their disbelief astray. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of sincerity and consistency in faith, and of the consequences of hypocrisy and false belief.
orig: من دون الله قالوا ضلوا عنا بل لم نكن ندعو من قبل شيئا كذلك يضل الله الكافرين

translation: That is because you rejoiced in the earth without right, and because you were celebrating.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the reason for a certain punishment or consequence that has befallen the listeners or readers. The reason for this punishment is their rejoicing in the earth without right, meaning that they were enjoying worldly pleasures and riches without being mindful of God or showing gratitude for their blessings. Additionally, they were celebrating, possibly referring to their arrogance and pride in their wealth and status. The verse serves as a reminder that ultimate happiness and joy come from leading a righteous life and pleasing God, rather than being preoccupied with worldly pleasures and material wealth.
orig: ذلكم بما كنتم تفرحون في الأرض بغير الحق وبما كنتم تمرحون

translation: Enter the gates of Hell, abiding therein forever, for evil is the dwelling place of the proud.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the fate of the proud, who will enter the gates of Hell and abide therein forever. The verse emphasizes the wretchedness of their destination, indicating that the punishment of Hell is a fitting consequence for their arrogance and pride. The verse serves as a warning to those who are arrogant and boastful, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: ادخلوا أبواب جهنم خالدين فيها فبئس مثوى المتكبرين

translation: So be patient, indeed the promise of Allah is truth. And whether We show you some of what We have promised them, or We take you in death, to Us is their return.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the promise of God and the need for patience. The verse reminds the listener that the promise of God is true and that they will either see some of the punishment that God has promised for the disbelievers or they will die before it happens. Either way, the verse emphasizes that the people will ultimately return to God. The verse serves as a reminder of the power and certainty of God's promises and the need for patience in the face of adversity.
orig: فاصبر إن وعد الله حق فإما نرينك بعض الذي نعدهم أو نتوفينك فإلينا يرجعون

translation: And We have already sent messengers before you, some of them We have mentioned to you and some of them We have not mentioned to you. And no messenger comes to them except that they ridicule him. So We destroy those who are unjust, and it is inevitable that the disbelievers will be gathered together to hell.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the messengers that were sent by God before the Prophet Muhammad, some of whom are mentioned in the Qur'an and some are not. It highlights the fact that all messengers were met with ridicule and rejection by their people. The verse emphasizes the fate of those who reject God's messengers and commit injustice, stating that they will be destroyed. It also mentions that the disbelievers will inevitably be gathered together in hell. The verse serves as a reminder of the consequences of rejecting God's messengers and committing injustice, and the certainty of God's punishment for those who do so.
orig: ولقد أرسلنا رسلا من قبلك منهم من قصصنا عليك ومنهم من لم نقصص عليك وما كان لرسول أن يأتي بآية إلا بإذن الله فإذا جاء أمر الله قضي بالحق وخسر هنالك المبطلون

translation: It is Allah who has made for you the animals, upon which you ride, and from them you eat.
interpretation: The verse highlights the blessings of Allah by mentioning the animals, which serve as a means of transportation and as a source of food. This emphasizes the greatness of Allah, who has provided for His creatures in such a way that they can benefit from the animals in multiple ways. The verse also serves as a reminder of the importance of being grateful for these blessings and using them in a responsible and ethical manner.
orig: الله الذي جعل لكم الأنعام لتركبوا منها ومنها تأكلون

translation: And in it (the sky) you have a sign (of Allah's Sustainer): your journey by night and by day (takes place) through it. And through it you seek His bounty, and indeed you are ever guided therein.
interpretation: The verse highlights the significance of the sky as a sign of God's existence and power. It emphasizes the importance of the sky in facilitating human life, serving as a means of transportation and a source of sustenance. The verse reminds people of their dependence on God and the guidance He provides, encouraging them to seek His bounty and be grateful for His blessings. The verse encourages a sense of appreciation and gratitude towards God for the blessings and guidance that are taken for granted.
orig: ولكم فيها منافع ولتبلغوا عليها حاجة في صدوركم وعليها وعلى الفلك تحملون

translation: And We will show them Our signs in the horizons and within themselves until it becomes clear to them that it is the truth.
interpretation: The verse speaks about how God will show people His signs, both in the world around them (horizons) and within themselves, as a way of guiding them to the truth. The phrase 'until it becomes clear to them that it is the truth' implies that the signs will continue to be shown until people can no longer deny the truth of God's existence and message. The verse serves as a reminder of the many ways that God communicates with people and the importance of being open to and recognizing these signs.
orig: ويريكم آياته فأي آيات الله تنكرون

translation: Have they not traveled through the land and seen how was the end of those before them? They were greater than them in power, and they cultivated the earth more. So, what they earned did not avail them.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the fate of previous civilizations that were more powerful and advanced than the current one. Despite their strength and achievements, they were destroyed and their deeds were of no benefit to them in the end. The verse encourages people to reflect on the past and learn from the mistakes of those who came before them. It serves as a reminder that material wealth and power are temporary and that the ultimate judge of human actions is God.
orig: أفلم يسيروا في الأرض فينظروا كيف كان عاقبة الذين من قبلهم كانوا أكثر منهم وأشد قوة وآثارا في الأرض فما أغنى عنهم ما كانوا يكسبون

translation: But when their messengers came to them with clear proofs, they rejoiced in what they had of knowledge, and they denied what they were told of.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the response of people to the messengers of God who brought clear proofs and evidence of the truth. Instead of accepting the message and following the guidance of the messengers, the people rejoiced in their own knowledge and rejected the message. This rejection was not based on any evidence or proof, but rather on their denial and mockery of the message and the messengers. The verse serves as a warning to those who reject the message of God and the guidance of His messengers, reminding them of the consequences of their denial and arrogance.
orig: فلما جاءتهم رسلهم بالبينات فرحوا بما عندهم من العلم وحاق بهم ما كانوا به يستهزئون

translation: But when they saw Our punishment, they said, 'We believe in God alone and reject what we used to associate with Him.'
interpretation: The verse describes the reaction of people when they see the punishment of God. Despite having previously associated partners with God, they now claim to believe in God alone and reject their previous beliefs. However, their declaration of faith comes only when they are faced with the punishment, indicating that their faith may not be genuine or sincere. The verse serves as a reminder that true faith should not be based on fear or self-preservation, but rather on a deep understanding and acceptance of God's oneness and the recognition of one's own shortcomings and sins. The verse also highlights the importance of consistent and sincere faith, rather than a faith that is motivated by fear or circumstances.
orig: فلما رأوا بأسنا قالوا آمنا بالله وحده وكفرنا بما كنا به مشركين

translation: For their faith could not help them once they saw Our punishment. Such is the punishment of God, complete and devastating. In it, the disbelievers perish.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the powerlessness of faith in the face of God's punishment. Even though the people may have had faith, it was of no use once they saw the punishment of God. The verse emphasizes the overwhelming and devastating nature of God's punishment, which leads to the destruction of the disbelievers. The verse serves as a reminder of the futility of disbelief and the power of God's punishment.
orig: فلم يك ينفعهم إيمانهم لما رأوا بأسنا سنت الله التي قد خلت في عباده وخسر هنالك الكافرون

translation:
By the heaven and the starfalling,
By the moon when it follows,
By the day when it displays,
By the night when it covers,
By the sky and Him who built it,
By the earth and Him who spread it,
By the soul and Him who proportioned it,
And inspired it with knowledge of wickedness and piety,
Successful is he who purifies it,
And failure is he who corrupts it.
interpretation: This passage, known as Surah Al-Shams (The Sun), is a series of oaths by various elements of nature and the human soul, emphasizing the importance of the themes of guidance, free will, and responsibility. The passage serves as a reminder that humans have the capacity for both good and evil, and that the ultimate success or failure lies in the choices they make. The passage encourages people to strive for purity of soul, and warns of the consequences of corruption. The passage also highlights the power and majesty of God, who created and controls the natural world and the human soul.
orig: حم

translation: A revelation from the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate.
interpretation: The verse affirms that the Qur'an is a revelation from God, who is described as the Most Merciful and the Most Compassionate. This description highlights the loving and caring nature of God, and emphasizes the importance of the message being revealed. The verse serves as a reminder of the divine origin of the Qur'an, and the significance of its teachings for believers.
orig: تنزيل من الرحمن الرحيم

translation: A book whose verses have been detailed, a Qur'an in Arabic for a people who know.
interpretation: The verse refers to the Qur'an as a book that has been divided into clear and distinct verses for the benefit of the people. The Qur'an is in Arabic, which emphasizes the importance of the language in understanding and preserving the message of the revelation. The verse suggests that the Qur'an is intended for people who are knowledgeable and capable of understanding its message, and serves as a reminder for them to reflect upon its teachings.
orig: كتاب فصلت آياته قرآنا عربيا لقوم يعلمون

translation: As a bearer of good news and a warner, yet most of them turn away, so they hear not.
interpretation: The verse describes the Prophet Muhammad's role as a bearer of good news and a warner, yet most people turn away from his message and refuse to listen. The verse highlights the rejection and obstinacy of the people, who despite being given the truth, choose to ignore it. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of being receptive to the message of Islam and the consequences of rejecting it.
orig: بشيرا ونذيرا فأعرض أكثرهم فهم لا يسمعون

translation: And they said, 'Our hearts are unaware of that to which you call us, and there is a veil over our ears, and between us and you is a barrier. So, do as you will, and we will do (as we will).'
interpretation: The verse describes the response of a group of people to the message brought by the speaker (who is likely a prophet or a messenger of God). The people claim that they do not understand the message and that there is a barrier between them and the speaker. They say that they will continue to do as they please, regardless of the message. The verse highlights the rejection and disbelief of the people, and the unwillingness to accept the truth. It serves as a reminder of the challenges faced by the prophets and messengers in delivering the message of God and the importance of perseverance in the face of rejection.
orig: وقالوا قلوبنا في أكنة مما تدعونا إليه وفي آذاننا وقر ومن بيننا وبينك حجاب فاعمل إننا عاملون

translation: Say, 'Indeed, I am only a human being like you, to whom has been revealed that your god is but one God. So fear Him and seek His forgiveness.' And woe to the polytheists.
interpretation: The verse addresses the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, and instructs him to declare his humanity and his role as a messenger, bringing the revelation that the people's god is one. The verse urges the people to worship and seek forgiveness from this one God, emphasizing the importance of monotheism. The verse also warns those who commit shirk, or the association of partners with God, with a severe warning of 'woe' or punishment. The verse highlights the fundamental Islamic belief in the oneness of God and the importance of seeking His forgiveness and avoiding polytheism.
orig: قل إنما أنا بشر مثلكم يوحى إلي أنما إلهكم إله واحد فاستقيموا إليه واستغفروه وويل للمشركين

translation: Those who do not give zakat and are disbelievers in the hereafter.
interpretation: The verse describes those who do not give zakat, a form of almsgiving in Islam, and do not believe in the hereafter. The verse categorizes these people as disbelievers, emphasizing the importance of both zakat and belief in the hereafter in Islamic teachings. The verse serves as a reminder to give zakat and to have faith in the hereafter, and also serves as a warning to those who do not, highlighting the consequences of disbelief in Islamic teachings.
orig: الذين لا يؤتون الزكاة وهم بالآخرة هم كافرون

translation: For those who believe and do righteous deeds, there is a reward that will never be cut off.
interpretation: The verse promises a reward for those who have faith and do good deeds. This reward will not be cut off or taken away, indicating its permanence and abundance. The verse serves as a motivation for believers to continue practicing their faith and doing good deeds, and a reassurance that their efforts will be recognized and rewarded by God.
orig: إن الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات لهم أجر غير ممنون

translation: Say, 'Do you then disbelieve in Him who created the earth in two days and attribute to Him equals? That is the Lord of the worlds.'
interpretation: The verse addresses the disbelievers who reject the power and oneness of the Creator of the earth. It highlights the futility and absurdity of attributing equals to the Creator, who has the power and ability to create the earth in two days. The verse emphasizes the greatness and uniqueness of the Creator, reminding the disbelievers of the foolishness of their actions and the consequences of their disbelief. The verse serves as a call to the disbelievers to reflect and ponder upon the power and might of the Creator, and to recognize and submit to His oneness and greatness.
orig: قل أئنكم لتكفرون بالذي خلق الأرض في يومين وتجعلون له أندادا ذلك رب العالمين

translation: And He placed in it (i.e. the Bayt al-Ma'mur in heaven) statues of His angels, and He made in it a lamp, and He blessed it, and He placed therein the sustenance of all beings for a specified term, (all) according to the measure determined by Him. Verily, in this are signs for those who reflect.
interpretation: This verse describes the creation of the Bayt al-Ma'mur, a celestial structure located above the seventh heaven, and the blessings that God has placed within it. The verse highlights the presence of angels, a lamp, and the sustenance for all beings. These elements serve as signs for those who reflect, emphasizing the importance of contemplation and understanding of God's creation. The verse also suggests that everything in the universe is created according to God's measure and determination, and that everything occurs in a specified term.
orig: وجعل فيها رواسي من فوقها وبارك فيها وقدر فيها أقواتها في أربعة أيام سواء للسائلين

translation: Then He ascended to the heaven while it was smoke, and said to it and to the earth, 'Come both of you willingly or unwillingly.' They both said, 'We come willingly.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about God's command to the heavens and the earth to come willingly or unwillingly. The heavens and the earth respond by saying that they come willingly. The verse emphasizes God's power and control over all of creation and the obedience of the heavens and the earth to His command. The verse can also be interpreted as a symbol of God's creation of the world and the submission of all things to His will.
orig: ثم استوى إلى السماء وهي دخان فقال لها وللأرض ائتيا طوعا أو كرها قالتا أتينا طائعين

translation: And He completed them seven heavens in two days and revealed in each heaven its command. And We adorned the lowest heaven with lamps and protection - that is the determination of the Exalted in Might, the Knowing.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the creation of the seven heavens in two days and the revelation of God's command in each heaven. The verse highlights the beauty of the lowest heaven, which is adorned with lamps and protected. The verse emphasizes the power and knowledge of God, who has the ability to determine and create the heavens. The verse serves as a reminder of God's greatness and the wonders of His creation.
orig: فقضاهن سبع سماوات في يومين وأوحى في كل سماء أمرها وزينا السماء الدنيا بمصابيح وحفظا ذلك تقدير العزيز العليم

translation: But if they turn away (from your message, O Muhammad), then say, 'I have warned you of a strike like the strike of the 'Ad and Thamud.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the Prophet Muhammad's (pbuh) warning to his people, if they turn away from his message. The warning is about a punishment that is similar to the punishment of the 'Ad and Thamud, two ancient tribes who were destroyed by God due to their disbelief and disobedience. The verse emphasizes the gravity of the situation and the urgency for the people to heed the warning and change their ways before it is too late. It also highlights the Prophet's (pbuh) role as a warner and his duty to convey the message of God, regardless of the people's response.
orig: فإن أعرضوا فقل أنذرتكم صاعقة مثل صاعقة عاد وثمود

translation: When the messengers came to them from among them and from behind them, saying: 'Worship none but Allah.' They said: 'If our Lord had willed, He would have sent down angels. So indeed, we are, in regard to what you are sent with, disbelievers.'
interpretation: The verse describes the response of the people to the messengers of God, who called upon them to worship only Allah. The people rejected the message and accused the messengers of lying, claiming that if God truly intended to send a message, He would have sent angels instead. The verse highlights the disbelief and rejection of the people in the face of divine guidance, and their refusal to accept the truth even when it comes from among them and behind them. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of accepting and following the message of the prophets, and the consequences of rejecting it.
orig: إذ جاءتهم الرسل من بين أيديهم ومن خلفهم ألا تعبدوا إلا الله قالوا لو شاء ربنا لأنزل ملائكة فإنا بما أرسلتم به كافرون

translation: But as for 'Ad, they were arrogant upon the earth without right, and they said, 'Who is stronger than us in strength?' Did they not consider that Allah who created them was more than able over them? And they were rejecting Our signs.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the people of 'Ad, who were arrogant and disbelievers. They rejected the signs of God and denied His power, despite the fact that it was He who created them. The verse emphasizes the power of God and the weakness of human beings, reminding them that God is the one who has ultimate control and power. The verse serves as a warning to those who are arrogant and deny the signs of God, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's power.
orig: فأما عاد فاستكبروا في الأرض بغير الحق وقالوا من أشد منا قوة أولم يروا أن الله الذي خلقهم هو أشد منهم قوة وكانوا بآياتنا يجحدون

translation: And We sent upon them a whirling wind on days of disaster, to taste humiliating punishment in the life of the world, and (so that) perhaps they would (be warned and) be of those who believe.
interpretation: The verse speaks about God's punishment of a group of people who were sent a whirling wind as a form of punishment. This punishment was meant to humiliate them and serve as a warning in their worldly life. The verse also implies that this punishment was a consequence of their disbelief and lack of faith. The ultimate goal of this punishment was to bring them to belief and faith.
orig: فأرسلنا عليهم ريحا صرصرا في أيام نحسات لنذيقهم عذاب الخزي في الحياة الدنيا ولعذاب الآخرة أخزى وهم لا ينصرون

translation: But as for Thamud, We guided them, but they preferred blindness over guidance; so the shock of a painful punishment seized them, because of what they used to earn.
interpretation: The verse talks about the people of Thamud who were guided by God but chose to ignore the guidance and instead followed their own desires. As a result, they were hit by a sudden and severe punishment. The verse highlights the consequences of rejecting God's guidance and following one's own desires. It serves as a reminder that those who persist in wrongdoing and ignore the guidance of God will ultimately face severe consequences.
orig: وأما ثمود فهديناهم فاستحبوا العمى على الهدى فأخذتهم صاعقة العذاب الهون بما كانوا يكسبون

translation: And We saved those who believed and used to be aware of God.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the salvation of those who had faith in God and were mindful of Him. The verse highlights the importance of faith and righteousness, and the promise of God's protection and deliverance for those who uphold these qualities.
orig: ونجينا الذين آمنوا وكانوا يتقون

translation: And the day when God will gather the enemies [of Islam] to the fire; they will be marched in ranks.
interpretation: The verse describes the Day of Judgment when God will gather the enemies of Islam and march them towards the fire. The phrase 'they will be march in ranks' indicates the order and discipline of the procession, emphasizing the power and control of God over the situation. The verse serves as a reminder of the ultimate fate of those who oppose Islam and a warning to those who may be contemplating it. It also reaffirms the belief in the Day of Judgment and the power of God over all of creation.
orig: ويوم يحشر أعداء الله إلى النار فهم يوزعون

translation: Until, when they came upon it, it was said to them, 'Indeed, your hearing and your vision and your hearts will not avail you at all.',
interpretation: This verse speaks about the moment when people are confronted with the reality of their actions and the consequences of their sins. Despite having the faculties of hearing, seeing, and feeling, they will not be able to help them in this situation. The verse emphasizes the powerlessness of humans in the face of divine judgment and serves as a reminder that all the faculties and abilities that humans possess will not be of any use when they are faced with the consequences of their actions.
orig: حتى إذا ما جاءوها شهد عليهم سمعهم وأبصارهم وجلودهم بما كانوا يعملون

translation: And they said to their skins, 'Why do you testify against us?' They said, 'Allah, who gives speech to all things, has made us speak, and He created you the first time, and to Him you are returned.'
interpretation: The verse describes a conversation between the disbelievers and their own skins, which are said to testify against them on the Day of Judgment. The skins respond by attributing their ability to speak to God, who gave speech to all things. The skins also remind the disbelievers that God created them the first time and that they will return to Him on the Day of Judgment. The verse emphasizes the power and authority of God, who is able to make inanimate objects speak and who holds ultimate control over all of creation. The verse also highlights the accountability of the disbelievers, who will be held responsible for their actions on the Day of Judgment and will have no power to deny or defend themselves.
orig: وقالوا لجلودهم لم شهدتم علينا قالوا أنطقنا الله الذي أنطق كل شيء وهو خلقكم أول مرة وإليه ترجعون

translation: And you cannot hide yourselves, lest your ears and your eyes and your skins testify against you; but you thought that Allah knew not much of what you did.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the all-knowing nature of God, who is aware of every action and thought of human beings. The verse states that even if people try to hide their sins, their senses, including their ears, eyes, and skin, will testify against them. This serves as a reminder that people cannot escape the consequences of their actions, even if they think they are hiding their sins. The verse encourages people to be mindful of their actions and to strive for righteousness, as God is aware of everything they do.
orig: وما كنتم تستترون أن يشهد عليكم سمعكم ولا أبصاركم ولا جلودكم ولكن ظننتم أن الله لا يعلم كثيرا مما تعملون

translation: And that is what you were thinking about your Lord, that He would not send upon you (any punishment). So you became among the losers.
interpretation: The verse addresses the disbelievers who underestimated the power and capability of their Lord to punish them for their disbelief and transgression. The verse highlights the irony of their situation, as they had thought that they would not be punished, but ultimately they became among the losers. The verse serves as a reminder that underestimating God's power and judgment is a grave mistake, and that those who do so will ultimately face the consequences of their actions.
orig: وذلكم ظنكم الذي ظننتم بربكم أرداكم فأصبحتم من الخاسرين

translation: But if they are patient, yet the Fire will be a dwelling-place for them; and if they seek a decision, then surely decision belongs to Allah.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the consequences of two possible reactions from people when faced with a difficult situation. If they choose to be patient, their punishment will be the Fire. If they seek a decision or resolution, they should know that the ultimate decision rests with God. The verse highlights the inevitability of punishment for those who are being tested and the importance of patience and trust in God's judgment.
orig: فإن يصبروا فالنار مثوى لهم وإن يستعتبوا فما هم من المعتبين

translation: And We had already established them in such a way that We let them fully enjoy the provisions, and they built houses among them, so We suddenly seized them while they were unaware.
interpretation: The verse speaks about a group of people who were given blessings and provisions by God, and they lived in comfort and prosperity. However, they became ungrateful and unaware of the blessings they received, and they were seized by God's punishment while they were unaware and unprepared. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the punishment and the unawareness of the people, which highlights the importance of gratitude and mindfulness of God's blessings. The verse serves as a reminder to be mindful of God's blessings and to be grateful for them, as well as a warning of the consequences of ungratefulness and heedlessness.
orig: وقيضنا لهم قرناء فزينوا لهم ما بين أيديهم وما خلفهم وحق عليهم القول في أمم قد خلت من قبلهم من الجن والإنس إنهم كانوا خاسرين

translation: And those who disbelieved say, 'Do not listen to this Qur'an and make noise and distract [you]' so that you may overcome.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the response of the disbelievers to the Qur'an. They tell people not to listen to it and make noise and distractions in order to prevent them from understanding and accepting the message of the Qur'an. The verse highlights the opposition and rejection of the disbelievers towards the divine message and their attempts to hinder others from accepting it. The verse serves as a reminder for the believers to remain steadfast and firm in their faith and not to be swayed by the negative influences of the disbelievers.
orig: وقال الذين كفروا لا تسمعوا لهذا القرآن والغوا فيه لعلكم تغلبون

translation: So shall We punish the unbelievers with a terrible punishment, and We shall requite them according to the worst of their deeds.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the punishment that will be given to the unbelievers. It emphasizes the severity of the punishment and the certainty of retribution. The punishment will be in proportion to the evil deeds of the unbelievers, indicating that the consequences of their actions will be just and fair. The verse serves as a warning to those who reject the truth and continue to commit sins, reminding them of the severe consequences of their actions and the justice of God's punishment.
orig: فلنذيقن الذين كفروا عذابا شديدا ولنجزينهم أسوأ الذي كانوا يعملون

translation: That is the reward of the enemies of Allah: the Fire, in which they will abide eternally, as a recompense for their disbelief in Allah's signs.
interpretation: The verse describes the punishment of those who are enemies of Allah, which is the Fire of Hell where they will dwell eternally. This punishment is a consequence of their disbelief in Allah's signs and their rejection of the truth. The verse emphasizes the severity of the punishment, which is eternal, and the importance of belief in Allah and His signs.
orig: ذلك جزاء أعداء الله النار لهم فيها دار الخلد جزاء بما كانوا بآياتنا يجحدون

translation: And those who disbelieved said, 'Our Lord, show us those who led us astray from among the jinn and the humans, that we may put them under our feet, so that they may be among the lowest.'
interpretation: The verse describes the disbelievers' request to God to show them those who had misguided them among the jinn and humans, so that they could subjugate them and place them among the lowest. This request reflects the disbelievers' pride and arrogance, as well as their desire for power and control over others. The verse serves as a reminder of the dangers of arrogance and the importance of humility and submission to God's will.
orig: وقال الذين كفروا ربنا أرنا اللذين أضلانا من الجن والإنس نجعلهما تحت أقدامنا ليكونا من الأسفلين

translation: For those who say, 'Our Lord is Allah' and then remain steadfast - the angels will descend upon them, [saying], 'Do not fear and do not grieve but receive good tidings of the Paradise that you were promised.'
interpretation: This verse speaks of the reward for those who declare their faith in Allah and then remain steadfast in their belief. These individuals will be greeted by angels who will assure them that they have nothing to fear or grieve about. Instead, they will receive good tidings of the Paradise that they have been promised. The verse serves as a source of comfort and motivation for believers, reminding them that their steadfastness will be rewarded in the afterlife.
orig: إن الذين قالوا ربنا الله ثم استقاموا تتنزل عليهم الملائكة ألا تخافوا ولا تحزنوا وأبشروا بالجنة التي كنتم توعدون

translation: We are your protectors in this life and in the hereafter. You will have therein whatever your souls desire, and you will have therein whatever you request.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the role of God as the protector and provider for the believers in both this life and the hereafter. It promises that the believers will receive all that their souls desire and all that they ask for in the afterlife. The verse serves as a reminder of the ultimate reward that awaits the believers, and the importance of maintaining faith and trust in God. It also highlights the greatness and generosity of God, who has the power to grant all desires and requests.
orig: نحن أولياؤكم في الحياة الدنيا وفي الآخرة ولكم فيها ما تشتهي أنفسكم ولكم فيها ما تدعون

translation: A forgiving, merciful descended
interpretation: The phrase speaks about God's attributes of being forgiving and merciful, and the act of descending. While the exact meaning of this verse is debated among scholars, one interpretation is that it refers to God's forgiveness and mercy being close and accessible to all, and that God is always ready to forgive those who repent and seek forgiveness. The verse can serve as a reminder of God's compassion and mercy, and of the opportunity for redemption and forgiveness that is always available to those who seek it.
orig: نزلا من غفور رحيم

translation: And who is better in speech than one who calls to Allah and does righteousness and says, 'Indeed, I am of the Muslims.'
interpretation: The verse highlights the merits of a person who calls people towards Allah (God) and performs righteous deeds. Such a person also identifies themselves as a Muslim, emphasizing their commitment to the faith. By praising this individual's speech, the verse encourages the importance of da'wah (inviting people to Islam) and righteous actions, and highlights the positive impact of a person's words and actions in their declaration of faith.
orig: ومن أحسن قولا ممن دعا إلى الله وعمل صالحا وقال إنني من المسلمين

translation: Not equal are the good deed and the bad deed. Repel [evil] with good, and the one who is enemy to you will become as if he was a close friend.
interpretation: The verse highlights the importance of responding to evil with good and emphasizes the transformative power of such actions. By responding to hostility with kindness and generosity, one can transform an enemy into a friend. This verse encourages Muslims to be patient and steadfast in the face of adversity and to strive for reconciliation and harmony. It also underscores the idea that good deeds are not equal to bad deeds, and that the former can have a greater impact on individuals and communities.
orig: ولا تستوي الحسنة ولا السيئة ادفع بالتي هي أحسن فإذا الذي بينك وبينه عداوة كأنه ولي حميم

translation: And it will not be encountered except by those who are patient, and it will not be encountered except by one with a great portion.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the encountering of a certain event or situation, which is not specified in the verse. The verse emphasizes that this event or situation will only be encountered by those who are patient and have the ability to endure hardships. Additionally, the event or situation will only be encountered by those who have been given a great portion or share. This could mean that the event or situation is a reward or blessing that is only given to a select few. Overall, the verse highlights the importance of patience and endurance in facing life's challenges, and the idea that certain rewards or blessings are reserved for those who have proven themselves worthy.
orig: وما يلقاها إلا الذين صبروا وما يلقاها إلا ذو حظ عظيم

translation: And if a suggestion from Satan assails your mind, then seek refuge in God; indeed, He is the Hearing, the Knowing.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the presence of Satan and his attempts to influence the believers. It advises that if one is afflicted by the whispers of Satan, they should seek refuge in God, who is the All-Hearing and All-Knowing. The verse emphasizes the importance of seeking God's protection and relying on His mercy and guidance. It is a reminder that God is always present and responsive to the needs of His believers, and that they can find solace and guidance in Him during times of temptation and struggle.
orig: وإما ينزغنك من الشيطان نزغ فاستعذ بالله إنه هو السميع العليم

translation: And of His signs are the night and the day and the sun and the moon - do not prostrate to the sun or to the moon, but rather prostrate to Allah, who created them, if it is Him you worship.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the greatness of Allah by mentioning some of His signs, including the night, day, sun, and moon. The verse then commands against prostrating to the sun or moon, and instead instructs to prostrate to Allah, the creator of these celestial bodies. The verse further highlights the importance of worshiping Allah alone. The verse serves as a reminder of the oneness of Allah and the importance of directing all worship towards Him, and not towards any of His creations.
orig: ومن آياته الليل والنهار والشمس والقمر لا تسجدوا للشمس ولا للقمر واسجدوا لله الذي خلقهن إن كنتم إياه تعبدون

translation: But if they become arrogant, then those who are with your Lord glorify Him night and day, and they are never tired.
interpretation: The verse contrasts the arrogance of certain people with the constant and tireless glorification of God by those who are with the Lord. The verse suggests that even if the arrogant people refuse to acknowledge God or His power, the glorification of God continues without end. The verse may serve as a reminder that arrogance and pride are not only harmful to oneself, but also prevent one from recognizing and appreciating the greatness of God. At the same time, the verse offers a message of comfort and hope, emphasizing that God's glory and power are eternal and unchanging, regardless of the actions or attitudes of humans.
orig: فإن استكبروا فالذين عند ربك يسبحون له بالليل والنهار وهم لا يسأمون

translation: And among His signs is that you see the earth humbled, but when We send down water upon it, it vibrates and swells. Indeed, He who gave it life is able to give life to the dead. Indeed, He is over all things competent.
interpretation: The verse highlights the power and control of God over all things by using the example of the earth and water. The earth is described as being 'humbled' or 'subdued', and when water is sent down upon it, it vibrates and swells. This is presented as one of the signs of God, emphasizing His ability to give life to the dead. The verse serves as a reminder of God's power and control over all things, and that He is capable of bringing the dead back to life, indicating His omnipotence.
orig: ومن آياته أنك ترى الأرض خاشعة فإذا أنزلنا عليها الماء اهتزت وربت إن الذي أحياها لمحيي الموتى إنه على كل شيء قدير

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve in Our verses - We will surely drive them into a fire. As for the disbelievers, is there not for them a knowing sentinel?
interpretation: The verse speaks about the fate of those who disbelieve in the signs or verses of God. They will be driven into a fire as a punishment for their disbelief. The verse emphasizes the inevitability of this punishment, as if to say that there is no escape for the disbelievers. The second part of the verse asks a rhetorical question, implying that the disbelievers will have no help or support on the Day of Judgment. The verse serves as a warning to those who reject the signs of God and a reminder of the consequences of their actions. It encourages people to do good deeds, as they will be held accountable for their actions on the Day of Judgment.
orig: إن الذين يلحدون في آياتنا لا يخفون علينا أفمن يلقى في النار خير أم من يأتي آمنا يوم القيامة اعملوا ما شئتم إنه بما تعملون بصير

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve in the reminder (the Qur'an) when it came to them - indeed, it is a Book of Exalted Power.
interpretation: The verse highlights the disbelief of certain people in the message of the Qur'an when it was revealed to them. The verse emphasizes the significance of the Qur'an by describing it as a "Book of Exalted Power", indicating its divine origin and the importance of its message. The verse serves as a reminder of the consequences of rejecting the truth and the power of the Qur'an as a means of guidance and enlightenment for those who choose to believe.
orig: إن الذين كفروا بالذكر لما جاءهم وإنه لكتاب عزيز

translation: Falsehood cannot come to it from before it or from behind it, [it is] a revelation from the Wise, the Praiseworthy.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the protection of the Qur'an from any falsehood. It emphasizes that falsehood cannot approach the Qur'an from either the front or the back, meaning that it is completely safeguarded from any errors or distortions. The verse states that the Qur'an is a revelation from the Wise, the Praiseworthy, highlighting its divine origin and the perfection of its message. This verse serves to affirm the authenticity and truth of the Qur'an, and to assure the believers of its protection from any corruption or falsification.
orig: لا يأتيه الباطل من بين يديه ولا من خلفه تنزيل من حكيم حميد

translation: Nothing is said to you except what was said to the messengers before you. Indeed, your Lord is, of forgiveness, most forgiving, and, of painful punishment, severe.
interpretation: The verse is reminding the Prophet Muhammad that he is not the first messenger to receive opposition and rejection, but that all prophets before him faced similar challenges. The verse also emphasizes the nature of God as both all-forgiving and severe in punishment, reminding the Prophet and the believers to have patience and trust in God's plan, even in the face of adversity.
orig: ما يقال لك إلا ما قد قيل للرسل من قبلك إن ربك لذو مغفرة وذو عقاب أليم

translation: And if We had made it a non-Arabic Qur'an, they would have said, 'Why are its verses not distinguished?' Say, 'It is, for those who believe, a guidance and a cure.' And those who do not believe - there is deafness in their ears, and for them it is blindness. Those are being called from a distant place.
interpretation: The verse addresses the objections of the disbelievers to the Qur'an, who questioned why its verses were not in a foreign language. The verse responds by stating that the Qur'an is a guidance and a cure for those who believe. However, for those who do not believe, there is deafness in their ears and blindness in their hearts. These people are being called from a distant place, indicating that they are far from the truth and guidance of the Qur'an. The verse emphasizes the importance of faith and the consequences of disbelief, highlighting the healing and guidance that the Qur'an offers to those who are receptive to it.
orig: ولو جعلناه قرآنا أعجميا لقالوا لولا فصلت آياته أأعجمي وعربي قل هو للذين آمنوا هدى وشفاء والذين لا يؤمنون في آذانهم وقر وهو عليهم عمى أولئك ينادون من مكان بعيد

translation: And We already gave Moses the Scripture, but there came to him a disagreement concerning it. And if it were not for a word that had preceded from your Lord, it would have been judged between them. And indeed, they are in suspicious disquiet concerning it.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the disagreement that arose among the people regarding the scripture that was given to Moses. Despite having the guidance from God, they were still uncertain and skeptical about its teachings. The verse highlights the fact that if it were not for God's prior decree, the matter would have been resolved. However, the people's skepticism and uncertainty persisted, and they remained in a state of doubt and confusion regarding the scripture.
orig: ولقد آتينا موسى الكتاب فاختلف فيه ولولا كلمة سبقت من ربك لقضي بينهم وإنهم لفي شك منه مريب

translation: Whoever does righteousness, it is for his soul, and whoever does evil, it is against it. And your Lord is not unjust to the servants.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of individual accountability for one's actions, stating that good deeds will benefit the individual while bad deeds will harm them. The verse also reaffirms the justice of God, emphasizing that He does not wrong His servants. The verse encourages individuals to strive for righteousness and avoid evil, as they are the ones who will ultimately bear the consequences of their actions.
orig: من عمل صالحا فلنفسه ومن أساء فعليها وما ربك بظلام للعبيد

translation: To Him belongs knowledge of the Hour. And no fruit emerges from its sheath, nor does a female conceive or give birth, except by His knowledge. And on the Day when He will call them, 'Where are My associates?' They will say, 'We have not testified to any of this!'
interpretation: The verse highlights the omniscience and power of God, who has knowledge of the Hour (the Day of Judgment), and who is aware of every event, including the growth of fruits, the conception and birth of every creature, which all occur with His knowledge. The verse emphasizes the futility of associating partners with God, as it will be clear on the Day of Judgment, when God will call out to those who had associated partners with Him, and they will be unable to deny their false beliefs and actions.
orig: إليه يرد علم الساعة وما تخرج من ثمرات من أكمامها وما تحمل من أنثى ولا تضع إلا بعلمه ويوم يناديهم أين شركائي قالوا آذناك ما منا من شهيد

translation: And abandoned them, in their disbelief, as to what they had been calling upon before, and they thought that there would be no punishment for them.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the punishment of those who rejected God's message and continued in their disbelief. The verse highlights that God abandoned them, leaving them to their own devices, as they persisted in their previous ways of worship and rejected the truth. Furthermore, the verse emphasizes that the disbelievers thought that there would be no punishment for them, indicating their lack of fear and awareness of the consequences of their actions.
orig: وضل عنهم ما كانوا يدعون من قبل وظنوا ما لهم من محيص

translation: Man is not weary of invoking (or supplicating) good (things), but if evil touches him, he is utterly desperate.
interpretation: The verse highlights the human tendency to seek help and invoke blessings when things are going well, but to lose hope and become desperate when faced with adversity. It serves as a reminder of the importance of maintaining faith and seeking God's help at all times, not just in times of need. The verse suggests that people should not take their blessings for granted and should be mindful of the fleeting nature of worldly pleasures. It also encourages perseverance and patience in the face of hardships and challenges, as giving up and losing hope only leads to despair and desolation.
orig: لا يسأم الإنسان من دعاء الخير وإن مسه الشر فيئوس قنوط

translation: And if We give man a taste of mercy from Us, after adversity has touched him, he says, 'This is mine, and I do not think that the Hour will come.' But if he is returned to Us, then indeed, [for him is] whatever he was given, and what is with his Lord is better for those who have believed and put their trust in their Lord. And those who disbelieve, for them is a painful punishment.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the attitude of people who receive God's mercy after experiencing hardship. Despite experiencing God's mercy, they become arrogant and deny the Day of Judgment. The verse reminds us that whatever we have is a gift from God and that what is with God is better for those who believe and trust in Him. The verse serves as a warning to those who deny God and the Day of Judgment, reminding them of the painful punishment that awaits them.
orig: ولئن أذقناه رحمة منا من بعد ضراء مسته ليقولن هذا لي وما أظن الساعة قائمة ولئن رجعت إلى ربي إن لي عنده للحسنى فلننبئن الذين كفروا بما عملوا ولنذيقنهم من عذاب غليظ

translation: But when We bestow favor upon man, he turns away and distances himself; and when evil touches him, then he is full of extensive prayer.
interpretation: The verse describes the behavior of people when they receive blessings from God and when they face hardships. When people are blessed with good fortune, they often become arrogant, turn away from God, and forget to be grateful. However, when they encounter difficulties and are faced with adversity, they quickly turn to God and pray earnestly. The verse serves as a reminder to be grateful for God's blessings and to maintain a consistent relationship with God, regardless of the circumstances.
orig: وإذا أنعمنا على الإنسان أعرض ونأى بجانبه وإذا مسه الشر فذو دعاء عريض

translation: Say, 'Have you considered if it (i.e., guidance) comes from Allah and you disbelieve in it, who could be more misguided than one in extreme error?'
interpretation: The verse addresses the Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) and commands him to ask the disbelievers if they have considered the consequences of rejecting divine guidance, even after acknowledging its source as being from Allah. The verse emphasizes the severity of their misguidance and the great error they are in by rejecting the truth. The verse serves as a reminder to the disbelievers of the importance of accepting and following divine guidance, and the dire consequences of rejecting it.
orig: قل أرأيتم إن كان من عند الله ثم كفرتم به من أضل ممن هو في شقاق بعيد

translation: We will show them Our signs in the horizons and within themselves until it becomes clear to them that it is the truth. But is it not enough that your Lord is a witness over all things?
interpretation: The verse speaks about how God will show people signs of His existence and power both in the universe (horizons) and within themselves, until they recognize the truth. The verse emphasizes the sufficiency of God's witness over all things and the ultimate accountability of people before Him. The verse encourages people to reflect on the signs of God and to recognize the truth, emphasizing the importance of faith and accountability.
orig: سنريهم آياتنا في الآفاق وفي أنفسهم حتى يتبين لهم أنه الحق أولم يكف بربك أنه على كل شيء شهيد

translation: Lo! They indeed are in a confused dispute concerning their Lord. Lo! They look on Him as distant, Lo! He is indeed surrounding all things.
interpretation: The verse highlights the confusion and misunderstanding of certain people regarding their relationship with their Lord. They view Him as distant, uninvolved in their lives. However, the verse emphasizes that this perception is incorrect. In reality, their Lord encompasses all things, indicating His all-encompassing knowledge and power. This verse encourages reflection on the true nature of God and the need to deepen one's understanding and relationship with the Divine.
orig: ألا إنهم في مرية من لقاء ربهم ألا إنه بكل شيء محيط

translation: By the sky and the night visitant (the star that appears at night)
interpretation: The verse is a form of oath, where the speaker swears by the sky and the night visitor (interpreted as the star that appears at night). This oath serves to emphasize the importance and truth of what is being said. The exact meaning of the verse is open to interpretation, but it is often understood as a reflection on the mysteries and wonders of the universe and a recognition of the power and majesty of God. The verse invites the reader to contemplate the beauty and complexity of the night sky and to consider the deeper meaning and significance of what they are seeing.
orig: حم

translation: None
interpretation: No interpretation
orig: عسق

translation: Thus does He reveal to you and to those before you, God, the Exalted in Might, the Wise.
interpretation: The verse speaks about God revealing His message through the prophet Muhammad and to the previous prophets. The verse emphasizes the continuity of the message, indicating that the revelation received by the prophet Muhammad is in line with the previous revelations. The verse also highlights the power and wisdom of God, who is the source of the revelation. The verse serves as a reminder of the divine origin of the message and the importance of following it, as it comes from the all-powerful and all-wise God.
orig: كذلك يوحي إليك وإلى الذين من قبلك الله العزيز الحكيم

translation: To Him belongs all that is in the heavens and all that is on the earth. And He is the Most High, the Great.
interpretation: The verse affirms the power and sovereignty of God, stating that all that exists in the heavens and on the earth belongs to Him. The verse emphasizes His greatness and exaltedness, using the terms 'Most High' and 'Great' to describe His attributes. The verse serves as a reminder of the greatness of God and His control over all things, and encourages believers to submit to His will and authority.
orig: له ما في السماوات وما في الأرض وهو العلي العظيم

translation: The heavens are almost rent asunder from above, and the angels celebrate the praise of their Lord, and ask forgiveness for those on the earth. Surely Allah is the All-forgiving, the All-compassionate.
interpretation: The verse describes the majesty and power of God, as the heavens are described as being on the verge of being torn apart. The angels are depicted as praising God and seeking forgiveness for those on earth. The verse emphasizes the mercy and compassion of God, as it highlights the fact that the angels are seeking forgiveness for all of humanity. The verse serves as a reminder of the greatness and power of God, as well as His infinite mercy and compassion towards His creations.
orig: تكاد السماوات يتفطرن من فوقهن والملائكة يسبحون بحمد ربهم ويستغفرون لمن في الأرض ألا إن الله هو الغفور الرحيم

translation: And those who take protectors besides Him [say], 'We only worship them that they may bring us nearer to Allah in position.' Indeed, Allah will judge between them concerning that over which they differ. Indeed, Allah does not guide he who is a liar and a disbeliever.
interpretation: The verse speaks about people who take protectors or intermediaries besides God, claiming that they worship them in order to be brought closer to God. The verse clarifies that God will be the one to judge between them regarding their dispute. The verse also emphasizes that God does not guide those who are liars and disbelievers, highlighting the importance of having faith in God alone and not associating any partners with Him.
orig: والذين اتخذوا من دونه أولياء الله حفيظ عليهم وما أنت عليهم بوكيل

translation: And thus have We sent to you (O Muhammad) an Arabic Qur'an that you may warn the mother city (Makkah) and those around it, and warn on the Day of Assembly (the Day of Resurrection), there is no doubt about it, a party in Paradise and a party in the blaze (Hellfire).
interpretation: This verse speaks about the revelation of the Qur'an in Arabic to the Prophet Muhammad as a warning to the people of Makkah and its surroundings. The verse also mentions the Day of Assembly, or the Day of Resurrection, where the fate of all people will be determined, either to enter Paradise or the blaze of Hellfire. The verse emphasizes the certainty of this event, and the importance of the warning message of the Qur'an. It serves as a reminder of the importance of being prepared for the Day of Judgment, and the consequences of not heeding the warning.
orig: وكذلك أوحينا إليك قرآنا عربيا لتنذر أم القرى ومن حولها وتنذر يوم الجمع لا ريب فيه فريق في الجنة وفريق في السعير

translation: And if Allah had willed, He could have made them a single nation, but they continue to differ, except whom He wills of His mercy. And the wrongdoers will have no protector or helper.
interpretation: The verse highlights the power of Allah to unite humanity, but instead, people continue to differ and disagree. The verse emphasizes that only those who are chosen by Allah's mercy will be united. The wrongdoers, those who disobey Allah and cause harm to others, will not have anyone to protect or help them. This verse can be interpreted as a reminder of the importance of seeking Allah's mercy and guidance, and the consequences of disobedience and wrongdoing.
orig: ولو شاء الله لجعلهم أمة واحدة ولكن يدخل من يشاء في رحمته والظالمون ما لهم من ولي ولا نصير

translation: Or have they taken other than Allah as protectors, while Allah is the Protector, and He gives life to the dead and has power over all things?
interpretation: The verse questions whether the people have taken other than Allah as protectors, emphasizing Allah's position as the true Protector. The verse highlights Allah's power and abilities, such as giving life to the dead and having power over all things, to contrast the false protectors that the people have taken. The verse serves as a reminder to the people to turn towards Allah and seek His protection, and to not rely on false protectors who cannot provide them with the same level of protection and care as Allah.
orig: أم اتخذوا من دونه أولياء فالله هو الولي وهو يحيي الموتى وهو على كل شيء قدير

translation: And in whatever you differ, the judgment thereof is with Allah. That is Allah, my Lord, in Him I put my trust and to Him I turn penitent.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the ultimate authority of Allah in matters of judgment and dispute. It reminds the believers that any differences or disputes they may have are ultimately to be resolved by Allah. The verse also highlights the importance of placing trust in Allah and turning to Him in repentance. The speaker in the verse expresses their own commitment to this principle, stating that they put their trust in Allah and turn to Him in repentance. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of relying on and seeking guidance from Allah in all aspects of life.
orig: وما اختلفتم فيه من شيء فحكمه إلى الله ذلكم الله ربي عليه توكلت وإليه أنيب

translation: Creator of the heavens and the earth, He has made for you from yourselves spouses, and from the animals a sustenance for you, in what He has created there is surely like you. He is the Hearing, the Seeing.
interpretation: The verse highlights the greatness of God as the Creator of the heavens and the earth, and emphasizes His power and wisdom in creating spouses for humans from among themselves and providing sustenance from the animals. The verse also emphasizes the interconnectedness and interdependence of all of God's creation, and the fact that there is nothing like God. The verse serves as a reminder of God's power and wisdom, and the importance of recognizing and being grateful for the blessings that He has bestowed upon us.
orig: فاطر السماوات والأرض جعل لكم من أنفسكم أزواجا ومن الأنعام أزواجا يذرؤكم فيه ليس كمثله شيء وهو السميع البصير

translation: To Him belong the keys of the heavens and the earth. He extends provision to whom He wills and restricts. Indeed, He is, of all things, Knowing.
interpretation: The verse affirms that God has control over the heavens and the earth and that He has the power to provide for whomever He wills. The verse emphasizes God's knowledge and power over all things, indicating that God's actions are not arbitrary but based on His wisdom and knowledge. The verse serves as a reminder of God's control and power over all aspects of life and the importance of putting one's trust in God, who knows and provides for all of His creation.
orig: له مقاليد السماوات والأرض يبسط الرزق لمن يشاء ويقدر إنه بكل شيء عليم

translation: We have ordained for you a religion which We have enjoined upon Noah and which We have revealed to you, and which We have enjoined upon Abraham and Moses and Jesus, saying, 'Establish the religion and do not be divided in it.' Great is that to which you call them, and Allah will take account of it. He will bring forth those who are mindful of Him into a light of goodness from Him and guide them to Him by a straight path.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the religion of Islam, which was ordained by God and taught by all the prophets, including Noah, Abraham, Moses, and Jesus. The verse commands the believers to establish this religion and not to divide into different sects and groups. The verse emphasizes the importance of this religion and the greatness of the call to it. The verse also mentions that God will take account of this call and will bring forth those who are mindful of Him into a light of goodness from Him. The verse serves as a reminder to the believers to adhere to the teachings of Islam and to strive for unity and solidarity in the community.
orig: شرع لكم من الدين ما وصى به نوحا والذي أوحينا إليك وما وصينا به إبراهيم وموسى وعيسى أن أقيموا الدين ولا تتفرقوا فيه كبر على المشركين ما تدعوهم إليه الله يجتبي إليه من يشاء ويهدي إليه من ينيب

translation: And they were not divided until after knowledge had come to them, out of jealousy between them. And if not for a word that had preceded from your Lord for a specified term, it would have been judged between them. And indeed, those who inherited the Scripture after them are in disquieting doubt concerning it.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the division among people that occurred after the revelation of knowledge, caused by jealousy and envy. The verse suggests that if it were not for a prior decree from God, a judgement would have been made between them. The verse highlights the existence of doubts and uncertainties among those who inherited the scripture after the initial revelation. The verse serves as a reminder of the negative consequences of jealousy and envy, and the importance of unity and adherence to the teachings of the scripture.
orig: وما تفرقوا إلا من بعد ما جاءهم العلم بغيا بينهم ولولا كلمة سبقت من ربك إلى أجل مسمى لقضي بينهم وإن الذين أورثوا الكتاب من بعدهم لفي شك منه مريب

translation: Therefore, invite (people) to the way of your Lord with wisdom and good instruction, and argue with them in a way that is best. Indeed, your Lord is most knowing of who has strayed from His way, and He is most knowing of who is guided. And if you obey most of those upon the earth, they will mislead you from the way of Allah. They follow not except assumption, and they are not but falsifying. Indeed, your Lord knows best who strays from His way, and He knows best who are the guided.
interpretation: The verse encourages the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to invite people to the way of his Lord with wisdom and good instruction, and to argue with them in a way that is best. It emphasizes that God is the most knowing of who has strayed and who is guided. The verse also warns against following the majority of people on earth, who may mislead from the way of God. It highlights that these people follow nothing but assumption and falsehood. The verse reiterates that God knows best who strays from His way and who are the guided, emphasizing God's omniscience and guidance.
orig: فلذلك فادع واستقم كما أمرت ولا تتبع أهواءهم وقل آمنت بما أنزل الله من كتاب وأمرت لأعدل بينكم الله ربنا وربكم لنا أعمالنا ولكم أعمالكم لا حجة بيننا وبينكم الله يجمع بيننا وإليه المصير

translation: But those who argue about God after He has been acknowledged, their arguments are invalid in the sight of their Lord. Anger is upon them, and they will have a severe punishment.
interpretation: The verse addresses those who continue to argue or debate about God, even after their doubts or questions have been addressed and answered. Such arguments are considered invalid or fruitless in the sight of God. The verse warns that anger is upon these individuals, indicating their displeasure or wrath from God. Additionally, the verse states that they will face a severe punishment, emphasizing the seriousness of persisting in argumentation or doubt after receiving a response.
orig: والذين يحاجون في الله من بعد ما استجيب له حجتهم داحضة عند ربهم وعليهم غضب ولهم عذاب شديد

translation: It is Allah who has sent down the Book with truth and the balance. And what will make you know that perhaps the Hour is near.
interpretation: The verse affirms that it is Allah who has revealed the scripture with truth and a standard for judgment (the balance). The verse then raises a question to make the reader reflect on the nearness of the Day of Judgment (the Hour). The verse emphasizes the importance of adhering to the teachings of the scripture and upholding justice, as the Day of Judgment is approaching. The verse serves as a warning and a reminder for people to prepare themselves for the inevitable Day of Judgment.
orig: الله الذي أنزل الكتاب بالحق والميزان وما يدريك لعل الساعة قريب

translation: Those who disbelieve in it (the Qur'an) hasten to its (punishment) failure, and those who believe are fearful of it and know that it is the truth. Indeed, those who dispute concerning the Hour are in extreme error.
interpretation: The verse contrasts the attitudes of those who disbelieve in the Qur'an and those who believe. Those who disbelieve are eager for its (punishment) failure, while those who believe are fearful of it and know that it is the truth. The verse emphasizes the reality of the punishment and the extreme error of those who deny or dispute the coming of the Hour (Judgment Day). It serves as a reminder of the importance of believing in and following the teachings of the Qur'an, and the consequences of disbelief and denial.
orig: يستعجل بها الذين لا يؤمنون بها والذين آمنوا مشفقون منها ويعلمون أنها الحق ألا إن الذين يمارون في الساعة لفي ضلال بعيد

translation: Allah is subtle in His love towards His servants, He provides for whom He wills. And He is the Powerful, the Exalted.
interpretation: The verse highlights Allah's love and care for His servants, describing it as subtle and nuanced. It emphasizes Allah's power and ability to provide for whoever He chooses. The verse serves as a reminder of Allah's greatness and the importance of recognizing and appreciating His blessings.
orig: الله لطيف بعباده يرزق من يشاء وهو القوي العزيز

translation: Whoever desires the harvest of the Hereafter, We increase for him in his harvest. And whoever desires the harvest of this world, We give him of it, but there is no provision for him in the Hereafter.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the different outcomes for those who strive for different goals in life. Those who strive for the rewards of the Hereafter will be granted more in return, while those who focus solely on the rewards of this world will only receive temporary satisfaction, but will have no provision in the Hereafter. The verse encourages believers to prioritize their actions and intentions towards the eternal rewards of the Hereafter, rather than being consumed by the temporary pleasures of this world.
orig: من كان يريد حرث الآخرة نزد له في حرثه ومن كان يريد حرث الدنيا نؤته منها وما له في الآخرة من نصيب

translation: Or have they associates who have legislated for them in the religion that which Allah has not given permission? And had it not been for the word of judgement, it would have been decreed between them. And indeed the wrongdoers - for them is a painful punishment.
interpretation: The verse warns against following any partners or associates who create their own laws in religion, which have not been given permission by God. The verse highlights that if it were not for the final judgement, these associates would have caused division and conflict between people. The verse emphasizes that those who commit wrongdoing and establish false laws in religion will face a severe and painful punishment from God.
orig: أم لهم شركاء شرعوا لهم من الدين ما لم يأذن به الله ولولا كلمة الفصل لقضي بينهم وإن الظالمين لهم عذاب أليم

translation: You see the unjust fearful of what they have earned, and it has overtaken them, and those who believe and do righteous deeds are in gardens of paradise, receiving what they desire from their Lord. That is the great bounty.
interpretation: The verse contrasts the fates of the unjust and the righteous. The unjust are fearful of the consequences of their actions, which have overtaken them. On the other hand, those who believe in God and do good deeds are promised a place in gardens of paradise, where they will receive their rewards from God. The verse emphasizes the great bounty that God bestows upon the righteous, and serves as a reminder that the consequences of one's actions, whether good or bad, will ultimately be realized.
orig: ترى الظالمين مشفقين مما كسبوا وهو واقع بهم والذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات في روضات الجنات لهم ما يشاءون عند ربهم ذلك هو الفضل الكبير

translation: That is (the bounty) whereof Allah gives glad tidings to His servants who believe and do righteous deeds. Say: I do not ask of you any reward for it but love for my near relatives. And whoever earns good, We shall give him more of good therein. Surely, Allah is Oft-Forgiving, Most Ready to appreciate (the deeds of those who are obedient to Him).
interpretation: This verse speaks about the rewards that Allah has promised to his believers who do good deeds. The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) is told not to ask for any reward for his preaching except for the love of his relatives. The verse encourages the doing of good deeds and assures that Allah will reward those who earn good with even more goodness. The verse highlights Allah's forgiving and appreciative nature towards those who are obedient to Him.
orig: ذلك الذي يبشر الله عباده الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات قل لا أسألكم عليه أجرا إلا المودة في القربى ومن يقترف حسنة نزد له فيها حسنا إن الله غفور شكور

translation: Or do they say, 'He has invented a lie about Allah?' If Allah wills, He will seal your heart. And Allah eliminates falsehood and establishes the truth by His words. Indeed, He is Knowing of that within the breasts.
interpretation: The verse addresses those who accuse the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) of fabricating the Qur'an. It reminds them that Allah has the power to seal the hearts of those who reject the truth, and that He is the one who eliminates falsehood and establishes the truth. The verse emphasizes Allah's knowledge of the inner thoughts and intentions of people, and the ultimate reality of His words. It serves as a warning to those who deny the truth, reminding them of the power and wisdom of Allah, and the consequences of rejecting His message.
orig: أم يقولون افترى على الله كذبا فإن يشإ الله يختم على قلبك ويمح الله الباطل ويحق الحق بكلماته إنه عليم بذات الصدور

translation: And He it is who accepts repentance from His servants, and pardons sins, and He knows what you do.
interpretation: The verse highlights God's mercy and forgiveness towards His servants. By accepting repentance and pardoning sins, God offers an opportunity for people to correct their mistakes and start anew. The verse also emphasizes God's omniscience, as He knows all that people do. This serves as a reminder of God's boundless mercy and the importance of seeking forgiveness and striving to lead a righteous life.
orig: وهو الذي يقبل التوبة عن عباده ويعفو عن السيئات ويعلم ما تفعلون

translation: And those who believe and do righteous deeds, He will give them in return their wages in full. And Allah does not like the wrongdoers.
interpretation: The verse contrasts the fate of believers who do righteous deeds with that of wrongdoers. It emphasizes that those who believe and do good will receive their full reward from God, while the wrongdoers will face a severe punishment. The verse encourages believers to continue doing good deeds and to have faith in God's justice and mercy. It also serves as a warning to those who persist in wrongdoing, reminding them of the consequences of their actions.
orig: ويستجيب الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات ويزيدهم من فضله والكافرون لهم عذاب شديد

translation: And if Allah (swt) were to extend provision for His servants, they would surely indulge in excess on the earth; but He sends down by measure as He wills. Indeed, He is, of His servants, Acquainted and Seeing.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the provision that Allah (swt) gives to His servants. If Allah (swt) were to give them unlimited provision, they would indulge in excess and sin. However, Allah (swt) sends down provision in a measured way, according to His will. The verse emphasizes that Allah (swt) is aware of the needs of His servants and sees their actions. The verse serves as a reminder that Allah (swt) is all-knowing and all-seeing, and that He provides for His servants in a way that is best for them.
orig: ولو بسط الله الرزق لعباده لبغوا في الأرض ولكن ينزل بقدر ما يشاء إنه بعباده خبير بصير

translation: And it is He who sends down the rain after they have lost hope and spreads His mercy. And He is the protector, the praiseworthy.
interpretation: The verse speaks about God's power and mercy. It highlights God's ability to send down rain and provide sustenance even after people have lost hope. The verse emphasizes the generosity and compassion of God, who not only provides for His creation but also does so with mercy. The verse also mentions that God is the protector and praiseworthy, emphasizing His greatness and worthiness of praise. This verse serves as a reminder of God's power and mercy, and encourages believers to turn to Him in times of need and despair.
orig: وهو الذي ينزل الغيث من بعد ما قنطوا وينشر رحمته وهو الولي الحميد

translation: And among His signs is the creation of the heavens and the earth, and whatever creatures He has scattered in them; and He has the power to gather them together whenever He will.
