interpretation: The verse speaks about the creation of the heavens and the earth, and the scattering of creatures in them as a sign of God's power. The verse emphasizes that God has the power to gather all the creatures together whenever He will, indicating His complete and total control over all of creation. The verse serves as a reminder of God's power and greatness, and the need for humans to recognize and submit to His will.
orig: ومن آياته خلق السماوات والأرض وما بث فيهما من دابة وهو على جمعهم إذا يشاء قدير

translation: And whatever of misfortune befalls you, it is because of what your hands have earned, and (yet) He pardons much.
interpretation: The verse states that any hardship or misfortune that befalls a person is a result of their own actions and the consequences of their deeds. However, despite this, God is forgiving and pardons many sins and mistakes. This verse encourages people to reflect on their actions and take responsibility for the consequences, while also recognizing the mercy and compassion of God in forgiving and overlooking many of their mistakes.
orig: وما أصابكم من مصيبة فبما كسبت أيديكم ويعفو عن كثير

translation: And you are not, within the earth, incapable, and you have not, besides Allah, any protecting friend or helper.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the power and control of Allah, reminding people that they are not self-sufficient and that they have no protector or helper besides Him. The phrase 'you are not, within the earth, incapable' suggests that people do not have the ability or strength to protect themselves on their own, and the phrase 'you have not, besides Allah, any protecting friend or helper' reinforces the idea that people are dependent on Allah for their safety and well-being. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of relying on and trusting in Allah, and of the futility of relying on one's own strength or the help of others.
orig: وما أنتم بمعجزين في الأرض وما لكم من دون الله من ولي ولا نصير

translation: And among His signs are the ships in the sea like mountains.
interpretation: The verse uses the image of ships in the sea as a metaphor to describe the power and majesty of God. By comparing the ships to mountains, the verse conveys a sense of awe and wonder at the sight of these massive vessels traversing the vast expanse of the sea. This image serves as a reminder of the greatness of God and His ability to create and control the natural world. At the same time, it encourages people to reflect on the signs of God in their surroundings and to recognize His power and wisdom.
orig: ومن آياته الجوار في البحر كالأعلام

translation: If He wills, He can still the wind so that its motion becomes steady over you, then surely in that are signs for a people who are patient and thankful.
interpretation: The verse speaks about God's power and control over the natural elements, specifically the wind. It highlights God's ability to calm the wind and make it steady, which is presented as a sign for those who are patient and thankful. The verse emphasizes the importance of patience and gratitude in understanding and appreciating the signs of God in the natural world. It reminds the believers that God is in control of all things and that they should be patient and thankful in all situations, recognizing that everything comes from God.
orig: إن يشأ يسكن الريح فيظللن رواكد على ظهره إن في ذلك لآيات لكل صبار شكور

translation: Or leave them in their ignorance for a while.
interpretation: The verse speaks about God's decision to leave certain people in their state of ignorance and error for a period of time. The verse implies that God has the power and knowledge to intervene and guide people towards the right path, but chooses to delay his intervention for a while. This delay can be seen as an act of mercy and a test for the people, as it gives them the opportunity to reflect on their actions and seek guidance. However, it also emphasizes the importance of taking advantage of the time and opportunities that God gives us, as we do not know when our time will run out.
orig: أو يوبقهن بما كسبوا ويعف عن كثير

translation: And let those who oppose the signs of God know that for them there is no place of escape.
interpretation: The verse addresses those who argue and dispute about the signs (ayat) of God, which can be interpreted as the signs of God's existence and power in the world. The verse warns these people that they have no place of escape or refuge from the consequences of their actions. This can be interpreted as a warning that those who deny or reject the signs of God will not be able to escape the consequences of their actions, whether in this life or the next.
orig: ويعلم الذين يجادلون في آياتنا ما لهم من محيص

translation: And whatever you have been given is but a provision of this world's life, and what is with Allah is better and more lasting for those who believe and put their trust in their Lord.
interpretation: The verse reminds people that the wealth and possessions they have in this world are temporary and fleeting, and that true and lasting happiness and blessings come from having faith in God and putting their trust in Him. The verse encourages people to have a higher perspective and not to be overly attached to material things, but rather to focus on the eternal and spiritual rewards that come from a close relationship with God.
orig: فما أوتيتم من شيء فمتاع الحياة الدنيا وما عند الله خير وأبقى للذين آمنوا وعلى ربهم يتوكلون

translation: And those who avoid the great sins and indecencies, and when they are angry, they forgive.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the characteristics of righteous people who avoid committing major sins and lewd acts. Moreover, when they become angry, they are able to forgive others. This verse highlights the importance of self-control, forgiveness, and avoiding sins and immoral behavior. It serves as a moral guideline for believers, encouraging them to strive for righteousness and to exercise patience and forgiveness in their interactions with others.
orig: والذين يجتنبون كبائر الإثم والفواحش وإذا ما غضبوا هم يغفرون

translation: And those who have responded to their Lord and established prayer and whose affair is [determined by] consultation among themselves, and from what We have provided for them, they spend.
interpretation: The verse describes the believers who have a strong relationship with their Lord, establish prayer, and make decisions through consultation and consensus. They also spend from the provisions that God has given them. This verse emphasizes the importance of a strong faith, regular prayer, and communal decision-making among believers. It also promotes the value of generosity and sharing one's blessings with others.
orig: والذين استجابوا لربهم وأقاموا الصلاة وأمرهم شورى بينهم ومما رزقناهم ينفقون

translation: And those who, when tyranny strikes them, they defend themselves.
interpretation: The verse speaks about individuals who, when faced with oppression and tyranny, respond by defending themselves. The verse highlights the importance of standing up for oneself and not being passive in the face of injustice. The verse serves as a reminder that individuals have the right and responsibility to defend themselves and their rights, and it encourages a proactive approach to dealing with oppression.
orig: والذين إذا أصابهم البغي هم ينتصرون

translation: A bad deed deserves a bad retribution. So whoever pardons and makes reconciliation will receive his reward from Allah. Surely, Allah does not love the unjust.
interpretation: The verse explains the principle of 'an eye for an eye' in terms of punishment for bad deeds. However, it also highlights the virtue of forgiveness and reconciliation, stating that those who pardon and seek to reconcile will be rewarded by Allah. The verse emphasizes that Allah does not approve of injustice and unrighteousness, and encourages believers to practice forgiveness and seek reconciliation as an alternative to revenge and enmity.
orig: وجزاء سيئة سيئة مثلها فمن عفا وأصلح فأجره على الله إنه لا يحب الظالمين

translation: But for he who has endured patiently after wrongdoing to him - indeed, that is of the greatest constancy.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the virtue of patience and perseverance in the face of injustice. The phrase 'after wrongdoing to him' suggests that the person has been wronged or treated unjustly, but instead of seeking revenge or retaliation, they choose to endure with patience. The verse praises this quality of patience and perseverance, calling it one of the greatest forms of steadfastness or constancy. The verse encourages believers to remain patient and steadfast in the face of adversity, and to trust in God's justice and wisdom, even when they are faced with injustice and wrongdoing.
orig: ولمن انتصر بعد ظلمه فأولئك ما عليهم من سبيل

translation: The way (of life) for those who do wrong to people and act unjustly in the land is that they will have a painful punishment.
interpretation: The verse describes the fate of those who commit wrongdoings and act unjustly towards others. It emphasizes that their way of life will lead to a painful punishment. The verse serves as a warning to those who engage in unjust and harmful behaviors, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: إنما السبيل على الذين يظلمون الناس ويبغون في الأرض بغير الحق أولئك لهم عذاب أليم

translation: But for he who perseveres and forgives, indeed, that is of the determination of things.
interpretation: The verse highlights the virtue of patience and forgiveness, emphasizing that these qualities are a sign of determination and strength. By using the phrase 'for he who perseres and forgives', the verse suggests that these two qualities are interconnected and that they are both necessary for success. The phrase 'that is of the determination of things' reinforces the idea that patience and forgiveness are not just desirable qualities, but essential ones. The verse encourages believers to strive for these qualities in their daily lives, and to see them as a sign of their commitment to their faith and their community.
orig: ولمن صبر وغفر إن ذلك لمن عزم الأمور

translation: And if Allah should lead you astray, there is no protector for you after that. And you will see the wrongdoers, when they see the punishment, saying, 'Is there any way to return?'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the ultimate authority of God in guiding or misguiding people. If God leads someone astray, there is no one who can protect or help them after that. The verse then describes the state of the wrongdoers when they see the punishment, expressing their regret and asking if there is any way to return. The verse emphasizes the importance of following God's guidance and avoiding wrongdoing, as the consequences of going against God's will are severe and irreversible.
orig: ومن يضلل الله فما له من ولي من بعده وترى الظالمين لما رأوا العذاب يقولون هل إلى مرد من سبيل

translation: And you will see them presented therein, prostrating themselves, in humility from the awe of their Lord, looking on (as in awe). And they say, 'The disbelievers - the losers today, those who lost themselves and their families, in the Fire of Hell.',
interpretation: The verse describes the fate of the disbelievers on the Day of Judgment. They will be presented before God in a state of humility and awe, prostrating themselves. They will look on in fear and realize the magnitude of their mistake. The verse emphasizes the ultimate loss of the disbelievers, who will lose not only themselves but also their families in the Fire of Hell. This verse serves as a reminder of the importance of faith and the consequences of disbelief.
orig: وتراهم يعرضون عليها خاشعين من الذل ينظرون من طرف خفي وقال الذين آمنوا إن الخاسرين الذين خسروا أنفسهم وأهليهم يوم القيامة ألا إن الظالمين في عذاب مقيم

translation: And they had no protectors apart from Allah, then they were lost. And whoever Allah leaves astray, then there is no guide for him.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the ultimate power and control of Allah, and the helplessness of human beings in the face of His will. The verse emphasizes that the people mentioned in the verse had no protectors or allies who could help or save them from Allah's punishment. The verse also highlights the danger of being led astray by Allah, and the fact that there is no guide or way out for those whom Allah has left in error. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of seeking Allah's guidance and mercy, and the futility of relying on worldly powers and alliances for protection and support.
orig: وما كان لهم من أولياء ينصرونهم من دون الله ومن يضلل الله فما له من سبيل

translation: Respond to your Lord before there comes to you a day from Allah of which there is no repelling. No refuge will there be for you on that day, nor will there be for you any denial.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of responding to Allah's call and being mindful of the Day of Judgment. The verse warns that this day will come without warning and that there will be no escape or denial on that day. The verse encourages believers to repent and turn to Allah, and to not let the passing of time lull them into a false sense of security. It serves as a reminder that the Day of Judgment is inevitable, and that all actions will be accounted for, and that the only refuge is through Allah's mercy.
orig: استجيبوا لربكم من قبل أن يأتي يوم لا مرد له من الله ما لكم من ملجإ يومئذ وما لكم من نكير

translation: But if they turn away, then upon you is only the clear conveyance. And indeed, We will not send you as a guard over them. And indeed, it is not for the one who is brought the truth to become frustrated. And when We bestow favor upon the human, he turns away and distances himself; but when evil touches him as a result of what his hands have put forward, then indeed, man is ungrateful.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the role of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) as a conveyer of the truth, and that he is not responsible for the rejection or acceptance of the message by the people. The verse also highlights the behavior of humans towards blessings and trials. When humans are given blessings, they turn away from God and become ungrateful, but when they are faced with trials and difficulties, they realize their mistakes and repent. The verse serves as a reminder for the Prophet (peace be upon him) and the believers to be patient and persistent in conveying the message, and to leave the outcome to God.
orig: فإن أعرضوا فما أرسلناك عليهم حفيظا إن عليك إلا البلاغ وإنا إذا أذقنا الإنسان منا رحمة فرح بها وإن تصبهم سيئة بما قدمت أيديهم فإن الإنسان كفور

translation: To Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. He creates what He wills. He bestows female (offspring) upon whom He wills and bestows male (offspring) upon whom He wills.
interpretation: The verse affirms the power and sovereignty of Allah over all of creation. It emphasizes that Allah has the power to create whatever He wills and that He has the power to bestow children of either gender upon whom He wills. The verse serves as a reminder of the limits of human control and the ultimate power and wisdom of Allah.
orig: لله ملك السماوات والأرض يخلق ما يشاء يهب لمن يشاء إناثا ويهب لمن يشاء الذكور

translation: Or He pairs them as males and females, and makes whom He wills sterile. Indeed, He is Knowing and Competent.
interpretation: The verse speaks about God's power in creating and controlling all aspects of life, including the creation of males and females and the ability to make some people sterile. The verse emphasizes God's knowledge and ability to do all things, and highlights His control over the creation of life and the ability to determine who will be sterile. The verse serves as a reminder of God's power and greatness and the limitations of human control over the natural world.
orig: أو يزوجهم ذكرانا وإناثا ويجعل من يشاء عقيما إنه عليم قدير

translation: And it is not given to any human that Allah should speak to him except by revelation or from behind a veil, or by sending a messenger to reveal by His permission what He wills. Indeed, He is Exalted and Wise.
interpretation: The verse explains the ways in which Allah communicates with humans. It states that Allah does not speak to humans directly, but rather through revelation, from behind a veil, or by sending a messenger to reveal His will. The verse emphasizes that Allah's knowledge and power are beyond human comprehension, and that He communicates with humans in a way that is appropriate for their understanding. The verse serves as a reminder of Allah's greatness, wisdom and power, and the limitations of human knowledge and understanding.
orig: وما كان لبشر أن يكلمه الله إلا وحيا أو من وراء حجاب أو يرسل رسولا فيوحي بإذنه ما يشاء إنه علي حكيم

translation: And thus have We sent to you (O Muhammad) a Spirit (i.e., Gabriel) of Our command. You knew not what the Scripture was, nor what the Faith. But We have made it (i.e., the Quran) a light wherewith We guide whosoever of Our slaves We will. And lo! You verily guide (mankind) to the Straight Path
interpretation: The verse speaks about the revelation of the Quran to the Prophet Muhammad through the Angel Gabriel. The verse highlights the fact that the Prophet was unaware of the Scripture and the Faith before this revelation. The verse explains that the Quran is a light that God uses to guide whomever He wills from among His servants. The verse also emphasizes the role of the Prophet in guiding people to the Straight Path, which is the path of truth and righteousness.
orig: وكذلك أوحينا إليك روحا من أمرنا ما كنت تدري ما الكتاب ولا الإيمان ولكن جعلناه نورا نهدي به من نشاء من عبادنا وإنك لتهدي إلى صراط مستقيم

translation: The way (path) of God, to whom belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. Indeed, to God all matters will be returned.
interpretation: The verse affirms that the way or path belongs to God, and that everything in the heavens and the earth belongs to Him. It emphasizes the ultimate power and control of God over all things. The verse also reminds that all matters and affairs will be returned to God, implying that God will judge all actions and hold people accountable for their deeds. The verse encourages the believers to follow the path of God, which is the path of righteousness and submission to God's will.
orig: صراط الله الذي له ما في السماوات وما في الأرض ألا إلى الله تصير الأمور

translation:
By the heaven and the starfalling,
By the moon when it follows,
By the day when it displays,
By the night when it covers,
By the sky and Him who built it,
By the earth and Him who spread it,
By Nafs and Him who proportioned it,
And inspired it (with knowledge of) what is wrong for it and (what is) right for it,
He is indeed successful who purifies it,
And he is indeed failed who corrupts it.
interpretation: The verse is a series of oaths or affirmations, where the speaker swears by various celestial and earthly bodies, as well as the human soul (Nafs), attesting to the truth of what is being revealed. The verse emphasizes the importance of the human soul and its capacity for both good and evil, and the significance of guiding and purifying it towards righteousness. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of moral conduct and the consequences of corrupting the soul, with success being attained by those who purify it and failure by those who corrupt it.
orig: حم

translation: And the manifest Book.
interpretation: The verse refers to the Qur'an as the 'manifest Book', highlighting its clarity and accessibility. The Qur'an is described as a guide for humanity, providing clear and detailed guidance for all aspects of life. The verse emphasizes the importance of the Qurn in providing a clear and unambiguous path for those who seek to follow God's will.
orig: والكتاب المبين

translation: Indeed, We have made it a Qur'an in Arabic that you may understand.
interpretation: The verse is emphasizing the importance of the Arabic language in the revelation of the Qur'an. It highlights the fact that the Qur'an was revealed in Arabic so that people may understand its message and meanings. This verse serves as a reminder that the Qur'an's language is a significant aspect of its preservation and understanding, and that the Arabic language holds a special place in conveying the divine message of Islam.
orig: إنا جعلناه قرآنا عربيا لعلكم تعقلون

translation: And indeed, it is in the Mother of the Book with Us, indeed, that it is sublime, wise.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the 'Mother of the Book' which is with God and contains the divine wisdom and knowledge. The verse emphasizes the sublime and wise nature of the book, indicating its importance and significance. The verse can be interpreted as a reference to the ultimate source of all knowledge and guidance, which is with God and accessible to humanity through revelation and divine guidance.
orig: وإنه في أم الكتاب لدينا لعلي حكيم

translation:
Then shall I surely beat out for you a parable, so that you must needs be surely mindful,
That you were (once) a people (who were guilty of) spreading corruption!
interpretation: The verse speaks about a parable that will be used to remind the listeners of their past wrongdoings. The parable serves as a warning to make them mindful of their actions. The verse highlights the people's past corruption, indicating the gravity of their sins. The verse emphasizes the importance of reflection and self-awareness, encouraging the listeners to change their ways and avoid repeating their past mistakes.
orig: أفنضرب عنكم الذكر صفحا أن كنتم قوما مسرفين

translation: And how many a prophet have We sent among the first [people].
interpretation: The verse highlights the number of prophets that God had sent to the early communities as a means of guidance and warning. This verse serves to remind the readers of the continuity of God's message and the consistency of His approach towards humanity. Despite the passage of time and the change of circumstances, God has consistently sent prophets to guide and warn people, and this verse emphasizes the importance of heeding the message of the prophets and following their teachings.
orig: وكم أرسلنا من نبي في الأولين

translation: And We never sent a prophet to them but they ridiculed him.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the consistent pattern of people rejecting and ridiculing the prophets sent by God to guide them. This verse emphasizes that the rejection of prophets is not a new phenomenon, but has been a recurring pattern throughout history. The verse serves as a reminder that those who reject and mock God's messengers will face consequences for their actions. It also highlights the importance of respect and open-mindedness towards prophets and their messages, and the danger of closed-mindedness and arrogance in the face of divine guidance.
orig: وما يأتيهم من نبي إلا كانوا به يستهزئون

translation: And We destroyed others who were stronger than them in power. And the example of the former peoples has preceded.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of peoples or societies who were stronger than those being addressed, emphasizing the power and authority of God. The second part of the verse refers to the 'example of the former peoples' which serves as a warning and reminder to those being addressed, indicating that the same fate can befall them if they do not change their ways and heed the lessons from history.
orig: فأهلكنا أشد منهم بطشا ومضى مثل الأولين

translation: And if you asked them who created the heavens and the earth, they would surely say: 'The All-Mighty, the All-Knowing, has created them.'
interpretation: The verse highlights the fact that even though people may deny or ignore the signs of God, they still acknowledge His existence and power when asked directly. The question of who created the heavens and the earth is used as an example of a question that, if asked, would elicit the response that it was 'The All-Mighty, the All-Knowing' who created them. This serves as a reminder that the signs of God are all around us and that even those who deny or ignore them still have an innate understanding of the existence of a higher power.
orig: ولئن سألتهم من خلق السماوات والأرض ليقولن خلقهن العزيز العليم

translation: Who has made the earth a bed for you, and the sky a ceiling, and caused water to come down from the sky, and brought forth with it fruits as a provision for you. So, do not set up equals to God, knowingly.
interpretation: The verse highlights the greatness of God's creation and His generosity towards human beings. It reminds people of the blessings they have received from God, such as the earth as a bed, the sky as a ceiling, the water that brings forth fruits, and the provision that sustains life. The verse then commands people not to associate partners with God, emphasizing the importance of monotheism and the rejection of idolatry. The overall message of the verse is one of gratitude and devotion towards God, recognizing His role as the provider and sustainer of all life.
orig: الذي جعل لكم الأرض مهدا وجعل لكم فيها سبلا لعلكم تهتدون

translation: And it is He who sends down water from the sky in measured amounts, then We revive with it a dead land - thus will you be brought forth.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the power of God in sending down water from the sky to bring life to a dead land. This is a metaphor for the resurrection of the dead on the Day of Judgment. The verse emphasizes the control that God has over life and death and the certainty of the resurrection. It serves as a reminder of the power and majesty of God and the transience of this world.
orig: والذي نزل من السماء ماء بقدر فأنشرنا به بلدة ميتا كذلك تخرجون

translation: And He who created all the pairs, and appointed for you ships and animals on which you ride.
interpretation: The verse highlights God's role as the creator of all pairs, emphasizing His power and authority over all of creation. The verse then mentions the specific gifts God has given to humanity in the form of ships and animals, which serve as a means of transportation. The verse reminds people to be grateful for these blessings and to recognize that they come from God. The verse can also be seen as a reminder of the interconnectedness of all life and the responsibility of humans to treat other living beings with respect and compassion.
orig: والذي خلق الأزواج كلها وجعل لكم من الفلك والأنعام ما تركبون

translation: So that you may mount upon it, and then remember the favor of your Lord when you are mounted thereon, and say, 'Exalted is He who has subjected this to us, and we were not capable of it ourselves.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the power and grace of God, who has subjected the earth and its resources to humanity. The verse instructs the reader to mount upon the earth and remember the favor of their Lord, acknowledging their dependence on God for their sustenance and well-being. The phrase 'we were not capable of it ourselves' emphasizes the power and might of God, and the gratitude and humility that should be the response of the believer. The verse serves as a reminder of the relationship between humanity and God, and the importance of recognizing and acknowledging the blessings and mercies that come from God.
orig: لتستووا على ظهوره ثم تذكروا نعمة ربكم إذا استويتم عليه وتقولوا سبحان الذي سخر لنا هذا وما كنا له مقرنين

translation: And indeed, to our Lord we are to return.
interpretation: The verse is a reminder that all of humanity will ultimately return to their Lord and be held accountable for their actions in this life. It is a statement of faith in the ultimate justice of God and the inevitability of the Day of Judgment. It serves as a call to piety and righteousness, urging people to remember that their actions have consequences and that they will be answerable to God for them. The verse also emphasizes the transience of this worldly life and the eternal nature of the hereafter, encouraging people to focus on their relationship with their Creator and to strive for righteousness in preparation for the Day of Judgment.
orig: وإنا إلى ربنا لمنقلبون

translation: And they made some of His servants to bepartisan. Indeed, man is clearly ungrateful.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the actions of people who divide and create factions among the servants or followers of God. The verse highlights the ungrateful nature of humans, using the Arabic word 'kafur' which means 'ungrateful' or 'ingrate'. The verse serves as a reminder that despite the blessings and mercies of God, humans have a tendency to be ungrateful and create divisions among themselves. It is a call to remember the oneness of God and to avoid creating factions and divisions among the believers.
orig: وجعلوا له من عباده جزءا إن الإنسان لكفور مبين

translation: Or did He (God) choose daughters for Himself and prefer you with sons?
interpretation: The verse is a rhetorical question, challenging the notion that God would favor certain people over others based on gender. The verse emphasizes the absurdity of the idea that God would choose daughters for Himself and prefer sons for humans. The verse promotes the idea of equality and fairness, and challenges the cultural and societal biases that were prevalent during the time of the revelation of the Qur'an. The verse serves as a reminder that God does not discriminate and that all people are equal in His eyes, regardless of their gender.
orig: أم اتخذ مما يخلق بنات وأصفاكم بالبنين

translation: And when We point out to a person a sign/example/lesson from the mercy of his Lord, his face becomes darkened and he is full of despair.
interpretation: The verse describes the reaction of a person when they are presented with a sign or lesson from God's mercy. Instead of being grateful and humbled, the person becomes displeased and full of despair. This negative reaction is a reflection of their inner state and their rejection of God's blessings. The verse serves as a warning to those who take God's mercy for granted and fail to appreciate the signs and lessons that are presented to them.
orig: وإذا بشر أحدهم بما ضرب للرحمن مثلا ظل وجهه مسودا وهو كظيم

translation: Or [consider such an example] as he who passed by a township which had fallen into ruin. He said, 'How will Allah bring this to life after its death?' So Allah caused him to die for a hundred years; then He revived him. He said, 'How long have you remained [dead]?' The man said, 'I have remained a day or part of a day.' He said, 'Rather, you have remained one hundred years. Look at your food and your drink; it has not changed with time. And look at your donkey; and thus We make you a sign for the people. And look at the bones [of this donkey] - how We raise them and then We cover them with flesh.' And when it became clear to him, he said, 'I know that Allah is over all things competent.'
interpretation: The verse presents a parable of a person who passes by a ruined town and wonders how it could ever be restored to life. As a sign of His power, God causes the man to die for a hundred years and then brings him back to life. The man is amazed to find that his food and drink have not decayed, and that even the bones of his donkey have been restored to life. The story serves as a reminder of God's power and ability to bring about change and renewal, even in seemingly hopeless situations. It also highlights the importance of recognizing God's power and having faith in His ability to bring about positive change.
orig: أومن ينشأ في الحلية وهو في الخصام غير مبين

translation: And they made the angels who are servants of the Most Merciful into females. Did they witness their creation? Their testimony will be recorded and they will be asked.
interpretation: The verse criticizes the disbelievers who assign female gender to the angels, an act of disrespect towards the divine entities. The verse questions their claim, asking if they witnessed the creation of the angels. The verse emphasizes that the testimony of their claim will be recorded and they will be held accountable for it. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of respecting and acknowledging the divine entities and the consequences of disrespecting them.
orig: وجعلوا الملائكة الذين هم عباد الرحمن إناثا أشهدوا خلقهم ستكتب شهادتهم ويسألون

translation: And they say, 'If the Merciful had willed, we would not have worshipped them.' They have no knowledge of that; they only conjecture.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the disbelievers who deny the power and wisdom of God, and attribute their worship of false deities to the will of God. The verse highlights the ignorance of the disbelievers, who have no knowledge of the divine will and wisdom. The verse emphasizes that the worship of false deities is not predestined or willed by God, but rather a result of the misguided choices of the disbelievers. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of recognizing and submitting to the power and wisdom of God, and avoiding the worship of false deities and the ignorance that leads to it.
orig: وقالوا لو شاء الرحمن ما عبدناهم ما لهم بذلك من علم إن هم إلا يخرصون

translation: Or have We given them a book beforehand to which they are holding on?
interpretation: The verse is a rhetorical question that challenges the disbelievers who reject the message brought by the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). The verse asks if they had received a revelation before the Qur'an that they are holding on to, which is a clear reference to the scriptures of the Jews and Christians. The verse implies that the message of the Qur'an is in line with the previous revelations, and that the disbelievers' rejection of it is unjustified. The verse serves as a reminder to the people to reflect on the signs of God and to accept the truth that is being presented to them.
orig: أم آتيناهم كتابا من قبله فهم به مستمسكون

translation: Nay, they say: 'We found our forefathers upon a religion, and we are guided by their footsteps.'
interpretation: The verse criticizes the people who blindly follow the religion of their ancestors, without examining its truth or falsehood. The people in question admit that they are following the footsteps of their forefathers, but they fail to consider whether this path is actually leading them to the right destination. The verse challenges this mindset and encourages the audience to reflect on their beliefs and actions, rather than simply following tradition. The verse can be seen as a call for independent thinking and critical evaluation of one's beliefs and values.
orig: بل قالوا إنا وجدنا آباءنا على أمة وإنا على آثارهم مهتدون

translation: And thus We did not send before you any warner to a town except that its wealthy said, 'Indeed, we found our fathers upon a religion, and we are, in their footsteps, following.',
interpretation: The verse highlights the common human tendency to resist change and cling to tradition, even if it is misguided. When a prophet was sent to a town, the wealthy and powerful members of the community would often reject his message and instead choose to follow the religion of their ancestors. The verse suggests that this is not a new phenomenon, but has occurred repeatedly throughout history. The verse may serve as a reminder to be open-minded and receptive to new ideas, rather than blindly following tradition and custom.
orig: وكذلك ما أرسلنا من قبلك في قرية من نذير إلا قال مترفوها إنا وجدنا آباءنا على أمة وإنا على آثارهم مقتدون

translation: They say, 'If you had come to us with a sign, we would have followed the message you were sent with.' Yet when the truth came to them, they said, 'Why was this message not sent down to him when his forefathers had it?'
interpretation: The verse highlights the hypocrisy and disbelief of the people, who demand a sign as a condition for belief, but when the truth is presented to them, they reject it. The people's demand for a sign is a stalling tactic and a way to avoid accepting the truth. The verse underscores the futility of such demands and the closed-mindedness of those who make them. The verse may also serve as a reminder to the believers to not be like the disbelievers and to accept the truth when it is presented to them.
orig: قال أولو جئتكم بأهدى مما وجدتم عليه آباءكم قالوا إنا بما أرسلتم به كافرون

translation: So We took revenge on them, and see the end of the liars.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the punishment of those who were liars and deceivers. The phrase 'see the end of the liars' emphasizes the inevitability of the consequences of their actions and serves as a warning to those who persist in falsehood and deception. The verse reminds the readers that God is aware of their actions and will ultimately hold them accountable for their deceit.
orig: فانتقمنا منهم فانظر كيف كان عاقبة المكذبين

translation: And [mention] when Abraham said to his father and his people, 'Indeed, I am free of that which you worship,'
interpretation: The verse recounts the story of Abraham's rejection of the idolatrous practices of his father and people. Abraham asserts his disassociation from their false gods and declares his belief in the one true God. This verse serves as a powerful example of faith and courage, as Abraham stands up for his beliefs in the face of opposition and rejection. It also highlights the importance of monotheism and the rejection of false deities and idolatrous practices in Islam.
orig: وإذ قال إبراهيم لأبيه وقومه إنني براء مما تعبدون

translation: Except him who guides me; indeed, he will be of the rightly guided.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the importance of guidance and being on the right path. The speaker asserts that the only one who can guide them is the one who created them, and that this guidance will lead to righteousness. The verse emphasizes the role of the creator in providing guidance and direction, and the importance of following the right path towards righteousness and salvation.
orig: إلا الذي فطرني فإنه سيهدين

translation: And made it a word to remain in his rear, perhaps they may return.
interpretation: The verse speaks about a word or message that has been left behind as a reminder for those who come after. The verse suggests that this message will remain as a legacy, serving as a reminder for future generations to reflect upon. The phrase 'perhaps they may return' implies that the message may inspire people to reflect on their actions and return to the right path.
orig: وجعلها كلمة باقية في عقبه لعلهم يرجعون

translation: But these rejoice, and their forefathers, while glory lies in wait for them, unaware.
interpretation: The verse speaks about people and their ancestors who are heedless and unaware of the impending doom that awaits them. The word 'rejoice' indicates their state of oblivion and their lack of concern for the consequences of their actions. The phrase 'glory lies in wait for them' refers to the imminent punishment from God, which they are not aware of. The verse serves as a warning to those who are complacent and content with their sinful ways, reminding them that God's punishment is inevitable and that they should not take their blessings for granted.
orig: بل متعت هؤلاء وآباءهم حتى جاءهم الحق ورسول مبين

translation: And when the truth came to them, they said, 'This is magic,' and they disbelieved in it.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the people's rejection of the truth when it was presented to them. Instead of accepting it, they labeled it as magic and refused to believe in it. This verse highlights the human tendency to reject what goes against their preconceived notions and beliefs, even when faced with the truth. It serves as a reminder that truth should be accepted and embraced, regardless of one's initial perceptions or biases.
orig: ولما جاءهم الحق قالوا هذا سحر وإنا به كافرون

translation: And they said, 'Why was this Qur'an not revealed to a man from the two towns (of Mecca and Ta'if)?'
interpretation: The verse is a statement made by the disbelievers of Mecca, questioning why the Qur'an was not revealed to someone from their own community, specifically from the two major towns of Mecca and Ta'if. They reject the message of the Qur'an and its revelation through the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), and they seek to discredit it by asking for a sign that would be more relatable and acceptable to them. The verse highlights the closed-mindedness and rejection of the divine message by the disbelievers, and it serves as a reminder of the importance of having an open heart and mind towards the message of God, regardless of its source or form.
orig: وقالوا لولا نزل هذا القرآن على رجل من القريتين عظيم

translation: And they have apportioned (the) mercy of your Lord. We have apportioned among them their livelihood in the life of this world and raised some of them above others in degrees so that some of them may take others in subjugation. And your Lord's mercy is better than what they amass.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the division of resources and power among people, and the different levels of status they hold. Despite these differences, the verse emphasizes that God's mercy is greater than any material possessions or power that people may accumulate. The verse serves as a reminder that ultimately, it is God's mercy that is the greatest source of benefit and well-being for people, and that they should not be deceived by the temporary and fleeting nature of worldly possessions and status.
orig: أهم يقسمون رحمت ربك نحن قسمنا بينهم معيشتهم في الحياة الدنيا ورفعنا بعضهم فوق بعض درجات ليتخذ بعضهم بعضا سخريا ورحمت ربك خير مما يجمعون

translation: And if not that the people were a single nation, We would have provided for those who disbelieve in the Most Merciful roofs of silver for their houses and stairs on which to ascend.
interpretation: The verse highlights the mercy and generosity of God, who would have given luxurious and extravagant dwellings to those who disbelieve in Him, if it were not for the fact that humanity is one nation. This emphasizes the unity of humanity, and the idea that God's punishment is not arbitrary, but rather a response to the actions of those who reject His mercy. The verse serves as a reminder that God's justice and mercy are intertwined, and that those who reject His mercy will face His punishment. At the same time, it underscores the unity of humanity, suggesting that the actions of one group can have consequences for all. The verse can be understood as a call for unity and solidarity, and a warning against the dangers of division and disbelief.
orig: ولولا أن يكون الناس أمة واحدة لجعلنا لمن يكفر بالرحمن لبيوتهم سقفا من فضة ومعارج عليها يظهرون

translation: And their houses are doors upon doors, where they recline.
interpretation: The verse describes the dwellings of a group of people as having many doors and inner chambers, where they lounge or rest. The exact meaning of this description is open to interpretation, but one possible interpretation is that the dwellings are spacious and luxurious, with many rooms and entrances. This could symbolize the abundance and comfort that these people enjoy in their lives. However, the context of the verse and the overall message of the Surah suggest that this abundance and comfort has led these people to become arrogant and heedless of God's signs, and as a result, they are warned of a severe punishment.
orig: ولبيوتهم أبوابا وسررا عليها يتكئون

translation: And He it is Who adorns for you the grass of the earth, (showing) kindness to the believers; and if it were not for God's grace and mercy on you, (all of) you would have been among the losers.
interpretation: The verse highlights God's kindness and generosity towards believers by providing them with the resources they need to live. The grass of the earth is used as an example of this generosity. The verse emphasizes that these blessings are not only for this life, but also for the hereafter. The verse serves as a reminder of God's mercy and grace, and the importance of recognizing and being grateful for these blessings. It also serves as a warning that without God's grace and mercy, one would be among the losers.
orig: وزخرفا وإن كل ذلك لما متاع الحياة الدنيا والآخرة عند ربك للمتقين

translation: And whoever turns away from the remembrance of the Most Merciful, We assign to him a devil as a companion.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the consequences of turning away from the remembrance of the Most Merciful (one of the names of God in Islam). The verse indicates that those who turn away from God and his teachings will be assigned a devil as a companion. This implies that such individuals will be led astray from the right path and will be under the influence of evil. The verse serves as a warning to the importance of remembering and worshipping God, and the negative consequences of forgetting or ignoring Him.
orig: ومن يعش عن ذكر الرحمن نقيض له شيطانا فهو له قرين

translation: And indeed, they had planned to deceive Him while they were unaware, and they thought that they were guided.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the deceitful plans of certain people against God, while they were under the false impression that they were guided. The verse highlights the delusion of these people, who thought they were on the right path while they were actually planning to mislead others and going against God's way. This verse serves as a reminder of the dangers of self-deception and the importance of staying on the path of righteousness and truth.
orig: وإنهم ليصدونهم عن السبيل ويحسبون أنهم مهتدون

translation: Until, when Our help came to them, they said, 'O, if only there had been between us and you a distance of the two easts! Indeed, they would have been able to be Zāhiqun.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the regret of the disbelievers when they were faced with the help of God, which came to the believers. The disbelievers realized their mistake and expressed their regret for not being able to distance themselves from the believers. The phrase 'a distance of the two easts' emphasizes the great distance they wished was between them and the believers. The verse highlights the consequences of disbelief and the regret of those who rejected the truth.
orig: حتى إذا جاءنا قال يا ليت بيني وبينك بعد المشرقين فبئس القرين

translation: And today, (for) you will not be helped at all, because you were unjust.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the day of judgement and the consequences of injustice. It emphasizes that on this day, those who have committed unjust dejustices will not receive any help or support. The verse serves as a warning for those who are committing unjust acts, reminding them that they will face the consequences of their actions on the day of judgement and will not receive any help or support.
orig: ولن ينفعكم اليوم إذ ظلمتم أنكم في العذاب مشتركون

translation:
Or [do] you think that you will be left alone while you are unaware,
Or that you will guide the blind while you are unclear?
interpretation: The verse is a rhetorical question addressed to the listener, challenging their assumption that they will be left unpunished for their unawareness or that they can guide others out of their misguidance while being unclear themselves. The verse highlights the importance of awareness and clarity in one's actions and the consequences of being unaware and unclear. It serves as a reminder that both the leader and the led are responsible for their actions and that true guidance can only come from a clear and aware state of mind.
orig: أفأنت تسمع الصم أو تهدي العمي ومن كان في ضلال مبين

translation: But if We let him (the unjust person) have a taste of Our punishment, surely We will take him by the forelock (a sign of complete control),
interpretation: The verse describes the punishment of an unjust person, indicating that God has complete control over him. The forelock is a symbol of leadership and guidance, representing God's authority and power over the unjust person. The verse emphasizes the inevitability of punishment for those who persist in their wrongdoing and the ultimate victory of justice.
orig: فإما نذهبن بك فإنا منهم منتقمون

translation: Or have We shown you the greatest thing (i.e. the Day of Resurrection)? Surely! We have power over it.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the Day of Resurrection, which is described as the 'greatest thing'. The verse emphasizes God's power and control over this event, indicating that it will surely happen. The verse can be interpreted as a reminder of the reality of the Day of Resurrection and a warning to those who deny it or ignore its significance. It also serves as a reminder of God's power and control over all things, and the inevitability of His decree.
orig: أو نرينك الذي وعدناهم فإنا عليهم مقتدرون

translation: So hold fast to what has been revealed to you. Indeed, you are on a straight path.
interpretation: The verse is a command to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to hold fast to the revelation he has received from God, which is the Qur'an. The verse emphasizes the importance of adhering to the teachings of the Qur'an and following its guidance. The verse also indicates that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) is on a straight path, which refers to the right and true religion of Islam. The verse can be seen as a source of reassurance and guidance for Muslims, reminding them of the importance of holding fast to the teachings of the Qur'an and following the straight path of Islam.
orig: فاستمسك بالذي أوحي إليك إنك على صراط مستقيم

translation: And indeed, it is a reminder for you and your people, and you all will be questioned.
interpretation: The verse is a reminder for both the Prophet Muhammad and his people that they will be held accountable for their actions on the Day of Judgment. The phrase 'you all will be questioned' emphasizes the certainty of this event and serves as a warning for the people to prepare for it by living a righteous life.
orig: وإنه لذكر لك ولقومك وسوف تسألون

translation: And ask those of Our messengers whom We sent before you: 'Have We made, besides the Most Merciful, deities to be worshiped?'
interpretation: The verse is a command to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to ask the previous messengers of God about the existence of any deities worthy of worship besides the Most Merciful (one of the names of God). The verse emphasizes the oneness of God and the importance of worshiping Him alone. It also highlights the continuity of the message of all the prophets, who all brought the same message of monotheism and the worship of the one true God. The verse serves as a reminder that there is no other god but Allah, and that all other deities are false and unworthy of worship.
orig: واسأل من أرسلنا من قبلك من رسلنا أجعلنا من دون الرحمن آلهة يعبدون

translation: And indeed We sent Moses with Our signs to Pharaoh and his establishment, but he said, 'Indeed, I am a messenger of the Lord of the worlds.'
interpretation: The verse relates the story of Moses being sent by God to Pharaoh and his people with divine signs as proof of his prophethood. However, Pharaoh and his establishment rejected Moses' message and refused to believe in the Lord of the worlds. This verse highlights the rejection of divine guidance by the powerful and the arrogant, and the persistence of prophets in fulfilling their mission despite facing opposition and denial.
orig: ولقد أرسلنا موسى بآياتنا إلى فرعون وملئه فقال إني رسول رب العالمين

translation: But when Our verses are recited to them as clear evidences, they say, 'This is only mankind who wishes to turn you away from that which your forefathers were worshipping.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the people's rejection and mockery of the signs of God, despite their clarity and relevance. The people refuse to accept the truth and instead claim that the one who is delivering the message is only trying to turn them away from their traditional beliefs. The verse highlights the closed-mindedness and stubbornness of those who reject the message of God, and their unwillingness to consider any alternative to their established ways of thinking and worship.
orig: فلما جاءهم بآياتنا إذا هم منها يضحكون

translation: And We do not send down upon them any sign except that it is greater than its companion, and We seize them with punishment, so perhaps they might return.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the sending of signs from God to people as a form of guidance, but they do not heed these signs. Instead, they are punished for their disbelief and disobedience. The verse emphasizes the greatness of the signs sent by God, and the severity of the punishment that follows. The punishment is meant to serve as a wake-up call, in hopes that the people might return to the path of righteousness. However, if they continue to reject God's signs and persist in their wrongdoing, they will face further punishment.
orig: وما نريهم من آية إلا هي أكبر من أختها وأخذناهم بالعذاب لعلهم يرجعون

translation: And they said, 'O you to whom the Reminder has been sent down, indeed, you are a madman!', [Qur'an, 15:6]
interpretation: The verse describes the disbelievers' response to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) when he received the revelation from God. They accused him of being a madman, rejecting the message that he brought. The verse highlights the common response of those who reject the truth and refuse to follow the guidance of God. It serves as a reminder that the message of Islam may be met with rejection and mockery, but that it remains the truth and the path to salvation.
orig: وقالوا يا أيه الساحر ادع لنا ربك بما عهد عندك إننا لمهتدون

translation: But when We removed the punishment from them, behold, they were committing crimes.
interpretation: The verse describes the behavior of people who, after experiencing divine punishment, immediately returned to committing sins and transgressions. The removal of the punishment was not a sign of God's forgiveness, but rather a test of the people's gratitude and obedience. The verse serves as a warning that divine punishment may recur if people do not take advantage of the opportunity to repent and change their ways.
orig: فلما كشفنا عنهم العذاب إذا هم ينكثون

translation: And Pharaoh called out among his people, saying: 'O my people! Is not mine the dominion of Egypt, and these rivers flowing beneath me? What, then, do you not see?'
interpretation: Pharaoh is boasting about his power and control over Egypt and the rivers that flow through the land. He is questioning his people and asking them why they do not acknowledge his authority. The verse highlights Pharaoh's arrogance and pride, and sets the stage for the confrontation between Pharaoh and Moses, who will challenge Pharaoh's authority and call on him to release the Israelites from slavery. The verse serves as a reminder of the dangers of arrogance and the importance of humility and submission to God's will.
orig: ونادى فرعون في قومه قال يا قوم أليس لي ملك مصر وهذه الأنهار تجري من تحتي أفلا تبصرون

translation: Or am I better than this one who is despised and barely able to speak?
interpretation: The verse is a rhetorical question, comparing the speaker to someone who is considered insignificant and has difficulty speaking. The speaker is implying that, despite their own flaws, they are still better than the person being described. This verse may be used in a context where the speaker is trying to assert their worth or value in comparison to someone else.
orig: أم أنا خير من هذا الذي هو مهين ولا يكاد يبين

translation: But if not (i.e., if you do not believe) - then (at least) let a token from the your Lord be set upon you, or a manifest punishment.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the consequences of not believing in God's message. The verse offers two options for the disbelievers: either a token (a sign or a miracle) from God or a manifest punishment. The verse emphasizes the importance of faith and the consequences of rejecting God's message. It serves as a warning to those who deny the truth, reminding them of the impending punishment for their disbelief.
orig: فلولا ألقي عليه أسورة من ذهب أو جاء معه الملائكة مقترنين

translation: But their brother Aaron was among them, so he said, 'O my people, follow me and obey my command.', Indeed, they had been a transgressing people.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the people of Moses, who were transgressors, and their brother Aaron, who tried to guide them towards the right path. Despite Aaron's efforts, the people followed their own desires and continued to transgress. The verse highlights the role of a leader in guiding people towards the right path and the consequences of disobedience and transgression. It serves as a reminder of the importance of obedience to the rightful leaders and the dangers of following one's desires over the command of God.
orig: فاستخف قومه فأطاعوه إنهم كانوا قوما فاسقين

translation: But when they defiantly disobeyed Us, We exacted retribution from them and drowned them all.
interpretation: The verse describes the punishment of a group of people who defiantly disobeyed God. The punishment they received was that they were all drowned. This verse emphasizes the consequences of disobedience and defiance towards God, reminding the readers that God will not let such actions go unpunished. The verse also serves as a warning to those who choose to defy God's commands and a reminder of the power and authority of God.
orig: فلما آسفونا انتقمنا منهم فأغرقناهم أجمعين

translation: And We made them (the previous nations) preceding generations, and examples to later peoples.
interpretation: The verse refers to previous nations who were made as examples for future generations. By making them preceding generations, their experiences, actions, and consequences serve as lessons for those who come after them. This comparison highlights the significance of learning from history and using it as a guide for the future. The verse emphasizes the importance of understanding the consequences of actions and how they can impact future generations. It serves as a reminder that the actions of individuals and communities have a lasting impact and can influence the course of history.
orig: فجعلناهم سلفا ومثلا للآخرين

translation: And when the son of Mary was criticized, they said, 'An infidel! How can he eat food while being a servant to Allah?'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the criticism and disbelief faced by Jesus, the son of Mary, by people who questioned his humanity and divine nature. The verse highlights the disbelievers' rejection of Jesus as a prophet of God, and their accusations of him being an infidel despite his devotion and servitude to God. The verse serves as a reminder of the rejection and persecution faced by prophets and messengers of God, and the importance of recognizing and accepting their message despite the challenges and criticisms from others.
orig: ولما ضرب ابن مريم مثلا إذا قومك منه يصدون

translation: And they said, 'Our gods are better than He is, or, rather, they are equivalent to Him.' No, but they are a contentious people.
interpretation: The verse describes a conversation where the disbelievers are rejecting the message of the one true God and instead, they are praising their own gods, claiming that their gods are better or equal to the one true God. The response from the text is that they are not equal or better, but rather, the disbelievers are a contentious people, who argue and dispute without basis. The verse serves as a reminder that there is only one true God, and that the worship of false gods is a futile and misguided endeavor.
orig: وقالوا أآلهتنا خير أم هو ما ضربوه لك إلا جدلا بل هم قوم خصمون

translation: Indeed, he is only a servant on whom We have bestowed favor, and We made him an example for the Children of Israel.
interpretation: The verse speaks about a servant (who is understood to be the Prophet Muhammad) who has been shown great favor by God. The servant is made an example (or a 'sign') for the Children of Israel, which implies that the servant has a significant role in conveying God's message and serving as a model of righteousness and obedience. The verse highlights the special relationship between the servant and God, and the important mission that the servant has been given in the context of God's plan for humanity.
orig: إن هو إلا عبد أنعمنا عليه وجعلناه مثلا لبني إسرائيل

translation: And if We had willed, We could have made of you angels succeeding [one another] on the earth.
interpretation: The verse speaks about God's power and authority, stating that if He had willed, He could have made humans into angels who succeed each other on the earth. This verse emphasizes the immense power of God and His ability to do as He pleases. It also highlights the fact that humans are not the only beings in existence and that God has the power to create and control other beings, such as angels. This verse can serve as a reminder of God's greatness and our dependence on Him.
orig: ولو نشاء لجعلنا منكم ملائكة في الأرض يخلفون

translation: Indeed, knowledge of the Hour is with Allah [Alone]. So be not deceived that you will be able to outstrip it. Rather, follow Me. This is a straight path.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of following the path of righteousness and obedience to God, as the exact time of the Hour (Day of Judgment) is known only to Him. The verse warns against complacency and a false sense of security, as one cannot escape the inevitable Day of Judgment. By following God's path, one can ensure a righteous and fulfilling life, and ultimately attain salvation in the afterlife.
orig: وإنه لعلم للساعة فلا تمترن بها واتبعون هذا صراط مستقيم

translation: And let not Satan tempt you; indeed, he is to you a clear enemy.
interpretation: The verse warns against the deception and temptation of Satan, who is described as a clear enemy of humanity. By emphasizing Satan's enmity, the verse highlights the importance of being vigilant and resisting his temptations. This verse serves as a reminder to Muslims to seek protection from Satan and to stay on the path of righteousness and obedience to God.
orig: ولا يصدنكم الشيطان إنه لكم عدو مبين

translation: And when Jesus came with clear proofs, he said, 'I have come to you with wisdom and to make clear to you some of what you differ about. So fear Allah and obey me.',
interpretation: The verse speaks about the coming of Jesus and his message to the people. Jesus brought 'clear proofs' or evidence to support his message. He came to the people with wisdom and the intention of resolving some of the disagreements that they had. The verse encourages the people to fear God and to obey Jesus. This verse can be interpreted as a call for unity and a reminder of the importance of following the guidance of a prophet. It emphasizes the importance of using wisdom and reason to understand and resolve disagreements and the importance of following the guidance of a prophet in order to be on the right path and avoid the wrath of God.
orig: ولما جاء عيسى بالبينات قال قد جئتكم بالحكمة ولأبين لكم بعض الذي تختلفون فيه فاتقوا الله وأطيعون

translation: Indeed, Allah is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him. This is the straight path.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the oneness of God and the need to worship Him alone. The phrase 'Indeed, Allah is my Lord and your Lord' is a reminder of the unity and equality of all people before God. The verse commands all people to worship God and follow the 'straight path' - a metaphor for the right and true way of life. The verse serves as a call to all people to submit to God, follow His teachings, and avoid straying from the right path.
orig: إن الله هو ربي وربكم فاعبدوه هذا صراط مستقيم

translation: And the factions among them differed, so woe to the wrongdoers from the punishment of a painful day.
interpretation: The verse highlights the disagreements and divisions among certain groups of people, and warns of the consequences for those who commit wrongdoing. The phrase 'punishment of a painful day' refers to the severe and unavoidable punishment that will be faced by those who commit injustices. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of unity and justice, and the consequences of straying from these principles.
orig: فاختلف الأحزاب من بينهم فويل للذين ظلموا من عذاب يوم أليم

translation: Do they then look at nothing else but the sky, (waiting) for the fulfillment of its fate, that it should be cleft asunder?
interpretation: The verse addresses people who are so certain of an impending doom that they only look at the sky, waiting for its destruction. The verse criticizes this behavior and implies that these people are missing out on the present by focusing too much on the future. The phrase 'that it should be cleft asunder' refers to the splitting of the sky, a catastrophic event that some early Arabian tribes believed would signal the end of the world. The verse serves as a reminder to live in the present and not to be consumed by fear or anxiety about the future.
orig: هل ينظرون إلا الساعة أن تأتيهم بغتة وهم لا يشعرون

translation: The Day shall surely come when some of you shall rise up against others, except the righteous.
interpretation: The verse speaks about a day of conflict and division, where some people will rise up against others. However, it also emphasizes that there will be a group of people, the righteous, who will not be a part of this conflict. This verse may serve as a warning of the dangers of division and conflict, and a reminder of the importance of righteousness and maintaining unity and peace.
orig: الأخلاء يومئذ بعضهم لبعض عدو إلا المتقين

translation: O believers, there is no fear for you today nor are you grieved.
interpretation: The verse addresses the believers, offering them reassurance and comfort. It informs them that they have nothing to fear or grieve about on that day. The verse may be referring to the Day of Judgment, where the believers will be saved and will not have to fear God's punishment. Alternatively, it may be referring to a specific event or situation where the believers were facing difficulties or challenges, but have now been relieved of them. The verse serves as a source of comfort and reassurance for the believers, reminding them of God's protection and care for them.
orig: يا عباد لا خوف عليكم اليوم ولا أنتم تحزنون

translation: Those who have believed in our signs and have been submitters.
interpretation: The verse describes a group of people who have believed in the signs (ayat) of God and have submitted (aslama) themselves to God. The verse highlights the importance of faith and submission to God, emphasizing that these qualities are essential for those who wish to be guided and saved. The verse can also be seen as a reminder that true faith must be accompanied by righteous actions, as belief alone is not enough. Ultimately, the verse serves as a message of hope and guidance for all those who seek to follow the path of God.
orig: الذين آمنوا بآياتنا وكانوا مسلمين

translation: Enter Paradise, you and your wives, delighted.
interpretation: The verse is a promise from God to the believers that they will enter Paradise, along with their spouses, and experience eternal joy and delight. It is a reward for their faith and righteous deeds, and a symbol of the ultimate happiness and fulfillment that awaits them in the afterlife.
orig: ادخلوا الجنة أنتم وأزواجكم تحبرون

translation: That He it is who sends down on you the rain from the sky, and with it We bring forth the greenery (plants), from which you get the raw material of your pasture(s).
interpretation: The verse emphasizes God's role as the provider and sustainer of life, by sending down rain from the sky to bring forth greenery and pasture. The verse serves as a reminder of God's power and control over the natural world and the dependence of human beings on God's bounty. It also highlights the importance of appreciating and utilizing the resources provided by God in a responsible and sustainable manner.
orig: يطاف عليهم بصحاف من ذهب وأكواب وفيها ما تشتهيه الأنفس وتلذ الأعين وأنتم فيها خالدون

translation: And that is the Paradise which you have been made to inherit because of what you used to do.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the reward of Paradise that has been given to the believers as a result of their good deeds. The verse emphasizes the connection between actions and consequences, and the importance of leading a righteous life. It serves as a motivation for believers to continue doing good deeds and to strive for Paradise. The verse also reminds that the reward of Paradise is not something that is given without any effort, but it is something that is earned through righteous actions.
orig: وتلك الجنة التي أورثتموها بما كنتم تعملون

translation: In it there are fruits, from it you eat
interpretation: The verse is referring to a place or thing that has an abundance of fruits, and that these fruits are a source of nourishment for the people. The verse may be referring to a specific location, such as a garden or orchard, or it may be used metaphorically to describe a source of blessings and provisions. The verse highlights the importance of utilizing and enjoying the resources that are provided to us, and the blessings that come from being grateful for and using these resources in a responsible and sustainable way.
orig: لكم فيها فاكهة كثيرة منها تأكلون

translation: Indeed, the criminals will be in punishment of Hell, abiding therein [forever].
interpretation: The verse asserts that criminals will be punished in Hell and will remain there eternally. The verse emphasizes the severity and permanence of the punishment for those who commit wrongdoing, serving as a warning to those who engage in immoral and unjust actions and a reminder of the severe consequences of their actions.
orig: إن المجرمين في عذاب جهنم خالدون

translation: Allah does not task a soul beyond its capacity. Indeed, it will have [the consequence of] what it earned, and it will bear [the consequence of] what it earned.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the principle of justice in Islam and the idea that each person is responsible for their own actions and will be held accountable for them in the afterlife. The verse reassures the believers that Allah does not burden a soul with more than it can bear, and that each person will receive the consequences of their actions, whether good or bad. The verse serves as a reminder to the believers to strive for righteousness and to avoid sin, as they will be responsible for the consequences of their actions on the Day of Judgment.
orig: لا يفتر عنهم وهم فيه مبلسون

translation: And We wronged them not, but they were unjust to themselves.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes that it was not God who wronged the people, but rather, they wronged themselves through their own unjust actions. This highlights the principle of individual responsibility and accountability for one's actions, and the idea that God is just and does not wrong people without cause. The verse may serve as a reminder to those who blame others or external circumstances for their problems, to instead look inward and reflect on their own actions and choices.
orig: وما ظلمناهم ولكن كانوا هم الظالمين

translation: And they will call, 'O Malik, let your Lord put an end to us!' He will say, 'Indeed, you will remain.',
interpretation: The verse speaks about the fate of the people of hell who, in their suffering, will call out to Malik, the angel in charge of hell, to ask God to end their punishment. However, they will be told that they will not be released from their suffering. The verse emphasizes the eternal nature of the punishment for those who have committed great sins and have not repented. It serves as a warning to those who continue to commit sins and do not seek forgiveness, reminding them of the grave consequences of their actions.
orig: ونادوا يا مالك ليقض علينا ربك قال إنكم ماكثون

translation: We have certainly brought you, [O Muhammad], the truth, but most of you are averse to the truth.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the prophet Muhammad (PBUH) bringing the truth (Islam) to the people, but most of them reject or are reluctant to accept it. The verse highlights the difficulty of conveying the truth to those who are not receptive or unwilling to accept it, emphasizing the importance of being open-minded and receptive to the truth, even if it goes against one's preconceived notions or beliefs.
orig: لقد جئناكم بالحق ولكن أكثركم للحق كارهون

translation: Have they then taken a clear decision (to reject Islam)? Then indeed We are Deciders.
interpretation: The verse is addressing those who have rejected Islam and taken a clear decision to oppose it. The verse emphasizes that God is the ultimate Decider, and that the fate of those who reject His message is in His hands. The verse serves as a reminder that God has the power to decide the outcome of all things, and that those who reject His message will face the consequences of their actions.
orig: أم أبرموا أمرا فإنا مبرمون

translation: Or do they think that I cannot hear their secrets and their private conversations? No, indeed, but My messengers record them.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes God's omniscience and all-encompassing knowledge, stating that He is aware of people's secrets and private conversations. The phrase 'My messengers record them' suggests that God's knowledge is not limited to the present moment, but extends to past and future as well. The verse serves as a reminder that nothing is hidden from God, and that people should be mindful of their actions and words, even when they think they are unobserved.
orig: أم يحسبون أنا لا نسمع سرهم ونجواهم بلى ورسلنا لديهم يكتبون

translation: Say, 'If the Most Merciful had a son, then I would be the first of the worshippers.'
interpretation: The verse is a rhetorical question posed by the Prophet Muhammad, challenging the claim made by some Arab tribes during his time that the Most Merciful (one of the names of God) had a son. The verse is a denial of this claim and an affirmation of the Islamic belief in the oneness of God, with no partners or children. The verse also emphasizes the Prophet's devotion and worship of God, stating that if such a claim were true, he would be the first among the worshippers of the son of God. The verse serves as a reminder of the Islamic belief in the oneness of God and the importance of worshipping Him alone.
orig: قل إن كان للرحمن ولد فأنا أول العابدين

translation: Glorified be my Lord, the Lord of the heavens and the Lord of the earth, the Lord of the Throne, above what they describe.
interpretation: The verse is a glorification of God as the Lord of the heavens, the earth, and the throne. It emphasizes God's greatness and power, and rejects the false descriptions of God by others. The verse serves as a reminder of the true nature of God, and encourages the reader to reject any false notions or idolatrous beliefs. It also highlights the transcendence of God, as God is above what they describe.
orig: سبحان رب السماوات والأرض رب العرش عما يصفون

translation: So leave them to their play and vain talk until they meet their Day which they are promised.
interpretation: The verse instructs the Prophet Muhammad to leave the disbelievers alone and allow them to continue in their heedlessness and rejection of his message. The verse implies that the disbelievers are occupied with trivial matters, engaging in futile discussions and amusements. The verse also mentions the 'Day' that the disbelievers are promised, which is the Day of Judgment. The verse conveys the idea that the disbelievers will continue in their ways until they are confronted with the reality of the Hereafter, when it will be too late for them to change their ways.
orig: فذرهم يخوضوا ويلعبوا حتى يلاقوا يومهم الذي يوعدون

translation: And He is the One who is God in the heaven and God in the earth, and He is the Wise, the Knowing.
interpretation: The verse affirms the oneness and uniqueness of God, stating that He is the only deity in the heavens and the earth. The repetition of 'God' emphasizes the point and affirms that God's sovereignty and power extend over all of creation. The attributes of 'the Wise' and 'the Knowing' further emphasize God's power and knowledge, highlighting His ability to manage all affairs and His understanding of all things. The verse may serve as a reminder of God's greatness and a call for submission to His will.
orig: وهو الذي في السماء إله وفي الأرض إله وهو الحكيم العليم

translation: Blessed is He in Whose Hand is the dominion of the heavens and the earth, and whatever is between them, and with Whom is knowledge of the Hour. And to Him you will be returned.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the greatness and power of God, who has control over everything in the heavens, the earth, and in between. It emphasizes God's knowledge and awareness of the 'Hour' or the Day of Judgment. The verse serves as a reminder of God's power and control over all aspects of existence, and of the inevitability of the Day of Judgment. It encourages people to reflect on their actions and to prepare themselves for the ultimate return to God.
orig: وتبارك الذي له ملك السماوات والأرض وما بينهما وعنده علم الساعة وإليه ترجعون

translation: And those whom they invoke instead of Him have no power of intercession, except for one who bears witness to the truth and they know [that person's claim is true].
interpretation: The verse asserts that those who are worshipped besides God have no power of intercession, except for those who are recognized as truthful and just. This highlights the unique power of God, who has no partners or equals. The verse serves as a reminder that true intercession can only come from those who are righteous and have knowledge of the truth. It also emphasizes the futility of worshipping false deities, as they have no power or authority. The verse encourages believers to seek intercession only from those who are worthy of it and to rely solely on God for help and guidance.
orig: ولا يملك الذين يدعون من دونه الشفاعة إلا من شهد بالحق وهم يعلمون

translation: And if you asked them who created them, they would surely say, 'Allah.'
interpretation: The verse highlights the universal belief in a Creator, even among those who may not follow Islamic teachings. The statement that people would attribute their creation to 'Allah' if asked serves to emphasize the inherent knowledge of a higher power that is present in all of humanity. This verse can be interpreted as a reminder of the unity of all people in their belief in a Creator, and as an invitation to reflect on the significance of this belief in daily life.
orig: ولئن سألتهم من خلقهم ليقولن الله فأنى يؤفكون

translation: And it was said, 'O Lord, indeed these are a people who do not believe.'
interpretation: The verse is a quote from someone who is expressing their concern and frustration about a group of people who do not believe. The speaker is appealing to a higher power, addressing God as 'Lord' and seeking His help or intervention. The verse suggests that the non-believers are a cause of distress or conflict, and the speaker is seeking divine intervention to address the situation. The verse can be seen as a call for guidance and support in the face of disbelief and rejection of faith.
orig: وقيله يا رب إن هؤلاء قوم لا يؤمنون

translation: So move away from them and say, 'Peace be upon you.' They will soon come to know.
