interpretation: The verse instructs the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) to disengage from those who reject his message and maintain his dignity by saying 'Peace be upon you.' The verse suggests that the unbelievers will eventually come to understand and recognize the truth, but only after it is too late for them to change their ways. The verse encourages patience and perseverance in the face of rejection and opposition, and emphasizes the importance of maintaining one's moral and ethical standards in all situations.
orig: فاصفح عنهم وقل سلام فسوف يعلمون

translation: By the heaven and the starsetter (Orion, the constellation of the three stars in a line, the big dipper)
interpretation: The verse begins with a solemn oath by the heavens and the starsetter (Orion, the constellation of the three stars in a line, the big dipper), emphasizing the importance of the message that follows. The verse is a reminder of God's power and control over the universe and serves as a means of instilling awe and reverence in the hearts of the believers. It also highlights the intricate and precise arrangement of the stars and constellations, which is a testament to God's greatness and wisdom.
orig: حم

translation: And the explicit Book.
interpretation: The verse refers to the Qur'an as the 'explicit Book', emphasizing its clarity and unambiguous nature. The Qur'an is a guide for humanity, providing clear and detailed instructions on how to live a righteous and fulfilling life. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of following the teachings of the Qur'an, which offers a clear path to success and salvation.
orig: والكتاب المبين

translation: Indeed, we sent it down during a blessed night. Indeed, we were warning [mankind].
interpretation: The verse speaks about the revelation of a sacred message during a blessed night. The verse emphasizes the divine origin of the message, as it was sent down by a higher power. The message serves as a warning to humanity, reminding them to be aware and vigilant. This interpretation suggests that the message is of great importance and significance, and that it carries a divine message that should be taken seriously by those who receive it.
orig: إنا أنزلناه في ليلة مباركة إنا كنا منذرين

translation: In it (the heaven) every matter of decree is distinguished.
interpretation: The verse refers to the heaven as a place where every matter or affair is determined and distinguished. This implies that the heaven is the source of all events and decisions, and that everything that happens in the world is decreed and controlled by a wise and all-knowing power. This interpretation highlights the idea of divine providence and predestination, emphasizing the ultimate control of God over all aspects of life and the universe.
orig: فيها يفرق كل أمر حكيم

translation: A commandment from Us! Indeed, We have sent (many) messengers.
interpretation: The verse speaks about a commandment from God, emphasizing its divine origin. It also mentions that God has sent many messengers to convey His message. The verse could be interpreted as a reminder of the importance of following God's commandments and listening to His messengers, who were sent to guide humanity towards the right path.
orig: أمرا من عندنا إنا كنا مرسلين

translation: A mercy from your Lord. Indeed, He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.
interpretation: The verse speaks about God's mercy and His attributes of being All-Hearing and All-Knowing. The verse emphasizes that the mercy being spoken of is from one's Lord, indicating a personal and direct connection between the recipient of the mercy and the giver of the mercy. The attributes of being All-Hearing and All-Knowing highlight God's omniscience and His ability to hear and respond to the prayers and needs of His creatures. The verse serves as a reminder of God's boundless mercy and His all-encompassing knowledge and power.
orig: رحمة من ربك إنه هو السميع العليم

translation: Lord of the heavens and the earth, and whatever is between them, if you are able to be certain [of it].
interpretation: The verse is a reminder of the greatness and power of God, who is the Lord of the heavens, the earth, and all that lies between them. The phrase 'if you are able to be certain [of it]' is a rhetorical device used to emphasize the impossibility of having complete knowledge or certainty about God's power and control. The verse encourages the reader to have faith and trust in God, recognizing the limits of their own understanding and knowledge.
orig: رب السماوات والأرض وما بينهما إن كنتم موقنين

translation: No god is there but He, the Living, the Everlasting. Slain not is He, nor doth He sleep. Unto Him belongeth whatsoever is in the heavens and whatsoever is in the earth. Who is he that intercedeth with Him save by His leave? He knoweth that which is before them and that which is behind them, and they comprehend not anything of His knowledge save what He will. His throne extends over the heavens and the earth, and the preservation of them oppresses Him not; and He is the High, the Great.
interpretation: The verse is a powerful declaration of the oneness of God, emphasizing His divine attributes of being the only God, the Everlasting, the One who gives life and takes it away. The verse also emphasizes that God is not like His creation, He does not die or sleep, and His knowledge is beyond comprehension. The verse also highlights God's power and sovereignty over all of creation, as He knows all that is before and after, and nothing escapes His knowledge. The verse serves as a reminder of God's greatness and His complete control over all aspects of life and death.
orig: لا إله إلا هو يحيي ويميت ربكم ورب آبائكم الأولين

translation: No, they are in doubt, playing.
interpretation: The verse highlights the attitude of disbelievers who are in doubt about the truth of Islam and engage in frivolous activities instead of contemplating and reflecting on the signs of God. The verse suggests that they are not taking their faith seriously and are preoccupied with trivial pursuits. The verse serves as a warning to those who are not taking their faith seriously, urging them to reflect on the truth and avoid falling into disbelief.
orig: بل هم في شك يلعبون

translation: So wait for the day when the sky will bring forth a visible smoke.
interpretation: The verse speaks about a day of reckoning when the sky will release a visible smoke as a sign of impending doom. This verse is a warning of a coming disaster and serves as a call to be prepared for the consequences of one's actions. It emphasizes the inevitability of the day of judgment, and the need for people to be mindful of their actions and to repent before it is too late.
orig: فارتقب يوم تأتي السماء بدخان مبين

translation: A painful punishment will enshroud mankind.
interpretation: The verse speaks of a painful punishment that will envelop or enshroud all of humanity. This punishment is likely a reference to the Day of Judgment, when all people will be held accountable for their actions and receive their just deserts. The use of the word 'enshroud' suggests that the punishment will be all-encompassing and inescapable, leaving no one unscathed. The verse serves as a warning to humanity, urging people to prepare for the inevitable reckoning and to strive for righteousness in this life.
orig: يغشى الناس هذا عذاب أليم

translation: ‘Our Lord, remove from us the punishment, indeed we are believers.’
interpretation: The verse is a supplication from a group of believers, asking their Lord to remove the punishment from them, as they have faith in Him. It highlights the importance of faith and the relationship between the believers and their Lord. It also shows the humility and vulnerability of the believers as they seek protection and mercy from their Lord, emphasizing the significance of seeking God's help and guidance in times of hardship and distress.
orig: ربنا اكشف عنا العذاب إنا مؤمنون

translation: Then how will they be reminded, when a clear Messenger has come to them?
interpretation: The verse is a rhetorical question that highlights the futility of reminding those who have already been given clear guidance in the form of a messenger. It emphasizes the importance of heeding the message of the prophet and the consequences of ignoring it. The verse serves as a reminder to those who have been given the guidance to recognize and follow the message of the prophet and not to ignore it or take it lightly.
orig: أنى لهم الذكرى وقد جاءهم رسول مبين

translation: Then turn away from him (i.e. Prophet Muhammad) and say, 'He is a madman.'
interpretation: The verse is addressing the disbelievers who rejected the message of Prophet Muhammad. It describes their response to his teachings as turning away from him and accusing him of being insane. The verse highlights the rejection and disbelief of those who refuse to accept the truth and instead, label the prophet as mad. It serves as a reminder of the opposition and persecution faced by the prophet and his followers, and the importance of remaining steadfast and firm in the face of such adversity.
orig: ثم تولوا عنه وقالوا معلم مجنون

translation: Indeed, We send the punishment only gradually, so that you may return (to obedience).
interpretation: The verse speaks about the gradual nature of God's punishment, which is sent so that people may have the opportunity to reflect and return to obedience. The verse reminds people that God's punishment is not sent all at once, but rather in a way that allows them to understand the consequences of their actions and to change their ways. The verse serves as a call to repentance and a reminder of God's mercy and willingness to forgive those who turn away from their sins.
orig: إنا كاشفو العذاب قليلا إنكم عائدون

translation: The day of the great clamor, indeed We will take revenge.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the day of the great clamor, which is a day of reckoning and punishment from God. The verse emphasizes that God will take revenge on that day, indicating the severity of the punishment and the consequences of people's actions. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the certainty of God's judgment and the severity of the consequences of their actions.
orig: يوم نبطش البطشة الكبرى إنا منتقمون

translation: And indeed, We did test the people of Pharaoh before them, and there came to them a noble messenger.
interpretation: The verse speaks about a test that was given to the people of Pharaoh in the past. This test was in the form of a noble messenger who was sent to them. The verse can be interpreted as a reminder that God tests different communities throughout history, and that these tests often come in the form of messengers and prophets who bring divine guidance and teachings. This verse may also serve as a reminder that those who reject or ignore these messengers will face consequences, as was the case with the people of Pharaoh.
orig: ولقد فتنا قبلهم قوم فرعون وجاءهم رسول كريم

translation: And when Musa said to his people: 'O my people, indeed I have perceived a clear sign from my Lord that indeed, He has sent me to you as a messenger.',
interpretation: In this verse, Musa (Moses) is speaking to his people and informing them that he has received a clear sign from his Lord that he has been sent to them as a messenger. The verse emphasizes Musa's certainty and confidence in his mission as a messenger from God. It also highlights the importance of prophets as a means of guidance and communication between God and his people.
orig: أن أدوا إلي عباد الله إني لكم رسول أمين

translation: But do not exalt yourselves against God. I have come to you with clear authority.
interpretation: The verse is a warning against arrogance and self-importance, specifically in relation to God. The command 'do not exalt yourselves against God' emphasizes the importance of humility and recognizing one's place in the world. The statement 'I have come to you with clear authority' suggests that the speaker has been sent by God with a specific purpose and message. The verse could be interpreted as a warning to those who reject or ignore the message of the speaker, as they will face the consequences of their actions.
orig: وأن لا تعلوا على الله إني آتيكم بسلطان مبين

translation: And indeed I call upon my Lord and your Lord to bring about between us a fair judgment.
interpretation: The verse is a call for justice and fairness between the speaker and those they are addressing. The speaker invokes the shared Lord of both parties as a witness and a guarantor of the fairness of the judgment. The verse may be understood as a plea for a peaceful resolution of a conflict or a dispute, or as a call for an impartial assessment of a situation. Ultimately, the verse emphasizes the importance of justice and fairness in human relationships, and the role of the divine in upholding these values.
orig: وإني عذت بربي وربكم أن ترجمون

translation: But if you do not believe, then keep away from me.
interpretation: The verse is spoken by the Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) and is addressed to those who do not believe in his message. The Prophet is giving them a clear choice: either believe in the message or keep away from him. The verse emphasizes the importance of faith and the rejection of those who refuse to accept the truth. It also highlights the separation between the believers and the non-believers, and the need for the Prophet to distance himself from those who reject his message.
orig: وإن لم تؤمنوا لي فاعتزلون

translation: He called upon his Lord, saying, 'These, my people, are sinners.'
interpretation: The verse describes a person who turns to God in prayer and expresses his concern about the sinners among his people. The person acknowledges the wrongdoing of his people and seeks divine intervention to address the situation. The verse highlights the individual's awareness of the moral decay and corruption in his community, and his desire for change and redemption.
orig: فدعا ربه أن هؤلاء قوم مجرمون

translation: And He (it is) who takes away the souls at night, and He knows what you have earned by day.
interpretation: The verse speaks about God's power over the souls of human beings and His knowledge of their actions. The verse emphasizes that God takes away the souls of people at night, indicating that He has control over the life and death of every creature. The second part of the verse highlights God's omniscience, emphasizing that He knows everything that people do during the day. The verse serves as a reminder of God's power and knowledge, encouraging people to be mindful of their actions and to live in accordance with His will.
orig: فأسر بعبادي ليلا إنكم متبعون

translation: And leave the sea as simmering. Indeed, they are a drowned host.
interpretation: The verse describes the sea as being in a state of agitation or 'simmering', and then makes a comparison to a group of people who have drowned or 'a drowned host'. The verse may be interpreted as a metaphor for the fate of those who oppose or reject God's message. Just as the sea's agitation is a sign of its power and unpredictability, the fate of the 'drowned host' serves as a warning to those who defy God's will. The verse emphasizes the inevitability of God's judgment and the consequences of disbelief.
orig: واترك البحر رهوا إنهم جند مغرقون

translation: How many gardens and springs have they left behind!
interpretation: The verse is a rhetorical question that highlights the loss and regret of those who have left behind their gardens and springs. The gardens and springs are symbols of prosperity, abundance, and blessings. The verse emphasizes the idea of abandonment and waste, and it implies that those who have left them behind have lost a great opportunity. The context of the verse is the story of the people of 'Ad and Thamud, who were destroyed because of their disbelief and disobedience. The verse serves as a warning and a reminder of the consequences of rejection of God's blessings and guidance.
orig: كم تركوا من جنات وعيون

translation: And a planted root and a standing place of honor.
interpretation: The verse is a metaphorical description of two things that are firmly established and unshakable. The 'planted root' refers to something that is deeply rooted and secure, while the 'standing place of honor' refers to a position of respect and esteem. The verse may be emphasizing the importance of having a solid foundation and a strong presence, whether it be in one's personal life or in the community. It could also be a reminder that these things are not easily achieved and require effort, patience, and perseverance.
orig: وزروع ومقام كريم

translation: And they were ungrateful for the blessings we had given them.
interpretation: The verse refers to people who were ungrateful for the blessings and favors that God had bestowed upon them. The phrase 'they were ungrateful' (fākheen) implies that they failed to acknowledge and appreciate the blessings, and instead took them for granted. This verse serves as a reminder to be thankful for the blessings and gifts that one has, and not to take them for granted. It highlights the importance of recognizing and appreciating the good in one's life, and not to be ungrateful for it.
orig: ونعمة كانوا فيها فاكهين

translation: Thus do We inherit the towns (populations) that had wronged themselves. Indeed, in this is a sign for people who understand.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of communities that had wronged themselves and how God inherits the earth by destroying them and replacing them with new communities. The verse emphasizes the significance of this event as a sign for those who understand, indicating that it serves as a reminder and a warning for people to take heed and learn from the fate of those who had wronged themselves. The verse highlights the importance of understanding the message and the consequences of not adhering to the right path, as well as the inevitability of divine justice.
orig: كذلك وأورثناها قوما آخرين

translation: And the heaven and the earth did not weep for them, nor were they repentant.
interpretation: The verse describes the final state of a group of people who have been destroyed, emphasizing that they received no mercy or sympathy from the heavens and the earth, nor did they show any sign of repentance or remorse for their actions. The image of the heavens and the earth not weeping for them underscores the severity of their sins, and the lack of repentance highlights the finality of their fate. This verse serves as a reminder of the importance of repentance and seeking forgiveness, and the consequences of ignoring the signs of God's displeasure.
orig: فما بكت عليهم السماء والأرض وما كانوا منظرين

translation: And indeed, We rescued the Children of Israel from the painful punishment.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the rescue of the Children of Israel from a painful punishment. The verse highlights the power and mercy of God in saving His people from harm. This event is a significant moment in the history of the Israelites and is a reminder of God's protection and care for those who believe in Him.
orig: ولقد نجينا بني إسرائيل من العذاب المهين

translation: Pharoah, indeed he was exalted among the transgressors.
interpretation: The verse refers to Pharoah, who was a powerful and oppressive leader. The phrase 'exalted among the transgressors' highlights his status as a leader who was guilty of excessive wrongdoing. This verse may serve as a reminder of the dangers of power and pride, and the consequences of using that power to oppress others.
orig: من فرعون إنه كان عاليا من المسرفين

translation: And We had certainly chosen them over the worlds
interpretation: The verse speaks about the special status and privilege that was given to a particular group of people, whom God had chosen above all other nations or communities ('the worlds'). The phrase 'over the worlds' emphasizes the exclusive and superior nature of their selection. The verse implies that this selection was made with full knowledge and awareness on the part of God, as indicated by the phrase 'on knowledge' (علم). The interpretation of this verse can vary depending on the context, but it generally conveys the idea of God's favor and blessings towards a particular group of people, and the responsibility that comes with it.
orig: ولقد اخترناهم على علم على العالمين

translation: And We gave them clear signs in what was sent to them, but they turned away from it.
interpretation: The verse speaks about people who were given clear signs (ayat) or evidence from God, but they rejected and turned away from it. The verse highlights the rejection of truth by those who are stubborn and unwilling to accept it. It serves as a reminder that God's signs and revelations are clear and accessible, but it is up to the people to accept or reject them. The consequences of rejection are not specified in this verse, but it implies a missed opportunity for guidance and a continued state of ignorance or misguidance.
orig: وآتيناهم من الآيات ما فيه بلاء مبين

translation: Indeed, they say:
interpretation: The verse is a statement indicating that some people are making a certain claim or expressing a certain viewpoint. The specific content of what they are saying is not provided in the verse, but is left to be specified in the context. The verse could be used to introduce a quote or to highlight a particular attitude or belief held by a group of people. The verse serves to draw attention to the views of these individuals, and may be used to challenge or refute their claims in the following text.
orig: إن هؤلاء ليقولون

translation: Indeed, it is only our first death, and we are not being unreturned.
interpretation: The verse speaks about death and the afterlife. It suggests that death is not the end, but rather a transition to another stage of existence. The phrase 'our first death' implies that there will be more deaths or transitions to come. The second part of the verse, 'and we are not being unreturned', emphasizes the belief in the resurrection of the dead and the Day of Judgment. The verse serves as a reminder of the fleeting nature of life and the importance of preparing for the afterlife.
orig: إن هي إلا موتتنا الأولى وما نحن بمنشرين

translation: And bring to us our fathers if you are truthful.
interpretation: The verse is a challenge from the disbelievers to the prophet Muhammad (PBUH) and his followers, to bring their ancestors back to life if they are truthful in their claim that they are messengers of God. The verse is a display of the disbelievers' rejection and denial of the message of Islam and their refusal to accept the truth. It also highlights the miraculous nature of the prophet's message and the power of God, who is capable of bringing the dead back to life.
orig: فأتوا بآبائنا إن كنتم صادقين

translation: Are those better or the town which We destroyed of old? They were more unjust than these.
interpretation: The verse compares the people of the present time with the people of the past who were destroyed by God's punishment. The verse suggests that the people of the past were more unjust and sinful than the people of the present. The verse serves as a reminder that God's punishment is not limited to a certain time or place, and that the people of the present should take heed of the fate of the people of the past. The verse encourages the people to reflect on their actions and to strive for righteousness and justice.
orig: أهم خير أم قوم تبع والذين من قبلهم أهلكناهم إنهم كانوا مجرمين

translation: And We did not create the heavens and the earth and what is between them as a game.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes that the creation of the heavens, the earth, and everything in between (including all of existence) is not a trivial matter or a game. Rather, it is a serious and purposeful act of the divine creator. This verse can be interpreted as a reminder of the significance and value of all of creation, and a warning against frivolous or careless actions towards the world and its inhabitants. It can also be seen as a rebuke against those who deny the existence of a higher power, suggesting that the intricate complexity and order of the universe cannot be the result of mere chance or accident.
orig: وما خلقنا السماوات والأرض وما بينهما لاعبين

translation: We created them not except with truth, but most of them do not know.
interpretation: The verse affirms that all living beings were created with a purpose and a specific design (truth). However, most of them are unaware of this truth. This verse can be interpreted as a reminder that everything in the world has a purpose and a reason for its existence. The verse also highlights the limited human understanding and knowledge, and the fact that many people are unaware of the deeper truths and meanings of life.
orig: ما خلقناهما إلا بالحق ولكن أكثرهم لا يعلمون

translation: Indeed, the Day of Distinction is their appointed time, all of them.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the Day of Judgment, known as the Day of Distinction, which is the appointed time for all people. It emphasizes the inevitability of this day and the fact that it will come for all people, without exception. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of being prepared for this day and the need for individuals to consider their actions and repent for any wrongdoings before it is too late.
orig: إن يوم الفصل ميقاتهم أجمعين

translation: A day (when) a man will not avail (another) man in aught, nor will they (be able to) help themselves.
interpretation: The verse speaks about a day of judgement when no one will be able to help or save anyone else, including themselves. This day is described as a time when all worldly power and wealth will be of no use, and people will realize the futility of their earthly pursuits. The verse emphasizes the importance of preparing for the afterlife and seeking God's mercy and forgiveness, as it is the only means of salvation on that day.
orig: يوم لا يغني مولى عن مولى شيئا ولا هم ينصرون

translation: But except whom Allah has mercy on, indeed, He is the Exalted in Might, the Most Merciful.
interpretation: The verse affirms that only those who receive God's mercy will be saved. The verse emphasizes God's power and greatness, as well as His mercy. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of seeking God's mercy and the ultimate power and control that God holds over all of creation.
orig: إلا من رحم الله إنه هو العزيز الرحيم

translation: Indeed, the tree of Zaqqum
interpretation: The verse refers to the tree of Zaqqum, which is mentioned in the Qur'an as a symbol of punishment and suffering for those who reject faith and commit sins. The tree is described as producing fruit that is bitter and foul-smelling, and as being a source of torment for those who have to eat from it in the afterlife. The tree of Zaqqum serves as a warning to those who persist in their disbelief and wrongdoing, reminding them of the painful consequences of their actions and the reality of the afterlife.
orig: إن شجرت الزقوم

translation: Food of the sinner
interpretation:
The phrase 'food of the sinner' is not a direct quote from the Qur'an, but it is a common interpretation of the Arabic phrase "طعام الأثيم" (ta'am al-athim). This phrase is used in the Qur'an (Surah Al-A'raf, verse 157) in the context of describing the fate of the disbelievers on the Day of Judgment. The full verse is:

'But as for those who are given to selfish greed, they will be fire's fuel.'

In this context, the phrase "food of the sinner" is understood to refer to the punishment of the disbelievers, who will be consumed by the fire of Hell. This punishment is described as their 'food' because it is what they will be consumed by and sustained by in the Hereafter. The phrase serves as a warning to those who are heedless of the consequences of their actions and the fate that awaits them if they do not repent and turn to God.
orig: طعام الأثيم

translation: Like a parched pot that boils over.
interpretation: The verse uses the metaphor of a pot that is left on the fire and becomes so hot that it begins to boil over. The pot represents a person who has reached a breaking point due to their own sins and wrongdoings. The boiling over symbolizes the consequences of their actions and the uncontrollable nature of the situation. The verse serves as a warning to those who persist in their sins and wrongdoings, urging them to repent before it is too late.
orig: كالمهل يغلي في البطون

translation: None
interpretation: No interpretation
orig: كغلي الحميم

translation: Take it and carry it to the direction of Hell!
interpretation: The verse is a command to take or seize something and then carry it towards Hell. While the specific context of the verse is not provided, it can be interpreted as a metaphorical warning to those who commit sins or engage in unrighteous deeds. By ordering the person to carry the object towards Hell, the verse emphasizes the consequences of their actions and the risk of being associated with evil and damnation. It serves as a reminder of the importance of avoiding sin and striving towards righteousness.
orig: خذوه فاعتلوه إلى سواء الجحيم

translation: Then pour upon his head from the punishment of the boiling water.
interpretation: The verse describes the punishment of a wrongdoer, where boiling water will be poured upon his head. The verse can be interpreted as a metaphor for the severe consequences of one's actions and the intense suffering that can result from committing sins. This verse serves as a warning to those who engage in wrongdoing, reminding them of the severe punishment that awaits them if they do not repent and change their ways.
orig: ثم صبوا فوق رأسه من عذاب الحميم

translation: Taste! Indeed, you are the powerful, the generous.
interpretation: The verse is a form of address to someone who is described as powerful and generous. The command 'taste' is a metaphorical way of saying that the person will experience the consequences of their actions. The rest of the verse is a reminder of the person's position and status, highlighting the contrast between their power and generosity, and the consequences they are about to face. The interpretation of the verse depends on the context in which it appears, but it can be seen as a warning or a rebuke, urging the person to reflect on their actions and to consider the implications of their behavior.
orig: ذق إنك أنت العزيز الكريم

translation: Indeed, this is what you were eager for.
interpretation: The verse is a statement made by God, addressing a group of people who had been eagerly awaiting or wishing for a certain outcome or event. The verse confirms that what they had been seeking has now come to pass. The interpretation of this verse depends on the context in which it is used, but it generally conveys a sense of irony or sarcasm, as if to say 'you asked for it, now you have it'.
orig: إن هذا ما كنتم به تمترون

translation: Indeed, the righteous will be in a secure place.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the ultimate destination of the righteous people, who will be in a secure and safe place. This verse offers hope and reassurance to those who strive for righteousness and piety, promising them a peaceful and secure resting place. The verse can also be seen as a reminder for people to strive for righteousness and piety, so that they too can attain this secure place.
orig: إن المتقين في مقام أمين

translation: In gardens and rivers
interpretation: The phrase 'In gardens and rivers' is a description of the blessings and rewards that will be given to the righteous in the afterlife. It is a metaphor for the lush and abundant gardens of paradise, where rivers flow. It represents the ultimate bliss and happiness that is promised to those who live a righteous life and follow the teachings of Islam. The phrase serves as a source of hope and motivation for believers, reminding them of the ultimate goal and purpose of their existence.
orig: في جنات وعيون

translation: They will wear green garments of fine silk and heavy brocade, facing one another.
interpretation: The verse describes the scene of people wearing beautiful and luxurious green garments, made of fine silk and heavy brocade, facing each other. While the verse is not clear about the context or the identity of these people, it is often interpreted as a description of the people in heaven, wearing the finest and most beautiful clothes as a reward for their good deeds in this world. The image of people facing each other could symbolize the unity and harmony among them, or the joy of meeting and reuniting with loved ones in heaven. Overall, the verse conveys a sense of beauty, joy, and serenity, reflecting the blessings and rewards of heaven.
orig: يلبسون من سندس وإستبرق متقابلين

translation: And We have made for them wives from among the jinn.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the creation of wives for a group of people from the jinn. The verse is a reference to a specific story in Islamic tradition, where a group of jinn heard the recitation of the Quran and were so moved by it that they embraced Islam. As a reward for their faith, God created wives for them from among the jinn. The verse serves to emphasize the power of the Quran to touch the hearts of even the most unexpected of listeners and to bring them to the path of righteousness.
orig: كذلك وزوجناهم بحور عين

translation: They call therein with every kind of fruit, secure.
interpretation: The verse describes a place where all kinds of fruit are available, and the people who live there are safe and secure. The verse may be referring to the blessings and bounties of Paradise, where the believers will have access to every type of fruit and will live in peace and safety. The verse can be seen as a promise of God's rewards for the righteous and a source of comfort and hope for those who strive for righteousness.
orig: يدعون فيها بكل فاكهة آمنين

translation: They will not taste death therein except the first death, and We will save them from the punishment of the Blaze.
interpretation: The verse speaks about a group of people who will not experience any harm or death in a certain place, except for the natural death that all humans must face. Moreover, God will protect them from the punishment of hellfire. The verse can be interpreted as a promise of safety and security from harm and punishment for these people. It can also be seen as a reminder of the ultimate power and protection of God, who has the ability to save believers from any harm and danger.
orig: لا يذوقون فيها الموت إلا الموتة الأولى ووقاهم عذاب الجحيم

translation: That is from the grace of your Lord; that is the great success.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the grace and favor of God, which is the source of true success. The verse emphasizes that the greatest success is achieved through the grace of God, indicating that all human efforts and abilities are ultimately dependent on God's blessings and mercy. The verse serves as a reminder to be grateful for God's grace and to seek His help and guidance in all aspects of life.
orig: فضلا من ربك ذلك هو الفوز العظيم

translation: But We have made it easy in your language so that they may remember.
interpretation: The verse is speaking about the revelation of the Qur'an in the Arabic language. The ease with which the Qur'an was revealed in the Arabic language was a deliberate act by God, so that the people would be able to understand and reflect upon its message. The verse emphasizes the importance of reflection and remembrance of God's message, and the role of the Arabic language in facilitating this understanding.
orig: فإنما يسرناه بلسانك لعلهم يتذكرون

translation: So be patient, indeed they, [too,] are waiting.
interpretation: The verse is a reminder to the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) to be patient in the face of adversity and hostility from the disbelievers. The phrase 'they, [too,] are waiting' refers to the fact that the disbelievers are also waiting, either for the Prophet to falter or for a sign of weakness. The verse encourages the Prophet to remain steadfast and resolute, and to trust in God's plan. It also serves as a reminder to the believers to be patient and persevere in the face of hardship and difficulties, and to have faith that God's promise will ultimately be fulfilled.
orig: فارتقب إنهم مرتقبون

translation:
By the heaven and the starfalling,
By the moon when it follows,
By the day when it displays,
By the night when it covers,
By the sky and Him who built it,
By the earth and Him who spread it,
By Nafs and Him who proportioned it,
And inspired it (with knowledge of) what is wrong for it and (what is) right for it,
He is indeed successful who purifies it,
And he is indeed failed who corrupts it.
interpretation: The verse is a series of oaths, swearing by various elements of the universe (heaven, starfalling, moon, day, night, sky, earth, nafs) and their creator, emphasizing the importance of the message being conveyed. The message is a warning of the consequences of the actions of the self (nafs), specifically the importance of purifying it by following the right path and avoiding the wrong. The verse suggests that the ultimate success or failure of a person is determined by how they manage their self and its desires. It encourages people to strive for purifying their self and avoiding corruption.
orig: حم

translation: The revelation of the Book is from Allah, the Exalted in Power, the Wise.
interpretation: The verse affirms that the Qur'an is a revelation from Allah, who is the Exalted in Power and the Wise. This means that the Qur'an is not a human creation, but a divine guidance sent down by Allah through the Angel Gabriel to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). The attributes of Allah mentioned in the verse, the Exalted in Power and the Wise, emphasize the importance and significance of the Qur'an as a source of knowledge and guidance. It also highlights the power and wisdom of Allah, who has sent down the Qur'an for the guidance of humanity.
orig: تنزيل الكتاب من الله العزيز الحكيم

translation: Indeed, in the heavens and the earth are signs for the believers.
interpretation: The verse highlights the existence of signs or evidence of God's existence and power in the universe, which are intended for the believers to reflect upon and strengthen their faith. These signs can be found both in the heavens (cosmos, stars, planets etc.) and on earth (natural phenomena, living creatures, etc.). The verse encourages believers to observe and ponder over these signs, as they serve as a reminder of God's greatness and wisdom, and as a means of strengthening one's faith and relationship with God.
orig: إن في السماوات والأرض لآيات للمؤمنين

translation: And in your creation, and what He scattered (of creatures) therein, are signs for a people who are certain.
interpretation: The verse highlights the wonders of creation, both in the creation of human beings and in the variety of creatures that inhabit the earth. These wonders are described as signs, or evidence, of God's existence and power. The verse suggests that these signs are intended for those who are certain, or believers, who can understand and appreciate the deeper meaning and purpose of creation. The verse emphasizes the importance of recognizing and reflecting on these signs, as they serve as a means of guidance and understanding for those who seek the truth.
orig: وفي خلقكم وما يبث من دابة آيات لقوم يوقنون

translation: And the difference between the day and the night, and what Allah has sent down of provision from the sky, reviving therewith the earth after its death and the turning about of the winds, are signs for a people who reason.
interpretation: The verse highlights various natural phenomena such as the difference between day and night, the provision sent down from the sky, the revival of the earth after its death, and the turning about of the winds as signs from God. These signs are meant for a people who use their intellect and reason. The verse emphasizes the importance of observing and reflecting upon the natural world as a way to understand and appreciate the signs of God. It serves as a reminder that the natural world is not merely a random occurrence but a deliberate and purposeful creation by God, and that those who are able to reflect upon these signs will be able to understand and appreciate the greatness of the Creator.
orig: واختلاف الليل والنهار وما أنزل الله من السماء من رزق فأحيا به الأرض بعد موتها وتصريف الرياح آيات لقوم يعقلون

translation: These are the verses of Allah which We recite to you in truth. So by what exposition after Allah and His verses are they believers?
interpretation: The verse challenges the disbelievers to present any argument or evidence that is worthier of belief than the verses of Allah. It emphasizes the truthfulness of the verses of Allah and the futility of believing in any other argument or evidence. The verse is a call to the disbelievers to reflect on the truth of Islam and to abandon their disbelief. It also serves as a reminder to the believers of the importance of holding firm to the verses of Allah and not being swayed by false arguments and evidence.
orig: تلك آيات الله نتلوها عليك بالحق فبأي حديث بعد الله وآياته يؤمنون

translation: Woe to every slanderer, unjust.
interpretation: The verse is a condemnation of those who spread falsehoods and engage in unjust acts. The word 'woe' is a warning of impending doom or punishment. The verse serves as a reminder that those who engage in such actions will face severe consequences. It emphasizes the importance of truthfulness and justice, and the consequences of deviating from these principles.
orig: ويل لكل أفاك أثيم

translation: Indeed, he (the disbeliever) to whom the verses of Allah are recited, then he turns away from them in arrogance as if he has not heard them. So announce to him a painful punishment.
interpretation: The verse describes the attitude of a disbeliever who, after hearing the verses of the Qur'an being recited, turns away from them in arrogance and disregard, acting as if he has not heard them. The verse then warns of a painful punishment for such behavior. This verse highlights the importance of paying attention to and reflecting on the message of the Qur'an, and the consequences of rejecting it through arrogance and pride.
orig: يسمع آيات الله تتلى عليه ثم يصر مستكبرا كأن لم يسمعها فبشره بعذاب أليم

translation: And when We bestow upon man a mercy from Us and he associates therewith others for which he has no knowledge, then indeed, he is ungrateful
interpretation: The verse speaks about the ingratitude of people who, after receiving a blessing from God, associate others with Him in worship. These people do not have any knowledge about the ones they associate with God, yet they still commit shirk (associating partners with God), which is a grave sin in Islam. The verse serves as a reminder that associating others with God is a form of ingratitude for the blessings that He has bestowed upon us. It emphasizes the importance of being mindful of our actions and avoiding shirk, as it is a grave sin that will incur a severe punishment from God.
orig: وإذا علم من آياتنا شيئا اتخذها هزوا أولئك لهم عذاب مهين

translation: Behind them is Hell, and that which they have earned will not avail them at all, nor those (false deities) which they have taken as protectors besides Allah. For them is a great torment.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the fate of those who have earned Hell through their actions and have taken false deities as protectors instead of Allah. The verse emphasizes that their efforts and false protectors will not benefit them in any way. The verse serves as a warning to those who choose to reject Allah and worship false deities, reminding them of the severe punishment that awaits them in Hell.
orig: من ورائهم جهنم ولا يغني عنهم ما كسبوا شيئا ولا ما اتخذوا من دون الله أولياء ولهم عذاب عظيم

translation: This is the guidance. And those who disbelieve in the signs of their Lord, for them is a punishment of painful displacement.
interpretation: The verse distinguishes between those who follow the guidance (presumably referring to the guidance of Islam) and those who reject the signs of their Lord. The latter group is warned of a punishment that is both painful and severe, described as a 'displacement'. This punishment could refer to the physical displacement and upheaval that can result from divine retribution, or it could refer to a more metaphorical displacement from God's grace and mercy. Regardless of the exact nature of the punishment, the verse serves as a warning to those who reject the signs of God and refuse to follow the path of guidance.
orig: هذا هدى والذين كفروا بآيات ربهم لهم عذاب من رجز أليم

translation: It is Allah who has subjected the sea for you that the ships may sail through it by His command and that you may seek His bounty; and perhaps you will be grateful.
interpretation: The verse highlights the power and control of Allah over the sea and how He has made it subservient to the needs of humans. The sea is a means of transportation for ships and a source of provision for people. By subjecting the sea to human use, Allah is providing an opportunity for people to seek His blessings and to express their gratitude. The verse serves as a reminder of Allah's mercy and generosity towards humans and emphasizes the importance of expressing gratitude for the blessings received.
orig: الله الذي سخر لكم البحر لتجري الفلك فيه بأمره ولتبتغوا من فضله ولعلكم تشكرون

translation: And He has subjected to you whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, all from Him. Indeed in that are signs for a people who reflect.
interpretation: The verse highlights the power and mercy of God by stating that He has subjected all that is in the heavens and the earth to humans. This includes all of the resources and blessings that people have at their disposal. The verse emphasizes that these blessings are from God, and that they serve as signs or evidence of His existence and power for those who reflect or ponder upon them. The verse encourages people to be grateful for these blessings and to use them in a responsible and mindful way, recognizing that they come from God and are a test for humanity.
orig: وسخر لكم ما في السماوات وما في الأرض جميعا منه إن في ذلك لآيات لقوم يتفكرون

translation: Say to those who have believed, 'Forgive those who do not expect the days of God, so that He may give requital to a people for what they used to earn.'
interpretation: The verse addresses the believers and instructs them to forgive those who do not anticipate the days of God, meaning those who do not fear God's punishment or judgment. By forgiving these individuals, the believers are allowing God to repay them for their past actions. The verse emphasizes the importance of forgiveness and highlights the role of God in meting out justice and punishment.
orig: قل للذين آمنوا يغفروا للذين لا يرجون أيام الله ليجزي قوما بما كانوا يكسبون

translation: Whoever does righteousness, it is for their own soul. And whoever does evil, it is against their own soul. Then to your Lord you will be returned.
interpretation: The verse explains the concept of individual responsibility and accountability for one's actions. It emphasizes that each person is responsible for their own actions, and that the consequences of those actions affect the individual. Acts of righteousness bring positive consequences for the person, while evil actions bring negative consequences. Ultimately, all people will return to their Lord and be held accountable for their actions.
orig: من عمل صالحا فلنفسه ومن أساء فعليها ثم إلى ربكم ترجعون

translation: And We had already given the children of Israel the scripture, and wisdom, and the prophethood, and provided them with good things, and preferred them above the worlds.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the blessings that God bestowed upon the children of Israel, including the scripture (Torah), wisdom, prophethood, and provision of good things. The verse also highlights that the children of Israel were preferred above all other nations. This verse emphasizes the special relationship between God and the children of Israel and the privileges they have received. It also serves as a reminder of the responsibilities that come with these blessings, and the importance of using them for the betterment of society and the worship of God.
orig: ولقد آتينا بني إسرائيل الكتاب والحكم والنبوة ورزقناهم من الطيبات وفضلناهم على العالمين

translation: And We gave them clear signs in the matter, but they differed among themselves; indeed, your Lord will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection concerning that over which they used to differ.
interpretation: The verse speaks about a group of people who were given clear signs and evidence in a matter, but they still differed and disagreed among themselves. The verse emphasizes that despite having clear evidence, people can still choose to interpret and understand it differently. However, the verse also reminds that ultimately, their Lord will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection regarding the matter they differed in. The verse highlights the importance of seeking truth and understanding, and the reality that all matters will be ultimately judged by God.
orig: وآتيناهم بينات من الأمر فما اختلفوا إلا من بعد ما جاءهم العلم بغيا بينهم إن ربك يقضي بينهم يوم القيامة فيما كانوا فيه يختلفون

translation: Then We put you [Prophet Muhammad] on a straight path concerning the matter, so follow it and do not follow the desires of those who do not know.
interpretation: The verse addresses the Prophet Muhammad and gives him guidance on how to deal with the matter at hand. It instructs him to follow the straight path that has been revealed to him and not to be swayed by the desires of those who lack knowledge. The verse emphasizes the importance of adhering to the guidance and teachings of Islam and not being influenced by the whims of those who are ignorant of its principles. It serves as a reminder to the Prophet and to all Muslims to stay steadfast on the path of righteousness and not to be swayed by the desires and opinions of others.
orig: ثم جعلناك على شريعة من الأمر فاتبعها ولا تتبع أهواء الذين لا يعلمون

translation: Indeed, they will not avail you against Allah at all. Indeed, the wrongdoers are allies of one another, but Allah is the ally of the righteous.
interpretation: The verse contrasts the fate of the wrongdoers with that of the righteous. It emphasizes that the wrongdoers, who are allies of one another, will not be able to protect themselves from Allah's punishment. On the other hand, Allah is the ally of the righteous, providing them with support and protection. The verse serves as a reminder that one's actions have consequences, and that choosing the path of righteousness leads to a stronger and more secure alliance with Allah.
orig: إنهم لن يغنوا عنك من الله شيئا وإن الظالمين بعضهم أولياء بعض والله ولي المتقين

translation: This is a clear sign for the people and guidance and mercy for a people who believe.
interpretation: The verse speaks about a clear sign from God, which serves as a guidance and mercy for those who believe. The verse emphasizes the importance of faith and belief in understanding and making use of the signs of God. It suggests that only those who believe can truly benefit from the guidance and mercy that God offers. The verse can be seen as a message of hope for believers, promising them divine guidance and mercy, while also serving as a reminder of the importance of faith in accessing these blessings.
orig: هذا بصائر للناس وهدى ورحمة لقوم يوقنون

translation: Or do those who have done evil deeds think that We will make them equal to those who have believed and done righteous deeds, [just] as if they were the same in their life and death? Evil is that which they judge.
interpretation: The verse highlights the fundamental difference between those who do evil deeds and those who believe and do righteous deeds. The verse emphasizes that God will not treat them equally in their life and death, and that the judgement of those who think otherwise is severely misguided. The verse serves as a reminder that actions have consequences and that God will judge each person according to their deeds. The verse also warns against the danger of false equivalence and the importance of recognizing and upholding the distinction between right and wrong.
orig: أم حسب الذين اجترحوا السيئات أن نجعلهم كالذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات سواء محياهم ومماتهم ساء ما يحكمون

translation: And God created the heavens and the earth in truth, and so that every soul may be recompensed for what it has earned, and they will not be wronged.
interpretation: The verse affirms the creation of the heavens and the earth by God and emphasizes the principle of justice, in which every soul will be recompensed for its actions. The verse emphasizes that no one will be wronged or treated unjustly, and that the consequences of one's actions will be justly deserved. This verse can be seen as a source of comfort and reassurance, as it affirms that God's justice will ultimately prevail and that each person will receive what they deserve for their actions, whether good or bad.
orig: وخلق الله السماوات والأرض بالحق ولتجزى كل نفس بما كسبت وهم لا يظلمون

translation: Have you seen he who has taken his own desire as his god, and whom God has led astray knowingly, and has set a seal upon his hearing and his heart, and has put a cover over his sight? Who then can guide him after God? Will you not, then, take heed?
interpretation: The verse describes the fate of those who have chosen their own desires over God, and have been led astray as a result. The verse emphasizes the deliberate nature of God's actions, as He has knowingly led these people astray and has sealed their senses, preventing them from seeing the truth. The verse serves as a warning to those who may be following their own desires, reminding them of the dangers of straying from God's path. The verse also highlights the ultimate power of God, as it asks who can guide someone after God, implying that no one has the power to change the fate of those who have been led astray by God.
orig: أفرأيت من اتخذ إلهه هواه وأضله الله على علم وختم على سمعه وقلبه وجعل على بصره غشاوة فمن يهديه من بعد الله أفلا تذكرون

translation: And they say, 'What is there but our life in this world? We die and we live, and nothing but time destroys us.' They have no knowledge of that; they only conjecture.
interpretation: The verse describes the disbelievers' denial of the afterlife and their belief that death is merely a return to nonexistence. They argue that they live and die according to the natural order of things and that time is the only force that destroys them. However, the verse points out that they have no knowledge of this, and their beliefs are based only on conjecture. The verse serves as a rebuke to those who reject the existence of the afterlife and affirms the ultimate truth of the Day of Judgment.
orig: وقالوا ما هي إلا حياتنا الدنيا نموت ونحيا وما يهلكنا إلا الدهر وما لهم بذلك من علم إن هم إلا يظنون

translation: And when Our verses are recited to them clearly, those who disbelieve say, 'Bring us our fathers if you are truthful.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the response of the disbelievers when God's verses are recited to them. Instead of accepting the truth and acknowledging their wrongdoings, they ask for their fathers to be brought back as a sign of proof. This response reflects their denial and rejection of the truth. The verse highlights the stubbornness of the disbelievers and their unwillingness to accept the truth, even when it is presented to them clearly. It serves as a reminder that faith and belief cannot be inherited, and each person is responsible for their own actions and beliefs.
orig: وإذا تتلى عليهم آياتنا بينات ما كان حجتهم إلا أن قالوا ائتوا بآبائنا إن كنتم صادقين

translation: Say, 'Allah gives you life, then He causes you to die, then He will gather you to the Day of Resurrection. There is no doubt about it, but most of the people do not know.',
interpretation: The verse speaks about the power and control of Allah over the life and death of human beings. It emphasizes that Allah gives life, causes death, and will gather all people on the Day of Resurrection. The verse highlights the lack of knowledge and understanding of most people regarding the reality of life and death and the significance of the Day of Resurrection. It serves as a reminder of the ultimate truth and the transient nature of this worldly life, and the importance of being mindful of one's actions and accountability to Allah.
orig: قل الله يحييكم ثم يميتكم ثم يجمعكم إلى يوم القيامة لا ريب فيه ولكن أكثر الناس لا يعلمون

translation: To God belongs the kingdom of the heavens and the earth, and on the Day of Resurrection, the unsuccessful will lose.
interpretation: The verse asserts the sovereignty of God over the heavens and the earth, and emphasizes that on the Day of Judgment, those who are unsuccessful or unbelievers will lose. The verse highlights the ultimate power and authority of God and the transient nature of worldly achievements. It serves as a reminder of the importance of faith and righteousness, and the consequences of disbelief and wickedness on the Day of Judgment.
orig: ولله ملك السماوات والأرض ويوم تقوم الساعة يومئذ يخسر المبطلون

translation: And you see every nation kneeling, every nation will be called to its record (on the Day of Judgment). Today you will be recompensed for what you used to do.
interpretation: The verse describes the scene on the Day of Judgment, where every nation will be gathered and called to account for their actions. The people will be in a state of humility and submission, as they are made to kneel before God. The verse emphasizes the certainty of divine justice, as people will be recompensed for their deeds, whether good or bad. This is a reminder of the importance of leading a righteous life, and of the inevitability of the Day of Judgment.
orig: وترى كل أمة جاثية كل أمة تدعى إلى كتابها اليوم تجزون ما كنتم تعملون

translation: This is a Book that recites to you truthfully. Indeed, We were recording what you were doing.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the Qur'an as a book that recites the truth to people. It emphasizes that the actions of people are being recorded, implying that they will be held accountable for their deeds. The verse serves as a reminder of the power of the Qur'an as a source of truth and guidance, and of the importance of leading a righteous life, knowing that one's actions are being recorded and will be judged.
orig: هذا كتابنا ينطق عليكم بالحق إنا كنا نستنسخ ما كنتم تعملون

translation: But as for those who believe and do good deeds, He will admit them into His mercy. That is the clear victory.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the fate of those who have faith in God and do good deeds. They will be granted entry into God's mercy, which is described as the true and clear victory. The verse highlights the importance of faith and righteous actions, and the ultimate reward that awaits those who lead a virtuous life. It serves as a source of hope and motivation for believers, reminding them of the blessings that come with faith and good deeds.
orig: فأما الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات فيدخلهم ربهم في رحمته ذلك هو الفوز المبين

translation: But as for those who disbelieved, is it not true that when the verses were recited to them, they would not believe? And they would deny them, so they were arrogant and were a transgressing people.
interpretation: The verse addresses the disbelievers and their response to the verses (ayat) of the Quran being recited to them. Despite hearing the verses, they did not believe and instead denied them, showing arrogance and committing transgressions. The verse highlights the rejection of the truth by the disbelievers, and their arrogant and sinful nature. It serves as a reminder of the consequences of disbelief and the importance of accepting and submitting to the truth.
orig: وأما الذين كفروا أفلم تكن آياتي تتلى عليكم فاستكبرتم وكنتم قوما مجرمين

translation: And when it is said, 'Indeed, the promise of Allah is truth, and the Hour [i.e., the Day of Judgment] is coming without doubt,' you say, 'We do not know what is the Hour. We assume only assumption, and we are not certain.',
interpretation: The verse addresses the people who are skeptical about the coming of the Day of Judgment, despite the believers' certainty of its arrival. These people express their uncertainty and disbelief by saying that they do not know when it will happen, and that they can only make assumptions about it, indicating that they are not convinced of its reality. The verse serves as a reminder that the Day of Judgment is a certainty and that the disbelievers' rejection of it does not change this fact. It also highlights the importance of faith and trust in God's promises, as well as the consequences of disbelief and denial of the truth.
orig: وإذا قيل إن وعد الله حق والساعة لا ريب فيها قلتم ما ندري ما الساعة إن نظن إلا ظنا وما نحن بمستيقنين

translation: And the evil of what they did struck them, and they became overwhelmed with what they used to mock at.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the consequences of the evil deeds of certain people, who used to mock and scoff at the idea of divine retribution. The verse states that they were eventually struck by the very evil they had perpetrated, and they became overwhelmed by it. The verse serves as a reminder that no one can escape the consequences of their actions, and that those who mock and scoff at religious teachings will ultimately face the reality of their words. It is a warning against arrogance and a call for humility and reverence towards the divine.
orig: وبدا لهم سيئات ما عملوا وحاق بهم ما كانوا به يستهزئون

translation: And it will be said today: 'We forget you as you have forgotten the meeting of this day of yours, and your refuge is the Fire, and you have no helpers.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the Day of Judgment and the fate of those who denied and forgot it. On that day, they will be reminded of their rejection and forgetfulness of the meeting with their Lord. They will be told that their destination is the Fire and that they have no protectors or helpers. The verse emphasizes the reality of the Day of Judgment and the consequences of ignoring or denying it. It serves as a warning to those who neglect or underestimate the significance of this day and a reminder to be mindful of the ultimate fate of their souls.
orig: وقيل اليوم ننساكم كما نسيتم لقاء يومكم هذا ومأواكم النار وما لكم من ناصرين

translation: That is because you took the signs of Allah in jest, and worldly life deceived you.
interpretation: The verse explains the reason for the punishment of a certain group of people. They took the signs of Allah, meaning the revelations and the messages sent by Allah, as a joke and did not take them seriously. They were also deceived by the worldly life, meaning they were more concerned with their materialistic desires and pleasures than with the hereafter. The verse serves as a reminder that such an attitude will not be accepted by Allah and will result in punishment. It also emphasizes the importance of taking the signs of Allah seriously, understanding their meanings and acting upon them, and not being deceived by the materialistic aspects of this world.
orig: ذلكم بأنكم اتخذتم آيات الله هزوا وغرتكم الحياة الدنيا فاليوم لا يخرجون منها ولا هم يستعتبون

translation: To Allah belongs the praise, the Lord of the heavens and the Lord of the earth, the Lord of the worlds.
interpretation: The verse is a declaration of praise and gratitude to Allah, the one and only God. It emphasizes Allah's sovereignty over all of creation, including the heavens, the earth, and all the worlds. The verse serves as a reminder of Allah's greatness, power, and authority over all things and highlights His position as the only deity worthy of worship and praise.
orig: فلله الحمد رب السماوات ورب الأرض رب العالمين

translation: And unto Him belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth, and He is over all things competent.
interpretation: The verse affirms the power and authority of God over all things in the heavens and the earth. The phrase 'And unto Him belongs the dominion' emphasizes that God is the ultimate owner and ruler of all creation. The phrase 'He is over all things competent' highlights God's ability and competence to manage and control all aspects of the universe. This verse serves as a reminder of God's greatness and power, and encourages believers to have faith and trust in His abilities.
orig: وله الكبرياء في السماوات والأرض وهو العزيز الحكيم

translation: By the heaven and the night visitor.
interpretation: The verse is a form of oath, invoking the heavens and the night visitor (which could refer to the star or the angel of the night). The purpose of the oath is to emphasize the importance of the message that follows. The verse serves as an introduction to a revelation, preparing the listener or reader for the divine message that is about to be revealed. The interpretation of the exact message that follows this verse would depend on the context and the following verses, but the verse itself serves to create a sense of awe and reverence, emphasizing the significance of the revelation that is about to be revealed.
orig: حم

translation: The revelation of the Book is from Allah, the Exalted in Power, the Wise.
interpretation: The verse affirms that the Qur'an is a revelation from Allah, who is described as being 'Exalted in Power' and 'Wise'. This description of Allah highlights his supreme authority and his perfect wisdom, emphasizing the divine origin of the Qur'an and the perfection of its teachings. The verse serves as a reminder of the divine source of the Qur'an and its ultimate authority, inviting the reader to submit to its teachings and to seek guidance from its wisdom.
orig: تنزيل الكتاب من الله العزيز الحكيم

translation: We created not the heavens and the earth and all that is between them in play, We created them not except with truth, but most of them know not. And surely, the Day of Decision is their appointed time, and that is a day of distress for the unbelievers.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the purposefulness and truth in the creation of the heavens, the earth, and all that lies between them. It highlights the fact that many people do not understand or appreciate the significance of this creation. The verse also introduces the concept of the 'Day of Decision', which is a specific and inevitable time of reckoning for all people. This day will be a time of distress for unbelievers, indicating that the consequences of their disbelief and rejection of truth will be severe.
orig: ما خلقنا السماوات والأرض وما بينهما إلا بالحق وأجل مسمى والذين كفروا عما أنذروا معرضون

translation: Say, 'Do you see what you invoke besides Allah? Show me what they have created of the earth; or have they a share in the heavens?' Or bring me a book before this or a remnant of knowledge, if you are truthful.'
interpretation: The verse is a challenge to the polytheists and disbelievers to prove the power and existence of the deities they worship besides Allah. The verse asks them to show any creation of their deities on earth or any share they have in the heavens. The verse also challenges them to bring a book or a remnant of knowledge that supports their belief, if they are truthful. The verse emphasizes the uniqueness and power of Allah, and the futility of worshiping false deities. It calls the disbelievers to reflect and consider the true nature of their beliefs and the consequences of their actions.
orig: قل أرأيتم ما تدعون من دون الله أروني ماذا خلقوا من الأرض أم لهم شرك في السماوات ائتوني بكتاب من قبل هذا أو أثارة من علم إن كنتم صادقين

translation: And who is more astray than one who calls upon another god besides Allah, who will not respond to him until the Day of Resurrection, and they, of their call, are unaware.
interpretation: The verse highlights the futility of worshipping false gods and the dire consequences of such actions. It emphasizes that these false gods will not respond to the calls of their worshippers until the Day of Judgment, and even then, it will be too late. The verse serves as a warning to those who choose to worship anything other than the one true God, Allah, and reminds them that their worship is in vain and that they are unaware of the consequences of their actions.
orig: ومن أضل ممن يدعو من دون الله من لا يستجيب له إلى يوم القيامة وهم عن دعائهم غافلون

translation: And when the people are gathered, they will be enemies to one another, and they will be deniers of their worship.
interpretation: The verse describes the Day of Judgment, when people will be resurrected and gathered together. On this day, they will become enemies to one another, despite having been allies or companions in this world. Moreover, they will deny and disown the very objects of their worship, whether they be idols, other deities, or even their own deeds and accomplishments. This verse emphasizes the transient nature of worldly relationships and the ultimate insignificance of earthly pursuits in the face of divine judgment.
orig: وإذا حشر الناس كانوا لهم أعداء وكانوا بعبادتهم كافرين

translation: And when Our verses are recited to them clearly, those who disbelieve say of the truth when it comes to them, 'This is clear magic.'
interpretation: The verse describes the response of the disbelievers when they hear the clear and evident signs (verses) of God. Instead of accepting the truth and submitting to God, they reject it and label it as 'clear magic'. This shows their denial and rejection of the truth, and their unwillingness to accept anything that contradicts their beliefs and desires. The verse serves as a warning to those who reject the signs of God and a reminder that their denial and rejection will not change the truth.
orig: وإذا تتلى عليهم آياتنا بينات قال الذين كفروا للحق لما جاءهم هذا سحر مبين

translation: Or do they say, 'He has fabricated it?' Say, 'Then bring ten forged chapters like it, and call upon whomever you can besides Allah, if you are truthful.',
interpretation: The verse challenges the disbelievers who accused Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) of fabricating the Qur'an. The challenge is to produce ten similar chapters if they believe that the Qur'an is not from God. The verse also asks them to seek help from whoever they can besides Allah, if they are truthful in their accusation. The verse emphasizes the inability of humans to produce anything comparable to the Qur'an, and the futility of seeking help from anyone other than Allah. The verse serves as a reminder of the divine origin of the Qur'an and the powerlessness of those who deny it.
orig: أم يقولون افتراه قل إن افتريته فلا تملكون لي من الله شيئا هو أعلم بما تفيضون فيه كفى به شهيدا بيني وبينكم وهو الغفور الرحيم

translation: Say, 'I am not a new thing among the messengers, nor do I know what will be done with me or with you. I only follow what is revealed to me, and I am not but a clear warner.'
interpretation: The verse is spoken from the perspective of a prophet or messenger of God, who is denying any unique or extraordinary status among the other prophets. The prophet emphasizes their lack of knowledge about the outcome of their mission and the fate of the people they are warning. The prophet is only following the revelation they have received and sees themselves as a clear and distinct warner, conveying the message of God to the people. The verse highlights the humility and obedience of the prophet, who is not acting on their own accord but rather fulfilling their divinely appointed role.
orig: قل ما كنت بدعا من الرسل وما أدري ما يفعل بي ولا بكم إن أتبع إلا ما يوحى إلي وما أنا إلا نذير مبين

translation: Say, 'Have you considered if it is from Allah and you disbelieved in it while a witness from the children of Israel has testified to something similar and you were arrogant?' Indeed, Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people.
interpretation: The verse is a challenge to the disbelievers to consider the consequences if the message brought by the prophet is indeed from Allah, and yet they reject it. The verse mentions a witness from the children of Israel who has testified to something similar, indicating that the message is consistent with previous revelations. Despite this, the disbelievers remained arrogant and rejected the message. The verse concludes by emphasizing that Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people, highlighting the importance of heeding the message and avoiding arrogance and disbelief.
orig: قل أرأيتم إن كان من عند الله وكفرتم به وشهد شاهد من بني إسرائيل على مثله فآمن واستكبرتم إن الله لا يهدي القوم الظالمين

translation: And those who disbelieved say to those who believed, 'If it had been good, we would have preceded you to it.' So now they are the ones who deny it, and they will soon know.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the disbelievers rejecting the faith of the believers and claiming that if the guidance and blessings they received were good, they would have preceded the believers to it. However, the verse points out that they did not understand or follow the guidance, and now they deny it. The verse implies that the disbelievers will soon realize their mistake and the consequences of their denial, indicating that they will eventually come to understand the true value of the guidance and blessings that they rejected.
orig: وقال الذين كفروا للذين آمنوا لو كان خيرا ما سبقونا إليه وإذ لم يهتدوا به فسيقولون هذا إفك قديم

translation: And before it was the Book of Moses, an example and a mercy, and this is a Book confirming in the Arabic language, to warn those who do wrong, and good news for the doers of good.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the Qur'an being a continuation and confirmation of the teachings of the Torah, brought by Moses, and being a guide and mercy for the people. The verse highlights that the Qur'an is in the Arabic language to make it accessible to the people of that time. The verse serves as a warning to those who commit wrong, that the Qur'an is a reminder of the consequences of their actions. On the other hand, it brings good news for those who do good, emphasizing the reward for their good deeds.
orig: ومن قبله كتاب موسى إماما ورحمة وهذا كتاب مصدق لسانا عربيا لينذر الذين ظلموا وبشرى للمحسنين

translation: Indeed, those who have said, 'Our Lord is Allah' and then remained upright - there will be no fear concerning them, nor will they grieve.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the promise of protection and peace for those who have declared their faith in Allah and have remained steadfast in their belief. These individuals have nothing to fear and will not experience sorrow. The verse serves as a reassurance for the believers, emphasizing the importance of maintaining a strong faith and commitment to Allah in the face of adversity. It highlights the rewards of staying true to one's faith and the tranquility that comes with it.
orig: إن الذين قالوا ربنا الله ثم استقاموا فلا خوف عليهم ولا هم يحزنون

translation: Those are the people of Paradise, abiding therein eternally as a reward for what they used to do.
interpretation: The verse describes the people who will enter Paradise and live there eternally as a reward for their good deeds. The verse emphasizes the eternal nature of their reward, highlighting the justice of God in giving them what they deserve based on their actions. The verse serves as a motivation for believers to do good deeds and strive for Paradise, reminding them that their actions in this life will determine their fate in the hereafter.
orig: أولئك أصحاب الجنة خالدين فيها جزاء بما كانوا يعملون

translation: And We have enjoined upon man [care] for his parents. His mother carried him, [increasing her] in weakness upon weakness, and his weaning is in two years. Be grateful to Me and to your parents; to Me is the [final] destination. But if they endeavor to make you associate with Me that of which you have no knowledge, do not obey them but accompany them in [this] world with appropriate kindness and follow the way of those who turn back to Me [in repentance]. Then to Me will be your return, and I will inform you about what you used to do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of showing gratitude and respect to one's parents, particularly the mother who carries and nourishes the child for an extended period of time. The verse highlights the mother's sacrifice and the child's dependence on her. At the same time, the verse warns against following parental guidance that contradicts Islamic teachings. The verse encourages believers to be kind and respectful to their parents, even if they do not share the same faith or beliefs. Ultimately, the verse reminds believers that they will be held accountable for their actions and will return to God, who will judge them based on their deeds.
orig: ووصينا الإنسان بوالديه إحسانا حملته أمه كرها ووضعته كرها وحمله وفصاله ثلاثون شهرا حتى إذا بلغ أشده وبلغ أربعين سنة قال رب أوزعني أن أشكر نعمتك التي أنعمت علي وعلى والدي وأن أعمل صالحا ترضاه وأصلح لي في ذريتي إني تبت إليك وإني من المسلمين

translation: Those are the ones upon whom We have bestowed favor, and of them are those who have attained their goals. And of the companions of the right hand - [it is] a promise in truth which they will not be denied.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the believers who have been given blessings by God and have achieved success in their lives. These individuals will be among the companions of the right hand, which is a promise of paradise that will be fulfilled and not denied to them. The verse highlights the blessings and rewards that will be given to the believers in the afterlife, in contrast to the punishment that was described in the previous verse. It serves as a reminder of the ultimate destination of the believers and the blessings that await them in the afterlife.
orig: أولئك الذين نتقبل عنهم أحسن ما عملوا ونتجاوز عن سيئاتهم في أصحاب الجنة وعد الصدق الذي كانوا يوعدون

translation: And who says to his parents, 'Why do you demand that I worship Allah?' And [they reply], 'We have made him experience beauty and prior generations have experienced it.' And he says, 'What, then, is my reward for that?' [They reply], 'Perhaps Allah will be pleased with you and perhaps you will attain forgiveness.' So he says, 'And how can I worship one whom I do not see?' [They reply], 'Have you considered Al-Lat and Al-'Uzza?' And he says, 'And what are Al-Lat and Al-'Uzza?' [They reply], 'They are two idols; rather, we worship them along with some of the stars.' He said, 'What, then, is the retribution of those who do that?' [They reply], 'A painful punishment.' So he said, 'What, then, do you think about the one who created the earth in two days and attributed to Him equals so that He became equal to four?' [They reply], 'We have not heard of this in the latest story nor in the first.' Then he said, 'Are those who know equal to those who do not know?' [They reply], 'And how have you come to this conclusion?' [He replied], 'Rather, I have come to this conclusion by the signs and by the fact that I am guided.' So they said, 'If you should worship other than Allah, you have certainly gone far astray.'
interpretation: The verse describes a conversation between an individual and his parents about the worship of Allah.
