The individual questions why he should worship Allah, and his parents explain that they have made him experience beauty and that previous generations have also experienced it. They further explain that worshiping Allah may result in His pleasure and forgiveness. The individual then asks how he can worship someone he cannot see, and the parents mention the idols Al-Lat and Al-'Uzza. The individual questions the retribution for those who worship these idols, and the parents reply that it will be a painful punishment. The conversation continues with the individual expressing his disbelief in the idea of creating the earth in two days and attributing equals to Him, leading to the parents' admission that they have not heard of this in the latest or first story. The individual then asks if those who know are equal to those who do not know, and the parents question how he has come to this conclusion. The individual responds that he has come to this conclusion by the signs and by being guided. The parents then warn that if he should worship other than Allah, he has certainly gone far astray. The verse highlights the importance of worshiping Allah and the consequences of worshiping false idols. It also emphasizes the importance of seeking knowledge, being guided, and understanding the signs of Allah.
orig: والذي قال لوالديه أف لكما أتعدانني أن أخرج وقد خلت القرون من قبلي وهما يستغيثان الله ويلك آمن إن وعد الله حق فيقول ما هذا إلا أساطير الأولين

translation: Those are they for whom the word has come true among the previous generations of jinn and men. Indeed they were losers.
interpretation: The verse refers to a group of people who have faced the consequences of their actions, similar to previous generations of jinn and humans who were destroyed for their sins. The phrase 'for whom the word has come true' implies that these people have experienced the fulfillment of a divine decree or warning. The verse concludes by stating that they were indeed losers, emphasizing the negative outcome of their actions and the futility of their disbelief and disobedience.
orig: أولئك الذين حق عليهم القول في أمم قد خلت من قبلهم من الجن والإنس إنهم كانوا خاسرين

translation: But for every (person) there is a rank according to what he has done, and He (God) recompenses them for their actions, and they will not be wronged.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the principle of individual accountability and justice in the afterlife. Each person will be given a rank or position based on their actions and deeds in this life. God will recompense them fairly for what they have done, and no one will be wronged or treated unjustly. This verse serves as a reminder of the importance of good deeds and righteous actions, as they will determine a person's standing in the hereafter. It also provides reassurance that God's justice will ultimately prevail and that everyone will receive their due rewards or punishments.
orig: ولكل درجات مما عملوا وليوفيهم أعمالهم وهم لا يظلمون

translation: And on the Day when the disbelievers will be presented to the Fire,
interpretation: No interpretation
orig: ويوم يعرض الذين كفروا على النار أذهبتم طيباتكم في حياتكم الدنيا واستمتعتم بها فاليوم تجزون عذاب الهون بما كنتم تستكبرون في الأرض بغير الحق وبما كنتم تفسقون

translation: And remember the brother of 'Ad, when he warned his people in the sand dunes, and the warner had passed among them before and after him, 'Worship none but Allah. Indeed, I fear for you the punishment of a tremendous day.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the brother of 'Ad, a prophet who warned his people in the sand dunes (a reference to the valley of al-Ahqaf) to worship only Allah and avoid the punishment of a tremendous day. The verse highlights the persistence of the prophet in delivering the message of Allah, as he had warned his people before and after the passage of the warner. The message of the verse is a call to worship Allah and avoid the punishment of the Day of Judgment. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of heeding the warnings of the prophets and avoiding the consequences of ignoring their message.
orig: واذكر أخا عاد إذ أنذر قومه بالأحقاف وقد خلت النذر من بين يديه ومن خلفه ألا تعبدوا إلا الله إني أخاف عليكم عذاب يوم عظيم

translation: They said, 'You have come to us only to bewitch us away from our gods! So bring us what you have promised us, if you are of the truthful.'
interpretation: The verse describes the disbelievers' response to the prophet's message. They accused him of coming to them only to lead them away from their gods, and they demanded that he bring about what he had promised them. The verse highlights the disbelievers' rejection of the prophet's message and their refusal to believe in him, despite his truthfulness. It also emphasizes their attachment to their false gods and their unwillingness to abandon them. The verse serves as a reminder of the challenges faced by the prophets and the difficulties they encountered in spreading the message of God.
orig: قالوا أجئتنا لتأفكنا عن آلهتنا فأتنا بما تعدنا إن كنت من الصادقين

translation: He said, 'Knowledge is only with Allah, and I convey to you what I have been sent with, but you do not comprehend.'
interpretation: The verse is a statement made by a prophet or a messenger of God, emphasizing the ultimate source of all knowledge, which is God. The speaker acknowledges that they have been sent by God to convey a message or a revelation, but at the same time, they express their frustration or disappointment towards the people who refuse to understand or comprehend the message. The verse suggests a sense of powerlessness on the part of the speaker, who is unable to make the people understand or accept the message, despite their best efforts. The verse may serve as a reminder that true understanding and knowledge can only come from God, and that humans must humble themselves and be open to receiving divine guidance in order to gain a deeper understanding of the world and their place in it.
orig: قال إنما العلم عند الله وأبلغكم ما أرسلت به ولكني أراكم قوما تجهلون

translation: So when they saw it as a cloud coming towards their valley, they said, 'This is a cloud bringing us rain!' Rather, it is what you were asking to be hastened: a punishment harsh and grievous.
interpretation: The verse describes the people's reaction when they see a cloud approaching their valley, mistaking it for a rain-bringing cloud. However, the cloud brings a harsh and grievous punishment instead. The verse serves as a warning to those who are heedless of the consequences of their actions and disregard the signs of God. The punishment is described as something that the people had hastened towards, indicating that it is a result of their own actions and that they have no one but themselves to blame for it.
orig: فلما رأوه عارضا مستقبل أوديتهم قالوا هذا عارض ممطرنا بل هو ما استعجلتم به ريح فيها عذاب أليم

translation: Everything is being destroyed by the command of its Lord, so when they awoke, they saw nothing but (the remains of) their homes. Thus do We recompense the criminal peoples.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of all things by the command of their Lord, emphasizing the power and authority of God. The verse highlights the sudden and complete nature of the destruction, as the people saw nothing but the remains of their homes when they awoke. The verse serves as a reminder of the transience of worldly possessions and the ultimate power of God. The punishment of the 'criminal peoples' serves as a warning to those who engage in unjust and criminal acts, emphasizing the certainty of divine retribution.
orig: تدمر كل شيء بأمر ربها فأصبحوا لا يرى إلا مساكنهم كذلك نجزي القوم المجرمين

translation: And We had certainly given them that which We have given you, and We had made for them fingers of hands among the trees, and We made for them rivers to flow beneath them. So will they not believe? And We destroyed towns around them. Then is there anyone who will remember? And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about God's provision for previous nations and the blessings He bestowed upon them, similar to what He has given to the current generation. Despite these blessings, the previous nations disbelieved in God's signs and rejected His message. The verse highlights the consequences of their actions, as God destroyed the towns around them. The verse serves as a reminder for the current generation, urging them to reflect and learn from the fate of the previous nations. The verse once again emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of God's punishment, which came in the morning or at noon, leaving no time for the people to repent or prepare for it.
orig: ولقد مكناهم فيما إن مكناكم فيه وجعلنا لهم سمعا وأبصارا وأفئدة فما أغنى عنهم سمعهم ولا أبصارهم ولا أفئدتهم من شيء إذ كانوا يجحدون بآيات الله وحاق بهم ما كانوا به يستهزئون

translation: And We have certainly destroyed (many) towns around you and diversified the signs/verses, perhaps they might return (to the right path).
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were close to the people to whom the Qur'an was being revealed. The destruction of these towns was a consequence of their disbelief and rejection of the signs and verses of God. The verse highlights the diversity of the signs and verses that were sent to the people, indicating that God gave them many opportunities and chances to reflect, repent and return to the right path. However, despite these efforts, the people did not return to the right path. The verse serves as a reminder of the consequences of disbelief and rejection of God's signs and verses, and emphasizes the importance of reflecting, repenting and returning to the right path.
orig: ولقد أهلكنا ما حولكم من القرى وصرفنا الآيات لعلهم يرجعون

translation: Had it not been for God's supporting those who were unjust to themselves, they would have arrived at destruction. But they found no one to help them. Such is the reach of their falsehoods and lies. And they were not able to create.
interpretation: The verse highlights the role of God in protecting and supporting those who have wronged themselves, preventing them from reaching their inevitable destruction. Despite their falsehoods and lies, they were unable to create or achieve anything of value. The verse serves as a reminder of the consequences of self-destructive behavior and the ultimate power of God over all things.
orig: فلولا نصرهم الذين اتخذوا من دون الله قربانا آلهة بل ضلوا عنهم وذلك إفكهم وما كانوا يفترون

translation: And when We directed a group of jinn to you, listening to the Qur'an, when they came to it, they said, 'Be quiet.' And when it was finished, they returned to their people as warners.
interpretation: The verse describes a moment when a group of jinn were directed by God to listen to the Qur'an when it was being recited. When they arrived and heard the recitation, they instructed those present to be quiet so they could listen carefully. After the recitation was finished, they returned to their own people as warners, bringing the message of the Qur'an to their community. The verse highlights the significance of the Qur'an and its power to reach and impact even the jinn, emphasizing the importance of attentive and respectful listening to the sacred text.
orig: وإذ صرفنا إليك نفرا من الجن يستمعون القرآن فلما حضروه قالوا أنصتوا فلما قضي ولوا إلى قومهم منذرين

translation: They said, 'O our people, indeed we have heard a Book revealed after Moses, confirming what was before it, guiding to the truth and to a straight path.'
interpretation: The verse describes a group of people who have heard and acknowledged the revelation of a new scripture that confirms and builds upon the teachings of the previous scripture, Moses. They recognize that this new revelation guides them to the truth and to a straight path. This verse highlights the continuity of God's message and the importance of recognizing and following the guidance that has been revealed through His prophets.
orig: قالوا يا قومنا إنا سمعنا كتابا أنزل من بعد موسى مصدقا لما بين يديه يهدي إلى الحق وإلى طريق مستقيم

translation: O our people, respond to the caller of Allah and believe in Him; He will forgive for you your sins and will protect you from a painful punishment.
interpretation: The verse addresses the listeners, urging them to respond to the call of Allah and to believe in Him. By doing so, they will be forgiven for their sins and protected from a painful punishment. The verse emphasizes the importance of responding to the call of Allah and the benefits of believing in Him, including forgiveness and protection from punishment. The verse also highlights the power of Allah to forgive sins and protect from punishment, and the importance of faith in achieving these benefits.
orig: يا قومنا أجيبوا داعي الله وآمنوا به يغفر لكم من ذنوبكم ويجركم من عذاب أليم

translation: And who is more unjust than he who is reminded of the verses of his Lord, then turns away from them? Rather, forgets what his hands have put forth. So We have placed over their hearts veils lest they understand it, and in their ears deafness. And if you invite them to guidance, they will never be guided, ever.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the unjust behavior of those who, after being reminded of the verses of their Lord, turn away from them and forget their own actions. The verse emphasizes the severe consequences of such behavior, as God has placed veils over their hearts and deafness in their ears, preventing them from understanding and accepting guidance. The verse stresses the futility of inviting such people to guidance, as they are doomed to be lost and misguided.
orig: ومن لا يجب داعي الله فليس بمعجز في الأرض وليس له من دونه أولياء أولئك في ضلال مبين

translation: Have they not seen that Allah, who created the heavens and the earth and was not fatigued by their creation, is able to give life to the dead? Yes, indeed; He is capable of all things.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the power and ability of Allah, the creator of the heavens and the earth. It highlights the fact that Allah was not fatigued by the creation of the universe, implying His limitless power and ability. The verse then goes on to state that Allah is able to give life to the dead, which serves as a reminder of His power over life and death. The verse concludes by reaffirming Allah's ability to do all things, emphasizing His sovereignty and omnipotence.
orig: أولم يروا أن الله الذي خلق السماوات والأرض ولم يعي بخلقهن بقادر على أن يحيي الموتى بلى إنه على كل شيء قدير

translation: And on the Day when the unbelievers will be exposed to the Fire (it will be said): 'Is this not the truth?' They will say: 'Yes, by our Lord!' He will say: 'Taste then the chastisement, for that you were denying.'
interpretation: The verse describes the Day of Judgment when unbelievers will be presented with the Fire (Hell) and will be asked if the Fire is not the truth. They will acknowledge that it is the truth, but it will be too late for them. God will then command them to taste the punishment for their denial and disbelief. The verse emphasizes the reality of the Hereafter and the consequences of disbelief. It also highlights the futility of denying the truth, as it will ultimately be proven on the Day of Judgment.
orig: ويوم يعرض الذين كفروا على النار أليس هذا بالحق قالوا بلى وربنا قال فذوقوا العذاب بما كنتم تكفرون

translation: So be patient, as were the steadfast messengers of strength, and do not seek to hasten for them. And how (was it) that they who were given the scripture did not (immediately) prosper? Rather, they were seized by the pang of death after (a delay of) an hour of the day, so do not doubt that the disbelievers will be struck (by punishment).
interpretation: The verse speaks about the importance of patience and perseverance in the face of adversity, using the example of the steadfast messengers. It also warns against seeking immediate results or rushing things, emphasizing that the righteous and those given the scripture (i.e. the Jews and Christians) did not immediately prosper. The verse then describes the sudden and unexpected punishment that came upon them, striking them after a delay of only an hour of the day. This serves as a reminder that the disbelievers will also be punished, and that one should not doubt the certainty of this punishment.
orig: فاصبر كما صبر أولو العزم من الرسل ولا تستعجل لهم كأنهم يوم يرون ما يوعدون لم يلبثوا إلا ساعة من نهار بلاغ فهل يهلك إلا القوم الفاسقون

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve and avert [people] from the way of Allah have gone far astray.
interpretation: The verse highlights the negative consequences of disbelief and actively preventing others from following the path of God. Those who reject faith and obstruct others from the way of Allah have strayed far from the right path. The verse serves as a warning to those who deny the truth and actively hinder others from the path of God, emphasizing the severity of their actions and the negative impact it has on their lives.
orig: الذين كفروا وصدوا عن سبيل الله أضل أعمالهم

translation: And those who believe and do righteous deeds and believe in what has been sent down upon Muhammad - and it is the truth from their Lord - He will remove from them their misdeeds and improve their condition.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the rewards for those who believe in the message sent down upon the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) and do good deeds. The verse highlights the significance of faith and righteous deeds, emphasizing that those who possess both will have their sins forgiven and their condition improved by God. The verse serves as a source of hope and motivation for believers, reminding them that their efforts towards righteousness and faith will not go unnoticed, and that God will reward them for their efforts.
orig: والذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات وآمنوا بما نزل على محمد وهو الحق من ربهم كفر عنهم سيئاتهم وأصلح بالهم

translation: That is because those who disbelieved have followed falsehood, while those who believed have followed the truth from their Lord. Thus does Allah present to the people their examples.
interpretation: The verse explains the reason for the differences between people in their beliefs and actions. Those who disbelieve follow falsehood and error, while those who believe follow the truth and guidance from their Lord. The verse highlights the consequences of following either falsehood or truth, and how these choices shape the destiny of individuals. The verse also emphasizes that God presents examples to people through these contrasting paths, so that they may reflect and make informed choices. It serves as a reminder of the significance of choosing the right path and following the truth.
orig: ذلك بأن الذين كفروا اتبعوا الباطل وأن الذين آمنوا اتبعوا الحق من ربهم كذلك يضرب الله للناس أمثالهم

translation: So when you meet those who disbelieve [in battle], strike [their] necks until, when you have inflicted slaughter upon them, then secure [their] bonds. And afterward either [as a] grace or ransom until the war lays down its burdens. That [is the command]. And if Allah had willed, He could have taken vengeance upon them [Himself], but [He ordered armed struggle] to test some of you by means of others. And those who are killed in the way of Allah - never will He waste their deeds.
interpretation: The verse gives instructions for the treatment of disbelievers in battle. It commands the believers to strike the necks of the disbelievers until they are defeated and then secure their bonds. After that, they may either show them grace or take them as ransom until the war ends. The verse emphasizes that the decision to fight the disbelievers is a test from God, and that it is only by His will that the believers are victorious. The verse also mentions that those who are killed in the way of God will not have their deeds wasted, indicating the great reward that awaits them in the afterlife.
orig: فإذا لقيتم الذين كفروا فضرب الرقاب حتى إذا أثخنتموهم فشدوا الوثاق فإما منا بعد وإما فداء حتى تضع الحرب أوزارها ذلك ولو يشاء الله لانتصر منهم ولكن ليبلو بعضكم ببعض والذين قتلوا في سبيل الله فلن يضل أعمالهم

translation: He will guide them and improve their condition.
interpretation: The verse speaks about God's guidance and improvement of the condition of certain people. The verse emphasizes God's role in guiding and improving the condition of people. The verse serves as a reminder that God is always there to help and support those who seek His guidance and are open to improvement. It also highlights the idea that through God's guidance and help, people can improve their condition and situation.
orig: سيهديهم ويصلح بالهم

translation: And He will admit them to Gardens beneath which rivers flow, wherein they will abide forever.
interpretation: The verse speaks about God admitting people into Paradise, which is described as gardens beneath which rivers flow, where the people will live forever. The verse offers a promise of eternal bliss and happiness to those who are worthy of it. It is a reward for the righteous and a motivation for them to continue on the path of righteousness.
orig: ويدخلهم الجنة عرفها لهم

translation: O you who believe! If you help (in the cause of) Allah, He will help you and make your foothold firm.
interpretation: The verse is a promise from God to those who believe and support His cause. It assures them that if they help God, He will help them in return and make their footsteps firm. This means that God will give them strength and stability, and will support them in their endeavors. The verse encourages believers to take an active role in supporting God's cause and to have faith that God will be with them every step of the way, providing them with the help and support they need to succeed.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا إن تنصروا الله ينصركم ويثبت أقدامكم

translation: And those who disbelieved, may misfortune be upon them, and misguided is their deeds.
interpretation: The verse is a curse upon those who disbelieve in God and His message. The phrase 'may misfortune be upon them' implies a negative outcome for the disbelievers, while 'misguided is their deeds' indicates that their actions are not being guided by God and are therefore misguided and unlikely to bring them success or happiness. The verse serves as a warning to those who reject God's message and emphasizes the negative consequences of disbelief.
orig: والذين كفروا فتعسا لهم وأضل أعمالهم

translation: That is because they hated what Allah has sent down, so He has made their deeds fruitless.
interpretation: The verse explains that the reason for the nullification of the deeds of certain people is their rejection and hatred towards what has been sent down by Allah, referring to the guidance and teachings of Islam. The verse emphasizes the consequence of opposing and disregarding the divine guidance, resulting in the futility of their actions and deeds. This interpretation serves as a reminder that those who reject Allah's guidance and teachings will ultimately face the consequences of their actions, and their deeds will be of no avail.
orig: ذلك بأنهم كرهوا ما أنزل الله فأحبط أعمالهم

translation: Have they not traveled through the land, so that they might have hearts with which to understand, or ears with which to hear? For it is not the eyes that are blind, but the hearts which are within the breasts.
interpretation: The verse is a rhetorical question, addressed to those who deny the signs of God. It asks whether they have traveled through the land and observed the fate of those who came before them, so that they might gain understanding and wisdom. The verse emphasizes the importance of using one's senses, not just physical sight but also insight and discernment, to reflect on the lessons of history and the consequences of disbelief. It suggests that the true blindness is not physical but spiritual, residing in the heart. The verse serves as a call to contemplation and reflection, encouraging people to use their faculties of perception and reason to understand the signs of God and the fate of those who reject His message.
orig: أفلم يسيروا في الأرض فينظروا كيف كان عاقبة الذين من قبلهم دمر الله عليهم وللكافرين أمثالها

translation: That is because Allah is the protector of those who have believed and the disbelievers have no protector.
interpretation: The verse highlights the fundamental difference between believers and disbelievers in their relationship with Allah. The believers are under Allah's protection, while the disbelievers have no such protection. This verse emphasizes the importance of faith and its impact on one's relationship with Allah, and serves as a reminder that those who reject Allah's message are ultimately on their own, without His support or guidance.
orig: ذلك بأن الله مولى الذين آمنوا وأن الكافرين لا مولى لهم

translation: Indeed, Allah will admit those who believe and do righteous deeds to Gardens beneath which rivers flow. And those who disbelieve - they will enjoy and eat as cattle eat, and the Fire will be their home.
interpretation: The verse contrasts the fates of those who believe and do righteous deeds with those who disbelieve. Believers are promised gardens beneath which rivers flow, a symbol of paradise and eternal bliss. On the other hand, those who disbelieve are described as enjoying and eating like cattle, a metaphor for their heedless and unreflective way of life. The verse concludes by stating that the fire will be their home, a stark reminder of the consequences of their disbelief and rejection of God's message.
orig: إن الله يدخل الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات جنات تجري من تحتها الأنهار والذين كفروا يتمتعون ويأكلون كما تأكل الأنعام والنار مثوى لهم

translation: And how many a town stronger than your town [Mecca] have We destroyed, which were unjust. So, We left it in ruins and emptied it of inhabitants.
interpretation: The verse highlights the power and capability of God in destroying communities that were stronger than Mecca, which was the town of the Prophet Muhammad. These communities were destroyed because of their injustice and transgression. The verse emphasizes the inevitability of the destruction of unjust communities and the futility of their strength and power in the face of God's punishment. It serves as a warning to the people of Mecca, and by extension, to all people, to heed the message of the Prophet Muhammad and turn away from their ways of injustice before it is too late.
orig: وكأين من قرية هي أشد قوة من قريتك التي أخرجتك أهلكناهم فلا ناصر لهم

translation: Is he who is on clear evidence from his Lord like him to whom evil deeds are made attractive, and he follows his desires?
interpretation: The verse contrasts two types of people: those who have clear evidence from their Lord (i.e. the believers who follow God's guidance) and those who are led astray by their desires and follow their whims (i.e. the unbelievers). The verse suggests that the latter group is deceived by the attractiveness of their evil deeds, which makes them oblivious to the truth and the guidance of God. The verse serves as a warning to the believers to beware of the deception of their desires and to stay steadfast on the path of God's guidance.
orig: أفمن كان على بينة من ربه كمن زين له سوء عمله واتبعوا أهواءهم

translation: Like the Garden which the righteous are promised: in it are rivers of water that will not go rancid, and rivers of milk the taste of which will not change, and rivers of wine enjoyable to those who drink, and rivers of purified honey, and for them in it is every fruit and forgiveness from their Lord. (Like) those who are unmindful will be as if they were intoxicated, except that they are not intoxicated: rather, it is the punishment of Allah that is severe.
interpretation: The verse describes the blessings that the righteous have been promised in the afterlife, including rivers of water, milk, wine, and honey, and every kind of fruit. The verse emphasizes the purity and constancy of these blessings, as opposed to the earthly pleasures that are subject to change and decay. The verse also describes the fate of those who are unmindful and do not strive for righteousness, comparing them to drunkards who are unaware of their surroundings. However, the verse clarifies that they are not actually drunk, but rather experiencing the severe punishment of God. The verse serves as a reminder of the great rewards of righteousness and the dire consequences of heedlessness and sin.
orig: مثل الجنة التي وعد المتقون فيها أنهار من ماء غير آسن وأنهار من لبن لم يتغير طعمه وأنهار من خمر لذة للشاربين وأنهار من عسل مصفى ولهم فيها من كل الثمرات ومغفرة من ربهم كمن هو خالد في النار وسقوا ماء حميما فقطع أمعاءهم

translation: And among them are those who listen to you until, when they go out from you, they say to those who have been given knowledge, 'What is it that he has said just now?' Those are the ones upon whom Allah has sealed their hearts, and they have followed their desires.
interpretation: The verse describes a group of people who listen to the message of the prophet, but once they leave his presence, they mock and question what was said. The verse reveals the true nature of these people, whose hearts have been sealed by God, causing them to be stubborn and resistant to the truth. They are also described as following their desires, indicating that they are guided by their own selfish and worldly interests rather than by the guidance of God. The verse serves as a warning to the believers about the danger of such people, who may appear outwardly pious and respectful, but inwardly are far from the truth.
orig: ومنهم من يستمع إليك حتى إذا خرجوا من عندك قالوا للذين أوتوا العلم ماذا قال آنفا أولئك الذين طبع الله على قلوبهم واتبعوا أهواءهم

translation: And those who are guided, He increases them in guidance and gives them their righteousness.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the positive outcome for those who are guided or follow the right path. The verse emphasizes that God increases the guidance for those who are already on the right path, and also gives them their righteousness. This suggests that the process of guidance and righteousness is continuous and ongoing, and that God's blessings are not limited to a certain point in time. The verse serves as a source of encouragement and motivation for those who are striving to follow the right path, reminding them that their efforts will be rewarded by God with increased guidance and righteousness.
orig: والذين اهتدوا زادهم هدى وآتاهم تقواهم

translation: Do they then wait for anything other than the Hour that it should come upon them suddenly? But its signs have already come. Then how can they remember (or receive admonition) when it has come to them?
interpretation: The verse warns of the coming of the Hour (Day of Judgment) and the suddenness of its arrival, and the fact that its signs have already appeared. The verse questions the disbelievers' lack of preparation and their waiting for something other than the Hour. It emphasizes the impossibility of remembering or receiving admonition when the Hour has already come, indicating the finality of the event and the lack of opportunity for repentance or preparation. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of being prepared and mindful of the signs of the Hour at all times.
orig: فهل ينظرون إلا الساعة أن تأتيهم بغتة فقد جاء أشراطها فأنى لهم إذا جاءتهم ذكراهم

translation: So know that there is no deity except Allah and seek forgiveness for your sin and for the believing men and women. And Allah knows of your movement and your resting place.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of knowing and acknowledging the oneness of God and seeking forgiveness for one's sins, as well as for the sins of other believers, both men and women. The verse reminds the reader that God is aware of their actions, both when they are active and when they are at rest. The verse encourages the reader to seek forgiveness regularly and to recognize the power and greatness of God. It also serves as a reminder of the importance of being mindful of one's actions and seeking forgiveness for any wrongdoings.
orig: فاعلم أنه لا إله إلا الله واستغفر لذنبك وللمؤمنين والمؤمنات والله يعلم متقلبكم ومثواكم

translation: And those who believe say, 'Why has not a surah been sent down?' But when a surah is sent down, containing fighting, you will see those in whose hearts is a disease looking at you with the look of one overcome by death. And worse is that which they conceal.
interpretation: The verse describes the reaction of some believers who question why a surah (chapter) of the Quran has not been revealed that contains fighting or war. When such a surah is revealed, the verse describes the fear and anxiety in the hearts of those who are hypocrites or have weak faith, as they look at the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) with a look of one overcome by death. The verse highlights the stark contrast between the true believers who are ready to fight in the way of God and the hypocrites who are filled with fear and doubt. The verse serves as a warning to those who harbor hypocrisy and doubt in their hearts and reminds them of the consequences of their actions.
orig: ويقول الذين آمنوا لولا نزلت سورة فإذا أنزلت سورة محكمة وذكر فيها القتال رأيت الذين في قلوبهم مرض ينظرون إليك نظر المغشي عليه من الموت فأولى لهم

translation: Obedience and dutifulness to parents, and (the command to) As-Siraat-ul-Mustaqeem (the right/straight path). So when the matter is resolved, it would be (best) if they had fulfilled the command of Allah.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of obedience and dutifulness to parents and staying on the right path. It highlights that when a matter is resolved, it would be in the best interest of individuals if they had fulfilled the command of Allah. The verse serves as a reminder of the significance of obedience to parents and adhering to the right path, and the ultimate benefit that comes from fulfilling the commands of Allah.
orig: طاعة وقول معروف فإذا عزم الأمر فلو صدقوا الله لكان خيرا لهم

translation: What, do you think if you were to rebel that you would then harm (anything) in the earth or (any) mischief (could you do)?
interpretation: The verse is addressing those who might consider rebelling and causing corruption and mischief in the land. The question is posed in a rhetorical manner, implying that such actions would not harm the earth or cause any real damage. This is because the power and control of the earth and all that is in it belongs solely to God. The verse serves as a warning to those who may be considering engaging in destructive and corrupt behavior, reminding them that no matter how much they may think they can harm or destroy, their actions are ultimately futile and powerless against the will of God.
orig: فهل عسيتم إن توليتم أن تفسدوا في الأرض وتقطعوا أرحامكم

translation: Those are the ones whom Allah has cursed, so he deafened them and blinded their vision.
interpretation: The verse refers to a group of people who have been cursed by Allah due to their actions. As a result of this curse, they have been struck with deafness and blindness, both physical and/or metaphorical. This punishment prevents them from understanding and accepting the truth, and from following the right path. The verse serves as a warning to those who reject the message of Islam, highlighting the severe consequences of disbelief and disobedience.
orig: أولئك الذين لعنهم الله فأصمهم وأعمى أبصارهم

translation: Then do they not reflect upon the Qur'an, or are there locks upon their hearts?
interpretation: The verse is a rhetorical question that challenges the listeners or readers of the Qur'an to ponder and reflect upon its meaning and message. It suggests that some people are not engaging with the Qur'an in a meaningful way, either because they are not reflecting on its meaning or because they have closed their hearts to its message. The verse serves as a reminder to be open-minded and receptive to the guidance of the Qur'an, and to engage with it in a thoughtful and reflective way.
orig: أفلا يتدبرون القرآن أم على قلوب أقفالها

translation: Indeed, those who have turned away after clear proofs have come to them, it is all the same for them whether you warn them or do not warn them; they will not believe.
interpretation: The verse speaks about those who have rejected the guidance (the truth) after it has become clear to them. The verse emphasizes that it makes no difference whether they are warned or not, as they will not believe. This verse is a reminder that the responsibility of guiding people lies with God, and that people have the freedom to choose whether or not they will follow the guidance. It also highlights the futility of trying to convince those who have made up their minds to reject the truth.
orig: إن الذين ارتدوا على أدبارهم من بعد ما تبين لهم الهدى الشيطان سول لهم وأملى لهم

translation: That is because they said to those who disliked what Allah has revealed, 'We will follow what we found our fathers doing.' But what if their fathers had no sense at all, and no guidance?
interpretation: The verse speaks about the people who rejected the message of Allah and followed the traditions of their ancestors instead. The verse criticizes this attitude, questioning whether the ancestors had any wisdom or guidance. The verse implies that blindly following tradition is not a valid reason for disobeying Allah's commands. The verse serves as a reminder that each person is responsible for their own actions and should not blindly follow the ways of others, but instead seek guidance from Allah.
orig: ذلك بأنهم قالوا للذين كرهوا ما نزل الله سنطيعكم في بعض الأمر والله يعلم إسرارهم

translation: But how (will it be) when the angels take them in death, striking their faces and their backs?
interpretation: The verse describes the moment of death for unbelievers, when angels come to take their souls. The violent language used in the verse, with the angels 'striking' their faces and backs, emphasizes the fear and terror that will be experienced at that moment. This verse serves as a warning to those who reject the message of Islam, reminding them of the reality of death and the judgement that will follow. The verse also emphasizes the power and authority of the angels, who are God's messengers, carrying out His will.
orig: فكيف إذا توفتهم الملائكة يضربون وجوههم وأدبارهم

translation: That is because they followed what angered Allah and disliked His pleasure, so He rendered their deeds worthless.
interpretation: The verse explains the reason for the punishment of certain people: they followed their desires and what angered God, and rejected and disliked what pleased Him. As a result, God rendered their deeds worthless, meaning they will not be rewarded for them in the afterlife. The verse emphasizes the importance of following God's commands and avoiding sin, as the consequences of not doing so can lead to the nullification of one's good deeds.
orig: ذلك بأنهم اتبعوا ما أسخط الله وكرهوا رضوانه فأحبط أعمالهم

translation: Or do those in whose hearts is disease think that Allah will not actualize His promise?
interpretation: The verse addresses those who have a sickness in their hearts, meaning that they have doubts and lack faith in God. The verse questions whether these people truly believe that God will not fulfill His promise, referring to the consequences of their disbelief and wrongdoing. The verse serves as a warning to those who harbor doubts about God and His power, reminding them that God always keeps His promises and that they should not underestimate His abilities.
orig: أم حسب الذين في قلوبهم مرض أن لن يخرج الله أضغانهم

translation: And if We willed, We could show them to you so that you would know them by their markings, and you would recognize them by the tone of their speech. And Allah is Knowing of your deeds.
interpretation: The verse highlights God's power and knowledge, stating that if God willed, He could make known to the believers the true nature of the disbelievers, so that they could be recognized by their physical appearance and their speech. The verse emphasizes that God is aware of all actions and deeds, and that nothing is hidden from Him. The verse may serve as a reminder to the believers to trust in God's knowledge and power, and to be mindful of their own actions and deeds, as they will ultimately be held accountable for them.
orig: ولو نشاء لأريناكهم فلعرفتهم بسيماهم ولتعرفنهم في لحن القول والله يعلم أعمالكم

translation: And We will surely test you until We know those of you who strive and are patient, and We will test your affairs.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the inevitability of trials and tests for the believers. The purpose of these tests is to distinguish between those who are sincere in their faith and those who are not. The test will reveal the true character of the believers, specifically their patience and perseverance. The verse emphasizes that these tests will not only be limited to one's faith but will also include their worldly affairs. The verse serves as a reminder that these tests are a part of the human experience and that it is through these trials that God's knowledge of his servants is increased.
orig: ولنبلونكم حتى نعلم المجاهدين منكم والصابرين ونبلو أخباركم

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve and deny the way of Allah and oppose the Messenger after guidance has become clear to them - they will not harm Allah at all, and Allah will render worthless their deeds.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the consequences of disbelief and opposition towards the way of God and the Prophet Muhammad. Those who persist in their disbelief and oppose the Prophet after guidance has been made clear to them will not harm God in any way, and their deeds will be rendered worthless by God. The verse emphasizes the importance of accepting and following the guidance of God and the Prophet, and the severe consequences of rejecting it.
orig: إن الذين كفروا وصدوا عن سبيل الله وشاقوا الرسول من بعد ما تبين لهم الهدى لن يضروا الله شيئا وسيحبط أعمالهم

translation: O you who have believed, obey Allah and obey the Messenger and do not invalidate your deeds.
interpretation: The verse is a command to the believers to obey God and His Messenger, and to not render their good deeds void. The verse emphasizes the importance of obedience and the serious consequences of disobedience. It serves as a reminder to the believers to be mindful of their actions, to follow the guidance of God and His Messenger, and to strive to perform good deeds that are pleasing to God.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا أطيعوا الله وأطيعوا الرسول ولا تبطلوا أعمالكم

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieved and averted [people] from the path of Allah and then died while they were disbelievers - never will Allah forgive them.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the severity of disbelief and actively preventing others from following the path of Allah. The verse clearly states that those who die in a state of disbelief, after having rejected the truth and obstructed others from it, will not be forgiven by Allah. This verse serves as a warning to those who reject the message of Islam and actively work against its spread, highlighting the grave consequences of their actions and the importance of repentance and belief in Allah.
orig: إن الذين كفروا وصدوا عن سبيل الله ثم ماتوا وهم كفار فلن يغفر الله لهم

translation: So do not lose heart, nor fall into despair. And call not one another by [offensive] names. A name of evil:
interpretation: No interpretation
orig: فلا تهنوا وتدعوا إلى السلم وأنتم الأعلون والله معكم ولن يتركم أعمالكم

translation: This worldly life is only a play and amusement, and indeed, if you believe and fear Allah, then He will give you your rewards and not ask you about your wealth.
interpretation: The verse highlights the fleeting and insignificant nature of worldly life, describing it as a mere play and amusement. At the same time, the verse encourages belief and fear of Allah, emphasizing that if one truly believes and fears Allah, they will receive their due rewards in the afterlife. The latter part of the verse also emphasizes that Allah will not ask about their wealth, indicating that the focus should be on striving for the afterlife and not on accumulating wealth in this world.
orig: إنما الحياة الدنيا لعب ولهو وإن تؤمنوا وتتقوا يؤتكم أجوركم ولا يسألكم أموالكم

translation: But if they ask you about it, after knowledge has come to you, then say, 'Its details are known only to Allah.'
interpretation: This verse is addressing the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, and instructing him on how to respond if he is asked about the details of God's decree or knowledge. The verse advises the Prophet to respond by stating that the details are known only to God. This response demonstrates humility and recognition of the limits of human knowledge. It also serves as a reminder that ultimate knowledge and understanding belong to God alone, and that humans should be humble in the face of the Divine. The verse encourages the Prophet to remain focused on conveying the message of Islam and to avoid getting drawn into debates or discussions about the details of God's decree.
orig: إن يسألكموها فيحفكم تبخلوا ويخرج أضغانكم

translation: Here you are calling upon one another to spend in the way of Allah, but among you is he who is stingy, and whoever is stingy is only stingy against himself. And Allah is the free of need, and you are the needy. And if you turn away, He will replace you with another people, then they will not be like you.
interpretation: The verse addresses a group of people who are encouraging each other to spend in the way of Allah, but some among them are stingy. The verse highlights that the stingy person is harming only himself, as Allah is free of need and it is the people who are in need. The verse also warns that if these people turn away from the command of Allah, they will be replaced by another people who will not be like them. The verse emphasizes the importance of generosity and giving in the way of Allah and the consequences of being stingy and turning away from Allah's command.
orig: ها أنتم هؤلاء تدعون لتنفقوا في سبيل الله فمنكم من يبخل ومن يبخل فإنما يبخل عن نفسه والله الغني وأنتم الفقراء وإن تتولوا يستبدل قوما غيركم ثم لا يكونوا أمثالكم

translation: We have opened for you a clear opening.
interpretation: The verse is a promise from God to the believers that He will open for them a clear path or opportunity. This could be interpreted as a promise of success, guidance, or assistance in overcoming a difficult situation. The verse may also serve as a reminder to the believers to be grateful for the blessings and opportunities that they have been given and to use them in a way that is pleasing to God.
orig: إنا فتحنا لك فتحا مبينا

translation: That Allah may forgive for you what is past of your sins and what is to come and complete His favor upon you and guide you on a straight path.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the forgiveness and mercy of Allah towards the believers. The verse emphasizes the completeness of Allah's favor upon the believers, as it encompasses both the sins they have committed in the past and those they will commit in the future. The verse also highlights the guidance of Allah, leading the believers on a straight path. The verse serves as a reminder of the boundless mercy and forgiveness of Allah, as well as the importance of seeking His guidance and following the right path.
orig: ليغفر لك الله ما تقدم من ذنبك وما تأخر ويتم نعمته عليك ويهديك صراطا مستقيما

translation: And Allah will surely give you victory with a mighty victory.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the certainty of God's help and support for the believers. The word 'victory' is used here in a broad sense, encompassing all forms of success and triumph, whether spiritual or material. The phrase 'mighty victory' emphasizes the grandeur and significance of the victory that God will grant. The verse serves as a source of hope and motivation for the believers, reminding them that God is on their side and will grant them victory in the face of adversity.
orig: وينصرك الله نصرا عزيزا

translation: He it is who sent down As-Sakinah (calmness and tranquility) into the hearts of the believers, that they may grow more in faith along with their (present) faith. And to Allah belong the hosts of the heavens and the earth. And Allah is Ever All-Knower, All-Wise.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the descent of As-Sakinah, a sense of peace and tranquility, into the hearts of the believers. This increase in faith and serenity comes in addition to their existing faith. The verse emphasizes that the heavens and the earth, and all that they contain, belong to God, who has complete knowledge and wisdom. The verse may serve as a reminder to the believers of the blessings and support they receive from God, and of His boundless knowledge and wisdom.
orig: هو الذي أنزل السكينة في قلوب المؤمنين ليزدادوا إيمانا مع إيمانهم ولله جنود السماوات والأرض وكان الله عليما حكيما

translation: For the believers, both men and women, are Gardens, with rivers flowing beneath, to abide in them, and goodly dwellings in Gardens of Eden. And (also) approval from God: that is the great triumph.
interpretation: The verse describes the reward for the believers, both men and women, in the afterlife. They will be granted access to beautiful gardens with flowing rivers and comfortable dwellings. This reward is a result of their faith and is considered a great triumph. The verse emphasizes the equality of men and women in the afterlife, and the great blessings that await those who believe.
orig: ليدخل المؤمنين والمؤمنات جنات تجري من تحتها الأنهار خالدين فيها ويكفر عنهم سيئاتهم وكان ذلك عند الله فوزا عظيما

translation: And We shall punish the hypocrites, men and women, and the idolaters, men and women, who associate others with Allah. They have prepared a painful doom for themselves, and Allah is wroth with them and has cursed them and prepared for them Hell - a hapless journey!
interpretation: The verse speaks about the punishment of hypocrites, both men and women, as well as idolaters, both men and women, who associate others with God. These people have brought a painful doom upon themselves and have earned the wrath of God. They have been cursed by God and Hell has been prepared for them. The verse serves as a warning to those who engage in hypocrisy and idolatry, emphasizing the severe consequences of these actions and the unavoidable nature of God's punishment.
orig: ويعذب المنافقين والمنافقات والمشركين والمشركات الظانين بالله ظن السوء عليهم دائرة السوء وغضب الله عليهم ولعنهم وأعد لهم جهنم وساءت مصيرا

translation: And to God belong the armies of the heavens and the earth. And God is Exalted in Might, Wise.
interpretation: The verse affirms that the armies of both the heavens and the earth belong to God, emphasizing God's power and control over all of creation. The verse also highlights God's attributes of being Exalted in Might and Wise, indicating that God's actions and decisions are based on a wise and just plan. The verse serves as a reminder of God's power and sovereignty, and encourages believers to have trust and reliance on God in all matters.
orig: ولله جنود السماوات والأرض وكان الله عزيزا حكيما

translation: Indeed, We have sent you as a witness and a bringer of good news and a warner.
interpretation: The verse is speaking to the Prophet Muhammad, informing him that his role is to serve as a witness to the truth, a bringer of good news, and a warner of the consequences of rejecting the message of Islam. The verse emphasizes the importance of the Prophet's mission and the gravity of his responsibility. It also highlights the significance of his role as a witness, as his actions and words serve as evidence of the truth of Islam. The verse also implies that the Prophet's message is one of hope and good news, as well as a warning of the consequences of not heeding the message. This verse serves as a reminder to the Prophet and to all Muslims of the importance of their role in spreading the message of Islam and serving as witnesses to its truth.
orig: إنا أرسلناك شاهدا ومبشرا ونذيرا

translation: That you believe in Allah and His Messenger and strive in the way of Allah with your property and your lives. That you honor Allah and His Messenger. And that you worship Allah alone, not associating anything with Him.
interpretation: The verse is a command to the believers to have faith in Allah and His Messenger, and to strive in the way of Allah with all their resources, both material and physical. It also commands them to honor Allah and His Messenger, and to worship Allah alone, without associating any partners with Him. The verse emphasizes the importance of complete devotion and commitment to Allah and His Messenger, and the importance of avoiding any form of shirk (associating partners with Allah). It serves as a reminder to the believers of their duties towards Allah and His Messenger, and the importance of fulfilling these duties in order to attain success in this life and the hereafter.
orig: لتؤمنوا بالله ورسوله وتعزروه وتوقروه وتسبحوه بكرة وأصيلا

translation: Indeed, those who pledge allegiance to you, they are pledging allegiance to Allah. The hand of Allah is over their hands. So he who breaks his pledge breaks it only to the detriment of himself. And he who fulfills what he has promised Allah - He will give him a great reward.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the significance of the pledge of allegiance to the Prophet Muhammad, emphasizing that it is ultimately a pledge to Allah. The verse highlights the power and authority of Allah, as His hand is placed above the hands of those who make the pledge. Those who break their pledge of allegiance harm only themselves and will face the consequences of their actions. On the other hand, those who fulfill their pledge will receive a great reward from Allah. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of keeping one's promises and fulfilling one's obligations, and of the ultimate authority and power of Allah.
orig: إن الذين يبايعونك إنما يبايعون الله يد الله فوق أيديهم فمن نكث فإنما ينكث على نفسه ومن أوفى بما عاهد عليه الله فسيؤتيه أجرا عظيما

translation: They will say to the believers from
interpretation: No interpretation
orig: سيقول لك المخلفون من الأعراب شغلتنا أموالنا وأهلونا فاستغفر لنا يقولون بألسنتهم ما ليس في قلوبهم قل فمن يملك لكم من الله شيئا إن أراد بكم ضرا أو أراد بكم نفعا بل كان الله بما تعملون خبيرا

translation: But you thought that the Messenger and the believers would never return to their families ever, and that pleased you with your ignorance. And you thought an ill thought and you were a people exceedingly foolish.
interpretation: The verse is addressing a group of people who had a false sense of security and thought that the Messenger and the believers would never return to their families. This thought pleased them and reinforced their ignorance. The verse also mentions that they had a negative and harmful thought, and it characterizes them as a foolish people. The verse serves as a critique of those who underestimate the power of the Messenger and the believers, and it highlights the danger of ignorance and false sense of security.
orig: بل ظننتم أن لن ينقلب الرسول والمؤمنون إلى أهليهم أبدا وزين ذلك في قلوبكم وظننتم ظن السوء وكنتم قوما بورا

translation: And whoever does not believe in Allah and His Messenger, then indeed, We have prepared for the disbelievers a blaze.
interpretation: The verse states that a severe punishment has been prepared for those who do not believe in Allah and his messenger. The verse emphasizes the certainty of the punishment, which has been specifically prepared for the disbelievers. The verse serves as a warning to those who do not believe in Allah and his messenger, reminding them of the severe consequences of their disbelief.
orig: ومن لم يؤمن بالله ورسوله فإنا أعتدنا للكافرين سعيرا

translation: To God belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. He forgives whomever He wills and punishes whomever He wills. And God is all-forgiving, all-merciful.
interpretation: The verse affirms God's sovereignty over the heavens and the earth and His power to forgive or punish whomever He wills. The verse emphasizes God's mercy and forgiveness, but also His ability to mete out punishment. The verse serves as a reminder of God's power and justice, and encourages believers to seek God's forgiveness and to strive to live righteously.
orig: ولله ملك السماوات والأرض يغفر لمن يشاء ويعذب من يشاء وكان الله غفورا رحيما

translation: Those who stay behind will say, when you go to take the spoils, 'Let us follow you.' They want to change the words of God. Say, 'You will not follow us; thus did God speak before.' Then they will say, 'No, you are jealous of us.' But they understand only a little.
interpretation: The verse addresses the hypocrisy of certain individuals who express a desire to follow the believers in their pursuit of battle and the acquisition of spoils, but in reality, they seek to alter the commands of God. The believers are instructed to reject their offer and remind them of God's previous decree. These individuals will then accuse the believers of jealousy, but in reality, they have a limited understanding of the true message of God. The verse highlights the importance of adhering to the commands of God and the dangers of following those who seek to distort His message.
orig: سيقول المخلفون إذا انطلقتم إلى مغانم لتأخذوها ذرونا نتبعكم يريدون أن يبدلوا كلام الله قل لن تتبعونا كذلكم قال الله من قبل فسيقولون بل تحسدوننا بل كانوا لا يفقهون إلا قليلا

translation: Say to the desert Arabs who were left behind: 'You will be called to a people of mighty military force. You will fight them, or they will surrender. If you obey, Allah will give you a good reward. But if you turn away, as you turned away before, He will punish you with a painful punishment.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about a call to battle for the desert Arabs who were left behind. They are given two options: to fight or to surrender. If they choose to obey and fight, they will be rewarded with goodness from Allah. However, if they choose to disobey, they will be punished with a severe punishment. This verse emphasizes the importance of obedience and the consequences of disobedience. It serves as a reminder to the desert Arabs, and to all believers, of the importance of following Allah's commands and the certainty of His judgment.
orig: قل للمخلفين من الأعراب ستدعون إلى قوم أولي بأس شديد تقاتلونهم أو يسلمون فإن تطيعوا يؤتكم الله أجرا حسنا وإن تتولوا كما توليتم من قبل يعذبكم عذابا أليما

translation: There is no blame upon the blind, nor is there blame upon the lame, nor is there blame upon the sick. And whoever believes in Allah and does good - they will be admitted to gardens beneath which rivers flow. But whoever disbelieves - they will be punished with a painful punishment.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the mercy and compassion of God towards those who are physically unable to perform certain tasks, such as the blind, the lame, and the sick. It reminds believers that they will not be held accountable for their physical limitations. However, the verse also makes it clear that those who believe in God and do good will be rewarded with paradise, while those who disbelieve will face a painful punishment. The verse encourages believers to have faith in God and to do good deeds, as this is the path to salvation and eternal happiness in the afterlife.
orig: ليس على الأعمى حرج ولا على الأعرج حرج ولا على المريض حرج ومن يطع الله ورسوله يدخله جنات تجري من تحتها الأنهار ومن يتول يعذبه عذابا أليما

translation: Certainly, Allah was pleased with the believers when they pledged allegiance to you under the tree, and He knew what was in their hearts, so He sent down tranquility upon them and rewarded them with a victory near at hand.
interpretation: The verse describes the moment when the believers pledged their allegiance to the Prophet Muhammad under a tree, and how Allah was pleased with their sincerity and devotion. The verse highlights Allah's knowledge of their inner thoughts and feelings, and how He responded by sending down tranquility upon them. As a reward for their faith and commitment, Allah granted them a swift and decisive victory. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of maintaining a strong and unwavering faith in Allah, and the blessings that come from following His path with sincerity and devotion.
orig: لقد رضي الله عن المؤمنين إذ يبايعونك تحت الشجرة فعلم ما في قلوبهم فأنزل السكينة عليهم وأثابهم فتحا قريبا

translation: And abundant spoils which they will take, and Allah is Exalted in Might, Wise.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the spoils of war that the believers will acquire. The verse emphasizes the abundance of the spoils, indicating that they will be plentiful. The verse ends by reminding the reader of God's greatness and wisdom, implying that the acquisition of the spoils is in accordance with God's will and plan. The verse may serve as a source of encouragement and motivation for the believers, reminding them of the rewards that come with fighting in the way of God and the certainty of His support and guidance.
orig: ومغانم كثيرة يأخذونها وكان الله عزيزا حكيما

translation: Allah has promised you many spoils which you will take, and He has hastened this for you and withheld the hands of people from you, and that it may be a sign for the believers. And He may guide you to a straight path.
interpretation: The verse speaks about Allah's promise of many spoils to the believers, which they will acquire. The verse emphasizes that these spoils have been hastened for them, and that their hands have been held back from fighting. This is a sign for the believers, a confirmation of their faith and a guidance for them to follow the right path. The verse serves as a reminder of the blessings that Allah bestows upon the believers, and of the guidance that He provides for them.
orig: وعدكم الله مغانم كثيرة تأخذونها فعجل لكم هذه وكف أيدي الناس عنكم ولتكون آية للمؤمنين ويهديكم صراطا مستقيما

translation: And you will not will, unless Allah wills. Indeed, Allah is over all things competent.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the power and control that God has over all things, stating that humans do not have the ability to do anything unless God wills it. The verse serves as a reminder of the limitations of human power and the ultimate authority of God. It highlights the importance of recognizing and submitting to God's will in all aspects of life.
orig: وأخرى لم تقدروا عليها قد أحاط الله بها وكان الله على كل شيء قديرا

translation: And if those who disbelieved fought you, they would have turned their backs; then they would not find any protector or helper.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the cowardice and weakness of the disbelievers in the face of conflict. If they were to fight the believers, they would quickly retreat and flee, leaving behind no one to protect or support them. This verse emphasizes the lack of strength and support for the disbelievers, and serves as a reminder of the power and protection that comes from belief in God. It also highlights the fleeting and uncertain nature of worldly alliances and support, and encourages believers to seek strength and protection in their faith and obedience to God.
orig: ولو قاتلكم الذين كفروا لولوا الأدبار ثم لا يجدون وليا ولا نصيرا

translation: The command of Allah that has already gone forth (past) cannot be changed, and you will never find a refuge from the command of Allah.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the power and authority of Allah's command and the inevitability of its fulfillment. The command of Allah, once decreed, cannot be altered or changed. The verse also highlights the futility of seeking refuge from Allah's command, as it is all-encompassing and all-powerful. The verse serves as a reminder of the sovereignty of Allah and the importance of submitting to His will.
orig: سنة الله التي قد خلت من قبل ولن تجد لسنة الله تبديلا

translation: And it is He who held back their hands from you and your hands from them in the valley of Makkah after He had given you the victory over them. And Allah, over all things, is all-seeing.
interpretation: The verse describes an event where God intervened and prevented fighting between two parties in the valley of Makkah, after the believers had been victorious over the opposing side. The verse highlights God's control over all things and his ability to see and know all that takes place. The verse may serve as a reminder of God's power and intervention in human affairs and his ultimate control over the outcome of events.
orig: وهو الذي كف أيديهم عنكم وأيديكم عنهم ببطن مكة من بعد أن أظفركم عليهم وكان الله بما تعملون بصيرا

translation: They are the ones who disbelieved and kept you away from the Sacred Mosque and the offerings, preventing them from reaching their destination. Had it not been for believing men and believing women whom you did not know, so that you may trample them and thus incur guilt unknowingly. Thus, God admits into His mercy whom He wills. Had they separated, We would have punished those who disbelieved among them with a painful punishment.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the actions of the disbelievers who prevented the believers from reaching the Sacred Mosque and the offerings. The verse highlights the negative consequences of their actions, such as the possibility of unknowingly committing a sin by trampling on the believers. The verse also emphasizes God's mercy and His ability to admit whom He wills into His mercy. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of respecting the rights of others, especially in religious practices, and the consequences of hindering others from fulfilling their religious obligations.
orig: هم الذين كفروا وصدوكم عن المسجد الحرام والهدي معكوفا أن يبلغ محله ولولا رجال مؤمنون ونساء مؤمنات لم تعلموهم أن تطئوهم فتصيبكم منهم معرة بغير علم ليدخل الله في رحمته من يشاء لو تزيلوا لعذبنا الذين كفروا منهم عذابا أليما

translation: When those who disbelieved put arrogance in their hearts, the arrogance of ignorance, then Allah sent down tranquility upon His Messenger and upon the believers and sent down soldiers (i.e., angels) which you did not see, and punished those who disbelieved. And that is the recompense of the disbelievers.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the punishment of those who rejected faith and were arrogant in their disbelief. Despite their arrogance, Allah sent down tranquility upon the Prophet Muhammad and the believers, and sent down soldiers (angels) to support them. The disbelievers were punished, and this was their just recompense. The verse highlights the consequences of arrogance and rejection of faith, and the support and tranquility that Allah provides to the believers in the face of adversity.
orig: إذ جعل الذين كفروا في قلوبهم الحمية حمية الجاهلية فأنزل الله سكينته على رسوله وعلى المؤمنين وألزمهم كلمة التقوى وكانوا أحق بها وأهلها وكان الله بكل شيء عليما

translation: Indeed, God's messenger has told the truth in the vision. You will surely enter the Masjid al-Haram, if God wills, in safety, your heads shaved and hair cut short, not fearing. He knew what you did not know, and He has arranged before that a victory near.
interpretation: The verse speaks about a vision that God's messenger had, which came true when the Muslims were able to enter the Masjid al-Haram safely, after their hair had been shaved or cut short, and without fear. The verse emphasizes God's knowledge and power, as He knew what the Muslims did not know and had arranged a victory for them. The verse serves as a reminder of God's support and protection for the believers and the fulfillment of His promises.
orig: لقد صدق الله رسوله الرؤيا بالحق لتدخلن المسجد الحرام إن شاء الله آمنين محلقين رءوسكم ومقصرين لا تخافون فعلم ما لم تعلموا فجعل من دون ذلك فتحا قريبا

translation: He it is Who sent His Messenger with guidance and the religion of truth, that He may make it conqueror of all religion, however much the idolaters may dislike it. Sufficient is Allah for a witness.
interpretation: The verse affirms that it is God who sent His messenger with guidance and the true religion, with the purpose of making it triumphant over all other religions. Despite the opposition from the idolaters, God's religion will ultimately prevail. The verse emphasizes the power and significance of God's religion and the futility of opposing it. The verse also highlights that God alone is sufficient as a witness.
orig: هو الذي أرسل رسوله بالهدى ودين الحق ليظهره على الدين كله وكفى بالله شهيدا

translation: Muhammad is the messenger of Allah; and those with him are firm of heart against the unbelievers, full of mercy amongst themselves. You will see them bowing and prostrating themselves in prayer, seeking bounty from Allah and (His) acceptance. The mark of their prostration is on their foreheads. Such is their likeness in the Taurat and their likeness in the Gospel - like a seed which has sprouted, then strengthened, then risen firm on its stalk, pleasing the sowers - that He may enrage the unbelievers with them. Allah has promised those who believe and do good deeds forgiveness and a great reward.
interpretation: The verse highlights the characteristics of the followers of Muhammad and their devotion to prayer and seeking Allah's bounty and acceptance. The mark of prostration on their foreheads is a symbol of their piety and dedication. The verse also mentions the similarities between the followers of Muhammad and the descriptions of righteous people in the Taurat and the Injeel. The verse serves as a reminder of the rewards of faith and good deeds, and the contrast between the believers and the unbelievers. It emphasizes the importance of faith and good deeds, and the promise of forgiveness and great reward for those who believe and do good deeds.
orig: محمد رسول الله والذين معه أشداء على الكفار رحماء بينهم تراهم ركعا سجدا يبتغون فضلا من الله ورضوانا سيماهم في وجوههم من أثر السجود ذلك مثلهم في التوراة ومثلهم في الإنجيل كزرع أخرج شطأه فآزره فاستغلظ فاستوى على سوقه يعجب الزراع ليغيظ بهم الكفار وعد الله الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات منهم مغفرة وأجرا عظيما

translation: O you who have believed, do not precede Allah and His Messenger but fear Allah. Indeed, Allah is Hearing and Knowing.
interpretation: The verse addresses those who have believed, reminding them not to precede Allah and His Messenger, which means to not take the lead or take matters into their own hands before Allah and His Messenger. The verse emphasizes the importance of obedience and submission to Allah and His Messenger. It also reminds the believers to fear Allah, as He is all-hearing and all-knowing, and that He is aware of their actions and intentions. The verse serves as a reminder for the believers to be mindful of their behavior and to act in accordance with the teachings of Islam.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تقدموا بين يدي الله ورسوله واتقوا الله إن الله سميع عليم

translation: O you who have believed, do not raise your voices above the voice of the Prophet and do not speak to him in a loud manner as you speak to one another, lest your deeds become worthless while you perceive not.
interpretation: The verse addresses the believers and instructs them not to raise their voices above the voice of the Prophet and not to speak to him in a loud manner. The reason for this is to prevent their deeds from becoming worthless without them realizing it. The verse emphasizes the importance of respecting and listening to the Prophet and the consequences of not doing so. The verse serves as a reminder to the believers to be mindful of their behavior and to show respect to the Prophet in their speech and actions.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا ترفعوا أصواتكم فوق صوت النبي ولا تجهروا له بالقول كجهر بعضكم لبعض أن تحبط أعمالكم وأنتم لا تشعرون

translation: Indeed, those who lower their voices in the presence of the Messenger of Allah - those are the ones whose hearts Allah has tested for reverence. For them is forgiveness and a great reward.
interpretation: The verse highlights the behavior of those individuals who lower their voices in the presence of the Messenger of Allah (Prophet Muhammad) as a sign of reverence and respect. The verse indicates that Allah has tested the hearts of these individuals, and as a result, they have been granted forgiveness and a great reward. The verse emphasizes the importance of showing respect and reverence to the Messenger of Allah and suggests that those who do so are among the righteous and beloved by Allah.
orig: إن الذين يغضون أصواتهم عند رسول الله أولئك الذين امتحن الله قلوبهم للتقوى لهم مغفرة وأجر عظيم

translation: Indeed, those who call you from behind the curtains are most of them unintelligent.
interpretation: The verse criticizes those who question or challenge the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) from behind the curtains of the mosque, where he would seclude himself for prayer and contemplation. The verse suggests that the majority of these people lack understanding or wisdom, and are not guided by true faith or knowledge. The verse serves as a reminder that true understanding and wisdom come from a sincere and devoted relationship with God, and not from idle questioning or criticism of the Prophet (PBUH).
orig: إن الذين ينادونك من وراء الحجرات أكثرهم لا يعقلون

translation: And if they had exercised patience until We came to them, it would have been better for them. And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the importance of patience and the benefits that come with it. If the people had exercised patience and waited for God's help, it would have been better for them. The verse emphasizes God's forgiveness and mercy towards those who are patient and have faith in Him. It serves as a reminder that patience is a virtue and that God will reward those who are patient and have faith in Him.
orig: ولو أنهم صبروا حتى تخرج إليهم لكان خيرا لهم والله غفور رحيم

translation: O you who have believed, when there comes to you a disobedient one with information, investigate, lest you harm a people out of ignorance and become, over what you have done, regretful.
interpretation: The verse addresses the believers and advises them on how to handle information brought by a disobedient person. It commands them to investigate and verify the information before taking any action. This is to prevent harming innocent people through ignorance and regret. The verse emphasizes the importance of taking a cautious approach before making a judgment or taking action, and highlights the negative consequences of acting on unverified information.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا إن جاءكم فاسق بنبإ فتبينوا أن تصيبوا قوما بجهالة فتصبحوا على ما فعلتم نادمين

translation: And know that among you is the Messenger of Allah. If he were to obey you in much of the matter, you would be in difficulty. But Allah has made you love faith and adorned it in your hearts and has made disbelief, immorality, and disobedience hateful to you. Those are the guided.
interpretation: The verse highlights the role of the Messenger of Allah (Prophet Muhammad) as a guide and leader for the community. The verse emphasizes that if the Prophet were to obey the people in most matters, it would lead to difficulty. This is because Allah has chosen to guide the people through the Prophet and has instilled in their hearts a love for faith and a hatred for disbelief, immorality, and disobedience. Those who follow this guidance are considered the guided ones, i.e. those who are on the right path.
orig: واعلموا أن فيكم رسول الله لو يطيعكم في كثير من الأمر لعنتم ولكن الله حبب إليكم الإيمان وزينه في قلوبكم وكره إليكم الكفر والفسوق والعصيان أولئك هم الراشدون

translation: But favor is from Allah and bounty, and Allah is Knowing and Wise.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes that all favors and blessings come from God, and He is the one who bestows them upon His creations. The verse also highlights that God is all-knowing and wise, indicating that He has the power and knowledge to give and withhold blessings as He sees fit. This verse can be seen as a reminder to be grateful for the blessings and favors that we have received from God, and to trust in His wisdom and knowledge even when we do not understand His actions.
orig: فضلا من الله ونعمة والله عليم حكيم

translation: And if two factions among the believers should fight, then make peace between them. And if one of them should transgress against the other, then fight the transgressing party until it returns to the command of Allah. Then, if it returns, make peace between them with justice and equity. Indeed, Allah loves those who act equitably.
interpretation: The verse outlines a process for resolving conflicts between two groups of believers. It emphasizes the importance of making peace between the two parties, and only resorting to fighting if one of them commits transgression. The fighting should continue until the transgressing party returns to the command of Allah, which can be interpreted as a call for repentance and a return to the right path. Once the transgressing party has returned to the right path, the emphasis is again on making peace between the two parties with justice and equity. The verse highlights the importance of fairness, justice and equity in resolving conflicts and the love of Allah for those who act equitably.
orig: وإن طائفتان من المؤمنين اقتتلوا فأصلحوا بينهما فإن بغت إحداهما على الأخرى فقاتلوا التي تبغي حتى تفيء إلى أمر الله فإن فاءت فأصلحوا بينهما بالعدل وأقسطوا إن الله يحب المقسطين

translation: The believers are but brothers, so make peace between your brothers and fear Allah that perhaps you will be shown mercy.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of unity and harmony among believers, who are likened to brothers. It commands believers to make peace between their brothers and encourages them to fear God, with the hope that they will be shown mercy. The verse highlights the role of believers in promoting peace and reconciliation among themselves and the importance of avoiding conflicts and divisions. It also reminds believers of the ultimate goal of their actions, which is to seek God's mercy and pleasure.
orig: إنما المؤمنون إخوة فأصلحوا بين أخويكم واتقوا الله لعلكم ترحمون

translation: O you who have believed, let not a people ridicule [another] people; perhaps they may be better than them; nor let women ridicule [other] women; perhaps they may be better than them. And do not insult one another and do not call each other by [offensive] nicknames. Wretched is the name of disobedience after faith. And whoever does not repent - then it is those who are the wrongdoers.
interpretation: The verse addresses the believers and advises them not to ridicule or insult others, as they may be better than them. The verse emphasizes the importance of respect and kindness towards others and warns against using offensive nicknames. The verse also encourages repentance and warns against disobedience after having faith. The verse serves as a reminder to the believers to uphold the values of respect, kindness, and humility, and to avoid behavior that can harm or belittle others.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا يسخر قوم من قوم عسى أن يكونوا خيرا منهم ولا نساء من نساء عسى أن يكن خيرا منهن ولا تلمزوا أنفسكم ولا تنابزوا بالألقاب بئس الاسم الفسوق بعد الإيمان ومن لم يتب فأولئك هم الظالمون
