interpretation: The verse describes the punishment of those who disbelieved among the People of the Scripture, likely referring to the Jews or Christians. They were expelled from their homes and their fortresses could not protect them from God's punishment. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the punishment, as God came upon them from a place they did not expect. The verse also highlights the destruction of their homes, which they ruined with their own hands and the hands of the believers. The verse serves as a lesson for those who have eyes, urging them to reflect and learn from the consequences of the disbelievers' actions.
orig: هو الذي أخرج الذين كفروا من أهل الكتاب من ديارهم لأول الحشر ما ظننتم أن يخرجوا وظنوا أنهم مانعتهم حصونهم من الله فأتاهم الله من حيث لم يحتسبوا وقذف في قلوبهم الرعب يخربون بيوتهم بأيديهم وأيدي المؤمنين فاعتبروا يا أولي الأبصار

translation: And if not that Allah had decreed upon them the exile, He would have punished them in the worldly life, and they would have had in the Hereafter the punishment of the Fire.
interpretation: The verse speaks about a group of people who were not punished in this life, but would have been punished if not for Allah's decree of exile for them. The verse highlights the mercy of Allah, who gives respite and a chance for repentance, even to those who deserve punishment. However, the verse also warns of the severe consequences of their actions, as they will face the punishment of the Fire in the Hereafter. The verse serves as a reminder of the ultimate justice of Allah, who will hold every soul accountable for its deeds.
orig: ولولا أن كتب الله عليهم الجلاء لعذبهم في الدنيا ولهم في الآخرة عذاب النار

translation: That is because they opposed Allah and His Messenger. And whoever opposes Allah - then indeed, Allah is severe in penalty.
interpretation: The verse highlights the severe consequences of opposing Allah and His Messenger. The phrase 'because they opposed Allah and His Messenger' indicates that the people mentioned in the verse rejected the message of Islam and the authority of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). The verse warns that whoever opposes Allah will face severe punishment, emphasizing the power and authority of Allah. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of obedience and submission to Allah and His Messenger.
orig: ذلك بأنهم شاقوا الله ورسوله ومن يشاق الله فإن الله شديد العقاب

translation: And you cut down in the rainy season the palm trees, or you left them standing on their stumps, it was by the leave of God, and so that He might disgrace the profligate.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the cutting down of palm trees during the rainy season and leaving them standing on their stumps, both of which were done with God's permission. The verse suggests that these actions were allowed to happen in order to bring disgrace upon the wrongdoers or the profligate. The verse may be interpreted as a reminder that God is in control of all things and that He can use even seemingly insignificant actions to bring about His will and to reveal the true nature of those who persist in their wrongdoing.
orig: ما قطعتم من لينة أو تركتموها قائمة على أصولها فبإذن الله وليخزي الفاسقين

translation: And Allah had certainly fulfilled His promise to you when you were killing them by His permission until when you lost courage and fell to disputing about the matter and disobeyed after He had shown you that which you love. Some of you desired the worldly life, and others were concerned about the hereafter. Then He turned you away from them that He might test you. And He has already forgiven you, and Allah is the possessor of bounty for the believers.
interpretation: The verse speaks about a situation where God had given the Muslims permission to fight their enemies and they were successful, but then they lost courage and started to argue and disobey. Some of them were more concerned about worldly matters while others were worried about the afterlife. As a result, God turned them away from their enemies and tested them. Despite their disobedience, God had already forgiven them and is capable of showing mercy and giving blessings to the believers.
orig: وما أفاء الله على رسوله منهم فما أوجفتم عليه من خيل ولا ركاب ولكن الله يسلط رسله على من يشاء والله على كل شيء قدير

translation: Whatever Allah has bestowed upon His Messenger (Muhammad SAW) from the people of the townships, it is for Allah, His Messenger (Muhammad SAW), the kindred (of Messenger Muhammad SAW), the orphans, Al-Masakin (the poor) and the wayfarer, so that it may not become a thing taken by turns among the rich among you, and whatever the Messenger (Muhammad SAW) gives you, take it, and whatever he forbids you, abstain (from it), and fear Allah. Verily, Allah is Severe in punishment.
interpretation: The verse outlines the distribution of the spoils of war that were given to Prophet Muhammad (SAW) from the people of the townships. The verse emphasizes that the distribution is for the benefit of Allah, the Prophet, the relatives of the Prophet, the orphans, the poor, and the travelers. This is to ensure that the distribution is fair and does not become a source of conflict among the rich. The verse also commands the believers to obey the Prophet and follow his commands. The verse ends with a warning that Allah is severe in punishment for those who disobey His commands and do not follow the Prophet.
orig: ما أفاء الله على رسوله من أهل القرى فلله وللرسول ولذي القربى واليتامى والمساكين وابن السبيل كي لا يكون دولة بين الأغنياء منكم وما آتاكم الرسول فخذوه وما نهاكم عنه فانتهوا واتقوا الله إن الله شديد العقاب

translation: For the poor emigrants who were expelled from their homes and their properties, seeking the favor of God and His approval, and assisting God and His messenger - those are the truthful ones.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the poor emigrants who were forced to leave their homes and properties due to their faith in God and their support for the Prophet Muhammad. These emigrants are described as truthful and are praised for their actions, which include seeking God's favor and approval, and assisting God and His messenger. The verse highlights the sacrifices and struggles of these early Muslims, and serves as a reminder of the rewards that await those who remain steadfast in their faith and support for the religion, even in the face of adversity and persecution.
orig: للفقراء المهاجرين الذين أخرجوا من ديارهم وأموالهم يبتغون فضلا من الله ورضوانا وينصرون الله ورسوله أولئك هم الصادقون

translation: And [as for] those who have settled in the city and in faith before them, they love those who have emigrated to them, and do not find in their hearts a need for what they have been given, but prefer [the emigrants] over themselves, though they are in privation. And whoever is protected from the stinginess of his soul - it is those who will be the successful.
interpretation: The verse highlights the virtues of those who have settled in a city and embraced the faith before the arrival of new immigrants. These people welcome and support the immigrants, sharing their resources and putting the needs of the newcomers above their own. Despite their own hardships, they do not feel envy or resentment towards the immigrants. The verse emphasizes that those who can control their selfish desires and prioritize the well-being of others will be the ones who achieve true success in this life and the hereafter.
orig: والذين تبوءوا الدار والإيمان من قبلهم يحبون من هاجر إليهم ولا يجدون في صدورهم حاجة مما أوتوا ويؤثرون على أنفسهم ولو كان بهم خصاصة ومن يوق شح نفسه فأولئك هم المفلحون

translation: And those who came after them say, 'Our Lord, forgive us and our brothers who preceded us in faith, and do not put in our hearts bitterness towards those who have believed. Our Lord, indeed You are Kind and Merciful.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the believers who come after the early Muslims and ask for forgiveness for themselves and their brothers who preceded them in faith. They also ask God not to put bitterness or resentment in their hearts towards the believers. The verse emphasizes the importance of unity and brotherhood among the believers and the need to forgive and seek forgiveness. The verse also highlights the merciful nature of God, addressing Him as 'Our Lord, indeed You are Kind and Merciful'.
orig: والذين جاءوا من بعدهم يقولون ربنا اغفر لنا ولإخواننا الذين سبقونا بالإيمان ولا تجعل في قلوبنا غلا للذين آمنوا ربنا إنك رءوف رحيم

translation: Have you not seen those who claim to believe in what has been revealed to you and what was revealed before you? They seek the judgment of the unrighteous, even though they were commanded to reject them. And Satan seeks to lead them far astray. When it is said to them, 'Come to what Allah has revealed and to the Messenger,' you see the hypocrites turn away from you in aversion. How then, when disaster strikes them because of what their hands have put forth, will they come to you swearing by Allah, 'We intended nothing but good conduct and reconciliation'?
interpretation: The verse speaks about the hypocrisy of certain individuals who claim to believe in the teachings of Islam and the previous scriptures, but in reality, they seek the judgment of the unrighteous and are led astray by Satan. Despite being commanded to reject the unrighteous and follow the guidance of Allah and His Messenger, they turn away in aversion when invited to do so. The verse highlights the duplicity of these individuals, who, when faced with the consequences of their actions, will come swearing by Allah that they only intended good conduct and reconciliation. The verse serves as a warning to those who claim to believe but do not act upon their faith, reminding them of the importance of following the guidance of Allah and the dangers of hypocrisy.
orig: ألم تر إلى الذين نافقوا يقولون لإخوانهم الذين كفروا من أهل الكتاب لئن أخرجتم لنخرجن معكم ولا نطيع فيكم أحدا أبدا وإن قوتلتم لننصرنكم والله يشهد إنهم لكاذبون

translation: If they withdraw, they will not withdraw from you except that you withdraw; and if they fight, they will not support you; and if you support them, they will turn their backs; then they will not be supported.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the untrustworthiness and disloyalty of certain people. If they withdraw from a conflict or difficult situation, they will not allow others to go with them. If they fight, they will not provide support or assistance. If they are supported, they will ultimately turn their backs on their supporters. And once they have done so, they will not receive any further support or help. The verse highlights the unreliable nature of these individuals and serves as a warning to those who may consider forming alliances or partnerships with them.
orig: لئن أخرجوا لا يخرجون معهم ولئن قوتلوا لا ينصرونهم ولئن نصروهم ليولن الأدبار ثم لا ينصرون

translation: That is because they fear you more than they fear Allah, and Allah is most deserving of being feared. That is because they are a people who do not understand.
interpretation: The verse explains that people fear human beings, in this case the disbelievers feared the believers, more than they fear Allah. This shows their lack of understanding and their misplaced priorities. The verse emphasizes that Allah is the one who is most deserving of fear, and the people's fear of other human beings is misguided. The verse serves as a reminder to focus one's fear and reverence on Allah, and to prioritize the worship and obedience of Allah over the fear of other human beings.
orig: لأنتم أشد رهبة في صدورهم من الله ذلك بأنهم قوم لا يفقهون

translation: They will not fight you all except in fortified towns or from behind walls. Their violence among themselves is severe. You think they are together, but their hearts are diverse. That is because they are a people who do not reason.
interpretation: The verse describes the tactics of the enemies of the Muslims, who will not engage in open combat but rather fight from fortified towns or behind walls. The verse highlights the internal divisions and discord among the enemies, despite their outward appearance of unity. The verse attributes their irrational behavior to their lack of reason or understanding, emphasizing the futility of their resistance against the Muslims.
orig: لا يقاتلونكم جميعا إلا في قرى محصنة أو من وراء جدر بأسهم بينهم شديد تحسبهم جميعا وقلوبهم شتى ذلك بأنهم قوم لا يعقلون

translation: Like those before them, they tasted the bad consequence of their affair, and they have a painful punishment.
interpretation: The verse draws a parallel between the current unjust people and the people of the past who were also unjust and tasted the bitter consequences of their actions. The verse warns that the current unjust people will also face a painful punishment, just like the people of the past. The verse emphasizes the inevitability of the punishment for those who commit injustice, and serves as a warning to those who are currently engaged in unjust actions.
orig: كمثل الذين من قبلهم قريبا ذاقوا وبال أمرهم ولهم عذاب أليم

translation: Like the devil, when he said to man, 'Disbelieve', but when he disbelieved, he said, 'Indeed, I am free of you. Indeed, I fear Allah, Lord of the worlds.'
interpretation: The verse compares a disbeliever to Satan, who invites people to disbelief. When a person follows Satan's call and disbelieves, Satan immediately disassociates himself from that person and declares that he fears Allah, the Lord of the worlds. This verse highlights the treacherous and deceitful nature of Satan, who leads people astray and then abandons them. It also serves as a warning to those who are following Satan's path, reminding them that Satan does not have their best interests in mind and will not save them from the consequences of their actions.
orig: كمثل الشيطان إذ قال للإنسان اكفر فلما كفر قال إني بريء منك إني أخاف الله رب العالمين

translation: Their end is that they will be in the Fire, abiding therein, and that is the reward of the unjust.
interpretation: The verse describes the fate of those who are unjust, stating that their end will be to reside in the Fire forever. The phrase 'that is the reward of the unjust' emphasizes the certainty of this punishment and the connection between the actions of the unjust and their consequences. The verse serves as a warning to those who commit injustices, reminding them of the severe consequences of their actions and the eternal nature of the punishment that awaits them.
orig: فكان عاقبتهما أنهما في النار خالدين فيها وذلك جزاء الظالمين

translation: O you who have believed, fear Allah and consider what you have prepared for the coming days and fear Allah, for surely, Allah is aware of what you do.
interpretation: The verse addresses the believers and urges them to fear Allah and reflect on the provisions they have made for the future. The verse emphasizes the importance of being mindful of one's actions and striving for righteousness. The phrase 'for surely, Allah is aware of what you do' serves as a reminder that God sees and knows all, encouraging the believers to lead a life that is pleasing to Him. The verse encourages believers to be mindful of their actions and their consequences, and to strive for righteousness with the knowledge that God is aware of all that they do.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا اتقوا الله ولتنظر نفس ما قدمت لغد واتقوا الله إن الله خبير بما تعملون

translation: And be not like those who forgot Allah, so He made them forget themselves. Those are the Fasiqoon (the rebellious, disobedient to Allah).
interpretation: The verse warns against forgetting or neglecting Allah, as those who do so will be made to forget themselves. This means that they will lose their sense of direction and purpose in life. The verse characterizes such people as 'Fasiqoon', which refers to those who rebel or disobey Allah's commands. The verse emphasizes the importance of remembering and acknowledging Allah in one's life, as neglecting Him can lead to negative consequences. The verse serves as a reminder to prioritize one's relationship with Allah and to avoid becoming one of the 'Fasiqoon'.
orig: ولا تكونوا كالذين نسوا الله فأنساهم أنفسهم أولئك هم الفاسقون

translation: Not equal are the dwellers of the Fire and the dwellers of Paradise. The dwellers of Paradise - they are the victorious.
interpretation: The verse highlights the fundamental difference between the fate of those who will reside in the fire (Hell) and those who will reside in Paradise. The verse makes it clear that the two groups are not equal and that the ultimate winners or victorious are those who will enter Paradise. This verse can be seen as a reminder of the importance of striving for righteousness and seeking God's pleasure, as it is this that will determine one's ultimate destination in the afterlife.
orig: لا يستوي أصحاب النار وأصحاب الجنة أصحاب الجنة هم الفائزون

translation: Had We sent down this Qur'an on a mountain, you would have seen it humbled and split asunder out of fear of Allah. Such are the parables We set forth for mankind that they may reflect.
interpretation: The verse describes the power and authority of the Qur'an, using the metaphor of a mountain being destroyed by the revelation of the Qur'an. The mountain's destruction symbolizes the overwhelming power and truth of the Qur'an, and the fear it instills in all who hear it. The verse emphasizes the importance of reflection and contemplation, encouraging people to think deeply about the messages of the Qur'an. The verse serves as a reminder of the power of God's words and the importance of heeding them.
orig: لو أنزلنا هذا القرآن على جبل لرأيته خاشعا متصدعا من خشية الله وتلك الأمثال نضربها للناس لعلهم يتفكرون

translation: He is Allah, other than whom there is no deity, the Sovereign, the Pure, the Perpetual Giver of Life, the Self-Existing by Whose leave all else that exists subsists. There is no deity but He, the Lord of Power, the Ever-Giver of Peace, the Guardian of Faith, the Preserver of Safety, the Exalted in Might, the Irresistible, the Supreme: Glory be to Allah, high is He above all that they associate with Him.
interpretation: The verse affirms the oneness of God, stating that there is no deity but Allah. It describes God as the Sovereign, the Pure, and the Ever-Living. These attributes emphasize God's power, self-sufficiency, and unique nature. The verse also highlights God's role as the Giver of Life, the Guardian of Faith, and the Preserver of Safety, indicating God's concern for and protection of all of creation. The verse serves as a reminder of God's greatness and majesty, and encourages believers to worship and serve only the one true God.
orig: هو الله الذي لا إله إلا هو عالم الغيب والشهادة هو الرحمن الرحيم

translation: He is Allah, other than whom there is no deity, the Sovereign, the Pure, the Perfection, the Guardian, the Almighty, the Compeller, the Supremely Great. Exalted is Allah above whatever they associate with Him.
interpretation: The verse is a powerful declaration of the oneness and greatness of Allah. It asserts that Allah is the only deity worthy of worship and that He possesses all the divine attributes of sovereignty, purity, perfection, guardianship, almightiness, compulsion, and supreme greatness. The verse also emphasizes Allah's transcendence above all the false gods and associations that people attribute to Him. The verse serves as a reminder of the greatness of Allah and the insignificance of all other things in comparison. It calls for the exclusive worship of Allah and the rejection of all false deities and associations.
orig: هو الله الذي لا إله إلا هو الملك القدوس السلام المؤمن المهيمن العزيز الجبار المتكبر سبحان الله عما يشركون

translation: He is God, the Creator, the Evolver, the Shaper. To Him belong the most beautiful names. All that is in the heavens and the earth glorifies Him, and He is the Mighty, the Wise.
interpretation: The verse affirms the oneness of God and His attributes as the Creator, Evolver, and Shaper of all that exists. It emphasizes the power and wisdom of God, as all that is in the heavens and the earth glorifies Him. The verse also highlights the beauty of God's names, suggesting that a deeper understanding of these names can lead to a greater appreciation of God's majesty and power. The verse serves as a reminder of the greatness of God and the importance of recognizing and praising His attributes.
orig: هو الله الخالق البارئ المصور له الأسماء الحسنى يسبح له ما في السماوات والأرض وهو العزيز الحكيم

translation: O you who have believed, do not take My enemies and your enemies as allies, extending to them affection while they have disbelieved in what has come to you of the truth, expelling the Messenger and you because you believe in Allah, your Lord. If you go out to strive in My cause and seek My approval, [do not extend affection to them] unless they have responded to you with war; then indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful. And know that Allah does not prevent the reward for good to those who do good - those who spend (in Allah's cause), whether in prosperity or adversity, who restrain anger, and who pardon the people. And Allah loves the doers of good; and those who, when they commit an immorality or wrong themselves [by transgression], remember Allah and seek forgiveness for their sins - and who can forgive sins except Allah? - and [who] do not persist in what they have done while they know.
interpretation: The verse addresses the believers, warning them against taking the disbelievers as allies and extending affection towards them, despite their rejection of the truth and their enmity towards the Prophet and the believers. The verse emphasizes the importance of loyalty to Allah and the importance of striving in Allah's cause, seeking His approval. The verse encourages the believers to forgive and restrain their anger, and to seek Allah's forgiveness when they commit sins. The verse highlights the importance of doing good, whether in prosperity or adversity, and Allah's love for those who do good. The verse serves as a reminder of Allah's forgiveness and mercy towards those who repent, and the consequences of persisting in wrongdoing.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تتخذوا عدوي وعدوكم أولياء تلقون إليهم بالمودة وقد كفروا بما جاءكم من الحق يخرجون الرسول وإياكم أن تؤمنوا بالله ربكم إن كنتم خرجتم جهادا في سبيلي وابتغاء مرضاتي تسرون إليهم بالمودة وأنا أعلم بما أخفيتم وما أعلنتم ومن يفعله منكم فقد ضل سواء السبيل

translation: If they dispute with you, say you are indeed Muslims. But how could they reach you when their longing is that you should disbelieve.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the response of Muslims when they are disputed by non-believers. The verse instructs them to declare their faith and not to engage in fruitless arguments. The verse highlights the negative intentions of the non-believers, who only wish for the Muslims to abandon their faith. The verse serves as a reminder to Muslims to remain steadfast in their beliefs and not to be swayed by the opinions and actions of those who do not believe.
orig: إن يثقفوكم يكونوا لكم أعداء ويبسطوا إليكم أيديهم وألسنتهم بالسوء وودوا لو تكفرون

translation: Your relatives and your children will not benefit you on the Day of Resurrection. He will separate between you. And Allah is Seeing of what you do.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of one's actions and the fact that on the Day of Judgment, no one will be able to help or save another. Each person will be accountable for their own deeds and no amount of wealth, power, or relationships will be able to change the outcome. The verse serves as a reminder that God sees and knows all that we do, and that we will be judged accordingly.
orig: لن تنفعكم أرحامكم ولا أولادكم يوم القيامة يفصل بينكم والله بما تعملون بصير

translation: You have had a good example in Abraham and those with him, when they said to their people, 'Indeed, we are free of you and of what you worship other than Allah. We have disbelieved in you, and there has appeared between us and you hostility and hatred forever until you believe in Allah alone' - except Abraham's saying to his father, 'Indeed, I will ask forgiveness for you, but I have no power from Allah to do you any good.' Our Lord, to You we have made our plea and to You we have repented. And to You is the destination.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the steadfastness of Prophet Abraham and his followers in their belief in one God, even in the face of hostility and hatred from their people. The verse highlights the firmness of their conviction and their rejection of the idolatrous practices of their society. The exception made for Abraham's plea for forgiveness for his father emphasizes the importance of maintaining ties of kinship and the prophetic mission of intercession. The verse serves as a model for those facing similar challenges and a reminder of the ultimate destination of all human beings to Allah.
orig: قد كانت لكم أسوة حسنة في إبراهيم والذين معه إذ قالوا لقومهم إنا برآء منكم ومما تعبدون من دون الله كفرنا بكم وبدا بيننا وبينكم العداوة والبغضاء أبدا حتى تؤمنوا بالله وحده إلا قول إبراهيم لأبيه لأستغفرن لك وما أملك لك من الله من شيء ربنا عليك توكلنا وإليك أنبنا وإليك المصير

translation: Our Lord, do not make us a trial for the disbelievers, and forgive us, our Lord. Indeed, it is You who is the Exalted in Might, the Wise.
interpretation: The verse is a supplication to God from the believers, seeking His protection from being a trial or test for the disbelievers. The believers recognize that they can be used as a means of testing the patience and faith of the disbelievers, and they seek refuge in God from this. The verse also includes a plea for forgiveness from God, emphasizing His power and wisdom. The verse highlights the importance of seeking God's protection and guidance in all aspects of life, and the importance of recognizing one's own vulnerability and need for divine assistance.
orig: ربنا لا تجعلنا فتنة للذين كفروا واغفر لنا ربنا إنك أنت العزيز الحكيم

translation: Indeed in them (the prophets and their followers) is an excellent example for those who have hope in Allah and the Last Day and remember Allah often.
interpretation: The verse highlights the exemplary conduct of the prophets and their followers as a source of inspiration for those who have faith in Allah and the Day of Judgment. By remembering Allah often, believers can strive to emulate the righteousness and virtues of the prophets, and in doing so, attain nearness to Allah. The verse emphasizes the importance of setting positive examples and striving towards righteousness in order to attain Allah's pleasure.
orig: لقد كان لكم فيهم أسوة حسنة لمن كان يرجو الله واليوم الآخر ومن يتول فإن الله هو الغني الحميد

translation: Perhaps Allah will bring about affection between you and those of them with whom you are in dispute, for Allah is competent; and Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the possibility of reconciliation between the believers and their enemies through the power of Allah. The verse emphasizes Allah's ability to bring about affection and love between two conflicting parties and highlights His qualities of forgiveness and mercy. This verse serves as a reminder of the power of Allah's intervention and the possibility of reconciliation, even in the face of conflict and enmity.
orig: عسى الله أن يجعل بينكم وبين الذين عاديتم منهم مودة والله قدير والله غفور رحيم

translation: Allah does not forbid you from those who do not fight you because of religion and do not expel you from your homes - from being righteous toward them and acting justly toward them. Indeed, Allah loves those who act justly.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of treating justly and kindly those who do not pose a threat to Muslims and their way of life. The verse advises Muslims not to engage in hostilities against those who have not fought them or expelled them from their homes. Instead, Muslims are encouraged to be righteous and just in their dealings with such people. The verse highlights the value of justice in Islam and the importance of showing kindness and compassion towards others, even if they are not Muslim. The verse serves as a reminder that Allah loves those who act justly and treat others with kindness and fairness.
orig: لا ينهاكم الله عن الذين لم يقاتلوكم في الدين ولم يخرجوكم من دياركم أن تبروهم وتقسطوا إليهم إن الله يحب المقسطين

translation: Allah only forbids you from those who fought you in religion and expelled you from your homes and helped in your expulsion - that you make allies of them. And whoever makes allies of them, then it is those who are the wrongdoers.
interpretation: The verse prohibits Muslims from forming alliances with those who have fought them in religion, expelled them from their homes, and helped in their expulsion. The verse emphasizes the importance of maintaining loyalty and avoiding alliances with those who have caused harm and injustice to the Muslim community. By forming alliances with such individuals or groups, one becomes a transgressor and wrongdoer. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of maintaining a clear distinction between friends and enemies, and avoiding any actions or relationships that may compromise one's religious beliefs or values.
orig: إنما ينهاكم الله عن الذين قاتلوكم في الدين وأخرجوكم من دياركم وظاهروا على إخراجكم أن تولوهم ومن يتولهم فأولئك هم الظالمون

translation: O you who have believed, when the believing women come to you as emigrants, examine them. Allah is most knowing as to their faith. And if you know them to be believers, then do not return them to the disbelievers. They are not permitted for them, nor are they permitted for them. And give them what they have spent. And there is no blame upon you if you marry them when you have given them their due compensation. And do not hold on to the ties of disbelief. Ask for what you have spent and let them ask for what they have spent. That is the judgment of Allah. He judges between you. And Allah is Knowing and Wise.
interpretation: The verse addresses the believers and gives them instructions on how to deal with believing women who come to them as emigrants. The believers are told to examine the women and determine their faith, as Allah is most knowing of their belief. If the women are found to be believers, then they are not to be returned to the disbelievers. The verse emphasizes the importance of maintaining ties with the believers and severing ties with the disbelievers. The verse also mentions the importance of financial integrity and fairness in the treatment of these women. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of upholding the principles of the faith and the consequences of abandoning them.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا إذا جاءكم المؤمنات مهاجرات فامتحنوهن الله أعلم بإيمانهن فإن علمتموهن مؤمنات فلا ترجعوهن إلى الكفار لا هن حل لهم ولا هم يحلون لهن وآتوهم ما أنفقوا ولا جناح عليكم أن تنكحوهن إذا آتيتموهن أجورهن ولا تمسكوا بعصم الكوافر واسألوا ما أنفقتم وليسألوا ما أنفقوا ذلكم حكم الله يحكم بينكم والله عليم حكيم

translation: And if a wife of yours has passed away to the disbelievers, then your turn is to marry any of them who has been accessible to you as a wife, giving to them their bride-gift as is prescribed, fearing Allah, in Whom you believe.
interpretation: This verse speaks about the regulations for marriage in the case where a wife has passed away and her husband is considering marrying a woman from among the disbelievers. The verse states that if this is the case, then the man is allowed to marry a woman from among the disbelievers, but only if she is accessible to him as a wife and he gives her the bride-gift as prescribed. The verse ends with a reminder to fear Allah and to adhere to the faith that they believe in. The verse emphasizes the importance of following the prescribed regulations for marriage and maintaining one's faith and fear of Allah.
orig: وإن فاتكم شيء من أزواجكم إلى الكفار فعاقبتم فآتوا الذين ذهبت أزواجهم مثل ما أنفقوا واتقوا الله الذي أنتم به مؤمنون

translation: O Prophet, when believing women come to you pledging to you that they will not associate anything with God, will not steal, will not commit unlawful sexual intercourse, will not kill their children, will not bring forth a slander they have invented of their own, and will not disobey you in any righteous matter - then accept their pledge and ask God to forgive them. Indeed, God is ever-forgiving and merciful.
interpretation: The verse outlines the conditions of the pledge that believing women make to the Prophet Muhammad. These conditions include not associating anything with God, not stealing, not committing adultery, not killing their children, not spreading false rumors, and not disobeying the Prophet in any righteous matter. By accepting their pledge, the Prophet is asked to seek forgiveness for them from God, who is described as being ever-forgiving and merciful. The verse emphasizes the importance of upholding these moral and ethical principles and the role of the Prophet in guiding and supporting the believers in their commitment to these principles.
orig: يا أيها النبي إذا جاءك المؤمنات يبايعنك على أن لا يشركن بالله شيئا ولا يسرقن ولا يزنين ولا يقتلن أولادهن ولا يأتين ببهتان يفترينه بين أيديهن وأرجلهن ولا يعصينك في معروف فبايعهن واستغفر لهن الله إن الله غفور رحيم

translation: O you who have believed, do not take the disbelievers as allies instead of the believers. Do you wish to give Allah against yourselves a clear case?
interpretation: The verse warns Muslims not to form alliances with disbelievers, instead of believers. It emphasizes the seriousness of this act and its potential consequences, stating that it is akin to taking a clear stance against Allah. The verse serves as a reminder for Muslims to maintain their unity and loyalty to their faith, and to avoid forming relationships that may compromise their beliefs and actions.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تتولوا قوما غضب الله عليهم قد يئسوا من الآخرة كما يئس الكفار من أصحاب القبور

translation: Glorified be Allah, [High exalted is He] above all that they associate with Him, in the heavens and the earth. And He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise.
interpretation: The verse is a glorification of God, emphasizing His greatness and power. It highlights God's supremacy over all that is associated with Him in the heavens and the earth. The verse further describes God as the Exalted in Might, the Wise, emphasizing His power and wisdom. This verse serves as a reminder of God's greatness and encourages the believers to glorify and praise Him.
orig: سبح لله ما في السماوات وما في الأرض وهو العزيز الحكيم

translation: O you who have believed, why do you say what you do not do?
interpretation: The verse is addressed to the believers and it is a rhetorical question reminding them of the importance of aligning their words with their actions. The verse is a call for integrity and authenticity, and it serves as a reminder that hypocrisy and insincerity are not acceptable in Islam. It encourages the believers to be truthful, consistent, and mindful of their speech, and to strive for coherence between their words and deeds.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا لم تقولون ما لا تفعلون

translation: Surely, the greatest of the sins with Allah is that you say what you do not do.
interpretation: The verse highlights the seriousness of hypocrisy and insincerity in the eyes of Allah. To claim or promise something but not follow through or act upon it is considered a grave sin. This verse serves as a reminder to be truthful and consistent in one's words and actions, and to avoid making false promises or statements.
orig: كبر مقتا عند الله أن تقولوا ما لا تفعلون

translation: Indeed, Allah loves those who fight in His cause in a row as if they were a solid structure.
interpretation: The verse highlights the love of Allah for those who fight in His cause, emphasizing the importance of unity and solidarity among believers. The imagery of a 'solid structure' indicates the strength and cohesion of the believers as they stand together in battle. The verse serves as a motivation for Muslims to strive for unity and solidarity, and to strive for the cause of Allah with determination and perseverance.
orig: إن الله يحب الذين يقاتلون في سبيله صفا كأنهم بنيان مرصوص

translation: And when Moses said to his people, 'O my people, why do you harm me, while you know that I am a messenger of God to you?' But when they swerved, God swerved their hearts. And God does not guide the transgressing people.'
interpretation: The verse describes a moment when Moses expresses his frustration to his people for causing harm to him, despite knowing that he is a messenger of God. When his people disobey and stray from the path of righteousness, God causes their hearts to swerve as well. The verse emphasizes the importance of following the guidance of God's messenger and the consequences of disobedience. Those who transgress and disobey God's message will not be guided by Him.
orig: وإذ قال موسى لقومه يا قوم لم تؤذونني وقد تعلمون أني رسول الله إليكم فلما زاغوا أزاغ الله قلوبهم والله لا يهدي القوم الفاسقين

translation: And when Jesus, son of Mary, said, 'O children of Israel! Indeed, I am the messenger of Allah to you, confirming what is before me of the Torah and bringing good news of a messenger to come after me, whose name is Ahmad.' But when he came to them with clear proofs, they said, 'This is clear magic.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about Jesus, son of Mary, announcing his prophethood and the coming of a messenger after him, whose name is Ahmad. Despite Jesus' clear proofs and miracles, the people of Israel rejected him and called him a magician. The verse emphasizes the rejection and disbelief of the people in the face of clear evidence and truth, highlighting their stubbornness and refusal to accept the message of God. The verse serves as a reminder of the consequences of disbelief and the importance of accepting and following the message of the prophets.
orig: وإذ قال عيسى ابن مريم يا بني إسرائيل إني رسول الله إليكم مصدقا لما بين يدي من التوراة ومبشرا برسول يأتي من بعدي اسمه أحمد فلما جاءهم بالبينات قالوا هذا سحر مبين

translation: And who is more unjust than one who invents a lie about Allah or denies the truth [when it has come] to him? Is there not in Hell a dwelling place for the disbelievers?
interpretation: The verse highlights the grave sin of lying about Allah or denying the truth, even as one is being called to Islam. The verse emphasizes the severity of this offense by comparing it to the punishment of the disbelievers in Hell. The verse serves as a warning to those who are tempted to reject or distort the truth, reminding them of the dire consequences of their actions and the ultimate destination of those who persist in their disbelief.
orig: ومن أظلم ممن افترى على الله الكذب وهو يدعى إلى الإسلام والله لا يهدي القوم الظالمين

translation: They wish to extinguish the light of Allah with their mouths, but Allah will perfect His light, although the disbelievers dislike it.
interpretation: The verse highlights the struggle between truth and falsehood, represented by the light of Allah and the attempts of some people to extinguish it. Despite their efforts, the light of Allah will always prevail and be perfected, regardless of the opposition and dislike of the disbelievers. The verse emphasizes the ultimate victory of truth and the futility of trying to suppress it.
orig: يريدون ليطفئوا نور الله بأفواههم والله متم نوره ولو كره الكافرون

translation: He it is Who sent His Messenger with the guidance and the religion of truth, that He may make it prevail over all religions, however much the idolaters may be averse.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the mission of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) as a messenger of God, who was sent with guidance and the religion of truth. The verse highlights the purpose of his mission, which is to make this religion prevail over all other religions. Despite the opposition of the idolaters, the religion of truth will ultimately be victorious. The verse emphasizes the importance of following the guidance of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and the truth of the religion of Islam, and the ultimate victory of Islam over all other religions.
orig: هو الذي أرسل رسوله بالهدى ودين الحق ليظهره على الدين كله ولو كره المشركون

translation: O you who believe! Shall I guide you to a commerce that will save you from a painful torment?
interpretation: The verse is addressing the believers and offering them a 'commerce' or transaction that will save them from a painful punishment. This commerce refers to the act of obedience and worship of God, which will result in salvation and protection from the torment of Hellfire. The verse emphasizes the importance of seeking God's pleasure and engaging in righteous deeds, as it leads to the ultimate success and happiness in this world and the hereafter.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا هل أدلكم على تجارة تنجيكم من عذاب أليم

translation: You believe in God and His messenger and strive in the way of God with your wealth and your lives. That is better for you, if you only knew.
interpretation: The verse is encouraging believers to have faith in God and His messenger and to strive in the way of God, using both their wealth and their lives. The verse suggests that this is a beneficial course of action for the believers, but adds the caveat that they must have knowledge of this fact. The verse may be interpreted as a call to action for believers, urging them to actively work towards the betterment of their community and the advancement of their faith, using all the resources at their disposal. The verse implies that the ultimate reward for such actions will be great, but that this may not be immediately apparent to those who engage in them.
orig: تؤمنون بالله ورسوله وتجاهدون في سبيل الله بأموالكم وأنفسكم ذلكم خير لكم إن كنتم تعلمون

translation: He will forgive you your sins and will admit you to gardens beneath which rivers flow, and to beautiful mansions in gardens of perpetuity. That is the supreme triumph.
interpretation: The verse speaks of God's forgiveness and the reward that awaits the believers in the afterlife. It describes the gardens of perpetuity, which have rivers flowing beneath them and beautiful mansions, as the ultimate victory and triumph. The verse serves as a source of hope and motivation for the believers, reminding them that their sins will be forgiven and that they will be rewarded with eternal bliss in the afterlife if they remain steadfast in their faith and obedience to God.
orig: يغفر لكم ذنوبكم ويدخلكم جنات تجري من تحتها الأنهار ومساكن طيبة في جنات عدن ذلك الفوز العظيم

translation: And another (favor that you love) from Allah is that He is your supporter; and gives you victory soon and gives good tidings to the believers.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the blessings that come from Allah, highlighting three specific favors: first, that Allah is the supporters of the believers; second, that Allah will grant them victory in the near future; and third, that Allah will give good tidings to the believers. The verse emphasizes the importance of having faith in Allah, as it is through this faith that one can receive His support, victory, and good news. The verse serves as a source of encouragement and hope for the believers, reminding them of Allah's love and support for them in their struggles.
orig: وأخرى تحبونها نصر من الله وفتح قريب وبشر المؤمنين

translation: O you who have believed, be supporters of Allah, as when Jesus, the son of Mary, said to the disciples, 'Who are my supporters for Allah?' The disciples said, 'We are supporters of Allah.' And a faction of the Children of Israel believed and another faction disbelieved. So We supported those who believed against their enemy, and they became dominant.
interpretation: The verse calls on believers to support God, using the example of Jesus and his disciples who pledged their support for God. The verse highlights the division among the Children of Israel between those who believed and those who disbelieved. It emphasizes the support that God gave to the believers, leading them to victory over their enemies and becoming dominant. The verse encourages believers to follow the example of Jesus and his disciples and to support God, implying that they too will receive God's support and victory over their enemies.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا كونوا أنصار الله كما قال عيسى ابن مريم للحواريين من أنصاري إلى الله قال الحواريون نحن أنصار الله فآمنت طائفة من بني إسرائيل وكفرت طائفة فأيدنا الذين آمنوا على عدوهم فأصبحوا ظاهرين

translation: Exalted is He who is in the heaven and the earth, the Sovereign, the Holy, the Almighty, the Wise.
interpretation: The verse is a declaration of the greatness and power of God, who is described as being exalted and sovereign over both the heavens and the earth. The attributes of God that are mentioned in the verse highlight His holiness, might, and wisdom, emphasizing His perfection and supremacy. The verse serves as a reminder of the majesty of God and encourages the believers to recognize and submit to His power and wisdom.
orig: يسبح لله ما في السماوات وما في الأرض الملك القدوس العزيز الحكيم

translation: He it is Who sent among the unlettered ones a Messenger of their own, to recite unto them His revelations, and to make them grow, and to teach them the Book and wisdom, though before that they were indeed in error manifest.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the mission of a Prophet who was sent by God to a group of people who were uneducated and living in error. The Prophet's role was to recite the revelations of God to them, to help them grow spiritually, and to teach them the Book (the Qur'an) and wisdom. The verse highlights the importance of the Prophet's role in guiding the people out of their state of ignorance and error. It also emphasizes the significance of the Qur'an and wisdom in the spiritual development of the people. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of education, guidance, and spiritual growth in the life of a community.
orig: هو الذي بعث في الأميين رسولا منهم يتلو عليهم آياته ويزكيهم ويعلمهم الكتاب والحكمة وإن كانوا من قبل لفي ضلال مبين

translation: And the last of them were overtaken by the same (punishment) while they were unjust.
interpretation: The verse refers to a group of people who were punished for their injustice, similar to the people mentioned in the previous verses. The phrase 'the last of them' implies that they were aware of the punishment that had befallen their predecessors, yet they continued in their unjust ways and were ultimately overtaken by the same fate. The verse serves as a reminder that those who persist in injustice will eventually face the consequences of their actions, regardless of any warning or example set before them.
orig: وآخرين منهم لما يلحقوا بهم وهو العزيز الحكيم

translation: That is the grace of Allah which He bestows upon whom He wills, and Allah is the possessor of great bounty.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the grace (fadl) of Allah, which is a blessing or favor that Allah bestows upon His creations. The verse emphasizes that this grace is given to whoever Allah wills, highlighting Allah's power and sovereignty. The verse also mentions that Allah is the possessor of great bounty (al-fadl al-azim), implying that His grace and blessings are abundant and limitless. The verse serves as a reminder of Allah's generosity and mercy towards His creations, and encourages believers to be grateful for the blessings they receive.
orig: ذلك فضل الله يؤتيه من يشاء والله ذو الفضل العظيم

translation: Like those who carried the Torah, then did not carry it (properly), are like asses carrying books. What a terrible example are the people who reject the signs of God! And God does not guide the unjust people.
interpretation: The verse uses a metaphor to criticize those who claim to follow the teachings of the Torah but do not act upon them. These people are compared to asses carrying books, which is a derogatory comparison meant to highlight their hypocrisy. The verse emphasizes the importance of not just possessing knowledge, but also implementing it in one's life. The verse also mentions the consequences of rejecting God's signs and warns that God will not guide those who are unjust. The verse serves as a reminder to be consistent in one's beliefs and actions and to not just claim to follow a religion, but to truly live it.
orig: مثل الذين حملوا التوراة ثم لم يحملوها كمثل الحمار يحمل أسفارا بئس مثل القوم الذين كذبوا بآيات الله والله لا يهدي القوم الظالمين

translation: Say, 'O you who have been given knowledge! If you claim that you indeed are the favorites of Allah to the exclusion of all the other people, then wish for death, if you are truthful.'
interpretation: The verse is addressed to those who claim to have knowledge and consider themselves as the favorites of God, above all other people. The verse challenges them to prove their claim by wishing for death, if they are truthful. The verse emphasizes the importance of sincerity and truthfulness, and it serves as a reminder that mere claims and beliefs are not enough, but actions and deeds are what truly matter. The verse also highlights the significance of death as a test of one's faith and convictions, and the ultimate leveler of all worldly distinctions and privileges.
orig: قل يا أيها الذين هادوا إن زعمتم أنكم أولياء لله من دون الناس فتمنوا الموت إن كنتم صادقين

translation: And they do not await it (the Hour) with longing, eagerly, because of what (hands) their own hands have sent forth, and Allah is aware of the unjust.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the unjust who do not eagerly await the Day of Judgment (the Hour) because of the evil deeds they have committed. They are not prepared for it or hoping for a positive outcome. The verse emphasizes that God is aware of their injustices and unrighteous actions, and it serves as a reminder of the consequences of their actions and the impending Day of Judgment.
orig: ولا يتمنونه أبدا بما قدمت أيديهم والله عليم بالظالمين

translation: Say, 'Indeed, the death from which you flee - indeed, it will reach you. Then you will be returned to the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, and He will inform you about what you used to do.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the inevitability of death and the Day of Judgment. The verse reminds people that they cannot escape death, no matter how much they try to avoid it. After death, people will be brought back to life and will be held accountable for their actions. The verse emphasizes the omniscience of God, who knows both the unseen and the witnessed, and who will inform people about their deeds. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of leading a righteous life and preparing for the Day of Judgment.
orig: قل إن الموت الذي تفرون منه فإنه ملاقيكم ثم تردون إلى عالم الغيب والشهادة فينبئكم بما كنتم تعملون

translation: O you who have believed, when the call is made for prayer on the day of congregation, then proceed to the remembrance of Allah and leave trade. That is better for you if you were to know.
interpretation: The verse is addressing the believers and instructing them on how to behave on the day of congregation, or Jumu'ah, which is a specific day of the week for Muslims. When the call to prayer is made, the believers are told to proceed to the remembrance of Allah, or the mosque, and to leave their trade or other worldly activities. This is presented as a better option for them if they were to know. The verse emphasizes the importance of prioritizing religious obligations over worldly matters, and encourages the believers to seize the opportunity to remember and worship Allah on this special day.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا إذا نودي للصلاة من يوم الجمعة فاسعوا إلى ذكر الله وذروا البيع ذلكم خير لكم إن كنتم تعلمون

translation: And when the prayer is completed, then disperse in the land and seek the bounty of Allah and remember Allah much that you may prosper.
interpretation: This verse is a guidance for Muslims after they have completed their prayer. It encourages them to go out in the world and seek God's blessings and provisions. At the same time, it reminds them to remember and worship God frequently, with the hope that they will be successful in their endeavors. The verse emphasizes the importance of maintaining a strong connection with God and seeking His guidance and blessings in all aspects of life.
orig: فإذا قضيت الصلاة فانتشروا في الأرض وابتغوا من فضل الله واذكروا الله كثيرا لعلكم تفلحون

translation: And when they see some commerce or amusement, they rush toward it and leave you standing. Say, 'What is with Allah is better than amusement and commerce.' And Allah is the best of providers.'
interpretation: The verse addresses a group of people who are easily distracted by worldly pursuits such as commerce and entertainment, and who neglect their responsibilities towards the speaker (who could be a prophet or a messenger of God) by leaving him (or the message) behind. The verse advises the speaker to remind these people that what Allah has promised is better than any worldly pleasure or material gain. The verse emphasizes that Allah is the ultimate provider, and that true satisfaction and fulfillment can only be found in seeking His pleasure and following His guidance.
orig: وإذا رأوا تجارة أو لهوا انفضوا إليها وتركوك قائما قل ما عند الله خير من اللهو ومن التجارة والله خير الرازقين

translation: When the hypocrites come to you, they say: 'We bear witness that you are indeed the Messenger of Allah.' And Allah knows that you are indeed His Messenger, and Allah bears witness that the hypocrites are indeed liars.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the hypocrites who claim to believe in the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) but in reality, they do not. They come to the Prophet and declare their faith, but Allah knows their true intentions. The verse emphasizes the fact that the hypocrites are liars, and it serves as a reminder that Allah knows the true intentions of people, even if they try to hide them. It also serves as a warning to those who claim to believe but do not act upon their belief and may be deceiving the believers and the Prophet.
orig: إذا جاءك المنافقون قالوا نشهد إنك لرسول الله والله يعلم إنك لرسوله والله يشهد إن المنافقين لكاذبون

translation: They took their oaths as a shield and thus turned away from the path of Allah. Indeed, they have been evil in their deeds.
interpretation: The verse criticizes those who use their oaths or religious rituals as a means to justify their wrongdoing and turn away from the path of God. By doing so, they are only harming themselves and committing evil acts. This verse serves as a reminder to be truthful and sincere in one's beliefs and actions, and not to use religion as a pretext for wrongful behavior.
orig: اتخذوا أيمانهم جنة فصدوا عن سبيل الله إنهم ساء ما كانوا يعملون

translation: That is because they believed, then disbelieved, so their hearts were sealed, so they understand not.
interpretation: The verse explains the reason for the punishment of certain people. They had believed in the truth but then disbelieved, causing their hearts to become sealed. As a result, they were unable to understand or comprehend the truth. This verse highlights the importance of remaining steadfast in faith, as disbelief and rejection of the truth can lead to a hardening of the heart and a loss of understanding and comprehension.
orig: ذلك بأنهم آمنوا ثم كفروا فطبع على قلوبهم فهم لا يفقهون

translation: And when you look at them, their bodies astonish you, and when they hear your speech, they are like one being stabbed, paying no attention. When they recognize any mention of them, they become as if they were rotten wood, disunited. Pay heed to them; God will surely punish them: how can you be deluded by them?
interpretation: The verse describes the disbelievers' reaction to the truth when it is presented to them. Their bodies are described as astonishing, and when they hear the truth, it is as if they are being stabbed, showing their discomfort and rejection. They pay no attention to the truth, and when they recognize any mention of it, they become disunited and weak, like rotten wood. The verse encourages the believers to be aware of the disbelievers and their tactics and to be cautious of them. It reminds the believers that God will surely punish the disbelievers for their rejection of the truth, and warns them not to be deceived by their outward appearance or actions.
orig: وإذا رأيتهم تعجبك أجسامهم وإن يقولوا تسمع لقولهم كأنهم خشب مسندة يحسبون كل صيحة عليهم هم العدو فاحذرهم قاتلهم الله أنى يؤفكون

translation: And when it is said to them, 'Come, the Messenger of Allah will ask forgiveness for you,' they turn their heads, and you see them evading while they are arrogant.
interpretation: The verse describes the behavior of certain people when they are invited to seek forgiveness from Allah through the Messenger of Allah. Instead of heeding the call, they turn away and refuse to participate, displaying arrogance and evasiveness. This behavior is a reflection of their haughty and prideful nature, which prevents them from humbling themselves before Allah and seeking His mercy. The verse serves as a criticism of such individuals, highlighting their rejection of the opportunity for forgiveness and their preference for self-importance over submission to Allah.
orig: وإذا قيل لهم تعالوا يستغفر لكم رسول الله لووا رءوسهم ورأيتهم يصدون وهم مستكبرون

translation: Whether you ask forgiveness for them or do not ask forgiveness for them, (in either case) Allah will not forgive them. Indeed, Allah does not guide the transgressing people.
interpretation: The verse states that if one asks for forgiveness for the unjust people or does not ask for their forgiveness, it will not make a difference, as Allah will not forgive them. The verse emphasizes the severity of the consequences of transgression and that Allah will not guide those who commit such acts. This verse serves as a reminder that individual actions have consequences and that those who commit injustices will face the consequences of their actions, regardless of any intercession on their behalf.
orig: سواء عليهم أستغفرت لهم أم لم تستغفر لهم لن يغفر الله لهم إن الله لا يهدي القوم الفاسقين

translation: They say, 'You shall not spend a thing on those who are with the Messenger of God until they break camp.' Yet the treasures of the heavens and the earth belong to God. But the hypocrites do not understand.
interpretation: The verse addresses a group of people who refuse to provide financial support to those who are with the Messenger of God (Prophet Muhammad) until they leave their current location, indicating their reluctance to support the Prophet and his mission. The verse emphasizes that all wealth ultimately belongs to God, and that the hypocrites, who fail to understand the true nature of wealth and its purpose, are not able to comprehend this concept.
orig: هم الذين يقولون لا تنفقوا على من عند رسول الله حتى ينفضوا ولله خزائن السماوات والأرض ولكن المنافقين لا يفقهون

translation: They say, 'If we return to the city, the mightiest among us will surely drive out the weakest of us.' But to God belongs the true might, and to His Messenger, and to the believers. But the hypocrites do not know.
interpretation: The verse describes a situation where some people are expressing their doubts and fears about returning to their city, believing that the powerful among them will drive out the weak. The verse emphasizes that true power belongs to God and His Messenger, as well as the believers. The hypocrites, who are those who outwardly support the believers but inwardly oppose them, do not understand this truth. The verse serves as a reminder of the true source of power and the falsehood of the hypocrites' beliefs.
orig: يقولون لئن رجعنا إلى المدينة ليخرجن الأعز منها الأذل ولله العزة ولرسوله وللمؤمنين ولكن المنافقين لا يعلمون

translation: O believers, let not your wealth and your children divert you from the remembrance of Allah. And whoever does that, then those are the losers.
interpretation: The verse warns believers not to let their wealth and children distract them from the remembrance of God. The verse emphasizes the importance of keeping God in mind and not allowing material possessions or familial obligations to take precedence over one's faith. The verse concludes by stating that those who allow themselves to be distracted from the remembrance of God are the true losers. The verse serves as a reminder to prioritize one's faith and relationship with God above all else, and not to let worldly concerns take precedence over spiritual matters.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تلهكم أموالكم ولا أولادكم عن ذكر الله ومن يفعل ذلك فأولئك هم الخاسرون

translation: And spend [in the way of Allah] from what We have provided for you before death comes to one of you and he says, 'My Lord, if only You would delay me for a brief term so I would give charity and be among the righteous.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the regret of a person who did not spend in the way of Allah before their death came. They express their desire to have more time to give charity and be among the righteous. The verse highlights the importance of using one's wealth for good deeds and being mindful of the inevitability of death. It serves as a reminder to not delay in doing good, as the opportunity to do so can be lost at any moment.
orig: وأنفقوا من ما رزقناكم من قبل أن يأتي أحدكم الموت فيقول رب لولا أخرتني إلى أجل قريب فأصدق وأكن من الصالحين

translation: And not a soul will Allah delay when its term comes, and Allah is acquainted with what you do.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the inevitability of the appointed time of death for every soul and the fact that Allah is aware of all human actions. The phrase 'not a soul will Allah delay' implies that the appointed time of death is fixed and unchangeable, and that no one will be able to escape it. This serves as a reminder of the importance of being always prepared for the approaching of one's term and the importance of leading a righteous life, as Allah is aware of all that we do.
orig: ولن يؤخر الله نفسا إذا جاء أجلها والله خبير بما تعملون

translation: Glorified be Allah, [highly exalted is He] above all that they associate with Him, in the heavens and the earth. His is the dominion, and to Him belongs all the praise, and He is over all things competent.
interpretation: The verse is a declaration of the greatness and power of God, who is above all that is associated with Him in the heavens and the earth. It emphasizes that all dominion and praise belong to Him, and that He is competent over all things, indicating His complete control and sovereignty over the entire universe. The verse serves as a reminder of the greatness of God and the insignificance of all created beings in comparison to Him.
orig: يسبح لله ما في السماوات وما في الأرض له الملك وله الحمد وهو على كل شيء قدير

translation: It is He who created you, and among you is the disbeliever, and among you is the believer. And Allah is Seeing of what you do.
interpretation: The verse highlights that God is the creator of all human beings, and that among them are both believers and disbelievers. This statement emphasizes the power and control that God has over all of humanity, and the diversity that exists within it. The verse also reminds us that God is aware of all of our actions, and that nothing goes unnoticed. This is a reminder to be mindful of our actions and to strive towards righteousness.
orig: هو الذي خلقكم فمنكم كافر ومنكم مؤمن والله بما تعملون بصير

translation: He created the heavens and the earth with truth and formed you and perfected your forms, and to Him is the final destination.
interpretation: The verse speaks about God's creation of the heavens and the earth with truth and His formation and perfecting of human beings. The verse highlights God's power and ability to create and perfect His creations. The verse also emphasizes that human beings should be grateful for their creation and perfect forms and should remember that their final destination is with God. The verse encourages believers to lead a righteous life and to remember that they will be held accountable for their actions in the hereafter.
orig: خلق السماوات والأرض بالحق وصوركم فأحسن صوركم وإليه المصير

translation: He knows what is in the heavens and the earth and knows what you conceal and what you declare. And Allah is Knowing of that within the breasts.
interpretation: The verse highlights God's all-encompassing knowledge, emphasizing that He is aware of everything in the heavens and the earth, as well as what people conceal and what they declare. The verse reminds people that there is no secret that can be hidden from God, and that He has complete knowledge of everything, including the innermost thoughts and intentions of people. This serves as a reminder of God's omniscience and omnipresence, and encourages people to lead righteous lives and be mindful of their actions and words.
orig: يعلم ما في السماوات والأرض ويعلم ما تسرون وما تعلنون والله عليم بذات الصدور

translation: Has there not come to you the story of those who disbelieved before, then tasted the consequence of their disbelief, and theirs is a painful punishment.
interpretation: The verse refers to the story of the previous disbelievers who rejected God's message and faced the consequences of their disbelief. The verse serves as a reminder that the outcome of disbelief is painful and severe. It emphasizes the importance of reflecting on the lessons from history and the experiences of previous nations, so that people can draw parallels and learn from them. The verse encourages believers to reflect on the consequences of disbelief and to take heed, so that they do not follow in the footsteps of those who have gone before and faced divine retribution.
orig: ألم يأتكم نبأ الذين كفروا من قبل فذاقوا وبال أمرهم ولهم عذاب أليم

translation: That is because their messengers came to them with clear proofs, but they said, 'Show us a sign.' So they rejected them, and consequently, God was not in need of them, and God is free of need, worthy of praise.
interpretation: The verse explains why certain towns were destroyed, attributing it to their rejection of the messengers who were sent to them with clear proofs and signs. Despite the evidence presented to them, they demanded more proof and ultimately rejected the messengers. The verse emphasizes that God does not need the unbelievers, and that God is self-sufficient, free of any need for His creation. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of accepting and following the guidance sent by God.
orig: ذلك بأنه كانت تأتيهم رسلهم بالبينات فقالوا أبشر يهدوننا فكفروا وتولوا واستغنى الله والله غني حميد

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve have claimed that they will never be resurrected. Say, 'Yes, by my Lord, you will surely be resurrected; then you will be informed of what you have done. And that is easy for Allah.'
interpretation: The verse addresses the disbelievers who deny the resurrection after death. The speaker (Prophet Muhammad) affirms their resurrection and informs them that they will be held accountable for their actions. The ease with which Allah can resurrect the dead is emphasized, indicating the power and ability of Allah over all things. The verse serves as a reminder of the inevitability of the Day of Judgment and the need for believers to prepare for it by doing good deeds and avoiding sin.
orig: زعم الذين كفروا أن لن يبعثوا قل بلى وربي لتبعثن ثم لتنبؤن بما عملتم وذلك على الله يسير

translation: But believe in Allah and His Messenger and the Light which We have sent down. And Allah, with what you do, is Acquainted.
interpretation: The verse is a command for the believers to have faith in Allah, His messenger, and the light (guidance) that has been revealed. It emphasizes the all-encompassing knowledge of Allah, who is aware of all that the believers do. The verse serves as a reminder for the believers to have faith and to follow the guidance that has been revealed to them, and to be mindful of the fact that Allah is aware of their actions and will hold them accountable for them.
orig: فآمنوا بالله ورسوله والنور الذي أنزلنا والله بما تعملون خبير

translation: A day will come when We will gather you for the Day of Gathering, that is the Day of Loss. Whoever believes in God and does righteous deeds, We will absolve them of their sins and admit them to gardens beneath which rivers flow, remaining in them forever. That is the supreme success.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the Day of Judgment, referred to as the Day of Gathering and the Day of Loss. The verse emphasizes the importance of faith and righteous deeds, as those who believe in God and do good will have their sins forgiven and will be admitted to gardens beneath which rivers flow. This is described as the supreme success. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of leading a righteous life and the rewards that come with it, as well as the consequences of not doing so.
orig: يوم يجمعكم ليوم الجمع ذلك يوم التغابن ومن يؤمن بالله ويعمل صالحا يكفر عنه سيئاته ويدخله جنات تجري من تحتها الأنهار خالدين فيها أبدا ذلك الفوز العظيم

translation: But as for those who disbelieved and denied our signs, they are the companions of the fire, abiding therein eternally, and it is an evil destination.
interpretation: The verse describes the fate of those who disbelieved in God and denied His signs. It states that they will be the companions of the fire, a metaphor for hell, and will remain there eternally. The verse emphasizes the severity of their actions and the dire consequences they will face. It serves as a warning to those who reject God's message and a reminder of the eternal punishment that awaits them.
orig: والذين كفروا وكذبوا بآياتنا أولئك أصحاب النار خالدين فيها وبئس المصير

translation: No calamity befalls on the earth or in yourselves but it is inscribed in the Book of Decrees before We bring it into existence. Verily, that is easy for Allah. So, whatever you have missed, and whatever has been taken away from you, is known to Allah. And whatever befalls you of disaster, it is because of what your hands have earned. And He pardons much.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the power and knowledge of God, who has predestined all events, both good and bad. The verse explains that whatever happens to people or the earth is already written in the 'Book of Decrees' before it happens. The verse reminds people that whatever they may miss or lose is known to God. The verse also states that any disaster that befalls people is a result of their own actions. However, the verse also highlights God's mercy and forgiveness, as He forgives much. The verse ultimately serves as a reminder of God's power, knowledge, and mercy, and encourages people to reflect on their actions and seek God's forgiveness.
orig: ما أصاب من مصيبة إلا بإذن الله ومن يؤمن بالله يهد قلبه والله بكل شيء عليم

translation: And obey Allah and obey the Messenger and if you turn away - then indeed, upon the Messenger is only the clear conveyance.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of obedience to Allah and His Messenger. It reminds the believers that if they choose to disobey, the responsibility for conveying the message clearly and truthfully lies solely with the Messenger. The verse serves as a warning to those who reject the message, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the ultimate accountability to Allah.
orig: وأطيعوا الله وأطيعوا الرسول فإن توليتم فإنما على رسولنا البلاغ المبين

translation: Surely, Allah is our Lord and your Lord; so, upon Allah should the believers rely.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the oneness of God and the belief that He is the Lord of all. It commands the believers to put their trust and reliance in Allah. The verse serves as a reminder that Allah is the ultimate source of guidance and protection for the believers, and that they should seek His help in all their affairs.
orig: الله لا إله إلا هو وعلى الله فليتوكل المؤمنون

translation: O you who have believed, indeed among your wives and your children are enemies for you, so beware of them. And if you pardon and overlook and forgive - then indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: The verse warns believers that some of their spouses and children may be their enemies and advises them to be cautious of them. Despite this warning, the verse encourages forgiveness and patience, stating that if the believers pardon, overlook, and forgive, then they will find that Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا إن من أزواجكم وأولادكم عدوا لكم فاحذروهم وإن تعفوا وتصفحوا وتغفروا فإن الله غفور رحيم

translation: Indeed, your wealth and your children are but a trial, and with God is a great reward.
interpretation: The verse highlights that wealth and children, which may often be seen as sources of happiness and security, are actually a test or trial from God. This is a reminder that material possessions and family ties can often lead people astray from the path of righteousness, and can become a source of arrogance and selfishness. The verse offers reassurance that God is aware of this trial and that those who remain steadfast in their faith and avoid becoming overly attached to worldly possessions will be rewarded with a great reward in the hereafter.
orig: إنما أموالكم وأولادكم فتنة والله عنده أجر عظيم

translation: And fear Allah as much as you are able and listen and obey and spend (in the way of Allah); it is better for yourselves. And whoever is protected from the stinginess of his soul - it is those who will be the successful.
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to fear and worship God as much as they are able and to listen, obey, and be generous. It emphasizes the importance of being mindful of one's actions and being generous, as it is beneficial for one's own self. The verse also highlights the concept of self-restraint and the danger of being stingy and selfish. It suggests that those who are able to control their selfish desires and are generous will be the ones who will be successful in the hereafter.
orig: فاتقوا الله ما استطعتم واسمعوا وأطيعوا وأنفقوا خيرا لأنفسكم ومن يوق شح نفسه فأولئك هم المفلحون

translation: If you loan Allah a goodly loan, He will double it for you and will forgive you. And Allah is most Appreciating, Forbearing.
interpretation: The verse encourages the act of giving loans or charity for the sake of Allah, emphasizing that it is a virtuous deed that will be rewarded generously. The reward for such a loan is not only the doubling of the amount by Allah, but also the forgiveness of sins. The verse highlights Allah's attributes of being Appreciative and Forbearing, indicating that He recognizes and rewards good deeds, and that He is patient and understanding towards human weaknesses and shortcomings.
orig: إن تقرضوا الله قرضا حسنا يضاعفه لكم ويغفر لكم والله شكور حليم

translation: The Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, the Exalted in Might, the Wise.
interpretation: The verse is a description of one of the attributes of God. It asserts that God has knowledge of both the unseen (ghayb) and the witnessed (shahada) realms. The unseen realm includes all that is hidden from human perception, such as the inner thoughts and intentions of people, while the witnessed realm includes all that can be perceived through the senses. The verse also attributes to God the qualities of being Exalted in Might (al-'Aziz) and Wise (al-Hakim), emphasizing God's power and knowledge. These attributes serve to emphasize God's greatness and majesty, and to remind believers of God's omniscience and omnipotence.
orig: عالم الغيب والشهادة العزيز الحكيم

translation: O Prophet, when you divorce women, divorce them for their waiting period and count the waiting period accurately, and fear Allah, your Lord. And do not turn them out of their houses, nor should they leave themselves, except that they commit a clear immorality. And those are the limits of Allah. And whoever exceeds the limits of Allah has certainly wronged himself. You do not know; perhaps Allah will bring about after that a matter.
interpretation: The verse gives instructions to the Prophet Muhammad on how to handle divorce, emphasizing the importance of following the proper waiting period and treating the divorced women with respect and fairness. The verse forbids turning women out of their homes or forcing them to leave, except in cases of clear immorality. The verse also emphasizes the importance of respecting the limits set by God and warns against exceeding them, as doing so would bring harm to oneself. The verse ends by reminding that only God knows what will happen in the future.
orig: يا أيها النبي إذا طلقتم النساء فطلقوهن لعدتهن وأحصوا العدة واتقوا الله ربكم لا تخرجوهن من بيوتهن ولا يخرجن إلا أن يأتين بفاحشة مبينة وتلك حدود الله ومن يتعد حدود الله فقد ظلم نفسه لا تدري لعل الله يحدث بعد ذلك أمرا

translation: And when their appointed term comes, then collect (them) in a fair way, and set free (them) in a fair way. And observe the contact with them (i.e., the covenant) as due from you. Surely Allah is aware of what you do. And (as for) him who fears Allah, He will make for him a way out (from difficulties),
interpretation: This verse sets out the rules for the treatment of women during and after a divorce. When the waiting period (appointed term) is over, the husband should either keep his wife in a fair way, meaning treat her kindly and justly, or set her free in a fair way, meaning giving her a fair divorce settlement. The husband is also instructed to fulfill any covenants or agreements made with his wife. The verse emphasizes the importance of treating one's spouse justly and with kindness, and it reminds the believers that God is aware of their actions. The verse also offers a promise of divine help and guidance for those who fear and respect God, indicating that God will provide a way out of difficulties for those who are mindful of Him.
orig: فإذا بلغن أجلهن فأمسكوهن بمعروف أو فارقوهن بمعروف وأشهدوا ذوي عدل منكم وأقيموا الشهادة لله ذلكم يوعظ به من كان يؤمن بالله واليوم الآخر ومن يتق الله يجعل له مخرجا

translation: And gives him provision from (sources) he knows not. And if he is trustful in Allah, sufficient is (Allah) for him. Indeed, Allah has already made a promise (to provide) for him. Indeed, Allah will surely accomplish His promise. And Allah has already set a measure for all things.
interpretation: The verse speaks about God's provision for His servants, emphasizing that God provides for them from sources that they are not aware of. The verse encourages trust and dependence on God, stating that He is sufficient for those who rely on Him. The verse also highlights God's promise to provide for His servants and His ability to fulfill that promise. The verse concludes by stating that God has set a measure for all things, emphasizing the order and wisdom in God's creation.
orig: ويرزقه من حيث لا يحتسب ومن يتوكل على الله فهو حسبه إن الله بالغ أمره قد جعل الله لكل شيء قدرا

translation: And for those of your women who fear menstruation, if you doubt, then their count is three months, and [also] for those who do not menstruate from among your wives, their term is three months; and for those who are pregnant, their term is until they give birth.
