interpretation: The verse outlines the waiting period (`iddah) for different categories of women: those who fear menstruation, those who do not menstruate, and those who are pregnant. The `iddah for those who fear menstruation or do not menstruate is three months, while the `iddah for those who are pregnant is until they give birth. The verse emphasizes the importance of treating women fairly and with respect during this period, and it serves as a guide for the regulation of marital and family life in accordance with Islamic law.
orig: واللائي يئسن من المحيض من نسائكم إن ارتبتم فعدتهن ثلاثة أشهر واللائي لم يحضن وأولات الأحمال أجلهن أن يضعن حملهن ومن يتق الله يجعل له من أمره يسرا

translation: That is the command of God which He has sent down to you (O Muhammad). And whoever fears God and keeps his duty to Him, He will remit his sins from him, and will enlarge his reward.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of fearing and obeying God, and the great rewards that come from doing so. The command referred to in the verse is the guidance and teachings brought by the Prophet Muhammad. Those who follow this guidance and fear God will have their sins forgiven and their rewards increased. This verse serves as a reminder of the importance of piety and obedience to God and the great blessings that come from following His commandments.
orig: ذلك أمر الله أنزله إليكم ومن يتق الله يكفر عنه سيئاته ويعظم له أجرا

translation: Reside in it [i.e., the holy land of Palestine] as you would have resided in it before, and fear Allah. And fear Me concerning the Symblic [i.e., the Kaaba at Mecca]. And give to the kindred his due, and to the poor and the wayfarer, and do not squander wastefully. Indeed, the wasteful are brothers of the devils, and ever has Satan been to his Lord ungrateful. And if you are in poverty, Allah will enrich you from His bounty, if He wills. Indeed, Allah is Expert in all things. And remember the favor of Allah upon you and His covenant with which He bound you when you said, 'We hear and we obey'; and fear Allah. Indeed, Allah knows very well what is within the breasts.
interpretation: This verse is a set of instructions given to the Muslims who are residing in the holy land of Palestine. It starts by telling them to reside there as they used to before, but with the fear of Allah. It also reminds them to be mindful of the Kaaba at Mecca. The verse then emphasizes the importance of fulfilling obligations towards relatives and the needy, and avoiding wasteful spending. It warns against becoming like the devils who are ungrateful towards their Lord. The verse also reassures the Muslims that if they are in poverty, Allah will enrich them from His bounty. The verse ends by reminding the Muslims of Allah's favor upon them and the covenant they made with Him, urging them to fear Allah and be mindful of their obligations towards Him.
orig: أسكنوهن من حيث سكنتم من وجدكم ولا تضاروهن لتضيقوا عليهن وإن كن أولات حمل فأنفقوا عليهن حتى يضعن حملهن فإن أرضعن لكم فآتوهن أجورهن وأتمروا بينكم بمعروف وإن تعاسرتم فسترضع له أخرى

translation: Let the one who has been given much of sustenance spend from what God has given him, and let him not be stingy. And the one who is stingy is only stingy to himself. And God is self-sufficient and praiseworthy. He will make things easy after difficulty.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the importance of giving and spending in the way of God, and the consequences of being stingy. The verse encourages those who have been given much by God to be generous and spend from their wealth. It emphasizes that God does not burden a soul beyond its capacity and that being stingy only harms oneself. The verse ends with a promise from God that He will make things easy after difficulty, indicating that generosity will be rewarded and that God will provide for those who give. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of being generous and the blessings that come from giving.
orig: لينفق ذو سعة من سعته ومن قدر عليه رزقه فلينفق مما آتاه الله لا يكلف الله نفسا إلا ما آتاها سيجعل الله بعد عسر يسرا

translation: But how many a town have We destroyed which was unjust to its Lord, so We took retribution from it, and to it returned after its destruction [the people] unto Us.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust to their Lord and rejected God's messengers. The verse emphasizes the severe punishment that was inflicted upon these towns and the return of their people to God after their destruction. The verse serves as a reminder of the consequences of disbelief and rejection of God's messengers and the ultimate accountability to God on the Day of Judgment.
orig: وكأين من قرية عتت عن أمر ربها ورسله فحاسبناها حسابا شديدا وعذبناها عذابا نكرا

translation: Tasted the evil result of her affair, and was punished for her disobedience.
interpretation: The verse speaks about a woman who experienced the bitter consequences of her actions and was punished for her disobedience. The verse highlights the negative outcome of the woman's actions, indicating that her disobedience led to her downfall. The verse serves as a warning to those who choose to disobey God's commands, reminding them of the negative consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: فذاقت وبال أمرها وكان عاقبة أمرها خسرا

translation: Allah has prepared for them a severe punishment. So fear Allah, O you of understanding who have believed. Indeed, Allah has sent down to you a reminder.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the severe punishment that Allah has prepared for those who disbelieve and do not fear Him. The verse addresses those who are believers and have understanding, urging them to fear Allah and take the reminder (the Quran) that has been sent down to them seriously. The verse serves as a warning to the believers not to follow the ways of the disbelievers and a reminder to fear Allah and be mindful of their actions.
orig: أعد الله لهم عذابا شديدا فاتقوا الله يا أولي الألباب الذين آمنوا قد أنزل الله إليكم ذكرا

translation: A Messenger recites to you clear verses from your Lord so that those who believe and do righteous deeds may be extracted from the darknesses into the light. And whoever believes in Allah and does righteousness - He will admit them to gardens beneath which rivers flow, wherein they will abide forever. Indeed, Allah has prepared for them a noble provision.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the role of the Messenger in reciting the verses of Allah to the people, and the impact of these verses on the believers who do righteous deeds. The verse emphasizes the contrast between darkness and light, symbolizing the transformation of the believers from a state of ignorance and misguidance to a state of enlightenment and guidance. The verse also highlights the reward for those who believe and do good deeds, which is eternal paradise with flowing rivers. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of faith and good deeds, and the blessings that await those who follow the path of righteousness.
orig: رسولا يتلو عليكم آيات الله مبينات ليخرج الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات من الظلمات إلى النور ومن يؤمن بالله ويعمل صالحا يدخله جنات تجري من تحتها الأنهار خالدين فيها أبدا قد أحسن الله له رزقا

translation: It is Allah who has created seven heavens and of the earth a similar number. Through the midst of them (all) descends His command: that you may know that Allah has power over all things, and that Allah comprehends all things in (His) knowledge.
interpretation: The verse highlights the power and knowledge of Allah by describing the creation of seven heavens and seven earths, and stating that Allah's command descends through the midst of them. This serves to emphasize Allah's control and authority over all things. The verse also states that Allah has power over all things and that Allah encompasses all things in knowledge, reinforcing the idea of Allah's all-encompassing power and knowledge.
orig: الله الذي خلق سبع سماوات ومن الأرض مثلهن يتنزل الأمر بينهن لتعلموا أن الله على كل شيء قدير وأن الله قد أحاط بكل شيء علما

translation: O Prophet, why do you prohibit what God has made lawful for you, seeking the pleasure of your wives? And God is Forgiving, Merciful.
interpretation: The verse addresses the Prophet Muhammad and advises him not to prohibit himself from things that God has made lawful for him. The verse suggests that the Prophet's motivation for this prohibition is to seek the pleasure of his wives. The verse ends by reminding the Prophet of God's forgiveness and mercy towards his servants.
orig: يا أيها النبي لم تحرم ما أحل الله لك تبتغي مرضات أزواجك والله غفور رحيم

translation: Allah has already ordained for you the dissolution of your oaths. And Allah is your protector, and He is the Knowing, the Wise.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the dissolution of oaths and reminds the believers that Allah is their protector and is all-knowing and wise. The verse implies that if an oath or a pledge causes harm or injustice, it can be dissolved or broken. This interpretation is supported by the following Hadith: 'The Prophet (peace be upon him) said: 'The oath is the binding tie of Allah, so do not break it. But if anyone breaks it, let him give compensation.' (Bukhari, Book 78, Hadith 620). The verse also emphasizes that Allah is the protector of the believers, and that He is all-knowing and wise, indicating that He knows the circumstances and intentions of the believers, and will guide them to the right decision.
orig: قد فرض الله لكم تحلة أيمانكم والله مولاكم وهو العليم الحكيم

translation: And when the Prophet disclosed a matter to one of his wives and when she made it known, and Allah informed him of it, he made clear a part of it and turned away from a part. And when he informed her of it, she said, 'Who informed you of this?' He said, 'The Knowing, the Informed [One] informed me.'
interpretation: The verse describes a situation where the Prophet Muhammad shared a secret with one of his wives, but she revealed it. When the Prophet was informed of her betrayal, he confronted her and revealed only part of the truth, while hiding the rest. When she asked him how he knew of her betrayal, he responded by saying that Allah, the All-Knowing and All-Aware, had informed him. The verse emphasizes the Prophet's trustworthiness and the importance of keeping secrets. It also highlights the all-knowing nature of Allah and his ability to reveal the truth, even when it is hidden.
orig: وإذ أسر النبي إلى بعض أزواجه حديثا فلما نبأت به وأظهره الله عليه عرف بعضه وأعرض عن بعض فلما نبأها به قالت من أنبأك هذا قال نبأني العليم الخبير

translation: Indeed, if you repent to Allah, your hearts will be satisfied, but if you continue to deny Him - then indeed, Allah is the Disposer of all things, and upon Him rests the dominion of the heavens and the earth. And Allah is over all things competent.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the power of repentance and the consequences of denying God. If one were to repent to God, their hearts will find peace. However, if they continue to deny God, then God has the power to dispose of all things and has control over the heavens and the earth. The verse emphasizes that God is all-powerful and capable of handling all things, and serves as a reminder of the importance of repentance and turning towards God.
orig: إن تتوبا إلى الله فقد صغت قلوبكما وإن تظاهرا عليه فإن الله هو مولاه وجبريل وصالح المؤمنين والملائكة بعد ذلك ظهير

translation: Perhaps, if he divorces you, his Lord will give him in your place spouses better than you, submissive, believing, pious, penitent, inclined to fasting, widows and virgins.
interpretation: This verse speaks about the possibility of a husband being given better spouses by God if he divorces his current wife. The qualities of these potential spouses are listed, including their submissiveness, faith, piety, repentance, dedication to worship, and status as widows or virgins. The verse may serve as a reminder to the wife of the importance of maintaining a righteous and pious character, and to the husband of the blessings that come with a righteous spouse. It may also serve as a warning to those who are hasty in divorce, reminding them of the potential consequences and the possibility of being replaced with someone better.
orig: عسى ربه إن طلقكن أن يبدله أزواجا خيرا منكن مسلمات مؤمنات قانتات تائبات عابدات سائحات ثيبات وأبكارا

translation: O you who have believed, protect yourselves and your families from a Fire whose fuel is people and stones, over which are [angels] severe and relentless, who do not disobey Allah in what He commands them but do what they are commanded.
interpretation: The verse commands the believers to protect themselves and their families from the Fire of Hell, which is fueled by people and stones. The verse warns of the severe and relentless angels that are over the Fire and who carry out the commands of Allah without disobedience. The verse emphasizes the importance of obedience to Allah and following His commands, as the angels do. The verse also highlights the serious consequences of disobedience and the reality of the Fire of Hell as a punishment for those who do not believe or commit sins.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا قوا أنفسكم وأهليكم نارا وقودها الناس والحجارة عليها ملائكة غلاظ شداد لا يعصون الله ما أمرهم ويفعلون ما يؤمرون

translation: O you who disbelieve, do not claim today that you were unaware [of the consequences of your disbelief]. You are only receiving what you used to do.
interpretation: The verse addresses the disbelievers and reminds them that they will not be able to claim ignorance on the Day of Judgment. They will receive the consequences of their actions and will not be able to offer any excuses. The verse emphasizes the importance of accountability and the inevitability of justice. It serves as a warning to those who deny the truth and encourages them to reflect on their actions and seek forgiveness before it is too late.
orig: يا أيها الذين كفروا لا تعتذروا اليوم إنما تجزون ما كنتم تعملون

translation: O you who have believed, repent to Allah with sincere repentance. Perhaps your Lord will remove from you your misdeeds and admit you to gardens beneath which rivers flow on the Day when Allah will not disgrace the Prophet and those who believed with him. Their light will proceed before them and on their right; they will say, 'Our Lord, perfect for us our light and forgive us. Indeed, You are over all things competent.'
interpretation: The verse calls upon the believers to repent to Allah with sincere repentance, holding out the possibility that their sins may be forgiven and they may be admitted to gardens beneath which rivers flow. The verse highlights the importance of repentance and the great reward that it brings. The verse also mentions the Prophet and the believers who are with him, emphasizing the importance of the community and the role of the Prophet as a leader. The verse ends with a prayer for the light of the believers to be perfected and for their sins to be forgiven, indicating the importance of seeking Allah's forgiveness and guidance.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا توبوا إلى الله توبة نصوحا عسى ربكم أن يكفر عنكم سيئاتكم ويدخلكم جنات تجري من تحتها الأنهار يوم لا يخزي الله النبي والذين آمنوا معه نورهم يسعى بين أيديهم وبأيمانهم يقولون ربنا أتمم لنا نورنا واغفر لنا إنك على كل شيء قدير

translation: O Prophet, strive against the disbelievers and the hypocrites, and be harsh against them. Their final abode is Hell, and what a terrible destination.
interpretation: The verse commands the Prophet Muhammad to strive against the disbelievers and the hypocrites, and to be firm and unyielding in his stance against them. The verse emphasizes the severity of their actions and the consequences they will face, which is eternal damnation in Hell. The verse serves as a reminder to the Prophet and the believers of the importance of standing firm against those who reject the message of Islam and spread discord among the community.
orig: يا أيها النبي جاهد الكفار والمنافقين واغلظ عليهم ومأواهم جهنم وبئس المصير

translation: Allah sets forth an example for those who disbelieve: the wife of Noah and the wife of Lot. They were under two of Our righteous servants, but they both betrayed them. So they (the servants) availed them (their wives) not against Allah at all, and it was said: 'Enter the Fire with those who enter.'
interpretation: The verse sets forth the examples of the wives of Noah and Lot as a warning for those who disbelieve. Despite being married to righteous men, they both betrayed their husbands and were ultimately punished for their actions. The verse emphasizes the powerlessness of the two women in the face of God's punishment and the finality of their fate. The verse serves as a reminder that there is no protection from God's wrath except through righteousness and obedience.
orig: ضرب الله مثلا للذين كفروا امرأت نوح وامرأت لوط كانتا تحت عبدين من عبادنا صالحين فخانتاهما فلم يغنيا عنهما من الله شيئا وقيل ادخلا النار مع الداخلين

translation: And God sets forth, for those who believe, the example of the wife of Pharaoh, when she said, 'My Lord, build for me near You a house in Paradise, and deliver me from Pharaoh and his deeds, and deliver me from the wrongdoing people.'
interpretation: The verse uses the story of the wife of Pharaoh as an example for believers. She calls upon God to build a house for her near Him in Paradise, and to save her from Pharaoh and his actions, as well as from the unjust people. This verse emphasizes the importance of seeking refuge and protection from evil and unjust people, and the ultimate desire to be in the presence of God in Paradise. It encourages believers to have faith and to call upon God in times of hardship and oppression, and to strive for righteousness and deliverance from wrongdoing.
orig: وضرب الله مثلا للذين آمنوا امرأت فرعون إذ قالت رب ابن لي عندك بيتا في الجنة ونجني من فرعون وعمله ونجني من القوم الظالمين

translation: And Mary, daughter of 'Imran, who guarded her chastity, so We breathed into her of Our spirit and she confirmed the words of her Lord and His Books and was one of the devout.
interpretation: The verse speaks about Mary, the mother of Jesus, and her virtues of chastity, faith, and devotion. The verse highlights that Mary was chosen by God and was granted a special status among women. The verse emphasizes Mary's purity and her commitment to her faith, as she guarded her chastity and confirmed the words of her Lord. The verse also mentions that Mary was one of the devout, indicating her strong and unwavering faith in God. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of faith, devotion, and purity in Islam.
orig: ومريم ابنت عمران التي أحصنت فرجها فنفخنا فيه من روحنا وصدقت بكلمات ربها وكتبه وكانت من القانتين

translation: Blessed is He in Whose hand is the kingdom, and He is over all things competent.
interpretation: The verse is a praise of God's power and sovereignty over all things. The phrase 'Blessed is He in Whose hand is the kingdom' is a recognition of God's ultimate authority and control over the universe. The statement 'and He is over all things competent' further emphasizes God's ability to manage and oversee all affairs, big or small. The verse serves as a reminder of God's greatness and the need for humans to submit to His will.
orig: تبارك الذي بيده الملك وهو على كل شيء قدير

translation: He who created death and life to test which of you is best in deed, and He is the Exalted in Might, the Forgiving.
interpretation: The verse speaks about God's creation of both life and death as a test for humanity, to see who among them will perform the best deeds. The verse emphasizes God's power and greatness, as the Exalted in Might, and His mercy, as the Forgiving. The verse encourages people to strive for excellence in their actions and reminds them that they will be held accountable for their deeds. The ultimate goal of the test is to distinguish between right and wrong, good and evil, and to reward those who pass the test with eternal life.
orig: الذي خلق الموت والحياة ليبلوكم أيكم أحسن عملا وهو العزيز الغفور

translation: Who created seven heavens in layers. You see no inconsistency in the creation of the Merciful. Then look again: do you see any flaw?
interpretation: The verse highlights the perfection and complexity of God's creation, specifically the seven heavens that are layered in a harmonious and consistent manner. The verse challenges the reader to find any inconsistency or flaw in God's creation, implying that it is impossible to do so. The verse serves as a reminder of God's power and greatness, emphasizing the importance of recognizing and submitting to His will.
orig: الذي خلق سبع سماوات طباقا ما ترى في خلق الرحمن من تفاوت فارجع البصر هل ترى من فطور

translation: Then turn your gaze twice, your gaze will return to you humbled and dejected.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the experience of a person who is struck with awe and humility after witnessing the power and majesty of God. The act of 'turning the gaze twice' suggests an intense and prolonged observation that leads to a profound realization of one's own insignificance and vulnerability. The phrase 'your gaze will return to you humbled and dejected' highlights the emotional impact of this experience, which leaves the person feeling small and defeated. The verse invites the reader to reflect on the limits of human knowledge and power, and to recognize the transcendence and sovereignty of God.
orig: ثم ارجع البصر كرتين ينقلب إليك البصر خاسئا وهو حسير

translation: And We have adorned the lowest heaven with lamps, and We have made them missiles for the devils, and We have prepared for them the punishment of the Blaze.
interpretation: The verse describes the beauty of the lower heaven, which is adorned with lamps. These lamps serve as a means of guidance and light for people on earth. At the same time, the verse mentions that the lamps are also used as missiles against the devils, indicating that they serve as a protection for the people and the world from the harm and influence of the devils. The verse ends by stating that a severe punishment has been prepared for the devils, which is described as the punishment of the Blaze. This punishment serves as a reminder of the consequences of disobedience and rebellion against God.
orig: ولقد زينا السماء الدنيا بمصابيح وجعلناها رجوما للشياطين وأعتدنا لهم عذاب السعير

translation: For those who disbelieve in their Lord, there is the punishment of Hell, and evil is the destination.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the punishment of Hell that awaits those who disbelieve in their Lord. It emphasizes the wretched and miserable end that awaits such people. The verse serves as a warning to those who reject or deny the existence of God, reminding them of the severe consequences of their disbelief and the eternal nature of the punishment that awaits them.
orig: وللذين كفروا بربهم عذاب جهنم وبئس المصير

translation: When they hear it, they will hear its sound like a rushing of water and the mooing of cattle.
interpretation: The verse describes the sound that the people will hear when a specific event takes place. The sound is compared to the rushing of water and the mooing of cattle, which suggests a loud and overwhelming noise. The use of these comparisons helps to create a vivid and memorable image in the reader's mind. The interpretation of this verse depends on the context in which it appears, but it could be seen as a warning or a description of a divine intervention. Regardless of the specific interpretation, the verse emphasizes the power and impact of the sound, which is sure to get the attention of those who hear it.
orig: إذا ألقوا فيها سمعوا لها شهيقا وهي تفور

translation: He (God) frowned and turned away, because there came to him the blind man (Muhammad), (wanting to learn), whereupon he said, 'Why does this one come to me?'
interpretation: The verse describes an incident where the Prophet Muhammad, who was receiving revelation from God, was approached by a blind man seeking knowledge. The Prophet was initially frustrated by the interruption, hence the mention of him frowning and turning away. However, the verse serves as a reminder for the Prophet and all believers to be patient and kind, even when they are occupied or inconvenienced. It emphasizes the importance of spreading knowledge and helping those who seek it, regardless of their circumstances.
orig: تكاد تميز من الغيظ كلما ألقي فيها فوج سألهم خزنتها ألم يأتكم نذير

translation: They said, 'Yes, indeed, a warner has come to us.' But we denied him and said, 'You are not but a fabricated falsehood.' And indeed, we do not believe that any revelation has come from God. You are nothing but in great error.'
interpretation: The verse describes the response of the disbelievers to the warning of a prophet or messenger. Despite acknowledging that a warner has come to them, they deny and reject him, accusing him of being a fabricated falsehood. They express their disbelief in the revelation from God, asserting that the prophet is nothing but in great error. The verse highlights the rejection and denial of the truth by those who refuse to believe, and the consequences of their disbelief in the revelation from God.
orig: قالوا بلى قد جاءنا نذير فكذبنا وقلنا ما نزل الله من شيء إن أنتم إلا في ضلال كبير

translation: And they said, 'If only we had heard or understood, we would not be among the companions of the blaze.'
interpretation: The verse is a statement made by the unbelievers, expressing their regret for not having listened to or understood the message of the prophet. They recognize that if they had listened or understood, they would not be facing the punishment of being among the companions of the blaze (a reference to hellfire). The verse highlights the importance of listening to and understanding the message of the prophet and the consequences of not doing so. It serves as a reminder to the believers to be mindful of the message and to heed the warnings of the prophet.
orig: وقالوا لو كنا نسمع أو نعقل ما كنا في أصحاب السعير

translation: So acknowledge your guilt, for you are of those who will be led to the Blaze.
interpretation: The verse is a warning to those who refuse to acknowledge their sins and wrongdoings. The phrase 'you are of those who will be led to the Blaze' refers to the punishment that awaits such individuals in the afterlife. The verse highlights the importance of taking responsibility for one's actions and recognizing the consequences of sin. It serves as a reminder of the importance of repentance and seeking forgiveness, as those who do not may face severe consequences for their actions.
orig: فاعترفوا بذنبهم فسحقا لأصحاب السعير

translation: Indeed, those who fear their Lord in secret will have forgiveness and a great reward.
interpretation: The verse highlights the importance of having fear and reverence for God, even in private and in secret. Those who have this fear of their Lord will be granted forgiveness and a great reward. The verse encourages believers to maintain their piety and devotion to God, even when no one is watching, and to trust in the promise of God's reward for their actions.
orig: إن الذين يخشون ربهم بالغيب لهم مغفرة وأجر كبير

translation: And hide your conversation or proclaim it, indeed, He is Knowing of that within the breasts.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the believers being given the choice to either hide or proclaim their conversation (belief or worship) as God is aware of what is within their hearts. This verse emphasizes the all-knowing nature of God, who is aware of the inner thoughts and intentions of individuals. It serves as a reminder that one's faith and actions should be true and sincere, regardless of whether they are hidden or public, as God is aware of both.
orig: وأسروا قولكم أو اجهروا به إنه عليم بذات الصدور

translation: Does He who created not know, while He is the All-Knower, the Most Subtle and Aware?
interpretation: The verse questions whether the One who created (referring to God) does not have knowledge, while He is the All-Knower, the Most Subtle and Aware. This verse emphasizes God's all-encompassing knowledge and awareness, and the idea that nothing escapes His notice. The verse serves as a reminder that God's creation and knowledge are not separate but rather that God has complete and perfect knowledge of all that He has created.
orig: ألا يعلم من خلق وهو اللطيف الخبير

translation: It is He who has made the earth subservient to you, so walk among its slopes and eat of His provision, and to Him is the resurrection.
interpretation: The verse highlights God's power and generosity by reminding people of His role in providing them with a fertile earth that sustains their lives. The verse encourages people to enjoy the bounties of the earth and to appreciate God's blessings. At the same time, the verse reminds people that they will ultimately return to God, who is the source of all life and the ultimate judge of all actions. The verse encourages people to live in harmony with the earth and to use its resources responsibly, recognizing that they are accountable to God for their actions.
orig: هو الذي جعل لكم الأرض ذلولا فامشوا في مناكبها وكلوا من رزقه وإليه النشور

translation: Have you considered him who took his pleasure in his transgression, while he saw the punishment as distant?
interpretation: The verse speaks about a person who indulged in sin and transgression, and yet, remained unconcerned about the consequences of their actions. The verse highlights the individual's denial of the impending punishment, as they viewed it as distant and unlikely to occur. This verse serves as a warning to those who engage in sinful behavior and become complacent, thinking that they will not be held accountable for their actions. It reminds them that God's punishment is inevitable and that they should not ignore the signs of their wrongdoing.
orig: أأمنتم من في السماء أن يخسف بكم الأرض فإذا هي تمور

translation: Or have you considered the one in the heaven that His punishment may come to you by morning or by afternoon?
interpretation: The verse speaks about the impending punishment from the one in the heavens, referring to God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the punishment, which may come by morning or by afternoon, indicating that people will have no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in disbelief and disregard for God's signs, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: أم أمنتم من في السماء أن يرسل عليكم حاصبا فستعلمون كيف نذير

translation: And indeed, those before them also lied, so how was the outcome for them?
interpretation: The verse is a reminder and a warning to those who deny the truth and reject faith, just as previous nations had done before them. The phrase 'how was the outcome for them' is a rhetorical question that implies that the fate of the disbelievers is always one of punishment and destruction. The verse serves as a warning to the listeners and readers to reflect on the consequences of their actions and to turn away from falsehood and unbelief towards the truth and faith.
orig: ولقد كذب الذين من قبلهم فكيف كان نكير

translation: Or have they not seen the birds above them, with wings outstretched, and [how] He [Allah] supports them? And none holds them up except the Most Merciful. Indeed, He is, of all things, Seeing.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the power and control of Allah, using the example of birds in flight. The verse asks if people have not seen the birds with their outstretched wings, and notes that it is only through the will of Allah that they are able to fly. The verse emphasizes the all-seeing and all-knowing nature of Allah, who sees and controls all things. The verse serves as a reminder of the power and greatness of Allah, and the dependence of all creation on His will and mercy.
orig: أولم يروا إلى الطير فوقهم صافات ويقبضن ما يمسكهن إلا الرحمن إنه بكل شيء بصير

translation: Is this he who is an army for you to aid you against the Recompense from Allah? The disbelievers are not but in delusion.
interpretation: The verse is a rhetorical question addressed to those who rely on their worldly power and alliances for protection, rather than putting their trust in Allah. The verse suggests that such reliance is misguided, as the so-called 'army' will not be able to protect them from the Recompense (punishment) of Allah. The verse also implies that those who deny or disbelieve in Allah are deluded or living in a state of false security. The verse serves as a reminder that ultimate power and protection belong to Allah, and that those who deny this fact are misguided and deluded.
orig: أمن هذا الذي هو جند لكم ينصركم من دون الرحمن إن الكافرون إلا في غرور

translation: Is he who provides for you if he withholds his provision, are you then in ungratefulness dissatisfied?
interpretation: The verse addresses the attitude of people towards their sustenance provider, questioning whether they become ungrateful and dissatisfied when their sustenance is withheld. The verse emphasizes the importance of being grateful for the blessings received and not taking them for granted. It serves as a reminder that the provider of sustenance has the power to withhold it, and that ingratitude and dissatisfaction are signs of a lack of faith and trust in God's wisdom and justice.
orig: أمن هذا الذي يرزقكم إن أمسك رزقه بل لجوا في عتو ونفور

translation: Or is he who walks while bowed, his head bowed in humility, more guided, or he who walks proudly upon a straight path?
interpretation: The verse contrasts two types of people: those who walk with humility and those who walk with pride. The person who walks with humility is described as having their head bowed, while the person who walks with pride is described as walking proudly. The verse asks which of these two people is more guided. The verse emphasizes the importance of humility and the dangers of pride. It suggests that those who are humble and mindful of God are on the right path, while those who are proud and arrogant may be straying from the path of guidance.
orig: أفمن يمشي مكبا على وجهه أهدى أمن يمشي سويا على صراط مستقيم

translation: Say, 'It is He who has created you, and endowed you with hearing, sight, and hearts; little thanks you give!'
interpretation: The verse is a command to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to declare that it is God who has created human beings and given them the faculties of hearing, sight, and understanding. The verse highlights the ingratitude of human beings, who fail to express gratitude for the blessings they have received. The verse serves as a reminder of the greatness of God and the smallness of human beings, and encourages believers to be mindful of their duties towards their Creator and to express gratitude for the blessings they have received.
orig: قل هو الذي أنشأكم وجعل لكم السمع والأبصار والأفئدة قليلا ما تشكرون

translation: Say, 'It is He who has produced you on the earth, and to Him you will be gathered back.'
interpretation: The verse emphasizes God's role as the creator of all life and the ultimate destination of all souls. By saying 'It is He who has produced you on the earth', the verse reminds people of their origins and their dependence on God for their existence. The second part of the verse, 'and to Him you will be gathered back', serves as a reminder of the transience of life and the inevitability of death. The verse can be interpreted as a call for people to remember God and to prepare for the afterlife, as it highlights the ultimate destination of all souls and the ultimate power of God over all creation.
orig: قل هو الذي ذرأكم في الأرض وإليه تحشرون

translation: And they say, 'When will this promise be (fulfilled), if you are truthful?'
interpretation: The verse is spoken from the perspective of the disbelievers who are questioning the promise of God and the believers who are reminding them of it. The disbelievers are skeptical and doubtful about the promise of God, and they are challenging the believers to prove the truth of their message by asking 'when' the promise will be fulfilled. The verse highlights the lack of faith and the denial of the disbelievers, and the patience and steadfastness of the believers in the face of adversity.
orig: ويقولون متى هذا الوعد إن كنتم صادقين

translation: Say, 'Indeed, the knowledge is only with Allah, and indeed, I am only a clear warner.'
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the ultimate source of all knowledge, which is God. The speaker, who is believed to be the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), acknowledges his own limitations and admits that his role is merely to convey the message of God as a clear and distinct warner. This verse can be seen as a reminder of the limits of human knowledge and understanding, and the importance of relying on divine guidance and revelation for ultimate truth and wisdom.
orig: قل إنما العلم عند الله وإنما أنا نذير مبين

translation: But when they saw it, they despised it and turned away their faces in disgust, and said, 'This is clearly magic!'
interpretation: The verse describes the reaction of the disbelievers when they saw a sign or miracle from God. Instead of being open-minded and considering the possibility that it could be a message from a higher power, they immediately rejected it and turned away in disgust. They dismissed it as 'clearly magic', indicating their closed-mindedness and unwillingness to consider any perspective other than their own. The verse serves as a reminder that those who reject God's signs and messages will face consequences for their disbelief and rejection.
orig: فلما رأوه زلفة سيئت وجوه الذين كفروا وقيل هذا الذي كنتم به تدعون

translation: Say, 'Do you see, if Allah should destroy me and those with me or have mercy upon us, who would then protect the disbelievers from a painful punishment?'
interpretation: The verse is a rhetorical question posed by the Prophet Muhammad, addressing the disbelievers who rejected his message. The verse asks whether, in the face of God's punishment or mercy, anyone could protect the disbelievers from a painful punishment. The verse emphasizes the ultimate power and control that God has over all of His creations and the futility of the disbelievers' attempts to resist or escape from His punishment. The verse serves as a warning to the disbelievers and a reminder of the futility of their efforts to resist God's will.
orig: قل أرأيتم إن أهلكني الله ومن معي أو رحمنا فمن يجير الكافرين من عذاب أليم

translation: Say, 'He is the Most Merciful (Ar-Rahman). We believe in Him and we put our trust in Him. So you will come to know who is in clear error (Mubeen).'
interpretation: The verse is a command to the Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) to declare his faith and trust in Allah, who is described as the Most Merciful (Ar-Rahman). By making this declaration, the Prophet challenges the disbelievers to reflect upon who is truly in error. The verse emphasizes the importance of faith and trust in Allah, and serves as a reminder that ultimately, it is Allah who has knowledge of the truth and who has the power to guide or misguide. The verse also serves as a challenge to the disbelievers, inviting them to consider their own beliefs and actions, and to reflect upon the consequences of their rejection of the truth.
orig: قل هو الرحمن آمنا به وعليه توكلنا فستعلمون من هو في ضلال مبين

translation: Say, 'Have you considered: if your water were to disappear underground, who then could bring you flowing water?'
interpretation: The verse is a rhetorical question, addressed to those who deny or reject the message of the prophet. It asks them to consider the hypothetical situation where their water supply disappears, and then asks who could bring them water. The purpose of this question is to make the listeners reflect on their own vulnerability and dependence on a stable water supply, and to highlight the importance of having a source of water in a desert environment. The verse also serves to emphasize the power and control that God has over the natural world, and the idea that only God can provide for their needs. The verse ultimately serves to remind the listeners of their need for God, and the importance of following the guidance of the prophet.
orig: قل أرأيتم إن أصبح ماؤكم غورا فمن يأتيكم بماء معين

translation: Nun. By the pen and what they inscribe.
interpretation: The verse is a powerful and poetic opening that sets the stage for the revelation of the Qur'an. The letter "Nun" is one of the mysterious and disconnected letters that appear at the beginning of several chapters in the Qur'an, and its meaning is known only to God. The verse then goes on to mention the "pen" and "what they inscribe," which is a metaphor for the power of words and writing. The verse suggests that the Qur'an is a revelation that has been written down and preserved for all time, and that its message is of the utmost importance. The verse may also be interpreted as a reminder of the power of the written word to shape reality and to convey divine truth, and of the responsibility that comes with the ability to write and communicate.
orig: ن والقلم وما يسطرون

translation: You are not, by the grace of your Lord, mad.
interpretation: The verse is denying the suggestion that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) is mad or insane. Instead, it asserts that the Prophet's experiences and revelations are due to the grace and favor of his Lord. The verse is a response to those who rejected the Prophet and his message, and it emphasizes the divine origin of the Qur'an and the Prophet's mission. The verse also serves as a source of comfort and reassurance for the Prophet, reminding him that he is not alone in his struggle and that he is chosen and supported by God.
orig: ما أنت بنعمة ربك بمجنون

translation: And indeed, for you is a reward unperceivable.
interpretation: The verse speaks about a reward that is being promised to the listener or reader. The reward is described as 'unperceivable', indicating that it is something that cannot be seen or understood in the physical world. This reward is a promise from God, and is a form of compensation for the struggles and difficulties faced by the believers in their earthly lives. The verse serves as a reminder of the existence of a greater reward that awaits the believers in the afterlife, and encourages them to remain steadfast and patient in their faith.
orig: وإن لك لأجرا غير ممنون

translation: And indeed, you are of a great creation.
interpretation: The verse is addressing a second person, praising and acknowledging the greatness of their creation. The interpretation of this verse can be seen as a reminder of the value and worth of human beings, who are created with a unique purpose and potential. It can also serve as a reminder of the responsibility that comes with this greatness, to use one's abilities and talents for good and to fulfill one's purpose in life.
orig: وإنك لعلى خلق عظيم

translation: Then he will surely see and they will surely see.
interpretation: The verse speaks about a person who will be able to see or understand something, and others who will also be able to see or understand the same thing. The verse emphasizes the certainty of this event, using the word 'surely' twice. The verse may be referring to a specific situation or revelation, or it could be a general statement about the ability of people to see or understand the truth. The exact meaning of the verse depends on the context in which it is used.
orig: فستبصر ويبصرون

translation: So by which of your Lord's favors will you deny (the Day of Reckoning)?
interpretation: The verse is a rhetorical question addressed to the disbelievers who deny the Day of Judgment. It reminds them of the blessings and favors they have received from their Lord and asks how they can deny the truth of the Day of Reckoning in light of these blessings. The verse is a call for reflection and an invitation for the disbelievers to ponder the blessings they have received and to recognize the signs of their Lord. It also serves as a warning that they will be held accountable for their actions on the Day of Judgment and that they will not be able to deny it then.
orig: بأييكم المفتون

translation: Indeed, your Lord is most knowing of those who stray from His way, and He is most knowing of those who are guided.
interpretation: The verse affirms that Allah has complete knowledge of those who stray from His path and those who are guided. The verse emphasizes Allah's all-encompassing knowledge and His ability to distinguish between those who are lost and those who are on the right path. This verse serves as a reminder that Allah is aware of every individual's actions and intentions, and that ultimately, He is the one who guides and leads astray. It also serves as a source of comfort for the believers, reminding them that Allah is all-knowing and all-seeing, and that He will guide them to the right path.
orig: إن ربك هو أعلم بمن ضل عن سبيله وهو أعلم بالمهتدين

translation: So do not follow the deniers
interpretation: The verse advises the believers not to follow the deniers or those who reject the message of Islam. By following them, one risks straying from the path of truth and righteousness. The verse emphasizes the importance of staying firm on the path of faith and not being swayed by the deniers or those who spread doubt and misguidance.
orig: فلا تطع المكذبين

translation: And if you pour it (the drink) on them, they would not be warmed.
interpretation: The verse speaks about a drink that, if poured on someone, would not warm them. The verse is metaphorical and is used in the Qist context to describe the condition of the hearts of the unbelievers, who are described as being spiritually cold and unresponsive to the message of Islam. The verse serves to emphasize the severity of their condition and the futility of trying to reach them through normal means. It also serves as a warning to the believers to beware of the dangers of associating with the unbelievers and to keep their distance from them.
orig: ودوا لو تدهن فيدهنون

translation: And follow not every whimsical opinion.
interpretation: The verse advises against following every whimsical opinion or capricious desire, and emphasizes the importance of adhering to guidance and wisdom. It serves as a reminder that not every opinion or desire should be followed blindly, and that one should exercise caution and seek guidance in order to discern between right and wrong. The verse encourages discernment and critical thinking, and warns against being swayed by every passing fancy or fleeting impulse.
orig: ولا تطع كل حلاف مهين

translation: Two-horned blowers of the trumpet
interpretation: The phrase 'Two-horned blowers of the trumpet' is a metaphorical description of the angels who will blow the trumpet on the Day of Judgment. The two horns represent the dual nature of the event, signaling both the end of the world and the beginning of a new era. The blowing of the trumpet will be a powerful and terrifying sound that will signal the resurrection of the dead and the final judgment of all souls. This phrase serves as a reminder of the reality of the Day of Judgment and the need for individuals to prepare for it by living a righteous life.
orig: هماز مشاء بنميم

translation: A refuge from evil, a repeatedly doing sinner.
interpretation: The phrase speaks of a 'refuge from evil' and a 'repeatedly doing sinner'. The interpretation of this phrase is not immediately clear from the text alone, as it is a fragment from a larger context. However, one possible interpretation could be that the 'refuge from evil' refers to a source of protection or safety from wrongdoing, while the 'repeatedly doing sinner' refers to a person who persistently engages in unrighteous behavior. The phrase could be a rhetorical contrast, highlighting the stark contrast between the protection offered by the refuge and the danger posed by the sinner. Alternatively, it could be a metaphorical description of a situation or a person, where the refuge represents a positive quality or characteristic, and the sinner represents a negative one. The exact interpretation would depend on the larger context in which this phrase is used.
orig: مناع للخير معتد أثيم

translation: Then indeed, after that, He will inherit the guilty.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the ultimate fate of the guilty, who will be inherited by God after their death. The verse emphasizes the certainty of this fate, as it follows the phrase 'then indeed, after that', indicating that it is an inevitable consequence of their actions. The verse serves as a reminder of the transience of worldly life and the eternal nature of the hereafter, urging the guilty to repent and seek forgiveness before it is too late.
orig: عتل بعد ذلك زنيم

translation: that he was wealthy and had sons
interpretation: The verse refers to someone who was wealthy and had children. This description could be used to emphasize the person's status and position in society, or to highlight the blessings that they had received from God. However, the verse does not provide any further context or information about the person or their story, so it is difficult to interpret the meaning without additional information.
orig: أن كان ذا مال وبنين

translation: When our verses are recited to him, he says: 'Fables of the ancients.'
interpretation: The verse refers to a person who rejects the signs or revelations of God, and dismisses them as old stories or myths. This person is not open to the truth, and instead of accepting and reflecting on the message, they reject it and mock it. The verse serves as a warning to those who deny the revelations of God, and emphasizes the importance of being receptive to the truth and recognizing the signs of God.
orig: إذا تتلى عليه آياتنا قال أساطير الأولين

translation: We shall mark him on the nose (with a sign).
interpretation: The verse refers to a person who is being punished for their wrongdoing. The phrase 'We shall mark him on the nose' is a metaphor for a visible sign or mark of shame and disgrace that will be placed on the person as a consequence of their actions. The verse serves as a warning to those who disobey God's commands and engage in unrighteous behavior, reminding them of the negative consequences that will follow their actions.
orig: سنسمه على الخرطوم

translation: We shall adorn them as We adorned the inhabitants of Paradise, when they made a promise with Us to avoid fornication. Indeed, We will not break Our promise.
interpretation: The verse speaks about God's promise to adorn the believers in the same way that the inhabitants of Paradise were adorned. The inhabitants of Paradise made a promise to God to avoid fornication, and God will fulfill His promise to them. The verse emphasizes the importance of keeping promises and the rewards that come with it. The verse also serves as a reminder to the believers to remain steadfast in their faith and to strive for righteousness. The verse also highlights the concept of God's justice and how He rewards those who are obedient and fulfill their promises.
orig: إنا بلوناهم كما بلونا أصحاب الجنة إذ أقسموا ليصرمنها مصبحين

translation: but they will not encompass it.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the limitations of human knowledge and understanding. The specific context in which this verse appears refers to the unbelievers who try to argue against the truth of Islam. The verse emphasizes that, despite their best efforts, they will never be able to fully grasp or comprehend the truth of Islam. The verse serves as a reminder that there are certain things that are beyond human comprehension and that ultimately, it is only through faith and submission to God that one can find true understanding and guidance.
orig: ولا يستثنون

translation: A party of your Lord has passed by (their) houses while they were asleep.
interpretation: The verse describes a group from God passing by the homes of some people while they were asleep. This event is a sign of God's presence and knowledge, emphasizing that nothing escapes His notice. The verse may serve as a reminder that God sees and knows all, even when people are unaware and unmindful of His presence. It encourages people to be mindful of their actions and to strive for righteousness, as God is always watching and aware of their deeds.
orig: فطاف عليها طائف من ربك وهم نائمون

translation: And you will surely find them, as I found them, in the morning, prostrating themselves.
interpretation: The verse describes a scene where the disbelievers are found prostrating themselves in the morning, as if in worship. However, this outward display of devotion is not genuine, but rather a result of fear and coercion. The repetition of 'you will surely find them' emphasizes the certainty and inevitability of this scene. The verse serves as a reminder of the insincerity of those who only turn to God out of fear or external pressure, and the importance of true and sincere faith.
orig: فأصبحت كالصريم

translation: And they will call out to them, '(O) stone(s)',
interpretation: The verse describes the scene of the Day of Judgment, where people are calling out for help, but instead of receiving any aid, they are addressing inanimate objects, such as stones. The verse emphasizes the severity of the Day of Judgment, where people will be in a state of desperation and fear, and even the stones will not be able to help them. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of preparing for the afterlife and seeking God's mercy.
orig: فتنادوا مصبحين

translation: So go to your harvest in the morning, if you are truthful.
interpretation: The verse is a continuation of a conversation between the Prophet Moses and the Samiri, who had created a golden calf for the Israelites to worship. The Prophet Moses is telling the Samiri to go to his harvest in the morning if he is truthful, implying that the Samiri had been lying or deceiving the people. The verse can be interpreted as a call for accountability and honesty, emphasizing the importance of being truthful in one's actions and words. The verse may also be seen as a metaphorical way of saying that the Samiri's false beliefs and practices will not provide him with any sustenance or benefit, and that he will ultimately be held accountable for his actions.
orig: أن اغدوا على حرثكم إن كنتم صارمين

translation: So go forth, (you men) in bands or (go) single,
interpretation: The verse is a command from God to the believers to go forth and fight in His cause. It is a call to action, urging the believers to take up arms and defend their faith. The verse suggests that the believers can either go forth in groups or individually, indicating that the decision to participate in the fight is a personal one, but the importance lies in taking action and standing up for what one believes in.
orig: فانطلقوا وهم يتخافتون

translation: That not today shall the poor enter it (the holy land) along with you.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the exclusion of the poor from entering the holy land along with the rest of the people. The verse highlights the division and discrimination that exists among people, where some are granted access while others are denied. The verse serves as a reminder that wealth and status should not be the criteria for excluding or including people from sacred spaces. Instead, it promotes the idea of equality and inclusivity, emphasizing that the holy land should be accessible to all, regardless of their financial status.
orig: أن لا يدخلنها اليوم عليكم مسكين

translation: And they set out, in the morning, with power.
interpretation: The verse describes a group of people who leave their town in the morning, presumably to carry out some task or mission. The use of the phrase 'with power' suggests that they are well-equipped and confident in their abilities. However, the context of this verse is not provided, so it is unclear what the purpose of their journey is or what will happen to them. The verse may serve as a contrast to the previous verse, which speaks about the destruction of unjust towns, emphasizing the stark contrast between the fate of the unrighteous and the powerful.
orig: وغدوا على حرد قادرين

translation: When they saw it, they said, 'Indeed, we are, concerning [this], astray.'
interpretation: The verse describes a group of people who, upon seeing something (the nature of which is not specified in the verse), realize that they have been lost or misguided. The verse can be interpreted as a moment of realization or awakening for these individuals, as they come to terms with the fact that they have strayed from the right path. This realization could be in regards to their actions, beliefs, or understanding of a situation. The verse serves as a reminder that recognizing one's own mistakes or shortcomings is an important step towards self-improvement and growth.
orig: فلما رأوها قالوا إنا لضالون

translation: But indeed, we are prohibited
interpretation: The verse is a continuation of a conversation between the people of a town and their prophet. The people are expressing their disbelief and rejecting the message of the prophet. They claim that they are prohibited from following the path of guidance and righteousness. The verse emphasizes the idea of being restricted or forbidden, highlighting the people's unwillingness to accept the truth and their stubbornness in following their own desires and misguided ways.
orig: بل نحن محرومون

translation: Said one of them, 'Did I not tell you that if you did not glorify [Allah] you would surely be punished?'
interpretation: The verse relates a conversation among a group of people, where one of them warns the others about the consequence of not glorifying or praising God. The verse highlights the importance of worshipping and acknowledging God, and the consequences of neglecting this duty. The person who warned the group is portrayed as having a sense of responsibility towards the group, and as having a better understanding of the importance of worship. The verse serves as a reminder to the believers of the importance of praising and glorifying God, and the consequences of not doing so.
orig: قال أوسطهم ألم أقل لكم لولا تسبحون

translation: They said, 'Exalted is our Lord! We have been wrongdoers.'
interpretation: The verse is a statement of repentance and recognition of wrongdoing by a group of people. They acknowledge their mistakes and express their remorse by saying 'Exalted is our Lord! We have been wrongdoers.' This shows their understanding of the gravity of their actions and their submission to the will of God. The verse highlights the importance of repentance and the acknowledgement of one's mistakes as a path towards forgiveness and redemption.
orig: قالوا سبحان ربنا إنا كنا ظالمين

translation: And some of them walk towards others, swearing to God (saying): 'If you should come to us, indeed we will be with you in faith!'
interpretation: The verse describes a scene where some people are approaching others, making a pledge to God that they will join them in faith if they come to them. The verse highlights the hypocrisy and insincerity of these people, who are quick to make promises but slow to fulfill them. The verse serves as a warning against making false promises and emphasizes the importance of sincerity and commitment in one's faith.
orig: فأقبل بعضهم على بعض يتلاومون

translation: They said, 'Woe to us! We were indeed wrongdoers.'
interpretation: The verse shows the regret and remorse of the people who, when faced with punishment, admit their wrongdoing and express their regret. This verse serves as a reminder of the importance of acknowledging one's mistakes and seeking forgiveness, as well as the reality that the consequences of our actions will eventually catch up with us.
orig: قالوا يا ويلنا إنا كنا طاغين

translation: Perhaps our Lord will substitute for us better than it. Indeed, to our Lord do we turn penitent.
interpretation: The verse expresses a hopeful and submissive attitude towards a difficult situation. The speaker and their community are expressing the possibility that their current state or circumstances may be replaced by something better through the will of their Lord. At the same time, they acknowledge their dependence on their Lord and their penitence towards Him. The verse can be interpreted as a reminder of the power of divine intervention and the importance of seeking God's mercy and forgiveness in the face of adversity.
orig: عسى ربنا أن يبدلنا خيرا منها إنا إلى ربنا راغبون

translation: So is the punishment, and the punishment of the Hereafter is greater, if they only knew.
interpretation: The verse compares the punishment in this world to the punishment of the Hereafter, emphasizing that the latter is much greater. The use of the phrase 'if they only knew' highlights the regret and remorse that the disbelievers will feel when they realize the consequences of their actions in the Hereafter. The verse serves as a warning to those who ignore the signs of God and continue to live in sin, urging them to reflect and change their ways before it is too late.
orig: كذلك العذاب ولعذاب الآخرة أكبر لو كانوا يعلمون

translation: Indeed, for the righteous with their Lord are gardens of delight.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the reward that awaits the righteous with their Lord. The gardens of delight symbolize the ultimate bliss and happiness that the righteous will experience in the afterlife. The verse serves as a source of hope and motivation for those who strive to lead a righteous life, reminding them of the beautiful reward that awaits them in the hereafter.
orig: إن للمتقين عند ربهم جنات النعيم

translation: Then will I make the Muslims like the criminals.
interpretation: The verse is a hypothetical statement made by the disbelievers, who are expressing their disdain for the Muslims. They are suggesting that the Muslims are no better than criminals and that they should be treated as such. However, the verse can also be interpreted as a warning from God, highlighting the consequences of rejecting faith and following the path of disbelief. The verse serves as a reminder to the believers to uphold their faith and adhere to the teachings of Islam, and to the disbelievers to reflect on their actions and consider the consequences of their rejection of the truth.
orig: أفنجعل المسلمين كالمجرمين

translation: What is [the matter] with you that you judge?
interpretation: The verse is a rhetorical question posed by the Qur'an to those who are judging or passing judgement on others. The verse challenges the authority and legitimacy of their judgement, implying that they do not have the right or the knowledge to judge others. The verse serves as a reminder that only God has the right to judge and that humans should be wary of passing judgement on others.
orig: ما لكم كيف تحكمون

translation: Or have you received a scripture wherein you learn?
interpretation: The verse is a challenge to the disbelievers who rejected the message of the Prophet Muhammad (pbuh). It asks them if they have received a scripture, referring to the Qur'an, that they can study and learn from. The verse implies that the Qur'an is a source of knowledge and guidance, and those who reject it are missing out on an opportunity to learn and better themselves. The verse serves as a reminder that the Qur'an is a valuable source of guidance for those who seek it, and a warning to those who reject it that they are missing out on an important opportunity.
orig: أم لكم كتاب فيه تدرسون

translation: Indeed, in that (the Qur'an) is that which you choose.
interpretation: The verse is giving the agency of choice to the people in regards to the Qur'an. It suggests that the Qur'an contains guidance and teachings that people can choose to follow or ignore. The verse can be seen as an invitation for people to reflect on the message of the Qur'an and make a conscious decision about how they will engage with it. The verse also implies that the Qur'an has something for everyone, and it is up to the individual to extract what is beneficial for them. Ultimately, the verse emphasizes the importance of personal responsibility and accountability in one's relationship with the divine message.
orig: إن لكم فيه لما تخيرون

translation: Or have you not considered that upon us is the establishment of your promise until the Day of Resurrection? Indeed, you will not cause failure [to Us].
interpretation: The verse is addressing the disbelievers who challenge the power and ability of God to establish His promise of resurrection and judgement. The verse reminds them that the establishment of the promise is under the control of God until the Day of Resurrection and that they cannot harm or defeat God in any way. The verse serves as a reminder of the power and control of God and the futility of challenging or opposing Him.
orig: أم لكم أيمان علينا بالغة إلى يوم القيامة إن لكم لما تحكمون

translation: Then ask them, 'Which of your Lord's proofs have you invented?',
interpretation: The verse is a challenge to the disbelievers to provide evidence or proof for their rejection of Islam and their rejection of the signs of Allah. It is a call for them to reflect on their beliefs and actions, and to consider the consequences of their disbelief. The verse is also a reminder that the only evidence or proof that is acceptable is that which is provided by Allah, and that any evidence or proof that is invented or fabricated by humans is not acceptable.
orig: سلهم أيهم بذلك زعيم

translation: Or have they associates (false gods) who can protect them? Then let them produce their associates, if they are truthful.
interpretation: The verse challenges the disbelievers who worship false gods to bring forth their deities if they truly believe in their power and protection. The verse implies that the disbelievers are unable to do so, as their gods have no power or existence. The verse serves to expose the falsehood and futility of idol worship, and invites the disbelievers to reflect on the truth of Islam and the power of the one true God.
orig: أم لهم شركاء فليأتوا بشركائهم إن كانوا صادقين

translation: The day when the leg will be uncovered and they will be invited to prostrate, but they will not be able [to do so].
interpretation: The verse describes the Day of Judgment when the people's sins will be exposed and they will be called to prostrate in submission to God. However, the verse warns that they will be unable to do so, indicating the severity of their sins and the consequences of their rejection of God's guidance. The verse emphasizes the importance of repentance and submission to God in this life, as it will be too late on the Day of Judgment.
orig: يوم يكشف عن ساق ويدعون إلى السجود فلا يستطيعون

translation: Their eyes humbled, they fell down in submission. And they had been invited to prostration before, while they were whole and sound.
interpretation: The verse describes the humbling of people who had previously rejected the call to worship and submit to God. The phrase 'their eyes humbled' suggests a recognition of their past mistakes and a newfound humility. The phrase 'they fell down in submission' indicates their acceptance of the truth and their willingness to submit to God. The reference to their previous invitation to prostration, while they were 'whole and sound', highlights the contrast between their past rejection and their present acceptance of the truth. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of responding to the call to worship and submit to God, and the consequences of rejecting it.
orig: خاشعة أبصارهم ترهقهم ذلة وقد كانوا يدعون إلى السجود وهم سالمون

translation: And leave Me with those who deny this message; We will lead them on step by step, from places they know not.
interpretation: The verse speaks about those who deny or reject the message (presumably referring to the message of Islam or the Qur'an). The verse instructs the Prophet Muhammad to leave them alone and entrust their fate to God. The verse also indicates that God will lead these people astray, causing them to wander in confusion and ignorance. The verse serves as a warning to those who reject the message of Islam, emphasizing the consequences of their disbelief and the inevitability of God's judgment.
orig: فذرني ومن يكذب بهذا الحديث سنستدرجهم من حيث لا يعلمون

translation: And I will give them hope, then I will surely overcome them.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the speaker's intention to give hope to a group of people, but ultimately, the speaker will overcome them. The verse may be referring to the deceptive nature of the speaker, who lures the people with false promises and hope, only to ultimately defeat them. The verse can serve as a cautionary tale about being wary of false promises and not to be deceived by those who make them.
orig: وأملي لهم إن كيدي متين

translation: Or do you ask them for a wage, so they are burdened with debt?
interpretation: The verse speaks about the responsibility of the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) towards the people he is guiding. The verse asks if the Prophet asks for a wage for his efforts, and then answers that the people are already burdened with debt and struggling. The verse emphasizes the selflessness and generosity required of the Prophet, and by extension, all those who strive to guide and help others. It serves as a reminder that the work of spreading knowledge and guidance should not be motivated by personal gain or financial reward, but by a sincere desire to help and serve others. The verse also highlights the difficult circumstances of the people, who are already burdened and struggling, and the importance of being sensitive to their needs and limitations.
orig: أم تسألهم أجرا فهم من مغرم مثقلون

translation: Or have they a deity other than Allah? Then indeed, they would be upon nothing.
interpretation: The verse questions the belief of those who claim to have a deity other than Allah, stating that if this were true, they would be in a state of nothingness or non-existence. This implies that the only true deity is Allah, and any other deity is false and without power or significance. The verse serves as a reminder of the oneness of Allah and the futility of worshipping any other deity.
orig: أم عندهم الغيب فهم يكتبون

translation: So be patient for the decision of your Lord, and be not like the companion of the fish, when he cried out (for help), while he was in deep distress.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the importance of being patient and having faith in God's plan, using the story of the companion of the fish as an example. The companion of the fish cried out for help while he was in deep distress, indicating a lack of patience and trust in God's plan. The verse serves as a reminder to have patience and faith during difficult times, and not to despair or panic. It encourages believers to trust in God's decision and to remain steadfast in their faith.
orig: فاصبر لحكم ربك ولا تكن كصاحب الحوت إذ نادى وهو مكظوم

translation: But if not for the grace of his Lord, he would indeed have been cast off into the Desolation, an outcast.
interpretation: The verse speaks about an individual who has been saved from a terrible fate by the grace of their Lord. The verse highlights the fact that the person would have been cast off into the Desolation and become an outcast if it were not for the mercy of their Lord. The verse serves as a reminder of the power and grace of God, who has the ability to save or condemn individuals based on His will. It also emphasizes the importance of gratitude and acknowledges the fact that all blessings come from God.
orig: لولا أن تداركه نعمة من ربه لنبذ بالعراء وهو مذموم

translation: So his Lord chose him and made him one of the righteous.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the story of a man who was chosen by his Lord and made righteous. The verse emphasizes the significance of being chosen by God and the transformation that it brings, turning the man into one of the righteous. The verse serves as a reminder that God has the power to choose and guide anyone He wills, and that those who are chosen and follow God's guidance will be made righteous.
orig: فاجتباه ربه فجعله من الصالحين

translation: And those who disbelieve would almost strike you down with their eyes when they hear the reminder, and they say, 'Indeed, he is mad.'
interpretation: The verse describes the reaction of the disbelievers when they hear the message of Islam. They are skeptical and dismissive, and some of them even react with hostility and disrespect. They refuse to believe in the message and its messenger, and they try to undermine and discredit the message. The verse emphasizes the negative and dismissive attitude of the disbelievers, and it highlights the contrast between their rejection of the truth and the faith of the believers. The verse serves as a reminder of the challenges and difficulties that the Prophet Muhammad faced in his mission to spread the message of Islam, and it highlights the importance of staying strong and steadfast in the face of adversity and opposition.
orig: وإن يكاد الذين كفروا ليزلقونك بأبصارهم لما سمعوا الذكر ويقولون إنه لمجنون

translation: And it is nothing except a reminder to the worlds.
interpretation: The verse is emphasizing that the message being conveyed is a reminder, and it is intended for all of humanity. It is a call to remember and reflect on the truth and to recognize the signs of God's existence and power. This reminder is a reminder of the Day of Judgment, the need for repentance, and the importance of living a righteous life. It serves as a wake-up call for those who have strayed from the path of righteousness and an affirmation for those who are on the right path.
orig: وما هو إلا ذكر للعالمين

translation: N
interpretation: N
orig: الحاقة

translation: N
interpretation: N
orig: ما الحاقة

translation: And what will make you understand what the Event is?
interpretation: The verse is asking the reader about their understanding of 'the Event' (al-Haqqah), which is a term used in the Qur'an to refer to the Day of Judgment. The verse is emphasizing the importance of understanding and recognizing the significance of this event. The interpretation of this verse is that it is a call to contemplate and reflect on the reality of the Day of Judgment, and to prepare for it by living a righteous and just life.
orig: وما أدراك ما الحاقة

translation: The Thamud and 'Ad denied (their messengers) by (using) clear signs.
interpretation: The verse refers to the rejection of the messengers by the people of Thamud and 'Ad, despite receiving clear signs and evidence. This verse emphasizes the disbelief and denial of these two communities, even in the face of clear evidence. The verse serves as a reminder of the consequences of disbelief and the importance of accepting and following the guidance of the messengers.
orig: كذبت ثمود وعاد بالقارعة

translation: But as for Thamud, they were destroyed by the wrongdoing.
interpretation: The verse refers to the destruction of the people of Thamud, who were punished for their wrongdoing or transgression. The verse serves as a reminder of the consequences of disobedience and sin, and emphasizes the power and justice of God in dealing with those who reject His message and engage in transgression.
orig: فأما ثمود فأهلكوا بالطاغية

translation: But as for 'Aad, they were destroyed by a furious screaming wind.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of the people of 'Aad, a historical community mentioned in the Qur'an. The verse describes their destruction as being caused by a "furious screaming wind", indicating the overwhelming and catastrophic nature of the punishment they received. The verse serves as a reminder of the power and authority of God and the consequences of ignoring His signs and messages.
orig: وأما عاد فأهلكوا بريح صرصر عاتية

translation: And We made them (the towns) leaders to be led astray, and We made between them and the towns which We had blessed (for them) gardens and springs, and We made between them and the towns a barrier, so clearly evident, and travelers on the road between them (the towns) said, 'Oh,
interpretation: No interpretation
orig: سخرها عليهم سبع ليال وثمانية أيام حسوما فترى القوم فيها صرعى كأنهم أعجاز نخل خاوية

translation: Then see you any remnant of them?
interpretation: The verse is a rhetorical question that challenges the reader to observe if there are any survivors or remnants of a group of people who were previously mentioned. The verse likely refers to a group of people who were destroyed or punished by God for their sins and injustices, and the question serves to emphasize the completeness and finality of their destruction. The verse may also be interpreted as a warning to those who are similar to the destroyed group, urging them to reflect on the consequences of their actions and the possibility of facing a similar fate.
orig: فهل ترى لهم من باقية

translation: And Pharaoh and those before him and the leaders who were wrongdoers
interpretation: The verse refers to Pharaoh and those who came before him, as well as the leaders who were guilty of wrongdoing. The verse is likely referring to past civilizations and leaders who were unjust and oppressive. The inclusion of Pharaoh, a well-known figure of tyranny in Islamic and Biblical traditions, emphasizes the magnitude of the wrongdoing and the severity of the consequences. The verse serves as a reminder of the consequences of oppression and the importance of justice.
orig: وجاء فرعون ومن قبله والمؤتفكات بالخاطئة

translation: They disobeyed the messenger of their Lord, so He took them in a seizure that was overwhelming.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the punishment of those who disobey the messenger of their Lord. The verse emphasizes the overwhelming and powerful nature of the 'seizure' that God took them in, indicating the severity of their disobedience. The verse serves as a reminder that disobedience towards God's messenger and His commands will result in severe consequences.
orig: فعصوا رسول ربهم فأخذهم أخذة رابية

translation: But when the water (of the flood)overflowed, We carried you (mankind) in the floating (ark).
interpretation: The verse refers to the story of Prophet Noah's Ark, where God sent a great flood to destroy the corrupt and unjust people of that time. The verse highlights God's power and control over the natural elements and His ability to save and protect those who are righteous. The verse serves as a reminder that God is always with His believers, even in the most trying and difficult times, and that He will protect and save them from harm.
orig: إنا لما طغى الماء حملناكم في الجارية

translation: We shall make it a lesson and a reminder for you and clear (understandable) advertisement.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the making of something (it is not specified what) into a lesson, a reminder, and a clear advertisement for the people. The purpose of this is to teach and guide the people, making them aware of the message and its significance. The verse may be referring to a previous event or a prophecy, using it as an example or a warning for the people. The verse highlights the importance of lessons and reminders in the process of understanding and learning, and the role of clear communication in conveying the message effectively.
orig: لنجعلها لكم تذكرة وتعيها أذن واعية

translation: And when We blow the Trumpet, a single Blast,
