interpretation: The verse speaks about the Day of Judgment and the blowing of the Trumpet by the angel Israfil. This event marks the beginning of the resurrection and the gathering of all souls before God. The verse highlights the singularity of the Blast, emphasizing the suddenness and inevitability of the event. The verse serves as a reminder of the nearness of the Day of Judgment and the importance of being prepared for it by living a righteous life.
orig: فإذا نفخ في الصور نفخة واحدة

translation: And the earth and the mountains were lifted up and shaken together (in one convulsion).
interpretation: The verse describes the powerful and awe-inspiring scene of the earth and the mountains being lifted up and shaken together. This imagery conveys a sense of great upheaval and destruction, emphasizing the overwhelming power of God. The verse may be interpreted as a warning of the Day of Judgment, when the earth and the mountains will be destroyed and the people will be resurrected and judged for their actions. It serves as a reminder of the transient nature of this world and the importance of striving for righteousness and preparedness for the hereafter.
orig: وحملت الأرض والجبال فدكتا دكة واحدة

translation: The event occurred that day.
interpretation: This verse speaks of a significant event that took place on a particular day. The Arabic word "واقعة" (waqa'ah) can be translated as a sudden or unexpected event, often with negative connotations, such as a disaster or punishment. However, without additional context, it is difficult to provide a specific interpretation of the meaning of this event. The verse may be referring to a specific event mentioned elsewhere in the Qur'an or it may be a more general reference to the Day of Judgment or other significant events in Islamic theology. Ultimately, the interpretation of this verse depends on the broader context in which it is situated.
orig: فيومئذ وقعت الواقعة

translation: And the heaven did split, so it was (like) a smooth-stretched out leaf.
interpretation: The verse describes the splitting of the heaven, comparing it to a smooth-stretched out leaf. This imagery conveys a sense of delicacy and fragility of the heaven, emphasizing the power and might of God who has the ability to split it. The verse may also suggest a sense of awe and wonder, inviting the reader to contemplate the mysteries of the universe and the greatness of God.
orig: وانشقت السماء فهي يومئذ واهية

translation: And the angels will be on its edges, and the angels will bear the Throne of your Lord above them that Day, eight [of them].
interpretation: The verse describes the Day of Judgment and the role of the angels during this event. The angels will be positioned on the edges or borders of the event, while eight of them will bear the Throne of God above them. The verse highlights the majesty and power of God, as well as the role of the angels in the divine plan. It serves as a reminder of the reality of the Day of Judgment and the ultimate accountability of all human beings for their actions in this life.
orig: والملك على أرجائها ويحمل عرش ربك فوقهم يومئذ ثمانية

translation: On that day you will be exposed, not hiding from one another.
interpretation: The verse describes the Day of Judgment, when all people will be laid bare and nothing will be hidden. The idea of 'not hiding from one another' emphasizes the complete transparency and openness of this day, when all secrets will be revealed and people will be unable to conceal their true selves or actions. This serves as a reminder of the importance of leading an honest and virtuous life, free from deceit and hypocrisy.
orig: يومئذ تعرضون لا تخفى منكم خافية

translation: But as for him who is given his record in his left hand, he will say, 'Oh, I wish I had not been given my record
interpretation: The verse speaks about the fate of those who receive their record, or account of their deeds, in their left hand on the Day of Judgment. These individuals will regret their actions and wish they had not received their record because it is a sign of their punishment. The verse emphasizes the importance of leading a righteous life and the consequences of not doing so. It serves as a warning to those who are neglectful of their duties towards God and their fellow human beings.
orig: فأما من أوتي كتابه بيمينه فيقول هاؤم اقرءوا كتابيه

translation: I thought that I would certainly meet my account.
interpretation: The verse expresses the speaker's acceptance and recognition of the inevitability of being held accountable for their actions. The phrase 'meet my account' can be interpreted as a reference to the Day of Judgment, when all people will be judged for their deeds and receive their just reward or punishment. The verse can serve as a reminder of the importance of leading a righteous life and preparing for the afterlife.
orig: إني ظننت أني ملاق حسابيه

translation: And he is in (a state of) happy, satisfying life.
interpretation: The verse speaks about an individual who is living a content and fulfilling life. The Arabic word 'عيشة' (`ayisha`) means 'life', and the word 'راضية' (`raḍiyya`) means 'satisfying' or 'pleasing'. Together, they convey a sense of happiness and contentment. The verse may be referring to the blessings and rewards that God bestows upon the believers in this life, or it may be a description of the blissful state of the believers in the hereafter. The verse serves as a reminder of the blessings and bounties that God has provided for His servants, and the importance of being grateful and thankful for these gifts.
orig: فهو في عيشة راضية

translation: In a lofty garden
interpretation: The phrase 'In a lofty garden' is a description of paradise in Islamic teachings, indicating a place of great beauty, peace, and tranquility. The word 'lofty' suggests a high and exalted position, reflecting the high status of those who will reside there. The image of a garden also conveys a sense of abundance and fertility, symbolizing the blessings and rewards that will be bestowed upon the righteous in the afterlife.
orig: في جنة عالية

translation: Its (the olive tree's) two sides (branches)
interpretation: The verse is referring to the two sides or branches of the olive tree. The two sides could represent the different parts of the tree that produce olives, or it could be a metaphor for the abundance and generosity of the tree's blessings. The verse emphasizes the goodness and benefits of the olive tree, which is considered a valuable and useful tree in Islamic culture and tradition.
orig: قطوفها دانية

translation: Eat and drink freely, being sinful only in so far as you are unthankful.
interpretation: The verse gives permission to people to eat and drink and enjoy the blessings of life, but with a warning not to be ungrateful for these blessings. The phrase 'being sinful only in so far as you are unthankful' highlights the importance of gratitude and shows that being ungrateful for God's blessings is a form of sin. This verse can be interpreted as a reminder to be mindful of the blessings that we have and to express gratitude for them, rather than taking them for granted.
orig: كلوا واشربوا هنيئا بما أسلفتم في الأيام الخالية

translation: But as for him who is given his record in his left hand, he will say, 'Oh, I wish I had not been given my record
interpretation: The verse speaks about the fate of those who receive their record, or account of their deeds, in their left hand on the Day of Judgment. These are the people who have neglected their duties towards God and have indulged in sin and transgression. The verse expresses their regret and remorse when they see the record of their deeds and realize the consequences of their actions. The verse serves as a warning to those who are heedless of their responsibilities and accountability before God, urging them to repent and mend their ways before it is too late.
orig: وأما من أوتي كتابه بشماله فيقول يا ليتني لم أوت كتابيه

translation: And I do not know what my account will be.
interpretation: The verse is spoken from the perspective of someone who is uncertain about the outcome of their actions and the judgment they will face. It reflects a sense of humility and recognition of the limits of human knowledge and control. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of seeking guidance and striving for righteousness in order to prepare for the inevitable judgment day.
orig: ولم أدر ما حسابيه

translation: Ah, would that she had been judged!
interpretation: The verse is a lament from a speaker who wishes that a certain woman had been judged or punished for her actions. The verse could be referring to a specific situation where the woman had done something wrong and the speaker believes that she deserves to be punished for it. The verse emphasizes the speaker's frustration and dissatisfaction with the current situation and their belief that justice has not been served. The verse can also be seen as a reminder of the importance of accountability for one's actions and the consequences of those actions.
orig: يا ليتها كانت القاضية

translation: has not increased me except in loss.
interpretation: The statement expresses the idea that wealth and material possessions do not bring about any real gain or benefit. In fact, the speaker asserts that their wealth has only caused them to lose out or suffer. This statement could be interpreted as a warning against the pursuit of wealth and material gain as the sole purpose of life, and a reminder that true fulfillment and happiness come from other sources, such as spirituality, relationships, and personal growth.
orig: ما أغنى عني ماليه

translation: My authority has been taken away from me
interpretation: The statement expresses the loss or removal of one's power or authority. It suggests that the speaker has been stripped of their position of control and influence, and is no longer in a position of dominance or leadership.
orig: هلك عني سلطانيه

translation: Take and hold it (by) force.
interpretation: This verse is a command from God to the Prophet Muhammad and his followers to take and hold firmly to the religion of Islam, even if it requires the use of force. The verse is often interpreted as a justification for jihad, or holy war, in defense of the Muslim community and its way of life. However, it is important to note that the use of force is only permissible in self-defense and in accordance with Islamic law and ethical principles. The verse should not be used to justify aggression or violence against innocent people.
orig: خذوه فغلوه

translation: Then the Hellfire, indeed, will be the recompense.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the punishment of Hellfire that awaits those who have done wrong and committed sins. The verse emphasizes the certainty of this punishment and its severity, serving as a warning to those who continue to sin. The Hellfire is described as the recompense, or the payment, for the wrong actions of the sinners, reflecting the idea that every action has a consequence and that God's justice will ultimately be served.
orig: ثم الجحيم صلوه

translation: Then follow after their footsteps, the footsteps of those who have been favored (by Allah), (and) who have not earned any sin. Surely, they are guides to you in the world.
interpretation: The verse speaks about following the path of those who have been favored by Allah and have not earned any sin. These individuals are held up as examples and guides for others in this world. The verse implies that by following their path, one can also achieve success and avoid sin. The number seventy (seventy arms length) is a metaphor for a large distance and emphasizes the idea that the guidance of these individuals can be found even from a great distance.
orig: ثم في سلسلة ذرعها سبعون ذراعا فاسلكوه

translation: He (it) indeed did not believe in God, the Exalted.
interpretation: The verse is a statement about someone or something that did not believe in God, the Exalted. This statement could be a description of a person's disbelief or a rejection of God's power and greatness. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of faith in God and the consequences of disbelief.
orig: إنه كان لا يؤمن بالله العظيم

translation: And let not those who are miserly with what Allah has given them of His bounty think that it is good for them. Rather, it is bad for them.
interpretation: The verse speaks about those who are stingy with their wealth and resources, and do not give in charity or help those in need. The verse emphasizes that such behavior is not beneficial or praiseworthy, but rather it is harmful and detrimental. The verse serves as a reminder that wealth and resources are blessings from God, and should be used for the benefit of oneself and others. The verse encourages generosity and kindness towards the poor and needy, and warns against miserliness and hoarding wealth.
orig: ولا يحض على طعام المسكين

translation: He will not have today a warm friend.
interpretation: The verse speaks about a person who, on the Day of Judgment, will not have any supporters or allies who can protect or help them. The phrase 'warm friend' implies someone who is close and loyal, who can provide comfort and assistance in times of need. However, on the Day of Judgment, such a person will be alone and without any help, facing the consequences of their actions. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of leading a righteous life and building good relationships with others, as these may be the only things that can provide comfort and support in the afterlife.
orig: فليس له اليوم هاهنا حميم

translation: And no food will there be except from a tree, moistened (by water).
interpretation: The verse speaks about the scarcity of food in the hereafter, where there will be no food except for what grows on trees that are constantly moistened or irrigated. The verse emphasizes the stark contrast between the abundance of food in this world and the scarcity of food in the hereafter, serving as a reminder of the fleeting nature of worldly pleasures and the importance of preparing for the hereafter. It also highlights the importance of water and irrigation in sustaining life and the significance of these elements in the hereafter.
orig: ولا طعام إلا من غسلين

translation: They eat not (anything) but the sinners.
interpretation: The verse refers to a specific group of people who eat only that which is unlawful or forbidden. By doing so, they are considered sinners. The verse serves as a reminder that engaging in such actions has consequences, and that those who choose to act in this way will be considered sinners.
orig: لا يأكله إلا الخاطئون

translation: No indeed! I swear by what you see.
interpretation: The verse is a solemn oath by God, who swears by 'what you see' - a reference to the tangible, visible world that people experience through their senses. The verse could be interpreted as a reminder of the power and majesty of God, who created and controls the world that people see and experience every day. The verse may also be seen as a call to reflect on the significance of the visible world and to consider the deeper, unseen realities that underlie it. Ultimately, the verse is a powerful affirmation of the existence and authority of God, who is the creator and sustainer of all that exists.
orig: فلا أقسم بما تبصرون

translation: And you will not see (it, i.e., the unbelievers' punishment) a manifest blow (that will destroy them)
interpretation: No interpretation
orig: وما لا تبصرون

translation: Indeed, it is the word of a noble messenger.
interpretation: The verse is a confirmation of the divine origin of the message brought by a noble and respected messenger. The verse may have been revealed in response to those who questioned the authenticity or truth of the message, emphasizing that it is not the words of a mortal, but rather the word of a noble and exalted messenger, who is worthy of respect and obedience.
orig: إنه لقول رسول كريم

translation: And it is not the word of a poet; little do you believe.
interpretation: The verse is a response to those who rejected the message of the Qur'an, comparing it to the ramblings of a madman or the words of a poet. The verse categorically denies this claim, asserting that the Qur'an is not the creation of a poet. The second part of the verse, 'little do you believe', is a rebuke and a reminder of the lack of faith of those who rejected the message. The verse emphasizes the divine origin of the Qur'an, setting it apart from human creations and highlighting the importance of faith in accepting its message.
orig: وما هو بقول شاعر قليلا ما تؤمنون

translation: And not by the word of a soothsayer shall you remember.
interpretation: The verse is a continuation of a series of oaths taken by God, emphasizing the importance of the message being conveyed. The phrase 'not by the word of a soothsayer' is a metaphorical way of saying that the revelation being given is not something that could have been conjured up by a soothsayer or fortune-teller. Instead, it is a divine message that is being revealed through the Prophet Muhammad. The verse serves as a reminder of the authenticity and truth of the Qur'an, and the fact that it is not a creation of human imagination or invention.
orig: ولا بقول كاهن قليلا ما تذكرون

translation: A revelation from the Lord of the worlds.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the Qur'an being a revelation from the Lord of the worlds. This statement emphasizes the divine origin of the Qur'an and its importance as a source of guidance for all of humanity. The verse serves as a reminder of the greatness and power of God, who is the Lord of all that exists, and of the significance of the Qur'an as a means of connecting with and understanding the divine will.
orig: تنزيل من رب العالمين

translation: But if you [Muhammad] say, 'If only a treasure were mine!'
interpretation: The verse is addressing the Prophet Muhammad, reminding him that even if he were to desire wealth and treasure, he should not be disheartened or lose hope. The verse may serve as a reminder that true success and happiness do not come from material possessions, but from one's relationship with God. The verse can also be seen as a message of encouragement, reminding the Prophet to stay focused on his mission and not to be distracted by worldly desires.
orig: ولو تقول علينا بعض الأقاويل

translation: to take from him at the right hand
interpretation: The phrase 'لأخذنا منه باليمين' in the Qur'an is a reference to the act of taking something from a person's right hand. In Islamic culture, the right hand is considered to be the hand of honor and strength. Therefore, taking something from a person's right hand implies a position of power and authority. In the Qur'an, this phrase is often used in the context of the Day of Judgment, when God will take the souls of the believers with His right hand, indicating His mercy and compassion towards them. The phrase may also be interpreted as a symbol of God's justice and power, as He takes the lives of all creatures at the appointed time.
orig: لأخذنا منه باليمين

translation: Then We cut them down in their two sides.
interpretation: The verse describes a situation where a group of people were divided into two sides and then destroyed. The phrase 'cut them down in their two sides' is a metaphor for the complete and utter destruction of this group of people. This verse may be referring to a specific historical event, or it may be a more general statement about the fate of those who oppose God and engage in unrighteous actions. The verse serves as a warning to those who would oppose God, highlighting the severe consequences of such actions.
orig: ثم لقطعنا منه الوتين

translation: Not one of you but will pass over it: this is, with your Lord, a decree which must be accomplished.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the inevitability of death, stating that every person will have to cross over it. This is a decree from your Lord that cannot be avoided. The verse serves as a reminder of the reality of death and the importance of being prepared for it. It encourages people to live their lives in a way that is pleasing to God and to strive for righteousness, as they will ultimately be held accountable for their actions on the Day of Judgment.
orig: فما منكم من أحد عنه حاجزين

translation: And indeed, it is a reminder for the righteous.
interpretation: The verse speaks about a reminder that is being addressed specifically to the righteous people. The verse highlights the importance of this reminder for the righteous, who are striving to live a life in accordance with God's will. It serves as a source of guidance and motivation for them to continue on their path of righteousness, and a reminder of the rewards that await them in the hereafter.
orig: وإنه لتذكرة للمتقين

translation: And indeed, we know that among you are liars.
interpretation: The verse is addressing a group of people and acknowledging that there are liars among them. The statement is a direct and firm rebuke of those who are being untruthful. It suggests that the truth will ultimately be revealed and that deception will not go unnoticed or unpunished. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of honesty and integrity, and the consequences of dishonesty.
orig: وإنا لنعلم أن منكم مكذبين

translation: And truly it is a regret for the disbelievers.
interpretation: The verse refers to the regret that the disbelievers will feel on the Day of Judgment. The regret will be for their disbelief and rejection of God's message. The verse emphasizes the deep sense of loss and remorse that the disbelievers will experience, as they realize the gravity of their actions and the consequences of their disbelief. The verse serves as a warning to those who reject God's message, urging them to reflect on their actions and turn to God before it is too late.
orig: وإنه لحسرة على الكافرين

translation: And certainly is the promise of fulfillment (of punishment for the unjust)
interpretation: The verse affirms the certainty of the promise of punishment for the unjust. It serves as a reminder of the inevitability of the consequences of sin and wrongdoing. The verse emphasizes the truth and reliability of the divine promise, and encourages the believers to reflect on their actions and turn away from injustice.
orig: وإنه لحق اليقين

translation: Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High.
interpretation: The verse is a command from God to the listener to glorify and praise the name of their Lord, who is described as being the Most High. The command serves as a reminder of the greatness and majesty of God, and the importance of recognizing and acknowledging His power and authority. The verse encourages the listener to engage in an act of worship and devotion, and to cultivate a deep sense of reverence and respect for God.
orig: فسبح باسم ربك العظيم

translation: A supplicant asked about the punishment that has befallen.
interpretation: The verse speaks about a person who has asked about a punishment that has already occurred. The verse could be interpreted as a response to a question about the reason for a specific calamity or disaster that has befallen a community. The verse implies that the punishment is a consequence of the actions of the people, and serves as a reminder of the importance of righteousness and obedience to God.
orig: سأل سائل بعذاب واقع

translation: For the disbelievers, there is no protector.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the vulnerability of the disbelievers, highlighting that they do not have a protector. This verse can be interpreted as a warning to those who reject faith and the guidance of Allah, emphasizing the consequences of their actions. The verse can also be understood as a reminder that true protection and security can only come from Allah, and that those who reject His guidance and mercy are ultimately left without any means of protection.
orig: للكافرين ليس له دافع

translation: From God, the owner of the ways of ascent.
interpretation: The verse speaks of God as the one who has control over the ways of ascent or the paths to heaven. This can be interpreted as a reminder of God's power and control over all aspects of existence, including the journey of the soul after death. The verse may also be seen as a statement of faith, recognizing God as the one who has the power to elevate or exalt individuals to the highest levels of spiritual development and closeness to Him.
orig: من الله ذي المعارج

translation: The angels and the Spirit will ascend to Him in a Day the measure whereof is (like) fifty thousand years.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the angels and the Spirit (often interpreted as the Archangel Gabriel) ascending to God on a Day that is equivalent to fifty thousand human years. This verse is meant to convey the majesty and grandeur of God, and the relative brevity and insignificance of human existence. The verse suggests that the events of this world and the passage of time are but a fleeting moment in the presence of God, and serves as a reminder of the ultimate reality and significance of the divine.
orig: تعرج الملائكة والروح إليه في يوم كان مقداره خمسين ألف سنة

translation: So be patient, (it is) a beautiful patience.
interpretation: The verse encourages the believer to be patient in the face of difficulties and hardships. The word 'patience' here refers to the ability to remain calm, composed, and steadfast in the face of adversity, and to endure suffering without becoming frustrated or losing hope. The phrase 'a beautiful patience' highlights the virtue of patience, and its importance in the life of a believer. The verse teaches that patience is not only a means of overcoming challenges, but also a source of beauty and grace, and a manifestation of one's faith and trust in God's plan and wisdom.
orig: فاصبر صبرا جميلا

translation: They see it distant.
interpretation: The verse is referring to the disbelievers who see the Day of Judgment as something far off and unlikely to happen. They are heedless of the signs and warnings of the approaching Day and continue to live in sin and disobedience. The verse serves as a reminder that the Day of Judgment is inevitable and that it is near, regardless of how it may seem to the disbelievers.
orig: إنهم يرونه بعيدا

translation: and We will surely see it near
interpretation: The verse speaks about the nearness of a certain event or phenomenon, which is being observed or awaited. The use of the word 'We' implies a sense of collective observation or anticipation. The verse may be referring to the nearness of God's judgment or the fulfillment of a prophecy. The verse emphasizes the immediacy of the event and encourages the reader to be prepared for its arrival.
orig: ونراه قريبا

translation: On the Day when the sky will be like molten brass.
interpretation: The verse describes the state of the sky on the Day of Judgment, when it will be transformed into a molten, liquid-like state of brass. This imagery conveys a sense of overwhelming heat and destruction, emphasizing the cataclysmic nature of the Day of Judgment. The verse serves as a reminder of the impending Day of Judgment, urging people to prepare for it by living righteously and avoiding sin.
orig: يوم تكون السماء كالمهل

translation: And the mountains will be like carded wool.
interpretation: The verse describes the transformation of the mountains into something resembling carded wool, which is a reference to their complete destruction and leveling. This imagery is used to depict the Day of Judgment and the end of the world as we know it. The mountains, which are considered stable and permanent in this world, will be destroyed and changed into something unrecognizable, signifying the overwhelming power and authority of God over His creation. The verse serves as a reminder of the impermanence of this worldly life and the inevitability of the Day of Judgment, and encourages people to prepare for it by living righteously and following God's commands.
orig: وتكون الجبال كالعهن

translation: And
interpretation: No interpretation
orig: ولا يسأل حميم حميما

translation: They will see the criminals in chains, their garments torn to shreds, as they burn in the Blazing Fire.
interpretation: The verse describes the fate of the criminals on the Day of Judgment. They will be seen in chains, their garments torn to shreds, as they suffer in the Blazing Fire. The verse emphasizes the humiliation and degradation of the criminals, who will be unable to escape the punishment for their sins. It serves as a warning to those who commit crimes and engage in immoral behavior, reminding them of the severe consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's judgment.
orig: يبصرونهم يود المجرم لو يفتدي من عذاب يومئذ ببنيه

translation: And his wife and his brother.
interpretation: The verse refers to two individuals, a wife and a brother, in relation to an unspecified person. The meaning of the verse depends on the context in which it is used. However, the general interpretation is that it mentions two people who are closely related to someone, either through marriage or blood relation. The verse could be referring to their behavior, actions, or characteristics, or it could be emphasizing the importance of their roles or relationships. Ultimately, the interpretation of the verse depends on the specific context in which it is used in the Qur'an.
orig: وصاحبته وأخيه

translation: And We have already sent messengers before you, [O Muhammad], among the sectors of the ancient peoples.
interpretation: The verse refers to the prophets and messengers that were sent by God before the Prophet Muhammad to different communities and nations in the past. The verse highlights the continuity of God's message and the consistency of His approach in sending messengers to guide humanity towards the right path. The verse serves as a reminder that the message of Islam is not new, but rather a continuation and fulfillment of the previous messages and prophecies.
orig: وفصيلته التي تؤويه

translation: And if every one among the creatures of the earth died, yet would He let live a people thereon.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the power and control of God over all of creation, stating that even if every living creature on earth were to die, God would still choose to keep a people alive. This verse highlights the mercy and compassion of God, even in the face of destruction. It also serves as a reminder of the ultimate power and authority of God, who has the ability to give and take life as He pleases.
orig: ومن في الأرض جميعا ثم ينجيه

translation: No! Indeed, it is a reminder.
interpretation: The verse is a negation of a previous statement and emphasizes that what follows is not a mere fabrication, but a reminder and a warning. It serves to grab the attention of the listener or reader, preparing them for the message that is to come. The verse can be seen as a call to attentiveness and reflection, encouraging the reader to ponder the meaning of the reminder and to take it to heart.
orig: كلا إنها لظى

translation: I apologize, but the Arabic text you provided appears to be incomplete or incorrect. The phrase you provided, "نزاعة للشوى" (niza'at lishshawy), does not appear in the Qur'an. Please provide the correct and complete verse for me to interpret. Thank you.
interpretation: No interpretation
orig: نزاعة للشوى

translation: Invite to the way of your Lord with wisdom and good instruction, and argue with them in a way that is best. Indeed, your Lord is most knowing of who has strayed from His way, and He is most knowing of who is [rightly] guided.
interpretation: The verse instructs the prophet Muhammad (PBUH) to invite people to the way of God with wisdom and good instruction. It emphasizes the importance of using reason and argumentation in a respectful and considerate manner. The verse reminds the prophet that God is all-knowing and that the ultimate outcome is in His hands. The verse serves as a guidance for the prophet and for all Muslims to engage in dawah (inviting others to Islam) in a wise and respectful manner, recognizing that the outcome is ultimately in God's hands.
orig: تدعو من أدبر وتولى

translation: And he gathered (them) and was arrogant.
interpretation: The verse speaks about a person who has gathered people, likely in a position of power or leadership, and has done so with arrogance and pride. The verse serves as a warning against arrogance and the dangers it poses, reminding the reader that even those who have amassed power and wealth can be subject to divine judgement if they do not use their position for good and instead act with arrogance and pride.
orig: وجمع فأوعى

translation: Indeed, man was created anxious:
interpretation: The verse highlights the inherent anxiety and fear that is a part of the human condition. This anxiety may stem from the uncertainty of life, the fear of death, or the struggle to find meaning and purpose in one's existence. The verse can be seen as a reminder of the human's vulnerability and need for guidance and reassurance, which can be found in faith and submission to God's will.
orig: إن الإنسان خلق هلوعا

translation: When evil touches a person
interpretation: The verse describes the experience of a person who is afflicted by evil or hardship. The verse can be understood as a reminder that everyone will face difficult times and challenges in their lives. It can also be seen as a call to be patient and steadfast in the face of adversity, trusting that God will provide a way through the hardship.
orig: إذا مسه الشر جزوعا

translation: And when the good is kept away from them.
interpretation: The verse refers to a situation where people are prevented from receiving or experiencing goodness or blessings. This could be due to their own actions, such as disbelief, disobedience, or injustice. The verse may serve as a reminder that God is the ultimate source of all goodness and blessings, and that He has the power to withhold them from those who do not deserve them or who turn away from Him. It may also be a call for people to reflect on their actions and to turn back to God in repentance and obedience, in order to receive His blessings and mercy.
orig: وإذا مسه الخير منوعا

translation: except the believers
interpretation: The phrase 'except the believers' refers to those who have faith in God and follow His teachings. In this context, it implies that the believers will be spared from the punishment that is being described in the verse. The verse may be emphasizing the importance of faith and righteousness as a means of protection from divine retribution, and encouraging people to turn to God and seek His mercy and forgiveness.
orig: إلا المصلين

translation: Those who are constant in prayer.
interpretation: The verse refers to individuals who are steadfast and consistent in their performance of prayer. It highlights the importance of maintaining a regular and uninterrupted practice of prayer in one's daily life. This verse serves as a reminder to Muslims of the significance of prayer in their relationship with God and the importance of maintaining a consistent and dedicated approach to their religious obligations.
orig: الذين هم على صلاتهم دائمون

translation: And those who are wealthy but have a known right in their wealth.
interpretation: The verse speaks about those individuals who possess wealth and have a known right or claim upon it. This likely refers to the obligation of the wealthy to give a portion of their wealth to the poor and needy, as prescribed in Islamic teachings. The verse highlights the importance of fulfilling these obligations and ensuring that one's wealth is distributed fairly and justly. It serves as a reminder that wealth is not solely for the benefit of the individual, but also carries a responsibility towards the wider community.
orig: والذين في أموالهم حق معلوم

translation: For the seeker and the dispossessed.
interpretation: The phrase 'For the seeker and the dispossessed' is a description of those who are in need and destitute. It highlights the importance of helping and supporting those who are less fortunate, and emphasizes the value of empathy, compassion, and generosity in Islam. It serves as a reminder that those who are in a position of power and privilege have a responsibility to help those who are in need, and that true piety is not just about personal devotion, but also about caring for the welfare of others.
orig: للسائل والمحروم

translation: And those who believe in the Day of Judgment.
interpretation: The verse affirms the belief in the Day of Judgment, which is a fundamental tenet of Islam. The verse speaks of those who have faith in the Day of Judgment, implying that belief in this event is an essential aspect of being a true believer. The Day of Judgment is described as a day of accountability, when all deeds will be weighed and rewards or punishments will be given according to one's actions in this world. The verse encourages believers to uphold their faith and to prepare for the Day of Judgment through righteous deeds and good conduct.
orig: والذين يصدقون بيوم الدين

translation: And those who, when disaster strikes them, say, 'Indeed we belong to Allah, and indeed to Him we will return.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the attitude of believers in the face of calamity or hardship. When they are afflicted with a disaster, they respond with patience and acceptance, recognizing that everything comes from God and that they will ultimately return to Him. This response reflects a deep faith and trust in God, as well as a sense of submission to His will. It also highlights the believers' understanding of the transient nature of this world and the permanence of the hereafter. The verse serves as a reminder for Muslims to remain steadfast and patient in the face of adversity, and to always keep their ultimate return to God in mind.
orig: والذين هم من عذاب ربهم مشفقون

translation: Indeed, the punishment of their Lord is not absent.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the certainty of God's punishment for those who disbelieve and commit injustices. The phrase 'not absent' suggests that the punishment is inevitable and cannot be avoided. It serves as a warning to those who deny God and engage in unjust actions, reminding them that the consequences of their actions will come and they will not be able to escape from them.
orig: إن عذاب ربهم غير مأمون

translation: And those who guard their private parts.
interpretation: The verse highlights the importance of modesty and chastity, emphasizing the need for individuals to protect and safeguard their private parts. This verse serves as a reminder of the value of self-restraint and self-discipline in matters of intimacy and sexual conduct, and encourages believers to uphold the moral values of modesty and chastity in their daily lives.
orig: والذين هم لفروجهم حافظون

translation: except their spouses or those their right hands possess, for indeed, they will not be blamed
interpretation: The verse provides an exception to the rule of modesty and covering of the body for women. According to the verse, women are not required to cover themselves in front of their husbands or those whom they possess (slaves). This exception is given because these men are considered to be close and intimate with the women, and therefore, there is no harm or blame in their uncovering in front of them. This verse is often used to support the Islamic practice of allowing women to uncover in front of their husbands and close male relatives.
orig: إلا على أزواجهم أو ما ملكت أيمانهم فإنهم غير ملومين

translation: But as for him who desires (anything) beyond that, so for him there will be a chastisement of a painful kind.
interpretation: The verse warns of the consequences for those who seek more than what has been decreed by God. The punishment for such individuals will be severe and painful. This verse can be interpreted as a reminder of the limits set by God and the importance of accepting and being content with one's lot. It can also serve as a warning to those who are never satisfied and are always striving for more, regardless of the cost or consequences.
orig: فمن ابتغى وراء ذلك فأولئك هم العادون

translation: And those who are keeping their trusts and their covenants.
interpretation: The verse highlights the importance of fulfilling one's trusts and covenants, and recognizes those who uphold these responsibilities. The verse serves as a reminder of the significance of honesty, integrity, and reliability in one's actions and relationships. Those who are mentioned in this verse are praised for their adherence to their promises and their commitment to protecting the rights and interests of others.
orig: والذين هم لأماناتهم وعهدهم راعون

translation: And those who are firm in their testimonials (or promises).
interpretation: The verse speaks about those individuals who are steadfast and unwavering in their commitments and testimonies. These individuals are reliable and can be trusted to uphold their promises and responsibilities. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of being truthful and reliable in one's actions and words, and of the rewards that come from being consistent and firm in one's beliefs and commitments.
orig: والذين هم بشهاداتهم قائمون

translation: And those who are careful about their prayers.
interpretation: The verse highlights the importance of being mindful and diligent about performing one's prayers. It speaks to the character of those who prioritize their connection with God through prayer, and who make an effort to maintain this connection through consistent practice. This verse serves as a reminder of the significance of prayer in the Islamic faith, and encourages believers to prioritize and protect their prayer practices.
orig: والذين هم على صلاتهم يحافظون

translation: Therein they shall have all that they will desire, and with Us is yet more.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the blessings and rewards that will be given to the righteous in Heaven. The verse emphasizes the abundance of blessings and the limitless generosity of God, stating that the righteous will have 'all that they will desire' and yet, there is still more with God. The verse serves as a source of hope and motivation for those who are striving for righteousness and piety, reminding them of the great blessings that await them in the Hereafter.
orig: أولئك في جنات مكرمون

translation: But what of those who disbelieved before them? They are lost.
interpretation: The verse is a rhetorical question that compares the fate of the disbelievers who lived before the time of the Prophet Muhammad with the fate of the listeners of the Qur'an. The answer to the question is that those who disbelieved before are lost, implying that they are doomed to suffer eternal punishment in the afterlife. The verse serves as a warning to the listeners of the Qur'an, urging them to believe and avoid the same fate as the disbelievers of the past.
orig: فمال الذين كفروا قبلك مهطعين

translation: On the right and on the left, are two gardens.
interpretation: The verse describes the presence of two gardens, one on the right side and the other on the left side. This imagery is often used in the Qur'an to depict paradise or a place of great beauty and abundance. The gardens symbolize the blessings and rewards that God bestows upon those who are righteous and obedient. The verse may also serve as a reminder that God's blessings are all-encompassing and surround us from all sides, and that we should be grateful for the many gifts that we often take for granted.
orig: عن اليمين وعن الشمال عزين

translation: And every person is hoping to enter the Paradise of Abundance.
interpretation: The verse highlights the human longing and desire for eternal happiness and bliss in the afterlife. The 'Paradise of Abundance' refers to the ultimate destination of the righteous and the pious in the hereafter. The verse emphasizes the shared human aspiration for eternal joy and contentment, regardless of one's background, status, or circumstances. It serves as a reminder of the ultimate purpose of human existence and the importance of striving for righteousness in pursuit of this goal.
orig: أيطمع كل امرئ منهم أن يدخل جنة نعيم

translation: No, indeed, We created them from that which they do not know.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the power and knowledge of God in creating human beings. It suggests that humans are created from something beyond their comprehension or understanding. The verse can be interpreted as a reminder of the limitations of human knowledge and understanding in the face of divine power and wisdom. It may also serve as a call for humility and recognition of the divine in the creation of life.
orig: كلا إنا خلقناهم مما يعلمون

translation: Nay, I swear by the Lord of the easts and the wests, verily we are able.
interpretation: The verse is a solemn oath by the Lord of the easts and the wests, emphasizing the power and ability of the speaker. The phrase 'verily we are able' suggests that the speaker is making a promise or a threat, and is confident in their ability to carry it out. The verse may be referring to God's power and ability to carry out His will, or it may be spoken by a prophet or a messenger, asserting their authority and determination to deliver God's message. The verse can be interpreted as a reminder of the power and sovereignty of God, or as a statement of resolve and determination by the speaker.
orig: فلا أقسم برب المشارق والمغارب إنا لقادرون

translation: So that We may exchange better than them and they taste not of it
interpretation: The verse speaks about God's ability to replace something bad with something good. The phrase 'So that We may exchange better than them' implies that God can replace something that is not pleasing with something that is better. The second part of the verse, 'and they taste not of it', refers to the people who will not be able to enjoy the benefits of the new and better situation. This verse can be interpreted as a reminder of God's power and mercy, and as a promise of a better future for those who are patient and steadfast in their faith.
orig: على أن نبدل خيرا منهم وما نحن بمسبوقين

translation: So leave them to their play and vain talk until they meet their Day which they are promised.
interpretation: The verse instructs the Prophet Muhammad to leave the disbelievers alone in their disbelief and to let them continue in their heedless behavior. The phrase 'play and vain talk' refers to their frivolous and empty pursuits. The verse emphasizes that the disbelievers will ultimately face the consequences of their actions on the Day of Judgment, which they have been promised. The verse serves as a reminder that the disbelievers' rejection of the truth will not last forever and that they will ultimately be held accountable for their actions.
orig: فذرهم يخوضوا ويلعبوا حتى يلاقوا يومهم الذي يوعدون

translation: The day they will emerge from the graves swiftly as if they were racing towards a goal.
interpretation: This verse describes the Day of Judgment when people will emerge from their graves and rush towards the place of judgment. The image of people emerging quickly from their graves and racing towards a goal conveys a sense of urgency and seriousness. The verse emphasizes the seriousness of the Day of Judgment and the need for people to prepare for it. The image of people rushing towards a goal also conveys a sense of accountability, as they will be held accountable for their actions in this life. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of preparing for the Day of Judgment and living a righteous life.
orig: يوم يخرجون من الأجداث سراعا كأنهم إلى نصب يوفضون

translation: Their gaze is cast down in humiliation, they are seized by a penalty that day which they were promised.
interpretation: The verse describes the fate of those who were once proud and haughty, but are now humiliated and filled with fear. They are experiencing the consequences of their actions, as they are being punished on the day they had been warned about. The verse emphasizes the significance of the day of judgment, and the reality of the punishment for those who do not heed the warnings and continue to commit wrongdoings.
orig: خاشعة أبصارهم ترهقهم ذلة ذلك اليوم الذي كانوا يوعدون

translation: Indeed, We sent Noah to his people, [saying], 'Warn your people before there comes to them a painful punishment.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the mission of the prophet Noah, who was sent by God to warn his people of an impending punishment. The verse emphasizes the importance of prophetic warnings and the urgency for the people to heed the message before it is too late. The verse serves as a reminder of the role of prophets as messengers of God's will and the consequences of ignoring their warnings.
orig: إنا أرسلنا نوحا إلى قومه أن أنذر قومك من قبل أن يأتيهم عذاب أليم

translation: He said, 'O my people, I am indeed to you a clear warner.'
interpretation: The verse relays a message from a prophet or a messenger to his people, warning them of the consequences of their actions. The messenger emphasizes the clarity and explicitness of his warning, indicating that the people have no excuse for ignoring it. The verse highlights the role of prophets and messengers as conveyors of God's message, and the importance of heeding their warnings and guidance.
orig: قال يا قوم إني لكم نذير مبين

translation: Worship Allah and associate nothing with Him, and to parents do good, and to relatives, orphans, the needy, the near neighbor, the neighbor farther away, the companion at your side, the traveler, and those whom your right hands possess. Indeed, Allah does not like those who are self-deluding and boastful.
interpretation: The verse outlines the various groups of people that Muslims should treat with kindness, respect, and generosity. This includes parents, relatives, the needy, neighbors, travelers, and slaves. The verse emphasizes the importance of worshiping Allah alone and avoiding arrogance and self-delusion. The verse serves as a reminder to Muslims of their responsibilities towards others and the importance of humility and devotion to Allah.
orig: أن اعبدوا الله واتقوه وأطيعون

translation: He will forgive you your sins and will delay you for a specified term. Indeed, the promise of Allah, when it comes, is not delayed.
interpretation: The verse speaks about God's forgiveness and mercy towards the believers. It emphasizes that God will forgive their sins and give them more time to repent and reform. However, the verse also reminds that the promise of God's punishment will ultimately be fulfilled, and it will not be delayed or postponed once it arrives. The verse encourages the believers to seek God's forgiveness, repent and use the time given to them wisely and prepare for the Day of Judgment.
orig: يغفر لكم من ذنوبكم ويؤخركم إلى أجل مسمى إن أجل الله إذا جاء لا يؤخر لو كنتم تعلمون

translation: He (Noah) said, 'My Lord, I have called my people night and day.'
interpretation: The verse is a statement made by the prophet Noah, expressing his frustration and disappointment at his people's rejection of his message. Noah had been preaching to his people day and night, trying to guide them towards the right path, but they had not listened. The verse emphasizes the persistence and dedication of Noah in his mission, despite the lack of response from his people. It also highlights the importance of da'wah (inviting others to Islam) and the patience and perseverance required in the face of rejection and opposition.
orig: قال رب إني دعوت قومي ليلا ونهارا

translation: And never came to them a sign from their Lord except they turned away from it.
interpretation: The verse highlights the people's rejection and denial of their Lord's signs and messages. Despite the continuous efforts of the Lord to guide them, the people persistently ignored and turned away from the signs, choosing to remain in their state of disbelief. The verse emphasizes the people's closed-mindedness and unwillingness to accept the truth, even when presented with clear and undeniable evidence.
orig: فلم يزدهم دعائي إلا فرارا

translation: And indeed, whenever I called them to seek forgiveness from Him, they stuck their fingers in their ears, covered themselves with their garments, persisted in their refusal, and became arrogant.
interpretation: The verse describes the response of people when they were called to seek forgiveness from God. Instead of heeding the call, they chose to reject it by blocking their ears, covering themselves, persisting in their refusal, and becoming arrogant. The verse highlights the stubbornness and pride of these people, who refuse to acknowledge their sins and seek forgiveness from God. The verse serves as a warning to those who follow a similar path, emphasizing the importance of humility, self-reflection, and seeking forgiveness from God.
orig: وإني كلما دعوتهم لتغفر لهم جعلوا أصابعهم في آذانهم واستغشوا ثيابهم وأصروا واستكبروا استكبارا

translation: Then indeed, I called to them aloud
interpretation: The verse speaks about the speaker's (who is believed to be the Prophet Muhammad) efforts to warn and guide the people who have gone astray. Despite the speaker's clear and loud call, the people did not listen or heed his warning. The verse highlights the importance of listening and responding to the guidance of the prophets and the consequences of ignoring their message.
orig: ثم إني دعوتهم جهارا

translation: Then I will surely reveal to them My signs, and I will surely make an entrance for them of every kind.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the revelation of divine signs and the creation of various means of access for the people. The verse suggests that these signs and means of access will be made clear and visible to the people, and that they will be provided with everything they need. The verse can be interpreted as a message of hope and reassurance from God, who will provide for and guide those who seek His guidance and follow His signs.
orig: ثم إني أعلنت لهم وأسررت لهم إسرارا

translation: And say, 'Ask forgiveness of your Lord. Indeed, He is ever a forgiver.'
interpretation: The verse addresses the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) and instructs him to tell the people to seek forgiveness from their Lord. This is a direct command from Allah (SWT) to His servants, urging them to repent and seek His mercy. The verse emphasizes Allah's (SWT) boundless forgiveness and His readiness to accept the repentance of His servants. It serves as a reminder of the importance of seeking forgiveness and turning to Allah (SWT) in times of need and distress.
orig: فقلت استغفروا ربكم إنه كان غفارا

translation: The sky sends down on you in showers.
interpretation: The verse describes the sky sending down rain in a continuous and steady stream. This can be interpreted as a blessing from God, providing sustenance and nourishment for the earth and all living things. It can also be seen as a symbol of God's mercy and compassion, as water is essential for life. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of appreciating and being grateful for the natural resources that God provides for us.
orig: يرسل السماء عليكم مدرارا

translation: And He will give you sustenance from (your) presence, and children, and will give you gardens and give you rivers.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the blessings that God will bestow upon the believers, including sustenance, children, gardens, and rivers. The verse emphasizes the generosity and abundance of God's blessings, and His ability to provide for His servants. The verse serves as a reminder of the blessings that God has given to the believers, and encourages them to be grateful and thankful for His bounty.
orig: ويمددكم بأموال وبنين ويجعل لكم جنات ويجعل لكم أنهارا

translation: What is [the matter] with you that you do not strive for the greatness of God?
interpretation: The verse is a rhetorical question addressed to the listeners or readers, urging them to strive for the cause of God and seek His greatness. It implies that the listeners or readers are neglecting their duty towards God, and the verse serves as a reminder for them to fulfill their religious obligations and work towards achieving spiritual growth and nearness to God.
orig: ما لكم لا ترجون لله وقارا

translation: And We have certainly created you over stages/phases.
interpretation: The verse highlights the process of creation of human beings, emphasizing that it was not a single event but a gradual process that occurred over multiple stages or phases. This interpretation is supported by modern scientific understanding of human development, which occurs over a series of stages from conception to birth. The verse can also be seen as a reminder of the complexity and intricacy of God's creation, and a call for humans to reflect on their own existence and purpose.
orig: وقد خلقكم أطوارا

translation: Do you not see how Allah has created seven heavens in layers?
interpretation: The verse highlights the majesty and power of Allah by describing the creation of the seven heavens in layers. This description serves as a reminder of the greatness of Allah and the wonders of His creation. The verse may also be seen as a call to reflect on the mysteries of the universe and to recognize the existence and oneness of Allah. The verse encourages contemplation and reflection on the natural world as a means of understanding and deepening one's faith.
orig: ألم تروا كيف خلق الله سبع سماوات طباقا

translation: And He made the moon a light in it and the sun a lamp.
interpretation: The verse describes the creation of the universe and the role of the moon and the sun in it. The moon is described as a 'light' and the sun as a 'lamp', indicating their importance and significance in the functioning of the universe. The verse emphasizes the order and harmony in the creation of the universe and the role of the celestial bodies in maintaining the balance and order in the universe.
orig: وجعل القمر فيهن نورا وجعل الشمس سراجا

translation: And it is Allah who produces gardens, trellised and untrellised, and palm trees and crops of different kinds, and olives and pomegranates, similar and dissimilar.
interpretation: The verse highlights the power and ability of Allah to create and grow various types of plants and crops. The list of examples, including gardens, palm trees, olives, and pomegranates, is meant to emphasize the diversity and abundance of what Allah can produce. The phrase 'similar and dissimilar' further emphasizes the variety and complexity of Allah's creation. The verse serves as a reminder of Allah's power and greatness, and encourages believers to reflect on and appreciate the natural world around them.
orig: والله أنبتكم من الأرض نباتا

translation: Then He will return you to it and produce you in it [on the Day of Resurrection] in groups
interpretation: The verse speaks about the Day of Resurrection when God will return people to this world and gather them in groups. This return to the world will be for the purpose of judgment, and the groups refer to the different categories of people who will be judged according to their deeds. The verse emphasizes the power and control of God over all things, and the certainty of the Day of Resurrection.
orig: ثم يعيدكم فيها ويخرجكم إخراجا

translation: And Allah has made for you the earth spread out.
interpretation: The verse highlights the mercy and generosity of Allah in making the earth a spacious and habitable place for human beings. The word 'spread out' implies that the earth has been made vast and expansive, providing ample space for human beings to live and thrive. This verse serves as a reminder of the blessings that Allah has bestowed upon humanity and the need to be grateful for these blessings.
orig: والله جعل لكم الأرض بساطا

translation: So that you may follow her paths, the paths of those before you.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the importance of learning from the past and following the paths of those who came before. By doing so, one can gain knowledge, wisdom, and guidance. The verse can be interpreted as an invitation to study the history, traditions, and teachings of previous generations, and to apply that knowledge in one's own life. It can also be seen as a reminder that there is value in the experiences and lessons of the past, and that by following them, one can avoid making the same mistakes and achieve success in their endeavors.
orig: لتسلكوا منها سبلا فجاجا

translation: Noah said, 'My Lord, indeed they have disobeyed me and followed those whose wealth and children have not increased them except in loss.'
interpretation: In this verse, Noah is expressing his frustration and disappointment towards his people who have disobeyed him and followed the lead of those who are wealthy and have many children, but who have not gained any true benefit or increase in goodness from these worldly possessions. Noah recognizes that these people are actually losing out in the sight of God by choosing to follow the wealthy and powerful instead of following the path of God. This verse serves as a reminder that wealth and status in this world do not guarantee success or righteousness in the next life, and that true increase and benefit comes from following God and His messenger.
orig: قال نوح رب إنهم عصوني واتبعوا من لم يزده ماله وولده إلا خسارا

translation: and they planned a great plot
interpretation: The verse refers to the planning of a great plot or scheme by a group of people. The implication is that this plot is sinister and potentially harmful. The verse may be warning against such scheming and reminding the reader of the potential consequences of such actions.
orig: ومكروا مكرا كبارا

translation: And they have said: 'Do not leave your gods, nor should you leave Wadd or Suwa'
interpretation: No interpretation
orig: وقالوا لا تذرن آلهتكم ولا تذرن ودا ولا سواعا ولا يغوث ويعوق ونسرا

translation: And they have indeed led astray many, and do not increase the wrongdoers except in error.
interpretation: The verse highlights the negative influence of certain individuals who have led many people astray. The verse emphasizes that these wrongdoers will not only continue to err themselves but will also increase the error of others. The verse serves as a warning to those who follow the wrong path and a reminder of the negative consequences of leading others astray.
orig: وقد أضلوا كثيرا ولا تزد الظالمين إلا ضلالا

translation: Because of what they had earned, they were drowned and then were put into a fire, and they found no one besides Allah to help them.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the punishment of people who had committed sins and earned their negative fate. They were drowned and then put into a fire, which symbolizes the severity of their punishment. The verse emphasizes the isolation of these people, who found no one besides Allah to help them, indicating the ultimate power and justice of God. The verse serves as a reminder of the consequences of sinful actions and the importance of seeking God's mercy and forgiveness.
orig: مما خطيئاتهم أغرقوا فأدخلوا نارا فلم يجدوا لهم من دون الله أنصارا

translation: And Noah said, 'My Lord, do not leave on the earth any unbelievers.
interpretation: In this verse, the prophet Noah is making a plea to God to not leave any unbelievers on the earth. This verse can be interpreted as a reflection of the prophet's frustration and disappointment in the lack of faith and acceptance of his message by the people around him. It can also be seen as a reflection of the severity of the situation and the need for decisive action. Ultimately, it highlights the importance of faith and the consequences of rejecting God's message.
orig: وقال نوح رب لا تذر على الأرض من الكافرين ديارا

translation: Indeed, if you leave them, they will mislead your servants and not give birth except to an ungrateful, disbelieving [offspring].
interpretation: The verse warns against leaving unbelievers who will lead the servants of the believer astray and give birth to a wicked and disbelieving offspring. The verse emphasizes the negative consequences of associating with unbelievers and the importance of maintaining a strong faith and encouraging others to follow the right path.
orig: إنك إن تذرهم يضلوا عبادك ولا يلدوا إلا فاجرا كفارا

translation: My Lord, forgive me and my parents and the believers on the Day the account is established! And have mercy on the believers, men and women, and do not increase the wrongdoers except in destruction.
interpretation: The verse is a supplication to God for forgiveness and mercy. The speaker asks for forgiveness for themselves and their parents, as well as for all believers on the Day of Judgment. They also request mercy for all male and female believers. The verse concludes with a plea for the wrongdoers to not be increased in destruction, implying a desire for their guidance and salvation. Overall, the verse emphasizes the importance of seeking forgiveness and mercy, and expresses a concern for the well-being of all believers, regardless of gender.
orig: رب اغفر لي ولوالدي ولمن دخل بيتي مؤمنا وللمؤمنين والمؤمنات ولا تزد الظالمين إلا تبارا

translation: Say, [O Muhammad], 'Has there been sent down upon me (something) of the remembrance (i.e., the Qur'an) that he (i.e., Satan) taught him (i.e., one of the jinn)?'
interpretation: In this verse, the Prophet Muhammad is instructed to respond to the accusation that he is merely reciting a teaching from Satan, rather than a revelation from God. The verse emphasizes the divine origin of the Qur'an and the Prophet's role as a recipient of the revelation. It serves as a reaffirmation of the authenticity and truth of the Qur'an, and a response to the skepticism and disbelief of those who deny its divine origin.
orig: قل أوحي إلي أنه استمع نفر من الجن فقالوا إنا سمعنا قرآنا عجبا

translation: Guides to the right path, so that we believe in Him, and we put not any partner beside our Lord.
interpretation: The verse speaks about God as the one who guides to the right path, and as a result of this guidance, the believers have certainty in their faith in Him and do not associate any partners with their Lord. The verse emphasizes the importance of following God's guidance and the importance of having a pure and unwavering faith in God, free from any form of shirk (associating partners with God). It serves as a reminder of the importance of having a strong and unwavering faith in God, and the dangers of associating partners with Him.
orig: يهدي إلى الرشد فآمنا به ولن نشرك بربنا أحدا

translation: And exalted is the Majesty of our Lord! He has taken neither a spouse nor a son.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the greatness and majesty of God, who is above all human characteristics and limitations. The verse explicitly denies that God has taken a spouse or a son, affirming the Islamic belief in the oneness and uniqueness of God. This verse can be seen as a response to the Christian belief in the divinity of Jesus, who is considered by Christians to be the son of God. The verse affirms that God is independent of all creation and does not need a spouse or a son to fulfill any need or desire.
orig: وأنه تعالى جد ربنا ما اتخذ صاحبة ولا ولدا

translation: And that he used to say, 'I am against Allah on a clear path.'
interpretation: The verse is a quote of Pharaoh's statement of his opposition and defiance towards Allah. Pharaoh claimed to have a clear and straightforward path, implying that he was confident in his power and authority. However, his statement is a reflection of his arrogance, ignorance, and rejection of Allah's signs. The verse serves as a reminder of the dangers of arrogance and the importance of recognizing and submitting to Allah's power and authority.
orig: وأنه كان يقول سفيهنا على الله شططا

translation: And we (the jinn and mankind) thought that We would never be brought to account before Allah.
interpretation: The verse highlights the arrogance and ignorance of mankind and the jinn, who thought that they would never be held accountable for their actions. This verse serves as a reminder that everyone will eventually be brought before Allah and will be held accountable for their deeds. It emphasizes the importance of living a righteous and pious life, and the need to always be aware of one's actions and their consequences.
orig: وأنا ظننا أن لن تقول الإنس والجن على الله كذبا

translation: And indeed, there were men among humankind who took refuge with men of the jinn, but they (only) increased them in arrogance.
interpretation: The verse speaks about certain individuals from among humanity who sought protection from other beings, the jinn, but instead of finding safety, they were further led astray and became more arrogant. This verse highlights the dangers of seeking guidance and protection from sources other than Allah, and the negative consequences of following one's whims and desires. It serves as a reminder that true guidance and protection can only come from Allah, and that following other paths can lead to destruction and ruin.
orig: وأنه كان رجال من الإنس يعوذون برجال من الجن فزادوهم رهقا

translation: And they thought, as you thought, that Allah would never send anyone.
interpretation: The verse is addressing a group of people who are skeptical about the idea of resurrection and judgment day. They believed that death is the end of existence and that there will be no accountability for their actions. The verse challenges their disbelief and compares it to the disbelief of the readers of the QQur'an, emphasizing that they held the same wrong belief. The verse serves as a reminder that the resurrection and judgment day are real and that all people will be held accountable for their actions.
orig: وأنهم ظنوا كما ظننتم أن لن يبعث الله أحدا

translation: And We have already touched the sky and found it full of strong guards and flames.
interpretation: The verse describes the sky as being guarded by strong and powerful forces and filled with flames. This imagery can be interpreted as a metaphor for the power and might of God, who is in control of the heavens and the earth. The verse emphasizes the majesty and awe-inspiring nature of God, and the idea that the natural world is under His protection and guidance. It may also serve as a reminder of the limits of human knowledge and understanding, as the sky is described as something that has been 'touched' but not fully comprehended or understood.
orig: وأنا لمسنا السماء فوجدناها ملئت حرسا شديدا وشهبا

translation: And We were, [of Our own accord,] staying in some of them [the towns] for a duration, so if you [O Muhammad] should enter [one of them], you would find their people in absolute despair, never to emerge.
interpretation: The verse describes the fate of certain towns that were abandoned by their inhabitants, who were found in a state of despair and unable to leave. The verse implies that the people had lost all hope and were unable to escape their situation. The verse may be referring to the fate of past civilizations that were destroyed or abandoned due to their sins and disbelief. It serves as a reminder to those who reject the message of Islam and commit sins, that they too may face a similar fate if they do not repent and turn back to God.
orig: وأنا كنا نقعد منها مقاعد للسمع فمن يستمع الآن يجد له شهابا رصدا

translation: And I do not know which of you it may be that I will touch with punishment, them or they who are behind them, a punishment from your Lord that is inevitable.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the uncertainty of when and where God's punishment will come, and who it will affect. The verse emphasizes the inevitability of God's punishment, and the fact that it could affect anyone, whether it be the person being addressed or those who come after them. The verse serves as a reminder of the power and authority of God, and the need for all people to be mindful of their actions and to seek guidance from their Lord.
orig: وأنا لا ندري أشر أريد بمن في الأرض أم أراد بهم ربهم رشدا

translation: And I, I am one of the righteous, and we were of two kinds.
interpretation: The verse speaks about a division or separation between two groups of people, with the speaker identifying as part of the righteous group. The verse implies that there is a clear distinction between the righteous and those who are not, and that the speaker aligns themselves with the former group. The verse may be emphasizing the importance of moral conduct and the consequences of one's actions, with the speaker asserting their own righteousness and separating themselves from those who do not meet that standard.
orig: وأنا منا الصالحون ومنا دون ذلك كنا طرائق قددا

translation: And We thought that We would never be overtaken by God in the earth, and never would we be evicted from our place.
interpretation: The verse expresses the arrogance and overconfidence of certain individuals who believed that they were invincible and that they would never be defeated or expelled from their land. The phrase 'We thought' indicates that their belief was misguided and that they were wrong in their assumption. The verse serves as a reminder that no one is above God's power and that even the most powerful can be brought down by His will. The verse may also serve as a warning against arrogance and overconfidence, reminding people that they should not take their blessings for granted and should always be mindful of God's power and will.
orig: وأنا ظننا أن لن نعجز الله في الأرض ولن نعجزه هربا

translation: And when we heard the guidance, we believed in it. So whoever believes in their Lord, there will be no fear for them, nor will they grieve.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the believers who, upon hearing the guidance (referring to the message of Islam), believed in it. The verse emphasizes the positive outcome of having faith in one's Lord, as it brings peace of mind and protection from fear and grief. The verse serves as a reminder of the benefits of believing in God and the peace that it brings, contrasting it with the fear and grief experienced by those who do not have faith.
orig: وأنا لما سمعنا الهدى آمنا به فمن يؤمن بربه فلا يخاف بخسا ولا رهقا

translation: And I am of those who submit, and among the righteous. So whoever submits, then indeed, for them is the way made clear.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the speaker's identity as a submitter to God's will and as one of the righteous. The verse goes on to say that those who submit (to God) will have a clear way for them. This verse highlights the importance of submission to God, and the promise of guidance for those who do so. The verse can be seen as a message of hope and assurance for those who strive to live a righteous life and follow the path of God.
orig: وأنا منا المسلمون ومنا القاسطون فمن أسلم فأولئك تحروا رشدا

translation: But as for the deviators, they will be fuel for the Fire.
interpretation: The verse refers to the 'deviators' or those who stray from the right path, and states that they will become fuel for the Fire. This is a metaphor for the severe punishment that awaits such individuals in the afterlife. The verse serves as a warning to those who choose to ignore God's teachings and follow their own desires and whims, emphasizing the grave consequences of their actions.
orig: وأما القاسطون فكانوا لجهنم حطبا

translation: And if they had adhered to the right way, We would certainly have provided them with abundant water.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the promise of God to provide abundant water to the people if they adhere to the right way or follow the path of righteousness. The verse implies that the provision of sustenance and blessings from God is linked to the obedience and submission of the people. It serves as a motivation for the people to follow the path of righteousness and a reminder of the blessings that come with it.
orig: وأن لو استقاموا على الطريقة لأسقيناهم ماء غدقا

translation: So that We may make them taste it, and they have surely tasted the punishment of humiliation because they rejected Our signs.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the punishment that God has prepared for those who reject His signs and deny His message. The phrase 'So that We may make them taste it' indicates that the punishment is a form of retribution for their disbelief, and a means for them to understand the gravity of their actions. The phrase 'they have surely tasted the punishment of humiliation' emphasizes that this punishment has already begun, and that it is a form of shame and disgrace for the disbelievers. The verse serves as a warning to those who reject God's signs and message, reminding them of the consequences of their disbelief and the humiliation that awaits them.
orig: لنفتنهم فيه ومن يعرض عن ذكر ربه يسلكه عذابا صعدا

translation: And that the mosques are for Allah, so do not invoke with Allah anyone.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of monotheism and the sanctity of mosques. It commands that mosques should be used solely for the worship of Allah, and that no one else should be associated with Him in worship. This commandment serves as a reminder of the oneness of Allah and the importance of maintaining the purity of the worship of Allah in the mosques.
orig: وأن المساجد لله فلا تدعوا مع الله أحدا

translation: And when Abraham invoked His Lord [Allah] with these words: 'My Lord! They have indeed led astray many among men.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the prophet Abraham (Ibrahim in Arabic) expressing his concern about the people who have been led astray from the right path. Abraham turns to his Lord, Allah, in prayer, seeking His help and guidance. The verse emphasizes the role of the prophets as intercessors and advocates for their people, and highlights the importance of seeking divine guidance and help in the face of adversity and temptation.
orig: وأنه لما قام عبد الله يدعوه كادوا يكونون عليه لبدا

translation: Say, 'Indeed, I only invite to my Lord and do not associate with Him anyone.'
interpretation: The verse is a statement by the Prophet Muhammad, instructing him to declare his belief and his invitation to others to follow the path of his Lord, Allah. The verse emphasizes the Prophet's commitment to the worship of Allah alone, without associating any partners with Him. This declaration of faith and rejection of polytheism is a fundamental principle of Islam, and the verse serves as a reminder of the importance of maintaining the unity and purity of Allah's worship, and the rejection of any form of shirk (associating partners with Allah).
orig: قل إنما أدعو ربي ولا أشرك به أحدا

translation: Say, 'I do not have power over you for harm or guidance.'
interpretation: The verse is a message from the Prophet Muhammad, directed towards the disbelievers who rejected his message and threatened him. The verse emphasizes the Prophet's lack of control over the actions and fate of the disbelievers, and his inability to force them to accept the truth. The verse also highlights the fact that the Prophet's role is only to convey the message of Islam, and it is up to the people to choose whether or not to accept it. The verse serves as a reminder of the powerlessness of humans in controlling the actions and beliefs of others, and the importance of leaving the matter of guidance and salvation in the hands of God.
orig: قل إني لا أملك لكم ضرا ولا رشدا

translation: Say, 'None can protect me from Allah, nor can I find a refuge besides Him.'
