The punishment will be sent down upon them in a narrow part of the valley, emphasizing the overwhelming and inescapable nature of the punishment. The verse serves as a warning to the disbelievers, urging them to repent and turn to God before it is too late.
orig: فوقاهم الله شر ذلك اليوم ولقاهم نضرة وسرورا

translation: And their reward for their patience will be Gardens of Eden, with rivers flowing beneath - their eternal home. Such is the reward of those who are virtuous.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the reward of those who are patient and virtuous. They will be granted Gardens of Eden, a symbol of eternal paradise, with rivers flowing beneath. This reward is promised to those who have shown patience and perseverance in the face of adversity. The verse serves as a source of hope and motivation for those who strive to live a righteous life, reminding them of the great reward that awaits them in the afterlife.
orig: وجزاهم بما صبروا جنة وحريرا

translation: Seated in it, they were unaware of the Hereafter. No sun was shining on them, nor any cold wind.
interpretation: The verse describes a group of people who are so engrossed in their present life that they are oblivious to the Hereafter. The phrase 'no sun was shining on them' symbolizes the absence of light and guidance in their lives, while 'nor any cold wind' represents the lack of trials and tribulations that could awaken them from their heedlessness. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of preparing for the Hereafter and seeking guidance from God, as well as the need to be aware of the signs of the Day of Judgment.
orig: متكئين فيها على الأرائك لا يرون فيها شمسا ولا زمهريرا

translation: And cast over them the shadow of death, and made lowest their gardens bringing them low.
interpretation: The verse describes the punishment of a group of people by casting a shadow of death over them and humbling their gardens. The 'shadow of death' symbolizes the impending doom and destruction of the people, while the humbling of their gardens suggests the loss of their prosperity and wealth. The verse may be interpreted as a metaphor for the downfall of a civilization or a community that has become corrupt and unjust. It serves as a warning that even the most prosperous and powerful can be brought low by divine judgment.
orig: ودانية عليهم ظلالها وذللت قطوفها تذليلا

translation: And it will be circulated among them a cup [of wine] from [a spring] within Paradise, as if it were a flowing spring.
interpretation: The verse describes the blessings that will be bestowed upon the believers in Paradise. A cup of wine will be circulated among them, coming from a spring within Paradise. The description of the cup being as if it were a flowing spring suggests an abundance of this blessing, and the ease with which it will be available to the believers. The verse serves as a promise of the rewards that await the faithful, emphasizing the bountiful and luxurious nature of Paradise.
orig: ويطاف عليهم بآنية من فضة وأكواب كانت قواريرا

translation: Scales of justice, they have perfected (them)
interpretation: The verse refers to the scales that will be used on the Day of Judgment to weigh the good and bad deeds of every person. The phrase 'they have perfected (them)' implies that these scales are completely fair and just, without any possibility of error or bias. This verse serves as a reminder that every person will be held accountable for their actions and that the scales will ensure a fair and just outcome for all, regardless of their status or power in this world.
orig: قوارير من فضة قدروها تقديرا

translation: And they will be given to drink therein a drink that will intoxicate them, its mixture is of Zanjabil.
interpretation: The verse describes the punishment of the wrongdoers in the hereafter. They will be made to drink a drink that will intoxicate them, causing them to lose their senses and reason. The drink is described as having a mixture of Zanjabil, which is believed to be a fragrant plant or root, possibly ginger. This imagery of a intoxicating drink is used metaphorically to depict the intense suffering and anguish that the wrongdoers will experience in the hereafter. The verse serves as a warning to those who disobey God and engage in sinful behavior, reminding them of the severe consequences that await them in the hereafter.
orig: ويسقون فيها كأسا كان مزاجها زنجبيلا

translation: Eyes to be feared because they are a witness.
interpretation: The verse refers to the 'eyes' that serve as witnesses to the actions of individuals. These 'eyes' could refer to the physical eyes of others who observe one's actions, or to the metaphorical 'eyes' of God, who sees all. The verse emphasizes the importance of being mindful of one's actions, as they are constantly being observed and will be held accountable for them. The fear or 'reverence' that the verse speaks of serves as a reminder to live with integrity, honesty, and righteousness, as one's actions will ultimately be judged.
orig: عينا فيها تسمى سلسبيلا

translation: And around them will ( circulate) boys of everlasting youth: if you see them, you would think them scattered pearls.
interpretation: The verse describes the blessings that the righteous will receive in paradise, specifically the presence of 'boys of everlasting youth' who will serve them. The beauty and purity of these youths is likened to scattered pearls, emphasizing their perfection and desirability. The verse serves as a promise of reward for those who live righteously and a motivation for good deeds, as well as a source of comfort and hope for those who have lost young loved ones. The verse also highlights the boundless generosity and mercy of God towards those who believe in Him.
orig: ويطوف عليهم ولدان مخلدون إذا رأيتهم حسبتهم لؤلؤا منثورا

translation: And when you see, then look again, and you will see a distant horizon full of blessings and great kingdom.
interpretation: This verse speaks about the promise of blessings and great kingdom that will be seen in the distance. The repetition of 'see' emphasizes the importance of being observant and having a keen eye. The verse could be interpreted as a metaphor for the rewards of patience and perseverance, encouraging the believers to remain steadfast in their faith and to keep their eyes on the ultimate goal of attaining God's blessings and kingdom. It also serves as a reminder that the blessings and kingdom are not immediately present, but rather, they are to be found in the distance, requiring patience and endurance to reach.
orig: وإذا رأيت ثم رأيت نعيما وملكا كبيرا

translation: Above them are their garments of green brocade and silk, and adornments of silver; their Lord will give them a drink of pure wine.
interpretation: The verse describes the blessings that will be given to the righteous in the afterlife. They will be given garments of green brocade and silk, adornments of silver, and will be given pure wine to drink by their Lord. The green color of the garments symbolizes the lush gardens of paradise, and the pure wine represents the ultimate pleasure and satisfaction. The verse emphasizes the generosity and abundance of God's blessings for the righteous and the great reward that awaits them in the afterlife.
orig: عاليهم ثياب سندس خضر وإستبرق وحلوا أساور من فضة وسقاهم ربهم شرابا طهورا

translation: Indeed, this was for you a reminder, and indeed, (as for) your effort, it has been appreciated.
interpretation: The verse is a message from God to the listeners, informing them that the previous verses or events were a reminder for them. It also acknowledges their efforts and informs them that it has been appreciated. This verse may have been revealed during a time of difficulty or struggle for the early Muslims, and it serves as a source of encouragement and motivation for them. It reminds the listeners that their efforts and struggles are not going unnoticed and that they will be rewarded for them.
orig: إن هذا كان لكم جزاء وكان سعيكم مشكورا

translation: Indeed, it is We who have sent down to you the Qur'an as a revelation.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes that the Qur'an is a revelation sent down by God, and that it is a continuous process of sending down the Qur'an, rather than a one-time event. This serves to remind the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) and the believers of the divine origin of the Qur'an and its importance in their lives. It also highlights the significance of the Qur'an as a source of guidance and wisdom for all of humanity.
orig: إنا نحن نزلنا عليك القرآن تنزيلا

translation: So be patient for the decision of your Lord, and do not be like the one who goes astray and becomes ignorant.
interpretation: The verse advises the believers to be patient and to wait for the decision of their Lord, meaning that they should trust in God's plan and not lose faith or become impatient. The verse also warns against following the example of those who are astray and have no knowledge or understanding of the truth. These people are ignorant of the consequences of their actions and are therefore more likely to make mistakes and stray from the path of righteousness. The verse encourages the believers to be steadfast and to seek knowledge and understanding, so that they can avoid the mistakes of the ignorant and stay on the path of righteousness.
orig: فاصبر لحكم ربك ولا تطع منهم آثما أو كفورا

translation: And mention the name of your Lord in the morning and in the evening.
interpretation: This verse is a command to the believers to remember and mention the name of their Lord at the beginning and end of each day. This can be interpreted as a reminder to be mindful of God's presence and power at all times, and to seek His guidance and protection throughout the day. It can also be seen as a way to express gratitude and devotion to God, by dedicating the first and last parts of the day to Him. This verse encourages Muslims to maintain a constant connection with their Lord, and to make Him an integral part of their daily routine.
orig: واذكر اسم ربك بكرة وأصيلا

translation: And of the night, prolong [your] prostration to Him and exit, soon after, prostrating.
interpretation: The verse encourages Muslims to engage in nightly prayer and prostration as a form of worship and devotion to God. By exhorting the reader to 'prostrate' and 'exit, soon after, prostrating,' the verse emphasizes the importance of maintaining focus and dedication during prayer, and of making it a consistent and integral part of one's daily routine. The verse also highlights the spiritual benefits of engaging in nightly prayer, and the sense of peace and tranquility that it can bring.
orig: ومن الليل فاسجد له وسبحه ليلا طويلا

translation: Indeed, they love the immediate and leave behind for themselves a heavy day.
interpretation: The verse speaks about people who prefer immediate gratification and pleasure, and neglect the responsibilities and consequences of their actions. The 'heavy day' that they leave behind for themselves refers to the Day of Judgment, which will be a day of great hardship and difficulty. The verse serves as a warning to those who are more concerned with the pleasures of this world, and neglect the importance of preparing for the next. It emphasizes the importance of considering the long-term consequences of our actions and striving to live a righteous life in accordance with God's will.
orig: إن هؤلاء يحبون العاجلة ويذرون وراءهم يوما ثقيلا

translation: We created them, then We strengthened their creation, then when We will, We replace them with others like them, in a manner known to Us.
interpretation: The verse speaks about God's power and control over the creation of human beings. It highlights that God created human beings, strengthened their creation, and when He wills, He has the power to replace them with others. The verse emphasizes the idea that God has complete control over life and death, and that He can replace people with others at any time, in a manner that is known only to Him. The verse serves as a reminder of God's power and greatness, and the need for people to be mindful of their actions and to live in accordance with His will.
orig: نحن خلقناهم وشددنا أسرهم وإذا شئنا بدلنا أمثالهم تبديلا

translation: Indeed, this is a reminder. So whoever wills may take a path to his Lord.
interpretation: The verse speaks about a reminder or a message being given, and invites people to reflect on it and take heed. The verse emphasizes the freedom of choice given to humans and their ability to choose their own path. The verse suggests that the reminder is a means for people to find their way back to their Lord, and those who choose to reflect and act upon the reminder will be guided towards their Lord.
orig: إن هذه تذكرة فمن شاء اتخذ إلى ربه سبيلا

translation: And you do not will except that Allah wills. Indeed, Allah is Knowing and Wise.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the power and knowledge of Allah, stating that humans can only will and act within the boundaries of Allah's will. The verse reminds humans that Allah is all-knowing and wise, and that all that happens is in accordance with His will and wisdom. The verse serves as a reminder of the limitations of human power and knowledge, and encourages submission and acceptance of Allah's will.
orig: وما تشاءون إلا أن يشاء الله إن الله كان عليما حكيما

translation: Whoever wants may enter My mercy.' And as for the unjust, I have prepared a painful punishment.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the offer of God's mercy to all of humanity, and the warning of a painful punishment for the unjust. The verse emphasizes the free will of individuals, as it is up to each person to choose whether or not to enter God's mercy. At the same time, it also makes clear that there will be consequences for those who choose to commit injustices, and that a painful punishment has been prepared for them. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of striving for righteousness and seeking God's mercy.
orig: يدخل من يشاء في رحمته والظالمين أعد لهم عذابا أليما

translation: And the messengers have already passed on before them, in their footsteps have passed on the messengers.
interpretation: The verse highlights the continuity of prophethood and the consistency of the message brought by the messengers of God. The verse emphasizes that the messengers have already come and gone before, leaving behind their teachings and examples, and that these teachings and examples have been passed on from one generation to the next. The verse serves as a reminder that the message of God has always been consistent and that the guidance is available for those who seek it.
orig: والمرسلات عرفا

translation: The (thunder)claps of clouds are from (the) striking.
interpretation: The verse describes the sound of thunder as coming from the striking or collision of clouds. This is a scientifically accurate description of the phenomenon of thunder, which is caused by the rapid expansion and contraction of air caused by the electrical discharge between clouds or between a cloud and the ground. The verse can be seen as a demonstration of the Qur'an's consistency with the laws of nature and its ability to provide scientifically accurate information. It can also be seen as a reminder of the power and majesty of God, who controls the forces of nature and is able to bring about such awe-inspiring phenomena as thunder and lightning.
orig: فالعاصفات عصفا

translation: And the distributors, they distributed.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the role of 'distributors' in the process of distribution. The Arabic word used here, 'nasharat', means 'distributors' or 'those who distribute'. The verb 'nashar' means 'to distribute' or 'to spread'. The verse highlights the function of these distributors in the distribution process, implying that the distribution was carried out by them. The verse does not provide any further context or information about the distributors or the nature of the distribution, so a specific interpretation is not possible without additional information.
orig: والناشرات نشرا

translation: So the (existent) distinctions are distinct.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the clear and distinct nature of the distinctions or divisions that have been made. The verse emphasizes the clarity and distinctness of these divisions, indicating that they are clear and evident. The verse may be referring to the divisions between right and wrong, truth and falsehood, or other such distinctions. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of recognizing and understanding these distinctions, and of making the right choices based on this understanding.
orig: فالفارقات فرقا

translation: And mention the sister of Ayub (Job)
interpretation: The verse refers to the story of Prophet Ayub (Job) and mentions his wife, who stood by him during his hardships and trials. The verse emphasizes the importance of remembering and acknowledging the support and patience of family members and loved ones during difficult times. It also highlights the role of women in supporting and strengthening their husbands in the face of adversity and hardships.
orig: فالملقيات ذكرا

translation: As an excuse or a pledge.
interpretation: The phrase 'عذرا أو نذرا' in the Qur'an can be translated to 'As an excuse or a pledge' in English. The interpretation of this phrase depends on the context in which it is used. When used in the context of making a pledge or promise to God, it can be interpreted as a commitment or a solemn vow. On the other hand, when used in the context of seeking forgiveness or making an excuse, it can be interpreted as a justification or explanation for one's actions. Overall, the phrase emphasizes the importance of sincerity and commitment in one's relationship with God, whether it be through making a pledge or seeking forgiveness.
orig: عذرا أو نذرا

translation: You are only promised the inevitable.
interpretation: The verse is a reminder that humans will inevitably face the consequences of their actions, whether they are good or bad. The 'inevitable' in this context refers to the Day of Judgment, when all human beings will be held accountable for their deeds. The verse encourages people to prepare for this inevitable day by living a righteous life and avoiding sin and injustice. It also serves as a warning to those who deny the existence of the afterlife or underestimate its significance, reminding them that they will not escape the consequences of their disbelief and wrongdoing.
orig: إنما توعدون لواقع

translation: And when the stars are obliterated
interpretation: The verse describes the end of time and the Day of Judgment, when the stars will be obliterated or disappear. This event is a sign of the overwhelming power and authority of God, who has control over all of creation. The verse emphasizes the magnitude and significance of this event, and the insignificance of humanity in comparison. It serves as a reminder of the transience of life and the importance of preparing for the afterlife.
orig: فإذا النجوم طمست

translation: And when the sky splits apart
interpretation: The verse speaks about the dramatic and catastrophic event of the sky splitting apart. This event is often associated with the Day of Judgment in Islamic eschatology and is described as a sign of the end of the world. The verse emphasizes the overwhelming and awe-inspiring nature of this event and serves as a reminder of the power and majesty of God. It also serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, urging them to repent and turn back to God before it is too late.
orig: وإذا السماء فرجت

translation: And when the mountains are made to pass away
interpretation: This verse speaks about the end of the world and the Day of Judgment. The phrase 'when the mountains are made to pass away' is a metaphor for the complete and utter destruction of the world as we know it. The verse emphasizes the overwhelming and cataclysmic nature of the event, which will be so powerful that even the mountains, which are often seen as symbols of stability and permanence, will be destroyed. The verse serves as a reminder of the transience of this world and the inevitability of the Day of Judgment, and encourages believers to prepare for that day by living righteously and following God's commands.
orig: وإذا الجبال نسفت

translation: And when the messengers were given good news [of Allah's help] and they said, 'Our Lord, increase us in [our] strength and make us firm [in our] feet and help us against the disbelieving people.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the prayer of the messengers of God when they received good news of God's help and support. They asked God to increase their strength, make them firm in their faith and actions, and help them against the disbelievers. The verse highlights the struggles and challenges faced by the messengers and their reliance on God for help and support. It also emphasizes the importance of steadfastness and perseverance in the face of adversity and the importance of seeking God's help and guidance in all matters.
orig: وإذا الرسل أقتت

translation: For what day have We postponed?
interpretation: The verse is a rhetorical question posed by the Qur'an, asking for what day or event has the punishment been postponed. The verse suggests that the Day of Judgment or punishment is inevitable and cannot be postponed indefinitely. It serves as a reminder that the consequences of one's actions will eventually come due, and that delaying repentance or righteous actions will not prevent the reckoning. The verse encourages believers to prepare for the inevitable day of judgment and to strive for righteousness in their daily lives.
orig: لأي يوم أجلت

translation: For the Day of Sorting out.
interpretation: The phrase 'For the Day of Sorting out' refers to the Day of Judgment, when all deeds will be accounted for and people will be divided into two groups: those who will go to heaven and those who will go to hell. The phrase emphasizes the importance of this day, which will determine the eternal fate of every individual. It is a reminder to live a righteous life and prepare for this inevitable day.
orig: ليوم الفصل

translation: And what can make you know what is the Day of Sorting?
interpretation: The verse poses a rhetorical question, emphasizing the unknown and uncertain nature of the 'Day of Sorting' or 'Day of Judgment'. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of being prepared for this ultimate day of reckoning, when all deeds will be weighed and judged by God. The verse encourages believers to strive for righteousness and piety, as the outcome of the Day of Judgment is not known and the consequences of one's actions will be severe.
orig: وما أدراك ما يوم الفصل

translation: Woe to the disbelievers on that day.
interpretation: The verse is a warning of a coming day of judgement and doom for the disbelievers. The exclamation 'Woe' expresses intense pain and suffering, indicating the severity of the day. The phrase 'on that day' emphasizes the imminence and inevitability of the day, and the fact that it is a specific and unavoidable point in time. The verse serves as a reminder of the consequences of disbelief and rejection of the truth, and the ultimate fate of those who persist in their disbelief.
orig: ويل يومئذ للمكذبين

translation: Have We not destroyed the first [people]
interpretation: The verse is a rhetorical question, implying that the answer is yes. It speaks about the destruction of previous civilizations or communities that had existed before. The purpose of this verse is to remind the listeners or readers of the power and authority of God, who has the ability to destroy entire communities if they disobey His commands or go against His will. This verse can serve as a warning to those who are heedless or arrogant, urging them to reflect on the consequences of their actions and to turn back to God before it is too late.
orig: ألم نهلك الأولين

translation: Then shall follow them the later ones.
interpretation: The verse refers to a group of people who will come after another group. The exact nature of these two groups and the context of their appearance is not specified in the verse, leaving it open to interpretation. However, the verse implies that the actions or fate of the first group will have some impact or relevance to the second group, who will follow in their footsteps. This verse could be interpreted as a warning or a reminder that our actions have consequences, and that those who come after us will be affected by the choices we make.
orig: ثم نتبعهم الآخرين

translation: Thus do We deal with the criminals.
interpretation: The verse is a statement by God that He will deal with criminals in a similar manner. The previous verses may have described the punishment of criminals, and this verse emphasizes that this is the established practice of God. The verse may serve as a warning to those who are committing crimes, and as a reassurance to those who are oppressed by criminals that God will bring justice.
orig: كذلك نفعل بالمجرمين

translation: Woe to the liars, on that day.
interpretation: The verse is a warning of an impending doom for the liars on a specific day. The day is not specified, but the tone is ominous, indicating that it is a day of reckoning. The word 'makdhubin' refers to those who are persistent in their lying and deception, and the verse serves as a reminder that they will not escape the consequences of their actions. The severity of the warning suggests that the punishment for these individuals will be severe and unavoidable.
orig: ويل يومئذ للمكذبين

translation: Did We not create you from a despised water?
interpretation: The verse is a rhetorical question, reminding people of their origins and emphasizing the power of God in creating them from what might be considered an insignificant and lowly substance. The verse may serve as a reminder of human vulnerability and dependence on God, and may also be interpreted as a call for humility and gratitude towards the Creator. The verse can also be seen as a reminder of the unity of all living beings, as all are created from the same basic elements.
orig: ألم نخلقكم من ماء مهين

translation: And We made them (the previous generations) leaders inviting to the Fire; and on the Day of Resurrection, they will not be helped.
interpretation: The verse refers to certain leaders of previous generations who were made 'leaders inviting to the Fire', meaning they led their people towards a path that ultimately leads to the Hellfire. These leaders were given power and authority, but they used it in a negative way, leading their people astray and causing them harm. The second part of the verse states that on the Day of Resurrection, these leaders will not receive any help or support, highlighting the consequences of their actions and the ultimate fate of those who lead others towards destruction.
orig: فجعلناه في قرار مكين

translation: To a degree that is known.
interpretation: The phrase refers to the limit or extent of something, specifically the amount of knowledge or understanding that a person has. The phrase implies that there is a limit to what a person can know or understand, and that this limit is known to God. The phrase can be used to remind people of the boundaries of their knowledge and understanding, and to encourage them to humbly acknowledge the limitations of their own abilities.
orig: إلى قدر معلوم

translation: And We have indeed measured out [precisely] Our provision [for you].
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the divine control and measurement of the resources and provisions that God has allotted for humanity. The phrase 'We have indeed measured out' conveys a sense of precision and accuracy in the distribution of resources, and the phrase 'Our provision' refers to the blessings and provisions that God has given to humanity. The verse serves as a reminder that all that humans have is given by God, and that they should be grateful for it and use it wisely.
orig: فقدرنا فنعم القادرون

translation: Woe to the liars on that day.
interpretation: The verse is a warning of an impending doom for the liars on a specific day. The day is not specified, leaving it to be understood as the Day of Judgment. The warning is a reminder of the consequences of lying and deceiving, which is a major sin in Islam. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in falsehood and deceit, urging them to repent and turn to the truth before it is too late.
orig: ويل يومئذ للمكذبين

translation: Have We not made the earth a place to settle?
interpretation: The verse is a rhetorical question that highlights the bounty and provisions that God has given to humanity through the earth. The verse emphasizes the idea that the earth has been created as a place for people to live and thrive, with all the resources and means of sustenance that they need. The verse serves as a reminder of God's generosity and blessings towards humanity, and encourages people to be grateful and thankful for what they have been given.
orig: ألم نجعل الأرض كفاتا

translation: the living and the dead
interpretation: The phrase 'the living and the dead' is a reference to all of humanity, both those who are currently alive and those who have already passed away. It emphasizes the all-encompassing knowledge and power of God, who has power and control over all of His creation, both the living and the dead.
orig: أحياء وأمواتا

translation: And We placed therein [i.e., Sheba] mighty pillars, and gave you to drink of sweet water.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the blessings that God bestowed upon the people of Sheba. The verse mentions two specific blessings: the presence of mighty pillars (which could refer to architectural structures or natural formations) and the provision of sweet water for their consumption. These blessings serve as a reminder of God's generosity and favor towards the people of Sheba. However, the verse also serves as a test for the people, as they must be grateful and thankful for these blessings, and not become arrogant or ungrateful. The verse may also serve as a warning, as the people of Sheba were known in Islamic tradition for their eventual rejection of God's message and their descent into decadence and sin.
orig: وجعلنا فيها رواسي شامخات وأسقيناكم ماء فراتا

translation: Woe to the liars, on that day.
interpretation: The verse is a warning to those who are liars and deny the truth. The phrase 'woe to the liars' indicates a severe punishment or consequence that will befall them on the 'day' mentioned. This day is often interpreted to mean the Day of Judgment, but it could also refer to any day of reckoning or accountability. The verse serves as a reminder that lies and deception will not go unpunished and that those who persist in them will face severe consequences.
orig: ويل يومئذ للمكذبين

translation: Go to that which you used to deny.
interpretation: The verse is a command to the disbelievers to go or proceed to the punishment that they had previously denied or disbelieved in. It serves as a reminder that their denial and disbelief will not protect them from the consequences of their actions, and that they will ultimately have to face the reality of what they had previously rejected. The verse emphasizes the inevitability of the reckoning and the importance of accepting the truth, rather than denying it.
orig: انطلقوا إلى ما كنتم به تكذبون

translation: Go to the shade of the tree which has three branches.
interpretation: The verse is a command to the listeners to seek shade under a specific tree, one that has three branches. The tree is a symbol of rest, peace, and protection. The verse can be interpreted as a metaphorical instruction for people to seek guidance, support, or wisdom from a source that has these qualities. The number three may symbolize completeness or wholeness, emphasizing the idea that the tree has all the necessary qualities to provide shade and protection. Overall, the verse encourages people to seek guidance and shelter from reliable and trustworthy sources.
orig: انطلقوا إلى ظل ذي ثلاث شعب

translation: No protector is there, nor any to give succor, from the flame.
interpretation: The verse describes a situation of complete helplessness and despair in the face of a raging fire or flame. There is no one who can provide protection or help, emphasizing the power and intensity of the fire. The verse may be used to describe the punishment of hellfire in Islamic teachings, or any other situation of overwhelming destruction. It serves as a reminder of the power of God and the insignificance of human beings in the face of His wrath.
orig: لا ظليل ولا يغني من اللهب

translation: Indeed, it (the she-camel) drinks while they (the people of Thamud) were negligent.
interpretation: The verse refers to the story of the she-camel that was sent as a miracle to the people of Thamud. Despite the clear sign from God, the people were negligent and failed to heed the warning. The verse highlights their carelessness and disregard for the divine message, emphasizing the consequences of their actions. The verse serves as a reminder to be mindful of God's signs and to not be negligent in responding to them.
orig: إنها ترمي بشرر كالقصر

translation: As if it was a shining expanse of yellow
interpretation: The verse uses a simile to describe the appearance of something, comparing it to 'a shining expanse of yellow' (jamalat safra). The precise meaning of the verse depends on the context in which it is used, but in general, it suggests that the thing being described is bright, expansive, and yellow in color. The verse may be used to evoke a sense of awe or wonder, highlighting the beauty or majesty of the thing being described.
orig: كأنه جمالت صفر

translation: Woe to the liars, on that day.
interpretation: The verse is a warning of the impending doom for liars on the day of judgment. The word 'woe' expresses a strong feeling of grief, distress or regret. The verse highlights the severity of lying and the consequences of such actions on the 'day of judgment'. The verse may also serve as a reminder to be truthful and honest in all actions and words.
orig: ويل يومئذ للمكذبين

translation: This is a day on which they will not speak.
interpretation: The verse speaks about a specific day, on which the people being referred to will not be able to speak. This day is likely a day of judgment or reckoning, where the people will be held accountable for their actions and will be unable to offer any excuses or explanations for their behavior. The verse emphasizes the seriousness of the day and the gravity of the situation, and serves as a reminder of the importance of living a righteous and just life in preparation for the inevitable day of judgment.
orig: هذا يوم لا ينطقون

translation: And no messenger came to them but they ridiculed him.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the people's rejection and mockery of the messengers sent by God. The verse emphasizes the consistent pattern of behavior of these people, who did not give the messengers a chance and instead dismissed and mocked them. The verse serves as a reminder that those who reject and mock the messengers and the message they bring will face consequences. It also highlights the importance of showing respect and openness to the messengers and their message.
orig: ولا يؤذن لهم فيعتذرون

translation: Woe to the deceivers on that day.
interpretation: The verse is a warning of an impending doom for the deceivers or liars on a specific day. The day is not specified, but the tone is ominous and final, indicating that the day of reckoning is inevitable. The verse serves as a reminder that deception and lying are grave sins that will not go unpunished and that those who engage in such behavior should repent before it is too late.
orig: ويل يومئذ للمكذبين

translation: This is the Day of Sorting out which we have appointed for you.
interpretation: The verse announces the Day of Judgment, a day that has been predestined for all people. It emphasizes the idea of sorting out or separating, indicating that this day will be a time when people will be divided according to their deeds. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of one's actions and their consequences, and the inevitability of the Day of Judgment.
orig: هذا يوم الفصل جمعناكم والأولين

translation: But if you [people] are planning a conspiracy, then indeed, My plan is superior.
interpretation: The verse is a response from God to those who are plotting or conspiring against Him or His messenger. The verse asserts that any plot or conspiracy of the people is nothing compared to the plan of God, which is always superior and will ultimately prevail. The verse serves as a reminder to those who would challenge God or His messenger that they are ultimately powerless against the will of God and that their efforts are in vain. The verse may also serve as a warning to those who would plot against others, reminding them that their plans will ultimately be uncovered and that they will be held accountable for their actions.
orig: فإن كان لكم كيد فكيدون

translation: Woe to the deceivers on that day.
interpretation: The verse is a warning of the impending doom for those who are deceitful and dishonest. It emphasizes the severity of the punishment that awaits them on the Day of Judgment. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of honesty and truthfulness, and the consequences of deceit and falsehood.
orig: ويل يومئذ للمكذبين

translation: Indeed, the righteous will be in shade and springs.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the reward that will be given to the righteous on the Day of Judgment. They will be provided with shade and springs, which symbolize comfort, peace, and abundance. The verse highlights the blessings that will be given to those who have lived a righteous life, and it serves as a source of hope and motivation for believers to strive for righteousness and piety.
orig: إن المتقين في ظلال وعيون

translation: And fruits of whatever they desire
interpretation: The verse speaks about the blessings and provisions that God bestows upon people, including the fruits that they desire. The verse emphasizes the generosity and kindness of God, who provides for His creations and fulfills their desires. The verse serves as a reminder of the blessings that we often take for granted, and it encourages us to be grateful and thankful for the gifts that we receive from God.
orig: وفواكه مما يشتهون

translation: Eat and drink, but waste not by extravagance, certainly He (God) likes not the extravagant.
interpretation: The verse encourages people to enjoy the blessings of food and drink, but with moderation and gratitude. It reminds them not to be wasteful or extravagant, as God does not approve of such behavior. This interpretation emphasizes the importance of balance and mindfulness in the consumption of resources and the need to avoid excess and extravagance.
orig: كلوا واشربوا هنيئا بما كنتم تعملون

translation: Indeed, we reward the doers of good in like manner.
interpretation: The verse affirms that those who do good will be rewarded in a manner that is commensurate with their good deeds. The verse emphasizes the just nature of God's reward system, where every action has a consequence, and good deeds will be rewarded with good. The verse serves as a motivation for people to do good, reminding them that their actions are not going unnoticed and that they will be rewarded for their efforts in this life and/or the hereafter.
orig: إنا كذلك نجزي المحسنين

translation: Woe to the deceivers on that day.
interpretation: The verse is a warning of the punishment that will befall the deceivers on a specific day. The Arabic word 'makdhub' means one who tells lies or deceives, and the word 'yawm' means day. The verse emphasizes the severity of the punishment for those who engage in deception and falsehood, and the certainty of the day of reckoning.
orig: ويل يومئذ للمكذبين

translation: Eat and drink, but be thinly aware, that you are unjust.
interpretation: The verse is a warning to those who indulge in pleasure and luxury without regard for their actions or the consequences. The command to 'eat and drink' is a metaphor for the pursuit of worldly desires, while 'be thinly aware' is a warning to be mindful of one's actions and to recognize that they are unjust. The verse serves as a reminder that the pursuit of pleasure and luxury should not come at the expense of one's moral compass and that indulgence without regard for the consequences can lead to negative outcomes.
orig: كلوا وتمتعوا قليلا إنكم مجرمون

translation: Woe to the disbelievers on that day.
interpretation: The verse is a warning of an impending doom for the disbelievers on a specific day. The day is not specified, but the tone of the verse suggests that it is a day of judgment or reckoning. The word 'woe' expresses a strong feeling of grief, distress, or regret, indicating the severity of the situation for the disbelievers. The verse serves as a reminder of the consequences of disbelief and the importance of faith and submission to God.
orig: ويل يومئذ للمكذبين

translation: And when it is said to them, 'Prostrate yourselves', they do not prostrate themselves.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the rejection of a call to worship and submission to God. The phrase 'when it is said to them' implies a command or request for the people to prostrate themselves in prayer or worship. However, the people being referred to do not comply with this request, indicating their rejection of the call to worship and submission to God. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of obedience to God and the consequences of rejecting His commands.
orig: وإذا قيل لهم اركعوا لا يركعون

translation: Woe to the disbelievers
interpretation: The verse is a warning of an impending doom for the disbelievers. It serves as a reminder that they will face severe consequences for their denial and rejection of the truth.
orig: ويل يومئذ للمكذبين

translation: And upon what [kind of] statement after this will they believe?
interpretation: The verse is questioning the credulity of the disbelievers, it is saying that after receiving the message and the proofs, what other statement or evidence will they believe in. It implies that the disbelievers have been given clear signs and messages but they still deny and reject it. The verse suggests that it is unlikely that they will believe in any new statement or evidence, as their hearts are closed to the truth.
orig: فبأي حديث بعده يؤمنون

translation: Do they not then reflect?
interpretation: The verse is a rhetorical question addressed to the disbelievers, urging them to ponder and reflect upon the signs of God. It suggests that the disbelievers are not engaging in deep thought or contemplation, and are instead ignoring the evidence of God's power and authority. The verse serves as a call to the disbelievers to consider their ways and to turn to God, reminding them of the importance of reflection and contemplation in understanding the world and their place in it.
orig: عم يتساءلون

translation: about the great news/tiding/announcement
interpretation: The phrase could be referring to any important news, announcement, or message of significance. However, without more context, it is difficult to provide a more specific interpretation.
orig: عن النبإ العظيم

translation: They are in varying differences.
interpretation: The verse speaks about a group of people who are divided and in conflict with one another. The Arabic word 'muchtilifun' comes from the root 'kh-l-f' which means 'to differ' or 'to disagree'. The verse highlights the internal strife and divisions that exist within the group. The interpretation of this verse can vary depending on the context in which it is used. However, in general, it can be understood as a warning about the dangers of disunity and division among a people, and the negative consequences that can result from such discord.
orig: الذي هم فيه مختلفون

translation: Nay, they will indeed know!
interpretation: The verse is a response to those who reject the message of Islam and deny the truth. It emphasizes that they will eventually come to know and acknowledge the truth on the Day of Judgment. The verse serves as a reminder that all actions and beliefs will be judged and that denial and rejection of the truth will not protect one from the consequences on the Day of Judgment.
orig: كلا سيعلمون

translation: Then they will surely know.
interpretation: The verse is a statement of certainty that the disbelievers, who rejected the truth and continued in their disbelief, will eventually come to know the truth. The Arabic word 'saya'lamoon' is in the future tense and carries a sense of emphasis, indicating that the knowledge they will gain will be complete and undeniable. This knowledge will come after they have faced the consequences of their disbelief and experienced the reality of the hereafter. The verse serves as a reminder that no one will be able to deny the truth on the Day of Judgment, and it encourages the believers to be patient and steadfast in their faith, knowing that the ultimate victory belongs to the truth and those who uphold it.
orig: ثم كلا سيعلمون

translation: Have We not made the earth a resting place?
interpretation: The verse is a rhetorical question that highlights the provision and mercy of God towards humanity. It asks whether or not God has made the earth a resting place or a cradle for humans. This implies that the earth is a place of comfort, safety, and rest for people. It serves as a reminder of the blessings that God has bestowed upon humanity and the need to be grateful for these blessings.
orig: ألم نجعل الأرض مهادا

translation: And the mountains as pegs
interpretation: The verse uses the metaphor of mountains as 'pegs' or 'stakes' to convey a sense of stability and firmness in the earth. The image of mountains being driven into the ground like pegs suggests a strong and unyielding foundation for the earth. This metaphor provides a sense of reassurance and stability, emphasizing the power and control of God over the natural world.
orig: والجبال أوتادا

translation: And We have created you as pairs.
interpretation: The verse highlights the creation of human beings as pairs or in couples. This can be interpreted as a reference to the biological fact that humans generally come in pairs of male and female. However, it can also be interpreted in a broader sense to mean that humans are created as pairs in terms of their complementary roles, strengths, and weaknesses. This can include the relationship between spouses, family members, friends, and society as a whole. The verse may serve as a reminder of the importance of balance, harmony, and cooperation in relationships and in the community.
orig: وخلقناكم أزواجا

translation: And We made your sleep (a) rest
interpretation: The verse speaks about the blessings that God has given to human beings, including the ability to rest and rejuvenate during sleep. The word "sleep" in this verse is described as "sabatan", which means a "period of relaxation and rest". The verse emphasizes the importance of sleep as a means of replenishing one's energy and strength, and as a way of restoring one's physical and mental well-being. It serves as a reminder of the many blessings that God has bestowed upon human beings, and encourages gratitude and appreciation for these gifts.
orig: وجعلنا نومكم سباتا

translation: And We made the night as a garment.
interpretation: The verse describes the night as a 'garment' that has been placed by God. The metaphor of the night as a garment suggests that it is a covering or protection that envelops the earth and its inhabitants. This can be interpreted as a reminder of the order and wisdom in God's creation, where the night and day alternate in a regular pattern, providing rest and activity, light and darkness, in a balanced and harmonious way. The verse can also be seen as a symbol of the mysterious and enigmatic nature of the night, which covers and conceals, revealing only what God wills, and inviting reflection and contemplation.
orig: وجعلنا الليل لباسا

translation: And We have made the day for livelihood.
interpretation: The verse explains that God has made the day for the purpose of providing sustenance and livelihood for His creations. This interpretation highlights the importance of the day as a time for work and productivity, and emphasizes the role of God in providing for His creations. The verse can also be seen as a reminder of the blessings of the day, and the need for humans to be grateful for these blessings and make the most of their time. The verse can also be understood as a reflection of the harmony and order in the universe, where every aspect of creation has a purpose and a role to play.
orig: وجعلنا النهار معاشا

translation: And We have built above you seven strong [heavens]
interpretation: The verse refers to the seven heavens that God has built above the earth, which are described as being 'strong'. This verse is part of a larger passage that emphasizes God's power and control over the universe. The 'seven heavens' are mentioned elsewhere in the Qur'an, and are often interpreted as a symbol of the complexity and grandeur of God's creation. This verse may also serve as a reminder of God's protection and care for those on earth, as the heavens are depicted as a solid structure above them.
orig: وبنينا فوقكم سبعا شدادا

translation: And We have made it a lantern and a warning.
interpretation: The verse refers to the Qur'an as a source of guidance and a warning. The word "sirajan" (سراجا) means a lantern or a source of light, indicating that the Qur'an provides guidance and enlightenment to its followers. The word "hajjan" (وهاجا) means a warning or a reminder, suggesting that the Qur'an also serves as a warning to those who ignore its teachings. The verse emphasizes the dual role of the Qur'an as both a source of guidance and a warning, highlighting its importance in the lives of Muslims.
orig: وجعلنا سراجا وهاجا

translation: And We have sent down, from the clouds, pure water.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the sending down of pure water from the clouds by God. The word 'pure' (thajjaj) implies that the water is free from impurities, and is thus suitable for the purification of both the earth and the bodies of living beings. The verse highlights the importance of water in the natural world and the role it plays in sustaining life. It also serves as a reminder of God's power and control over the natural elements and His provision for His creation.
orig: وأنزلنا من المعصرات ماء ثجاجا

translation: But We shall bring forth for them gardens and springs.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the blessings that God will bestow upon the righteous believers in the hereafter. The 'gardens and springs' symbolize the abundance of blessings that the believers will receive, including eternal paradise and the pleasure of being in the presence of God. The verse serves as a source of hope and motivation for the believers to remain steadfast on the path of righteousness, and a reminder of the rewards that await them in the afterlife.
orig: لنخرج به حبا ونباتا

translation: And gardens enclosed
interpretation: The verse refers to the image of enclosed gardens, which symbolize the blessings and rewards that await the righteous and the faithful in the afterlife. The enclosed gardens are a metaphor for the protection, security, and abundance that God provides for those who believe in Him and follow His teachings. The gardens are described as 'enclosed', emphasizing their exclusivity and the idea that only those who have earned God's favor will be granted access to them. The verse serves as a source of hope and comfort for the believers, reminding them of the beautiful rewards that await them in the afterlife if they remain steadfast in their faith and obedience to God.
orig: وجنات ألفافا

translation: Indeed, the Day of Judgment is the appointed time.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the certainty and inevitability of the Day of Judgment, referring to it as the 'appointed time'. This implies that the Day of Judgment is a fixed and unchangeable event, and that all of humanity will be held accountable for their actions on that day. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of living a righteous and virtuous life, and of the need to prepare for the Day of Judgment, which is described as a time of reckoning and accountability.
orig: إن يوم الفصل كان ميقاتا

translation: On the Day when He will blow the Trumpet, and you will come forth in crowds
interpretation: The verse speaks about the Day of Judgment, when God will blow the Trumpet and all of humanity will be resurrected and will appear before God in large groups or crowds. The verse emphasizes the grand and awe-inspiring nature of this event, as all of humanity will be gathered together and will stand before God to be judged for their actions and deeds in the worldly life. The verse serves as a reminder of the inevitability of this Day and the need for individuals to prepare for it by living a righteous and virtuous life.
orig: يوم ينفخ في الصور فتأتون أفواجا

translation: And We opened the heavens, and it became (many) doors.
interpretation: The verse describes the opening of the heavens, which then became 'abwaba', which can be translated as 'doors' or 'gates'. This imagery is used metaphorically to convey the idea of the heavens being opened wide, revealing the power and majesty of God. The verse may be interpreted as a reference to the revelation of divine knowledge or blessings, which come down from the heavens, symbolizing the connection between the divine and the human world. This verse can also be seen as a reminder of the limitless power of God, who can open the heavens and reveal its secrets at will.
orig: وفتحت السماء فكانت أبوابا

translation: And the mountains will pass away as if they were a mirage.
interpretation: The verse describes the transient and fleeting nature of the physical world, using the powerful imagery of mountains passing away like a mirage. The verse suggests that even the most permanent and enduring features of the earth, such as mountains, are subject to change and impermanence. This imagery serves as a reminder of the insignificance of worldly possessions and the transient nature of life. Ultimately, the verse calls on the reader to focus on the eternal and unchanging nature of God, in contrast to the ephemeral nature of the physical world.
orig: وسيرت الجبال فكانت سرابا

translation: Indeed, Hell has been lying in wait,
interpretation: The verse describes Hell as lying in wait, emphasizing its readiness and eagerness to receive those who are destined for it. The verse serves as a warning to those who persist in their disbelief and wrongdoing, reminding them of the imminent and inevitable punishment that awaits them if they do not repent and change their ways.
orig: إن جهنم كانت مرصادا

translation: For the transgressors is a painful punishment.
interpretation: The verse states that those who are transgressors (or commit sins) will face a painful punishment. The punishment is a consequence of their actions and a reminder of the importance of obedience and submission to God's will. The verse serves as a warning to those who engage in sinful behavior and a reminder of the consequences of their actions.
orig: للطاغين مآبا

translation: you will not dwell in it (the fire) two (periods)
interpretation: The verse speaks about the punishment of being in the fire and the brief duration of one's stay there. The phrase 'two (periods)' is interpreted as a metaphor for a short period of time. The verse is emphasizing the swift and brief nature of the punishment. This verse serves as a warning to those who persist in their wrongdoing and injustice, reminding them of the transient nature of this world and the eternal consequences of their actions.
orig: لابثين فيها أحقابا

translation: They will not taste therein coolness nor drink,
interpretation: The verse describes the punishment of the unbelievers in the hereafter. They will not experience any coolness or be able to drink any water, both of which are basic necessities for human survival. This implies that their existence will be a state of constant suffering and deprivation. This verse serves as a warning to those who reject faith and live a life of sin, emphasizing the severe consequences of their actions.
orig: لا يذوقون فيها بردا ولا شرابا

translation: except a pair of mates or a few languid ones
interpretation: The verse is describing a group of animals, specifically mentioning two types: a pair of mates and a few languid ones. The exact meaning of these animals is not specified, but the context suggests that they are insignificant or unimportant in comparison to something greater. The verse is part of a passage describing the majesty and power of God's creation, emphasizing the smallness and weakness of human beings in the face of God's greatness.
orig: إلا حميما وغساقا

translation: Reward of the treacherous.
interpretation: The phrase refers to the punishment that will be given to those who are treacherous and unfaithful. It is a warning to those who betray trusts, break promises, and act in deceitful ways. The punishment for such actions will be severe and fitting for their crimes, serving as a consequence for their wrongdoings.
orig: جزاء وفاقا

translation: They were, indeed, not expecting to be held to account.
interpretation: The verse highlights the disbelievers' lack of anticipation or preparedness for the Day of Judgment. It emphasizes their denial and rejection of the concept of accountability, indicating their heedlessness and immersion in worldly pleasures. The verse serves as a reminder that all actions, whether good or bad, will ultimately be accounted for and that no one will escape God's judgment.
orig: إنهم كانوا لا يرجون حسابا

translation: And they disbelieved in our signs (ayat) with disbelief.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the disbelief of certain people in the signs (ayat) of God. The word 'ayat' can refer to the verses of the Qzur'an or to any of the signs or evidence of God's existence and power. The verse emphasizes the rejection and denial of these signs, which is described as a form of disbelief (kufr). The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of accepting and recognizing the signs of God, and of the consequences of rejecting them. It also highlights the importance of faith and belief in God's message and guidance.
orig: وكذبوا بآياتنا كذابا

translation: And We have already (beforehand) recorded everything in a clear register.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the divine power of God in recording and preserving every event and action. The 'clear register' refers to the preservation of all deeds, both good and bad, in God's knowledge. The verse serves as a reminder that nothing is hidden from God and that every action will be accounted for in the afterlife, encouraging believers to lead a righteous life.
orig: وكل شيء أحصيناه كتابا

translation: Taste (the punishment)! Indeed, We will not increase you except in punishment.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the punishment that will be inflicted upon the wrongdoers. It emphasizes that the punishment will not be a one-time event, but rather, it will continue to increase. The phrase 'taste (the punishment)' implies that the punishment is a bitter experience that the wrongdoers will have to endure. The verse serves as a warning to those who persist in their wrongdoing and disobedience, reminding them that the consequences of their actions will be severe and unending.
orig: فذوقوا فلن نزيدكم إلا عذابا

translation: Indeed, for the righteous is a good final end.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the reward that awaits the righteous in the afterlife. The phrase 'good final end' refers to the ultimate destination of the righteous, which is a positive and desirable outcome. The verse serves as a source of hope and motivation for those who strive to lead a righteous life, reminding them that their efforts will be rewarded in the afterlife.
orig: إن للمتقين مفازا

translation: gardens and grapes
interpretation: The phrase 'gardens and grapes' is a metaphor for the blessings and bounties that God bestows upon his creation. It can also symbolize the rewards that await the righteous in the afterlife. The use of this phrase highlights the abundance and generosity of God, and serves as a reminder of the blessings that we should be grateful for.
orig: حدائق وأعنابا

translation: And like scattered dust.
interpretation: The verse uses the simile of scattered dust to describe the insignificance and transience of human beings. This simile conveys the idea that human beings are fragile and fleeting, and that their existence is temporary and transient. The verse encourages people to reflect on their mortality and the fleeting nature of their lives, and to use this reflection as a motivation to seek out the truth and to live a life of purpose and meaning.
orig: وكواعب أترابا

translation: Like a mirage in a desert: they thought it was water,
interpretation: The verse uses the simile of a mirage in a desert to describe something that appears to be real or true but is actually false or deceptive. The people in this verse thought they had found water, but it was only a mirage. This can be interpreted as a warning against false hopes and illusions, and as a reminder to be cautious and discerning in order to distinguish between what is real and what is not.
orig: وكأسا دهاقا

translation: They hear therein (in the heaven) no vain discourse, nor the cry of the sustainer of falsehood.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the purity of the heaven, where no vain or false words are heard. It emphasizes the majesty and truth of the divine realm, which is free from any form of falsity or frivolous speech. This can be interpreted as a reminder of the importance of truthfulness and sincerity in our words and actions, and the significance of striving for a higher level of consciousness and spirituality, where our thoughts and speech are guided by the highest principles of morality and ethics.
orig: لا يسمعون فيها لغوا ولا كذابا

translation: A recompense from your Lord, an accepted reckoning.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the reward that believers will receive from their Lord for their good deeds. The reward is described as a 'recompense' and an 'accepted reckoning', indicating that it is both just and pleasing to God. The verse serves as a reminder of the benefits of good deeds and the blessings that await believers in the afterlife.
orig: جزاء من ربك عطاء حسابا

translation: Lord of the heavens and the earth, and whatever is between them, the Most Merciful, they own not even a word [i.e. to say against Him].
interpretation: The verse affirms the power and authority of the Lord of the heavens and the earth and everything in between, emphasizing His boundless mercy. It also asserts that the created beings do not have the power to say or do anything against the will of the Most Merciful. This verse can be interpreted as a reminder of the greatness of God and the insignificance of human beings, and a call for humility and submission to His will.
orig: رب السماوات والأرض وما بينهما الرحمن لا يملكون منه خطابا

translation: A day when the spirit and the angels will stand in rows, they will not speak except for him whom the Most Merciful permits, and they will say, 'Right [is the judgement of] your Lord.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the Day of Judgment, when the spirit and the angels will gather and stand in rows. They will not speak unless given permission by the Most Merciful, and when they do speak, they will affirm the justice of God's judgement. The verse emphasizes the solemnity and reverence of this day, and the absolute authority of God's judgement. It serves as a reminder of the power and majesty of God, and the insignificance of humanity in comparison. It encourages believers to submit to God's will and to seek His mercy.
orig: يوم يقوم الروح والملائكة صفا لا يتكلمون إلا من أذن له الرحمن وقال صوابا

translation: That is the truth (i.e. the Day of Judgment), so whoever wills may take a way to his Lord.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the Day of Judgment and the reality of this day. It is a reminder that this day will come and that each person will be held accountable for their actions. The verse offers a choice to the reader, they can either take a way to their Lord, which can be interpreted as a call to repentance and returning to God, or they can choose to ignore the warning and continue on their current path. The verse emphasizes the importance of the decision that each person must make and the consequences that follow.
orig: ذلك اليوم الحق فمن شاء اتخذ إلى ربه مآبا

translation: We have certainly warned you of a near punishment on the Day when man will see what his hands have sent forth, and the disbeliever will say, 'Oh, I wish I were dust!',
interpretation: The verse speaks about a warning of an impending punishment on a specific day, when people will be confronted with the consequences of their actions. The disbeliever, in particular, will express regret and wish that they had been mere dust, indicating a deep sense of remorse for their disbelief and rejection of the truth. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of taking responsibility for one's actions and the reality of accountability on the Day of Judgment.
orig: إنا أنذرناكم عذابا قريبا يوم ينظر المرء ما قدمت يداه ويقول الكافر يا ليتني كنت ترابا

translation: And the waders, overwhelmed.
interpretation: The verse is a continuation of the previous verses in Surah Al-Qamar, describing the fate of the disbelievers at the time of reckoning. The "waders" refers to those who will be wading or plunging into the Fire of Hell. The word "overwhelmed" suggests that they will be completely submerged and consumed by the Fire. The verse serves as a warning to those who reject the message of Islam, emphasizing the severe consequences of their disbelief.
orig: والنازعات غرقا

translation: And the male devils—every builder and arranger.
interpretation: The verse is referring to the devils who are actively involved in their evil actions. The phrase 'male devils' is a metaphorical description of the devils, and the words 'builder and arranger' describe their role in leading people astray and causing corruption. The verse highlights the active and intentional nature of their actions, and serves as a reminder of the existence and influence of evil forces in the world.
orig: والناشطات نشطا

translation: And the waves of the sea lift up ( clouds) high
interpretation: The verse describes the power and majesty of the waves of the sea as they lift up clouds high in the sky. This verse is a reminder of the greatness of God's creation and His ability to control and command the natural elements. It serves as a call to contemplation and reflection on the signs of God in the natural world, and a reminder of His power and wisdom.
orig: والسابحات سبحا

translation: The preceding ones have already passed away.
interpretation: The verse refers to the passing away of previous generations or events, emphasizing their departure and the fact that they are no longer present. The interpretation of this verse can vary depending on the context in which it is used, but it generally serves as a reminder of the transience of life and the inevitability of change. It can also be seen as a call to move on from the past and focus on the present or future.
orig: فالسابقات سبقا

translation: And as for those who are being rebellious, the command belongs to God.
interpretation: The verse asserts that the ultimate authority and power belong to God, and those who are being rebellious or disobedient will ultimately be held accountable by Him. The verse may be referring to those who rebel against God and His messengers, or those who rebel against just authority. In either case, the verse reminds the reader that no one can escape God's judgment and that everyone will be held accountable for their actions.
orig: فالمدبرات أمرا

translation: The day that the painful cry is made
interpretation: The verse speaks about a specific day, referred to as 'the day that the painful cry is made'. This day is described as a time of great distress and suffering, marked by a painful cry or shout. The verse may be referring to the Day of Judgment, when God will separate the righteous from the wicked and mete out justice. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, urging them to repent and turn towards God before it is too late.
orig: يوم ترجف الراجفة

translation: It follows it closely.
interpretation: The phrase 'It follows it closely' refers to the metaphorical 'shadow' or 'cloud' of doom and destruction that follows the unjust and wicked. This shadow symbolizes the impending punishment or retribution that will inevitably befall those who persist in their wrongdoing. The verse serves as a warning that no one can escape the consequences of their actions, and that the just and righteous have nothing to fear from this shadow, while the unjust and wicked cannot escape it. It emphasizes the importance of leading a righteous and just life, and the need to avoid falling into the trap of wrongdoing and sin.
orig: تتبعها الرادفة

translation: Hearts were that day luminous
interpretation: The verse describes the state of the believers' hearts on the Day of Resurrection as being luminous or radiant. This imagery conveys the idea that the believers' hearts will be pure, free from sin and filled with the light of faith and knowledge of God. It also suggests that the believers will be able to see and understand the truth clearly on that day, as their hearts will be free from the veils of ignorance and doubt. This verse serves as a reminder of the importance of cultivating a pure and enlightened heart, and of the rewards that await those who strive for spiritual growth and development.
orig: قلوب يومئذ واجفة

translation: Submissive are their eyes.
interpretation: The verse describes the humble and submissive posture of the people who have recognized the greatness and power of God. Their eyes are described as being 'submissive', indicating their complete surrender and submission to God's will. This verse serves as a reminder of the importance of humility and submission in one's relationship with God, and encourages believers to maintain a humble and submissive attitude towards God in all aspects of their lives.
orig: أبصارها خاشعة

translation: They say, 'Are we then to be returned to the dust?'
interpretation: The verse is a continuation of a conversation between the disbelievers and God's messengers, where the disbelievers express their disbelief in the resurrection and the Day of Judgment. They question whether they will be returned to the dust, meaning that they will cease to exist after death and will not be resurrected. The verse emphasizes the disbelievers' denial of the afterlife and their rejection of the idea that their actions in this life will be judged and held accountable.
orig: يقولون أإنا لمردودون في الحافرة

translation: If We had willed, We could have made you (all) into angels (of equal grade).
interpretation: The verse emphasizes God's power and authority over all of creation. The statement 'If We had willed, We could have made you (all) into angels (of equal grade)' highlights the fact that God has the ability to change the nature of things and to transform one form of creation into another. The use of the word 'angels' in this verse is not meant to be taken literally, but rather as a symbol of a higher, more perfect form of existence. The verse serves as a reminder of God's greatness and the limitations of human understanding and power.
orig: أإذا كنا عظاما نخرة

translation: They said, 'That is but a lost game.'
interpretation: The verse is part of a conversation between the disbelievers and the prophet Moses, where the disbelievers are rejecting the signs of God and calling the message of Moses a 'lost game'. The phrase 'lost game' implies that the message of Moses has no value or benefit in their eyes. The verse highlights the rejection and lack of understanding of the disbelievers towards the message of God, and serves as a reminder of the importance of recognizing and accepting the truth.
orig: قالوا تلك إذا كرة خاسرة

translation: For it is but a single shout,
interpretation: The verse speaks of a 'shout' or a 'blast' that is a warning or a reminder. The phrase 'it is but a single shout' emphasizes the suddenness and the finality of the warning. The verse suggests that the warning will come without warning, and its impact will be immediate and irreversible. The verse serves as a call to action for those who hear it, urging them to heed the warning and prepare for the consequences.
orig: فإنما هي زجرة واحدة

translation: And when they are in the afternoon
interpretation: The verse is describing a group of people who are engaged in a specific activity during the afternoon. The context of the verse is important for understanding the exact meaning and significance of this activity. However, on its own, the verse suggests that the people are preoccupied with something that is taking place during the afternoon hours. The verse could be implying that the people are so engrossed in their activity that they are unaware of the passage of time and the approach of evening. Alternatively, the verse may be emphasizing the significance of the afternoon as a specific time of day when certain events or revelations occur. The exact interpretation of the verse depends on its context within the Qarter of the Qur'an.
orig: فإذا هم بالساهرة

translation: Was there any story told to you (O Muhammad) of Moses?
interpretation: The verse is a question directed to the Prophet Muhammad asking if he has been told the story of Moses. This question is likely posed in the context of a conversation or a teaching session, where the story of Moses is about to be discussed. The verse serves to introduce the topic of the discussion and to engage the listener or reader in the narrative. It highlights the importance of knowing and understanding the stories of the past prophets, as they serve as lessons and examples for the believers.
orig: هل أتاك حديث موسى

translation: When his Lord called him in the sacred valley of Tuwa.
interpretation: The verse recounts the story of the prophet Moses, and specifically the moment when God called him in the sacred valley of Tuwa. This moment marks a turning point in Moses' life, as it is when God chooses him for a mission and speaks to him directly. The verse emphasizes the significance of this moment and the special relationship between Moses and God, as well as the holy nature of the place where this encounter takes place.
orig: إذ ناداه ربه بالواد المقدس طوى

translation: Go to Pharaoh, indeed, he has transgressed.
interpretation: The verse is a command to the Prophet Moses to go to Pharaoh and confront him about his tyranny and transgression. The verse emphasizes Pharaoh's wrongdoing and his rejection of God's message. The verse sets the stage for the confrontation between Moses and Pharaoh, highlighting the power dynamic and the significance of the message that Moses has been sent to deliver. The verse also serves as a reminder of the consequences of transgression and the importance of heeding God's message.
orig: اذهب إلى فرعون إنه طغى

translation: And say, 'Are you waiting except that Allah should send upon you punishment from above you or from beneath your feet?'
interpretation: The verse addresses the Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) and instructs him to ask the disbelievers if they are waiting for Allah's punishment to come upon them from above (such as from the sky) or from beneath their feet (such as from the earth). The verse emphasizes the imminent and inevitable punishment that awaits those who reject Allah's message and persist in their disbelief and transgression. It serves as a warning and a call to repentance for the disbelievers, urging them to turn to Allah before it is too late.
orig: فقل هل لك إلى أن تزكى

translation: And I will guide you to your Lord so you may be afraid (of Him).
interpretation: The verse speaks about guiding someone towards their Lord so that they may develop a sense of fear and reverence for Him. The fear mentioned here is not a fear of punishment, but rather a healthy respect and recognition of one's place in the presence of the Almighty. This guidance is a blessing and a mercy from the one who is guiding, as it opens the door to a deeper understanding and relationship with the Lord.
orig: وأهديك إلى ربك فتخشى

translation: So let them taste it, the consequence of their disbelief. And away with the unjust people.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the punishment of the disbelievers and the unjust people. The phrase 'let them taste it' implies that the punishment is a direct result of their disbelief and unjust actions. The second part of the verse, 'and away with the unjust people', emphasizes the complete removal of these people and their wickedness. This verse serves as a reminder of the consequences of disbelief and unjust actions and the ultimate fate of those who persist in them.
orig: فأراه الآية الكبرى

translation: He (the prophet Noah) denied and was arrogant.
interpretation: The verse refers to the story of the prophet Noah and his people. It highlights Noah's denial and arrogance towards the message of God, which he was tasked to deliver to his people. This verse serves as a reminder of the consequences of rejecting God's message and the importance of humility and obedience towards God's commands.
orig: فكذب وعصى

translation: Then he turned away eagerly
interpretation: The verse describes a person who, after receiving a revelation or message, turns away from it in a hurried or eager manner. The interpretation of this verse could be that the person was not receptive to the message or revelation, and actively rejected or ignored it. Alternatively, it could also mean that the person was overwhelmed by the message and needed time to process or understand it. Regardless of the specific reason, the verse highlights the individual's rejection of the message and their desire to distance themselves from it.
orig: ثم أدبر يسعى

translation: Summon (with a blow of the trumpet), so he will announce
interpretation: The verse speaks about the sounding of the trumpet on the Day of Judgment, which will signal the beginning of the resurrection and the gathering of all souls. The verse emphasizes the role of the angel who will blow the trumpet and make the announcement, signaling the end of the world and the beginning of the final judgment.
orig: فحشر فنادى

translation: And he said, 'My Lord is the Most High,'
interpretation: The verse is a quote from the Prophet Ibrahim (Abraham) as he was thrown into the fire by his people. Despite the danger he was in, Ibrahim remained steadfast in his faith and declared that his Lord is the Most High, indicating his belief in God's supremacy, power, and protection. The verse emphasizes the importance of faith and trust in God, especially during times of hardship and persecution.
orig: فقال أنا ربكم الأعلى

translation: And Allah took them with a punishment of the first (life) and the last (afterlife).
interpretation: The verse speaks about the punishment of those who have transgressed and committed wrongdoing.
