The verse serves as a warning against such behavior and invites the reader to reflect on the consequences of their actions and the possibility of facing a similar punishment.
orig: وإذا مروا بهم يتغامزون

translation: And when they turn away to [their] allies, they turn away disapprovingly.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the behavior of people who, when faced with the truth or a message they do not like, turn away from it and seek the company of those who share their disbelief or rejection. The phrase 'they turn away disapprovingly' implies a sense of arrogance and dismissiveness, as if they are above considering the message being presented to them. This verse serves as a critique of such behavior, reminding the reader of the importance of being open-minded and receptive to new ideas and messages, even if they are challenging or uncomfortable.
orig: وإذا انقلبوا إلى أهلهم انقلبوا فكهين

translation: And when they saw them, they said, 'Indeed, these are astray.',
interpretation: The verse describes the reaction of some people when they saw a group of believers. Instead of acknowledging the truth of their beliefs or showing respect, they dismissed them as being astray. The verse highlights the closed-mindedness and lack of understanding of those who reject or dismiss the beliefs and values of others, and serves as a reminder that true guidance and judgment come only from God.
orig: وإذا رأوهم قالوا إن هؤلاء لضالون

translation: And We never sent guardians before you [O Muhammad] to previous nations.
interpretation: The verse highlights that Prophet Muhammad is not the first prophet to be sent by God, but he is unique in that no other prophet was sent with guardians or protectors before him. This implies that the responsibility of delivering God's message and guiding people towards the right path lies solely on the Prophet Muhammad. The verse emphasizes the significance of the Prophet's mission and the importance of following his teachings, as he is the final messenger of God and the ultimate source of guidance for all of humanity.
orig: وما أرسلوا عليهم حافظين

translation: Today, those who disbelieved will be laughing at the believers
interpretation: The verse speaks about the contrasting fates of the believers and the disbelievers on the Day of Judgment. The disbelievers will be in a state of mockery and laughter, while the believers are the subject of their ridicule. However, this laughter will be short-lived, as the disbelievers will soon come to realize the gravity of their situation. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of faith and the consequences of disbelief.
orig: فاليوم الذين آمنوا من الكفار يضحكون

translation: Upon their necks you can see them looking.
interpretation: The verse describes the physical position of a group of people, with their heads and eyes looking down or up, possibly in a state of defeat, humiliation, or submission. The context of the verse is important for understanding the exact meaning and the identity of these people. However, the verse can be interpreted as a reminder of the ultimate power and control of God, who can elevate or humble anyone at will.
orig: على الأرائك ينظرون

translation: Is the garment of the disbelievers that which they used to do?
interpretation: The verse is a question posed by the Qur'an, asking whether the 'garment' of the disbelievers is what they used to do. The 'garment' in this verse is a metaphor for the actions and deeds of the disbelievers. The verse challenges the disbelievers to consider the consequences of their actions and to reflect on the worthlessness of their deeds. The verse serves as a reminder that the actions and deeds of individuals will be evaluated and judged by God. The verse encourages the disbelievers to reconsider their ways and to turn towards God before it is too late.
orig: هل ثوب الكفار ما كانوا يفعلون

translation: When the sky splits apart
interpretation: The verse speaks of a cataclysmic event, where the sky is split apart. This event is often understood by scholars as a reference to the Day of Judgment, when the world as we know it will come to an end and humanity will be judged for their actions. The imagery of the sky splitting apart conveys a sense of awe and terror, emphasizing the overwhelming power and authority of God. The verse serves as a reminder of the fragility of human existence and the need to prepare for the inevitable day of reckoning.
orig: إذا السماء انشقت

translation: And she mentioned (the praise of) her Lord and believed in the words of her Lord (the Qur'an) and confirmed (the faith) of her Lord (by worshipping none but Allah Alone).
interpretation: The verse speaks about a woman who praised her Lord, believed in the words of her Lord (the Qur'an), and confirmed her faith by worshipping none but Allah Alone. The verse emphasizes the importance of faith and belief in the words of Allah, and the importance of worshipping Allah Alone without associating any partners with Him. The verse serves as an example for believers to follow, by praising and thanking their Lord, having faith in His words, and worshipping Him alone.
orig: وأذنت لربها وحقت

translation: And when the earth is stretched
interpretation: The verse is a part of a series of verses that describe the Day of Judgment. The 'earth being stretched' is a metaphor for the dramatic changes that will take place on the Day of Judgment. The verse emphasizes the overwhelming and awe-inspiring nature of the events that will occur on that day, and serves as a reminder of the power and majesty of God. The verse also highlights the transience of the world and the insignificance of human existence in comparison to the eternal and all-encompassing nature of God's power.
orig: وإذا الأرض مدت

translation: And cast We therein that which was within it, and destroyed it.
interpretation: The verse describes the destruction of something, possibly a town or community, by casting or raining down something destructive upon it, causing its complete destruction. The verse emphasizes the complete and utter destruction of the place, leaving nothing behind. This verse can be interpreted as a reminder of the power and might of God, who can destroy anything He wills, and a warning to those who are unjust and disobedient.
orig: وألقت ما فيها وتخلت

translation: And she mentioned/invoked her Lord and submitted (to Him).
interpretation: The verse speaks about a person (implied by the feminine gender) who turns to her Lord in devotion and submission. This act of invoking God and submitting to Him can be understood as an act of worship, where the person is acknowledging and recognizing her dependence on God and her commitment to follow His will. This verse can serve as a reminder of the importance of maintaining a strong and devoted relationship with God, and the significance of submission and obedience to Him.
orig: وأذنت لربها وحقت

translation: O mankind, indeed you are laboring toward your Lord with [earnest] striving and then you will meet Him.
interpretation: The verse addresses all of humanity, reminding them that their ultimate goal and purpose is to strive towards their Lord. The verse emphasizes the importance of this striving and reminds people that it is a continuous process that will continue until they meet their Lord. The verse may be interpreted as a call for people to reflect on their actions and motivations, and to strive towards a deeper and more meaningful relationship with their Creator.
orig: يا أيها الإنسان إنك كادح إلى ربك كدحا فملاقيه

translation: But as for him who is given his record in his left hand
interpretation: The verse speaks about the Day of Judgment and the distribution of records of deeds for each person. This particular part of the verse refers to those who receive their record in their left hand, which is a sign of bad news and condemnation. This interpretation suggests that the person has not lived a righteous life and their deeds are being accounted for in a negative way. This verse serves as a reminder of the importance of good deeds and the consequences of neglecting them.
orig: فأما من أوتي كتابه بيمينه

translation: And he will indeed be given a light punishment.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the punishment that will be given to an unspecified person. The punishment is described as 'light', indicating that it will not be as severe as the punishment given to others. The verse may serve as a warning to those who commit less serious sins, reminding them that they will still be held accountable for their actions and will receive a punishment, even if it is not as harsh as the punishment received by those who commit more serious sins.
orig: فسوف يحاسب حسابا يسيرا

translation: And it will be turned over to its people rejoicing
interpretation: The verse speaks about a blessing or a source of happiness being given to a people. The phrase 'it will be turned over to its people rejoicing' suggests that the people will receive this blessing with joy and happiness. The exact nature of the blessing is not specified in the verse, leaving it open to interpretation. However, the verse emphasizes the positive and joyful reaction of the people, highlighting the significance and value of the blessing they are receiving.
orig: وينقلب إلى أهله مسرورا

translation: But as for he who is given his record in his left hand.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the fate of a person who receives their record (of deeds) in their left hand on the Day of Judgment. This is a sign of a negative outcome, indicating that the person's deeds were not pleasing to God. The verse serves as a warning to those who are neglectful of their duties towards God, reminding them of the importance of leading a righteous life and the consequences of not doing so.
orig: وأما من أوتي كتابه وراء ظهره

translation: Then after that,
interpretation: No interpretation
orig: فسوف يدعو ثبورا

translation: And he will enter the Fire, reclining,
interpretation: The verse describes the fate of an individual who will enter Hellfire and will be made to recline or lie down in it. The image of reclining or lying down in the Fire conveys the idea of complete submission and helplessness, and serves as a stark reminder of the severe consequences of one's actions. The verse may be referring to a particular individual or it may serve as a warning to all those who persist in their wrongdoing and fail to heed the call to repentance.
orig: ويصلى سعيرا

translation: There was certainly a man among them who was grateful.
interpretation: The verse highlights the existence of a grateful person among a group of people. This person stands out in contrast to the others, who may not have been grateful for the blessings they received. The verse serves as a reminder that gratitude is an important quality and that it is possible to find grateful people even in difficult or challenging circumstances.
orig: إنه كان في أهله مسرورا

translation: He certainly thought that he would never return.
interpretation: The verse is speaking about someone who was under the delusion that he would never have to return or face accountability for his actions. This person may have been arrogant and thought that he was above reproach and would never be punished for his sins. The verse serves as a reminder that no one is exempt from God's judgment and that all people will be held accountable for their actions on the Day of Judgment.
orig: إنه ظن أن لن يحور

translation: Indeed, his Lord is ever attentive to him.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the attentiveness of an individual's Lord towards them. The verse emphasizes the constant awareness and watchfulness of God, who is always observing and attentive to his servants. This verse can be seen as a source of comfort and reassurance, reminding the reader that they are never alone and that their Lord is always with them, aware of their every action and thought.
orig: بلى إن ربه كان به بصيرا

translation: Nay, I swear by the afterglow of sunset;
interpretation: The verse begins with a solemn oath, emphasizing the importance of what is to follow. The speaker swears by the afterglow of sunset, which could be a reference to the beauty and tranquility of the natural world, or perhaps a symbol of the fleeting nature of life and the importance of using one's time wisely. The exact meaning of the oath is open to interpretation, but it is clear that the speaker is making a serious and emphatic statement.
orig: فلا أقسم بالشفق

translation: And by the night and what it carries (of the day)
interpretation: The verse is a form of oath, where the night and its significance are being sworn upon. The 'what it carries' refers to the day, indicating the transition from night to day. This verse can be interpreted as a reflection on the cyclical nature of time, where the night gives way to the day and vice versa. It highlights the beauty and power of the natural world, and the order and predictability of the universe, which are all signs of God's creation and wisdom.
orig: والليل وما وسق

translation: And when the moon is eclipsed
interpretation: The verse speaks about the occurrence of a lunar eclipse. The verse is part of a larger passage that describes various natural phenomena and the proper Islamic response to them. In this context, the verse serves as a reminder of the power and majesty of God, who is responsible for creating and controlling the heavens and the earth. Muslims are instructed to respond to such events with prayer and reflection, as a means of drawing closer to God and seeking His forgiveness and guidance.
orig: والقمر إذا اتسق

translation: That you may be layered one above another
interpretation: The phrase speaks about the arrangement of something, possibly people or objects, in layers, one above the other. The context in which this phrase appears in the Qur'an will provide a better understanding of its exact meaning and application. However, in general, it can be interpreted as an image of order, organization, or stratification.
orig: لتركبن طبقا عن طبق

translation: And why do they not believe?
interpretation: The verse is a rhetorical question that expresses the speaker's confusion or surprise at the fact that some people do not believe. The verse may be interpreted as a call to reflection and contemplation, encouraging the reader to consider why some people reject faith despite the evidence and arguments presented to them. The verse may also be seen as a reminder that faith is a personal choice and responsibility, and that each individual must make their own decision about whether or not to believe.
orig: فما لهم لا يؤمنون

translation: And when the Qur'an is recited to them, they do not prostrate themselves.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the people's rejection and disbelief in the Qur'an. Despite hearing the recitation of the Qur'an, they do not prostrate themselves in submission and acceptance of its message. This verse highlights the importance of responding to the guidance of the Qur'an and the consequences of rejecting it. It serves as a reminder of the importance of openness and humility towards the message of the Qur'an, and the significance of submission to God's will.
orig: وإذا قرئ عليهم القرآن لا يسجدون

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve - they are liars.
interpretation: The verse is a condemnation of the unbelievers who reject the message of Islam. The verse portrays them as liars, highlighting the falsehood of their disbelief. The verse serves as a reminder to the believers of the true nature of the unbelievers and the importance of holding fast to their faith.
orig: بل الذين كفروا يكذبون

translation: And Allah is most knowing of what is within yourselves.
interpretation: The verse affirms that Allah has complete knowledge of the inner thoughts, feelings, and intentions of all human beings. This is a reminder that Allah is all-knowing and all-seeing, and that nothing can be hidden from Him. The verse may serve as a comfort to those who are struggling with their inner demons, reminding them that Allah is aware of their struggles and that they can seek His guidance and support. It may also serve as a warning to those who are hiding unjust or sinful intentions, reminding them that they cannot escape Allah's knowledge and judgment.
orig: والله أعلم بما يوعون

translation: And give good news to those who disbelieve of a painful punishment.
interpretation: The verse is a warning to the disbelievers of an impending painful punishment. It serves as a reminder that their rejection of the truth will not go unpunished and that they should expect to face severe consequences for their actions. This verse emphasizes the reality of accountability for one's beliefs and actions and the importance of accepting the truth.
orig: فبشرهم بعذاب أليم

translation: But those who believe and do good deeds, for them is a reward that will never be cut off.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the promise of reward for those who believe in God and do good deeds. The reward promised to them is one that will never be cut off, indicating its eternal and unending nature. This verse serves as a source of hope and motivation for believers, reminding them that their good actions will not go unnoticed or unrewarded in the hereafter.
orig: إلا الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات لهم أجر غير ممنون

translation: And the heaven with its constellations.
interpretation: The verse refers to the sky and its stars or constellations. The verse highlights the wonders of the universe and the greatness of God's creation. This can be interpreted as a reminder of God's power and majesty, and the need for humans to submit to and worship Him. It can also be seen as a call for humans to reflect on the natural world and the lessons it contains, such as the order, harmony, and interconnectedness of all things.
orig: والسماء ذات البروج

translation: And the appointed day.
interpretation: The verse refers to the 'appointed day', which is a term used in the Qryan to describe the Day of Judgment or the end of the world. This day is described as a time when all of humanity will be judged for their actions and deeds, and it is considered to be a day of great significance and consequence. The verse may serve as a reminder of the importance of leading a righteous and just life, as the appointed day will bring a final reckoning for all people.
orig: واليوم الموعود

translation: And witness and be witnessed.
interpretation: The phrase 'And witness and be witnessed' is a metaphorical expression that emphasizes the importance of both observing and being observed in one's actions and behavior. It is a call for individuals to not only be mindful of their own actions, but also to be aware that they are being observed and held accountable for their deeds. This phrase encourages people to strive for righteousness and to live in accordance with moral and ethical principles, as they will ultimately be held accountable for their actions on the Day of Judgment. The phrase can also be interpreted as a reminder that God sees and knows all, and that nothing can be hidden from Him.
orig: وشاهد ومشهود

translation: We killed the people of the ditch
interpretation: The verse refers to a specific event in Islamic history, where the people of a town called Al-Khandaq (the ditch) were punished for their rejection of Prophet Muhammad and their oppression of Muslims. The people of Al-Khandaq dug a ditch around their town and refused to let the Muslims enter, leading to a prolonged siege. However, when the people of Al-Khandaq ran out of food and water, they resorted to cannibalism and infanticide. As a result, God punished them by causing a severe sandstorm that buried the people of Al-Khandaq, killing them all. The verse serves as a reminder of the consequences of oppression, rejection of truth, and the severity of God's punishment.
orig: قتل أصحاب الأخدود

translation: The Fire, its fuel wood.
interpretation: The verse is a metaphor for Hellfire and its fuel, which is described as wood. The wood serves as a source of sustenance for the fire, emphasizing its intensity and destructive nature. The verse may serve as a warning to those who commit sins and engage in unjust actions, reminding them of the severe consequences of their actions and the impending punishment in the afterlife.
orig: النار ذات الوقود

translation: When they were upon it, sitting upon it.
interpretation: The verse describes a group of people sitting or staying in a place, likely a town or city. The context of the verse suggests that this place will be subject to punishment or destruction from God due to the injustice of its inhabitants. The verse serves as a reminder of the transience of human existence and the importance of living a righteous life in accordance with God's will.
orig: إذ هم عليها قعود

translation: And they were witnesses to what they were doing to the believers.
interpretation: The verse refers to individuals who were aware of and complicit in the persecution of the believers. The phrase 'they were witnesses' implies that they saw the harm and injustice inflicted upon the believers but did not intervene or object. The verse serves as a condemnation of those who stand by and allow wrongdoing to occur, emphasizing the importance of taking a stand against injustice and defending the oppressed.
orig: وهم على ما يفعلون بالمؤمنين شهود

translation: And We did not punish them except that they were ungrateful to Allah, the Exalted in Might, the Praiseworthy.
interpretation: The verse explains that the only reason for the punishment of a certain group of people was their ingratitude towards Allah, who is described as being Exalted in Might and Praiseworthy. The verse emphasizes the importance of showing gratitude and appreciation towards God, and warns of the consequences of ingratitude. It also serves as a reminder that punishment is a consequence of actions, and that ungratefulness towards God is a grave sin.
orig: وما نقموا منهم إلا أن يؤمنوا بالله العزيز الحميد

translation: He to whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth, and Allah is over all things competent.
interpretation: The verse affirms the power and sovereignty of God over all of creation, emphasizing that He has control over both the heavens and the earth. The statement "and Allah is over all things competent" further emphasizes God's ability and power to manage and control all things. The verse serves as a reminder of God's greatness and power, and encourages believers to have faith and trust in Him.
orig: الذي له ملك السماوات والأرض والله على كل شيء شهيد

translation: Indeed, those who test the believers, the men and the women, and then do not repent, for them is the punishment of Hell, and for them is the punishment of the burning fire.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the severe punishment that awaits those who test the faith of believers, both men and women, and then do not repent. The punishment for these people is the fire of Hell, which is described as a burning fire. The verse emphasizes the importance of faith and the serious consequences of testing or attacking it. The verse serves as a warning to those who may be tempted to test or harm the faith of others, warning them of the severe punishment that awaits them if they do not repent.
orig: إن الذين فتنوا المؤمنين والمؤمنات ثم لم يتوبوا فلهم عذاب جهنم ولهم عذاب الحريق

translation: For those who believe and do righteous deeds, for them are Gardens beneath which rivers flow, that is the great victory.
interpretation: The verse promises a reward for those who have faith and do good deeds, in the form of Gardens through which rivers flow. This is described as 'the great victory'. The verse emphasizes the blessings and joys that await the believers in the afterlife, and encourages them to continue on the path of faith and righteousness. The verse also serves as a reminder to those who are not believers or do not do good deeds, that they will not receive this reward and will not be victorious in the afterlife.
orig: إن الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات لهم جنات تجري من تحتها الأنهار ذلك الفوز الكبير

translation: Indeed, the punishment of your Lord is severe.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the severity of God's punishment for those who are living in sin and disobedience. It serves as a warning to remind people of the consequences of their actions and the power of God's punishment. The verse encourages people to turn away from their sins and seek forgiveness, as God's punishment is not to be taken lightly.
orig: إن بطش ربك لشديد

translation: It is He who begins (the process of) creation; then repeats it; and for Him it is extremely easy.
interpretation: The verse highlights the power and ability of God to create and recreate. The phrase 'It is He who begins (the process of) creation' refers to God's role as the initiator of all creation, while 'then repeats it' refers to God's ability to recreate or repeat the process of creation. The phrase 'for Him it is extremely easy' emphasizes the ease with which God can create and recreate, and serves as a reminder of God's omnipotence and power. The verse can be seen as a statement of God's greatness and a reminder of the limitations of human abilities in comparison to God's power.
orig: إنه هو يبدئ ويعيد

translation: And He is the Forgiving, the Loving.
interpretation: The verse describes one of the attributes of God, highlighting His forgiving and loving nature. This description serves as a reminder of God's mercy and compassion, and His willingness to forgive those who repent and turn back to Him. The verse encourages believers to seek God's forgiveness and to cultivate a loving relationship with Him, based on trust and devotion.
orig: وهو الغفور الودود

translation: Owner of the Throne, the Glorious
interpretation: The verse is a description of one of the attributes of God. The 'Owner of the Throne' refers to God's sovereignty and control over all of creation. The 'Glorious' is a description of God's majesty and splendor. Together, these attributes convey the greatness and power of God, emphasizing His supremacy and transcendence above all of His creation.
orig: ذو العرش المجيد

translation: He will do whatever He wills.
interpretation: The verse is a statement of God's power and sovereignty, emphasizing that He has the ability to do whatever He wants. This statement conveys the idea that God's actions are not limited by any external forces, and that His will is always accomplished. The verse serves as a reminder of God's omnipotence and His ultimate control over all things, and it encourages believers to submit to His will and trust in His wisdom and justice.
orig: فعال لما يريد

translation: Has there come to you the story of the armies?
interpretation: The verse is a question addressed to the listeners or readers, asking them if they have heard the story of the armies. It is a rhetorical question, and the answer is assumed to be no, indicating that the listeners or readers are about to hear a new and important story. The story of the armies is believed to refer to the Battle of Badr, which is a significant event in Islamic history, where a small group of Muslims defeated a larger and stronger army of non-believers. The verse serves as an introduction to the story of the battle and the lessons that can be learned from it.
orig: هل أتاك حديث الجنود

translation: Pharaoh and Thamud
interpretation: The phrase 'Pharaoh and Thamud' is a reference to two ancient civilizations that are mentioned several times in the Qur'an. Pharaoh refers to the ruler of ancient Egypt who is depicted as a tyrant and oppressor, and Thamud refers to an ancient Arabian people who are also described as being unjust and disobedient to God. In this context, the phrase 'Pharaoh and Thamud' serves as a reminder of the consequences of arrogance, oppression, and disbelief, as both civilizations were destroyed by God for their sins.
orig: فرعون وثمود

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve - it is all the same to them whether you warn them or do not warn them - they will not believe.
interpretation: The verse highlights the closed-mindedness of the disbelievers, stating that it makes no difference whether they are warned or not, as they will not believe. This verse can be interpreted as a reminder that some people are resistant to guidance and that it is not the responsibility of the believers to force belief upon them. Instead, the believers are to deliver the message and leave the outcome to God.
orig: بل الذين كفروا في تكذيب

translation: But Allah is surrounding them from above and from beneath.
interpretation: The verse speaks about God's all-encompassing power and knowledge. The phrase 'But Allah is surrounding them from above and from beneath' emphasizes that God is all-knowing and all-powerful, and that there is no escape from His knowledge and power. The verse serves as a reminder of God's greatness and the futility of attempting to hide one's actions from Him. It is also a source of comfort for the believers, as it reminds them that God is always with them, protecting and watching over them.
orig: والله من ورائهم محيط

translation: No, it is a glorious Quran
interpretation: The verse affirms the greatness and majesty of the Quran. It is a reminder that the Quran is not an ordinary book, but a glorious and magnificent revelation from God. This verse serves as a call to respect and honor the Quran, and to recognize its divine origin and significance.
orig: بل هو قرآن مجيد

translation: In a preserved tablet.
interpretation: The phrase 'In a preserved tablet' refers to the idea that all of humanity's actions and destiny are recorded and preserved in a divine record. This record is seen as unchangeable and eternal, and it is kept in a safe and secure location, often symbolized by a 'tablet'. The image of a preserved tablet emphasizes the idea of God's omniscience and omnipotence, and it serves as a reminder that all of our actions are known and accounted for, and that we will be held responsible for them on the Day of Judgment.
orig: في لوح محفوظ

translation: And the sky and the visitor [star/comet/meteor/etc. in the sky/space/heavens]
interpretation: The verse is a reminder of the greatness and majesty of the creation of the heavens and the stars or celestial bodies within it. The verse serves to inspire awe and reverence towards the Creator and encourages contemplation of the wonders of the universe. It can also be interpreted as a reference to the signs of God's existence and power that can be observed in the natural world. The verse may also serve as a metaphor for the transience and insignificance of human existence in comparison to the vastness and complexity of the universe.
orig: والسماء والطارق

translation: And what will make you know what the Overturner is?
interpretation: The verse is a rhetorical question that introduces the concept of the 'Overturner' or 'The Disturber', which is one of the names of God in Islam. This name refers to God's power to overturn and change the established order of things. The verse encourages the reader to reflect on the mysteries of the universe and the power of God. It serves as a reminder of the limits of human knowledge and understanding and the ultimate power and control of God over all things.
orig: وما أدراك ما الطارق

translation: I'm sorry, the Arabic text you provided appears to be a portion of a Surah (chapter) name from the Qur'an, not a verse. The Surah name you provided is "Al-Najm" which means "The Star", and "Al-Thaqib" is one of its verses (ayahs). Here's the translation and interpretation of the verse: By the sky with its piercing (stars)
interpretation: This verse is a form of oath, where the piercing stars in the sky are being sworn upon. The verse is a metaphorical way of emphasizing the importance and truth of the message being conveyed. The piercing stars could symbolize the clarity and guidance they provide, or their seemingly fixed and unchanging nature. Overall, the verse serves to convey the idea of certainty and truth, emphasizing the importance of the message that follows.
orig: النجم الثاقب

translation: Indeed, over each person is a guardian.
interpretation: The verse affirms that every individual has a guardian or protector over them, who is responsible for their well-being and guidance. This guardian could refer to the angels who record our deeds and protect us, or it could refer to the innate conscience and moral sense that guides us towards what is right. The verse emphasizes the individual's responsibility and accountability for their actions, as well as the constant presence and watchfulness of the divine power. It serves as a reminder of the importance of living a righteous and virtuous life, guided by the principles of justice, compassion, and wisdom.
orig: إن كل نفس لما عليها حافظ

translation: Let mankind consider from what they were created.
interpretation: The verse invites humans to reflect on the process of their creation and to ponder over it. This reflection is expected to lead humans to a better understanding of themselves, their purpose in life and their relationship with their Creator. It also encourages them to appreciate the complexity and beauty of the creation process and to recognize the power and wisdom of the Creator. This verse can also be seen as a call for humility and gratitude, as it reminds humans of their origins and their dependence on their Creator.
orig: فلينظر الإنسان مم خلق

translation: Creates from water poured forth.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the power of God in creating life from water. The verse emphasizes the role of water in the creation of life, indicating that water is a fundamental element in the creation of all living beings. The verse serves as a reminder of the greatness and power of God, who is able to create life from something as simple and basic as water.
orig: خلق من ماء دافق

translation: Emerges from between the backbone and the ribs.
interpretation: The verse is referring to the emergence of the Dabbah (a creature) from a specific part of a human or animal's body, between the backbone and the ribs. The exact meaning of this verse is debated among scholars, with some interpreting it as a metaphorical or symbolic description of the emergence of evil or sin. However, a more common interpretation is that it refers to the physical emergence of a creature, such as a lamb, from the womb of its mother during childbirth. This interpretation highlights the miracle of life and the power of God in creating and sustaining all living beings.
orig: يخرج من بين الصلب والترائب

translation: Indeed, he, over himself, is powerful.
interpretation: The verse speaks about an individual's ability to control and have power over their own actions and decisions. The verse emphasizes the importance of taking responsibility for one's own life and making choices that align with one's values and goals. The verse serves as a reminder that ultimately, each person has the power to shape their own destiny and determine their own success or failure.
orig: إنه على رجعه لقادر

translation: The day when (false) displays are broken down.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the Day of Judgment, when all false displays and pretenses will be destroyed. On this day, people's true nature and intentions will be revealed, and they will be held accountable for their actions. The verse serves as a reminder that nothing can hide from God, and that people will be judged based on their deeds and intentions, not on their appearances or pretenses.
orig: يوم تبلى السرائر

translation: And he will have no power nor helper.
interpretation: The verse speaks about a person who will be in a state of powerlessness and without any help or support. This verse can be understood as a warning or a reminder that even those who are currently in a position of power and strength can be brought down to a state of helplessness. It can also be seen as a statement of the ultimate truth that no one can escape the consequences of their actions and that ultimately, everyone will be accountable for their deeds, regardless of their current status or position in life.
orig: فما له من قوة ولا ناصر

translation: And [by] the sky that returns [rain]
interpretation: The verse is a part of a series of oaths that God swears by in the Qur'an. In this verse, God swears by the sky that returns [rain]. This refers to the sky's role in the water cycle, where it receives water in the form of vapor and returns it to the earth as rain. The verse emphasizes the order and regularity of the natural phenomena and the power of God in controlling and maintaining them. The verse can also be seen as a reminder of the blessings that God has bestowed upon humanity through the natural world, and the need for humanity to be grateful and thankful for these blessings.
orig: والسماء ذات الرجع

translation: And the earth, how it was outstretched
interpretation: The verse highlights the vastness and expanse of the earth and its creation as a sign of God's power and greatness. The word 'outstretched' implies a deliberate and purposeful act of creation, emphasizing the majesty and grandeur of the Creator. This verse serves as a reminder of the greatness of God and the wonders of His creation, inviting believers to reflect on the power and wisdom behind the creation of the earth and the universe.
orig: والأرض ذات الصدع

translation: Indeed, this is a decisive word
interpretation: The verse is a clear and definitive statement, indicating that what is being referred to is a matter of great importance and certainty. The exact nature of the 'decisive word' is not specified in the verse, allowing for a range of interpretations depending on the context. However, the overall message of the verse is one of certainty and decisiveness, emphasizing the importance of the subject matter being discussed.
orig: إنه لقول فصل

translation: And it is not a joke.
interpretation: The phrase 'And it is not a joke' is a response to those who may have dismissed or made light of the previous statement or warning. The statement emphasizes the seriousness and truth of the previous statement, and serves as a reminder that the consequences of ignoring the warning will be severe. The phrase can also be interpreted as a call for serious reflection and contemplation on the part of the listener or reader.
orig: وما هو بالهزل

translation: They are devising a plot
interpretation: The verse speaks about people who are conspiring and plotting against others. The verse highlights the intentional and deliberate nature of their actions, as they are actively 'devising' a 'plot'. The verse may serve as a warning about the dangers of such behavior and the consequences of acting on harmful intentions.
orig: إنهم يكيدون كيدا

translation: And I will make sure [of the sin you have committed, I will punish you for it].
interpretation: The verse is a statement of punishment from God. The person being addressed has committed a sin, and God is promising to make sure that they are punished for it. The verse emphasizes the certainty of the punishment, with God's determination to follow through on it. The verse serves as a warning to those who would commit sin, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's judgement.
orig: وأكيد كيدا

translation: Then let the disbelievers wait; indeed, they will be the losers.
interpretation: The verse states that the disbelievers will be made to wait, and that they will ultimately be the losers. This verse could be interpreted as a statement of the certainty of divine justice and the ultimate triumph of truth over falsehood. It may also serve as a warning to those who reject the message of Islam, reminding them of the consequences of their disbelief and the inevitability of divine retribution.
orig: فمهل الكافرين أمهلهم رويدا

translation: Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High.
interpretation: The verse is a command to the reader to glorify and praise the name of their Lord, who is the Most High. It emphasizes the greatness and majesty of God, and encourages the reader to recognize and acknowledge His power and authority. This verse can serve as a reminder to the believer to express their devotion and reverence to God, and to maintain a humble and grateful attitude towards Him.
orig: سبح اسم ربك الأعلى

translation: who created and proportioned
interpretation: The phrase speaks about God's power and ability to create and shape all of creation. It highlights the idea that God is the creator of all things and that everything in the universe is proportioned and designed according to His will. This phrase can be seen as a reminder of God's greatness and power, and as a call to humility and submission to His will.
orig: الذي خلق فسوى

translation: And [He] who has measured out [the earth's] provision, then guided [its inhabitants] thereon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about God's role in providing sustenance for the inhabitants of the earth and guiding them. The verse emphasizes God's control and knowledge of the exact amount of provision that the earth can offer, and His guidance of the living beings towards it. The verse serves as a reminder of God's power and wisdom, and of the fact that all that exists in the world is subject to His will and control.
orig: والذي قدر فهدى

translation: And who has brought forth the pasture
interpretation: The verse is a part of a series of rhetorical questions asked by Allah, emphasizing His power and control over all things. The phrase 'And who has brought forth the pasture' is a rhetorical question that highlights Allah's role as the provider and sustainer of all life. The verse serves as a reminder of Allah's power and control over nature and the dependence of all living beings on Him.
orig: والذي أخرج المرعى

translation: And made it an empty waste.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the desolation and destruction of something, possibly a town or a community, which was once thriving and populated. The phrase 'made it an empty waste' conveys the complete and utter destruction of the place, leaving it barren and desolate. This verse could be interpreted as a warning of the potential consequences of neglect, abandonment, or divine punishment, resulting in the destruction of once-prosperous communities.
orig: فجعله غثاء أحوى

translation: And We will surely test you with something of fear and hunger, and loss of wealth and lives and fruits; but give good news to the patient.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the various trials and tribulations that people will face in their lives, including fear, hunger, loss of wealth, loss of lives, and loss of crops. Despite these hardships, the verse encourages patience and offers hope for those who remain steadfast. The verse reminds believers that these trials are a test from God, and that they should remain patient and steadfast in their faith, as good news and rewards await them in the afterlife.
orig: سنقرئك فلا تنسى

translation: But except as Allah wills; indeed, He knows the declaration and that which is concealed.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the power and knowledge of God, who has control over everything that is declared openly and everything that is hidden. The verse suggests that God's will is supreme and that nothing can happen without His knowledge or permission. This can be seen as a reminder of God's omnipotence and omniscience, and a call for humility and submission to His will.
orig: إلا ما شاء الله إنه يعلم الجهر وما يخفى

translation: And make things easy, and do not make things difficult.
interpretation: The verse is a command from God to the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) to make things easy for people and not to make things difficult for them. This verse can be interpreted as a general principle for all Muslims to follow, by making things easy for others and avoiding unnecessary difficulties and hardships. It also encourages Muslims to be understanding, patient, and accommodating towards others, and not to burden them with unnecessary burdens and obstacles. This verse serves as a reminder for Muslims to be kind, compassionate and helpful towards others, and to avoid creating unnecessary difficulties for them.
orig: ونيسرك لليسرى

translation: And mention, indeed, the reminder benefits the believers.
interpretation: The verse highlights the importance of remembering and mentioning (dhikr) the message of God. The verse suggests that the reminder (dhikr) is beneficial for the believers, implying that it serves as a means of guidance and inspiration for them. The verse may also suggest that the reminder can help believers to stay on the right path and avoid straying from the teachings of God. Overall, the verse emphasizes the value of the reminder in the spiritual journey of the believers.
orig: فذكر إن نفعت الذكرى

translation: He (God) will surely remind (those) who fear (Him),
interpretation: The verse speaks about the reminder from God to those who have fear of Him. This reminder could be in the form of blessings, lessons, or warnings, and it serves as a means of guidance and a reminder of God's power and control over all things. The verse highlights the importance of having fear of God and the rewards that come with it, such as being reminded and guided by Him.
orig: سيذكر من يخشى

translation: And keep away from it the evil one.
interpretation: The verse is a command from God to keep away the 'evil one' from something. The 'evil one' typically refers to Satan or any other source of evil and corruption. The verse emphasizes the importance of protecting oneself and one's community from the harmful and destructive influences of evil. It serves as a reminder to be vigilant and proactive in guarding against the forces of evil, and to seek God's protection and guidance in doing so.
orig: ويتجنبها الأشقى

translation: Who will roast at the great Fire
interpretation: The verse is a rhetorical question that implies a statement about the fate of certain individuals. It suggests that those who are being referred to will be punished by being cast into a great fire. The fire is likely a metaphor for the intense suffering and hardship that these individuals will face as a result of their actions. The verse may serve as a warning or a reminder of the consequences of wrongdoing and the importance of leading a righteous life.
orig: الذي يصلى النار الكبرى

translation: Then he will not die therein nor live.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the fate of certain individuals who will not experience death or life in a particular place or situation. The exact meaning of this verse is open to interpretation and can depend on the context in which it is used. However, one possible interpretation is that the verse is referring to the state of those who have done great evil and are condemned to eternal punishment. They will not experience the relief of death or the hope of a new beginning, but will instead be trapped in a state of suffering and despair. This verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, emphasizing the seriousness of their actions and the potential for severe consequences.
orig: ثم لا يموت فيها ولا يحيى

translation: Surely, he succeeds who purifies himself.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the ultimate success and prosperity of the person who purifies themselves, both physically and spiritually. The verse suggests that the act of purification is a means of achieving success and implies that the pursuit of purity is a worthwhile and valuable goal. The verse may also be interpreted as a reminder that the responsibility for one's own spiritual and moral well-being lies with the individual, and that the path to success and prosperity requires personal effort and dedication.
orig: قد أفلح من تزكى

translation: And remember the name of your Lord and devote yourself to it in prayer.
interpretation: The verse is a command for the believer to remember and invoke the name of their Lord, and to devote themselves to prayer. This verse emphasizes the importance of a constant remembrance of God and the establishment of a regular prayer practice. It encourages the believers to maintain a strong and consistent connection with their Lord through prayer and invocation, which will bring them peace, guidance and protection.
orig: وذكر اسم ربه فصلى

translation: But you prefer the life of this world
interpretation: The verse highlights the human tendency to prioritize worldly pleasures and desires over spiritual and moral values. The phrase 'but you prefer' implies a criticism or reproach, suggesting that this preference for worldly life is misguided or wrong. The verse may serve as a reminder to focus on the hereafter and to strive for righteousness and piety in preparation for the Day of Judgment.
orig: بل تؤثرون الحياة الدنيا

translation: But the Hereafter is better and more enduring.
interpretation: The verse contrasts the temporary nature of this world with the eternal and everlasting nature of the Hereafter. It suggests that despite the allure and attractions of this world, the Hereafter is a superior and more desirable destination. The verse encourages believers to focus on the Hereafter, rather than becoming overly attached to this world and its material pleasures. It serves as a reminder that the true purpose of human existence is to prepare for the Hereafter, and that ultimate happiness and fulfillment can only be found in the next life.
orig: والآخرة خير وأبقى

translation: Indeed, this is in the first pages (of the Scripture).
interpretation: The verse is a reference to the previous revelations and scriptures, indicating that the message being conveyed in the Qur'an is not new, but rather a continuation of the same divine guidance that was given to previous prophets and communities. By stating that this is 'in the first pages', the verse emphasizes the importance of understanding and recognizing the continuity and consistency of the divine message throughout history. This serves as a reminder that the truth and guidance brought by the Qur'an and the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) is not something new, but rather a continuation of the same message that was given to the prophets and messengers before him.
orig: إن هذا لفي الصحف الأولى

translation: The rolls/scriptures of Abraham and Moses.
interpretation: The verse refers to the holy scriptures revealed to the prophets Abraham and Moses, namely the Zabur (Psalms) and the Tawrat (Torah) respectively. It highlights the significance and reverence of these scriptures in Islamic tradition as being divinely revealed and holding sacred knowledge and guidance for believers.
orig: صحف إبراهيم وموسى

translation: Have you heard of the Day of Resurrection?
interpretation: The Day of Resurrection is a time of judgment and reckoning for all of humanity, when the dead will be resurrected and brought to account for their actions in this life. It is a day of great fear and trepidation for those who have not lived righteously, and a day of joy and triumph for those who have. The Qur'an emphasizes the importance of preparing for this day by living a life of piety, obedience, and good works.
orig: هل أتاك حديث الغاشية

translation: And on that day, (some) faces will be humbled.
interpretation: The verse describes the Day of Judgment, when some people will be humbled and feel shame and regret for their actions in this world. The verse emphasizes the stark contrast between the temporary pleasures of this world and the eternal consequences of one's actions, reminding people to prepare for the Day of Judgment and to strive for righteousness and piety.
orig: وجوه يومئذ خاشعة

translation: A practicer of usury
interpretation: The term 'عاملة ناصبة' (‘amilatun naasi-bah) in Arabic appears in the Qur'an and is often translated as 'a practicer of usury'. This term refers to someone who charges interest or engages in other unethical financial practices that exploit others. The Qur'an strictly prohibits usury and condemns those who engage in it. The term 'عاملة ناصبة' serves as a warning to those who engage in such practices and highlights the importance of ethical financial dealings in Islam.
orig: عاملة ناصبة

translation: They will be enveloped by a Fire fiercely glowing.
interpretation: The verse describes the fate of the unbelievers who reject God's message and refuse to submit to His will. They will be punished in the hereafter by being enveloped by a Fire that is fiercely glowing. The image of the Fire serves as a powerful symbol of the intense and unbearable suffering that awaits those who persist in their disbelief and rejection of God.
orig: تصلى نارا حامية

translation: He will be given to drink from a flowing spring.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the provision of a flowing spring as a source of drink for someone. The verse may be interpreted as a metaphor for the blessings and abundance that will be granted to the righteous in the afterlife. It could also be interpreted as a literal description of the physical delights that will be available to the believers in heaven. Regardless of the interpretation, the verse conveys the idea of a plentiful and never-ending supply of water, symbolizing the ultimate satisfaction and contentment that will be experienced by those who have attained salvation.
orig: تسقى من عين آنية

translation: They have no food except for the fetid
interpretation: The verse describes the dire situation of a group of people who have no food except for that which is rotten or impure. The term 'fetid' (ضريع) is used to describe food that is spoiled or contaminated, and is unfit for consumption. The verse highlights the severity of their hunger and the desperation of their situation, as they are forced to eat food that is harmful to their health. The verse may be interpreted as a warning against greed and hoarding, reminding people of the consequences of their actions and the importance of sharing and being mindful of the needs of others.
orig: ليس لهم طعام إلا من ضريع

translation: He is not fat and cannot satisfy his hunger.
interpretation: The verse is a metaphorical description of a person who is spiritually impoverished and unable to fulfill their inner needs or desires. The phrase 'not fat' refers to the person's lack of spiritual or intellectual nourishment, while 'cannot satisfy his hunger' means that the person is unable to find meaning, purpose, or fulfillment in their life. The verse suggests that true satisfaction and fulfillment can only be found through spiritual growth and development, and that material possessions or worldly success cannot ultimately satisfy one's deepest needs and desires.
orig: لا يسمن ولا يغني من جوع

translation: Beautiful faces on that day (i.e. the Day of Judgment).
interpretation: The verse speaks about the beauty of the faces of certain individuals on the Day of Judgment. While the verse does not specify who these individuals are, the context suggests that they are those who have lived righteously and obediently to God. The beauty of their faces is a reflection of their inner purity and goodness. This verse serves as a source of hope and comfort for the believers, reminding them that their good deeds will be recognized and rewarded in the afterlife.
orig: وجوه يومئذ ناعمة

translation: Striving to please Him.
interpretation: The phrase 'لسعيها راضية' (las'a'hā rāḍiyatun) is from Surah Al-Fatihah, the first chapter of the Qur'an. It is a part of a supplication to God, and it means 'striving to please Him'. The interpretation of this phrase is that the believer is constantly striving and making an effort to please God, seeking His approval and satisfaction in all their actions and deeds. It highlights the importance of having a strong desire to worship and serve God, and to continuously work towards earning His pleasure.
orig: لسعيها راضية

translation: In a high garden.
interpretation: The phrase 'In a high garden' is a description of paradise in Islamic tradition. It is a place of beauty, peace, and tranquility, elevated above the troubles and hardships of this world. This phrase is often used to evoke a sense of longing and hope for the rewards of the afterlife, and to encourage believers to strive for righteousness and good deeds in this life in order to attain entry into this high garden in the next.
orig: في جنة عالية

translation: And hear not therein vain speech.
interpretation: The verse advises against listening to idle or useless speech in a place of worship. It emphasizes the importance of maintaining a sacred and respectful atmosphere in such places. The verse serves as a reminder to focus on the purpose of being in a place of worship, which is to worship and connect with God, rather than engaging in meaningless or frivolous conversations.
orig: لا تسمع فيها لاغية

translation: In it is a flowing stream.
interpretation: The verse refers to the presence of a flowing stream or water source in a particular location. This could be interpreted as a blessing or a sign of fertility and abundance. The verse may also be metaphorical, referring to the flow of knowledge, wisdom, or spiritual nourishment that can be found in a particular place or situation. Ultimately, the interpretation of this verse depends on the context in which it appears and the broader themes of the surrounding verses.
orig: فيها عين جارية

translation: In it is a lifted sarcophagus.
interpretation: The verse refers to a sarcophagus that is raised or lifted. The exact meaning of this sarcophagus and its significance is not clear from the verse alone and requires additional context. Some interpretations suggest that it may be a reference to a sarcophagus that is raised on pillars or a sarcophagus that is placed in a prominent location. Regardless of its specific meaning, the verse highlights the presence of this sarcophagus in a particular location, emphasizing its significance and importance.
orig: فيها سرر مرفوعة

translation: And stacked-up cups
interpretation: The phrase 'And stacked-up cups' is a metaphor for the abundance of blessings and provisions that God has given to the people. The image of cups being stacked one on top of another suggests an abundance and surplus of these blessings. This phrase serves as a reminder of the generosity and kindness of God towards his creations and the importance of being grateful for these blessings.
orig: وأكواب موضوعة

translation: And strutting through the streets.
interpretation: The verse describes the behavior of people who are arrogant and boastful, strutting through the streets with an air of superiority and self-importance. This verse serves as a reminder that such behavior is displeasing to God and that true greatness comes from humility and piety.
orig: ونمارق مصفوفة

translation: And Zachariah, when he called upon his Lord, saying, 'My Lord, do not leave me alone; you are the best of inheritors.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the Prophet Zachariah's prayer to God, asking Him not to leave him alone and reminding God that He is the best of inheritors. The verse highlights the importance of seeking God's help and support in times of need and recognizing that God is the ultimate source of all blessings and provisions. The verse also emphasizes the importance of trusting in God and seeking His guidance and protection, as He is the best of all inheritors, who will ultimately take care of His servants in this world and the hereafter.
orig: وزرابي مبثوثة

translation: Do they not look at the camels, how We have created them?
interpretation: The verse is a rhetorical question, inviting people to reflect on the creation of camels. It highlights the intricate design and complexity of camels, implying that they must have a creator. The verse is an invitation to consider the power and wisdom of the creator, and to recognize and submit to the greatness of God. It is also a reminder of the importance of appreciating and reflecting on the wonders of creation.
orig: أفلا ينظرون إلى الإبل كيف خلقت

translation: And how (exalted) is My punishment and how (extended) are My ropes!
interpretation: This verse is a reminder of the greatness and severity of God's punishment, and the vastness of His power and control. The verse serves as a warning to those who deny God or commit sins, urging them to reflect on the consequences of their actions. The verse also emphasizes the idea that God's punishment is inevitable and cannot be avoided, no matter how far or high one may think they are. The verse encourages people to submit to God's will and to seek His mercy and forgiveness.
orig: وإلى السماء كيف رفعت

translation: And to the mountains, how are they rooted?
interpretation: The verse is a rhetorical question that highlights the power and control of God over all of creation. By asking 'how are the mountains rooted', the verse is emphasizing the stability and permanence of the mountains, and at the same time, it is pointing out that even the most solid and unchanging aspects of the earth are subject to God's will. The verse serves as a reminder of God's greatness and sovereignty, and it emphasizes the idea that God is the creator and sustainer of all things.
orig: وإلى الجبال كيف نصبت

translation: And how have We spread out the earth?
interpretation: The verse is a rhetorical question that emphasizes the power and ability of God in creating and shaping the earth. The verse serves as a reminder of God's greatness and control over all of creation. It encourages reflection and contemplation of the natural world and the intricate systems and patterns that exist within it. The verse also highlights the importance of appreciating and respecting the earth and its resources, recognizing that it is a creation of God and that it serves a larger purpose in the grand scheme of the universe.
orig: وإلى الأرض كيف سطحت

translation: And indeed, it is only a reminder to you, [O Muhammad], of the previous reminders.
interpretation: The verse is a reminder to the Prophet Muhammad that his role is only to convey the message of Islam to the people, and it is up to them to accept or reject it. The 'previous reminders' refer to the messages and teachings of previous prophets and scriptures. This verse emphasizes the continuity of the message of Islam and the consistency of God's guidance throughout history. It also highlights the importance of the role of the Prophet Muhammad as a messenger and a warner, and the responsibility of the people to heed his message.
orig: فذكر إنما أنت مذكر

translation: I am not responsible for you [after I have delivered the message].
interpretation: The phrase is spoken by the Prophet Muhammad, indicating that he is no longer responsible for the people's guidance after he has delivered the message of Islam to them. It highlights the importance of personal responsibility and accountability in accepting or rejecting the message, and emphasizes that the Prophet Muhammad has fulfilled his duty of conveying the message to the people.
orig: لست عليهم بمصيطر

translation: except those who repent and believe
interpretation: The phrase 'except those who repent and believe' refers to those individuals who have turned away from their previous ways of disbelief and have embraced faith. The act of repentance and belief signifies a change of heart and a commitment to follow the teachings of Islam. This phrase suggests that those who truly repent and believe will be spared from the punishment mentioned earlier in the verse.
orig: إلا من تولى وكفر

translation: Allah will punish him with the greatest punishment.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the punishment of an individual by God. The phrase 'the greatest punishment' implies a severe and intense form of retribution, indicating the seriousness of the actions of the person being punished. The verse serves as a reminder of the ultimate authority and power of God, and the consequences of actions that go against His will.
orig: فيعذبه الله العذاب الأكبر

translation: Indeed, to Us is their return.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes that everything, including the return of people to their Creator, is ultimately under God's control. It suggests that all people will eventually return to God and be held accountable for their actions in this world. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of living a righteous life and preparing for the ultimate return to God.
orig: إن إلينا إيابهم

translation: Then indeed, upon Us is their account.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes that God will hold those who have done wrong accountable for their actions. The phrase 'then indeed' suggests that the responsibility for judgment and recompense lies solely with God. The verse serves as a reminder of the ultimate justice and fairness of God, and of the fact that every person will be held accountable for their deeds on the Day of Judgment.
orig: ثم إن علينا حسابهم

translation: By the dawn
interpretation: The verse begins with an oath by the dawn, which is a symbol of the beginning of a new day and a new opportunity for repentance and forgiveness. The oath serves to emphasize the importance and solemnity of the message that follows. The interpretation of this verse is that it serves as a reminder of the opportunity for redemption and forgiveness that every new day brings, and encourages the reader to take advantage of this opportunity by turning away from sin and seeking God's forgiveness.
orig: والفجر

translation: And the night of power
interpretation: The verse refers to 'Laylat al-Qadr' or the Night of Power, which is a significant night during the holy month of Ramadan in Islamic tradition. It is believed to be the night when the Qur'an was first revealed to the Prophet Muhammad, and is considered a night of great blessings and spiritual significance. Muslims often spend this night in worship, prayer, and reflection, seeking God's forgiveness and guidance.
orig: وليال عشر

translation: And by the even and the odd
interpretation: The verse is a part of a series of oaths taken by God, where He swears by various creations and phenomena. Here, God swears by 'the even' and 'the odd', which can be interpreted as an allusion to numbers and the mathematical order of the universe. The verse can be seen as a reminder of the intricate and complex nature of God's creation, and the perfect balance and harmony that exists in the world. It can also be understood as a call to contemplation and reflection, encouraging people to ponder upon the mysteries of the universe and the power of the Creator.
orig: والشفع والوتر

translation: And by the night as it recedes.
interpretation: The verse contains an oath by the night as it recedes, indicating the gradual disappearance of the night and the arrival of the day. This image sets the stage for a reflection on the passage of time and the fleeting nature of life. The verse can be interpreted as a reminder of the importance of making the most of one's time and preparing for the end of life, which will come inevitably, just as the night gives way to the day.
orig: والليل إذا يسر

translation: Is there upon him (i.e. Esa/Jesus) any duty of making sin offerings, so that he should be purified?
interpretation: The verse is questioning whether Jesus, the son of Mary, had any obligation to offer sacrifices or atone for sins, as was the custom in Jewish law. The verse implies that Jesus was free from sin and therefore did not need to offer sacrifices or atone for any wrongdoings. This is in line with Islamic teachings that Jesus was a prophet of God, sinless and free from any wrongdoing or imperfection.
orig: هل في ذلك قسم لذي حجر

translation: Have you not seen how your Lord dealt with 'Ad
interpretation: The verse is a rhetorical question asking the reader if they have reflected on how God dealt with the people of 'Ad, a biblical and quranic tribe that is said to have been destroyed by a powerful wind. The verse serves as a reminder of the consequences of disbelief and disobedience towards God, urging the reader to reflect on the fate of past nations who were destroyed as a result of their actions.
orig: ألم تر كيف فعل ربك بعاد

translation: Iram of the pillars
interpretation: The phrase 'Iram of the pillars' is a metaphorical description of a lost ancient civilization that was known for its grand architecture and structures, specifically its 'pillars'. The exact identity of Iram is unknown, but it is believed to have been located in the Arabian Peninsula. The Qur'an mentions Iram as an example of a civilization that was destroyed by God due to its people's arrogance and rejection of God's messengers. The verse serves as a reminder of the transience of human achievements and the importance of heeding God's message.
orig: إرم ذات العماد

translation: She/it is not created of that which is in the earth.
interpretation: The verse speaks of something or someone that is unique and not created from the same elements that make up the earth. This could be interpreted as a reference to the divine or supernatural, emphasizing the otherworldly and extraordinary nature of the subject in question. The verse could be referring to a prophet, an angel, or God Himself, who is not created from the same elements as the earth and its inhabitants.
orig: التي لم يخلق مثلها في البلاد

translation: And Thamud, who hewed out the rocks in the valley.
interpretation: The verse refers to the people of Thamud, who are known in Islamic tradition for their ability to carve and shape rocks. By mentioning this specific characteristic, the verse highlights the power and skill of the Thamud people, making their subsequent destruction by God's punishment all the more striking and impactful. The verse serves as a reminder that no matter how powerful or skilled a people may be, they are still subject to God's will and judgement.
orig: وثمود الذين جابوا الصخر بالواد

translation: And Pharaoh of the stakes
interpretation: The phrase 'And Pharaoh of the stakes' is a reference to the Pharaoh who was a powerful and tyrannical ruler, and who is often referred to in the Qur'an. The phrase 'of the stakes' is thought to refer to Pharaoh's power and authority, as the word for 'stakes' (awtaad) can also mean 'pillars' or 'supports'. This phrase serves to emphasize Pharaoh's strength and position of power, and sets the stage for the Qur'anic narrative in which God sends Moses to confront Pharaoh and call him to account for his oppression of the Israelites.
orig: وفرعون ذي الأوتاد

translation: Those who transgressed in the land
interpretation: The phrase refers to people who have committed transgressions or sins in the land they inhabit. It can also refer to those who have oppressed or wronged others and acted unjustly. The verse serves as a reminder that such actions have consequences and that those who engage in such behavior will be held accountable for their actions.
orig: الذين طغوا في البلاد

translation: And they increased therein much corruption
interpretation: The verse highlights the severity of the actions of the people in a particular place, as they had committed a great deal of corruption and wrongdoing. The verse serves as a warning to those who engage in corruption and transgression, emphasizing the grave consequences of their actions.
orig: فأكثروا فيها الفساد

translation: Pour upon them His punishment, their Lord.
interpretation: The verse describes the punishment that will be inflicted upon a group of people by their Lord. The phrase 'pour upon them' gives a sense of intensity and severity of the punishment, and emphasizes that it will be unavoidable and overwhelming. The verse serves as a warning to those who reject God's message and continue to commit injustices, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the power of God's punishment.
orig: فصب عليهم ربك سوط عذاب

translation: Indeed, your Lord is watchful.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the idea that God is always watching and aware of His creation's actions. The word 'watchful' (مرصاد) implies that God is not only aware but also actively observing and taking note of every occurrence, even the smallest details. This serves as a reminder of God's omniscience and omnipresence, encouraging believers to live their lives in accordance with His will and commandments.
orig: إن ربك لبالمرصاد

translation: But as for man, when his Lord tries him and is generous to him and favors him, he says, 'My Lord has honored me.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the attitude of man when he is tested by his Lord and is subsequently blessed with good fortune. Instead of being grateful and humble, the person boasts and feels superior, attributing his success to his own abilities. The verse serves as a reminder that all blessings come from God and that true gratitude is expressed through humility and good actions.
orig: فأما الإنسان إذا ما ابتلاه ربه فأكرمه ونعمه فيقول ربي أكرمن

translation: And if He tests him, He being fully aware of his capacity, he says, 'My Lord has humiliated me.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about a person who, when faced with a test or hardship from God, instead of being patient and grateful, complains and feels humiliated by his situation. The verse highlights the individual's lack of gratitude and trust in God's wisdom and justice. The verse serves as a reminder to be patient and thankful during times of hardship, and to have faith that God only tests those whom He loves and that there is a greater purpose behind every test or hardship.
orig: وأما إذا ما ابتلاه فقدر عليه رزقه فيقول ربي أهانن

translation: Nay, but you do not honor the orphan
interpretation: The verse highlights the failure of certain individuals to show respect and kindness towards orphans. The word 'nay' is used to negate the idea that people treat orphans well, and emphasizes the opposite, that they do not show them the honor and respect they deserve. The verse serves as a reminder to be kind and compassionate towards those who are vulnerable and in need of care and support.
orig: كلا بل لا تكرمون اليتيم

translation: And do not withhold your charity which has been bestowed upon you.
interpretation: The verse is a command from God to not withhold or hoard the charity and blessings that have been given to the believers. This verse emphasizes the importance of sharing one's wealth and resources with those in need and not being stingy or selfish. The verse serves as a reminder that the blessings and wealth that one has are not solely for their own benefit, but also for the benefit of the wider community and those who are less fortunate. It encourages the believers to be generous and giving, and to use their resources to support and uplift others.
orig: ولا تحاضون على طعام المسكين

translation: And you consume the inheritance with devouring [greed],
interpretation: The verse addresses a group of people who are consuming the inheritance of others with greed and a lack of regard for the rightful owners or the proper distribution of the inheritance. The verse speaks to the immorality of their actions, and the negative consequences that may come from their behavior.
orig: وتأكلون التراث أكلا لما

translation: And you love wealth with a love intense.
interpretation: The verse highlights the intense love and desire that people have for wealth and material possessions. This verse can be seen as a critique of the excessive attachment to wealth, which can distract people from the more important things in life, such as their relationship with God and their duties towards other people. It can also be seen as a warning against the dangers of greed and materialism, which can lead people to engage in unjust and immoral behavior in order to acquire more wealth. Ultimately, the verse reminds us that while wealth can bring comfort and security, it cannot bring true happiness or fulfillment, and that the pursuit of wealth should not come at the expense of one's moral values and spiritual well-being.
orig: وتحبون المال حبا جما

translation: Nay, when the earth is shaken with a mighty shaking.
interpretation: The verse describes a powerful earthquake that shakes the earth. The word 'nay' is used to negate the previous statement and emphasize the severity of the earthquake. The phrase 'when the earth is shaken with a mighty shaking' indicates the intensity and destruction caused by the earthquake. The verse may be seen as a warning of the power and wrath of God, reminding people of their vulnerability and dependence on God's mercy.
orig: كلا إذا دكت الأرض دكا دكا

translation: And your Lord came, and the angels, rank upon rank.
interpretation: The verse describes the majestic and awe-inspiring arrival of God and the angels, arranged in rows or ranks. This verse is often interpreted as a reference to the Day of Judgment, when God will come to judge humanity and the angels will be present as witnesses. The verse conveys a sense of grandeur and solemnity, emphasizing the power and authority of God and the significance of the Day of Judgment.
orig: وجاء ربك والملك صفا صفا

translation: And the Day it (Hell) will be shown, (it will be said): 'Seize him and drag him into the midst of the Blazing Fire.', And then cast him into a chain whose length is the distance between two journeys of the Respite (i.e. a very long chain).', 'Indeed, he used not to believe in Allah, the Most Great,'
interpretation: This verse describes the punishment of unbelievers on the Day of Judgment. They will be seized and dragged into the midst of the Blazing Fire and cast into a chain whose length is the distance between two journeys of the Respite. The verse emphasizes the severity of the punishment and the consequences of disbelief in Allah, the Most Great. It serves as a warning to those who reject the belief in Allah and highlights the ultimate fate of unbelievers on the Day of Judgment.
orig: وجيء يومئذ بجهنم يومئذ يتذكر الإنسان وأنى له الذكرى

translation: He says, 'Would that I had preceded my life!'
interpretation: The verse is a statement of regret made by someone who is looking back on their life and wishes they had made different choices. The person is expressing a desire to go back in time and start over, having learned from their past mistakes. The verse may be interpreted as a reminder to live a life of purpose and meaning, and to consider the consequences of one's actions before it is too late.
orig: يقول يا ليتني قدمت لحياتي

translation: That day, no one will be punished but himself.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the individual responsibility and accountability on the Day of Judgment. Each person will be punished for their own sins and actions, and no one else will bear the consequences on their behalf. This verse serves as a reminder of the importance of personal responsibility, and the significance of individual actions and choices in determining one's fate in the afterlife.
orig: فيومئذ لا يعذب عذابه أحد

translation: And no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the principle of individual responsibility and accountability. Each person is responsible for their own actions and will not be held accountable for the sins or wrongdoings of others. This principle is a fundamental teaching in Islamic belief and serves as a reminder to strive for personal righteousness and avoid following the wrong actions of others.
orig: ولا يوثق وثاقه أحد

translation: O tranquil soul
interpretation: The verse addresses the soul that has found peace and contentment through submission to God. It is a message of praise and encouragement, reminding the soul to maintain its tranquility and continue on the path of righteousness.
